verses.text: And they said <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to each other⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “each to his companion”</note> “Come, let us make bricks and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞burn them thoroughly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “burn to burning”</note> And they had brick for stone and they had tar for mortar.

verses.name: Genesis 11:4
verses.text: And they said, “Come, let us build ourselves a city and a tower whose top <transChange type="added">reaches to</transChange> the heavens. And let us make a name for ourselves, lest we be scattered over the face of the whole earth.”  <div eID="gen112" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 11:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv59"/><div sID="gen113" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv59"/>Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> Yahweh came down to see the city and the tower that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞humankind⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons of Adam” or “sons of humankind”</note> was building.

verses.name: Genesis 11:6
verses.text: And Yahweh said, “Behold, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they are one people with one language⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “one people and one language to all of them”</note> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞this is only the beginning of what they will do⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “and this they begin to do”</note> So<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> now nothing that they intend to do will be impossible for them.

verses.name: Genesis 11:7
verses.text: Come, let us go down and confuse their language there, so that they will not understand <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞each other’s language⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “each the language of his companion”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 11:8
verses.text: So Yahweh scattered them from there over the face of the whole earth, and they stopped building the city.

verses.name: Genesis 11:9
verses.text: Therefore its name was called Babel, for there Yahweh confused the language of the whole earth, and there Yahweh scattered them over the face of the whole earth.  <div eID="gen113" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 11:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv60"/><title type="x-s">The Descendants of Shem</title> <div sID="gen114" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv60"/>These are the generations<note placement="foot">Or “family records”</note> of Shem. When Shem <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞was one hundred years old⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the son of one hundred years”</note> he fathered Arphaxad, two years after the flood.

verses.name: Genesis 11:11
verses.text: And Shem lived five hundred years after he fathered Arphaxad, and he fathered <transChange type="added">other</transChange> sons and daughters.

verses.name: Genesis 11:12
verses.text: When Arphaxad had lived thirty-five years, he fathered Shelah.

verses.name: Genesis 11:13
verses.text: And Arphaxad lived four hundred and three years after he fathered Shelah, and he fathered <transChange type="added">other</transChange> sons and daughters.

verses.name: Genesis 11:14
verses.text: When Shelah had lived thirty years, he fathered Eber.

verses.name: Genesis 11:15
verses.text: And Shelah lived four hundred and three years after he fathered Eber, and he fathered <transChange type="added">other</transChange> sons and daughters.

verses.name: Genesis 11:16
verses.text: When Eber had lived thirty-four years, he fathered Peleg.

verses.name: Genesis 11:17
verses.text: And Eber lived four hundred and thirty years after he fathered Peleg, and he fathered <transChange type="added">other</transChange> sons and daughters.

verses.name: Genesis 11:18
verses.text: When Peleg had lived thirty years, he fathered Reu.

verses.name: Genesis 11:19
verses.text: And Peleg lived two hundred and nine years after he fathered Reu, and he fathered <transChange type="added">other</transChange> sons and daughters.

verses.name: Genesis 11:20
verses.text: When Reu had lived thirty-two years, he fathered Serug.

verses.name: Genesis 11:21
verses.text: And Reu lived two hundred and seven years after he fathered Serug, and he fathered <transChange type="added">other</transChange> sons and daughters.

verses.name: Genesis 11:22
verses.text: When Serug had lived thirty years, he fathered Nahor.

verses.name: Genesis 11:23
verses.text: And Serug lived two hundred years after he fathered Nahor, and he fathered <transChange type="added">other</transChange> sons and daughters.

verses.name: Genesis 11:24
verses.text: When Nahor had lived twenty-nine years, he fathered Terah.

verses.name: Genesis 11:25
verses.text: And Nahor lived one hundred and nineteen years after he fathered Terah, and he fathered <transChange type="added">other</transChange> sons and daughters.

verses.name: Genesis 11:26
verses.text: When Terah had lived seventy years, he fathered Abram, Nahor, and Haran.  <div eID="gen114" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 11:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv61"/><title type="x-s">The Descendants of Terah</title> <div sID="gen115" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv61"/>Now<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> these are the generations<note placement="foot">Or “family records”</note> of Terah. Terah fathered Abram, Nahor, and Haran, and Haran fathered Lot.

verses.name: Genesis 11:28
verses.text: And Haran died in the presence of Terah his father in the land of his birth, in Ur of the Chaldeans.

verses.name: Genesis 11:29
verses.text: And Abram and Nahor took wives for themselves. The name of the wife of Abram <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Sarai, and the name of the wife of Nahor <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Milcah, the daughter of Haran, the father of Milcah and Iscah.

verses.name: Genesis 11:30
verses.text: And Sarai was barren; she had no child.

verses.name: Genesis 11:31
verses.text: And Terah took Abram his son, and Lot, the son of Haran, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his grandson⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the son of his son”</note> and Sarai his daughter-in-law, the wife of Abram his son, and went out with them from Ur of the Chaldeans to go to the land of Canaan. And they went to Haran, and they settled there.

verses.name: Genesis 11:32
verses.text: And the days of Terah <transChange type="added">were</transChange> two hundred and five years, and Terah died in Haran.  <chapter eID="Gen.11"/>

verses.name: Genesis 12:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv62"/><title type="x-s">The Call of Abram</title> <div sID="gen116" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv62"/>And Yahweh said to Abram, “Go out from your land and from your relatives, and from the house of your father, to the land that I will show you.

verses.name: Genesis 12:2
verses.text: And I will make you a great nation, and I will bless you, and I will make your name great. And you will be a blessing.

verses.name: Genesis 12:3
verses.text: And I will bless those who bless you, and those who curse you I will curse. And all families of the earth will be blessed in you.”  <div eID="gen116" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 12:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv63"/><title type="x-s">Abram’s Journey</title> <div sID="gen117" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv63"/>And Abram went <transChange type="added">out</transChange> as Yahweh had told him, and Lot went with him. Now Abram <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞was seventy-five years old⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the son of five years and seventy years”</note> when he went out from Haran.

verses.name: Genesis 12:5
verses.text: And Abram took Sarai his wife, and Lot <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his nephew⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the son of his brother”</note> and all their possessions that they had gathered, and all the persons that they had acquired in Haran, and they went out to go to the land of Canaan. And they went to the land of Canaan.

verses.name: Genesis 12:6
verses.text: And Abram traveled through the land up to the place of Shechem, to the Oak of Moreh. Now the Canaanites <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in the land at that time.

verses.name: Genesis 12:7
verses.text: And Yahweh appeared to Abram and said, “To your offspring I will give this land.” And he built an altar there to Yahweh, who had appeared to him.

verses.name: Genesis 12:8
verses.text: And he moved on from there to the hill country, east of Bethel. And he pitched his tent at Bethel on the west, and at Ai on the east. And he built an altar there to Yahweh. And he called on the name of Yahweh.

verses.name: Genesis 12:9
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And Abram kept moving on⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “And Abram moved on, going and moving on”</note> toward the Negev.

verses.name: Genesis 12:10
verses.text: And there was a famine in the land. And Abram went down to Egypt to dwell as an alien there, for the famine was severe in the land.

verses.name: Genesis 12:11
verses.text: And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> as he drew near to enter into Egypt, he said to Sarai his wife, “Look now, I know that you are a woman beautiful of appearance,

verses.name: Genesis 12:12
verses.text: and it shall happen <transChange type="added">that</transChange>, if the Egyptians see you, then they will say, ‘This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> his wife,’ then they will kill me but let you live.

verses.name: Genesis 12:13
verses.text: Please say you are my sister so that it will go well for me on your account. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Then I will live⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And my soul will live”</note> on account of you.”

verses.name: Genesis 12:14
verses.text: And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> as Abram came into Egypt, the Egyptians saw the woman, that she <transChange type="added">was</transChange> very beautiful.

verses.name: Genesis 12:15
verses.text: And the officials of Pharaoh saw her, and they praised her <transChange type="added">beauty</transChange> to Pharaoh. And the woman was taken to the house of Pharaoh.

verses.name: Genesis 12:16
verses.text: And he dealt well with Abram on account of her, and he had sheep, cattle, male donkeys, male servants, female servants, female donkeys, and camels.

verses.name: Genesis 12:17
verses.text: Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> Yahweh afflicted Pharaoh and his household with severe plagues on account of the matter of Sarai the wife of Abram.

verses.name: Genesis 12:18
verses.text: Then Pharaoh called for Abram and said, “What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> this you have done to me? Why did you not tell me that she <transChange type="added">was</transChange> your wife?

verses.name: Genesis 12:19
verses.text: Why did you say ‘She <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my sister,’ so that I took her to myself as a wife? Now then, here <transChange type="added">is</transChange> your wife. Take her and go.”

verses.name: Genesis 12:20
verses.text: And Pharaoh commanded his men concerning him, and then sent him and his wife and all that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> with him away.  <chapter eID="Gen.12"/>

verses.name: Genesis 13:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv64"/><title type="x-s">The Parting of Abram and Lot</title> <div sID="gen118" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv64"/>Then Abram went up from Egypt, he and his wife and all that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> with him. And Lot <transChange type="added">went</transChange> with him to the Negev.

verses.name: Genesis 13:2
verses.text: Now Abram <transChange type="added">was</transChange> very wealthy in livestock, in silver, and in gold.

verses.name: Genesis 13:3
verses.text: And he went according to his journey from the Negev, then to Bethel, to the place where his tent was at the beginning, between Bethel and Ai,

verses.name: Genesis 13:4
verses.text: to the place where he had made an altar at the beginning. And Abram called on the name of Yahweh there.

verses.name: Genesis 13:5
verses.text: And Lot, who went with Abram, also had herds and tents.

verses.name: Genesis 13:6
verses.text: And the land could not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞support them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “lift them up”</note> so as to live together, because their possessions were so many that<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> they were not able to live together.

verses.name: Genesis 13:7
verses.text: And there was a quarrel between the herdsmen of the livestock of Abram and the herdsmen of the livestock of Lot. Now at that time the Canaanites and the Perizzites were living in the land.

verses.name: Genesis 13:8
verses.text: Then Abram said to Lot, “Please, let there not be quarreling between me and you, and between my shepherds and your shepherds, for we men <transChange type="added">are</transChange> brothers.

verses.name: Genesis 13:9
verses.text: Is not the whole land before you? Separate yourself from me. If <transChange type="added">you want what is on</transChange> the left, then I will go right; if <transChange type="added">you want what is on</transChange> the right, I will go left.”

verses.name: Genesis 13:10
verses.text: And Lot lifted up his eyes and saw the whole plain of the Jordan, that all of it <transChange type="added">was</transChange> well-watered land—<transChange type="added">this was</transChange> before Yahweh destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah—like the garden of Yahweh, like the land of Egypt <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in the direction of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “your going”</note> Zoar.

verses.name: Genesis 13:11
verses.text: So<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> Lot chose for himself all the plain of the Jordan. And Lot journeyed from the east, and so they separated <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from each other⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “each from his brother”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 13:12
verses.text: Abram settled in the land of Canaan, and Lot settled in the cities of the plain. And he pitched his tent toward Sodom.

verses.name: Genesis 13:13
verses.text: Now the men of Sodom <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞were extremely wicked sinners against Yahweh⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “were wicked and sinners against Yahweh very”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 13:14
verses.text: And Yahweh said to Abram after Lot had separated from him, “Now, lift up your eyes and look from the place where you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> to the north, and to the south, and to the east and to the west,

verses.name: Genesis 13:15
verses.text: for all the land which you see I will give to you, and to your descendants, forever.

verses.name: Genesis 13:16
verses.text: I will make your descendants like the dust of the earth which, if anyone were able to count the dust of the earth, your descendants would be <transChange type="added">so</transChange> counted.

verses.name: Genesis 13:17
verses.text: Arise, go through the length of the land and through its breadth, for I will give it to you.”

verses.name: Genesis 13:18
verses.text: So<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> Abram pitched his tent, and he came and settled at the oaks of Mamre, which <transChange type="added">were</transChange> at Hebron. And there he built an altar to Yahweh.  <chapter eID="Gen.13"/>

verses.name: Genesis 14:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv65"/><title type="x-s">Abram Rescues Lot</title> <div sID="gen119" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv65"/>And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> in the days of Amraphel, the king of Shinar, Arioch, the king of Ellasar, Kedorlaomer, the king of Elam, and Tidal, the king of Goiim,

verses.name: Genesis 14:2
verses.text: made war with Bera, the king of Sodom, and Birsha, the king of Gomorrah, Shinab, the king of Admah, and Shemeber, the king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela (that <transChange type="added">is</transChange>, Zoar).

verses.name: Genesis 14:3
verses.text: All these joined forces at the valley of Siddim (that <transChange type="added">is</transChange>, the sea of the salt).

verses.name: Genesis 14:4
verses.text: Twelve years they had served Kedorlaomer, but in the thirteenth year they rebelled.

verses.name: Genesis 14:5
verses.text: In the fourteenth year Kedorlaomer and the kings who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him came and defeated the Rephaim in Ashteroth-Karnaim, and the Zuzim in Ham, and the Emim in Shaveh-Kiriathaim,

verses.name: Genesis 14:6
verses.text: And the Horites in their hill country of Seir, as far as El-Paran, which is at the wilderness.

verses.name: Genesis 14:7
verses.text: Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> they turned back and came to En-Mishpat (that <transChange type="added">is</transChange>, Kadesh). And they defeated the whole territory of the Amalekites, and also the Amorites who were living in Hazazon-Tamar.

verses.name: Genesis 14:8
verses.text: Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> the king of Sodom, the king of Gomorrah, the king of Admah, the king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela (that is, Zoar) went out, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they took up battle position⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And they took up position with them for battle”</note> in the Valley of Siddim

verses.name: Genesis 14:9
verses.text: with Kedorlaomer, king of Elam, and Tidal, king of Goiim, and Amraphel, king of Shinar, and Arioch, king of Ellasar, four kings against five.

verses.name: Genesis 14:10
verses.text: Now<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> the Valley of Siddim <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞was full of tar pits⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “pits, pits of tar”</note> And the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞fell into them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “they fell there”</note> but the rest fled to the mountains.

verses.name: Genesis 14:11
verses.text: So<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> they<note placement="foot">In context, the enemy</note> took all the possessions of Sodom and Gomorrah and all their provisions, and they left.

verses.name: Genesis 14:12
verses.text: And they<note placement="foot">In context, the enemy</note> took Lot, the son of the brother of Abram, and his possessions, and left. (Now he had been living in Sodom.)

verses.name: Genesis 14:13
verses.text: Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> one who escaped came and told Abram the Hebrew. And he was living at the oaks of Mamre the Amorite, brother of Eshcol and brother of Aner. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞They were allies with Abram⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “And they were owners of a covenant of Abram”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 14:14
verses.text: When<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> Abram heard that his <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞relative⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “brother”</note> was taken captive, he summoned his trained men, born in his house, three hundred and eighteen <transChange type="added">of them</transChange>, and he went in pursuit up to Dan.

verses.name: Genesis 14:15
verses.text: And he divided <transChange type="added">his trained men</transChange> against them at night, he and his servants. And he defeated them and pursued them to Hobah, which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> north of Damascus.

verses.name: Genesis 14:16
verses.text: And he brought back all the possessions. And he also brought back Lot, his <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞relative⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “brother”</note> and his possessions, and the women and the people as well.  <div eID="gen119" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 14:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv66"/><title type="x-s">Abram Meets Melchizedek</title> <div sID="gen120" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv66"/>After his return from defeating Kedorlaomer and the kings who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him, the king of Sodom went out to meet him at the Valley of Shaveh (that <transChange type="added">is</transChange>, the Valley of the King).

verses.name: Genesis 14:18
verses.text: And Melchizedek, the king of Salem, brought out bread and wine. (He was the priest of God Most High).

verses.name: Genesis 14:19
verses.text: And he blessed him and said, <div eID="gen120" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen121"/> <l level="1" sID="gen122"/>“Blessed <transChange type="added">be</transChange> Abram by God Most High,<l eID="gen122" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen123"/>Maker of heaven and earth. <l eID="gen123" level="2"/>

verses.name: Genesis 14:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv67"/><l level="1" sID="gen124"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv67"/>And blessed <transChange type="added">be</transChange> God Most High<l eID="gen124" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen125"/>who delivered your enemies into your hand.”<l eID="gen125" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen121"/> <div sID="gen126" type="x-p"/> And he<note placement="foot">That is, Abram</note> gave to him a tenth of everything.

verses.name: Genesis 14:21
verses.text: And the king of Sodom said to Abram, “Give me the people, but the possessions take for yourself.”

verses.name: Genesis 14:22
verses.text: And Abram said to the king of Sodom, “I have raised my hand to Yahweh, God Most High, Maker of heaven and earth,

verses.name: Genesis 14:23
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞that neither a thread nor⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “that not from a thread and up to”</note> a thong of a sandal would I take from all that <transChange type="added">belongs</transChange> to you, that you might not say, ‘I made Abram rich.’

verses.name: Genesis 14:24
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Nothing besides what⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “besides me only which”</note> the servants have eaten and the share of the men who went out with me <transChange type="added">will I take.</transChange> Let Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre take their share.”  <chapter eID="Gen.14"/>

verses.name: Genesis 15:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv68"/><title type="x-s">Yahweh’s Covenant with Abram</title> <div sID="gen127" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv68"/>After these things the word of Yahweh came<note placement="foot">Literally “was”</note> to Abram in a vision, saying: “Do not be afraid, Abram; I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> your shield, <transChange type="added">and</transChange> your reward <transChange type="added">shall be</transChange> very great.”

verses.name: Genesis 15:2
verses.text: Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> Abram said, “O Yahweh, my Lord, what will you give me? <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I continue to be⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “I am going”</note> childless, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞my heir⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the son of the inheritance of my house”</note> is Eliezer of Damascus.”

verses.name: Genesis 15:3
verses.text: And Abram said, “Look, you have not given me a descendant, and here, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a member of my household⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a son of my house”</note> is <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞my heir⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “inheriting me”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 15:4
verses.text: And behold, the word of Yahweh <transChange type="added">came</transChange> to him saying, “This <transChange type="added">person</transChange> will not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞be your heir⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “inherit you”</note> but <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞your own son will be your heir⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “he who goes out from your body, he will inherit you”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 15:5
verses.text: And he brought him outside and said, “Look toward the heavens and count the stars if you are able to count them.” And he said to him, “So shall your offspring be.”

verses.name: Genesis 15:6
verses.text: And he believed in Yahweh, and he reckoned it to him <transChange type="added">as</transChange> righteousness.

verses.name: Genesis 15:7
verses.text: And he said to him, “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> Yahweh, who brought you out from Ur of the Chaldeans to give this land to you, to possess it.”

verses.name: Genesis 15:8
verses.text: And he said, “O Yahweh God, how shall I know <transChange type="added">that</transChange> I will possess it?”

verses.name: Genesis 15:9
verses.text: And he said to him, “Take for me a three-year-old heifer, and a three-year-old female goat, and a three-year-old ram, and a turtledove and a young pigeon.”

verses.name: Genesis 15:10
verses.text: And he took for him all these and cut them in pieces down the middle. And he put each piece opposite <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the other⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “its companion”</note> but the birds he did not cut.

verses.name: Genesis 15:11
verses.text: And the birds of prey came down on the carcasses, but Abram drove them away.

verses.name: Genesis 15:12
verses.text: And it happened, as the sun <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞went down⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to go”</note> then a deep sleep fell upon Abram and, behold, a great terrifying darkness fell upon him.

verses.name: Genesis 15:13
verses.text: And he said to Abram, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞You must surely know⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “knowing you must know”</note> that your descendants shall be as aliens in a land <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞not their own⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “not to them”</note> And they shall serve them<note placement="foot">Some nation hostile to Abram’s descendants (Egypt in later history)</note> and they<note placement="foot">Some nation hostile to Abram’s descendants (Egypt in later history)</note> shall oppress them four hundred years.

verses.name: Genesis 15:14
verses.text: And also the nation that they<note placement="foot">That is, Abram’s descendants</note> serve I will judge. Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> afterward they shall go out with great possessions.

verses.name: Genesis 15:15
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">as for</transChange> you, you shall go to your ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> in peace; you shall be buried in a good old age.

verses.name: Genesis 15:16
verses.text: And the fourth generation shall return here, for the guilt of the Amorites <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞is not yet complete⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “is not complete up to now”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 15:17
verses.text: And after the sun had gone down and it <transChange type="added">was</transChange> dusk, behold, a smoking firepot and a flaming torch passed between those half pieces.

verses.name: Genesis 15:18
verses.text: On that day Yahweh <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞made⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “cut”</note> a covenant with Abram saying, “To your offspring I will give this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the Euphrates river,

verses.name: Genesis 15:19
verses.text: <transChange type="added">the land of</transChange> the Kenites, the Kenizzites, the Kadmonites,

verses.name: Genesis 15:20
verses.text: the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Rephaim,

verses.name: Genesis 15:21
verses.text: the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Girgashites, and the Jebusites.”  <chapter eID="Gen.15"/>

verses.name: Genesis 16:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv69"/><title type="x-s">Sarai and Hagar</title> <div sID="gen128" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv69"/>Now<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> Sarai, the wife of Abram, had borne him no children. And she had a female Egyptian servant, and her name <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Hagar.

verses.name: Genesis 16:2
verses.text: And Sarai said to Abram, “Look, please, Yahweh has prevented me from bearing children. Please go in to my servant; perhaps <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I will have children by her⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “I will be built from her”</note> And Abram listened to the voice of Sarai.

verses.name: Genesis 16:3
verses.text: Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> Sarai, the wife of Abram, took Hagar, her Egyptian servant, after Abram had lived ten years in the land of Canaan, and gave her to Abram her husband as his wife.

verses.name: Genesis 16:4
verses.text: And he went in to Hagar, and she conceived. And <transChange type="added">when</transChange> she<note placement="foot">That is, Hagar</note> saw that she had conceived, then her mistress grew small in her eyes.

verses.name: Genesis 16:5
verses.text: And Sarai said to Abram, “may my harm <transChange type="added">be</transChange> upon you. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I had my servant sleep with you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “I put my servant in your lap”</note> and when she saw that she had conceived, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞she no longer respected me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “I grew small in her eyes”</note> May Yahweh judge between me and you!”

verses.name: Genesis 16:6
verses.text: And Abram said to Sarai, “Look, your servant <transChange type="added">is</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞under your authority⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “in your hand”</note> Do to her that which is good in your eyes.” And Sarai mistreated her, and she<note placement="foot">That is, Hagar</note> fled from her presence.  <div eID="gen128" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 16:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv70"/><title type="x-s">Hagar and the Angel of Yahweh</title> <div sID="gen129" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv70"/>And the angel of Yahweh found her at a spring of water in the wilderness, at the spring by the road of Shur.

verses.name: Genesis 16:8
verses.text: And he said to Hagar, the servant of Sarai, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞From where⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “where from this”</note> have you come, and where are you going?” And she said, “I am fleeing from the presence of Sarai my mistress.”

verses.name: Genesis 16:9
verses.text: Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> the angel of Yahweh said to her, “Return to your mistress and submit yourself under <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞her authority⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “her hand”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 16:10
verses.text: And the angel of Yahweh said to her, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I will greatly multiply⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “multiplying I will multiply”</note> your offspring, so that they cannot be counted for <transChange type="added">their</transChange> abundance.”

verses.name: Genesis 16:11
verses.text: And the angel of Yahweh said to her: <div eID="gen129" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen130"/> <l level="1" sID="gen131"/>“Behold, you are pregnant<l eID="gen131" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen132"/>and shall have a son.<l eID="gen132" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen133"/>And you shall call his name Ishmael,<l eID="gen133" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen134"/>for Yahweh has listened to your suffering. <l eID="gen134" level="2"/>

verses.name: Genesis 16:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv71"/><l level="1" sID="gen135"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv71"/>And he shall be a wild donkey of a man,<l eID="gen135" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen136"/>his hand <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> against everyone,<l eID="gen136" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen137"/>and the hand of everyone <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> against him,<l eID="gen137" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen138"/>and he will live <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in hostility with all his brothers⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “against the face of all his brothers”</note> <l eID="gen138" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen130"/>

verses.name: Genesis 16:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv72"/><div sID="gen139" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv72"/>So<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> she called the name of Yahweh who spoke to her, “You are El-Roi,”<note placement="foot">“God of seeing”</note> for she said, “Here I have seen after he who sees me.”

verses.name: Genesis 16:14
verses.text: Therefore the well was called Beer-Lahai-Roi; behold, it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> between Kadesh and Bered.

verses.name: Genesis 16:15
verses.text: And Hagar had a child for Abram, a son. And Abram called the name of his son whom Hagar bore to him, Ishmael.

verses.name: Genesis 16:16
verses.text: And Abram <transChange type="added">was</transChange> eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael to Abram.  <chapter eID="Gen.16"/>

verses.name: Genesis 17:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv73"/><title type="x-s">Abram and Circumcision, the Sign of the Covenant</title> <div sID="gen140" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv73"/>When<note placement="foot">Literally “And it happened that”</note> Abram was ninety-nine years old Yahweh appeared to Abram. And he said to him, “I am El-Shaddai;<note placement="foot">Often translated, “God Almighty”</note> walk before me and be blameless

verses.name: Genesis 17:2
verses.text: so that<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> I may make my covenant between me and you, and may multiply you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞exceedingly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “with very very”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 17:3
verses.text: Then Abram fell upon his face and God spoke with him, saying,

verses.name: Genesis 17:4
verses.text: “<transChange type="added">As for</transChange> me, behold, my covenant <transChange type="added">shall be</transChange> with you, and you shall be the father of a multitude of nations.

verses.name: Genesis 17:5
verses.text: Your name shall no longer be called Abram, but your name shall be Abraham, for I will make you the father of a multitude of nations.

verses.name: Genesis 17:6
verses.text: And I will make you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞exceedingly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “with very very”</note> fruitful. I will make you a nation, and kings shall go out from you.

verses.name: Genesis 17:7
verses.text: And I will establish my covenant between me and you, and between your offspring after you, throughout their generations as an everlasting covenant to be as God for you and to your offspring after you.

verses.name: Genesis 17:8
verses.text: And I will give to you and to your offspring after you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the land in which you are living as an alien⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “a land of your sojournings”</note> all the land of Canaan, as an everlasting property. And I will be to them as God.”  <div eID="gen140" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 17:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv74"/><div sID="gen141" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv74"/>And God said to Abraham, “Now <transChange type="added">as for</transChange> you, you must keep my covenant, you and your offspring after you, throughout their generations.

verses.name: Genesis 17:10
verses.text: This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my covenant which you shall keep, between me and you, and <transChange type="added">also</transChange> with<note placement="foot">Or “between”</note> your offspring after you: Every male among you shall be circumcised.

verses.name: Genesis 17:11
verses.text: And you shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin, and it shall be a sign of the covenant between me and you.

verses.name: Genesis 17:12
verses.text: And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞at eight days of age⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a son of eight days”</note> you shall yourselves circumcise every male belonging to your generations and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the servant born in your house and the one bought from any foreigner⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “those born of house and acquisition of money from every son of a foreigner”</note> who is not from your offspring.

verses.name: Genesis 17:13
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞You must certainly circumcise⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “circumcising you will circumcise”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the servant born in your house and the one bought from any foreigner⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “those born of house and acquisition of money from every son of a foreigner”</note> And my covenant shall be with your flesh as an everlasting covenant.

verses.name: Genesis 17:14
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">as for any</transChange> uncircumcised male who has not circumcised the flesh of his foreskin, that person shall be cut off from his<note placement="foot">Literally “her”; the reference is still to a male; the pronoun is feminine because “person” (<hi type="italic">nephesh</hi>) is grammatically feminine</note> people. He has broken my covenant.

verses.name: Genesis 17:15
verses.text: And God said to Abraham, “<transChange type="added">as for</transChange> Sarai your wife, you shall not call her name Sarai, for Sarah <transChange type="added">shall be</transChange> her name.

verses.name: Genesis 17:16
verses.text: And I will bless her; moreover, I give to you from her a son. And I will bless her, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞she shall give rise to nations⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “she shall become to nations”</note> Kings of peoples shall come<note placement="foot">Or “be”</note> from her.”

verses.name: Genesis 17:17
verses.text: And Abraham fell upon his face and laughed. And he said in his heart, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Can a child be born to a man a hundred years old⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to a man one hundred years old can he be born?”</note> or <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞can Sarah bear a child at ninety⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?”<note placement="foot">Literally “can ninety-year-old Sarah bear a child?”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 17:18
verses.text: And Abraham said to God, “Oh that Ishmael might live before you!”

verses.name: Genesis 17:19
verses.text: And God said, “No, but Sarah your wife shall bear a son for you, and you shall call his name Isaac. And I will establish my covenant with him as an everlasting covenant to his offspring after him.

verses.name: Genesis 17:20
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">as for</transChange> Ishmael, I have heard you. Behold, I will bless him and I will make him fruitful, and I will multiply him <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞exceedingly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “with very very”</note> He shall father twelve princes, and I will make him a great nation.

verses.name: Genesis 17:21
verses.text: But my covenant I will establish with Isaac, whom Sarah shall bear to you at this appointed time next year.”

verses.name: Genesis 17:22
verses.text: When<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> he finished speaking with him, God went up from Abraham.

verses.name: Genesis 17:23
verses.text: And Abraham took Ishmael his son and all who were born of his house, and all <transChange type="added">those</transChange> acquired by his money, every male among the men of Abraham’s house, and he circumcised the flesh of their foreskin on the same day that God spoke with him.

verses.name: Genesis 17:24
verses.text: Abraham <transChange type="added">was</transChange> ninety-nine years old when he circumcised the flesh of his foreskin.

verses.name: Genesis 17:25
verses.text: And Ishmael his son <transChange type="added">was</transChange> thirteen years old when he circumcised the flesh of his foreskin.

verses.name: Genesis 17:26
verses.text: Abraham and his son Ishmael <transChange type="added">were</transChange> circumcised on the same day.

verses.name: Genesis 17:27
verses.text: And all the men of his house, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞those born in the house, and those acquired by money from a foreigner⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “born of house and acquisition of money from the son of a foreigner”</note> were circumcised with him.  <chapter eID="Gen.17"/>

verses.name: Genesis 18:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv75"/><title type="x-s">Yahweh Appears to Abraham as a Man</title> <div sID="gen142" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv75"/>And Yahweh appeared to him<note placement="foot">Abraham</note> by the oaks of Mamre. And he was sitting in the doorway of the tent at the heat of the day.

verses.name: Genesis 18:2
verses.text: And he lifted up his eyes and saw, and behold, three men were standing near<note placement="foot">Or “by”; the context requires some distance for Abraham to run to them</note> him. And he saw <transChange type="added">them</transChange> and ran from the doorway of the tent to meet them. And he bowed down to the ground.

verses.name: Genesis 18:3
verses.text: And he said, “My lord, if I have found favor in your eyes do not pass by your servant.

verses.name: Genesis 18:4
verses.text: Let a little water be brought and wash your feet, and rest under the tree.

verses.name: Genesis 18:5
verses.text: And let me bring a piece of bread, then<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> refresh <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞yourselves⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “your heart”</note> Afterward you can pass on, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞once⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for therefore”</note> you have passed by with your servant.” Then they said, “Do so as you have said.”

verses.name: Genesis 18:6
verses.text: Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> Abraham hastened into the tent to Sarah, and he said, “Quickly—make three seahs of fine flour for kneading and make bread cakes!”

verses.name: Genesis 18:7
verses.text: And Abraham ran to the cattle and took a <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞calf⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “a son of cattle”</note> tender and good, and gave it to the servant, and he made haste to prepare it.

verses.name: Genesis 18:8
verses.text: Then he took curds and milk, and the calf which he prepared, and set <transChange type="added">it</transChange> before them. And he was standing by them under the tree while<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> they ate.

verses.name: Genesis 18:9
verses.text: And they said to him, “Where <transChange type="added">is</transChange> Sarah your wife?” And he said, “Here, in the tent.”

verses.name: Genesis 18:10
verses.text: And he<note placement="foot">Yahweh</note> said, “I will certainly return to you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in the spring⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “at the time of life”</note> and look, Sarah your wife <transChange type="added">will have</transChange> a son.” Now Sarah <transChange type="added">was</transChange> listening at the doorway of the tent, and which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> behind him.

verses.name: Genesis 18:11
verses.text: Now Abraham and Sarah <transChange type="added">were</transChange> old, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞advanced in age⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “going in the days”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the way of women⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the road according to women”</note> had ceased to be for Sarah.

verses.name: Genesis 18:12
verses.text: So<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> Sarah laughed to herself saying, “After I am worn out and my husband is old, shall <transChange type="added">this</transChange> pleasure be to me?”

verses.name: Genesis 18:13
verses.text: Then Yahweh said to Abraham, “What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> this <transChange type="added">that</transChange> Sarah laughed, saying, ‘Is it indeed true <transChange type="added">that</transChange> I will bear a child, now <transChange type="added">that</transChange> I have grown old?’

verses.name: Genesis 18:14
verses.text: Is anything too difficult for Yahweh? At the appointed time I will return to you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in the spring⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “at the time of life”</note> and Sarah <transChange type="added">shall have</transChange> a son.”

verses.name: Genesis 18:15
verses.text: But Sarah denied <transChange type="added">it</transChange>, saying, “I did not laugh,” because she was afraid. He<note placement="foot">Yahweh</note> said, “No, but you did laugh.”  <div eID="gen142" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 18:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv76"/><div sID="gen143" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv76"/>Then the men set out from there, and they looked down upon Sodom. And Abraham went with them <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to send them on their way⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “to send them away”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 18:17
verses.text: Then Yahweh said, “Shall I conceal from Abraham what I <transChange type="added">am going</transChange> to do?

verses.name: Genesis 18:18
verses.text: Abraham will surely become a great and strong nation, and all the nations of the earth will be blessed on account of him.

verses.name: Genesis 18:19
verses.text: For I have chosen<note placement="foot">Or “have known”</note> him, that he will command his children and his household after him that they will keep the way of Yahweh, to do righteousness and justice, so that Yahweh may bring upon Abraham that which he said to him.”

verses.name: Genesis 18:20
verses.text: Then Yahweh said, “Because the outcry of Sodom and Gomorrah <transChange type="added">is</transChange> great and because their sin <transChange type="added">is</transChange> very <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞serious⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “heavy”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 18:21
verses.text: I will go down and I will see. Have they done altogether according to its cry of distress <transChange type="added">which</transChange> has come to me? If not, I will know.”  <div eID="gen143" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 18:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv77"/><title type="x-s">Abraham Intercedes for Sodom</title> <div sID="gen144" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv77"/>And the men turned from there and went toward Sodom. And Abraham <transChange type="added">was</transChange> still standing before Yahweh.

verses.name: Genesis 18:23
verses.text: And Abraham drew near <transChange type="added">to Yahweh</transChange> and said, “Will you also sweep away the righteous with the wicked?

verses.name: Genesis 18:24
verses.text: If perhaps there are fifty righteous in the midst of the city, will you also sweep <transChange type="added">them</transChange> away and not forgive the place on account of the fifty righteous in her midst?

verses.name: Genesis 18:25
verses.text: Far be it from you to do such a thing as this, to kill <transChange type="added">the</transChange> righteous with <transChange type="added">the</transChange> wicked, that<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> the righteous would be as the wicked! Far be it from you! Will not the Judge of all the earth do justice?”

verses.name: Genesis 18:26
verses.text: And Yahweh said, “If I find fifty righteous in Sodom, in the midst of the city, then I will forgive the whole place for their sake.”

verses.name: Genesis 18:27
verses.text: Then Abraham answered and said, “Look, please, I was bold to speak to my Lord, but I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> dust and ashes.

verses.name: Genesis 18:28
verses.text: Perhaps the fifty righteous are lacking five—will you destroy the whole city on account of the five?” And he answered, “I will not destroy <transChange type="added">it</transChange> if I find forty-five there.”

verses.name: Genesis 18:29
verses.text: And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞once again he spoke⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And he added again to speak”</note> to him and said, “What if<note placement="foot">Or “Perhaps”</note> forty are found there?” And he answered, “I will not do <transChange type="added">it</transChange> on account of the forty.”

verses.name: Genesis 18:30
verses.text: And he said, “Please, let not my Lord be angry, and I will speak. What if<note placement="foot">Or “Perhaps”</note> thirty be found there?” And he answered, “I will not do <transChange type="added">it</transChange> if I find thirty there.”

verses.name: Genesis 18:31
verses.text: And he said, “Please, now, I was bold to speak to my Lord. What if<note placement="foot">Or “Perhaps”</note> twenty be found there?” And he answered, “I will not destroy <transChange type="added">it</transChange> for the sake of the twenty.”

verses.name: Genesis 18:32
verses.text: And he said, “Please, let not my Lord be angry, and I will speak only once more. What if<note placement="foot">Or “Perhaps”</note> ten are found there?” And he answered, “I will not destroy <transChange type="added">it</transChange> for the sake of the ten.”

verses.name: Genesis 18:33
verses.text: Then Yahweh left,<note placement="foot">Or “went”</note> as he finished speaking to Abraham, and Abraham returned to his place.  <chapter eID="Gen.18"/>

verses.name: Genesis 19:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv78"/><title type="x-s">The Rescue of Lot from Sodom</title> <div sID="gen145" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv78"/>And the two angels came to Sodom in the evening. And Lot was sitting in the gateway of Sodom. Then Lot saw <transChange type="added">them</transChange> and stood up to meet them. And he bowed down <transChange type="added">with his</transChange> face to the ground.

verses.name: Genesis 19:2
verses.text: And he said, “Behold, my lords, please turn aside into the house of your servant and spend the night and wash your feet. Then you can rise early and go on your way.” And they said, “No, but we will spend the night in the square.”

verses.name: Genesis 19:3
verses.text: But <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he urged them strongly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “he pressed upon them very”</note> and they turned aside with him and came into his house. And he made a meal for them and baked unleavened bread, and they ate.

verses.name: Genesis 19:4
verses.text: Before they laid down, the men of the city, the men of Sodom, both young and old, all the people <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to the last man⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “from the end”</note> surrounded the house.

verses.name: Genesis 19:5
verses.text: And they called to Lot and said to him, “Where <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the men who came to you tonight? Bring them out to us so that we may know<note placement="foot">Hebrew idiom for sexual intercourse (cp. <reference osisRef="Gen.4.1">Gen 4:1</reference>)</note> them.”

verses.name: Genesis 19:6
verses.text: But Lot went out to them at the entrance, and he shut the door behind him.

verses.name: Genesis 19:7
verses.text: And he said, “No, my brothers, please do not do <transChange type="added">such a</transChange> wrong <transChange type="added">thing</transChange>.

verses.name: Genesis 19:8
verses.text: Behold, I have two daughters who have not known<note placement="foot">Hebrew idiom for sexual intercourse (cp. <reference osisRef="Gen.4.1">Gen 4:1</reference>)</note> a man. Please, let me bring them out to you; then do to them as it seems good in your eyes. Only to these men do not do this thing, since they came under<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞ my roof⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “my beam”</note> for protection.”

verses.name: Genesis 19:9
verses.text: But they said, “Step aside!” Then they said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞This fellow⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the one”</note> came to dwell as a foreigner and he acts as a judge! Now we shall do worse to you than them!” And they pressed very hard against the man, against Lot, and they drew near to break the door.

verses.name: Genesis 19:10
verses.text: Then the men reached out <transChange type="added">with</transChange> their hands and brought Lot in to them, into the house, and they shut the door.

verses.name: Genesis 19:11
verses.text: And the men who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> at the entrance of the house they struck with blindness, both small and great, and they were unable to find the entrance.

verses.name: Genesis 19:12
verses.text: Then the men said to Lot, “Who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> here with you? Bring out from the place <transChange type="added">your</transChange> sons-in-law, and your sons and your daughters, and all who <transChange type="added">are</transChange> with you in the city.

verses.name: Genesis 19:13
verses.text: For we are <transChange type="added">about to</transChange> destroy this place, because their cry has become great before Yahweh. Yahweh sent us to destroy it.”

verses.name: Genesis 19:14
verses.text: Then Lot went out and spoke to his sons-in-law <transChange type="added">who were</transChange> taking<note placement="foot">That is, marrying</note> his daughters and said, “Get up! Go out from this place, because Yahweh is going to destroy the city!” But <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞it seemed like a joke⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “it was as one making fun”</note> in the eyes of his sons-in-law.

verses.name: Genesis 19:15
verses.text: And as the dawn came up the angels urged Lot saying, “Get up, take your wife and your two daughters <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who are staying with you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “who are found”</note> lest you be destroyed with the punishment of the city.”

verses.name: Genesis 19:16
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">when</transChange> he lingered, the men seized him by his hand and his wife’s hand, and his two daughters by hand, on account of the mercy of Yahweh upon him. And they brought him out and set him outside of the city.

verses.name: Genesis 19:17
verses.text: And after bringing them outside <transChange type="added">one</transChange> said, “Flee for your life; do not look behind you, and do not stand anywhere in the plain. Flee to the mountains lest you be destroyed.”

verses.name: Genesis 19:18
verses.text: And Lot said to them, “No, please, my lords.

verses.name: Genesis 19:19
verses.text: Behold, your servant has found favor in your eyes and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you have shown me great kindness⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “your kindness which you have done to me you have made great”</note> in saving my life. But I cannot flee to the mountains, lest the disaster overtake me and I die.

verses.name: Genesis 19:20
verses.text: Behold, this city <transChange type="added">is</transChange> near <transChange type="added">enough</transChange> to flee there, and it <transChange type="added">is a</transChange> little <transChange type="added">one</transChange>. Please, let me flee there. Is it not a little <transChange type="added">one</transChange>? Then my life shall be saved.”

verses.name: Genesis 19:21
verses.text: And he said to him, “Behold, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I will grant this favor as well⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “I am lifting up your face also concerning this thing”</note> that I will not overthrow the city of which you have spoken.

verses.name: Genesis 19:22
verses.text: Escape there quickly, for I cannot do <transChange type="added">this</transChange> thing until you get there.” Therefore, there name of the city was called Zoar.  <div eID="gen145" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 19:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv79"/><title type="x-s">The Destruction of Sodom</title> <div sID="gen146" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv79"/><transChange type="added">After</transChange> the sun <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞had risen⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “had gone out”</note> upon the earth and Lot had entered Zoar,

verses.name: Genesis 19:24
verses.text: Yahweh rained down from heaven upon Sodom and Gomorrah brimstone and fire from Yahweh.

verses.name: Genesis 19:25
verses.text: And he overthrew those cities and the whole plain, and the inhabitants of the cities and the vegetation of the ground.

verses.name: Genesis 19:26
verses.text: But his<note placement="foot">That is, Lot’s</note> wife looked <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞back⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “behind him”</note> and she became a pillar of salt.

verses.name: Genesis 19:27
verses.text: And Abraham arose early in the morning <transChange type="added">and went</transChange> to the place where he had stood before Yahweh.

verses.name: Genesis 19:28
verses.text: And he looked down upon the surface of Sodom and Gomorrah, and upon the whole surface of the land, the plain. And he saw that,<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> behold, the smoke of the land went up like the smoke of a smelting furnace.

verses.name: Genesis 19:29
verses.text: So it was, when God destroyed the cities of the plain that God remembered Abraham and sent Lot out from the midst of the overthrow, when he overthrew the cities in which Lot lived.  <div eID="gen146" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 19:30
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv80"/><title type="x-s">Lot and His Daughters</title> <div sID="gen147" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv80"/>And Lot went out from Zoar and settled in the hill country<note placement="foot">Or “mountain”</note> with his two daughters, for he was afraid to stay in Zoar. So he lived in a cave, he and his two daughters.

verses.name: Genesis 19:31
verses.text: And the firstborn <transChange type="added">daughter</transChange> said to the younger one, “Our father is old, and there is no man in the land to come in to us according to the manner of all the land.

verses.name: Genesis 19:32
verses.text: Come, let us give our father wine to drink and let us lie with him<note placement="foot">Idiom for “have sexual intercourse with him”</note> that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞we may secure descendants through our father⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “that we might preserve offspring from our father”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 19:33
verses.text: And they gave their father wine to drink that night, and the firstborn went and lay with her father, but he did not know when she lay down or when she got up.

verses.name: Genesis 19:34
verses.text: And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange>, the next day the firstborn said to the younger one, “Look, I laid with my father last night. Let us give him wine to drink also tonight, then go and lie with him that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞we may secure descendants through our father⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “that we might preserve offspring from our father”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 19:35
verses.text: And they gave their father wine to drink again that night, and the younger got up and lay with him, but he did not know when she lay down or when she got up.

verses.name: Genesis 19:36
verses.text: And the two daughters of Lot became pregnant by their father.

verses.name: Genesis 19:37
verses.text: The firstborn gave birth to a son, and she called his name Moab. He <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the father of Moab until this day.

verses.name: Genesis 19:38
verses.text: And the younger, she also gave birth to a son, and she called his name Ben-Ammi. He <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the father of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> until this day.  <chapter eID="Gen.19"/>

verses.name: Genesis 20:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv81"/><title type="x-s">Abraham and Abimelech</title> <div sID="gen148" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv81"/>And Abraham journeyed from there to the land of the Negev, and he settled between Kadesh and Shur. And he dwelled as an alien in Gerar.

verses.name: Genesis 20:2
verses.text: And Abraham said about Sarah his wife, “She <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my sister.” And Abimelech king of Gerar sent and took Sarah.

verses.name: Genesis 20:3
verses.text: And God came to Abimelech in a dream at night. And he said to him, “Look, you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> a dead man on account of the woman you have taken. For she <transChange type="added">is</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a married woman⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “married of a husband” or “a woman owned by a husband”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 20:4
verses.text: Now Abimelech had not approached her, so he said, “my Lord, will you even kill a righteous people?”

verses.name: Genesis 20:5
verses.text: Did not he himself say to me, ‘She <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my sister’? And she herself said, ‘He <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my brother.’ With integrity of my heart and with cleanness of my hands I did this.”

verses.name: Genesis 20:6
verses.text: Then God said to him in the dream, “Yes,<note placement="foot">Or “Also”</note> I know that in the integrity of your heart you did this, and I also <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞kept you from sinning⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “kept back from sinning”</note> against me. Therefore, I did not allow you to touch her.

verses.name: Genesis 20:7
verses.text: So now, return the wife of the man, for he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a prophet, so that he will pray for you and you will live. And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞if you do not return her⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “If there is not for you a returning”</note> know that you will certainly die, and all that <transChange type="added">are</transChange> yours.”  <div eID="gen148" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 20:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv82"/><div sID="gen149" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv82"/>So Abimelech rose early in the morning. And he called all his servants and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞told them all these things⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “said all these things in their ears”</note> and the men were very afraid.

verses.name: Genesis 20:9
verses.text: And Abimelech called for Abraham and said to him, “What have you done to us? And how have I sinned against you that you brought upon me and upon my kingdom a great sin? You have done things to me that should not be done.”

verses.name: Genesis 20:10
verses.text: And Abimelech said to Abraham, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞What were you thinking⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “What have you seen?”</note> that you did this thing?”

verses.name: Genesis 20:11
verses.text: And Abraham said, “Because I thought, surely there is no fear of God in this place; they will kill me on account of the matter of my wife.

verses.name: Genesis 20:12
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Besides⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “And also moreover”</note> she <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my sister, the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother. And she became my wife.

verses.name: Genesis 20:13
verses.text: And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> as God caused me to wander from the house of my father I said to her, ‘This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> your loyal kindness that you must do for me at every place where we come: say concerning me, “He <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my brother.” ’ ”

verses.name: Genesis 20:14
verses.text: And Abimelech took sheep and cattle and male slaves and female slaves, and he gave <transChange type="added">them</transChange> to Abraham. And he returned Sarah his wife to him.

verses.name: Genesis 20:15
verses.text: And Abimelech said, “Here <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my land before you; settle <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞where it pleases you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “in the good in your eyes”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 20:16
verses.text: And to Sarah he said, “Look, I have given a thousand <transChange type="added">pieces of</transChange> silver to your brother. It <transChange type="added">shall be</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞an exoneration⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “a covering of the eyes”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞You are vindicated before all who are with you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “to all who are with you and with all you are vindicated”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 20:17
verses.text: And Abraham prayed to God, and God healed Abimelech and his wife and his female servants so that they <transChange type="added">could</transChange> bear children <transChange type="added">again</transChange>.

verses.name: Genesis 20:18
verses.text: For Yahweh had completely closed up all the wombs of the house of Abimelech because of the matter of Sarah, the wife of Abraham.  <chapter eID="Gen.20"/>

verses.name: Genesis 21:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv83"/><title type="x-s">The Birth of Isaac</title> <div sID="gen150" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv83"/>And Yahweh visited Sarah as he had said. And Yahweh did to Sarah as he had promised.

verses.name: Genesis 21:2
verses.text: And she conceived, and Sarah bore to Abraham a son in his old age at the appointed time that God had told him.

verses.name: Genesis 21:3
verses.text: And Abraham called the name of his son who was born to him, whom Sarah bore to him, Isaac.

verses.name: Genesis 21:4
verses.text: And Abraham circumcised Isaac his son <transChange type="added">when he was</transChange> eight days old, as God had commanded him.

verses.name: Genesis 21:5
verses.text: And Abraham <transChange type="added">was</transChange> one hundred years old when Isaac his son was born to him.

verses.name: Genesis 21:6
verses.text: And Sarah said, “God has made laughter for me; all who hear will laugh for me.”

verses.name: Genesis 21:7
verses.text: And she said, “Who would announce to Abraham <transChange type="added">that</transChange> Sarah would nurse children? Yet I have borne a son <transChange type="added">to Abraham</transChange> in his old age.”  <div eID="gen150" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 21:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv84"/><title type="x-s">Hagar and Ishmael</title> <div sID="gen151" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv84"/>And the child grew and was weaned. And Abraham made a great feast on the day Isaac was weaned.

verses.name: Genesis 21:9
verses.text: And Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian, whom she had borne Abraham, mocking.

verses.name: Genesis 21:10
verses.text: Then she said to Abraham, “Drive out this slave woman and her son, for the son of this slave woman will not be heir with my son, with Isaac.”

verses.name: Genesis 21:11
verses.text: And the matter <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞displeased Abraham very much⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “was very bad in the eyes of Abraham”</note> on account of his son.

verses.name: Genesis 21:12
verses.text: Then God said to Abraham, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Do not be displeased⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Do not let it be bad”</note> on account of the boy and on account of the slave woman. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Listen to everything that Sarah said to you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “Everything Sarah said to you, listen with respect to her voice”</note> for through Isaac <transChange type="added">your</transChange> offspring will be named.

verses.name: Genesis 21:13
verses.text: And I will also make the son of the slave woman into a nation, for he is your offspring.”

verses.name: Genesis 21:14
verses.text: Then Abraham rose up early in the morning and took bread and a skin of water and gave <transChange type="added">it</transChange> to Hagar, putting <transChange type="added">it</transChange> on her shoulder. And he sent her away with the child, and she went, wandering about in the wilderness, in Beersheba.

verses.name: Genesis 21:15
verses.text: And when the water was finished from the skin, she put the child under one of the bushes.

verses.name: Genesis 21:16
verses.text: And she went and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞she sat a good distance away⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “she sat with respect to her, opposite, far away, as the shooting of a bow”</note> for she said, “Let me not see the child’s death.” So she sat away from him and lifted up her voice and wept.

verses.name: Genesis 21:17
verses.text: And God heard the cry<note placement="foot">Or “voice”</note> of the boy and the angel of God called to Hagar from the heavens and said to her, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞What is the matter⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “What to you”</note> Hagar? Do not be afraid, for God has heard the cry<note placement="foot">Or “voice”</note> of the boy <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from where he is⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “in which he is there”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 21:18
verses.text: Get up, take up the boy and take him with your hand, for I will make him a great nation.”

verses.name: Genesis 21:19
verses.text: And God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water. And she went and filled the skin with water and gave a drink to the boy.

verses.name: Genesis 21:20
verses.text: And God was with the boy, and he grew and lived in the wilderness. And he became <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞an expert with a bow⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “an archer with the bow”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 21:21
verses.text: And he lived in the wilderness of Paran. And his mother took a wife for him from the land of Egypt.  <div eID="gen151" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 21:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv85"/><title type="x-s">The Covenant Between Abraham and Abimelech</title> <div sID="gen152" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv85"/>And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> at that time, Abimelech and Phicol, the commander of his army, said to Abraham, “God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> with you, in all that you do.

verses.name: Genesis 21:23
verses.text: So now, swear to me here by God <transChange type="added">that</transChange> you will not deal with me falsely, or with my descendants, or my posterity. According to the kindness that I have done to you, you shall <transChange type="added">pledge</transChange> to do with me and with the land where you have dwelled as an alien.”

verses.name: Genesis 21:24
verses.text: And Abraham said, “I swear.”

verses.name: Genesis 21:25
verses.text: Then Abraham complained to Abimelech on account of the well of water that servants of Abimelech had seized.

verses.name: Genesis 21:26
verses.text: And Abimelech said, “I do not know who did this thing, neither did you tell me, nor have I heard <transChange type="added">of it</transChange> except for today.”

verses.name: Genesis 21:27
verses.text: And Abraham took sheep and cattle and gave <transChange type="added">them</transChange> to Abimelech. And the two of them <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞made⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “cut”</note> a covenant.

verses.name: Genesis 21:28
verses.text: Then Abraham set <transChange type="added">off</transChange> seven ewe-lambs of the flock by themselves.

verses.name: Genesis 21:29
verses.text: And Abimelech said to Abraham, “What <transChange type="added">is the meaning of</transChange> these seven ewe-lambs that you have set <transChange type="added">off</transChange> by themselves?”

verses.name: Genesis 21:30
verses.text: And he said, “You shall take the seven ewe-lambs from my hand <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as proof on my behalf⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for the sake that it shall be a witness for me”</note> that I dug this well.”

verses.name: Genesis 21:31
verses.text: Therefore that place is called Beersheba, because there the two of them swore an oath.

verses.name: Genesis 21:32
verses.text: And they <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞made⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “cut”</note> a covenant at Beersheba. And Abimelech, and Phicol his army commander stood and returned to the land of the Philistines.

verses.name: Genesis 21:33
verses.text: And he<note placement="foot">That is, Abraham</note> planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba, and there he called on the name of Yahweh, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the everlasting God⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “El-Olam”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 21:34
verses.text: And Abraham dwelled as an alien in the land of the Philistines many days.  <chapter eID="Gen.21"/>

verses.name: Genesis 22:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv86"/><title type="x-s">God Tests Abraham</title> <div sID="gen153" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv86"/>And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> after these things, God tested Abraham. And he said to him, “Abraham!” And he said, “Here I <transChange type="added">am</transChange>.”

verses.name: Genesis 22:2
verses.text: And he said, “Take your son, your only child, Isaac, whom you love, and go to the land of Moriah, and offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains where<note placement="foot">Or “that”</note> I will tell you.”

verses.name: Genesis 22:3
verses.text: And Abraham rose up early in the morning and saddled his donkey. And he took two of his servants with him, and Isaac his son. And he chopped wood for a burnt offering. And he got up and went to the place which God had told him.

verses.name: Genesis 22:4
verses.text: On the third day Abraham lifted up his eyes, and he saw the place at a distance.

verses.name: Genesis 22:5
verses.text: And Abraham said to his servants, “You stay here with the donkey, and I and the boy will go up there. We will worship, then we will return to you.”

verses.name: Genesis 22:6
verses.text: And Abraham took the wood of the burnt offering and placed <transChange type="added">it</transChange> on Isaac his son. And he took the fire in his hand and the knife, and the two of them went together.

verses.name: Genesis 22:7
verses.text: And Isaac said to Abraham his father, “My father!” And he said, “Here I <transChange type="added">am</transChange>, my son.” And he said, “Here is the fire and the wood, but where is the lamb for a burnt offering?”

verses.name: Genesis 22:8
verses.text: And Abraham said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞God will provide⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “God will see to it” or “God will see for himself”</note> the lamb for a burnt offering, my son.” And the two of them went together.  <div eID="gen153" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 22:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv87"/><div sID="gen154" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv87"/>And they came to the place that God had told him. And Abraham built an altar there and arranged the wood. Then he bound Isaac his son and placed him on the altar atop the wood.

verses.name: Genesis 22:10
verses.text: And Abraham stretched out his hand and took the knife to slaughter his son.

verses.name: Genesis 22:11
verses.text: And the angel of Yahweh called to him from heaven and said, “Abraham! Abraham!” And he said, “Here I <transChange type="added">am</transChange>.”

verses.name: Genesis 22:12
verses.text: And he said, “Do not stretch out your hand against the boy; do not do anything to him.
