For now I know that you are <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞one who fears⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a fearer”</note> God, since you have not withheld your son, your only child, from me.”

verses.name: Genesis 22:13
verses.text: And Abraham lifted up his eyes and looked. And behold, a ram was caught in the thicket by his horns. And Abraham went and took the ram, and offered it as a burnt offering in place of his son.

verses.name: Genesis 22:14
verses.text: And Abraham called the name of that place “Yahweh <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞will provide⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,”<note placement="foot">Literally “will see”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞for which reason⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “which”</note> it is said today, “on the mountain of Yahweh <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞it shall be provided⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “it/he shall be seen”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 22:15
verses.text: And the angel of Yahweh called to Abraham a second time from heaven.

verses.name: Genesis 22:16
verses.text: And he said, “I swear by myself, declares Yahweh, that because you have done this thing and have not withheld your son, your only child,

verses.name: Genesis 22:17
verses.text: that I will certainly bless you and greatly multiply your offspring as the stars of heaven, and as the sand that is by the shore of the sea. And your offspring will take possession of the gate of his enemies.

verses.name: Genesis 22:18
verses.text: All the nations of the earth will be blessed through your offspring, because you have listened to my voice.”

verses.name: Genesis 22:19
verses.text: And Abraham returned to his servants, and they got up and went together to Beersheba. And Abraham lived in Beersheba.  <div eID="gen154" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 22:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv88"/><div sID="gen155" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv88"/>And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> after these things, it was told to Abraham, “Look, Milcah has also borne children to your brother Nahor:

verses.name: Genesis 22:21
verses.text: Uz his firstborn and Buz his brother, and Kemuel the father of Aram,

verses.name: Genesis 22:22
verses.text: and Kesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel.”

verses.name: Genesis 22:23
verses.text: (Now, Bethuel fathered Rebekah). These eight Milcah bore to Nahor, the brother of Abraham.

verses.name: Genesis 22:24
verses.text: And his concubine, whose name was Reumah, also bore Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah.  <chapter eID="Gen.22"/>

verses.name: Genesis 23:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv89"/><title type="x-s">Sarah’s Death and Burial</title> <div sID="gen156" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv89"/>And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Sarah lived⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the lives of Sarah were”</note> one hundred and twenty-seven years; <transChange type="added">these were</transChange> the years of the life of Sarah.

verses.name: Genesis 23:2
verses.text: And Sarah died in Kiriath Arba; that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> Hebron, in the land of Canaan.

verses.name: Genesis 23:3
verses.text: And Abraham went to mourn for Sarah and to weep for her. And Abraham rose up from his dead, and he spoke to the Hittites<note placement="foot">Or “sons of Heth”</note> <transChange type="added">and</transChange> said,

verses.name: Genesis 23:4
verses.text: “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> a stranger and an alien among you; give to me <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞my own burial site⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “ownership of a grave”</note> among you so that I may bury my dead from before me.”

verses.name: Genesis 23:5
verses.text: And the Hittites<note placement="foot">Or “sons of Heth”</note> answered Abraham <transChange type="added">and</transChange> said to him,

verses.name: Genesis 23:6
verses.text: “Hear us, my lord, you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> a mighty prince<note placement="foot">Or “prince of God”</note> in our midst. Bury your dead in the choicest of our burial sites. None of us <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞will withhold his burial site⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “will withhold from himself his burial site</note> from you <transChange type="added">for</transChange> burying your dead.”

verses.name: Genesis 23:7
verses.text: And Abraham rose up and bowed to the people of the land, to the Hittites.<note placement="foot">Or “sons of Heth”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 23:8
verses.text: And he spoke with them, saying, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞If you are willing⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “if there is with your inner selves / souls”</note> <transChange type="added">that</transChange> I bury my dead from before me, hear me and intercede for me with Ephron the son of Zohar,

verses.name: Genesis 23:9
verses.text: that he may sell<note placement="foot">Or “give”</note> to me the cave of Machpelah which <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞belongs to him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “which is to him”</note> which is at the end of his field. At full value let him sell<note placement="foot">Or “give”</note> it to me in your midst as <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a burial site⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “ownership of a grave”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 23:10
verses.text: Now Ephron was sitting among the Hittites.<note placement="foot">Or “sons of Heth”</note> And Ephron the Hittite answered Abraham in the hearing of the Hittites<note placement="foot">Or “sons of Heth”</note> with respect to all <transChange type="added">who were</transChange> entering the gate of his city, <transChange type="added">and</transChange> said,

verses.name: Genesis 23:11
verses.text: “No, my lord, hear me. I give you the field and the cave which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in it, I <transChange type="added">also</transChange> give it to you in the sight of the children of my people I give it to you. Bury your dead.”

verses.name: Genesis 23:12
verses.text: And Abraham bowed before the people of the land.

verses.name: Genesis 23:13
verses.text: And he spoke to Ephron in the hearing of the people of the land, saying, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞If only you will hear me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Only if you perhaps hear me”</note>—I give the price of the field. Take <transChange type="added">it</transChange> from me that I may bury my dead there.”

verses.name: Genesis 23:14
verses.text: And Ephron answered Abraham, saying to him,

verses.name: Genesis 23:15
verses.text: “My lord, hear me. A <transChange type="added">piece of</transChange> land <transChange type="added">worth</transChange> four hundred shekels of silver—what <transChange type="added">is</transChange> that between me and you? Bury your dead.”

verses.name: Genesis 23:16
verses.text: Then Abraham listened to Ephron, and Abraham weighed for Ephron the silver that he had named<note placement="foot">Or “spoken”</note> in the hearing of the Hittites:<note placement="foot">Or “sons of Heth”</note> four hundred shekels of silver <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞at the merchants’ current rate⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “passing to the merchant”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 23:17
verses.text: So the field of Ephron which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in the Machpelah, which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> near Mamre—the field and the cave which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in it, with all the trees that <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in the field, which <transChange type="added">were</transChange> within all its surrounding boundaries—<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞passed⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “went up”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 23:18
verses.text: to Abraham as a property in the presence of the Hittites,<note placement="foot">Or “sons of Heth”</note> with respect to all <transChange type="added">who were</transChange> entering the gate of his city.

verses.name: Genesis 23:19
verses.text: And thus afterward Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah near Mamre; that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> Hebron, in the land of Canaan.

verses.name: Genesis 23:20
verses.text: And the field and the cave which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in it <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞passed⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “went up”</note> to Abraham as <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a burial site⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “ownership of a grave”</note> from the Hittites.<note placement="foot">Or “sons of Heth”</note>  <chapter eID="Gen.23"/>

verses.name: Genesis 24:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv90"/><title type="x-s">Isaac and Rebekah</title> <div sID="gen157" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv90"/>Now Abraham <transChange type="added">was</transChange> old, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞advanced in age⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “going in the days”</note> and Yahweh had blessed Abraham in everything.

verses.name: Genesis 24:2
verses.text: And Abraham said to his servant, the oldest of his house, who had charge of all he had, “Please put your hand under my thigh

verses.name: Genesis 24:3
verses.text: that I may make you swear by Yahweh, the God of heaven and the God of earth, that you will not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites in whose midst I am dwelling,

verses.name: Genesis 24:4
verses.text: but that you will go to my land and to my family, and take a wife for my son, for Isaac.”

verses.name: Genesis 24:5
verses.text: And the servant said to him, “Perhaps the woman will not be willing <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to follow⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to go after”</note> me to this land—must I then return your son to the land from whence you came?”

verses.name: Genesis 24:6
verses.text: Abraham said to him, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞You must take care⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “let it be careful to you”</note> that you do not return my son there.

verses.name: Genesis 24:7
verses.text: Yahweh, the God of heaven who took me from the house of my father and from the land of my family, and who spoke to me and swore to me, saying, ‘to your offspring I will give this land,’ he will send his angel before you, and you shall take a wife for my son from there.

verses.name: Genesis 24:8
verses.text: And if the woman is not willing <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to follow⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to go after”</note> you, then you shall be released from this oath of mine—only you must not return my son there.”

verses.name: Genesis 24:9
verses.text: Then the servant put his hand under the thigh of Abraham his master, and he swore to him concerning this matter.

verses.name: Genesis 24:10
verses.text: And the servant took ten camels from his master’s camels, and he went with all <transChange type="added">kinds of</transChange> his master’s good things in his hand. And he arose and went to Aram-Naharaim, to the city of Nahor.

verses.name: Genesis 24:11
verses.text: And he made the camels kneel outside the city at the well of water, at the time of evening, toward the time <transChange type="added">the women</transChange> went out to draw water.

verses.name: Genesis 24:12
verses.text: And he said, “O Yahweh, God of my master Abraham, please grant me success today and show loyal love to my master Abraham.

verses.name: Genesis 24:13
verses.text: Behold, I am standing by the spring of water, and the daughters of the men of the city are going out to draw water.

verses.name: Genesis 24:14
verses.text: And let it be <transChange type="added">that</transChange> the girl to whom I shall say, ‘Please, offer your jar that I may drink’ and <transChange type="added">who</transChange> says, ‘Drink—and I will also water your camels,’ she <transChange type="added">is the one</transChange> you have chosen for your servant, for Isaac. By her I will know that you have shown loyal love to my master.”

verses.name: Genesis 24:15
verses.text: And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> before he had finished speaking, behold, Rebekah—who was born to Bethuel, son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, the brother of Abraham—came out, and her jar <transChange type="added">was</transChange> on her shoulder.

verses.name: Genesis 24:16
verses.text: Now the girl <transChange type="added">was</transChange> very pleasing in appearance. <transChange type="added">She was</transChange> a virgin; no man had known her. And she went down to the spring, filled her jar, and came up.

verses.name: Genesis 24:17
verses.text: And the servant ran to meet her. And he said, “Please, let me drink a little of the water from your jar.”

verses.name: Genesis 24:18
verses.text: And she said, “Drink, my lord.” And she quickly lowered her jar in her hand and gave him a drink.

verses.name: Genesis 24:19
verses.text: When<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> she finished giving him a drink she said, “I will also draw water for your camels until they finish drinking.”

verses.name: Genesis 24:20
verses.text: And she quickly emptied her jar into the trough and ran again to the well to draw water. And she drew water for all his camels.

verses.name: Genesis 24:21
verses.text: And the man <transChange type="added">was</transChange> gazing at her silently to know <transChange type="added">if</transChange> Yahweh had made his journey successful or not.

verses.name: Genesis 24:22
verses.text: And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> as the camels finished drinking the man took a gold ring of a half shekel in weight and two bracelets for her arms, ten shekels in weight,

verses.name: Genesis 24:23
verses.text: and said, “Please tell me, whose daughter <transChange type="added">are</transChange> you? Is there a place <transChange type="added">at</transChange> the house of your father for us to spend the night?”

verses.name: Genesis 24:24
verses.text: And she said to him, “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> the daughter of Bethuel, son of Milcah, whom she bore to Nahor.”

verses.name: Genesis 24:25
verses.text: Then she said to him, “We have both straw and fodder in abundance, as well as a place to spend the night.”

verses.name: Genesis 24:26
verses.text: And the man knelt down and worshiped Yahweh.

verses.name: Genesis 24:27
verses.text: And he said, “Blessed <transChange type="added">be</transChange> Yahweh, God of my master Abraham, who has not withheld<note placement="foot">Or “abandoned”</note> his loyal love and his faithfulness from my master. I <transChange type="added">was</transChange> on the way <transChange type="added">and</transChange> Yahweh led me <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the house of my master’s brother.”

verses.name: Genesis 24:28
verses.text: Then the girl ran and reported these things to the household of her mother.  <div eID="gen157" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 24:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv91"/><div sID="gen158" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv91"/>Now Rebekah had a brother, and his name <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Laban. And Laban ran out to the man toward the spring.

verses.name: Genesis 24:30
verses.text: And when he saw the ring and the bracelets on the arms of his sister and heard the words of Rebekah his sister, <transChange type="added">who</transChange> said, “Thus the man spoke to me,” he went to the man. And behold, <transChange type="added">he was</transChange> standing with the camels at the spring.

verses.name: Genesis 24:31
verses.text: And he said, “Come, O blessed <transChange type="added">one</transChange> of Yahweh. Why do you stand outside? Now I have prepared the house and a place for the camels.”

verses.name: Genesis 24:32
verses.text: And the man came to the house and unloaded the camels. And he gave straw and fodder to the camels, and water to wash his feet and the feet of the men who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him.

verses.name: Genesis 24:33
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And food was placed before him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it was placed before him”</note> to eat. And he said, “I will not eat until <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I have told my errand⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “I have spoken my word”</note> And he said, “Speak.”

verses.name: Genesis 24:34
verses.text: And he said, “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> the servant of Abraham.

verses.name: Genesis 24:35
verses.text: Now Yahweh has blessed my master exceedingly, and he has become great. He has given to him sheep and cattle, silver and gold, male slaves and female slaves, and camels and donkeys.

verses.name: Genesis 24:36
verses.text: And Sarah, the wife of my master, has borne a son to my master after her old age. And he<note placement="foot">That is, Abraham</note> has given to him all that he has.

verses.name: Genesis 24:37
verses.text: And my master made me swear, saying, ‘Do not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites in whose land I am living.

verses.name: Genesis 24:38
verses.text: But you shall go to the house of my father, and to my family, and you shall take a wife for my son.’

verses.name: Genesis 24:39
verses.text: And I said to my master, ‘Perhaps the woman will not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞follow⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “go after”</note> me.’

verses.name: Genesis 24:40
verses.text: And he said to me, ‘Yahweh, before whom I have walked, shall send his angel with you and will make your journey successful. And you shall take a wife for my son from my family, and from the house of my father.

verses.name: Genesis 24:41
verses.text: Then you shall be released from my oath, when you come to my family. And if they will not give <transChange type="added">a woman</transChange> to you, then you will be released from my oath.’

verses.name: Genesis 24:42
verses.text: Then today I came to the spring, and I said, ‘O Yahweh, God of my master Abraham, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞if you would please make my journey successful⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “if there is you making successful my journey”</note> upon which I am going.

verses.name: Genesis 24:43
verses.text: Behold, I am standing by the spring of water. Let it be <transChange type="added">that</transChange> the young woman who comes out to draw water and to whom I say, “Please give me a little water to drink from your jar,”

verses.name: Genesis 24:44
verses.text: let her say to me, “Drink; I will also draw water for your camels,” she <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the woman whom Yahweh has appointed for the son of my master.’

verses.name: Genesis 24:45
verses.text: I had not yet finished speaking to myself<note placement="foot">Or “to my heart”</note> when, behold, Rebekah was coming out with<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> her jar on her shoulder. And she went down to the spring and drew water. And I said to her, ‘Please give me a drink.’

verses.name: Genesis 24:46
verses.text: And she hastened and let down her jar <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from her shoulder⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from upon her”</note> and said, ‘Drink, and I will give a drink to your camels also.’ Then I drank and she gave a drink to the camels also.

verses.name: Genesis 24:47
verses.text: Then I asked her and said, ‘Whose daughter <transChange type="added">are</transChange> you?’ And she said, ‘The daughter of Bethuel, son of Nahor, whom Milcah bore to him.’ And I put the ring on her nose and the bracelets on her arms.

verses.name: Genesis 24:48
verses.text: And I knelt down and worshiped Yahweh, and I praised Yahweh, the God of my master Abraham, who led me on the right way, to take the daughter of the brother of my master for his son.

verses.name: Genesis 24:49
verses.text: So now, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞if you are going to deal loyally and truly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “if there is you doing loyal love and faithfulness”</note> with my master, tell me. And if not, tell me, so that I may turn to the right or to the left.”<note placement="foot">An idiom for “so that I might know what to do”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 24:50
verses.text: Then Laban and Bethuel answered, and they said, “The matter has gone out from Yahweh; we are not able to speak bad or good to you.

verses.name: Genesis 24:51
verses.text: Here <transChange type="added">is</transChange> Rebekah before you. Take <transChange type="added">her</transChange> and go; let her be a wife for the son of your master as Yahweh has spoken.”

verses.name: Genesis 24:52
verses.text: And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> when the servant of Abraham heard their words he bowed down to the ground to Yahweh.

verses.name: Genesis 24:53
verses.text: And the servant brought out silver jewelry and gold jewelry, and garments, and he gave <transChange type="added">them</transChange> to Rebekah. And he gave precious gifts to her brother and to her mother.

verses.name: Genesis 24:54
verses.text: And he and the men who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him ate and drank, and they spent the night. And they got up in the morning, and he said, “Let me go to my master.”

verses.name: Genesis 24:55
verses.text: And her brother and her mother said, “Let the girl remain with us ten days <transChange type="added">or so</transChange>; after <transChange type="added">that</transChange> she may go.”

verses.name: Genesis 24:56
verses.text: And he said to them, “Do not delay me. Now, Yahweh has made my journey successful. Let me go. I must go to my master.”

verses.name: Genesis 24:57
verses.text: And they said, “Let us call the girl and ask <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞her opinion⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “her mouth”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 24:58
verses.text: And they called Rebekah and said to her, “Will you go with this man?” And she said, “I will go.”

verses.name: Genesis 24:59
verses.text: So they sent away Rebekah their sister, and her nurse, and the servant of Abraham and his men.

verses.name: Genesis 24:60
verses.text: And they blessed Rebekah and said to her, “You <transChange type="added">are</transChange> our sister; may you become countless thousands; and may your offspring take possession of the gate of his enemies.”

verses.name: Genesis 24:61
verses.text: And Rebekah and her maidservants arose, and they mounted the camels and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞followed⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “went after”</note> the man. And the servant took Rebekah and left.  <div eID="gen158" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 24:62
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv92"/><div sID="gen159" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv92"/>Now Isaac <transChange type="added">was</transChange> coming from the direction of Beer-Lahai-Roi. And he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> living in the land of the Negev.

verses.name: Genesis 24:63
verses.text: And Isaac went out to meditate in the field <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞early in the evening⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “at the turning of evening”</note> and he lifted up his eyes and saw—behold, camels were coming.

verses.name: Genesis 24:64
verses.text: And Rebekah lifted up her eyes and saw Isaac. And she got down from the camel.

verses.name: Genesis 24:65
verses.text: And she said to the servant, “Who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> this man walking around in the field to meet us?” And the servant said, “That <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my master.” And she took her<note placement="foot">Or “the”</note> veil and covered herself.

verses.name: Genesis 24:66
verses.text: And the servant told Isaac all the things that he had done.

verses.name: Genesis 24:67
verses.text: And Isaac brought her to the tent of Sarah his mother. And he took Rebekah, and she became his wife. And Isaac loved her and was comforted after <transChange type="added">the death of</transChange> his mother.  <chapter eID="Gen.24"/>

verses.name: Genesis 25:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv93"/><title type="x-s">The Death and Descendants of Abraham</title> <div sID="gen160" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv93"/>Now Abraham again took a wife, and her name <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Keturah.

verses.name: Genesis 25:2
verses.text: And she bore to him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.

verses.name: Genesis 25:3
verses.text: And Jokshan fathered Sheba and Dedan. And the sons of Dedan were Asshurim and Letushim and Leummim.

verses.name: Genesis 25:4
verses.text: And the sons of Midian <transChange type="added">were</transChange> Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abidah, and Eldaah. All of these <transChange type="added">were</transChange> the children of Keturah.

verses.name: Genesis 25:5
verses.text: And Abraham gave all he had to Isaac.

verses.name: Genesis 25:6
verses.text: But to the sons of Abraham’s concubines Abraham gave gifts. And while he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> still living he sent them away eastward, <transChange type="added">away</transChange> from his son Isaac, to the land of the east.

verses.name: Genesis 25:7
verses.text: Now these <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the days of the years of <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the life of Abraham⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>:<note placement="foot">Literally “the years of the life of Abraham which he lived”</note> one hundred and seventy-five years.

verses.name: Genesis 25:8
verses.text: And Abraham passed away and died in a good old age, old and full of years. And he was gathered to his people.

verses.name: Genesis 25:9
verses.text: And Isaac and Ishmael his sons buried him in the cave of Machpelah, in the field of Ephron, son of Zohar the Hittite, that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> east of Mamre,

verses.name: Genesis 25:10
verses.text: the field that Abraham had bought from the Hittites.<note placement="foot">Or “sons of Heth”</note> There Abraham was buried and Sarah his wife.

verses.name: Genesis 25:11
verses.text: And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> after the death of Abraham God blessed Isaac his son, and Isaac settled at Beer-Lahai-Roi.  <div eID="gen160" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 25:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv94"/><div sID="gen161" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv94"/>Now these <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the generations<note placement="foot">Or “family records”</note> of Ishmael, the son of Abraham, that Hagar the Egyptian, the maidservant of Sarah, bore to Abraham.

verses.name: Genesis 25:13
verses.text: And these are the names of the sons of Ishmael, by their names according to their family records. The firstborn of Ishmael <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Nebaioth, then Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,

verses.name: Genesis 25:14
verses.text: Mishma, Dumah, Massa,

verses.name: Genesis 25:15
verses.text: Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.

verses.name: Genesis 25:16
verses.text: These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the sons of Ishmael, and these <transChange type="added">are</transChange> their names by their villages and by their encampments—12 leaders according to their tribes.

verses.name: Genesis 25:17
verses.text: Now these <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the years of the life of Ishmael: 137 years. And he passed away and died, and was gathered to his people.

verses.name: Genesis 25:18
verses.text: They settled from Havilah to Shur, which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> opposite<note placement="foot">Or “upon the face of”</note> Egypt, going toward Asshur, opposite;<note placement="foot">Or “upon the face of”</note> he <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞settled⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “fell”</note> opposite<note placement="foot">Or “upon the face of”</note> all his brothers.  <div eID="gen161" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 25:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv95"/><title type="x-s">Jacob and Esau</title> <div sID="gen162" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv95"/>Now these <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the generations<note placement="foot">Or “family records”</note> of Isaac, the son of Abraham. Abraham fathered Isaac,

verses.name: Genesis 25:20
verses.text: And Isaac was <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forty years old⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a son of forty years”</note> when he took Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel the Aramean of Paddan-Aram, the sister of Laban the Aramean, as his wife.

verses.name: Genesis 25:21
verses.text: And Isaac prayed to Yahweh on behalf of his wife, for she <transChange type="added">was</transChange> barren. And Yahweh responded to his prayer, and Rebekah his wife conceived.

verses.name: Genesis 25:22
verses.text: And the children in her womb jostled each other, and she said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞If it is going to be like this, why be pregnant⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?”<note placement="foot">Literally “if so, why this I?”</note> And she went to inquire of Yahweh.

verses.name: Genesis 25:23
verses.text: And Yahweh said to her, “Two nations <transChange type="added">are</transChange> in your womb, and two peoples <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from birth⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from your bowels”</note> shall be divided. And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞one people shall be stronger than the other⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “people than people shall be stronger”</note> And <transChange type="added">the</transChange> elder shall serve <transChange type="added">the</transChange> younger.”

verses.name: Genesis 25:24
verses.text: And when her days to give birth were completed,<note placement="foot">Or “full”</note> then—behold—twins <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in her womb.

verses.name: Genesis 25:25
verses.text: And the first came out red, all <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his body⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “of him”</note> <transChange type="added">was</transChange> like a hairy coat, so they called his name Esau.

verses.name: Genesis 25:26
verses.text: And afterward his brother came out, and his hand grasped the heel of Esau, so his name was called Jacob. And Isaac <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞was sixty years old⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a son of sixty years”</note> at their birth.

verses.name: Genesis 25:27
verses.text: And the boys grew up. And Esau <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a skilled<note placement="foot">Or “knowing” (knowledgeable)</note> hunter, a man of the field, but Jacob <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a peaceful man, living <transChange type="added">in</transChange> tents.

verses.name: Genesis 25:28
verses.text: And Isaac loved Esau because <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he could eat of his game⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “game in his mouth”</note> but Rebekah loved Jacob.

verses.name: Genesis 25:29
verses.text: Once<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> Jacob cooked a thick stew, and Esau came in from the field, and he was exhausted.

verses.name: Genesis 25:30
verses.text: And Esau said to Jacob, “Give me <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞some of that red stuff⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “some of the red, this red”</note> to gulp down, for I am exhausted!” (Therefore his name was called Edom).

verses.name: Genesis 25:31
verses.text: Then Jacob said, “Sell me your birthright <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞first⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “as the day”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 25:32
verses.text: And Esau said, “Look, I am going to die; now what <transChange type="added">is</transChange> this birthright to me?”

verses.name: Genesis 25:33
verses.text: Then Jacob said, “Swear to me <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞first⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “as the day”</note> And he swore to him, and sold his birthright to Jacob.

verses.name: Genesis 25:34
verses.text: Then Jacob gave Esau bread, and thick lentil stew, and he ate and drank. Then he got up and went away. So Esau despised his birthright.  <chapter eID="Gen.25"/>

verses.name: Genesis 26:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv96"/><title type="x-s">Isaac and Abimelech</title> <div sID="gen163" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv96"/>And there was a famine in the land, besides the former famine which was in the days of Abraham. And Isaac went to Abimelech, king of the Philistines, to Gerar.

verses.name: Genesis 26:2
verses.text: And Yahweh appeared to him and said, “Do not go down to Egypt; dwell in the land which I will show to you.

verses.name: Genesis 26:3
verses.text: Dwell as an alien in this land, and I will be with you, and will bless you, for I will give all these lands to you and to your descendants, and I will establish the oath that I swore to Abraham you father.

verses.name: Genesis 26:4
verses.text: And I will multiply your descendants like the stars of heaven, and I will give to your descendants all these lands. And all nations of the earth will be blessed through your offspring,

verses.name: Genesis 26:5
verses.text: because Abraham listened to my voice and kept my charge: my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.”  <div eID="gen163" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 26:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv97"/><div sID="gen164" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv97"/>So Isaac settled in Gerar.

verses.name: Genesis 26:7
verses.text: When the men of the place asked concerning his wife, he said, “She <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my sister,” for he was afraid to say, “my wife,” thinking<note placement="foot">Or “lest”</note> “the men of the place will kill me on account of Rebekah, for <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞she was beautiful⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “good of appearance”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 26:8
verses.text: And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange>, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞when he had been there a long time⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “when the days there were long to him”</note> Abimelech the king of the Philistines looked through the window, and saw—behold—Isaac <transChange type="added">was</transChange> fondling Rebekah his wife.

verses.name: Genesis 26:9
verses.text: And Abimelech called Isaac<note placement="foot">Or “to Isaac”</note> and said, “Surely she <transChange type="added">is</transChange> your wife. Now why did you say ‘She <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my sister’?” And Isaac said to him, “Because I thought I would die on account of her.”

verses.name: Genesis 26:10
verses.text: And Abimelech said, “What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> this you have done to us? One of the people might easily have slept with your wife! Then you would have brought guilt upon us!”

verses.name: Genesis 26:11
verses.text: Then Abimelech instructed all the people, saying, “The <transChange type="added">one who</transChange> touches this man or his wife shall certainly die.”  <div eID="gen164" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 26:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv98"/><div sID="gen165" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv98"/>And Isaac sowed in that land and reaped in that <transChange type="added">same</transChange> year a hundredfold, and Yahweh blessed him.

verses.name: Genesis 26:13
verses.text: And the man <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞became wealthier and wealthier⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “became great and went, going and became great”</note> until he was exceedingly wealthy.

verses.name: Genesis 26:14
verses.text: And he possessed sheep and cattle and many servants, so that the Philistines envied him.

verses.name: Genesis 26:15
verses.text: And the Philistines stopped up all the wells that the servants of his father had dug in the days of Abraham his father. They filled them with earth.

verses.name: Genesis 26:16
verses.text: And Abimelech said to Isaac, “Go <transChange type="added">away</transChange> from us, for you have become much too powerful for us.”

verses.name: Genesis 26:17
verses.text: So Isaac departed from there and camped in the valley of Gerar, and settled there.

verses.name: Genesis 26:18
verses.text: And Isaac dug again the wells of water which they had dug in the days of his father Abraham, which the Philistines had stopped up after the death of Abraham. And he gave<note placement="foot">Or “called”</note> to them <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the same names⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “names as names”</note> which his father had given<note placement="foot">Or “called”</note> them.

verses.name: Genesis 26:19
verses.text: And when the servants of Isaac dug in the valley, they found a well of fresh water there.

verses.name: Genesis 26:20
verses.text: Then the herdsmen of Gerar quarreled with the herdsmen of Isaac, saying, “The water is ours.” And he called the name of the well Esek, because they contended with him.

verses.name: Genesis 26:21
verses.text: And they dug another well, and they quarreled over it also. And he called its name Sitnah.

verses.name: Genesis 26:22
verses.text: Then he moved from there and dug another well, and they did not quarrel over it. And he called its name Rehoboth, and said, “Now Yahweh has made room for us, and we shall be fruitful in the land.”

verses.name: Genesis 26:23
verses.text: And from there he went up to Beersheba.

verses.name: Genesis 26:24
verses.text: And Yahweh appeared to him that night and said, “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> the God of your father Abraham. Do not be afraid, for I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> with you, and I will bless you and make your descendants numerous for the sake of my servant Abraham.”

verses.name: Genesis 26:25
verses.text: And he built an altar there and called on the name of Yahweh. And he pitched his tent there, and the servants of Isaac dug a well there.

verses.name: Genesis 26:26
verses.text: Then Abimelech went to him from Gerar with Ahuzzath his friend and Phicol his army commander.

verses.name: Genesis 26:27
verses.text: And Isaac said to them, “Why have you come to me? You hate me and sent me away from you.”

verses.name: Genesis 26:28
verses.text: And they said, “We see clearly that Yahweh has been with you, so we thought<note placement="foot">Or “said”</note> let there be an oath between us—between us and you—and let us <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞make⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “cut”</note> a covenant with you

verses.name: Genesis 26:29
verses.text: that you may not do us harm just as we have not touched you, but have only done good to you and sent you away in peace. You <transChange type="added">are</transChange> now blessed by Yahweh.”

verses.name: Genesis 26:30
verses.text: So he made a meal for them, and they ate and drank.

verses.name: Genesis 26:31
verses.text: And they arose early in the morning and each one swore to the other,<note placement="foot">Or “to his brother”</note> and Isaac sent them away. And they left him in peace.

verses.name: Genesis 26:32
verses.text: And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> on that same day the servants of Isaac came and told him about the well that they had dug. And they said, “We have found water!”

verses.name: Genesis 26:33
verses.text: And he called it Sheba. Therefore the name of the city <transChange type="added">is</transChange> Beersheba unto this day.  <div eID="gen165" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 26:34
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv99"/><div sID="gen166" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv99"/>And <transChange type="added">when</transChange> Esau was forty years old he took as wife Judith, daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Basemath, daughter of Elon the Hittite.

verses.name: Genesis 26:35
verses.text: And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they made life bitter⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “they caused bitterness of spirit”</note> for Isaac and Rebekah.  <chapter eID="Gen.26"/>

verses.name: Genesis 27:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv100"/><title type="x-s">Jacob Steals Esau’s Blessing</title> <div sID="gen167" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv100"/>And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> when Isaac <transChange type="added">was</transChange> old and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his eyesight was weak⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “his eyes were weak from seeing”</note> he called Esau his older son and said to him, “My son.” And he<note placement="foot">That is, Esau</note> said to him, “Here I <transChange type="added">am</transChange>.”

verses.name: Genesis 27:2
verses.text: And he said, “Look, I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> old; I do not know the day of my death.

verses.name: Genesis 27:3
verses.text: So now, take your weapons, your quiver and your bow, and go out to the field and hunt food for me.

verses.name: Genesis 27:4
verses.text: Then make for me tasty food like I love, and bring <transChange type="added">it</transChange> to me. And I will eat <transChange type="added">it</transChange> so that I<note placement="foot">Or “my soul”</note> can bless you before I die.  <div eID="gen167" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 27:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv101"/><div sID="gen168" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv101"/>Now Rebekah <transChange type="added">was</transChange> listening as Isaac spoke to Esau his son, and <transChange type="added">when</transChange> Esau went to the field to hunt wild game to bring <transChange type="added">back</transChange>,

verses.name: Genesis 27:6
verses.text: Rebekah said to Jacob her son, “Look, I heard your father speaking to Esau your brother saying,

verses.name: Genesis 27:7
verses.text: ‘Bring wild game to me and prepare tasty food so I can eat <transChange type="added">it</transChange> and bless you before Yahweh before my death.’

verses.name: Genesis 27:8
verses.text: So now, my son, listen to my voice, to what I command you.

verses.name: Genesis 27:9
verses.text: Go to the flock and take two good young goats from it for me, and I will prepare them <transChange type="added">as</transChange> tasty food for your father, just as he likes.

verses.name: Genesis 27:10
verses.text: Then you must take it to your father and he will eat <transChange type="added">it</transChange> so that he may bless you before his death.”

verses.name: Genesis 27:11
verses.text: Then Jacob said to his mother, “Behold, Esau my brother <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a hairy man, but I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> a smooth man.

verses.name: Genesis 27:12
verses.text: Perhaps my father will feel me and I will be in his eyes <transChange type="added">as</transChange> a mocker, and he will bring upon me a curse and not a blessing.”

verses.name: Genesis 27:13
verses.text: Then his mother said to him, “Your curse be upon me, my son, only listen to my voice—go and get <transChange type="added">them</transChange> for me.”

verses.name: Genesis 27:14
verses.text: So he went and took <transChange type="added">them</transChange>, and brought <transChange type="added">them</transChange> to his mother, and his mother prepared tasty food as his father liked.

verses.name: Genesis 27:15
verses.text: Then Rebekah took <transChange type="added">some of</transChange> her older son Esau’s best garments that <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with her in the house, and she put <transChange type="added">them</transChange> on Jacob her younger son.

verses.name: Genesis 27:16
verses.text: And she put the skins of the young goats over his hands and over the smooth <transChange type="added">part of</transChange> his neck.

verses.name: Genesis 27:17
verses.text: And she put the tasty food and the bread that she had made into the hand of Jacob, her son.

verses.name: Genesis 27:18
verses.text: And he went to his father and said, “My father.” And he said, “Here I <transChange type="added">am</transChange>. Who <transChange type="added">are</transChange> you, my son?”

verses.name: Genesis 27:19
verses.text: And Jacob said to his father, “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> Esau, your firstborn. I have done as you told me. Please get up, sit up and eat from my wild game so that you<note placement="foot">Or “your soul”</note> may bless me.”

verses.name: Genesis 27:20
verses.text: Then Isaac said to his son, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞How⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “what is this?”</note> did you find it so quickly, my son?” And he said, “Because Yahweh your God <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞caused me to find it⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “made it to happen before me”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 27:21
verses.text: Then Isaac said to Jacob, “Please, come near and let me feel you, my son. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Are you really⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “are you this one?”</note> my son Esau or not?”

verses.name: Genesis 27:22
verses.text: And Jacob drew near to Isaac his father. And he felt him and said, “The voice <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the voice of Jacob, but the hands <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the hands of Esau.”

verses.name: Genesis 27:23
verses.text: And he did not recognize him because his hands were hairy like the hands of Esau his brother. And he blessed him.

verses.name: Genesis 27:24
verses.text: And he said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Are you really⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “are you this one?”</note> my son Esau?” And he said, “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange>.”

verses.name: Genesis 27:25
verses.text: Then he said, “Bring <transChange type="added">it</transChange> near to me that I may eat from the game of my son, so that I<note placement="foot">Or “my soul”</note> may bless you.” And he brought <transChange type="added">it</transChange> to him, and he ate. And he brought wine to him, and he drank.

verses.name: Genesis 27:26
verses.text: Then his father Isaac said to him, “Come near and kiss me, my son.”

verses.name: Genesis 27:27
verses.text: And he drew near and kissed him. And he<note placement="foot">That is, Isaac</note> smelled the smell of his garments, and he blessed him and said, <div eID="gen168" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen169"/> <l level="1" sID="gen170"/>“Look, the smell of my son <transChange type="added">is</transChange> like the smell of a field that Yahweh has blessed! <l eID="gen170" level="1"/>

verses.name: Genesis 27:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv102"/><l level="1" sID="gen171"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv102"/>May God give you of the dew of heaven<l eID="gen171" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen172"/>and of the fatness of the earth,<l eID="gen172" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen173"/>and abundance of grain and new wine. <l eID="gen173" level="2"/>

verses.name: Genesis 27:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv103"/><l level="1" sID="gen174"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv103"/>Let peoples serve you,<l eID="gen174" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen175"/>and nations bow down to you;<l eID="gen175" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen176"/>Be lord of your brothers,<l eID="gen176" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen177"/>and may the sons of your mother bow down to you.<l eID="gen177" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen178"/>Cursed be those cursing you,<l eID="gen178" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen179"/>and blessed be those blessing you.” <l eID="gen179" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen169"/>

verses.name: Genesis 27:30
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv104"/><div sID="gen180" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv104"/>And as soon as Isaac had finished blessing Jacob, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞immediately after⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “it was only”</note> Jacob had gone out from the presence of Isaac his father, Esau his brother came <transChange type="added">back</transChange> from his hunting.

verses.name: Genesis 27:31
verses.text: He too prepared tasty food and brought <transChange type="added">it</transChange> to his father. And he said to his father, “Let my father arise and eat from the wild game of his son, that you<note placement="foot">Or “your soul”</note> may bless me.”

verses.name: Genesis 27:32
verses.text: And Isaac his father said to him, “Who <transChange type="added">are</transChange> you?” And he said, “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> your son, your firstborn, Esau.”

verses.name: Genesis 27:33
verses.text: Then Isaac <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞trembled violently⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “trembled a great trembling unto exceeding”</note> Then he said, “Who then <transChange type="added">was</transChange> he that hunted wild game and brought <transChange type="added">it</transChange> to me, and I ate <transChange type="added">it</transChange> all before you came, and I blessed him? Moreover, he will be blessed!”

verses.name: Genesis 27:34
verses.text: When Esau heard the words of his father he cried out <transChange type="added">with</transChange> a great and exceedingly bitter cry of distress. And he said to his father, “Bless me as well, my father!”

verses.name: Genesis 27:35
verses.text: And he said, “Your brother came in deceit and took your blessing.”

verses.name: Genesis 27:36
verses.text: Then he said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Isn’t that why he is named Jacob⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?<note placement="foot">Literally “that his name is called Jacob?”</note> He has deceived me these two times. He took my birthright and, look, now he has taken my blessing!” Then he said, “Have you not reserved a blessing for me?”

verses.name: Genesis 27:37
verses.text: Then Isaac answered and said to Esau, “Behold, I have made him lord over you and I have given him all his brothers as servants, and <transChange type="added">with</transChange> grain and wine I have sustained him. Now what can I do for you, my son?”

verses.name: Genesis 27:38
verses.text: And Esau said to his father, “Have you only one blessing, my father? Bless me also, my father!” And Esau lifted up his voice and wept.

verses.name: Genesis 27:39
verses.text: Then Isaac his father answered and said to him, <div eID="gen180" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen181"/> <l level="1" sID="gen182"/>“Your home shall be from<note placement="foot">Or “away from”</note> the fatness of the land,<l eID="gen182" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen183"/>and from the dew of heaven above. <l eID="gen183" level="2"/>

verses.name: Genesis 27:40
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv105"/><l level="1" sID="gen184"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv105"/>But by your sword you shall live,<l eID="gen184" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen185"/>and you shall serve your brother.<l eID="gen185" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen186"/>But it shall be <transChange type="added">that</transChange> when free yourself<l eID="gen186" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen187"/>you shall tear off his yoke from your neck. <l eID="gen187" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen181"/>

verses.name: Genesis 27:41
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv106"/><div sID="gen188" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv106"/>Then Esau held a grudge against Jacob on account of the blessing with which his father had blessed him. And Esau said in his heart,<note placement="foot">That is, “to himself”</note> “The days of mourning for my father are coming, then I will kill Jacob my brother.”

verses.name: Genesis 27:42
verses.text: But the words of Esau her older son were told to Rebekah. And she sent and called for her younger son Jacob. And she said to him, “Look, Esau your brother <transChange type="added">is</transChange> consoling himself concerning you, <transChange type="added">intending</transChange> to kill you.

verses.name: Genesis 27:43
verses.text: Now then, my son, listen to my voice; arise and flee to Haran to Laban my brother.

verses.name: Genesis 27:44
verses.text: Stay with him a few days until the wrath of your brother has turned—

verses.name: Genesis 27:45
verses.text: until the anger of your brother turns from you and he has forgotten what you have done to him. Then I will send and bring you from there. Why should I lose the two of you in one day?”

verses.name: Genesis 27:46
verses.text: Then Rebekah said to Isaac, “I loathe my life because of the Hittite women.<note placement="foot">Or “daughters of the Hittites”</note> If Jacob takes a wife from Hittite women<note placement="foot">Or “daughters of the Hittites”</note> like these, from the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞native women⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “daughters of the land”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞what am I living for⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?”<note placement="foot">Literally “What is life to me?”</note>  <chapter eID="Gen.27"/>

verses.name: Genesis 28:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv107"/><title type="x-s">Jacob Flees to Haran</title> <div sID="gen189" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv107"/>Then Isaac called Jacob and blessed him. And he instructed him and said to him, “You must not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan.

verses.name: Genesis 28:2
verses.text: Arise, go to Paddan-Aram, to the house of Bethuel, your mother’s father, and take for yourself a wife from there, from the daughters of Laban your mother’s brother.

verses.name: Genesis 28:3
verses.text: Now, may El-Shaddai<note placement="foot">Often translated “God Almighty”</note> bless you, and make you fruitful, and multiply you, so that you become an assembly of peoples.

verses.name: Genesis 28:4
verses.text: And may he give you the blessing of Abraham, to you and to your descendants with you, that you may take possession of the land of your sojourning, which God gave to Abraham.”

verses.name: Genesis 28:5
verses.text: Then Isaac sent Jacob away, and he went to Paddan-Aram, to Laban the son of Bethuel the Aramean, the brother of Rebekah, the mother of Jacob and Esau.

verses.name: Genesis 28:6
verses.text: Now Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him away to Paddan-Aram, to take for himself a wife from there, and<note placement="foot">Or “when”</note> he blessed him and instructed him, saying, “You must not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan,”

verses.name: Genesis 28:7
verses.text: and <transChange type="added">that</transChange> Jacob listened to his father and to his mother and went to Paddan-Aram.

verses.name: Genesis 28:8
verses.text: Then Esau saw that the daughters of Canaan <transChange type="added">were</transChange> evil in the eyes of Isaac his father,

verses.name: Genesis 28:9
verses.text: then Esau went to Ishmael and took Mahalath, the daughter of Ishmael, son of Abraham, sister of Nebaioth, as a wife, in addition to the wives he had.  <div eID="gen189" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 28:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv108"/><title type="x-s">Jacob’s Dream</title> <div sID="gen190" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv108"/>Then Jacob went out from Beersheba and went to Haran.

verses.name: Genesis 28:11
verses.text: And he arrived at a <transChange type="added">certain</transChange> place and spent the night there, because the sun had set. And he took <transChange type="added">one</transChange> of the stones of the place and put <transChange type="added">it</transChange> under his head and slept at that place.

verses.name: Genesis 28:12
verses.text: And he dreamed, and behold, a stairway was set on the earth, and its top touched the heavens. And behold, angels of God <transChange type="added">were</transChange> going up and going down on it.

verses.name: Genesis 28:13
verses.text: And behold, Yahweh <transChange type="added">was</transChange> standing beside him,<note placement="foot">Or “above it”</note> and he said, “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> Yahweh, the God of Abraham your father, and the God of Isaac. The ground on which you <transChange type="added">were</transChange> sleeping I will give to you and to your descendants.

verses.name: Genesis 28:14
verses.text: Your descendants shall be like the dust of the earth, and you will spread out to the west, and to the east, and to the north and to the south. And all the families of the earth will be blessed through you and through your descendants.

verses.name: Genesis 28:15
verses.text: Now behold, I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> with you, and I will keep you wherever you go. And I will bring you to this land, for I will not leave you until I have done what I have promised to you.”

verses.name: Genesis 28:16
verses.text: Then Jacob awoke from his sleep and said, “Surely Yahweh <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞is indeed⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “there is”</note> in this place and I did not know!”

verses.name: Genesis 28:17
verses.text: Then he was afraid and said, “How awesome <transChange type="added">is</transChange> this place! <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞This is nothing else than the house of God⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “there is not this but the house of God”</note> and this is the gate of heaven!”

verses.name: Genesis 28:18
verses.text: And Jacob rose early in the morning, and he took the stone that he had put under his head and set it up <transChange type="added">as</transChange> a stone pillar, and poured oil on top of it.

verses.name: Genesis 28:19
verses.text: And he called the name of that place Bethel; however, the name of the city <transChange type="added">was</transChange> formerly Luz.

verses.name: Genesis 28:20
verses.text: And Jacob made a vow<note placement="foot">Or “vowed a vow”</note> saying, “If God will be with me and protect me on this way that I am going, and gives me food to eat and clothing to wear,

verses.name: Genesis 28:21
verses.text: and <transChange type="added">if</transChange> I return in peace to the house of my father, then Yahweh will become my God.

verses.name: Genesis 28:22
verses.text: And this stone that I have set up <transChange type="added">as</transChange> a pillar shall be the house of God, and <transChange type="added">of</transChange> all that you give to me I will certainly give a tenth to you.”  <chapter eID="Gen.28"/>

verses.name: Genesis 29:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv109"/><title type="x-s">Jacob Flees to Haran</title> <div sID="gen191" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv109"/>And Jacob <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞continued his journey⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “lifted up his feet”</note> and went to the land of the Easterners.<note placement="foot">Or “children of the east”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 29:2
verses.text: And he looked, and behold, <transChange type="added">there was</transChange> a well in the field, and behold, there <transChange type="added">were</transChange> three flocks of sheep lying beside it, for out of that well the flocks were watered. And the stone on the mouth of the well <transChange type="added">was</transChange> large.

verses.name: Genesis 29:3
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange> all the flocks were gathered there, they rolled away the stone from the mouth of the well. And they watered the sheep and returned the stone upon the mouth of the well to its place.

verses.name: Genesis 29:4
verses.text: And Jacob said to them, “My brothers, where <transChange type="added">are</transChange> you from?” And they said, “We <transChange type="added">are</transChange> from Haran.”

verses.name: Genesis 29:5
verses.text: And he said to them, “Do you know Laban, son of Nahor?” And they said, “We know <transChange type="added">him</transChange>.”

verses.name: Genesis 29:6
verses.text: And he said to them, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Is he well⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?”<note placement="foot">Literally “Is it well for him?”</note> And they said, “<transChange type="added">He is</transChange> well. Now look, Rachel his daughter is coming with the sheep.”

verses.name: Genesis 29:7
verses.text: And he said, “Look, <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> still <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞broad daylight⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “high day”</note> it is not the time <transChange type="added">for</transChange> the livestock to be gathered. Give water to the sheep and go, pasture them.”

verses.name: Genesis 29:8
verses.text: And they said, “We are not able, until all the flocks are gathered. Then the stone is rolled away from the mouth of the well, and we water the sheep.”

verses.name: Genesis 29:9
verses.text: While he was speaking with them, Rachel came with the sheep which belonged to her father, for she was pasturing <transChange type="added">them</transChange>.

verses.name: Genesis 29:10
verses.text: And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange>, when Jacob saw Rachel, the daughter of Laban, his mother’s brother, and the sheep of Laban, his mother’s brother, Jacob drew near and rolled away the stone from the mouth of the well and watered the sheep of Laban, his mother’s brother.

verses.name: Genesis 29:11
verses.text: And Jacob kissed Rachel, and lifted up his voice and wept.

verses.name: Genesis 29:12
verses.text: And Jacob told Rachel that he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> the relative of her father, and that he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> the son of Rebekah. And she ran and told her father.

verses.name: Genesis 29:13
verses.text: And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> when Laban heard the message about Jacob, the son of his sister, he ran to meet him. And he embraced him and kissed him, and brought him to his house. And he told Laban all these things.

verses.name: Genesis 29:14
verses.text: And Laban said to him, “Surely you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> my flesh and my bone!” And he stayed with him a month.  <div eID="gen191" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 29:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv110"/><title type="x-s">Jacob’s Marriages</title> <div sID="gen192" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv110"/>Then Laban said to Jacob, “<transChange type="added">Just</transChange> because you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> my brother should you work for me for nothing? Tell me what your wage <transChange type="added">should be</transChange>.”

verses.name: Genesis 29:16
verses.text: Now Laban had two daughters. The name of the older <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Leah, and the name of the younger <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Rachel.

verses.name: Genesis 29:17
verses.text: Now the eyes of Leah <transChange type="added">were</transChange> dull, but Rachel was beautiful in form and appearance.

verses.name: Genesis 29:18
verses.text: And Jacob loved Rachel and said, “I will serve you seven years for Rachel your younger daughter.”

verses.name: Genesis 29:19
verses.text: Then Laban said, “Better <transChange type="added">that</transChange> I give her to you than I give her to another man. Stay with me.”

verses.name: Genesis 29:20
verses.text: And Jacob worked for Rachel seven years, but they were as a few days in his eyes because he loved her.

verses.name: Genesis 29:21
verses.text: And Jacob said to Laban, “Give <transChange type="added">me</transChange> my wife, that I may go in to her, for <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞my time⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “my days”</note> is completed.”

verses.name: Genesis 29:22
verses.text: So Laban gathered all the men of the place and prepared a feast.

verses.name: Genesis 29:23
verses.text: And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> in the evening he took Leah his daughter and brought her to him, and he went in to her.

verses.name: Genesis 29:24
verses.text: And Laban gave Zilpah his female servant to her, to Leah his daughter <transChange type="added">as</transChange> a female servant.

verses.name: Genesis 29:25
verses.text: And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> in the morning, behold, it <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Leah! And he said to Laban, “What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> this you have done to me? Did I not serve with you for Rachel? Now why did you deceive me?”

verses.name: Genesis 29:26
verses.text: Then Laban said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞It is not the custom⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “it is not thus done”</note> in our country to give the younger before the firstborn.

verses.name: Genesis 29:27
verses.text: Complete the week of this one,<note placement="foot">Leah; the wedding feast would last one week</note> then I will also give you the other, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞on the condition that you will work for me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “with respect to the work that you will work with me yet”</note> another seven years.”

verses.name: Genesis 29:28
verses.text: And Jacob did so. So he completed the week of this <transChange type="added">one</transChange>,<note placement="foot">That is, Leah</note> then he gave Rachel his daughter to him as a wife.

verses.name: Genesis 29:29
verses.text: And Laban gave Bilhah his female servant to Rachel his daughter as a female servant.

verses.name: Genesis 29:30
verses.text: Then he also went in to Rachel, and he loved Rachel more than Leah. And he served with him yet another seven years.  <div eID="gen192" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 29:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv111"/><title type="x-s">Jacob’s Children</title> <div sID="gen193" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv111"/>When Yahweh saw that Leah <transChange type="added">was</transChange> unloved he opened her womb, but Rachel <transChange type="added">was</transChange> barren.

verses.name: Genesis 29:32
verses.text: Then Leah conceived and gave birth to a son, and she called his name Reuben, for she said, “Because Yahweh has noticed my misery, that I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> unloved. Now my husband will love me.”

verses.name: Genesis 29:33
verses.text: And she conceived again and gave birth to a son. And she said, “<transChange type="added">It is</transChange> because Yahweh has heard that I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> unloved that he gave me this <transChange type="added">son</transChange> also.” And she called his name Simeon.

verses.name: Genesis 29:34
verses.text: And she conceived again and gave birth to a son. Then she said, “Now this time my husband will be joined to me, for I have borne him three sons.” Therefore, she called his name Levi.

verses.name: Genesis 29:35
verses.text: And she conceived again and gave birth to a son. And she said, “This time I will praise Yahweh.” Therefore she called his name Judah. And she ceased bearing children.  <chapter eID="Gen.29"/>

verses.name: Genesis 30:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv112"/><title type="x-s">Jacob’s Children</title> <div sID="gen194" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv112"/>When Rachel saw that she could not bear children to Jacob, Rachel envied her sister. And she said to Jacob, “Give me children—if not, I will die!”

verses.name: Genesis 30:2
verses.text: And Jacob <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞became angry⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “became hot of nose”</note> with Rachel. And he said, “<transChange type="added">Am</transChange> I in the place of God, who has withheld from you the fruit of the womb?”

verses.name: Genesis 30:3
verses.text: Then she said, “Here <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my servant girl Bilhah; go in to her that she may bear children <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as my surrogate⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “upon my knees”</note> Then I will even <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞have children⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “be built up”</note> by her.”

verses.name: Genesis 30:4
verses.text: Then she gave him Bilhah, her female servant, as a wife, and Jacob went in to her

verses.name: Genesis 30:5
verses.text: And Bilhah conceived and gave birth to a son for Jacob.

verses.name: Genesis 30:6
verses.text: Then Rachel said, “God has judged me, and has also heard my voice, and has given me a son.” Therefore she called his name Dan.

verses.name: Genesis 30:7
verses.text: And Bilhah, Rachel’s servant, conceived again and bore a second son to Jacob.

verses.name: Genesis 30:8
verses.text: And Rachel said, “I have struggled a mighty struggle with my sister and have prevailed.” And she called his name Naphtali.

verses.name: Genesis 30:9
verses.text: When Leah saw that she had ceased bearing children, she took Zilpah her female servant and gave her to Jacob as a wife.

verses.name: Genesis 30:10
verses.text: And Zilpah, the female slave of Leah, bore a son to Jacob.

verses.name: Genesis 30:11
verses.text: Then Leah said, “Good fortune!” And she called his name Gad.

verses.name: Genesis 30:12
verses.text: And Zilpah, Leah’s female servant, bore a second son to Jacob.

verses.name: Genesis 30:13
verses.text: Then Leah said, “How happy <transChange type="added">am</transChange> I! For women have called me happy.” So she called his name Asher.  <div eID="gen194" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 30:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv113"/><div sID="gen195" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv113"/>And in the days of the wheat harvest, Reuben went and found mandrakes in the field and he brought them to Leah his mother. And Rachel said to Leah, “Please give me some of your son’s mandrakes.”

verses.name: Genesis 30:15
verses.text: And she said to her, “<transChange type="added">Is</transChange> your taking my husband <transChange type="added">such</transChange> a small <transChange type="added">thing</transChange> that you will also take the mandrakes of my son?” Then Rachel said, “Then he may sleep with you tonight in exchange for your son’s mandrakes.”

verses.name: Genesis 30:16
verses.text: When Jacob came in from the field in the evening, Leah went out to meet him. And she said, “Come in to me, for <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I have hired⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “I have fully paid for”</note> you with my son’s mandrakes.” And he slept with her that night.

verses.name: Genesis 30:17
verses.text: And God listened to Leah and she conceived and gave birth to a fifth son for Jacob.

verses.name: Genesis 30:18
verses.text: Then Leah said, “God has given <transChange type="added">me</transChange> my wage since I gave my servant girl to my husband.” And she called his name Issachar.

verses.name: Genesis 30:19
verses.text: And Leah conceived again and gave birth to a sixth son for Jacob.

verses.name: Genesis 30:20
verses.text: And Leah said, “God has endowed me with a good gift. This time my husband will acknowledge me, because I bore him six sons.” And she called his name Zebulun.

verses.name: Genesis 30:21
verses.text: And afterward she gave birth to a daughter. And she called her name Dinah.

verses.name: Genesis 30:22
verses.text: Then God remembered Rachel and listened to her, and God opened her womb.

verses.name: Genesis 30:23
verses.text: And she conceived and gave birth to a son. And she said, “God has taken away my disgrace.”

verses.name: Genesis 30:24
verses.text: And she called his name Joseph, saying, “Yahweh has added to me another son.”  <div eID="gen195" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 30:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv114"/><title type="x-s">Jacob’s Prosperity</title> <div sID="gen196" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv114"/>And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> as soon as Rachel had given birth to Joseph, Jacob said to Laban, “Send me away that I may go to my place and my land.

verses.name: Genesis 30:26
verses.text: Give <transChange type="added">me</transChange> my wives and my children for which I have served you, and let me go. For you yourself know my service that I have rendered to you.”

verses.name: Genesis 30:27
verses.text: But Laban said to him, “Please, if I have found favor in your eyes, I have learned by divination that Yahweh has blessed me because of you.”

verses.name: Genesis 30:28
verses.text: And he said, “Name your wage to me and I will give <transChange type="added">it</transChange>.”

verses.name: Genesis 30:29
verses.text: Then he said to him, “You yourself know how I have served you and how your livestock have been with me.<note placement="foot">I.e., “How well they have done under my care”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 30:30
verses.text: For you had little before me, and it has increased abundantly. And Yahweh has blessed you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞wherever I turned⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “to my foot”</note> So then, when shall I provide for my own family also?”

verses.name: Genesis 30:31
verses.text: And he said, “What shall I give you?” And Jacob said, “Do not give me anything. If you will do this thing for me, I will again feed your flocks and keep <transChange type="added">them</transChange>.

verses.name: Genesis 30:32
verses.text: Let me pass through all your flocks today, removing all the speckled and spotted sheep from them, along with<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> every dark-colored sheep among the sheep, and the spotted and speckled among the goats. That<note placement="foot">Or “it”</note> shall be my wages.

verses.name: Genesis 30:33
verses.text: And my righteousness will answer for me <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞later⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “on the day tomorrow”</note> when you come concerning my wages before you. Every <transChange type="added">one</transChange> that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not speckled or spotted among the goats, or dark-colored among the sheep shall be stolen <transChange type="added">if it is</transChange> with me.”

verses.name: Genesis 30:34
verses.text: Then Laban said, “Look! Very well. It shall be according to your word.”

verses.name: Genesis 30:35
verses.text: But that day he<note placement="foot">That is, Laban</note> removed the streaked and spotted male goats and all the speckled and spotted female goats, all that had white on it, and every dark-colored ram, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞put them in the charge of his sons⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “he gave into the hands of his sons”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 30:36
verses.text: And he put a journey of three days between him and Jacob, and Jacob pastured the remainder of Laban’s flock.

verses.name: Genesis 30:37
verses.text: Then Jacob took fresh branches of poplar, almond, and plane trees and peeled white strips on them, exposing the white which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> on the branches.

verses.name: Genesis 30:38
verses.text: And he set the branches that he had peeled in front of the flocks, in the troughs <transChange type="added">and</transChange> in the water containers. And they were in heat when they came to drink.

verses.name: Genesis 30:39
verses.text: And the flocks mated by the branches, so the flocks bore streaked, speckled, and spotted.

verses.name: Genesis 30:40
verses.text: And Jacob separated the lambs and turned the faces of the flocks toward the streaked and all the dark-colored in Laban’s flocks. And he put his own herds apart, and did not put them with the flocks of Laban.

verses.name: Genesis 30:41
verses.text: And whenever any of the stronger of the flocks were in heat, Jacob put the branches <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in full view⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “before the eyes of”</note> of the flock in the troughs that they might mate among the branches.

verses.name: Genesis 30:42
verses.text: But with the more feeble of the flock he would not put <transChange type="added">them there</transChange>. So the feebler were Laban’s and the stronger <transChange type="added">were</transChange> Jacob’s.

verses.name: Genesis 30:43
verses.text: And the man became <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞exceedingly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “very, very”</note> rich and had large flocks, female slaves, male slaves, camels, and donkeys.  <chapter eID="Gen.30"/>

verses.name: Genesis 31:1
