verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv115"/><title type="x-s">Jacob Flees from Laban</title> <div sID="gen197" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv115"/>Now he<note placement="foot">That is, Jacob</note> heard the words of the sons of Laban, saying, “Jacob has taken all that our father has,” and “From that which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> our father’s he has gained all this wealth.”

verses.name: Genesis 31:2
verses.text: Then Jacob saw the face of Laban and, behold, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞it was not like it had been in the past⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “there was not with him like yesterday or the day before”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 31:3
verses.text: And Yahweh said to Jacob, “Return to the land of your ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and to your family, and I will be with you.”

verses.name: Genesis 31:4
verses.text: So Jacob sent and called Rachel and Leah to the field, to his flocks,

verses.name: Genesis 31:5
verses.text: and he said to them, “Look, I see the face of your father, that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞it is not like it has been toward me in the past⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “it is not to me like yesterday or the day before”</note> But the God of my father is with me.

verses.name: Genesis 31:6
verses.text: Now you yourselves know that I have served your father with all my strength,

verses.name: Genesis 31:7
verses.text: and your father has cheated me and changed my wages ten times, but God has not allowed him to harm me.

verses.name: Genesis 31:8
verses.text: If thus he said, ‘Speckled shall be your wage,’ then all the flock bore speckled. And <transChange type="added">if</transChange> he said, ‘Streaked shall be your wage,’ then all the flock bore streaked.

verses.name: Genesis 31:9
verses.text: God has taken away your father’s livestock and given <transChange type="added">them</transChange> to me.

verses.name: Genesis 31:10
verses.text: Now it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> at the time of the mating of the flock I lifted up my eyes and saw in a dream, and behold, the rams mounting the flock <transChange type="added">were</transChange> streaked, speckled, and dappled.

verses.name: Genesis 31:11
verses.text: Then the angel of God said to me in the dream, ‘Jacob,’ and I said, ‘Here I <transChange type="added">am</transChange>.’

verses.name: Genesis 31:12
verses.text: And he said, ‘Lift up your eyes and see—all the rams mounting the flock <transChange type="added">are</transChange> streaked, speckled, and dappled, for I have seen all that Laban is doing to you.

verses.name: Genesis 31:13
verses.text: I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> the God of Bethel where you anointed a stone pillar, where you made a vow to me. Now get up, go out from this land and return to the land of your birth.’ ”

verses.name: Genesis 31:14
verses.text: Then Rachel and Leah answered and said to him, “<transChange type="added">Is there</transChange> yet a portion for us, and an inheritance in the house of our father?

verses.name: Genesis 31:15
verses.text: Are we not regarded <transChange type="added">as</transChange> foreigners by him, because he has sold us and completely consumed our money?

verses.name: Genesis 31:16
verses.text: For all the wealth that God has taken away from our father, it belongs to us and to our sons. So now, all that God has said to you, do.”

verses.name: Genesis 31:17
verses.text: Then Jacob got up and put his children and his wives on the camels.

verses.name: Genesis 31:18
verses.text: And he drove all his livestock and his possessions that he had acquired, the livestock of his possession that he had acquired in Paddan-Aram, in order to go to Isaac his father, to the land of Canaan.  <div eID="gen197" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 31:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv116"/><div sID="gen198" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv116"/>Now Laban had gone to shear his sheep, and Rachel stole the idols<note placement="foot">Hebrew <hi type="italic">teraphim</hi></note> that belonged to her father.

verses.name: Genesis 31:20
verses.text: And Jacob <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞tricked⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “stole the heart of”</note> Laban the Aramean by not telling him that he <transChange type="added">intended to</transChange> flee.

verses.name: Genesis 31:21
verses.text: Then he fled with all that he had, and arose and crossed the Euphrates<note placement="foot">Or “the river”</note> and set his face toward the hill country of Gilead.

verses.name: Genesis 31:22
verses.text: And on the third day it was told to Laban that Jacob had fled.

verses.name: Genesis 31:23
verses.text: Then he took his kinsmen with him and pursued after him, a seven-day journey, and he caught up with him in the hill country of Gilead.

verses.name: Genesis 31:24
verses.text: And God came to Laban the Aramean in a dream at night and said to him, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Take care⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “watch to yourself”</note> that you not speak with Jacob, whether good or evil.”

verses.name: Genesis 31:25
verses.text: And Laban overtook Jacob. Now Jacob had pitched his tent in the hill country, and Laban and his kinsmen pitched <transChange type="added">their tents</transChange> in the hill country of Gilead.

verses.name: Genesis 31:26
verses.text: Then Laban said to Jacob, “What have you done that you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞tricked me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “stole my heart”</note> and have carried off my daughters like captives of the sword?

verses.name: Genesis 31:27
verses.text: Why did you hide <transChange type="added">your intention</transChange> to flee and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞trick me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “steal my heart”</note> and did not tell me so that I would have sent you away with joy and song and tambourine and lyre?

verses.name: Genesis 31:28
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">why</transChange> did you not give me opportunity to kiss my grandsons<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> and my daughters <transChange type="added">goodbye</transChange>? Now you have behaved foolishly <transChange type="added">by</transChange> doing <transChange type="added">this</transChange>.

verses.name: Genesis 31:29
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞It is in my power⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “there is power in my hand”</note> to do harm to you, but the God of your father spoke to me last night saying, ‘<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Take care⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “watch to yourself”</note> from speaking with Jacob, whether good or evil.’

verses.name: Genesis 31:30
verses.text: Now, you have surely gone because you desperately longed for the house of your father, <transChange type="added">but</transChange> why did you steal my gods?”

verses.name: Genesis 31:31
verses.text: Then Jacob answered and said to Laban, “Because I <transChange type="added">was</transChange> afraid, for I thought, ‘Lest you take your daughters from me by force.’

verses.name: Genesis 31:32
verses.text: <transChange type="added">But</transChange> with whomever you find your gods, he shall not live. In the presence of your kinsmen <transChange type="added">now</transChange> identify what <transChange type="added">is</transChange> with me <transChange type="added">that is</transChange> yours and take it.” Now Jacob did not know that Rachel had stolen them.

verses.name: Genesis 31:33
verses.text: Then Laban went into Jacob’s tent and Leah’s tent and the tent of the two female servants and did not find <transChange type="added">his gods</transChange>. And he came out of Leah’s tent and went into Rachel’s tent.

verses.name: Genesis 31:34
verses.text: Now Rachel had taken the idols and put them in the saddle bag of the camel and sat on them. And Jacob searched the whole tent thoroughly but did not find them.

verses.name: Genesis 31:35
verses.text: And she said to her father, “Let there not be anger in the eyes of my lord, for I am not able to rise before you, for the way of women <transChange type="added">is</transChange> with me. And he searched carefully and did not find the idols.

verses.name: Genesis 31:36
verses.text: Then Jacob became angry and quarreled with Laban. Jacob answered and said to Laban, “What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my offense? What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my sin that you pursued after me?

verses.name: Genesis 31:37
verses.text: For you have searched all my possessions and what did you find among all the possessions of my household? Set it before my kinsmen and your kinsmen that they may decide between the two of us!

verses.name: Genesis 31:38
verses.text: These twenty years I <transChange type="added">was</transChange> with you; your ewes and your female goats did not miscarry, and the rams of your flocks I did not eat.

verses.name: Genesis 31:39
verses.text: I brought no mangled carcass to you—I bore its loss. From my hand you sought it, whether stolen by day or stolen by night.

verses.name: Genesis 31:40
verses.text: <transChange type="added">There</transChange> I was, during the day the heat consumed me, and the cold by night, and my sleep fled from my eyes.

verses.name: Genesis 31:41
verses.text: These twenty years <transChange type="added">I have been</transChange> in your house. I served you fourteen years for your two daughters and six years for your flock, and you have changed my wages ten times.

verses.name: Genesis 31:42
verses.text: If the God of my father, the God of Abraham and the Fear of Isaac had not been with me, indeed now you would have sent me away empty-handed. God saw my misery and the labor of my hands and rebuked you last night.”

verses.name: Genesis 31:43
verses.text: Then Laban answered and said to Jacob, “The daughters <transChange type="added">are</transChange> my daughters and the grandsons<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> are my grandsons,<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> and the flocks <transChange type="added">are</transChange> my flocks, and all that you see, it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> mine. Now, what can I do for these my daughters today, or for their children whom they have borne?

verses.name: Genesis 31:44
verses.text: So now, come, let us <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞make⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “cut”</note> a covenant, you and I, and let it be a witness between me and you.”

verses.name: Genesis 31:45
verses.text: And Jacob took a stone and set it up <transChange type="added">as</transChange> a stone pillar.

verses.name: Genesis 31:46
verses.text: And Jacob said to his kinsmen, “Gather stones.” And they took stones and made a pile of stones, and they ate there by the pile of stones.

verses.name: Genesis 31:47
verses.text: And Laban called it Jegar Sahadutha,<note placement="foot">Aramaic for “the heap of witness”</note> but Jacob called it Galeed.<note placement="foot">Hebrew for “the heap of witness”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 31:48
verses.text: Then Laban said, “This pile of stones <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a witness between me and you today.” Therefore its name is called Galeed,<note placement="foot">Hebrew for “the heap of witness”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 31:49
verses.text: and Mizpah,<note placement="foot">Hebrew for “watchpost”</note> because he said, “Yahweh watch between me and you when <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞we are out of sight of each other⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “each from his neighbor is concealed”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 31:50
verses.text: If you mistreat my daughters, and if you take wives besides my daughters, <transChange type="added">when</transChange> there is no man with us, see—God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a witness between me and you.”

verses.name: Genesis 31:51
verses.text: And Laban said to Jacob, “See, this pile of stones, and see the pillar that I have set up between me and you.

verses.name: Genesis 31:52
verses.text: This pile of stones <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a witness, and the pillar <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a witness, that I will not pass beyond this pile of stones to you, and that you will not pass beyond this pile of stones and this pillar to me intending harm.

verses.name: Genesis 31:53
verses.text: May the God of Abraham and the God of Nahor, the God of their father<note placement="foot">That is, Terah</note> judge between us.” Then Jacob swore by the Fear of his father Isaac.

verses.name: Genesis 31:54
verses.text: And Jacob sacrificed a sacrifice on the hill, and he called his kinsmen to eat the meal.<note placement="foot">Or “food, bread”</note> And they ate the meal<note placement="foot">Or “food, bread”</note> and spent the night on the hill.

verses.name: Genesis 31:55
verses.text: <note placement="foot"><reference osisRef="Gen.31.55-Gen.32.32">Genesis 31:55–32:32 </reference>in the English Bible is 32:1–33 in the Hebrew Bible</note> And Laban arose early in the morning and kissed his grandsons<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> and his daughters, and blessed them. Then Laban departed and returned to his homeland.  <chapter eID="Gen.31"/>

verses.name: Genesis 32:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv117"/><title type="x-s">Jacob Fears Esau</title> <div sID="gen199" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv117"/>And Jacob went on his way, and angels of God met him.

verses.name: Genesis 32:2
verses.text: And when he saw them, Jacob said, “This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the camp of God!” And he called the name of that place Mahanaim.  <div eID="gen199" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 32:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv118"/><div sID="gen200" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv118"/>Then Jacob sent messengers before him to Esau his brother, to the land of Seir, the territory of Edom.

verses.name: Genesis 32:4
verses.text: And he instructed them, saying, “Thus you must say to my lord, to Esau, ‘Thus says your servant Jacob, I have dwelled as an alien with Laban, and I have remained <transChange type="added">there</transChange> until now.

verses.name: Genesis 32:5
verses.text: And I have acquired cattle, male donkeys, flocks, and male and female slaves, and I have sent to tell my lord, to find favor in your eyes.’ ”

verses.name: Genesis 32:6
verses.text: And the messengers returned to Jacob <transChange type="added">and</transChange> said, “We came to your brother, to Esau, and he is coming to meet you, and four hundred men <transChange type="added">are</transChange> with him.”

verses.name: Genesis 32:7
verses.text: Then Jacob was very frightened and distressed. So he divided the people, flocks, cattle, and camels that <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him into two companies.

verses.name: Genesis 32:8
verses.text: And he thought, “If Esau comes to one company and destroys it, the remaining company will be <transChange type="added">able</transChange> to escape.”

verses.name: Genesis 32:9
verses.text: Then Jacob said, “O God of my father Abraham, and God of my father Isaac, O Yahweh, who said to me, ‘Return to your land and to your family, and I will deal well with you.’

verses.name: Genesis 32:10
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I am not worthy⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “I am small”</note> of all the loyal love and all the faithfulness that you have shown<note placement="foot">Or “done”</note> your servant, for with <transChange type="added">only</transChange> my staff I crossed this Jordan, and now I have become two camps.

verses.name: Genesis 32:11
verses.text: Please rescue me from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau, for I fear him, lest he come and attack mother and children <transChange type="added">alike</transChange>.

verses.name: Genesis 32:12
verses.text: Now you yourself said, ‘I will surely deal well with you and make your offspring as the sand of the sea that cannot be counted for abundance.’ ”  <div eID="gen200" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 32:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv119"/><div sID="gen201" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv119"/>And he lodged there that night. Then he took <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from what he had with him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from that which was going from his hand”</note> a gift for Esau his brother:

verses.name: Genesis 32:14
verses.text: two hundred female goats, twenty male goats, two hundred ewes, twenty rams,

verses.name: Genesis 32:15
verses.text: thirty milk camels with their young, forty cows, ten bulls, twenty female donkeys, and ten male donkeys.

verses.name: Genesis 32:16
verses.text: And he put <transChange type="added">them</transChange> under the hand of his servants, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞herd by herd⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “every herd by its own”</note> and said to his servants, “Cross on ahead before me, and put some distance <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞between herds⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “between a herd and between a herd”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 32:17
verses.text: And he instructed the foremost, saying, “When Esau my brother comes upon you and asks you, saying, ‘Whose <transChange type="added">are</transChange> you and where are you going? To whom do these <transChange type="added">animals</transChange> belong ahead of you?’

verses.name: Genesis 32:18
verses.text: Then you must say, ‘To your servant, to Jacob. It <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a gift sent to my lord, to Esau. Now behold, he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> also <transChange type="added">coming</transChange> after us.’ ”

verses.name: Genesis 32:19
verses.text: And he also instructed the second <transChange type="added">servant</transChange> and the third, and everyone <transChange type="added">else</transChange> who <transChange type="added">was</transChange> behind the herds, saying, “You must speak to Esau according to this word when you find him.

verses.name: Genesis 32:20
verses.text: And moreover, you shall say, ‘Look, your servant Jacob <transChange type="added">is</transChange> behind us.’ ” For he thought, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Let me appease him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “let me cover his face”</note> with the gift going before me, and afterward I will see his face. Perhaps he will <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞show me favor⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “lift up my face”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 32:21
verses.text: So the gift passed on before him, but he himself spent that night in the camp.  <div eID="gen201" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 32:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv120"/><title type="x-s">Jacob Wrestles with God</title> <div sID="gen202" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv120"/>That night he arose and took his two wives, his two female servants, and his eleven children and crossed the ford of the Jabbok.

verses.name: Genesis 32:23
verses.text: And he took them and sent them across the stream. Then he sent across all his possessions.

verses.name: Genesis 32:24
verses.text: And Jacob remained alone, and a man wrestled with him until the breaking of the dawn.

verses.name: Genesis 32:25
verses.text: And when he<note placement="foot">That is, the man</note> saw that he could not prevail against him, he struck his hip socket, so that Jacob’s hip socket was sprained as he wrestled with him.

verses.name: Genesis 32:26
verses.text: Then he<note placement="foot">That is, the man</note> said, “Let me go, for dawn is breaking.” But he answered, “I will not let you go unless you bless me.”

verses.name: Genesis 32:27
verses.text: Then he said to him, “What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> your name?” And he said, “Jacob.”

verses.name: Genesis 32:28
verses.text: And he said, “Your name shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel,<note placement="foot">“Israel” means “he struggles with God,” or “God struggles”</note> for you have struggled with God and with men and have prevailed.”

verses.name: Genesis 32:29
verses.text: Then Jacob asked and said, “Please tell me your name.” And he said, “Why do you ask this—for my name?” And he blessed him there.

verses.name: Genesis 32:30
verses.text: Then Jacob called the name of the place Peniel <transChange type="added">which means</transChange> “I have seen God face to face and my life was spared.”

verses.name: Genesis 32:31
verses.text: Then the sun rose upon him as he passed Penuel, and he was limping because of his hip.

verses.name: Genesis 32:32
verses.text: Therefore the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> do not eat the sinew of the sciatic nerve that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> upon the socket of the hip unto this day, because he struck the socket of the thigh of Jacob at the sinew of the sciatic nerve.  <chapter eID="Gen.32"/>

verses.name: Genesis 33:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv121"/><title type="x-s">Jacob Meets Esau and Settles at Shechem</title> <div sID="gen203" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv121"/>And Jacob lifted up his eyes and looked. And behold, Esau <transChange type="added">was</transChange> coming and four hundred men <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him. And he<note placement="foot">That is, Jacob</note> divided the children among Leah and among Rachel, and among the two of his female servants.

verses.name: Genesis 33:2
verses.text: And he put the female slaves and their children first, then Leah and her children next, then Rachel with Joseph last.

verses.name: Genesis 33:3
verses.text: And he himself passed on before them and bowed down to the ground seven times until he came to his brother.

verses.name: Genesis 33:4
verses.text: But Esau ran to meet him, and embraced him, and fell upon his neck and kissed him, and they wept.

verses.name: Genesis 33:5
verses.text: Then Esau lifted up his eyes and saw the women and the children and said, “Who <transChange type="added">are</transChange> these with you?” And he said, “The children whom God has graciously given your servant.”

verses.name: Genesis 33:6
verses.text: Then the female servants drew near, they and their children, and they bowed down.

verses.name: Genesis 33:7
verses.text: Then Leah and her children drew near and bowed down, and afterward Joseph and Rachel drew near and they bowed down.

verses.name: Genesis 33:8
verses.text: And he<note placement="foot">That is, Esau</note> said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞What do you mean by⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “What to you?”</note> all this company that I have met?” Then he said, “To find favor in the eyes of my lord.”

verses.name: Genesis 33:9
verses.text: Then Esau said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I have enough⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “There is to me abundance”</note> my brother; <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞keep what you have⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “let what is to you be to you”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 33:10
verses.text: And Jacob said, “No, please, if I have found favor in your eyes, you must take my gift from my hand, for then I have seen your face <transChange type="added">which is</transChange> like seeing the face of God, and you have received me.

verses.name: Genesis 33:11
verses.text: Please take my gift which has been brought to you, for God has dealt graciously with me, and because <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I have enough⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “There is to me abundance”</note> And he urged him, so he took <transChange type="added">it</transChange>.

verses.name: Genesis 33:12
verses.text: Then he<note placement="foot">That is, Esau</note> said, “Let us journey and go <transChange type="added">on</transChange>, and I will go ahead of you.”

verses.name: Genesis 33:13
verses.text: But he said to him, “My lord knows that the children <transChange type="added">are</transChange> frail, and the flocks and the cattle <transChange type="added">which are</transChange> nursing <transChange type="added">are a concern</transChange> to me. Now <transChange type="added">if</transChange> they drove them hard for a day all the flocks would die.

verses.name: Genesis 33:14
verses.text: Let my lord pass on before his servant and I will move along slowly at the pace<note placement="foot">Or “foot”</note> of the livestock that are ahead of me, and at the pace<note placement="foot">Or “foot”</note> of the children until I come to my lord in Seir.”

verses.name: Genesis 33:15
verses.text: And Esau said, “Let me leave some of my people with you.” But he said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞What need is there⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?<note placement="foot">Literally “What is this?”</note> Let me find favor in the eyes of my lord.”

verses.name: Genesis 33:16
verses.text: So Esau turned that day on his way to Seir.

verses.name: Genesis 33:17
verses.text: But Jacob traveled on to Succoth, and he built for himself a house, and he made shelters for his livestock. Therefore he called the name of the place Succoth.

verses.name: Genesis 33:18
verses.text: And Jacob came safely to the city of Shechem which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in the land of Canaan, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞on his way⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “at his coming”</note> from Paddan-Aram. And he camped before the city.

verses.name: Genesis 33:19
verses.text: And he bought a piece of land where he pitched his tent for one hundred pieces of money<note placement="foot">Hebrew <hi type="italic">kesitah</hi></note> from the hand of the sons of Hamor, father of Shechem.

verses.name: Genesis 33:20
verses.text: And there he erected an altar and called it “El Elohe Israel.”<note placement="foot">That is, “<hi type="italic">El</hi> the God of Israel”</note>  <chapter eID="Gen.33"/>

verses.name: Genesis 34:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv122"/><title type="x-s">The Rape of Dinah and the Massacre at Shechem</title> <div sID="gen204" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv122"/>Now Dinah the daughter of Leah, whom she had borne to Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land.

verses.name: Genesis 34:2
verses.text: And Shechem, the son of Hamor the Hivite, the prince of the land, saw her. And he took her and lay with her and raped her.

verses.name: Genesis 34:3
verses.text: And his soul clung to Dinah, the daughter of Jacob, and he loved the girl and spoke <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞tenderly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the heart”</note> to the girl.

verses.name: Genesis 34:4
verses.text: So Shechem said to Hamor his father, saying, “Get this girl for me as a wife.”  <div eID="gen204" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 34:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv123"/><div sID="gen205" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv123"/>And Jacob heard that Dinah his daughter had been defiled, but his sons were with his flocks in the field. And Jacob kept silent until they came.

verses.name: Genesis 34:6
verses.text: And Hamor, father of Shechem, went out to Jacob to speak with him.

verses.name: Genesis 34:7
verses.text: And the sons of Jacob came in from the field when they heard <transChange type="added">it</transChange>. And the men were distressed and very angry because he had done a disgraceful thing in Israel by having sexual relations with the daughter of Jacob—<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞something that⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and thus”</note> should not be done.

verses.name: Genesis 34:8
verses.text: And Hamor spoke with them saying, “Shechem my son <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞is in love with⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “his soul longs for”</note> your daughter. Please give her to him for a wife.

verses.name: Genesis 34:9
verses.text: Make marriages with us. Give us your daughters and take our daughters for yourselves.

verses.name: Genesis 34:10
verses.text: You shall dwell with us and the land shall be before you; settle and trade in it, and acquire <transChange type="added">property</transChange> in it.”

verses.name: Genesis 34:11
verses.text: Then Shechem said to her father and to her brothers, “Let me find favor in your eyes, and whatever you say to me I will do.

verses.name: Genesis 34:12
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Make the bride price and gift as high as you like⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “Increase upon me very bride price and gift”</note> I will give what you say to me. But give me the girl as a wife.”

verses.name: Genesis 34:13
verses.text: Then the sons of Jacob answered Shechem and his father Hamor speaking deceitfully, because he had defiled Dinah their sister.

verses.name: Genesis 34:14
verses.text: And they said to them, “We cannot do this thing, to give our sister to a man who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> uncircumcised, for that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a disgrace for us.

verses.name: Genesis 34:15
verses.text: Only on this <transChange type="added">condition</transChange> will we give consent to you; if you will become like us—every male among you to be circumcised.

verses.name: Genesis 34:16
verses.text: Then we will give our daughters to you, and we will take for ourselves your daughters, and we will live with you and become one family.

verses.name: Genesis 34:17
verses.text: But if you will not listen to us, to be circumcised, then we will take our daughters and we will go.”

verses.name: Genesis 34:18
verses.text: And their words were good in the eyes of Hamor and in the eyes of Shechem, the son of Hamor.

verses.name: Genesis 34:19
verses.text: And the young man did not delay to do the thing, for he wanted the daughter of Jacob. Now he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> the most honored of his father’s house.

verses.name: Genesis 34:20
verses.text: Then Hamor and his son Shechem came to the gate of their city, and they spoke to the men of their city, saying,

verses.name: Genesis 34:21
verses.text: “These men <transChange type="added">are</transChange> at peace with us. Let them dwell in the land and let them trade in it. Now, behold, the land is <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞broad enough for them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “broad on sides before them”</note> Let us take their daughters as wives, and let us give our daughters to them.

verses.name: Genesis 34:22
verses.text: Only on this <transChange type="added">condition</transChange> will they give consent to us, to live with us <transChange type="added">and</transChange> to become one family—when every male among us <transChange type="added">is</transChange> circumcised as they are circumcised.

verses.name: Genesis 34:23
verses.text: Will not their livestock and their property and all their animals <transChange type="added">be</transChange> ours? Only let us give consent to them so they will live among us.”

verses.name: Genesis 34:24
verses.text: And all those who went out of the gate of his city listened to Hamor and Shechem. Every male was circumcised, all those who went out of the gate of his city.

verses.name: Genesis 34:25
verses.text: And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> on the third day, while they were in pain, two of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, the brothers of Dinah, each took his sword and came against the unsuspecting city and killed all the males.

verses.name: Genesis 34:26
verses.text: They killed Hamor and his son Shechem with the edge of the sword, and they took Dinah from the house of Shechem and went out.

verses.name: Genesis 34:27
verses.text: The <transChange type="added">other</transChange> sons of Jacob came upon the slain and plundered the city, because they had defiled their sister.

verses.name: Genesis 34:28
verses.text: They took their flocks and their cattle and their donkeys, and whatever <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in the field.

verses.name: Genesis 34:29
verses.text: They captured and plundered all that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in the houses—all their wealth, their little ones, and their women.

verses.name: Genesis 34:30
verses.text: Then Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, “You have brought trouble on me, making me stink among the inhabitants of the land, among the Canaanites and the Perizzites! I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> few in number! If they gather against me and attack me, I will be destroyed—I and my household!”

verses.name: Genesis 34:31
verses.text: But they said, “Shall he treat our sister like a prostitute?”  <chapter eID="Gen.34"/>

verses.name: Genesis 35:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv124"/><title type="x-s">Jacob Goes Back to Bethel</title> <div sID="gen206" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv124"/>And God said to Jacob, “Arise, go up to Bethel and dwell there, and make an altar to the God who appeared to you when you fled from before Esau your brother.”

verses.name: Genesis 35:2
verses.text: Then Jacob said to his household and to all who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him, “Get rid of the foreign gods that <transChange type="added">are</transChange> in your midst and purify yourselves and change your garments.

verses.name: Genesis 35:3
verses.text: Then let us make ready and let us go up to Bethel, so that I can make an altar there to the God who answered me in the day of my trouble, and who has been with me on the way that I have gone.”

verses.name: Genesis 35:4
verses.text: So they gave to Jacob all the foreign gods that <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in their hands, and the ornamental rings that <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in their ears. And Jacob buried them under the oak which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> near Shechem.

verses.name: Genesis 35:5
verses.text: Then they set out on their journey, and the terror of God was upon the cities that <transChange type="added">were</transChange> all around them, so that they did not pursue after the sons of Jacob.

verses.name: Genesis 35:6
verses.text: And Jacob came to Luz which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in the land of Canaan (that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> Bethel), he and all the people that <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him.

verses.name: Genesis 35:7
verses.text: And he built an altar there and called the place El-Bethel, for there God had appeared to him when he fled before his brother.

verses.name: Genesis 35:8
verses.text: And Deborah, the nurse of Rebekah, died. And she was buried below Bethel, under the oak. And its name was called Allon-Bacuth.<note placement="foot">“The Oak of Weeping”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 35:9
verses.text: And God appeared to Jacob again when he came from Paddan-Aram, and he blessed him.

verses.name: Genesis 35:10
verses.text: And God said to him, “Your name <transChange type="added">is</transChange> Jacob. Your name shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel shall be your name.” Then his name was called Israel.

verses.name: Genesis 35:11
verses.text: And God said to him, “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> El-Shaddai.<note placement="foot">Possibly “God Almighty,” but more likely “God of the Wilderness”</note> Be fruitful and multiply. A nation and an assemblage of nations shall be from you, and kings shall go out from your loins.

verses.name: Genesis 35:12
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">as for</transChange> the land that I gave to Abraham and to Isaac, I will give it to you. And to your descendants after you I will give the land.

verses.name: Genesis 35:13
verses.text: And God went up from him at the place where he spoke with him.

verses.name: Genesis 35:14
verses.text: And Jacob set up a pillar at the place where God had spoken with him, a pillar of stone. And he poured out a drink offering upon it, and poured oil on it.

verses.name: Genesis 35:15
verses.text: And Jacob called the name of the place where God had spoken with him Bethel.  <div eID="gen206" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 35:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv125"/><title type="x-s">The Death of Rachel</title> <div sID="gen207" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv125"/>Then they journeyed from Bethel. And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞when they were still some distance⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “there was still the stretch of land”</note> from Ephrath, Rachel went into labor. And she had hard labor.

verses.name: Genesis 35:17
verses.text: And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞when her labor was the most difficult⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “at her distress at giving birth”</note> the midwife said to her, “Do not be afraid <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞for you have another son⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “for this one also to you is a son”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 35:18
verses.text: And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> when her life was departing (for she was dying), she called his name Ben-Oni.<note placement="foot">“Son of my sorrow”</note> But his father called him Benjamin.<note placement="foot">“Son of the right hand”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 35:19
verses.text: And Rachel died and she was buried on the way to Ephrath (that <transChange type="added">is</transChange>, Bethlehem).

verses.name: Genesis 35:20
verses.text: And Jacob erected a pillar at her burial site. That <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the pillar of the burial site of Rachel unto this day.

verses.name: Genesis 35:21
verses.text: And Israel journeyed <transChange type="added">on</transChange> and pitched his tent beyond the tower of Eder.<note placement="foot">Or “Migdal-Eder”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 35:22
verses.text: And while Israel was living in that land Reuben went and had sexual relations with Bilhah, his father’s concubine. And Israel heard <transChange type="added">about it</transChange>. <div eID="gen207" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">The Twelve Sons of Jacob</title> <div sID="gen208" type="x-p"/> Now the sons of Jacob <transChange type="added">were</transChange> twelve.

verses.name: Genesis 35:23
verses.text: The sons of Leah: The firstborn of Jacob <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Reuben. Then Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun.

verses.name: Genesis 35:24
verses.text: The sons of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin.

verses.name: Genesis 35:25
verses.text: The sons of Bilhah, the female servant of Rachel: Dan and Naphtali.

verses.name: Genesis 35:26
verses.text: The sons of Zilpah, the female servant of Leah: Gad and Asher. These <transChange type="added">were</transChange> the sons of Jacob who were born to him in Paddan-Aram.  <div eID="gen208" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 35:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv126"/><title type="x-s">The Death of Isaac</title> <div sID="gen209" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv126"/>And Jacob came to Isaac his father <transChange type="added">at</transChange> Mamre, <transChange type="added">or</transChange> Kiriath-Arba (that <transChange type="added">is</transChange>, Hebron), where Abraham and Isaac dwelled as aliens.

verses.name: Genesis 35:28
verses.text: Now the days of Isaac were one hundred and eighty years.

verses.name: Genesis 35:29
verses.text: And Isaac passed away and died, and was gathered to his people, old and full of days. And his sons Esau and Jacob buried him.  <chapter eID="Gen.35"/>

verses.name: Genesis 36:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv127"/><title type="x-s">The Descendants of Esau</title> <div sID="gen210" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv127"/>Now these <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the descendants of Esau (that <transChange type="added">is</transChange>, Edom).

verses.name: Genesis 36:2
verses.text: Esau took his wives from the daughters of Canaan: Adah, daughter of Elon, the Hittite, and Oholibamah, daughter of Anah, the daughter of Zibeon, the Hivite,

verses.name: Genesis 36:3
verses.text: and Basemath, the daughter of Ishmael, the sister of Nebaioth.

verses.name: Genesis 36:4
verses.text: And Adah bore to Esau Eliphaz; and Basemath bore Reuel;

verses.name: Genesis 36:5
verses.text: and Oholibamah bore Jeush and Jalam, and Korah. These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the sons of Esau who were born to him in the land of Canaan.

verses.name: Genesis 36:6
verses.text: And Esau took his wives and his sons and his daughters, and all the persons of his household, and his sheep and goats, and all his cattle, and all the goods that he had acquired in the land of Canaan, and went to a land away from his brother Jacob.

verses.name: Genesis 36:7
verses.text: For their possessions were <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞too many to live together⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “much from living together”</note> so that the land of their sojourning was not able to support them on account of their livestock.

verses.name: Genesis 36:8
verses.text: So Esau dwelled in the hill country of Seir (Esau, that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> Edom).  <div eID="gen210" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 36:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv128"/><div sID="gen211" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv128"/>Now these <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the descendants of Esau, the father of Edom, in the hill country of Seir.

verses.name: Genesis 36:10
verses.text: These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the names of the sons of Esau: Eliphaz, the son of Adah, the wife of Esau; Reuel, the son of Basemath, the wife of Esau.

verses.name: Genesis 36:11
verses.text: The sons of Eliphaz were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, and Kenaz.

verses.name: Genesis 36:12
verses.text: (Now Timnah was the concubine of Eliphaz, the son of Esau. And she bore Amalek to Eliphaz.) These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the sons of Adah, the wife of Esau.

verses.name: Genesis 36:13
verses.text: Now these <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the sons of Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah. These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the sons of Basemath, the wife of Esau.

verses.name: Genesis 36:14
verses.text: Now these <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the sons of Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah, daughter of Zibeon, the wife of Esau: She bore to Esau Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.

verses.name: Genesis 36:15
verses.text: These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the chiefs of the sons of Esau. The sons of Eliphaz, the firstborn of Esau: the chiefs of Teman, Omar, Zepho, Kenaz,

verses.name: Genesis 36:16
verses.text: Korah, Gatam, and Amalek. These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the chiefs of Eliphaz in the land of Edom. These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the sons of Adah.

verses.name: Genesis 36:17
verses.text: Now these <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the sons Reuel, the son of Esau: the chiefs Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah. These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the chiefs of Reuel in the land of Edom. These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the sons of Basemath, the wife of Esau.

verses.name: Genesis 36:18
verses.text: Now these <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the sons of Oholibamah, the wife of Esau: the chiefs Jeush, Jalam, and Korah. These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the chiefs born of Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah, the wife of Esau.

verses.name: Genesis 36:19
verses.text: These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the sons of Esau, and these <transChange type="added">are</transChange> their chiefs (that <transChange type="added">is</transChange>, Edom).

verses.name: Genesis 36:20
verses.text: These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the sons of Seir, the Horite, the inhabitants of the land: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,

verses.name: Genesis 36:21
verses.text: Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan. These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the chiefs of the Horites, the sons of Seir in the land of Edom.

verses.name: Genesis 36:22
verses.text: And the sons of Lotan were Hori and Hemam. And Lotan’s sister <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Timna.

verses.name: Genesis 36:23
verses.text: Now these <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the sons of Shobal: Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.

verses.name: Genesis 36:24
verses.text: Now these <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the sons of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah—he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> Anah who found the hot springs in the desert while he pastured the donkeys of Zibeon his father.

verses.name: Genesis 36:25
verses.text: Now these <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the sons of Anah: Dishon and Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah.

verses.name: Genesis 36:26
verses.text: Now these <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the sons of Dishon: Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Keran.

verses.name: Genesis 36:27
verses.text: These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the sons of Ezer: Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.

verses.name: Genesis 36:28
verses.text: These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the sons of Dishan: Uz and Aran.

verses.name: Genesis 36:29
verses.text: These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the chiefs of the Horites: the chiefs Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,

verses.name: Genesis 36:30
verses.text: Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan. These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the chiefs of the Horites, according to their chiefs in the land of Seir.  <div eID="gen211" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 36:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv129"/><title type="x-s">The Kings of Edom</title> <div sID="gen212" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv129"/>Now these <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the kings who reigned in the land of Edom before any king ruled over the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 36:32
verses.text: Bela the son of Beor reigned in Edom. And the name of his city <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Dinhabah.

verses.name: Genesis 36:33
verses.text: And Bela died, and Jobab, the son of Zerah from Bozrah, reigned in his place.

verses.name: Genesis 36:34
verses.text: And Jobab died, and Husham from the land of the Temanites reigned in his place.

verses.name: Genesis 36:35
verses.text: And Husham died, and Hadad, son of Bedad, who defeated Midian in the field<note placement="foot">Or “country”</note> of Moab reigned in his place. And the name of his city <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Avith.

verses.name: Genesis 36:36
verses.text: And Hadad died, and Samlah from Masrekah reigned in his place.

verses.name: Genesis 36:37
verses.text: And Samlah died, and Shaul from Rehoboth <transChange type="added">on</transChange> the Euphrates<note placement="foot">Or “the River”</note> reigned in his place.

verses.name: Genesis 36:38
verses.text: And Shaul died, and Baal-Hanan, the son of Acbor, reigned in his place.

verses.name: Genesis 36:39
verses.text: And Baal-Hanan the son of Acbor died, and Hadar reigned in his place. And the name of his city <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Pau, and the name of his wife <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred, daughter of Mezahab.

verses.name: Genesis 36:40
verses.text: Now these <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the names of the chiefs of Esau according to their families, according to their dwelling places, by their names: the chiefs Timna, Alvah, Jetheth,

verses.name: Genesis 36:41
verses.text: Oholibamah, Elah, Pinon,

verses.name: Genesis 36:42
verses.text: Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar,

verses.name: Genesis 36:43
verses.text: Magdiel, and Iram. These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the chiefs of Edom (that <transChange type="added">is</transChange>, Esau, the father of Edom) according to their settlements in the land of their possession.  <chapter eID="Gen.36"/>

verses.name: Genesis 37:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv130"/><title type="x-s">The Dreams of Joseph</title> <div sID="gen213" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv130"/>And Jacob settled in the land of the sojourning of his father, in the land of Canaan.

verses.name: Genesis 37:2
verses.text: These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the generations<note placement="foot">Or “family records”</note> of Jacob. Joseph, <transChange type="added">being</transChange> seventeen years old, was shepherding the flock with his brothers. Now he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a helper with the sons of Bilhah and the sons of Zilpah, the wives of his father. And Joseph brought a bad report of them to his father.

verses.name: Genesis 37:3
verses.text: Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his sons, for he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a son of his old age. And he made a robe with long sleeves<note placement="foot">Or “of many colors”</note> for him.

verses.name: Genesis 37:4
verses.text: When his brothers saw that their father loved him more than all his brothers, they hated him and were not able to speak peaceably to him.  <div eID="gen213" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 37:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv131"/><div sID="gen214" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv131"/>And Joseph dreamed a dream, and he told <transChange type="added">it</transChange> to his brothers. And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they hated him even more⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “they added still to hate him”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 37:6
verses.text: And he said to them, “Listen now to this dream that I dreamed.

verses.name: Genesis 37:7
verses.text: Now behold, we were binding sheaves in the midst of the field and, behold, my sheaf stood up and it remained standing. Then behold, your sheaves gathered around and bowed down to my sheaf.”

verses.name: Genesis 37:8
verses.text: Then his brothers said to him, “Will you really rule over us?” And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they hated him even more⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “they added still to hate him”</note> on account of his dream and because of his words.

verses.name: Genesis 37:9
verses.text: Then he dreamed yet another dream and told it to his brothers. And he said, “Behold, I dreamed a dream again, and behold, the sun and the moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me.”

verses.name: Genesis 37:10
verses.text: And he told <transChange type="added">it</transChange> to his father and to his brothers. And his father rebuked him and said to him, “What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> this dream that you have dreamed? Will I and your mother and your brothers indeed come to bow down to the ground to you?”

verses.name: Genesis 37:11
verses.text: And his brothers were jealous of him, but his father kept the matter <transChange type="added">in mind</transChange>.  <div eID="gen214" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 37:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv132"/><title type="x-s">Joseph Sold Into Slavery by his Brothers</title> <div sID="gen215" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv132"/>Now his brothers went to pasture the flock of their father in Shechem.

verses.name: Genesis 37:13
verses.text: And Israel said to Joseph, “Are not your brothers pasturing in Shechem? Come, let me send you to them.” And he said, “Here I <transChange type="added">am</transChange>.”

verses.name: Genesis 37:14
verses.text: Then he said to him, “Go now, see <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞if it goes well for your brothers and for the flock⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “see the peace of your brothers and the peace of the flock”</note> then return word to me.” And he sent him from the valley of Hebron, and he arrived at Shechem.

verses.name: Genesis 37:15
verses.text: And a man found him, and behold, he<note placement="foot">That is, Joseph</note> was wandering about in a field. And the man asked him, “What do you seek?”

verses.name: Genesis 37:16
verses.text: And he said, “I am seeking my brothers. Tell me, please, where they are pasturing.”

verses.name: Genesis 37:17
verses.text: And the man said, “They have moved on from here, for I heard <transChange type="added">them</transChange> saying, ‘Let us go to Dothan.’ ” Then Joseph went after his brothers and found them in Dothan.

verses.name: Genesis 37:18
verses.text: And they saw him from a distance. And before he drew near to them, they conspired against him to kill him.

verses.name: Genesis 37:19
verses.text: And each said to his brothers, “Look, this master of dreams is coming.

verses.name: Genesis 37:20
verses.text: Now then, come, let us kill him and throw him in one of the pits. Then we will say a wild animal devoured him. Then we will see what his dreams become.”

verses.name: Genesis 37:21
verses.text: And Reuben heard <transChange type="added">it</transChange> and delivered him from their hand and said, “We must not take his life.”

verses.name: Genesis 37:22
verses.text: And Reuben said to them, “You must not shed blood. Throw him into this pit that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in the desert, but do not lay a hand on him”—so that he might rescue him from their hand to return him to his father.

verses.name: Genesis 37:23
verses.text: And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> as Joseph came to his brothers they stripped Joseph of his robe, the robe with long sleeves,<note placement="foot">Or “of many colors”</note> that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> upon him.

verses.name: Genesis 37:24
verses.text: And they took him and threw him into the pit (the pit <transChange type="added">was</transChange> empty; there was no water in it).

verses.name: Genesis 37:25
verses.text: Then they sat down to eat <transChange type="added">some</transChange> food. And they lifted up their eyes and looked, and behold, a caravan of Ishmaelites was coming from Gilead. And their camels were carrying aromatic gum and balm and spices <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞on the way⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “going to bring down”</note> to Egypt.

verses.name: Genesis 37:26
verses.text: Then Judah said to his brothers, “What profit <transChange type="added">is there</transChange> if we kill our brother and conceal his blood?

verses.name: Genesis 37:27
verses.text: Come, let us sell him to the Ishmaelites, but our hand shall not be against him, for he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> our brother, our own flesh.” And his brothers agreed.

verses.name: Genesis 37:28
verses.text: Then Midianite traders passed by. And they<note placement="foot">That is, the brothers</note> drew Joseph up and brought <transChange type="added">him</transChange> up from the pit, and they sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites for twenty <transChange type="added">pieces of</transChange> silver. And they brought Joseph to Egypt.

verses.name: Genesis 37:29
verses.text: Then Reuben returned to the pit and, behold, Joseph was not in the pit. And he tore his clothes.

verses.name: Genesis 37:30
verses.text: And he returned to his brothers and said, “The boy <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞is gone⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!<note placement="foot">Literally “is not”</note> Now I, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞what can I do⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?”<note placement="foot">Literally “where am I going?”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 37:31
verses.text: Then they took the robe of Joseph and slaughtered a goat, and dipped the robe in the blood.

verses.name: Genesis 37:32
verses.text: Then they sent the robe with long sleeves<note placement="foot">Or “of many colors”</note> and they brought <transChange type="added">it</transChange> to their father and said, “We found this; please examine <transChange type="added">it</transChange>. <transChange type="added">Is</transChange> it the robe of your son or not?”

verses.name: Genesis 37:33
verses.text: And he recognized it and said, “The robe of my son! A wild animal has devoured him! Joseph <transChange type="added">is</transChange> surely torn to pieces!”

verses.name: Genesis 37:34
verses.text: And Jacob tore his clothes and put sackcloth on his loins and mourned for his son many days.

verses.name: Genesis 37:35
verses.text: And all his sons and daughters tried to console him, but he refused to be consoled. And he said, “No, I shall go down to my son, to Sheol, mourning.” And his father wept for him.

verses.name: Genesis 37:36
verses.text: And the Midianites sold him in Egypt to Potiphar, a court official of Pharaoh, a commander of the imperial guard.  <chapter eID="Gen.37"/>

verses.name: Genesis 38:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv133"/><title type="x-s">Judah and Tamar</title> <div sID="gen216" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv133"/>And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> at that time Judah went down from his brothers and pitched his tent near a certain Adullamite, whose name <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Hirah.

verses.name: Genesis 38:2
verses.text: And Judah saw the daughter of a certain Canaanite there whose name <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Shua. And he took her and went in to her.

verses.name: Genesis 38:3
verses.text: And she conceived and bore a son, and he called his name Er.

verses.name: Genesis 38:4
verses.text: And she conceived again and bore a son, and he called his name Onan.

verses.name: Genesis 38:5
verses.text: And once again she bore a son, and she called his name Shelah. And he<note placement="foot">That is, Judah</note> was in Chezib when she bore him.

verses.name: Genesis 38:6
verses.text: And Judah took a wife for Er his firstborn, and her name <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Tamar.

verses.name: Genesis 38:7
verses.text: And Er, the firstborn of Judah, was evil in the eyes of Yahweh, and Yahweh killed him.

verses.name: Genesis 38:8
verses.text: Then Judah said to Onan, “Go in to the wife of your brother and perform the duty of a brother-in-law to her, and raise up offspring for your brother.”

verses.name: Genesis 38:9
verses.text: But Onan knew that the offspring would not be for him, so whenever he went in to the wife of his brother he would waste <transChange type="added">it</transChange> on the ground<note placement="foot">Meaning he would spill his semen on the ground</note> so as not to give offspring to his brother.

verses.name: Genesis 38:10
verses.text: And what he did was evil in the sight of Yahweh, so he killed him also.

verses.name: Genesis 38:11
verses.text: Then Judah said to Tamar, his daughter-in-law, “Stay a widow in your father’s house until Shelah my son grows up,” for <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he feared he would also die⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “he thought lest he also will die”</note> like his brother. So Tamar went and stayed in the house of her father.

verses.name: Genesis 38:12
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And in the course of time⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And the days increased”</note> the daughter of Shua, the wife of Judah, died. When Judah was consoled he went up to his sheepshearers, he and his friend Hirah the Adullamite, to Timnah.

verses.name: Genesis 38:13
verses.text: And it was told to Tamar, saying, “Look, your father-in-law is going up to Timnah to shear his sheep.”

verses.name: Genesis 38:14
verses.text: So she removed the clothes of her widowhood and covered <transChange type="added">herself</transChange> with the veil and disguised herself. And she sat at the entrance to Eynayim, which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> on the way to Timnah, for she saw that Shelah was grown but she had not been given to him as a wife.

verses.name: Genesis 38:15
verses.text: And Judah saw her and reckoned her to <transChange type="added">be</transChange> a prostitute, for she had covered her face.

verses.name: Genesis 38:16
verses.text: And he turned aside to her at the roadside and said, “Please come, let me come in to you,” for he did not know that she <transChange type="added">was</transChange> his daughter-in-law. And she said, “What will you give to me that you may come in to me?”

verses.name: Genesis 38:17
verses.text: And he said, “I will send a kid from the goats of the flock.” And she said, “<transChange type="added">Only</transChange> if you give a pledge until you send <transChange type="added">it</transChange>.”

verses.name: Genesis 38:18
verses.text: And he said, “What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the pledge that I must give to you?” And she said, “your seal, your cord, and your staff that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in your hand.” And he gave <transChange type="added">them</transChange> to her and went in to her. And she conceived by him.

verses.name: Genesis 38:19
verses.text: And she arose and left, and she removed her veil from herself and put on the garments of her widowhood.

verses.name: Genesis 38:20
verses.text: And Judah sent the kid from the goats by the hand of his friend the Adullamite to take <transChange type="added">back</transChange> the pledge from the hand of the woman, but he could not find her.

verses.name: Genesis 38:21
verses.text: So he asked the men of her place, saying, “Where <transChange type="added">is</transChange> that cult prostitute <transChange type="added">that was</transChange> at Eynayim by the roadside?” And they said, “There is no cult prostitute here.”

verses.name: Genesis 38:22
verses.text: Then he returned to Judah and said, “I could not find her. Morever, the men of the place said, ‘There is no cult prostitute here.’ ”

verses.name: Genesis 38:23
verses.text: And Judah said, “Let her take <transChange type="added">them</transChange> for herself, lest we be <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞laughed at⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “as contempt”</note> Behold, I sent this kid, but you could not find her.”

verses.name: Genesis 38:24
verses.text: And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞about three months later⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “it happened about three months”</note> it was told to Judah, “Tamar your daughter-in-law has played the whore, and now, behold, she has conceived by prostitution.” And Judah said, “Bring her out and let her be burned.”

verses.name: Genesis 38:25
verses.text: She was brought out, but she sent to her father-in-law saying, “By the man to whom these <transChange type="added">belong</transChange> I have conceived.” And she said, “Now discern<note placement="foot">Or “examine”</note> to whom these <transChange type="added">belong</transChange>: the seal and cord and the staff.”

verses.name: Genesis 38:26
verses.text: Then Judah recognized <transChange type="added">them</transChange> and said, “She is more righteous than I, since I did not give her to my son Shelah.” And he did not know<note placement="foot">“Know” is a euphemism for “have sexual relations with”</note> her again.

verses.name: Genesis 38:27
verses.text: And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> at the time she gave birth that, behold, twins <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in her womb.

verses.name: Genesis 38:28
verses.text: And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> at her labor one <transChange type="added">child</transChange> put out a hand. And the midwife took <transChange type="added">it</transChange> and tied a crimson thread on his hand saying, “This <transChange type="added">one</transChange> came out first.”

verses.name: Genesis 38:29
verses.text: Then his hand drew back and, behold, his brother came out, and she said, “What a breach you have made for yourself!” And she called his name Perez.

verses.name: Genesis 38:30
verses.text: And afterward his brother who <transChange type="added">had</transChange> the crimson thread on his hand came out. And his name was called Zerah.  <chapter eID="Gen.38"/>

verses.name: Genesis 39:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv134"/><title type="x-s">Joseph in Potiphar’s House</title> <div sID="gen217" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv134"/>Now Joseph had been brought down to Egypt, and Potiphar, a court official of Pharaoh, commander of the guard, an Egyptian, bought him from the hand of the Ishmaelites who had brought him down there.

verses.name: Genesis 39:2
verses.text: And Yahweh was with Joseph, and he became a successful man. And he was in the house of his master, the Egyptian.

verses.name: Genesis 39:3
verses.text: And his master observed that Yahweh <transChange type="added">was</transChange> with him, and everything that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in his hand to do Yahweh made successful.

verses.name: Genesis 39:4
verses.text: And Joseph found favor in his eyes and he served him. Then he appointed him<note placement="foot">That is, Joseph</note> over his house and all that he owned he put into his hand.

verses.name: Genesis 39:5
verses.text: And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> from the time he appointed him over his house and over all that he had, Yahweh blessed the house of the Egyptian on account of Joseph. And the blessing of Yahweh was upon all that he had in the house and in the field.

verses.name: Genesis 39:6
verses.text: And he left all that he had in the hand of Joseph, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he did not worry about anything⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “he did not know with him anything”</note> except the food that he ate. Now Joseph was <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞well built and handsome⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “beautiful of form and beautiful of appearance”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 39:7
verses.text: And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> after these things his master’s wife cast her eyes on Joseph, and she said, “Lie with me.”

verses.name: Genesis 39:8
verses.text: But he refused and said to his master’s wife, “Look, my master <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞does not worry about⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “does not know with me”</note> what <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in the house, and everything he owns he has put in my hand.

verses.name: Genesis 39:9
verses.text: He has no greater <transChange type="added">authority</transChange> in this house than me, and he has not withheld anything from me except you, since you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> his wife. Now how could I do this great wickedness and sin against God?”

verses.name: Genesis 39:10
verses.text: And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> as she spoke to Joseph <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞day after day⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “day, day”</note> he did not heed her to lie beside her or to be with her.

verses.name: Genesis 39:11
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞But one particular day⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and it happened as this day”</note> he came into the house to do his work and none of the men of the house were there in the house,

verses.name: Genesis 39:12
verses.text: she seized him by his garment <transChange type="added">and</transChange> said, “Lie with me!” And he left his garment in her hand and fled, and he went outside.

verses.name: Genesis 39:13
verses.text: And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> when she saw that he left his garment in her hand and fled outside,

verses.name: Genesis 39:14
verses.text: she called to the men of her house and said to them, “Look! He<note placement="foot">That is, Potiphar</note> brought a Hebrew man to us to mock us! He came to me to lie with me, and I cried out with a loud voice.

verses.name: Genesis 39:15
verses.text: And when he heard <transChange type="added">me</transChange>, that I raised my voice and called out, he left his garment beside me and fled, and he went outside.”

verses.name: Genesis 39:16
verses.text: Then she put his garment beside her until his master came to his house.

verses.name: Genesis 39:17
verses.text: Then she spoke to him according to these words, saying, “The Hebrew slave that you brought to us came to me to make fun of me.

verses.name: Genesis 39:18
verses.text: And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> as I raised my voice and called out, he left his garment beside me and fled outside.”

verses.name: Genesis 39:19
verses.text: And when his master heard the words of his wife that she spoke to him, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞This is what your servant did to me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,”<note placement="foot">Literally “according to these words your servant did to me”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he became very angry⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “his nostrils became hot”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 39:20
verses.text: And Joseph’s master took him and put him into prison, the place that the king’s prisoners were confined. And he was there in prison.

verses.name: Genesis 39:21
verses.text: And Yahweh was with Joseph, and showed loyal love to him, and gave him favor in the eyes of the chief of the prison.

verses.name: Genesis 39:22
verses.text: And the chief of the prison put all the prisoners that <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in the prison into the hand of Joseph. And everything that was done there, he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> the one who did <transChange type="added">it</transChange>.

verses.name: Genesis 39:23
verses.text: The chief of the prison <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞did not worry about⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “did not pay heed to”</note> anything in his<note placement="foot">That is, Joseph’s</note> hand, since Yahweh <transChange type="added">was</transChange> with him. And whatever he did Yahweh made <transChange type="added">it</transChange> successful.  <chapter eID="Gen.39"/>

verses.name: Genesis 40:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv135"/><title type="x-s">Joseph Interprets Dreams in Prison</title> <div sID="gen218" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv135"/>And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> after these things the cupbearer of the king of Egypt and <transChange type="added">his</transChange> baker did wrong against their lord, against the king of Egypt.

verses.name: Genesis 40:2
verses.text: And Pharaoh was angry with his two officials, with the chief cupbearer and chief baker.

verses.name: Genesis 40:3
verses.text: And he put them in custody in the house of the chief of the guard, into the prison where Joseph was confined.

verses.name: Genesis 40:4
verses.text: And the chief of the guard appointed Joseph <transChange type="added">to be</transChange> with them, and he attended them. And they were in custody <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞many days⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “days”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 40:5
verses.text: And the two of them, the cupbearer and the baker of the king of Egypt, who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> confined in the prison, dreamed a dream, each his own dream, with its own interpretation.

verses.name: Genesis 40:6
verses.text: When Joseph came to them in the morning he looked at them, and behold, they were troubled.

verses.name: Genesis 40:7
verses.text: And he asked the court officials of Pharaoh that <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him in the custody of his master’s house, “Why <transChange type="added">are</transChange> your faces sad today?”

verses.name: Genesis 40:8
verses.text: And they said to him, “We <transChange type="added">each</transChange> dreamed a dream, but there is no one to interpret it.” And Joseph said to them, “Do not interpretations belong to God? Please tell <transChange type="added">them</transChange> to me.”

verses.name: Genesis 40:9
verses.text: Then the chief cupbearer told his dream to Joseph, and he said to him, “In my dream, now behold, <transChange type="added">there was</transChange> a vine before me,

verses.name: Genesis 40:10
verses.text: and on the vine <transChange type="added">were</transChange> three branches. And as it budded, its blossoms came up, <transChange type="added">and</transChange> its clusters of grapes grew ripe.

verses.name: Genesis 40:11
verses.text: And the cup of Pharaoh <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in my hand, and I took the grapes and squeezed them into the cup of Pharaoh. Then I placed the cup into the hand of Pharaoh.”

verses.name: Genesis 40:12
verses.text: Then Joseph said to him, “This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> its interpretation: The three branches, they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> three days.

verses.name: Genesis 40:13
verses.text: In three days Pharaoh will lift up your head and will restore you to your office. And you shall put the cup of Pharaoh into his hand as <transChange type="added">was</transChange> formerly the custom, when you were his cupbearer.

verses.name: Genesis 40:14
verses.text: But remember me when it goes well with you, and please may you show kindness with respect to me, and mention me to Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house.

verses.name: Genesis 40:15
verses.text: For I was surely kidnapped from the land of the Hebrews, and here also I have done nothing that they should put me in this pit.”

verses.name: Genesis 40:16
verses.text: And when the chief baker saw that the interpretation <transChange type="added">was</transChange> good he said to Joseph, “I also <transChange type="added">dreamed</transChange>. In my dream, now behold, <transChange type="added">there were</transChange> three baskets of bread upon my head.

verses.name: Genesis 40:17
verses.text: And in the upper basket <transChange type="added">were</transChange> all sorts of baked foods for Pharaoh, but the birds were eating them out of the basket upon my head.”

verses.name: Genesis 40:18
verses.text: Then Joseph answered and said, “This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> its interpretation: The three baskets, they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> three days.

verses.name: Genesis 40:19
verses.text: In three days Pharaoh will lift your head from you and hang you on a pole,<note placement="foot">Or “tree”</note> and the birds will eat your flesh from you.”

verses.name: Genesis 40:20
verses.text: And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> on the third day, <transChange type="added">which was</transChange> Pharaoh’s birthday, he made a feast for all his servants. And he lifted up the head of the chief cupbearer and the head of the chief baker in the midst of his servants.

verses.name: Genesis 40:21
verses.text: And he restored the chief cupbearer to his cupbearing <transChange type="added">position</transChange>. And he placed the cup in the hand of Pharaoh.

verses.name: Genesis 40:22
verses.text: But the chief baker he hanged as Joseph had interpreted to them.

verses.name: Genesis 40:23
verses.text: But the chief cupbearer did not remember Joseph, but forgot him.  <chapter eID="Gen.40"/>

verses.name: Genesis 41:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv136"/><title type="x-s">Joseph Interprets Pharaoh’s Dreams</title> <div sID="gen219" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv136"/>And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> after <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞two full years⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “two years of days”</note> Pharaoh dreamed, and behold, he was standing by the Nile.

verses.name: Genesis 41:2
verses.text: And behold, seven cows, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞well built and fat⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “beautiful of appearance and healthy of flesh”</note> were coming up from the Nile, and they grazed among the reeds.

verses.name: Genesis 41:3
verses.text: And behold, seven other cows came up after them from the Nile, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞ugly and gaunt⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “Poor of appearance and thin of flesh”</note> and they stood beside those<note placement="foot">Or “the”</note> cows on the bank of the Nile.

verses.name: Genesis 41:4
verses.text: And the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞ugly and gaunt⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Poor of appearance and thin of flesh”</note> cows ate the seven <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞well built and fat⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “beautiful of appearance and healthy of flesh”</note> cows. Then Pharaoh awoke.

verses.name: Genesis 41:5
verses.text: And he fell asleep and dreamed a second time, and behold, seven ears of grain, plump and good, were coming out of one stalk.

verses.name: Genesis 41:6
verses.text: And behold, seven thin ears of grain, scorched by the east wind, sprouted up after them.

verses.name: Genesis 41:7
