verses.text: And the thin ears of grain swallowed up the seven plump and full ears of grain. Then Pharaoh awoke, and behold, <transChange type="added">it was</transChange> a dream.

verses.name: Genesis 41:8
verses.text: And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> in the morning his spirit was troubled, and he sent and called all of the magicians<note placement="foot">Or “soothsayer priests”</note> of Egypt, and all its wise men, and Pharaoh told his dream to them. But <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they had no interpretation⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “there was no interpretation with them”</note> for Pharaoh.

verses.name: Genesis 41:9
verses.text: Then the chief of the cupbearers spoke with Pharaoh, saying, “I remember my sins today.

verses.name: Genesis 41:10
verses.text: Pharaoh was angry with his servants, and he put me and the chief baker in the custody of the house of the chief of the guard.

verses.name: Genesis 41:11
verses.text: And we dreamed a dream one night, I and he, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞each with a dream that had a meaning⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “each according to his dream we dreamed”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 41:12
verses.text: And there with us <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a young man, a Hebrew servant of the chief of the guard, and we told him <transChange type="added">the dream</transChange>, and he interpreted our dreams for us, each according to his dream he interpreted.

verses.name: Genesis 41:13
verses.text: And it happened just as he interpreted to us, so it was. He<note placement="foot">That is, Pharaoh</note> restored me to my office, and him<note placement="foot">That is, the chief baker</note> he<note placement="foot">That is, Pharaoh</note> hanged.”

verses.name: Genesis 41:14
verses.text: Then Pharaoh sent and called <transChange type="added">for</transChange> Joseph, and they brought him quickly from the prison. And he shaved and changed his clothing, and came to Pharaoh.

verses.name: Genesis 41:15
verses.text: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I dreamed a dream, but there is none to interpret it. Now, I have heard concerning you <transChange type="added">that when</transChange> you hear a dream <transChange type="added">you can</transChange> interpret it.”

verses.name: Genesis 41:16
verses.text: Then Joseph answered Pharaoh saying, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞It is not in my power⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “besides me”</note> God will answer <transChange type="added">concerning</transChange> the well-being of Pharaoh.”

verses.name: Genesis 41:17
verses.text: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, “<transChange type="added">Now</transChange> in my dream, behold, I was standing on the bank of the Nile,

verses.name: Genesis 41:18
verses.text: and behold, seven cows, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞well built and fat⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “beautiful of appearance and healthy of flesh”</note> were coming up from the Nile, and they grazed among the reeds.

verses.name: Genesis 41:19
verses.text: And behold, seven other cows came up after them from the Nile, very <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞ugly and gaunt⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Poor of appearance and thin of flesh”</note>—never have I seen <transChange type="added">any</transChange> as them in all the land of Egypt for ugliness.

verses.name: Genesis 41:20
verses.text: And the thin and ugly cows ate the former seven healthy cows.

verses.name: Genesis 41:21
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">when</transChange> they went into their bellies<note placement="foot">Or “inner parts”</note> it could not be known that they went into their bellies,<note placement="foot">Or “inner parts”</note> for their appearance <transChange type="added">was</transChange> as ugly as at the beginning. Then I awoke.

verses.name: Genesis 41:22
verses.text: Then I saw in my dream and behold, seven ears of grain were coming out of one stalk, full and good.

verses.name: Genesis 41:23
verses.text: And behold, seven withered ears of grain, thin <transChange type="added">and</transChange> scorched by the east wind, sprouted up after them.

verses.name: Genesis 41:24
verses.text: And the thin ears of grain swallowed up the seven good ears of grain. And I told the magicians,<note placement="foot">Or “soothsayer priests”</note> but there was none to explain <transChange type="added">it</transChange> to me.”

verses.name: Genesis 41:25
verses.text: Then Joseph said to Pharaoh, “The dreams of Pharaoh <transChange type="added">are</transChange> one. God has revealed to Pharaoh what he is about to do.

verses.name: Genesis 41:26
verses.text: The seven good cows, they are seven years, and the seven good ears of grain, they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> seven years. The dreams <transChange type="added">are</transChange> one.

verses.name: Genesis 41:27
verses.text: And the seven thin and ugly cows coming up after them, they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> seven years, and the seven empty ears of grain, scorched by the east wind, they are <transChange type="added">also</transChange> seven years of famine.

verses.name: Genesis 41:28
verses.text: This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the word that I have spoken to Pharaoh; God has shown Pharaoh what he is about to do.

verses.name: Genesis 41:29
verses.text: Behold, seven years of great abundance are coming throughout the whole land of Egypt.

verses.name: Genesis 41:30
verses.text: Then seven years of famine will arise after them, and all the abundance in the land of Egypt will be forgotten. The famine will consume the land.

verses.name: Genesis 41:31
verses.text: Abundance in the land will not be known because of the famine <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞that follows⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “that thus afterwards”</note> for it will be very heavy.

verses.name: Genesis 41:32
verses.text: Now concerning the repetition of the dream twice to Pharaoh, <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> because the matter <transChange type="added">is</transChange> established by God, and God will do <transChange type="added">it</transChange> quickly.

verses.name: Genesis 41:33
verses.text: Now then, let Pharaoh select a man <transChange type="added">who is</transChange> discerning and wise, and let him set him over the land of Egypt.

verses.name: Genesis 41:34
verses.text: Let Pharaoh do <transChange type="added">this</transChange>, and let him appoint supervisors over the land, and let him take one-fifth from the land of Egypt in the seven years of abundance.

verses.name: Genesis 41:35
verses.text: Then let them gather all the food of these coming good years and let them pile up grain under the hand of Pharaoh <transChange type="added">for</transChange> food in the cities, and let them keep <transChange type="added">it</transChange>.

verses.name: Genesis 41:36
verses.text: Then the food shall be as a deposit for the land for the seven years of the famine that will be in the land of Egypt, that the land will not perish on account of the famine.”  <div eID="gen219" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 41:37
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv137"/><title type="x-s">Joseph Rises to Power</title> <div sID="gen220" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv137"/>And the plan<note placement="foot">Or “word”</note> was good in the eyes of Pharaoh and in the eyes of all his servants.

verses.name: Genesis 41:38
verses.text: Then Pharaoh said to his servants, “Can we find a man like this in whom is the spirit of God?”

verses.name: Genesis 41:39
verses.text: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Since God has made all of this known to you there is no one as discerning and wise as you.

verses.name: Genesis 41:40
verses.text: You shall be over my house, and to your word<note placement="foot">Or “mouth”</note> all my people shall submit. Only <transChange type="added">with respect to</transChange> the throne will I be greater than you.”

verses.name: Genesis 41:41
verses.text: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, “See, I have set you over all the land of Egypt.”

verses.name: Genesis 41:42
verses.text: Then Pharaoh removed his signet ring from his finger and put it on the finger of Joseph. And he clothed him with garments of fine linen, and he put a chain of gold around his neck.

verses.name: Genesis 41:43
verses.text: And he had him ride in his second chariot. And they cried out before him, “Kneel!” And Pharaoh set him over all the land of Egypt.

verses.name: Genesis 41:44
verses.text: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> Pharaoh, but without your consent no one will lift his hand or his foot in all the land of Egypt.”

verses.name: Genesis 41:45
verses.text: And Pharaoh called the name of Joseph Zaphenath-paneah and gave him Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, as a wife. And Joseph went out over the land of Egypt.

verses.name: Genesis 41:46
verses.text: Now Joseph <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞was thirty years old⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a son of thirty years”</note> when he stood before Pharaoh, the king of Egypt. And Joseph went out from the presence of Pharaoh and traveled through the whole land of Egypt.

verses.name: Genesis 41:47
verses.text: And the land produced a plenty in the seven years of abundance.

verses.name: Genesis 41:48
verses.text: And he gathered all the food of the seven years which <transChange type="added">occurred</transChange> in the land of Egypt. And he stored the food in the cities. The food of the field that surrounded <transChange type="added">each</transChange> city he stored in its midst.

verses.name: Genesis 41:49
verses.text: And Joseph piled up grain like the sand of the sea in great abundance until he stopped counting <transChange type="added">it</transChange>, for <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞it could not be counted⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “there was no number”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 41:50
verses.text: Before the years of famine came, Asenath, daughter of Potiphera priest of On, bore two sons to him.

verses.name: Genesis 41:51
verses.text: And Joseph called the name of the firstborn Manasseh, for <transChange type="added">he said</transChange>, “God has caused me to forget all my hardship and all my father’s house.”

verses.name: Genesis 41:52
verses.text: And the name of the second he called Ephraim, for <transChange type="added">he said</transChange>, “God has made me fruitful in the land of my misfortune.”

verses.name: Genesis 41:53
verses.text: And the seven years of abundance which <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in the land of Egypt came to an end.

verses.name: Genesis 41:54
verses.text: And the seven years of famine began to come as Joseph had said. And there was famine in all of the countries, but in the land of Egypt there was food.

verses.name: Genesis 41:55
verses.text: And when all the land of Egypt was hungry the people cried out to Pharaoh for food. And Pharaoh said to all the land of Egypt, “Go to Joseph; what he says to you, you must do.”

verses.name: Genesis 41:56
verses.text: And the famine was over the whole land, and Joseph opened all the storehouses<note placement="foot">Hebrew “that which was in them”</note> and sold <transChange type="added">food</transChange> to the Egyptians. And the famine was severe in the land of Egypt.

verses.name: Genesis 41:57
verses.text: And every land came to Egypt to Joseph to buy grain, for the famine was severe in every land.  <chapter eID="Gen.41"/>

verses.name: Genesis 42:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv138"/><title type="x-s">Joseph’s Brothers Go to Egypt for Food</title> <div sID="gen221" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv138"/>When Jacob realized that there was grain in Egypt, Jacob said to his sons, “Why do you look at one another?”

verses.name: Genesis 42:2
verses.text: Then he said, “Look, I have heard that there is grain in Egypt. Go down there and buy grain for us there that we may live and not die.”

verses.name: Genesis 42:3
verses.text: And the ten brothers of Joseph went down to buy grain from Egypt.

verses.name: Genesis 42:4
verses.text: But Jacob did not send Benjamin, the brother of Joseph, for <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he feared harm would come to him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “he thought, lest harm encounter him”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 42:5
verses.text: Then the sons of Israel went to buy grain amid those <transChange type="added">other people</transChange> who went <transChange type="added">as well</transChange>, for there was famine in the land of Canaan.

verses.name: Genesis 42:6
verses.text: Now Joseph was the governor over the land. He <transChange type="added">was</transChange> the one who sold <transChange type="added">food</transChange> to all the people of the land. And the brothers of Joseph came and bowed down to him with their faces to the ground.

verses.name: Genesis 42:7
verses.text: And Joseph saw his brothers and recognized them, but he pretended to be a stranger to them. And he spoke with them harshly and said to them, “From where have you come?” And they said, “From the land of Canaan to buy food.”

verses.name: Genesis 42:8
verses.text: And Joseph recognized his brothers, but they did not recognize him.

verses.name: Genesis 42:9
verses.text: And Joseph remembered the dreams which he had dreamed concerning them, and he said to them, “You are spies! You have come to see the nakedness of the land!”

verses.name: Genesis 42:10
verses.text: And they said to him, “No, my lord, but your servants have come to buy food.

verses.name: Genesis 42:11
verses.text: We all are sons of one man. We <transChange type="added">are</transChange> honest <transChange type="added">men</transChange>. We, your servants, are not spies.”

verses.name: Genesis 42:12
verses.text: Then he said to them, “No, but you have come to see the nakedness of the land.”

verses.name: Genesis 42:13
verses.text: Then they said, “We, your servants, <transChange type="added">are</transChange> twelve brothers, the sons of one man in the land of Canaan, but behold, the youngest <transChange type="added">is</transChange> with our father today, and one is no more.”

verses.name: Genesis 42:14
verses.text: But Joseph said to them, “It <transChange type="added">is</transChange> what I said to you—you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> spies.

verses.name: Genesis 42:15
verses.text: By this you shall be tested. By the life of Pharaoh you will not go out from here unless your youngest brother comes here.

verses.name: Genesis 42:16
verses.text: Send one of you, and let him bring your brother, but you will be kept in prison so that your words might be tested <transChange type="added">to see</transChange> if <transChange type="added">there is</transChange> truth with you. And if not, by the life of Pharaoh surely you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> spies.”

verses.name: Genesis 42:17
verses.text: Then he gathered them into the prison for three days.

verses.name: Genesis 42:18
verses.text: On the third day Joseph said to them, “Do this and you will live; I fear God.

verses.name: Genesis 42:19
verses.text: If you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> honest, let one of your brothers be kept in prison <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞where you are now being kept⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “in the house of your custody”</note> but <transChange type="added">the rest of</transChange> you go, carry grain for the famine for your households.

verses.name: Genesis 42:20
verses.text: You must bring your youngest brother to me, and then your words will be confirmed and you will not die.” And they did so.

verses.name: Genesis 42:21
verses.text: Then each said to his brother, “Surely we <transChange type="added">are</transChange> guilty on account of our brother when we saw the anguish of his soul when he pleaded for mercy to us and we would not listen. Therefore this trouble has come to us.”

verses.name: Genesis 42:22
verses.text: Then Reuben answered them, saying, “Did I not say to you, do not sin against the boy? But you did not listen, and now, behold, his blood has been sought.”

verses.name: Genesis 42:23
verses.text: Now they did not know that Joseph understood, for the interpreter <transChange type="added">was</transChange> between them.

verses.name: Genesis 42:24
verses.text: And he turned away from them and wept. Then he returned to them and spoke to them, and took Simeon from them and tied him up in front of them.

verses.name: Genesis 42:25
verses.text: Then Joseph gave orders to fill their bags with grain and to return their money to each sack, and to give them provisions for the journey. Thus he did for them.

verses.name: Genesis 42:26
verses.text: Then they loaded their grain upon their donkeys and went <transChange type="added">away</transChange> from there.

verses.name: Genesis 42:27
verses.text: And one <transChange type="added">of them later</transChange> opened his sack to give fodder to his donkey at the lodging place and saw his money—behold, it <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in the mouth of his sack.

verses.name: Genesis 42:28
verses.text: And he said to his brothers, “My money was returned and moreover, behold, <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> in my sack!” Then <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞their hearts failed them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “their heart went out”</note> and each of them trembled <transChange type="added">and</transChange> said, “What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> this God has done to us?”  <div eID="gen221" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 42:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv139"/><div sID="gen222" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv139"/>And when they came to Jacob their father in the land of Canaan they told him everything <transChange type="added">that</transChange> had happened to them, saying,

verses.name: Genesis 42:30
verses.text: “The man, the lord of the land, spoke harshly to us and treated us as <transChange type="added">if we were</transChange> spying out the land.

verses.name: Genesis 42:31
verses.text: But we said to him, ‘We <transChange type="added">are</transChange> honest; we are not spies.

verses.name: Genesis 42:32
verses.text: We <transChange type="added">are</transChange> twelve brothers, the sons of our father. One is no more and the youngest <transChange type="added">is</transChange> with our father now in the land of Canaan.’

verses.name: Genesis 42:33
verses.text: Then the man, the lord of the land, said to us, ‘By this I will know that you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> honest. Leave one <transChange type="added">brother</transChange> with me, and take <transChange type="added">food for</transChange> the famine in your households and go.

verses.name: Genesis 42:34
verses.text: And bring your youngest brother to me. Then I will know that you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> not spies but you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> honest. And I will give your brother <transChange type="added">back</transChange> to you, and you will trade in the land.’ ”

verses.name: Genesis 42:35
verses.text: And it happened <transChange type="added">that when</transChange> they emptied their sacks, behold, each one’s pouch of money <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in his sack. And when they and their father saw the pouches of their money, they were greatly distressed.

verses.name: Genesis 42:36
verses.text: And Jacob their father said to them, “You have bereaved me—Joseph is no more and Simeon is no more, and Benjamin you would take! All of this <transChange type="added">is</transChange> against me!

verses.name: Genesis 42:37
verses.text: Then Reuben said to his father, “You may kill my two sons if I do not bring him back to you. Put him in my hand and I myself will return him to you.”

verses.name: Genesis 42:38
verses.text: But he said, “My son shall not go down with you, for his brother is dead and he alone remains. <transChange type="added">If</transChange> harm meets him on the journey that you would take, you would bring down my gray head in sorrow to Sheol.”  <chapter eID="Gen.42"/>

verses.name: Genesis 43:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv140"/><title type="x-s">Joseph’s Brothers Return to Egypt</title> <div sID="gen223" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv140"/>Now the famine in the land <transChange type="added">was</transChange> severe.

verses.name: Genesis 43:2
verses.text: And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> as they finished eating the grain which they had brought from Egypt their father said to them, “Return and buy a little food for us.”

verses.name: Genesis 43:3
verses.text: Then Judah said to him, “The man solemnly admonished us, saying, ‘You shall not see my face unless your brother <transChange type="added">is</transChange> with you.’

verses.name: Genesis 43:4
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞If you will send⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “if there is a sending”</note> our brother with us, we will go down and buy food for you,

verses.name: Genesis 43:5
verses.text: but <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞if you will not send⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “if there is no sending”</note> <transChange type="added">him</transChange>, we will not go down, for the man said to us, ‘You shall not see my face unless your brother <transChange type="added">is</transChange> with you.’ ”

verses.name: Genesis 43:6
verses.text: Then Israel said, “Why did you bring trouble to me by telling the man you still had a brother?”

verses.name: Genesis 43:7
verses.text: And they said, “The man asked explicitly about us and about our family, saying, ‘Is your father still alive? Do you have a brother?’ And we answered him according to these words. How could we know that he would say, ‘Bring down your brother’?”

verses.name: Genesis 43:8
verses.text: Then Judah said to his father Israel, “Send the boy with me, and let us arise and go, so that we will live and not die—you, we, and our children.

verses.name: Genesis 43:9
verses.text: I myself will be surety for him. You may seek him from my hand. If I do not bring him back to you and present him before you, then I will stand guilty before you forever.

verses.name: Genesis 43:10
verses.text: Surely if we had not hesitated by this <transChange type="added">time</transChange> we would have returned twice.”

verses.name: Genesis 43:11
verses.text: Then their father Israel said to them, “If <transChange type="added">it must be</transChange> so then do this. Take some of the best products of the land in your bags and take them down to the man as a gift—a little balm and honey, aromatic gum and myrrh, and pistachios and almonds.

verses.name: Genesis 43:12
verses.text: And take double <transChange type="added">the</transChange> money in your hands. Take back the money that was returned in the mouth of your sacks. Perhaps it <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a mistake.

verses.name: Genesis 43:13
verses.text: And take your brother. Now arise and return to the man.

verses.name: Genesis 43:14
verses.text: And may El-Shaddai<note placement="foot">Often translated “God Almighty”</note> grant you compassion before the man that he may release your other brother to you and Benjamin. As for me, if I am bereaved, I am bereaved.”  <div eID="gen223" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 43:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv141"/><div sID="gen224" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv141"/>So the men took this gift, and they took double money in their hands, and Benjamin, and they rose up and went down to Egypt and stood before Joseph.

verses.name: Genesis 43:16
verses.text: When Joseph saw Benjamin with them he said to the one who <transChange type="added">was</transChange> over his household, “Bring the men into the house and slaughter and prepare <transChange type="added">an animal</transChange>, for the men shall eat with me at noon.”

verses.name: Genesis 43:17
verses.text: And the man did as Joseph had said, and the man brought the men into the house of Joseph.

verses.name: Genesis 43:18
verses.text: And the men were afraid when they were brought into the house of Joseph. And they said “We were brought <transChange type="added">here</transChange> on account of the money that was returned to our sacks the first time, that he might attack us and fall upon us to take us as slaves with our donkeys.”

verses.name: Genesis 43:19
verses.text: So they approached the man who <transChange type="added">was</transChange> over Joseph’s house and spoke to him at the doorway of the house.

verses.name: Genesis 43:20
verses.text: And they said, “Please, my lord, we surely came down once before to buy food,

verses.name: Genesis 43:21
verses.text: but when we came to the place of lodging and we opened our sacks, then behold, each one’s money <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in the mouth of his sack—our money in its <transChange type="added">full</transChange> weight—so we have returned <transChange type="added">with</transChange> it in our hands.

verses.name: Genesis 43:22
verses.text: Now, other money we have brought down in our hand to buy food. We do not know who put our money in our sacks.”

verses.name: Genesis 43:23
verses.text: And he said, “Peace to you; do not be afraid. Your God and the God of your father must have given you a treasure in your sacks; your money came to me.” And he brought Simeon out to them.

verses.name: Genesis 43:24
verses.text: Then the man brought the men into Joseph’s house and he gave them water and washed their feet, and gave fodder to their donkeys.

verses.name: Genesis 43:25
verses.text: Then they laid out<note placement="foot">Or “prepared”</note> the gift until Joseph came at noon, for they had heard that they were to eat food there.

verses.name: Genesis 43:26
verses.text: And when Joseph came into the house they brought the gift that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in their hand into the house to him, and they bowed down before him to the ground.

verses.name: Genesis 43:27
verses.text: And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he greeted them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “he asked peace for them”</note> and said, “Is your father well, the old man of whom you spoke? Is he still alive?”

verses.name: Genesis 43:28
verses.text: And they said, “Your servant our father <transChange type="added">is</transChange> well; he is still alive.” And they knelt and bowed down.

verses.name: Genesis 43:29
verses.text: Then he lifted up his eyes and saw Benjamin his brother, the son of his mother, and said, “Is this your youngest brother of whom you told me?” And he continued,<note placement="foot">Or “said”</note> “God be gracious to you, my son.”

verses.name: Genesis 43:30
verses.text: Then Joseph <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞hurried away⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “made haste”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞being overcome with emotion⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “his compassion boiled up”</note> toward his brother, and sought for <transChange type="added">a place</transChange> to cry. Then he went into a room and wept there.

verses.name: Genesis 43:31
verses.text: Then he washed his face and went out, now controlling himself, and said, “Serve the food.”

verses.name: Genesis 43:32
verses.text: And they served him<note placement="foot">That is, Joseph</note> by himself, and them by themselves, and the Egyptians who were eating with him by themselves, for Egyptians <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞could not dine⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “were not able to eat food”</note> with Hebrews, because that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a detestable thing to Egyptians.

verses.name: Genesis 43:33
verses.text: And they were seated before him <transChange type="added">from</transChange> the firstborn according to his birthright <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the youngest according to his youth. And the men <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞looked at one another⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “each to his companion”</note> amazed.

verses.name: Genesis 43:34
verses.text: And portions were served to them from <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his table⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “his presence”</note> and the portion of Benjamin was five times greater than the portion of any of them. And they drank and became drunk with him.  <chapter eID="Gen.43"/>

verses.name: Genesis 44:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv142"/><title type="x-s">Joseph Tests His Brothers</title> <div sID="gen225" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv142"/>Then he commanded <transChange type="added">the one</transChange> who <transChange type="added">was</transChange> over his household, saying, “Fill the sacks of the men <transChange type="added">with</transChange> food as much as they are able to carry, and put each one’s money in the mouth of his sack.

verses.name: Genesis 44:2
verses.text: And my cup—the cup of silver—you shall put into the mouth of the sack of the youngest, and the money for his grain. And he did according to the word of Joseph that he had commanded.

verses.name: Genesis 44:3
verses.text: <transChange type="added">When</transChange> the morning light <transChange type="added">came</transChange> the men were sent away, they and their donkeys.

verses.name: Genesis 44:4
verses.text: They went out of the city, <transChange type="added">and</transChange> had not gone far when Joseph said to <transChange type="added">the one</transChange> who <transChange type="added">was</transChange> over his house, “Arise! Pursue after the men and overtake them. Then you shall say to them, ‘Why have you repaid evil for good?

verses.name: Genesis 44:5
verses.text: Is this not that from which my master drinks? Now he himself certainly practices divination with it. You have done evil <transChange type="added">in</transChange> what you have done.’ ”

verses.name: Genesis 44:6
verses.text: When he overtook them he spoke these words to them.

verses.name: Genesis 44:7
verses.text: And they said to him, “Why has my lord spoken according to these words? Far be it from your servants to do such a thing!

verses.name: Genesis 44:8
verses.text: Behold, the money that we found in the mouth of our sacks we returned to you from the land of Canaan. Now why would we steal silver or gold from the house of my lord?

verses.name: Genesis 44:9
verses.text: Whoever is found with it from among your servants shall die. And moreover, we will become slaves to my lord.”

verses.name: Genesis 44:10
verses.text: Then he said, “Now also according to your words, thus will it be. He who is found with it shall be my slave, but you shall be innocent.”

verses.name: Genesis 44:11
verses.text: Then each man quickly brought down his sack to the ground, and each one opened his sack.

verses.name: Genesis 44:12
verses.text: And he searched, beginning with the oldest and finishing with the youngest. And the cup was found in the sack of Benjamin.

verses.name: Genesis 44:13
verses.text: Then they tore their clothes, and each one loaded his donkey and they returned to the city.  <div eID="gen225" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 44:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv143"/><div sID="gen226" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv143"/>And Judah and his brothers came to the house of Joseph—now he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> still there—they fell before him to the ground.

verses.name: Genesis 44:15
verses.text: Then Joseph said to them, “What is this deed that you have done? Did you not know that a man who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> like me surely practices divination?”

verses.name: Genesis 44:16
verses.text: And Judah said, “What can we say to my lord? What can we speak? Now how can we show ourselves innocent? God has found the guilt of your servants! Behold, we <transChange type="added">are</transChange> slaves to my lord, both we and also he in whose hand the cup was found.”

verses.name: Genesis 44:17
verses.text: But he said, “Far be it from me to do this! The man in whose hand the cup was found, he will become my slave. But as for you, go up in peace to your father.”

verses.name: Genesis 44:18
verses.text: But Judah drew near to him and said, “Please my lord, let your servant speak a word in the ears of my lord, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞let not your anger burn⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “let not your nose become hot”</note> against your servant, for <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you are like Pharaoh himself⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “like you like Pharaoh”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 44:19
verses.text: My lord had asked his servants, saying, ‘Do you have a father or a brother?’

verses.name: Genesis 44:20
verses.text: And we said to my lord, ‘We have an aged father, and a younger <transChange type="added">brother</transChange>, the child of his old age, and his brother died, and he alone remains from his mother, and his father loves him.’

verses.name: Genesis 44:21
verses.text: Then you said to your servants, ‘Bring him down to me that I may set my eyes upon him.’

verses.name: Genesis 44:22
verses.text: Then we said to my lord, ‘The boy cannot leave his father; if he should leave his father, then he<note placement="foot">That is, the father (Jacob/Israel)</note> would die.’

verses.name: Genesis 44:23
verses.text: Then you said to your servants, ‘Unless your youngest brother comes down with you, you shall not again see my face.’

verses.name: Genesis 44:24
verses.text: And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> we went up to your servant, my father, and told him the words of my lord.

verses.name: Genesis 44:25
verses.text: And when our father said, ‘Buy a little food for us,’

verses.name: Genesis 44:26
verses.text: then we said, ‘We cannot go down. If our youngest brother <transChange type="added">is</transChange> with us, then we shall go down. For we will not be able to see the face of the man unless our youngest brother <transChange type="added">is</transChange> with us.’

verses.name: Genesis 44:27
verses.text: Then your servant, my father, said to us, ‘You yourselves know that my wife bore two sons to me.

verses.name: Genesis 44:28
verses.text: One went out from me, and I said, “Surely he must have been torn to pieces,” and I have never seen him since.

verses.name: Genesis 44:29
verses.text: And if you take this one also from me, and he encounters harm, you will bring down my gray head in sorrow to Sheol.’

verses.name: Genesis 44:30
verses.text: So now, when I come to your servant, my father, and the boy is not with us—now his life is bound up with his life—

verses.name: Genesis 44:31
verses.text: it shall happen <transChange type="added">that</transChange> when he sees that the boy is gone, he will die. And your servants will bring down the gray head of your servant, our father, to Sheol with sorrow.

verses.name: Genesis 44:32
verses.text: For your servant is pledged as surety for the boy by my father, saying, If I do not bring him to you, then I shall be culpable to my father forever.

verses.name: Genesis 44:33
verses.text: So then, please let your servant remain in place of the boy as a slave to my lord, and let the boy go up with his brothers.

verses.name: Genesis 44:34
verses.text: For how can I go up to my father if the boy is not with me? <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I do not want to see⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “lest I see”</note> the misery which will find my father.”  <chapter eID="Gen.44"/>

verses.name: Genesis 45:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv144"/><title type="x-s">Joseph Reveals His Identity</title> <div sID="gen227" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv144"/>Then Joseph was not able to control himself before all who were standing by him. And he cried out, “Make every man go out from me!” So no one stood with him when Joseph made himself known to his brothers.

verses.name: Genesis 45:2
verses.text: And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he wept loudly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “he gave his voice with weeping”</note> so that the Egyptians heard <transChange type="added">it</transChange> and the household of Pharaoh heard <transChange type="added">it</transChange>.

verses.name: Genesis 45:3
verses.text: Then Joseph said to his brothers, “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> Joseph! Is my father still alive?” And his brothers were unable to answer him, for they were dismayed at his presence.

verses.name: Genesis 45:4
verses.text: So Joseph said to his brothers, “Come near to me, please.” And they drew near. And he said, “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> Joseph, your brother, whom you sold into Egypt.

verses.name: Genesis 45:5
verses.text: So now, do not be distressed and do not be angry <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞with yourselves⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in your eyes”</note> that you sold me here, for God sent me as deliverance before you.

verses.name: Genesis 45:6
verses.text: For these two years the famine <transChange type="added">has been</transChange> in the midst of the land, but <transChange type="added">there will be</transChange> five more years where there is no plowing or harvest.

verses.name: Genesis 45:7
verses.text: And God sent me before you <transChange type="added">all</transChange> to preserve for you a remnant in the land and to keep alive among you many survivors.

verses.name: Genesis 45:8
verses.text: So now, you yourselves did not send me here, but God put me here as father to Pharaoh and as master of all his household, and a ruler over all the land of Egypt.

verses.name: Genesis 45:9
verses.text: Hurry, and go up to my father and say to him, ‘Thus says your son Joseph, God has made me lord of all Egypt. Come down to me and do not delay.

verses.name: Genesis 45:10
verses.text: You shall settle in the land of Goshen so that you will be near me, you and your children and your grandchildren, and your flocks and your herds and all that you have.

verses.name: Genesis 45:11
verses.text: And I will provide for you there, because <transChange type="added">there are</transChange> still five years of famine—lest you and your household and all that you have become destitute.’

verses.name: Genesis 45:12
verses.text: Now behold, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin see, that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞it is I⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “it is my mouth”</note> who am speaking to you.

verses.name: Genesis 45:13
verses.text: And you must tell my father of all my honor in Egypt and all that you have seen. Now hurry and bring my father here.”

verses.name: Genesis 45:14
verses.text: Then he fell upon the neck of his brother Benjamin and wept, and Benjamin wept upon his neck.

verses.name: Genesis 45:15
verses.text: And he kissed all his brothers and wept upon them. And afterward his brothers spoke with him.

verses.name: Genesis 45:16
verses.text: Then the report was heard <transChange type="added">in</transChange> the house of Pharaoh, saying, “Joseph’s brothers have come.” And it pleased Pharaoh and his servants.

verses.name: Genesis 45:17
verses.text: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Say to your brothers: ‘Do this—load your donkeys and go back to the land of Canaan,

verses.name: Genesis 45:18
verses.text: and take your father and your households and come to me, and I will give you the best of the land of Egypt, and you shall eat the fat of the land.’

verses.name: Genesis 45:19
verses.text: And you <transChange type="added">Joseph</transChange>, are commanded <transChange type="added">to say</transChange> this: ‘Do this! Take wagons from the land of Egypt for your little ones and your wives, and bring your father and come!

verses.name: Genesis 45:20
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Do not worry⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “let not your eyes be troubled”</note> about your possessions, for the best of all the land of Egypt is yours.’ ”  <div eID="gen227" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 45:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv145"/><div sID="gen228" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv145"/>And the sons of Israel did so. And Joseph gave them wagons at the word of Pharaoh, and gave them provisions for the journey.

verses.name: Genesis 45:22
verses.text: To each and to all of them he gave sets of clothing, but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver and five sets of clothing.

verses.name: Genesis 45:23
verses.text: And to his father he sent <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as follows⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>:<note placement="foot">Literally “according to this”</note> ten donkeys carrying the best of Egypt, and ten donkeys carrying grain and food and provisions for his father for the journey.

verses.name: Genesis 45:24
verses.text: Then he sent his brothers away, and when they departed he said to them, “Do not be agitated on the journey.”

verses.name: Genesis 45:25
verses.text: So they went up from Egypt and came to the land of Canaan to Jacob their father.

verses.name: Genesis 45:26
verses.text: And they spoke to him, saying, “Joseph <transChange type="added">is</transChange> still alive, and he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> ruler over all the land of Egypt.” And his heart <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞went numb⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Or “became cold”</note> because he did not believe him.

verses.name: Genesis 45:27
verses.text: Then they told him all the words of Joseph that he had spoken to them. And when he saw the wagons that Joseph had sent to carry him, then the spirit of Jacob their father revived.

verses.name: Genesis 45:28
verses.text: And Israel said, “<transChange type="added">It is</transChange> enough. Joseph my son <transChange type="added">is</transChange> still alive. I will go and see him before I die.”  <chapter eID="Gen.45"/>

verses.name: Genesis 46:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv146"/><title type="x-s">Jacob and His Offspring Go to Egypt</title> <div sID="gen229" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv146"/>So Israel journeyed with all that he had, and he came to Beersheba and offered sacrifices to the God of his father, Isaac.

verses.name: Genesis 46:2
verses.text: And God spoke to Israel in visions of the night and said, “Jacob, Jacob.” And he said, “Here I <transChange type="added">am</transChange>.”

verses.name: Genesis 46:3
verses.text: Then he said, “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> the God of your father. Do not be afraid to go down to Egypt, for I will make you a great nation there.

verses.name: Genesis 46:4
verses.text: I myself will go down with you to Egypt, and I myself will also bring you up. And Joseph will place his hand over your eyes.”

verses.name: Genesis 46:5
verses.text: So Jacob arose from Beersheba. And the sons of Israel carried their father Jacob, and their little ones and their wives in the wagons Pharaoh had sent to transport him.

verses.name: Genesis 46:6
verses.text: And they took their livestock and their possessions that they had acquired in the land of Canaan. And they came to Egypt, Jacob and all his offspring with him,

verses.name: Genesis 46:7
verses.text: his sons and his sons’ sons with him, his daughters and his daughters’ daughters with him, into Egypt.  <div eID="gen229" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 46:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv147"/><div sID="gen230" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv147"/>Now these <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the names of the sons of Israel, who came into Egypt, Jacob and his sons. Reuben, the firstborn of Jacob

verses.name: Genesis 46:9
verses.text: and the sons of Reuben: Enoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.

verses.name: Genesis 46:10
verses.text: The sons of Simeon: Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jakin, Zohar, and Shaul, the son of a Canaanite woman.

verses.name: Genesis 46:11
verses.text: The sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.

verses.name: Genesis 46:12
verses.text: The sons of Judah: Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez, and Zerah (but Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan). And the sons of Perez were Hezron and Hamul.

verses.name: Genesis 46:13
verses.text: The sons of Issachar: Tolah, Puvah, Iob, and Shimron.

verses.name: Genesis 46:14
verses.text: The sons of Zebulun: Sered, Elon, and Jahleel.

verses.name: Genesis 46:15
verses.text: These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the sons of Leah that she bore to Jacob in Paddan-Aram, and Dinah his daughter. His sons and daughters <transChange type="added">were</transChange> thirty-three persons in all.

verses.name: Genesis 46:16
verses.text: The sons of Gad: Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arodi, and Areli.

verses.name: Genesis 46:17
verses.text: The sons of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah, and their sister Serah. And the sons of Beriah: Heber and Malkiel.

verses.name: Genesis 46:18
verses.text: There <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the sons of Zilpah, whom Laban gave to Leah his daughter, and she bore these to Jacob—sixteen persons.

verses.name: Genesis 46:19
verses.text: The sons of Rachel, Jacob’s wife: Joseph and Benjamin.

verses.name: Genesis 46:20
verses.text: And Ephraim and Manasseh, whom Asenath, daughter of Potiphera, priest of On bore to him, were born to Joseph in the land of Egypt.

verses.name: Genesis 46:21
verses.text: The sons of Benjamin: Bela, Beker, Ashbel, Gera, Naaman, Ehi, Rosh, Muppim, Huppim, and Ard.

verses.name: Genesis 46:22
verses.text: These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the sons of Rachel who were born to Jacob—fourteen persons in all.

verses.name: Genesis 46:23
verses.text: The sons of Dan: Hushim.

verses.name: Genesis 46:24
verses.text: The sons of Naphtali: Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.

verses.name: Genesis 46:25
verses.text: These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the sons of Bilhah whom Laban gave to Rachel his daughter, and she bore these to Jacob—seven persons in all.

verses.name: Genesis 46:26
verses.text: All the persons belonging to Jacob who came to Egypt <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who were his descendants⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “those going out of his loins”</note> not including the wives of the sons of Jacob <transChange type="added">were</transChange> sixty-six persons in all.

verses.name: Genesis 46:27
verses.text: And the sons of Joseph who were born to him in Egypt <transChange type="added">were</transChange> two persons. All the persons of the house of Jacob who came to Egypt <transChange type="added">were</transChange> seventy.  <div eID="gen230" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 46:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv148"/><div sID="gen231" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv148"/>He<note placement="foot">That is, Jacob</note> had sent Judah ahead of him to Joseph to appear before him<note placement="foot">That is, Jacob</note> in Goshen. And they came to the land of Goshen.

verses.name: Genesis 46:29
verses.text: Then Joseph harnessed his chariot and went up to meet Israel his father in Goshen. He presented himself to him and fell upon his neck and wept upon his neck a long time.

verses.name: Genesis 46:30
verses.text: Then Israel said to Joseph, “Now let me die since I have seen your face, for you are still alive.”

verses.name: Genesis 46:31
verses.text: Then Joseph said to his brothers and to his father’s household, “I will go up and report to Pharaoh, and I will say to him, ‘My brothers and my father’s household who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in the land of Canaan have come to me.

verses.name: Genesis 46:32
verses.text: And the men <transChange type="added">are</transChange> shepherds, for they are men of livestock, and they have brought their flocks and their cattle and all that they have.’

verses.name: Genesis 46:33
verses.text: And it shall be <transChange type="added">that</transChange> when Pharaoh calls you he will say, ‘What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> your occupation?’

verses.name: Genesis 46:34
verses.text: Then you must say, ‘You servants <transChange type="added">are</transChange> men of livestock from our childhood until now, both we and also our ancestors,’<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> so that you may dwell in the land of Goshen, for every shepherd <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a detestable thing to Egyptians.”  <chapter eID="Gen.46"/>

verses.name: Genesis 47:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv149"/><title type="x-s">Jacob Settles in Goshen</title> <div sID="gen232" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv149"/>So Joseph went and reported to Pharaoh. And he said, “My father and my brothers, with their flocks and their herds, and all that they have, have come from the land of Canaan. Now <transChange type="added">they are</transChange> here in the land of Goshen.”

verses.name: Genesis 47:2
verses.text: And from among his brothers he took five men and presented them before Pharaoh.

verses.name: Genesis 47:3
verses.text: And Pharaoh said to his brothers, “What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> your occupation?” And they said to Pharaoh, “Your servants <transChange type="added">are</transChange> keepers of sheep, both we and also our ancestors.”<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 47:4
verses.text: And they said to Pharaoh, “We have come to sojourn in the land, for there is no pasture for your servant’s flocks, for the famine <transChange type="added">is</transChange> severe in the land of Canaan. So now, please let your servants dwell in the land of Goshen.”

verses.name: Genesis 47:5
verses.text: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Your father and your brothers have come to you.

verses.name: Genesis 47:6
verses.text: The land of Egypt <transChange type="added">is</transChange> before you. Settle your father and your brothers in the best of the land. Let them live in the land of Goshen, and if you know there is among them men of ability, then appoint them overseers of my own livestock.”

verses.name: Genesis 47:7
verses.text: Then Joseph brought his father Jacob and presented him before Pharaoh. And Jacob blessed Pharaoh.

verses.name: Genesis 47:8
verses.text: Then Pharaoh said to Jacob, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞How old are you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?”<note placement="foot">Literally “How many are the days of the years of your life?”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 47:9
verses.text: And Jacob said to Pharaoh, “The days of the years of my sojourning <transChange type="added">are</transChange> one hundred and thirty years. Few and hard have been the days of the years of my life, and they have not reached the days of the years of the lives of my ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> in the days of their sojourning.”

verses.name: Genesis 47:10
verses.text: And Jacob blessed Pharaoh, and he went out from the presence of Pharaoh.

verses.name: Genesis 47:11
verses.text: And Joseph settled his father and his brothers, and he gave them property in the land of Egypt in the best part of the land, in the land of Rameses, as Pharaoh had instructed.

verses.name: Genesis 47:12
verses.text: And Joseph provided his father and his brothers and all the household of his father with food, according to the number of their children.  <div eID="gen232" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 47:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv150"/><title type="x-s">The Famine in Egypt Continues</title> <div sID="gen233" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv150"/>Now there was no food in all the land, for the famine <transChange type="added">was</transChange> very severe. And the land of Egypt languished, with the land of Canaan, on account of the famine.

verses.name: Genesis 47:14
verses.text: And Joseph collected all the money found in the land of Egypt and in the land of Canaan in exchange for the grain that they were buying. And Joseph brought the money into the house of Pharaoh.

verses.name: Genesis 47:15
verses.text: And when the money was spent in the land of Egypt and from the land of Canaan, all of Egypt came to Joseph, saying, “Give us food! Why should we die before you? For the money is used up.”

verses.name: Genesis 47:16
verses.text: And Joseph said, “Give your livestock and I will give you <transChange type="added">food</transChange> in exchange for your livestock if <transChange type="added">your</transChange> money is used up.”

verses.name: Genesis 47:17
verses.text: So they brought their herds to Joseph, and Joseph gave food to them in exchange for horses, their flocks, and their cattle and donkeys. And he provided them with food in exchange for all their livestock that year.

verses.name: Genesis 47:18
verses.text: When that year ended, they came to him in the following year and said to him, “We cannot hide from my lord that <transChange type="added">our</transChange> money and livestock belong to my lord. Nothing remains before my lord except our bodies and our land.

verses.name: Genesis 47:19
verses.text: Why should we die in front of you, both we and our land? Buy us and our land in exchange for food, then we and our land will be servants to Pharaoh. Then give us seed and we shall live and not die, and the land will not become desolate.”

verses.name: Genesis 47:20
verses.text: So Joseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh, for each Egyptian sold his field, for the famine <transChange type="added">was</transChange> severe upon them. And the land became Pharaoh’s.

verses.name: Genesis 47:21
verses.text: As for the people, he transferred them to the cities, from one end of the territory of Egypt to the other.

verses.name: Genesis 47:22
verses.text: Only the land of the priests he did not buy, for <transChange type="added">there was</transChange> an allotment for the priests from Pharaoh, and they <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞lived on⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “ate”</note> the allotment that Pharaoh gave to them. Therefore they did not sell their land.

verses.name: Genesis 47:23
verses.text: And Joseph said to the people, “Look, I have bought you and your land this day for Pharaoh. Here <transChange type="added">is</transChange> seed for you so you can sow the land.

verses.name: Genesis 47:24
verses.text: And it shall happen <transChange type="added">that</transChange> at the harvest, you must give a fifth to Pharaoh and four-fifths shall be yours, as seed for the field and for your food and for those who <transChange type="added">are</transChange> in your households, and as food for your little ones.”

verses.name: Genesis 47:25
verses.text: And they said, “You have saved our lives. <transChange type="added">If</transChange> we have found favor in the eyes of my lord, we will be servants to Pharaoh.”

verses.name: Genesis 47:26
verses.text: So Joseph made it a statute unto this day concerning the land of Egypt: one fifth to Pharaoh. Only the land of the priests alone did not belong to Pharaoh.

verses.name: Genesis 47:27
verses.text: So Israel settled in the land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen. And they acquired possessions in it and were fruitful and multiplied greatly.

verses.name: Genesis 47:28
verses.text: And Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years. And the days of Jacob, the years of his life, were one hundred and forty-seven years.

verses.name: Genesis 47:29
verses.text: When <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the time of Israel’s death drew near⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the days of Israel drew near to die”</note> he called to his son, to Joseph. And he said to him, “If I have found favor in your eyes, please put your hand under my thigh, that you might vow to deal kindly<note placement="foot">Or “loyal love”</note> and faithfully with me. Please do not bury me in Egypt,

verses.name: Genesis 47:30
verses.text: but let me lie with my ancestors.<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> Carry me out of Egypt and bury me in their burial site.” And he said, “I will do according to your word.”

verses.name: Genesis 47:31
verses.text: Then he said, “Swear to me.” And he swore to him. Then Israel bowed himself on the head of the bed.  <chapter eID="Gen.47"/>

verses.name: Genesis 48:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv151"/><title type="x-s">Jacob Blesses Ephraim and Manasseh</title> <div sID="gen234" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv151"/>And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> after these things, it was said to Joseph, “Behold, your father <transChange type="added">is</transChange> ill.” And he took his two sons with him, Ephraim and Manasseh.

verses.name: Genesis 48:2
verses.text: And it was told to Jacob, “Behold, your son Joseph has come to you.” Then Israel strengthened himself and he sat up in the bed.

verses.name: Genesis 48:3
verses.text: Then Jacob said to Joseph, “El-Shaddai<note placement="foot">Often translated “God Almighty”</note> appeared to me in Luz, in the land of Canaan, and blessed me,

verses.name: Genesis 48:4
verses.text: and said to me, ‘Behold, I will make you fruitful and make you numerous, and will make you a company of nations. And I will give this land to your offspring after you <transChange type="added">as</transChange> an everlasting possession.’

verses.name: Genesis 48:5
verses.text: And now, your two sons who were born to you in the land of Egypt before my coming to you in Egypt, are mine. Ephraim and Manasseh shall be mine as Reuben and Simeon <transChange type="added">are</transChange>.

verses.name: Genesis 48:6
verses.text: And your children whom you father after them shall be yours. By the name of their brothers they shall be called, with respect to their inheritance.

verses.name: Genesis 48:7
verses.text: As for me, when I came to Paddan-Aram Rachel died <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to my sorrow⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to me”</note> in the land of Canaan on the way when <transChange type="added">there was</transChange> still some distance to go to Ephrath. And I buried her there on the way to Ephrath (that <transChange type="added">is</transChange>, Bethlehem).”

verses.name: Genesis 48:8
verses.text: When Israel saw the sons of Joseph he said, “Who <transChange type="added">are</transChange> these?”

verses.name: Genesis 48:9
verses.text: Then Joseph said to his father, “They <transChange type="added">are</transChange> my sons whom God has given me here.” And he said, “Please bring them to me that I may bless them.”

verses.name: Genesis 48:10
verses.text: Now the eyes of Israel were dim<note placement="foot">Or “heavy” (i.e., his eyelids were heavy; his eyes were closed)</note> on account of old age; he was not able to see. So he brought them near to him, and he kissed them and embraced them.

verses.name: Genesis 48:11
verses.text: And Israel said to Joseph, “I did not expect to see your face and behold, God has also shown me your offspring.”

verses.name: Genesis 48:12
verses.text: Then Joseph removed them from his knees and bowed down with his face to the ground.

verses.name: Genesis 48:13
verses.text: And Joseph took the two of them, Ephraim at his right <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the left of Israel, and Manasseh at his left <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the right of Israel. And he brought them near to him.

verses.name: Genesis 48:14
verses.text: And Israel stretched out his right hand and put <transChange type="added">it</transChange> on the head of Ephraim (now he was the younger), and his left hand on the head of Manasseh, crossing his hands, for Manasseh <transChange type="added">was</transChange> the firstborn.

verses.name: Genesis 48:15
verses.text: And he blessed Joseph and said, <div eID="gen234" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen235"/> <l level="1" sID="gen236"/>“The God before whom my fathers, Abraham and Isaac, walked,<l eID="gen236" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen237"/>The God who shepherded me <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞all my life⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “since my duration”</note> unto this day, <l eID="gen237" level="2"/>

verses.name: Genesis 48:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv152"/><l level="1" sID="gen238"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv152"/>The angel who redeemed me from all evil,<l eID="gen238" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen239"/>may he bless the boys.<l eID="gen239" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen240"/>And through them let my name be perpetuated,<note placement="foot">Or “called”</note><l eID="gen240" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen241"/>and the name of my fathers, Abraham and Isaac.<l eID="gen241" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen242"/>And let them multiply into many in the midst of the earth. <l eID="gen242" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen235"/>

verses.name: Genesis 48:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv153"/><div sID="gen243" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv153"/>When Joseph saw that his father put his right hand on the head of Ephraim, he was displeased. And he took hold of his father’s hand to remove it from the head of Ephraim <transChange type="added">over</transChange> to the head of Manasseh.

verses.name: Genesis 48:18
verses.text: And Joseph said to his father, “Not so, my father; because this one <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the firstborn. Put your right <transChange type="added">hand</transChange> upon his head.”

verses.name: Genesis 48:19
verses.text: But his father refused and said, “I know, my son; I know. He also shall become a people, and he also shall be great, but his younger brother shall be greater than him, and his offspring shall become a multitude of nations.”

verses.name: Genesis 48:20
verses.text: So he blessed them that day, saying, <div eID="gen243" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen244"/> <l level="1" sID="gen245"/>Through you Israel shall pronounce blessing, saying,<l eID="gen245" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen246"/>‘May God make you like Ephraim and like Manasseh.’ ”<l eID="gen246" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen244"/> <div sID="gen247" type="x-p"/> So he put Ephraim before Manasseh.

verses.name: Genesis 48:21
verses.text: And Israel said to Joseph, “Behold, I <transChange type="added">am about</transChange> to die, but God will be with you and will bring you back to the land of your ancestors.<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note>

verses.name: Genesis 48:22
verses.text: And I have given to you one slope <transChange type="added">of land</transChange> rather than your brothers, which I took from the hand of the Amorites by my sword and with my bow.”  <chapter eID="Gen.48"/>

verses.name: Genesis 49:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv154"/><title type="x-s">Jacob Blesses His Twelve Sons</title> <div sID="gen248" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv154"/>Then Jacob called his sons and said, “Gather together so that I can tell you what will happen with you in <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞days to come⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the latter days”</note>  <div eID="gen248" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 49:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv155"/><lg sID="gen249"/> <l level="1" sID="gen250"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv155"/>Assemble and hear, O sons of Jacob!<l eID="gen250" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen251"/>Listen to Israel your father! <l eID="gen251" level="2"/>

verses.name: Genesis 49:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv156"/><l level="1" sID="gen252"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv156"/>Reuben, you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> my firstborn,<l eID="gen252" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen253"/>my strength, and the firstfruit of my vigor,<l eID="gen253" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen254"/>excelling in rank and excelling in power. <l eID="gen254" level="2"/>

verses.name: Genesis 49:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv157"/><l level="1" sID="gen255"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv157"/>Unstable<note placement="foot">Or “reckless”</note> as water, you shall not excel <transChange type="added">any longer</transChange>,<l eID="gen255" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen256"/>for you went up upon the bed of your father,<l eID="gen256" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen257"/>then defiled <transChange type="added">it</transChange>. You went up upon my couch! <l eID="gen257" level="2"/>

verses.name: Genesis 49:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv158"/><l level="1" sID="gen258"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv158"/>Simeon and Levi <transChange type="added">are</transChange> brothers;<l eID="gen258" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen259"/>weapons of violence <transChange type="added">are</transChange> their swords.<l eID="gen259" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen260"/>Let me<note placement="foot">Or “my soul”</note> not come into their council. <l eID="gen260" level="2"/>

verses.name: Genesis 49:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv159"/><l level="1" sID="gen261"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv159"/>Let not my person<note placement="foot">Or “my glory”</note> be joined to their company.<l eID="gen261" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen262"/>For in their anger they killed men,<l eID="gen262" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen263"/>and at their pleasure they hamstrung cattle. <l eID="gen263" level="2"/>

verses.name: Genesis 49:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv160"/><l level="1" sID="gen264"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv160"/>Cursed be their anger, for <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> fierce,<l eID="gen264" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen265"/>and their wrath, for <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> cruel.<l eID="gen265" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen266"/>I will divide them in Jacob,<l eID="gen266" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen267"/>and I will scatter them in Israel. <l eID="gen267" level="2"/>

verses.name: Genesis 49:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv161"/><l level="1" sID="gen268"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv161"/>Judah, <transChange type="added">as for</transChange> you, your brothers shall praise you.<l eID="gen268" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen269"/>Your hand <transChange type="added">shall be</transChange> on the neck of your enemies.<l eID="gen269" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen270"/>The sons of your father shall bow down to you. <l eID="gen270" level="2"/>

verses.name: Genesis 49:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv162"/><l level="1" sID="gen271"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv162"/>Judah <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a lion’s cub.<l eID="gen271" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen272"/>From the prey, my son, you have gone up.<l eID="gen272" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen273"/>He bowed down; he crouched like a lion and as a lioness.<l eID="gen273" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen274"/>Who shall rouse him? <l eID="gen274" level="2"/>

verses.name: Genesis 49:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv163"/><l level="1" sID="gen275"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv163"/>The scepter shall not depart from Judah,<l eID="gen275" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen276"/>nor the ruler’s staff between his feet,<l eID="gen276" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen277"/>until Shiloh comes.<l eID="gen277" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen278"/>And to him shall be the obedience of nations. <l eID="gen278" level="2"/>

verses.name: Genesis 49:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv164"/><l level="1" sID="gen279"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv164"/>Binding his donkey to the vine<l eID="gen279" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen280"/>and his donkey’s colt to the choice vine,<l eID="gen280" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen281"/>he washes his clothing in the wine<l eID="gen281" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen282"/>and his garment in the blood of grapes. <l eID="gen282" level="2"/>

verses.name: Genesis 49:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv165"/><l level="1" sID="gen283"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv165"/>The eyes <transChange type="added">are</transChange> darker than wine,<l eID="gen283" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen284"/>and the teeth whiter than milk. <l eID="gen284" level="2"/>

verses.name: Genesis 49:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv166"/><l level="1" sID="gen285"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv166"/>Zebulun shall settle by the shore of the sea.<l eID="gen285" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen286"/>He <transChange type="added">shall become</transChange> a haven for ships,<l eID="gen286" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen287"/>and his border <transChange type="added">shall be</transChange> at Sidon. <l eID="gen287" level="2"/>

verses.name: Genesis 49:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv167"/><l level="1" sID="gen288"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv167"/>Issachar <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a strong donkey,<l eID="gen288" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen289"/>crouching between the sheepfolds. <l eID="gen289" level="2"/>

verses.name: Genesis 49:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv168"/><l level="1" sID="gen290"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv168"/>He saw a resting place that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> good,<l eID="gen290" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen291"/>and land that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> pleasant.<l eID="gen291" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen292"/>So he bowed his shoulder to the burden<l eID="gen292" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen293"/>and became a servant of forced labor. <l eID="gen293" level="2"/>

verses.name: Genesis 49:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv169"/><l level="1" sID="gen294"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv169"/>Dan shall judge his people<l eID="gen294" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen295"/>as one of the tribes of Israel. <l eID="gen295" level="2"/>

verses.name: Genesis 49:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv170"/><l level="1" sID="gen296"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv170"/>Dan shall be a serpent on the way,<l eID="gen296" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen297"/>a viper on the road<l eID="gen297" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen298"/>that bites the heels of a horse,<l eID="gen298" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen299"/>so that its rider falls backward. <l eID="gen299" level="2"/>

verses.name: Genesis 49:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv171"/><l level="1" sID="gen300"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv171"/>I wait for your salvation, O Yahweh. <l eID="gen300" level="1"/>

verses.name: Genesis 49:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv172"/><l level="1" sID="gen301"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv172"/>Bandits shall attack Gad,<l eID="gen301" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen302"/>but he shall attack <transChange type="added">their</transChange> heels. <l eID="gen302" level="2"/>

verses.name: Genesis 49:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv173"/><l level="1" sID="gen303"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv173"/>Asher’s food <transChange type="added">is</transChange> delicious,<l eID="gen303" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen304"/>and he shall provide from the king’s delicacies. <l eID="gen304" level="2"/>

verses.name: Genesis 49:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv174"/><l level="1" sID="gen305"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv174"/>Naphtali <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a doe running free<l eID="gen305" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen306"/>that puts forth beautiful words. <l eID="gen306" level="2"/>

verses.name: Genesis 49:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv175"/><l level="1" sID="gen307"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv175"/>Joseph <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the bough<note placement="foot">Or “son”</note> of a fruitful vine,<l eID="gen307" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen308"/>a fruitful bough<note placement="foot">Or “son”</note> by a spring.<l eID="gen308" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen309"/>His branches climb over the wall. <l eID="gen309" level="2"/>

verses.name: Genesis 49:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv176"/><l level="1" sID="gen310"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv176"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞The archers⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the masters of the bow”</note> fiercely attacked him.<l eID="gen310" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen311"/>They shot arrows <transChange type="added">at him</transChange> and were hostile to him. <l eID="gen311" level="2"/>

verses.name: Genesis 49:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv177"/><l level="1" sID="gen312"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv177"/>But his bow remained in a steady position;<l eID="gen312" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen313"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his arms⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the arms of his hands”</note> were made agile<l eID="gen313" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen314"/>by the hands of the Mighty One of Jacob.<l eID="gen314" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen315"/>From there <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the Shepherd, the Rock of Israel. <l eID="gen315" level="2"/>

verses.name: Genesis 49:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv178"/><l level="1" sID="gen316"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv178"/>Because of the God of your father he will help you<l eID="gen316" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen317"/>and <transChange type="added">by</transChange> Shaddai<note placement="foot">Or “the Almighty”</note> he will bless you<l eID="gen317" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen318"/>with the blessings of heaven above,<l eID="gen318" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen319"/>blessings of the deep that crouches beneath,<l eID="gen319" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen320"/>blessings of the breasts and the womb. <l eID="gen320" level="2"/>

verses.name: Genesis 49:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv179"/><l level="1" sID="gen321"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv179"/>The blessings of your father<l eID="gen321" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen322"/>are superior to the blessings of my ancestors,<l eID="gen322" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen323"/>to the bounty of the everlasting hills.<l eID="gen323" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen324"/>May they be on the head of Joseph,<l eID="gen324" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen325"/>and on the forehead of the prince of his brothers. <l eID="gen325" level="2"/>

verses.name: Genesis 49:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv180"/><l level="1" sID="gen326"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv180"/>Benjamin <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a devouring wolf,<l eID="gen326" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen327"/>devouring the prey in the morning,<l eID="gen327" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen328"/>and dividing the plunder in the evening. <l eID="gen328" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen249"/>

verses.name: Genesis 49:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv181"/><title type="x-s">The Death and Burial of Jacob</title> <div sID="gen329" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv181"/>All these <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the twelve tribes of Israel, and this <transChange type="added">is</transChange> what their father said to them when he blessed them, each according to their blessing.

verses.name: Genesis 49:29
verses.text: Then he instructed them and said to them, “I am <transChange type="added">about to be</transChange> gathered to my people. Bury me among my ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> in the cave that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in the field of Ephron the Hittite,

verses.name: Genesis 49:30
verses.text: in the cave that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in the field of Machpelah that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> before<note placement="foot">Or “east of”</note> Mamre in the land of Canaan, which Abraham bought with the field from Ephron the Hittite as a burial site.

verses.name: Genesis 49:31
verses.text: There they buried Abraham and Sarah his wife. There they buried Isaac and Rebekah his wife. And there I buried Leah—

verses.name: Genesis 49:32
verses.text: the purchase of the field and the cave which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in it from the Hittites.”

verses.name: Genesis 49:33
verses.text: When Jacob finished instructing his sons he drew his feet up to the bed. Then he took his last breath and was gathered to his people.  <chapter eID="Gen.49"/>

verses.name: Genesis 50:1
