verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv182"/><title type="x-s">Jacob’s Funeral and Joseph’s Remaining Time in Egypt</title> <div sID="gen330" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv182"/>Then Joseph fell on the face of his father and wept upon him and kissed him.

verses.name: Genesis 50:2
verses.text: And Joseph instructed his servants the physicians to embalm his father. So the physicians embalmed Israel.

verses.name: Genesis 50:3
verses.text: Forty days <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞were required for it⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “were fulfilled for it”</note> for thus are the days <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞required for⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “fulfilled”</note> embalming. And the Egyptians wept for him seventy days.

verses.name: Genesis 50:4
verses.text: When the days of his weeping had passed, Joseph spoke to the household of Pharaoh, saying, “If I have found favor in your eyes, please speak in the hearing of Pharaoh, saying,

verses.name: Genesis 50:5
verses.text: ‘My father made me swear, saying, “Behold, I <transChange type="added">am about</transChange> to die. In the tomb that I have hewed out for myself in the land of Canaan—there you must bury me.” So then, please let me go up and let me bury my father; then I will return.’ ”

verses.name: Genesis 50:6
verses.text: Then Pharaoh said, “Go up and bury your father as he made you swear.”

verses.name: Genesis 50:7
verses.text: So Joseph went up to bury his father. And all the servants of Pharaoh, the elders of his household, and all the elders of the land of Egypt, went up with him,

verses.name: Genesis 50:8
verses.text: with all the household of Joseph, his brothers, and the household of his father. They left only their little children and their flocks and their herds in the land of Goshen.

verses.name: Genesis 50:9
verses.text: And there also went up with him chariots and horsemen. The company <transChange type="added">was</transChange> very great.

verses.name: Genesis 50:10
verses.text: When they came to the threshing floor of Atad, which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> beyond the Jordan, they lamented there with a very great and sorrowful wailing. And he made a mourning ceremony for his father seven days.

verses.name: Genesis 50:11
verses.text: And when the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the land, saw the mourning ceremony at the threshing floor of Atad they said, “This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a severe mourning for the Egyptians.” Therefore its name was called Abel-Mizraim, which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> beyond the Jordan.

verses.name: Genesis 50:12
verses.text: Thus his sons did to him just as he had instructed them.

verses.name: Genesis 50:13
verses.text: And his sons carried him to the land of Canaan and buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah, which field Abraham had bought as a burial site from Ephron the Hittite before<note placement="foot">Or “east of”</note> Mamre.

verses.name: Genesis 50:14
verses.text: And after burying his father, Joseph returned to Egypt, he and his brothers and all who had gone up with him to bury his father.  <div eID="gen330" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 50:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv183"/><div sID="gen331" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv183"/>And when the brothers of Joseph saw that their father <transChange type="added">was</transChange> dead, they said, “It may be <transChange type="added">that</transChange> Joseph will hold a grudge against us and pay us back dearly for all the evil that we did to him.”

verses.name: Genesis 50:16
verses.text: So they sent <transChange type="added">word</transChange> to Joseph saying, “Your father commanded <transChange type="added">us</transChange> before his death, saying,

verses.name: Genesis 50:17
verses.text: “Thus you must say to Joseph, ‘O, please now forgive the transgression of your brothers and their sin, for they did evil to you.’ So now, please forgive the transgression of the servants of the God of your father.” And Joseph wept when they spoke to him.

verses.name: Genesis 50:18
verses.text: Then his brothers went also and fell before him and said, “Behold, we <transChange type="added">are</transChange> your servants.”

verses.name: Genesis 50:19
verses.text: Then Joseph said to them, “Do not be afraid, for <transChange type="added">am</transChange> I in the place of God?

verses.name: Genesis 50:20
verses.text: As for you, you planned evil against me, <transChange type="added">but</transChange> God planned it for good, in order to do this—to keep many people alive—as <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> today.

verses.name: Genesis 50:21
verses.text: So then, do not be afraid. I myself will provide for you and your little ones. And he consoled them and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞spoke kindly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “spoke to their heart”</note> to them.  <div eID="gen331" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Genesis 50:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv184"/><title type="x-s">The Death of Joseph</title> <div sID="gen332" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv184"/>So Joseph remained in Egypt, he and the house of his father. And Joseph lived one hundred and ten years.

verses.name: Genesis 50:23
verses.text: And Joseph saw Ephraim’s children to the third generation. Moreover, the children of Makir, son of Manasseh, were born on the knees of Joseph.

verses.name: Genesis 50:24
verses.text: And Joseph said to his brothers, “I <transChange type="added">am about</transChange> to die, but God will certainly visit you and bring you up from this land to the land that he swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.”

verses.name: Genesis 50:25
verses.text: Then Joseph made the sons of Israel swear an oath, saying, “God will surely visit you, and you shall bring up my bones from here.”

verses.name: Genesis 50:26
verses.text: So Joseph died, <transChange type="added">being</transChange> one hundred and ten years old. They embalmed him and he was placed in a coffin in Egypt.  <chapter eID="Gen.50"/> <div eID="gen332" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen2" osisID="Gen" type="book"/>

verses.name: Exodus 1:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv185"/><title type="x-s">Israel and Oppression in Egypt</title> <div sID="gen334" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv185"/>And these <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the names of the sons of Israel who came <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Egypt; with Jacob, they each came with his <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞family⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>:<note placement="foot">Literally “house”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 1:2
verses.text: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah;

verses.name: Exodus 1:3
verses.text: Issachar, Zebulun, and Benjamin;

verses.name: Exodus 1:4
verses.text: Dan and Naphtali, Gad and Asher.

verses.name: Exodus 1:5
verses.text: And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞all those who descended from Jacob⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “every soul/individual/life, the ones going out from the loins of Jacob”</note> were seventy individuals,<note placement="foot">Or “souls,” “lives”</note> and Joseph was in Egypt.

verses.name: Exodus 1:6
verses.text: And Joseph died and all of his brothers and all of that generation.

verses.name: Exodus 1:7
verses.text: And the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> were fruitful and multiplied and were many and were very, very numerous, and the land was filled with them.  <div eID="gen334" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 1:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv186"/><div sID="gen335" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv186"/>And a new king rose over Egypt who did not know Joseph.

verses.name: Exodus 1:9
verses.text: And he said to his people, “Look, the people of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> <transChange type="added">are</transChange> greater and more numerous than us.

verses.name: Exodus 1:10
verses.text: Come, we must deal shrewdly with them, lest they become many, and when war happens, they also will join our enemies and will fight against us and go up from the land.”

verses.name: Exodus 1:11
verses.text: And they appointed commanders of forced labor over them in order to oppress them with their <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forced labor⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “burdens” or “burdensome labor”</note> and they built storage cities for Pharaoh—Pithom and Rameses.

verses.name: Exodus 1:12
verses.text: And as he oppressed them, so they became many, and so they spread out, and <transChange type="added">the Egyptians</transChange> were afraid because of the presence of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 1:13
verses.text: And the Egyptians ruthlessly compelled the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> to work.

verses.name: Exodus 1:14
verses.text: And they made their lives bitter with hard work with mortar and with bricks and with all <transChange type="added">sorts</transChange> of work in the field—with all their work in which they ruthlessly enslaved them.  <div eID="gen335" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 1:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv187"/><div sID="gen336" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv187"/>And the king of Egypt said to the Hebrew midwives—of whom the name of the one <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Shiphrah and the name of the second <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Puah—

verses.name: Exodus 1:16
verses.text: and he said, “When you help the Hebrews give birth, you will look upon the pairs of testicles; if he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a son, you will put him to death, and if she <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a daughter, she will live.”

verses.name: Exodus 1:17
verses.text: But the midwives feared God, and they did not do as the king of Egypt had said to them. They let the boys live.

verses.name: Exodus 1:18
verses.text: And the king of Egypt summoned the midwives, and he said to them, “Why have you done this thing and let the boys live?”

verses.name: Exodus 1:19
verses.text: And the midwives said to Pharaoh, “Because the Hebrew <transChange type="added">women are</transChange> not like the Egyptian women, because they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> vigorous; before the midwife comes to them, they have given birth.”

verses.name: Exodus 1:20
verses.text: And God did the midwives good, and the <transChange type="added">Israelite</transChange> people became many and were very numerous.

verses.name: Exodus 1:21
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And so⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and he/it was”</note> because the midwives feared God, he gave them <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞families⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “houses”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 1:22
verses.text: And Pharaoh commanded all his people, saying, “Every son who is born you will throw into the Nile, and every daughter you will let live.”  <chapter eID="Exod.1"/>

verses.name: Exodus 2:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv188"/><title type="x-s">The Birth and Early Life of Moses</title> <div sID="gen337" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv188"/>And a man from the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞family⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “house”</note> of Levi went, and he took <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a descendent of Levi⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “daughter of Levi”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 2:2
verses.text: And the woman conceived, and she gave birth to a son, and she saw him, that he was a fine baby, and she hid him three months.

verses.name: Exodus 2:3
verses.text: But when she could no longer hide him, she got a papyrus basket for him, and she coated it with tar and with pitch, and she placed the boy in it, and she placed <transChange type="added">it</transChange> among the reeds on the bank of the Nile.

verses.name: Exodus 2:4
verses.text: And his sister stood at a distance to know what would be done to him.

verses.name: Exodus 2:5
verses.text: And the daughter of Pharaoh went down to wash at the Nile, <transChange type="added">while</transChange> her maidservants were walking alongside the Nile, and she saw the basket in the midst of the reeds, and she sent her slave woman <transChange type="added">for it</transChange> and took it

verses.name: Exodus 2:6
verses.text: and opened <transChange type="added">it</transChange> and saw him—the boy—and it was a lad weeping, and she had compassion for him and said, “This <transChange type="added">must be</transChange> from the boys of the Hebrews.”<note placement="foot">Each instance of the implied “she” in verses 5 and 6 is the daughter of Pharaoh</note>

verses.name: Exodus 2:7
verses.text: And his sister said to the daughter of Pharaoh, “Shall I go and call for you a woman from the Hebrews <transChange type="added">who is</transChange> nursing <transChange type="added">so that</transChange> she will nurse the boy for you?”

verses.name: Exodus 2:8
verses.text: And the daughter of Pharaoh said to her, “Go.” And the girl went, and she called the mother of the boy.

verses.name: Exodus 2:9
verses.text: And the daughter of Pharaoh said, “Take this boy and nurse him for me, and I myself will give you wages, and the woman took the boy, and she nursed him.

verses.name: Exodus 2:10
verses.text: And the boy grew, and she brought him to the daughter of Pharaoh, and he became her son, and she called his name Moses, and she said, “Because I drew him out from the water.”  <div eID="gen337" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 2:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv189"/><div sID="gen338" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv189"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and he/it was”</note> in those days when Moses had grown up, he went out to his brothers, and he saw their <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forced labor⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “burdens” or “burdensome labor”</note> and he saw an Egyptian man striking a Hebrew man, one of his brothers.<note placement="foot">Or “a Hebrew man from his brothers”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 2:12
verses.text: And he turned here and there, and he saw no one,<note placement="foot">Literally “and he saw that there was not a man”</note> and he struck the Egyptian, and he hid him in the sand.

verses.name: Exodus 2:13
verses.text: And he went out on the second day, and there were two Hebrew men fighting, and he said to the guilty <transChange type="added">one</transChange>, “Why do you strike your neighbor?”

verses.name: Exodus 2:14
verses.text: And he said, “Who <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞appointed you as a commander⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “put you for a man, a commander” or “placed you for a man, a commander”</note> and a judge over us? <transChange type="added">Are</transChange> you intending to kill me like you killed the Egyptian?” And Moses was afraid, and he said, “Surely the matter has become known.”

verses.name: Exodus 2:15
verses.text: And Pharaoh heard this matter, and he sought to kill Moses, and Moses fled from Pharaoh, and he lived in the land of Midian, and he lived at <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a certain well⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the well”</note>  <div eID="gen338" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 2:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv190"/><div sID="gen339" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv190"/><transChange type="added">Now</transChange> the priest of Midian had seven daughters, and they came and drew water and filled the troughs to water their father’s flock.<note placement="foot">The Hebrew noun translated “flock” is used here and in verses 17 and 19 collectively for sheep or goats or a mix of the two</note>

verses.name: Exodus 2:17
verses.text: And the shepherds came and drove them away, but Moses stood up and came to their rescue and watered their flock.

verses.name: Exodus 2:18
verses.text: And they came to Reuel, their father, and he said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Why have you come so quickly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “why did you hasten coming”</note> today?”

verses.name: Exodus 2:19
verses.text: And they said, “An Egyptian man delivered us from the hand of the shepherds, and he even drew <transChange type="added">water</transChange> for us and watered the flock.”

verses.name: Exodus 2:20
verses.text: And he said to his daughters, “Where <transChange type="added">is</transChange> he? <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Why then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “why this”</note> have you left the man? <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Call him so that he can eat some food⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “call to or “summon/invite” him and he will eat bread”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 2:21
verses.text: And Moses agreed to stay with the man, and he gave Zipporah his daughter to Moses.

verses.name: Exodus 2:22
verses.text: And she bore a son, and he called his name Gershom because he said, “I am an alien in a foreign land.”<note placement="foot">The word translated “alien” sounds like the first syllable in the name Gershom. The second syllable sounds like the word for “there”</note>  <div eID="gen339" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 2:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv191"/><div sID="gen340" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv191"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and he/it was”</note> during those many days, the king of Egypt died, and the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> groaned because of the work, and they cried out, and their cry for help because of the work went up to God.

verses.name: Exodus 2:24
verses.text: And God heard their groaning, and God remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob,

verses.name: Exodus 2:25
verses.text: and God saw the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> and God took notice.<note placement="foot">Or “and God knew”</note>  <chapter eID="Exod.2"/>

verses.name: Exodus 3:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv192"/><title type="x-s">Yahweh’s Plan to Rescue the Israelites</title> <div sID="gen341" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv192"/>And Moses was a shepherd with the flock<note placement="foot">The Hebrew noun translated “flock” in this verse is used collectively for sheep or goats or a mix of the two.</note> of Jethro, his father-in-law, the priest of Midian, and he led the flock to the west <transChange type="added">of</transChange> the desert, and he came to the mountain of God, to Horeb.

verses.name: Exodus 3:2
verses.text: And the angel of Yahweh appeared to him in a flame of fire from the midst of a bush, and he looked, and there was the bush burning with fire, but the bush was not being consumed.

verses.name: Exodus 3:3
verses.text: And Moses said, “Let me turn aside and see this great sight. Why does the bush not burn up?”

verses.name: Exodus 3:4
verses.text: And Yahweh saw that he turned aside to see, and God called to him from the midst of the bush, and he said, “Moses, Moses.” And he said, “Here I <transChange type="added">am</transChange>.”

verses.name: Exodus 3:5
verses.text: And he said, “You must not come near to here. Take off your sandals from on your feet, because the place on which you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> standing, it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> holy ground.”

verses.name: Exodus 3:6
verses.text: And he said, “I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.” And Moses hid his face because he was afraid of looking at God.  <div eID="gen341" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 3:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv193"/><div sID="gen342" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv193"/>And Yahweh said, “Surely I have seen the misery of my people who <transChange type="added">are</transChange> in Egypt, and I have heard their cry of distress because of their oppressors, for I know their sufferings.

verses.name: Exodus 3:8
verses.text: And I have come down to deliver them from the hand of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Egyptians and to bring them up from this land to a good and wide land, to a land flowing with milk and honey, to the place of the Canaanites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Canaanite”</note> and the Hittites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Hittite”</note> and the Amorites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Amorite”</note> and the Perizzites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Perizzite”</note> and the Hivites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Hivite”</note> and the Jebusites.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Jebusite”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 3:9
verses.text: And now, look, the cry of distress of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> has come to me, and also I see the oppression <transChange type="added">with</transChange> which <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Egyptians <transChange type="added">are</transChange> oppressing them.

verses.name: Exodus 3:10
verses.text: And now come, and I will send you to Pharaoh, and <transChange type="added">you must</transChange> bring my people, the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> out from Egypt.”  <div eID="gen342" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 3:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv194"/><div sID="gen343" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv194"/>But Moses said to God, “Who <transChange type="added">am</transChange> I that I should go to Pharaoh and that I should bring the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> out from Egypt?”

verses.name: Exodus 3:12
verses.text: And he said, “Because I am with you, and this <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> the sign for you that I myself have sent you: When you bring the people out from Egypt, you will serve God on this mountain.”

verses.name: Exodus 3:13
verses.text: But Moses said to God, “Look, <transChange type="added">if</transChange> I go to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> and I say to them, ‘The God of your ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> has sent me to you,’ and they say to me, ‘What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> his name?’ <transChange type="added">then</transChange> what shall I say to them?”

verses.name: Exodus 3:14
verses.text: And God said to Moses, “I am that I am.” And he said, “So you must say to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> ‘I am sent me to you.’ ”  <div eID="gen343" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 3:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv195"/><div sID="gen344" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv195"/>And God said again to Moses, “So you must say to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> ‘Yahweh, the God of your ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has sent me to you. This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my name forever, and this <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my remembrance from generation <transChange type="added">to</transChange> generation.’

verses.name: Exodus 3:16
verses.text: Go and gather the elders of Israel and say to them, ‘Yahweh, the God of your ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> appeared to me, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying, “I have carefully attended to you and what has been done to you in Egypt.”

verses.name: Exodus 3:17
verses.text: And I said, “I will bring you up from the misery of Egypt to the land of the Canaanites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Canaanite”</note> and the Hittites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Hittite”</note> and the Amorites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Amorite”</note> and the Perizzites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Perizzite”</note> and the Hivites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Hivite”</note> and the Jebusites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Jebusite”</note> to a land flowing with milk and honey.” ’

verses.name: Exodus 3:18
verses.text: And they will listen to your voice, and you will go, you and the elders of Israel, to the king of Egypt, and you will say to him, ‘Yahweh, the God of the Hebrews has met with us, and now let us please go <transChange type="added">on</transChange> a journey of three days into the desert, and let us sacrifice to Yahweh our God.’  <div eID="gen344" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 3:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv196"/><div sID="gen345" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv196"/>But I myself know that the king of Egypt will not allow you to go <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞unless compelled by a strong hand⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “and not with a strong hand”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 3:20
verses.text: And I will stretch out my hand, and I will strike Egypt with all of my wonders that I will do in its midst, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞afterward⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “after so” or “after I do so”</note> he will release you.

verses.name: Exodus 3:21
verses.text: And I will give this people favor in the eyes of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Egyptians, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞and then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and he/it will be”</note> when you go, you will not go empty-handed.

verses.name: Exodus 3:22
verses.text: And a woman will ask from her neighbor and from the woman dwelling as an alien in her house <transChange type="added">for</transChange> objects of silver and objects of gold and garments, and you will put <transChange type="added">them</transChange> on your sons and on your daughters; and you will plunder Egypt.”  <chapter eID="Exod.3"/>

verses.name: Exodus 4:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv197"/><title type="x-s">Yahweh Provides Signs and Help for Speaking</title> <div sID="gen346" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv197"/>And Moses answered, and he said, “And if they do not believe me and they do not listen to my voice, but they say, ‘Yahweh did not appear to you?’ ”

verses.name: Exodus 4:2
verses.text: And Yahweh said to him, “What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> this in your hand?” And he said, “A staff.”

verses.name: Exodus 4:3
verses.text: And he said, “Throw it onto the ground.” And he threw it onto the ground, and it became a snake, and Moses fled from it.

verses.name: Exodus 4:4
verses.text: And Yahweh said to Moses, “Reach out your hand and grasp <transChange type="added">it</transChange> by its tail”—” (And he reached out his hand and grabbed it, and it became a staff in his palm.)—

verses.name: Exodus 4:5
verses.text: “so that they may believe that Yahweh, the God of their ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> appeared to you, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.”  <div eID="gen346" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 4:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv198"/><div sID="gen347" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv198"/>And Yahweh said to him again, “Put your hand into the fold of your garment.” And he put his hand into the fold of his garment, and he took it out, and, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to his surprise⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “look” or “behold”</note> his hand <transChange type="added">was</transChange> afflicted with a skin disease, like snow.

verses.name: Exodus 4:7
verses.text: And he said, “Return your hand to the fold of your garment.” And he returned his hand to the fold of his garment, and he took it out from the fold of his garment, and, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to his surprise⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “look” or “behold”</note> it was restored like the rest of his body.

verses.name: Exodus 4:8
verses.text: “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and he/it will be”</note> if they do not believe you and they will not listen to the voice of the former sign, <transChange type="added">then</transChange> they will believe the voice of the latter sign.

verses.name: Exodus 4:9
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and he/it will be”</note> if they also do not believe the second of these signs and they will not listen to your voice, <transChange type="added">then</transChange> you must take water from the Nile and pour <transChange type="added">it</transChange> onto the dry ground, and the water that you take from the Nile will become blood on the dry ground.”  <div eID="gen347" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 4:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv199"/><div sID="gen348" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv199"/>And Moses said to Yahweh, “Please, Lord, I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> not a man of words, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞neither recently nor in the past nor since your speaking⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “also from yesterday also from the day before also from then your speaking”</note> to your servant, because I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> heavy of mouth and of tongue.”

verses.name: Exodus 4:11
verses.text: And Yahweh said to him, “Who gave a mouth to humankind, or who makes mute or deaf or sighted or blind? <transChange type="added">Is it</transChange> not I, Yahweh?

verses.name: Exodus 4:12
verses.text: So then go, and I myself will be with your mouth, and I will teach you what you must speak.”

verses.name: Exodus 4:13
verses.text: And he said, “Please, Lord, do send <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞anyone else whom you wish to send⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “by the hand of someone you will send”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 4:14
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And Yahweh was angry with⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and the nose of Yahweh was hot against”</note> Moses and said, “<transChange type="added">Is there</transChange> not Aaron your brother the Levite? I know that he certainly can speak, and also there he is coming out to meet you, and when he sees you, he will rejoice in his heart.

verses.name: Exodus 4:15
verses.text: And you will speak to him, and you will put words in his mouth, and I myself will be with your mouth and with his mouth, and I will teach you what you must do.

verses.name: Exodus 4:16
verses.text: And he will speak for you to the people, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞and then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and he/it will be”</note> he will be to you as a mouth, and you will be to him as a god.

verses.name: Exodus 4:17
verses.text: And you must take this staff in your hand, with which you will do the signs.”  <div eID="gen348" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 4:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv200"/><title type="x-s">Moses Leaves Midian and Returns to Egypt</title> <div sID="gen349" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv200"/>And Moses went, and he returned to Jethro his father-in-law, and he said to him, “Please let me go, and let me return to my brothers who <transChange type="added">are</transChange> in Egypt, and let me see whether they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> yet alive. And Jethro said to Moses, “Go in peace.”

verses.name: Exodus 4:19
verses.text: And Yahweh said to Moses in Midian, “Go, return to Egypt because all the men have died who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> seeking your life.”  <div eID="gen349" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 4:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv201"/><div sID="gen350" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv201"/>And Moses took his wife and his sons and had them ride on the donkey, and he returned to the land of Egypt, and Moses took the staff of God in his hand.

verses.name: Exodus 4:21
verses.text: And Yahweh said to Moses, “When you go to return to Egypt, see all of the wonders that I have put in your hand, and do them before Pharaoh, and I myself will harden his heart, and he will not release the people.

verses.name: Exodus 4:22
verses.text: And you must say to Pharaoh, ‘Thus says Yahweh, “Israel <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my son, my firstborn.”

verses.name: Exodus 4:23
verses.text: And I said to you, “Release my son and let him serve me,” but you refused to release him. Look, I <transChange type="added">am about</transChange> to kill your son, your firstborn.’ ”  <div eID="gen350" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 4:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv202"/><div sID="gen351" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv202"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and he/it was”</note> on the way, at the place of overnight lodging, Yahweh encountered him and sought to kill him.

verses.name: Exodus 4:25
verses.text: But Zipporah took a flint <transChange type="added">knife</transChange>, and she cut off the foreskin of her son, and she touched his feet, and she said, “Yes, you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> a bridegroom of blood to me.”

verses.name: Exodus 4:26
verses.text: And he left him alone. At that time she said, “A bridegroom of blood,” because of the circumcision.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “circumcisions”</note>  <div eID="gen351" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 4:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv203"/><div sID="gen352" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv203"/>And Yahweh said to Aaron, “Go to the desert to meet Moses.” And he went and encountered him at the mountain of God and kissed him.

verses.name: Exodus 4:28
verses.text: And Moses told Aaron all the words of Yahweh, who had sent him—and all the signs that he had commanded him.  <div eID="gen352" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 4:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv204"/><div sID="gen353" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv204"/>And Moses and Aaron went, and they gathered all of the elders of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 4:30
verses.text: And Aaron spoke all the words that Yahweh had spoken to Moses, and he did the signs before the eyes of the people.

verses.name: Exodus 4:31
verses.text: And the people believed when they heard that Yahweh had attended to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> and that he had seen their misery, and they knelt down and they worshiped.  <chapter eID="Exod.4"/>

verses.name: Exodus 5:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv205"/><title type="x-s">Pharaoh Rejects Yahweh’s Authority and Makes Israel’s Troubles Worse</title> <div sID="gen354" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv205"/>And afterward, Moses and Aaron went, and they said to Pharaoh, “Thus says Yahweh the God of Israel, ‘Release my people so that they may hold a festival for me in the desert.’ ”

verses.name: Exodus 5:2
verses.text: And Pharaoh said, “Who is Yahweh that I should listen to his voice to release Israel? I do not know Yahweh, and also I will not release Israel.”  <div eID="gen354" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 5:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv206"/><div sID="gen355" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv206"/>And they said, “The God of the Hebrews has met with us. Please let us go <transChange type="added">on</transChange> a three-day journey into the desert, and let us sacrifice to Yahweh our God, lest he strike us with plague or with sword.”

verses.name: Exodus 5:4
verses.text: And the king of Egypt said, “Why, Moses and Aaron, do you take<note placement="foot">Or “let loose,” “let run wild” (compare 32:25)</note> the people from their work? Go to your <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forced labor⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!”<note placement="foot">Literally “burdens” or “burdensome labor”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 5:5
verses.text: And Pharaoh said, “Look, the people of the land <transChange type="added">are</transChange> now many, and you want to stop them from their <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forced labor⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “burdens” or “burdensome labor”</note>  <div eID="gen355" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 5:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv207"/><div sID="gen356" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv207"/>And on that day Pharaoh commanded the slave drivers over the people and his foremen, saying,

verses.name: Exodus 5:7
verses.text: “You must no longer give straw to the people to make the bricks like <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “yesterday three days ago”</note> Let them go and gather straw for themselves.

verses.name: Exodus 5:8
verses.text: But the quota of the bricks that they <transChange type="added">were</transChange> making <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “yesterday three days ago”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you must require of them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “you will put on them”</note> You must not reduce from it, because they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> lazy. Therefore they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> crying out, saying, ‘Let us go and sacrifice to our God.’

verses.name: Exodus 5:9
verses.text: Let the work be heavier on the men so that they will do it and not pay attention to words of deception.”  <div eID="gen356" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 5:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv208"/><div sID="gen357" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv208"/>And the slave drivers of the people and their foremen went out, and they spoke to the people, saying, “Thus says Pharaoh, ‘I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> not giving you straw.

verses.name: Exodus 5:11
verses.text: You go, get straw for yourselves from whatever you find because not a thing is being reduced from your work.’ ”

verses.name: Exodus 5:12
verses.text: And the people spread out in all the land of Egypt to gather stubble for the straw.

verses.name: Exodus 5:13
verses.text: And the slave drivers <transChange type="added">were</transChange> insisting, saying, “Finish your work <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞for each day⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a thing of a day”</note> on its day, as <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞when there was straw⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “in the being of the straw”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 5:14
verses.text: And the foremen of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> whom Pharaoh’s slave drivers had appointed over them, were beaten by men who were saying, “Why have you not completed your portion of brickmaking <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as before, both yesterday and today⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?”<note placement="foot">Literally “as yesterday three days ago also yesterday also the day”</note>  <div eID="gen357" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 5:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv209"/><title type="x-s">The Foremen Complain to Pharaoh and Moses, and Moses Complains to Yahweh</title> <div sID="gen358" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv209"/>And the foremen of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> came and cried out to Pharaoh, saying, “Why do you treat your servants like this?

verses.name: Exodus 5:16
verses.text: Straw <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not being given to your servants, but <transChange type="added">they are</transChange> saying to us, ‘Make bricks!’ and, look, your servants <transChange type="added">are</transChange> being beaten, but it is the fault of<note placement="foot">The expression is difficult. The word translated “fault” or “sin” has pointing for a second-person feminine singular subject (“you sinned”), which does not go well with either “Pharaoh” or “your people” as a subject; but the noun translated “sin of” has the same consonants, leading to the possibility that the word should be understood as a noun</note> your people.”

verses.name: Exodus 5:17
verses.text: And he said, “You <transChange type="added">are</transChange> lazy, lazy! Therefore you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> saying, ‘Let us go; let us sacrifice to Yahweh.’

verses.name: Exodus 5:18
verses.text: And now go, work, but straw will not be given to you, and you must give the full quota of bricks.”  <div eID="gen358" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 5:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv210"/><div sID="gen359" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv210"/>And the foremen of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> saw they were in trouble <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞with the saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “saying”</note> “You will not reduce from your bricks <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞for each day⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a thing of a day”</note> on its day.”

verses.name: Exodus 5:20
verses.text: And they met Moses and Aaron, <transChange type="added">who were</transChange> waiting to meet them when they <transChange type="added">were</transChange> going out from Pharaoh.

verses.name: Exodus 5:21
verses.text: And they said to them, “May Yahweh look upon you and judge because you have caused our fragrance to stink in the eyes of Pharaoh and in the eyes of his servants <transChange type="added">so as</transChange> to put a sword into their hand to kill us.”

verses.name: Exodus 5:22
verses.text: And Moses returned to Yahweh and said, “Lord, why have you brought trouble to this people? Why ever did you send me?

verses.name: Exodus 5:23
verses.text: And from the time I came to Pharaoh to speak in your name, he has brought trouble to this people, and you have certainly not delivered your people.”  <chapter eID="Exod.5"/>

verses.name: Exodus 6:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv211"/><title type="x-s">Yahweh Discusses His Name and Israel’s Future</title> <div sID="gen360" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv211"/>And Yahweh said to Moses, “Now you will see what I will do to Pharaoh, because with a strong hand he will release them, and with a strong hand he will drive them out from his land.”  <div eID="gen360" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 6:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv212"/><div sID="gen361" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv212"/>And God spoke to Moses, and he said to him, “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> Yahweh.

verses.name: Exodus 6:3
verses.text: And I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob as God Shaddai,<note placement="foot">Often translated as “Almighty”</note> but by my name Yahweh I was not known to them.

verses.name: Exodus 6:4
verses.text: And I not only established my covenant with them to give to them the land of Canaan, the land of their sojournings, in which they dwelt as aliens,

verses.name: Exodus 6:5
verses.text: but also I myself heard the groaning of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> whom <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Egyptians <transChange type="added">are</transChange> making to work, and I remembered my covenant.

verses.name: Exodus 6:6
verses.text: Therefore say to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> ‘I am Yahweh, and I will bring you out from under the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forced labor⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “burdens” or “burdensome labor”</note> of Egypt, and I will deliver you from their slavery, and I will redeem you with an outstretched arm and with great punishments.

verses.name: Exodus 6:7
verses.text: And I will take you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as my people⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to/for me for a people”</note> and I will be <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞your God⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to/for you for a God”</note> and you will know that I am Yahweh your God, who brought you out from under the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forced labor⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “burdens” or “burdensome labor”</note> of Egypt.

verses.name: Exodus 6:8
verses.text: And I will bring you to the land <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞that I swore⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “that I raised my hand”</note> to give to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, and I will give it to you <transChange type="added">as</transChange> a possession. I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> Yahweh.”  <div eID="gen361" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 6:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv213"/><div sID="gen362" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv213"/>And Moses spoke thus to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> but they did not listen to Moses, because of <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞discouragement⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a lack of spirit” or “shortness of spirit”</note> and because of hard work.  <div eID="gen362" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 6:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv214"/><div sID="gen363" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv214"/>And Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.name: Exodus 6:11
verses.text: “Go, speak to Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, and let him release the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> from his land.”

verses.name: Exodus 6:12
verses.text: And Moses spoke before Yahweh, saying, “Look, the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> do not listen to me, and how will Pharaoh listen to me, since I am <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a poor speaker⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?”<note placement="foot">Literally “uncircumcised of lips”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 6:13
verses.text: And Yahweh spoke to Moses and to Aaron, and he commanded them <transChange type="added">to go</transChange> to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> and to Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, to bring the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> out from the land of Egypt.  <div eID="gen363" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 6:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv215"/><title type="x-s">The Genealogy of Moses and Aaron</title> <div sID="gen364" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv215"/>These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the heads of <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞their families⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the house of their fathers”</note> <div eID="gen364" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen365" type="x-p"/> The sons of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel, <transChange type="added">are</transChange> Enoch and Pallu, Hezron and Carmi. These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the clans of Reuben.  <div eID="gen365" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 6:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv216"/><div sID="gen366" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv216"/>And the sons of Simeon <transChange type="added">are</transChange> Jemuel and Jamin and Ohad and Jakin and Zohar and Shaul the son of the Canaanitess.<note placement="foot">Or “the Canaanite woman.” The Hebrew word is feminine</note> These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the clans of Simeon.  <div eID="gen366" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 6:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv217"/><div sID="gen367" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv217"/>And these <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the names of the sons of Levi according to their genealogies:<note placement="foot">Or “generations”</note> Gershon and Kohath and Merari, and the years of the life of Levi were <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞one hundred and thirty-seven years⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “seven and thirty and hundred of year”</note>  <div eID="gen367" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 6:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv218"/><div sID="gen368" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv218"/>The sons of Gershon <transChange type="added">are</transChange> Libni and Shimei according to their clans.  <div eID="gen368" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 6:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv219"/><div sID="gen369" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv219"/>And the sons of Kohath <transChange type="added">are</transChange> Amram and Izhar and Hebron and Uzziel, and the years of the life of Kohath <transChange type="added">were</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞one hundred and thirty-three years⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “three and thirty and hundred of year”</note>  <div eID="gen369" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 6:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv220"/><div sID="gen370" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv220"/>And the sons of Merari <transChange type="added">are</transChange> Mahli and Mushi. These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> clans of the Levites according to their genealogies.<note placement="foot">Or “generations”</note>  <div eID="gen370" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 6:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv221"/><div sID="gen371" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv221"/>And Amram took Jochebed his aunt for himself as a wife, and she bore for him Aaron and Moses, and the years of the life of Amram <transChange type="added">were</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞one hundred and thirty-seven years⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “seven and thirty and hundred of year”</note>  <div eID="gen371" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 6:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv222"/><div sID="gen372" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv222"/>And the sons of Izhar <transChange type="added">are</transChange> Korah and Nepheg and Zikri.  <div eID="gen372" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 6:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv223"/><div sID="gen373" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv223"/>And the sons of Uzziel <transChange type="added">are</transChange> Mishael and Elzaphan and Sithri.  <div eID="gen373" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 6:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv224"/><div sID="gen374" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv224"/>And Aaron took Elisheba the daughter of Amminadab, the sister of Nahshon, for himself as a wife, and she bore for him Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.  <div eID="gen374" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 6:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv225"/><div sID="gen375" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv225"/>And the sons of Korah <transChange type="added">are</transChange> Assir and Elkanah and Abiasaph. These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the clans of the Korahites.  <div eID="gen375" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 6:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv226"/><div sID="gen376" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv226"/>And Eleazar the son of Aaron took for himself <transChange type="added">one</transChange> from the daughters of Putiel as a wife, and she bore for him Phinehas. These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the heads of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞families⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “fathers”</note> of the Levites according to their clans.  <div eID="gen376" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 6:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv227"/><div sID="gen377" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv227"/><transChange type="added">It was</transChange> that Aaron and Moses to whom Yahweh said, “Bring the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> out from the land of Egypt according to their divisions.”

verses.name: Exodus 6:27
verses.text: They <transChange type="added">were</transChange> those who spoke to Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, in order to bring the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> out from Egypt. <transChange type="added">It was</transChange> that Moses and Aaron.  <div eID="gen377" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 6:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv228"/><div sID="gen378" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv228"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And so it was on a certain day⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and it was on a day”</note> Yahweh spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt.

verses.name: Exodus 6:29
verses.text: And Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying, “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> Yahweh. Speak to Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, all that I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> speaking to you.”

verses.name: Exodus 6:30
verses.text: And Moses said before Yahweh, “Look, I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a poor speaker⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “uncircumcised of lips”</note> And how will Pharaoh listen to me?”  <chapter eID="Exod.6"/>

verses.name: Exodus 7:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv229"/><title type="x-s">Yahweh Reviews Plans for Bringing the Israelites out of Egypt</title> <div sID="gen379" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv229"/>And Yahweh said to Moses, “See, I have made you <transChange type="added">as</transChange> a god to Pharaoh, and Aaron your brother will be your prophet.

verses.name: Exodus 7:2
verses.text: You will speak all that I will command you, and Aaron your brother will speak to Pharaoh, and he will release the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> from his land.

verses.name: Exodus 7:3
verses.text: And I myself will harden the heart of Pharaoh, and I will make my signs and my wonders numerous in the land of Egypt.

verses.name: Exodus 7:4
verses.text: And Pharaoh will not listen to you, and I will put my hand into Egypt and bring out my divisions, my people, the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> from the land of Egypt with great punishments.

verses.name: Exodus 7:5
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Egyptians will know that I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> Yahweh when I stretch out my hand over Egypt and bring the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> out from their midst.”  <div eID="gen379" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 7:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv230"/><div sID="gen380" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv230"/>And Moses and Aaron did <transChange type="added">it</transChange>; as Yahweh commanded them, so they did.

verses.name: Exodus 7:7
verses.text: (And Moses <transChange type="added">was</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞eighty years old⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “a son of eighty year”</note> and Aaron was <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞eighty-three years old⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a son of three and eighty year”</note> when they spoke to Pharaoh.)  <div eID="gen380" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 7:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv231"/><title type="x-s">Provision of a Wonder: Aaron’s Staff Becomes a Snake</title> <div sID="gen381" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv231"/>And Yahweh said to Moses and to Aaron, saying,

verses.name: Exodus 7:9
verses.text: “When Pharaoh speaks to you, saying, ‘Do a wonder for yourselves,’ you will say to Aaron, ‘Take your staff and throw it before Pharaoh, and it will become a snake.’ ”

verses.name: Exodus 7:10
verses.text: And Moses and Aaron came to Pharaoh, and they did so, as Yahweh had commanded. And Aaron threw his staff before Pharaoh and before his servants, and it became a snake.  <div eID="gen381" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 7:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv232"/><div sID="gen382" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv232"/>And Pharaoh also called the wise men and the sorcerers, and they also, the magicians of Egypt, did likewise with their secret arts.

verses.name: Exodus 7:12
verses.text: Each threw down his staff, and they became snakes, and Aaron’s staff swallowed up their staffs.

verses.name: Exodus 7:13
verses.text: And Pharaoh’s heart was hard, and he did not listen to them, as Yahweh had said.  <div eID="gen382" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 7:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv233"/><title type="x-s">Plague One: Blood</title> <div sID="gen383" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv233"/>And Yahweh said to Moses, “Pharaoh’s heart <transChange type="added">is</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞insensitive⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “heavy”</note> he refuses to release the people.

verses.name: Exodus 7:15
verses.text: Go to Pharaoh in the morning. Look, <transChange type="added">he is</transChange> going out to the water, and you must wait to meet him on the bank of the Nile, and you must take in your hand the staff that was changed into a snake.

verses.name: Exodus 7:16
verses.text: And you must say to him, ‘Yahweh, the God of the Hebrews, has sent me to you, saying, “Release my people that they may serve me in the desert, and, look, you have not listened until now.”

verses.name: Exodus 7:17
verses.text: Thus says Yahweh, “By this you will know that I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> Yahweh. Look, I <transChange type="added">am about to</transChange> strike with the staff that is in my hand the water that is in the Nile, and it will be changed to blood.

verses.name: Exodus 7:18
verses.text: And the fish that <transChange type="added">are</transChange> in the Nile will die, and the Nile will stink, and <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Egyptians will be unable to drink water from the Nile.” ’ ”  <div eID="gen383" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 7:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv234"/><div sID="gen384" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv234"/>And Yahweh said to Moses, “Say to Aaron, ‘Take your staff and stretch your hand out over the waters of Egypt and over their rivers, over their canals, and over their pools and over all of their reservoirs of water, so that they become blood,’ and blood will be in all the land of Egypt and in <transChange type="added">vessels of</transChange> wood and of stone.”  <div eID="gen384" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 7:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv235"/><div sID="gen385" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv235"/>And Moses and Aaron did so, as Yahweh had commanded, and he raised the staff and struck the water that was in the Nile before the eyes of Pharaoh and before the eyes of his servants, and all of the water that was in the Nile was changed to blood.

verses.name: Exodus 7:21
verses.text: And the fish that <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in the Nile died, and the Nile stank, and <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Egyptians were not able to drink water from the Nile, and the blood was in all the land of Egypt.  <div eID="gen385" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 7:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv236"/><div sID="gen386" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv236"/>And the magicians of Egypt did likewise with their secret arts, and Pharaoh’s heart was hard, and he did not listen to them, as Yahweh had spoken.

verses.name: Exodus 7:23
verses.text: And Pharaoh turned and went to his house, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he did not take also this to heart⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “he did not put his heart also to this”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 7:24
verses.text: And all of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Egyptians dug around the Nile <transChange type="added">for</transChange> water to drink, because they were unable to drink from the water of the Nile.  <div eID="gen386" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 7:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv237"/><div sID="gen387" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv237"/>And seven days passed after Yahweh struck the Nile.  <chapter eID="Exod.7"/>

verses.name: Exodus 8:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv238"/><title type="x-s">Plague Two: Frogs</title> <div sID="gen388" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv238"/><note placement="foot"><reference osisRef="Exod.8.1-Exod.8.32">Exodus 8:1–32 </reference>in the English Bible is 7:26–8:28 in the Hebrew Bible</note> And Yahweh said to Moses, “Go to Pharaoh, and say to him, ‘Thus says Yahweh, “Release my people so that they may serve me.”

verses.name: Exodus 8:2
verses.text: And if you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> refusing to release, look, I <transChange type="added">am going to</transChange> plague all of your territory with frogs.

verses.name: Exodus 8:3
verses.text: And the Nile will swarm with frogs, and they will go up and come into your house and into your <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞bedroom⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the inner room of your bed”</note> and onto your bed and into the house of your servants and among your people and into your ovens and into your kneading troughs.

verses.name: Exodus 8:4
verses.text: And the frogs will go up against you and against your people and against all of your servants.’ ”  <div eID="gen388" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 8:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv239"/><div sID="gen389" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv239"/>And Yahweh said to Moses, “Say to Aaron, ‘Stretch out your hand with your staff over the rivers, over the canals, and over the pools, and bring up the frogs on the land of Egypt.’ ”

verses.name: Exodus 8:6
verses.text: And Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt, and the frogs went up and covered the land of Egypt.

verses.name: Exodus 8:7
verses.text: And the magicians did likewise with their secret arts, and they brought up frogs over the land of Egypt.  <div eID="gen389" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 8:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv240"/><div sID="gen390" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv240"/>And Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron and said, “Pray to Yahweh, and let him remove the frogs from me and from my people, and let me release the people so that they can sacrifice to Yahweh.”

verses.name: Exodus 8:9
verses.text: And Moses said to Pharaoh, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I leave to you the honor⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “glorify yourself”</note> over me. When shall I pray for you and for your servants and for your people to cut off the frogs from you and from your houses? They will be left only in the Nile.”

verses.name: Exodus 8:10
verses.text: And he said, “Tomorrow.” And he said, “<transChange type="added">Let it be</transChange> according to your word so that you will know that there is no one like Yahweh our God.

verses.name: Exodus 8:11
verses.text: And the frogs will depart from you and from your house and from your servants. They will be left only in the Nile.”  <div eID="gen390" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 8:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv241"/><div sID="gen391" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv241"/>And Moses and Aaron went out from Pharaoh, and Moses cried out to Yahweh over the matter of the frogs that he had brought on Pharaoh.

verses.name: Exodus 8:13
verses.text: And Yahweh did according to the word of Moses, and the frogs died from the houses, from the courtyards, and from the fields.

verses.name: Exodus 8:14
verses.text: And they piled them <transChange type="added">in</transChange> countless heaps,<note placement="foot">Literally “heaps, heaps”</note> and the land stank.

verses.name: Exodus 8:15
verses.text: And Pharaoh saw that there was relief, and he made his heart <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞insensitive⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “heavy”</note> and he did not listen to them, as Yahweh had spoken.  <div eID="gen391" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 8:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv242"/><title type="x-s">Plague Three: Gnats</title> <div sID="gen392" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv242"/>And Yahweh said to Moses, “Say to Aaron, ‘Stretch out your staff and strike the dust of the land, and it will become gnats<note placement="foot">Exactly what troublesome insect is uncertain</note> in all the land of Egypt.’ ”

verses.name: Exodus 8:17
verses.text: And he did so, and Aaron stretched out his hand with his staff, and he struck the dust of the land, and it became gnats on the humans and on the animals; all of the dust of the land became gnats in all the land of Egypt.

verses.name: Exodus 8:18
verses.text: And the magicians did so with their secret arts to bring out the gnats, but they were not able, and the gnats were on the humans and on the animals.

verses.name: Exodus 8:19
verses.text: And the magicians said to Pharaoh, “It is the finger of God.” But the heart of Pharaoh was hard, and he did not listen to them, as Yahweh had spoken.  <div eID="gen392" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 8:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv243"/><title type="x-s">Plague Four: Flies</title> <div sID="gen393" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv243"/>And Yahweh said to Moses, “Start early in the morning and stand before Pharaoh. Look, <transChange type="added">he is</transChange> going out to the water, and you must say to him, ‘Thus says Yahweh, “Release my people so that they may serve me.”

verses.name: Exodus 8:21
verses.text: But if you are not <transChange type="added">about to</transChange> release my people, look, I <transChange type="added">am about</transChange> to send out flies among you and among your servants and among your people and in your houses; and the houses of Egypt will fill up with the flies and also the ground that they are on.

verses.name: Exodus 8:22
verses.text: But on that day I will distinguish<note placement="foot">Or “deal differently with”</note> the land of Goshen, where my people are staying, by there not being flies there, so that you will know that I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> Yahweh in the midst of the land.

verses.name: Exodus 8:23
verses.text: And I will put a distinction between my people and your people; this sign will be tomorrow.’ ”  <div eID="gen393" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 8:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv244"/><div sID="gen394" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv244"/>And Yahweh did so, and a <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞severe⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “heavy”</note> <transChange type="added">swarm of</transChange> flies came to the house of Pharaoh and the house of his servants and in all the land of Egypt; the land was ruined because of the flies.

verses.name: Exodus 8:25
verses.text: And Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron, and he said, “Go, sacrifice to your God in the land.”

verses.name: Exodus 8:26
verses.text: And Moses said, “To do so <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not right, because we will sacrifice to Yahweh our God a thing detestable to the Egyptians. Look, <transChange type="added">if</transChange> we sacrifice before their eyes the thing detestable to the Egyptians, will they not stone us?

verses.name: Exodus 8:27
verses.text: We will go a journey of three days into the desert, and we will sacrifice to Yahweh our God according to what he says to us.”  <div eID="gen394" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 8:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv245"/><div sID="gen395" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv245"/>And Pharaoh said, “I myself will release you, and you will sacrifice to Yahweh your God in the desert. Only surely you must not go far. Pray for me.”

verses.name: Exodus 8:29
verses.text: And Moses said, “Look, I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> going out from you, and I will pray to Yahweh so that the flies depart from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people tomorrow. Only let not Pharaoh again deceive <transChange type="added">us</transChange> by not releasing the people to sacrifice to Yahweh.”  <div eID="gen395" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 8:30
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv246"/><div sID="gen396" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv246"/>And Moses went out from Pharaoh and prayed to Yahweh.

verses.name: Exodus 8:31
verses.text: And Yahweh did according to the word of Moses and removed the flies from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people; not one was left.

verses.name: Exodus 8:32
verses.text: And Pharaoh made his heart <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞insensitive⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “heavy”</note> also this time, and he did not release the people.  <chapter eID="Exod.8"/>

verses.name: Exodus 9:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv247"/><title type="x-s">Plague Five: Livestock Death</title> <div sID="gen397" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv247"/>And Yahweh said to Moses, “Go to Pharaoh and say to him, ‘Thus says Yahweh, the God of the Hebrews, “Release my people so that they may serve me.”

verses.name: Exodus 9:2
verses.text: But if you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> refusing to release and you still <transChange type="added">are</transChange> keeping hold of them,

verses.name: Exodus 9:3
verses.text: look, the hand of Yahweh <transChange type="added">is</transChange> about to be <transChange type="added">present with</transChange> a very <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞severe⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “heavy”</note> plague on your livestock that are in the field, on the horses, on the donkeys, on the camels, on the cattle, and on the sheep and goats.

verses.name: Exodus 9:4
verses.text: But Yahweh will make a distinction between the livestock of Israel and the livestock of Egypt, and not a thing will die from all <transChange type="added">that belongs</transChange> to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.’ ”<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 9:5
verses.text: And Yahweh set an appointed time, saying, “Tomorrow Yahweh will do this thing in the land.”  <div eID="gen397" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 9:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv248"/><div sID="gen398" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv248"/>And Yahweh did this thing the next day; all the livestock of Egypt died, but from the livestock of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> not one died.

verses.name: Exodus 9:7
verses.text: And Pharaoh sent <transChange type="added">to check</transChange>, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞it turned out⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “look”</note> not even one from the livestock of Israel had died, but Pharaoh’s heart was <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞insensitive⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “heavy”</note> and he did not release the people.  <div eID="gen398" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 9:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv249"/><title type="x-s">Plague Six: Painful Sores</title> <div sID="gen399" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv249"/>And Yahweh said to Moses and to Aaron, “Take for yourselves full handfuls of soot from a smelting furnace, and let Moses sprinkle it toward the heavens before the eyes of Pharaoh.

verses.name: Exodus 9:9
verses.text: And it will become fine dust over all the land of Egypt, and it will become on humans and on animals a skin sore sprouting blisters in all the land of Egypt.”

verses.name: Exodus 9:10
verses.text: And they took the soot of the smelting furnace, and they stood before Pharaoh, and Moses sprinkled it toward the heavens, and it became skin sores sprouting blisters on humans and on animals.

verses.name: Exodus 9:11
verses.text: And the magicians were not able to stand before Moses because of the skin sores, for the skin sores were on the magicians and on all <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Egyptians.

verses.name: Exodus 9:12
verses.text: And Yahweh hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he did not listen to them, as Yahweh had spoken to Moses.  <div eID="gen399" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 9:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv250"/><title type="x-s">Plague Seven: Hail</title> <div sID="gen400" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv250"/>And Yahweh said to Moses, “Start early in the morning and stand before Pharaoh. Look, <transChange type="added">he is</transChange> going out to the water, and you must say to him, ‘Thus says Yahweh, the God of the Hebrews, “Release my people so that they may serve me.

verses.name: Exodus 9:14
