verses.text: For at this time I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> sending all of my plagues <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to you personally⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to your heart,” that is, in a way designed to receive attention</note> and among your servants and among your people so that you will know that there is no one like me in all the earth.

verses.name: Exodus 9:15
verses.text: For now I could have stretched out my hand, and I could have struck you and your people with the plague, and you would have perished from the earth.

verses.name: Exodus 9:16
verses.text: But for the sake of this I have caused you to stand—for the sake of showing you my strength and in order to proclaim my name in all the earth.

verses.name: Exodus 9:17
verses.text: Still you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> behaving haughtily to my people by not releasing them.

verses.name: Exodus 9:18
verses.text: Look, about <transChange type="added">this</transChange> time tomorrow, I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> going to cause very severe<note placement="foot">Literally “heavy”</note> hail to rain, the like of which has not been in Egypt from the day it was founded until now.

verses.name: Exodus 9:19
verses.text: And now send <transChange type="added">word</transChange>; bring into safety your livestock and all that <transChange type="added">belongs</transChange> to you in the field. The hail will come down on every human and animal that is found in the field and not gathered into the house, and they will die.” ’ ”  <div eID="gen400" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 9:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv251"/><div sID="gen401" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv251"/>Anyone from the servants of Pharaoh who feared the word of Yahweh caused his servants and livestock to flee to the houses.

verses.name: Exodus 9:21
verses.text: But whoever did not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞give regard to⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “put his heart to”</note> the word of Yahweh abandoned his servants and his livestock in the field.  <div eID="gen401" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 9:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv252"/><div sID="gen402" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv252"/>And Yahweh said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand to the heavens, and let there be hail in all the land of Egypt, on human and on animal and on all the vegetation of the field in the land of Egypt.”

verses.name: Exodus 9:23
verses.text: And Moses stretched out his staff to the heavens, and Yahweh gave thunder<note placement="foot">The word often translated “voice” or “sound” is also used to describe thunder, as in this chapter</note> and hail, and fire went <transChange type="added">to the</transChange> earth, and Yahweh caused hail to rain on the land of Egypt.

verses.name: Exodus 9:24
verses.text: And there was hail, and fire <transChange type="added">was</transChange> flashing back and forth in the midst of the very severe hail, the like of which was not in all the land of Egypt since it had become a nation.

verses.name: Exodus 9:25
verses.text: And the hail struck in all the land of Egypt all that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in the field, from human to animal, and the hail struck all the vegetation of the field and smashed every tree of the field.

verses.name: Exodus 9:26
verses.text: Only in the land of Goshen, where the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> <transChange type="added">were</transChange>, there was no hail.  <div eID="gen402" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 9:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv253"/><div sID="gen403" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv253"/>And Pharaoh sent and called Moses and Aaron and said to them, “I have sinned this time. Yahweh <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the righteous <transChange type="added">one</transChange>, and I and my people <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the wicked <transChange type="added">ones</transChange>.

verses.name: Exodus 9:28
verses.text: Pray to Yahweh. The thunder of God and hail <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞are enough⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “much/great from the being of the voices/thunder”</note> and I will release you, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you will no longer have to stay⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “you will not add to stand/remain”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 9:29
verses.text: And Moses said to him, “At my leaving the city, I will spread out my hands to Yahweh. The thunder will stop, and the hail will be no more, so that you will know that the earth <transChange type="added">belongs</transChange> to Yahweh.

verses.name: Exodus 9:30
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">as for</transChange> you and your servants, I know that you do not yet fear the presence of Yahweh God.”  <div eID="gen403" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 9:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv254"/><div sID="gen404" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv254"/>And the flax and the barley were struck, because the barley <transChange type="added">was in the</transChange> ear and the flax <transChange type="added">was in</transChange> bud.

verses.name: Exodus 9:32
verses.text: But the wheat and the spelt were not struck, because they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> late-ripening.  <div eID="gen404" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 9:33
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv255"/><div sID="gen405" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv255"/>And Moses went from Pharaoh out of the city, and he spread his hands to Yahweh, and the thunder and the hail stopped, and rain did not pour <transChange type="added">on the</transChange> earth.

verses.name: Exodus 9:34
verses.text: And Pharaoh saw that the rain and the hail and the thunder stopped, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he again sinned⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “he added to sin”</note> and made his heart <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞insensitive⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “he made his heart heavy”</note> he and his servants.

verses.name: Exodus 9:35
verses.text: And Pharaoh’s heart was hard, and he did not release the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> as Yahweh had said <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞by the agency of Moses⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “by the hand of Moses”</note>  <chapter eID="Exod.9"/>

verses.name: Exodus 10:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv256"/><title type="x-s">Plague Eight: Locusts</title> <div sID="gen406" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv256"/>And Yahweh said to Moses, “Go to Pharaoh, for I have made his heart <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞insensitive⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “heavy”</note> and the heart of his servants in order to put these signs of mine in his midst,

verses.name: Exodus 10:2
verses.text: so that you will tell in the ears of your child and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞your grandchild⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the son of your son”</note> that I dealt harshly with <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Egyptians and <transChange type="added">so that you will tell about</transChange> my signs that I have done among them, and so you will know that I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> Yahweh.”  <div eID="gen406" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 10:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv257"/><div sID="gen407" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv257"/>And Moses and Aaron came to Pharaoh, and they said to him, “Thus says Yahweh, the God of the Hebrews, ‘Until when will you refuse to submit before me? Release my people so that they may serve me.

verses.name: Exodus 10:4
verses.text: But if you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> refusing to release my people, look, I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> about to bring locusts into your territory tomorrow.

verses.name: Exodus 10:5
verses.text: And they will cover the surface of the land, and no one will be able to see the land, and they will eat the remainder of what is left—what is left over for you from the hail—and they will eat every sprouting tree <transChange type="added">belonging</transChange> to you from the field.

verses.name: Exodus 10:6
verses.text: And your houses will be full, and the houses of all your servants and the houses of all Egypt, <transChange type="added">something</transChange> that your fathers and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞your grandfathers⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the fathers of your fathers”</note> never saw from the day they were on the earth until this day.’ ” And he turned and went out from Pharaoh.  <div eID="gen407" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 10:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv258"/><div sID="gen408" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv258"/>And the servants of Pharaoh said to him, “Until when will this be a snare for us? Release the men so that they may serve Yahweh their God. Do you not yet know that Egypt is destroyed?”

verses.name: Exodus 10:8
verses.text: And Moses and Aaron were brought back to Pharaoh, and he said to them, “Serve Yahweh your God. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Who are the ones going⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?<note placement="foot">Literally “who and who the goers?”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 10:9
verses.text: And Moses said, “With our young and with our old we will go; with our sons and with our daughters, with our sheep and goats and with our cattle we will go because <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> the feast of Yahweh for us.”

verses.name: Exodus 10:10
verses.text: And he said to them, “Let Yahweh be thus with you <transChange type="added">as soon</transChange> as I release you and your dependents.<note placement="foot">Or “little children” or “little ones”</note> See that evil is before your faces.

verses.name: Exodus 10:11
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞No indeed⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “not so”</note> just the men<note placement="foot">This word for “men” indicates that Pharaoh means only the able-bodied men can go</note> go and serve Yahweh, since this <transChange type="added">is what</transChange> you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> seeking.” And he drove them out from the presence of Pharaoh.  <div eID="gen408" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 10:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv259"/><div sID="gen409" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv259"/>And Yahweh said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand over the land of Egypt with the locusts so that they may come up over the land of Egypt, and let them eat all the vegetation of the land, all that the hail left behind.”

verses.name: Exodus 10:13
verses.text: And Moses stretched out his staff over the land of Egypt, and Yahweh drove an east wind into the land all that day and all night. The morning came, and the east wind had brought the locusts.

verses.name: Exodus 10:14
verses.text: And the locusts went up over all the land of Egypt, and they settled in all the territory of Egypt, very <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞severe⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “heavy”</note> Before it there were not locusts like them, nor will there be after it.

verses.name: Exodus 10:15
verses.text: And they covered the surface of all the land, and the land was dark <transChange type="added">with them</transChange>, and they ate all the vegetation of the land and all the fruit of the trees that the hail had left, and no green was left in the trees nor in the vegetation of the field in all the land of Egypt.  <div eID="gen409" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 10:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv260"/><div sID="gen410" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv260"/>And Pharaoh hurried to call Moses and Aaron, and he said, “I have sinned against Yahweh your God and against you.

verses.name: Exodus 10:17
verses.text: And now forgive my sin surely this time, and pray to Yahweh your God so that he may only remove from me this death.”

verses.name: Exodus 10:18
verses.text: And he went out from Pharaoh, and he prayed to Yahweh.

verses.name: Exodus 10:19
verses.text: And Yahweh turned a very strong <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞west wind⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sea wind,” a wind from the Mediterranean Sea to the west</note> and lifted up the locusts and thrust them into the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Red Sea⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sea of reed”</note> and not one locust remained in all the territory of Egypt.

verses.name: Exodus 10:20
verses.text: And Yahweh hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he did not release the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note>  <div eID="gen410" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 10:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv261"/><title type="x-s">Plague Nine: Darkness</title> <div sID="gen411" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv261"/>And Yahweh said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward the heavens so that there may be darkness over the land of Egypt and so that <transChange type="added">a person can</transChange> feel darkness.”

verses.name: Exodus 10:22
verses.text: And Moses stretched out his hand toward the heavens, and there was darkness of night in all the land of Egypt <transChange type="added">for</transChange> three days.

verses.name: Exodus 10:23
verses.text: No one could see his brother, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞because of it no one could move from where they were⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a man did not rise from under it”</note> for three days, but there was light for the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> in their dwellings.  <div eID="gen411" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 10:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv262"/><div sID="gen412" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv262"/>And Pharaoh called Moses and said, “Go, serve Yahweh. Only your sheep and goats and your cattle must be left behind. Your dependents<note placement="foot">Or “little children” or “little ones”; the term here includes women and children and men too old or ill to fight</note> may also go with you.”

verses.name: Exodus 10:25
verses.text: And Moses said, “Even <transChange type="added">if</transChange> you yourself put into our hand sacrifices and burnt offerings and we offer <transChange type="added">them</transChange> to Yahweh our God,

verses.name: Exodus 10:26
verses.text: our livestock must also go with us. Not a hoof can be left because we must take from them to serve Yahweh our God. And we will not know <transChange type="added">with</transChange> what we are to serve Yahweh until we come there.”

verses.name: Exodus 10:27
verses.text: And Yahweh hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he was not willing to release them.

verses.name: Exodus 10:28
verses.text: And Pharaoh said to him, “Go from me. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Be careful⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “watch for you”</note> not to see my face again, because on the day of your seeing my face you will die.”

verses.name: Exodus 10:29
verses.text: And Moses said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞That is right⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “right you said”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I will not again see your face⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “I will not add again seeing of your face”</note>  <chapter eID="Exod.10"/>

verses.name: Exodus 11:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv263"/><title type="x-s">Announcement of the Tenth Plague: Death of the Firstborn</title> <div sID="gen413" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv263"/>And Yahweh said to Moses, “Still one plague I will bring upon Pharaoh and upon Egypt; afterward he will release you from here. At the moment of his releasing, he will certainly drive you completely out from here.

verses.name: Exodus 11:2
verses.text: Speak in the ears of the people, and let them ask, a man from his neighbor and a woman from her neighbor, <transChange type="added">for</transChange> objects of silver and objects of gold.”

verses.name: Exodus 11:3
verses.text: And Yahweh gave the people favor in the eyes of Egypt. Also the man Moses <transChange type="added">was</transChange> very great in the land of Egypt, in the eyes of the servants of Pharaoh and in the eyes of the people.  <div eID="gen413" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 11:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv264"/><div sID="gen414" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv264"/>And Moses said, “Thus says Yahweh, ‘About the middle of the night I <transChange type="added">will</transChange> go out through the midst of Egypt,

verses.name: Exodus 11:5
verses.text: and every firstborn in the land of Egypt will die, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sits on his throne to the firstborn of the slave woman who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> behind the pair of millstones and every firstborn animal.<note placement="foot">The Hebrew word often refers to domestic animals</note>

verses.name: Exodus 11:6
verses.text: And there will be a great cry of distress in all the land of Egypt, the like of which has not been nor will be again.<note placement="foot">Literally “which like it has not been and like it will not be again”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 11:7
verses.text: But against all the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> from a man to an animal, a dog will not even <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞bark⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “move his tongue” or “sharpen his tongue”</note> so that you will know that Yahweh makes a distinction between Egypt and Israel.’

verses.name: Exodus 11:8
verses.text: And all of these your servants will come down to me and bow to me, saying, ‘Go out, you and all the people who <transChange type="added">are</transChange> at your feet.’ And afterward I will go out.” And he went out from Pharaoh <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in great anger⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “with heat of nose”</note>  <div eID="gen414" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 11:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv265"/><div sID="gen415" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv265"/>And Yahweh said to Moses, “Pharaoh will not listen to you, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞so that my wonders may multiply⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for the sake of the multiplying of my wonders”</note> in the land of Egypt.”

verses.name: Exodus 11:10
verses.text: And Moses and Aaron did all these wonders before Pharaoh, and Yahweh hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he did not release the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> from his land.  <chapter eID="Exod.11"/>

verses.name: Exodus 12:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv266"/><title type="x-s">Instructions for the Feast of Passover</title> <div sID="gen416" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv266"/>And Yahweh said to Moses and to Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying,

verses.name: Exodus 12:2
verses.text: “This month <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> the beginning of months; it <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> for you the first of the months of the year.

verses.name: Exodus 12:3
verses.text: Speak to all the community of Israel, saying, ‘On the tenth of this month, they will each take for themselves <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a lamb for the family⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “a lamb/kid for the house of fathers.” The word translated “lamb” refers to a small livestock animal and could be either a young sheep or a young goat</note> a lamb for the household.

verses.name: Exodus 12:4
verses.text: And if the household is too small for a lamb, he and the neighbor nearest to his house will take <transChange type="added">one</transChange> according to the number of persons;<note placement="foot">Or “the number of selves”</note> you will count out portions of the lamb <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞according to how much each one can eat⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “a man for the mouth of his eating”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 12:5
verses.text: The lamb for you must be a male, without defect, in its first year; you will take <transChange type="added">it</transChange> from the sheep or from the goats.  <div eID="gen416" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 12:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv267"/><div sID="gen417" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv267"/>“<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞You will keep it⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “It will be for you for observation”</note> until the fourteenth day of this month, and all the assembly of the community of Israel will slaughter it <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞at twilight⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “between the evenings”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 12:7
verses.text: And they will take <transChange type="added">some</transChange> of the blood and put <transChange type="added">it</transChange> on the two doorposts and on the lintel on the houses in which they eat it.

verses.name: Exodus 12:8
verses.text: And they will eat the meat on this night; they will eat it fire-roasted and <transChange type="added">with</transChange> unleavened bread on <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞bitter herbs⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “bitter things”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 12:9
verses.text: You must not eat any of it raw or boiled, boiled in the water, but rather roasted with fire, its head with its legs and with its inner parts.

verses.name: Exodus 12:10
verses.text: And you must not leave any of it until morning; anything left from it until morning you must burn in the fire.

verses.name: Exodus 12:11
verses.text: And this is how you will eat it—<transChange type="added">with</transChange> your waists fastened, your sandals on your feet, and your staff in your hand, and you will eat it in haste. It <transChange type="added">is</transChange> Yahweh’s Passover.  <div eID="gen417" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 12:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv268"/><div sID="gen418" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv268"/>“And I will go through the land of Egypt during this night, and I will strike all of the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from human to animal, and I will do punishments among all of the gods of Egypt. I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> Yahweh.

verses.name: Exodus 12:13
verses.text: And the blood will be a sign for you on the houses where you are, and I will see the blood, and I will pass over you, and there will not be a destructive plague among you when I strike the land of Egypt.  <div eID="gen418" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 12:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv269"/><div sID="gen419" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv269"/>“And this day will become a memorial for you, and you will celebrate it as a religious feast for Yahweh throughout your generations; you will celebrate it as a lasting statute.

verses.name: Exodus 12:15
verses.text: You will eat unleavened bread for seven days. Surely on the first day you shall remove yeast from your houses, because anyone <transChange type="added">who</transChange> eats <transChange type="added">food with</transChange> yeast from the first day until the seventh day—that person will be cut off from Israel.

verses.name: Exodus 12:16
verses.text: It will be for you on the first day a holy assembly<note placement="foot">Or “summons,” “convocation”</note> and on the seventh day a holy assembly;<note placement="foot">Or “summons,” “convocation”</note> no work will be done on them; only what is eaten by every person, it alone will be prepared for you.  <div eID="gen419" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 12:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv270"/><div sID="gen420" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv270"/>“And you will keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread, because on this very day I brought out your divisions from the land of Egypt, and you will keep this day for your generations as a lasting statute.

verses.name: Exodus 12:18
verses.text: On the first <transChange type="added">day</transChange>, on the fourteenth day of the month, in the evening, you will eat unleavened bread until the evening of the twenty-first day of the month.

verses.name: Exodus 12:19
verses.text: For seven days yeast must not be found in your houses, because <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞anyone eating food with yeast⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “anyone eating yeasted food, that person”</note> will be cut off from the community of Israel—<transChange type="added">whether</transChange> an alien or a native of the land.

verses.name: Exodus 12:20
verses.text: You will eat no <transChange type="added">food with</transChange> yeast; in all of your dwellings you will eat unleavened bread.”  <div eID="gen420" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 12:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv271"/><div sID="gen421" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv271"/>And Moses called all the elders of Israel, and he said to them, “Select and take for yourselves sheep for your clans and slaughter the Passover sacrifice.

verses.name: Exodus 12:22
verses.text: And take a bunch of hyssop and dip <transChange type="added">it</transChange> into the blood that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in the basin and apply <transChange type="added">some</transChange> of the blood that is in the basin to the lintel and the two doorposts. And you will not go out, anyone from the doorway of his house, until morning.

verses.name: Exodus 12:23
verses.text: And Yahweh will go through to strike Egypt, and he will see the blood on the lintel and on the two doorposts, and Yahweh will pass over the doorway and will not allow the destroyer to come to your houses to strike <transChange type="added">you</transChange>.  <div eID="gen421" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 12:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv272"/><div sID="gen422" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv272"/>“And you will keep this event as a rule for you and for your children forever.<note placement="foot">Or “until eternity”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 12:25
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and it will be”</note> when you come into the land that Yahweh will give to you, as he said, you will keep this <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞religious custom⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “service” or “work”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 12:26
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and it will be”</note> when your children say to you, ‘What is this <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞religious custom⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “service” or “work”</note> for you?’<note placement="foot">Or “What does this service mean to you?”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 12:27
verses.text: you will say, ‘It <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a Passover sacrifice for Yahweh, who passed over the houses of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> in Egypt when he struck Egypt; and he delivered our houses.’ ” And the people knelt down and they worshiped.

verses.name: Exodus 12:28
verses.text: And the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> went, and they did as Yahweh had commanded Moses and Aaron; so they did.  <div eID="gen422" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 12:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv273"/><title type="x-s">Death of Firstborn and Deliverance from Egypt</title> <div sID="gen423" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv273"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and it was”</note> in the middle of the night, Yahweh struck all of the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh sitting on his throne to the firstborn of the captive who <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in the prison house and every firstborn of an animal.

verses.name: Exodus 12:30
verses.text: And Pharaoh got up <transChange type="added">at</transChange> night, he and all his servants and all Egypt, and a great cry of distress was in Egypt because there was not a house where there was no one dead.

verses.name: Exodus 12:31
verses.text: And he called Moses and Aaron <transChange type="added">at</transChange> night, and he said, “Get up, go out from the midst of my people, both you as well as the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> and go, serve Yahweh, as you have said.

verses.name: Exodus 12:32
verses.text: Take both your sheep and goats as well as your cattle, and go, and bless also me.”  <div eID="gen423" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 12:33
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv274"/><div sID="gen424" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv274"/>And <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Egyptians urged the people <transChange type="added">in order</transChange> to hurry their release<note placement="foot">Or “to hasten to release them”</note> from the land, because they said, “All of us will die!”<note placement="foot">Or “We all are dead!”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 12:34
verses.text: And the people lifted up their dough before it had yeast; their kneading troughs <transChange type="added">were</transChange> wrapped up in their cloaks on their shoulder.

verses.name: Exodus 12:35
verses.text: And the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> did according to the word of Moses, and they asked from <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Egyptians <transChange type="added">for</transChange> objects of silver and objects of gold and <transChange type="added">for</transChange> clothing.

verses.name: Exodus 12:36
verses.text: And Yahweh gave the people favor in the eyes of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Egyptians, and they granted <transChange type="added">their</transChange> requests, and they plundered <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Egyptians.  <div eID="gen424" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 12:37
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv275"/><div sID="gen425" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv275"/>And the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> set out from Rameses to Succoth; the men were about six hundred thousand on foot,<note placement="foot">Or “footmen,” “infantrymen.” The word probably has military connotations, as when it is used elsewhere in the numbering of soldiers (compare <reference osisRef="2Sam.10.6">2 Sam 10:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Kgs.20.29">1 Kgs 20:29</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Kgs.13.7">2 Kgs 13:7</reference>)</note> besides dependents.

verses.name: Exodus 12:38
verses.text: And also a <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞mixed multitude⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a large mixture” (compare <reference osisRef="Jer.25.20">Jer 25:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.30.5">Ezek 30:5</reference>)</note> went up with them and sheep and goats and cattle, very numerous livestock.

verses.name: Exodus 12:39
verses.text: And they baked the dough that they had brought out from Egypt <transChange type="added">as</transChange> cakes, unleavened bread, because it had no yeast when they were driven out from Egypt, and they were not able to delay, and also they had not made provisions for themselves.  <div eID="gen425" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 12:40
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv276"/><div sID="gen426" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv276"/>And the period of dwelling of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> that they dwelled in Egypt <transChange type="added">was</transChange> four hundred and thirty years.

verses.name: Exodus 12:41
verses.text: And at the end of four hundred and thirty years, on this exact day, all of Yahweh’s divisions went out from the land of Egypt.

verses.name: Exodus 12:42
verses.text: It <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a night of vigils<note placement="foot">Or “observances”</note> belonging to Yahweh for bringing them out from the land of Egypt; it is this night belonging to Yahweh with vigils for all of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> throughout their generations.  <div eID="gen426" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 12:43
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv277"/><div sID="gen427" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv277"/>And Yahweh said to Moses and Aaron, “This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the statute of the Passover: No foreigner may eat it.

verses.name: Exodus 12:44
verses.text: But any slave of a man, an acquisition by money, and you have circumcised him, then he may eat it.

verses.name: Exodus 12:45
verses.text: A temporary resident and a hired worker may not eat it.

verses.name: Exodus 12:46
verses.text: It will be eaten in one house; you will not bring part of the meat out from the house to the outside; and you will not break a bone of it.

verses.name: Exodus 12:47
verses.text: All of the community of Israel will prepare it.

verses.name: Exodus 12:48
verses.text: And when an alien dwells with you and he wants to prepare <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Passover for Yahweh, every male belonging to him must be circumcised, and then he may come near to prepare it, and he will be as the native of the land, but any uncircumcised <transChange type="added">man</transChange> may not eat it.

verses.name: Exodus 12:49
verses.text: One law will be for the native and for the alien who is dwelling in your midst.”  <div eID="gen427" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 12:50
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv278"/><div sID="gen428" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv278"/>And all the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> did as Yahweh had commanded Moses and Aaron; so they did.

verses.name: Exodus 12:51
verses.text: And it was on exactly this day Yahweh brought the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> out from the land of Egypt by their divisions.  <chapter eID="Exod.12"/>

verses.name: Exodus 13:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv279"/><title type="x-s">Unleavened Bread and Dedication of Firstborn to Commemorate the Rescue from Egypt</title> <div sID="gen429" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv279"/>And Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.name: Exodus 13:2
verses.text: “Consecrate to me every firstborn, the first offspring of every womb among the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> among humans<note placement="foot">Hebrew “human”</note> and among domestic animals;<note placement="foot">Hebrew “animal”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞it belongs to me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “to/for me it”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 13:3
verses.text: And Moses said to the people, “Remember this day when you went out from Egypt, from a house of slaves, because with strength of hand Yahweh brought you out from here, and <transChange type="added">food with</transChange> yeast will not be eaten.

verses.name: Exodus 13:4
verses.text: Today you are going out in the month of Abib.

verses.name: Exodus 13:5
verses.text: And when Yahweh brings you to the land of the Canaanites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Canaanite”</note> and the Hittites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Hittite”</note> and the Amorites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Amorite”</note> and the Hivites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Hivite”</note> and the Jebusites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Jebusite”</note>—which he swore to your ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> to give to you, a land flowing with milk and honey—you will perform this service in this month.

verses.name: Exodus 13:6
verses.text: Seven days you will eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> a feast for Yahweh.

verses.name: Exodus 13:7
verses.text: Unleavened bread will be eaten the seven days; <transChange type="added">food with</transChange> yeast will not be seen for you; and yeast will not be seen for you in all your territory.

verses.name: Exodus 13:8
verses.text: And you shall tell your son on that day, saying, ‘This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> because of what Yahweh did for me when I came out from Egypt.’

verses.name: Exodus 13:9
verses.text: And it will be as a sign on your hand and as a memorial between your eyes so that the law of Yahweh will be in your mouth, that with a strong hand Yahweh brought you out from Egypt.

verses.name: Exodus 13:10
verses.text: And you will keep this statute at its appointed time <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from year to year⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “from days to days”</note>  <div eID="gen429" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 13:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv280"/><div sID="gen430" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv280"/>“And when Yahweh brings you to the land of the Canaanite, as he swore to you and to your ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and he gives it to you,

verses.name: Exodus 13:12
verses.text: you will hand over every first offspring of a womb to Yahweh, and every first offspring dropped by a domestic animal that will belong to you, the males <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> for Yahweh.

verses.name: Exodus 13:13
verses.text: And every first offspring of a donkey you will redeem with small livestock, and if you will not redeem <transChange type="added">it</transChange>, then you will break its neck, and every firstborn human among your sons you will redeem.

verses.name: Exodus 13:14
verses.text: And when your son asks you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in the future⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “tomorrow”</note> saying, ‘What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> this?’ you will say to him, ‘With strength of hand Yahweh brought us out from Egypt, from a house of slaves.

verses.name: Exodus 13:15
verses.text: And when Pharaoh was stubborn to release us, Yahweh killed every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from firstborn human to firstborn domestic animal. Therefore I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> sacrificing to Yahweh every first offspring of a womb, the males, and every firstborn of my sons I redeem.’

verses.name: Exodus 13:16
verses.text: And it will be as a sign on your hand and as symbolic ornaments between your eyes that with strength of hand Yahweh brought us out from Egypt.”  <div eID="gen430" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 13:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv281"/><title type="x-s">Summary of Travel</title> <div sID="gen431" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv281"/>And when Pharaoh released the people, God did not lead them the way of the land of the Philistines, though it <transChange type="added">was</transChange> nearer, because God said, “Lest the people change their mind when they see war and return to Egypt.”

verses.name: Exodus 13:18
verses.text: So God led the people around <transChange type="added">by</transChange> the way of the desert <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Red Sea⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sea of reed”</note> and the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> went up in battle array from the land of Egypt.

verses.name: Exodus 13:19
verses.text: And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him because <transChange type="added">Joseph</transChange><note placement="foot">Hebrew “he”</note> had made the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> solemnly swear an oath, saying, “God will surely attend to you, and you will take up my bones from here with you.”

verses.name: Exodus 13:20
verses.text: And they set out from Succoth, and they encamped at Etham on the edge of the desert.

verses.name: Exodus 13:21
verses.text: And Yahweh was going before them by day in a column of cloud to lead them <transChange type="added">on</transChange> the way and <transChange type="added">by</transChange> night in a column of fire to give light to them to go by day and night.

verses.name: Exodus 13:22
verses.text: The column of cloud by day and the column of fire <transChange type="added">by</transChange> night did not depart from before the people.  <chapter eID="Exod.13"/>

verses.name: Exodus 14:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv282"/><title type="x-s">Yahweh Rescues Israel at the Red Sea</title> <div sID="gen432" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv282"/>And Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.name: Exodus 14:2
verses.text: “Speak to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> so that they turn and encamp before Pi-hahiroth, between Migdol <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞and the sea⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “and between the sea”</note> before Baal Zephon, <transChange type="added">which is</transChange> opposite it, you will camp by the sea.

verses.name: Exodus 14:3
verses.text: And Pharaoh will say of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> ‘They are wandering around in the land. The desert has closed in on them.’

verses.name: Exodus 14:4
verses.text: And I will harden the heart of Pharaoh, and he will chase after them, and I will be glorified through Pharaoh and through all his army, and <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Egyptians will know that I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> Yahweh.” And they did so.  <div eID="gen432" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 14:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv283"/><div sID="gen433" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv283"/>And it was told to the king of Egypt that the people fled, and the heart of Pharaoh was changed and <transChange type="added">that of</transChange> his servants toward the people, and they said, “What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> this we have done, that we have released Israel from serving us!”

verses.name: Exodus 14:6
verses.text: And he harnessed his chariot and took with him his people.

verses.name: Exodus 14:7
verses.text: And he took six hundred select chariots and all the chariots of Egypt and officers over all of them.

verses.name: Exodus 14:8
verses.text: And Yahweh hardened the heart of Pharaoh the king of Egypt, and he chased after the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> (Now the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> were going out <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞boldly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “with a raised/high hand”</note>)

verses.name: Exodus 14:9
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Egyptians chased after them, and they overtook them encamped at the sea—all the horses of the chariots of Pharaoh and his charioteers and his army—at Pi-hahiroth before Baal Zephon.  <div eID="gen433" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 14:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv284"/><div sID="gen434" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv284"/>And Pharaoh approached, and the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> lifted their eyes, and there were the Egyptians traveling after them! And they were very afraid, and the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> cried out to Yahweh.

verses.name: Exodus 14:11
verses.text: And they said to Moses, “Because there are no graves in Egypt? Is that why you have taken us to die in the desert? What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> this you have done to us by bringing us out from Egypt!

verses.name: Exodus 14:12
verses.text: Isn’t this the word we spoke to you in Egypt, saying, ‘Leave us alone <transChange type="added">so that</transChange> we can serve Egypt!’ because serving Egypt is better for us than our dying in the desert.”

verses.name: Exodus 14:13
verses.text: And Moses said to the people, “You must not be afraid. Stand <transChange type="added">still</transChange> and see the salvation of Yahweh, which he will accomplish for you today, because <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Egyptians whom you see today you will see never again.

verses.name: Exodus 14:14
verses.text: Yahweh will fight for you, and you must be quiet.”  <div eID="gen434" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 14:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv285"/><div sID="gen435" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv285"/>And Yahweh said to Moses, “Why do you cry out to me? Speak to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> so that they set out.<note placement="foot">Or “journey,” “move on,” “travel”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 14:16
verses.text: And you, lift up your staff and stretch out your hand over the sea and divide it <transChange type="added">so that</transChange> the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> can go in the middle of the sea on the dry land.

verses.name: Exodus 14:17
verses.text: And as for me, look, I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> about to harden the heart of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Egyptians <transChange type="added">so that</transChange> they come after them, and I will display my glory through Pharaoh and through all of his army, through his chariots and through his charioteers.

verses.name: Exodus 14:18
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Egyptians will know that I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> Yahweh when I display my glory through Pharaoh, through his chariots, and through his charioteers.”  <div eID="gen435" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 14:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv286"/><div sID="gen436" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv286"/>And the angel of God who was going before the camp of Israel set out and went behind them. And the column of cloud set out ahead of them, and it stood <transChange type="added">still</transChange> behind them,

verses.name: Exodus 14:20
verses.text: <transChange type="added">so that</transChange> it came between the camp of Egypt and the camp of Israel. And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞it was a dark cloud⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the cloud was and the darkness”</note> but it gave light to the night,<note placement="foot">Or “it illumined the night”</note> so that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞neither approached the other⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “this did not come near to this”</note> all night.  <div eID="gen436" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 14:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv287"/><div sID="gen437" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv287"/>And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and Yahweh moved the sea<note placement="foot">Or “caused the sea to go,” “drove the sea”</note> with a strong east wind all night, and he made the sea <transChange type="added">become</transChange> dry ground, and the waters were divided.

verses.name: Exodus 14:22
verses.text: And the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> entered the middle of the sea on the dry land. The waters <transChange type="added">were</transChange> a wall for them on their right and on their left.

verses.name: Exodus 14:23
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Egyptians gave chase<note placement="foot">Or “pursued,” “chased”</note> and entered after them—all the horses of Pharaoh, his chariots, and his charioteers—into the middle of the sea.

verses.name: Exodus 14:24
verses.text: And during the morning watch, Yahweh looked down to the Egyptian camp <transChange type="added">from</transChange> in the column of fire and cloud, and he threw the Egyptian camp into a panic.

verses.name: Exodus 14:25
verses.text: And he removed<note placement="foot">Or “let turn aside”</note> the wheels of their chariots so that they drove them with difficulty, and the Egyptians said, “We must flee away<note placement="foot">Or “let us flee,” “let me run away”; the verb is singular, but it is plural in context</note> from Israel because Yahweh <transChange type="added">is</transChange> fighting for them against Egypt.”  <div eID="gen437" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 14:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv288"/><div sID="gen438" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv288"/>And Yahweh said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand over the sea, and let the waters return over <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Egyptians, over their chariots, and over their charioteers.”

verses.name: Exodus 14:27
verses.text: And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and the sea returned <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞at daybreak⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “at the turning of morning”</note> to its normal level, and the Egyptians were fleeing <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞because of it⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to/for/from the meeting of it”</note> and Yahweh swept <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Egyptians into the middle of the sea.

verses.name: Exodus 14:28
verses.text: And the waters returned and covered the chariots and the charioteers—all the army of Pharaoh coming after them into the sea. Not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞even⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “up to,” “as far as”</note> one survived among them.

verses.name: Exodus 14:29
verses.text: But the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> walked on the dry land in the middle of the sea. The waters <transChange type="added">were</transChange> a wall for them on their right and on their left.

verses.name: Exodus 14:30
verses.text: And Yahweh saved Israel on that day from the hand<note placement="foot">Or “power”</note> of Egypt, and Israel saw the Egyptians dead on the shore of the sea.

verses.name: Exodus 14:31
verses.text: And Israel saw the great hand<note placement="foot">Or “power”</note> that Yahweh displayed against Egypt, and the people feared Yahweh, and they believed in Yahweh and in Moses his servant.  <chapter eID="Exod.14"/>

verses.name: Exodus 15:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv289"/><title type="x-s">Song of Victory at the Sea</title> <div sID="gen439" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv289"/>Then Moses and the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> sang this song to Yahweh, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞and they said⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “and they said, saying”</note> <div eID="gen439" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen440"/> <l level="1" sID="gen441"/>“Let me sing to Yahweh because he is highly exalted;<l eID="gen441" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen442"/><transChange type="added">the</transChange> horse and its rider he hurled into the sea. <l eID="gen442" level="2"/>

verses.name: Exodus 15:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv290"/><l level="1" sID="gen443"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv290"/>Yah<note placement="foot">a shortened form of “Yahweh”</note> is my strength and song, and he has become my salvation;<note placement="foot">Literally “he was for me for salvation”</note><l eID="gen443" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen444"/>this <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my God, and I will praise him—the God of my father—and I will exalt him. <l eID="gen444" level="2"/>

verses.name: Exodus 15:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv291"/><l level="1" sID="gen445"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv291"/>Yahweh <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a man of war; Yahweh <transChange type="added">is</transChange> his name. <l eID="gen445" level="1"/>

verses.name: Exodus 15:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv292"/><l level="1" sID="gen446"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv292"/>The chariots of Pharaoh and his army he cast into the sea,<l eID="gen446" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen447"/>and his choice adjutants were sunk in the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Red Sea⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sea of reed”</note> <l eID="gen447" level="2"/>

verses.name: Exodus 15:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv293"/><l level="1" sID="gen448"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv293"/>The deep waters covered them;<l eID="gen448" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen449"/>they went down into the depths like a stone. <l eID="gen449" level="2"/>

verses.name: Exodus 15:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv294"/><l level="1" sID="gen450"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv294"/>Yahweh, your right hand <transChange type="added">is</transChange> glorious in power;<l eID="gen450" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen451"/>Yahweh, your right hand destroyed <transChange type="added">the</transChange> enemy. <l eID="gen451" level="2"/>

verses.name: Exodus 15:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv295"/><l level="1" sID="gen452"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv295"/>And in the greatness of your majesty you overthrew those standing up <transChange type="added">to</transChange> you;<l eID="gen452" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen453"/>you released your fierce anger, and it consumed them like stubble. <l eID="gen453" level="2"/>

verses.name: Exodus 15:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv296"/><l level="1" sID="gen454"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv296"/>And by the breath of your nostrils waters were piled up;<l eID="gen454" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen455"/>waves stood like a heap;<l eID="gen455" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen456"/>deep waters in the middle of the sea congealed. <l eID="gen456" level="2"/>

verses.name: Exodus 15:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv297"/><l level="1" sID="gen457"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv297"/><transChange type="added">The</transChange> enemy said, ‘I will pursue, I will overtake, I will divide plunder,<l eID="gen457" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen458"/>my desire will be full <transChange type="added">of</transChange> them, I will draw my sword, my hand will destroy them.’ <l eID="gen458" level="2"/>

verses.name: Exodus 15:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv298"/><l level="1" sID="gen459"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv298"/>You blew with your breath; the sea covered them;<l eID="gen459" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen460"/>they dropped like lead in the mighty waters. <l eID="gen460" level="2"/>

verses.name: Exodus 15:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv299"/><l level="1" sID="gen461"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv299"/>Who is like you among the gods, Yahweh?<l eID="gen461" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen462"/>Who is like you—glorious in holiness, awesome <transChange type="added">in</transChange> praiseworthy actions, doing wonders?<note placement="foot">Hebrew “wonder”</note> <l eID="gen462" level="2"/>

verses.name: Exodus 15:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv300"/><l level="1" sID="gen463"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv300"/>You stretched out your right hand;<l eID="gen463" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen464"/>the earth swallowed them. <l eID="gen464" level="2"/>

verses.name: Exodus 15:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv301"/><l level="1" sID="gen465"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv301"/>In your loyal love you led <transChange type="added">the</transChange> people whom you redeemed;<l eID="gen465" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen466"/>in your strength you guided <transChange type="added">them</transChange> to the abode of your holiness.<note placement="foot">Or “your holy dwelling”</note> <l eID="gen466" level="2"/>

verses.name: Exodus 15:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv302"/><l level="1" sID="gen467"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv302"/>Peoples heard; they trembled;<l eID="gen467" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen468"/>anguish seized the inhabitants of Philistia. <l eID="gen468" level="2"/>

verses.name: Exodus 15:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv303"/><l level="1" sID="gen469"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv303"/>Then the chiefs of Edom were horrified; great distress seized the leaders of Moab;<l eID="gen469" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen470"/>all of the inhabitants of Canaan melted away. <l eID="gen470" level="2"/>

verses.name: Exodus 15:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv304"/><l level="1" sID="gen471"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv304"/>Terror and dread fell on them;<l eID="gen471" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen472"/>at the greatness of your arm they became silent like the stone,<l eID="gen472" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen473"/>until your people passed by, Yahweh,<l eID="gen473" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen474"/>until <transChange type="added">the</transChange> people whom you bought passed by. <l eID="gen474" level="2"/>

verses.name: Exodus 15:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv305"/><l level="1" sID="gen475"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv305"/>You brought them and planted them on the mountain of your inheritance,<l eID="gen475" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen476"/>a place you made for yourself to inhabit, Yahweh,<l eID="gen476" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen477"/>a sanctuary, Lord, <transChange type="added">that</transChange> your hands established. <l eID="gen477" level="2"/>

verses.name: Exodus 15:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv306"/><l level="1" sID="gen478"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv306"/>Yahweh will reign as king forever and ever.” <l eID="gen478" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen440"/>

verses.name: Exodus 15:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv307"/><div sID="gen479" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv307"/>When the horses<note placement="foot">Hebrew “horse”</note> of Pharaoh came into the sea with his chariots<note placement="foot">Hebrew “chariot”</note> and with his charioteers, Yahweh brought back upon them the waters of the sea, and the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> traveled on dry ground through the middle of the sea.

verses.name: Exodus 15:20
verses.text: And Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took her<note placement="foot">Literally “the tambourine”</note> tambourine in her hand, and all of the women went out after her with tambourines and with dances.

verses.name: Exodus 15:21
verses.text: And Miriam answered,<note placement="foot">Literally “answered to them”</note> “Sing to Yahweh because he is highly exalted; <transChange type="added">the</transChange> horse and its rider he hurled into the sea.”  <div eID="gen479" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 15:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv308"/><title type="x-s">Yahweh Provides Water at Marah</title> <div sID="gen480" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv308"/>And Moses caused Israel to set out from the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Red Sea⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sea of reed”</note> and they went out into the desert of Shur, and they traveled three days in the desert, and they did not find water.

verses.name: Exodus 15:23
verses.text: And they came to Marah, and they were not able to drink water from Marah because it was bitter. Therefore <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞it was named⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “its name was called”; the Hebrew word for “bitter” is pronounced “marah”</note> Marah.

verses.name: Exodus 15:24
verses.text: And the people grumbled against Moses, saying, “What shall we drink?”

verses.name: Exodus 15:25
verses.text: And he cried out to Yahweh, and Yahweh showed him <transChange type="added">a piece of</transChange> wood, and he threw <transChange type="added">it</transChange> into the water, and the water became sweet. There he made a rule and regulation for them, and there he tested them.

verses.name: Exodus 15:26
verses.text: And he said, “If you carefully listen to the voice of Yahweh your God and you do <transChange type="added">what is</transChange> right in his eyes and give heed to his commands and you keep all his rules, <transChange type="added">then</transChange> I will not bring about on you any of the diseases<note placement="foot">Hebrew “disease”</note> that I brought about on Egypt, because I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> Yahweh your healer.  <div eID="gen480" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 15:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv309"/><div sID="gen481" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv309"/>And they came to Elim, and twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees were there, and they encamped there at the water.  <chapter eID="Exod.15"/>

verses.name: Exodus 16:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv310"/><title type="x-s">Yahweh Provides Food in the Desert</title> <div sID="gen482" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv310"/>And they set out from Elim, and all the community of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> came to the desert of Sin, which is between Elim <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞and Sinai⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “and between Sinai”</note> in the fifteenth day of the second month of their going out from the land of Egypt.

verses.name: Exodus 16:2
verses.text: And all the community of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> grumbled against Moses and against Aaron in the desert.

verses.name: Exodus 16:3
verses.text: And the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> said to them, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞If only we had died⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “who will give our dying”</note> by the hand of Yahweh in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the pots<note placement="foot">Hebrew “pot”</note> of meat, when we ate bread <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞until we were full⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to contentment” or “to satisfaction”</note> because you have brought us out to this desert to kill all of this assembly with hunger.”

verses.name: Exodus 16:4
verses.text: And Yahweh said to Moses, “Look, I am going to rain down for you bread from the heavens, and the people will go out and gather enough for the day on its day; in that way I will test them: Will they go according to my law or not?

verses.name: Exodus 16:5
verses.text: And then on the sixth day, they will prepare what they bring, and it will be twice over what they will gather every <transChange type="added">other</transChange> day.”  <div eID="gen482" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 16:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv311"/><div sID="gen483" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv311"/>And Moses and Aaron said to all the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> “<transChange type="added">In the</transChange> evening, you will know that Yahweh has brought you out from the land of Egypt,

verses.name: Exodus 16:7
verses.text: and <transChange type="added">in the</transChange> morning, you will see the glory of Yahweh, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞for he hears⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “at/in his hearing”</note> your grumblings against Yahweh, and what <transChange type="added">are</transChange> we that you grumble against us?”

verses.name: Exodus 16:8
verses.text: And Moses said, “When in the evening Yahweh gives you meat to eat and bread in the morning <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to fill up on⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to be satisfied”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞for he hears⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “at/in his hearing”</note> your grumblings that you grumble against him—and what <transChange type="added">are</transChange> we? Your grumblings <transChange type="added">are</transChange> not against us but against Yahweh.”

verses.name: Exodus 16:9
verses.text: And Moses said to Aaron, “Say to all the community of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> ‘Come near before Yahweh because he has heard your grumblings.’ ”  <div eID="gen483" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 16:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv312"/><div sID="gen484" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv312"/>And at the moment of Aaron’s speaking to all the community of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> they turned to the desert, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞and just then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “look” or “behold”</note> the glory of Yahweh appeared in the cloud.

verses.name: Exodus 16:11
verses.text: And Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.name: Exodus 16:12
verses.text: “I have heard the grumblings of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> Speak to them, saying, ‘<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞At twilight⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “between the evenings”</note> you will eat meat, and in the morning you will be full <transChange type="added">with</transChange> bread, and you will know that I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> Yahweh your God.’ ”  <div eID="gen484" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 16:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv313"/><div sID="gen485" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv313"/>And so it was, in the evening, the quail came up and covered the camp, and in the morning, a layer of dew was all around the camp.

verses.name: Exodus 16:14
verses.text: And the layer of dew came up, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞and there⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “look” or “behold”</note> on the face of the desert was a fine granular substance, fine like frost on the ground.

verses.name: Exodus 16:15
verses.text: And the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> saw, and they said <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to each other⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “a man to his brother”</note> “What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> this?” because they did not know what it <transChange type="added">was</transChange>. And Moses said to them, “That <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the bread that Yahweh has given to you as food.

verses.name: Exodus 16:16
verses.text: This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the word that Yahweh commanded, ‘Gather from it, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞each according to what he can eat⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “a man for the mouth of his eating”</note> an omer per person<note placement="foot">Literally “skull” or “head”</note> according to the number of you.<note placement="foot">Or “the number of your selves”</note> You each shall take <transChange type="added">enough</transChange> for whoever <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in his tent.’ ”  <div eID="gen485" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 16:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv314"/><div sID="gen486" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv314"/>And the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> did so, and they gathered, some more and some less.

verses.name: Exodus 16:18
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange> they measured with the omer, the one gathering more had no surplus, and the one gathering less had no lack; they gathered <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞each according to what he could eat⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “a man for the mouth of his eating”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 16:19
verses.text: And Moses said to them, “Let no one leave any of it until morning.”

verses.name: Exodus 16:20
verses.text: But they did not listen to Moses. Some people<note placement="foot">Literally “men”</note> left <transChange type="added">some</transChange> of it until morning, and it bred worms and stank. And Moses was angry with them.

verses.name: Exodus 16:21
verses.text: And they gathered it morning by morning, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞each according to what he could eat⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “a man according to the mouth of his eating”</note> and it melted when the sun was hot.<note placement="foot">Literally “and the sun was hot, and he/it melted”</note>  <div eID="gen486" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 16:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv315"/><div sID="gen487" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv315"/>And when it was the sixth day, they gathered twice <transChange type="added">as much</transChange> bread, two omers for one <transChange type="added">person</transChange>, and all the leaders of the community came and told Moses.

verses.name: Exodus 16:23
verses.text: And he said to them, “This is what Yahweh has said. Tomorrow <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a rest period, a holy Sabbath for Yahweh. Bake what you <transChange type="added">want to</transChange> bake, and boil what you <transChange type="added">want to</transChange> boil. Put aside all the surplus for yourselves for safekeeping until the morning.”

verses.name: Exodus 16:24
verses.text: And they put it aside until the morning, as Moses had commanded, and it did not make a stench, and not a maggot was in it.

verses.name: Exodus 16:25
verses.text: And Moses said, “Eat it today, because today is a Sabbath for Yahweh. Today you will not find it in the field.

verses.name: Exodus 16:26
verses.text: Six days you will gather it, but on the seventh day, <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Sabbath, it will not be <transChange type="added">present</transChange> on it.”  <div eID="gen487" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 16:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv316"/><div sID="gen488" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv316"/>And on the seventh day <transChange type="added">some</transChange> of the people went out to gather, and they did not find <transChange type="added">any</transChange>.

verses.name: Exodus 16:28
verses.text: And Yahweh said to Moses, “How long do you<note placement="foot">Plural</note> refuse to keep my commands and my laws?

verses.name: Exodus 16:29
verses.text: See, because Yahweh has given to you the Sabbath, therefore he is giving to you on the sixth day bread for two days. Stay, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞each in his location⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “a man under him/it”</note> let no one go from his place on the seventh day.”

verses.name: Exodus 16:30
verses.text: And the people rested on the seventh day.  <div eID="gen488" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 16:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv317"/><div sID="gen489" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv317"/>And the house of Israel called its name “manna.” And it <transChange type="added">was</transChange> like coriander seed, white, and its taste <transChange type="added">was</transChange> like a wafer with honey.

verses.name: Exodus 16:32
verses.text: And Moses said, “This is the word that Yahweh has commanded. ‘A full omer of it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> for safekeeping for your generations so that they will see the bread that I fed you in the desert when I brought you from the land of Egypt.’ ”

verses.name: Exodus 16:33
verses.text: And Moses said to Aaron, “Take one jar and put there a full omer of manna. Leave it before Yahweh for safekeeping for your generations.”

verses.name: Exodus 16:34
verses.text: As Yahweh had commanded Moses, so Aaron left it before the testimony for safekeeping.

verses.name: Exodus 16:35
verses.text: And the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> ate the manna forty years, until their coming to an inhabited land; they ate the manna until their coming to the border of the land of Canaan.

verses.name: Exodus 16:36
verses.text: (And an omer <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a tenth of an ephah.)  <chapter eID="Exod.16"/>

verses.name: Exodus 17:1
