verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv318"/><title type="x-s">Water from a Rock</title> <div sID="gen490" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv318"/>And all the community of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> set out from the desert of Sin for their journeys according to the command of Yahweh, and they camped in Rephidim, and there was no water for the people to drink.

verses.name: Exodus 17:2
verses.text: And the people quarreled with Moses, and they said, “Give us water so that we can drink.” And Moses said to them, “Why do you quarrel with me? Why do you test Yahweh?”

verses.name: Exodus 17:3
verses.text: And the people thirsted for water, and the people grumbled against Moses and said, “Why <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞ever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Or “at all”; literally “this”</note> did you bring us up from Egypt to kill me<note placement="foot">The unexpected switch to first-person singular pronouns reflects the fact that the question summarizes a host of angry accusations and self-centered concern</note> and my sons and my cattle with thirst?”  <div eID="gen490" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 17:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv319"/><div sID="gen491" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv319"/>And Moses cried out to Yahweh, saying, “What will I do with this people? A little longer and they will stone me.”

verses.name: Exodus 17:5
verses.text: And Yahweh said to Moses, “Go on before the people and take with you <transChange type="added">some</transChange> from the elders of Israel, and the staff with which you struck the Nile take in your hand, and go.

verses.name: Exodus 17:6
verses.text: Look, I <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> standing before you there on the rock in Horeb, and you will strike the rock, and water will come out from it, and the people will drink.” <div eID="gen491" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen492" type="x-p"/> And Moses did so before the eyes of the elders of Israel.

verses.name: Exodus 17:7
verses.text: And he called the name of the place Massah and Meribah because of the quarrel of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> and because of their testing Yahweh <transChange type="added">by</transChange> saying, “Is Yahweh in our midst or not?”  <div eID="gen492" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 17:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv320"/><title type="x-s">Battle with the Amalekites</title> <div sID="gen493" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv320"/>And Amalek came and fought with Israel at Rephidim.

verses.name: Exodus 17:9
verses.text: And Moses said to Joshua, “Choose men for us, and go out, fight against Amalek tomorrow. I <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> standing on the top of the hill, and the staff of God <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> in my hand.”  <div eID="gen493" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 17:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv321"/><div sID="gen494" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv321"/>And Joshua did as Moses had said to him to fight with Amalek. And Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the top of the hill.

verses.name: Exodus 17:11
verses.text: And<note placement="foot">Literally “and it would be”</note> when Moses raised his hand, Israel would prevail, but when he rested his hand, Amalek would prevail.

verses.name: Exodus 17:12
verses.text: But the hands of Moses <transChange type="added">were</transChange> heavy, and they took a stone and placed it under him, and he sat on it; Aaron and Hur supported his hands, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞one on each side⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Or “one on one side and one on the other”; literally “one from this and one from this”</note> and his hands were steady until <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞sundown⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the coming in of the sun”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 17:13
verses.text: And Joshua defeated Amalek and his people with <transChange type="added">the</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞edge of the sword⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “mouth of the sword”</note>  <div eID="gen494" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 17:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv322"/><div sID="gen495" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv322"/>And Yahweh said to Moses, “Write this <transChange type="added">as</transChange> a memorial in the scroll and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞recite it in the hearing of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and put in the ears of”</note> Joshua, because I will utterly blot out the remembrance of Amalek from under the heavens.”  <div eID="gen495" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 17:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv323"/><div sID="gen496" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv323"/>And Moses built an altar, and he called its name Yahweh <transChange type="added">Is</transChange> My Banner.

verses.name: Exodus 17:16
verses.text: And he said, “Because a hand <transChange type="added">was</transChange> against the throne of Yah,<note placement="foot">Or “indeed a hand on the throne of Yah”; the phrase is unclear</note> a war <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> for Yahweh with Amalek from generation <transChange type="added">to</transChange> generation.”  <chapter eID="Exod.17"/>

verses.name: Exodus 18:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv324"/><title type="x-s">Jethro’s Visit to Moses at the Mountain of God</title> <div sID="gen497" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv324"/>And Jethro, the priest of Midian, the father-in-law of Moses, heard all that God had done for Moses and for Israel, his people, that Yahweh had brought Israel out from Egypt.

verses.name: Exodus 18:2
verses.text: And Jethro, the father-in-law of Moses, took Zipporah the wife of Moses after her sending away,

verses.name: Exodus 18:3
verses.text: and her two sons—the one whose name <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Gershom, for he had said, “I have been an alien in a foreign land,”

verses.name: Exodus 18:4
verses.text: and the one <transChange type="added">whose</transChange> name <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Eliezer, for “the God of my father <transChange type="added">was</transChange> my help, and he delivered me from the sword of Pharaoh.”

verses.name: Exodus 18:5
verses.text: And Jethro, the father-in-law of Moses, came and his sons and his wife to Moses, to the desert where he was camping there <transChange type="added">at</transChange> the mountain of God.

verses.name: Exodus 18:6
verses.text: And he said to Moses, “I, your father-in-law Jethro, <transChange type="added">am</transChange> coming to you and your wife and her two sons with her.”

verses.name: Exodus 18:7
verses.text: And Moses went out to meet his father-in-law, and he bowed, and he kissed him, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they each asked about the other’s welfare⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “they asked a man to his neighbor to welfare”</note> and they came into the tent.  <div eID="gen497" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 18:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv325"/><div sID="gen498" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv325"/>And Moses told his father-in-law all that Yahweh had done to Pharaoh and to Egypt on account of Israel, all the hardship that had found them on the way, and <transChange type="added">how</transChange> Yahweh delivered them.

verses.name: Exodus 18:9
verses.text: And Jethro rejoiced over all the good that Yahweh had done for Israel when he delivered them from the hand of Egypt.

verses.name: Exodus 18:10
verses.text: And Jethro said, “Blessed be Yahweh, who has delivered you from the hand of Egypt and from the hand of Pharaoh—who has delivered the people from under the hand of Egypt.

verses.name: Exodus 18:11
verses.text: Now I know that Yahweh is greater than all the gods, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞even in the matter where they the Egyptians dealt arrogantly against the Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “because in the thing that they dealt arrogantly over them”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 18:12
verses.text: And Jethro, the father-in-law of Moses, took a burnt offering and sacrifices for God, and Aaron and all the elders of Israel came to eat bread with the father-in-law of Moses before God.  <div eID="gen498" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 18:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv326"/><div sID="gen499" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv326"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it was”</note> the next day, Moses sat to judge the people, and the people stood before Moses from the morning until the evening.

verses.name: Exodus 18:14
verses.text: And the father-in-law of Moses saw all that he was doing for the people, and he said, “What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> this thing that you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> doing for the people? Why <transChange type="added">are</transChange> you sitting alone and all the people <transChange type="added">are</transChange> standing by you from morning until evening?”

verses.name: Exodus 18:15
verses.text: And Moses said to his father-in-law, “Because the people come to me to seek God.

verses.name: Exodus 18:16
verses.text: When <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they have an issue⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “a thing is to them”</note> it comes to me, and I judge between a man and his neighbor, and I make known God’s rule and his instructions.”  <div eID="gen499" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 18:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv327"/><div sID="gen500" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv327"/>And the father-in-law of Moses said to him, “The thing that you are doing is not good.

verses.name: Exodus 18:18
verses.text: Surely you will wear out, both you and this people who <transChange type="added">are</transChange> with you, because the thing <transChange type="added">is too</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞difficult⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “heavy”</note> for you. You are not able to do it alone.

verses.name: Exodus 18:19
verses.text: Now listen to my voice; I will advise you, and may God be with you. You be for the people before God, and you bring the issues to God.

verses.name: Exodus 18:20
verses.text: And you warn them <transChange type="added">of</transChange> the rules and the instructions, and you make known to them the way in which they must walk and the work that they must do.

verses.name: Exodus 18:21
verses.text: And you will select from all the people men of ability, fearers of God, trustworthy men, haters of <transChange type="added">dishonest</transChange> gain,<note placement="foot">Or “unjust profit”</note> and you will appoint <transChange type="added">such men</transChange> over them <transChange type="added">as</transChange> commanders of thousands, commanders of hundreds, commanders of fifties, and commanders of tens.

verses.name: Exodus 18:22
verses.text: And let them judge the people all the time, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞and⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and it will be”</note> every major issue they will bring to you, and every minor issue they will judge themselves. And <transChange type="added">so</transChange> lighten <transChange type="added">it</transChange> for yourself, and they will bear <transChange type="added">it</transChange> with you.

verses.name: Exodus 18:23
verses.text: If you will do this thing and God will command you, <transChange type="added">then</transChange> you will be able to endure, and also each of the people will go to his home<note placement="foot">Or “his place”</note> in peace.”  <div eID="gen500" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 18:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv328"/><div sID="gen501" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv328"/>And Moses listened to the voice of his father-in-law, and he did all that he had said.

verses.name: Exodus 18:25
verses.text: And Moses chose men of ability from all Israel, and he appointed them <transChange type="added">as</transChange> heads over the people, <transChange type="added">as</transChange> commanders of thousands, commanders of hundreds, commanders of fifties, and commanders of tens.

verses.name: Exodus 18:26
verses.text: And they judged the people all the time; the difficult issues<note placement="foot">Hebrew “issue”</note> they would bring to Moses, and every minor issue they would judge themselves.

verses.name: Exodus 18:27
verses.text: And Moses let his father-in-law go, and he went to his land.  <chapter eID="Exod.18"/>

verses.name: Exodus 19:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv329"/><title type="x-s">Preparation for Receiving the Covenant at Mount Sinai</title> <div sID="gen502" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv329"/>In the third month after the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> went out from the land of Egypt, on this day they came to the Sinai desert.

verses.name: Exodus 19:2
verses.text: They set out from Rephidim, and they came to the desert of Sinai, and they camped in the desert, and Israel camped there in front of the mountain.  <div eID="gen502" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 19:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv330"/><div sID="gen503" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv330"/>And Moses went up to God, and Yahweh called to him from the mountain, saying, “Thus you will say to the house of Jacob and you will tell the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 19:4
verses.text: ‘You yourselves have seen what I did to Egypt and <transChange type="added">how</transChange> I bore you on eagles’ wings and I brought you to me.

verses.name: Exodus 19:5
verses.text: And now if you will carefully listen to my voice and keep my covenant, you will be a treasured possession for me out of all the peoples, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞for all the earth is mine⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “because all of the earth is for me”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 19:6
verses.text: but you, you will <transChange type="added">belong</transChange> to me <transChange type="added">as</transChange> a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.’ These are the words that you will speak to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note>  <div eID="gen503" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 19:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv331"/><div sID="gen504" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv331"/>And Moses came and called the elders of the people, and he placed before them all these words that Yahweh had commanded him.

verses.name: Exodus 19:8
verses.text: And all the people together answered and said, “All that Yahweh has spoken we will do.” And Moses brought back the words of the people to Yahweh.

verses.name: Exodus 19:9
verses.text: And Yahweh said to Moses, “Look, I <transChange type="added">am going to</transChange> come to you in <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a thick cloud⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the cloud of the cloud”</note> in order that the people will hear when I speak with you and will also trust in you forever.” And Moses told the words of the people to Yahweh.  <div eID="gen504" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 19:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv332"/><div sID="gen505" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv332"/>And Yahweh said to Moses, “Go to the people and consecrate them today and tomorrow. They must wash their clothes,

verses.name: Exodus 19:11
verses.text: and they must be prepared for the third day, because on the third day, Yahweh will go down on Mount Sinai before the eyes of all the people.

verses.name: Exodus 19:12
verses.text: And you must set limits <transChange type="added">for</transChange> the people all around, saying, ‘Guard yourselves <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞against⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “watch to/for you”</note> going up to the mountain and touching its edge. Anyone touching the mountain will certainly be put to death.

verses.name: Exodus 19:13
verses.text: Not a hand will touch it, because he will certainly be stoned or certainly be shot; whether an animal or a man, he will not live.’ At the blowing of the ram’s horn they may go up to the mountain.”  <div eID="gen505" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 19:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv333"/><div sID="gen506" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv333"/>And Moses went down from the mountain to the people, and he consecrated the people, and they washed their clothes.

verses.name: Exodus 19:15
verses.text: And he said to the people, “Be ready <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞for the third day⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “for third of days”</note> Do not go near to a woman.”  <div eID="gen506" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 19:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv334"/><div sID="gen507" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv334"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and it was”</note> on the third day, when it was morning, there was thunder and lightning, and a heavy cloud over the mountain and a very loud ram’s horn sound, and all the people who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in the camp trembled.

verses.name: Exodus 19:17
verses.text: And Moses brought the people out from the camp to meet God, and they took their stand at the foot of the mountain.

verses.name: Exodus 19:18
verses.text: And Mount Sinai was all wrapped in smoke because Yahweh went down on it in the fire, and its smoke went up like the smoke of a smelting furnace, and the whole mountain trembled greatly.

verses.name: Exodus 19:19
verses.text: And the sound of the ram’s horn became <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞louder and louder⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “was going and strong very” (compare <reference osisRef="2Sam.3.1">2 Sam 3:1</reference>)</note> and Moses would speak, and God would answer him with a voice.  <div eID="gen507" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 19:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv335"/><div sID="gen508" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv335"/>And Yahweh went down on Mount Sinai, to the top of the mountain, and Yahweh called Moses to the top of the mountain, and Moses went up.

verses.name: Exodus 19:21
verses.text: And Yahweh said to Moses, “Go down, warn the people, lest they break through to Yahweh to see and many from them fall.

verses.name: Exodus 19:22
verses.text: And even the priests who come near Yahweh must consecrate themselves, lest Yahweh break out against them.”

verses.name: Exodus 19:23
verses.text: And Moses said to Yahweh, “The people are not able to go up to Mount Sinai, because you yourself warned us, saying, ‘Set limits <transChange type="added">around</transChange> the mountain and consecrate it.’ ”

verses.name: Exodus 19:24
verses.text: And Yahweh said to him, “Go, go down, and come up, you and Aaron with you and the priests, but the people must not break through to go up to Yahweh, lest he break out against them.”

verses.name: Exodus 19:25
verses.text: And Moses went down to the people, and he told them.<note placement="foot">Or “and he said to them”</note>  <chapter eID="Exod.19"/>

verses.name: Exodus 20:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv336"/><title type="x-s">Ten Commandments</title> <div sID="gen509" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv336"/>And God spoke all these words, saying,

verses.name: Exodus 20:2
verses.text: “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> Yahweh, your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt, from the house of slaves.  <div eID="gen509" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 20:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv337"/><div sID="gen510" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv337"/>“There shall be for you no other gods before me.  <div eID="gen510" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 20:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv338"/><div sID="gen511" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv338"/>“You shall not make for yourself a divine image <transChange type="added">with</transChange> any form that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in the heavens above or that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in the earth below or that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in the water below the earth.

verses.name: Exodus 20:5
verses.text: You will not bow down to them, and you will not serve them, because I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> Yahweh your God, a jealous God, punishing <transChange type="added">the</transChange> guilt of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> parents on the children on <transChange type="added">the</transChange> third and on <transChange type="added">the</transChange> fourth <transChange type="added">generations</transChange><note placement="foot">“Generations” is understood from comparison with parallel verses (compare <reference osisRef="Exod.34.6-Exod.34.7">Exod 34:6–7</reference>; <reference osisRef="Deut.7.9">Deut 7:9</reference>)</note> of those hating me,

verses.name: Exodus 20:6
verses.text: and showing loyal love to thousands <transChange type="added">of generations</transChange><note placement="foot">“Generations” is understood from comparison with parallel verses ( compare <reference osisRef="Exod.34.6-Exod.34.7">Exod 34:6–7</reference>; <reference osisRef="Deut.7.9">Deut 7:9</reference>)</note> of those loving me and of those keeping my commandments.  <div eID="gen511" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 20:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv339"/><div sID="gen512" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv339"/>“You shall not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞misuse the name of Yahweh your God⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “take up/bear/carry the name of Yahweh your God for what is worthless/false/empty”</note> because Yahweh will not leave unpunished anyone who <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞misuses his name⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “bears his name for what is false”</note>  <div eID="gen512" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 20:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv340"/><div sID="gen513" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv340"/>“Remember the day of the Sabbath, to consecrate it.

verses.name: Exodus 20:9
verses.text: Six days you will work, and you will do all your work.

verses.name: Exodus 20:10
verses.text: But the seventh day <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a Sabbath for Yahweh your God; you will not do any work—you or your son or your daughter, your male slave or your female slave, or your animal, or your alien who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in your gates—

verses.name: Exodus 20:11
verses.text: because <transChange type="added">in</transChange> six days Yahweh made the heavens and the earth, the sea and all that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in them, and on the seventh day he rested. Therefore Yahweh blessed the seventh day and consecrated it.  <div eID="gen513" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 20:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv341"/><div sID="gen514" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv341"/>“Honor your father and your mother, so that your days can be long on the land that Yahweh your God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> giving you.  <div eID="gen514" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 20:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv342"/><div sID="gen515" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv342"/>“You shall not murder.  <div eID="gen515" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 20:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv343"/><div sID="gen516" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv343"/>“You shall not commit adultery.  <div eID="gen516" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 20:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv344"/><div sID="gen517" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv344"/>“You shall not steal.  <div eID="gen517" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 20:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv345"/><div sID="gen518" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv345"/>“You shall not testify against your neighbor <transChange type="added">with</transChange> a false witness.  <div eID="gen518" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 20:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv346"/><div sID="gen519" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv346"/>“You shall not covet the house of your neighbor; you will not covet the wife of your neighbor or his male servant or his female servant or his ox or his donkey or anything that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> your neighbor’s.”  <div eID="gen519" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 20:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv347"/><div sID="gen520" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv347"/>And all the people <transChange type="added">were</transChange> seeing the thunder and the lightning and the sound of the ram’s horn and the mountain smoking, and the people saw, and they trembled, and they stood at a distance.

verses.name: Exodus 20:19
verses.text: And they said to Moses, “You speak with us, and we will listen, but let not God speak with us, lest we die.”

verses.name: Exodus 20:20
verses.text: And Moses said to the people, “Do not be afraid. God has come to test you so that his fear will be before you so that you do not sin.”

verses.name: Exodus 20:21
verses.text: And the people stood at a distance, and Moses approached the very thick cloud where God was.  <div eID="gen520" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 20:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv348"/><title type="x-s">Instructions for Building Altars</title> <div sID="gen521" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv348"/>And Yahweh said to Moses, “Thus you will say to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> ‘You yourselves have seen that I have spoken to you from the heavens.

verses.name: Exodus 20:23
verses.text: You will not make alongside me gods of silver, and gods of gold you will not make for yourselves.

verses.name: Exodus 20:24
verses.text: An altar of earth you will make for me, and you will sacrifice on it your burnt offerings and your fellowship offerings, your sheep and your cattle. In every place where I cause my name to be remembered,<note placement="foot">Or “proclaimed”</note> I will come to you, and I will bless you.

verses.name: Exodus 20:25
verses.text: And if you make an altar of stones for me, you will not build them <transChange type="added">as</transChange> hewn stone, because if you use your chisel on it, you have defiled it.

verses.name: Exodus 20:26
verses.text: You will not go up with steps onto my altar, that your nakedness not be exposed on it.’  <chapter eID="Exod.20"/>

verses.name: Exodus 21:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv349"/><title type="x-s">Regulations Regarding Hebrew Slaves</title> <div sID="gen522" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv349"/>“And these are the regulations that you will set before them.  <div eID="gen522" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 21:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv350"/><div sID="gen523" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv350"/>‘If you buy a Hebrew slave, he will serve six years, and in the seventh he will go out as free for nothing.<note placement="foot">Or “for no payment”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 21:3
verses.text: If he comes in single, he will go out single. If he is the husband of a wife, his wife will go out with him.

verses.name: Exodus 21:4
verses.text: If his master gives him a wife and she bears for him sons or daughters, the wife and her children will belong to her master, and <transChange type="added">the slave</transChange> will go out single.

verses.name: Exodus 21:5
verses.text: But if the slave explicitly says, “I love my master, my wife, and my children; I will not go out free,”

verses.name: Exodus 21:6
verses.text: his master will present him to God<note placement="foot">Or “present him to the judges”</note> and bring him to the door or to the doorpost, and his master will pierce his ear with an awl, and he will serve him forever.  <div eID="gen523" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 21:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv351"/><div sID="gen524" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv351"/>“ ‘And if a man sells his daughter as a slave woman, she will not go out as male slaves go out.

verses.name: Exodus 21:8
verses.text: If <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞she does not please her master⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “bad in the eyes of her master”</note> who selected her, he will allow her to be redeemed; he has no authority to sell her to foreign people, since he has dealt treacherously with her.

verses.name: Exodus 21:9
verses.text: And if he selects her for his son, he shall do for her according to the regulations for daughters.

verses.name: Exodus 21:10
verses.text: If he takes for himself another, he will not reduce her food, her clothing, or her right of cohabitation.

verses.name: Exodus 21:11
verses.text: And if he does not do for her these three, she shall go out for nothing; there will not be silver<note placement="foot">Or “money”</note> <transChange type="added">paid for her</transChange>.  <div eID="gen524" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 21:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv352"/><title type="x-s">Regulations Regarding Murder, Manslaughter, and Various Injuries</title> <div sID="gen525" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv352"/>“ ‘<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Whoever strikes someone⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “A striker of a man”</note> and he dies will surely be put to death.

verses.name: Exodus 21:13
verses.text: But if he did not lie in wait <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞and it was an accident⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “and God let him happen to his hand”</note> I will appoint for you a place to which he may flee.

verses.name: Exodus 21:14
verses.text: But if a man schemes against his neighbor to kill him by treachery,<note placement="foot">Or “with cunning” or “craftily”</note> you will take him from my altar to die.

verses.name: Exodus 21:15
verses.text: And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞whoever strikes⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a striker of”</note> his father or his mother will surely be put to death.  <div eID="gen525" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 21:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv353"/><div sID="gen526" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv353"/>“ ‘And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞whoever kidnaps someone⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a stealer of a man”</note> and sells him, or he is found in his possession,<note placement="foot">Literally “in his hand”</note> he will surely be put to death.  <div eID="gen526" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 21:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv354"/><div sID="gen527" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv354"/>“ ‘And one who curses his father or his mother will surely be put to death.  <div eID="gen527" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 21:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv355"/><div sID="gen528" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv355"/>“ ‘And if men quarrel and a man strikes his neighbor with a stone or with a fist and he does not die, but <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he is confined to bed⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “he falls to bed”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 21:19
verses.text: if he stands and walks about in the outside on his staff, the striker will be unpunished; he will only pay for his inactivity<note placement="foot">Literally “his sitting”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞toward his full recovery⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “and he indeed will recover”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 21:20
verses.text: And if a man strikes his male slave or his female slave with the rod and he dies under his hand, he will surely be avenged.

verses.name: Exodus 21:21
verses.text: Yet if he survives a day or two days, he will not be avenged, because he is his money.<note placement="foot">Or “property”; literally “his silver”</note>  <div eID="gen528" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 21:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv356"/><div sID="gen529" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv356"/>“ ‘And if men fight and they injure a pregnant woman, and her children go out and there is not serious injury, he will surely be fined as the woman’s husband demands concerning him <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞and as the judges determine⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “and he will give according to judgments” or “judges” or “arbitrators”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 21:23
verses.text: And if there is serious injury, you will give life in place of life,

verses.name: Exodus 21:24
verses.text: eye in place of eye, tooth in place of tooth, hand in place of hand, foot in place of foot,

verses.name: Exodus 21:25
verses.text: burn in place of burn, wound in place of wound, bruise in place of bruise.  <div eID="gen529" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 21:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv357"/><div sID="gen530" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv357"/>“ ‘And if a man strikes the eye of his male slave or the eye of his female slave and destroys it, he shall release him as free in place of his eye.

verses.name: Exodus 21:27
verses.text: And if he causes the tooth of his male slave or the tooth of his female slave to fall out, he will release him as free in place of his tooth.  <div eID="gen530" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 21:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv358"/><div sID="gen531" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv358"/>“ ‘And if an ox gores a man or a woman and he dies, the ox will surely be stoned, and its meat will not be eaten, and the owner of the ox <transChange type="added">is</transChange> innocent.

verses.name: Exodus 21:29
verses.text: But if it was a goring ox <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “yesterday three days ago”</note> and its owner was warned and did not restrain it and it kills a man or a woman, the ox will be stoned, and the owner also will be put to death.

verses.name: Exodus 21:30
verses.text: If a ransom is set on him, he will pay the redemption money for his life according to all that is set on him.

verses.name: Exodus 21:31
verses.text: If it gores a son or it gores a daughter, according to this regulation it shall be done to him.

verses.name: Exodus 21:32
verses.text: If the ox gores a male slave or a female slave, he will give thirty shekels of silver to his master, and the ox will be stoned.  <div eID="gen531" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 21:33
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv359"/><div sID="gen532" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv359"/>“ ‘If a man opens a pit or if a man digs a pit and he does not cover it and an ox or a donkey falls into it,

verses.name: Exodus 21:34
verses.text: the owner of the pit will pay restitution; he will pay silver to its owner, but the dead <transChange type="added">animal</transChange> will be for him.<note placement="foot">Or “will belong to him”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 21:35
verses.text: And if a man’s ox injures the ox of his neighbor and it dies, they will sell the living ox and divide the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞money⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “its silver”</note> and they will also divide the dead <transChange type="added">one</transChange>.

verses.name: Exodus 21:36
verses.text: Or if it was known that it was a goring ox <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “yesterday three days ago”</note> and its owner did not restrain it, he will surely make restitution, an ox in place of the ox, and the dead <transChange type="added">one</transChange> will be for him.  <chapter eID="Exod.21"/>

verses.name: Exodus 22:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv360"/><title type="x-s">Regulations Regarding Theft, Borrowing, and Accidental Damage or Loss</title> <div sID="gen533" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv360"/><note placement="foot"><reference osisRef="Exod.22.1-Exod.22.31">Exodus 22:1–31 </reference>in the English Bible is 21:37–22:30 in the Hebrew Bible</note> “ ‘If a man steals an ox or small livestock and slaughters it or sells it, he will make restitution with five cattle in place of the ox and with four sheep or goats in place of the small livestock.

verses.name: Exodus 22:2
verses.text: “ ‘If a thief is found in the act of breaking in and he is struck and he dies, there is not bloodguilt for him.

verses.name: Exodus 22:3
verses.text: (If the sun has risen over him, <transChange type="added">there is</transChange> bloodguilt for him. He will make full restitution. If <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he does not have enough⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “there is not to him”</note> he will be sold for his theft.

verses.name: Exodus 22:4
verses.text: If indeed the stolen item is found <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in his possession⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in his hand”</note> alive, from ox to donkey to small livestock, he will make double restitution.  <div eID="gen533" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 22:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv361"/><div sID="gen534" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv361"/>“ ‘If a man grazes <transChange type="added">his livestock</transChange> in a field or a vineyard and he releases his livestock and it grazes in the field of another, he will make restitution <transChange type="added">from</transChange> the best of his field and the best of his vineyard.  <div eID="gen534" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 22:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv362"/><div sID="gen535" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv362"/>“ ‘If a fire is started and finds thorn bushes and a stack of sheaves or the standing grain or the field is consumed, the one who started the fire will surely make restitution.  <div eID="gen535" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 22:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv363"/><div sID="gen536" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv363"/>“ ‘If a man gives to his neighbor money or objects to watch over and it is stolen from the house of the man, if the thief is found, he will make double restitution.

verses.name: Exodus 22:8
verses.text: If the thief is not found, the owner of the house will be brought <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to the sanctuary⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to God” or perhaps “to the judges”</note> <transChange type="added">to learn</transChange> whether or not he reached out his hand to his neighbor’s possession.

verses.name: Exodus 22:9
verses.text: Concerning every account of transgression—concerning an ox, concerning a donkey, concerning small livestock, concerning clothing, concerning all lost property—where <transChange type="added">someone</transChange> says, “This belongs to me,” the matter of the two of them will come to God;<note placement="foot">Or “the judges”</note> whomever God declares guilty will make double restitution to his neighbor.  <div eID="gen536" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 22:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv364"/><div sID="gen537" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv364"/>“ ‘If a man gives to his neighbor a donkey or an ox or small livestock or any beast to watch over and it dies or is injured or is captured <transChange type="added">when</transChange> there is no one who sees,

verses.name: Exodus 22:11
verses.text: the oath of Yahweh will be between the two of them <transChange type="added">concerning</transChange> whether or not he has reached out his hand to his neighbor’s possession, and its owner will accept <transChange type="added">this</transChange>, and he will not make restitution.

verses.name: Exodus 22:12
verses.text: But if indeed it was stolen from him, he will make restitution to its owner.

verses.name: Exodus 22:13
verses.text: If indeed it was torn to pieces, he will bring it as evidence—the mangled carcass; he will not make restitution.  <div eID="gen537" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 22:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv365"/><div sID="gen538" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv365"/>“ ‘If a man borrows from his neighbor and it is injured or dies <transChange type="added">while</transChange> its owner is not with it, he will make restitution.

verses.name: Exodus 22:15
verses.text: If its owner <transChange type="added">was</transChange> with it, he will not make restitution; if it was hired, it came with its hiring fee.  <div eID="gen538" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 22:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv366"/><title type="x-s">Regulations Regarding Various Offences</title> <div sID="gen539" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv366"/>“ ‘If a man seduces a virgin who is not engaged and he lies with her, he surely will give her bride price <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to have her as his wife⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “for him for a woman”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 22:17
verses.text: If her father absolutely refuses to give her to him, he will weigh out money according to the bride price for the virgin.  <div eID="gen539" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 22:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv367"/><div sID="gen540" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv367"/>“ ‘You will not let a witch live.  <div eID="gen540" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 22:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv368"/><div sID="gen541" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv368"/>“ ‘Anyone lying with an animal will surely be put to death.  <div eID="gen541" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 22:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv369"/><div sID="gen542" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv369"/>“ ‘Whoever sacrifices to the gods—not to Yahweh, to him alone—will be destroyed.  <div eID="gen542" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 22:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv370"/><title type="x-s">Regulations Regarding Foreigners and the Poor</title> <div sID="gen543" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv370"/>“ ‘You will not mistreat an alien, and you will not oppress him, because you were aliens in the land of Egypt.  <div eID="gen543" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 22:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv371"/><div sID="gen544" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv371"/>“ ‘You will not afflict any widow or orphan.

verses.name: Exodus 22:23
verses.text: If you indeed afflict him, yes, if he cries out at all to me, I will certainly hear his cry of distress.

verses.name: Exodus 22:24
verses.text: And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I will become angry⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “my nose will burn”</note> and I will kill you with the sword, and your wives will be widows and your children orphans.  <div eID="gen544" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 22:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv372"/><div sID="gen545" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv372"/>“ ‘If you lend money <transChange type="added">to</transChange> my people, <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the needy with you, you will not be to him as a creditor; you will not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞charge him interest⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “put on him interest”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 22:26
verses.text: If indeed you require the cloak of your neighbor as a pledge, you will return it to him at sundown,

verses.name: Exodus 22:27
verses.text: because it is his only garment; it is his cloak for his skin. In what will he sleep? <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it will be”</note> when he cries out to me, I will hear, because I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> gracious.  <div eID="gen545" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 22:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv373"/><title type="x-s">Regulations Regarding Tribute and Holiness</title> <div sID="gen546" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv373"/>“ ‘You will not curse God,<note placement="foot">Or “a judge”</note> and you will not curse a leader among your people.  <div eID="gen546" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 22:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv374"/><div sID="gen547" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv374"/>“ ‘You will not delay the fullness of your harvest and the juice from your press; you will give me the firstborn of your sons.

verses.name: Exodus 22:30
verses.text: You will do likewise for your ox and for your sheep and goats; seven days it will be with its mother; on the eighth, you will give it to me.

verses.name: Exodus 22:31
verses.text: And you will be men of holiness for me; and you will not eat meat <transChange type="added">from</transChange> a carcass mangled in the field; you will throw it to the dog.  <chapter eID="Exod.22"/>

verses.name: Exodus 23:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv375"/><title type="x-s">Regulations Regarding Justice</title> <div sID="gen548" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv375"/>“ ‘You will not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞spread⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “lift”</note> a false report. Do not lift your hand with <transChange type="added">the</transChange> wicked to be a malicious witness.

verses.name: Exodus 23:2
verses.text: You will not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞follow⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “be behind”</note> a majority<note placement="foot">Or “many” or “the many”</note> for evil, and you will not testify concerning a legal dispute to turn aside after a majority<note placement="foot">Or “many” or “the many”</note> to pervert <transChange type="added">justice</transChange>.

verses.name: Exodus 23:3
verses.text: You will not be partial to a powerless <transChange type="added">person</transChange><note placement="foot">Or “a poor person”</note> in his legal dispute.  <div eID="gen548" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 23:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv376"/><div sID="gen549" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv376"/>“ ‘If you come upon the ox of your enemy or his donkey going astray, you will certainly bring it back to him.

verses.name: Exodus 23:5
verses.text: If you see the donkey of your enemy lying down under its burden, you will refrain from abandoning him. You will surely arrange<note placement="foot">Or “restore” or “put in order”</note> <transChange type="added">it</transChange> with him.  <div eID="gen549" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 23:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv377"/><div sID="gen550" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv377"/>“ ‘You will not pervert the justice of your poor in his legal dispute.

verses.name: Exodus 23:7
verses.text: You will stay far from a <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞false charge⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “word of deception”</note> and do not kill the innocent and the righteous, because I will not declare the wicked righteous.<note placement="foot">Or “treat as innocent” or “acquit”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 23:8
verses.text: And you will not take a bribe, because the bribe makes <transChange type="added">the</transChange> sighted blind and ruins <transChange type="added">the</transChange> words of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> righteous.

verses.name: Exodus 23:9
verses.text: And you will not oppress an alien; you yourselves know the feelings<note placement="foot">Or “inner self” or “soul”</note> of the alien, because you were aliens in the land of Egypt.  <div eID="gen550" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 23:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv378"/><title type="x-s">Regulations Regarding Work and Festivals</title> <div sID="gen551" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv378"/>“ ‘And six years you will sow your land and gather its yield.

verses.name: Exodus 23:11
verses.text: But the seventh you will let it rest and leave it fallow, and the poor of your people will eat, and their remainder the animals<note placement="foot">Hebrew “animal”</note> of the field will eat. You will do likewise for your vineyard and for your olive trees.  <div eID="gen551" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 23:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv379"/><div sID="gen552" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv379"/>“ ‘Six days you will do your work, but on the seventh day you will stop so that your ox and your donkey will rest and the son of your slave woman and the alien will be refreshed.  <div eID="gen552" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 23:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv380"/><div sID="gen553" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv380"/>“ ‘And you will be attentive to all that I have said to you, and you will not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞profess⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “cause to remember,” “bring to remembrance,” or “mention” in prayer or praise</note> the name of other gods; it will not be heard in your mouth.  <div eID="gen553" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 23:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv381"/><div sID="gen554" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv381"/>“ ‘Three times in the year you will hold a festival for me.

verses.name: Exodus 23:15
verses.text: You will keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread; for seven days you will eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you at <transChange type="added">the</transChange> appointed time, the month of Abib, because in it you came out from Egypt, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞no one will⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “they will not”</note> appear before me empty-handed.

verses.name: Exodus 23:16
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">you will keep</transChange> the Feast of Harvest, <transChange type="added">with</transChange> the firstfruits of your work, what you sow in the field. And <transChange type="added">you will keep</transChange> the Feast of Harvest Gathering when the year goes out, when you gather your work from the field.

verses.name: Exodus 23:17
verses.text: Three times in the year all your men will appear before the Lord Yahweh.  <div eID="gen554" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 23:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv382"/><div sID="gen555" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv382"/>“ ‘You will not sacrifice the blood of my sacrifice together with <transChange type="added">food with</transChange> yeast, and you will not leave the fat of my feast overnight until morning.  <div eID="gen555" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 23:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv383"/><div sID="gen556" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv383"/>“ ‘The best of the firstfruits of your land you will bring to the house of Yahweh your God. <div eID="gen556" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen557" type="x-p"/> “ ‘You will not boil a young goat<note placement="foot">Or “kid”</note> in its mother’s milk.  <div eID="gen557" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 23:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv384"/><title type="x-s">Reasons for Loyal Obedience</title> <div sID="gen558" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv384"/>“ ‘Look, I <transChange type="added">am about to</transChange> send an angel before you to guard you on the way and to bring you to the place that I have prepared.

verses.name: Exodus 23:21
verses.text: Be attentive to him and listen to his voice; do not rebel against him, because he will not forgive your transgression, for my name is in him.

verses.name: Exodus 23:22
verses.text: But if you listen attentively to his voice and do all that I say, I will be an enemy to your enemies and a foe to your foes.

verses.name: Exodus 23:23
verses.text: When my angel goes before you and brings you to the Amorites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Amorite”</note> and the Hittites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Hittite”</note> and the Perizzites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Perizzite”</note> and the Canaanites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Canaanite”</note> and the Hivites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Hivite”</note> and the Jebusites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Jebusite”</note> I will wipe them out.  <div eID="gen558" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 23:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv385"/><div sID="gen559" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv385"/>“ ‘You will not bow to their gods, and you will not serve them, and you will not act according to their actions, because you will utterly demolish them, and you will utterly break their stone pillars.

verses.name: Exodus 23:25
verses.text: And you will serve Yahweh your God, and he will bless your bread and your water, and I will remove sickness from among you.

verses.name: Exodus 23:26
verses.text: There will be no one suffering miscarriage or infertile in your land. I will make full the number of your days.<note placement="foot">Or “give you a full life span”</note>  <div eID="gen559" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 23:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv386"/><div sID="gen560" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv386"/>“ ‘I will release my terror before you, and I will throw into confusion all the people against whom you come, and I will <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞make all your enemies turn their back to you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “give all your enemies to you back”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 23:28
verses.text: And I will send the hornet before you, and it will drive out the Hivites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Hivite”</note> the Canaanites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Canaanite”</note> and the Hittites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Hittite”</note> from before you.

verses.name: Exodus 23:29
verses.text: I will not drive them out from before you in one year, lest the land become a desolation and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the wild animals⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the animal of the field”</note> multiply against you.

verses.name: Exodus 23:30
verses.text: Little by little I will drive them out from before you until you are fruitful and take possession of the land.  <div eID="gen560" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 23:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv387"/><div sID="gen561" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv387"/>“ ‘And I will set your boundary from the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Red Sea⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sea of reed”</note> and up to the sea of the Philistines and from the desert up to the river,<note placement="foot">Or “the Euphrates”</note> because I will give the inhabitants of the land into your hand, and you will drive them out from before you.

verses.name: Exodus 23:32
verses.text: You will not make a covenant with them and with their gods.

verses.name: Exodus 23:33
verses.text: They will not live in your land, lest they cause you to sin against me when you serve their gods, for it will be a snare to you.’ ”  <chapter eID="Exod.23"/>

verses.name: Exodus 24:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv388"/><title type="x-s">Confirming the Covenant</title> <div sID="gen562" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv388"/>And to Moses he said, “Go up to Yahweh—you and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy from the elders of Israel—and you will worship at a distance.

verses.name: Exodus 24:2
verses.text: And Moses <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞alone⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Or “by himself”; literally “to the solitude of him”</note> will come near to Yahweh, and they will not come near, and the people will not go up with him.”  <div eID="gen562" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 24:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv389"/><div sID="gen563" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv389"/>And Moses came, and he told the people all the words of Yahweh and all the regulations. And all the people answered with one voice, and they said, “All the words that Yahweh has spoken we will do.”  <div eID="gen563" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 24:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv390"/><div sID="gen564" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv390"/>And Moses wrote all the words of Yahweh, and he rose early in the morning, and he built an altar at the base of the mountain and <transChange type="added">set up</transChange> twelve memorial stones for the twelve tribes of Israel.

verses.name: Exodus 24:5
verses.text: And he sent young men from the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> and they offered burnt offerings, and they sacrificed sacrifices <transChange type="added">as</transChange> fellowship offerings to Yahweh <transChange type="added">using</transChange> bulls.

verses.name: Exodus 24:6
verses.text: And Moses took half of the blood, and he put <transChange type="added">it</transChange> in bowls, and half of the blood he sprinkled on the altar.

verses.name: Exodus 24:7
verses.text: And he took the scroll of the covenant and read <transChange type="added">it</transChange> in the hearing of the people, and they said, “All that Yahweh has spoken we will do, and we will listen.”<note placement="foot">Or “we will attentively do” or “we will obediently do”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 24:8
verses.text: And Moses took the blood and sprinkled <transChange type="added">it</transChange> on the people, and he said, “Look, the blood of the covenant that Yahweh has made with you in accordance with all these words.”  <div eID="gen564" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 24:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv391"/><div sID="gen565" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv391"/>And Moses and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy from the elders of Israel went up.

verses.name: Exodus 24:10
verses.text: And they saw the God of Israel, and <transChange type="added">what was</transChange> under his feet <transChange type="added">was</transChange> like sapphire tile work and like the very heavens for clearness.

verses.name: Exodus 24:11
verses.text: And toward the leaders of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> he did not stretch out his hand, and they beheld God, and they ate, and they drank.  <div eID="gen565" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 24:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv392"/><title type="x-s">The Start of Forty Days and Nights on Mount Sinai</title> <div sID="gen566" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv392"/>And Yahweh said to Moses, “Come up to me <transChange type="added">on</transChange> the mountain, and be there, and I will give you the tablets of stone and the law and the commandments that I have written to instruct them.”

verses.name: Exodus 24:13
verses.text: And Moses got up, and Joshua, his assistant, and Moses went up to the mountain of God.  <div eID="gen566" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 24:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv393"/><div sID="gen567" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv393"/>And to the elders he said, “Wait for us here until we return to you. And look, Aaron and Hur are with you. Whoever <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞has a dispute⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “is owner of words”</note> will bring <transChange type="added">it</transChange> to you.”  <div eID="gen567" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 24:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv394"/><div sID="gen568" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv394"/>And Moses went up to the mountain, and the cloud covered the mountain.

verses.name: Exodus 24:16
verses.text: And the glory of Yahweh settled on Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it <transChange type="added">for</transChange> six days, and he called to Moses on the seventh day from the midst of the cloud.

verses.name: Exodus 24:17
verses.text: And the appearance of the glory of Yahweh <transChange type="added">was</transChange> like a consuming fire on the top of the mountain to the eyes of<note placement="foot">Or “in the sight of”</note> the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 24:18
verses.text: And Moses went into the midst of the cloud, and he went up the mountain, and Moses was on the mountain forty days and forty nights.  <chapter eID="Exod.24"/>

verses.name: Exodus 25:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv395"/><title type="x-s">Instruction to Collect Materials</title> <div sID="gen569" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv395"/>And Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.name: Exodus 25:2
verses.text: “Speak to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> and let them bring to me a contribution. You will receive my contribution from every man whose heart prompts him.

verses.name: Exodus 25:3
verses.text: And this is the contribution that you will receive from them—gold and silver and bronze,

verses.name: Exodus 25:4
verses.text: blue, purple, and crimson <transChange type="added">yarns</transChange>, and fine linen and goat hair,

verses.name: Exodus 25:5
verses.text: and red-dyed ram skins, and fine leather,<note placement="foot">The particular kind of leather is uncertain</note> and acacia wood,

verses.name: Exodus 25:6
verses.text: oil for the lamp, balsam oils for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense,

verses.name: Exodus 25:7
verses.text: onyx stones and stones for mountings on the ephod and the breast piece.

verses.name: Exodus 25:8
verses.text: And make a sanctuary for me, and I will dwell in the midst of them,

verses.name: Exodus 25:9
verses.text: according to all that I show you—the pattern of the tabernacle and the pattern of all its equipment—and so you will do.  <div eID="gen569" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 25:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv396"/><title type="x-s">Instructions for Making the Ark of the Covenant</title> <div sID="gen570" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv396"/>“And they will make an ark of acacia wood, two and a half cubits its length and a cubit and a half its width and a cubit and a half its height.

verses.name: Exodus 25:11
verses.text: And you will overlay it with pure gold, inside and outside you will overlay it, and you will make on it a gold molding all around.

verses.name: Exodus 25:12
verses.text: And you will cast for it four gold rings, and you will put <transChange type="added">them</transChange> on its four feet, with two rings on its one side and two rings on its second side.

verses.name: Exodus 25:13
verses.text: And you will make poles of acacia wood, and you will overlay them <transChange type="added">with</transChange> gold.

verses.name: Exodus 25:14
verses.text: And you will put the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark to carry the ark with them.

verses.name: Exodus 25:15
verses.text: In the rings of the ark will be the poles; they will not be removed from it.<note placement="foot">Literally “they will not turn aside from it”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 25:16
verses.text: And you will put into the ark the testimony that I will give to you.  <div eID="gen570" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 25:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv397"/><div sID="gen571" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv397"/>“And you will make an atonement cover of pure gold, two and a half cubits its length and a cubit and a half its width.

verses.name: Exodus 25:18
verses.text: And you will make two cherubim of gold; you will make them of hammered work at the two ends of the atonement cover.

verses.name: Exodus 25:19
verses.text: And make one cherub <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞at one end⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from end from this”</note> and one cherub <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞at the other end⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from end from this”</note> of the atonement cover; you will make the cherubim on its two ends.

verses.name: Exodus 25:20
verses.text: And the cherubim will be <transChange type="added">with</transChange> outspread wings above, covering with their wings over the atonement cover <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞and facing each other⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “and their faces a man to his brother”</note> the faces of the cherubim will be toward the atonement cover.

verses.name: Exodus 25:21
verses.text: And you will put the atonement cover above onto the ark, and into the ark you will put the testimony that I will give you.

verses.name: Exodus 25:22
verses.text: And I will meet you there, and I will speak with you from over the atonement cover, from between the two cherubim that <transChange type="added">are to be</transChange> on the ark of the testimony—all that I will command you to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note>  <div eID="gen571" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 25:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv398"/><title type="x-s">Instructions for Making a Table and a Lampstand</title> <div sID="gen572" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv398"/>“And you will make a table of acacia wood, two cubits its length and a cubit its width and a cubit and a half its height.

verses.name: Exodus 25:24
verses.text: And you will overlay it <transChange type="added">with</transChange> pure gold, and you will make for it a gold molding all around.

verses.name: Exodus 25:25
verses.text: And you will make for it a handbreadth rim all around, and you will make a gold molding for its rim all around.

verses.name: Exodus 25:26
verses.text: And you will make four gold rings for it, and you will put the rings on the four corners where its four <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞legs⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “feet”</note> <transChange type="added">are</transChange>.

verses.name: Exodus 25:27
verses.text: The rings will be near the rim as <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞holders⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “houses”</note> for poles to carry the table.

verses.name: Exodus 25:28
verses.text: And you will make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them <transChange type="added">with</transChange> gold, and the table will be carried with them.

verses.name: Exodus 25:29
verses.text: And you will make its plates and its ladles<note placement="foot">Or “bowls”</note> and its pitchers and its bowls with which <transChange type="added">libations</transChange> will be poured; of pure gold you will make them.

verses.name: Exodus 25:30
verses.text: And you will put on the table <transChange type="added">the</transChange> bread of presence <transChange type="added">to be</transChange> before me continually.  <div eID="gen572" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 25:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv399"/><div sID="gen573" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv399"/>“And you will make a lampstand of pure gold; the lampstand will be made of hammered work—its base and its branch,<note placement="foot">Or “reed”</note> its cups, its buds, and its blossoms will be from it.

verses.name: Exodus 25:32
verses.text: And six branches <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> going out from its sides, three branches of the lampstand from its one side and three branches of the lampstand from its second side.

verses.name: Exodus 25:33
verses.text: Three almond-flower cups <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> on the one branch <transChange type="added">with</transChange> a bud and a blossom, and three almond-flower cups <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> on the one branch <transChange type="added">with</transChange> a bud and a blossom—likewise for the six branches going out from the lampstand.

verses.name: Exodus 25:34
verses.text: And on the lampstand <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> four almond-flower cups, <transChange type="added">with</transChange> its buds and its blossoms.

verses.name: Exodus 25:35
verses.text: And a bud <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> under the two branches <transChange type="added">that come</transChange> from it, and a bud under the two branches from it, and a bud under the two branches from it, <transChange type="added">likewise</transChange> for the six branches coming out from the lampstand.

verses.name: Exodus 25:36
verses.text: Their buds and their branches will be from it, all of it one <transChange type="added">piece</transChange> of pure gold hammered work.

verses.name: Exodus 25:37
verses.text: And you will make its seven lamps, and its lamps will be set up, and it will give light <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in the space in front of it⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “on beyond its face”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 25:38
verses.text: And its snuffers and its fire pans <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> pure gold.

verses.name: Exodus 25:39
verses.text: It will be made <transChange type="added">from</transChange> a talent of pure gold, with all these <transChange type="added">pieces of</transChange> equipment.

verses.name: Exodus 25:40
verses.text: And see and make <transChange type="added">all</transChange> according to their pattern, which you were shown in the mountain.  <chapter eID="Exod.25"/>

verses.name: Exodus 26:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv400"/><title type="x-s">Instructions for Making the Tabernacle</title> <div sID="gen574" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv400"/>“And the tabernacle you will make <transChange type="added">with</transChange> ten curtains; you will make them of finely twisted linen and blue and purple and crimson <transChange type="added">yarns</transChange>, <transChange type="added">with</transChange> cherubim, the work of a skilled craftsman.

verses.name: Exodus 26:2
verses.text: The length of the one curtain <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> twenty-eight cubits, and the width <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> four cubits <transChange type="added">for</transChange> the one curtain; one measure <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> for all the curtains.

verses.name: Exodus 26:3
verses.text: Five curtains will be joined <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to one another⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “a woman to her sister”</note> and five curtains joined <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to one another⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “a woman to her sister”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 26:4
verses.text: And you will make loops of blue on the edge of the one curtain, at the end in the set; and you will do so on the edge of the end curtain in the second set.

verses.name: Exodus 26:5
verses.text: You will make fifty loops on the one curtain, and you will make fifty loops on the end of the curtain that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in the second set; the loops are to be opposite<note placement="foot">Or “interlinked” or “matching”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to one another⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “a woman to her sister”</note>

verses.name: Exodus 26:6
verses.text: And you will make fifty gold clasps and join the curtains <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to one another⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a woman to her sister”</note> with the clasps, so that the tabernacle will be one.  <div eID="gen574" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 26:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv401"/><div sID="gen575" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv401"/>“And you will make curtains of goat hair for a tent over the tabernacle; you will make them eleven curtains.

verses.name: Exodus 26:8
verses.text: The length of the one curtain <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> thirty cubits, and the width <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> four cubits <transChange type="added">for</transChange> the one curtain; one measure <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> for <transChange type="added">the</transChange> eleven curtains.

verses.name: Exodus 26:9
verses.text: And you will join five curtains together and six curtains together, and you will fold double the sixth curtain at the front of the tent.

verses.name: Exodus 26:10
verses.text: And you will make fifty loops on the edge of the one curtain at the end of the <transChange type="added">first</transChange> set and fifty loops on the edge of the curtain <transChange type="added">in</transChange> the second set.

verses.name: Exodus 26:11
verses.text: And you will make fifty bronze clasps, and you will put the clasps in the loops and join the tent, so that it will be one.  <div eID="gen575" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 26:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv402"/><div sID="gen576" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv402"/>“And the surplus in the curtains of the tent <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> an overhang; the surplus half curtain will hang over the back of the tabernacle.

verses.name: Exodus 26:13
