verses.text: and he said to Aaron, “Take for yourself <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a bull calf⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a bull-calf a son of cattle” or “a bull-calf a son of the herd”</note> as a sin offering and a ram as a burnt offering, without defect,<note placement="foot">An adjective in masculine plural to modify both animals; see NET</note> and present them <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the faces of”</note> Yahweh.

verses.name: Leviticus 9:3
verses.text: Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> you<note placement="foot">Singular</note> must speak to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> saying, ‘Take <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a he-goat⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a he-goat of goats”</note> as a sin offering and a bull calf and a male sheep, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞yearlings⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons of a year”</note> without defect,<note placement="foot">An adjective in masculine plural to modify both animals; see NET</note> as a burnt offering,

verses.name: Leviticus 9:4
verses.text: and an ox and a ram as fellowship offerings to sacrifice <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the faces of”</note> Yahweh, and a grain offering mixed with oil, because today Yahweh will appear to you.”<note placement="foot">Plural</note>

verses.name: Leviticus 9:5
verses.text: So<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> they took what Moses had commanded to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞front of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the faces of”</note> the tent of assembly, and the whole community presented themselves, and they stood <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the faces of”</note> Yahweh.  <div eID="gen732" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Leviticus 9:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv557"/><div sID="gen733" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv557"/>Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> Moses said, “This is the word that Yahweh commanded you<note placement="foot">Plural</note> to do <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞so that⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> the glory of Yahweh might appear to you.”<note placement="foot">Plural</note>

verses.name: Leviticus 9:7
verses.text: Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> Moses said to Aaron, “Approach<note placement="foot">Or “Draw near unto”</note> the altar and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞sacrifice⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “do” or “make”</note> your sin offering and your burnt offering, and make atonement for yourself and for the people. And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞sacrifice⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “do” or “make”</note> the people’s offering and make atonement for them, <transChange type="added">just</transChange> as Yahweh has commanded.”  <div eID="gen733" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Leviticus 9:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv558"/><div sID="gen734" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv558"/>Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> Aaron approached<note placement="foot">Or “drew near unto”</note> the altar, and he slaughtered the bull calf of the sin offering, which was for himself.

verses.name: Leviticus 9:9
verses.text: Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> Aaron’s sons presented the blood to him, and he dipped his finger in the blood, and he put <transChange type="added">it</transChange> on the altar’s horns, and he poured out the blood on the altar’s base.

verses.name: Leviticus 9:10
verses.text: And the fat and the kidneys and the lobe <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from the sin offering’s liver⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from the liver from the sin offering”</note> he turned into smoke on the altar, <transChange type="added">just</transChange> as Yahweh had commanded Moses,

verses.name: Leviticus 9:11
verses.text: but<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> the meat and the skin he burned <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞with fire⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in the fire”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞outside the camp⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “from an outside place to/of the camp”</note>  <div eID="gen734" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Leviticus 9:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv559"/><div sID="gen735" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv559"/>Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> he slaughtered the burnt offering, and Aaron’s sons brought the blood to him, and he sprinkled it on the altar all around;

verses.name: Leviticus 9:13
verses.text: and they brought the burnt offering to him by its pieces, as well as<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> the head, and he turned <transChange type="added">them</transChange> into smoke on the altar;

verses.name: Leviticus 9:14
verses.text: and he washed the inner parts<note placement="foot">Or “entrails”</note> and the lower leg bones, then<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> he turned <transChange type="added">them</transChange> into smoke upon the burnt offering on the altar.  <div eID="gen735" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Leviticus 9:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv560"/><div sID="gen736" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv560"/>Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> he presented the people’s offering, and he took the goat of the sin offering, which was for the people, and he slaughtered it and offered<note placement="foot">Or “he offered”</note> it <transChange type="added">as</transChange> a sin offering like the first one.

verses.name: Leviticus 9:16
verses.text: Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> he presented the burnt offering, and he <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞sacrificed⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “did” or “made”</note> it according to the regulation.

verses.name: Leviticus 9:17
verses.text: Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> he presented the grain offering, and he filled his palm <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞with some of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from”</note> it, and he turned it into smoke on the altar besides the morning’s burnt offering.

verses.name: Leviticus 9:18
verses.text: Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> he slaughtered the ox and the ram, the fellowship offerings that <transChange type="added">are</transChange> for the people, and Aaron’s sons brought the blood to him, and he sprinkled it on the altar all around.

verses.name: Leviticus 9:19
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">as for</transChange> the fat portions from the ox and from the ram (the fat tail and the layer of fat and the kidneys and the lobe of the liver),

verses.name: Leviticus 9:20
verses.text: they placed the fat portions on the breast sections, and he turned the fat portions into smoke on the altar.

verses.name: Leviticus 9:21
verses.text: Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> Aaron waved the breast sections and the right upper thigh as a wave offering <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the faces of”</note> Yahweh, <transChange type="added">just</transChange> as Moses had commanded.  <div eID="gen736" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Leviticus 9:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv561"/><div sID="gen737" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv561"/>Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> Aaron lifted his hand toward<note placement="foot">Or “to”</note> the people, and he blessed them, and he came down <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞after⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞sacrificing⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “doing” or “making”</note> the sin offering and the burnt offering and the fellowship offerings.

verses.name: Leviticus 9:23
verses.text: Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> Moses and Aaron entered the tent of assembly. When<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> they came out, they blessed<note placement="foot">Or “and they blessed”</note> the people, and Yahweh’s glory appeared to all the people.

verses.name: Leviticus 9:24
verses.text: Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> a fire went out <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from to the faces of”</note> Yahweh, and it consumed the burnt offering and the fat portions on the altar. And all the people saw it, so<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> they shouted <transChange type="added">for joy</transChange>, and they fell on their faces.  <chapter eID="Lev.9"/>

verses.name: Leviticus 10:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv562"/><title type="x-s">The Deaths of Nadab and Abihu</title> <div sID="gen738" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv562"/>And Aaron’s sons Nadab and Abihu each took his censer, and they put fire in them and placed incense on it;<note placement="foot">That is, the fire</note> then<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> they presented <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the faces of”</note> Yahweh illegitimate fire, which he had not commanded them.

verses.name: Leviticus 10:2
verses.text: So<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> fire went out <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from to the faces of”</note> Yahweh, and it consumed them so that<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> they died <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the faces of”</note> Yahweh.

verses.name: Leviticus 10:3
verses.text: Therefore<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> Moses said to Aaron, “This is what Yahweh spoke, saying, ‘Among those who are close to me I will show myself holy, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in the presence of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “upon the faces of”</note> all the people I will display my glory.’ ”<note placement="foot">Or “I will be glorified”</note> So<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> Aaron was silent.  <div eID="gen738" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Leviticus 10:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv563"/><div sID="gen739" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv563"/>Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> Moses summoned Mishael and Elzaphan the sons of Uzziel, Aaron’s uncle, and he said to them, “Come forward.<note placement="foot">Or “Come near” or “Approach”</note> Carry your brothers from <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the front of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the faces of”</note> the sanctuary to <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞outside the camp⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “from an outside place of the camp”</note>

verses.name: Leviticus 10:5
verses.text: So<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> they came forward,<note placement="foot">Or “came near” or “approached”</note> and they carried them <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞outside the camp⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to from an outside place of the camp”</note> in their tunics, just as Moses had ordered.  <div eID="gen739" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Leviticus 10:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv564"/><div sID="gen740" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv564"/>Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> Moses said to Aaron and to his sons Eleazar and Ithamar, “You must not let your hair hang loosely, and you must not tear your garments, so that<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> you will not die and he<note placement="foot">That is, God</note> will be angry with all the community. But<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> your brothers, all the house of Israel, may weep because of <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the burning that Yahweh caused⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the burning that Yahweh burned”</note>

verses.name: Leviticus 10:7
verses.text: but<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> you must not go out from the entrance to<note placement="foot">Or “of”</note> the tent of assembly lest you die, because Yahweh’s anointing oil is on you.” So<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> they did according to Moses’ word.  <div eID="gen740" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Leviticus 10:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv565"/><title type="x-s">Lasting Statutes</title> <div sID="gen741" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv565"/>Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> Yahweh spoke to Aaron, saying,

verses.name: Leviticus 10:9
verses.text: “You and your sons with you may not drink wine or<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> strong drink when you come to the tent of assembly, so that<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> you will not die—it is a lasting statute for your<note placement="foot">Plural</note> generations—

verses.name: Leviticus 10:10
verses.text: and to distinguish between the holy and the unholy,<note placement="foot">Or “the common”</note> as well as<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> between the unclean and the clean,

verses.name: Leviticus 10:11
verses.text: and to teach the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> all the rules that Yahweh has spoken to them <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞through⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by the hand of”</note> Moses.”  <div eID="gen741" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Leviticus 10:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv566"/><div sID="gen742" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv566"/>Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> Moses spoke to Aaron and to his sons Eleazar and Ithamar, “As for the remaining parts,<note placement="foot">Implied by plural form of noun and the immediate context</note> take the remainder of the grain offering from Yahweh’s offerings made by fire and eat it, the unleavened bread, beside the altar, because it is <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a most holy thing⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “a holiness of holinesses”</note>

verses.name: Leviticus 10:13
verses.text: And you shall eat it in a holy place, because it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> your allotted portion and the allotted portion of your sons from Yahweh’s offerings made by fire, for so I have been commanded.

verses.name: Leviticus 10:14
verses.text: And the wave offering’s breast section and the upper thigh of the contribution <transChange type="added">offering</transChange> you<note placement="foot">Plural</note> must eat in a clean place, you and your sons and your daughters with you, because they are given as your allotted portion and your sons’ allotted portion from the sacrifices of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>’<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> fellowship offerings.

verses.name: Leviticus 10:15
verses.text: They must bring the thigh of the contribution <transChange type="added">offering</transChange> and the breast section of the wave offering in addition to the offerings made by fire, <transChange type="added">consisting</transChange> of the fat portions, to wave as a wave offering <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the faces of”</note> Yahweh; and it will be for you and for your sons with you as a lasting rule, <transChange type="added">just</transChange> as Yahweh had commanded.”  <div eID="gen742" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Leviticus 10:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv567"/><title type="x-s">The Problem of the Uneaten Sin Offering</title> <div sID="gen743" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv567"/>Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> Moses sought all over for the goat of the sin offering and behold, it was burned up. So<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> he was angry with Aaron’s remaining sons Eleazar and Ithamar, saying,

verses.name: Leviticus 10:17
verses.text: “Why did you not eat the sin offering on the sanctuary’s site, because it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a most holy thing⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?<note placement="foot">Literally “a holiness of holinesses”</note> And he gave it to you to remove the community’s guilt, to make atonement for them <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the faces of”</note> Yahweh.

verses.name: Leviticus 10:18
verses.text: Look, its blood was not brought <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞inside the sanctuary⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Or “to the sanctuary inside” or “to the sanctuary within”</note> Certainly you should have eaten it in the sanctuary, as I commanded.”  <div eID="gen743" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Leviticus 10:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv568"/><div sID="gen744" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv568"/>So<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> Aaron said to Moses, “Look, today they presented their sin offering and their burnt offering <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the faces of”</note> Yahweh, and <transChange type="added">things</transChange> such as these have happened to me, and <transChange type="added">if</transChange> I were to eat a sin offering today, would it have been good in Yahweh’s eyes?”

verses.name: Leviticus 10:20
verses.text: When<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> Moses heard, it<note placement="foot">Or “and it”</note> was good in his eyes.  <chapter eID="Lev.10"/>

verses.name: Leviticus 11:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv569"/><title type="x-s">Clean and Unclean Animals</title> <div sID="gen745" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv569"/>Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> Yahweh spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying to them,

verses.name: Leviticus 11:2
verses.text: “Speak to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> saying, ‘These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the animals that you may eat from all the animals that <transChange type="added">are</transChange> on the land:

verses.name: Leviticus 11:3
verses.text: Any among the animals that has a divided hoof and has a split cleft in<note placement="foot">Hebrew “of”</note> the hoof, such<note placement="foot">Hebrew “her/it”</note> you may eat.

verses.name: Leviticus 11:4
verses.text: However,<note placement="foot">Or “Only”</note> these<note placement="foot">By context; Hebrew “this”</note> you may not eat from those that chew the cud and from those that have a<note placement="foot">Hebrew “the”</note> divided hoof: the camel, because it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a chewer of cud but it does not have a hoof that is divided—it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> unclean for you;

verses.name: Leviticus 11:5
verses.text: and the coney, because it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a chewer of cud but it does not have a hoof that is divided—it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> unclean for you;

verses.name: Leviticus 11:6
verses.text: and the hare, because it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a chewer of cud but it does not have a hoof that is divided—it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> unclean for you;

verses.name: Leviticus 11:7
verses.text: and the pig, because it has a divided hoof and has a split cleft in<note placement="foot">Hebrew “of”</note> the hoof but it does not chew cud—it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> unclean for you.

verses.name: Leviticus 11:8
verses.text: You must not eat from their meat, and you must not touch their dead body—they are unclean for you.  <div eID="gen745" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Leviticus 11:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv570"/><div sID="gen746" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv570"/>“ ‘These<note placement="foot">By context; Hebrew “This”</note> you may eat from all that are in the water: any in the water that has a fin and scales, whether in the seas or<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> in the streams—such<note placement="foot">Hebrew “them”</note> you may eat.

verses.name: Leviticus 11:10
verses.text: But any that does not have a fin and scales, <transChange type="added">whether</transChange> in the seas or<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> in the streams, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞among⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from”</note> all the water’s swarmers among all the living creatures that <transChange type="added">are</transChange> in the water—they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> a detestable thing to you.

verses.name: Leviticus 11:11
verses.text: And they shall be detestable to you; you must not eat from their meat, and you must detest their dead body.

verses.name: Leviticus 11:12
verses.text: Any that does not have a fin and scales in the water—it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a detestable thing to you.  <div eID="gen746" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Leviticus 11:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv571"/><div sID="gen747" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv571"/>“ ‘And these you must detest from the birds; they must not be eaten—they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> detestable: the eagle and the vulture and the short-toed eagle,

verses.name: Leviticus 11:14
verses.text: and the red kite and the black kite according to its kind,

verses.name: Leviticus 11:15
verses.text: every crow according to its kind,

verses.name: Leviticus 11:16
verses.text: and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the ostrich⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the daughter of the ostrich”</note> and the short-eared owl and the seagull and the hawk according to its kind,

verses.name: Leviticus 11:17
verses.text: and the little owl and the cormorant and the great owl,

verses.name: Leviticus 11:18
verses.text: and the barn owl and the desert owl and the carrion vulture,

verses.name: Leviticus 11:19
verses.text: and the stork, the heron according to its kind and the hoopoe and the bat.  <div eID="gen747" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Leviticus 11:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv572"/><div sID="gen748" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv572"/>“ ‘Any <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞winged insect⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “swarmer of the wing”</note> that walks on <transChange type="added">all</transChange> fours <transChange type="added">is</transChange> detestable to you.

verses.name: Leviticus 11:21
verses.text: Only this may you eat from any of <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the winged insects⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the swarmer of the wing”</note> that walk on <transChange type="added">all</transChange> fours—<transChange type="added">that</transChange> which has jointed legs above its feet for leaping upon the land.

verses.name: Leviticus 11:22
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞From these⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “These from them”</note> you may eat the locust according to its kind and the bald locust according to its kind and the cricket according to its kind and the grasshopper according to its kind.

verses.name: Leviticus 11:23
verses.text: But<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> any other<note placement="foot">Implied by context</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞winged insect⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “swarmer of wing”</note> that has four legs <transChange type="added">is</transChange> detestable to you.

verses.name: Leviticus 11:24
verses.text: And by these you shall become unclean—anyone who touches their dead body shall become unclean until the evening,

verses.name: Leviticus 11:25
verses.text: and anyone who carries their dead body must wash his garments, and he shall be unclean until the evening.  <div eID="gen748" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Leviticus 11:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv573"/><div sID="gen749" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv573"/>“ ‘<transChange type="added">With regard</transChange> to any animal that has a divided hoof but does not split the hoof, or<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> does not have a cud for chewing<note placement="foot">So HALOT 830 s.v. <reference osisRef="Lev.11.4">4</reference></note>—they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> unclean for you; anyone who touches them shall become unclean.

verses.name: Leviticus 11:27
verses.text: And anything that walks upon its paws among any of the animals<note placement="foot">Collective singular = plural by context</note> that walks on <transChange type="added">all</transChange> fours—they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> unclean for you; anyone who touches their dead body shall become unclean until the evening,

verses.name: Leviticus 11:28
verses.text: and the one who carries their dead body must wash his garments, and he shall be unclean until the evening—they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> unclean for you.  <div eID="gen749" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Leviticus 11:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv574"/><div sID="gen750" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv574"/>“ ‘And these<note placement="foot">By context; Hebrew “this”</note> are the unclean for you among the swarmers<note placement="foot">Collective singular = plural</note> that swarm on the land: the weasel and the mouse and the thorn-tailed lizard according to its kind,

verses.name: Leviticus 11:30
verses.text: and the gecko and the land crocodile and the lizard and the sand lizard and the chameleon.

verses.name: Leviticus 11:31
verses.text: These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the unclean for you among all the swarmers; anyone who touches them at their death shall become unclean until the evening.

verses.name: Leviticus 11:32
verses.text: And anything on which <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞one of them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from them”</note> falls at their death shall become unclean: any object of wood or garment or skin or sackcloth—any object that has performed work—must be placed in water, and it shall be unclean until the evening, and <transChange type="added">then</transChange> it shall be clean.

verses.name: Leviticus 11:33
verses.text: And any clay vessel<note placement="foot">Context indicates a vessel as distinguished from a tool or utensil</note> into which it falls shall become unclean, and you must break it.

verses.name: Leviticus 11:34
verses.text: Any of the food that could be eaten on which water <transChange type="added">from such a vessel</transChange> comes shall become unclean, and any liquid that could be drunk in any <transChange type="added">such</transChange> vessel shall become unclean.

verses.name: Leviticus 11:35
verses.text: And anything on which <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞one of their dead bodies⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from their dead body”</note> falls shall become unclean: an oven or<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> a stove must be broken<note placement="foot">Or “smashed” (NASB, HCSB, NET, NJPS) or “broken in pieces” (ASV, ESV, NRSV)</note>—they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> unclean and shall be unclean for you.

verses.name: Leviticus 11:36
verses.text: Surely<note placement="foot">So HALOT 45</note> a spring or<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> a cistern collecting water shall be clean, but that which touches their dead body shall become unclean.

verses.name: Leviticus 11:37
verses.text: And when <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞one of their dead bodies⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from their dead body”</note> falls on any <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞seed for sowing⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “seed plant that is to be sown”</note> it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> clean.

verses.name: Leviticus 11:38
verses.text: But<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> when water is put on the seed and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞one of their dead bodies⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from their dead body”</note> falls on it, it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> unclean for you.  <div eID="gen750" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Leviticus 11:39
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv575"/><div sID="gen751" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv575"/>“ ‘And when <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞one of the animals⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from the animal”</note> dies that is for you to eat, the one who touches its dead body shall become unclean until the evening.

verses.name: Leviticus 11:40
verses.text: And the one who eats <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞some of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from”</note> its dead body must wash his garments, and he shall be unclean until the evening; and the one who carries its dead body must wash his garments, and he shall be unclean until the evening.  <div eID="gen751" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Leviticus 11:41
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv576"/><div sID="gen752" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv576"/>“ ‘And any swarmer that swarms on the land <transChange type="added">is</transChange> detestable; it must not be eaten.

verses.name: Leviticus 11:42
verses.text: You must not eat<note placement="foot">Hebrew “eat them”</note> anything that moves upon its belly or<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> that walks on <transChange type="added">all</transChange> fours, even any <transChange type="added">with</transChange> numerous feet <transChange type="added">belonging</transChange> to any swarmer that swarms on the land, because they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> detestable.

verses.name: Leviticus 11:43
verses.text: You must not defile yourselves with any swarmer that swarms, and you must not make yourselves unclean by them and <transChange type="added">so</transChange> be made unclean by them,

verses.name: Leviticus 11:44
verses.text: because I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> Yahweh your God, and you must keep yourselves sanctified, so that<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> you shall be holy, because I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> holy. And you must not make yourselves unclean with any swarmer that moves along on the land,

verses.name: Leviticus 11:45
verses.text: because I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> Yahweh, who brought you up from the land of Egypt to be for you as God. Thus<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> you shall be holy, because I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> holy.  <div eID="gen752" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Leviticus 11:46
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv577"/><div sID="gen753" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv577"/>“ ‘This is the regulation of the animals<note placement="foot">Collective singulars in this verse are plural by context</note> and the birds and all living creatures that move along in the water and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞concerning⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “of”</note> all the creatures that swarm on the land,

verses.name: Leviticus 11:47
verses.text: to distinguish between the unclean and the clean and between the animal that is to be eaten and the animal that must not be eaten.’ ”  <chapter eID="Lev.11"/>

verses.name: Leviticus 12:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv578"/><title type="x-s">Purification After Childbirth</title> <div sID="gen754" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv578"/>Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.name: Leviticus 12:2
verses.text: “Speak to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> saying, ‘When a woman becomes pregnant and she gives birth to a male,<note placement="foot">Or “son”</note> then<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> she shall be unclean seven days—as <transChange type="added">in</transChange> the time of her menstrual bleeding, she shall become unclean.

verses.name: Leviticus 12:3
verses.text: And on the eighth day his foreskin’s flesh shall be circumcised.

verses.name: Leviticus 12:4
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">for</transChange> thirty-three days she shall stay in the blood of <transChange type="added">her</transChange> cleansing; she must not touch any holy <transChange type="added">object</transChange>, and she may not come to the sanctuary until the fulfilling of the days of her cleansing.

verses.name: Leviticus 12:5
verses.text: But<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> if she gives birth to a female,<note placement="foot">Or “daughter”</note> then<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> she shall be unclean for two weeks as in her menstruation, and for sixty-six days she shall stay <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞through⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Or “at” or “on”</note> the blood of <transChange type="added">her</transChange> cleansing.

verses.name: Leviticus 12:6
verses.text: And at the fulfilling of the days of her cleansing, <transChange type="added">whether</transChange> for a son or for a daughter, she must bring to the priest at the tent of assembly’s entrance a <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞yearling⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a son of his year”</note> male lamb as a burnt offering and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞young dove⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “son of a dove”</note> or a turtledove as a sin offering.

verses.name: Leviticus 12:7
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">the priest</transChange> shall present it <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the faces of”</note> Yahweh, and he shall make atonement for her, so that<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> she shall be clean from the flow of her blood. This is the regulation of childbearing<note placement="foot">Literally “the childbearing”</note> for the male<note placement="foot">Or “son”</note> or for the female.<note placement="foot">Or “daughter”</note>

verses.name: Leviticus 12:8
verses.text: And if <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞she cannot afford⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “her hand does not find enough”</note> a sheep,<note placement="foot">Or “small livestock”</note> then<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> she shall take two turtledoves or two <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞young doves⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons of a dove”</note>—one as a burnt offering and one as a sin offering—and the priest shall make atonement for her, so that<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> she shall be clean.’ ”  <chapter eID="Lev.12"/>

verses.name: Leviticus 13:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv579"/><title type="x-s">Regulations About Defiling Skin Diseases</title> <div sID="gen755" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv579"/>Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> Yahweh spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,

verses.name: Leviticus 13:2
verses.text: “When a <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞person⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “man”</note> has on his body’s skin a swelling or an epidermal eruption or a spot and it becomes<note placement="foot">Perfect of הָיָה followed by לְ; see HALOT 244 s.v. <reference osisRef="Lev.13.7">7</reference>.c</note> an infectious skin disease on his body’s skin, then<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> he shall be brought to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons the priests.

verses.name: Leviticus 13:3
verses.text: And the priest shall examine the infection on his body’s skin, and <transChange type="added">if</transChange> <transChange type="added">the</transChange> hair in the infection turns white and the appearance of the infection <transChange type="added">is</transChange> deeper than his body’s skin, it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> an infectious skin disease, and the priest shall examine it, and he shall declare him unclean.

verses.name: Leviticus 13:4
verses.text: But<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> if a spot is white on his body’s skin and its appearance is not deeper than the skin and its hair does not turn white, then<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> the priest shall confine the afflicted person <transChange type="added">for</transChange> seven days.

verses.name: Leviticus 13:5
verses.text: And the priest shall examine it on the seventh day, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞if⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “look” or “behold”</note> in his eyes, the infection has stayed unchanged, the infection has not spread on the skin, then<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> the priest shall confine him <transChange type="added">for</transChange> seven days <transChange type="added">a</transChange> second <transChange type="added">time</transChange>.

verses.name: Leviticus 13:6
verses.text: And the priest shall examine him on the seventh day <transChange type="added">for a</transChange> second <transChange type="added">time</transChange>, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞if⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “look” or “behold”</note> the infection has faded and the infection has not spread on the skin, then<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> the priest shall declare him clean—it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> an epidermal eruption; and he shall wash his garments, and so he shall be clean.

verses.name: Leviticus 13:7
verses.text: But<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> if the epidermal eruption spreads further on the skin after showing himself to the priest for his cleansing, then<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> he shall appear <transChange type="added">a</transChange> second <transChange type="added">time</transChange> to the priest.

verses.name: Leviticus 13:8
verses.text: And the priest shall examine <transChange type="added">it</transChange>,<note placement="foot">The direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞if⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “look” or “behold”</note> the epidermal eruption has spread on the skin, then<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> the priest shall declare him unclean—it is an infectious skin disease.  <div eID="gen755" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Leviticus 13:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv580"/><div sID="gen756" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv580"/>“When an infectious skin disease is on a person and he is brought to the priest,

verses.name: Leviticus 13:10
verses.text: the priest shall examine <transChange type="added">it</transChange>,<note placement="foot">The direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞if⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “look” or “behold”</note> a white swelling is on the skin and it turns the hair white and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞raw flesh⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “living of living flesh”</note> <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in the swelling,

verses.name: Leviticus 13:11
verses.text: it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a chronic infectious skin disease on his body’s skin, and the priest shall declare him unclean; he shall not confine him, because he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> unclean.

verses.name: Leviticus 13:12
verses.text: And if the infectious skin disease breaks out all over on the skin and the infectious skin disease covers all of the afflicted person’s skin from his head to his feed, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞so far as the priest can see⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “for all the sight of the eyes of the priest”</note>

verses.name: Leviticus 13:13
verses.text: then<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> the priest shall examine it,<note placement="foot">The direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞if⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “look” or “behold”</note> the infectious skin disease covers his whole body, then<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> he shall pronounce the afflicted person clean—all of it has turned white; he is clean.

verses.name: Leviticus 13:14
verses.text: But<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞whenever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “on a day”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞raw flesh⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “living flesh”</note> appears on him, he shall become unclean.

verses.name: Leviticus 13:15
verses.text: And the priest shall examine the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞raw flesh⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “living flesh”</note> and he shall pronounce him unclean—the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞raw flesh⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “living flesh”</note> <transChange type="added">is</transChange> unclean; it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> an infectious skin disease.

verses.name: Leviticus 13:16
verses.text: Or, when the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞raw flesh⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “living flesh”</note> returns and it has changed to white, then<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> he shall come to the priest,

verses.name: Leviticus 13:17
verses.text: and the priest shall examine him, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞if⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “look” or “behold”</note> the infection has changed to white, then<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> the priest shall pronounce the afflicted person clean—he is clean.  <div eID="gen756" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Leviticus 13:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv581"/><div sID="gen757" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv581"/>“And when <transChange type="added">someone’s</transChange> body <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞has⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “becomes on it”</note> a skin sore on his skin and it is healed

verses.name: Leviticus 13:19
verses.text: and a white swelling or a <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞pinkish⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “white red”</note> spot appears in the skin sore’s place, then<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> he shall show himself to the priest.

verses.name: Leviticus 13:20
verses.text: And the priest shall examine <transChange type="added">it</transChange>,<note placement="foot">The direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞if⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “look” or “behold”</note> its appearance is deeper than the skin and its hair has changed to white, then<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> the priest shall declare him unclean—it is an infectious skin disease; it has broken out in the skin sore.

verses.name: Leviticus 13:21
verses.text: And if the priest examines it and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞if⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “look” or “behold”</note> there is no white hair in it and it is not deeper than the skin and it is faded, then<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> the priest shall confine him <transChange type="added">for</transChange> seven days.

verses.name: Leviticus 13:22
verses.text: But<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> if it has spread further on the skin, then<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> the priest shall declare him unclean—it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> an infection.

verses.name: Leviticus 13:23
verses.text: But<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> if the spot has stayed unchanged, it has not spread, it is the skin sore’s scar, so<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> the priest shall declare him clean.  <div eID="gen757" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Leviticus 13:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv582"/><div sID="gen758" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv582"/>“Or when a body <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞has⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “it becomes”</note> a burn-spot <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “of”</note> fire on its skin and the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞raw flesh⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “living”</note> of the burn-spot is <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞pinkish⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “white red”</note> or white,

verses.name: Leviticus 13:25
verses.text: then<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> the priest shall examine it, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞if⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “look” or “behold”</note> the hair turns white in the spot and its appearance is deeper than the skin, it is an infectious skin disease—it has broken out in the burn-spot; so<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> the priest shall declare him unclean—it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> an infectious skin disease.

verses.name: Leviticus 13:26
verses.text: But<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> if the priest examines it and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞if⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “look” or “behold”</note> there is not white hair in the spot and it is not deeper than the skin and it is faded, then<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> the priest shall confine him <transChange type="added">for</transChange> seven days.

verses.name: Leviticus 13:27
verses.text: And the priest shall examine him on the seventh day; if it has spread further on the skin, then<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> the priest shall declare him unclean—it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> an infectious skin disease.

verses.name: Leviticus 13:28
verses.text: But<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> if it the spot has stayed unchanged in its place, it has not spread on the skin and it is faded, then it is the burn-spot’s swelling, so<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> the priest shall declare him clean, because it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the burn-spot’s scar.  <div eID="gen758" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Leviticus 13:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv583"/><div sID="gen759" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv583"/>“And when a man or a woman <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞has⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “becomes on him”</note> an infection on <transChange type="added">the</transChange> head or in <transChange type="added">the</transChange> beard,

verses.name: Leviticus 13:30
verses.text: then<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> the priest shall examine the infection, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞if⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “look” or “behold”</note> its appearance is deeper than the skin and in it is thin bright red hair, then<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> the priest shall declare it unclean—it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a diseased area of skin; it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> an infectious skin disease of the head or the beard.

verses.name: Leviticus 13:31
verses.text: But<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> if the priest examines the diseased area of the skin’s infection and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞if⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “look” or “behold”</note> its appearance is not deeper than the skin and there is no black hair in it, then<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> the priest shall confine the afflicted person <transChange type="added">with</transChange> the diseased area of skin <transChange type="added">for</transChange> seven days.

verses.name: Leviticus 13:32
verses.text: And the priest shall examine the infection on the seventh day, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞if⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “look” or “behold”</note> the diseased area of skin has not spread and it does not have bright red hair in it and the diseased area of the skin’s appearance is not deeper than the skin,

verses.name: Leviticus 13:33
verses.text: then<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> he shall shave himself, but<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> he shall not shave the diseased area of skin, and the priest shall confine the person with<note placement="foot">The direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> the diseased area of skin <transChange type="added">a</transChange> second <transChange type="added">time</transChange> <transChange type="added">for</transChange> seven days.

verses.name: Leviticus 13:34
verses.text: And the priest shall examine the diseased area of skin on the seventh day, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞if⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “look” or “behold”</note> the diseased area has not spread on the skin and its appearance is not deeper than the skin, then<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> the priest shall pronounce him clean, and he shall wash his garments, and he shall be clean.

verses.name: Leviticus 13:35
verses.text: But<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> if the diseased area of skin has not spread further on the skin after his cleansing,

verses.name: Leviticus 13:36
verses.text: then<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> the priest shall examine him, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞if⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “look” or “behold”</note> the diseased area of skin has spread on the skin, the priest shall not inspect for bright<note placement="foot">Hebrew “the bright”</note> red hair—he is unclean.

verses.name: Leviticus 13:37
verses.text: But<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> if, in his eyes, the diseased area of skin has stayed <transChange type="added">unchanged</transChange> and black hair has grown in it, the diseased area of skin is healed—he is clean, and the priest shall pronounce him clean.  <div eID="gen759" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Leviticus 13:38
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv584"/><div sID="gen760" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv584"/>“And when a man or a woman <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞has⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “becomes”</note> spots on their body’s skin, white spots,

verses.name: Leviticus 13:39
verses.text: then<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> the priest shall examine them,<note placement="foot">The direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞if⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “look” or “behold”</note> <transChange type="added">the</transChange> spots on their body’s skin <transChange type="added">are</transChange> <transChange type="added">a</transChange> faded white, it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a skin rash; it has broken out on the skin—it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> clean.  <div eID="gen760" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Leviticus 13:40
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv585"/><div sID="gen761" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv585"/>“And if a man becomes bald, his head <transChange type="added">is</transChange> bald, he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> clean.

verses.name: Leviticus 13:41
verses.text: And if he becomes bald <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from his forehead⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “from the forehead of his face”</note> his head <transChange type="added">is</transChange> bald, he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> clean.

verses.name: Leviticus 13:42
verses.text: But<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> if a <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞pinkish⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “white red”</note> infection occurs<note placement="foot">Or “becomes” or “happens”</note> on the bald spot or on the bald forehead, it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> an infectious skin disease that sprouts on his bald spot or on his bald forehead.

verses.name: Leviticus 13:43
verses.text: So<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> the priest shall examine him, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞if⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “look” or “behold”</note> the infection’s swelling is <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞pinkish⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “white red”</note> on his bald spot or on his bald forehead, like the appearance of an infectious skin disease on<note placement="foot">Literally “of”</note> the body,

verses.name: Leviticus 13:44
verses.text: he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a man afflicted with a skin disease—he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> unclean; the priest certainly shall declare him unclean—his infection <transChange type="added">is</transChange> on his head.  <div eID="gen761" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Leviticus 13:45
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv586"/><div sID="gen762" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv586"/>“As for<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> the person who is afflicted with a skin disease, his garments must be torn and his <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞hair⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “head”</note> must <transChange type="added">be allowed to</transChange> hang loosely, and he must cover <transChange type="added">his</transChange> upper lip, and he must call out, ‘Unclean! Unclean!’

verses.name: Leviticus 13:46
verses.text: <transChange type="added">For</transChange> all <transChange type="added">the</transChange> days <transChange type="added">during</transChange> which the infection <transChange type="added">is</transChange> on him, he shall be unclean; he must live alone; his dwelling <transChange type="added">must be</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞outside the camp⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “from an outside place of the camp”</note>  <div eID="gen762" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Leviticus 13:47
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv587"/><title type="x-s">Regulations About Contaminated Fabrics</title> <div sID="gen763" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv587"/>“And when the garment <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞has⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “becomes”</note> an infectious skin disease<note placement="foot">Perhaps better translated “mold” rather than “skin disease”</note> on it, on a wool garment<note placement="foot">Literally “a garment of wool”</note> or on a linen garment,<note placement="foot">Literally “a garment of linen”</note>

verses.name: Leviticus 13:48
verses.text: or on woven material or on a linen fabric, or<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> on wool or on leather or on any work of leather,

verses.name: Leviticus 13:49
verses.text: and <transChange type="added">if</transChange> the infection is yellowish green or reddish on the garment or on the leather or on the woven material or on the fabric or on any leather object,<note placement="foot">Literally “an object of leather”</note> it is an infectious skin disease<note placement="foot">Perhaps better translated “mold” rather than “skin disease”</note> and it shall be shown <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the priest.

verses.name: Leviticus 13:50
verses.text: And the priest shall examine the infection, and he shall confine the infected article <transChange type="added">for</transChange> seven days.

verses.name: Leviticus 13:51
verses.text: And he shall examine the infection on the seventh day; if the infection has spread on the garment or on the woven material or on the fabric or on the leather, for any work for which the leather is used, the infection <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a destructive skin disease<note placement="foot">Perhaps better translated “mold” rather than “skin disease”</note>—it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> unclean.

verses.name: Leviticus 13:52
verses.text: And he shall burn the garment or the woven material or the fabric, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞whether wool or linen⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “in/on the wool or in/on the linen”</note> or any leather object that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞has⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “becomes on/in it”</note> the infection, because it is an infectious skin disease,<note placement="foot">Perhaps better translated “mold” rather than “skin disease”</note> <transChange type="added">which is</transChange> destructive—it must be burned in the fire.  <div eID="gen763" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Leviticus 13:53
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv588"/><div sID="gen764" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv588"/>“But<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> if the priest examines it<note placement="foot">The direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞if⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “look” or “behold”</note> the infection has not spread on the garment or on the woven material or on the fabric or on any leather object,

verses.name: Leviticus 13:54
verses.text: then<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> the priest shall command, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞someone⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “he”</note> shall wash that on which the infection <transChange type="added">is</transChange>, and he shall confine it <transChange type="added">a</transChange> second <transChange type="added">time</transChange> <transChange type="added">for</transChange> seven days.

verses.name: Leviticus 13:55
verses.text: And the priest shall examine <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">The direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> after the infection has been washed off, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞if⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “look” or “behold”</note> the infection has not changed its outward appearance and the infection has not spread, it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> unclean; he must burn it in the fire; it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a fungus on its back or on its front.

verses.name: Leviticus 13:56
verses.text: But<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> if the priest examines it<note placement="foot">The direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞if⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “look” or “behold”</note> the infection is faded after it has been washed off, then<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> he shall tear it from the garment or from the leather or from the woven material or from the fabric.

verses.name: Leviticus 13:57
verses.text: And if it appears again on the garment or on the woven material or on the fabric or on any leather object, it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> spreading; you<note placement="foot">Singular</note> must burn in the fire that which <transChange type="added">has</transChange> the infection in it.

verses.name: Leviticus 13:58
verses.text: And the garment or the woven material or the fabric or any leather object that he might wash and the infection is removed from them then<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> shall be washed <transChange type="added">a</transChange> second <transChange type="added">time</transChange>, and it shall be clean.”  <div eID="gen764" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Leviticus 13:59
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv589"/><div sID="gen765" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv589"/>This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the regulation of the infectious skin disease<note placement="foot">Perhaps better translated “mold” rather than “skin disease”</note> in<note placement="foot">Hebrew “of”</note> the wool garment or the linen or the woven material or the fabric or any leather object to declare it clean or to declare it unclean.  <chapter eID="Lev.13"/>

verses.name: Leviticus 14:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv590"/><title type="x-s">Instructions for Cleansing Infectious Skin Diseases</title> <div sID="gen766" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv590"/>Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.name: Leviticus 14:2
verses.text: “This is the regulation of the person afflicted with a skin disease <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞at the time of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Or “on the day of”</note> his cleansing. And he shall be brought to the priest,

verses.name: Leviticus 14:3
verses.text: and the priest shall go <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞outside the camp⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to from an outside place of the camp”</note> and the priest shall examine him,<note placement="foot">The direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞if⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “look” or “behold”</note> the skin disease’s infection is healed on<note placement="foot">Hebrew “from”</note> the afflicted person,

verses.name: Leviticus 14:4
verses.text: then<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> the priest shall command, and he shall take two living, clean birds and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞cedar wood⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “wood of cedar”</note> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a crimson thread⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “crimson thread of the worm”</note> and hyssop for the one who presents himself for cleansing.

verses.name: Leviticus 14:5
verses.text: Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> the priest shall command someone<note placement="foot">The direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to slaughter one bird over fresh water in a clay vessel.

verses.name: Leviticus 14:6
verses.text: He must take the living bird and the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞cedar wood⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “wood of cedar”</note> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the crimson thread⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the crimson thread of the worm”</note> and the hyssop, and he shall dip them and the living bird in the bird’s blood slaughtered over the fresh water.

verses.name: Leviticus 14:7
verses.text: And he shall spatter <transChange type="added">the blood</transChange><note placement="foot">The direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> seven times on the one who presents himself for cleansing from the infectious skin disease, and he shall declare him clean, and he shall send the living bird <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞into the open field⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “toward the faces of the field”</note>

verses.name: Leviticus 14:8
verses.text: Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> the one who presents himself for cleansing shall wash his garments, and he shall shave off all his hair, and he shall wash himself in the water; thus<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> he shall be clean, and afterward he shall enter the camp, but<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> he shall stay <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞outside his tent⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from an outside place of his tent”</note> <transChange type="added">for</transChange> seven days.

verses.name: Leviticus 14:9
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it shall be”</note> on the seventh day he must shave off all his hair—he must shave his head and his beard and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his eyebrows⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the rims of his eyes”</note> and all the rest<note placement="foot">Implied by context</note> of his hair—and he shall wash his garments, and he shall wash his body in the water; thus<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> he shall be clean.  <div eID="gen766" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Leviticus 14:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv591"/><div sID="gen767" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv591"/>“And on the eighth day he must take two male lambs without defect and one ewe-lamb <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in its first year⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a daughter of her year”</note> without defect and three-tenths of an ephah<note placement="foot">Implied by context</note> of finely milled flour mixed with oil <transChange type="added">as</transChange> a grain offering and one log of oil.

verses.name: Leviticus 14:11
verses.text: And the priest who cleanses <transChange type="added">him</transChange><note placement="foot">The direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> shall present the man who presents himself for cleansing and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞these things⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “with them”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the faces of”</note> the tent of assembly’s entrance.

verses.name: Leviticus 14:12
verses.text: Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> the priest shall take the one male lamb, and he shall present it as a guilt offering, and the log of oil, and he shall wave them as a wave offering <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the faces of”</note> Yahweh.

verses.name: Leviticus 14:13
verses.text: And he shall slaughter the male lamb in the place where he slaughters the sin offering and the burnt offering in the sanctuary’s space,<note placement="foot">Or “place” or “area”</note> because as the sin offering belongs to the priest, so also the guilt offering—<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞it is a most holy thing⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “a holiness of holinesses is it”</note>

verses.name: Leviticus 14:14
verses.text: And the priest shall take <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞some of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from”</note> the guilt offering’s blood, and the priest shall put it<note placement="foot">The direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> on the right ear’s lobe of the one who presents himself for cleansing and on his right hand’s thumb and on his right foot’s big toe.

verses.name: Leviticus 14:15
verses.text: And the priest shall take <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞some of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from”</note> the log of oil, and he shall pour it<note placement="foot">The direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> on his<note placement="foot">Hebrew “the priest’s”</note> left palm;

verses.name: Leviticus 14:16
verses.text: and the priest shall dip his right finger in the oil that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> on his left palm, and he shall spatter <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞some of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from”</note> the oil with his finger seven times <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the faces of”</note> Yahweh.

verses.name: Leviticus 14:17
verses.text: Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> the priest shall put <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞some of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from”</note> the remaining oil, which is on his palm, on the right ear’s lobe of the one to be cleansed and on his right hand’s thumb and on his right foot’s big toe, on top of the guilt offering’s blood.<note placement="foot">See v. <reference osisRef="Lev.14.14">14</reference></note>

verses.name: Leviticus 14:18
verses.text: And the remaining oil that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> on the priest’s palm he shall put on the head of the one who presents himself for cleansing, and the priest shall make atonement for him <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the faces of”</note> Yahweh.

verses.name: Leviticus 14:19
verses.text: Thus<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> the priest shall <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞sacrifice⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “do” or “make”</note> the sin offering, and he shall make atonement for the one who presents himself for cleansing from his uncleanness, and afterward he shall slaughter the burnt offering.

verses.name: Leviticus 14:20
verses.text: Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> the priest shall offer the burnt offering and the grain offering on the altar, and the priest shall make atonement for him, and so he shall be clean.  <div eID="gen767" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Leviticus 14:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv592"/><div sID="gen768" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv592"/>“But<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> if he is poor and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he cannot afford⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “his hand is not producing”</note> it,<note placement="foot">The direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> then<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> he shall take one male lamb for a guilt offering as a wave offering to make atonement for himself and one-tenth of an ephah<note placement="foot">Implied by context</note> of finely milled flour mixed with oil for a grain offering, and a log of oil,

verses.name: Leviticus 14:22
verses.text: and two turtledoves or two <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞young doves⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons of dove”</note> that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he can afford⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “his hand can produce”</note> and one shall be a sin offering and the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞other⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “one”</note> a burnt offering.

verses.name: Leviticus 14:23
verses.text: And he shall bring them to the priest at the tent of assembly’s entrance <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the faces of”</note> Yahweh on the eighth day for his cleansing.

verses.name: Leviticus 14:24
verses.text: And the priest shall take the male lamb <transChange type="added">for</transChange> the guilt offering and the log of oil, and the priest shall wave them <transChange type="added">as</transChange> a wave offering <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the faces of”</note> Yahweh;

verses.name: Leviticus 14:25
verses.text: and he shall slaughter the male lamb of the guilt offering, and the priest shall take <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞some of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from”</note> the guilt offering’s blood, and he shall put it<note placement="foot">The direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> on the right ear’s lobe of the one who presents himself for cleansing and on his right hand’s thumb and on his right foot’s big toe.

verses.name: Leviticus 14:26
verses.text: Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> the priest shall pour out <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞some of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from”</note> the oil on his own<note placement="foot">Hebrew “the priest’s”</note> left palm,

verses.name: Leviticus 14:27
verses.text: and with his right finger the priest shall spatter <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞some of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from”</note> the oil that is on his left palm seven times <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the faces of”</note> Yahweh.

verses.name: Leviticus 14:28
verses.text: Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> the priest shall put <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞some of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from”</note> the oil that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> on his palm on the right ear’s lobe of the one who presents himself for cleansing and on his right hand’s thumb and on his right foot’s big toe on the place of the guilt offering’s blood.

verses.name: Leviticus 14:29
verses.text: And the remaining oil that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> on the priest’s palm he shall put on the head of the one who presents himself for cleansing to make atonement for him <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the faces of”</note> Yahweh.

verses.name: Leviticus 14:30
verses.text: And he shall <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞sacrifice⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “do” or “make”</note> one of the turtledoves or the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞young doves⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons of dove”</note> that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he can afford⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “his hand can produce”</note>

verses.name: Leviticus 14:31
verses.text: <transChange type="added">even</transChange><note placement="foot">Implied by context</note> what <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he can afford⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “his hand can produce”</note> the one as a sin offering and the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞other⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “one”</note> as a burnt offering in addition to the grain offering, and the priest shall make atonement for the one who presents himself for cleansing <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the faces of”</note> Yahweh.

verses.name: Leviticus 14:32
verses.text: This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the regulation of <transChange type="added">the one</transChange> on whom <transChange type="added">is</transChange> an infectious skin disease who <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞cannot afford⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “his hand cannot produce”</note> the cost<note placement="foot">The direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> for his cleansing.”  <div eID="gen768" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Leviticus 14:33
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv593"/><title type="x-s">Instructions for Cleansing Houses</title> <div sID="gen769" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv593"/>Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> Yahweh spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,

verses.name: Leviticus 14:34
verses.text: “When you come into the land of Canaan, which I <transChange type="added">am about to</transChange> give to you <transChange type="added">as your</transChange> possession, and I put <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞mildew⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “an infection of skin disease”</note> in a house <transChange type="added">in</transChange> the land of your possession,

verses.name: Leviticus 14:35
