verses.text: As to their price of redemption, from <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a one-month-old⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a son of a month”</note> you will redeem them according to your proper value, five shekels of silver according to the shekel of the sanctuary, which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> twenty gerah.

verses.name: Numbers 18:17
verses.text: Only the firstborn of an ox or the firstborn of a sheep or the firstborn of a goat you will not redeem; they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> holy. Their blood you will sprinkle over the altar, and their fat you will turn into smoke <transChange type="added">as</transChange> an offering made by fire, a fragrance of appeasement for Yahweh.

verses.name: Numbers 18:18
verses.text: But their flesh will be for you like the breast section of the wave offering, and it will be for you like the right upper thigh.

verses.name: Numbers 18:19
verses.text: All the contributions of holiness that the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> offer to Yahweh I have given to you and your sons and your daughters with you as an eternal decree; it is an eternal covenant of salt <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in the presence of”</note> Yahweh to you and your offspring with you.”

verses.name: Numbers 18:20
verses.text: Then Yahweh said to Aaron, “You will not receive an inheritance in their land, and there will not be a plot of ground for you in the midst of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note>  <div eID="gen1059" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 18:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv858"/><div sID="gen1060" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv858"/>“Behold, I have given to the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Levi every tithe in Israel as an inheritance in return for their service, which they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> doing, the work of the tent of assembly.

verses.name: Numbers 18:22
verses.text: The <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> will not come near again to the tent of assembly, or <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they will bear sin⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">The NRSV translates “they will incur guilt”</note> and die.

verses.name: Numbers 18:23
verses.text: The Levites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Levite”</note> will perform the service of the tent of assembly, and they will bear their guilt, an eternal decree for all your generations. But they will not receive an inheritance in the midst of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note>

verses.name: Numbers 18:24
verses.text: because the tithes<note placement="foot">Hebrew “tithe”</note> of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> that are <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞offered⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Hebrew “raised up”</note> to Yahweh as a contribution, I have given to the Levites as an inheritance; therefore I said to them, ‘They will not receive an inheritance in the midst of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.’ ”<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note>  <div eID="gen1060" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 18:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv859"/><div sID="gen1061" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv859"/>Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.name: Numbers 18:26
verses.text: “You will speak to the Levites and say to them, ‘When you receive the tithe from the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> that I have given to you from them for your inheritance, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you will present⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “you will raise up”</note> a contribution from it to Yahweh, a tithe from a tithe.

verses.name: Numbers 18:27
verses.text: Your contribution will be credited to you like the grain from the threshing floor and like the produce from the press.

verses.name: Numbers 18:28
verses.text: So <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you will present⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “you will raise up”</note> your own contribution to Yahweh from all your tithes that you receive from the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> from it you will give the contribution of Yahweh to Aaron the priest.

verses.name: Numbers 18:29
verses.text: From all your gifts <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you will present⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “you will raise up”</note> every contribution of Yahweh, from all its fat, the part <transChange type="added">that is</transChange> sacred.’

verses.name: Numbers 18:30
verses.text: You will say to them, ‘When <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you are presenting⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “you are raising up”</note> its fat, the rest will be credited to the Levites like a yield of the threshing floor and like a yield from the press.

verses.name: Numbers 18:31
verses.text: You may eat it anywhere, you and your household, because it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a wage in return for your service in the tent of assembly.

verses.name: Numbers 18:32
verses.text: You will not bear any sin because <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you have presented⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “you have raised up”</note> its fat; you will not defile the holy objects of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> or you will die.’ ”  <chapter eID="Num.18"/>

verses.name: Numbers 19:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv860"/><title type="x-s">Ashes of the Red Heifer</title> <div sID="gen1062" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv860"/>And Yahweh spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,

verses.name: Numbers 19:2
verses.text: “This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the decree of the law that Yahweh has commanded, saying, ‘Speak to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> and let them take to you a red heifer without a physical defect, on which a yoke <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞has not been placed⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “has not gone up”</note>

verses.name: Numbers 19:3
verses.text: And you will give it to Eleazar the priest, and it will be brought<note placement="foot">Or “he will bring it out”</note> out to a place outside the camp, and it will be slaughtered<note placement="foot">Or “he will slaughter it”</note> in his presence.

verses.name: Numbers 19:4
verses.text: Then Eleazar the priest will take <transChange type="added">some of</transChange> its blood on his finger and spatter it toward the mouth of the tent of assembly seven times.

verses.name: Numbers 19:5
verses.text: The heifer will be burned<note placement="foot">Hebrew “The heifer will burn”</note> in his sight; its skin, its meat, and its blood, in addition to its offal, will burn.

verses.name: Numbers 19:6
verses.text: The priest will take cedar wood, hyssop, and crimson thread, and he will throw them in the midst of <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the burning heifer⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the burning of the heifer”</note>

verses.name: Numbers 19:7
verses.text: The priest will wash his garments and his body in the water, and afterward he will come to the camp; the priest will be unclean until the evening.

verses.name: Numbers 19:8
verses.text: The one who burns it will wash his garments and his body in water; he will be unclean until the evening.

verses.name: Numbers 19:9
verses.text: A clean man will gather the ashes of the heifer, and he will put <transChange type="added">them</transChange> in a clean <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞place outside the camp⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “an outside place of the camp”</note> it will be for the community of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> as a requirement for waters of impurity; it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a purification <transChange type="added">offering</transChange>.

verses.name: Numbers 19:10
verses.text: The one who gathers the ashes of the heifer will wash his garments; he will be unclean until evening. It will be an eternal decree for the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> and for one who dwells as an alien in their midst.  <div eID="gen1062" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 19:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv861"/><div sID="gen1063" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv861"/>“ ‘The one who touches a corpse of <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞any person⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “any human person”</note> will be unclean for seven days.

verses.name: Numbers 19:12
verses.text: He will purify himself on the third day, and on the seventh day he will be clean. If he does not purify himself on the third day, he will not be clean on the seventh day.

verses.name: Numbers 19:13
verses.text: Anyone who touches a corpse, the person of a human being who died, and does not purify himself, defiles the tabernacle of Yahweh, and that person will be cut off from Israel because the waters of impurity were not sprinkled on him. He will still be unclean, and uncleanness <transChange type="added">is</transChange> on him.  <div eID="gen1063" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 19:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv862"/><div sID="gen1064" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv862"/>“ ‘This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the law of a person who dies in a tent: everyone who comes into the tent and all who <transChange type="added">are</transChange> in the tent will be unclean seven days.

verses.name: Numbers 19:15
verses.text: Every container that is opened that does not have a lid cord<note placement="foot">That is, “that does not have a lid tied shut”</note> on it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> unclean.

verses.name: Numbers 19:16
verses.text: Anyone <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in the open field⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “upon the face of a field”</note> who touches <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞one who has been slain⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the dead of sword”</note> or a corpse, or a bone of a person, or a burial site, he will be unclean for seven days.

verses.name: Numbers 19:17
verses.text: For the unclean <transChange type="added">person</transChange> they will take<note placement="foot">Hebrew “he will take”</note> from the powder of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞burnt purification offering⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Or “burning of the sin offering”</note> and they will put<note placement="foot">Hebrew “he will put”</note> running water into a container.

verses.name: Numbers 19:18
verses.text: A clean person will take hyssop and dip <transChange type="added">it</transChange> into the water and sprinkle <transChange type="added">it</transChange> on the tent and on all the objects and persons who were there, and on one who touched the bone, or the one slain, or the dead, or the burial site.

verses.name: Numbers 19:19
verses.text: The clean <transChange type="added">person</transChange> will spatter the unclean on the third day and on the seventh day; and on the seventh day he will purify him, and he will wash his garments; he will bathe in the waters, and in the evening he will be clean.

verses.name: Numbers 19:20
verses.text: But the man who is unclean and does not purify himself, that person will be cut off from the midst of the assembly because he defiled the sanctuary of Yahweh; the water of impurity was not sprinkled on him; he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> unclean.  <div eID="gen1064" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 19:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv863"/><div sID="gen1065" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv863"/>“ ‘It will be an eternal decree for them. The one who spatters the waters of impurity will wash his garments, and the one who touches the waters of impurity will be unclean until the evening.

verses.name: Numbers 19:22
verses.text: Anything that the unclean <transChange type="added">person</transChange> touches will be unclean, and the person who touches <transChange type="added">it</transChange> will be unclean until the evening.’ ”  <chapter eID="Num.19"/>

verses.name: Numbers 20:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv864"/><title type="x-s">Miriam Dies</title> <div sID="gen1066" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv864"/>Then the entire community of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> came <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the desert of Zin on the first month, and the people stayed in Kadesh; Miriam died and was buried there.  <div eID="gen1066" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 20:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv865"/><div sID="gen1067" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv865"/>There was no water for the community, and they were gathered before Moses and Aaron.

verses.name: Numbers 20:3
verses.text: And the people quarreled with Moses and spoke, saying, “If only we died when our brothers were dying <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in the presence of”</note> Yahweh!

verses.name: Numbers 20:4
verses.text: Why have you brought the assembly of Yahweh, us and our livestock, into this desert to die here?

verses.name: Numbers 20:5
verses.text: Why have you brought us from Egypt to bring us to this bad place? It is not a place of seed or figs<note placement="foot">Hebrew “fig”</note> or vines<note placement="foot">Hebrew “vine”</note> or pomegranate trees,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “tree”</note> and there is not water to drink.”

verses.name: Numbers 20:6
verses.text: And Moses and Aaron went from the presence of the assembly to the doorway of the tent of assembly. They fell on their faces, and the glory of Yahweh appeared to them.

verses.name: Numbers 20:7
verses.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.name: Numbers 20:8
verses.text: “Take the staff and summon the community, you and Aaron your brother, and speak to the rock before their eyes, and it will give water. Bring out for them water from the rock, and let the community and their livestock drink.”  <div eID="gen1067" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 20:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv866"/><div sID="gen1068" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv866"/>So Moses took the staff from <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in the presence of”</note> Yahweh just as he command him,

verses.name: Numbers 20:10
verses.text: and Moses and Aaron summoned the assembly to the presence of the rock, and he said to them, “Please listen, you rebels; can we bring out water for you from this rock?”

verses.name: Numbers 20:11
verses.text: Then Moses lifted up his hand and struck the rock with his staff twice. And abundant water went out, and the community and their livestock drank.

verses.name: Numbers 20:12
verses.text: But Yahweh said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you have not trusted in me, to regard me as holy <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in the sight of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Or “before the eyes of”</note> the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> you will not bring this assembly into the land that I have given to them.”

verses.name: Numbers 20:13
verses.text: Those <transChange type="added">were</transChange> the waters of Meribah, where the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> quarreled with Yahweh, and he showed himself holy among them.  <div eID="gen1068" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 20:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv867"/><div sID="gen1069" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv867"/>From Kadesh Moses sent messengers to the king of Edom: “Thus your brother Israel has said, ‘You know all the hardship that has found us;

verses.name: Numbers 20:15
verses.text: our ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> went down to Egypt, and we lived in Egypt <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a long time⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “many days”</note> and the Egyptians mistreated us and our ancestors.<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note>

verses.name: Numbers 20:16
verses.text: Then we cried to Yahweh, and he heard our voice; he sent an angel and brought us out from Egypt. And look, we <transChange type="added">are</transChange> in Kadesh, a city on the edge of your territory.

verses.name: Numbers 20:17
verses.text: Please let us go through your land. We will not go through a field or vineyard, and we will not drink water from a well. We will go along the road of the king; we will not turn aside right or left until we have gone through your territory.’ ”  <div eID="gen1069" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 20:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv868"/><div sID="gen1070" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv868"/>Then Edom said to him, “You will not pass through us<note placement="foot">Hebrew “me”</note> lest <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞we will go out⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Hebrew “I will go out”</note> to meet you with the sword.”

verses.name: Numbers 20:19
verses.text: The <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> said to him, “We will go up on the main road, and if we<note placement="foot">Hebrew “I”</note> and our livestock<note placement="foot">Hebrew “my livestock”</note> drink your water, we will pay for it.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “I will give their worth”</note> It is only a small matter; let us pass through on our feet.”<note placement="foot">Hebrew “I will go through on my feet”</note>

verses.name: Numbers 20:20
verses.text: But he said, “You will not go through.” And Edom went out to meet <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Hebrew “him”</note> with a large army and a strong hand.

verses.name: Numbers 20:21
verses.text: So Edom refused to give Israel passage through his territory, and Israel turned aside from him.  <div eID="gen1070" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 20:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv869"/><title type="x-s">Aaron Dies</title> <div sID="gen1071" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv869"/>And they set out from Kadesh. The <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> the whole community, came <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Mount Hor.

verses.name: Numbers 20:23
verses.text: Yahweh said to Moses and to Aaron on Mount Hor, on the boundary of the land of Edom, saying,

verses.name: Numbers 20:24
verses.text: “Let Aaron be gathered to his people; he will not come into the land that I have given to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> because you rebelled against <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞my word⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “my mouth”</note> at the waters of Meribah.

verses.name: Numbers 20:25
verses.text: Take Aaron and Eleazar his son, and take them up Mount Hor.

verses.name: Numbers 20:26
verses.text: Strip off Aaron’s garments, and put them on Eleazar his son; Aaron will be gathered <transChange type="added">to his people</transChange>, and he will die there.”

verses.name: Numbers 20:27
verses.text: So Moses did just as Yahweh commanded, and they went up to Mount Hor before the eyes of all the community.

verses.name: Numbers 20:28
verses.text: And Moses stripped off Aaron’s garments and put them on Eleazar his son. Aaron died there on the top of the mountain; and Moses and Eleazar went down from the mountain.

verses.name: Numbers 20:29
verses.text: All the community saw that Aaron died; so all the house of Israel wept for Aaron thirty days.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “day”</note>  <chapter eID="Num.20"/>

verses.name: Numbers 21:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv870"/><title type="x-s">Arad Captured</title> <div sID="gen1072" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv870"/>The Canaanite king of Arad, who was dwelling <transChange type="added">in</transChange> the Negev,<note placement="foot">An arid region south of the Judean hills</note> heard that Israel came <transChange type="added">along</transChange> the way of Atharim; he fought against Israel and took some of them captive.

verses.name: Numbers 21:2
verses.text: Israel made a vow to Yahweh, and they said, “If you will surely give this people into our<note placement="foot">Hebrew “my”</note> hand, then we<note placement="foot">Hebrew “I”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞will destroy⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “devote to God”</note> their cities.”

verses.name: Numbers 21:3
verses.text: Yahweh heard the voice of Israel; he gave <transChange type="added">to them</transChange> the Canaanites, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they destroyed them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “they devoted to God”</note> and their cities. They called the name of the place Hormah.  <div eID="gen1072" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 21:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv871"/><div sID="gen1073" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv871"/>They set out from Mount Hor <transChange type="added">by</transChange> the way of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Red Sea⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sea of reed”</note> to go around the land of Edom; but <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the people became impatient⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the life of the people became short”</note> along the way.

verses.name: Numbers 21:5
verses.text: The people spoke against God and against Moses, “Why have you brought us from Egypt to die in the desert? There is no food and no water, and our hearts detest <transChange type="added">this</transChange> miserable food.”  <div eID="gen1073" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 21:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv872"/><title type="x-s">The Bronze Serpent</title> <div sID="gen1074" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv872"/>And Yahweh sent among the people poisonous snakes; they bit the people, and many people from Israel died.

verses.name: Numbers 21:7
verses.text: The people came to Moses and said, “We have sinned because we have spoken against Yahweh and against you. Pray to Yahweh and let him remove the snakes<note placement="foot">Hebrew “snake”</note> from among us.” So Moses prayed for the people.

verses.name: Numbers 21:8
verses.text: And Yahweh said to Moses, “Make for yourself a snake and place it on a pole. When<note placement="foot">Hebrew “And it will happen”</note> anyone is bitten and looks at it, that person will live.”

verses.name: Numbers 21:9
verses.text: So Moses made a snake of bronze, and he placed it on the pole; whenever<note placement="foot">Hebrew “And it will happen”</note> a snake bit someone, and that person looked at the snake of bronze, he lived.  <div eID="gen1074" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 21:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv873"/><div sID="gen1075" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv873"/>The <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> set out and encamped at Oboth.

verses.name: Numbers 21:11
verses.text: They set out from Oboth and encamped at Iye Abarim in the desert, which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in front of Moab <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞toward the sunrise⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “from the east of the sun”</note>

verses.name: Numbers 21:12
verses.text: From there they set out and encamped at the valley of Zered.

verses.name: Numbers 21:13
verses.text: From there they set out and encamped beyond Arnon, which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in the desert that goes out from the boundary of the Amorites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Amorite”</note> because Arnon is the boundary of Moab, between Moab and the Amorites.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Amorite”</note>

verses.name: Numbers 21:14
verses.text: Therefore thus it is said in the scroll of the Wars of Yahweh, <div eID="gen1075" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen1076"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1077"/>“Waheb in Suphah,<l eID="gen1077" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1078"/>and the wadis of Arnon, <l eID="gen1078" level="2"/>

verses.name: Numbers 21:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv874"/><l level="1" sID="gen1079"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv874"/>and the slope of the wadis<l eID="gen1079" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1080"/>that spreads out to the dwelling of Ar<l eID="gen1080" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1081"/>and lies at the boundary of Moab.” <l eID="gen1081" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen1076"/>

verses.name: Numbers 21:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv875"/><div sID="gen1082" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv875"/>From there <transChange type="added">they went</transChange> to Beer, which is the water well where Yahweh spoke to Moses, “Gather the people, that I may give them water.”

verses.name: Numbers 21:17
verses.text: Then Israel sang this song, “Arise, well water! Sing to it!

verses.name: Numbers 21:18
verses.text: Well water that the princes dug, that the leaders of the people dug, with a staff <transChange type="added">and</transChange> with their rods.” And from <transChange type="added">the</transChange> desert <transChange type="added">they continued to</transChange> Mattanah,

verses.name: Numbers 21:19
verses.text: and from Mattanah <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Nahaliel, and from Nahaliel <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Bamoth;

verses.name: Numbers 21:20
verses.text: and from Bamoth to the valley that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in the territory of Moab, <transChange type="added">by</transChange> the top of Pisgah, which overlooks the surface of the wasteland.  <div eID="gen1082" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 21:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv876"/><title type="x-s">Sihon and Og Defeated</title> <div sID="gen1083" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv876"/>Israel sent messengers to Sihon, the king of the Amorites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Amorite”</note> saying,

verses.name: Numbers 21:22
verses.text: “Let us go through your land; we will not turn aside into a field or vineyard; we will not drink well water along the way of the king until we have gone through your territory.”

verses.name: Numbers 21:23
verses.text: But Sihon did not allow Israel to go through his territory. Sihon gathered all his people and went out to meet Israel; he came <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the desert, to Jahaz, and he fought against Israel.

verses.name: Numbers 21:24
verses.text: But Israel struck him with <transChange type="added">the</transChange> edge of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> sword, and they took possession of his land from Arnon to Jabbok, until the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons of Ammon”</note> because the boundary of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons of Ammon”</note> <transChange type="added">was</transChange> strong.

verses.name: Numbers 21:25
verses.text: Israel took all these cities, and Israel inhabited all the cities of the Amorites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Amorite”</note> in Heshbon, and in all its environs.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “her daughters;” other modern versions translate “its villages”</note>

verses.name: Numbers 21:26
verses.text: Because Heshbon <transChange type="added">was</transChange> the city of Sihon king of the Amorites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Amorite”</note> who had fought against the former king of Moab and taken all his land from his hand until Arnon.

verses.name: Numbers 21:27
verses.text: Thus the ones who quote proverbs say, <div eID="gen1083" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen1084"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1085"/>“Come <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Heshbon! Let it be built!<l eID="gen1085" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1086"/>And let the city of Sihon be established. <l eID="gen1086" level="2"/>

verses.name: Numbers 21:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv877"/><l level="1" sID="gen1087"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv877"/>Because fire went out from Heshbon,<l eID="gen1087" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1088"/>a flame from the city of Sihon;<l eID="gen1088" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1089"/>it consumed Ar of Moab,<l eID="gen1089" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1090"/>the lords of the<note placement="foot">Or “the dominant”</note> high places of Arnon. <l eID="gen1090" level="2"/>

verses.name: Numbers 21:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv878"/><l level="1" sID="gen1091"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv878"/>Woe to you, Moab!<l eID="gen1091" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1092"/>You have perished, people of Chemosh.<l eID="gen1092" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1093"/>He has given his sons as fugitives,<l eID="gen1093" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1094"/>and his daughters into captivity,<l eID="gen1094" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1095"/>to the king of the Amorites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Amorite”</note> Sihon. <l eID="gen1095" level="1"/>

verses.name: Numbers 21:30
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv879"/><l level="2" sID="gen1096"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv879"/>We destroyed them;<l eID="gen1096" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1097"/>Heshbon has perished up to Dibon;<l eID="gen1097" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1098"/>we laid waste up to Nophah,<l eID="gen1098" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1099"/>which <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞reaches⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “is up to”</note> Medeba.” <l eID="gen1099" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen1084"/>

verses.name: Numbers 21:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv880"/><div sID="gen1100" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv880"/>Thus Israel lived in the land of the Amorites.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Amorite”</note>

verses.name: Numbers 21:32
verses.text: Moses sent to explore Jaazer; they captured <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞its environs⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Hebrew “her daughters;” other modern versions translate “its villages”</note> and dispossessed the Amorites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Amorite”</note> who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> there.  <div eID="gen1100" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 21:33
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv881"/><div sID="gen1101" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv881"/>Then they turned and went up <transChange type="added">by</transChange> the way of the Bashan, and Og king of the Bashan and all his people went out to meet them for battle <transChange type="added">at</transChange> Edrei.

verses.name: Numbers 21:34
verses.text: And Yahweh said to Moses, “Do not fear him because I will give him and all his people and all his land into your hand. You will do to him just as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Amorite”</note> who was living in Heshbon.”

verses.name: Numbers 21:35
verses.text: And so they destroyed him and his sons, and all his people until they had not spared a survivor; and they took possession of his land.  <chapter eID="Num.21"/>

verses.name: Numbers 22:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv882"/><title type="x-s">Balak and Balaam</title> <div sID="gen1102" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv882"/>The <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> set out, and they encamped on the desert-plateau of Moab, across from Jericho beyond <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Jordan.

verses.name: Numbers 22:2
verses.text: Balak son of Zippor saw all that Israel did to the Amorites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Amorite”</note>

verses.name: Numbers 22:3
verses.text: and Moab was very terrified in the presence of the people because <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Hebrew “he” or “it”</note> were numerous; and Moab dreaded the presence of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note>

verses.name: Numbers 22:4
verses.text: And Moab said to the elders of Midian, “Now the crowd will lick up all around us, like a bull devours the grass of the field.” And Balak son of Zippor <transChange type="added">was</transChange> king of Moab at that time.

verses.name: Numbers 22:5
verses.text: He sent messengers to Balaam son of Beor <transChange type="added">at</transChange> Pethor, which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> by the river,<note placement="foot">That is, the Euphrates</note> in the land of the children of his people, to summon him, saying, “Look! A people went out from Egypt. Look! They cover <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the surface of the land⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “the eye of the land”</note> they <transChange type="added">are about</transChange> to dwell opposite me.

verses.name: Numbers 22:6
verses.text: Now, please go, curse this people for me because they<note placement="foot">Hebrew “he”</note> are stronger than me; perhaps I will be able to strike them<note placement="foot">Hebrew “he”</note> and drive them<note placement="foot">Hebrew “he”</note> out from the land because I know whoever you bless <transChange type="added">is</transChange> blessed, and whoever you cursed is cursed.”  <div eID="gen1102" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 22:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv883"/><div sID="gen1103" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv883"/>So the elders of Moab and the elders of Midian went <transChange type="added">with</transChange> a fee for divination in their hand; they came to Balaam and spoke the words of Balak to him.

verses.name: Numbers 22:8
verses.text: He said to them, “Spend the night here, and I will return, and I will return word to you, just as Yahweh speaks to me.” So the princes of Moab stayed with Balaam.

verses.name: Numbers 22:9
verses.text: And God came to Balaam and said, “Who <transChange type="added">are</transChange> these men with you?”

verses.name: Numbers 22:10
verses.text: And Balaam said to God, “Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, sent <transChange type="added">word</transChange> to me,

verses.name: Numbers 22:11
verses.text: ‘Look! A people went out from Egypt. Look! They cover <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the surface of the land⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the eye of the land”</note> Now, go, curse them<note placement="foot">Hebrew “him”</note> for me. Perhaps I will be able to attack them<note placement="foot">Hebrew “him”</note> and drive them<note placement="foot">Hebrew “him”</note> out.”

verses.name: Numbers 22:12
verses.text: God said to Balaam, “You will not go with them; you will not curse the people, because they<note placement="foot">Hebrew “he”</note> <transChange type="added">are</transChange> blessed.”

verses.name: Numbers 22:13
verses.text: Balaam got up in the morning, and he said to the princes of Balak, “Go to your land, because Yahweh refused to allow me to go with you.”

verses.name: Numbers 22:14
verses.text: The princes of Moab got up and went to Balak, and they said, “Balaam refused to come with us.”  <div eID="gen1103" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 22:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv884"/><div sID="gen1104" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv884"/>Balak again sent many princes, <transChange type="added">who were more</transChange> honored <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞than the former⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “than these”</note>

verses.name: Numbers 22:16
verses.text: They came to Balaam and said to him, “Thus says Balak son of Zippor, ‘Please, let nothing keep you from coming to me

verses.name: Numbers 22:17
verses.text: because I will surely honor you greatly, and all that you say to me I will do. Please, come; curse this people for me.’ ”

verses.name: Numbers 22:18
verses.text: Balaam answered and said to the servants of Balak, “Even though Balak gives to me his house full of silver and gold, I am not able to go beyond <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the command of Yahweh⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the mouth of Yahweh”</note> my God to do a little or a lot.

verses.name: Numbers 22:19
verses.text: And now please, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you also stay here⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “please stay in this”</note> the night, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞let me find out⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “let me know”</note> again what Yahweh will say with me.”

verses.name: Numbers 22:20
verses.text: And God came to Balaam <transChange type="added">at</transChange> night, and he said to him, “If the men have come to call you, get up <transChange type="added">and</transChange> go with them; but only the word that I will speak to you, you will do.”

verses.name: Numbers 22:21
verses.text: So Balaam got up in the morning and saddled his donkey, and he went with the princes of Moab.  <div eID="gen1104" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 22:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv885"/><title type="x-s">Balaam and the Angel</title> <div sID="gen1105" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv885"/>But <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞God became angry⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “God’s nose became hot”</note> because he was going, and the angel of Yahweh stood in the road as an adversary to him; he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> riding on his donkey, and two servants were with him.

verses.name: Numbers 22:23
verses.text: The donkey saw the angel of Yahweh standing in the road with his sword drawn in his hand, and the donkey turned aside from the road and went into the field. And Balaam struck the donkey to turn her back <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the road.

verses.name: Numbers 22:24
verses.text: The angel of Yahweh stood in the narrow path of the vineyards, <transChange type="added">with</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a wall on either side⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “a wall from this and a wall from this”</note>

verses.name: Numbers 22:25
verses.text: When the donkey saw the angel of Yahweh, she pressed herself into the wall, and she pressed the foot of Balaam into the wall, so he struck her again.

verses.name: Numbers 22:26
verses.text: Then the angel of Yahweh went further ahead and stood in a narrow place where there was not a way to turn aside <transChange type="added">to the</transChange> right or left.

verses.name: Numbers 22:27
verses.text: When the donkey saw the angel of Yahweh, she lay down under Balaam, so <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Balaam became angry⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “Balaam’s nose became hot”</note> and he struck the donkey with <transChange type="added">his</transChange> staff.

verses.name: Numbers 22:28
verses.text: Yahweh opened the mouth of the donkey, and she said to Balaam, “What did I do to you that you struck me these three times?”

verses.name: Numbers 22:29
verses.text: Balaam said to the donkey, “Because you made a mockery of me! If only I had a sword in my hand, I would kill you right now!”

verses.name: Numbers 22:30
verses.text: The donkey said to Balaam, “Am I not your donkey on which you have ridden all your life until this day? Have I been in the habit of doing this to you?” He said, “No.”  <div eID="gen1105" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 22:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv886"/><div sID="gen1106" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv886"/>Then Yahweh exposed the eyes of Balaam, and he saw the angel of Yahweh standing in the road with his sword drawn in his hand, and he bowed down and worshiped to his face.

verses.name: Numbers 22:32
verses.text: The angel of Yahweh said to him, “Why have you struck this donkey three times? Look, I have come out as an adversary because your conduct is perverse before me.

verses.name: Numbers 22:33
verses.text: The donkey saw me and turned aside from me these three times. If she had not turned aside from my face, then I would have killed you and kept her alive.”

verses.name: Numbers 22:34
verses.text: Balaam said to the angel of Yahweh, “I have sinned because I did not know that you <transChange type="added">were</transChange> standing to meet me in the road. Now, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞if it is displeasing to you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “if it is evil in your eyes”</note> I will turn back.”

verses.name: Numbers 22:35
verses.text: The angel of Yahweh said to Balaam, “Go with the men, but speak only the word that I will speak to you.” So Balaam went with the princes of Balak.  <div eID="gen1106" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 22:36
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv887"/><div sID="gen1107" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv887"/>When Balak heard that Balaam was coming, he went out to meet him by the city of Moab, which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> on the boundary of Aaron at the end of the territory.

verses.name: Numbers 22:37
verses.text: And Balak said to Balaam, “Did I not urgently send to meet with you? Why did you not come to me? Am I really not able to honor you?”

verses.name: Numbers 22:38
verses.text: Balaam said to Balak, “Look, I came to you now. Am I really able to speak anything at all? I speak the word that God puts in my mouth.”

verses.name: Numbers 22:39
verses.text: Balaam went with Balak, and they came <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Kiriath-Huzoth.

verses.name: Numbers 22:40
verses.text: And Balak sacrificed cattle and sheep, and he sent <transChange type="added">them</transChange> to Balaam and to the princes who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him.

verses.name: Numbers 22:41
verses.text: And it happened, in the morning Balak took Balaam and took him up to Bamoth-Baal, and he saw from there the end of the nation.  <chapter eID="Num.22"/>

verses.name: Numbers 23:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv888"/><title type="x-s">Balaam’s Oracles</title> <div sID="gen1108" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv888"/>Balaam said to Balak, “Build for me this: seven altars. And prepare for me this: seven bulls and seven rams.”

verses.name: Numbers 23:2
verses.text: And Balak did just as Balaam spoke, and Balak offered Balaam a bull and a ram on the altar.

verses.name: Numbers 23:3
verses.text: And Balaam said to Balak, “Station yourself at your burnt offering, and I will go; perhaps Yahweh will come to meet me, and whatever he shows me I will tell to you.” So he went <transChange type="added">to</transChange> a barren height.  <div eID="gen1108" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 23:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv889"/><div sID="gen1109" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv889"/>And God met with Balaam, and he said to him, “I have arranged seven altars, and I have offered a bull and a ram on the altar.”

verses.name: Numbers 23:5
verses.text: Yahweh put a word in the mouth of Balaam and said, “Return to Balak, and you must speak thus.”

verses.name: Numbers 23:6
verses.text: So he returned to him, and behold, he was standing beside his burnt offering, he and all the leaders of Moab.

verses.name: Numbers 23:7
verses.text: And he lifted up his oracle and said, <div eID="gen1109" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen1110"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1111"/>“From Aram Balak lead me,<l eID="gen1111" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1112"/>from the mountains of the east the king of Moab,<l eID="gen1112" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1113"/>‘Go for me, curse Jacob,<l eID="gen1113" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1114"/>and go, denounce Israel.’ <l eID="gen1114" level="2"/>

verses.name: Numbers 23:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv890"/><l level="1" sID="gen1115"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv890"/>How can I curse <transChange type="added">whom</transChange> God has not cursed,<l eID="gen1115" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1116"/>and how can I denounce <transChange type="added">whom</transChange> Yahweh has not denounced? <l eID="gen1116" level="2"/>

verses.name: Numbers 23:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv891"/><l level="1" sID="gen1117"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv891"/>Because from the top of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> rocks I see him,<l eID="gen1117" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1118"/>from hilltops I watch him.<l eID="gen1118" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1119"/>Behold, a people <transChange type="added">who</transChange> dwell alone,<l eID="gen1119" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1120"/>they do not consider themselves among the nations. <l eID="gen1120" level="2"/>

verses.name: Numbers 23:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv892"/><l level="1" sID="gen1121"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv892"/>Who can count the dust of Jacob,<l eID="gen1121" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1122"/>or <transChange type="added">as</transChange> a number the fourth part of Israel?<l eID="gen1122" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1123"/>Let my life die the death of an upright person,<l eID="gen1123" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1124"/>and let my end be like his!” <l eID="gen1124" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen1110"/>

verses.name: Numbers 23:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv893"/><div sID="gen1125" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv893"/>And Balak said to Balaam, “What have you done to me? I took you to curse my enemies, and look, you have surely blessed them!”

verses.name: Numbers 23:12
verses.text: He answered and said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Should I not speak⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Should I not observe to speak”</note> what Yahweh puts in my mouth?”  <div eID="gen1125" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 23:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv894"/><div sID="gen1126" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv894"/>Then Balak said, “Please walk with me to another place where you will see them, <transChange type="added">but</transChange> you will only see part of them and will not see all of them; and curse them for me from there.”

verses.name: Numbers 23:14
verses.text: So he took him to the field of Zophim to the top of Pisgah, and he built seven altars, and he offered a bull and a ram on <transChange type="added">each</transChange> altar.

verses.name: Numbers 23:15
verses.text: Balaam<note placement="foot">Hebrew “He”</note> said to Balak, “Station yourself here at the burnt offering while I myself meet with <transChange type="added">Yahweh</transChange> there.”

verses.name: Numbers 23:16
verses.text: Then Yahweh met with Balaam, and he put a word in his mouth, and he said, “Return to Balak, and you must speak thus.”

verses.name: Numbers 23:17
verses.text: He came to him, and behold, he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> standing at his burnt offering, and the princes of Moab with him. And Balak said to him, “What has Yahweh spoken?”

verses.name: Numbers 23:18
verses.text: Then <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he uttered⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “he lifted up”</note> his oracle, and said, <div eID="gen1126" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen1127"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1128"/>“Stand up, Balak, and hear;<l eID="gen1128" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1129"/>listen to me, son of Zippor! <l eID="gen1129" level="2"/>

verses.name: Numbers 23:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv895"/><l level="1" sID="gen1130"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv895"/>God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not a man, that he should lie,<l eID="gen1130" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1131"/>nor a son of humankind,<l eID="gen1131" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1132"/>that he should change his mind.<l eID="gen1132" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1133"/>Has he said, and will he not do <transChange type="added">it</transChange>?<l eID="gen1133" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1134"/>And has he spoken, and will he not fulfill it? <l eID="gen1134" level="1"/>

verses.name: Numbers 23:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv896"/><l level="2" sID="gen1135"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv896"/>Behold, I have received <transChange type="added">a command</transChange> to bless;<l eID="gen1135" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1136"/>when he has blessed, I cannot cause it to return. <l eID="gen1136" level="1"/>

verses.name: Numbers 23:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv897"/><l level="2" sID="gen1137"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv897"/>He has no regard <transChange type="added">for</transChange> evil in Jacob,<l eID="gen1137" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1138"/>and he does not see trouble in Israel;<l eID="gen1138" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1139"/>Yahweh his God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> with him,<l eID="gen1139" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1140"/>and a shout<note placement="foot">Or “a blast”</note> of a king is among them.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “him”</note> <l eID="gen1140" level="1"/>

verses.name: Numbers 23:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv898"/><l level="2" sID="gen1141"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv898"/>God, who brings them out from Egypt,<l eID="gen1141" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1142"/><transChange type="added">is</transChange> like the strength<note placement="foot">Or “like the horns”</note> of a wild ox for them.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “him”</note> <l eID="gen1142" level="1"/>

verses.name: Numbers 23:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv899"/><l level="2" sID="gen1143"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv899"/>Because <transChange type="added">there is</transChange> no sorcery against Jacob,<l eID="gen1143" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1144"/>and <transChange type="added">there is</transChange> no divination against Israel.<l eID="gen1144" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1145"/>Now<note placement="foot">Or “At the right time”</note> it will be said to Jacob and Israel,<l eID="gen1145" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1146"/>what God has done! <l eID="gen1146" level="2"/>

verses.name: Numbers 23:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv900"/><l level="1" sID="gen1147"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv900"/>Look! <transChange type="added">the</transChange> people will rise like the lion;<l eID="gen1147" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1148"/>he raises himself and will not lie down<l eID="gen1148" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1149"/>until he eats <transChange type="added">the</transChange> prey<l eID="gen1149" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1150"/>and drinks the blood of the slain.” <l eID="gen1150" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen1127"/>

verses.name: Numbers 23:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv901"/><div sID="gen1151" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv901"/>Then Balak said to Balaam, “Do not curse them<note placement="foot">Hebrew “him”</note> at all, nor bless them<note placement="foot">Hebrew “him”</note> at all!”

verses.name: Numbers 23:26
verses.text: But Balaam answered and said to Balak, “Did I not speak to you, saying, ‘Whatever Yahweh speaks I will do’?”  <div eID="gen1151" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 23:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv902"/><div sID="gen1152" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv902"/>Then Balak said to Balaam, “Please, come, I will take you to another place; perhaps <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞it will be acceptable to⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “it will be right in the eyes of”</note> God, and you will curse for me from there.”

verses.name: Numbers 23:28
verses.text: So Balak took Balaam <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the top of Peor, which looks down on the face of the Jeshimon.<note placement="foot">Or “the wasteland”</note>

verses.name: Numbers 23:29
verses.text: And Balaam said to Balak, “Build for me these seven altars, and prepare for me these seven bulls and seven rams.”

verses.name: Numbers 23:30
verses.text: Balak did just as Balaam said, and he offered a bull and a ram on <transChange type="added">each</transChange> altar.  <chapter eID="Num.23"/>

verses.name: Numbers 24:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv903"/><title type="x-s">Balaam Continues to Utter Oracles</title> <div sID="gen1153" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv903"/>And Balaam saw that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞it pleased⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “it was good in the eyes of Yahweh”</note> Yahweh to bless Israel, and he did not go <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as other times⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “as time on time”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to seek out⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to meet”</note> sorcery; instead, he set his face toward the desert.

verses.name: Numbers 24:2
verses.text: Balaam lift up his eyes, and he saw Israel dwelling according to its tribes, and the spirit of God was upon it.<note placement="foot">That is, Israel</note>

verses.name: Numbers 24:3
verses.text: He <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞uttered⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “lifted up”</note> his oracle and said, <div eID="gen1153" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen1154"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1155"/>“The declaration of Balaam son Beor,<l eID="gen1155" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1156"/>the declaration of the man <transChange type="added">whose</transChange> eyes are closed, <l eID="gen1156" level="2"/>

verses.name: Numbers 24:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv904"/><l level="1" sID="gen1157"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv904"/>the declaration of the hearer of God’s words,<note placement="foot">Or “God’s sayings”</note><l eID="gen1157" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1158"/>who sees the revelation of Shaddai,<note placement="foot">Often translated “the Almighty”</note><l eID="gen1158" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1159"/>falling down but <transChange type="added">whose</transChange> eyes are uncovered. <l eID="gen1159" level="1"/>

verses.name: Numbers 24:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv905"/><l level="2" sID="gen1160"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv905"/>How good are your tents, O Jacob,<l eID="gen1160" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1161"/>your dwellings, O Israel! <l eID="gen1161" level="1"/>

verses.name: Numbers 24:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv906"/><l level="2" sID="gen1162"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv906"/>They are spread out like valleys,<l eID="gen1162" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1163"/>like gardens on a river,<l eID="gen1163" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1164"/>like aloes planted by Yahweh,<l eID="gen1164" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1165"/>like cedars at <transChange type="added">the</transChange> waters. <l eID="gen1165" level="1"/>

verses.name: Numbers 24:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv907"/><l level="2" sID="gen1166"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv907"/>He will pour water from his buckets,<l eID="gen1166" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1167"/>and his offspring <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> like many waters;<l eID="gen1167" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1168"/>his king will be higher than Agag,<l eID="gen1168" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1169"/>and his kingdom will be exalted. <l eID="gen1169" level="1"/>

verses.name: Numbers 24:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv908"/><l level="2" sID="gen1170"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv908"/>God, who brings him out from Egypt,<l eID="gen1170" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1171"/><transChange type="added">is</transChange> like the strength<note placement="foot">Or “the horns”</note> of a wild ox for him.<l eID="gen1171" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1172"/>He will devour <transChange type="added">the</transChange> nations <transChange type="added">who are</transChange> his enemies;<l eID="gen1172" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1173"/>he will break their bones;<l eID="gen1173" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1174"/>he will pierce <transChange type="added">them with</transChange> his arrows. <l eID="gen1174" level="2"/>

verses.name: Numbers 24:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv909"/><l level="1" sID="gen1175"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv909"/>He crouches, he lies down like a lion,<l eID="gen1175" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1176"/>and like a lioness, who will rouse him?<l eID="gen1176" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1177"/><transChange type="added">They who</transChange> bless you will be blessed,<l eID="gen1177" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1178"/>and <transChange type="added">they who</transChange> curse you will be cursed.” <l eID="gen1178" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen1154"/>

verses.name: Numbers 24:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv910"/><div sID="gen1179" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv910"/>Then <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Balak became angry with⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the nose of Balak became hot against”</note> Balaam, and he clapped his hands and said to Balaam, “I called you to curse my enemies, but look, you have surely blessed <transChange type="added">them</transChange> these three times.

verses.name: Numbers 24:11
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Flee⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Flee for yourself”</note> to your place now. I said I would richly honor you, but look, Yahweh has withheld honor from you.”

verses.name: Numbers 24:12
verses.text: Balaam said to Balak, “Did I not speak to your messengers whom you sent to me, saying,

verses.name: Numbers 24:13
verses.text: ‘If Balak gave to me the fullness of his house full of silver and gold, I am not able to go beyond <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the command of Yahweh⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the mouth of Yahweh”</note> to do good or evil, from my heart; what Yahweh speaks, I will speak’?<note placement="foot">Hebrew “I will speak it”</note>

verses.name: Numbers 24:14
verses.text: And now, look, I <transChange type="added">am about</transChange> to go to my people; I will advise you what this people will do to your people <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in the following days⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “in the last of the days”</note>  <div eID="gen1179" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 24:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv911"/><div sID="gen1180" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv911"/>And he <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞uttered⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “lifted up”</note> his oracle and said, <div eID="gen1180" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen1181"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1182"/>“The declaration of Balaam son of Beor,<l eID="gen1182" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1183"/>and the declaration of the man whose eye is closed, <l eID="gen1183" level="2"/>

verses.name: Numbers 24:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv912"/><l level="1" sID="gen1184"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv912"/>the declaration of the hearer of God’s words,<note placement="foot">Or “God’s sayings”</note><l eID="gen1184" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1185"/>and the knower of the knowledge of the Most High,<l eID="gen1185" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1186"/>who sees the vision of Shaddai,<note placement="foot">Often translated “the Almighty”</note><l eID="gen1186" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1187"/>who is falling, and <transChange type="added">his</transChange> eyes <transChange type="added">are</transChange> revealed. <l eID="gen1187" level="2"/>

verses.name: Numbers 24:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv913"/><l level="1" sID="gen1188"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv913"/>I see him, but not now;<l eID="gen1188" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1189"/>I behold him, but not near;<l eID="gen1189" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1190"/>a star will go out from Jacob,<l eID="gen1190" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1191"/>and a scepter will rise from Israel;<l eID="gen1191" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1192"/>it will crush the foreheads of Moab<l eID="gen1192" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1193"/>and destroy all the children of Seth. <l eID="gen1193" level="2"/>

verses.name: Numbers 24:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv914"/><l level="1" sID="gen1194"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv914"/>Edom will be a captive;<l eID="gen1194" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1195"/>Seir, its enemies, will be a captive,<l eID="gen1195" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1196"/>and Israel <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> acting <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞courageously⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “with physical strength”</note> <l eID="gen1196" level="1"/>

verses.name: Numbers 24:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv915"/><l level="2" sID="gen1197"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv915"/>Someone<note placement="foot">Hebrew “He”</note> from Jacob will rule<l eID="gen1197" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1198"/>and will destroy a remnant<note placement="foot">Or “survivor”</note> from the city.” <l eID="gen1198" level="1"/>

verses.name: Numbers 24:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv916"/><l level="2" sID="gen1199"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv916"/>And he looked <transChange type="added">at</transChange> Amalek, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞uttered⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “lifted up”</note> his oracle, and said,<l eID="gen1199" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1200"/>“Amalek <transChange type="added">is</transChange> first<note placement="foot">Or “among”</note> of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> nations,<l eID="gen1200" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1201"/>but his future <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> forever ruin.” <l eID="gen1201" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen1181"/>

verses.name: Numbers 24:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv917"/><div sID="gen1202" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv917"/>And he looked <transChange type="added">at</transChange> the Kenites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Kenite”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞uttered⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “lifted up”</note> his oracle, and said, <div eID="gen1202" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen1203"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1204"/>“Steady <transChange type="added">is</transChange> your dwelling place;<l eID="gen1204" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1205"/>in the rock is your nest. <l eID="gen1205" level="2"/>

verses.name: Numbers 24:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv918"/><l level="1" sID="gen1206"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv918"/>Nevertheless, <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Kenite will be burned;<l eID="gen1206" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1207"/>how long will Asshur keep<note placement="foot">Hebrew “take”</note> you captive?” <l eID="gen1207" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen1203"/>

verses.name: Numbers 24:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv919"/><div sID="gen1208" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv919"/>Again he <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞uttered⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “lifted up”</note> his oracle and said, <div eID="gen1208" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen1209"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1210"/>“Woe, who will live when God establishes this?<note placement="foot">Hebrew “it”</note> <l eID="gen1210" level="1"/>

verses.name: Numbers 24:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv920"/><l level="2" sID="gen1211"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv920"/>The ships <transChange type="added">will come</transChange> from the hand of the Kittim,<l eID="gen1211" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1212"/>and they will afflict Asshur and will afflict Eber;<l eID="gen1212" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1213"/>also he <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> forever ruin.” <l eID="gen1213" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen1209"/>

verses.name: Numbers 24:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv921"/><div sID="gen1214" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv921"/>Then Balaam got up and went and returned to his place, and Balak also went on his way.  <chapter eID="Num.24"/>

verses.name: Numbers 25:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv922"/><title type="x-s">The Plague of Israel</title> <div sID="gen1215" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv922"/>When Israel dwelled in Shittim, the people began to prostitute<note placement="foot">Or “have sexual relations”</note> <transChange type="added">themselves</transChange> with the daughters of Moab.

verses.name: Numbers 25:2
verses.text: And they invited the people to the sacrifices of their gods, and the people ate and worshiped their gods.

verses.name: Numbers 25:3
verses.text: So Israel was joined together to Baal Peor, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Yahweh became angry⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the nose of Yahweh became hot”</note> with Israel.

verses.name: Numbers 25:4
verses.text: Yahweh said to Moses, “Take all <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the leaders⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the heads”</note> of the people and kill them before the sun, so the fierce anger of Yahweh will turn from Israel.”

verses.name: Numbers 25:5
verses.text: So Moses said to the judges of Israel, “Each <transChange type="added">of you</transChange> kill his men who are joined together with Baal Peor.”  <div eID="gen1215" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 25:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv923"/><div sID="gen1216" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv923"/>And behold, a man from the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> came and brought to his brothers a Midianite woman before the eyes of Moses and before the eyes of all of the community of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> and they <transChange type="added">were</transChange> weeping <transChange type="added">at</transChange> the doorway of the tent of assembly.

verses.name: Numbers 25:7
verses.text: When Phinehas son of Eleazar son of Aaron the priest saw, he got up from the midst of the community and took a spear in his hand.

verses.name: Numbers 25:8
verses.text: He went after the man of Israel into the woman’s section of the tent, and he drove the two of them, the man of Israel and the woman, into her belly. And the plague among the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> stopped.

verses.name: Numbers 25:9
verses.text: The ones who died in the plague were twenty-four thousand.  <div eID="gen1216" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 25:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv924"/><div sID="gen1217" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv924"/>Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.name: Numbers 25:11
verses.text: “Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, turned away my anger from among the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> when he was jealous with my jealousy in their midst, and I did not destroy the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> with my jealousy.

verses.name: Numbers 25:12
verses.text: Therefore say, ‘Behold, I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> giving to him my covenant of peace,

verses.name: Numbers 25:13
verses.text: and it will be for him and his <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞offspring⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “seed”</note> after him a covenant of an eternal priesthood because he was jealous for his God and made atonement for the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.’ ”<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note>  <div eID="gen1217" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 25:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv925"/><div sID="gen1218" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv925"/>The name of the man of Israel who was struck with the Midianite woman <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Zimri son of Salu, a leader of <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the family⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Or “the father’s house” or “the ancestor’s house”</note> of the Simeonites.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Simeonite”</note>

verses.name: Numbers 25:15
verses.text: The name of the Midianite woman who was struck <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Cozbi daughter of Zur, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a leader⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a head”</note> of a tribe of <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the family⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Or “the father’s house” or “the ancestor’s house”</note> in Midian.  <div eID="gen1218" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 25:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv926"/><div sID="gen1219" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv926"/>Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.name: Numbers 25:17
verses.text: “Attack the Midianites and strike them

verses.name: Numbers 25:18
verses.text: because they <transChange type="added">were</transChange> attacking you with their deception, <transChange type="added">with</transChange> which they have deceived you on the matter of Peor and on the matter of Cozbi the daughter of the leader of Midian, their sister who was struck on the day of the plague because of the matter of Peor.”  <chapter eID="Num.25"/>

verses.name: Numbers 26:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv927"/><title type="x-s">A New Census</title> <div sID="gen1220" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv927"/><note placement="foot"><reference osisRef="Num.26.1a">Numbers 26:1a </reference>in the English Bible is 25:19b in the Hebrew Bible</note> And it happened after the plague,<note placement="foot">In the Hebrew Bible, <reference osisRef="Num.26.1">Numbers 26:1 </reference>begins here</note>Yahweh said to Moses and to Eleazar son of Aaron the priest, saying,

verses.name: Numbers 26:2
verses.text: “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Take a census⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Lift up the heads”</note> of the community of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> from <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞those twenty years old⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a son of twenty years”</note> and above, according to <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞their families⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the house of their fathers”</note> all who are able to go out to war in Israel.”

verses.name: Numbers 26:3
verses.text: So Moses and Eleazar the priest spoke with them on the desert-plateau of Moab by <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Jordan <transChange type="added">across from</transChange> Jericho, saying,

verses.name: Numbers 26:4
verses.text: “<transChange type="added">Take a census of the community</transChange> from <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞those twenty years old⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a son of twenty years”</note> and above, just as Yahweh commanded Moses.” <div eID="gen1220" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1221" type="x-p"/> The Israelites who went out from the land of Egypt <transChange type="added">were</transChange>:  <div eID="gen1221" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 26:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv928"/><div sID="gen1222" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv928"/>Reuben, the firstborn of Israel, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Reuben: of Hanoch, the clan of the Hanochites; of Pallu, the clan of the Palluites;<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Palluite”</note>

verses.name: Numbers 26:6
verses.text: of Hezron, the clan of the Hezronites;<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Hezronite”</note> of Carmi, the clan of the Carmites.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Carmite”</note>

verses.name: Numbers 26:7
verses.text: These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the clans of the Reubenites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Reubenite”</note> and the ones counted of them were forty-three thousand seven hundred and thirty.

verses.name: Numbers 26:8
verses.text: The children of Pallu: Eliab.

verses.name: Numbers 26:9
verses.text: The children of Eliab: Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. These <transChange type="added">are the same</transChange> Dathan and Abiram who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> appointed of the community, who rebelled against Moses and Aaron in the company of Korah, when they rebelled against Yahweh,

verses.name: Numbers 26:10
verses.text: and the land opened its mouth and swallowed them with Korah, when that company died, when the fire consumed two hundred and fifty men, and they were a sign.<note placement="foot">That is, a warning sign</note>

verses.name: Numbers 26:11
verses.text: The children<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Korah, however, did not die.  <div eID="gen1222" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 26:12
