verses.name: Numbers 33:29
verses.text: They set out from Mithcah and camped at Hashmonah.

verses.name: Numbers 33:30
verses.text: They set out from Hashmonah and camped at Moserah.

verses.name: Numbers 33:31
verses.text: They set out from Moserah and camped at Bene-Jaakan.

verses.name: Numbers 33:32
verses.text: They set out from Bene-Jaakan and camped at Hor Haggidgad.

verses.name: Numbers 33:33
verses.text: They set out from Hor Haggidgad and camped at Jotbathah.

verses.name: Numbers 33:34
verses.text: They set out from Jotbathah and camped at Abronah.

verses.name: Numbers 33:35
verses.text: They set out from Abronah and camped at Ezion Geber.

verses.name: Numbers 33:36
verses.text: They set out from Ezion Geber and camped in the desert of Zin, that <transChange type="added">is</transChange>, Kadesh.

verses.name: Numbers 33:37
verses.text: They set out from Kadesh and camped at Mount Hor, at the edge of the land of Edom.  <div eID="gen1281" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 33:38
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv988"/><div sID="gen1282" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv988"/>Aaron the priest went up to Mount Hor at the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞command⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “mouth”</note> of Yahweh, and he died there in the fortieth year after the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> had gone out from the land of Egypt, in the fifth month on the first <transChange type="added">day</transChange> of the month.

verses.name: Numbers 33:39
verses.text: Aaron was one hundred and twenty-three years old when he died on Mount Hor.  <div eID="gen1282" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 33:40
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv989"/><div sID="gen1283" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv989"/>Now the Canaanite, the king of Arad, who <transChange type="added">was</transChange> living in the Negev<note placement="foot">An arid region south of the Judean hills</note> in the land of Canaan, heard of the coming of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note>  <div eID="gen1283" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 33:41
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv990"/><div sID="gen1284" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv990"/>Then they set out from Mount Hor and camped at Zalmonah.

verses.name: Numbers 33:42
verses.text: They set out from Zalmonah and camped at Punon.

verses.name: Numbers 33:43
verses.text: They set out from Punon and camped at Oboth.

verses.name: Numbers 33:44
verses.text: They set out from Oboth and camped at Iye Abarim, the boundary of Moab.

verses.name: Numbers 33:45
verses.text: They set out from Iyim and camped at Dibon Gad.

verses.name: Numbers 33:46
verses.text: They set out from Dibon Gad and camped at Almon-Diblatayim.

verses.name: Numbers 33:47
verses.text: They set out from Almon-Diblatayim and camped in the mountains of Abarim, before Nebo.

verses.name: Numbers 33:48
verses.text: They set out from the mountains of Abarim and camped on the desert-plateau of Moab by the Jordan <transChange type="added">across</transChange> Jericho.

verses.name: Numbers 33:49
verses.text: They camped by the Jordan, from Beth-Jeshimoth up to Abel Shittim, on the desert-plateau of Moab.  <div eID="gen1284" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 33:50
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv991"/><div sID="gen1285" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv991"/>Then Yahweh spoke to Moses on the desert-plateau of Moab by <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Jordan <transChange type="added">across</transChange> Jericho, saying,

verses.name: Numbers 33:51
verses.text: “Speak to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> and say to them, ‘When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan,

verses.name: Numbers 33:52
verses.text: you will drive out the inhabitants of the land from your presence, and you will destroy all their idols and all the images of their molten idols, and you will demolish all their high places;

verses.name: Numbers 33:53
verses.text: you will dispossess the land and live in it because I have given the land to you to possess it.

verses.name: Numbers 33:54
verses.text: You will distribute the land by lot according to your clans; to the larger group you will give a larger inheritance, and to the smaller group you will give less inheritance. However the lot falls for him, there the lot will be. You will distribute it according to the tribes of your ancestors.<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note>

verses.name: Numbers 33:55
verses.text: But if you do not drive out the inhabitants of the land from your presence, then it will happen that whomever you let remain of them will be like irritants in your eyes and like thorns in your sides; they will be your enemies in the land in which you live.

verses.name: Numbers 33:56
verses.text: And just as I planned to do <transChange type="added">to</transChange> them, I will do to you.’ ”  <chapter eID="Num.33"/>

verses.name: Numbers 34:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv992"/><title type="x-s">The Land of Canaan Is Divided</title> <div sID="gen1286" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv992"/>Then Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.name: Numbers 34:2
verses.text: “Command the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> and say to them, ‘When you come into the land of Canaan, this <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the land that was allotted to you as an inheritance, the land of Canaan according to its boundaries.

verses.name: Numbers 34:3
verses.text: Your southern edge will be from the desert of Zin toward the side of Edom, and your southern border will be from the end of the Salt Sea<note placement="foot">That is, the Dead Sea</note> to the east;

verses.name: Numbers 34:4
verses.text: your boundary will turn from the south to the ascent of Akrabbim<note placement="foot">Or “Scorpions”</note> and will pass over to Zin, and its limits will be from the south of Kadesh Barnea; it will continue to Hazar Addar and pass over to Azmon.

verses.name: Numbers 34:5
verses.text: The boundary will turn from Azmon to the valley of Egypt, and its limits will be to the sea.  <div eID="gen1286" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 34:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv993"/><div sID="gen1287" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv993"/>“ ‘Your western boundary will be the Great Sea;<note placement="foot">That is, the Mediterranean</note> this will be your western boundary.

verses.name: Numbers 34:7
verses.text: Your northern border will be from the Great Sea;<note placement="foot">That is, the Mediterranean</note> you will make a boundary from the Great Sea<note placement="foot">That is, the Mediterranean</note> to Mount Hor.

verses.name: Numbers 34:8
verses.text: From Mount Hor you will make a boundary to reach Hamath; the limits of the territory will be at Zedad.

verses.name: Numbers 34:9
verses.text: The boundary will go out to Ziphron, and its limits will be at Hazar Enan. This will be your boundary to the north.  <div eID="gen1287" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 34:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv994"/><div sID="gen1288" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv994"/>“ ‘You will mark out your eastern boundary from Hazar Enan to Shepham;

verses.name: Numbers 34:11
verses.text: the boundary will go down from Shepham to Riblah from the east side of Ain, and the boundary will go down and border on the eastern side of the Sea of Kinnereth.

verses.name: Numbers 34:12
verses.text: The boundary will go down to the Jordan, and its limits will be at the Salt Sea.<note placement="foot">That is, the Dead Sea</note> This will be your land according to its boundaries all around.’ ”  <div eID="gen1288" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 34:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv995"/><div sID="gen1289" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv995"/>So Moses commanded the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> saying, “This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the land that you will obtain as an inheritance for yourself by lot, which Yahweh commanded to give to the nine and a half tribes.

verses.name: Numbers 34:14
verses.text: For the tribe of the children of the Reubenites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Reubenite”</note> the children of the Gadites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Gadite”</note> and the half-tribe of Manasseh took their inheritance according to the house of their families.<note placement="foot">Or “their fathers”</note>

verses.name: Numbers 34:15
verses.text: The two and a half tribes have taken their inheritance from beyond the Jordan <transChange type="added">across</transChange> Jericho, east toward the sunrise.”  <div eID="gen1289" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 34:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv996"/><div sID="gen1290" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv996"/>Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.name: Numbers 34:17
verses.text: “These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the names of the men who divide up the land for your inheritance: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun.

verses.name: Numbers 34:18
verses.text: You will take one leader from every tribe to divide up the land for inheritance.

verses.name: Numbers 34:19
verses.text: These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the names of the men: of the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;

verses.name: Numbers 34:20
verses.text: of the tribe of the descendants of Simeon, Samuel son of Ammihud;

verses.name: Numbers 34:21
verses.text: of the tribe of Benjamin, Elidad son of Chislon;

verses.name: Numbers 34:22
verses.text: of the tribe of the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Dan, the leader Bukki son of Jogli;

verses.name: Numbers 34:23
verses.text: of the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Joseph, the tribe of the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Manasseh, the leader Hanniel son of Ephod.

verses.name: Numbers 34:24
verses.text: Of the tribe of the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Ephraim, the leader Kemuel son of Shiphtan;

verses.name: Numbers 34:25
verses.text: of the tribe of the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Zebulum, the leader Elizaphan son of Parnach;

verses.name: Numbers 34:26
verses.text: of the tribe of the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Issachar, the leader Paltiel son of Azzan;

verses.name: Numbers 34:27
verses.text: of the tribe of the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Asher, the leader Ahihud son of Shelomi;

verses.name: Numbers 34:28
verses.text: of the tribe of the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Naphtali, the leader Pedahel son of Ammihud.”

verses.name: Numbers 34:29
verses.text: These are those whom Yahweh commanded to allot to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> the land of Canaan.  <chapter eID="Num.34"/>

verses.name: Numbers 35:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv997"/><title type="x-s">Cities for the Levites</title> <div sID="gen1291" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv997"/>Yahweh spoke to Moses on the desert plains of Moab beyond the Jordan <transChange type="added">across</transChange> Jericho, saying,

verses.name: Numbers 35:2
verses.text: “Command the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> that they give to the Levites from the inheritance of their property cities to live in; and you will give to the Levites pastureland all around the cities.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “them”</note>

verses.name: Numbers 35:3
verses.text: The cities will be theirs to live in, and their pasturelands will be for their domestic animals, for their possessions, and their animals.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “animal”</note>  <div eID="gen1291" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 35:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv998"/><div sID="gen1292" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv998"/>“The pasturelands of the cities that you will give to the Levites <transChange type="added">will extend</transChange> from the wall of the city to <transChange type="added">a distance of</transChange> a thousand cubits all around.

verses.name: Numbers 35:5
verses.text: You will measure outside the city the eastern edge two thousand cubits, for the southern edge two thousand cubits, for the western edge two thousand cubits, and for the northern edge two thousand cubits, with the city in the middle; this will be for them the pasturelands of the cities.  <div eID="gen1292" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 35:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv999"/><div sID="gen1293" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv999"/>“All the cities that you will give the Levites will be six cities of refuge, to which the killer can flee; in addition to them you will give forty-two cities.

verses.name: Numbers 35:7
verses.text: All the cities that you will give to the Levites will be forty-eight cities, them with their pasturelands.

verses.name: Numbers 35:8
verses.text: And the cities that you will give from the property of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> you will take more from the larger group and less from the smaller group; each of them will give according to the portion of their inheritance according to the portion that he inherits.”  <div eID="gen1293" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 35:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1000"/><title type="x-s">Cities of Refuge</title> <div sID="gen1294" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1000"/>Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.name: Numbers 35:10
verses.text: “Speak to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> and say to them, ‘When you cross the Jordan <transChange type="added">into</transChange> the land of Canaan,

verses.name: Numbers 35:11
verses.text: you will select for yourselves cities for your cities of refuge, that a killer who has killed a person unintentionally can flee there.

verses.name: Numbers 35:12
verses.text: The cities will be to you a refuge from a redeemer, so that the killer will not die until he stands before the community for judgment.

verses.name: Numbers 35:13
verses.text: The cities that you are to give will be your six cities of refuge.

verses.name: Numbers 35:14
verses.text: You will give three cities across the Jordan and three cities in the land of Canaan; they will be cities of refuge.

verses.name: Numbers 35:15
verses.text: To the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> to the alien, and to the temporary resident in their midst there will be these six cities as a refuge to which anyone who unintentionally kills a person may flee.  <div eID="gen1294" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 35:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1001"/><div sID="gen1295" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1001"/>“ ‘But if he hit him with an object of iron, so that he dies, the killer must surely be put to death.

verses.name: Numbers 35:17
verses.text: And if he hit him with a stone in the hand, by which he will die, and he does die, he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a killer; the killer must surely be put to death.

verses.name: Numbers 35:18
verses.text: Or if he hit him with a wooden object, by which he will die, and he does die, he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a killer; the killer must surely be put to death.

verses.name: Numbers 35:19
verses.text: The blood avenger himself will put the killer to death; he must put him to death when meeting him.

verses.name: Numbers 35:20
verses.text: If he shoves him in hatred, or he throws something at him with intention, and he dies,

verses.name: Numbers 35:21
verses.text: or if he hits him in hostility with his hand, and he dies, the one that struck him will put to death the killer when meeting him.  <div eID="gen1295" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 35:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1002"/><div sID="gen1296" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1002"/>“ ‘Or if in an instant he shoved him, not in hostility, or threw something at him without intention,

verses.name: Numbers 35:23
verses.text: or with any stone, without seeing it dropped on him so that he dies, while <transChange type="added">he was</transChange> not seeking his injury,

verses.name: Numbers 35:24
verses.text: then the community will judge between the striker and between the blood avenger according to these ordinances.

verses.name: Numbers 35:25
verses.text: The community will deliver the killer from the hand of the blood avenger, and the community will restore him to the city of his refuge to which he fled; and he will live there in it until the death of the high priest who was anointed with holy oil.

verses.name: Numbers 35:26
verses.text: But if the killer surely goes out of the territory of the city of his refuge to which he fled,

verses.name: Numbers 35:27
verses.text: and the blood avenger finds him outside the territory of the city of his refuge, and the blood avenger kills the killer, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he will not be guilty of blood⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “there will not be blood for him”</note>

verses.name: Numbers 35:28
verses.text: because he must live in the city of his refuge until the death of the high priest. But after the death of the high priest the killer will return to the land of his property.

verses.name: Numbers 35:29
verses.text: These things will be as a decree of justice for you for your generations in all your dwellings.  <div eID="gen1296" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 35:30
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1003"/><div sID="gen1297" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1003"/>“ ‘If anyone kills a person, the killer will be put to death <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞according to the testimony⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “according to the mouth”</note> of witnesses, but someone cannot die on testimony of one person.

verses.name: Numbers 35:31
verses.text: Also, you will not take a ransom payment for the life of a killer who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> guilty of death; indeed, he must surely be put to death.

verses.name: Numbers 35:32
verses.text: You will not take a ransom payment for the one that flees to the city of his refuge, so that he may return to live in the land before the death of the priest.

verses.name: Numbers 35:33
verses.text: So you will not pollute the land in which you are; because blood pollutes the land, and no atonement can be made for the land for the blood that is poured out on it except with the blood of the one who poured it out.

verses.name: Numbers 35:34
verses.text: You will not defile the land on which you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> living because I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> living in the midst of it; I am Yahweh; I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> living in the midst of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.’ ”<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note>  <chapter eID="Num.35"/>

verses.name: Numbers 36:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1004"/><title type="x-s">Inheritance Through Marriage</title> <div sID="gen1298" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1004"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞The leaders⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “The heads”</note> of the families<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> of the clans of descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Gilead the son of Makir, the son of Manasseh, of the clans of the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Joseph came near and spoke <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “before the face of”</note> Moses and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “before the face of”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the leaders⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the heads”</note> of the families<note placement="foot">Hebrew “of the fathers”</note> of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note>

verses.name: Numbers 36:2
verses.text: And they said, “Yahweh commanded my lord to give the land by lot as an inheritance to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> and my lord was commanded by Yahweh to give the inheritance of Zelophehad our brother to his daughters.

verses.name: Numbers 36:3
verses.text: But if they become wives to one of the sons from <transChange type="added">another</transChange> tribe of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> their inheritance will disappear from the inheritance of our ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and it will be added to the inheritance of the tribe to which they belong; the lot of our inheritance would disappear.

verses.name: Numbers 36:4
verses.text: When the Jubilee of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞comes⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “will be”</note> it will be added to the inheritance of the tribe to which they belong; and their inheritance will disappear from the tribe of our father.”  <div eID="gen1298" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 36:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1005"/><div sID="gen1299" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1005"/>Then Moses commanded the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> by the command of Yahweh, saying, “The tribe of the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Joseph <transChange type="added">is</transChange> right <transChange type="added">regarding what they are</transChange> speaking.

verses.name: Numbers 36:6
verses.text: This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the word that Yahweh commanded the daughters of Zelophehad, saying, ‘<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Let them marry⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Let them be as wives”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞whomever they like⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “they will be as the good in their eyes”</note> only <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they must marry⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “they must be as wives”</note> from within the clan of the tribe of their father.

verses.name: Numbers 36:7
verses.text: Thus an inheritance of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> will not go around from tribe to tribe. Rather, the inheritance of each tribe of his father will remain with the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note>

verses.name: Numbers 36:8
verses.text: Every daughter who possesses an inheritance from the tribes of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> will <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞marry⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “be a wife to”</note> one of the clan of the tribe of her father, so that the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> will possess the inheritance of his ancestors.<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note>

verses.name: Numbers 36:9
verses.text: Therefore an inheritance will not go around from <transChange type="added">one</transChange> tribe to another tribe because the tribes of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> will each hold to their <transChange type="added">own</transChange> inheritance.’ ”  <div eID="gen1299" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 36:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1006"/><div sID="gen1300" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1006"/>Just as Yahweh commanded to Moses, so the daughters of Zelophehad did:

verses.name: Numbers 36:11
verses.text: Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah, the daughters of Zelophehad, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞married⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “were as wives to”</note> the sons of their uncles.

verses.name: Numbers 36:12
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞They married⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “They were as wives to”</note> those from the sons of Manasseh son of Joseph, and their inheritance <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞remained⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “was”</note> among the tribe of the clan of their ancestors.<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note>  <div eID="gen1300" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Numbers 36:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1007"/><div sID="gen1301" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1007"/>These <transChange type="added">were</transChange> the commands and the stipulations that Yahweh commanded by the hand of Moses<note placement="foot">Or “through Moses”</note> to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> on the desert-plateaus of Moab by the Jordan <transChange type="added">across</transChange> Jericho.  <chapter eID="Num.36"/> <div eID="gen1301" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen891" osisID="Num" type="book"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1008"/><title type="x-s">Preamble</title> <div sID="gen1303" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1008"/>These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the words that Moses spoke to all <transChange type="added">of</transChange> Israel <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞on the other side of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in the beyond of”</note> the Jordan in the desert,<note placement="foot">Or “the wilderness”</note> in the desert plateau<note placement="foot">Or “desert plain”; others render this as a named location, “Arabah”</note> opposite Suph, between Paran and between Tophel and Laban and Hazeroth and Dizahab.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:2
verses.text: It is <transChange type="added">a journey of</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞eleven days⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “one and ten days”</note> from Herob <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞by the way of Mount Seir⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by the mountain of Seir”</note> up to Kadesh Barnea.  <div eID="gen1303" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1009"/><div sID="gen1304" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1009"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And it was⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and it happened” or “and then”</note> in the fortieth year, on the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, Moses spoke to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> according to all that Yahweh had instructed him <transChange type="added">to speak</transChange> to them.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:4
verses.text: <transChange type="added">This happened</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞after defeating⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “after he had struck down”</note> Sihon king of the Amorites, who was reigning<note placement="foot">Or “dwelling,” and in this context “reigning”</note> in Heshbon, and Og the king of Bashan, who was reigning<note placement="foot">Or “dwelling,” and in this context “reigning”</note> in Ashtaroth in Edrei.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:5
verses.text: On the other side of<note placement="foot">Literally “in the beyond of”</note> the Jordan in the land of Moab Moses began to explain this law,<note placement="foot">Hebrew <hi type="italic">torah</hi></note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>:<note placement="foot">Literally “to say”</note>  <div eID="gen1304" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1010"/><title type="x-s">Historical Prologue</title> <div sID="gen1305" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1010"/>“Yahweh our God spoke to us at Horeb, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to say”</note> ‘You have stayed <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞long enough⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “much time”</note> at this mountain.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:7
verses.text: Turn <transChange type="added">now</transChange> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞move on⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “journey on with respect to yourselves” or “move yourselves out”</note> and go into the hill of the Amorites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Amorite”</note> and to all of the neighboring regions<note placement="foot">Or “peoples”</note> in the Jordan <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Valley⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Arabah,” arid stretches of land.</note> in the hill country and in the Negev and in the coastal area along the sea, into the land of the Canaanites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Canaanite”</note> and <transChange type="added">into</transChange> the Lebanon, as far as the great river Euphrates.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:8
verses.text: Look, I have set the land <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “before your face”</note> go and take possession of the land that Yahweh swore to your ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give <transChange type="added">it</transChange> to them and to their offspring after them.’  <div eID="gen1305" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1011"/><div sID="gen1306" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1011"/>“And I spoke to them at that time, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to say”</note> ‘I am not able to bear you alone.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:10
verses.text: Yahweh your God has multiplied you, and look; you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> today as the stars of the heaven <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in number⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “with respect to multitude/abundance”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:11
verses.text: Yahweh, the God of your ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> may he add to you as you are now a thousand times, and may he bless you just as he <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞promised you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “spoke to you”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:12
verses.text: How can I bear you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞by myself⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to me alone”</note> your burden and your load and your strife?

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:13
verses.text: Choose for yourselves <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞wise and discerning and knowledgeable men⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “men wise and discerning and knowledgeable”</note> for <transChange type="added">each of</transChange> your tribes, and I will appoint them as your leaders.’  <div eID="gen1306" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1012"/><div sID="gen1307" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1012"/>“And you answered me, and you said, ‘The thing you have said to do is good.’

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:15
verses.text: And so I took the leaders of your tribes, wise and knowledgeable men, and <transChange type="added">then</transChange> I appointed them as leaders over you <transChange type="added">as</transChange> commanders of <transChange type="added">groups of</transChange> thousands and commanders of <transChange type="added">groups of</transChange> hundreds and commanders of <transChange type="added">groups of</transChange> fifties and commanders of <transChange type="added">groups of</transChange> tens <transChange type="added">as</transChange> officials for your tribes.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:16
verses.text: And at that time I instructed your judges, saying, ‘<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞hear out your fellow men⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “hear between your brothers,” with the idea of listening carefully in this context</note> and then judge fairly<note placement="foot">Or “righteously”</note> between a man and between his brother and between <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his opponent who is a resident alien⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “between his resident alien/non-Israelite who dwells temporarily among Israel”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:17
verses.text: You must not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞be partial⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “recognize faces”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in your judgment⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “in the process of rendering a judgment”</note> hear out the small person as also the great person; <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞do not be intimidated by any person⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “do not fear before the faces of any man”</note> because the judgment is God’s; and the case that is too difficult<note placement="foot">Or “hard”</note> for you, bring <transChange type="added">it</transChange> to me, and I will hear it <transChange type="added">out</transChange>.’

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:18
verses.text: And so I instructed you at that time <transChange type="added">concerning</transChange> all <transChange type="added">of</transChange> the things that you should do.  <div eID="gen1307" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1013"/><div sID="gen1308" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1013"/>“Then we set out from Horeb, and we went <transChange type="added">through</transChange> the whole <transChange type="added">of</transChange> that great and terrible desert that you saw <transChange type="added">on</transChange> the way <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the hill country of the Amorites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Amorite”</note> as Yahweh our God had commanded us, and <transChange type="added">so</transChange> we came up to Kadesh Barnea.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:20
verses.text: I said to you, ‘<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞You have reached⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “You have come up to”</note> the hill country of the Amorites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Amorite”</note> that Yahweh our God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> giving to us.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:21
verses.text: See, Yahweh your God has set before you the land; go up and possess <transChange type="added">it</transChange> as Yahweh the God of your ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> said to you; do not fear and do not be dismayed.’  <div eID="gen1308" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1014"/><div sID="gen1309" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1014"/>“Then all of you approached me, and <transChange type="added">you</transChange> said, ‘Let us send men <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before us⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “before our faces” or “ahead of us”</note> and let them explore the land for us, and let them bring back <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a report⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a word”</note> to us concerning the way that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞we should take⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “we should go up by it”</note> <transChange type="added">and concerning</transChange> the cities that we shall come to.’

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:23
verses.text: The plan was good <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in my opinion⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “in my eyes”</note> and so I took from among you twelve men, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞one from each tribe⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “man one from the tribe”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:24
verses.text: And they <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞set out⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “turned”</note> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞went up into the hill country⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “went up toward the hill country mountain”</note> and they went up to the wadi<note placement="foot">A valley that is dry most of the year, but contains a stream during the rainy season</note> of Eschol, and they spied out <transChange type="added">the land</transChange>.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:25
verses.text: They took in their hands<note placement="foot">Hebrew “hand”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞some of the fruit⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from the fruit”</note> of the land, and they brought it down to us, and they brought to us back <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a report⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “a word”</note> and they said, ‘The land that Yahweh our God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> giving to us <transChange type="added">is</transChange> good.’

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:26
verses.text: But you were not willing to go up, and you rebelled against the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞command⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “mouth”</note> of Yahweh your God.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:27
verses.text: And you grumbled in your tents, and you said, ‘Because of the hatred of Yahweh <transChange type="added">toward</transChange> us he has brought us out from the land of Egypt to give us into the hand of the Amorites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Amorite”</note> to destroy us.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:28
verses.text: Where <transChange type="added">can</transChange> we go up? Our brothers have <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞made our hearts melt⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “caused to melt our hearts”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to say”</note> “The people are greater<note placement="foot">Or “bigger”</note> and taller than we are,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “than us”</note> <transChange type="added">and there are</transChange> great fortified cities <transChange type="added">reaching</transChange> up to heaven, and we saw the sons of the Anakites <transChange type="added">living</transChange> there.” ’  <div eID="gen1309" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1015"/><div sID="gen1310" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1015"/>“And so I said to you, ‘Do not be terrified, and do not fear them.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:30
verses.text: Yahweh your God, who is going <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to your faces”</note> will himself<note placement="foot">The Hebrew pronoun indicates emphasis</note> fight for you, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞just as⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “like all that”</note> he did for you in Egypt before your eyes,

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:31
verses.text: and <transChange type="added">just as he did</transChange> in the wilderness<note placement="foot">Or “desert”</note> when<note placement="foot">Or “where”</note> you saw that<note placement="foot">Or “how”</note> Yahweh your God carried you, just as someone<note placement="foot">Or “a man”</note> carries his son, all along the way that you traveled until <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you reached⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “you came”</note> this place.’

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:32
verses.text: But through all of this you did not trust in Yahweh your God,

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:33
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who goes⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “is the one going”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “before your faces”</note> on your<note placement="foot">Hebrew “the”</note> way, seeking a place for your encampment, in fire at night and in a cloud by day, to show you the way that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you should go⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “you should go in it”</note>  <div eID="gen1310" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:34
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1016"/><div sID="gen1311" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1016"/>“Then Yahweh heard the sound of your words, and he was angry, and he swore, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to say”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:35
verses.text: ‘No one of these men<note placement="foot">The beginning of an oath in Hebrew; the text emphatically denies anyone of that evil generation the privilege of seeing the promised land</note> of this evil generation will see the good land that I swore to give to your ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:36
verses.text: except Caleb, the son of Jephunneh; he himself<note placement="foot">Emphatic use of the pronoun</note> shall see it, and to him I will give the land upon which he has trodden and to his sons<note placement="foot">Or “descendants”</note> because <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he followed Yahweh unreservedly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.’<note placement="foot">Literally “he filled his hands after Yahweh”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:37
verses.text: Even with me Yahweh was angry because of you, saying, ‘Not even you shall enter there.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:38
verses.text: Joshua, the son of Nun, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞your assistant⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the one standing before you”</note> will go there; encourage him because he will cause Israel to inherit it.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:39
verses.text: And your little children, who you thought shall become plunder, and your sons, who do not today know good or bad, shall themselves<note placement="foot">The Hebrew pronoun is used for emphasis</note> go there, and I will give it to them, and they shall take possession of it.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:40
verses.text: But you turn and set out <transChange type="added">in the direction of</transChange> the wilderness by way of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Red Sea⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.’<note placement="foot">Literally “sea of reeds”</note>  <div eID="gen1311" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:41
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1017"/><div sID="gen1312" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1017"/>“You replied and said to me, ‘We have sinned against Yahweh, <transChange type="added">and now</transChange> we will go up and fight according to all that Yahweh our God commanded us’; and <transChange type="added">so</transChange> each man fastened on <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his battle gear⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “his vessels of battle”</note> and you regarded <transChange type="added">it</transChange> as easy to go up <transChange type="added">into</transChange> the hill country.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:42
verses.text: So Yahweh said to me, ‘Say to them, “You shall not go up, and you shall not fight because I am not in your midst; you will be defeated <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in the faces of your enemies”</note> your enemies.” ’

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:43
verses.text: So I spoke to you, but you did not listen; you rebelled against the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞command of Yahweh⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “mouth of Yahweh”</note> you behaved presumptuously, and you went up into the hill country.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:44
verses.text: The Amorites living in the hill country went out <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to oppose you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to meet you”</note> and chased you as a swarm of wild honey bees do; and so they <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞beat⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “cut”</note> you down in Seir as far as Hormah.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:45
verses.text: So you returned and wept <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before Yahweh⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “before the faces of Yahweh”</note> but Yahweh did not listen to your voice and did not pay <transChange type="added">any</transChange> attention to you.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 1:46
verses.text: You stayed in Kadesh many days; such were the days that you stayed <transChange type="added">there</transChange>.  <chapter eID="Deut.1"/> <div eID="gen1312" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 2:1
verses.text: “<transChange type="added">Then</transChange> we turned and set out <transChange type="added">toward</transChange> the wilderness<note placement="foot">Or “desert”</note> in the direction of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Red Sea⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sea of reeds”</note> as Yahweh told me, and we went around Mount Seir <transChange type="added">for</transChange> many days.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 2:2
verses.text: Yahweh spoke to me, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to say”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 2:3
verses.text: ‘<transChange type="added">Long</transChange> enough you have been skirting this mountain; turn yourselves north,

verses.name: Deuteronomy 2:4
verses.text: and instruct<note placement="foot">Or “command”</note> the people, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to say”</note> “You are about to cross through the territory of your brothers, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Esau, who are living in Seir; they will be afraid of you, and <transChange type="added">so</transChange> be very careful.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 2:5
verses.text: Do not get involved in battle<note placement="foot">Or “provoke”</note> with them, for I will not give you any of their land, not even <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a foot’s breadth⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a sole’s foot of space”</note> <transChange type="added">of it</transChange>; since I have given Mount Seir <transChange type="added">as</transChange> a possession for Esau.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 2:6
verses.text: You shall buy food from them so that you may eat; and also you shall purchase water from them with money so that you may drink.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 2:7
verses.text: The fact of the matter is, Yahweh your God has blessed you in <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞all the work you have done⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “the work of your hand”</note> he knows <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞your travels⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “your journeying”</note> <transChange type="added">with respect to</transChange> this great wilderness; forty years Yahweh your God <transChange type="added">has been</transChange> with you; you have not lacked a thing.” ’

verses.name: Deuteronomy 2:8
verses.text: And so we passed by our brothers, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Esau, who live in Seir, past the road of the Arabah,<note placement="foot">Or “Jordan Valley” since the Arabah is an extension of it</note> from Elath and Ezion Geber, and we turned and traveled along the route of the desert<note placement="foot">Or “wilderness”</note> of Moab.  <div eID="gen1313" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 2:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1018"/><div sID="gen1314" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1018"/>And Yahweh said to me, ‘You shall not attack Moab, and you shall not engage in war<note placement="foot">Or “battle”</note> with them, for I will not give you any of his land as a possession; I have given Ar to the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Lot <transChange type="added">as</transChange> a possession.’

verses.name: Deuteronomy 2:10
verses.text: (The Emim previously lived in it, a people large,<note placement="foot">Or “great” in the sense of influential</note> numerous, and tall, like the Anakites.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 2:11
verses.text: They were reckoned also <transChange type="added">as</transChange> Rephaim as the Anakites <transChange type="added">were</transChange>; but the Moabites called them Emim.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 2:12
verses.text: The Horites previously lived in Seir, but the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Esau dispossessed them and destroyed them <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from among themselves⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “from their presence”</note> as Israel did with respect to the land of their<note placement="foot">Literally “its/his”</note> possession that Yahweh gave to them.)

verses.name: Deuteronomy 2:13
verses.text: So <transChange type="added">now</transChange> arise and cross over the wadi<note placement="foot">A valley that is dry most of the year, but contains a stream during the rainy season</note> of Zered yourselves; and so we crossed the wadi<note placement="foot">A valley that is dry most of the year, but contains a stream during the rainy season</note> of Zered.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 2:14
verses.text: Now the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞length of time⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “days”</note> that we had traveled from Kadesh Barnea until the time when we crossed the wadi<note placement="foot">A valley that is dry most of the year, but contains a stream during the rainy season</note> of Zered <transChange type="added">was</transChange> thirty-eight years, until the perishing of all of that generation; <transChange type="added">that is</transChange>, the men of war from the midst of the camp as Yahweh had sworn to them.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 2:15
verses.text: The hand of Yahweh was against them to root them out from the midst of the camp until they perished completely.  <div eID="gen1314" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 2:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1019"/><div sID="gen1315" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1019"/>“<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it happened”</note> when all the men of war<note placement="foot">Or “battle”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞had died⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “had finished/completed to die”</note> from among the people,

verses.name: Deuteronomy 2:17
verses.text: Yahweh spoke to me, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to say”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 2:18
verses.text: ‘You <transChange type="added">are</transChange> about to cross over the boundary of Moab <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞today⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the day”</note> at Ar.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 2:19
verses.text: When you approach <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the border of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “opposite”</note> the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the sons/children of Ammon”</note> you shall not harass them, and you shall not get involved in battle with them, for I have not given the land of <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the sons/children of Ammon”</note> to you as a possession; because I have given it to the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Lot <transChange type="added">as</transChange> a possession.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 2:20
verses.text: (It is also considered the land of Rephaim; Rephaim lived in it <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞previously⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “before”</note> and the Ammonites called them Zamzummim,

verses.name: Deuteronomy 2:21
verses.text: a people great and numerous and as tall as the Anakites; Yahweh destroyed them from before them,<note placement="foot">That is, the Ammonites</note> and they dispossessed them and settled in place of them,

verses.name: Deuteronomy 2:22
verses.text: just as he did for the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Esau, who live in Seir, when he destroyed the Horites from <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from the face/presence of them”</note> and dispossessed them, and then they settled in their<note placement="foot">Hebrew “them”</note> place up to this day.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 2:23
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">also</transChange> the Avvites, who lived in villages as far as Gaza, <transChange type="added">and the</transChange> Caphtorim, who came out from Caphtor, destroyed them and <transChange type="added">then</transChange> settled in their place.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 2:24
verses.text: Arise,<note placement="foot">Or “Get up”</note> set out and cross over the wadi<note placement="foot">A valley that is dry most of the year, but contains a stream during the rainy season</note> of Arnon. Look! I have given Sihon the Amorite, the king of Heshbon, and his land into your hand; begin to take possession of <transChange type="added">it</transChange>, and engage with him in battle.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 2:25
verses.text: This day I will begin to place <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the dread of you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “your dread”</note> and the fear of you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “upon the faces of”</note> the peoples under all the heavens. They will hear <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the report about you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “your report”</note> and so they will shake and tremble <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞because of you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.’<note placement="foot">Literally “from before you”</note>  <div eID="gen1315" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 2:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1020"/><div sID="gen1316" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1020"/>“So I sent messengers from the wilderness<note placement="foot">Or “desert”</note> of Kedemoth to Sihon king of Heshbon; I sent terms of peace, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to say”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 2:27
verses.text: ‘Let me cross through your land <transChange type="added">and</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞only along the road⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in the road, in the road”</note> I will go; I will not turn aside to the right or <transChange type="added">to the</transChange> left.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 2:28
verses.text: Food for money you shall sell me, so that I may eat, and water for money you will give to me, so that I may drink; just let me cross on foot.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 2:29
verses.text: <transChange type="added">Just as</transChange> the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “the children/sons of”</note> of Esau did for me, who live in Seir, and the Moabites, who live in Ar, until I cross the Jordan into the land that Yahweh our God is giving to us.’

verses.name: Deuteronomy 2:30
verses.text: But Sihon king of Heshbon was not willing to let us cross through his <transChange type="added">territory</transChange> because Yahweh your God hardened his spirit and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞made him obstinate⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “made firm his heart”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in order to give him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to give him,” indicating purpose</note> into your hand, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞just as he has now done⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “as it is this day”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 2:31
verses.text: Yahweh said to me, ‘Look! I have begun to give <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞over to you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the face of you”</note> Sihon and his land; begin <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to take possession of his land⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.’<note placement="foot">Literally, “take possession in order to possess his land”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 2:32
verses.text: Then Sihon and all his people came out to meet us for battle at Jahaz.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 2:33
verses.text: And so Yahweh our God gave him over <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to us⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “before us”</note> and we struck him down, and his sons<note placement="foot">Or “descendants”</note> and all of his people.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 2:34
verses.text: So we captured all of his cities at that time, and we destroyed each town <transChange type="added">of</transChange> males and the women and the children; we did not leave behind a survivor.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 2:35
verses.text: We took only the livestock as spoil for ourselves,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “us”</note> and <transChange type="added">also</transChange> the booty of the cities that we had captured.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 2:36
verses.text: From Aroer, which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> on the edge of the wadi<note placement="foot">A valley that is dry most of the year, but contains a stream during the rainy season</note> of Arnon and the city that was in the wadi<note placement="foot">A valley that is dry most of the year, but contains a stream during the rainy season</note> on up to Gilead, there was not a city that was inaccessible to us; Yahweh our God gave <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞everything⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the whole”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to us⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “before us”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 2:37
verses.text: Only the land of <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “children/sons of Ammon”</note> you did not approach, all along the whole upper region of the Jabbok <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞River⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “wadi,” which here refers to a flowing river</note> and the towns of the hill country, <transChange type="added">according to all</transChange> that Yahweh our God had instructed.  <chapter eID="Deut.2"/> <div eID="gen1316" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 3:1
verses.text: “Then we turned, and we went up the road to Bashan, and Og the king of Bashan came out to meet us, he and all <transChange type="added">of</transChange> his army for the battle <transChange type="added">at</transChange> Edrei.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 3:2
verses.text: And Yahweh said to me, ‘You should not fear him, for I have given him and all <transChange type="added">of</transChange> his army<note placement="foot">Or “people”</note> and his land into your hand. And so you will do to him as you did to Sihon the king of the Amorites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Amorite”</note> who <transChange type="added">was</transChange> reigning in Heshbon.’

verses.name: Deuteronomy 3:3
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">so</transChange> Yahweh our God also gave Og the king of Bashan, and all of his army<note placement="foot">Or “people”</note> into our hand, and we struck him down until not a survivor remained to<note placement="foot">Or “for”</note> him.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 3:4
verses.text: And we captured all <transChange type="added">of</transChange> his towns<note placement="foot">Or “villages/cities small”</note> at that time; <transChange type="added">there</transChange> was not a city that we did not take from them.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 3:5
verses.text: All of these <transChange type="added">were</transChange> fortified towns with high walls, gates, and bars,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “bar”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞apart from⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “alone from”</note> very many <transChange type="added">of</transChange> the villages of the open country.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 3:6
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">so</transChange> we destroyed them just as we had done to Sihon the king of Heshbon; <transChange type="added">we destroyed</transChange> utterly each town of males, the women, and the little children.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 3:7
verses.text: But all <transChange type="added">of</transChange> the livestock and the booty of the towns we kept as spoil for ourselves.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “us”</note>  <div eID="gen1317" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 3:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1021"/><div sID="gen1318" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1021"/>“And so we took at that time the land from <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the control of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the hand of”</note> the two kings of the Amorites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Amorite”</note> who were <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞on the other side of the Jordan⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “in the beyond of the Jordan”</note> from the wadi<note placement="foot">A valley that is dry most of the year, but contains a stream during the rainy season</note> of Arnon up to <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Mount Hermon⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the mountain of Hermon”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 3:9
verses.text: (The Sidonians called Hermon ‘Sirion,’ and the Amorites called it ‘Senir.’)

verses.name: Deuteronomy 3:10
verses.text: All of the towns of the plateau and the whole of Gilead and all of Bashan up to Salecah and Edrei, the towns of the kingdom of Og in Bashan.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 3:11
verses.text: (For only Og, king of Bashan, was left from the remnant of the Rephaim. Indeed, his bedstead—it <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a bedstead of iron. It is in Rabbah of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> Nine cubits <transChange type="added">is</transChange> its length, and four cubits <transChange type="added">is</transChange> its width according to the cubit of a man.)  <div eID="gen1318" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 3:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1022"/><div sID="gen1319" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1022"/>And <transChange type="added">so</transChange> we took possession of this land at that time, from Aroer, which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> on the <transChange type="added">edge of the</transChange> wadi<note placement="foot">A valley that is dry most of the year, but contains a stream during the rainy season</note> of Arnon, and also half of the hill country of Gilead and its towns I gave to the Reubenites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Reubenite”</note> and to the Gadites.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Gadite”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 3:13
verses.text: And the remainder of Gilead and all of Bashan, the kingdom of Og, I gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh, the whole region of Argo. All of that <transChange type="added">area of</transChange> Bashan was called <transChange type="added">the</transChange> land of the Rephaim.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 3:14
verses.text: Jair the descendant<note placement="foot">Or “son”</note> of Manasseh acquired the whole region of Argob, up to the boundary of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and he called it,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “them”</note> that is Bashan, after his own name, Havvoth Jair, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as it still is today⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “up to this day”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 3:15
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">also</transChange> I gave Gilead to Makir.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 3:16
verses.text: And to the Reubenites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Reubenite”</note> and to the Gadites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Gadite”</note> I gave, from Gilead up to the wadi<note placement="foot">A valley that is dry most of the year, but contains a stream during the rainy season</note> of Arnon, the middle of the wadi<note placement="foot">A valley that is dry most of the year, but contains a stream during the rainy season</note> as a boundary and up to the Jabbok <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞River⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “wadi,” which here refers to a flowing river</note> the boundary of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 3:17
verses.text: And the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Jordan Valley⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Arabah”</note> with the Jordan River as its boundary, from Kinnereth<note placement="foot">Or “Chinnereth,” the Sea of Galilee</note> up to the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea,<note placement="foot">Or the Dead Sea</note> <transChange type="added">with</transChange> the slopes of Pisgah toward the east.  <div eID="gen1319" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 3:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1023"/><div sID="gen1320" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1023"/>“And I charged you <transChange type="added">all</transChange> at that time <transChange type="added">when I</transChange> said, “Yahweh has given you—to <transChange type="added">all of</transChange> you—this land to possess. All the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞warriors⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “men of valor”</note> shall cross over, ready to fight, before your brothers, the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 3:19
verses.text: Only your wives and your little children and your livestock (I know that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you have much livestock⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>)<note placement="foot">Literally “livestock much there is to you”</note> must stay in your towns that I have given you,

verses.name: Deuteronomy 3:20
verses.text: until Yahweh shall give rest to your brothers as <transChange type="added">he did</transChange> to you, and also they take possession <transChange type="added">of</transChange> the land that Yahweh your God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> giving to them beyond the Jordan; then they may return, each <transChange type="added">one</transChange> to his possession that I have given to them.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 3:21
verses.text: And I commanded Joshua at that time, saying, ‘Your eyes see all that Yahweh your God has done to these two kings; so Yahweh will do to all <transChange type="added">of</transChange> the kingdoms where you are about to cross over to.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 3:22
verses.text: You shall not fear them, for Yahweh your God is the <transChange type="added">one</transChange> fighting for you.  <div eID="gen1320" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 3:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1024"/><div sID="gen1321" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1024"/>“And I pleaded with Yahweh at that time, saying,

verses.name: Deuteronomy 3:24
verses.text: ‘Lord Yahweh, you have begun to show your servant your greatness and your strong hand, for what<note placement="foot">Hebrew “who”</note> god <transChange type="added">is there</transChange> in the heaven or on the earth who can do according to your works and according to your mighty deeds?

verses.name: Deuteronomy 3:25
verses.text: Let me cross over, please, and let me see the good land <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞that is beyond the Jordan⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “in the beyond of the Jordan”</note> this good hill country and Lebanon.’

verses.name: Deuteronomy 3:26
verses.text: But Yahweh was very angry with me because of you, and he would not listen to me, and Yahweh said, ‘<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Enough of that from you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!<note placement="foot">Literally “Much to you”</note> You shall not speak to me <transChange type="added">any</transChange> longer about this matter!

verses.name: Deuteronomy 3:27
verses.text: Go up <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the top of Pisgah and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞look around you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “lift up your eyes”</note> toward the west, toward the north, and toward the east, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞view⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “look”</note> <transChange type="added">the land</transChange> with your eyes, for you will not cross this Jordan.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 3:28
verses.text: Now instruct Joshua and support him and encourage him because he himself<note placement="foot">Emphatic use of the pronoun</note> will cross <transChange type="added">over</transChange> before this people and enable them to inherit the land that you will see.’

verses.name: Deuteronomy 3:29
verses.text: So we remained in the valley opposite Beth Peor.  <chapter eID="Deut.3"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 4:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1025"/><title type="x-s">Introduction to the Stipulations</title> <div sID="gen1322" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1025"/>“Now, Israel, listen to the rules and to the regulations that I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> teaching you to do, in order that you may live and you may go <transChange type="added">in</transChange> and you may take possession of the land that Yahweh, the God of your ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> <transChange type="added">is</transChange> giving to you.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 4:2
verses.text: You must not add to the word that I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> commanding you, and you shall not take away from it <transChange type="added">in order</transChange> to keep<note placement="foot">Or “observe”</note> the commands of Yahweh your God that I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> commanding you <transChange type="added">to observe</transChange>.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 4:3
verses.text: Your eyes have seen<note placement="foot">Literally “your eyes the seeing what”</note> what Yahweh did with<note placement="foot">Or “in”</note> the case of Baal Peor, for <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞each⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “every one of”</note> man that followed after Baal Peor Yahweh your God destroyed from your midst.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 4:4
verses.text: But you, the <transChange type="added">ones</transChange> holding fast to Yahweh your God, <transChange type="added">are</transChange> all alive <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞today⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the day”</note>  <div eID="gen1322" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 4:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1026"/><div sID="gen1323" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1026"/>See, I now teach<note placement="foot">Or “I have taught” (compare NASB, NEB)</note> you rules and regulations <transChange type="added">just</transChange> as Yahweh my God has commanded me, to observe <transChange type="added">them</transChange> <transChange type="added">just</transChange> so in the midst of the land where you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> going, to take possession of it.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 4:6
verses.text: And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you must observe them diligently⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “you must observe and you must do”</note> for that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> your wisdom and your insight before the eyes of the people, who will hear all <transChange type="added">of</transChange> these rules, and they will say, ‘Surely this great nation <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a wise and discerning people.’

verses.name: Deuteronomy 4:7
verses.text: For what great nation <transChange type="added">has</transChange> for it a god near to it as Yahweh our God, whenever<note placement="foot">Literally “in every matter/every time we call ”</note> we call <transChange type="added">upon</transChange> him?

verses.name: Deuteronomy 4:8
verses.text: And what <transChange type="added">other</transChange> great nation has for it<note placement="foot">Literally “which/that is for him it”</note> just rules and regulations just like<note placement="foot">Literally “as”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞this whole⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “all of”</note> law that I am setting <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the face of”</note> you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞today⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?<note placement="foot">Literally “the day”</note>  <div eID="gen1323" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 4:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1027"/><div sID="gen1324" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1027"/>“However, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞take care⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “watch”</note> for yourself and watch your inner self<note placement="foot">Or “soul”</note> closely, so that you do not forget the things that your eyes have seen, so that they do not slip from your mind all the days of your life; and you shall make them known to your children and to <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞your grandchildren⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the children of your children”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 4:10
