verses.text: indeed, you may set a king over you whom Yahweh your God will choose, from the midst of your countrymen<note placement="foot">Or “brothers”</note> you must set a king over you; you are not allowed to appoint over you a man, a foreigner, who is not your countryman.<note placement="foot">Or “brother”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 17:16
verses.text: Except, he may <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞not make numerous⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “not multiply”</note> for himself horses, and he may not allow the people to to go to Egypt <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in order to increase horses⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “in order to make numerous horse”</note> for Yahweh has said to you that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you may never return⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “not you may do again to return”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 17:17
verses.text: And he must not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞acquire many⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Or “make numerous”</note> wives for himself, so that his heart would turn aside; and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he must not accumulate silver and gold for himself excessively⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “gold and silver not he must make numerous for him very”</note>  <div eID="gen1401" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 17:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1095"/><div sID="gen1402" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1095"/>“<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it shall happen”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞when he is sitting⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “as/when his sitting”</note> on the throne of his kingdom, then he shall write for himself a copy of this law on a scroll <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the face of”</note> the Levitical priests.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 17:19
verses.text: And it shall be with him, and he shall read it<note placement="foot">Hebrew “in it”</note> all the days of his life, so that he may learn to revere Yahweh your God by <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞diligently observing⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by keeping ... to do them”</note> all the word of this law and these rules,

verses.name: Deuteronomy 17:20
verses.text: <transChange type="added">so as</transChange> not to exalt his heart above his countrymen<note placement="foot">Or “brothers”</note> and not to turn aside from the commandment to the right or to the left, so that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he may reign long over his kingdom⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “he may make long his days over his kingdom”</note> he and his children in the midst of Israel.”  <chapter eID="Deut.17"/> <div eID="gen1402" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 18:1
verses.text: “And there shall not be for the Levitical priests, the whole tribe of Levi, a plot of ground and an inheritance with Israel, <transChange type="added">rather</transChange> they may eat an offering made by fire <transChange type="added">as</transChange> their inheritance,<note placement="foot">The meaning of the Hebrew text here is uncertain; possibly it reads: “rather an offering by fire then they will eat as their inheritance/patrimony”</note> for Yahweh.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 18:2
verses.text: And there shall not be for them<note placement="foot">Hebrew “him”</note> an inheritance of land in the midst of his brothers; rather Yahweh is his inheritance, just as he <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞promised⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “spoke”</note> to them.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “him”</note>  <div eID="gen1403" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 18:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1096"/><div sID="gen1404" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1096"/>Now this shall be the share of the priest from the people, from <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞those who sacrifice the sacrifice⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the sacrificers of the sacrifice”</note> <transChange type="added">whether it is</transChange> an ox, sheep, or goat, and they shall give the priest the shoulder and the jawbones and the stomach.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 18:4
verses.text: The firstfruits<note placement="foot">Hebrew “firstfruit”</note> of your grain, your wine, and your olive oil and the firstfruits<note placement="foot">Hebrew “firstfruit”</note> of the fleece of your sheep you shall give to him.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 18:5
verses.text: For Yahweh your God has chosen him from <transChange type="added">among</transChange> all your tribes to stand to minister in the name of Yahweh, he and his sons <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “all of the days”</note>  <div eID="gen1404" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 18:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1097"/><div sID="gen1405" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1097"/>And if a<note placement="foot">Hebrew “the”</note> Levite comes from one of your <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞towns⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “gates”</note> from <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞anywhere in Israel⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “all of Israel”</note> where he is residing, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he may come whenever he desires⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “he may come in all the desire of his soul/inner self”</note> to the place that Yahweh will choose,

verses.name: Deuteronomy 18:7
verses.text: and he may minister in the name of Yahweh his God, <transChange type="added">just</transChange> like all his brothers, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the Levites who stand there⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the Levites the ones standing there”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the face of”</note> Yahweh.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 18:8
verses.text: They shall eat <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞equal portions⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “a portion like a portion”</note> apart from what he may receive from the sale of his patrimony.<note placement="foot">Hebrew meaning of these phrases/words is not certain; also could translate as “except what they receive from the sale of their fathers’ estates” (NASB); or “what he may inherit from his father’s family”</note>  <div eID="gen1405" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 18:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1098"/><div sID="gen1406" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1098"/>“When you come to the land that Yahweh your God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> giving to you, you must not learn to do like the detestable practices of those nations.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 18:10
verses.text: <transChange type="added">There</transChange> shall not be found among you one who makes his son or his daughter go through the fire, <transChange type="added">or</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞one who practices divination⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “a diviner of divination”</note> or an interpreter of signs,<note placement="foot">Or “soothsayer”</note> or an augur,<note placement="foot">Or “an interpreter of omens”</note> or sorcerer,

verses.name: Deuteronomy 18:11
verses.text: or one who casts magic spells, or one who consults <transChange type="added">a</transChange> spirit of the dead,<note placement="foot">Or “medium”</note> or spiritist, or one who inquires of the dead.<note placement="foot">Or “necromancer”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 18:12
verses.text: For everyone doing these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> <transChange type="added">is</transChange> detestable to Yahweh, and because of these detestable things Yahweh your God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> driving them out from <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the face of you”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 18:13
verses.text: You must be blameless before Yahweh your God.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 18:14
verses.text: For these nations that you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> about to dispossess listen to interpreters of signs<note placement="foot">Or “practice witchcraft”</note> and to diviners, but Yahweh your God has not allowed you to do the same.  <div eID="gen1406" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 18:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1099"/><div sID="gen1407" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1099"/>“Yahweh your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from your midst, from your countrymen,<note placement="foot">Or “your brothers”</note> <transChange type="added">and</transChange> to him you shall listen.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 18:16
verses.text: <transChange type="added">This is</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞according to all that you asked⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “just as all of that you asked”</note> from Yahweh your God at Horeb, on the day of the assembly, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to say”</note> ‘<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I do not want again to hear⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “not I want to do again to hear”</note> the voice of Yahweh my God, <transChange type="added">and</transChange> I do not want to see again this great fire, so that I may not die!’

verses.name: Deuteronomy 18:17
verses.text: And Yahweh said to me, ‘They are right <transChange type="added">in</transChange> what they have said.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 18:18
verses.text: I will raise up a prophet for them <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from among their countrymen⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from the midst of their brothers”</note> like you, and I will place<note placement="foot">Or “give”</note> my words into his mouth, and he shall speak to them <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞everything that I command him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “all of what I command him”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 18:19
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it will happen”</note> the man that will not listen to my words that he shall speak in my name, I will hold accountable.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 18:20
verses.text: However, the prophet that behaves presumptuously by speaking a word in my name that I have not commanded him to speak, and who speaks in the name of other gods, then that prophet shall die.’

verses.name: Deuteronomy 18:21
verses.text: And if you say <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to yourself⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “in your heart”</note> ‘How can we know the word that Yahweh has not spoken to him?’

verses.name: Deuteronomy 18:22
verses.text: <transChange type="added">Whenever</transChange> what the prophet spoke in the name of Yahweh, the thing does not take place and <transChange type="added">does</transChange> not come <transChange type="added">about</transChange>, that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the thing that Yahweh has not spoken to him.<note placement="foot">Or “that Yahweh has not spoken it”</note> Presumptuously the prophet spoke it; you shall not fear that<note placement="foot">Hebrew “the”</note> prophet.”  <chapter eID="Deut.18"/> <div eID="gen1407" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 19:1
verses.text: “When Yahweh your God has <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞exterminated⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “cut off”</note> the nations <transChange type="added">concerning whom</transChange> Yahweh your God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> giving to you their land, and you have dispossessed them, and you have settled in their towns and in their houses,

verses.name: Deuteronomy 19:2
verses.text: you shall set apart three cities for you in the midst of your land that Yahweh your God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> giving to you to take possession of it.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 19:3
verses.text: You shall prepare the roads<note placement="foot">Hebrew “road”</note> for yourselves, and you shall divide the regions of your land into thirds that Yahweh your God gives you as a possession, so that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞it will be available for any manslayer to flee there⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “it shall be to flee there all/anyone killing”</note>  <div eID="gen1408" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 19:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1100"/><div sID="gen1409" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1100"/>“Now this <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the case of the manslayer who may flee there and live <transChange type="added">there</transChange> who has killed his neighbor <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞unintentionally⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “with no knowledge”</note> and he did not hate him <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞previously⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “from yesterday and the day before”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 19:5
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞For example⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “And as”</note> when somebody goes with his neighbor into the forest to cut wood, and the iron <transChange type="added">head</transChange> slips from the handle <transChange type="added">of the tool</transChange> and strikes his neighbor and he dies, <transChange type="added">then</transChange> he may flee to one of these cities, and <transChange type="added">so</transChange> he may live.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 19:6
verses.text: <transChange type="added">He does this</transChange> lest the avenger of blood might pursue after the killer, because <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he is hot with anger⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “is hot his heart”</note> and he overtakes him, because it is a long distance to the city of refuge, and so <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he kills him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “he strikes him down as to his life/soul”</note> but <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he did not deserve a death sentence⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “for him there was not a judgment of death”</note> because he was not hating him <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “from yesterday and the day before”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 19:7
verses.text: Therefore I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> commanding you, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to say”</note> ‘You shall set apart three cities.’

verses.name: Deuteronomy 19:8
verses.text: Then if Yahweh your God enlarges your territory <transChange type="added">just</transChange> as he swore to your ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and gives<note placement="foot">Hebrew “will give”</note> to you all the land that he <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞promised⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “spoke”</note> to give to your ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 19:9
verses.text: <transChange type="added">then</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞if you diligently observe this entire commandment⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “if you observe all of the commandment the this to do it”</note> that I am commanding you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞today⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the day”</note> by loving Yahweh your God and by going<note placement="foot">Or “walking”</note> in his ways <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞at all times⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “all of the days”</note> then you shall add three more cities for yourselves to these three.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 19:10
verses.text: <transChange type="added">Do this</transChange> so that innocent blood will not be shed<note placement="foot">Hebrew “is not shed”</note> in the midst of your land that Yahweh your God is giving to you as an inheritance and thereby bloodguilt would be on you.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “shall be on you,” but conditional sense of imperfect is clear</note>  <div eID="gen1409" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 19:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1101"/><div sID="gen1410" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1101"/>But if someone hates<note placement="foot">Hebrew “is hating”</note> his neighbor and lies in wait for him and rises up<note placement="foot">Or “gets up”</note> against him <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞and murders him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “and strikes him mortally with regard to his life and he dies”</note> and <transChange type="added">the murderer</transChange> flees to one of these cities,

verses.name: Deuteronomy 19:12
verses.text: then the elders of his city shall send and take him from there, and they shall give him into the hand of the avenger of blood, and he shall be put to death.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 19:13
verses.text: Your eye shall not take pity on him, and you shall purge the guilt of innocent blood from Israel, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞so that good will be directed toward you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “and good shall be for you” or “it shall be good for you”</note>  <div eID="gen1410" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 19:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1102"/><div sID="gen1411" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1102"/>“You shall not move the boundary <transChange type="added">marker</transChange> of your neighbor that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞former generations⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the first settlers/ancestors”</note> set up on your property in the land that Yahweh your God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> giving to you to take possession of it.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 19:15
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞The testimony of a single witness may not be used to convict⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Not shall get up only a single witness against a man”</note> with respect to any crime and for any wrongdoing in any offense that a person<note placement="foot">Hebrew “he”</note> committed; on the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞evidence⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “mouth”</note> of two witnesses or on the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞evidence⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “mouth”</note> of three witnesses <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a charge shall be sustained⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “shall be established a case/charge”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 19:16
verses.text: If <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a malicious witness⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a witness of violence”</note> gets up <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to accuse⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “against”</note> anyone to testify against him falsely,

verses.name: Deuteronomy 19:17
verses.text: then the two men <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to whom the legal dispute pertains⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “who for them are the legal dispute”</note> shall stand <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the face of”</note> Yahweh, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the face of”</note> the priests and the judges who are <transChange type="added">in office</transChange> in those days.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 19:18
verses.text: Then judges shall make a thorough inquiry, and <transChange type="added">if</transChange> it turns out<note placement="foot">Or “in fact”</note> that the witness is a false witness <transChange type="added">and</transChange> he testified falsely against his brother,

verses.name: Deuteronomy 19:19
verses.text: then you shall do to him as he meant<note placement="foot">Or “planned”</note> to do to his brother, and so you shall purge the evil from your midst.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 19:20
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And the rest⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and those remaining”</note> shall hear and shall fear, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they shall not continue to do such a thing again⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and they shall not do again to do again”</note> as this evil thing in your midst.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 19:21
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞You must show no pity⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>:<note placement="foot">Literally “And not take pity your eye”</note> life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.”  <chapter eID="Deut.19"/> <div eID="gen1411" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 20:1
verses.text: “If you go out to war against your enemies and you see a horse and a chariot, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞an army⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a people”</note> larger that you, you shall not be afraid because of them; for Yahweh your God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> with you, the one who brought you from the land of Egypt.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 20:2
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it will happen”</note> when you approach the battle, then the priest shall come near and speak to the troops.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 20:3
verses.text: And he shall say to them, ‘Hear, Israel, you are near <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞today⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the day”</note> to the battle against your enemies; <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞do not lose heart⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “do not be faint/tender-hearted”</note> you shall not be afraid, and you shall not panic, and you shall not be terrified <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞because of them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “from their faces”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 20:4
verses.text: for Yahweh your God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> going with you to fight for you against your enemies to help you.’

verses.name: Deuteronomy 20:5
verses.text: And the officials shall speak to the troops, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to say”</note> ‘Who is the man who has built a new house and has not dedicated it? Let him go and return to this house, so that he does not die in battle and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞another man⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a man other”</note> dedicates it.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 20:6
verses.text: And who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the man that has planted a vineyard and has not enjoyed it? Let him go and let him return to his house, so that he does not die in battle and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞another man⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a man other”</note> enjoys it.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 20:7
verses.text: And who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the man who got engaged to a woman and <transChange type="added">has</transChange> not married her? Let him go and let him return to his house, so that he does not die in battle and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞another man⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a man other”</note> marries her.’

verses.name: Deuteronomy 20:8
verses.text: And the officials shall continue to speak to the troops, and they shall say, ‘<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞What man⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Who is the man”</note> is afraid <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞and disheartened⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?<note placement="foot">Literally “and soft/weak of the heart”</note> Let him go, and let him return to his house, and let him not cause the heart of his brothers to melt<note placement="foot">The verb has a causal meaning here</note> like his.’

verses.name: Deuteronomy 20:9
verses.text: And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞when the officials have finished speaking⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “it will happen as to finish the officials to speak”</note> to the army troops, then they shall appoint commanders of divisions at the head of the troops.  <div eID="gen1412" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 20:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1103"/><div sID="gen1413" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1103"/>“When you approach a city to fight against it, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you must offer it peace⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “you should call it for peace”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 20:11
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it will happen”</note> if <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they accept your terms of peace⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “if peace they reply to you”</note> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they surrender to you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “they open to you”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞and then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and it will happen”</note> all the people <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞inhabiting it⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “being found in it”</note> shall be forced labor for you, and they shall serve you.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 20:12
verses.text: But if they <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞do not accept your terms of peace⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “not they make peace with you”</note> and they want to make war with you, then you shall lay siege against it.<note placement="foot">That is, the city</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 20:13
verses.text: And Yahweh your God will give it into your hand, and you shall kill all its males with the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞edge⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “mouth”</note> of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> sword.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 20:14
verses.text: Only the women and the little children and the domestic animals<note placement="foot">Hebrew “animal”</note> and all that shall be in the city, all of its spoil you may loot for yourselves, and you may enjoy the spoil of your enemies that Yahweh you God has given to you.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 20:15
verses.text: Thus you shall do to all the far<note placement="foot">Or “distant”</note> cities from you, which are not from the cities of these nations located <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞nearby⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “here”</note>  <div eID="gen1413" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 20:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1104"/><div sID="gen1414" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1104"/>But from the cities of these peoples that Yahweh your God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> giving to you as an inheritance, you shall not let anything live that breathes.<note placement="foot">Or “is alive”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 20:17
verses.text: Rather, you shall utterly destroy them, the Hittites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Hittite”</note> and the Amorites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Amorite”</note> the Canaanites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Canaanite”</note> and the Perizzites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Perizzite”</note> the Hivites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Hivite”</note> and the Jebusites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Jebusite”</note> <transChange type="added">just</transChange> as Yahweh your God has commanded you,

verses.name: Deuteronomy 20:18
verses.text: so that they may not teach you to do like all their detestable things that they do for their gods and <transChange type="added">thereby</transChange> you sin against Yahweh your God.  <div eID="gen1414" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 20:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1105"/><div sID="gen1415" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1105"/>“If<note placement="foot">Or “when”</note> you besiege a town for many days to make war against it in order to seize it, you shall not destroy its trees by wielding an ax against them,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “it”</note> for you may eat from them,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “it”</note> and so you must not cut them<note placement="foot">Hebrew “it”</note> down. Are the trees of the field humans that they should come in siege <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞against you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?<note placement="foot">Literally “from your face”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 20:20
verses.text: Only<note placement="foot">Or “But”</note> the trees<note placement="foot">Hebrew “tree”</note> that you know <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞are not fruit trees⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “not a tree of food”</note> you may destroy and you may cut down, and you may build siege works against that city that is making war with you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞until it falls⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “it to fall”</note>  <chapter eID="Deut.20"/> <div eID="gen1415" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 21:1
verses.text: “If someone slain is found in the land that Yahweh your God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> giving to you to take possession of it <transChange type="added">and</transChange> <transChange type="added">is</transChange> lying in the field, <transChange type="added">and</transChange> it is not known who <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞killed him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “struck/smote him”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 21:2
verses.text: then your elders and your judges shall go out and shall measure <transChange type="added">the distance</transChange> to the cities that <transChange type="added">are</transChange> around the slain one.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 21:3
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it will happen”</note> the nearest city to the slain one, the elders of that city shall take a heifer of the herd that has not been worked with <transChange type="added">in the field</transChange>, that has not pulled a yoke,

verses.name: Deuteronomy 21:4
verses.text: and the elders of that city shall bring the heifer down to a <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞wadi that flows with water all year⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “an ever-flowing wadi”</note> and that has not been plowed and has not been sown; then <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞there they shall break the neck of the heifer in the wadi⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “they shall break there the neck with respect to the heifer in the ever-flowing wadi”; the Hebrew verb carries the meaning “to break the neck of”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 21:5
verses.text: Then the priests, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Levi, shall come near, for Yahweh your God has chosen them to bless in the name of Yahweh, and every legal dispute and every case of assault will be <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞subject to their ruling⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “on their mouth”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 21:6
verses.text: And all of the elders of that city nearest to the slain person shall wash their hands over the heifer <transChange type="added">with</transChange> the broken neck in the wadi.<note placement="foot">A valley that is dry most of the year, but contains a stream during the rainy season</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 21:7
verses.text: And they shall declare, and they shall say, ‘Our hands did not shed this blood, and our eyes did not see <transChange type="added">what was done</transChange>.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 21:8
verses.text: Forgive your people, Israel, whom you redeemed, Yahweh, and <transChange type="added">do</transChange> not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞allow⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “place/put”</note> the guilt of innocent blood in the midst of your people Israel, and let them be forgiven <transChange type="added">with regard to</transChange> blood.’

verses.name: Deuteronomy 21:9
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">so</transChange> you shall purge the innocent blood from your midst, because you must do the right thing in the eyes of Yahweh.  <div eID="gen1416" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 21:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1106"/><div sID="gen1417" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1106"/>“When you go out for battle against your enemies, and Yahweh your God gives them into your hand, and you lead the captives<note placement="foot">Hebrew “his captive” but singular pronoun refers to the many captives taken with plural sense</note> away,

verses.name: Deuteronomy 21:11
verses.text: and you see among the captives<note placement="foot">Hebrew “captive”</note> a woman beautiful in appearance, and you become attached to her and you want to take her as <transChange type="added">a</transChange> wife,

verses.name: Deuteronomy 21:12
verses.text: then you shall bring her into your household, and she shall shave her head, and she shall trim her nails.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 21:13
verses.text: And she shall remove the clothing of her captivity from her, and she shall remain in your house, and she shall mourn her father and her mother <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a full month⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “a month of days”</note> and after this <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you may have sex with her⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “you may go into her”</note> and you may marry her, and she may <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞become your wife⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “become for you as wife”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 21:14
verses.text: And then if you do not take delight in her, then you shall let her go <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to do whatever she wants⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “according to her desire/soul”</note> but you shall not treat her as a slave, since you have dishonored<note placement="foot">Or “humbled”</note> her.  <div eID="gen1417" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 21:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1107"/><div sID="gen1418" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1107"/>“If a man has two wives, <transChange type="added">and</transChange> the one <transChange type="added">is</transChange> loved and the <transChange type="added">other</transChange> one <transChange type="added">is</transChange> disliked and the one loved and the one that is disliked have borne for him sons, if it happens <transChange type="added">that</transChange> the firstborn son <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞belongs to the one that is disliked⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “is to the wife who is hated”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 21:16
verses.text: <transChange type="added">nevertheless</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞it will be the case that⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “it will happen”</note> on the day of bestowing his inheritance upon his sons, he will not be allowed to treat as the firstborn son the son of the beloved wife <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in preference to⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “over the faces of”</note> the son of the disliked <transChange type="added">wife</transChange>, <transChange type="added">who is</transChange> the firstborn <transChange type="added">son</transChange>.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 21:17
verses.text: But he shall acknowledge the firstborn son of the disliked <transChange type="added">wife</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞by giving⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to give”</note> him a double portion of <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞all that he has⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “all that is found for him”</note> for he is the firstfruit of his vigor;<note placement="foot">Or “the beginning of his strength”</note> to him is the legal claim of the birthright.<note placement="foot">Or “the just claim of the firstborn”</note>  <div eID="gen1418" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 21:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1108"/><div sID="gen1419" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1108"/>“<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞If a man has a stubborn and rebellious son⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “If shall be for a man, a son stubborn and rebellious”</note> who <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞does not listen to⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and there is no listening/obedience”</note> the voice of his father and to the voice of his mother, and they discipline him, and he does not obey<note placement="foot">Or “listen to”</note> them,

verses.name: Deuteronomy 21:19
verses.text: then his father and his mother shall take hold of him, and they shall bring him out to the elders of his city and to the gate of his <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞town⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “place”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 21:20
verses.text: and they shall say to the elders of his city, ‘This our son <transChange type="added">is</transChange> stubborn and rebellious; <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he does not obey us⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “there is no listening to our voice”</note> <transChange type="added">and</transChange> he is a glutton and a drunkard.’

verses.name: Deuteronomy 21:21
verses.text: Then all the men of his city shall stone him with stones and let him die; and so you shall purge the evil from your midst, and all of Israel will hear, and they will fear.  <div eID="gen1419" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 21:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1109"/><div sID="gen1420" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1109"/>“And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞if a man commits a sin punishable by death⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “when shall be against a man a sin of judgment of death”</note> and <transChange type="added">so</transChange> he is put to death and you hang him on a tree,

verses.name: Deuteronomy 21:23
verses.text: his dead body shall not hang on the tree, but certainly you shall bury him on that day, for cursed by God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> one that is <transChange type="added">being</transChange> hung; so you shall not defile your land<note placement="foot">Or “ground”</note> that Yahweh your God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> giving to you <transChange type="added">as an</transChange> inheritance.”  <chapter eID="Deut.21"/> <div eID="gen1420" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 22:1
verses.text: “You shall not watch the ox of your neighbor or his sheep or goat straying and ignore them; certainly you shall return them to your neighbor.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 22:2
verses.text: And if your countryman<note placement="foot">Or “brother”</note> is not near you or you do not know <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who he is⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “him”</note> then you shall bring it <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to your household⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to the midst of your house”</note> and it shall be<note placement="foot">Or “remain”</note> with you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞until your countryman seeks after it⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the seeking of your countryman after it”</note> and you shall return it to him.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 22:3
verses.text: And thus <transChange type="added">also</transChange> you shall do regarding<note placement="foot">Or “to”</note> his donkey, and thus you shall do concerning<note placement="foot">Or “to”</note> his garment, and so you shall do with respect to<note placement="foot">Or “to”</note> all of the lost property of your countryman<note placement="foot">Or “brother”</note> that is lost from him and you find it; you are not allowed to withhold help.  <div eID="gen1421" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 22:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1110"/><div sID="gen1422" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1110"/>“You shall not see the donkey of your neighbor or his ox fallen on the road and you ignore them; certainly you must help them <transChange type="added">get</transChange> up <transChange type="added">along</transChange> with him.  <div eID="gen1422" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 22:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1111"/><div sID="gen1423" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1111"/>“The apparel of a man shall not be <transChange type="added">put</transChange> on<note placement="foot">Literally “on”</note> a woman, and a man shall not wear the clothing of a woman, because everyone who does these things is detestable to Yahweh your God.  <div eID="gen1423" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 22:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1112"/><div sID="gen1424" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1112"/>“If a bird’s nest is found <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “before your face”</note> on the road in any tree or on the ground, <transChange type="added">and there are</transChange> chicks or eggs, and the mother <transChange type="added">is</transChange> lying down on the chicks or the eggs, you shall not take the mother along with the young;

verses.name: Deuteronomy 22:7
verses.text: you shall certainly let the mother go, but you may take the young for yourselves;<note placement="foot">Hebrew “for you”</note> do this <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞so that it may go well⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “he/it is good”</note> for you and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you may live long in the land⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “and you may make long/extend days”</note>  <div eID="gen1424" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 22:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1113"/><div sID="gen1425" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1113"/>“When you build a new house then<note placement="foot">Hebrew “and”</note> you shall make a parapet wall<note placement="foot">Or “fence/rail”</note> for your roof, so that you will not bring bloodguilt on your house <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞if anyone should fall from it⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “if should fall the falling from it”</note>  <div eID="gen1425" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 22:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1114"/><div sID="gen1426" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1114"/>“You shall not sow your vineyard <transChange type="added">with</transChange> differing kinds <transChange type="added">of seed</transChange>, so that you shall not forfeit <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the whole harvest⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the entire fullness”</note> <transChange type="added">both</transChange> the seed that you sowed and the yield of the vineyard.  <div eID="gen1426" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 22:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1115"/><div sID="gen1427" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1115"/>“You shall not plow with an ox and with a donkey <transChange type="added">yoked</transChange> together.  <div eID="gen1427" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 22:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1116"/><div sID="gen1428" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1116"/>“You shall not wear woven material <transChange type="added">made of</transChange> wool and linen <transChange type="added">mixed</transChange> together.  <div eID="gen1428" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 22:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1117"/><div sID="gen1429" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1117"/>“You shall make tassels for yourselves<note placement="foot">Hebrew “for you”</note> on the four corners of your clothing with which you cover <transChange type="added">yourself</transChange>.  <div eID="gen1429" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 22:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1118"/><div sID="gen1430" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1118"/>“If a man takes a woman and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he has sex with her⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “and he goes unto her”</note> but he then <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞dislikes her⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “hates her”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 22:14
verses.text: and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he accuses her falsely⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “he puts to her deeds of words”</note> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he defames her⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “he brings forth against her a bad name”</note> and he says ‘This woman I took and I lay with her and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I discovered that she was not a virgin⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,’<note placement="foot">Literally “I found not with her virginity”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 22:15
verses.text: then <transChange type="added">in defense</transChange> the father of the young woman shall take, along with her mother, and <transChange type="added">together</transChange> they must bring out the <transChange type="added">evidence of</transChange> the virginity of the young woman <transChange type="added">to display it</transChange> to the elders of the city <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞at the city gate⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “toward the city gate”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 22:16
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">then</transChange> the father of the young woman shall say to the elders, ‘I gave my daughter to this man as wife, but he <transChange type="added">now</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞dislikes⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “hates”</note> her,

verses.name: Deuteronomy 22:17
verses.text: and now look <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he has accused her falsely⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “he put deeds of words”</note> saying, “I did not find <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞your daughter a virgin⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,”<note placement="foot">Literally “to your daughter virginity”</note> but here is evidence of the virginity of my daughter’; and they shall spread the cloth out <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the face of”</note> the elders of the city.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 22:18
verses.text: Then the elders of that city shall take the man, and they shall discipline him.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 22:19
verses.text: Then they shall fine him <transChange type="added">a</transChange> hundred <transChange type="added">shekels of</transChange> silver, and they shall give <transChange type="added">them</transChange> to the father of the young woman, for <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he defamed an Israelite young woman⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “for he brought out a bad name against the virgin of Israel”</note> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞she shall become his wife⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “and for him she shall become as wife”</note> he will not be allowed <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to divorce her⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to send her out”</note> all his days.  <div eID="gen1430" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 22:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1119"/><div sID="gen1431" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1119"/>“But if <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞this charge⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the thing”</note> was true, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞and the signs of virginity were not found⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and they were not found evidence of virginity”</note> for the young woman,

verses.name: Deuteronomy 22:21
verses.text: and <transChange type="added">then</transChange> they shall bring out the young woman to the doorway of the house of her father, and the men of her city shall stone her with stones, and she shall die, because she did a disgraceful thing in Israel <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞by playing the harlot⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to play the harlot/to prostitute herself”</note> <transChange type="added">in</transChange> the house of her father, and so you shall purge the evil from your midst.  <div eID="gen1431" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 22:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1120"/><div sID="gen1432" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1120"/>“If a man is found lying <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞with a married woman⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “with a woman, a young woman of a husband”</note> then they shall both die; <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞both of them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “also/even the two of them”</note> the man who lay with the woman and the woman <transChange type="added">also</transChange>, so you shall purge the evil from Israel.  <div eID="gen1432" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 22:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1121"/><div sID="gen1433" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1121"/>“If it happens <transChange type="added">that</transChange> a young woman, a virgin, <transChange type="added">is</transChange> engaged to a man, <transChange type="added">and</transChange> a man finds her in the town and lies with her,

verses.name: Deuteronomy 22:24
verses.text: then you shall bring out <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞both of them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the two of them”</note> to the gate of that city, and you shall stone them with stones so that they shall die, the young woman because she did not cry out in the town, and the man because<note placement="foot">Literally “because of the fact that”</note> he violated his neighbor’s wife; and so you shall purge the evil from your midst.  <div eID="gen1433" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 22:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1122"/><div sID="gen1434" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1122"/>“But if the man finds the young engaged woman in the field and the man overpowers her and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he has sex with her⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “he lies down with her”</note> then the man only<note placement="foot">Or “alone”</note> must die who lay<note placement="foot">Or “slept”</note> with her.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 22:26
verses.text: But you shall not do anything<note placement="foot">Hebrew “a thing”</note> to the young woman, for there is not reckoned against<note placement="foot">Hebrew “to”</note> the young woman <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a sin deserving death⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “a sin of death”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞it is similar to when⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for as that”</note> a man rises up against his neighbor and murders him, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a fellow human being⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “a soul/individual person”</note> just so is this <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞case⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “thing/matter”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 22:27
verses.text: for he found her in the field, the engaged young woman cried out, but there was no<note placement="foot">Hebrew “there was not”</note> rescuer <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to help her⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “for her”</note>  <div eID="gen1434" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 22:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1123"/><div sID="gen1435" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1123"/>“If a man finds a young woman, a virgin <transChange type="added">who</transChange> is not engaged, and he seizes her and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he has sex with her⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “he lies with her”</note> and they are caught,

verses.name: Deuteronomy 22:29
verses.text: then <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the man who lay with her⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the man the one lying with her”</note> shall give to the father of the young woman fifty shekels of silver, and she shall become <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his wife⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for/as a wife”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞because⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in place of”</note> he violated her, and he is not allowed to divorce her <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞during his lifetime⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “all of his days”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 22:30
verses.text: <note placement="foot"><reference osisRef="Deut.22.30-Deut.23.25">Deuteronomy 22:30–23:25 </reference>in the English Bible is 23:1–26 in the Hebrew Bible</note> A man may not take the wife of his father, and so <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he may not dishonor his father⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “not he may reveal the skirt of the garment of his father”</note>  <chapter eID="Deut.22"/> <div eID="gen1435" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 23:1
verses.text: “No man <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞with crushed testicles⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “bruised of crushing”</note> or whose <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞male organ is cut off⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “cut off of male organ”</note> may come into the assembly of Yahweh.  <div eID="gen1436" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 23:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1124"/><div sID="gen1437" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1124"/>An illegitimate child may not come into the assembly of Yahweh; even <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the tenth generation none <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞of his descendants⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to him”</note> may come into the assembly of Yahweh.  <div eID="gen1437" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 23:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1125"/><div sID="gen1438" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1125"/>An Ammonite or a Moabite may not come into the assembly of Yahweh; even <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the tenth generation none <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞of his descendants⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to him”</note> may come into the assembly of Yahweh <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “until eternity”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 23:4
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞because⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “because of the event when”</note> they did not come to meet you with food and with water <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞when you came out of Egypt⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “at your going out of Egypt”</note> and also <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞because⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “because of the event when”</note> they<note placement="foot">Hebrew “he,” but with plural meaning</note> hired Balaam, son of Beor, from Pethor, in Aram Naharaim<note placement="foot">Or “Mesopotamia” = “between the rivers”</note> <transChange type="added">to act</transChange> against you to curse you.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 23:5
verses.text: But Yahweh your God was not willing to listen to Balaam, and Yahweh your God turned the curse into a blessing for you, because Yahweh your God loved you.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 23:6
verses.text: You shall not promote their welfare or their prosperity all your days <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “until eternity”</note>  <div eID="gen1438" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 23:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1126"/><div sID="gen1439" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1126"/>“You shall not abhor an Edomite, because he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> your brother; you shall not abhor an Egyptian because you were an alien in his land.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 23:8
verses.text: The children<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> that are born to them in the third generation may come <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞representing them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for them” or possibly “become members of”</note> in the assembly of Yahweh.  <div eID="gen1439" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 23:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1127"/><div sID="gen1440" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1127"/>“If<note placement="foot">Or “when”</note> you go out to encamp against your enemies, then you shall guard against <transChange type="added">doing</transChange> anything evil.  <div eID="gen1440" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 23:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1128"/><div sID="gen1441" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1128"/>“If <transChange type="added">there</transChange> is among you a man that is not clean because of a seminal emission <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞during the night⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “of the night”</note> he shall go outside the camp; he shall not come within the camp.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 23:11
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it will happen/come about that”</note> toward the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞coming⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “turning”</note> of the evening, he shall bathe with<note placement="foot">Hebrew “in” but this is instrumental use of this preposition</note> water, and at the going down<note placement="foot">The verb can mean “coming/going” and here it means “going”</note> of the sun, he may come to the midst of the camp.  <div eID="gen1441" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 23:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1129"/><div sID="gen1442" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1129"/>“And there shall be for you a designated place outside the camp; <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞and you shall go there to relieve yourself⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “and you shall go out there, outside to relieve yourself”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 23:13
verses.text: and a digging tool<note placement="foot">Or “spade”</note> shall be included in addition to your other utensils<note placement="foot">Hebrew “utensil”</note> for yourself; <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞and then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and it will happen”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞when you relieve yourself⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “at your sitting”</note> outside <transChange type="added">the camp</transChange> you shall dig with it, and <transChange type="added">then</transChange> you shall turn, and you shall cover your excrement.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 23:14
verses.text: For Yahweh your God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> walking about in the midst of your camp to deliver you and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to hand your enemies over to you before you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to give your enemies to the face of you”</note> and so let your camp be holy, so that he shall not see in it <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞anything indecent⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “nakedness of a thing”</note> and he shall turn away <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from going with you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “from behind/after you”</note>  <div eID="gen1442" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 23:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1130"/><div sID="gen1443" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1130"/>“And you shall not hand over a slave to his master who has escaped <transChange type="added">and fled</transChange> to you from his master.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 23:16
verses.text: He shall reside with you in your midst in the place that he chooses in one of <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞your towns wherever he pleases⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “in your gates good for him”</note> you shall not oppress him.  <div eID="gen1443" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 23:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1131"/><div sID="gen1444" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1131"/>“No woman <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞of Israel⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from the daughters of Israel”</note> shall be a temple prostitute, and no man <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞of Israel⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from the sons of Israel”</note> shall be a male shrine prostitute.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 23:18
verses.text: You may not bring the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞hire⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “gift”</note> of a prostitute or <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the earnings of a male prostitute⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the earnings of a dog”</note> into the house of Yahweh your God, for any vow offerings, because <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞both⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “both, the two of them”</note> are a detestable thing to Yahweh your God.  <div eID="gen1444" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 23:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1132"/><div sID="gen1445" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1132"/>“<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞You shall not charge your brother interest on money⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “You shall not lend on interest to your brother, interest of money”</note> interest on<note placement="foot">Hebrew “of”</note> food, or interest on<note placement="foot">Hebrew “of”</note> anything that one could lend<note placement="foot">Or “can lend”</note> on interest.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 23:20
verses.text: You may lend on interest to the foreigner, but to your countryman<note placement="foot">Or “brother”</note> you may not lend on interest, so that Yahweh your God may bless you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in all your undertakings⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in all the sendings out of your hand”</note> in <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the land where you are going⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the land that you are going there”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in order to take possession of it⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “to take possession”</note>  <div eID="gen1445" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 23:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1133"/><div sID="gen1446" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1133"/>“<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞When you make a vow⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “When/if you vow a vow”</note> to Yahweh your God, you shall not postpone <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞fulfillment of it⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to fulfill it”</note> for certainly Yahweh your God shall require it from you and if postponed <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you will incur guilt⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “it shall become against you as sin”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 23:22
verses.text: And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞if you refrain from vowing⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “if you refrain to make a vow”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you shall not incur guilt⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “it shall not become against you as sin”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 23:23
verses.text: The utterance of your lips <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you must perform diligently⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “you must observe and you shall do”</note> just as you have vowed freely to Yahweh your God whatever it was that you promised<note placement="foot">Or “spoke”</note> with your mouth.  <div eID="gen1446" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 23:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1134"/><div sID="gen1447" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1134"/>“When<note placement="foot">Or “If”</note> you come into the vineyard of your neighbor, then you may eat grapes <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as you please⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “according to your desire”</note> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞until you are full⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to your satiation”</note> but you shall not put <transChange type="added">any</transChange> into your container.  <div eID="gen1447" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 23:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1135"/><div sID="gen1448" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1135"/>“When<note placement="foot">Or “If”</note> you come into the standing grain of your neighbor, then you may pluck ears with your hand, but you may not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞swing⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “wave”</note> a sickle among the standing grain of your neighbor.”  <chapter eID="Deut.23"/> <div eID="gen1448" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 24:1
verses.text: “When<note placement="foot">Or “If”</note> a man takes a wife and he marries her <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞and then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and it will happen”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞she does not please him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “if not she finds favor in his eyes”</note> because he found <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞something objectionable⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “shameful/repulsive thing”</note> and writes her a letter of divorce and puts <transChange type="added">it</transChange> in her hand and sends her <transChange type="added">away</transChange> from his house,

verses.name: Deuteronomy 24:2
verses.text: and she goes from his house, and she goes <transChange type="added">out</transChange> and becomes <transChange type="added">a wife</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞for another man⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “for a man other”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 24:3
verses.text: and <transChange type="added">then</transChange> the second man dislikes her and he writes her a letter of divorce and places <transChange type="added">it</transChange> into her hand and sends her from his house, or if the second man dies who took her <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to himself⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to for him”</note> as a wife,

verses.name: Deuteronomy 24:4
verses.text: her first husband who sent her <transChange type="added">away</transChange> is not allowed <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to take her again⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to return to take her”</note> to become a wife to him after she has <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞been defiled⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “become unclean”</note> for that is a detestable thing <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the face of”</note> Yahweh, and <transChange type="added">so</transChange> you shall not mislead into sin the land that Yahweh your God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> giving to you <transChange type="added">as an</transChange> inheritance.  <div eID="gen1449" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 24:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1136"/><div sID="gen1450" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1136"/>“When<note placement="foot">Or “If”</note> a man takes a new wife he shall not go out with the army, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he shall not be obligated with anything⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “he shall not come across come over upon him to anything”</note> he shall be free from obligation, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to stay at home⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for his house”</note> for one year, and he shall bring joy <transChange type="added">to</transChange> his wife that he took.  <div eID="gen1450" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 24:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1137"/><div sID="gen1451" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1137"/>“A person<note placement="foot">Hebrew “he”</note> shall not take<note placement="foot">Or “require”</note> a pair of millstones or an upper millstone, for <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he is taking necessities of life as a pledge⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “for a life he is taking as a pledge”</note>  <div eID="gen1451" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 24:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1138"/><div sID="gen1452" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1138"/>“If a man is <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞caught⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “found”</note> kidnapping somebody from among his countrymen,<note placement="foot">Or “brothers”</note> the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> and he treats him as a slave or he sells him, then that kidnapper shall die, and so you shall purge the evil <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from among you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “from your midst”</note>  <div eID="gen1452" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 24:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1139"/><div sID="gen1453" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1139"/>Be watchful<note placement="foot">Or “Be careful”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞with respect to⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “against”</note> an outbreak of any infectious skin disease, by being very careful and by acting<note placement="foot">Or “doing”</note> according to all that the priests and the Levites have instructed you, just as I have commanded them, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞so you shall diligently observe⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “so you shall observe to do”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 24:9
verses.text: <transChange type="added">So</transChange> remember what Yahweh your God did to Miriam on the journey <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞when you went out from Egypt⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “in you to go out from Egypt”</note>  <div eID="gen1453" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 24:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1140"/><div sID="gen1454" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1140"/>“When you make a loan to your neighbor, a loan of any kind, you shall not go into his house <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to take his pledge⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “to pledge with respect to his pledge”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 24:11
verses.text: You shall wait outside, and the man <transChange type="added">to</transChange> whom you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> lending, he shall bring the pledge outside to you.

verses.name: Deuteronomy 24:12
verses.text: And if <transChange type="added">he is</transChange> a needy man, you shall not sleep in his pledge.<note placement="foot">“His pledge” refers to “a garment given as pledge”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 24:13
verses.text: You shall certainly return the pledge to him <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as the sun sets⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “as/at the moment of the going out of the sun”</note> so that he may sleep in his cloak and may bless you, and it shall be considered righteousness <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞on your behalf⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to you”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the face of”</note> Yahweh your God.  <div eID="gen1454" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 24:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1141"/><div sID="gen1455" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1141"/>“You shall not exploit a hired worker, <transChange type="added">who is</transChange> needy and poor, from among your fellow men or from <transChange type="added">among</transChange> your aliens<note placement="foot">Hebrew “alien”</note> who are in your land and in your <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞towns⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “gates”</note>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 24:15
verses.text: On his day you shall give his wage, and the sun shall not go <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞down⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “over him”</note> because he is poor and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his life depends on it⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “and to him it is a lifting up with respect to his life/soul”</note> do this so that he does not cry out against you to Yahweh, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞and you incur guilt⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “and it becomes against you as sin</note>  <div eID="gen1455" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Deuteronomy 24:16
