verses.text: And when Yahweh raised leaders<note placement="foot">Or “judges”</note> for them, Yahweh was with the leader,<note placement="foot">Or “judge”</note> and he delivered them from the hand of their enemies all the days of the leader,<note placement="foot">Or “judge”</note> for Yahweh was moved by their groaning because of their persecutors and oppressors.

verses.name: Judges 2:19
verses.text: But when the leader<note placement="foot">Or “judge”</note> died they relapsed and acted corruptly, more than their ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> following other gods, serving them,<note placement="foot">Or “worshiping them”</note> and bowing down to them. They would not give up their deeds or their stubborn ways.

verses.name: Judges 2:20
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞So the anger of Yahweh burned⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “So the nose of Yahweh became hot”</note> against Israel, and he said, “Because this people transgressed my covenant that I commanded their ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and have not obeyed my voice,

verses.name: Judges 2:21
verses.text: I will not again drive out anyone from before them from the nations that Joshua left when he died,

verses.name: Judges 2:22
verses.text: in order to test Israel whether or not they would observe the way of Yahweh, to walk in it just as their ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> did.”

verses.name: Judges 2:23
verses.text: So Yahweh left those nations; he did not drive them out at once, and he did not give them into the hand of Joshua.  <chapter eID="Judg.2"/>

verses.name: Judges 3:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1428"/><title type="x-s">Some Nations Remain in the Land</title> <div sID="gen1935" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1428"/>These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the nations that Yahweh left, to test Israel by them (<transChange type="added">that is, to test</transChange> all those who <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞had not experienced⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “did not know”</note> any of the wars of Canaan,

verses.name: Judges 3:2
verses.text: in order that the generations of Israel would know war, to teach those <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who had not experienced it⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “who had not known it”</note> before):

verses.name: Judges 3:3
verses.text: the five rulers of the Philistines, all the Canaanites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Canaanite”</note> the Sidonians,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Sidonian”</note> and the Hivites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Hivite”</note> living on Mount Lebanon, from Mount Baal Hermon up to Lebo-Hamath.

verses.name: Judges 3:4
verses.text: They were <transChange type="added">left</transChange> for testing Israel, to know <transChange type="added">whether</transChange> they would keep the commands of Yahweh that he commanded their ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> through the hand of Moses.

verses.name: Judges 3:5
verses.text: And the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> lived in the midst of the Canaanites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Canaanite”</note> the Hittites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Hittite”</note> the Amorites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Amorite”</note> the Perizzites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Perizzite”</note> the Hivites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Hivite”</note> and the Jebusites.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Jebusite”</note>

verses.name: Judges 3:6
verses.text: And they took their daughters as wives for themselves, and they gave their daughters to their sons, and they served their gods.<note placement="foot">Or “worshiped their gods”</note>  <div eID="gen1935" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 3:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1429"/><title type="x-s">Othniel</title> <div sID="gen1936" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1429"/>The <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> did evil in the eyes of Yahweh. They forgot Yahweh their God, and they served the Baals and the Asheroth.<note placement="foot">Asheroth are cultic poles set up next to an altar symbolizing the goddess Asherah</note>

verses.name: Judges 3:8
verses.text: And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the anger of Yahweh was kindled⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the nose of Yahweh became hot”</note> against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of Cushan-Rishathaim, the king of Aram Naharaim; and the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> served Cushan-Rishathaim eight years.

verses.name: Judges 3:9
verses.text: The <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> cried out to Yahweh, and Yahweh raised up a deliverer for the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> who delivered them, Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother.

verses.name: Judges 3:10
verses.text: And the spirit of Yahweh came upon him, and he judged Israel. He went out to war, and Yahweh gave Cushan-Rishathaim king of Aram into his hand, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he prevailed over⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “his hand was strong over”</note> Cushan-Rishathaim.

verses.name: Judges 3:11
verses.text: So the land rested forty years. Then Othniel son of Kenaz died.  <div eID="gen1936" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 3:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1430"/><title type="x-s">Ehud</title> <div sID="gen1937" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1430"/>And again the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> did evil in the eyes of Yahweh. So Yahweh strengthened Eglon king of Moab against Israel, because they did evil in the eyes of Yahweh.

verses.name: Judges 3:13
verses.text: He gathered to himself the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites and Amalekites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons of Ammon and Amalek” or “children of Ammon and Amalek”</note> and he went and defeated Israel, and they took possession of the city of palms.

verses.name: Judges 3:14
verses.text: And the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> served Eglon king of Moab eighteen years.  <div eID="gen1937" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 3:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1431"/><div sID="gen1938" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1431"/>And the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> cried out to Yahweh, and Yahweh raised up for them a deliverer, Ehud son of Gera, a Benjaminite and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a left-handed man⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “a man bound by his right hand”</note> And the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> sent a tribute to Eglon king of Moab <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞through him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “in his hand”</note>

verses.name: Judges 3:16
verses.text: Ehud made for himself a short, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞two-edged⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “with two mouths”</note> sword (a cubit in length), and he fastened it under his clothes on his right thigh.

verses.name: Judges 3:17
verses.text: Then he presented the tribute to Eglon king of Moab. Now Eglon <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a very fat man.

verses.name: Judges 3:18
verses.text: When Ehud<note placement="foot">That is, Eglon</note> had finished presenting the tribute, he sent away the people who carried the tribute.

verses.name: Judges 3:19
verses.text: But he turned back from the sculptured stones<note placement="foot">Or “Pesilim”; some translations translate the phrase as a proper name</note> that were near Gilgal, and he said, “I have <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a secret message⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a word of secrecy”</note> for you, O king.” And he<note placement="foot">Hebrew “he”</note> said, “Silence!” So all those standing in his presence went out,

verses.name: Judges 3:20
verses.text: and Ehud came to him <transChange type="added">while</transChange> he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> sitting alone in his cool upper room. And Ehud said, “I have a <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞message from God⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “word of God”</note> for you.” So he got up from his seat.

verses.name: Judges 3:21
verses.text: Then Ehud reached with his left hand for the sword on his right thigh, and he thrust it into his<note placement="foot">That is, Eglon’s</note> stomach.

verses.name: Judges 3:22
verses.text: And the handle also went <transChange type="added">in</transChange> after the blade, and the fat closed over the blade because he did not draw back the sword from his stomach; and it went protruding out the back.<note placement="foot">The Hebrew is uncertain; some translations have “and the dirt/entrails came out”</note>

verses.name: Judges 3:23
verses.text: And Ehud went out the vestibule, and he closed the doors of the upper room and locked <transChange type="added">them</transChange> behind him.  <div eID="gen1938" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 3:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1432"/><div sID="gen1939" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1432"/>After he left, his servants returned. When they saw <transChange type="added">that</transChange> the doors of the upper room <transChange type="added">were</transChange> locked, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they thought⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “they said”</note> “Surely he is <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞relieving himself⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “covering his feet”</note> in the cool inner room.”

verses.name: Judges 3:25
verses.text: And they waited so long they became embarrassed because he did not open the doors of the upper room. So they took the key and opened <transChange type="added">the doors</transChange>, and there their lord was lying on the ground dead.  <div eID="gen1939" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 3:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1433"/><div sID="gen1940" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1433"/>And Ehud escaped while they delayed. He passed by the sculptured stones<note placement="foot">Or “Pesilim;” some translations to translate the phrase as a proper name</note> and escaped to Seirah.

verses.name: Judges 3:27
verses.text: And when he arrived he sounded the trumpet in the hill country of Ephraim, and the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> went down from the hill country with him leading them.

verses.name: Judges 3:28
verses.text: And he said to them, “Follow after me! Yahweh has given Moab your enemies into your hand.” So they went down after him, and they captured the fords of the Jordan toward Moab; and they did not allow anyone to cross over.

verses.name: Judges 3:29
verses.text: And they struck Moab at that time, about ten thousand men, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞all strong and able men⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “all fat and men of strength”</note> no one escaped.

verses.name: Judges 3:30
verses.text: And Moab was subdued on that day under the hand of Israel. And the land rested eighty years.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “year”</note>  <div eID="gen1940" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 3:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1434"/><title type="x-s">Shamgar</title> <div sID="gen1941" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1434"/>And Shamgar son of Anath came after him, and he killed six hundred Philistines with the goad of an ox; he also delivered Israel.  <chapter eID="Judg.3"/>

verses.name: Judges 4:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1435"/><title type="x-s">Deborah and Barak</title> <div sID="gen1942" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1435"/>And again the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> did evil in the eyes of Yahweh, and Ehud died.

verses.name: Judges 4:2
verses.text: So Yahweh sold them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor. The commander of his army <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Sisera, and he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> living in Harosheth Haggoyim.

verses.name: Judges 4:3
verses.text: And the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> cried to Yahweh, as he had nine hundred iron chariots,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “chariot”</note> and he oppressed the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞cruelly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “with force”</note> for twenty years.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “year”</note>  <div eID="gen1942" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 4:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1436"/><div sID="gen1943" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1436"/>Now at that time Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lappidoth, <transChange type="added">was</transChange> judging<note placement="foot">Or “leading”</note> Israel.

verses.name: Judges 4:5
verses.text: And she used to sit under the palm tree of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim; and the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> went up to her for judgment.

verses.name: Judges 4:6
verses.text: She sent and called for Barak son of Abinoam from Kedesh Naphtali and said to him, “Has not Yahweh the God of Israel commanded you? ‘Go, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞march to⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “take the lead at”</note> Mount Tabor, and take ten thousand men from the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons/children”</note> of Naphtali and Zebulun.

verses.name: Judges 4:7
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I will draw out⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “I will draw to you”</note> Sisera, the commander of Jabin’s army, with his chariots and troops, to the wadi<note placement="foot">A valley that is dry most of the year, but contains a stream during the rainy season</note> of Kishon, and I will give him into your hand.’ ”

verses.name: Judges 4:8
verses.text: Barak said to her, “If you go with me, I will go; but if you do not go with me, I will not go.”

verses.name: Judges 4:9
verses.text: She said, “Surely I will go with you; however, there will be no glory for you in <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the path you are taking⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Or “the way you are going”</note> for Yahweh will sell Sisera into <transChange type="added">the</transChange> hand of a woman.” And Deborah stood up and went with Barak to Kedesh.

verses.name: Judges 4:10
verses.text: Barak summoned Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh; and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they went up behind him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “they went up in his feet”</note> ten thousand men, and Deborah went up with him.  <div eID="gen1943" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 4:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1437"/><div sID="gen1944" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1437"/>And Heber the Kenite <transChange type="added">was</transChange> separated from <transChange type="added">the other</transChange> Kenites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Kenite”</note> that is, from the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons/children”</note> of Hobab the father-in-law of Moses. And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he was encamped⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “he spread his tent”</note> at Elon-bezaanannim, which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> near Kedesh.  <div eID="gen1944" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 4:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1438"/><div sID="gen1945" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1438"/>When they<note placement="foot">The subject is not specified in Hebrew</note> reported to Sisera that Barak son of Abinoam had gone up to Mount Tabor,

verses.name: Judges 4:13
verses.text: Sisera summoned all his chariots—all nine hundred chariots<note placement="foot">Hebrew “chariot”</note> of iron—and the entire army that was with him from Harosheth Haggoyim to the wadi<note placement="foot">A valley that is dry most of the year, but contains a stream during the rainy season</note> of Kishon.

verses.name: Judges 4:14
verses.text: And Deborah said to Barak, “Get up! This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the day that Yahweh has given Sisera into your hand. Has Yahweh not gone out before you?” So Barak went out from Mount Tabor with ten thousand men following him.

verses.name: Judges 4:15
verses.text: And Yahweh threw Sisera and all his chariots and army into confusion<note placement="foot">Or “routed Sisera and all his chariots and army”</note> before <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the edge of Barak’s sword⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “the mouth of the sword before Barak”</note> and Sisera dismounted from <transChange type="added">his</transChange> chariot and fled on foot.

verses.name: Judges 4:16
verses.text: But Barak pursued after the chariots<note placement="foot">Hebrew “chariot”</note> and army as far as Harosheth Haggoyim, and all of Sisera’s army fell to <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the edge of the sword⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “the mouth of the sword”</note> no one was left.  <div eID="gen1945" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 4:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1439"/><div sID="gen1946" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1439"/>Sisera fled on foot to the tent of Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, because <transChange type="added">there was</transChange> peace between Jabin king of Hazor and the house of Heber the Kenite.

verses.name: Judges 4:18
verses.text: And Jael came out to meet Sisera, and she said to him, “Turn aside, my lord; turn aside to me and do not be afraid.” So he turned aside into her tent, and she covered him <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞with a blanket⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “with a covering/rug”</note>

verses.name: Judges 4:19
verses.text: And he said to her, “Please, give me a drink of water, because I am thirsty.” So she opened a skin vessel of milk and gave him a drink and covered him.

verses.name: Judges 4:20
verses.text: And he said to her, “Stand <transChange type="added">at</transChange> the doorway of the tent, and if anyone comes and asks you, and says, ‘Is there anyone here?’ You must answer, ‘No.’ ”

verses.name: Judges 4:21
verses.text: But Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, took in her hand a tent peg and a hammer, and she went softly<note placement="foot">Or “secretly”</note> to him and drove the peg into his temple, and it went through into the ground; he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> fast asleep since he was exhausted, and he died.

verses.name: Judges 4:22
verses.text: And behold, Barak <transChange type="added">was</transChange> pursuing Sisera, and Jael went out to meet him, and she said to him, “Come, and I will show you the man whom you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> seeking.” And he came with her and saw that Sisera was lying dead with the peg in his temple.

verses.name: Judges 4:23
verses.text: On that day God subdued Jabin king of Canaan before the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note>

verses.name: Judges 4:24
verses.text: And the hand of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞pressed harder⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “went harder”</note> and harder on Jabin king of Canaan, until they destroyed Jabin king of Canaan.  <chapter eID="Judg.4"/>

verses.name: Judges 5:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1440"/><title type="x-s">The Song of Deborah and Barak</title> <div sID="gen1947" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1440"/>And Deborah and Barak son of Abinoam sang on that day:  <div eID="gen1947" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 5:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1441"/><lg sID="gen1948"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1949"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1441"/>“When long hair hangs loosely in Israel,<l eID="gen1949" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1950"/>when the people willingly offer themselves,<l eID="gen1950" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen1951"/>bless Yahweh! <l eID="gen1951" level="3"/>

verses.name: Judges 5:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1442"/><l level="1" sID="gen1952"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1442"/>Hear, O kings! Give ear, O princes!<l eID="gen1952" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1953"/>I will sing to Yahweh;<l eID="gen1953" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1954"/>I will sing praise to Yahweh,<l eID="gen1954" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen1955"/>the God of Israel. <l eID="gen1955" level="3"/>

verses.name: Judges 5:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1443"/><l level="1" sID="gen1956"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1443"/>Yahweh, when you went down from Seir,<l eID="gen1956" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1957"/>when you marched from the region of Edom,<l eID="gen1957" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1958"/>the earth trembled, the heavens poured down,<l eID="gen1958" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1959"/>the clouds poured down water. <l eID="gen1959" level="2"/>

verses.name: Judges 5:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1444"/><l level="1" sID="gen1960"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1444"/>The mountains trembled<note placement="foot">Or “quaked”</note> before Yahweh,<l eID="gen1960" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1961"/>this Sinai, at the presence of Yahweh, the God of Israel. <l eID="gen1961" level="2"/>

verses.name: Judges 5:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1445"/><l level="1" sID="gen1962"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1445"/>“In the days of Shamgar son of Anath,<l eID="gen1962" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1963"/>in the days of Jael, the caravans had ceased,<l eID="gen1963" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1964"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the travelers⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the ones walking on the paths”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they kept to the byways⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “they went on the crooked roads”</note> <l eID="gen1964" level="2"/>

verses.name: Judges 5:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1446"/><l level="1" sID="gen1965"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1446"/>The warriors<note placement="foot">Others interpret this word as referring to the “rural dwellers”</note> ceased;<l eID="gen1965" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1966"/>they failed to appear in Israel,<l eID="gen1966" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1967"/>until I,<note placement="foot">Or “you”</note> Deborah, arose;<l eID="gen1967" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1968"/>I<note placement="foot">Or “you”</note> arose <transChange type="added">as</transChange> a mother in Israel. <l eID="gen1968" level="2"/>

verses.name: Judges 5:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1447"/><l level="1" sID="gen1969"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1447"/>God chose new <transChange type="added">leaders</transChange>,<note placement="foot">ESV, NRSV translate “when new gods were chosen”</note><l eID="gen1969" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1970"/>then war <transChange type="added">was at the</transChange> gates;<l eID="gen1970" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1971"/>a small shield or a spear was not seen<l eID="gen1971" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1972"/>among forty thousand in Israel. <l eID="gen1972" level="2"/>

verses.name: Judges 5:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1448"/><l level="1" sID="gen1973"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1448"/>My heart <transChange type="added">goes out</transChange> to the commanders of Israel,<l eID="gen1973" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1974"/>those offering themselves willingly among the people;<l eID="gen1974" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen1975"/>bless Yahweh! <l eID="gen1975" level="3"/>

verses.name: Judges 5:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1449"/><l level="1" sID="gen1976"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1449"/>The riders of white female donkeys,<l eID="gen1976" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1977"/><transChange type="added">those</transChange> sitting on saddle blankets,<l eID="gen1977" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen1978"/>and <transChange type="added">those</transChange> going on <transChange type="added">the</transChange> way, talk about it! <l eID="gen1978" level="3"/>

verses.name: Judges 5:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1450"/><l level="1" sID="gen1979"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1450"/>At the sound of <transChange type="added">those</transChange> dividing<note placement="foot">Meaning uncertain; other translations have “archers” (Tanakh), “musicians” (ESV, NRSV) or “singers” (NIV, HCSB)</note> <transChange type="added">the sheep</transChange><l eID="gen1979" level="1"/> <l level="3" sID="gen1980"/>among the watering places,<l eID="gen1980" level="3"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1981"/>there they will recount the righteous deeds of Yahweh,<l eID="gen1981" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1982"/>the righteous deeds for his warriors<note placement="foot">Hebrew “warrior”</note> in Israel.<l eID="gen1982" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1983"/>Then the people of Yahweh went down to the gates. <l eID="gen1983" level="1"/>

verses.name: Judges 5:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1451"/><l level="1" sID="gen1984"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1451"/>“Wake up, wake up, Deborah!<l eID="gen1984" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1985"/>Wake up, wake up, sing a song!<l eID="gen1985" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1986"/>Get up, Barak!<l eID="gen1986" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1987"/>Take captive your captives, O son of Abinoam. <l eID="gen1987" level="2"/>

verses.name: Judges 5:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1452"/><l level="1" sID="gen1988"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1452"/>Then <transChange type="added">the</transChange> remnant went down to <transChange type="added">the</transChange> nobles;<l eID="gen1988" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1989"/>the people of Yahweh went down for him<note placement="foot">Hebrew “me”</note> against <transChange type="added">the</transChange> mighty. <l eID="gen1989" level="2"/>

verses.name: Judges 5:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1453"/><l level="1" sID="gen1990"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1453"/>From Ephraim <transChange type="added">is</transChange> their root into Amalek,<l eID="gen1990" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1991"/>after you, Benjamin, with your family;<l eID="gen1991" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1992"/>from Makir <transChange type="added">the</transChange> commanders went down,<l eID="gen1992" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1993"/>and from Zebulun <transChange type="added">those</transChange> carrying <transChange type="added">the</transChange> scepter<l eID="gen1993" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen1994"/>of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> military commander. <l eID="gen1994" level="3"/>

verses.name: Judges 5:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1454"/><l level="1" sID="gen1995"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1454"/>And the chiefs<note placement="foot">Hebrew “my chiefs”; ancient translations read “the chiefs”</note> in Issachar <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with Deborah;<l eID="gen1995" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1996"/>and Issachar likewise <transChange type="added">was with</transChange> Barak;<l eID="gen1996" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1997"/>into the valley <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he was sent to get him from behind⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “he was sent at his feet”</note><l eID="gen1997" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen1998"/>Among the clans of Reuben<l eID="gen1998" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen1999"/><transChange type="added">were</transChange> great <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞decisions of the heart⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Or “thoughts of the heart”</note> <l eID="gen1999" level="2"/>

verses.name: Judges 5:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1455"/><l level="1" sID="gen2000"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1455"/>Why do you sit among the sheepfolds,<l eID="gen2000" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2001"/>to hear <transChange type="added">the</transChange> calling sounds of the herds?<l eID="gen2001" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2002"/>For the clans of Reuben,<l eID="gen2002" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2003"/><transChange type="added">there were</transChange> great searchings of the heart. <l eID="gen2003" level="2"/>

verses.name: Judges 5:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1456"/><l level="1" sID="gen2004"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1456"/>Gilead has remained<note placement="foot">Or “stayed”</note> beyond the Jordan.<l eID="gen2004" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2005"/>Why did Dan dwell as a foreigner <transChange type="added">with</transChange> ships?<l eID="gen2005" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2006"/>Asher sat at <transChange type="added">the</transChange> coast of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> waters,<l eID="gen2006" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2007"/>and by his coves he has been settling down. <l eID="gen2007" level="2"/>

verses.name: Judges 5:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1457"/><l level="1" sID="gen2008"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1457"/>Zebulun <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a people who scorned death,<l eID="gen2008" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2009"/>and Naphtali, on the heights of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> field. <l eID="gen2009" level="2"/>

verses.name: Judges 5:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1458"/><l level="1" sID="gen2010"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1458"/>“The kings came, they fought;<l eID="gen2010" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2011"/>then the kings of Canaan fought;<l eID="gen2011" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2012"/>at Taanach by the waters of Megiddo,<l eID="gen2012" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2013"/>they got no plunder in silver. <l eID="gen2013" level="2"/>

verses.name: Judges 5:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1459"/><l level="1" sID="gen2014"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1459"/>The stars fought from heaven;<l eID="gen2014" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2015"/>from their courses they fought against Sisera. <l eID="gen2015" level="2"/>

verses.name: Judges 5:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1460"/><l level="1" sID="gen2016"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1460"/>The wadi<note placement="foot">A valley that is dry most of the year, but contains a stream during the rainy season</note> torrent of Kishon swept them away,<l eID="gen2016" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2017"/>the raging wadi torrent,<l eID="gen2017" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen2018"/>the wadi torrent of Kishon.<l eID="gen2018" level="3"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2019"/>March on, my soul, <transChange type="added">with</transChange> strength! <l eID="gen2019" level="2"/>

verses.name: Judges 5:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1461"/><l level="1" sID="gen2020"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1461"/>“Then the hooves of the horse beat loudly,<l eID="gen2020" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2021"/>because of galloping, galloping of his stallions. <l eID="gen2021" level="2"/>

verses.name: Judges 5:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1462"/><l level="1" sID="gen2022"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1462"/>‘Curse Meroz,’ says the angel of Yahweh;<l eID="gen2022" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2023"/>‘curse bitterly its inhabitants,<l eID="gen2023" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2024"/>because they did not come to the help of Yahweh,<l eID="gen2024" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2025"/>to the help of Yahweh against the mighty.’ <l eID="gen2025" level="2"/>

verses.name: Judges 5:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1463"/><l level="1" sID="gen2026"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1463"/>“Most blessed of women is Jael,<l eID="gen2026" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2027"/>the wife of Heber the Kenite;<l eID="gen2027" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen2028"/>most blessed is she of women among tent dwellers. <l eID="gen2028" level="3"/>

verses.name: Judges 5:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1464"/><l level="1" sID="gen2029"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1464"/>He asked for water, <transChange type="added">and</transChange> she gave milk;<l eID="gen2029" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2030"/>in a drinking bowl for nobles, she brought curds. <l eID="gen2030" level="2"/>

verses.name: Judges 5:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1465"/><l level="1" sID="gen2031"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1465"/>She reached out her hand to the peg,<l eID="gen2031" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2032"/>and her right hand for the workman’s hammer;<l eID="gen2032" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2033"/>and she struck Sisera, crushed his head,<l eID="gen2033" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2034"/>and she shattered and pierced his temple. <l eID="gen2034" level="2"/>

verses.name: Judges 5:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1466"/><l level="1" sID="gen2035"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1466"/>Between her feet he sank, he fell, he lay.<l eID="gen2035" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2036"/>Between her feet he sank down, he fell;<l eID="gen2036" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen2037"/>Where he sank down, there he fell—<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞dead⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “devastated”</note> <l eID="gen2037" level="3"/>

verses.name: Judges 5:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1467"/><l level="1" sID="gen2038"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1467"/>“Through the window she looked down;<l eID="gen2038" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2039"/>the mother of Sisera cried out through the lattice,<l eID="gen2039" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2040"/>‘Why is his chariot delayed in coming?<l eID="gen2040" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2041"/>Why do the hoof beats<note placement="foot">Or “steps”</note> of his chariot tarry?’ <l eID="gen2041" level="2"/>

verses.name: Judges 5:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1468"/><l level="1" sID="gen2042"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1468"/>The wisest of her ladies answer her;<l eID="gen2042" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2043"/>she also answers the question herself: <l eID="gen2043" level="2"/>

verses.name: Judges 5:30
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1469"/><l level="1" sID="gen2044"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1469"/>‘Are they not finding and dividing the plunder?<l eID="gen2044" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2045"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞A bedmate or two bedmates for every man⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “a womb, two wombs for head of every man”</note><l eID="gen2045" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2046"/>colorful garments for Sisera,<l eID="gen2046" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2047"/>plunder of colorful garments,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “garment”</note><l eID="gen2047" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2048"/>beautifully finished colorful garments,<l eID="gen2048" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2049"/>on the neck of the plunderer?’ <l eID="gen2049" level="2"/>

verses.name: Judges 5:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1470"/><l level="1" sID="gen2050"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1470"/>So may all your enemies perish, O Yahweh,<l eID="gen2050" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2051"/>but those who love him are like the rising sun at its brightest.”<l eID="gen2051" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen1948"/> <div sID="gen2052" type="x-p"/> And the land had rest for forty years.  <chapter eID="Judg.5"/>

verses.name: Judges 6:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1471"/><title type="x-s">The Midianites Oppresses Israel</title> <div sID="gen2053" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1471"/>The <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> did evil in the eyes of Yahweh, and Yahweh gave them into the hand of the Midianites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Midianite”</note> for seven years.

verses.name: Judges 6:2
verses.text: The hand of the Midianites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Midianite”</note> prevailed over Israel; because of the presence of the Midianites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Midianite”</note> the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> made for themselves hiding places that <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in the mountains, caves, and strongholds.

verses.name: Judges 6:3
verses.text: And whenever Israel sowed seed, the Midianites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Midianite”</note> Amalekites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Amalekite”</note> and the people of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> east would come up against them.

verses.name: Judges 6:4
verses.text: They would camp against them and destroy the produce of the land <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as far as⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “until your coming to”</note> Gaza; they left no produce in Israel, or sheep, ox, or donkey.

verses.name: Judges 6:5
verses.text: For they, their livestock, and their tents would come up like a great number of locusts; they and their camels could not be counted; they came into the land and devoured it.

verses.name: Judges 6:6
verses.text: Israel was very poor because of the presence of the Midianites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Midianite”</note> and the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> cried out to Yahweh.  <div eID="gen2053" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 6:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1472"/><div sID="gen2054" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1472"/>When the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> cried out to Yahweh on account of the Midianites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Midianite”</note>

verses.name: Judges 6:8
verses.text: Yahweh sent a prophet to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> and he said to them, “Thus says Yahweh the God of Israel: ‘I brought you up from Egypt; I brought you from the house of slavery.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “slaves”</note>

verses.name: Judges 6:9
verses.text: I delivered you from the hand of Egypt and from the hand of all your oppressors, and drove them out from <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “your face/presence”</note> and I gave you their land.

verses.name: Judges 6:10
verses.text: And I said to you, ‘I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> Yahweh your God; do not fear<note placement="foot">Or “revere”</note> the gods of the Amorites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Amorite”</note> in whose land you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> living.’ But you have not listened to my voice.”  <div eID="gen2054" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 6:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1473"/><title type="x-s">The Angel of Yahweh Calls Gideon</title> <div sID="gen2055" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1473"/>The angel of Yahweh came and sat under the oak<note placement="foot">Or “terebinth”</note> that was at Ophrah that belonged to Jehoash the Abiezrite; and Gideon his son was threshing wheat in the winepress to hide it<note placement="foot">Or “keep it away”</note> from the Midianites.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Midianite”</note>

verses.name: Judges 6:12
verses.text: The angel of Yahweh appeared to him and said to him, “Yahweh <transChange type="added">is</transChange> with you, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you mighty warrior⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “strong/mighty of power”</note>

verses.name: Judges 6:13
verses.text: Gideon said to him, “Excuse me, my lord. <transChange type="added">If</transChange> Yahweh is with us, why then has all this happened to us? Where are all his wonderful deeds that our ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> recounted to us, saying, ‘Did not Yahweh bring us up from Egypt?’ But now Yahweh has forsaken us; he has given us into the palm of Midian.”

verses.name: Judges 6:14
verses.text: And Yahweh turned to him and said, “Go in this your strength, and you will deliver Israel from the palm of Midian. Did I not send you?”

verses.name: Judges 6:15
verses.text: He said to him, “Excuse me, my lord. How will I deliver Israel? Look, my clan <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the weakest in Manasseh, and I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> the youngest in my father’s house.”

verses.name: Judges 6:16
verses.text: And Yahweh said to him, “But I will be with you, and you will defeat Midian <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as if they are one man⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “as one man”</note>

verses.name: Judges 6:17
verses.text: And he<note placement="foot">That is, Gideon</note> said to him, “Please, if I have found favor in your eyes, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞show me a sign⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “make a sign for me”</note> that you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> speaking with me.

verses.name: Judges 6:18
verses.text: Please, do not depart from here until I come <transChange type="added">back</transChange> to you and bring out my gift and set it out before you.”<note placement="foot">Or “in your presence”</note> And he said, “I will stay until you return.”  <div eID="gen2055" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 6:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1474"/><div sID="gen2056" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1474"/>And Gideon went and prepared <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a young goat⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a kid of goat”</note> and unleavened cakes from an ephah of flour; he put meat in a basket, and the broth he put in a pot, and he brought them to him under the oak<note placement="foot">Or “terebinth”</note> and presented <transChange type="added">them</transChange>.

verses.name: Judges 6:20
verses.text: The angel of God said to him, “Take the meat and the unleavened cakes and put <transChange type="added">them</transChange> on this rock; pour the broth <transChange type="added">over it</transChange>.” And he did so.

verses.name: Judges 6:21
verses.text: Then the angel of Yahweh reached out the tip of the staff that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in his hand, and he touched the meat and the unleavened cakes; and fire went up from the rock and consumed the meat and the unleavened cakes. And the angel of Yahweh went <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from his sight⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “from his eyes”</note>

verses.name: Judges 6:22
verses.text: And Gideon realized that he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> the angel of Yahweh; and Gideon said, “Oh, my lord Yahweh! For now I have seen the angel of Yahweh face to face.”

verses.name: Judges 6:23
verses.text: And Yahweh said to him, “Peace be with you. Do not fear; you will not die.”

verses.name: Judges 6:24
verses.text: And Gideon built there an altar to Yahweh, and he called it “Yahweh <transChange type="added">is</transChange> peace.” To this day it is still in Ophrah <transChange type="added">of the</transChange> Abiezrites.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Abiezrite”</note>  <div eID="gen2056" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 6:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1475"/><div sID="gen2057" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1475"/>Now on that same night Yahweh said to him, “Take the bull of the cattle that belongs to your father, and a second bull seven years old, and pull down the altar of Baal that belongs to your father, and cut down the Asherah<note placement="foot">An Asherah is a cultic pole set up next to an altar symbolizing the goddess Asherah</note> that is beside it;

verses.name: Judges 6:26
verses.text: and build an altar to Yahweh your God on the top of this stronghold in the proper arrangement, and take a second bull and offer <transChange type="added">it as</transChange> a burnt offering with the wood of the Asherah<note placement="foot">An Asherah is a cultic pole set up next to an altar symbolizing the goddess Asherah</note> that you will cut down.

verses.name: Judges 6:27
verses.text: Gideon took ten men from his servants, and he did just as Yahweh told him;<note placement="foot">Or “spoke to him”</note> and because he was too afraid of his <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞father’s family⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “father’s house”</note> and the men of the city to do <transChange type="added">it during</transChange> the day, he did <transChange type="added">it during</transChange> night.  <div eID="gen2057" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 6:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1476"/><title type="x-s">Gideon Destroys the Altar of Baal</title> <div sID="gen2058" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1476"/>When the men of the city got up early in the morning, look, the altar of Baal and the Asherah<note placement="foot">An Asherah is a cultic pole set up next to an altar symbolizing the goddess Asherah</note> that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> beside it <transChange type="added">were</transChange> cut down, and the second bull was offered on the altar that had been built.

verses.name: Judges 6:29
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And they said to one another⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “And each man to his neighbor said”</note> “Who did this thing?” So they searched and inquired, and they said, “Gideon son of Jehoash did this thing.”

verses.name: Judges 6:30
verses.text: And the men of the city said to Jehoash, “Bring out your son so that he may die, for he has pulled down the altar of Baal and cut down the Asherah that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> beside it.”

verses.name: Judges 6:31
verses.text: But Jehoash said to all who stood against him,<note placement="foot">Or “who arrayed against him”</note> “Will you contend for Baal? Will you rescue him? Whoever contends for him will be put to death by the morning. If he is a god, let him contend for himself because <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his altar has been pulled down⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “because he has pulled down his altar”; the subject in Hebrew has not been specified</note>

verses.name: Judges 6:32
verses.text: Thus, on that day he<note placement="foot">That is, Gideon</note> was called Jerub-Baal, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞which means⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “saying”</note> “Let Baal contend against him,” because he had pulled down his altar.  <div eID="gen2058" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 6:33
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1477"/><div sID="gen2059" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1477"/>Then all the Midianites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Midianite”</note> Amalekites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Amalekite”</note> and the people of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> east gathered together and crossed <transChange type="added">the Jordan</transChange>; and they camped in the valley of Jezreel.

verses.name: Judges 6:34
verses.text: So the Spirit of Yahweh <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞took possession of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “clothed”</note> Gideon, and he blew on the trumpet, and the Abiezrites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Abiezerite”</note> were called to follow him.

verses.name: Judges 6:35
verses.text: He sent messengers throughout all Manasseh, and they were also called to follow him; and he sent messengers throughout Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali, and they went up to meet them.  <div eID="gen2059" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 6:36
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1478"/><title type="x-s">Gideon Tests Yahweh With the Fleece</title> <div sID="gen2060" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1478"/>Then Gideon said to God, “In order to see that you will deliver Israel by my hand, just as you have said,

verses.name: Judges 6:37
verses.text: I will place a fleece of wool on the threshing floor. If there is dew on the fleece only, and all of the ground <transChange type="added">is</transChange> dry, I will know that you will deliver Israel by my hand, just as you have said.”

verses.name: Judges 6:38
verses.text: And it was so. He arose early the next day and squeezed the fleece, and he wrung out dew from the fleece, a full drinking bowl of water.

verses.name: Judges 6:39
verses.text: And Gideon said to God, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Do not let your anger burn⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Do not let your nose become hot”</note> against me; let me speak once more. Please let me test once more with the fleece; let the fleece be dry, and let there be dew on the ground.”

verses.name: Judges 6:40
verses.text: And God did so that night; only the fleece was dry, and dew was on all the ground.  <chapter eID="Judg.6"/>

verses.name: Judges 7:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1479"/><title type="x-s">Gideon’s Three Hundred Men</title> <div sID="gen2061" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1479"/>Then Jerub-Baal (that <transChange type="added">is</transChange>, Gideon) rose early, and all the army that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> with him. They were camped beside the spring of Harod;<note placement="foot">Or “En-Harod”</note> the camp of Midian was north of the hill of Moreh, in the valley.

verses.name: Judges 7:2
verses.text: And Yahweh said to Gideon, “The troops that <transChange type="added">are</transChange> with you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> too many for me to give Midian into their hands; Israel will boast, saying, ‘My hand has delivered me.’

verses.name: Judges 7:3
verses.text: So then, please proclaim in the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞hearing⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “ears”</note> of the troops, saying, ‘Whoever <transChange type="added">is</transChange> fearful and trembling, let him return and depart from the Mount of Gilead.’ ” About twenty-two thousand troops returned, and ten thousand remained.

verses.name: Judges 7:4
verses.text: And Yahweh said to Gideon, “There <transChange type="added">are</transChange> still too many troops; bring them down to the water, and I will sift through them<note placement="foot">Or “test them”</note> for you there. For whomever I say to you, ‘This <transChange type="added">one</transChange> will go with you,’ he will go with you; and for all whom I say to you, ‘This <transChange type="added">one</transChange> will not go with you,’ he will not go.”

verses.name: Judges 7:5
verses.text: So he brought down the troops to the water, and Yahweh said to Gideon, “You must separate everyone who laps up the water to drink with his tongue like a dog from those <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who kneel⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “who kneels to his knees”</note>

verses.name: Judges 7:6
verses.text: The number of those lapping up <transChange type="added">the water</transChange> with their hand to their mouth was three hundred men; all the rest of the troops kneeled to drink the water.

verses.name: Judges 7:7
verses.text: And Yahweh said to Gideon, “I will deliver you with the three hundred men lapping up <transChange type="added">the water</transChange>; I will give Midian into your hand, so let the <transChange type="added">other</transChange> troops go, each to his own place.

verses.name: Judges 7:8
verses.text: So they took their provisions and their trumpets into their hand, and he sent all the men of Israel, each one, to his tent; but three hundred of the men he kept; the camp of Midian was below him in the valley.  <div eID="gen2061" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 7:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1480"/><div sID="gen2062" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1480"/>And that night Yahweh said to him, “Get up; go down against the camp, for I have given it into your hand.

verses.name: Judges 7:10
verses.text: But if you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> afraid, go down to the camp with Purah your servant,

verses.name: Judges 7:11
verses.text: and you will hear what they say; and afterward <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you will have courage⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “your hands will be strong”</note> and you will go down against the camp.” Then he went down with Purah his servant to the outpost of the armed men<note placement="foot">Or “edge of the men lined up in array”</note> that <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in the camp.

verses.name: Judges 7:12
verses.text: Now <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Midianites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Midianite”</note> Amalekites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Amalekite”</note> and all the people of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> east <transChange type="added">were</transChange> lying in the valley, like a great multitude of locusts; their camels were without number, as numerous as the sand that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> on the shore of the sea.

verses.name: Judges 7:13
verses.text: When Gideon came, a man <transChange type="added">was</transChange> recounting a dream<note placement="foot">Or “telling a dream”</note> to his friend, and he said, “Behold, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I had a dream⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “I dreamed a dream”</note> a round loaf of barley bread <transChange type="added">was</transChange> tumbling into the camp of Midian, and it came up to the tent, it struck it, and it fell and turned it upside down so that the tent fell.”

verses.name: Judges 7:14
verses.text: His friend answered him and said, “This cannot be anything except the sword of Gideon son of Jehoash, a man of Israel; God has given Midian and the entire camp into his hand.”  <div eID="gen2062" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 7:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1481"/><div sID="gen2063" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1481"/>When Gideon heard the recounting of the dream<note placement="foot">Or “telling of the dream”</note> and its interpretation, he bowed down and returned to the camp of Israel; and he said, “Get up, for Yahweh has given the camp of Midian into your hand.”

verses.name: Judges 7:16
verses.text: He divided the three hundred men <transChange type="added">into</transChange> three companies,<note placement="foot">Or “divisions”</note> and he put trumpets and empty jars in everyone’s hand, with torches inside the jars.

verses.name: Judges 7:17
verses.text: And he said to them, “Watch me and do the same. When I come to the edge of the camp, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞do just as I do⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “just as I will do, you must do”</note>

verses.name: Judges 7:18
verses.text: When I and all who <transChange type="added">are</transChange> with me blow on the trumpet, you must also blow on the trumpets and surround the camp, and you must say, ‘To Yahweh and to Gideon!’ ”  <div eID="gen2063" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 7:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1482"/><div sID="gen2064" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1482"/>So Gideon and the hundred men who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him came to the edge of the camp <transChange type="added">at</transChange> the beginning of the middle night-watch, when they had just finished setting up the guards, and they blew on the trumpets and smashed the jars that <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in their hands.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “hand”</note>

verses.name: Judges 7:20
verses.text: When three companies<note placement="foot">Or “divisions”</note> blew on the trumpets and broke the jars, they held in their left hand the torches and in their right hand the trumpets for blowing, and they cried, “A sword for Yahweh and for Gideon!”

verses.name: Judges 7:21
verses.text: And each stood <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in his place⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “under him”</note> all around the camp, and all the camp ran, and they cried out as they fled.

verses.name: Judges 7:22
verses.text: When they blew the three hundred trumpets, Yahweh set <transChange type="added">the</transChange> sword of each one against his neighbor throughout the whole camp, and the camp<note placement="foot">Or “army”</note> fled as far as Beth Shittah toward Zererah, up to Abel Meholah, the border by Tabbath.

verses.name: Judges 7:23
verses.text: And the men of Israel were called from Naphtali, from Asher, and from all of Manasseh, and they pursued after Midian.  <div eID="gen2064" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 7:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1483"/><div sID="gen2065" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1483"/>And Gideon sent messengers throughout all the hill country of Ephraim, saying, “Come down to oppose<note placement="foot">Or “meet”</note> Midian, and capture from them the waters up to Beth Barah and the Jordan.” He called out all the men of Ephraim, and they captured the waters up to Beth Barah and the Jordan.

verses.name: Judges 7:25
verses.text: And they captured the two commanders of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb, and they killed Oreb at the rock of Oreb, and they killed Zeeb at the wine press of Zeeb, while they chased Midian; and they brought the heads<note placement="foot">Hebrew “head”</note> of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon from beyond the Jordan.  <chapter eID="Judg.7"/>

verses.name: Judges 8:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1484"/><title type="x-s">Gideon Pursues Zebah and Zalmunna</title> <div sID="gen2066" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1484"/>The men of Ephraim said to him, “What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> this thing you have done to us, not calling us when you went to fight against the Midianites?”<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Midianite”</note> And they quarreled with him severely.

verses.name: Judges 8:2
verses.text: And he said to them, “What I have done now in comparison with you? Are not the gleanings of Ephraim better than the grape harvest of Abiezer?

verses.name: Judges 8:3
verses.text: God has given into your hand the commanders of Midian, Oreb, and Zeeb. What have I been able to do in comparison with you?” And their <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞anger⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “spirit”</note> against him subsided when <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he said that⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “he said this thing/word”</note>  <div eID="gen2066" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 8:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1485"/><div sID="gen2067" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1485"/>Then Gideon came to the Jordan, crossing it with the three hundred men who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him, weary and pursuing.

verses.name: Judges 8:5
verses.text: He said to the men of Succoth, “Please give loaves of bread to the people who <transChange type="added">are</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞following me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “at my feet”</note> for they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> weary, and I am pursuing Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian.”

verses.name: Judges 8:6
verses.text: The officials of Succoth said, “Is the hand<note placement="foot">Or “palm”</note> of Zebah and Zalmunna in your hand now, that we should give bread to your army?”

verses.name: Judges 8:7
verses.text: Gideon said, “Well then, when Yahweh gives Zebah and Zalmunna into my hand, I will trample your flesh with the thorns and briers of the wilderness.”

verses.name: Judges 8:8
verses.text: He went from there <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Penuel, and he spoke similarly to them; and the men of Penuel answered him just as the men of Succoth answered.

verses.name: Judges 8:9
verses.text: And he said also to the men of Penuel, saying, “When I return <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞safely⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “in peace”</note> I will tear down this tower.”  <div eID="gen2067" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 8:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1486"/><div sID="gen2068" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1486"/>Now Zebah and Zalmunna <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in Karkor, and their armies with them, about fifteen thousand men remained from the entire army<note placement="foot">Or “camp”</note> of the people of the east; those that fell in battle were one hundred and twenty thousand <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞swordsmen⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sword-drawing men”</note>

verses.name: Judges 8:11
verses.text: And Gideon went up the route of those who dwell in tents on the east of Nobah and Jogbehah, and he attacked the army<note placement="foot">Or “camp”</note> when it was off its guard.<note placement="foot">Or “unsuspecting”</note>

verses.name: Judges 8:12
verses.text: And Zebah and Zalmunna fled, and he pursued them and captured the two kings of Midian, Zebah and Zalmunna, and he routed<note placement="foot">Or “he frightened” or “he threw into panic”</note> the entire army.<note placement="foot">Or “camp”</note>  <div eID="gen2068" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 8:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1487"/><div sID="gen2069" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1487"/>Then Gideon son of Jehoash returned from the battle <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞by way of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from”</note> the ascent of Heres.<note placement="foot">Or “pass of Heres”</note>

verses.name: Judges 8:14
verses.text: He captured a young man <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from Succoth⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from the men of Succoth”</note> and questioned him. The young man listed<note placement="foot">Or “wrote down”</note> for him the commanders of Succoth and its elders, seventy-seven men.

verses.name: Judges 8:15
verses.text: He came to the men of Succoth, and he said, “Here <transChange type="added">is</transChange> Zebah and Zalmunna, about whom you taunted me, saying, ‘<transChange type="added">Is</transChange> the palm<note placement="foot">Or “hand”</note> of Zebah and Zalmunna in your hand now, that we should give food to your weary men?’ ”

verses.name: Judges 8:16
verses.text: He took the elders of the city and <transChange type="added">the</transChange> thorn bushes and briers of the wilderness, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he trampled⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “he taught,” but see v. <reference osisRef="Judeg.8.7">7</reference></note> the men of Succoth with them.

verses.name: Judges 8:17
verses.text: He broke down the tower of Penuel, and he killed the men of the city.  <div eID="gen2069" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 8:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1488"/><div sID="gen2070" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1488"/>And he said to Zebah and Zalmunna, “What type <transChange type="added">were</transChange> the men whom you killed at Tabor?” And they said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞They were like you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally, “like you, like them”</note> each <transChange type="added">one of them</transChange> had the appearance of the sons of the king.”

verses.name: Judges 8:19
verses.text: He said, “They <transChange type="added">were</transChange> my brothers, the sons of my mother. As Yahweh lives, if you had kept them alive I would not kill you.”

verses.name: Judges 8:20
verses.text: And he said to Jether, his firstborn, “Get up, kill them.” But the boy did not draw his sword, for he was afraid because he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> still a boy.

verses.name: Judges 8:21
verses.text: Zebah and Zalmunna said, “Get up yourself, and strike us, for as <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the man, so <transChange type="added">is</transChange> his power.”<note placement="foot">Or “strength”</note> So Gideon got up and killed Zebah and Zalmunna, and he took the crescent ornaments that were on the necks of their camels.  <div eID="gen2070" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 8:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1489"/><div sID="gen2071" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1489"/>The men of Israel said to Gideon, “Rule over us, both you and your sons, and your sons’ son, for you have delivered us from the hand of Midian.

verses.name: Judges 8:23
verses.text: But Gideon said to them, “I will not rule over you, and my son will not rule over you; Yahweh will rule over you.”

verses.name: Judges 8:24
verses.text: And Gideon said to them, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Let me make a request of you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “Let me ask from you a request”</note> that each of you give to me an ornamental ring from his plunder.” (They <transChange type="added">had</transChange> ornamental rings of gold, because they <transChange type="added">were</transChange> Ishmaelites.)

verses.name: Judges 8:25
verses.text: They said, “We will gladly give <transChange type="added">them</transChange>,” and they spread out a garment, and everyone threw there an ornamental ring of his plunder.

verses.name: Judges 8:26
verses.text: The weight of the ornamental rings of gold that he requested <transChange type="added">was</transChange> one thousand seven hundred <transChange type="added">shekels of</transChange> gold, apart from the crescents, pendants, and purple garments that <transChange type="added">were</transChange> on the kings of Midian, and apart from the pendants that <transChange type="added">were</transChange> on the necks of their camels.

verses.name: Judges 8:27
verses.text: Gideon made an ephod <transChange type="added">out of</transChange> it, and he put it in his town in Ophrah, and all Israel prostituted <transChange type="added">themselves</transChange> to it there, and it became a snare to Gideon and his family.

verses.name: Judges 8:28
verses.text: And Midian was subdued before the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> and they did not again lift up their head, and the land rested for forty years in the days of Gideon.  <div eID="gen2071" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 8:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1490"/><title type="x-s">The Death of Gideon</title> <div sID="gen2072" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1490"/>Jerub-Baal son of Joash lived in his own house.

verses.name: Judges 8:30
verses.text: Now Gideon had seventy sons, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his own offspring⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “from his own loins”</note> for he had many wives.

verses.name: Judges 8:31
verses.text: His concubine who <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in Shechem also bore for him a son, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he named him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “he set his name”</note> Abimelech.

verses.name: Judges 8:32
verses.text: And Gideon son of Joash died at a good old age, and he was buried in the tomb of Jehoash his father, in Ophrah <transChange type="added">of</transChange> the Abiezrites.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Abiezrite”</note>  <div eID="gen2072" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 8:33
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1491"/><div sID="gen2073" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1491"/>And it happened, as soon as Gideon died, the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> returned and prostituted <transChange type="added">themselves</transChange> after the Baals, and they made for themselves Baal-Berith as god.

verses.name: Judges 8:34
verses.text: The <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> did not remember Yahweh their God, who had delivered them from the hand of their enemies from all around,

verses.name: Judges 8:35
verses.text: nor did they show favor<note placement="foot">Or “loyalty”</note> to the house of Jerub-Baal (<transChange type="added">that is</transChange>, Gideon) in accordance with all the good that he did for Israel.  <chapter eID="Judg.8"/>

verses.name: Judges 9:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1492"/><title type="x-s">Abimelech Attempts to Become King</title> <div sID="gen2074" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1492"/>And Abimelech son of Jerub-Baal went to Shechem, to the relatives of his mother, and he said to them and to the house of his mother’s father,

verses.name: Judges 9:2
verses.text: “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Speak to⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Speak into the ears”</note> the lords of Shechem, ‘What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> better for you, that seventy men all from the sons of Jerub-Baal rule over you, or that one man rules over you?’ Remember that I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> your bone and your flesh.”

verses.name: Judges 9:3
verses.text: And his mother’s relatives spoke all these words concerning him <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in the ears of”</note> all the lords of Shechem; and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they supported Abimelech⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “it reached their heart after Abimelech”</note> for they said, “He is our relative.”<note placement="foot">Or “brother”</note>

verses.name: Judges 9:4
verses.text: And they gave to him seventy <transChange type="added">pieces of</transChange> silver from the temple<note placement="foot">Or “house”</note> of Baal-Berith, and Abimelech hired with them<note placement="foot">That is, the pieces of silver</note> worthless and reckless men, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they followed him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “They went after him”</note>

verses.name: Judges 9:5
verses.text: And he went to his father’s house at Ophrah, and he killed his brothers, the sons of Jerub-Baal, seventy men, on one stone. But Jotham the youngest son of Jerub-Baal survived, because he hid himself.

verses.name: Judges 9:6
verses.text: All the lords of Shechem and Beth-Millo gathered, and they went and made Abimelech as king, near <transChange type="added">the</transChange> oak<note placement="foot">Or “terebinth”</note> of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> pillar that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> at Shechem.  <div eID="gen2074" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 9:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1493"/><div sID="gen2075" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1493"/>And they told Jotham, and he went up and stood on the top of Mount Gerizim, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he cried out loud⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “he lifted his voice and called”</note> and said to them, “Listen to me, lords of Shechem, so that God may listen to you.  <div eID="gen2075" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 9:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1494"/><lg sID="gen2076"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2077"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1494"/>“The trees went certainly,<l eID="gen2077" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2078"/>to anoint a king over themselves.<l eID="gen2078" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2079"/>And they said to the olive tree,<l eID="gen2079" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2080"/>‘Rule over us.’ <l eID="gen2080" level="2"/>

verses.name: Judges 9:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1495"/><l level="1" sID="gen2081"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1495"/>And the olive tree replied,<l eID="gen2081" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2082"/>‘Should I stop <transChange type="added">producing</transChange> my oil,<l eID="gen2082" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen2083"/>which by me gods and men are honored,<l eID="gen2083" level="3"/> <l level="3" sID="gen2084"/>to go sway over the trees?’ <l eID="gen2084" level="3"/>

verses.name: Judges 9:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1496"/><l level="1" sID="gen2085"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1496"/>Then the trees said to the fig tree,<l eID="gen2085" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2086"/>‘You, come rule over us.’ <l eID="gen2086" level="2"/>

verses.name: Judges 9:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1497"/><l level="1" sID="gen2087"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1497"/>But the fig tree said to them,<l eID="gen2087" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2088"/>‘Should I stop <transChange type="added">producing</transChange> my sweetness,<l eID="gen2088" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen2089"/>and my good crop,<l eID="gen2089" level="3"/> <l level="3" sID="gen2090"/>to go sway over the trees?’ <l eID="gen2090" level="3"/>

verses.name: Judges 9:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1498"/><l level="1" sID="gen2091"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1498"/>And the trees said to the vine,<l eID="gen2091" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2092"/>‘You, come rule over us.’ <l eID="gen2092" level="2"/>

verses.name: Judges 9:13
