verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1499"/><l level="1" sID="gen2093"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1499"/>But the vine said to them,<l eID="gen2093" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2094"/>‘Should I stop <transChange type="added">producing</transChange> my wine<l eID="gen2094" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2095"/>that makes the gods and men happy,<l eID="gen2095" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen2096"/>to go sway over the trees?’ <l eID="gen2096" level="3"/>

verses.name: Judges 9:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1500"/><l level="1" sID="gen2097"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1500"/>So all the trees said to the thornbush,<l eID="gen2097" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2098"/>‘You, come rule over us.’ <l eID="gen2098" level="2"/>

verses.name: Judges 9:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1501"/><l level="1" sID="gen2099"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1501"/>And the thornbush said to the trees,<l eID="gen2099" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2100"/>‘If in good faith<note placement="foot">Or “honesty”</note> you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> anointing<l eID="gen2100" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2101"/>me as king over you,<l eID="gen2101" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen2102"/>then come and take refuge in my shade;<l eID="gen2102" level="3"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2103"/>if not, may fire go out from the thornbush<l eID="gen2103" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen2104"/>and devour the cedars of Lebanon.’ <l eID="gen2104" level="3"/> <lg eID="gen2076"/>

verses.name: Judges 9:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1502"/><div sID="gen2105" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1502"/>“So then, if you have acted in good faith<note placement="foot">Or “honesty”</note> and sincerity in making Abimelech king, and if you have dealt well with Jerub-Baal and his house, and have dealt with him <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞according to his accomplishments⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “according to the dealings of his hand”</note>—

verses.name: Judges 9:17
verses.text: for my father fought and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞risked his life⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “he threw his life in front”</note> for you and delivered you from the hand of Midian;

verses.name: Judges 9:18
verses.text: but today you have risen against the house of my father and killed his sons, seventy men on one stone, and you have made Abimelech, the son of his slave woman, a king over the lords of Shechem, because he is your relative<note placement="foot">Or “brother”</note>—

verses.name: Judges 9:19
verses.text: if you have acted in good faith<note placement="foot">Or “honesty”</note> and sincerity with Jerub-Baal and his house this day, then rejoice in Abimelech, and let him also rejoice in you.

verses.name: Judges 9:20
verses.text: But if not, let a fire come out from Abimelech and let it devour the lords of Shechem and Beth-Millo; and let a fire come out from the lords of Shechem, and from Beth-Millo, and let it devour Abimelech.”

verses.name: Judges 9:21
verses.text: And Jotham escaped and fled, and went to Beer; he remained there because of Abimelech his brother.  <div eID="gen2105" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 9:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1503"/><title type="x-s">The Downfall of Shechem and Abimelech</title> <div sID="gen2106" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1503"/>Abimelech ruled over Israel three years.

verses.name: Judges 9:23
verses.text: And God sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and the lords of Shechem, and the lords of Shechem dealt treacherously with Abimelech,

verses.name: Judges 9:24
verses.text: so that the violence done to the seventy brothers of Abimelech would be avenged and their blood be placed on Abimelech their brother, who killed them, and on the lords of Shechem, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who helped⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “who strengthened his hands”</note> to kill his brothers.

verses.name: Judges 9:25
verses.text: And the lords of Shechem set for him ambushes on the top of the mountains, and they robbed all who passed by them along the road; and it was reported to Abimelech.  <div eID="gen2106" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 9:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1504"/><div sID="gen2107" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1504"/>And Gaal son of Ebel and his relatives came, and they crossed over into Shechem, and the lords of Shechem <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞gave him confidence⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “put confidence into him”</note>

verses.name: Judges 9:27
verses.text: They went out <transChange type="added">into</transChange> the field and harvested their vineyards and trod <transChange type="added">them</transChange>, and they <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞held a festival⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “made a rejoicing”</note> And they went into the temple<note placement="foot">Or “house”</note> of their god, and they ate and drank and cursed Abimelech.

verses.name: Judges 9:28
verses.text: Then Gaal son of Ebed said, “Who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> Abimelech, and who <transChange type="added">are we of</transChange> Shechem that we should serve him? Is he not the son of Jerub-Baal, and <transChange type="added">is not</transChange> Zebul his chief officer?<note placement="foot">Or “overseer”</note> Serve the men of Hamor the father of Shechem. Why should we serve him?<note placement="foot">That is, Abimelech</note>

verses.name: Judges 9:29
verses.text: If only this people <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞were in my command⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!<note placement="foot">Literally “were in my hand”</note> Then I would remove Abimelech, and I would have said,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “he said”; the translation “I would have said” follows the LXX</note> ‘Increase your army and come out!’ ”  <div eID="gen2107" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 9:30
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1505"/><div sID="gen2108" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1505"/>When Zebul the commander of the city heard the words of Gaal son of Ebed, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he became angry⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “his nose became hot”</note>

verses.name: Judges 9:31
verses.text: and he sent messengers to Abimelech in Tormah, saying, “Look, Gaal son of Ebed and his relatives <transChange type="added">are</transChange> coming to Shechem, and they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> stirring up the city against you.

verses.name: Judges 9:32
verses.text: So then, get up <transChange type="added">by</transChange> night, you and the army that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> with you, and lie in ambush in the field.

verses.name: Judges 9:33
verses.text: And in the morning at sunrise, get up and rush the city; and look, when he and the troops who <transChange type="added">are</transChange> with him come out to you, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you must act according to whatever opportunity offers itself⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “you must do to him just as it will find your hand”</note>  <div eID="gen2108" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 9:34
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1506"/><div sID="gen2109" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1506"/>So Abimelech and all the army that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> with him got up <transChange type="added">by</transChange> night, and they lay in ambush against Shechem <transChange type="added">in</transChange> four divisions.<note placement="foot">Or “companies”</note>

verses.name: Judges 9:35
verses.text: Gaal son of Ebed went out and stood <transChange type="added">at</transChange> the entrance of the city gate, and Abimelech and the army that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> with him got up from the ambush.

verses.name: Judges 9:36
verses.text: When Gaal saw the army, he said to Zebul, “Look, people <transChange type="added">are</transChange> coming down from the top of the mountains!” And Zebul said to him, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞The shadows of the mountains look like people to you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “the shadows of the mountains you are seeing as men”</note>

verses.name: Judges 9:37
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And Gaal spoke again⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And he did again again Gaal to speak”</note> and said, “Look, people are coming down from Tabbur-erez, and one division<note placement="foot">Or “company”</note> is coming from the direction of Elon-meonenim.”<note placement="foot">Or “the Sorcerer’s Oak”</note>

verses.name: Judges 9:38
verses.text: And Zebul said to him, “Where then <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞is your boast⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “is your mouth”</note> you who said, ‘Who is Abimelech that we should serve him?’ Is this not the army that you rejected? Please, go out now and fight against them.”<note placement="foot">Hebrew “against him”</note>

verses.name: Judges 9:39
verses.text: So Gaal went out before the lords of Shechem and fought against Abimelech.

verses.name: Judges 9:40
verses.text: And Abimelech chased him, and he fled before him; many fell slain up to the entrance of the gate.

verses.name: Judges 9:41
verses.text: So Abimelech resided at Arumah, and Zebul drove out Gaal and his relatives<note placement="foot">Or “brothers”</note> from living in Shechem.  <div eID="gen2109" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 9:42
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1507"/><div sID="gen2110" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1507"/>On the next day the people went out <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the field; and it was reported to Abimelech,

verses.name: Judges 9:43
verses.text: so he took the army and divided them into three divisions,<note placement="foot">Or “companies”</note> and he laid an ambush in the field. And he saw the people <transChange type="added">were</transChange> coming out from the city, and he arose against them and killed them.

verses.name: Judges 9:44
verses.text: Then Abimelech and the divisions<note placement="foot">Or “companies”</note> that <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him dashed out and stood <transChange type="added">at</transChange> the entrance of the city gate, and the two divisions dashed out against all who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in the field, and they killed them.

verses.name: Judges 9:45
verses.text: Abimelech fought against the city all that day, and he captured the city and killed the people that <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in it; then he broke down the city and sowed it <transChange type="added">with</transChange> salt.  <div eID="gen2110" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 9:46
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1508"/><div sID="gen2111" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1508"/>When all the lords of the tower of Shechem heard, they went to the vault<note placement="foot">Or “cellar”</note> of the temple<note placement="foot">Or “house”</note> of El-Berith.

verses.name: Judges 9:47
verses.text: It was told to Abimelech that all the lords of the tower of Shechem had gathered.

verses.name: Judges 9:48
verses.text: So Abimelech went up Mount Zalmon, he and all his army that <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him, and Abimelech took the ax<note placement="foot">Hebrew “axes”</note> in his hand and cut down a bundle of brushwood, and he lifted it and put <transChange type="added">it</transChange> on his shoulder. And he said to the army that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> with him, “What you have seen me do, quickly do also.”

verses.name: Judges 9:49
verses.text: So the whole army cut down each one branch for himself and followed Abimelech, and they put <transChange type="added">them</transChange> against the vault<note placement="foot">Or “cellar”</note> and set the vault ablaze with fire on those <transChange type="added">inside</transChange>, so that all the men of the tower of Shechem died, about a thousand men and women.  <div eID="gen2111" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 9:50
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1509"/><div sID="gen2112" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1509"/>Then Abimelech went to Thebez, and he encamped against Thebez and captured it.

verses.name: Judges 9:51
verses.text: But there was a strong tower in the middle of the city, and all the men, women, and lords of the city fled there and shut themselves in; and they went up to the roof of the tower.

verses.name: Judges 9:52
verses.text: Abimelech came up to the tower and fought against it, and he came near the entrance of the tower to burn it with fire.

verses.name: Judges 9:53
verses.text: But a certain woman<note placement="foot">Or “But one woman”</note> threw an upper millstone on Abimelech’s head and cracked open his skull.

verses.name: Judges 9:54
verses.text: He called quickly to the young man carrying his weapons, and he said to him, “Draw your sword and kill me, so that they will not say of me, ‘A woman killed him.’ ” So the young man<note placement="foot">Hebrew “his young man”</note> stabbed him, and he died.

verses.name: Judges 9:55
verses.text: When the men of Israel saw that Abimelech was dead, each one went to his home.<note placement="foot">Or “place”</note>

verses.name: Judges 9:56
verses.text: So God repaid<note placement="foot">Or “returned”</note> the wickedness<note placement="foot">Or “evil”</note> that Abimelech committed against his father by killing his seventy brothers.

verses.name: Judges 9:57
verses.text: And God also repaid all the wickedness<note placement="foot">Or “evil”</note> of the men of Shechem on their heads, and the curse of Jotham son of Jerub-Baal fell on them.  <chapter eID="Judg.9"/>

verses.name: Judges 10:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1510"/><title type="x-s">The Philistines and Ammonites Afflict the Israelites</title> <div sID="gen2113" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1510"/>After Abimelech, Tola son of Puah son of Dod, a man of Issachar, rose up to deliver Israel; and he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> living at Shamir in the hill country of Ephraim.

verses.name: Judges 10:2
verses.text: And he judged Israel twenty-three years. And he died and was buried in Shamir.

verses.name: Judges 10:3
verses.text: After him Jair the Gileadite rose up, and he judged Israel twenty-two years.

verses.name: Judges 10:4
verses.text: And he had thirty sons who would ride on thirty donkeys, and they had thirty towns that <transChange type="added">are</transChange> in the land of Gilead that they called Havvoth Jair until this day.

verses.name: Judges 10:5
verses.text: And Jair died and was buried in Kamon.  <div eID="gen2113" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 10:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1511"/><div sID="gen2114" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1511"/>And again, the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> did evil in the eyes of Yahweh. They served the Baals, the Ashtaroth, the gods of Aram, Sidon, Moab, and the gods of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> and Philistines; they abandoned Yahweh and did not serve him.

verses.name: Judges 10:7
verses.text: And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the anger of Yahweh burned⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the nose of Yahweh became hot”</note> against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of the Philistines and the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note>

verses.name: Judges 10:8
verses.text: They crushed and oppressed the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> in that year; for eighteen years they crushed all the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> who were beyond the Jordan, in the land of the Amorites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Amorite”</note> which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in Gilead.

verses.name: Judges 10:9
verses.text: The <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> crossed the Jordan to fight also against Judah, Benjamin, and the house of Ephraim; and Israel was very distressed.  <div eID="gen2114" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 10:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1512"/><div sID="gen2115" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1512"/>Then the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> cried out to Yahweh, saying, “We have sinned against you; we have abandoned our God and served the Baals.”

verses.name: Judges 10:11
verses.text: And Yahweh said to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> “Did I not deliver you from the Egyptians,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “from Egypt”</note> the Amorites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Amorite”</note> from the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> and from the Philistines?<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Philistine”</note>

verses.name: Judges 10:12
verses.text: And when <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Sidonians, <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Amalekites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Amalekite”</note> and the Maonites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Maonite”</note> oppressed you, you cried out to me, and I delivered you from their hand.

verses.name: Judges 10:13
verses.text: Yet you have abandoned me and served other gods. Therefore I will no longer deliver you.

verses.name: Judges 10:14
verses.text: Go and cry out to the gods whom you have chosen; let them deliver you in the time of your trouble.”

verses.name: Judges 10:15
verses.text: And the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> said to Yahweh, “We have sinned; <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞do to us accordingly as you see fit⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “do to us according to the good in your eyes”</note> only please deliver us this day.”

verses.name: Judges 10:16
verses.text: So they removed the foreign gods from their midst and served Yahweh; and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he could no longer bear⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “his soul was short with”</note> the misery of Israel.  <div eID="gen2115" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 10:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1513"/><div sID="gen2116" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1513"/>And the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> were summoned,<note placement="foot">Or “were called to arms”</note> and they camped in Gilead. And the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> gathered and camped at Mizpah.

verses.name: Judges 10:18
verses.text: The people, the ones commanding Gilead, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞said to each other⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “said each to his neighbor”</note> “Who is the man that will begin to fight against the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> He will be as head over all the inhabitants of Gilead.”  <chapter eID="Judg.10"/>

verses.name: Judges 11:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1514"/><title type="x-s">Jephthah</title> <div sID="gen2117" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1514"/>Jephthah the Gileadite was a mighty warrior; he was the son of a prostitute, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Gilead was his father⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “Gilead fathered Jephthah”</note>

verses.name: Judges 11:2
verses.text: Gilead’s wife also bore for him sons; and the sons of <transChange type="added">his</transChange> wife grew up and drove Jephthah away, and they said to him, “You will not inherit the house of our father because you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the son of another woman.”

verses.name: Judges 11:3
verses.text: So Jephthah fled from the presence of his brothers, and he lived in the land of Tob. And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞outlaws⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “unprincipled/worthless men”</note> gathered around Jephthah and went with him.  <div eID="gen2117" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 11:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1515"/><div sID="gen2118" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1515"/>After a time the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> made war with Israel.

verses.name: Judges 11:5
verses.text: When the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> made war with Israel, the elders of Gilead went to bring Jephthah from the land of Tob.

verses.name: Judges 11:6
verses.text: And they said to Jephthah, “Come and be our commander, so that we may make war against the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note>

verses.name: Judges 11:7
verses.text: Jephthah said to the elders, “Did you not shun me and drive me out from the house of my father? Why do you come to me now when you have trouble?”

verses.name: Judges 11:8
verses.text: And the elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, “That being so, we have now returned to you, that you may go with us <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to fight⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to make war”</note> against the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> and become for us as head of all the inhabitants of Gilead.”

verses.name: Judges 11:9
verses.text: So Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead, “If you bring me back <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to fight⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to make war”</note> against the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> and Yahweh gives them <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞over to me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “before me”</note> will I be your head?”

verses.name: Judges 11:10
verses.text: And the elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, “Yahweh will be a <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞witness⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “hearer”</note> between us; we will act according to your word.”

verses.name: Judges 11:11
verses.text: So Jephthah went with the elders of Gilead, and the people made him head and commander over them. And Jephthah spoke all his words before Yahweh at Mizpah.  <div eID="gen2118" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 11:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1516"/><div sID="gen2119" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1516"/>And Jephthah sent messengers to the king of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> saying, “What <transChange type="added">is between</transChange> you and me that you have come to me to make war against my land?”

verses.name: Judges 11:13
verses.text: And the king of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> said to Jephthah’s messengers, “Because Israel took my land from <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Arnon up to the Jabbok and the Jordan when they came up from Egypt; so then, restore it peacefully.”

verses.name: Judges 11:14
verses.text: Once again Jephthah sent messengers to the king of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note>

verses.name: Judges 11:15
verses.text: and he said to him, “Thus says Jephthah, ‘Israel did not take the land of Moab or the land of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note>

verses.name: Judges 11:16
verses.text: because when they came up from Egypt, Israel went through the wilderness to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Red Sea⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sea of reed”</note> and went to Kadesh.

verses.name: Judges 11:17
verses.text: Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, “Please let us cross through your land,” but the king of Edom would not listen. And they also sent <transChange type="added">messengers</transChange> to the king of Moab, but he was not willing. So Israel stayed in Kadesh.

verses.name: Judges 11:18
verses.text: Then they traveled through the wilderness, went around the land of Edom and Moab, and came to <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the east⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from rise of sun”</note> side of the land of Moab, and they<note placement="foot">Hebrew “he”</note> encamped beyond <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Arnon; and they did not go into the territory of Moab because <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Arnon <transChange type="added">was</transChange> the border of Moab.

verses.name: Judges 11:19
verses.text: Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Amorite”</note> king of Heshbon; and Israel said to him, ‘Please let us cross through your land <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to our country⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.’<note placement="foot">Literally “to our place”</note>

verses.name: Judges 11:20
verses.text: But Sihon did not trust Israel to cross through his territory, so Sihon gathered all his people and then encamped at Jahaz; and he made war with Israel.

verses.name: Judges 11:21
verses.text: And Yahweh, the God of Israel, gave Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, and they defeated them; and Israel occupied all the land of the Amorites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Amorite”</note> inhabiting that land.

verses.name: Judges 11:22
verses.text: They occupied all the territory of the Amorites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Amorite”</note> from <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Arnon up to the Jabbok, and from the wilderness up to the Jordan.

verses.name: Judges 11:23
verses.text: So then Yahweh, the God of Israel, has driven out the Amorites<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Amorite”</note> from before his people Israel, and you want to possess it?

verses.name: Judges 11:24
verses.text: Do you not possess what Chemosh your god gave you to possess? Whoever Yahweh our God has driven out before us, we will possess it.

verses.name: Judges 11:25
verses.text: So then, <transChange type="added">are</transChange> you any better than Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab? Did he ever quarrel with Israel, or did he ever make war against them?

verses.name: Judges 11:26
verses.text: When Israel lived in Heshbon and its villages, and in Aroer and its villages, and in all the towns that <transChange type="added">are</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞along the Arnon⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “on the hands of the Arnon”</note> for three hundred years,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “year”</note> why did you not recover <transChange type="added">them</transChange> at that time?

verses.name: Judges 11:27
verses.text: I have not sinned against you; but you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the one who is doing wrong by making war against me. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Let Yahweh judge⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Let Yahweh the judge, judge”</note> today between the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> and the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note>

verses.name: Judges 11:28
verses.text: But the king of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> did not listen to the message that Jephthah sent to him.  <div eID="gen2119" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 11:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1517"/><title type="x-s">Jephthah Makes a Vow</title> <div sID="gen2120" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1517"/>And the Spirit of Yahweh came upon Jephthah, and he passed through Gilead and Manasseh. He passed through Mizpah of Gilead, and from Mizpah of Gilead he passed through <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note>

verses.name: Judges 11:30
verses.text: And Jephthah made a vow to Yahweh, and he said, “If indeed you will give the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> into my hand,

verses.name: Judges 11:31
verses.text: whatever<note placement="foot">Or “whoever”</note> comes out from the doors of my house to meet me when I return safely from the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> will be Yahweh’s, and I will offer it <transChange type="added">as</transChange> a burnt offering.”

verses.name: Judges 11:32
verses.text: And Jephthah crossed <transChange type="added">over</transChange> to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> to make war against them; and Yahweh gave them into his hand.

verses.name: Judges 11:33
verses.text: And he defeated them <transChange type="added">with</transChange> a very great blow, from Aroer as far as Minnith, twenty towns,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “town”</note> up to Abel Keramim. And the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> were subdued before the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note>  <div eID="gen2120" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 11:34
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1518"/><div sID="gen2121" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1518"/>Jephthah came to Mizpah, to his house, and behold his daughter came out to meet him with tambourines and dancing. She <transChange type="added">was</transChange> his only child; he did not have a son or daughter except her.

verses.name: Judges 11:35
verses.text: And the moment he saw her, he tore his clothes and said, “Ah! My daughter, you have caused me to bow down, and you have become my trouble. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I made an oath⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “I have opened wide my mouth”</note> to Yahweh, and I cannot take <transChange type="added">it</transChange> back.”

verses.name: Judges 11:36
verses.text: She said to him, “My father, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you made an oath⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “you have opened wide your mouth”</note> to Yahweh. Do to me according to what has gone out from your mouth, since Yahweh gave vengeance to you against your enemies, the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note>

verses.name: Judges 11:37
verses.text: And she said to her father, “Let this thing be done for me: grant me two months so that I may go wander<note placement="foot">Hebrew “down”</note> on the mountains and lament over my virginity, I and my companions.

verses.name: Judges 11:38
verses.text: And he said, “Go.” He sent her away <transChange type="added">for</transChange> two months, and she went with her friends, and she lamented over her virginity on the mountains.

verses.name: Judges 11:39
verses.text: At the end of the two months she returned to her father, and he did to her <transChange type="added">according to</transChange> his vow; and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞she did not sleep with a man⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “she did not know a man”</note> And it became an annual custom in Israel

verses.name: Judges 11:40
verses.text: for the daughters of Israel to go and lament the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite for forty days of the year.  <chapter eID="Judg.11"/>

verses.name: Judges 12:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1519"/><title type="x-s">Tribal Conflict Between Gilead and Ephraim</title> <div sID="gen2122" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1519"/>The men of Ephraim were called to arms, and they crossed <transChange type="added">over</transChange> to Zaphon and said to Jephthah, “Why did you cross <transChange type="added">over</transChange> and make war against the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> and why did you not call us to go with you? We will burn down your house over you with fire.”

verses.name: Judges 12:2
verses.text: And Jephthah said to them, “I and my people were engaged in great conflict with the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> I called you, but you did not deliver me from their hand.

verses.name: Judges 12:3
verses.text: I saw that you would not deliver <transChange type="added">us</transChange>; <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I risked my own life⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “I put my life in my hand”</note> and I crossed over to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> and Yahweh gave them into my hand. Why have you come up to me this day to fight against me?”

verses.name: Judges 12:4
verses.text: Jephthah gathered all the men of Gilead, and he made war with Ephraim; and the men of Gilead defeated Ephraim because they said, “You <transChange type="added">are</transChange> fugitives of Ephraim, you Gileadites, in the midst of Ephraim and Manasseh.”

verses.name: Judges 12:5
verses.text: Then Gilead captured the fords of the Jordan from Ephraim, and whenever a fugitive of Ephraim said, “Let me cross <transChange type="added">over</transChange>,” the men of Gilead said to him, “<transChange type="added">Are</transChange> you an Ephraimite?” <transChange type="added">When</transChange> he said, “No,”

verses.name: Judges 12:6
verses.text: they said to him, “Please say Shibboleth,” and <transChange type="added">if</transChange> he said, “Sibboleth”—because he could not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞pronounce it⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “speak it”</note> correctly—they grabbed him and executed him at the fords of Jordan. At that time forty-two thousand from Ephraim fell.  <div eID="gen2122" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 12:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1520"/><div sID="gen2123" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1520"/>Jephthah judged Israel six years. Then Jephthah the Gileadite died, and he was buried in <transChange type="added">one of</transChange> the cities of Gilead.  <div eID="gen2123" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 12:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1521"/><title type="x-s">Ibzan, Elon, and Abdon</title> <div sID="gen2124" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1521"/>After him Ibzan from Bethlehem judged Israel.

verses.name: Judges 12:9
verses.text: He had thirty sons. He gave his thirty daughters away in marriage outside <transChange type="added">his clan</transChange> and brought in from outside thirty young women for his sons. He judged Israel for seven years.

verses.name: Judges 12:10
verses.text: Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> Ibzan died and was buried in Bethlehem.  <div eID="gen2124" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 12:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1522"/><div sID="gen2125" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1522"/>After him Elon the Zebulunite judged Israel, and he judged Israel ten years.

verses.name: Judges 12:12
verses.text: Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> Elon the Zebulunite died and was buried in Aijalon in the land of Zebulun.  <div eID="gen2125" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 12:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1523"/><div sID="gen2126" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1523"/>After him Abdon the son of Hillel the Pirathonite judged Israel.

verses.name: Judges 12:14
verses.text: He had forty sons and thirty grandsons that rode on seventy male donkeys. He judged Israel for eight years.

verses.name: Judges 12:15
verses.text: Then<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> Abdon the son of Hillel the Pirathonite died and was buried in Pirathon, in the land of Ephraim in the hill country of the Amalekites.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Amalekite”</note>  <chapter eID="Judg.12"/>

verses.name: Judges 13:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1524"/><title type="x-s">Samson’s Parents</title> <div sID="gen2127" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1524"/>And again, the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> did evil in the eyes of Yahweh, and Yahweh gave them into the hand of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines forty years.  <div eID="gen2127" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 13:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1525"/><div sID="gen2128" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1525"/>There was a certain man from Zorah, from the tribe of the Danites, and his name <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Manoah; his wife <transChange type="added">was</transChange> infertile and did not bear children.

verses.name: Judges 13:3
verses.text: And an angel of Yahweh appeared to the woman, and he said to her, “Behold, you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> infertile and have not borne <transChange type="added">children</transChange>, but you will conceive and bear a son.

verses.name: Judges 13:4
verses.text: So then, be careful and do not drink wine or strong drink, and do not eat anything unclean,

verses.name: Judges 13:5
verses.text: because you <transChange type="added">will</transChange> conceive and bear a son. No razor <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞will touch⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “will go upon”</note> his head, because the boy will be a <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Nazirite of God⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “consecrated of God” or “devoted of God”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from birth⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “from the womb”</note> And it is he who will begin to deliver Israel from <transChange type="added">the</transChange> hand of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines.”

verses.name: Judges 13:6
verses.text: And the woman came and told her husband, saying, “A man of God came to me, and his appearance <transChange type="added">was</transChange> like the appearance of an angel of God, very awesome. I did not ask him from where he <transChange type="added">came</transChange>, and he did not tell me his name.

verses.name: Judges 13:7
verses.text: And he said to me, ‘Look, you <transChange type="added">will</transChange> conceive and bear a son, so then, do not drink wine or strong drink, and do not eat anything unclean, for the boy will be a Nazirite of God from birth<note placement="foot">Or “the womb”</note> until the day of his death.’ ”  <div eID="gen2128" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 13:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1526"/><div sID="gen2129" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1526"/>Then Manoah prayed to Yahweh and said, “Excuse me, my Lord, please let the man of God whom you sent again come to us and teach us what we should do concerning the boy who will be born.”

verses.name: Judges 13:9
verses.text: And God listened to the voice of Manoah, and an angel of God came again to the woman; she <transChange type="added">was</transChange> sitting in the field, but Manoah her husband was not with her.

verses.name: Judges 13:10
verses.text: The woman quickly ran and told her husband, and she said to him, “Look! The man who came to me the <transChange type="added">other</transChange> day appeared to me.”

verses.name: Judges 13:11
verses.text: So Manoah got up and went after his wife, and he came to the man and said to him, “<transChange type="added">Are</transChange> you the man that spoke to the woman?” And he said, “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange>.”

verses.name: Judges 13:12
verses.text: And Manoah said to him, “Now <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞when your words come true⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “when your words will come”</note> what will be the boy’s <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞manner of life⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “measure”</note> and work?”

verses.name: Judges 13:13
verses.text: And the angel of Yahweh said to Manoah, “Let the woman be attentive to all that I said.

verses.name: Judges 13:14
verses.text: She should not eat of anything that comes from the vine, or drink wine or strong drink, or eat anything unclean; she should keep all that I commanded.”  <div eID="gen2129" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 13:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1527"/><div sID="gen2130" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1527"/>And Manoah said to the angel of Yahweh, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Please stay⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “Please, let us hold you back”</note> and let us prepare a <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞young goat⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “kid of goat”</note> for you.”

verses.name: Judges 13:16
verses.text: The angel of Yahweh said to Manoah, “If you keep me, I will not eat your food, but if you prepare a burnt offering for Yahweh, you can offer it (for Manoah did not know that he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> an angel of Yahweh).”

verses.name: Judges 13:17
verses.text: And Manoah said to the angel of Yahweh, “What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> your name so that when your words come <transChange type="added">true</transChange> we may honor you?”

verses.name: Judges 13:18
verses.text: But the angel of Yahweh said to him, “Why do you ask my name? It <transChange type="added">is too</transChange> wonderful.”  <div eID="gen2130" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 13:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1528"/><div sID="gen2131" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1528"/>And Manoah took the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞young goat⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “kid of goat”</note> and the grain offering, and he offered it to Yahweh on the rock, to the one who performs miracles.<note placement="foot">Or “the one who works wonders”</note> And Manoah and his wife <transChange type="added">were</transChange> watching.

verses.name: Judges 13:20
verses.text: And when the flame went up toward the heaven from the altar, the angel of Yahweh went up in the flame of the altar to heaven while Manoah and his wife <transChange type="added">were</transChange> watching. And they fell on their faces to the ground.

verses.name: Judges 13:21
verses.text: The angel of Yahweh did not appear again to Manoah and his wife, and then Manoah knew that he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a messenger<note placement="foot">Or “angel”</note> of Yahweh.

verses.name: Judges 13:22
verses.text: And Manoah said to his wife, “We will certainly die because we have seen God.”

verses.name: Judges 13:23
verses.text: But his wife said to him, “If Yahweh wanted to kill us he would not have taken<note placement="foot">Or “accepted”</note> from our hand the burnt offering and the grain offering, or shown us all these things, or now announced to us things such as these.”  <div eID="gen2131" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 13:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1529"/><div sID="gen2132" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1529"/>The woman bore a son, and she called him Samson; the boy grew big, and Yahweh blessed him.

verses.name: Judges 13:25
verses.text: And the Spirit of Yahweh began to stir him in the camp of Dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol.  <chapter eID="Judg.13"/>

verses.name: Judges 14:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1530"/><title type="x-s">Samson Marries</title> <div sID="gen2133" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1530"/>And Samson went down to Timnah, and he saw a woman in Timnah from the daughters of the Philistines.

verses.name: Judges 14:2
verses.text: He went up and told his father and mother, and he said, “I saw a woman in Timnah from the daughters of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines; so then, take her for me as a wife.”

verses.name: Judges 14:3
verses.text: But his father and mother said to him, “Is there not a wife among the daughters of your relatives, or among all our<note placement="foot">Hebrew “my”</note> people, that you must take a wife from the uncircumcised Philistines?” But Samson said to his father, “Take her for me because <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞she pleases me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “she is right in my eyes”</note>

verses.name: Judges 14:4
verses.text: His father and mother did not know that this <transChange type="added">was</transChange> from Yahweh; he was seeking for an occasion against <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines. Now at that time <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines <transChange type="added">were</transChange> ruling<note placement="foot">Or “having control”</note> in Israel.  <div eID="gen2133" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 14:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1531"/><div sID="gen2134" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1531"/>And Samson and his father and mother went down to Timnah, and they came to the vineyards of Timnah, and suddenly a young lion <transChange type="added">came</transChange> roaring to meet him.

verses.name: Judges 14:6
verses.text: And the Spirit of Yahweh rushed upon him, and he tore the lion apart as one might tear apart a male kid goat (<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he was bare-handed⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>).<note placement="foot">Literally “there was nothing in his hand”</note> But he did not tell his father and mother what he had done.

verses.name: Judges 14:7
verses.text: Then he went down and talked to the woman, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞she pleased Samson⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “she did what was right in the eyes of Samson”</note>

verses.name: Judges 14:8
verses.text: And he returned after awhile <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to marry her⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to take her”</note> and he turned aside to see the carcass of the lion, and there <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a swarm of wild honey bees in the body of the lion, and honey.

verses.name: Judges 14:9
verses.text: He scraped it out into his hands, and he went on, eating <transChange type="added">it</transChange> as he went. And he went to his father and mother and gave <transChange type="added">some</transChange> to them, and they ate it. But he did not tell them that he had scraped the honey from the body of the lion.  <div eID="gen2134" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 14:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1532"/><div sID="gen2135" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1532"/>His father went down to the woman, and Samson prepared there a feast, as young men were accustomed to doing this.

verses.name: Judges 14:11
verses.text: When they saw him, they took thirty companions, and they were with him.

verses.name: Judges 14:12
verses.text: And Samson said to them, “Let me tell you a riddle. If you can fully explain it to me within the seven days of the feast, and find <transChange type="added">it out</transChange>, I will give to you thirty linen garments and thirty festal garments.

verses.name: Judges 14:13
verses.text: But if you are unable to explain it to me, you must give me thirty linen garments and thirty festal garments.” So they said to him, “Tell your riddle; let us hear it.”

verses.name: Judges 14:14
verses.text: He said to them, <div eID="gen2135" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen2136"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2137"/>“From the eater came out food,<l eID="gen2137" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2138"/>From <transChange type="added">the</transChange> strong came out sweet.”<l eID="gen2138" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen2136"/> <div sID="gen2139" type="x-p"/> But they were unable to explain the riddle for three days.  <div eID="gen2139" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 14:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1533"/><div sID="gen2140" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1533"/>When it was the fourth<note placement="foot">Hebrew “seventh”; other ancient translations have “fourth”</note> day, they said to Samson’s wife, “Entice your husband and tell us the riddle, or we will burn you and your father’s house with fire. Have you invited us to rob us?”

verses.name: Judges 14:16
verses.text: And Samson’s wife wept before him, and she said, “You must hate me; you do not love me. You told the riddle to <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞my people⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the sons/children of my people”</note> but you have not explained <transChange type="added">it</transChange> to me.” He said to her, “I have not explained <transChange type="added">it</transChange> to my father and mother. <transChange type="added">Why</transChange> should I explain it to you?”

verses.name: Judges 14:17
verses.text: She wept before him the seven days of their feast; and it happened, because she nagged him, on the seventh day he explained <transChange type="added">it</transChange> to her, and she told the riddle to <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞her people⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the sons/children of her people”</note>

verses.name: Judges 14:18
verses.text: The men of the city said to him on the seventh day before the sun went <transChange type="added">down</transChange>, <div eID="gen2140" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen2141"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2142"/>“What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> sweeter than honey?<l eID="gen2142" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2143"/>What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> stronger than a lion?”<l eID="gen2143" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen2141"/> <div sID="gen2144" type="x-p"/> And he said to them, <div eID="gen2144" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen2145"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2146"/>“If you had not plowed with my heifer,<l eID="gen2146" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2147"/>you would not have found out my riddle.” <l eID="gen2147" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen2145"/>

verses.name: Judges 14:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1534"/><div sID="gen2148" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1534"/>And the Spirit of Yahweh rushed on him, and he went down to Ashkelon. He killed thirty men from them, and he took their belongings, and he gave festal garments to the ones that explained the riddle. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞He was angry⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “his nose was hot”</note> and he went up to his father’s house.

verses.name: Judges 14:20
verses.text: And Samson’s wife was <transChange type="added">given</transChange> to his companion who <transChange type="added">was</transChange> his best man.<note placement="foot">Or “friend”</note>  <chapter eID="Judg.14"/>

verses.name: Judges 15:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1535"/><title type="x-s">Samson Defeats the Philistines</title> <div sID="gen2149" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1535"/>After a while, at the time of the wheat harvest, Samson visited his wife with a <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞young goat⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “kid of goat”</note> He said, “I want to go to my wife’s private room.” But her father would not allow him to enter.

verses.name: Judges 15:2
verses.text: Her father said, “I really thought that you hated her, so I gave her to your companion. <transChange type="added">Is</transChange> not her younger sister more beautiful than she? Please, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞take her instead⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “let her be in the place of her”</note>

verses.name: Judges 15:3
verses.text: And Samson said to them, “This time, as far as the Philistines are concerned, when I do something evil I am without blame.”

verses.name: Judges 15:4
verses.text: And Samson went and captured three hundred foxes, and he took torches. He turned <transChange type="added">them</transChange> tail to tail, and he put one torch between two tails.

verses.name: Judges 15:5
verses.text: He set fire to the torches and let <transChange type="added">the foxes</transChange> go into the standing grain of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines, and he burned both the stacks<note placement="foot">Hebrew “stack”</note> of sheaves and the standing grain, up to the vineyards<note placement="foot">Hebrew “vineyard”</note> of olive groves.

verses.name: Judges 15:6
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines said, “Who has done this?” And they said, “Samson the son-in-law of the Timnite, because he took his wife and gave her to his companion.” And <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines went up and burned her and her father with fire.

verses.name: Judges 15:7
verses.text: Samson said to them, “If you want to behave like this, <transChange type="added">I swear</transChange> I will not rest unless I have taken revenge on you.”

verses.name: Judges 15:8
verses.text: And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he gave them a thorough beating⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “he struck them hip and thigh with a great blow”</note> and he went down and stayed in the cleft of the rock of Etam.  <div eID="gen2149" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 15:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1536"/><div sID="gen2150" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1536"/>Then <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines came up and encamped in Judah, and they overran Lehi.

verses.name: Judges 15:10
verses.text: And the men of Judah said, “Why have you come up against us?” And they said, “To bind Samson; to do to him just as he did to us.”

verses.name: Judges 15:11
verses.text: Then three thousand men from Judah went down to the cleft of the rock of Etam, and they said to Samson, “Do you not know that the Philistines <transChange type="added">are</transChange> ruling over us? What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> this <transChange type="added">that</transChange> you have done to us?” And he said to them, “Just as they did to me, so I have done to them.”

verses.name: Judges 15:12
verses.text: They said to him, “We have come down to bind you and give you over into the hand of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines.” And Samson said to them, “Swear to me that you will not attack me yourselves.”

verses.name: Judges 15:13
verses.text: They said to him, “No, we will only bind you and give you into their hand; we will certainly not kill you.” So they bound him with two new ropes, and they brought him up from the rock.  <div eID="gen2150" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 15:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1537"/><div sID="gen2151" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1537"/>As he came up to Lehi, <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines came shouting to meet him; and the Spirit of Yahweh rushed on him, and the ropes that <transChange type="added">were</transChange> on his arms became like flax that has burned with fire, and his bindings melted from his hands.

verses.name: Judges 15:15
verses.text: And he found a fresh jawbone of a donkey; he reached down and took it and killed one thousand men with it.

verses.name: Judges 15:16
verses.text: And Samson said, <div eID="gen2151" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen2152"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2153"/>“With the jawbone of the donkey,<l eID="gen2153" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2154"/>heap upon heap;<l eID="gen2154" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2155"/>with the jawbone of the donkey,<l eID="gen2155" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2156"/>I struck dead one thousand men.” <l eID="gen2156" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen2152"/>

verses.name: Judges 15:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1538"/><div sID="gen2157" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1538"/>And it happened, when he finished speaking he threw the jawbone from his hand; and he called that place Ramath Lehi.<note placement="foot">That is, “Hill of the Jawbone”</note>  <div eID="gen2157" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 15:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1539"/><div sID="gen2158" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1539"/>And he was very thirsty, and he called to Yahweh and said, “You gave this great victory into the hand of your servant, but now I must die of thirst and fall into the hand of the uncircumcised?”

verses.name: Judges 15:19
verses.text: So God split the hollow place that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> at Lehi, and water came out from it; and he drank, and his spirit returned, and he was revived. Thus he called its name <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞The Spring of Ha-Qore⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the spring of the one who called” or “En-hakkore”</note> which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> at Lehi to this day.

verses.name: Judges 15:20
verses.text: And he judged Israel in the days of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines twenty years.  <chapter eID="Judg.15"/>

verses.name: Judges 16:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1540"/><title type="x-s">Samson and Delilah</title> <div sID="gen2159" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1540"/>Samson went down to Gaza; there he saw a prostitute and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞had sex with her⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “went into her”</note>

verses.name: Judges 16:2
verses.text: The Gazites <transChange type="added">were told</transChange>, “Samson has come here,” so they surrounded <transChange type="added">the place</transChange> and lay in ambush for him all night at the city gate. They kept silent all night, saying, “<transChange type="added">We will wait</transChange> until the morning light, and then we will kill him.”

verses.name: Judges 16:3
verses.text: But Samson lay until the middle of the night; he got up in the middle of the night and took hold of the doors of the city gate and the two door posts, tore them loose with the bar, put them on his shoulders, and carried them up to the top of the hill that is <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in front of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “on the face of”</note> Hebron.  <div eID="gen2159" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 16:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1541"/><div sID="gen2160" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1541"/>After this he fell in love <transChange type="added">with</transChange> a woman in the wadi<note placement="foot">A valley that is dry most of the year, but contains a stream during the rainy season</note> of Sorek, and her name <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Delilah.

verses.name: Judges 16:5
verses.text: And the rulers of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines came up to her and said, “Entice him and find out what makes his strength so great, and how we can overpower him, so that we may bind him up in order to subdue him; each of us will give you eleven hundred pieces of silver.

verses.name: Judges 16:6
verses.text: So Delilah said to Samson, “Please tell me what makes your strength so great, and with what can you be tied up to subdue you?”

verses.name: Judges 16:7
verses.text: Samson said to her, “If you tie me up with seven fresh bowstrings that are not dried up, I will become weak like everyone else.”

verses.name: Judges 16:8
verses.text: So the rulers of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines brought up to her seven fresh bowstrings that were not dried up, and she tied him up with them.

verses.name: Judges 16:9
verses.text: The ambush <transChange type="added">was</transChange> sitting <transChange type="added">in wait</transChange> for her in an inner room. And she said to him, “<transChange type="added">The</transChange> Philistines <transChange type="added">are</transChange> upon you Samson!” And he snapped the bowstrings just as flax fiber snaps when it comes close to fire. And <transChange type="added">the secret of</transChange> his strength remained unknown.

verses.name: Judges 16:10
verses.text: Delilah said to Samson, “Look, you have mocked me and told me lies. Please tell me how you can be bound.”

verses.name: Judges 16:11
verses.text: He said to her, “If they tie me tightly with new ropes that have not been used, I will become weak and be like everyone else.”

verses.name: Judges 16:12
verses.text: So Delilah took new ropes and tied him up with them, and she said to him, “<transChange type="added">The</transChange> Philistines <transChange type="added">are</transChange> upon you, Samson!” (The ambush <transChange type="added">was</transChange> sitting in an inner room.) But he snapped them from his arms like thread.  <div eID="gen2160" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 16:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1542"/><div sID="gen2161" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1542"/>And Delilah said to Samson, “Until now you have mocked me and told lies to me. Tell me how you can be bound.” And he said to her, “If you weave seven locks of my head with warp-threads.”<note placement="foot">Many modern translations include an additional phrase found in the Greek translation: “and fasten it with a pin, then I will become weak and be like everyone else. So while he slept, Delilah took the seven locks of his head and wove them”</note>

verses.name: Judges 16:14
verses.text: She fastened <transChange type="added">it</transChange> with the pin and said to him, “<transChange type="added">The</transChange> Philistines <transChange type="added">are</transChange> upon you, Samson!” And Samson woke up from his sleep and tore loose the loom pin of the web and the warp-threads.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “warp-thread”</note>  <div eID="gen2161" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 16:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1543"/><div sID="gen2162" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1543"/>And she said to him, “How can you say, ‘I love you,’ when your heart is not with me? You have mocked me these three times, and you have not told me how your strength is <transChange type="added">so</transChange> great.”

verses.name: Judges 16:16
verses.text: And because she nagged him day after day with her words, and pestered him, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his soul grew impatient to the point of death⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “his inner self grew tired/impatient to death”</note>

verses.name: Judges 16:17
verses.text: So <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he confided everything to her⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “he told her all his heart”</note> and he said to her, “A razor <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞has never touched⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “has never gone up”</note> my head, for I am a <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Nazirite of God⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “consecrated of God” or “devoted of God”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from birth⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “from the womb of my mother”</note> If I am shaved my strength will leave me, and I will become weak, like everyone else.  <div eID="gen2162" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 16:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1544"/><div sID="gen2163" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1544"/>Delilah realized that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he had confided in her⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “he had told her all his heart”</note> so she sent and called the rulers of the Philistines, saying, “Come up one more time, for <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he has confided in me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “he has told me all his heart”</note> And the rulers of the Philistines came up, and they brought the money <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞with them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “in their hand”</note>

verses.name: Judges 16:19
verses.text: And she put him to sleep on her lap; then she called the men<note placement="foot">Hebrew “man”</note> and shaved off seven locks of his head. Then she began to subdue him,<note placement="foot">Or “humiliate him”</note> and his strength went away from him.

verses.name: Judges 16:20
verses.text: And she said to him, “<transChange type="added">The</transChange> Philistines <transChange type="added">are</transChange> upon you, Samson!” And he woke up from his sleep and said, “I will go out just like every other time and shake myself free,” but he did not know that Yahweh had left him.

verses.name: Judges 16:21
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines seized him, gouged his eyes, and brought him to Gaza. They tied him up with bronze shackles, and he became a grinder <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in the prison⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “in the house of the prisoners”</note>

verses.name: Judges 16:22
verses.text: But the hair of his head began to grow back after it had been shaved off.  <div eID="gen2163" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 16:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1545"/><div sID="gen2164" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1545"/>The rulers of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines had gathered to sacrifice a great sacrifice to Dagon their god and to rejoice. And they said, “Our god has given Samson our enemy into our hand.”

verses.name: Judges 16:24
verses.text: And the people saw him, and they praised their god, for they said, “Our god has given into our hand those who hate us, devastate our land, and have <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞killed many of us⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “made numerous our slain”</note>

verses.name: Judges 16:25
verses.text: After awhile, when their hearts<note placement="foot">Hebrew “heart”</note> were merry, they said, “Call Samson and let him entertain us.” And they called Samson <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from the prison⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “from the house of the prisoner”</note> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he entertained them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “he made sport before them”</note> And they made him stand between the pillars.

verses.name: Judges 16:26
verses.text: Then Samson said to the servant who was holding him by his hand, “Position me so that I can touch the pillars on which the house<note placement="foot">Or “temple”</note> rests, so I can lean on them.”

verses.name: Judges 16:27
verses.text: And the house<note placement="foot">Or “temple”</note> was full of men and women, and all of the rulers of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines <transChange type="added">were</transChange> there—about three thousand men and women were on the roof watching the performance of Samson.  <div eID="gen2164" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 16:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1546"/><title type="x-s">Samson’s Revenge</title> <div sID="gen2165" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1546"/>And Samson called to Yahweh and said, “My Lord Yahweh, remember me! Please give me strength this one time, O God, so that I can repay <transChange type="added">with</transChange> one act of revenge to <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines for my eyes.”

verses.name: Judges 16:29
verses.text: And Samson reached out and held two of the middle pillars on which the house<note placement="foot">Or “temple”</note> <transChange type="added">was</transChange> resting, and he leaned on them, one on his right and one on his left.

verses.name: Judges 16:30
verses.text: And Samson said, “Let me die with the Philistines.” And he pushed<note placement="foot">Or “he caused to bend”</note> with all his strength, and the house<note placement="foot">Or “temple”</note> fell on the rulers and all of the people who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him. And the dead whom he killed in his death were more than those he killed in his life.  <div eID="gen2165" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 16:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1547"/><div sID="gen2166" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1547"/>His brothers and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his whole family⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “all the house of his father”</note> came down and picked him up; and they brought him up and buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol in the tomb of Manoah his father; he judged Israel twenty years.  <chapter eID="Judg.16"/>

verses.name: Judges 17:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1548"/><title type="x-s">Micah’s Idolatry</title> <div sID="gen2167" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1548"/>There was a man from the hill country of Ephraim; his name <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Micah.

verses.name: Judges 17:2
verses.text: And he said to his mother, “The eleven hundred <transChange type="added">pieces</transChange> of silver that were taken from you, and about which you also pronounced a curse <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in my hearing⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “In my ears”</note> are with me; I took it.” And his mother said, “Blessed be my son by Yahweh.”

verses.name: Judges 17:3
verses.text: He returned the eleven hundred pieces<note placement="foot">Hebrew “piece”</note> of silver to his mother, and his mother thought, “I will certainly consecrate to Yahweh the pieces<note placement="foot">Hebrew “piece”</note> of silver from my hand for my son to make an idol of cast metal; now then, I will return them<note placement="foot">Hebrew “it”</note> to you.”

verses.name: Judges 17:4
verses.text: When he returned the pieces<note placement="foot">Hebrew “piece”</note> of silver to his mother, his mother took two hundred pieces<note placement="foot">Hebrew “piece”</note> of silver, and she gave it to the smith, and he made it <transChange type="added">into</transChange> an idol of cast metal; and it was in the house of Micah.

verses.name: Judges 17:5
verses.text: The man Micah had for himself <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a shrine⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “a house of god”</note> and he made an ephod and teraphim, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he appointed one of his sons⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “he filled the hand of one of his sons”</note> who became a priest for him.

verses.name: Judges 17:6
verses.text: In those days there was no king in Israel, and each one did what was right in his own eyes.  <div eID="gen2167" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 17:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1549"/><div sID="gen2168" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1549"/>There was a young man from Bethlehem in Judah, from the clan of Judah; he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a Levite and <transChange type="added">was</transChange> dwelling as a foreigner<note placement="foot">Or “alien”</note> there.

verses.name: Judges 17:8
verses.text: And the man went from the town of Bethlehem in Judah to live as a foreigner<note placement="foot">Or “alien”</note> wherever he could find <transChange type="added">a place</transChange>. And he came <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the hill country of Ephraim, to the house of Micah, to continue his journey.

verses.name: Judges 17:9
verses.text: And Micah said to him, “From where do you come?” And he said to him, “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah; I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> going to dwell as a foreigner<note placement="foot">Or “alien”</note> wherever I can find <transChange type="added">a place</transChange>.”

verses.name: Judges 17:10
verses.text: And Micah said to him, “Stay with me and be to me a father and a priest, and I will give to you ten pieces<note placement="foot">Hebrew “piece”</note> of silver a year, a set of clothes, and your food.” So the Levite went <transChange type="added">with him</transChange>.

verses.name: Judges 17:11
verses.text: The Levite agreed to stay with the man; and the young man became as one of his sons.

verses.name: Judges 17:12
verses.text: So Micah <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞appointed the Levite⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “filled the hand of the Levite”</note> and the young man became a priest for him; and he was in the house of Micah.

verses.name: Judges 17:13
verses.text: And Micah said, “Now I know Yahweh will make me prosperous, because the Levite has become my priest.”  <chapter eID="Judg.17"/>

verses.name: Judges 18:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1550"/><title type="x-s">The Tribe of Dan Seeks Territory</title> <div sID="gen2169" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1550"/>In those days there was no king in Israel. And in those days the tribe of the Danites <transChange type="added">was</transChange> seeking territory for itself to live in, because until that day it had not been allotted territory among the tribes of Israel.

verses.name: Judges 18:2
verses.text: The descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons/children”</note> of Dan sent from the whole number of their clan five <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞capable men⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons of physical strength”</note> from Zorah and Eshtaol to spy out the land and to explore it. And they said to them, “Go, explore the land.” And they went to the hill country of Ephraim, to the house of Micah, and they spent the night there.<note placement="foot">Or “they lodged there”</note>

verses.name: Judges 18:3
verses.text: While they <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with the house of Micah, they recognized the voice of the young Levite, and they turned aside there and said to him, “Who brought you here?
