What <transChange type="added">are</transChange> you doing in this place, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞what is your business here⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?”<note placement="foot">Literally “What is for you here?”</note>

verses.name: Judges 18:4
verses.text: And he said to them, “Micah did such and such for me and hired me, and I became his priest.”

verses.name: Judges 18:5
verses.text: And they said to him, “Please inquire of God that we may know whether our journey that we <transChange type="added">are</transChange> going on will be successful.”

verses.name: Judges 18:6
verses.text: And the priest said to them, “Go in peace. Yahweh <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in front of you on the journey you want to go on.”  <div eID="gen2169" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 18:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1551"/><div sID="gen2170" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1551"/>And the five men went and came to Laish, and they observed the people who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> living according to the customs of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Sidonians, quiet and unsuspecting, and lacking nothing in the land, and possessing restraint.<note placement="foot">Or perhaps “prosperity”; the Hebrew of this word is uncertain</note> And they <transChange type="added">were</transChange> far from <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Sidonians and had no word with anyone.

verses.name: Judges 18:8
verses.text: They came to their relatives<note placement="foot">Or “brothers”</note> at Zorah and Eshtaol, and their relatives<note placement="foot">Or “brothers”</note> said to them, “What <transChange type="added">do</transChange> you <transChange type="added">report</transChange>?”

verses.name: Judges 18:9
verses.text: And they said to them, “Come, let us go up against them; for we have seen the land, and <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> very good. Will you do nothing? Do not hesitate to go, to enter, to possess the land.

verses.name: Judges 18:10
verses.text: When you go you will come to an unsuspecting people, and the land <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞is spread out on all sides⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “is wide of hands”</note> God has given a place into your hands where there is no lack of anything that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> on the earth.”  <div eID="gen2170" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 18:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1552"/><div sID="gen2171" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1552"/>Six hundred men from the clan of the Danites from Zorah and Eshtaol, armed <transChange type="added">with</transChange> weapons of war, set out from there.

verses.name: Judges 18:12
verses.text: They went up and encamped at Kiriath Jearim in Judah. Therefore they called this place Camp of Dan<note placement="foot">That is “Mahaneh-dan”</note> to this day; it is west of Kiriath Jearim.

verses.name: Judges 18:13
verses.text: From there they crossed <transChange type="added">over to</transChange> the hill country of Ephraim, and they came to the house of Micah.  <div eID="gen2171" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 18:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1553"/><div sID="gen2172" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1553"/>And the five men that went out to spy out the land (<transChange type="added">that is</transChange>, Laish) responded and said to their relatives,<note placement="foot">Or “brothers”</note> “Do you know that there are in these houses an ephod, teraphim, and an idol of cast metal? So then, consider what you must do.”

verses.name: Judges 18:15
verses.text: So they turned to that direction, and they came to the house of the young Levite, the house of Micah, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they greeted him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “they asked for him in peace”</note>

verses.name: Judges 18:16
verses.text: And six hundred men from the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons/children”</note> of Dan, armed <transChange type="added">with</transChange> their weapons of war, <transChange type="added">were</transChange> standing <transChange type="added">at</transChange> the entrance of the gate.

verses.name: Judges 18:17
verses.text: And the five men that went to spy out the land went up, and they entered there <transChange type="added">and</transChange> took the carved divine image, ephod, teraphim, and the molten image. The priest <transChange type="added">was</transChange> standing <transChange type="added">at</transChange> the entrance of the gate <transChange type="added">with</transChange> the six hundred men armed <transChange type="added">with</transChange> the weapons of war.

verses.name: Judges 18:18
verses.text: When these went to Micah’s house, they took the divine carved image, ephod, the teraphim, and the molten image, and the priest asked them, “What <transChange type="added">are</transChange> you doing?”

verses.name: Judges 18:19
verses.text: And they said to him, “Keep quiet! Put your hand on your mouth and come with us and be for us a father and a priest. Is it better being a priest for a house of one man or being a priest for a tribe and clan in Israel?”

verses.name: Judges 18:20
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞The priest accepted the offer⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “It was good in the heart of the priest”</note> and he took the ephod, teraphim, and molten image and went along with the people.  <div eID="gen2172" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 18:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1554"/><div sID="gen2173" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1554"/>And they turned<note placement="foot">Or “resumed their journey”</note> and went and put the little children, the livestock, and the valuable property in front of them.

verses.name: Judges 18:22
verses.text: When they were at a distance from the house, Micah and the men who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in the houses that <transChange type="added">were</transChange> near the house of Micah cried out, and they overtook the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons/children”</note> of Dan.

verses.name: Judges 18:23
verses.text: And they called to the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons/children”</note> of Dan, who turned around to face them, and they said to Micah, “What is the matter with you that you assembled together?”

verses.name: Judges 18:24
verses.text: He said, “You took away my gods that I had made, and the priest, and then you go <transChange type="added">away</transChange>. What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> now left for me? How can you say to me, ‘What is the matter?’ ”

verses.name: Judges 18:25
verses.text: And the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons/children”</note> of Dan said to him, “You should not let your voice be heard among us, so that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞ill-tempered men⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “men of bitter soul”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞will not attack you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “will not fall on you”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞and take your life⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and you will lose your life”</note> and the lives of your household.”

verses.name: Judges 18:26
verses.text: And the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons/children”</note> of Dan went their way. When Micah saw that they <transChange type="added">were</transChange> stronger than him, he turned to return to his house.  <div eID="gen2173" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 18:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1555"/><div sID="gen2174" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1555"/>And they took what Micah had made, and his priest, and they came to Laish, to a quiet and unsuspecting people, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they put them to the sword⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “they put them to the mouth of the sword”</note> and burned the city with fire.

verses.name: Judges 18:28
verses.text: There was no deliverer, because it <transChange type="added">was</transChange> far from Sidon, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they had had no dealings with anyone⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “a thing was not for them with anyone”</note> It was in the valley that belonged to Beth-rehob, and they rebuilt<note placement="foot">Hebrew “built”</note> the city and lived in it.

verses.name: Judges 18:29
verses.text: And they called the name of the city Dan, after Dan their ancestor,<note placement="foot">Or “father”</note> who was born to Israel; but the former name of the city <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Laish.

verses.name: Judges 18:30
verses.text: And the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons/children”</note> of Dan set up for themselves the carved divine image, and Jonathan son of Gershom, son of Manasseh,<note placement="foot">Other ancient versions read “Moses”</note> he and his sons were priests for the tribe of the Danites until the time of the captivity of the land.

verses.name: Judges 18:31
verses.text: So they set up for themselves the carved divine image that Micah had made, all the days that the house of God <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in Shiloh.  <chapter eID="Judg.18"/>

verses.name: Judges 19:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1556"/><title type="x-s">The Concubine and the Levite</title> <div sID="gen2175" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1556"/>In those days there was no king in Israel; there was a man, a Levite, who dwelled as a foreigner<note placement="foot">Or “alien”</note> in the remote areas of the hill country of Ephraim. And he took for himself a concubine from Bethlehem in Judah.

verses.name: Judges 19:2
verses.text: But his concubine felt repugnance toward him,<note placement="foot">Other modern translations read “his concubine played the harlot against him”</note> and she left him and went to her father’s house, to Bethlehem in Judah; she was there some four months.

verses.name: Judges 19:3
verses.text: So her husband set out, and he went after her to speak <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞tenderly to her⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to her heart”</note> to bring her back. He took with him his servant and a pair of donkeys. And she brought him <transChange type="added">to</transChange> her father’s house, and the father of the young woman saw him and was glad to meet him.

verses.name: Judges 19:4
verses.text: His father-in-law, the young woman’s father, urged him to stay with him three days; and they ate and drank, and they spent the night there.

verses.name: Judges 19:5
verses.text: On the fourth day, they rose early in the morning, and he prepared to go, but the father of the young woman said to his son-in-law, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Refresh yourself⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Refresh your heart”</note> <transChange type="added">with</transChange> a bit of food, and afterward you may go.”

verses.name: Judges 19:6
verses.text: So the two of them sat and ate and drank together, and the father of the young woman said to the man, “Please, agree to spend the night and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞enjoy yourself⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “and let your heart be good”</note>

verses.name: Judges 19:7
verses.text: The man got up to go, but his father-in-law urged him, and he returned and spent the night there.

verses.name: Judges 19:8
verses.text: On the fifth day he rose early in the morning to go, and the father of the young woman said, “Please, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞enjoy yourself⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,”<note placement="foot">Literally “and let your heart be good”</note> and they lingered until the day declined, and the two of them ate.

verses.name: Judges 19:9
verses.text: And the man got up to go—he, his concubine, and his servant—but his father-in-law, the father of the young woman, said to him, “Please, the day has worn on to evening; please, spend the night, the day has drawn to a close. Spend the night here and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞enjoy yourself⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “and let your heart be good”</note> You can rise early tomorrow for your journey and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞go to your home⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “go to your tent”</note>  <div eID="gen2175" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 19:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1557"/><div sID="gen2176" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1557"/>But the man was not willing to spend the night, and he got up and went; and he arrived opposite Jebus (that is, Jerusalem). <transChange type="added">He had</transChange> with him a pair of saddled donkeys and his concubine.

verses.name: Judges 19:11
verses.text: They <transChange type="added">were</transChange> near Jebus, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the day was far spent⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the day went down very”</note> and the servant said to his master, “Please, come, let us turn aside to this city of the Jebusites,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Jebusite”</note> and let us spend the night in it.”

verses.name: Judges 19:12
verses.text: But his master said to him, “We will not turn aside to the city of foreigners,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “foreigner”</note> who are not from the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> we will cross over up to Gibeah.”

verses.name: Judges 19:13
verses.text: And he said to his servant, “Come, let us approach one of these places; we will spend the night in Gibeah or in Ramah.”

verses.name: Judges 19:14
verses.text: So they crossed over and went their way, and the sun went down on them beside Gibeah, which belongs to Benjamin.

verses.name: Judges 19:15
verses.text: And they turned aside there to enter <transChange type="added">and</transChange> to spend the night at Gibeah. And they went and sat in the open square of the city, but no one <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞took them in to spend the night⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “was receiving them to their house to spend the night”</note>  <div eID="gen2176" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 19:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1558"/><div sID="gen2177" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1558"/>Then behold, an old man <transChange type="added">was</transChange> coming from his work from the field in the evening, and the man <transChange type="added">was</transChange> from the hill country of Ephraim, and he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> dwelling as a foreigner<note placement="foot">Or “alien”</note> in Gibeah. (The people of the place were descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons/children”</note> of Benjamin.)

verses.name: Judges 19:17
verses.text: And the old man raised his eyes and saw the traveler in the open square of the city, and he said, “Where are you going, and from where do you come?”

verses.name: Judges 19:18
verses.text: And he said to him, “We <transChange type="added">are</transChange> crossing over from Bethlehem in Judah up to the remote areas of the hill country of Ephraim, where I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> from. I went to Bethlehem in Judah, but <transChange type="added">now</transChange> I am going to Yahweh’s house,<note placement="foot">Or “my house,” according to the LXX and some modern translations (NASB, NRSV)</note> but no one <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞took me in to spend the night⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “was receiving me to their house”</note>

verses.name: Judges 19:19
verses.text: There is both straw and fodder for our donkeys, and also bread and wine for me, for your servant,<note placement="foot">That is, the concubine</note> and for the young man who is with your servant; there is no lack of anything.”

verses.name: Judges 19:20
verses.text: And the old man said, “Peace to you. I will take care of your needs; however, you must not spend the night in the open square.”

verses.name: Judges 19:21
verses.text: So he brought him to his house, and he fed the donkeys; they washed their feet, ate, and drank.  <div eID="gen2177" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 19:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1559"/><div sID="gen2178" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1559"/>While <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they were enjoying themselves⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “their hearts were being good”</note> behold, the men of the city, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the perverse lot⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons of uselessness”</note> surrounded the house, pounding on the door. And they said to the old man, the owner of the house, “Bring out the man who came to your house so that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞we may have sex with him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “we may know him”</note>

verses.name: Judges 19:23
verses.text: So the man, the owner of the house, went out to them and said to them, “No, my brothers, do not act wickedly; since this man has come into my house, do not do this disgraceful thing.

verses.name: Judges 19:24
verses.text: Here is my virgin daughter and his concubine. Please, let me bring them out; do violence to them,<note placement="foot">Or “rape them”</note> and do to them <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞whatever you please⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the good in your eyes”</note> Do not do this disgraceful thing to this man.”

verses.name: Judges 19:25
verses.text: But the men were not willing to listen to him, and the man seized his concubine and brought <transChange type="added">her</transChange> out to them; and they had intercourse with her, and they abused her all night until the morning; they let her go at the approach of dawn.

verses.name: Judges 19:26
verses.text: And the woman came as the morning appeared, and she fell <transChange type="added">at</transChange> the entrance of the man’s house where her master was, until daylight.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “light”</note>  <div eID="gen2178" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 19:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1560"/><div sID="gen2179" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1560"/>In the morning her master got up, and he opened the doors of the house and went out to go on his journey, and behold, his concubine <transChange type="added">was</transChange> falling<note placement="foot">Or “spread out”</note> <transChange type="added">at</transChange> the entrance of the house, with her hand on the threshold.

verses.name: Judges 19:28
verses.text: And he said to her, “Get up, let us go,” but there was no answer. So he put her on the donkey, and the man got up and went to his place.

verses.name: Judges 19:29
verses.text: When he entered his house he took a knife, and he grasped his concubine and cut her into twelve pieces; and he sent her throughout the whole territory of Israel.

verses.name: Judges 19:30
verses.text: All who saw <transChange type="added">it</transChange> said, “Nothing like this has <transChange type="added">ever</transChange> been since the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> went up from the land of Egypt until this day. Take note of it, consider <transChange type="added">it</transChange>, and speak <transChange type="added">up</transChange>.”  <chapter eID="Judg.19"/>

verses.name: Judges 20:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1561"/><title type="x-s">The Punishment of Benjamin</title> <div sID="gen2180" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1561"/>All the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> went out, from Dan to Beersheba, including the land of Gilead, and they gathered as one body<note placement="foot">Hebrew “man”</note> to Yahweh <transChange type="added">at</transChange> Mizpah.

verses.name: Judges 20:2
verses.text: And the leaders of all the people, all the tribes of Israel, presented themselves in the assembly of the people of God, four hundred thousand sword-bearing infantry.

verses.name: Judges 20:3
verses.text: (The descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons/children”</note> of Benjamin heard that the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> had gone up to Mizpah.) And the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons of Israel” or “children of “Israel”</note> said, “Tell us, how did this evil act occur?”

verses.name: Judges 20:4
verses.text: The Levite, the husband of the murdered woman, answered and said, “I came to Gibeah, which belongs to Benjamin, I and my concubine, to spend the night.

verses.name: Judges 20:5
verses.text: The lords of Gibeah rose up against me and surrounded the house at night. They intended to kill me, and they raped my concubine, and she died.

verses.name: Judges 20:6
verses.text: Then I grabbed my concubine and cut her into pieces, and I sent her throughout all the territory of Israel’s inheritance; for they committed a shameful and disgraceful thing in Israel.

verses.name: Judges 20:7
verses.text: Look, all you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Make your decision⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “give your word”</note> and advice here.”  <div eID="gen2180" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 20:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1562"/><div sID="gen2181" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1562"/>All the people got up as one body,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “man”</note> saying, “Not one of us will go to his tent, or will any of us return to his house.

verses.name: Judges 20:9
verses.text: So then, this is what we will do to Gibeah: <transChange type="added">we will go up</transChange> against her by lot.

verses.name: Judges 20:10
verses.text: We will take ten men of one hundred from all the tribes of Israel, and one hundred of one thousand, and one thousand of ten thousand, to bring provisions to the troops, to repay <transChange type="added">them</transChange> when they come to Gibeah<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Geba”</note> of Benjamin for all the disgraceful things<note placement="foot">Hebrew “thing”</note> they did in Israel.”

verses.name: Judges 20:11
verses.text: And all the men of Israel were gathered to the city as one body<note placement="foot">Hebrew “man”</note> united.  <div eID="gen2181" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 20:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1563"/><div sID="gen2182" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1563"/>Then the tribes of Israel sent men throughout all the tribes of Benjamin, saying, “What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> this wickedness that happened among you?

verses.name: Judges 20:13
verses.text: So then, hand over the men, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the perverse lot⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons of uselessness”</note> who are in Gibeah, so that we may kill them and purge this wickedness from Israel.” But the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons/children”</note> of Benjamin were not willing to listen to the voice of their relatives,<note placement="foot">Or “brothers”</note> the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note>

verses.name: Judges 20:14
verses.text: And the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons/children”</note> of Benjamin were gathered from the cities to Gibeah to go out for battle against the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note>

verses.name: Judges 20:15
verses.text: From the cities the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons/children”</note> of Benjamin were counted on that day twenty-six thousand <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞sword-wielding men⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “men drawing sword”</note> besides the inhabitants of Gibeah, who were counted seven hundred well-trained<note placement="foot">Or “chosen”</note> men.

verses.name: Judges 20:16
verses.text: From all these troops <transChange type="added">were</transChange> seven hundred well-trained<note placement="foot">Or “choice/chosen”</note> men <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who were left-handed⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “bound by his right hand”</note> each one could sling with a stone at a hair and not miss.

verses.name: Judges 20:17
verses.text: And the men of Israel besides Benjamin were counted four hundred thousand <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞sword-wielding men⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “men drawing sword”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞all were warriors⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “all were men of war”</note>  <div eID="gen2182" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 20:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1564"/><div sID="gen2183" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1564"/>Then the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> got up and went up to Bethel, and they inquired of God, saying, “Who will go up first for the battle against the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons/children”</note> of Benjamin?” And Yahweh said, “Judah <transChange type="added">will go</transChange> first.”

verses.name: Judges 20:19
verses.text: And the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> got up in the morning, and they encamped against Gibeah.

verses.name: Judges 20:20
verses.text: Then the men of Israel marched out for the battle against Benjamin, and the men of Israel took up positions against them <transChange type="added">for</transChange> battle at Gibeah.

verses.name: Judges 20:21
verses.text: The descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons/children”</note> of Benjamin went out from Gibeah, and they struck down on that day twenty-two thousand men of Israel to the ground.

verses.name: Judges 20:22
verses.text: But the troops, the men of Israel, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞encouraged themselves⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “took heart”</note> and again they arranged <transChange type="added">their</transChange> battle <transChange type="added">lines</transChange> in the place where they had arranged themselves the first day.

verses.name: Judges 20:23
verses.text: The <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> went up and wept before Yahweh until evening and inquired of Yahweh, saying, “Should we again draw near from the battle against the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons/children”</note> of Benjamin, our relatives?”<note placement="foot">Hebrew “my brother”</note> And Yahweh said, “Go up against them.”<note placement="foot">Hebrew “him”</note>  <div eID="gen2183" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 20:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1565"/><div sID="gen2184" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1565"/>And the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> drew near to the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons/children”</note> of Benjamin on the second day.

verses.name: Judges 20:25
verses.text: And Benjamin went out from Gibeah to meet them on the second day, and they struck down the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> again, eighteen thousand men to the ground; all of these were <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞sword-wielding⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “drawers of sword”</note>

verses.name: Judges 20:26
verses.text: And all the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> and all the troops went up and came to Bethel and wept; and they sat there before Yahweh and fasted on that day until evening; and they offered burnt offerings and fellowship offerings before Yahweh.

verses.name: Judges 20:27
verses.text: And the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> inquired of Yahweh (In those days the ark of the covenant of God <transChange type="added">was</transChange> there,

verses.name: Judges 20:28
verses.text: and Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron, <transChange type="added">was</transChange> standing <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before it⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “before presence of it/him”</note> to minister in those days), saying, “Should we go out once more to battle against the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons/children”</note> of Benjamin our relatives,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “my brother”</note> or should we stop?” And Yahweh said, “Go up tomorrow; I will give them<note placement="foot">Hebrew “him”</note> into your hand.”  <div eID="gen2184" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 20:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1566"/><div sID="gen2185" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1566"/>So Israel stationed an ambush all around Gibeah.

verses.name: Judges 20:30
verses.text: And the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> went up against the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons/children”</note> of Benjamin on the third day, and they took up positions against Gibeah as before.

verses.name: Judges 20:31
verses.text: The descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons/children”</note> of Benjamin went out to meet the troops, and they lured <transChange type="added">them</transChange> away from the city and began to inflict casualties on the troops as before, on the main road, one of which goes up <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Bethel, the other to Gibeah; <transChange type="added">and</transChange> in the field <transChange type="added">there were</transChange> about thirty men of Israel.

verses.name: Judges 20:32
verses.text: And the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons/children”</note> of Benjamin thought,<note placement="foot">Or “said”</note> “They are being defeated before us <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as previously⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,”<note placement="foot">Literally “on the first”</note> and the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> said, “Let us flee and lure them<note placement="foot">Hebrew “him”</note> away from the city to the main roads.”

verses.name: Judges 20:33
verses.text: And all the men of Israel got up from their places<note placement="foot">Hebrew “place”</note> and took up positions in Baal Tamar; and the ambush of Israel charged from their places,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “place”</note> from the vicinity of Gibeah.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Geba”</note>

verses.name: Judges 20:34
verses.text: Then ten thousand well-trained<note placement="foot">Or “choice/chosen”</note> men from all Israel came out against Gibeah, and the battle became fierce;<note placement="foot">Or “the battle became heavy”</note> they did not know that disaster was about to <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞close in⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “touching”</note> on them.

verses.name: Judges 20:35
verses.text: And Yahweh defeated Benjamin in the presence of Israel, and the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> destroyed on that day twenty-five thousand one hundred men of Benjamin, all of them <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞sword-wielding⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “drawing sword”</note>  <div eID="gen2185" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 20:36
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1567"/><div sID="gen2186" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1567"/>The descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons/children”</note> of Benjamin saw that they were defeated, and the men of Israel gave ground<note placement="foot">Or “a place” or “space”</note> to Benjamin because they trusted the ambush that they had set against Gibeah.

verses.name: Judges 20:37
verses.text: And the ambush came quickly and advanced against Gibeah, and it <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞put the whole city to the sword⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “struck the whole city with the mouth of the sword”</note>

verses.name: Judges 20:38
verses.text: Now the appointed time for the men of Israel with the ambush was that they sent up for them a great amount of smoke from the city.

verses.name: Judges 20:39
verses.text: And the men of Israel turned in the battle, and Benjamin began to inflict casualties on about thirty men of Israel because they thought,<note placement="foot">Or “said”</note> “They will be completely defeated before us as in the first battle.”

verses.name: Judges 20:40
verses.text: And the cloud of smoke began to go up from the city in a column of smoke, and Benjamin turned backward, and behold, the whole city was going up <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in smoke⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!<note placement="foot">Literally “to heaven”</note>

verses.name: Judges 20:41
verses.text: And the men of Israel turned, and the men of Benjamin were dismayed because they saw that disaster was <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞closing in⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “touching”</note> on them.

verses.name: Judges 20:42
verses.text: And they retreated from before the men of Israel to the way of the wilderness, but the battle caught up to them, and <transChange type="added">those</transChange> who <transChange type="added">came</transChange> from the cities<note placement="foot">Other ancient translations “city”</note> destroyed them in the midst of them.

verses.name: Judges 20:43
verses.text: They surrounded Benjamin; they pursued them<note placement="foot">Hebrew “him”</note> without rest<note placement="foot">Or “at Nohah,” a location</note> and trod them<note placement="foot">Hebrew “him”</note> down opposite Gibeah to the east.

verses.name: Judges 20:44
verses.text: And eighteen thousand men from Benjamin fell, all of them <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞able men⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “men of strength”</note>

verses.name: Judges 20:45
verses.text: And they turned and fled toward the wilderness, to the rock of Rimmon, but they cut down on the main roads five thousand men; and they pursued after them up to Gidom, and they struck down two thousand men.

verses.name: Judges 20:46
verses.text: So all of Benjamin who fell on that day were twenty-five thousand <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞sword-wielding men⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “men drawing sword”</note> all of these were <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞able men⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “men of strength”</note>

verses.name: Judges 20:47
verses.text: But six hundred turned and fled toward the wilderness, to the rock of Rimmon, and they remained at the rock of Rimmon <transChange type="added">for</transChange> four months.

verses.name: Judges 20:48
verses.text: And the men of Israel returned to the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons/children”</note> of Benjamin, and they put them to <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the edge of the sword⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally the mouth of the sword”</note> both the inhabitants of city and <transChange type="added">the</transChange> animals that were found; they also set on fire all the cities that they found.  <chapter eID="Judg.20"/>

verses.name: Judges 21:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1568"/><title type="x-s">A Decision Is Made About the Tribe of Benjamin</title> <div sID="gen2187" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1568"/>The men of Israel had sworn at Mizpah, saying, “None of us will give his daughter to Benjamin as a wife.”

verses.name: Judges 21:2
verses.text: And the people of Bethel came and sat there until evening before God, and they lifted their voices and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞wept bitterly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “they cried a great weeping”</note>

verses.name: Judges 21:3
verses.text: And they said, “Why, Yahweh, God of Israel, has it happened today in Israel that one tribe is lacking from Israel?”

verses.name: Judges 21:4
verses.text: On the next day the people rose early, and they built there an altar and sacrificed burnt offerings and fellowship offerings.

verses.name: Judges 21:5
verses.text: And the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> said, “Who in the assembly has not come up from all the tribes of Israel to Yahweh?” For a solemn oath was <transChange type="added">taken</transChange> concerning whoever did not come up to Yahweh at Mizpah, saying, “He will certainly be put to death.”

verses.name: Judges 21:6
verses.text: But the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> had compassion for Benjamin, their relatives,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “his brother”</note> and they said, “Today one tribe is cut off from Israel.

verses.name: Judges 21:7
verses.text: What will we do for them—for the <transChange type="added">ones</transChange> being left over—for wives? For we have sworn by Yahweh not to give to them our daughters as wives.”  <div eID="gen2187" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 21:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1569"/><div sID="gen2188" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1569"/>They asked, “Which one is there from the tribes of Israel who did not come up to Yahweh at Mizpah?” And behold, no one came from Jabesh-gilead to the camp, to the assembly.

verses.name: Judges 21:9
verses.text: The people were counted, and no one was there from the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead.

verses.name: Judges 21:10
verses.text: And the congregation sent there twelve thousand men from the troops, and they commanded them, saying, “Go, strike the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead with <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the edge of the sword⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the mouth of the sword”</note> and the women and children.

verses.name: Judges 21:11
verses.text: This is the thing you will do: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you will destroy⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “you will devote to destruction”</note> every man and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞every woman who had sex with a man⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “every woman who knows the bed of a man”</note>

verses.name: Judges 21:12
verses.text: And they found among the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead four hundred young virgins<note placement="foot">Hebrew “virgin”</note> who had not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞had sex with a man⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “known a man, as far as the bed of a male”</note> and they brought them to the camp at Shiloh, which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in the land of Canaan.  <div eID="gen2188" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 21:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1570"/><div sID="gen2189" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1570"/>Then the congregation sent and spoke all <transChange type="added">this</transChange> to the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons/children”</note> of Benjamin who were at the rock of Rimmon, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they assured them they would not be hurt⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “they proclaimed peace to them”</note>

verses.name: Judges 21:14
verses.text: And Benjamin returned at that time, and they gave to them the women whom they kept alive from Jabesh-gilead; but they were not enough for them.  <div eID="gen2189" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Judges 21:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1571"/><div sID="gen2190" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1571"/>And the people felt sorry for Benjamin because <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Yahweh weakened the tribes of Israel⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “Yahweh make a breach with the tribes of Israel”</note>

verses.name: Judges 21:16
verses.text: So the elders of the congregation said, “What should we do for the remaining <transChange type="added">ones</transChange> for wives, since the women from Benjamin have been destroyed?”

verses.name: Judges 21:17
verses.text: And they said, “<transChange type="added">There must be</transChange> a remnant for Benjamin, so that a tribe will not be blotted out from Israel.

verses.name: Judges 21:18
verses.text: But we cannot give them wives from our daughters.” (For the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> swore, saying, “Cursed be <transChange type="added">anyone</transChange> who gives a wife to Benjamin.”)

verses.name: Judges 21:19
verses.text: And they said, “Look, the annual feast of Yahweh <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in Shiloh, which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> to the north of Bethel, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞east⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “rising of the sun”</note> of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> main road that goes up from Bethel to Shechem, and south of Lebonah.

verses.name: Judges 21:20
verses.text: They instructed the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons/children”</note> of Benjamin, saying, “Go, lie in ambush in the vineyards,

verses.name: Judges 21:21
verses.text: and watch and look; when the daughters of Shiloh dance in the dances, come out from the vineyards and seize for yourselves a wife from the daughters of Shiloh, and go to the land of Benjamin.

verses.name: Judges 21:22
verses.text: And if their fathers or their brothers complain to us, we will say to them, ‘Allow us to have them, because we did not capture a wife for each man in the battle, and because you did not give <transChange type="added">them</transChange> to them, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞or else⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “as the time”</note> you would have been guilty.’ ”

verses.name: Judges 21:23
verses.text: The descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons/children”</note> of Benjamin did likewise, and they took wives for each of them from the dancers whom they seized, and they went and returned to their territory, and they rebuilt the cities and they lived in them.

verses.name: Judges 21:24
verses.text: So the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> dispersed from there at that time according to tribe and family; and they went out from there, each one to their own territory.

verses.name: Judges 21:25
verses.text: In those days there was no king in Israel; each one did what was right in his own eyes.  <chapter eID="Judg.21"/> <div eID="gen2190" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen1922" osisID="Judg" type="book"/>

verses.name: Ruth 1:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1572"/><title type="x-s">Elimelech Takes His Family to Live in Moab</title> <div sID="gen2192" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1572"/>And it happened in the days <transChange type="added">when</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the judges ruled⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the judging of the judges”</note> there was a famine in the land, and a man from Bethlehem of Judah went <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to reside⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to dwell as an alien”</note> in the countryside of Moab—he and his wife and his two sons.

verses.name: Ruth 1:2
verses.text: And the name of the man <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Elimelech, and the name of his wife <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Naomi, and the name<transChange type="added">s</transChange> of his two sons <transChange type="added">were</transChange> Mahlon and Kilion. <transChange type="added">They were</transChange> Ephraimites from Bethlehem <transChange type="added">in</transChange> Judah. And they went <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the countryside of Moab and remained there.  <div eID="gen2192" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ruth 1:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1573"/><div sID="gen2193" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1573"/>But Elimelech the husband of Naomi died and she was left behind <transChange type="added">with</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞her two sons⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “she and her two sons”</note>

verses.name: Ruth 1:4
verses.text: And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they took⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “they lifted up”</note> for themselves Moabite wives. The name of the one <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Orpah and the name of the other <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Ruth. And they lived there about ten years.

verses.name: Ruth 1:5
verses.text: But <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞both⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the two of them”</note> Mahlon and Kilion died, and the woman was left without her two sons and without her husband.  <div eID="gen2193" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ruth 1:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1574"/><title type="x-s">Naomi Returns with Ruth</title> <div sID="gen2194" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1574"/>And she got up, she and her daughters-in-law, and returned from the countryside of Moab, because she had heard in the countryside of Moab that Yahweh had <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞come to the aid of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “had considered”</note> his people to give food to them.

verses.name: Ruth 1:7
verses.text: So she set out from the place <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞where she was⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “which she was there”</note> and her two daughters-in-law with her, and they went on the way to return to the land of Judah.  <div eID="gen2194" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ruth 1:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1575"/><div sID="gen2195" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1575"/>But Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law, “Go, each <transChange type="added">of you</transChange> return to her mother’s house. May Yahweh <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞show kindness to you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “do loyal love with you”</note> <transChange type="added">just</transChange> as you did with the dead and with me.

verses.name: Ruth 1:9
verses.text: May Yahweh <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞grant that you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “give to you”</note> find a resting place, each <transChange type="added">in</transChange> the house of her husband.” And she kissed them, and they lifted up their voice<transChange type="added">s</transChange> and cried.  <div eID="gen2195" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ruth 1:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1576"/><div sID="gen2196" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1576"/>And they said to her, “<transChange type="added">No,</transChange> we want to return with you to your people.”

verses.name: Ruth 1:11
verses.text: And Naomi said, “Return, my daughters. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Why do you still want to go with me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?<note placement="foot">Literally “To what do you want to go still for me?”</note> Are there sons <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in my womb⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in my intestines”</note> that may be husbands for you?

verses.name: Ruth 1:12
verses.text: Turn back, my daughters! Go, for <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I am too old to have a husband⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “I am too old from being to a man”</note> If I should think there is hope for me, even if I should have a husband <transChange type="added">this</transChange> night, and even if I should bear sons,

verses.name: Ruth 1:13
verses.text: would you therefore wait until they were grown? Would you therefore <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞refrain from marrying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?<note placement="foot">Literally “Would you therefore let yourself be hindered to not belong to a man?”</note> No, my daughters, for it is far more bitter to me than <transChange type="added">to</transChange> you. For the hand of Yahweh has gone out against me.”

verses.name: Ruth 1:14
verses.text: And they lifted up their voices and cried again. And Orpah kissed her mother-in-law <transChange type="added">goodbye</transChange>, but Ruth clung to her.

verses.name: Ruth 1:15
verses.text: And she said, “Look, your sister-in-law has returned to her people and to her gods. Return after your sister-in-law <transChange type="added">too</transChange>.”  <div eID="gen2196" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ruth 1:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1577"/><div sID="gen2197" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1577"/>But Ruth said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Do not urge⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “You shall not press me”</note> me to leave you or to return from <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞following you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!<note placement="foot">Literally “from behind you”</note> For where you go, I will go, and where you lodge, I will lodge. Your people <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> my people and your God <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> my God.

verses.name: Ruth 1:17
verses.text: Where you die I will die, and there I will be buried. So may Yahweh do to me, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞and even more, unless⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and so may he do again, that”</note> death <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞separates you and me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!”<note placement="foot">Literally “makes a separation between you and between me”</note>

verses.name: Ruth 1:18
verses.text: <transChange type="added">When Naomi</transChange> saw that she was determined to go with her, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞she said no more⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “she ceased to speak to her”</note>  <div eID="gen2197" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ruth 1:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1578"/><div sID="gen2198" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1578"/><transChange type="added">So</transChange> the two of them went until they came to Bethlehem. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And when they came⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it happened at the moment of coming”</note> to Bethlehem, all of the town was stirred because of them. And they said, “<transChange type="added">Is</transChange> this Naomi?”

verses.name: Ruth 1:20
verses.text: And she said to them, “You should not call me Naomi; call me Mara, for Shaddai<note placement="foot">Often translated “the Almighty”</note> has <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞caused me to be very bitter⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “caused very bitterness to me”</note>

verses.name: Ruth 1:21
verses.text: I went <transChange type="added">away</transChange> full, but Yahweh brought me back empty-handed! Why call me Naomi <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞when Yahweh has testified against me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and Yahweh answered against me”</note> and Shaddai<note placement="foot">Often translated “the Almighty”</note> has brought calamity upon me?”

verses.name: Ruth 1:22
verses.text: So Naomi returned, and Ruth the Moabite her daughter-in-law with her, returning from the countryside of Moab. And they came <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Bethlehem at <transChange type="added">the</transChange> beginning of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> harvest of barley.  <chapter eID="Ruth.1"/>

verses.name: Ruth 2:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1579"/><title type="x-s">Ruth Meets Boaz</title> <div sID="gen2199" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1579"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Now⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and for”</note> Naomi <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞had a relative of her husband⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “was an acquaintance of a man of her husband”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a prominent rich man⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a man mighty of wealth”</note> from the clan of Elimelech, <transChange type="added">whose</transChange> name was Boaz.

verses.name: Ruth 2:2
verses.text: And Ruth the Moabite said to Naomi, “Please let me go <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the field and glean among the ears of grain after <transChange type="added">someone</transChange> in whose eyes I <transChange type="added">may</transChange> find favor.” And she said to her, “Go, my daughter.”

verses.name: Ruth 2:3
verses.text: So she went and came and gleaned in the field behind the reapers. And she happened <transChange type="added">by</transChange> chance <transChange type="added">upon</transChange> the tract of field <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞belonging to⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “was for”</note> Boaz, who <transChange type="added">was</transChange> from the clan of Elimelech.

verses.name: Ruth 2:4
verses.text: And look, Boaz came from Bethlehem and said to the reapers, “<transChange type="added">May</transChange> Yahweh <transChange type="added">be</transChange> with you.” And they said to him, “<transChange type="added">May</transChange> Yahweh bless you.”

verses.name: Ruth 2:5
verses.text: And Boaz said to his servant <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in charge of the reapers⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the one standing over the reapers”</note> “To whom <transChange type="added">does</transChange> this young woman <transChange type="added">belong</transChange>?”

verses.name: Ruth 2:6
verses.text: And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the servant in charge of the reapers⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the servant the one standing over the reapers”</note> said, “She <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a Moabite girl returning with Naomi from the countryside of Moab.

verses.name: Ruth 2:7
verses.text: And she said, ‘Please let me glean and let me gather among the sheaves behind the reapers.’ So she came and remained from the morning up to now. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞She is sitting for a little while in the house⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “this one she is sitting a little in the house”</note>  <div eID="gen2199" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ruth 2:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1580"/><div sID="gen2200" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1580"/>And Boaz said to Ruth, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Listen carefully⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally, “You have heard”</note> my daughter, go no longer to glean in another field. Moreover, do not leave from this one, but <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞stay close⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “cling”</note> with my young women.

verses.name: Ruth 2:9
verses.text: Keep your eyes on the field that they reap and go after them. Have I not ordered the servants not to bother you? And if you get thirsty, you shall go to the containers and drink from where the servants have drawn.”

verses.name: Ruth 2:10
verses.text: And she fell on her face and bowed down to the ground and said to him, “Why have I found favor in your eyes by recognizing me—for I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> a foreigner?”

verses.name: Ruth 2:11
verses.text: And Boaz answered and said to her, “All that you have done for your mother-in-law after the death of your husband was fully told to me. <transChange type="added">How</transChange> you left your father and mother and the land of your birth, and you went to a people that you did not know <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “yesterday three days ago”</note>

verses.name: Ruth 2:12
verses.text: May Yahweh reward your work and may a full reward be <transChange type="added">given to</transChange> you from Yahweh, the God of Israel, under whose wings you came to take refuge.”

verses.name: Ruth 2:13
verses.text: And she said, “May I find favor in your eyes, my lord, for you have comforted me and have spoken <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞kindly to your servant⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “on the heart of your servant”</note> and I am not one of your servants.”  <div eID="gen2200" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ruth 2:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1581"/><div sID="gen2201" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1581"/>And Boaz said to her <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞at mealtime⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “at the time of the food”</note> “Come here and eat from the bread and dip your morsel in the wine vinegar.” So she sat beside the gleaners, and he offered to her roasted grain. And she ate and was satisfied, and she had some left over.

verses.name: Ruth 2:15
verses.text: And she got up to glean, and Boaz instructed his servants saying, “Let her also glean between the sheaves and do not reproach her.

verses.name: Ruth 2:16
verses.text: And also pull out for her from your bundles and leave <transChange type="added">it</transChange> so that she may glean—and do not rebuke her.”  <div eID="gen2201" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ruth 2:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1582"/><div sID="gen2202" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1582"/>So she gleaned in the field until the evening and she beat out what she had gleaned, and it was about an ephah <transChange type="added">of</transChange> barley.

verses.name: Ruth 2:18
verses.text: And she picked <transChange type="added">it</transChange> up and went <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the town. Her mother-in-law saw how much she had gleaned. And she took <transChange type="added">it</transChange> out and gave to her what she had left over <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞after being satisfied⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “from her satiety”</note>

verses.name: Ruth 2:19
verses.text: And her mother-in-law said to her, “Where did you glean <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞today⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the day”</note> and where did you work? May he who took notice of you be blessed.” And she told her mother-in-law <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞with whom she had worked⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “who she had worked with him”</note> and said, “The name of the man who I worked with today <transChange type="added">is</transChange> Boaz.”

verses.name: Ruth 2:20
verses.text: And Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, “<transChange type="added">May</transChange> he be blessed by Yahweh, whose loyal love has not forsaken the living or the dead.” And Naomi said to her, “The man is a close relative for us, he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> one of our redeemers.”

verses.name: Ruth 2:21
verses.text: And Ruth the Moabite said, “Also, he said to me, ‘You shall stay close with the servants which are mine until they have finished all of the harvest which is mine.’ ”

verses.name: Ruth 2:22
verses.text: And Naomi said to Ruth her daughter-in-law, “<transChange type="added">It is</transChange> good, my daughter, that you go out with his maidservants so that you will not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞be bothered⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “they touch on you”</note> in another field.”

verses.name: Ruth 2:23
verses.text: So she stayed close with the maidservants <transChange type="added">of</transChange> Boaz to glean until the end of the barley harvest and wheat harvest. And she lived with her mother-in-law.  <chapter eID="Ruth.2"/>

verses.name: Ruth 3:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1583"/><title type="x-s">Ruth Meets Boaz at the Threshing Floor</title> <div sID="gen2203" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1583"/>Now Naomi her mother-in-law said to her, “My daughter, should I not seek for you security that <transChange type="added">things</transChange> may be good for you?

verses.name: Ruth 3:2
verses.text: So then, <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not Boaz our kinsman whose maidservants you were with? Look, he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> winnowing the barley at the threshing floor tonight.

verses.name: Ruth 3:3
verses.text: Wash, anoint yourself, put your clothing on, and go down to the threshing floor. Do not make yourself known to the man until he finishes eating and drinking.

verses.name: Ruth 3:4
verses.text: And when he lies, take notice of the place where he lies. And you shall go and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞uncover⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “open”</note> his feet and lie <transChange type="added">down</transChange>, and he shall tell you what to do.”

verses.name: Ruth 3:5
verses.text: And she said to her, “I will do all that you say.”  <div eID="gen2203" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ruth 3:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1584"/><div sID="gen2204" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1584"/>And she went down to the threshing floor and did all that her mother-in-law had instructed her.

verses.name: Ruth 3:7
verses.text: And Boaz ate and drank <transChange type="added">until</transChange> his heart was <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞merry⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “good”</note> and then he came to lie at the end of the grain heap. And she came in quietly and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞uncovered⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “opened”</note> his feet and lay down.

verses.name: Ruth 3:8
verses.text: And it happened in the middle of the night the man was startled and he reached out and behold, a woman <transChange type="added">was</transChange> lying at his feet.

verses.name: Ruth 3:9
verses.text: And he said, “Who <transChange type="added">are</transChange> you?” And she said, “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> Ruth, your servant. Spread <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞your garment⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “your wing”</note> over your servant because you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> a redeemer.”

verses.name: Ruth 3:10
verses.text: And he said, “You <transChange type="added">are</transChange> blessed by Yahweh my daughter. You did better <transChange type="added">in this</transChange> last kindness than the first by not going after young men, whether poor or rich.

verses.name: Ruth 3:11
verses.text: And so then my daughter, do not be afraid. All that you ask I will do for you, for the entire assembly of my people knows that you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> a worthy woman.

verses.name: Ruth 3:12
verses.text: Now truly I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> a redeemer, but there is also a redeemer <transChange type="added">of a</transChange> closer relationship than me.

verses.name: Ruth 3:13
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Stay tonight,⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Spend the night tonight”</note> and in the morning, if he wants to redeem you, good; but if he is not willing to redeem, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞then as Yahweh lives,⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the life of Yahweh”</note> I will redeem you. Lie down until the morning.”  <div eID="gen2204" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ruth 3:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1585"/><div sID="gen2205" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1585"/>So she lay at his feet until morning and got up before <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞anyone could recognize each other⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “a man could recognize his friend”</note> And he said, “It must not be known that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the woman”</note> came <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the threshing floor.”

verses.name: Ruth 3:15
verses.text: And he said, “Bring the cloak that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> on you and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞hold it out⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “hold on her”</note> And she held it out and he measured six <transChange type="added">measures of</transChange> barley and put it on her <transChange type="added">cloak</transChange>. Then she went <transChange type="added">into</transChange> the city.

verses.name: Ruth 3:16
verses.text: And she came to her mother-in-law, and she said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞How did it go for you,⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “who are you?”</note> my daughter?” And she told her all that the man did for her.

verses.name: Ruth 3:17
verses.text: And she said, “These six measures of barley he gave to me, for he said, ‘You shall not go empty-handed to your mother-in-law.’ ”

verses.name: Ruth 3:18
verses.text: And she said, “Wait, my daughter, until you know how the matter turns out, for the man will not rest but will settle the matter today.”  <chapter eID="Ruth.3"/>

verses.name: Ruth 4:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1586"/><title type="x-s">Boaz Redeems Ruth</title> <div sID="gen2206" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1586"/>And Boaz had gone up <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the <transChange type="added">city</transChange> gate and sat there. And look, the redeemer of whom Boaz had spoken <transChange type="added">was</transChange> passing by. And he said, “Come over here to sit, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞friend⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “certain someone”</note> And he came over and sat.

verses.name: Ruth 4:2
verses.text: And he took ten men from the elders of the city and said, “Sit here.” And they sat.

verses.name: Ruth 4:3
verses.text: And he said to the redeemer, “Naomi, who returned from the countryside <transChange type="added">of</transChange> Moab, is selling the tract of land which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> for our brother Elimelech.

verses.name: Ruth 4:4
verses.text: And I thought <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I would tell you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “I would open your ear”</note> and say, ‘<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Buy it in the presence of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Buy before”</note> those sitting and before the elders of my people,’ if you want to redeem <transChange type="added">it</transChange>, redeem <transChange type="added">it</transChange>. But if you do not want to redeem, tell me so that I may know, for there is no one except you to redeem <transChange type="added">it</transChange>, and I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> after you.” And he said, “I want to redeem <transChange type="added">it</transChange>.”

verses.name: Ruth 4:5
verses.text: And Boaz said, “On the day of your acquiring the field from the hand of Naomi, you also acquire Ruth the Moabite, the wife of the dead <transChange type="added">man</transChange>, <transChange type="added">in order</transChange> to raise up <transChange type="added">for</transChange> the name of the dead his inheritance.”

verses.name: Ruth 4:6
verses.text: And the redeemer said, “I am not able to redeem for myself, lest I ruin my inheritance. You redeem for yourself my kinsman-redemption, for I am not able to redeem <transChange type="added">it</transChange>.”  <div eID="gen2206" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ruth 4:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1587"/><div sID="gen2207" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1587"/>(Now this <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞was the custom in former times⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “before faces”</note> in Israel concerning the kinsman-redemption and transfer of property: to confirm the matter, a man removed his sandal and gave <transChange type="added">it</transChange> to his fellow countryman. This <transChange type="added">was</transChange> the manner of attesting in Israel.)

verses.name: Ruth 4:8
verses.text: So the redeemer said to Boaz, “Acquire <transChange type="added">it</transChange> for yourself,” and he removed his sandal.

verses.name: Ruth 4:9
verses.text: And Boaz said to the elders and all of the people, “You <transChange type="added">are</transChange> witnesses today that I have acquired all that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> for Elimelech and that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> for Kilion and Mahlon from the hand of Naomi.

verses.name: Ruth 4:10
verses.text: And also Ruth the Moabite, the wife of Mahlon, I have acquired as a wife, to raise up the name of the dead over his inheritance, so that the name of the dead may not be cut off from his relatives and from the gate of his <transChange type="added">birth</transChange> place. You <transChange type="added">are</transChange> witnesses today.”

verses.name: Ruth 4:11
verses.text: And all of the people who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> at the gate and the elders said, “<transChange type="added">We are</transChange> witnesses. May Yahweh make the woman coming into your house as Rachel and as Leah, who <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞together⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the two of them”</note> built the house of Israel. May you have strength in Ephrathah and bestow a name in Bethlehem.

verses.name: Ruth 4:12
verses.text: And may your house be like the house of Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah from the offspring that Yahweh will give to you from this young woman.”  <div eID="gen2207" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ruth 4:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1588"/><title type="x-s">The Lineage of King David</title> <div sID="gen2208" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1588"/>So Boaz took Ruth and she became his wife. And he went <transChange type="added">in</transChange> to her, and Yahweh <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞enabled her to conceive⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “gave to her conception”</note> and she bore a son.

verses.name: Ruth 4:14
verses.text: And the women said to Naomi, “Blessed be Yahweh who today <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞did not leave you without a redeemer⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!<note placement="foot">Literally “did not allow to be missing for you a redeemer”</note> And may his name be renowned in Israel!

verses.name: Ruth 4:15
verses.text: He shall be for you a restorer of life and a sustainer in your old age, for your daughter-in-law who loves you, who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> better for you than seven sons, has borne him.”

verses.name: Ruth 4:16
verses.text: And Naomi took the child and she put him on her bosom and became his nurse.

verses.name: Ruth 4:17
verses.text: And the women of the neighborhood gave him a name, saying, “A son has been born to Naomi.” And they called his name Obed. He <transChange type="added">was</transChange> the father of Jesse, the father of David.  <div eID="gen2208" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ruth 4:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1589"/><div sID="gen2209" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1589"/>Now these are the descendants of Perez: Perez fathered Hezron,

verses.name: Ruth 4:19
verses.text: and Hezron fathered Ram, and Ram fathered Amminadab,

verses.name: Ruth 4:20
verses.text: and Amminadab fathered Nahshon, and Nahshon fathered Salmon,

verses.name: Ruth 4:21
verses.text: and Salmon fathered Boaz, and Boaz fathered Obed,

verses.name: Ruth 4:22
verses.text: and Obed fathered Jesse, and Jesse fathered David.  <chapter eID="Ruth.4"/> <div eID="gen2209" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen2191" osisID="Ruth" type="book"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 1:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1590"/><title type="x-s">The Family of Elkanah</title> <div sID="gen2211" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1590"/>There was a certain man from Ramathaim Zophim, from the hill country of Ephraim, whose name was Elkanah the son of Jeroham, the son of Elihu, the son of Tohu, the son of Zuph, an Ephraimite.<note placement="foot">Or “Ephrathite”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 1:2
verses.text: He had two wives; the name of the first <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Hannah, and the name of the second <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Peninnah. Now Peninnah had children, but Hannah had no children.

verses.name: I Samuel 1:3
verses.text: Now this man used to go up from his town <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞year by year⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from days to days”</note> to worship and to sacrifice to Yahweh of hosts in Shiloh, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞where⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and there”</note> the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, <transChange type="added">were</transChange> priests to Yahweh.

verses.name: I Samuel 1:4
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞On⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it happened on”</note> the day Elkanah sacrificed, he would give portions to his wife Peninnah and to all her sons and daughters.

verses.name: I Samuel 1:5
verses.text: But to Hannah he would give <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a double portion⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “a portion of two faces”</note> because he loved Hannah, though Yahweh had closed her womb.

verses.name: I Samuel 1:6
verses.text: (Now her rival wife would provoke her severely in order to upset her because Yahweh had closed her womb.)

verses.name: I Samuel 1:7
verses.text: And so he used to do<note placement="foot">So Hebrew; because of the abrupt change of subject some revocalize the verb to read “it used to be”</note> year after year; <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞whenever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Or “as often as”; literally “from enough”</note> she went up to the house of Yahweh, she<note placement="foot">That is, Penninah</note> would provoke her so that she<note placement="foot">That is, Hannah</note> would weep and would not eat.

verses.name: I Samuel 1:8
verses.text: So Elkanah her husband would say to her: “Hannah, why do you weep and why do you not eat? And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞why are you heartsick⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?<note placement="foot">Literally “why is your heart evil”</note> Am I not better to you than ten sons?”

verses.name: I Samuel 1:9
verses.text: Then Hannah got up after eating and drinking at Shiloh.
