(Now Eli the priest <transChange type="added">was</transChange> sitting on his chair by the doorpost of the temple<note placement="foot">This is not the temple of Solomon (ca. 966 <sc>bc</sc>), but rather the tabernacle that first resided at Shiloh after the conquest of Joshua.</note> of Yahweh.)

verses.name: I Samuel 1:10
verses.text: She <transChange type="added">was</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞deeply troubled⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “bitter of soul”</note> so she prayed to Yahweh and wept bitterly.

verses.name: I Samuel 1:11
verses.text: She <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞made a vow⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “vowed a vow”</note> and said: “O Yahweh of hosts, if you will look with compassion on the misery of your female servant, and will remember me, and not forget your female servant, and will give to your female servant <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a male child⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “an offspring of men”</note> then I will give him to Yahweh all the days of his life, and a razor will never pass over his head.”<note placement="foot">“A razor will never pass over his head” indicates that Hannah promised to dedicate her son to Yahweh as a Nazirite, according to the terms of Num 6:1–21</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 1:12
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞While⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it happened that when”</note> she continued to pray before Yahweh, Eli was observing her mouth.

verses.name: I Samuel 1:13
verses.text: Now Hannah had been speaking in her heart; her lips <transChange type="added">were</transChange> moving, but her voice could not be heard, so Eli considered her <transChange type="added">to be</transChange> drunk.

verses.name: I Samuel 1:14
verses.text: Then Eli said to her, “How long will you behave like someone <transChange type="added">who is</transChange> drunk? Put away your wine!”

verses.name: I Samuel 1:15
verses.text: But Hannah answered and said, “No, my lord. I am a woman <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞deeply distressed⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “difficult of spirit”</note> but I have not drunk wine <transChange type="added">or</transChange> strong drink. <transChange type="added">Rather</transChange>, I have poured out my soul before Yahweh.

verses.name: I Samuel 1:16
verses.text: Do not regard your female servant as <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞worthless⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “as a daughter of Belial/daughter of worthlessness”</note> but because of the extent of my worries and my provocation I have spoken all of this.”

verses.name: I Samuel 1:17
verses.text: Then Eli answered and said, “Go in peace, and may the God of Israel grant your request that you have asked of him.”

verses.name: I Samuel 1:18
verses.text: And she said, “May your female slave find favor in your sight.” Then the woman went on her way and ate <transChange type="added">something</transChange>, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞her face did not look sad any longer⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “her faces were not for her any longer”</note>  <div eID="gen2211" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 1:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1591"/><title type="x-s">The Birth of Samuel</title> <div sID="gen2212" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1591"/>Then they rose early in the morning and worshiped before Yahweh <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞and returned⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and they returned and went”</note> to their house at Ramah. Then Elkanah <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞had sexual relations with⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “knew”</note> Hannah his wife, and Yahweh remembered her.

verses.name: I Samuel 1:20
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞In due time⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “At the turning of the days”</note> Hannah conceived and gave birth to a son. She called his name Samuel, for <transChange type="added">she said</transChange>, “I requested him from Yahweh.”  <div eID="gen2212" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 1:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1592"/><div sID="gen2213" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1592"/>So the man Elkanah went up with all his household <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to make the annual sacrifice⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to sacrifice the sacrifice of days”</note> to Yahweh and <transChange type="added">to pay</transChange> his vow.

verses.name: I Samuel 1:22
verses.text: But Hannah did not go up, for she said to her husband, “Once the boy <transChange type="added">is</transChange> weaned, I will bring him, so that he may appear before Yahweh; and he will remain there forever.”

verses.name: I Samuel 1:23
verses.text: So her husband Elkanah said to her, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Do what seems right to you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “do what is good in your eyes”</note> stay until you wean him. Only may Yahweh fulfill his word.” So the woman remained and nursed her son until she weaned him.

verses.name: I Samuel 1:24
verses.text: Then she brought him up with her when she had weaned him, <transChange type="added">along</transChange> with three bulls, one ephah of flour, and a skin<note placement="foot">Or “a clay jar”</note> of wine. She brought him to the house of Yahweh at Shiloh while the boy <transChange type="added">was still</transChange> young.

verses.name: I Samuel 1:25
verses.text: They slaughtered the bull, and they brought the boy to Eli.

verses.name: I Samuel 1:26
verses.text: She said, “Excuse me, my lord. As <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you live⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “your soul lives”</note> my lord, I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> the woman who stood with you in this <transChange type="added">place</transChange> to pray to Yahweh.

verses.name: I Samuel 1:27
verses.text: I prayed for this boy, and Yahweh has given me my request that I asked from him.

verses.name: I Samuel 1:28
verses.text: I in turn have lent him to Yahweh. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞As long as he lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “All the days that he lives”</note> he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> lent to Yahweh.” Then they worshiped Yahweh there.  <chapter eID="1Sam.1"/> <div eID="gen2213" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 2:1
verses.text: Then Hannah prayed and said, <div eID="gen2214" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen2215"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2216"/>“My heart exults in Yahweh, my strength <transChange type="added">is</transChange> exalted in Yahweh; <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I grin⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “my mouth is broad”</note> over my enemies, for I rejoice over your salvation. <l eID="gen2216" level="1"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 2:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1593"/><l level="1" sID="gen2217"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1593"/>There is no one holy like Yahweh, for there is no one besides you,<l eID="gen2217" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2218"/>and there is no rock like our God. <l eID="gen2218" level="2"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 2:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1594"/><l level="1" sID="gen2219"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1594"/>Do not increase speaking <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞very proud⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “proud, proud”</note> words!<l eID="gen2219" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2220"/>Let no arrogance go forth from your mouth,<l eID="gen2220" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2221"/>for Yahweh is a God of knowledge<l eID="gen2221" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2222"/><transChange type="added">whose</transChange> deeds are not weighed.<note placement="foot">So Masoretic Hebrew text (<hi type="italic">Kethib</hi>); the reading tradition (<hi type="italic">Qere)</hi> reads “and by him deeds are weighed”</note> <l eID="gen2222" level="2"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 2:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1595"/><l level="1" sID="gen2223"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1595"/>The bows of mighty warriors <transChange type="added">are</transChange> shattered,<l eID="gen2223" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2224"/>but those who stumble gird <transChange type="added">themselves with</transChange> strength. <l eID="gen2224" level="2"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 2:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1596"/><l level="1" sID="gen2225"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1596"/>Those who were full must hire themselves out for bread,<l eID="gen2225" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2226"/>but those who are hungry will become fat.<l eID="gen2226" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2227"/>As for the infertile, she will bear seven,<l eID="gen2227" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2228"/>but <transChange type="added">she who has</transChange> many sons withers away. <l eID="gen2228" level="2"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 2:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1597"/><l level="1" sID="gen2229"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1597"/>Yahweh kills and restores alive,<l eID="gen2229" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2230"/>he brings down <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Sheol<note placement="foot">“Sheol” is a Hebrew term for the place where the dead reside, i.e., the underworld.</note> and raises up. <l eID="gen2230" level="2"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 2:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1598"/><l level="1" sID="gen2231"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1598"/>Yahweh makes poor and makes rich;<l eID="gen2231" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2232"/>he brings low and also exalts. <l eID="gen2232" level="2"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 2:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1599"/><l level="1" sID="gen2233"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1599"/>He raises up the poor from <transChange type="added">the</transChange> dust.<l eID="gen2233" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2234"/>From <transChange type="added">the</transChange> ash heap he lifts up the needy,<l eID="gen2234" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2235"/>to cause them to sit with noble people<l eID="gen2235" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2236"/>and to cause them to inherit a seat of honor.<l eID="gen2236" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2237"/>For the pillars of the earth belong to Yahweh<l eID="gen2237" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2238"/>and he has set the inhabited world on them. <l eID="gen2238" level="2"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 2:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1600"/><l level="1" sID="gen2239"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1600"/>He will guard the feet of his faithful<note placement="foot">Or “loyal”</note> ones,<l eID="gen2239" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2240"/>but the wicked will be destroyed<note placement="foot">Or “will be silenced”</note> in the darkness,<l eID="gen2240" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2241"/>because a man will not prevail by <transChange type="added">his</transChange> might. <l eID="gen2241" level="2"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 2:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1601"/><l level="1" sID="gen2242"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1601"/>Yahweh will shatter<note placement="foot">Singular verb supported by Syriac, Targums, Septuagint, and Old Latin versions.</note> his adversaries;<note placement="foot">The Masoretic Hebrew text (<hi type="italic">Kethib</hi>) has the singular “adversary”; the reading tradition (<hi type="italic">Qere)</hi> reads the plural</note><l eID="gen2242" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2243"/>he will thunder against them in the heavens.<l eID="gen2243" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2244"/>Yahweh will judge the ends of the earth.<l eID="gen2244" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2245"/>He will give strength to his king<l eID="gen2245" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2246"/>and will exalt the might of his anointed one. <l eID="gen2246" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen2215"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 2:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1602"/><div sID="gen2247" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1602"/>Then Elkanah went to Ramah, to his house. Now the boy was serving Yahweh <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in the presence of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in the face of”</note> Eli the priest.  <div eID="gen2247" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 2:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1603"/><title type="x-s">The Family of Eli the Priest</title> <div sID="gen2248" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1603"/>Now the sons of Eli <transChange type="added">were</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞worthless scoundrels⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “sons of Belial”</note> they did not know<note placement="foot">Or “acknowledge”</note> Yahweh.

verses.name: I Samuel 2:13
verses.text: And the custom of the priests with the people <transChange type="added">was this</transChange>: When any man <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞brought a sacrifice⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “was sacrificing a sacrifice” and so throughout 1 &amp;amp; 2 Samuel</note> as the meat was boiling, the servant of the priest would take a three-pronged meat fork in his hand

verses.name: I Samuel 2:14
verses.text: and would thrust it into the pan or into the kettle or into the cauldron or into the cooking pot. All that the meat fork brought up the priest would take for himself. This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> what they used to do to all of the Israelites who came there at Shiloh.

verses.name: I Samuel 2:15
verses.text: Also, before they <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞offered up⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “caused to go up in smoke”</note> the fat as a burnt offering, the servant of the priest would come and say to the man who was sacrificing, “Give the priest meat for roasting, for he will not take boiled meat from you, but only <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞raw⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “with the life”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 2:16
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">if</transChange> the man said to him, “Let them burn the fat completely <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞first⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “as the day”</note> then take for yourself as <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “as your soul”</note> desire,” then he would say to him, “No!<note placement="foot">According to the reading tradition (<hi type="italic">Qere)</hi></note> Give it now! If not, I will take it by force!”

verses.name: I Samuel 2:17
verses.text: So the sin of the young men was very great in the sight of Yahweh, because the men treated the offering of Yahweh with contempt.  <div eID="gen2248" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 2:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1604"/><title type="x-s">Samuel’s Life in the Tabernacle</title> <div sID="gen2249" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1604"/>Now Samuel <transChange type="added">was</transChange> serving before Yahweh, as a boy wearing a linen ephod.

verses.name: I Samuel 2:19
verses.text: His mother used to make for him a small robe and take it to him <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞year by year⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from days to days”</note> whenever she came up with her husband to offer the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞annual sacrifice⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the sacrifice of days”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 2:20
verses.text: And Eli would bless Elkanah and his wife, and he said, “May Yahweh give you an offspring from this woman in place of the petitioned <transChange type="added">one</transChange> that she requested from Yahweh.” Then they went to their home.

verses.name: I Samuel 2:21
verses.text: Yahweh took note of Hannah, and she conceived and gave birth to three sons and two daughters, while the young man Samuel grew up with Yahweh.  <div eID="gen2249" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 2:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1605"/><title type="x-s">Eli Rebukes His Evil Sons</title> <div sID="gen2250" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1605"/>Now Eli was very old, and he heard all that his sons were doing to all Israel and that they <transChange type="added">were</transChange> having sexual relations with the women who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> serving <transChange type="added">at</transChange> the entrance of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> tent of assembly.<note placement="foot">Or “meeting”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 2:23
verses.text: And he asked them, “Why are you doing all these things that I am hearing, <transChange type="added">namely</transChange>, your evil dealings with all these people?

verses.name: I Samuel 2:24
verses.text: No, my sons, the report <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not good that I am hearing the people of Yahweh spreading.

verses.name: I Samuel 2:25
verses.text: If a man sins against a man, then God can intercede for him. But if a man sins against Yahweh, who can intercede for him?” But they did not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞obey⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “listen to the voice of”</note> their father, because Yahweh wanted to kill them.

verses.name: I Samuel 2:26
verses.text: But the boy Samuel <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞continued to grow in stature and in favor⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “was going and being great and good”</note> with Yahweh and with the people.  <div eID="gen2250" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 2:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1606"/><title type="x-s">Yahweh Rebukes Eli</title> <div sID="gen2251" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1606"/>Now a man of God came to Eli and said to him: “Thus says Yahweh: ‘Did I not clearly reveal myself to the house of your ancestor<note placement="foot">Or “father,” meaning Aaron</note> when they were in Egypt under the house of Pharaoh?

verses.name: I Samuel 2:28
verses.text: And I chose him from all the tribes of Israel to be a priest to me, to go up to my altar, to burn incense, and to bear an ephod before me. I gave to the house of your ancestor<note placement="foot">Or “father”</note> all the offerings made by fire by the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 2:29
verses.text: Why do you despise my sacrifice and my offering which I commanded <transChange type="added">for my</transChange> dwelling place, while you honored your sons more than me by making yourselves fat from the best of all the offerings of my people Israel?

verses.name: I Samuel 2:30
verses.text: Therefore,’ <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞declares⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the declaration of”</note> Yahweh the God of Israel, ‘though I solemnly said that your house and the house of your ancestor<note placement="foot">Or “father”</note> would walk before me forever, but now,’ <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞declares⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the declaration of”</note> Yahweh, ‘far be it from me, for those who honor me I will honor, but those who despise me, I will treat with contempt!

verses.name: I Samuel 2:31
verses.text: Look, days <transChange type="added">are</transChange> coming when I will cut off your <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞strength⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “arm,” figurative of “strength” in the context of “descendants”</note> and the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞strength⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “arm,” figurative of “strength” in the context of “descendants”</note> of the house of your ancestor<note placement="foot">Or “father”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞so that no one in your house will live to old age⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “from being old in your house”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 2:32
verses.text: You will look at the distress of my dwelling place, <transChange type="added">despite</transChange> all the good caused for Israel, but there will never be an old <transChange type="added">man</transChange> in your household <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!<note placement="foot">Literally “all the days”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 2:33
verses.text: The only one I will not cut off from my altar <transChange type="added">is you</transChange>.<note placement="foot">Understanding the <hi type="italic">beth</hi> preposition as a <hi type="italic">beth essentiae</hi></note> Rather, to cause your eyes to fail and to cause your soul to grieve, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞all the members of your household⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “all the abundance of your house”</note> will die as men.<note placement="foot">Or “in their prime”; some Greek and other manuscripts supply “sword” (“will die by the sword of men”)</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 2:34
verses.text: This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the sign for you that will come regarding your two sons Hophni and Phinehas: they will both die on the same day!

verses.name: I Samuel 2:35
verses.text: But I will raise up for myself a reliable<note placement="foot">Or “faithful”</note> priest; he will do just according to what is in my heart and in my soul. I will build for him a lasting<note placement="foot">Hebrew “faithful” or “reliable”</note> house and he will walk continually before my anointed one <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “all the days”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 2:36
verses.text: All the remainder of your household will come to bow down <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to”</note> him for a bit of silver or a loaf of bread and will say, “Please assign me to one of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞priestly offices⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “priesthoods”</note> so that I can eat a morsel of bread.” ’ ”  <chapter eID="1Sam.2"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 3:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1607"/><title type="x-s">Samuel’s First Encounter with Yahweh</title> <div sID="gen2252" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1607"/>Now the boy Samuel was serving Yahweh <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in the presence⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in the face of”</note> of Eli. The word of Yahweh was rare in those days; visions were not widespread.

verses.name: I Samuel 3:2
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it happened”</note> one day when Eli was lying in his place (now his eyes had begun <transChange type="added">to grow</transChange> weak so that he was not able to see)

verses.name: I Samuel 3:3
verses.text: and the lamp of God had not yet gone out, Samuel was lying in the temple<note placement="foot">Although the Hebrew text reads “temple,” this is a reference to the tabernacle (see 1:3, 9)</note> of Yahweh where the ark of God <transChange type="added">was</transChange>.

verses.name: I Samuel 3:4
verses.text: Then Yahweh called out to Samuel and he said, “Here I am!”

verses.name: I Samuel 3:5
verses.text: And he ran to Eli and said, “Here I am, because you called me.” But he said, “I did not call <transChange type="added">you</transChange>. Go back and lie down.” So he went and lay down.

verses.name: I Samuel 3:6
verses.text: And Yahweh called Samuel again, so Samuel got up and went to Eli and said, “Here I am, because you called me.” And he said, “I did not call you, my son. Go back <transChange type="added">and</transChange> lie down.”

verses.name: I Samuel 3:7
verses.text: Now Samuel did not yet know Yahweh, and the word of Yahweh had not yet been revealed to him.

verses.name: I Samuel 3:8
verses.text: Again Yahweh called Samuel a third time, so he got up and went to Eli and said, “Here I am, because you called me.” Then Eli realized that Yahweh was calling the boy.

verses.name: I Samuel 3:9
verses.text: So Eli said to Samuel “Go lie down. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞If he calls⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it will happen that if he calls”</note> to you, then you must say, ‘Speak Yahweh, because your servant <transChange type="added">is</transChange> listening.’ ” So Samuel went and lay down in his place.  <div eID="gen2252" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 3:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1608"/><div sID="gen2253" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1608"/>Then Yahweh came and stood <transChange type="added">there</transChange> and called out <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “as an occurrence, in an occurrence”</note> “Samuel! Samuel!” And Samuel said, “Speak, because your servant <transChange type="added">is</transChange> listening.”

verses.name: I Samuel 3:11
verses.text: So Yahweh said to Samuel, “Look, I am doing something in Israel <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞which will cause⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “about which”</note> the two ears of everyone who hears it to tingle.

verses.name: I Samuel 3:12
verses.text: On that day I will fulfill against Eli all that I have spoken against his household, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from beginning to end⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “begin and finish”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 3:13
verses.text: I will make him know that I am about to judge his household forever because of the iniquity that he knew, for his sons <transChange type="added">were</transChange> bringing curses on themselves,<note placement="foot">LXX reads “were cursing God”</note> but he did not rebuke them.

verses.name: I Samuel 3:14
verses.text: Therefore I swore to the house of Eli <transChange type="added">that</transChange> the iniquity of the house of Eli would not be atoned for<note placement="foot">Or “be expiated”</note> by sacrifice or by offering forever.”  <div eID="gen2253" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 3:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1609"/><div sID="gen2254" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1609"/>So Samuel lay down until morning; then he opened the doors of the house of Yahweh, but Samuel was afraid of telling the vision to Eli.

verses.name: I Samuel 3:16
verses.text: Then Eli called Samuel and said, “Samuel, my son!” And he said, “Here I am.”

verses.name: I Samuel 3:17
verses.text: And he said, “What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the message<note placement="foot">Or “word”</note> that he spoke to you? Please do not conceal it from me. May God <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞punish you severely⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “do to you and so may he add”</note> if you conceal anything from me of all the words that he told you.”

verses.name: I Samuel 3:18
verses.text: So Samuel told him all the words and did not conceal <transChange type="added">anything</transChange> from him. And he<note placement="foot">That is, Eli</note> said, “He is Yahweh, he will do <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞what is⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the”</note> good in his <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞sight⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “eyes”</note>  <div eID="gen2254" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 3:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1610"/><div sID="gen2255" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1610"/>And Samuel grew up, and Yahweh was with him. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞He did not allow any of his prophecies to go unfulfilled⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “He let none from all of his words fall to the ground.”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 3:20
verses.text: All Israel from Dan to Beersheba realized that Samuel was faithful<note placement="foot">Or “reliable” or “trustworthy”</note> as a prophet to Yahweh.

verses.name: I Samuel 3:21
verses.text: And Yahweh appeared again in Shiloh, for Yahweh revealed himself to Samuel in Shiloh through the word of Yahweh.  <chapter eID="1Sam.3"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 4:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1611"/><title type="x-s">The Battle of Aphek</title> <div sID="gen2256" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1611"/>And the word of Samuel came to all Israel. Now Israel went out to meet <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines for battle, and they encamped at Ebenezer, and <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines encamped at Aphek.

verses.name: I Samuel 4:2
verses.text: <transChange type="added">The</transChange> Philistines lined up for the battle to meet Israel, and the battle was prolonged<note placement="foot">Or “drawn out”</note> until Israel was defeated before the Philistines, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and they”</note> killed about four thousand men <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞on the battlefield⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “in the battle line in the field”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 4:3
verses.text: When the army<note placement="foot">Or “people”</note> came back to the camp, the elders of Israel asked, “Why has Yahweh defeated us today before the Philistines? Let us bring the ark of the covenant of Yahweh to us from Shiloh so that it may come into our midst and deliver<note placement="foot">Or “save”</note> us from the hand of our enemies.”

verses.name: I Samuel 4:4
verses.text: So the army sent to Shiloh and brought from there the ark of the covenant of Yahweh of hosts who sits <transChange type="added">between</transChange> the cherubim. And the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, <transChange type="added">were</transChange> there with the ark of the covenant of God.

verses.name: I Samuel 4:5
verses.text: Now when the ark of the covenant of Yahweh arrived at the camp, all Israel <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞let out a loud shout⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “shouted a great shout”</note> so that the earth shook.  <div eID="gen2256" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 4:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1612"/><div sID="gen2257" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1612"/>When <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines heard the noise of the shouting, they said, “What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the noise of this loud shouting in the camp of the Hebrews?” Then they learned that the ark of Yahweh had come into the camp.

verses.name: I Samuel 4:7
verses.text: So <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines were afraid, for they said, “God has come<note placement="foot">Or “gods have come”</note> to the camp.” And they said, “Woe to us, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞for this has never happened before!⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “it has not happened like this since yesterday and since the day before that”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 4:8
verses.text: Woe to us! Who can deliver us from the hand of these mighty gods? These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the <transChange type="added">same</transChange> gods who struck the Egyptians with all <transChange type="added">sorts of</transChange> plagues in the desert.

verses.name: I Samuel 4:9
verses.text: Take courage and be men, <transChange type="added">you</transChange> Philistines, lest you end up serving the Hebrews just like they have served you. Be men and fight!”

verses.name: I Samuel 4:10
verses.text: So <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines fought and Israel was defeated and each man fled to his tent, for the slaughter was very great. Thirty thousand foot soldiers from Israel fell.

verses.name: I Samuel 4:11
verses.text: Furthermore, the ark of God was captured,<note placement="foot">Or “taken”</note> and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, died.  <div eID="gen2257" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 4:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1613"/><div sID="gen2258" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1613"/>A man of Benjamin ran from the battle line and came <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Shiloh that same day, and his clothes <transChange type="added">were</transChange> torn and earth <transChange type="added">was</transChange> on his head.

verses.name: I Samuel 4:13
verses.text: When he came, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞there was⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “look”</note> Eli sitting on his chair <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞by the side of the road⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by the hand of the road”</note> watching, because his heart was anxious about the ark of God. Now the man had come <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to give his report⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to tell”</note> in the city, and all the city cried out.

verses.name: I Samuel 4:14
verses.text: When Eli heard the noise of the outcry, he said, “What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the noise of this commotion?” Then the man <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞came quickly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “hastened and came”</note> and told Eli.

verses.name: I Samuel 4:15
verses.text: Now Eli <transChange type="added">was</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞ninety-eight years old⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a son of ninety and eight years”</note> and his eyes <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞stayed fixed ahead⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “were standing”</note> and he was not able to see.

verses.name: I Samuel 4:16
verses.text: And the man said to Eli, “I am the <transChange type="added">one</transChange> who has come from the battle line! I have fled today from the battle line!” And he said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞What exactly happened⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “what is the thing/matter”</note> my son?”

verses.name: I Samuel 4:17
verses.text: Then the messenger answered and said, “Israel has fled before <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines. There has been a great defeat among the troops. Also, your two sons have died, Hophni and Phinehas, and the ark of God has been captured.”

verses.name: I Samuel 4:18
verses.text: Just as he mentioned the ark of God, he<note placement="foot">That is, Eli</note> fell from his chair backwards against the side of the gate. He broke his neck and died, because the man was old and heavy. He had judged Israel forty years.  <div eID="gen2258" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 4:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1614"/><div sID="gen2259" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1614"/>Now his daughter-in-law, the wife of Phinehas, <transChange type="added">was</transChange> pregnant and <transChange type="added">about</transChange> to give birth. When she heard the news concerning the capture of the ark of God and that her father-in-law and her husband had died, she <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞went into labor⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “bowed down”</note> and gave birth, because her labor pains came upon her.

verses.name: I Samuel 4:20
verses.text: Just before the time of her death, those <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞attending her⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “standing over her”</note> said, “Do not fear, for you have given birth to a son.” But she did not answer, or <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞pay any attention⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “set her heart”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 4:21
verses.text: She called the boy Ichabod,<note placement="foot">The name “Ichabod” means “no glory”</note> saying, “The glory has departed from Israel,” referring to the capture of the ark of God and concerning her father-in-law and husband.

verses.name: I Samuel 4:22
verses.text: And she said, “The glory has departed from Israel, because the ark of God was captured.”<note placement="foot">Or “taken”</note>  <chapter eID="1Sam.4"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 5:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1615"/><title type="x-s">The Ark of the Covenant among the Philistines</title> <div sID="gen2260" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1615"/>Now <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines had captured<note placement="foot">Or “taken”</note> the ark of God and brought it from Ebenezer to Ashdod.

verses.name: I Samuel 5:2
verses.text: Then <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines took the ark of God and brought it to the temple of Dagon and placed it beside Dagon.

verses.name: I Samuel 5:3
verses.text: When the Ashdodites got up early the next morning, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞there was⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “look”</note> Dagon fallen with his face to the ground before the ark of Yahweh! So they took Dagon and returned him to his place.

verses.name: I Samuel 5:4
verses.text: When they got up early in the morning the next day, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞there was⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “look”</note> Dagon fallen again with his face to the ground before the ark of Yahweh! The head of Dagon and the palms of his two hands were cut off, lying at<note placement="foot">Hebrew “to”</note> the threshold; only the body<note placement="foot">The phrase may suggest that only the “fish” part of Dagon was left</note> of Dagon was left.

verses.name: I Samuel 5:5
verses.text: (Therefore the priests of Dagon and all who come into the house of Dagon do not tread on the threshold of Dagon in Ashdod until this <transChange type="added">very</transChange> day.)  <div eID="gen2260" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 5:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1616"/><div sID="gen2261" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1616"/>Now the hand of Yahweh was heavy against the Ashdodites and he destroyed them and struck them with tumors,<note placement="foot">The Masoretic Hebrew text (<hi type="italic">Kethib</hi>) reads “boils”; the reading tradition (<hi type="italic">Qere)</hi> has “tumors”</note> both in Ashdod and its territories.

verses.name: I Samuel 5:7
verses.text: The men of Ashdod saw <transChange type="added">that</transChange> it <transChange type="added">was</transChange> so, and they said, “The ark of the God of Israel should not remain with us, because his hand <transChange type="added">is</transChange> harsh on us and on Dagon our god!”

verses.name: I Samuel 5:8
verses.text: So they sent and gathered all the rulers of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines to them, and they asked, “What shall we do with the ark of the God of Israel?” And they said, “Let the ark of the God of Israel be brought around toward Gath.” So they moved the ark of the God of Israel <transChange type="added">to Gath</transChange>.  <div eID="gen2261" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 5:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1617"/><div sID="gen2262" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1617"/>After they moved it, the hand of Yahweh was against the city, causing a very great confusion, and he struck the men of the city <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from the youngest to the oldest⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “from small up to great”</note> causing tumors<note placement="foot">The Masoretic Hebrew text (<hi type="italic">Kethib</hi>) reads “boils”; the reading tradition (<hi type="italic">Qere)</hi> has “tumors”</note> to break out on them.

verses.name: I Samuel 5:10
verses.text: So they sent the ark of God <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Ekron. But when the ark of God came <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Ekron, the Ekronites cried out, saying, “They have brought around the ark of the God of Israel to kill us and our<note placement="foot">Hebrew “me and my”</note> people!”

verses.name: I Samuel 5:11
verses.text: So they sent and gathered all the rulers of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines, and they said, “Send away the ark of the God of Israel and let it return to its place, so that it will not kill us and our people.” For a <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞deadly confusion⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a confusion of death”; indicates a genitive of attribute</note> was throughout all the city; the hand of God was very heavy there.

verses.name: I Samuel 5:12
verses.text: The men who did not die were struck with <transChange type="added">the</transChange> tumors,<note placement="foot">The Masoretic Hebrew text (<hi type="italic">Kethib</hi>) reads “boils”; the reading tradition (<hi type="italic">Qere)</hi> has “tumors”</note> so that the cry of the city for help went up <transChange type="added">to</transChange> heaven.  <chapter eID="1Sam.5"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 6:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1618"/><title type="x-s">The Return of the Ark of Covenant</title> <div sID="gen2263" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1618"/>Now the ark of Yahweh had been in the territory of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines <transChange type="added">for</transChange> seven months,

verses.name: I Samuel 6:2
verses.text: and <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines called to the priests and to those who practiced divination, saying, “What should we do with the ark of Yahweh? Inform us how we should send it to its place.”

verses.name: I Samuel 6:3
verses.text: They said, “If you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> sending the ark of the God of Israel away, you must not send it away empty, but by all means return it with a guilt offering. Then you will be healed and it will become known to you why his hand <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not turned aside from you.”

verses.name: I Samuel 6:4
verses.text: And they said, “What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the guilt offering that we should return to him?” They said, “The number of the rulers of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines <transChange type="added">is</transChange> five. Therefore send five gold tumors<note placement="foot">The Masoretic Hebrew text (<hi type="italic">Kethib</hi>) reads “boils”; the reading tradition (<hi type="italic">Qere)</hi> has “tumors”</note> and five gold mice, because one plague <transChange type="added">was</transChange> on all of you and all your rulers.

verses.name: I Samuel 6:5
verses.text: You must make images of your tumors<note placement="foot">The Masoretic Hebrew text (<hi type="italic">Kethib</hi>) reads “boils”; the reading tradition (<hi type="italic">Qere)</hi> has “tumors”</note> and images of your mice that <transChange type="added">are</transChange> ravaging the land, and you must give glory to the God of Israel. Perhaps he will lighten his hand on you and on your gods and on your land.

verses.name: I Samuel 6:6
verses.text: Why should you harden your hearts like <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Egyptians and Pharaoh hardened their heart? Is it not just like when he dealt with them wantonly so that they sent them away and they left?

verses.name: I Samuel 6:7
verses.text: So then, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞prepare⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “take and make”</note> one new utility cart and two milking cows that have never had a yoke on them, and you must harness the cows to the utility cart and then turn their calves from following them to their stall.

verses.name: I Samuel 6:8
verses.text: And you must take the ark of Yahweh and place it on the utility cart with the gold objects that you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> returning to him as a guilt offering. You must place <transChange type="added">them</transChange> in the container<note placement="foot">Or perhaps “chest” or “bag”</note> beside <transChange type="added">the ark</transChange> and then send it <transChange type="added">off</transChange> so that it goes away.

verses.name: I Samuel 6:9
verses.text: You must watch; if it goes up by the way of its territory to Beth Shemesh, he has caused this great disaster to <transChange type="added">come on</transChange> us. But if not, then we will know his hand has not struck us; it <transChange type="added">was by</transChange> chance <transChange type="added">that</transChange> this happened to us.

verses.name: I Samuel 6:10
verses.text: So the men did so; they took two milking cows and harnessed them to the utility cart, but they shut up their calves in the stall.

verses.name: I Samuel 6:11
verses.text: Then they put the ark of Yahweh on the utility cart with the container<note placement="foot">Or perhaps “chest” or “bag”</note> <transChange type="added">holding</transChange> the gold mice and the images of their tumors.

verses.name: I Samuel 6:12
verses.text: The cows went straight on the way on the road to Beth Shemesh, on the one main road, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞lowing as they went⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “they went going and lowing”</note> They did not turn aside to the right or to the left, and the rulers of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines <transChange type="added">were</transChange> walking after them up to the border of Beth Shemesh.  <div eID="gen2263" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 6:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1619"/><div sID="gen2264" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1619"/>Now <transChange type="added">the people of</transChange> Beth Shemesh <transChange type="added">were</transChange> reaping the wheat harvest in the valley. They lifted their eyes and saw the ark, and they were glad to see <transChange type="added">it</transChange>.

verses.name: I Samuel 6:14
verses.text: The utility cart came to the field of Joshua <transChange type="added">of</transChange> Beth Shemesh and stopped there where there <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a large stone. They split the wood of the utility cart and sacrificed the cows <transChange type="added">as</transChange> a burnt offering to Yahweh.

verses.name: I Samuel 6:15
verses.text: Then the Levites took down the ark of Yahweh and the container<note placement="foot">Or perhaps “chest” or “bag”</note> that was beside it, in which were the gold objects, and they set them on the large stone.<note placement="foot">The Masoretic Hebrew text reads “Abel” here; some Hebrew manuscripts and LXX read “stone” (see 6:14–15)</note> Then the men of Beth Shemesh offered burnt offerings, and they <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞made⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sacrificed”</note> sacrifices to Yahweh on that day.

verses.name: I Samuel 6:16
verses.text: The five rulers of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines saw <transChange type="added">it</transChange> and returned <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Ekron that <transChange type="added">same</transChange> day.  <div eID="gen2264" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 6:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1620"/><div sID="gen2265" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1620"/>Now these <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the gold tumors which <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines returned <transChange type="added">as</transChange> a guilt offering to Yahweh: one for Ashdod, one for Gaza, one for Ashkelon, one for Gath, one for Ekron.

verses.name: I Samuel 6:18
verses.text: And the gold mice <transChange type="added">according to</transChange> the number of all the cities of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines, for their five rulers, from <transChange type="added">the</transChange> fortified city to the unwalled village of the open country as far as the great stone, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞where they set⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “which they set down on it”</note> the ark of Yahweh until this day in the field of Joshua <transChange type="added">of</transChange> Beth Shemesh.

verses.name: I Samuel 6:19
verses.text: He<note placement="foot">That is, Yahweh</note> struck seventy men<note placement="foot">Though the MT has “seventy men, fifty thousand men” (= 50,070), it is likely the original was “seventy men”</note> among the men of Beth Shemesh because they looked into the ark of Yahweh. So the people mourned because Yahweh had struck a great blow among the people.

verses.name: I Samuel 6:20
verses.text: Then the men of Beth Shemesh asked, “Who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> able to stand before Yahweh, this holy God? And to whom shall it<note placement="foot">That is, the ark of the covenant (alternatively read as “he,” referring to Yahweh)</note> go up from us?”

verses.name: I Samuel 6:21
verses.text: So they sent messengers to the inhabitants of Kiriath Jearim saying, “<transChange type="added">The</transChange> Philistines have returned the ark of Yahweh. Come down and take it up to yourselves.”  <chapter eID="1Sam.6"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 7:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1621"/><title type="x-s">Revival and Victory at Mizpah</title> <div sID="gen2266" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1621"/>The men of Kiriath Jearim came and brought up the ark of Yahweh, and they brought it to the house of Abinadab in Gibeah. They consecrated Eleazer his son to guard the ark of Yahweh.

verses.name: I Samuel 7:2
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞From⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it happened from”</note> the day the ark stayed in Kiriath Jearim, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞days multiplied and became twenty years⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and the days were numerous, and they were twenty years”</note> while all the house of Israel mourned after Yahweh.

verses.name: I Samuel 7:3
verses.text: And Samuel spoke to all the house of Israel, saying, “If with all your heart you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> turning to Yahweh, remove the foreign gods and Ashtoreths<note placement="foot">Hebrew plural “Ashtaroth” (Ashtoreth was the female consort of Ba’al)</note> from your midst. Commit your hearts to Yahweh and serve him alone. Then he will deliver you from the hand of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines.”

verses.name: I Samuel 7:4
verses.text: So the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> removed the Baals<note placement="foot">Hebrew plural “Be’alim” (Ba’al was a major Canaanite deity)</note> and the Ashtoreths, and they served Yahweh alone.  <div eID="gen2266" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 7:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1622"/><div sID="gen2267" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1622"/>Then Samuel said, “Gather all Israel to Mizpah, and I will pray to Yahweh for you.”

verses.name: I Samuel 7:6
verses.text: So they gathered to Mizpah and drew water and poured <transChange type="added">it</transChange> out before Yahweh. They fasted on that day and said there, “We have sinned against Yahweh!” So Samuel judged the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> at Mizpah.

verses.name: I Samuel 7:7
verses.text: <transChange type="added">Now</transChange> when <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines heard that the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> had gathered at Mizpah, the rulers of the Philistines went up against Israel. And when the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> heard of it, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they were afraid of the Philistines⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “and they were afraid from (= because of) the presence of the Philistines”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 7:8
verses.text: Then the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> said to Samuel, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞You must not cease⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “You must not be silent from us”</note> from crying out to Yahweh our God, so that he will deliver us from the hand of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines.”

verses.name: I Samuel 7:9
verses.text: So Samuel took a single <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞nursing lamb⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “lamb of milk”</note> and sacrificed <transChange type="added">it</transChange> as a whole burnt offering to Yahweh. Then Samuel cried out to Yahweh on behalf of Israel, and Yahweh answered him.

verses.name: I Samuel 7:10
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞While⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it happened”</note> Samuel <transChange type="added">was</transChange> sacrificing the burnt offering, <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines drew near for the battle against Israel. But Yahweh thundered against <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines with a great noise on that day and threw them into confusion so that they were defeated before Israel.

verses.name: I Samuel 7:11
verses.text: Then the men of Israel went out from Mizpah and pursued <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines and they struck them down as far as below Beth Car.  <div eID="gen2267" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 7:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1623"/><div sID="gen2268" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1623"/>So Samuel took a single stone and put <transChange type="added">it</transChange> between Mizpah and Shen, and he named it Ebenezer and said, “Up to here Yahweh has helped us.”

verses.name: I Samuel 7:13
verses.text: So the Philistines were subdued and they did not come into the territory of Israel again, and the hand of Yahweh was against <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines all the days of Samuel.

verses.name: I Samuel 7:14
verses.text: The towns<note placement="foot">Or “cities”</note> which <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines had taken from Israel <transChange type="added">were</transChange> returned to Israel from Ekron to Gath, and Israel delivered their territories from the hand of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines. Then there was peace between Israel and the Amorites.  <div eID="gen2268" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 7:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1624"/><title type="x-s">The Circuit Ministry of Samuel</title> <div sID="gen2269" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1624"/>Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.

verses.name: I Samuel 7:16
verses.text: He used to go <transChange type="added">on the circuit</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from year to year⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “from what is required year in year”</note> He went around Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah, and he judged Israel <transChange type="added">in</transChange> all these places.

verses.name: I Samuel 7:17
verses.text: Then <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he returned⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and his return was”</note> to Ramah, because his house was there, and there he judged Israel, and he built an altar to Yahweh there.  <chapter eID="1Sam.7"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 8:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1625"/><title type="x-s">Israel’s Demand for a King</title> <div sID="gen2270" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1625"/>When Samuel grew old he appointed his sons as judges over Israel.

verses.name: I Samuel 8:2
verses.text: The name of his firstborn son <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Joel, and the name of his second son <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Abijah. <transChange type="added">They were</transChange> judges in Beersheba.

verses.name: I Samuel 8:3
verses.text: But his sons did not walk in his ways; they turned aside after gain, they took bribes, and they perverted justice.  <div eID="gen2270" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 8:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1626"/><div sID="gen2271" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1626"/>So all the elders of Israel gathered together and came to Samuel at Ramah.

verses.name: I Samuel 8:5
verses.text: They said to him, “Look, you are old and your sons do not follow in your ways. So then appoint a king for us to judge<note placement="foot">Or “to rule”</note> us, like all the nations.

verses.name: I Samuel 8:6
verses.text: But the matter <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞was displeasing to Samuel⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “was evil in the eyes of Samuel”</note> when they said, “Give us a king to judge<note placement="foot">Or “to rule”</note> us,” so Samuel prayed to Yahweh.  <div eID="gen2271" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 8:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1627"/><div sID="gen2272" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1627"/>Then Yahweh said to Samuel, “Listen to the voice of the people concerning all that they say to you; for they have not rejected you, but they have rejected me from being king over them.

verses.name: I Samuel 8:8
verses.text: Like all the deeds they have done from the day I brought them up from Egypt until this day, they have forsaken me and have served other gods—so they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> doing to you also.

verses.name: I Samuel 8:9
verses.text: And so then, listen to their voice. However, you must earnestly warn them; you must explain to them the custom of the king who will rule over them.”  <div eID="gen2272" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 8:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1628"/><div sID="gen2273" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1628"/>So Samuel spoke all the words of Yahweh to the people who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> requesting a king from him.

verses.name: I Samuel 8:11
verses.text: He said, “This will be the custom of the king who will reign over you: he will take your sons and appoint them to his chariots and his horsemen, and they will run before his chariots.

verses.name: I Samuel 8:12
verses.text: He will appoint for himself commanders of thousands and commanders of fifties, and <transChange type="added">those</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to do his plowing⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to plow his plowing”</note> and to reap his harvest, and <transChange type="added">those</transChange> to make weapons of war and the equipment for his chariots.

verses.name: I Samuel 8:13
verses.text: He will take your daughters as <transChange type="added">his</transChange> perfume makers and as cooks and as bakers.

verses.name: I Samuel 8:14
verses.text: He will take the best of your fields and your vineyards and your olive trees and will give <transChange type="added">them</transChange> to his servants.

verses.name: I Samuel 8:15
verses.text: He will take a tenth of your seed and your vineyards and give <transChange type="added">it</transChange> to his high officials and to his servants.

verses.name: I Samuel 8:16
verses.text: He will take your male slaves and your female slaves and the best of your young men<note placement="foot">LXX reads “cattle”</note> and your donkeys and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞will use them for his projects⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “will put them to his work”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 8:17
verses.text: He will take a tenth of your flocks,<note placement="foot">The Hebrew term refers collectively to both sheep and goats (small livestock animals)</note> and you <transChange type="added">yourselves</transChange> will become his servants.

verses.name: I Samuel 8:18
verses.text: So you will cry out on that day because of your king whom you have chosen for yourselves, but Yahweh will not answer you on that day!”

verses.name: I Samuel 8:19
verses.text: However, the people refused to listen to the voice of Samuel and they said, “No, but there must be a king over us,

verses.name: I Samuel 8:20
verses.text: so that we <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞also⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “even we”</note> may be like all the nations, and our king may rule us and go out before us and fight our battles.”  <div eID="gen2273" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 8:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1629"/><div sID="gen2274" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1629"/>Now when Samuel heard all the words of the people, he repeated them in the ears of Yahweh.

verses.name: I Samuel 8:22
verses.text: Then Yahweh said to Samuel, “Listen to their voice, and appoint a king for them.” So Samuel spoke to the men of Israel, “Each of you go to his <transChange type="added">own</transChange> town.”  <chapter eID="1Sam.8"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 9:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1630"/><title type="x-s">Saul, the Requested King, Introduced</title> <div sID="gen2275" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1630"/>Now there was a man from Benjamin whose name was Kish, the son of Abiel, the son of Zeror, the son of Becorath, the son of Aphiah, the son of a Benjaminite, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a very wealthy man⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “a man mighty of wealth” or “a man mighty of valor”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 9:2
verses.text: He had a son whose name was Saul,<note placement="foot">The name “Saul” means “the requested one”</note> a young and handsome man. There was not a man from the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> more handsome than he <transChange type="added">was</transChange>; from his shoulders up, he was taller than all the people.  <div eID="gen2275" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 9:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1631"/><div sID="gen2276" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1631"/>Now the female donkeys of Kish the father of Saul got lost, and Kish said to Saul his son, “Please take one of the servants with you and get up; go and seek the female donkeys.”

verses.name: I Samuel 9:4
verses.text: So he passed through the hill country of Ephraim; he passed through the land of Shalisha but they did not find <transChange type="added">them</transChange>. They passed through the land of Shaalim but they were not there. He passed through the land of Benjamin but did not find <transChange type="added">them</transChange>.  <div eID="gen2276" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 9:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1632"/><div sID="gen2277" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1632"/>When they entered the land of Zuph, Saul said to his servant who <transChange type="added">was</transChange> with him, “Come, let us return, lest my father cease <transChange type="added">caring about</transChange> the female donkeys and worry about us!”

verses.name: I Samuel 9:6
verses.text: But he<note placement="foot">That is, Saul’s servant</note> said to him, “Look, a man of God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in this town, and the man <transChange type="added">is</transChange> honored. All that he says certainly comes true. So then let us go there; perhaps he will tell us about our journey on which we have gone.”

verses.name: I Samuel 9:7
verses.text: So Saul said to his servant, “Look, we may go, but what should we bring to the man? For the bread <transChange type="added">is</transChange> gone from our bags, and there <transChange type="added">is</transChange> no present to bring to the man of God. What <transChange type="added">do we have</transChange> with us?”

verses.name: I Samuel 9:8
verses.text: The servant again answered Saul and said, “Look, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I have⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “what was found”</note> in my hand a quarter shekel of silver! I will give it to the man of God so that he will tell us our way.”

verses.name: I Samuel 9:9
verses.text: (Formerly in Israel, when a man went to inquire of God, he would say: “Come, let us go up to the seer.” For the prophet of today was formerly called a seer.)

verses.name: I Samuel 9:10
verses.text: So Saul said to his servant, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Your suggestion is a good one⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “Your word is good”</note> Come, let us go.” And they went to the town where the man of God <transChange type="added">was</transChange>.  <div eID="gen2277" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 9:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1633"/><div sID="gen2278" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1633"/>They <transChange type="added">were</transChange> going up the ascent of the town when they found young women going out to draw water. They said to them, “Is there the seer here?”

verses.name: I Samuel 9:12
verses.text: They answered them and said, “There is. Look, <transChange type="added">he is</transChange> just in front of you! Hurry now, because he has come to the town today, because there <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a sacrifice for the people today at the high place.

verses.name: I Samuel 9:13
verses.text: As soon as you enter the town, you will find him, before he goes up to the high place to eat. For the people will not eat until he comes, because he must bless the sacrifice. Then afterward the invited <transChange type="added">guests</transChange> will eat. So then, go up, because you will find him today!”

verses.name: I Samuel 9:14
verses.text: So they went up to the town. As they <transChange type="added">were</transChange> entering into the middle of the town, Samuel was coming forth to meet them, to go up to the high place.  <div eID="gen2278" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 9:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1634"/><div sID="gen2279" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1634"/>Now Yahweh <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞had revealed this to⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “had opened the ear”</note> Samuel the day before Saul arrived, saying,

verses.name: I Samuel 9:16
verses.text: “This time tomorrow I will send to you a man from the land of Benjamin, and you must anoint him as leader over my people Israel. He will deliver my people from the hand of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines. For I have seen <transChange type="added">the suffering of</transChange> my people, because their cry <transChange type="added">of distress</transChange> has come to me.”

verses.name: I Samuel 9:17
verses.text: When Samuel saw Saul, Yahweh answered him, “Here <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the man about whom I told you! This <transChange type="added">is the</transChange> one <transChange type="added">who</transChange> will govern my people.”  <div eID="gen2279" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 9:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1635"/><div sID="gen2280" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1635"/>Then Saul approached Samuel in the middle of the gate and said, “Please tell me, where <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the house of the seer?”

verses.name: I Samuel 9:19
verses.text: Samuel answered Saul and said, “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> the seer. Go up <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞ahead of me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “before my face”</note> to the high place, and you will eat with me today; then I will send you away in the morning. I will tell you all that is <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞on your mind⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “in your heart”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 9:20
verses.text: And as for your female donkeys that were lost <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞three days ago⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the day three of the days”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞do not be concerned about them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “you shall not put your heart to them”</note> because they have been found. For whom <transChange type="added">is</transChange> all the desire of Israel? Is it not for you and for all the house of your father?”  <div eID="gen2280" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 9:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1636"/><div sID="gen2281" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1636"/>Saul answered and said, “<transChange type="added">Am</transChange> I not a Benjaminite, from the smallest of the tribes of Israel, and my family the humblest of all the families of the tribes of Benjamin? Why do you speak to me <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in this way⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?”<note placement="foot">Literally “according to this word”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 9:22
verses.text: So Samuel took Saul and his servant and brought them to a room in the building and gave them a place at the head of <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the invited guests⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the ones being invited”</note> There were about thirty men.

verses.name: I Samuel 9:23
verses.text: Then Samuel said to the cook, “Bring the portion that I gave to you, about which I said to you, ‘Keep it with you.’ ”

verses.name: I Samuel 9:24
verses.text: So the cook took up the shank and what was on it and put it before Saul, and he<note placement="foot">That is, Samuel</note> said, “Look, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the saved portion⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “what was being kept”</note> is placed <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to your face”</note>—eat, because it has been kept for you for the appointed time,” <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞and he said⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “saying”</note> “I have invited the people.” So Saul ate with Samuel that day.  <div eID="gen2281" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 9:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1637"/><div sID="gen2282" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1637"/>When they came down from the high place to the town, he spoke with Saul on the roof.

verses.name: I Samuel 9:26
verses.text: They got up early, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞and as dawn was breaking⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “as the dawn was going up”</note> Samuel called to Saul on the roof, saying, “Get up, so that I can send you away.” So Saul got up and the two of them, he and Samuel, went outside.

verses.name: I Samuel 9:27
verses.text: As they were going down to the outskirts of the town, Samuel said to Saul, “Tell the servant to pass on before us. When he has passed, you stand here <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a while⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “as the day”</note> so that I can make known to you <transChange type="added">the</transChange> word of God.”  <chapter eID="1Sam.9"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 10:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1638"/><title type="x-s">Saul Is Anointed as King</title> <div sID="gen2283" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1638"/>Then Samuel took a flask of oil and poured it over his head and kissed him and said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Has not⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Is it not that”</note> Yahweh anointed you as leader over his inheritance?

verses.name: I Samuel 10:2
verses.text: As you go from with me <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞today⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the day”</note> you will find two men near the burial site of Rachel in the territory of Benjamin at Zelzah. They will say to you, ‘The female donkeys that you went to search for have been found.’ Now look, your father <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞is no longer concerned about⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “has given up the matter of”</note> the female donkeys and has begun worrying about you,<note placement="foot">Here the pronoun is plural, referring to Saul and his servant</note> saying, ‘What should I do about my son?’

verses.name: I Samuel 10:3
verses.text: Then you will go on from there and further you will come to the oak of Tabor. There three men will meet you, who <transChange type="added">are</transChange> going up to God at Bethel. One will be carrying three male kid goats, one will be carrying three loaves of bread, and one will be carrying a skin of wine.

verses.name: I Samuel 10:4
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞They will ask how you are doing⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “they will ask peace for you”</note> and will give you two loaves, which you will take from their hand.

verses.name: I Samuel 10:5
verses.text: After this, you will come to the Gibeah of God,<note placement="foot">Or “to Gibeath Elohim,” which means “the hill of God”</note> where there are sentries<note placement="foot">Or “garrisons” or “overseers”</note> of the Philistines. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Just as you enter⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and will it happen that as you enter”</note> the town there, you will meet a procession of prophets coming down from the high place, with harp, tambourine, flute, and zither before them, and they will be prophesying.

verses.name: I Samuel 10:6
verses.text: Then the Spirit of Yahweh will rush upon you,<note placement="foot">Or “will come upon you in power”</note> and you will prophesy with them; and you will turn into <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a different person⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “another man”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 10:7
verses.text: When these signs come to you, do for yourself what your hand finds <transChange type="added">to do</transChange>, for God <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> with you.

verses.name: I Samuel 10:8
verses.text: Then you will go down before me to Gilgal. Look, I am coming down to you to offer burnt offerings <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞and to make⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to sacrifice sacrifices of”</note> fellowship offerings. You must wait seven days until I come to you. Then I will let you know what you should do.”

verses.name: I Samuel 10:9
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Just as he turned⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it happened as he turned”</note> his shoulder to depart from Samuel, God <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞changed his⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “gave for him another”</note> heart. And all these signs were fulfilled on that day.  <div eID="gen2283" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 10:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1639"/><div sID="gen2284" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1639"/>When they went from there to Gibeah, a procession of prophets met him, and the Spirit of God rushed upon him,<note placement="foot">Or “came upon him in power”</note> and he prophesied among them.

verses.name: I Samuel 10:11
