verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And when⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and it happened”</note> all who knew him <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞formerly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “three days from yesterday”</note> saw that he prophesied with prophets, the people said to one another, “What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> this <transChange type="added">that</transChange> has happened to the son of Kish? <transChange type="added">Is</transChange> Saul also among the prophets?”

verses.name: I Samuel 10:12
verses.text: And a man from there responded and said, “And who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> their father?” Therefore it became a proverb: “<transChange type="added">Is</transChange> Saul also among the prophets?”

verses.name: I Samuel 10:13
verses.text: When he finished prophesying, he went to the high place.

verses.name: I Samuel 10:14
verses.text: Then Saul’s uncle said to him and to his servant, “Where did you go?” And he said, “To search <transChange type="added">for</transChange> the female donkeys; and when we saw none, we went to Samuel.”

verses.name: I Samuel 10:15
verses.text: So Saul’s uncle said to him, “Please tell me, what did Samuel say to you?”

verses.name: I Samuel 10:16
verses.text: Then Saul said to his uncle, “He told us for certain that the female donkeys had been found.” But he did not tell him about the matter of the kingship <transChange type="added">of</transChange> which Samuel had spoken.  <div eID="gen2284" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 10:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1640"/><div sID="gen2285" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1640"/>Then Samuel summoned the people to Yahweh at Mizpah,

verses.name: I Samuel 10:18
verses.text: and he said to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> “Thus says Yahweh the God of Israel: ‘I brought Israel up from Egypt, and I delivered you from the hand of the Egyptians and from the hand of all the kingdoms that <transChange type="added">were</transChange> oppressing you.’

verses.name: I Samuel 10:19
verses.text: But you today have rejected your God who always delivers you from all of your calamities and your distresses. You have said to him, ‘No, but you must appoint a king over us!’ So then present yourselves before Yahweh by your tribes and by your clans.”  <div eID="gen2285" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 10:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1641"/><div sID="gen2286" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1641"/>So Samuel brought near all the tribes of Israel, and the tribe of Benjamin was selected by lot.

verses.name: I Samuel 10:21
verses.text: Then he brought near the tribe of Benjamin according to its families, and the family of Matri was selected by lot. Then Saul the son of Kish was chosen, and they sought him, but he could not be found.

verses.name: I Samuel 10:22
verses.text: So they inquired again of Yahweh, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Did the man come here⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?”<note placement="foot">Literally “Did he come still here a man”</note> And Yahweh said, “Look, he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> hiding himself among the baggage.”

verses.name: I Samuel 10:23
verses.text: So they ran and took him from there, and when he took his stand among the people, he was taller than all the people from his shoulders and up.

verses.name: I Samuel 10:24
verses.text: Then Samuel said to all the people, “Do you see him whom Yahweh has chosen? For there is no one like him among all the people!” And all the people shouted and said, “Long live the king!”  <div eID="gen2286" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 10:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1642"/><div sID="gen2287" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1642"/>Then Samuel told the people the custom of the kingship, and he wrote <transChange type="added">the rules</transChange> down on a scroll and laid <transChange type="added">it</transChange> before Yahweh. Then Samuel sent all the people away, each to his own house.

verses.name: I Samuel 10:26
verses.text: And Saul also went to his house at Gibeah, and the troops whose hearts<note placement="foot">Hebrew “heart”</note> God had touched went with him.

verses.name: I Samuel 10:27
verses.text: However, some <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞worthless men⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons of wickedness”</note> said, “How can this man deliver us?” So they despised him and brought no gift to him, but he kept silent.<note placement="foot">The Dead Sea Scrolls contained a nearly complete scroll of 1 and 2 Samuel, the oldest Hebrew manuscript extant. There is a story therein that provides a setting for the acts of Nahash in 1 Samuel 11, which otherwise seems to occur obtrusively. This story may be translated: “Now Nahash, king of the Ammonites, harshly tormented the Gadites and the Reubenites, and he gouged out all their right eyes, and struck terror and dread in Israel. No Israelite beyond the Jordan remained whose right eye was not gouged out by Nahash king of the Ammonites, except for seven thousand men who had fled from the Ammonites and entered Jabesh Gilead. About a month later …” This early text leaves off with 11:1 at this point</note>  <chapter eID="1Sam.10"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 11:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1643"/><title type="x-s">Saul Defeats the Ammonites</title> <div sID="gen2288" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1643"/>Now Nahash the Ammonite went up and encamped against Jabesh Gilead. All the men of Jabesh said to Nahash, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Make a treaty with us⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Cut with us a covenant”</note> and we will serve you.”

verses.name: I Samuel 11:2
verses.text: But Nahash the Ammonite said to them, “On this <transChange type="added">condition</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I will make a treaty⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “I will cut”</note> with you, by gouging out the right eye of each of you, so that I can make it a disgrace for all Israel.”

verses.name: I Samuel 11:3
verses.text: So the elders of Jabesh said to him, “Leave us alone for seven days so that we may send messengers in all the territory of Israel, and if there <transChange type="added">is</transChange> no deliverer for us, then we will come out to you.”

verses.name: I Samuel 11:4
verses.text: When the messengers came to Gibeah of Saul, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they reported these things to⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “they spoke the words in the ears of”</note> the people. Then all the people lifted up their voices and wept.

verses.name: I Samuel 11:5
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Just then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “And look/behold”</note> Saul was coming from the field behind the cattle. Saul said, “What <transChange type="added">is the matter</transChange> with the people, that they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> weeping?” So they recounted to him the words of the men of Jabesh.  <div eID="gen2288" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 11:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1644"/><div sID="gen2289" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1644"/>Then the Spirit of God rushed upon Saul when he heard these words, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he became very angry⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “his nose became very hot”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 11:7
verses.text: So he took a yoke of oxen and cut them into pieces and sent <transChange type="added">them</transChange> throughout all the territory of Israel by the hand of the messengers, saying, “Whoever <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not going out after Saul and after Samuel, so will it be done to his oxen.” Then the fear of Yahweh fell on the people and they went out as one man.

verses.name: I Samuel 11:8
verses.text: He mustered them at Bezek; the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> <transChange type="added">were</transChange> three hundred thousand, and the men of Judah <transChange type="added">were</transChange> thirty thousand.

verses.name: I Samuel 11:9
verses.text: They said to the messengers who had come, “Thus you will say to the men of Jabesh Gilead: ‘Tomorrow deliverance for you will come <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞when the sun is hot⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.’ ”<note placement="foot">Literally “at the heating of the sun”</note> When the messengers went and told the men of Jabesh, they rejoiced.

verses.name: I Samuel 11:10
verses.text: The men of Jabesh said, “Tomorrow we will come out to you and you may do to us <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞whatever seems good to you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “as all of the good that is in your eyes”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 11:11
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And the⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and it happened the”</note> next day Saul placed the people in three divisions. Then they came into the middle of the camp <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞at the early morning watch⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “at the night watch of the morning”</note> and struck down <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Ammon”</note> until the heat of the day. It happened that the remainder were scattered <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞so that no two among them remained together⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “and they did not remain among them two together”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 11:12
verses.text: Then the people said to Samuel, “Who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the one who asked, ‘Will Saul reign over us?’ Give the men to us that we may kill them.”

verses.name: I Samuel 11:13
verses.text: But Saul said, “No one will be put to death on this day, because <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞today⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the day”</note> Yahweh has provided deliverance in Israel.”  <div eID="gen2289" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 11:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1645"/><div sID="gen2290" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1645"/>Then Samuel said to the people, “Come, let us go to Gilgal, and let us renew the kingship there.”

verses.name: I Samuel 11:15
verses.text: So all the people went to Gilgal and they made Saul king there before Yahweh in Gilgal. They sacrificed fellowship offerings there before Yahweh. Then Saul rejoiced there greatly <transChange type="added">along with</transChange> all the men of Israel.  <chapter eID="1Sam.11"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 12:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1646"/><title type="x-s">Samuel’s Charge to Israel</title> <div sID="gen2291" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1646"/>Then Samuel said to all Israel, “Look, I have listened to your voice regarding all that you have said to me, so I have set a king over you.

verses.name: I Samuel 12:2
verses.text: And so then here <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the king walking about before you. Now I am old and gray, but my sons (look at them!) <transChange type="added">are</transChange> with you; and I have walked about before you from my youth until this day.

verses.name: I Samuel 12:3
verses.text: Here I am! Testify against me before Yahweh and before his anointed one! Whose ox have I taken? Or whose donkey have I taken? Or whom have I exploited? Whom have I oppressed? Or from whose hand have I taken a bribe, that I may shut my eyes <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞regarding⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “with”</note> him?–then I will restore it to you.”

verses.name: I Samuel 12:4
verses.text: Then they said, “You have not exploited us or oppressed us, and you have not taken anything from the hand of anyone.”

verses.name: I Samuel 12:5
verses.text: So he said to them, “Yahweh <transChange type="added">is</transChange> witness against you, and his anointed one <transChange type="added">is</transChange> witness this day, that you have not found anything in my hand.” Then they said, “<transChange type="added">He is</transChange> witness.”

verses.name: I Samuel 12:6
verses.text: Then Samuel said to the people, “Yahweh <transChange type="added">is witness</transChange>, who appointed Moses and Aaron, and who brought your ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> up from the land of Egypt.

verses.name: I Samuel 12:7
verses.text: So then take your stand, so that I may judge you before Yahweh with <transChange type="added">regard to</transChange> all the <transChange type="added">deeds of</transChange> justice<note placement="foot">Or “righteous deeds”</note> of Yahweh that he performed with both you and your ancestors.<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note>  <div eID="gen2291" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 12:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1647"/><div sID="gen2292" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1647"/>“When Jacob came to Egypt, your ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> cried out to Yahweh, so he sent Moses and Aaron, and they brought your ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> out from Egypt and settled them in this place.

verses.name: I Samuel 12:9
verses.text: But they forgot Yahweh their God, so he sold them into the hand of Sisera, commander of the hosts of Hazor, and into the hand of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines, and into the hand of the king of Moab, and they fought against them.

verses.name: I Samuel 12:10
verses.text: So they cried out to Yahweh and said, ‘We have sinned, because we have forsaken Yahweh and have served the Baals<note placement="foot">Hebrew plural “Be’alim” (Ba’al was a major Canaanite deity)</note> and the Ashtoreths.<note placement="foot">Hebrew plural “Ashtoroth” (Ashtoreth was the female consort of Ba’al)</note> But now deliver us from the hand of our enemies and we will serve you!’

verses.name: I Samuel 12:11
verses.text: So Yahweh sent Jerub-Baal and Bedan<note placement="foot">Many English translations follow the LXX here and read “Barak”</note> and Jephthah and Samuel. Then he delivered you from the hand of your enemies all around, and you lived <transChange type="added">in</transChange> security.  <div eID="gen2292" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 12:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1648"/><div sID="gen2293" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1648"/>“And when you saw that Nahash, the king of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> was coming against you, you said to me, ‘No! A king shall reign over us,’ although Yahweh your God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> your king.

verses.name: I Samuel 12:13
verses.text: So then look! <transChange type="added">Here is</transChange> the king you have chosen, for whom you have asked! Look, Yahweh has placed a king over you!

verses.name: I Samuel 12:14
verses.text: If you will fear Yahweh, and serve him, and listen to his voice, and not be rebellious against <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞what Yahweh says⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the mouth of Yahweh”</note> and both you and the king who rules over you will <transChange type="added">follow</transChange> after Yahweh your God, <transChange type="added">all will be well</transChange>.

verses.name: I Samuel 12:15
verses.text: But, if you do not listen to the voice of Yahweh, and you rebel against <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞what Yahweh says⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the mouth of Yahweh”</note> then the hand of Yahweh will be against you<note placement="foot">Here LXX reads “against you and against your king”</note> as it was against your ancestors.<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 12:16
verses.text: So then take your stand again and see this great thing that Yahweh <transChange type="added">is going to</transChange> do before your eyes.

verses.name: I Samuel 12:17
verses.text: <transChange type="added">Is</transChange> the wheat harvest not today? I will call out to Yahweh so that he still sends thunder and rain, so that you will know and will see that your wickedness <transChange type="added">is</transChange> great that you have done in the eyes of Yahweh by asking for a king for yourselves.”  <div eID="gen2293" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 12:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1649"/><div sID="gen2294" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1649"/>So Samuel called out to Yahweh, and Yahweh brought thunder and rain that <transChange type="added">same</transChange> day, so all the people feared Yahweh and Samuel greatly.

verses.name: I Samuel 12:19
verses.text: Then all the people said to Samuel, “Pray for your servants to Yahweh your God so that we will not die, because we have added to all our sins by requesting a king for ourselves.”

verses.name: I Samuel 12:20
verses.text: And Samuel said to the people, “Do not fear! You have done all this evil; only do not turn aside from <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞following⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “after”</note> Yahweh. But you must serve Yahweh with all your heart.

verses.name: I Samuel 12:21
verses.text: And do not turn aside after the triviality,<note placement="foot">That is, the triviality of lifeless idols. The same Hebrew word, <hi type="italic">tohu</hi>, is used in Genesis 1:2 to describe the pre-created state of the earth.</note> which have no value and cannot deliver, for they are triviality.

verses.name: I Samuel 12:22
verses.text: For Yahweh will not forsake his people for the sake of his great name, because Yahweh has decided to make you his <transChange type="added">own</transChange> people.

verses.name: I Samuel 12:23
verses.text: Also, as for me, far be it from me <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞that I should sin⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from sinning”</note> against Yahweh by ceasing to pray for you! I will instruct you in the good and righteous way.

verses.name: I Samuel 12:24
verses.text: Only fear Yahweh and serve him faithfully with all of your heart. For consider <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞what great things he has done for you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “what he made great with you”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 12:25
verses.text: But if you continue to do wickedness, both you and your king will be swept away.”  <chapter eID="1Sam.12"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 13:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1650"/><title type="x-s">Saul Rules over Israel</title> <div sID="gen2295" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1650"/>Saul <transChange type="added">was thirty</transChange><note placement="foot">A few LXX manuscripts have “thirty,” but the number of years is missing from the Masoretic Hebrew text</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞years old⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a son of years”</note> at the beginning of his reign, and he reigned forty-two years<note placement="foot">The Masoretic Hebrew text reads “two years” here, but this number seems far too small; either it is not correct or part of the number is missing (the present translation supplies “forty”); other English versions differ as to Saul’s age at coronation and the total years of his reign</note> over Israel.

verses.name: I Samuel 13:2
verses.text: He chose for himself three thousand from Israel. Two thousand <transChange type="added">of these</transChange> were with Saul at Micmash in the hill country of Bethel, and a thousand were with Jonathan at Gibeah in Benjamin. He sent away the rest of the people, each to his tent.

verses.name: I Samuel 13:3
verses.text: Jonathan defeated the garrison of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> at Geba, and <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines heard <transChange type="added">about it</transChange>. Then Saul blew the trumpet throughout all the land, saying, “Let the Hebrews hear!”

verses.name: I Samuel 13:4
verses.text: And all Israel did hear, saying, “Saul has defeated the garrison of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines; and also, Israel has become a stench among <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines!” So the people were called out after Saul at Gilgal.  <div eID="gen2295" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 13:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1651"/><title type="x-s">Saul’s Blunder</title> <div sID="gen2296" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1651"/>And the Philistines assembled to fight with Israel, thirty thousand chariots and six thousand horsemen and an army as numerous as sand which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> on the seashore. And they came up and encamped at Micmash, east of Beth Aven.  <div eID="gen2296" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 13:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1652"/><div sID="gen2297" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1652"/>When the men of Israel saw that <transChange type="added">it was</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞too difficult⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “too narrow”</note> for them, because the army was hard pressed, the people hid themselves in the caves, in the thorn bushes, in the cliffs, in the vaults<note placement="foot">Or “cellars” or “tombs” ‘ or “strongholds”</note> and in the wells.

verses.name: I Samuel 13:7
verses.text: <transChange type="added">Some</transChange> of the Hebrews crossed over the Jordan to the land of Gad and Gilead. But Saul was still at Gilgal, and all the army <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞followed him trembling⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “trembled after him”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 13:8
verses.text: He waited seven days according to the appointed time Samuel determined, but Samuel did not come to Gilgal, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the army started to slip away from him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the people scattered away from him”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 13:9
verses.text: So Saul said, “Bring here to me the burnt offering and the fellowship offerings.” Then he offered up the burnt offering.

verses.name: I Samuel 13:10
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Just as⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it happened as”</note> he finished offering the burnt sacrifice, Samuel was coming. So Saul went out to meet him <transChange type="added">and</transChange> to bless him.

verses.name: I Samuel 13:11
verses.text: But Samuel said, “What have you done?” Saul said, “Because I saw that the army <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞was scattering⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “dispersed themselves”</note> from me and you did not come <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞at the appointed time⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “according to the appointed time of the days”</note> and <transChange type="added">that the</transChange> Philistines had gathered at Micmash,

verses.name: I Samuel 13:12
verses.text: therefore I said, ‘Now <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines will come down against me at Gilgal, and I have not yet implored the face of Yahweh.’ So I forced myself and offered the burnt offering.”  <div eID="gen2297" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 13:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1653"/><div sID="gen2298" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1653"/>Then Samuel said to Saul, “You have behaved foolishly! You have not kept the command of Yahweh your God which he commanded you. For then, Yahweh would have established your kingdom over Israel forever.

verses.name: I Samuel 13:14
verses.text: But now, your kingdom will not endure. Yahweh has sought for himself a man according to his <transChange type="added">own</transChange> heart, and Yahweh has appointed him as leader over his people, because you have not kept what Yahweh commanded you.”  <div eID="gen2298" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 13:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1654"/><div sID="gen2299" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1654"/>Then Samuel got up and went up from Gilgal to Gibeah of Benjamin. And Saul mustered the people who were found with him, about six hundred men.

verses.name: I Samuel 13:16
verses.text: Saul and Jonathan his son and the army that remained with them <transChange type="added">were</transChange> staying in Geba <transChange type="added">of</transChange> Benjamin, and <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines encamped at Micmash.

verses.name: I Samuel 13:17
verses.text: The <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞raiders⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “destroyers”</note> went out from the camp of the Philistines in three divisions. One division turned on the road<note placement="foot">Or “way”</note> to Ophrah toward the land of Shual.

verses.name: I Samuel 13:18
verses.text: One division turned on the road<note placement="foot">Or “way”</note> to Beth Horon, and one turned on the road<note placement="foot">Or “way”</note> toward the border overlooking the valley of Zeboim toward the wilderness.  <div eID="gen2299" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 13:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1655"/><div sID="gen2300" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1655"/>Now no skilled craftsman could be found in all the land of Israel, for <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines had said, “So that the Hebrews cannot make swords or spears for themselves.”

verses.name: I Samuel 13:20
verses.text: So all Israel <transChange type="added">went</transChange> down to <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines, each to have his plowshare, his mattock, his axe, and his iron plowshare<note placement="foot">So the Masoretic Hebrew text; LXX reads “sickle”</note> sharpened.

verses.name: I Samuel 13:21
verses.text: The charge<note placement="foot">Or “fee”</note> was <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞two-thirds of a shekel⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a pim” (possibly a stone weight used as a measure)</note> for the plowshare and for the mattock, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a third of a shekel for the pick⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and for three, a pick” (uncertain; perhaps meaning “a third of a shekel,” or a three-pronged pick”</note> and for the axe, and to set the goading sticks.

verses.name: I Samuel 13:22
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞So⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally, “And it happened”</note> on the day of battle, there was not a sword or a spear found in the hands of all the army that was with Saul and Jonathan, but <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Saul and his son Jonathan had them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally, “it could be found for Saul and for Jonathan his son”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 13:23
verses.text: Now the garrison of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines went out to the pass of Micmash.  <chapter eID="1Sam.13"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 14:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1656"/><title type="x-s">Jonathan Leads the Counterattack</title> <div sID="gen2301" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1656"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞One day⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it happened the day”</note> Jonathan the son of Saul said to <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his armor bearer⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the young man carrying his weapons”</note> “Come and let us go over to the garrison of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> over there.” But he did not tell his father.

verses.name: I Samuel 14:2
verses.text: Now Saul <transChange type="added">was</transChange> staying at the outskirts of Gibeah under the pomegranate tree that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in Migron, and the troops that <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him <transChange type="added">were</transChange> about six hundred men.

verses.name: I Samuel 14:3
verses.text: Now Ahijah, the son of Ahitub (the brother of Ichabod), the son of Phinehas, the son of Eli the priest of Yahweh at Shiloh, was carrying an ephod. The troops did not know that Jonathan had gone.

verses.name: I Samuel 14:4
verses.text: Now between the passes where Jonathan sought to go over to the garrison of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines <transChange type="added">there was</transChange> a crag of rock <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞on one side⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from the beyond from this”</note> and a crag of rock <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞on the other⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “from the beyond from this”</note> The name of the one <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Bozez and the name of the other <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Seneh.

verses.name: I Samuel 14:5
verses.text: The one crag on the north <transChange type="added">was</transChange> opposite Micmash and the other on the south <transChange type="added">was</transChange> opposite Geba.

verses.name: I Samuel 14:6
verses.text: So Jonathan said to <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his armor bearer⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the young man carrying his weapons”</note> “Come, let us go over to the garrisons of these uncircumcised; perhaps Yahweh will act for us, for there is no hindrance for Yahweh to save by many or by few.”

verses.name: I Samuel 14:7
verses.text: And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his armor bearer⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the one carrying his weapons”</note> said, “Do all that is in your heart <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞that you are inclined to do⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “turn/incline for yourself”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I am with you all of the way⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!<note placement="foot">Literally “Behold, I am with you according to your heart”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 14:8
verses.text: Then Jonathan said, “Look, we <transChange type="added">are about to</transChange> go over to the men; and we will show ourselves to them.

verses.name: I Samuel 14:9
verses.text: If they say to us: ‘Wait until we reach you,’ <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞then we will stand as we are⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and we will stand under us”</note> and not go up to them.

verses.name: I Samuel 14:10
verses.text: But if they say, ‘Come up to us,’ then we will go up, for Yahweh has given them into our hand, and this <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> the sign for us.”

verses.name: I Samuel 14:11
verses.text: So the two of them showed themselves to the garrison of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines, and <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines said, “The Hebrews <transChange type="added">are</transChange> coming out from the holes in which they have hidden themselves.”

verses.name: I Samuel 14:12
verses.text: Then the men of the garrison answered Jonathan and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his armor bearer⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the one carrying his weapons”</note> “Come up to us and we will show you something!” Then Jonathan said to <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his armor bearer⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the one carrying his weapons”</note> “Come up after me, for Yahweh has given them into the hand of Israel!”

verses.name: I Samuel 14:13
verses.text: So Jonathan went up on his hands and his feet, with <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his armor bearer⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the one carrying his weapons”</note> after him. They fell before Jonathan and then <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his armor bearer⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the one carrying his weapons”</note> would kill them after him.

verses.name: I Samuel 14:14
verses.text: So was the first attack <transChange type="added">in</transChange> which Jonathan and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his armor bearer⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the one carrying his weapons”</note> killed about twenty men within about half of a furrow in an acre of <transChange type="added">an</transChange> open field.

verses.name: I Samuel 14:15
verses.text: Then there was terror<note placement="foot">Or “panic”</note> in the camp, in the open field, and among all the army of the garrison. Even the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞raiders⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “destroyers”</note> trembled. The earth shook, and it became <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a very great panic⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “like the panic/terror of God”; some interpreters understand this to be a panic caused by God, while others understand the expression merely as a superlative (“a very great panic”)</note>  <div eID="gen2301" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 14:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1657"/><div sID="gen2302" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1657"/>And the lookouts of Saul in Gibeah of Benjamin saw <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞that⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and look”</note> the multitude <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞surged back and forth⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “waved, going here and there”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 14:17
verses.text: Saul said to the troops that <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him, “Please call the roll and see who has gone from us.” So they called the roll <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞and found that⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and look”</note> Jonathan and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his armor bearer⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the one carrying his weapons”</note> were not <transChange type="added">present</transChange>.

verses.name: I Samuel 14:18
verses.text: Then Saul said to Ahijah, “Bring near the ark of God”<note placement="foot">LXX reads “bring near the ephod”</note> (for the ark of God was <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞at that time⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “on that day”</note> with the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>).<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 14:19
verses.text: While<note placement="foot">Hebrew “And”</note> Saul was still speaking to the priest, the tumult in the camp of the Philistines <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞increased more and more⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “and it went, going and increasing”</note> so Saul said to the priest, “Withdraw your hand!”

verses.name: I Samuel 14:20
verses.text: Then Saul and all the troops who were with him were assembled on command and came up to the battle, and look! Each <transChange type="added">Philistine’s</transChange> sword <transChange type="added">was</transChange> against his friend; <transChange type="added">and there was</transChange> a very great confusion.

verses.name: I Samuel 14:21
verses.text: The Hebrews who had been for <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞previously⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “as yesterday three days ago”</note> who had gone up with them into the camp all around, even they <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞joined the Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “were with Israel”</note> who were with Saul and Jonathan.

verses.name: I Samuel 14:22
verses.text: All the men of Israel who had hidden themselves in the hill country of Ephraim heard that <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines had fled, so even they pursued them closely in the battle.

verses.name: I Samuel 14:23
verses.text: So on that day Yahweh delivered Israel, and the battle shifted to Beth Aven.  <div eID="gen2302" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 14:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1658"/><title type="x-s">Saul’s Oath Leads to Trouble</title> <div sID="gen2303" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1658"/>Now the men of Israel were hard pressed on that day, because Saul had made the army take an oath, saying, “Cursed be the man who eats <transChange type="added">any</transChange> food until evening, when I will have avenged myself on my enemies!” So none of the army tasted <transChange type="added">any</transChange> food.

verses.name: I Samuel 14:25
verses.text: (Now all <transChange type="added">the people of</transChange> the land used to go into the forest, for there was honey on the surface of the ground.)

verses.name: I Samuel 14:26
verses.text: When the army came to the forest, look! <transChange type="added">There was</transChange> honey flowing, but no one put his hand to his mouth, for the army was afraid of the solemn oath.  <div eID="gen2303" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 14:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1659"/><div sID="gen2304" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1659"/>However, Jonathan had not heard about the oath of his father with the army, so he extended the end of the staff which was in his hand, and he dipped it into the honeycomb.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “the honeycomb of the honey”</note> Then he put his hand to his mouth and his eyes gleamed.<note placement="foot">The Masoretic Hebrew text (<hi type="italic">Kethib</hi>) reads “saw”; the reading tradition (<hi type="italic">Qere)</hi> reads “gleamed”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 14:28
verses.text: Then a man from the army informed <transChange type="added">him</transChange> and said, “Your father made the army swear a solemn <transChange type="added">oath</transChange>, saying, ‘Cursed be the man who eats food today,’ ” so the army <transChange type="added">is</transChange> exhausted.

verses.name: I Samuel 14:29
verses.text: Then Jonathan said, “My father has brought trouble on the land! See now that my eyes have brightened because I have tasted a little of this honey.

verses.name: I Samuel 14:30
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞How much more could have been done⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “even that if”</note> if the troops had eaten freely today from the plunder of their enemies that they had found! For now the loss among <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not great.”

verses.name: I Samuel 14:31
verses.text: They defeated <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines that day from Micmash to Aijalon, and the troops were very weary.  <div eID="gen2304" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 14:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1660"/><div sID="gen2305" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1660"/>Then the troops took the plunder: they took sheep and cattle and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞calves⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the children of cattle”</note> and slaughtered <transChange type="added">them</transChange> on the ground and the troops ate <transChange type="added">them all</transChange> with the blood.

verses.name: I Samuel 14:33
verses.text: So they reported <transChange type="added">it</transChange> to Saul, saying, “Look! The troops <transChange type="added">are</transChange> sinning against Yahweh by eating <transChange type="added">the animals</transChange> with the blood!” And he said, “You have dealt treacherously! Roll to me a large stone <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞today⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!”<note placement="foot">Literally “the day”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 14:34
verses.text: Then Saul said, “Disperse <transChange type="added">yourselves</transChange> among the troops and say to them, ‘Bring to me each <transChange type="added">one</transChange> his ox and each his sheep and slaughter them in this <transChange type="added">place</transChange> and eat, but do not sin against Yahweh by eating <transChange type="added">the animals</transChange> with the blood.’ ” So all the troops brought <transChange type="added">them</transChange>, each <transChange type="added">leading</transChange> his ox in his hand that night, and slaughtered <transChange type="added">it</transChange> there.  <div eID="gen2305" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 14:35
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1661"/><title type="x-s">Jonathan Rescued from His Father Saul</title> <div sID="gen2306" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1661"/>Then Saul built an altar to Yahweh; <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞it was the first altar he built⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “with it he began to build an altar”</note> to Yahweh.

verses.name: I Samuel 14:36
verses.text: Saul said, “Let us go down after <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines <transChange type="added">by</transChange> night, and let us plunder them until the morning light, and let us not leave <transChange type="added">alive</transChange> a man among them.” So they said, “Do all that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> good in your eyes.” But the priest said, “Let us draw near to God here.”

verses.name: I Samuel 14:37
verses.text: So Saul inquired of God, “Should I go down after <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines? Will you give them into the hand of Israel?” But he did not answer him on that day.

verses.name: I Samuel 14:38
verses.text: Then Saul said, “Come here, all <transChange type="added">you</transChange> leaders of the people, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞so that we find out⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and know and see”</note> what the sin was this day.

verses.name: I Samuel 14:39
verses.text: For as Yahweh lives, who delivers Israel, <transChange type="added">I swear</transChange> that even if it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in Jonathan my son, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he will certainly die⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!”<note placement="foot">Literally “surely dying he will die”</note> But nobody from all the army answered him.

verses.name: I Samuel 14:40
verses.text: Then he said to all Israel, “You will be <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞on one side⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “opposite one”</note> and I and my son Jonathan will be <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞on the other⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “opposite one”</note> And the army said to Saul, “Do <transChange type="added">what is</transChange> good in your eyes.”

verses.name: I Samuel 14:41
verses.text: Then Saul said to Yahweh the God of Israel, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Render a decision perfectly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “give what is perfect”; the LXX includes additional words not found in the Masoretic Hebrew text but included in a number of modern English versions: “If this guilt is on me or in my son Jonathan, give Urim, but if this guilt is in your people Israel, give Thummim”</note> Jonathan and Saul were chosen <transChange type="added">by lot</transChange> and the people went out.

verses.name: I Samuel 14:42
verses.text: Then Saul said, “Let them cast <transChange type="added">the lot</transChange> between me and my son Jonathan,” and Jonathan was chosen.

verses.name: I Samuel 14:43
verses.text: So Saul said, “Tell me what you have done.” So Jonathan told him and said, “I <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞merely tasted⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “tasted I tasted”</note> a little honey with the end of the staff that was in my hand. Here I am, I must die.”

verses.name: I Samuel 14:44
verses.text: Then Saul said, “So may God do <transChange type="added">to me</transChange> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞more⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “so may he add”</note> you will certainly die today, Jonathan!”

verses.name: I Samuel 14:45
verses.text: But the army said to Saul, “Must Jonathan die, who accomplished this great victory in Israel? Far from it! As Yahweh lives, not a hair from his head will fall to the ground, for he has worked with God this day.” So the army ransomed Jonathan and he did not die.  <div eID="gen2306" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 14:46
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1662"/><div sID="gen2307" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1662"/>Saul went up from <transChange type="added">pursuing the</transChange> Philistines, and <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines went to their place.

verses.name: I Samuel 14:47
verses.text: So Saul took the kingship over Israel, and he fought all around against his enemies, against Moab, against the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> against Edom, against the kings of Zobah, and against the Philistines. He inflicted punishment against all who rebelled.

verses.name: I Samuel 14:48
verses.text: He acted bravely and defeated <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Amalekites and rescued Israel from the hand of those who plundered it.  <div eID="gen2307" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 14:49
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1663"/><div sID="gen2308" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1663"/>Now the sons of Saul were Jonathan, Ishvi, and Malki-Shua; the names of his two daughters <transChange type="added">were as follows</transChange>: the name of the firstborn <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Merab and the younger <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Michal.

verses.name: I Samuel 14:50
verses.text: The name of Saul’s wife <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Ahinoam the daughter of Ahimaaz, and the name of the commander of his army <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Abner, the son of Ner, Saul’s uncle.

verses.name: I Samuel 14:51
verses.text: Now Kish <transChange type="added">was</transChange> the father of Saul, but Ner, the father of Abner, <transChange type="added">was</transChange> the son of Abiel.  <div eID="gen2308" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 14:52
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1664"/><div sID="gen2309" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1664"/>Warfare was severe against <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines all the days of Saul. Whenever Saul saw <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞anyone who was a mighty warrior⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “each man who was a mighty warrior”</note> or <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞any brave man⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “each son of ability”</note> he <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞conscripted him into his service⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “he gathered him to himself”</note>  <chapter eID="1Sam.14"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 15:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1665"/><title type="x-s">Israel Defeats the Amalekites</title> <div sID="gen2310" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1665"/>Then Samuel said to Saul, “Yahweh sent me to anoint you as king over his people Israel. So then, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞listen to the words⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “listen to the voice of the words”</note> of Yahweh!

verses.name: I Samuel 15:2
verses.text: Thus says Yahweh of hosts: ‘I have observed what Amalek did to Israel, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞how he opposed him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “what he placed against him in the way”</note> when he went up from Egypt.

verses.name: I Samuel 15:3
verses.text: So then, go and attack Amalek and utterly destroy all that is his! You must not spare him, but kill both man and woman, both child and nursing infant, both ox and sheep, both camel and donkey.’ ”  <div eID="gen2310" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 15:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1666"/><div sID="gen2311" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1666"/>Saul summoned the army and mustered them at Telaim; two hundred thousand foot soldiers and ten thousand men of Judah.

verses.name: I Samuel 15:5
verses.text: Then Saul came up to the city of Amalek and set an ambush in the wadi.<note placement="foot">A valley that is usually dry but contains a stream during the rainy season</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 15:6
verses.text: Saul said to the Kenites, “Go, leave! Withdraw from among the Amalekites so that I do not destroy you with them. You have shown loyal love to all the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> when they came up from Egypt.” So the Kenites left from among <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Amalekites.

verses.name: I Samuel 15:7
verses.text: Then Saul defeated <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Amalekites from Havilah as one goes to Shur which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞east of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “upon the face of”</note> Egypt.

verses.name: I Samuel 15:8
verses.text: He captured Agag the king of Amalek alive, but all the people he utterly destroyed with the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞edge⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “mouth”</note> of the sword.

verses.name: I Samuel 15:9
verses.text: However, Saul and the army spared Agag and the best of the sheep and the cattle and the second <transChange type="added">best</transChange> of the young fatlings and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞all that was valuable⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “all the good things”</note> they were not willing to utterly destroy them. But all the possessions that were despised or worthless, they utterly destroyed.  <div eID="gen2311" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 15:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1667"/><title type="x-s">Samuel Announces the Downfall of Saul</title> <div sID="gen2312" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1667"/>Then the word of Yahweh came to Samuel, saying,

verses.name: I Samuel 15:11
verses.text: “I regret that I made Saul king, for he has turned back from following me and has not kept my word.” <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Samuel became angry⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “it became hot for Samuel”</note> and he cried out to Yahweh all night.

verses.name: I Samuel 15:12
verses.text: Then Samuel got up early in the morning to meet Saul. Samuel was told, “Saul has gone to Carmel, and look, he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> setting up a monument for himself.” Then he turned around and crossed over and went down to Gilgal.  <div eID="gen2312" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 15:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1668"/><div sID="gen2313" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1668"/>When Samuel came to Saul, Saul said to him, “May you be blessed by Yahweh! I have kept the word of Yahweh.”

verses.name: I Samuel 15:14
verses.text: But Samuel said, “Then what <transChange type="added">is</transChange> this bleating of the sheep <transChange type="added">that I hear</transChange> in my ears and the lowing of the cattle that I am hearing?”

verses.name: I Samuel 15:15
verses.text: Saul said, “They have brought them from <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Amalekites; the troops spared the best of the sheep and the cattle in order to sacrifice them to Yahweh your God. But the rest we have utterly destroyed.”

verses.name: I Samuel 15:16
verses.text: Then Samuel said to Saul, “Stop and let me tell you what Yahweh said to me last night.” So he said to him, “Speak.”  <div eID="gen2313" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 15:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1669"/><div sID="gen2314" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1669"/>Samuel said, “Even though you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> small in your <transChange type="added">own</transChange> eyes, are you not the head of the tribes of Israel? Yahweh has anointed you as king over Israel.

verses.name: I Samuel 15:18
verses.text: When Yahweh sent you on your way, he said to you: ‘Go! You must utterly destroy the sinners, <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Amalekites, and you must fight against them until you<note placement="foot">The Masoretic Hebrew text reads “they”; LXX, Peshitta, and Targum read “you”</note> have destroyed them.’

verses.name: I Samuel 15:19
verses.text: Why did you not listen to the voice of Yahweh and fall with shouting on the plunder? You have done evil in the sight of Yahweh!”

verses.name: I Samuel 15:20
verses.text: Then Saul said to Samuel, “I have listened to the voice of Yahweh, and I have gone on the way that Yahweh sent me! I brought Agag the king of Amalek, and the Amalekites I have utterly destroyed.

verses.name: I Samuel 15:21
verses.text: The troops took from the plunder, sheep and cattle, the best of the things devoted to destruction, to sacrifice to Yahweh your God at Gilgal.”  <div eID="gen2314" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 15:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1670"/><div sID="gen2315" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1670"/>Then Samuel said, <div eID="gen2315" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen2316"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2317"/>“Is there <transChange type="added">as much</transChange> delight for Yahweh in burnt offerings and sacrifices<l eID="gen2317" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2318"/>as <transChange type="added">there is</transChange> in <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞obeying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “listening to the voice of”</note> Yahweh?<l eID="gen2318" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2319"/>Look! <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞To obey⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Listening”</note> <transChange type="added">is</transChange> better than sacrifice;<l eID="gen2319" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2320"/>to give heed than the fat of rams. <l eID="gen2320" level="2"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 15:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1671"/><l level="1" sID="gen2321"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1671"/>For rebellion <transChange type="added">is like</transChange> the sin of divination;<l eID="gen2321" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2322"/>arrogance <transChange type="added">is like</transChange> iniquity and idolatry.<l eID="gen2322" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2323"/>Because you have rejected the word of Yahweh,<l eID="gen2323" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2324"/>he has rejected you from <transChange type="added">being</transChange> king!” <l eID="gen2324" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen2316"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 15:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1672"/><div sID="gen2325" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1672"/>Then Saul said to Samuel, “I have sinned because I have transgressed <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the commandment of Yahweh⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the mouth of Yahweh”</note> and your words, for I feared the troops and I listened to their voice.

verses.name: I Samuel 15:25
verses.text: So then, please pardon my sin and return with me <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞so that I can worship⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “so that I can bow down to”</note> Yahweh.”

verses.name: I Samuel 15:26
verses.text: But Samuel said to Saul, “I will not return with you, for you have rejected the word of Yahweh, and he has rejected you from being king over Israel!”  <div eID="gen2325" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 15:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1673"/><div sID="gen2326" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1673"/>As Samuel turned around to go, he<note placement="foot">That is, Saul</note> caught hold of the hem of his robe, and it tore.

verses.name: I Samuel 15:28
verses.text: Then Samuel said to him, “Yahweh has torn the kingdom of Israel from you today and has given it to your neighbor <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who is better than you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the better than you”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 15:29
verses.text: Moreover, the Glory of Israel will not break faith and will not regret, for he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not a human that he should regret.”

verses.name: I Samuel 15:30
verses.text: Then he<note placement="foot">That is, Saul</note> said, “I have sinned! Now please honor me before the elders of my people and before Israel, and return with me <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞so that I can worship⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “so that I can bow down to”</note> Yahweh your God.”

verses.name: I Samuel 15:31
verses.text: So Samuel returned after Saul, and Saul <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞worshiped⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “bowed down to”</note> Yahweh.  <div eID="gen2326" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 15:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1674"/><div sID="gen2327" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1674"/>Then Samuel said, “Bring Agag the king of Amalek out to me!” Agag came to him confidently,<note placement="foot">Or “trembling”; literally “in chains/bonds” (HALOT 609 s.v. 2); the meaning here is uncertain (LXX has “trembling”)</note> for Agag thought, “Surely the bitterness of death <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞is over⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “has turned aside”; other English versions follow the LXX and Peshitta and omit “has turned aside,” reading “Surely the bitterness of death!”</note>  <div eID="gen2327" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 15:33
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1675"/><div sID="gen2328" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1675"/>Samuel said, <div eID="gen2328" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen2329"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2330"/>“Just as your sword bereaved women,<l eID="gen2330" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2331"/>so will your mother be bereaved among women!”<l eID="gen2331" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen2329"/> <div sID="gen2332" type="x-p"/> Then Samuel hacked Agag to pieces in the presence of Yahweh at Gilgal.  <div eID="gen2332" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 15:34
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1676"/><div sID="gen2333" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1676"/>Then Samuel went to Ramah and Saul went up to his house in Gibeah of Saul.

verses.name: I Samuel 15:35
verses.text: Samuel <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞did not see Saul again⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “did not add to see Saul”</note> until the day of his death, but Samuel mourned over Saul, and Yahweh regretted that he made Saul king over Israel.  <chapter eID="1Sam.15"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 16:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1677"/><title type="x-s">David Is Anointed</title> <div sID="gen2334" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1677"/>Then Yahweh said to Samuel, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞How long⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Until when”</note> will you mourn about Saul? I have rejected him from being king over Israel! Fill up your horn <transChange type="added">with</transChange> oil and go. I will send you to Jesse the Bethlehemite, for I have chosen a king for myself among his sons.”

verses.name: I Samuel 16:2
verses.text: But Samuel said, “How can I go? If Saul hears, he will kill me.” Yahweh said, “You must take a heifer from the herd <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞with you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “in/with your hand”</note> and you must say, ‘I have come to sacrifice to Yahweh.’

verses.name: I Samuel 16:3
verses.text: You will invite Jesse to the sacrifice and I will make known to you what you must do. You will anoint for me <transChange type="added">the one</transChange> whom I tell you.”  <div eID="gen2334" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 16:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1678"/><div sID="gen2335" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1678"/>So Samuel did what Yahweh said. He came to Bethlehem, and the elders of the city came trembling to meet him. They said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Have you come in peace⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?”<note placement="foot">Literally “Is your coming peace?”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 16:5
verses.text: He said, “<transChange type="added">I come in</transChange> peace. I have come to sacrifice to Yahweh. Sanctify yourselves and come with me to the sacrifice.” So he sanctified Jesse and his sons and invited them to the sacrifice.  <div eID="gen2335" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 16:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1679"/><div sID="gen2336" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1679"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞When they came⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “And it happened at their coming”</note> he<note placement="foot">That is, Samuel</note> saw Eliab and said, “Surely his anointed one <transChange type="added">is</transChange> before Yahweh!”

verses.name: I Samuel 16:7
verses.text: But Yahweh said to Samuel, “Do not look at his appearance or at the height of his stature, because I have rejected him. For <transChange type="added">God does</transChange> not <transChange type="added">see</transChange> what man sees, for a man <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞looks on the outward appearance⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sees as far as the eyes”</note> but Yahweh <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞looks on the heart⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “sees as far as the heart”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 16:8
verses.text: Then Jesse called Abinadab and made him pass before Samuel, and he said, “This one also Yahweh has not chosen.”

verses.name: I Samuel 16:9
verses.text: So Jesse made Shammah pass <transChange type="added">before Samuel</transChange>, but he said, “Yahweh also has not chosen this one.”

verses.name: I Samuel 16:10
verses.text: And Jesse made seven of his sons pass before Samuel, but Samuel said to Jesse, “Yahweh has not chosen any of these.”  <div eID="gen2336" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 16:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1680"/><div sID="gen2337" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1680"/>Then Samuel said to Jesse, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Are all the young men here⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?”<note placement="foot">Literally “Are the boys finished?”</note> And he said, “The youngest still remains, but look, he is shepherding the flock.” And Samuel said to Jesse, “Send and bring him, for we cannot <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞sit down⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “turn”; for “sit down” see HALOT 739 s.v. 2.c</note> until he comes here.”

verses.name: I Samuel 16:12
verses.text: So he sent and brought him. Now he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> ruddy with beautiful eyes and of <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞handsome⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “good”</note> appearance. And Yahweh said, “Arise, anoint him, for this <transChange type="added">is</transChange> he.”

verses.name: I Samuel 16:13
verses.text: So Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the midst of his brothers. Then the Spirit of Yahweh rushed upon David from that day <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞on⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “and forward”</note> Then Samuel got up and went to Ramah.  <div eID="gen2337" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 16:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1681"/><title type="x-s">Saul in Torment</title> <div sID="gen2338" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1681"/>Now the Spirit of Yahweh departed from Saul and an evil spirit from Yahweh tormented him.

verses.name: I Samuel 16:15
verses.text: So the servants of Saul said to him, “Look please, an evil spirit from God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> tormenting you.

verses.name: I Samuel 16:16
verses.text: Please, let our lord command your servants <transChange type="added">who are</transChange> before you! Let them seek a man skilled in playing on the lyre. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞When⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it will happen that”</note> the evil spirit from God is upon you, he can play <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞on it⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “with his hand”</note> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you will feel better⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “and it will be good for you”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 16:17
verses.text: So Saul said to his servants, “Please select a man <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who plays a stringed instrument well⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “doing well to play a stringed instrument”</note> and bring <transChange type="added">him</transChange> to me.”  <div eID="gen2338" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 16:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1682"/><div sID="gen2339" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1682"/>One of the servants answered and said, “Look, I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite <transChange type="added">who is</transChange> skillful in playing a stringed instrument, a <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞brave man, a warrior, prudent in speech, and handsome⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “a hero of ability, a man of war, discerning of word, and a man of appearance”</note> And Yahweh <transChange type="added">is</transChange> with him.”

verses.name: I Samuel 16:19
verses.text: So Saul sent messengers to Jesse and said, “Send me David your son who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> with the sheep.”

verses.name: I Samuel 16:20
verses.text: And Jesse took a donkey <transChange type="added">loaded with</transChange> bread and a skin of wine and one <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞young goat⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “kid of a goat”</note> and sent <transChange type="added">them</transChange> to Saul by the hand of David his son.

verses.name: I Samuel 16:21
verses.text: So David came to Saul and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞entered his service⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “stood before him”</note> He<note placement="foot">That is, Saul</note> loved him greatly and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he became Saul’s armor bearer⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “he became for him a carrier of weapons”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 16:22
verses.text: Then Saul sent <transChange type="added">word</transChange> to Jesse, saying, “Please let David stand before me, because he has found favor <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in my sight⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “in my eyes”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 16:23
verses.text: So whenever the <transChange type="added">evil</transChange> spirit from God came to Saul, David would take the stringed instrument and play it with his hand. Then <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞it would bring relief⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “it would be relieved”</note> for Saul; <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he would feel better⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “it would be good for him”</note> and the evil spirit would depart from him.  <chapter eID="1Sam.16"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 17:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1683"/><title type="x-s">The Philistine Champion Taunts Israel</title> <div sID="gen2340" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1683"/><transChange type="added">The</transChange> Philistines gathered their camps<note placement="foot">Or “armies”</note> for battle and they were gathered <transChange type="added">at</transChange> Socoh which <transChange type="added">belongs</transChange> to Judah. They camped between Socoh and Azekah in Ephes Dammim.

verses.name: I Samuel 17:2
verses.text: Then Saul and the men of Israel were gathered and encamped in the valley of Elah, and they formed ranks <transChange type="added">for the</transChange> battle to meet <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines.

verses.name: I Samuel 17:3
verses.text: <transChange type="added">The</transChange> Philistines were standing on the hill on one side and <transChange type="added">the army of</transChange> Israel was standing on the hill on the other side with the valley between them.

verses.name: I Samuel 17:4
verses.text: Then <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a champion⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a man of the space between”</note> went out from the camps of the Philistines, whose name was Goliath from Gath. His height was six cubits and a span.<note placement="foot">A cubit was about eighteen inches and a span about nine inches, so the Masoretic Hebrew text gives the height of nine feet, nine inches. Ancient Greek versions variously give Goliath’s height as four, five, or sixteen cubits.</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 17:5
verses.text: A bronze helmet was on his head, and he was clothed with scale body armor; the weight of the body armor was five thousand bronze shekels.

verses.name: I Samuel 17:6
verses.text: Bronze greaves<note placement="foot">Or “shin guards”</note> were on his legs,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “feet”</note> and a bronze javelin <transChange type="added">was slung</transChange> between his shoulders.

verses.name: I Samuel 17:7
verses.text: The shaft of his spear was like a weaver’s beam and the point of his spear <transChange type="added">weighed</transChange> six hundred iron shekels. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞His shield bearer⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “The one who carried his shield”</note> was walking in front of him.  <div eID="gen2340" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 17:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1684"/><div sID="gen2341" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1684"/>He stood and called to the battle lines of Israel and said to them, “Why have you come out to form ranks <transChange type="added">for</transChange> battle? <transChange type="added">Am</transChange> I not the Philistine, and you the servants of Saul? Commission for yourselves a man and let him come down to me.

verses.name: I Samuel 17:9
verses.text: If he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> able to fight with me and he defeats me, then we will be your servants; but if I prevail over him and defeat him, then you will be our servants and you will serve us.”

verses.name: I Samuel 17:10
verses.text: Then the Philistine said, “I hereby defy the battle lines of Israel today! Give me a man so that we may fight each other!”

verses.name: I Samuel 17:11
verses.text: When Saul and all Israel heard these words of the Philistine, they were dismayed and very afraid.  <div eID="gen2341" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 17:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1685"/><title type="x-s">David Enters the Scene of Battle</title> <div sID="gen2342" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1685"/>Now David was the son of an Ephrathite. This <transChange type="added">man was</transChange> from Bethlehem of Judah, and his name was Jesse. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞He had⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And for him were”</note> eight sons; in the days of Saul this man was old, yet he still walked among<note placement="foot">The LXX reads “he went in years”; that is, he was advanced in years</note> the men.

verses.name: I Samuel 17:13
verses.text: The three oldest sons of Jesse had gone and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞followed⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “went after”</note> Saul to the battle. The names of his three sons who went to the battle were Eliab the firstborn, his second <transChange type="added">oldest</transChange> was Abinadab, and the third was Shammah.

verses.name: I Samuel 17:14
verses.text: Now David was the youngest. The three oldest <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞followed⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “went after”</note> Saul,

verses.name: I Samuel 17:15
verses.text: but David went <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞back and forth⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “was going and was returning”</note> from Saul to feed the sheep of his father in Bethlehem.

verses.name: I Samuel 17:16
verses.text: Now the Philistine came forward early and late, and he took his stand <transChange type="added">for</transChange> forty days.  <div eID="gen2342" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 17:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1686"/><div sID="gen2343" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1686"/>Then Jesse said to his son David, “Please take for your brothers an ephah of this roasted grain and these ten loaves of bread, and bring <transChange type="added">them</transChange> quickly to the camp for your brothers.

verses.name: I Samuel 17:18
verses.text: And these ten portions of cheese you will bring to the commander of the thousand; <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞find out how your brothers are doing⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “make a careful inspection as far as peace concerning your brothers”</note> and take their pledge.”<note placement="foot">That is, some pledge or token of assurance that they had received the goods</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 17:19
verses.text: Now Saul and they<note placement="foot">That is, David’s brothers</note> and all the men of Israel <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in the valley of Elah fighting <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines.  <div eID="gen2343" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 17:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1687"/><div sID="gen2344" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1687"/>David rose early in the morning and left the sheep with a keeper, and he took <transChange type="added">the provisions</transChange> and went as Jesse had commanded him. He came to the encampment while the troops <transChange type="added">were</transChange> going to the battle line, and they raised the war cry.

verses.name: I Samuel 17:21
verses.text: Israel and <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines drew up <transChange type="added">in</transChange> battle lines, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞one battle line against the other⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “battle line to oppose battle line”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 17:22
verses.text: David left the baggage <transChange type="added">he had</transChange> with him in the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞care⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “hand”</note> of the baggage keeper, ran to the battle line, and came and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞asked how his brothers were doing⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “asked his brothers as far as peace”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 17:23
