verses.text: While he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> speaking to them, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the champion⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the man of the space between”</note> whose name was Goliath the Philistine from Gath, was coming up from the caves<note placement="foot">So the Masoretic Hebrew text (<hi type="italic">Kethib</hi>); the reading tradition (<hi type="italic">Qere</hi>) and LXX have “ranks”</note> of the Philistines. He spoke <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞just as he had previously⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “according to these words”</note> and David heard <transChange type="added">his words</transChange>.

verses.name: I Samuel 17:24
verses.text: When all the men of Israel saw the man, they fled from his presence and were very afraid.

verses.name: I Samuel 17:25
verses.text: And the men of Israel said, “Did you see this man who has come up? For he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> going up to defy Israel! It will be <transChange type="added">that</transChange> the man who defeats him, the king will make him<note placement="foot">That is, the man who defeats Goliath</note> very rich with great wealth and will give him his daughter in marriage and will make his father’s house free in Israel.”<note placement="foot">That is, free from taxation</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 17:26
verses.text: Now David had spoken to the men <transChange type="added">who were</transChange> standing with him, saying, “What will be done for the man who defeats this Philistine and removes <transChange type="added">the</transChange> disgrace from Israel? For who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> this uncircumcised Philistine that he defies the battle lines of the living God?”

verses.name: I Samuel 17:27
verses.text: And the troops had spoken to him according to this word, saying, “So it will be done for the man who defeats<note placement="foot">Or “kills”</note> him.”  <div eID="gen2344" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 17:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1688"/><div sID="gen2345" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1688"/>His oldest brother Eliab heard while he was speaking to the men, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞and Eliab became very angry against David⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and the nose of Eliab became hot concerning David”</note> and said, “Why have you come down today, and with whom have you left those few sheep in the wilderness? I know your presumptuousness and the evil of your heart! For you have come down in order to see the battle!”

verses.name: I Samuel 17:29
verses.text: David replied, “What have I done now? <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I merely asked a question⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!<note placement="foot">Literally “Is this not a word?”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 17:30
verses.text: He turned around from him to another opposite <transChange type="added">him</transChange> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he spoke to him in the same way⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “and he said according to this word”</note> and the people<note placement="foot">Or “troops”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞answered him as before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “returned to him a word as the first word”</note>  <div eID="gen2345" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 17:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1689"/><title type="x-s">David Appears before Saul</title> <div sID="gen2346" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1689"/>Now the words which David had spoken were heard and they reported <transChange type="added">them</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “before the face/in the presence of”</note> Saul, and he summoned him.

verses.name: I Samuel 17:32
verses.text: David said to Saul, “Do not let anyone’s heart fail concerning him! Your servant will go and fight with this Philistine.”

verses.name: I Samuel 17:33
verses.text: But Saul said to David, “You will not be able to go against this Philistine to fight with him, because you are <transChange type="added">only</transChange> a boy, whereas <transChange type="added">he has</transChange> been a man of war since his childhood!”

verses.name: I Samuel 17:34
verses.text: And David said to Saul, “Your servant has been a shepherd of the flock for his father. If the lion or the bear would come and carry off a sheep from the group,

verses.name: I Samuel 17:35
verses.text: I would go out after it and strike it down and rescue <transChange type="added">the sheep</transChange> from its mouth. If it rose against me, I would grab <transChange type="added">it</transChange> by its beard and strike it down and kill it.

verses.name: I Samuel 17:36
verses.text: Your servant has struck down both the lion and the bear, and this uncircumcised Philistine will be like one of them, because he defied the battle lines of the living God.”  <div eID="gen2346" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 17:37
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1690"/><div sID="gen2347" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1690"/>And David said, “Yahweh, who rescued me from the hand of the lion and from the hand of the bear, will rescue me from the hand of this Philistine!” Then Saul said to David, “Go and may Yahweh be with you!”

verses.name: I Samuel 17:38
verses.text: Then Saul clothed David with his <transChange type="added">own</transChange> fighting attire and put a helmet of bronze on his head and clothed him <transChange type="added">with</transChange> body armor.

verses.name: I Samuel 17:39
verses.text: Then David strapped on his sword over his fighting attire, but he tried in vain to walk <transChange type="added">around</transChange>, for he was not trained to use <transChange type="added">them</transChange>. So David said to Saul, “I am not able to walk with these, because I am not trained to use <transChange type="added">them</transChange>.” So David removed them.

verses.name: I Samuel 17:40
verses.text: Then he took his staff in his hand, picked out for himself five smooth stones from the wadi,<note placement="foot">A valley that is usually dry but contains a stream during the rainy season</note> and he put them in his shepherd’s bag, in the pouch. And with his sling in his hand, he approached the Philistine.  <div eID="gen2347" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 17:41
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1691"/><div sID="gen2348" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1691"/>Then the Philistine <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞came on, getting nearer and nearer⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “went going and near”</note> to David, with <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his shield bearer⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the man carrying the shield”</note> in front of him.

verses.name: I Samuel 17:42
verses.text: When the Philistine looked and saw David, he despised him, for he was <transChange type="added">only</transChange> a boy and ruddy with a handsome appearance.

verses.name: I Samuel 17:43
verses.text: So the Philistine said to David, “<transChange type="added">Am</transChange> I a dog, that you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> coming to me with sticks?” Then the Philistine cursed David by his gods.

verses.name: I Samuel 17:44
verses.text: The Philistine said to David, “Come to me so that I can give your flesh to the birds of heaven and to the wild animals of the field!”

verses.name: I Samuel 17:45
verses.text: Then David said to the Philistine, “You <transChange type="added">are</transChange> coming to me with a sword and with a spear and with a javelin, but I am coming to you in the name of Yahweh of hosts, the God of the battle lines of Israel, whom you have defied!

verses.name: I Samuel 17:46
verses.text: This day Yahweh will deliver you into my hand, and I will strike you down <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞and cut off your head⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!<note placement="foot">Literally “and I will remove your head from upon you”</note> Then I will give <transChange type="added">the</transChange> corpses of the army of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines this day to the birds of heaven and to the animals of the earth, so that all the earth may know that there is a God <transChange type="added">who is</transChange> for Israel.

verses.name: I Samuel 17:47
verses.text: And all of this assembly will know that Yahweh does not rescue with sword or with spear, for the battle <transChange type="added">belongs</transChange> to Yahweh, and he will give you into our hands!”  <div eID="gen2348" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 17:48
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1692"/><title type="x-s">David Defeats Goliath</title> <div sID="gen2349" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1692"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞When⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it happened that when”</note> the Philistine got up and came and drew near to meet David, David <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞ran quickly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “made quickly and he ran”</note> to the battle line to meet the Philistine.

verses.name: I Samuel 17:49
verses.text: Then David put his hand into the bag and took a stone from it and slung <transChange type="added">it</transChange>. He struck the Philistine on his forehead, and the stone sank into his forehead, and he fell on his face to the ground.

verses.name: I Samuel 17:50
verses.text: So David prevailed over the Philistine with the sling and with the stone, and he struck down the Philistine and killed him, but there was no sword in David’s hand.  <div eID="gen2349" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 17:51
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1693"/><div sID="gen2350" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1693"/>Then David ran and stood over the Philistine and took his sword and drew it from its sheath and killed him and cut off his head with it. When the Philistines saw that their champion was dead, they fled.

verses.name: I Samuel 17:52
verses.text: The men of Israel and Judah got up, raised the war cry, and pursued <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as far as⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “up to your coming to”</note> the valley<note placement="foot">So the Masoretic Hebrew text; LXX reads “Gath”</note> and up to the gates of Ekron. So the slain of the Philistines fell on the way<note placement="foot">Or “road”</note> to Shaaraim up to Gath and as far as Ekron.

verses.name: I Samuel 17:53
verses.text: Then the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> returned from pursuing <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines and plundered their camp.

verses.name: I Samuel 17:54
verses.text: And David took the head of the Philistine and brought it to Jerusalem and placed his weapons in his tent.  <div eID="gen2350" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 17:55
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1694"/><div sID="gen2351" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1694"/>Now when Saul saw David going out to meet the Philistine, he said to Abner, the commander of the army, “Whose son <transChange type="added">is</transChange> this young man, Abner?” And Abner said, “As your soul lives, O king, I do not know.”

verses.name: I Samuel 17:56
verses.text: Then the king said, “You inquire whose son this young man <transChange type="added">is</transChange>.”

verses.name: I Samuel 17:57
verses.text: So when David returned from striking down the Philistine, Abner took him and brought him before Saul. The head of the Philistine <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in his hand.

verses.name: I Samuel 17:58
verses.text: Then Saul said to him, “Whose son are you, young man?” And David said, “<transChange type="added">I am</transChange> the son of your servant Jesse the Bethlehemite.”  <chapter eID="1Sam.17"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 18:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1695"/><title type="x-s">The Friendship of David and Jonathan</title> <div sID="gen2352" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1695"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞When⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it happened as”</note> he finished speaking to Saul, the soul of Jonathan became attached to the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his <transChange type="added">own</transChange> soul.

verses.name: I Samuel 18:2
verses.text: Saul took him on that <transChange type="added">very</transChange> day and did not allow him to return to his father’s house.

verses.name: I Samuel 18:3
verses.text: Then Jonathan made a covenant with David, because he loved him as his <transChange type="added">own</transChange> soul.

verses.name: I Samuel 18:4
verses.text: Jonathan stripped off the robe <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞that he was wearing⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “which was on him”</note> and gave it to David, along with his fighting attire,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “gown,” in this context “fighting tunic,” perhaps “armor”</note> and even his sword, his bow, and his belt.  <div eID="gen2352" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 18:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1696"/><title type="x-s">David’s Successes Arouse Saul’s Suspicions</title> <div sID="gen2353" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1696"/>David went out <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞whenever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in all that”</note> Saul sent him, and he succeeded. So Saul appointed him over the men of the war, and it <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞pleased⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “was good in the eyes of”</note> all the people and even <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞pleased⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “was good in the eyes of”</note> the servants of Saul.

verses.name: I Samuel 18:6
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞When they were coming back⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it happened at their coming”</note> after David had returned from striking down the Philistine, the women went out from all the cities of Israel singing and dancing to meet King Saul with tambourines, with joy, and with three-stringed instruments.

verses.name: I Samuel 18:7
verses.text: And the women sang as they danced, and they said, <div eID="gen2353" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen2354"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2355"/>“Saul has struck down his thousands,<l eID="gen2355" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2356"/>but David his ten thousands!” <l eID="gen2356" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen2354"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 18:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1697"/><div sID="gen2357" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1697"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Saul became very angry⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “And it was very hot for Saul”</note> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞this saying displeased him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “this thing was bad in his eyes”</note> and he thought, “They have attributed to David ten thousands, but to me they have attributed thousands! <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞What more can he have but the kingdom⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?”<note placement="foot">Literally “And still for him is only the kingdom”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 18:9
verses.text: So Saul was watching<note placement="foot">The Masoretic Hebrew text (<hi type="italic">Kethib</hi>) reads “sin”; the translation follows the reading tradition (<hi type="italic">Qere)</hi> which has “eyeing” or “watching”</note> David <transChange type="added">with suspicion</transChange> from that day onward.  <div eID="gen2357" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 18:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1698"/><div sID="gen2358" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1698"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞On⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it happened from”</note> the next day, the evil spirit from God rushed upon Saul, and he prophesied in the middle of the house. Now David was playing the lyre with his hand on that day <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as usual⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “as day on day”</note> and the spear was in Saul’s hand.

verses.name: I Samuel 18:11
verses.text: Then Saul hurled the spear and thought, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I will pin David to the wall⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “I will strike David and to the wall”</note> But David eluded him twice.

verses.name: I Samuel 18:12
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Now Saul was threatened by the presence of David⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And Saul was afraid from the presence of David”</note> because Yahweh was with him, but had departed from Saul.

verses.name: I Samuel 18:13
verses.text: So Saul removed him <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from his presence⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “from with him”</note> and made him commander of a thousand, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞so he<note placement="foot">That is, David</note> marched in and out at the front of the army⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “for he was going out and was coming in before the army”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 18:14
verses.text: And David was achieving success in all his ways and Yahweh <transChange type="added">was</transChange> with him,

verses.name: I Samuel 18:15
verses.text: but when Saul saw that he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> very successful, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he was severely threatened by him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “he was terrified from his face”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 18:16
verses.text: However, all of Israel and Judah <transChange type="added">were</transChange> loving David, for he was going forth and marching ahead of them.  <div eID="gen2358" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 18:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1699"/><title type="x-s">David Marries Saul’s Daughter Michal</title> <div sID="gen2359" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1699"/>Then Saul said to David, “Here <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my older daughter Merab. I will give her to you as <transChange type="added">your</transChange> wife. Only be <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a brave warrior⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a son of valor”</note> for me and fight the battles of Yahweh.” For Saul thought, “My hand will not be against him, but let the hand of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines be against him.”

verses.name: I Samuel 18:18
verses.text: But David said to Saul, “Who <transChange type="added">am</transChange> I, and <transChange type="added">who are</transChange> my relatives, the clan of my father in Israel, that I should be a son-in-law to the king?”

verses.name: I Samuel 18:19
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞But⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it happened”</note> at the time Saul’s daughter Merab <transChange type="added">was</transChange> to be given to David, she was given <transChange type="added">instead</transChange> to Adriel the Meholathite as wife.  <div eID="gen2359" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 18:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1700"/><div sID="gen2360" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1700"/>Now Saul’s daughter Michal loved David, so they told Saul, and the matter <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞pleased him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “was right in his eyes”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 18:21
verses.text: And Saul thought, “I will give her to him, so that she may be a snare for him and the hand of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines may be against him.” So Saul said to David, “For a second <transChange type="added">time</transChange> you can become my son-in-law today.”

verses.name: I Samuel 18:22
verses.text: Then Saul commanded his servants, “Speak to David in secret, saying, ‘Look, the king <transChange type="added">is</transChange> pleased with you, and all his servants love you. So then, become a son-in-law of the king.’ ”

verses.name: I Samuel 18:23
verses.text: And Saul’s servants spoke these words <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to David privately⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “in the ears of David”</note> But David said, “Is it insignificant <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in your sight⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in your eyes”</note> to become the son-in-law of the king, <transChange type="added">as</transChange> I am a poor and lightly esteemed man?”

verses.name: I Samuel 18:24
verses.text: So the servants of Saul informed him, saying, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞This is what David said⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “According to these words David spoke”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 18:25
verses.text: Then Saul said, “This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> what you must say to David: ‘<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞The king desires no bride price⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “There is not a desire for the king for a bride price”</note> except for a hundred foreskins of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines, to avenge himself on the enemies of the king.’ ” (Now Saul had planned to allow David to fall by the hand of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines.)

verses.name: I Samuel 18:26
verses.text: So his servants told David these words, and the matter <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞pleased David⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “was right in the eyes of David”</note> to become the son-in-law of the king as <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the specified time had not expired⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the days were not full”</note>  <div eID="gen2360" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 18:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1701"/><div sID="gen2361" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1701"/>And David got up, and he and his men went and struck down two hundred men <transChange type="added">of the</transChange> Philistines. Then David brought their foreskins, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they presented the full number⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “they filled them up”</note> to become the king’s son-in-law. Then Saul gave him Michal his daughter as <transChange type="added">his</transChange> wife.

verses.name: I Samuel 18:28
verses.text: When Saul <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞realized⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “saw and knew”</note> that Yahweh was with David and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his own daughter Michal⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Michal the daughter of Saul”</note> loved him,

verses.name: I Samuel 18:29
verses.text: Saul <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞was threatened by David still more⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “added to be afraid from the presence of David”</note> so Saul <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞became a perpetual enemy of David⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “was an enemy with David all the days”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 18:30
verses.text: Then the commanders of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines went out <transChange type="added">for battle</transChange>, and as often as they went out, David succeeded more than all the servants of Saul, and his name became very esteemed.  <chapter eID="1Sam.18"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 19:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1702"/><title type="x-s">Jonathan Intercedes for David</title> <div sID="gen2362" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1702"/>Now Saul spoke to Jonathan his son and to all his servants about killing David, but Saul’s son Jonathan <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞liked David very much⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “delighted in David very”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 19:2
verses.text: So Jonathan informed David, saying, “My father Saul <transChange type="added">is</transChange> trying to kill you; now please take care! In the morning you should stay in the hiding place and conceal yourself.

verses.name: I Samuel 19:3
verses.text: I will go out and stand <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞at my father’s side⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “at the hand of my father”</note> in the field where you are, and I will speak about you to my father; <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞if I find out anything⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “if I see and what?”</note> I will tell <transChange type="added">it</transChange> to you.”

verses.name: I Samuel 19:4
verses.text: So Jonathan spoke well about David to his father Saul and said to him, “The king should not sin against his servant David, because he has not sinned against you, and because his service for you <transChange type="added">has been</transChange> very good.

verses.name: I Samuel 19:5
verses.text: He put his life in his hand and attacked the Philistine, and Yahweh brought about a great victory for all of Israel, and you saw <transChange type="added">it</transChange> and rejoiced! Now why should you sin against innocent blood by killing David without cause?”

verses.name: I Samuel 19:6
verses.text: And Saul listened to the voice of Jonathan and swore, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞As Yahweh lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the life of Yahweh”</note> he will not be put to death!”

verses.name: I Samuel 19:7
verses.text: Jonathan called to David and told him all of these words. Then Jonathan brought David to Saul and he was before him as <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞formerly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “yesterday three days ago”</note>  <div eID="gen2362" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 19:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1703"/><title type="x-s">David Has to Flee Again</title> <div sID="gen2363" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1703"/>War came again, so David went out and fought against <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞defeated them thoroughly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “he struck them down with a great blow”</note> so that they fled before him.

verses.name: I Samuel 19:9
verses.text: Then the evil spirit from Yahweh came upon Saul while he was sitting in his house <transChange type="added">with</transChange> his spear in his hand. And David <transChange type="added">was</transChange> playing a stringed instrument in <transChange type="added">his</transChange> hand.

verses.name: I Samuel 19:10
verses.text: So Saul tried <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to pin David to the wall with the spear⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to strike with the spear on David and to the wall”</note> but <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he eluded Saul⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “he escaped from the presence of Saul”</note> so that he struck the spear into the wall, and David fled and escaped that <transChange type="added">same</transChange> night.  <div eID="gen2363" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 19:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1704"/><div sID="gen2364" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1704"/>Then Saul sent messengers to David’s house to guard him and to kill him in the morning, but Michal his wife told David, saying, “If <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you do not save your life⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “you are not saving your life”</note> tonight, <transChange type="added">then</transChange> tomorrow you <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> killed!”

verses.name: I Samuel 19:12
verses.text: So Michal lowered David through the window, and he went and fled and escaped.

verses.name: I Samuel 19:13
verses.text: Then Michal took the household god<note placement="foot">Hebrew <hi type="italic">teraphim</hi></note> and put it on the bed and put a quilt of goat’s hair at its head and covered <transChange type="added">it</transChange> with the clothes.

verses.name: I Samuel 19:14
verses.text: And Saul sent messengers to arrest David, but she said, “He <transChange type="added">is</transChange> ill.”

verses.name: I Samuel 19:15
verses.text: So Saul sent the messengers to see David, saying, “Bring him up to me in the bed, so that I can kill him.”

verses.name: I Samuel 19:16
verses.text: When the messengers came, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to their surprise⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and look”</note> the idol <transChange type="added">was</transChange> on the bed <transChange type="added">with</transChange> the quilt of goat’s hair at the head.

verses.name: I Samuel 19:17
verses.text: Then Saul said to Michal, “Why have you deceived me like this and sent away my enemy, so that he escaped?” Michal said to Saul, “He said to me, ‘Let me go, why should I kill you?’ ”  <div eID="gen2364" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 19:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1705"/><div sID="gen2365" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1705"/>So David fled and escaped, and he came to Samuel at Ramah and told him all that Saul had done to him. Then he and Samuel went and stayed in Naioth.

verses.name: I Samuel 19:19
verses.text: And it was told to Saul, “David <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in Naioth in Ramah.”

verses.name: I Samuel 19:20
verses.text: So Saul sent messengers to capture David. When they saw the company of the prophets prophesying and Samuel standing <transChange type="added">as</transChange> chief over them, then the Spirit of God came upon Saul’s messengers, and they also prophesied.

verses.name: I Samuel 19:21
verses.text: So they told Saul, and he sent other messengers, and they also prophesied. Again Saul sent messengers a third <transChange type="added">time</transChange>, and they also prophesied.

verses.name: I Samuel 19:22
verses.text: Then he also went to Ramah. When he came to the great cistern which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in Secu, he asked and said, “Where <transChange type="added">are</transChange> Samuel and David?” Someone said, “Look <transChange type="added">they are</transChange> in Naioth in Ramah.”

verses.name: I Samuel 19:23
verses.text: So he went there to Naioth in Ramah and the Spirit of God came upon him also, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he walked along prophesying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “he went going and he prophesied”</note> until he came to Naioth in Ramah.

verses.name: I Samuel 19:24
verses.text: He also stripped <transChange type="added">off</transChange> his clothes and prophesied before Samuel. He lay naked all that day and all night. Therefore they say, “<transChange type="added">Is</transChange> Saul also among the prophets?”  <chapter eID="1Sam.19"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 20:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1706"/><title type="x-s">Jonathan Supports David over Saul</title> <div sID="gen2366" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1706"/>Then David fled from Naioth in Ramah and came and said before Jonathan, “What have I done? What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my guilt and what <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my sin before your father that <transChange type="added">he is</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞trying to kill me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?<note placement="foot">Literally “seeking my life”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 20:2
verses.text: And he said to him, “Far from it! You will not die! Look, my father does not do<note placement="foot">The Masoretic Hebrew text (<hi type="italic">Kethib</hi>) reads “he does to/for him”; the translation follows the reading tradition (<hi type="italic">Qere)</hi> which has “does not do”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞anything large or small unless he reveals it to me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “a large thing or a small thing and he does not reveal to my ear”</note> Why should my father hide this thing or anything from me?”

verses.name: I Samuel 20:3
verses.text: Then David <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞took an oath⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “swore”</note> again and said, “Your father knows very well that I have found favor in your eyes, and he thought, ‘Do not let Jonathan know this, lest he worry.’ But <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as Yahweh lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the life of Yahweh”</note> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as your soul lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the life of your soul”</note> surely <transChange type="added">there is</transChange> merely a step between me and death!”

verses.name: I Samuel 20:4
verses.text: Then Jonathan said to David, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Whatever you wish⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “What your soul says”</note> I will do for you.”

verses.name: I Samuel 20:5
verses.text: David said to Jonathan, “Look, tomorrow <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the new moon, and I should certainly sit with the king to eat. You must send me away so that I can hide myself in the field until the third evening.

verses.name: I Samuel 20:6
verses.text: If your father misses me at all, then you must say, ‘David earnestly asked from me to run to Bethlehem his city, for <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the yearly sacrifice⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the sacrifice of the days”</note> <transChange type="added">is</transChange> there for all the clan.’

verses.name: I Samuel 20:7
verses.text: If he says ‘Good,’ <transChange type="added">it will mean</transChange> peace for your servant; but if he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> very angry, know that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he has decided to do me harm⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the evil has been determined from with him”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 20:8
verses.text: So you must show loyal love to your servant, for you have brought your servant into a covenant of Yahweh with you. But if there <transChange type="added">is</transChange> guilt in me, <transChange type="added">then</transChange> kill me yourself! But why should you bring me to your father?”

verses.name: I Samuel 20:9
verses.text: Then Jonathan said, “Far be it from you! For if I know for certain that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞my father decided evil should come upon you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the evil is determined from with my father to come over you”</note> would I not have told it to you?”

verses.name: I Samuel 20:10
verses.text: Then David said to Jonathan, “Who will tell me if what your father answers you <transChange type="added">is</transChange> harsh?”

verses.name: I Samuel 20:11
verses.text: And Jonathan said to David, “Come, let us go out to the field.” So the two of them went out to the field.  <div eID="gen2366" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 20:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1707"/><div sID="gen2367" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1707"/>Then Jonathan said to David, “Yahweh the God of Israel <transChange type="added">is my witness</transChange><note placement="foot">The phrase “is my witness” is supplied based on the Syriac version</note> that I will question my father <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞by this time the day after tomorrow⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “as the time tomorrow the third”</note> And look, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞if he is well disposed toward you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “if he is good to David”</note> will I not send word to you and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞disclose it to you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?<note placement="foot">Literally “I will reveal it to your ear”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 20:13
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞So may Yahweh punish Jonathan and more⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “So may Yahweh do to Jonathan and so may he add”</note> if <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞my father decides to do you harm⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the evil over you is regarded as good by my father”</note> and if <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I fail to disclose it to you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “I will reveal it to your ear”</note> and send word to you that you can go safely. And may Yahweh be with you, as he has been with my father.

verses.name: I Samuel 20:14
verses.text: And not while I am still alive, will you not show the loyal love of Yahweh with me, that I may not die?<note placement="foot">Or perhaps “and if I die, may you not …”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 20:15
verses.text: And do not cut off your loyal love from <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞my family⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “my house”</note> forever, not even when Yahweh <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞exterminates⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “cuts off”</note> each of the enemies of David from the face of the earth.”

verses.name: I Samuel 20:16
verses.text: So Jonathan <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞made a covenant⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “cut a covenant”</note> with the house of David, saying, “May Yahweh <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞call the enemies of David to account⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “seek from the hand of the enemies of David”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 20:17
verses.text: And Jonathan again made David swear an oath, because he loved him; for with the love of his soul he loved him.  <div eID="gen2367" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 20:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1708"/><div sID="gen2368" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1708"/>Then Jonathan said to him, “Tomorrow <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the new moon, and you will be missed, for your seat will stay empty.

verses.name: I Samuel 20:19
verses.text: On the third day you must go down quickly and go to the place where you hid yourself <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞on the day all this started⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “on the day of the deed”</note> and remain beside the stone Ezel.

verses.name: I Samuel 20:20
verses.text: I will shoot three arrows <transChange type="added">to the</transChange> side as <transChange type="added">if</transChange> I were shooting at a target.

verses.name: I Samuel 20:21
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And look”</note> I will send word to my servant, ‘Go, find the arrows!’ If I clearly say to the boy, ‘Look, the arrows are <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞on this side of you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “from you and here”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞bring⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “take”</note> it,’ then<note placement="foot">Hebrew “and”</note> come, for it means peace for you. And there is no problem, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as Yahweh lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the life of Yahweh”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 20:22
verses.text: But if I say this to the young man, ‘Look, the arrows <transChange type="added">are</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞beyond you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,’<note placement="foot">Literally “from you and beyond”</note> go, for Yahweh has sent you away.

verses.name: I Samuel 20:23
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">as for</transChange> the matter about which you and I spoke, look, Yahweh <transChange type="added">is</transChange> between you and me forever.”  <div eID="gen2368" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 20:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1709"/><div sID="gen2369" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1709"/>So David hid himself in the field. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞When the new moon came⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “And it was the new moon”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the king was seated at the feast⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the king sat at the food to eat”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 20:25
verses.text: The king sat at his seat <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “as occurrence at occurrence”</note> the seat by the wall, and Jonathan got up, and Abner sat beside Saul, but David’s place was empty.

verses.name: I Samuel 20:26
verses.text: But Saul said nothing on that day, for he thought, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Something happened to him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “It is incident”</note> He <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not <transChange type="added">ceremonially</transChange> clean; surely he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not clean.”

verses.name: I Samuel 20:27
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it happened”</note> on the next day, the second day of the new moon, that David’s place was empty. So Saul asked Jonathan his son, “Why did the son of Jesse not come either yesterday or today to the feast?”

verses.name: I Samuel 20:28
verses.text: Jonathan answered Saul, “David earnestly asked permission from me <transChange type="added">to go</transChange> up to Bethlehem.

verses.name: I Samuel 20:29
verses.text: He said, ‘Send me away, please, for our clan sacrifice <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in the city, and my brother commanded<note placement="foot">Or “urged”</note> me <transChange type="added">to be present</transChange>. So then, if I have found favor in your eyes, please let me slip away and see my brothers.’ Therefore he has not come to the table of the king.”

verses.name: I Samuel 20:30
verses.text: Then <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Saul became angry⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the nose of Saul became hot”</note> at Jonathan and said to him, “You son of a perverse, rebellious woman!<note placement="foot">Or “bastard of a wayward woman” (HALOT 796)</note> Do I not know that you have chosen the son of Jesse to your shame and to the shame of your mother’s nakedness?

verses.name: I Samuel 20:31
verses.text: For <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as long as⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “all the days which”</note> the son of Jesse is alive on the earth, you and your kingdom will not be established! So then, send and bring him to me, for <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he will surely die⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!”<note placement="foot">Literally “he is a son of death”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 20:32
verses.text: But Jonathan answered his father Saul and said to him, “Why should he be put to death? What has he done?”

verses.name: I Samuel 20:33
verses.text: Then Saul hurled his<note placement="foot">Hebrew “the”</note> spear at him to kill him. So Jonathan knew <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞that his father had decided⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “it was complete from with his father”</note> to kill David.  <div eID="gen2369" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 20:34
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1710"/><div sID="gen2370" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1710"/>Jonathan got up from the table <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞enraged⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “with burning of nose”</note> and did not eat on the second day of the new moon because he was upset about David, because his father had disgraced him.

verses.name: I Samuel 20:35
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it happened”</note> in the morning Jonathan went out to the field for the appointment with David, and a young boy<note placement="foot">Or “young servant”</note> <transChange type="added">was</transChange> with him.

verses.name: I Samuel 20:36
verses.text: He said to his servant,<note placement="foot">Or “boy”</note> “Run, please find the arrows that I am shooting!” The boy<note placement="foot">Or “servant”</note> ran, and he shot the arrow to pass <transChange type="added">over</transChange> him.

verses.name: I Samuel 20:37
verses.text: When the boy came up to the place of the arrow that Jonathan had shot, Jonathan called out after the boy and said, “<transChange type="added">Is</transChange> not the arrow <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞beyond you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?”<note placement="foot">Literally “from you and beyond”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 20:38
verses.text: Then Jonathan called out after the boy, “Quick, hurry, do not linger!” And Jonathan’s servant collected the arrows and came to his master.

verses.name: I Samuel 20:39
verses.text: But the boy did not know anything <transChange type="added">about this</transChange>; only Jonathan and David knew the matter.

verses.name: I Samuel 20:40
verses.text: Jonathan gave his weapons to his servant and said to him, “Go, bring <transChange type="added">them</transChange> to the city.”

verses.name: I Samuel 20:41
verses.text: The boy left, and then David got up from the south side,<note placement="foot">So Masoretic Hebrew text; LXX reads “from the mound” (of stones)</note> and he fell on his face to the ground and bowed three times. And they kissed <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞each other⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “each his friend”</note> and wept <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞together⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “each with his friend”</note> but David <transChange type="added">wept</transChange> the most.

verses.name: I Samuel 20:42
verses.text: Jonathan said to David, “Go in peace, because we have sworn, the two of us, <transChange type="added">an oath</transChange> in the name of Yahweh, saying, “Yahweh will be between me and you, and between my offspring and your offspring forever.”<note placement="foot">In the Hebrew Bible, <reference osisRef="1Sam.1.21">1 Sam 21 </reference>begins here. <reference osisRef="1Sam.20.42b-1Sam.21.15">1 Samuel 20:42b–21:15 </reference>in the English Bible is 21:1–16 in the Hebrew Bible</note> Then he got up and left, and Jonathan went into the city.  <chapter eID="1Sam.20"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 21:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1711"/><title type="x-s">David Encounters the Priests of Nob</title> <div sID="gen2371" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1711"/>Now David came to Nob, to Ahimelech the priest. And Ahimelech came trembling to meet David, and he said to him, “Why are you alone and there are no men with you?”

verses.name: I Samuel 21:2
verses.text: So David said to Ahimelech the priest, “The king charged me <transChange type="added">with</transChange> a matter and said to me, ‘No one must know anything about this matter <transChange type="added">on</transChange> which I am sending you, <transChange type="added">with</transChange> which I have charged you and the servants.’ ” So <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I have arranged to meet with my servants at a certain place⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “I have made an appointment with my servants/young men to a place, a certain one”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 21:3
verses.text: Now then, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞what do you have at hand⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?<note placement="foot">Literally “what is there under your hand”</note> Give me five loaves of bread or <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞whatever is here⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “that which is found”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 21:4
verses.text: The priest answered David and said, “There is no ordinary bread <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞here at hand⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “under my hand”</note> there is only holy bread, <transChange type="added">but</transChange> only if the young men have kept themselves from women.”

verses.name: I Samuel 21:5
verses.text: David answered the priest and said to him, “Indeed, women <transChange type="added">were</transChange> held back from us <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as it has been when I’ve gone out before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “as yesterday three days ago my going out”</note> And the things<note placement="foot">Or possibly “equipment” or “weapons”</note> of the young men are holy when<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> it is an ordinary journey. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞How much more⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And even that”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞today⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the day”</note> will the things<note placement="foot">Or possibly “equipment” or “weapons”</note> be holy?”

verses.name: I Samuel 21:6
verses.text: So the priest gave him <transChange type="added">the</transChange> holy <transChange type="added">bread</transChange>, for there was no bread there except the bread of the Presence, which was removed from before Yahweh, in order to set hot bread <transChange type="added">there</transChange> on the day when it was taken away.  <div eID="gen2371" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 21:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1712"/><div sID="gen2372" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1712"/>Now there was a man from the servants of Saul on that day, detained before Yahweh, whose name <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Doeg the Edomite, the chief of Saul’s shepherds.

verses.name: I Samuel 21:8
verses.text: David asked Ahimelech, “Is there not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞at your disposal⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “under your hand”</note> a spear or a sword? For I took neither my sword nor my weapons with me because the king’s matter was urgent.”

verses.name: I Samuel 21:9
verses.text: So the priest said, “The sword of Goliath the Philistine whom you killed in the valley of Elah <transChange type="added">is</transChange> here, wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod. If you want to take it for yourself, <transChange type="added">then</transChange> take it, for there is no other except it here.” And David said, “There is none like it; give it to me.”  <div eID="gen2372" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 21:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1713"/><title type="x-s">David Flees to Achish in Gath</title> <div sID="gen2373" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1713"/>So David got up and fled on that day from the presence of Saul, and he came to Achish the king of Gath.

verses.name: I Samuel 21:11
verses.text: The servants of Achish said to him, “<transChange type="added">Is</transChange> not this David the king of the land? <transChange type="added">Is</transChange> it not for this <transChange type="added">one</transChange> that they sang in the dances, saying, ‘Saul killed his thousands, but David his ten thousands?’ ”

verses.name: I Samuel 21:12
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞David took these words seriously⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “David put these words in his heart”</note> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞felt severely threatened by⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “he was very afraid from the face of”</note> Achish the king of Gath.

verses.name: I Samuel 21:13
verses.text: So he changed his behavior <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in their eyes”</note> and pretended to be mad <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in their presence⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “in their hands”</note> He made scratches on the doors of the gate and let his saliva run down into his beard.

verses.name: I Samuel 21:14
verses.text: Then Achish said to his servants, “Look, you see a madman! Why did you bring him to me?

verses.name: I Samuel 21:15
verses.text: Do I lack madmen that you have brought this one to act like a madman before me? Should this one enter my household?”  <chapter eID="1Sam.21"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 22:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1714"/><title type="x-s">Saul Takes Revenge on the Priests Who Helped David</title> <div sID="gen2374" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1714"/>David went from there and escaped to the cave of Adullam. When his brothers and all his father’s household<note placement="foot">Or “family”</note> heard, they came down to him there.

verses.name: I Samuel 22:2
verses.text: Every man in distress and every man who had a creditor and every embittered man gathered to him, and he became <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞their commander⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “over them as commander”</note> Now there <transChange type="added">were</transChange> about four hundred men with him.

verses.name: I Samuel 22:3
verses.text: And David went up from there to Mizpah of Moab. He said to the king of Moab, “Please let my father and my mother <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞stay⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “come/go out”</note> with you until I know what God will do for me.”

verses.name: I Samuel 22:4
verses.text: So <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he brought them before the king of Moab⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “he led them into the presence of the king of Moab”</note> and they stayed with him all the days David was in the stronghold.  <div eID="gen2374" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 22:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1715"/><div sID="gen2375" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1715"/>Then Gad the prophet said to David, “You should not stay in the stronghold; leave and go into the land of Judah.” So David left and came <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the forest of Hereth.

verses.name: I Samuel 22:6
verses.text: Now Saul heard that David and the men who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him had been located. Saul <transChange type="added">was</transChange> sitting at Gibeah under the tamarisk <transChange type="added">tree</transChange> at Ramah. Now his spear <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in his hand and all his servants <transChange type="added">were</transChange> stationed around him.

verses.name: I Samuel 22:7
verses.text: Then Saul said to the servants who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> standing around him, “Please listen, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Benjaminites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!<note placement="foot">Literally “children of Benjamin”</note> Will the son of Jesse give you all fields and vineyards? Will he make all of you commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds?

verses.name: I Samuel 22:8
verses.text: For all of you have conspired against me, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞no one discloses to me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “there is no one revealing to my ear”</note> the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞making⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “cutting”</note> of an agreement between my son and the son of Jesse! None of you have had sympathy for me or <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞disclosed to me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “revealing to my ear”</note> that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞my son commissioned my servant against me to ambush me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “my son has raised my servant against me to an ambush”</note> as <transChange type="added">has been done</transChange> this day!”  <div eID="gen2375" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 22:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1716"/><div sID="gen2376" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1716"/>But Doeg the Edomite, who <transChange type="added">was</transChange> stationed among the servants of Saul, answered and said, “I saw the son of Jesse going to Nob, to Ahimelech the son of Ahitub.

verses.name: I Samuel 22:10
verses.text: And he inquired of Yahweh for him and gave him provisions and gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine.”

verses.name: I Samuel 22:11
verses.text: So the king sent to summon Ahimelech the son of Ahitub the priest, and all his father’s household, the priests who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> at Nob. So all of them came to the king.

verses.name: I Samuel 22:12
verses.text: Saul said, “Listen please, son of Ahitub.” He said, “Here I <transChange type="added">am</transChange>, my lord.”

verses.name: I Samuel 22:13
verses.text: Then Saul said to him, “Why did you conspire against me, you and the son of Jesse, when you gave to him bread and a sword, and by inquiring of God for him so that he might arise against me to ambush <transChange type="added">me</transChange> as <transChange type="added">has been done</transChange> this day?”

verses.name: I Samuel 22:14
verses.text: But Ahimelech answered the king and said, “And who among all your servants <transChange type="added">is</transChange> as faithful as David? He <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the son-in-law of the king who moves <transChange type="added">quickly</transChange> to safeguard you and is honored in your house.

verses.name: I Samuel 22:15
verses.text: <transChange type="added">Only</transChange> today I began to inquire of God for him. Far be it from me that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the king should impute anything against his servant⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the king will not put against his servant a matter”</note> or against my father’s household, for your servant has not known any of this matter, little or much.”

verses.name: I Samuel 22:16
verses.text: Then the king said, “You must certainly die, Ahimelech, you and all your father’s household!”

verses.name: I Samuel 22:17
verses.text: So the king said to the runners <transChange type="added">who were</transChange> stationed around him, “Turn and kill the priests of Yahweh, because <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they also support David⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “also their hand is with David”</note> and because they knew that he was fleeing and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞did not disclose it to me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “did not reveal it to his ear”; the Masoretic Hebrew text (<hi type="italic">Kethib</hi>) reads “his,” but the reading tradition (<hi type="italic">Qere)</hi> has “my”</note> But the servants of the king <transChange type="added">were</transChange> not willing to raise their hand to attack the priests of Yahweh.

verses.name: I Samuel 22:18
verses.text: Then the king said to Doeg, “You turn and attack the priests!” So Doeg the Edomite turned and attacked the priests himself, and on that day he killed eighty-five men who wore <transChange type="added">the</transChange> linen ephod.

verses.name: I Samuel 22:19
verses.text: And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he put to the sword⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “he killed with the mouth of the sword”</note> Nob, the city of the priests, from man to woman, from child to infant, and ox and donkey and sheep;<note placement="foot">Or “goats”; literally, “small livestock animals”</note> all <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to the sword⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “with the mouth of the sword”</note>  <div eID="gen2376" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 22:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1717"/><div sID="gen2377" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1717"/>But, one of the sons of Ahimelech the son of Ahitub, whose name was Abiathar, escaped and fled after David.

verses.name: I Samuel 22:21
verses.text: Abiathar told David that Saul had killed the priests of Yahweh.

verses.name: I Samuel 22:22
verses.text: Then David said to Abiathar, “I knew on that day that Doeg the Edomite was there, that he would certainly tell Saul. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I am responsible for the deaths of all your father’s household⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!<note placement="foot">Literally “I have turned against all the life of your father’s house”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 22:23
verses.text: Stay with me! Do not fear, because he who seeks my life seeks your life. You are in good care with me.”  <chapter eID="1Sam.22"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 23:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1718"/><title type="x-s">David Defeats the Philistines at Keilah</title> <div sID="gen2378" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1718"/>Now they told David, “Look, <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines <transChange type="added">are</transChange> fighting in Keilah and they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> raiding the threshing floors.”

verses.name: I Samuel 23:2
verses.text: So David inquired of Yahweh, saying, “Shall I go and attack these Philistines?” And Yahweh said to David, “Go and attack the Philistines and save<note placement="foot">Or “deliver” or “rescue”</note> Keilah.”

verses.name: I Samuel 23:3
verses.text: But David’s men said to him, “Look, we <transChange type="added">are</transChange> afraid here in Judah. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞How much more⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “also for”</note> <transChange type="added">if</transChange> we go <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Keilah to the battle lines of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines?”

verses.name: I Samuel 23:4
verses.text: So David again inquired of Yahweh, and Yahweh answered him and said, “Get up, go down <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Keilah, for I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> giving <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines into your hand.”

verses.name: I Samuel 23:5
verses.text: So David and his men went to Keilah and fought with <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines. They drove off their livestock and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞dealt them a heavy blow⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “he struck them with a great smiting”</note> So David saved<note placement="foot">Or “delivered” or “rescued”</note> the inhabitants of Keilah.  <div eID="gen2378" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 23:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1719"/><title type="x-s">David Flees from Saul at Keilah</title> <div sID="gen2379" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1719"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Now when Abiathar the son of Ahimelech fled⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it happened that at the fleeing of Abiathar son of Ahimelech”</note> to David <transChange type="added">at</transChange> Keilah, he went down <transChange type="added">with</transChange> an ephod in his hand.

verses.name: I Samuel 23:7
verses.text: When it was told to Saul that David had gone to Keilah, Saul said, “God <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞has given him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “has made him a stranger”</note> into my hand, because he has shut himself in by going into a city with <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞two barred gates⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “two gates and a bar”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 23:8
verses.text: Saul then summoned all of the army for the battle, to go down <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Keilah to lay a siege against David and his men.

verses.name: I Samuel 23:9
verses.text: When David learned that Saul <transChange type="added">was</transChange> plotting evil against him, he said to Abiathar the priest, “Bring the ephod here.”

verses.name: I Samuel 23:10
verses.text: And David said, “O Yahweh, God of Israel, your servant has clearly heard that Saul <transChange type="added">is</transChange> seeking to come to Keilah to destroy the city because of me.

verses.name: I Samuel 23:11
verses.text: Will the rulers of Keilah deliver me into his hand? Will Saul come down as your servant has heard? O Yahweh, God of Israel, please tell your servant!” And Yahweh said, “He will come down.”

verses.name: I Samuel 23:12
verses.text: Then David said, “Will the rulers of Keilah deliver me and my men into the hand of Saul?” And Yahweh said, “They will deliver <transChange type="added">you</transChange>.”

verses.name: I Samuel 23:13
verses.text: So David and his men got up, about six hundred men, and went out from Keilah and wandered wherever they could go. When it was told to Saul that David had escaped from Keilah, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he stopped his pursuit⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “he ceased to go out”</note>  <div eID="gen2379" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 23:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1720"/><title type="x-s">David Eludes Saul’s Pursuit</title> <div sID="gen2380" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1720"/>David remained in the wilderness, in the strongholds, and in the hill country in the wilderness of Ziph. And Saul sought him <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞continually⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “all the days”</note> but God did not give him into his hand.

verses.name: I Samuel 23:15
verses.text: When David realized that Saul had gone out to seek his life, David was in the wilderness of Ziph at Horesh.

verses.name: I Samuel 23:16
verses.text: So Jonathan the son of Saul got up and went to David <transChange type="added">at</transChange> Horesh, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞encouraged him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “he strengthened his hand”</note> through God.

verses.name: I Samuel 23:17
verses.text: He said to him, “Do not be afraid, for the hand of my father Saul will not find you. You will be king over Israel, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I will be second to you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “I shall be for you as second”</note> My father Saul knows <transChange type="added">this</transChange> also.”

verses.name: I Samuel 23:18
verses.text: Then the two of them <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞made⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “cut”</note> a covenant before Yahweh. David remained at Horesh, and Jonathan went to his house.  <div eID="gen2380" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 23:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1721"/><div sID="gen2381" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1721"/>Then <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Ziphites went up to Saul at Gibeah, saying, “<transChange type="added">Is</transChange> not David hiding among us in the strongholds at Horesh on the hill of Hakilah, which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> south of Jeshimon?

verses.name: I Samuel 23:20
verses.text: So then, O king, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞whenever you want⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for all the wanting of your soul”</note> to come down, come down, and <transChange type="added">it will be</transChange> for us to deliver him into the hand of the king.”

verses.name: I Samuel 23:21
verses.text: And Saul said to them, “May you be blessed by Yahweh, for you have shown me compassion!

verses.name: I Samuel 23:22
verses.text: Go, please, make certain again! Find out and see <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞exactly where he is⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “his place where his foot is”</note> and who has seen him there! For they have said to me, ‘He <transChange type="added">is</transChange> very cunning.’

verses.name: I Samuel 23:23
verses.text: Look, find out all of the hiding places where he hides. Then return to me <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞with dependable information⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to being established”</note> and I will go with you. And then if he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> there in the land, then I will seek him among all the thousands of Judah.”

verses.name: I Samuel 23:24
verses.text: Then they got up and went to Ziph before Saul. <div eID="gen2381" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2382" type="x-p"/> Now David and his men <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in the wilderness of Maon in the Arabah, to the south of Jeshimon.

verses.name: I Samuel 23:25
verses.text: And Saul and his men went to seek <transChange type="added">him</transChange>, and they told David, so he went down <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the rock and stayed in the wilderness of Maon. When Saul heard <transChange type="added">this</transChange>, he pursued David <transChange type="added">into</transChange> the wilderness of Maon.

verses.name: I Samuel 23:26
verses.text: Saul went <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞on one side of the mountain⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “from the side of the mountain from this”</note> and David and his men <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞went on the other side of the mountain⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “from the side of the mountain from this”</note> David was hurrying to get away from Saul, while Saul and his men <transChange type="added">were</transChange> closing in on David and his men to capture them.

verses.name: I Samuel 23:27
verses.text: But a messenger came to Saul, saying, “Hurry and come, because <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines have made a raid on the land!”

verses.name: I Samuel 23:28
verses.text: So Saul returned from pursuing David, and he went to confront<note placement="foot">Hebrew “to meet”</note> the Philistines. Therefore, they called that place the Rock of Division.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Sela’ Hammahlekot”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 23:29
verses.text: <note placement="foot"><reference osisRef="1Sam.23.29-1Sam.24.22">1 Sam 23:29–24:22 </reference>in the English Bible is 24:1–23 in the Hebrew Bible</note> David went up from there and stayed in the strongholds of En Gedi.  <chapter eID="1Sam.23"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 24:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1722"/><title type="x-s">David Spares Saul in the Cave at En Gedi</title> <div sID="gen2383" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1722"/>When Saul returned from <transChange type="added">pursuing the</transChange> Philistines, they told him, “Look, David <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in the wilderness of En Gedi.”

verses.name: I Samuel 24:2
verses.text: So Saul took three thousand chosen men from all Israel, and he and his men went to search <transChange type="added">for</transChange> David <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in the direction of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “on the face of”</note> the Rocks of the Mountain Goats.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “of the Jael”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 24:3
verses.text: He came to the sheep pens beside the road, and a cave <transChange type="added">was</transChange> there. Then Saul went in <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to relieve himself⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “to cover his feet”</note> Now David and his men <transChange type="added">were</transChange> sitting in the innermost part of the cave.

verses.name: I Samuel 24:4
verses.text: And David’s men said to him, “Look, today <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the day about which Yahweh said to you, ‘See, I am giving your enemy<note placement="foot">The Masoretic Hebrew text (<hi type="italic">Kethib</hi>) reads “enemies,” but the reading tradition (<hi type="italic">Qere)</hi> has the singular “enemy”</note> into your hand, and you can do to him <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞whatever seems good to you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.’ ”<note placement="foot">Literally “as that which is good in your eyes”</note> So David got up and secretly cut the hem of Saul’s robe.

verses.name: I Samuel 24:5
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it happened”</note> afterward David <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞felt guilty⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the heart of David struck him”</note> because he had cut <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the hem of Saul’s robe⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the hem which was for Saul”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 24:6
verses.text: He said to his men, “Far be it from me in<note placement="foot">Hebrew “from”</note> Yahweh, that I do this thing to my lord, to Yahweh’s anointed one, by stretching out my hand against him! For he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the anointed one of Yahweh.”

verses.name: I Samuel 24:7
verses.text: So David rebuked his men with the words and did not allow them to rise against Saul. And Saul got up from the cave, and he went on his<note placement="foot">Hebrew “the”</note> way.  <div eID="gen2383" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 24:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1723"/><div sID="gen2384" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1723"/>Then David got up afterward and went out of the cave and called after Saul, “My lord the king!” When Saul looked after him, David knelt down <transChange type="added">with his</transChange> face to the ground and bowed down.

verses.name: I Samuel 24:9
verses.text: Then David said to Saul, “Why do you listen to the words of people who say: ‘Look, David <transChange type="added">is</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞seeking to do you harm⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>’?<note placement="foot">Literally “seeking your evil”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 24:10
verses.text: Look, this day your eyes have seen that Yahweh gave you today into my hand in the cave, and some said to kill you. But <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I took pity⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “she took pity,” with “she” = “my eye,” a common Hebrew expression</note> on you and said, ‘I will not stretch out my hand against my lord, because he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> Yahweh’s anointed one.’

verses.name: I Samuel 24:11
verses.text: Now, my father, see, yes, see, the hem of your robe in my hand! For <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞when I cut⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “at my cutting”</note> the hem of your robe I did not kill you. Know and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞realize⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “see”</note> that there is no evil or rebellion in my hand. I did not sin against you, but you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> hunting down my life to take it.

verses.name: I Samuel 24:12
verses.text: May Yahweh judge between me and you, and may Yahweh avenge me on you, but my hand will not be against you!

verses.name: I Samuel 24:13
verses.text: Just as the ancient proverb says, ‘From the wicked, wickedness goes out,’ but my hand will not be against you!

verses.name: I Samuel 24:14
verses.text: After whom did the king of Israel go out? After whom are you pursuing? After a dead dog? After one flea?

verses.name: I Samuel 24:15
verses.text: May Yahweh be <transChange type="added">the</transChange> judge, and let him judge between me and you, and may he see and plead my case. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞May he vindicate me against you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!”<note placement="foot">Literally “May he judge me from your hand”</note>  <div eID="gen2384" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 24:16
