verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1724"/><div sID="gen2385" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1724"/>When David finished speaking these words to Saul, Saul said, “<transChange type="added">Is</transChange> this your voice, my son David?” And Saul lifted up his voice and wept.

verses.name: I Samuel 24:17
verses.text: Then he said to David, “You are more righteous than I, for you have repaid me the good, but I have repaid you the evil.

verses.name: I Samuel 24:18
verses.text: You have explained to me today that you have dealt well with me, how<note placement="foot">Hebrew “that”</note> Yahweh delivered me into your hand but you did not kill me.

verses.name: I Samuel 24:19
verses.text: For a man has found his enemy but sent him on <transChange type="added">his</transChange> way safely. Now may Yahweh reward you with good in return for this day, for what you have done for me.

verses.name: I Samuel 24:20
verses.text: So now then, look, I know that you will certainly be king and the kingdom of Israel will be established in your hand.

verses.name: I Samuel 24:21
verses.text: So then, swear to me by Yahweh that you will not cut off my <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞descendants⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “seed”</note> after me and that you will not wipe out my name from my father’s house.”

verses.name: I Samuel 24:22
verses.text: So David swore <transChange type="added">this on oath</transChange> to Saul, and Saul went to his house, but David and his men went up to the stronghold.  <chapter eID="1Sam.24"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 25:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1725"/><title type="x-s">Samuel’s Death</title> <div sID="gen2386" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1725"/>Now Samuel died, and all Israel assembled and mourned for him. They buried him at his house at Ramah. Then David got up and went down to the wilderness of Paran.  <div eID="gen2386" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 25:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1726"/><title type="x-s">David and Abigail</title> <div sID="gen2387" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1726"/>Now there was a man in Maon, whose business <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in Carmel. The man was very rich and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞owned⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “there were for him”</note> three thousand sheep and a thousand goats. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Now⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it happened”</note> the shearing of his sheep <transChange type="added">was taking place</transChange> in Carmel.

verses.name: I Samuel 25:3
verses.text: The name of the man <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Nabal,<note placement="foot">The name “Nabal” means “foolish”</note> and the name of his wife was Abigail.<note placement="foot">The name “Abigail” means “my father delights”</note> Now the woman was wise and beautiful, but the man was stubborn and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞mean⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “bad of deeds”</note> and he was as his heart.<note placement="foot">The Masoretic Hebrew text (<hi type="italic">Kethib</hi>) reads “as his heart,” whereas the reading tradition (<hi type="italic">Qere)</hi> reads “Calebite”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 25:4
verses.text: David heard in the wilderness that Nabal <transChange type="added">was</transChange> shearing his sheep.

verses.name: I Samuel 25:5
verses.text: So David sent ten young men, and David said to the young men, “Go up to Carmel and go to Nabal; <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you will greet him in my name⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “you will ask for him in my name as far as peace”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 25:6
verses.text: Then you must say to him, ‘<transChange type="added">Long</transChange> life <transChange type="added">to you</transChange>, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞may it go well with you, with your house, and with all that is yours⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “you are peace and your house is peace and all that is yours is peace”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 25:7
verses.text: Now I have heard that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you have shearers⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “shearing is for you”</note> Now while your shepherds <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with us, we did not mistreat them, and nothing of theirs <transChange type="added">was</transChange> missing, all the days they were in Carmel.

verses.name: I Samuel 25:8
verses.text: Ask your servants<note placement="foot">Or “young men”</note> and they will tell you! Let the young men<note placement="foot">Or “the servants”; “young men” is used here to connect with v. 5</note> find favor in your eyes because we have come on a feast day. Please give <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞whatever you have on hand⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “what your hand finds”</note> for your servants and for your son David.”  <div eID="gen2387" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 25:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1727"/><div sID="gen2388" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1727"/>So David’s young men came and they spoke all these words to Nabal in the name of David. Then they waited.

verses.name: I Samuel 25:10
verses.text: But Nabal answered David’s servants and said, “Who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> David? And who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the son of Jesse? Today, <transChange type="added">there</transChange> are many servants breaking away from the presence of their masters.

verses.name: I Samuel 25:11
verses.text: Should I take my bread and my water and my meat which I have slaughtered for my shearers and give <transChange type="added">it</transChange> to men whom I do not know where they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> from?

verses.name: I Samuel 25:12
verses.text: So David’s young men turned on their way and returned and came and told him according to all these words.

verses.name: I Samuel 25:13
verses.text: Then David said to his men, “Each man strap on his sword!” So each one strapped on his sword, and David also strapped on his sword. About four hundred men went up after David, while two hundred remained with the baggage.  <div eID="gen2388" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 25:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1728"/><div sID="gen2389" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1728"/>But a young man of the servants told Abigail, Nabal’s wife, saying, “Look, David sent messengers from the desert to greet<note placement="foot">Hebrew “bless”</note> our master, but he addressed them angrily,

verses.name: I Samuel 25:15
verses.text: even though the men <transChange type="added">were</transChange> very good to us; we were not mistreated and did not miss anything all the days we went about with them <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞while we were⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “at our being”</note> in the field.

verses.name: I Samuel 25:16
verses.text: They were a wall to us both night and day, all <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the days we were⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the days of our being”</note> with them keeping the sheep.

verses.name: I Samuel 25:17
verses.text: And so then, know and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞consider⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “see”</note> what you should do, for evil has been decided against our master and against all his household, and he is such <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a wicked man⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “a son of uselessness”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞nobody can reason with him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!”<note placement="foot">Literally “from speaking to him”</note>  <div eID="gen2389" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 25:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1729"/><div sID="gen2390" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1729"/>Then Abigail <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞quickly took⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “hastened and took”</note> two hundred loaves of bread, two skins of wine, five prepared sheep, five seahs of roasted grain, a hundred raisin cakes, and two hundred fig cakes, and she put <transChange type="added">them</transChange> on the donkeys.

verses.name: I Samuel 25:19
verses.text: Then she said to her servants, “Go ahead before me; look, I am coming after you,” but she did not tell her husband Nabal.

verses.name: I Samuel 25:20
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “And it happened”</note> <transChange type="added">as</transChange> she <transChange type="added">was</transChange> riding on the donkey and <transChange type="added">was</transChange> going down the ravine of the mountain, David and his men <transChange type="added">were</transChange> coming down to meet her, and she met them.

verses.name: I Samuel 25:21
verses.text: Now David had said, “Surely <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in vain⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for the vanity”</note> I guarded all that this fellow had in the desert. And nothing was missed of all that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> his, but he returned evil against me in place of good!

verses.name: I Samuel 25:22
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞May God severely punish the enemies of David⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “May God do so to the enemies of David”; following the LXX some English versions omit the words “the enemies of”</note> and again do thus if I leave behind <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞anything that is his⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from all that is for him”</note> until the morning, not even <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞one male⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!”<note placement="foot">Literally “from one urinating against a wall”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 25:23
verses.text: When Abigail saw David, she hurried and got down from the donkey and fell on her face before <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞David’s anger⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the nostrils of David”</note> and she bowed down to the ground.

verses.name: I Samuel 25:24
verses.text: She fell at his feet and said, “On me, my lord, <transChange type="added">be</transChange> the guilt! Please let your female servant speak <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to you personally⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!<note placement="foot">Literally “in your ears”</note> Hear the words of your female servant!

verses.name: I Samuel 25:25
verses.text: Please do not let my lord set his heart against <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞this worthless man⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “this man of wickedness”</note> Nabal; for as his name, so is he. Nabal is his name, and stupidity is with him! But I, your female servant, did not see the young men<note placement="foot">Or “the servants”</note> of my lord whom you sent.

verses.name: I Samuel 25:26
verses.text: So then, my lord, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as Yahweh lives and as your soul lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the life of Yahweh and the life of your soul”</note> since Yahweh restrained you from bloodguilt <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞by taking matters into your own hand⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “saving your hand for you”</note> so then, may your enemies be like Nabal, even <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞those who seek to do my lord harm⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the seeking to my lord evil”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 25:27
verses.text: So then, this gift which your female servant has brought to my lord, may it be given to the young men <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who follow my lord⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the ones going about at the feet of my lord”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 25:28
verses.text: Please forgive the transgression of your female servant, because Yahweh will certainly make a lasting house<note placement="foot">That is, a lasting dynasty</note> for my lord, because my lord is fighting the battles of Yahweh, and evil will not be found in you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as long as you live⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “from your days”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 25:29
verses.text: Should a man arise to pursue you and to seek your life, may the life of my lord be wrapped in the pouch<note placement="foot">Or “bag”</note> of the living with Yahweh your God. But as for the life of your enemy, he will sling it from within<note placement="foot">Hebrew “in the midst of”</note> the pocket of the sling!

verses.name: I Samuel 25:30
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it will happen”</note> when Yahweh has done for my lord according to all the good that he has spoken concerning you, and has appointed you as leader over Israel,

verses.name: I Samuel 25:31
verses.text: then this will not be an obstacle for you or a stumbling block of conscience for my lord <transChange type="added">either</transChange> by the shedding of blood without cause or by <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞my lord taking matters into his own hands⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the saving of my lord for himself”</note> And when Yahweh does good to my lord, then remember your female servant.”  <div eID="gen2390" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 25:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1730"/><div sID="gen2391" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1730"/>Then David said to Abigail, “Blessed be Yahweh the God of Israel who has sent you this day to meet me!

verses.name: I Samuel 25:33
verses.text: And blessed be your discretion, and blessed be you who have prevented me this day from bloodguilt and <transChange type="added">from</transChange> delivering myself by my own hand.

verses.name: I Samuel 25:34
verses.text: But <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as Yahweh lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the life of Yahweh”</note> the God of Israel who has prevented me from harming you, if you had not hurried and come to meet me, surely there would not have been <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞one male⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “one urinating against a wall”</note> left alive for Nabal by the light of morning!”

verses.name: I Samuel 25:35
verses.text: Then David took from her hand what she had brought for him, and he said to her, “Go up to your house in peace. See, I have listened to your voice, and I have <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞granted your request⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “lifted up your face”</note>  <div eID="gen2391" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 25:36
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1731"/><div sID="gen2392" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1731"/>Then Abigail went to Nabal, and look, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he was holding a feast⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a feast was for him”</note> in his house like the feast of the king. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Nabal was enjoying himself⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the heart of Nabal was good on him”</note> and he was very drunk, so she did not tell him a thing, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞nothing at all⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “small or large”</note> until the light of morning.

verses.name: I Samuel 25:37
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it happened”</note> in the morning when the wine had gone out of Nabal, his wife told him these words. Then his heart died <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞within him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “in his midst”</note> and he became like a stone.

verses.name: I Samuel 25:38
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “And it happened”</note> about ten days later, Yahweh struck Nabal and he died.  <div eID="gen2392" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 25:39
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1732"/><div sID="gen2393" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1732"/>When David heard that Nabal had died, he said, “Blessed be Yahweh who has vindicated the case of my reproach from the hand of Nabal, and he has kept back his servant from evil; but Yahweh has returned the evil of Nabal on his <transChange type="added">own</transChange> head.” Then David sent and spoke with Abigail to take her for his wife.

verses.name: I Samuel 25:40
verses.text: So the servants of David came to Abigail at Carmel, and they spoke to her, saying, “David has sent us to you to take you for his wife.”

verses.name: I Samuel 25:41
verses.text: She got up and bowed down <transChange type="added">with</transChange> her face to the ground and said, “Here is your female servant, as a slave to wash the feet of my lord’s servants.”

verses.name: I Samuel 25:42
verses.text: Then Abigail <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞quickly got up⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “hastened and got up”</note> and rode on the donkey, along with five of her maidservants who <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞attended her⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the ones going about at her feet”</note> and she went after the messengers of David and became his wife.  <div eID="gen2393" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 25:43
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1733"/><div sID="gen2394" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1733"/>David had also taken Ahinoam from Jezreel, and both of them became his wives.

verses.name: I Samuel 25:44
verses.text: (Now Saul had given his daughter Michal, David’s wife, to Palti the son of Laish, who <transChange type="added">was</transChange> from Gallim.)  <chapter eID="1Sam.25"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 26:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1734"/><title type="x-s">David Again Spares Saul</title> <div sID="gen2395" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1734"/>The Ziphites came to Saul at Gibeah, saying, “<transChange type="added">Is</transChange> not David hiding on the hill of Hakilah opposite Jeshimon?”

verses.name: I Samuel 26:2
verses.text: Then Saul got up and went down to the wilderness of Ziph, and three thousand chosen men of Israel with him, to seek David in the wilderness of Ziph.  <div eID="gen2395" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 26:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1735"/><div sID="gen2396" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1735"/>Now Saul was on the hill of Hakilah, which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> opposite Jeshimon by the road, but David was staying in the wilderness. When he realized that Saul had come to the wilderness after him,

verses.name: I Samuel 26:4
verses.text: David sent spies, and he learned that Saul had come <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞for certain⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “to be established”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 26:5
verses.text: Then David got up and came to the place where Saul had encamped, and David saw the place where Saul <transChange type="added">was</transChange> lying down, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as well as⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and”</note> Abner the son of Ner, the commander of his army. (Now Saul <transChange type="added">was</transChange> lying in the encampment, and the army <transChange type="added">was</transChange> encamping around him.)  <div eID="gen2396" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 26:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1736"/><div sID="gen2397" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1736"/>David answered and said to Ahimelech the Hittite and to Abishai the son of Zeruiah the brother of Joab, saying, “Who will go down with me to Saul, in the camp?” And Abishai said, “I will go down with you.”

verses.name: I Samuel 26:7
verses.text: So David and Abishai came to the army <transChange type="added">by</transChange> night, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞there was⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “look” or “behold”</note> Saul lying asleep in the encampment with<note placement="foot">Hebrew “and”</note> his spear thrust into the ground near his head, and Abner and the army <transChange type="added">were</transChange> lying all around him.

verses.name: I Samuel 26:8
verses.text: Then Abishai said to David, “God has handed over your enemy into your hand today! So then, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞please let me pin him to the ground with the spear⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “let me strike him please with the spear and in the ground”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞one time⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “one occurrence”</note> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I will not strike him twice⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “I will not repeat for him”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 26:9
verses.text: But David said to Abishai, “Do not destroy<note placement="foot">Or “kill”</note> him! For who has stretched out his hand against Yahweh’s anointed one and remained blameless?”

verses.name: I Samuel 26:10
verses.text: And David said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞As Yahweh lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “The life of Yahweh”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞certainly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “if surely”</note> Yahweh will strike him, or his day will come and he will die, or he will go down in the battle and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞perish⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “will be carried away”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 26:11
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Yahweh forbid me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Far be it from me from Yahweh”</note> from stretching out my hand against Yahweh’s anointed one! So then, please take the spear that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> near his head and the jar of water, and let us go.”

verses.name: I Samuel 26:12
verses.text: So David took the spear and the jar of water from <transChange type="added">near</transChange> Saul’s head, and they went <transChange type="added">away</transChange>. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞No one saw, no one knew, and no one awakened⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “there was not anyone seeing and there was not anyone knowing and there was not anyone awakening”</note> for all of them <transChange type="added">were</transChange> sleeping because a deep sleep of Yahweh had fallen upon them.  <div eID="gen2397" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 26:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1737"/><div sID="gen2398" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1737"/>Then David went to the other side and stood on the top of the hill at a distance; the distance <transChange type="added">was</transChange> great between them.

verses.name: I Samuel 26:14
verses.text: David called out to the army and to Abner the son of Ner, “Will you not answer, Abner?” And Abner answered and said, “Who <transChange type="added">are</transChange> you <transChange type="added">that</transChange> you call to the king?”

verses.name: I Samuel 26:15
verses.text: So David said to Abner, “<transChange type="added">Are</transChange> you not a man? And who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> like you in Israel? Why did you not keep watch over your lord the king? For one of the people came to destroy<note placement="foot">Or “to kill”</note> your lord the king.

verses.name: I Samuel 26:16
verses.text: This thing that you have done <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not good. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞As Yahweh lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the life of Yahweh”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞surely you people deserve to die⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “you are sons of death”</note> since you have not kept watch over your lord, over Yahweh’s anointed one! So then, see where the king’s spear <transChange type="added">is</transChange> and the jar of water that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> near his head!”

verses.name: I Samuel 26:17
verses.text: Then Saul recognized David’s voice and said, “<transChange type="added">Is</transChange> this your voice, my son David?” And David said, “<transChange type="added">It is</transChange> my voice, my lord the king.”

verses.name: I Samuel 26:18
verses.text: Then he said, “Why <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my lord pursuing after his servant? For what have I done? And what evil <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in my hand?

verses.name: I Samuel 26:19
verses.text: And so then, please let my lord the king listen to the words of his servant: If Yahweh has incited you against me, may he delight in an offering; but if <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞it is mortals⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “it is the sons of humankind”</note> may they be accursed <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the face of”</note> Yahweh, for they have driven me away today from sharing in the inheritance of Yahweh, saying, ‘Go, serve other gods!’

verses.name: I Samuel 26:20
verses.text: And so then, do not let my blood fall to the ground <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞away from⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from before”</note> the presence of Yahweh, for the king of Israel has gone out to seek a single flea, as one hunts a partridge in the mountains.”  <div eID="gen2398" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 26:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1738"/><div sID="gen2399" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1738"/>Then Saul said, “I have sinned! Come back, David my son, for I will not harm you again, because my life <transChange type="added">was</transChange> precious in your eyes this day. Look, I have acted like a fool and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞have made a terrible mistake⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “have gone greatly astray”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 26:22
verses.text: David answered and said, “Here is the king’s spear; let one of the young men<note placement="foot">Or “servants”</note> come over and take it.

verses.name: I Samuel 26:23
verses.text: Yahweh repays to each <transChange type="added">one</transChange> his righteousness and his faithfulness, for Yahweh gave you into my hand today, but I was not willing to stretch out my hand against Yahweh’s anointed.

verses.name: I Samuel 26:24
verses.text: Look, as your life was precious in my eyes this day, may my life be great in the eyes of Yahweh, and may he rescue me from all trouble.”

verses.name: I Samuel 26:25
verses.text: Then Saul said to David, “Blessed are you, my son David; <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you will not only do many things, but also will always succeed⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!”<note placement="foot">Literally “you will do many things and also always you will prevail”</note> Then David went on his way and Saul returned to his place.  <chapter eID="1Sam.26"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 27:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1739"/><title type="x-s">David Returns to Achish</title> <div sID="gen2400" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1739"/>Then David <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞thought to himself⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “said to his heart”</note> “Now I will perish one day by the hand of Saul! There is nothing better for me but <transChange type="added">that</transChange> I must certainly escape to the land of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines. Then Saul will desist from searching for me further in all of the territories of Israel, and so I will escape from his hand.”

verses.name: I Samuel 27:2
verses.text: So David got up and crossed over, he and the six hundred men who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him, to Achish the son of Maoch, the king of Gath.

verses.name: I Samuel 27:3
verses.text: David settled with Achish in Gath, he and his men, each with his household.<note placement="foot">Or “family”</note> David took along his two wives Ahinoam <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from Jezreel⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the Jezreelitess”</note> and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.

verses.name: I Samuel 27:4
verses.text: And it was reported to Saul that David had fled <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Gath, so <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he no longer searched for him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “he does <hi type="italic">Qere</hi> did not again to seek him longer”</note>  <div eID="gen2400" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 27:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1740"/><div sID="gen2401" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1740"/>Then David said to Achish, “Please, if I have found favor in your eyes, then let them give me a place in one of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞country towns⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “towns of the open field”</note> that I can live there. Why should your servant live in <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the royal city⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the city of the king”</note> with you?”

verses.name: I Samuel 27:6
verses.text: So Achish gave him Ziklag on that day. (Therefore, Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah until this day.)

verses.name: I Samuel 27:7
verses.text: The number of days that David lived in the countryside of the Philistines <transChange type="added">was</transChange> one year and four months.  <div eID="gen2401" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 27:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1741"/><div sID="gen2402" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1741"/>Now David and his men went up and raided the Geshurites and the Girzites and the Amalekites, for they had been living <transChange type="added">in</transChange> the land for a long time <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in the direction of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “as you come”</note> Shur and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as far as⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “up to”</note> the land of Egypt.

verses.name: I Samuel 27:9
verses.text: So David struck the land and did not leave a man or a woman alive; he took the sheep,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “flock,” referring to either sheep or goats or both</note> the cattle, the donkeys, the camels, and the clothing. Then he returned and came to Achish.

verses.name: I Samuel 27:10
verses.text: And Achish said, “Against whom have you raided today?” David said, “Against the Negev of Judah and against the Negev of the Jerahmeelites and against the Negev of the Kenites.”

verses.name: I Samuel 27:11
verses.text: And David did not leave alive a man or a woman to bring <transChange type="added">them back</transChange> to Gath, thinking,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “saying”</note> “So that they will not report about us, saying, ‘David did thus and so.’ ” Thus was his practice all the days that he lived in the countryside of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines.

verses.name: I Samuel 27:12
verses.text: And Achish trusted David, saying, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞He has made himself utterly hated⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Stinking he stink” = “he really stinks”</note> among his people in Israel, and he will be my servant forever.”  <chapter eID="1Sam.27"/> <div eID="gen2402" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 28:1
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Now⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it happened”</note> in those days <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines gathered their forces for war to fight against Israel. So Achish said to David, “Certainly you realize that you must go out with me in the army, you and your men.”

verses.name: I Samuel 28:2
verses.text: David said to Achish, “Very well, you will know what your servant can do.” Achish said to David, “Very well, I will make you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞my bodyguard⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the keeper of my head”</note> for life.”  <div eID="gen2403" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 28:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1742"/><title type="x-s">Saul Inquires of the Medium at Endor</title> <div sID="gen2404" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1742"/>(Now Samuel had died, and all Israel had mourned for him, and they had buried him in Ramah, his <transChange type="added">own</transChange> city. And Saul had expelled the mediums<note placement="foot">Or “necromancers”</note> and the soothsayers from the land.)

verses.name: I Samuel 28:4
verses.text: Then <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines assembled and came and encamped at Shunem, so Saul assembled all Israel, and they encamped at Gilboa.

verses.name: I Samuel 28:5
verses.text: When Saul saw the army of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines, he was afraid and his heart trembled greatly.

verses.name: I Samuel 28:6
verses.text: And Saul inquired of Yahweh, but Yahweh did not answer him, not by dreams or by the Urim<note placement="foot">A device for revealing God’s decisions; see Exod 28:30; Num 27:21; Neh 7:65; Prov 16:33</note> or by the prophets.

verses.name: I Samuel 28:7
verses.text: So Saul said to his servants, “Search for me <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a woman who is a medium⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a woman of an owner of a spirit of the dead” (= “a woman who owns a ritual pit for summoning spirits of the dead”)</note> so that I may go to her and inquire of her.” His servants said to him, “Look <transChange type="added">there is</transChange> a woman who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a medium in Endor.”

verses.name: I Samuel 28:8
verses.text: So Saul disguised himself and put on other clothes, and he went <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞with two of his men⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “and two of his men with him”</note> And they came to the woman by night and he said, “Please consult a spirit for me through <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the ritual pit⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the spirit of the dead”</note> and bring up for me <transChange type="added">the one</transChange> whom I tell you.”

verses.name: I Samuel 28:9
verses.text: But the woman said to him, “Look, you know what Saul did, how he exterminated the mediums<note placement="foot">Or “necromancers”</note> and the soothsayers from the land! Why <transChange type="added">are</transChange> you setting a trap for my life to kill me?”

verses.name: I Samuel 28:10
verses.text: Then Saul swore to her by Yahweh, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞As Yahweh lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “The life of Yahweh”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you will not be punished⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “guilt will not meet you”</note> for this thing.”

verses.name: I Samuel 28:11
verses.text: So the woman asked, “Whom shall I bring up for you?” He said, “Bring up Samuel for me.”

verses.name: I Samuel 28:12
verses.text: When the woman saw Samuel, she cried out with a loud voice, and the woman said to Saul, “Why did you deceive me? You <transChange type="added">are</transChange> Saul!”

verses.name: I Samuel 28:13
verses.text: The king said to her, “Do not be afraid! What do you see?” And the woman said to Saul, “I see a god<note placement="foot">Or “a divine being”</note> coming up from the ground!”

verses.name: I Samuel 28:14
verses.text: Then he said to her, “What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> his appearance?” She said, “An old man <transChange type="added">is</transChange> coming up, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he is wrapped in a robe⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “he is wrapping himself with a robe”</note> Then Saul realized that it was Samuel, and he knelt <transChange type="added">with</transChange> his face to the ground and bowed down.  <div eID="gen2404" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 28:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1743"/><div sID="gen2405" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1743"/>Then Samuel said to Saul, “Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?” And Saul said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I am in distress⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!<note placement="foot">Literally “Great distress is for me”</note> For the Philistines are about to make war against me, but God has turned away from me, and he does not answer me any more, not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞by the prophets⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by the hand of the prophets”</note> or by the dreams. So I called to you to let me know what I should do.”

verses.name: I Samuel 28:16
verses.text: Then Samuel said, “Why do you ask me, since Yahweh has turned away from you and has become your enemy?

verses.name: I Samuel 28:17
verses.text: Yahweh has done to you just as he spoke by my hand! Yahweh has torn the kingdom from your hand and has given it to your neighbor, to David.

verses.name: I Samuel 28:18
verses.text: Because you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞did not obey⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “did not listen to”</note> Yahweh and did not carry out the fierce anger of his <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞wrath⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “face”</note> against Amalek, therefore Yahweh has done this thing to you today.

verses.name: I Samuel 28:19
verses.text: And Yahweh will also give Israel with you into the hands of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines, and tomorrow you and your sons <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> with me, and Yahweh will also give the army of Israel into <transChange type="added">the</transChange> hand of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines.”

verses.name: I Samuel 28:20
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Then Saul immediately fell prostrate⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Saul did at once and fell with the fullness of his height”</note> to the ground, and he was very afraid because of the words of Samuel; there was no more strength in him, for he had not eaten food all day and all night.

verses.name: I Samuel 28:21
verses.text: Then the woman came to Saul and realized that he was absolutely<note placement="foot">Hebrew “very”</note> terrified, so she said to him, “Look, your female servant <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞has obeyed you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “has listened to your voice”</note> and I have <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞risked my life⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “I have put my life in my palm”</note> I have listened to your words that you have spoken to me.

verses.name: I Samuel 28:22
verses.text: So then, you also please listen to the voice of your female servant, and let me set before you a morsel of bread, and <transChange type="added">you</transChange> eat so that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you will have strength⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “it will be your strength”</note> in you when you go on your<note placement="foot">Hebrew “the”</note> way.”

verses.name: I Samuel 28:23
verses.text: But he refused and said, “I will not eat!” However, his servants urged him, and the woman also. So he listened <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to what they said⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “their voice”</note> and he got up from the ground and sat on the bed.

verses.name: I Samuel 28:24
verses.text: Now the woman had a fattened bull calf in the house, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞so she quickly slaughtered it⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and she did quickly and she slaughtered it”</note> and took flour, kneaded <transChange type="added">dough</transChange>, and baked him <transChange type="added">some</transChange> unleavened bread.

verses.name: I Samuel 28:25
verses.text: She brought it before Saul and his servants, and they ate. Then they got up and went away that <transChange type="added">very</transChange> night.  <chapter eID="1Sam.28"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 29:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1744"/><title type="x-s">David Leaves the Service of Achish</title> <div sID="gen2406" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1744"/>Now <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines assembled all their forces at Aphek, and Israel <transChange type="added">was</transChange> encamped at the spring that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in Jezreel.

verses.name: I Samuel 29:2
verses.text: The rulers of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines <transChange type="added">were</transChange> passing on according to hundreds and thousands, David and his men passing on at the rear with Achish.

verses.name: I Samuel 29:3
verses.text: Then the commanders of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines said, “What <transChange type="added">are</transChange> these Hebrews <transChange type="added">doing here</transChange>?” And Achish said to the commanders of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines, “Is this not David, the servant of Saul, the king of Israel, who has been with me <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞for days and years⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?<note placement="foot">Literally “these days or these years”</note> I have not found anything <transChange type="added">threatening</transChange> in him from the day of his desertion until this day!”

verses.name: I Samuel 29:4
verses.text: But the commanders of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines were angry with him and they said to him, “Send the man back so that he might return to his place where you have assigned him! But he will not go down with us into the battle, so that he does not become an adversary to us in the battle. By what could this fellow make himself favorable to his lord? Is it not with the heads of these men?

verses.name: I Samuel 29:5
verses.text: <transChange type="added">Is</transChange> this not David about whom they sing in the dances, saying, <div eID="gen2406" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen2407"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2408"/>‘Saul has killed his thousands,<l eID="gen2408" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2409"/>but David his ten thousands’?” <l eID="gen2409" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen2407"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 29:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1745"/><div sID="gen2410" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1745"/>So Achish called David and said to him, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞As Yahweh lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “The life of Yahweh”</note> certainly you were honest, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I am pleased to have you marching with me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “good in my eyes your going out and your coming in with me”</note> in the campaign.<note placement="foot">Or “army”</note> For I have not found any wrong in you from the day you came to me until this day, but in the eyes of the rulers, you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> not good.

verses.name: I Samuel 29:7
verses.text: So then, return and go in peace, so that you do not do <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞something that displeases⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “bad/evil in the eyes of”</note> the rulers of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines.”

verses.name: I Samuel 29:8
verses.text: Then David said to Achish, “But what have I done? And what have you found in your servant from the day that I <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞entered your service⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “that I was to your face” = “was before you”</note> until this day, that I should not go and fight against the enemies of my lord the king?”

verses.name: I Samuel 29:9
verses.text: And Achish answered and said to David, “I know that you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> good in my eyes, like an angel of God! However, the commanders of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines have said, ‘He must not go up with us into the battle.’

verses.name: I Samuel 29:10
verses.text: So then, rise early in the morning, <transChange type="added">you</transChange> and the servants of your lord who came with you. When you rise early in the morning and it is light <transChange type="added">enough</transChange> for you, leave.

verses.name: I Samuel 29:11
verses.text: So David set out early, he and his men, to leave in the morning to return to the land of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines, but <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines went up <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Jezreel.  <chapter eID="1Sam.29"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 30:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1746"/><title type="x-s">David Recovers His Loved Ones</title> <div sID="gen2411" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1746"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Now⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it happened”</note> when David and his men came <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Ziklag on the third day, <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Amalekites had raided <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Negev and Ziklag. When they attacked Ziklag, they burned it with fire.

verses.name: I Samuel 30:2
verses.text: They took captive the women<note placement="foot">LXX adds “and all”</note> who were in it, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from the youngest to the oldest⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “from small and up to great”</note> They did not kill anyone, but carried <transChange type="added">them</transChange> off and went on their way.

verses.name: I Samuel 30:3
verses.text: When David and his men came to the city, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they saw⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “and look”</note> and <transChange type="added">it</transChange> was burned with fire, and their wives, their sons, and their daughters had been taken captive.

verses.name: I Samuel 30:4
verses.text: Then David and the people who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him raised their voices and wept until there was not <transChange type="added">enough</transChange> strength in them to weep.

verses.name: I Samuel 30:5
verses.text: Two of David’s wives had been taken captive. Ahinoam <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from Jezreel⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the Jezreelitess”</note> and Abigail, the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.

verses.name: I Samuel 30:6
verses.text: And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞David was in a very precarious situation⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “it was very pressed for David”</note> for the people spoke of stoning him, for the souls of all the people were bitter, each <transChange type="added">one</transChange> over his sons and his daughters. But David strengthened himself in Yahweh his God.  <div eID="gen2411" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 30:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1747"/><div sID="gen2412" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1747"/>Then David said to Abiathar the priest, the son of Ahimelech, “Please bring the ephod here for me.” So Abiathar brought the ephod to David.

verses.name: I Samuel 30:8
verses.text: And David inquired of Yahweh, saying, “Should I pursue after this band <transChange type="added">of raiders</transChange>? Will I overtake them?” He said to him, “Pursue <transChange type="added">them</transChange>, for you will certainly overtake them, and you will certainly rescue them.”

verses.name: I Samuel 30:9
verses.text: So David went, he and the six hundred men who were with him, and they came to the Wadi<note placement="foot">A valley that is usually dry but contains a stream during the rainy season</note> Besor, but the rest remained.

verses.name: I Samuel 30:10
verses.text: David pursued, he and four hundred men; but two hundred men stayed because they were too exhausted to pass over the Wadi Besor.  <div eID="gen2412" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 30:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1748"/><div sID="gen2413" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1748"/>Then they found an Egyptian man in the open country and brought him to David, and they gave him food and he ate; they also gave him water.

verses.name: I Samuel 30:12
verses.text: They gave him a slice of fig cake and two raisin cakes; he ate and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞this revived him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “his spirit returned to him”</note> because he had not eaten food or drunk water <transChange type="added">for</transChange> three days and three nights.

verses.name: I Samuel 30:13
verses.text: Then David said to him, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞To whom do you belong⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “To whom are you”</note> and from where <transChange type="added">are</transChange> you? The young man said, “I am an Egyptian young man, a servant of an Amalekite man, but my master abandoned me because I became ill three days ago.

verses.name: I Samuel 30:14
verses.text: We raided the Negev of the Kerethites and that <transChange type="added">which belongs</transChange> to Judah and then the Negev of Caleb, and we burned Ziklag with fire.”

verses.name: I Samuel 30:15
verses.text: So David asked him, “Will you take me down to this band <transChange type="added">of raiders</transChange>?” He said, “Swear to me by God that you will not kill me and that you will not deliver me into my master’s hand! Then I will take you down to this band.”

verses.name: I Samuel 30:16
verses.text: So he took him down, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞there they were⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “look”</note> spread out over the surface of all the land, eating and drinking and dancing because of all of the abundant plunder which they had taken from the land of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines and from the land of Judah.

verses.name: I Samuel 30:17
verses.text: Then David attacked them from twilight until the evening of the next day. Not a man of them escaped <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞except⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “but if”</note> four hundred young men who rode <transChange type="added">off</transChange> on camels and fled.

verses.name: I Samuel 30:18
verses.text: So David recovered all that <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Amalekites had taken; David also rescued his two wives.

verses.name: I Samuel 30:19
verses.text: None of theirs <transChange type="added">was</transChange> missing <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from the smallest to the greatest⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “from the small and up to the great”</note> even sons and daughters, from <transChange type="added">the</transChange> plunder up to everything they had taken for themselves; David brought back everything.

verses.name: I Samuel 30:20
verses.text: And David took all of the sheep,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “flock,” referring to either sheep or goats or both</note> and the cattle they drove along in front of that livestock, and they said, “This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> David’s plunder.”  <div eID="gen2413" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 30:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1749"/><div sID="gen2414" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1749"/>Then David came to <transChange type="added">the</transChange> two hundred men <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who had been too exhausted to follow⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “who were exhausted from going after”</note> David; they had left them behind at the Wadi<note placement="foot">A valley that is usually dry but contains a stream during the rainy season</note> Besor. They went out to meet David and to meet the people who were with him. David came near with the people and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞asked them how they were doing⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “asked for them as far as peace”</note>

verses.name: I Samuel 30:22
verses.text: Then all the corrupt and useless men among the men who went with David reacted and said, “Because they did not go with us, we will not give them <transChange type="added">anything</transChange> from the plunder which we recovered, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞except⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “but if”</note> each <transChange type="added">man may take</transChange> his own wife and children. They must take them along and go!”

verses.name: I Samuel 30:23
verses.text: But David said to them, “You should not do so, my brothers, with what Yahweh has given to us! He has preserved us and has given the <transChange type="added">raiding</transChange> band that came against us into our hand.

verses.name: I Samuel 30:24
verses.text: And who would listen to you regarding this matter? For as the share of the one who went down into the battle, so the share of the one who remained with the baggage will be. They will share alike.”

verses.name: I Samuel 30:25
verses.text: So<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> from that day and beyond, he made it a rule and a regulation for Israel until this day.  <div eID="gen2414" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 30:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1750"/><div sID="gen2415" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1750"/>Then David came to Ziklag, and he sent some of the plunder to the elders of Judah, to his friends, saying, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Here is⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Look”</note> a gift for you from the plunder of the enemies of Yahweh!”

verses.name: I Samuel 30:27
verses.text: <transChange type="added">It was</transChange> for those in Bethel, for those in Ramoth of the Negev, for those in Jattir,

verses.name: I Samuel 30:28
verses.text: for those in Aroer, for those in Siphmoth, for those in Eshtemoa,

verses.name: I Samuel 30:29
verses.text: for those in Racal, for those in the towns of the Jerahmeelites, for those in the towns of the Kenites,

verses.name: I Samuel 30:30
verses.text: for those in Hormah, for those in Bor Ashan, for those in Athach,

verses.name: I Samuel 30:31
verses.text: for those in Hebron, and for all the places <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞where David and his men had roamed⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “where David had gone about there, he and his men”</note>  <chapter eID="1Sam.30"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 31:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1751"/><title type="x-s">Saul and Jonathan Die on Mount Gilboa</title> <div sID="gen2416" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1751"/>Now <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines <transChange type="added">were</transChange> fighting against Israel, and the men of Israel fled before <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines, and they fell slain on Mount Gilboa.

verses.name: I Samuel 31:2
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines overtook Saul and his sons, and <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines killed Jonathan and Abinadab and Malki-Shua, the sons of Saul.

verses.name: I Samuel 31:3
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Saul was in the thick of the battle⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “The battle weighed heavily on Saul”</note> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the archers⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the shooters, the men with the bow”</note> spotted<note placement="foot">Hebrew “found”</note> him, and he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> badly wounded by the archers.

verses.name: I Samuel 31:4
verses.text: Then Saul said to <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his armor bearer⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the carrier of his weapons”</note> “Draw your sword and thrust me through with it, so that these uncircumcised do not come and thrust me through and make a fool of me!” But <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his armor bearer⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the carrier of his weapons”</note> <transChange type="added">was</transChange> not willing <transChange type="added">to do so</transChange> because he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> very afraid. So Saul took the sword and fell on it.

verses.name: I Samuel 31:5
verses.text: And when <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his armor bearer⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the carrier of his weapons”</note> saw that Saul <transChange type="added">was</transChange> dead, he also fell on his sword and died with him.

verses.name: I Samuel 31:6
verses.text: So Saul died, and his three sons, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his armor bearer⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the carrier of his weapons”</note> <transChange type="added">and</transChange> all his men together that <transChange type="added">same</transChange> day.  <div eID="gen2416" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 31:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1752"/><div sID="gen2417" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1752"/>And when the men of Israel who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> on the other side of the valley and <transChange type="added">those</transChange> who were beyond the Jordan saw that the men of Israel had fled and that Saul and his sons were dead, they abandoned the towns and fled. Thus <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines came and lived in them.  <div eID="gen2417" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 31:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1753"/><div sID="gen2418" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1753"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally, “And it happened”</note> the next day, <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines came to strip the dead and they found Saul and his three sons lying <transChange type="added">dead</transChange> on Mount Gilboa.

verses.name: I Samuel 31:9
verses.text: So they cut off his head and stripped off his armor. Then they sent <transChange type="added">messengers</transChange> around in the land of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines to proclaim <transChange type="added">victory in</transChange> the temples<note placement="foot">Or “houses”</note> of their idols and <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the people.

verses.name: I Samuel 31:10
verses.text: And they put his armor <transChange type="added">in</transChange> the temple<note placement="foot">Or “house”</note> of the Ashtoreth,<note placement="foot">Hebrew plural “Ashtaroth” (Ashtoreth was the female consort of Ba’al)</note> and they fastened his corpse to the wall of Beth Shan.

verses.name: I Samuel 31:11
verses.text: When the inhabitants of Jabesh Gilead heard about it, what <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines had done to Saul,

verses.name: I Samuel 31:12
verses.text: all of <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the valiant men⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the men of ability”</note> set out and went all night and took the corpse of Saul and the corpses of his sons from the wall of Beth Shan, and they came to Jabesh and burned them there.

verses.name: I Samuel 31:13
verses.text: Then they took their bones and buried <transChange type="added">them</transChange> under the tamarisk in Jabesh, and they fasted <transChange type="added">for</transChange> seven days.  <chapter eID="1Sam.31"/> <div eID="gen2418" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen2210" osisID="1Sam" type="book"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 1:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1754"/><title type="x-s">The Report of Saul’s Death by the Amalekite</title> <div sID="gen2420" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1754"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞After⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it happened after”</note> the death of Saul, David returned from defeating the Amalekites and he stayed at Ziklag two days.

verses.name: II Samuel 1:2
verses.text: On the third day, a man came from the camp from <transChange type="added">being with</transChange> Saul, with his clothes torn and with dirt on his head. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞When he came⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it happened at his coming”</note> to David, he fell to the ground and bowed down.

verses.name: II Samuel 1:3
verses.text: David said to him, “Where did you come from?” He said to him, “I have escaped from the camp of Israel.”

verses.name: II Samuel 1:4
verses.text: Then David said to him, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞How did things go⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?<note placement="foot">Literally “What was the thing”</note> Please tell me.” He answered, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞When⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “That”</note> the army fled from the battle, and many of the people fell; also, Saul and Jonathan his son died.”

verses.name: II Samuel 1:5
verses.text: Then David asked the young man who <transChange type="added">was</transChange> reporting to him, “How do you know that Saul and his son Jonathan died?”

verses.name: II Samuel 1:6
verses.text: The young man who <transChange type="added">was</transChange> reporting to him said, “I merely happened to be on Mount Gilboa. Here Saul <transChange type="added">was</transChange> leaning on his spear, and look, the chariots and the horsemen <transChange type="added">were</transChange> getting close to him.

verses.name: II Samuel 1:7
verses.text: When he turned around and saw me, he called to me, and I said, ‘Here I <transChange type="added">am</transChange>.’

verses.name: II Samuel 1:8
verses.text: Then he said to me, ‘Who <transChange type="added">are</transChange> you?’ And I said to him, ‘I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> an Amalekite.’

verses.name: II Samuel 1:9
verses.text: He said to me, ‘Please stand over me and kill me, for convulsions have seized me, even though my life <transChange type="added">is still</transChange> in me.’

verses.name: II Samuel 1:10
verses.text: So I stood over him and killed him, for I knew that he could not live after his falling; I took the crown that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> on his head and <transChange type="added">the</transChange> bracelet which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> on his arm; and here, I have brought them to my lord.

verses.name: II Samuel 1:11
verses.text: David grabbed <transChange type="added">at</transChange> his clothes and tore them, <transChange type="added">as did</transChange> all of the men who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him.

verses.name: II Samuel 1:12
verses.text: Then they mourned and wept and fasted over Saul and Jonathan his son until the evening, <transChange type="added">as well</transChange> as over the people of Yahweh and over the house of Israel because they had fallen by the sword.

verses.name: II Samuel 1:13
verses.text: Then David said to the young man who <transChange type="added">was</transChange> reporting to him, “Where <transChange type="added">are</transChange> you from?” And he said, “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> the son of an alien man. I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> an Amalekite.”

verses.name: II Samuel 1:14
verses.text: David said to him, “How <transChange type="added">is it that</transChange> you <transChange type="added">were</transChange> not afraid to stretch out your hand to destroy Yahweh’s anointed one?”

verses.name: II Samuel 1:15
verses.text: Then David called to one of the young men and said to him, “Come near; strike him.” So he struck him down and he died.

verses.name: II Samuel 1:16
verses.text: David said to him, “Your blood <transChange type="added">is</transChange> on your head, for your mouth has testified against you by saying, ‘I killed Yahweh’s anointed one!’ ”  <div eID="gen2420" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 1:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1755"/><title type="x-s">David Laments Jonathan with the “Song of the Bow”</title> <div sID="gen2421" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1755"/>Then David sang this funeral song over Saul and over Jonathan his son.

verses.name: II Samuel 1:18
verses.text: And he ordered “The Bow” to be taught to the children of Judah. Look, it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> written on the scroll of Jashar.<note placement="foot">The Book of Jashar (“the upright”) is also mentioned in Josh 10:13.</note>  <div eID="gen2421" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 1:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1756"/><lg sID="gen2422"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2423"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1756"/>“The glory of Israel <transChange type="added">is</transChange> on your high places; how <transChange type="added">the</transChange> mighty have fallen! <l eID="gen2423" level="1"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 1:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1757"/><l level="1" sID="gen2424"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1757"/>Do not tell it in Gath; do not proclaim it in the streets of Ashkelon,<l eID="gen2424" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2425"/>lest the daughters of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines rejoice,<l eID="gen2425" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2426"/>lest the daughters of the uncircumcised exult. <l eID="gen2426" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 1:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1758"/><l level="1" sID="gen2427"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1758"/>O mountains of Gilboa, <transChange type="added">let there be</transChange> no dew or rain upon you<l eID="gen2427" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2428"/>or on the fields of <transChange type="added">grain for</transChange> offerings,<l eID="gen2428" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2429"/>for there the small shield of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> mighty <transChange type="added">was</transChange> defiled,<l eID="gen2429" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2430"/>the small shield of Saul <transChange type="added">was</transChange> not anointed with oil. <l eID="gen2430" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 1:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1759"/><l level="1" sID="gen2431"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1759"/>From the blood of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> slain, from the fat of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> mighty,<l eID="gen2431" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2432"/>the bow of Jonathan did not turn back,<l eID="gen2432" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2433"/>and the sword of Saul did not return <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞without effect⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “empty handedly”</note> <l eID="gen2433" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 1:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1760"/><l level="1" sID="gen2434"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1760"/>Saul and Jonathan <transChange type="added">were</transChange> beloved and pleasant in their lives<l eID="gen2434" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2435"/>and <transChange type="added">were</transChange> not separated in their death.<l eID="gen2435" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2436"/>They <transChange type="added">were</transChange> swifter than eagles, stronger than lions. <l eID="gen2436" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 1:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1761"/><l level="1" sID="gen2437"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1761"/>O daughters of Israel, weep over Saul,<l eID="gen2437" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2438"/>the one who clothed you with crimson,<l eID="gen2438" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2439"/>the one who <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞adorned your clothing with golden ornaments⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “put gold ornaments on your clothing”</note> <l eID="gen2439" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 1:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1762"/><l level="1" sID="gen2440"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1762"/>How <transChange type="added">the</transChange> mighty have fallen in the midst of the battle;<l eID="gen2440" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2441"/>Jonathan <transChange type="added">lies</transChange> slain on your high places. <l eID="gen2441" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 1:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1763"/><l level="1" sID="gen2442"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1763"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I am distressed⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Distress is for me”</note> over you, my brother Jonathan.<l eID="gen2442" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2443"/>you <transChange type="added">were</transChange> very dear to me;<l eID="gen2443" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2444"/>your love <transChange type="added">was</transChange> more wonderful to me than the love of women. <l eID="gen2444" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 1:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1764"/><l level="1" sID="gen2445"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1764"/>How <transChange type="added">the</transChange> mighty have fallen and the weapons of warfare perished.” <l eID="gen2445" level="1"/><lg eID="gen2422"/> <chapter eID="2Sam.1"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 2:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1765"/><title type="x-s">David Moves to Hebron</title> <div sID="gen2446" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1765"/>It happened after this that David inquired of Yahweh, saying, “Shall I go up into one of the cities of Judah?” And Yahweh said to him, “Go up.” David asked, “Where shall I go up?” And he said, “To Hebron.”

verses.name: II Samuel 2:2
verses.text: So David went up there <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞along with⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and also”</note> his two wives, Ahinoam <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from Jezreel⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the Jezreelitess”</note> and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:3
verses.text: Also, David brought up his men who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him, each <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞with⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and”</note> his household, and they settled in the towns of Hebron.  <div eID="gen2446" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 2:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1766"/><title type="x-s">David Anointed King over Judah at Hebron</title> <div sID="gen2447" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1766"/>Then the men of Judah came, and they anointed David there as king over the house of Judah, and they told David, “The men of Jabesh-Gilead buried Saul.”

verses.name: II Samuel 2:5
verses.text: So David sent messengers to the men of Jabesh-Gilead and said to them, “May you be blessed by Yahweh because you did this loyal love with your lord, with Saul, and you buried him.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:6
verses.text: Now may Yahweh show loyal love and faithfulness with you. I will also show the good with you that you have done in this matter.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:7
verses.text: So then, let your hands be strong and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞be valiant⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “as sons of ability”</note> for your lord Saul <transChange type="added">is</transChange> dead, and the house of Judah has anointed me as king over them.”  <div eID="gen2447" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 2:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1767"/><title type="x-s">Ish-Bosheth over Israel</title> <div sID="gen2448" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1767"/>But Abner the son of Ner, the commander of Saul’s army, had taken Ish-Bosheth the son of Saul and brought him over <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Mahanaim.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:9
verses.text: He made him king over Gilead, over the Ashurites, over Jezreel, over Ephraim, over Benjamin, and over Israel, all of it.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:10
verses.text: Ish-Bosheth the son of Saul <transChange type="added">was</transChange> forty years old when he became king over Israel and he reigned two years; however, the house of Judah <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞followed⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “were after”</note> David.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:11
verses.text: The number of days that David was king over Hebron, over the house of Judah, <transChange type="added">was</transChange> seven years and six months.  <div eID="gen2448" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 2:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1768"/><title type="x-s">War between Judah and Israel</title> <div sID="gen2449" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1768"/>Abner the son of Ner and the servants of Ish-Bosheth the son of Saul went out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:13
verses.text: Then Joab the son of Zeruiah and the servants of David went out, and they met at the pool of Gibeon. The one group sat on one side of the pool, and the other sat on the other side.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:14
verses.text: Abner said to Joab, “Let the young men come up and fight in our presence.” And Joab said, “Let them come up.”

verses.name: II Samuel 2:15
verses.text: So they came forward and passed by in number: twelve for Benjamin and for Ish-Bosheth the son of Saul, and twelve from the servants of David.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:16
verses.text: Then each seized his <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞opponent⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “neighbor”</note> by the head and each thrust his sword in the side of his opponent, so they fell together. So they<note placement="foot">Hebrew “he”</note> called the name of that place Helkath Hazzurim,<note placement="foot">Helkath Hazzurim possibly means “the slippery slope”</note> which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in Gibeon.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:17
verses.text: Then the battle <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞became increasingly fierce⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and it was/became strong/fierce until very”</note> on that day, and Abner and the men of Israel <transChange type="added">were</transChange> defeated before the servants of David.  <div eID="gen2449" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 2:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1769"/><div sID="gen2450" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1769"/>The three sons of Zeruiah were there, Joab and Abishai and Asahel. Now Asahel <transChange type="added">was</transChange> swift with his feet as one of the gazelles which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in the open field.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:19
verses.text: So Asahel pursued<note placement="foot">Hebrew “pursued after”</note> Abner, and he did not turn aside to the right or to the left from going after Abner.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:20
verses.text: Abner turned around and said, “<transChange type="added">Are</transChange> you this Asahel?” And he said, “Yes.”

verses.name: II Samuel 2:21
