verses.text: Abner said to him, “Turn aside to your right or to your left; seize for yourself one of the young men, and take his belongings for yourself.” But Asahel <transChange type="added">was</transChange> not willing to turn aside from him.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:22
verses.text: So Abner said to Asahel <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞once again⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “and he again did again”</note> “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞For your own sake⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “for yourself”</note> turn aside <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from following me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “from after me”</note> Why should I strike you down to the ground? How could I <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞show my face⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “lift up my face”</note> to Joab your brother?”

verses.name: II Samuel 2:23
verses.text: But he refused to turn away, so Abner struck him in the stomach with the butt of the spear, and the spear went out of his back. He fell there and he died <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞on the spot⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “in his place”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it happened”</note> all who came to the place where Asahel fell and died <transChange type="added">just</transChange> stood there.  <div eID="gen2450" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 2:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1770"/><div sID="gen2451" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1770"/>So Joab and Abishai pursued<note placement="foot">Hebrew “pursued after”</note> Abner <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞when⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and”</note> the sun went down. And they came to the hill country of Ammah, which is <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before Giah⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “lies on the face of Giah”</note> <transChange type="added">on</transChange> the way to the wilderness of Gibeon.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:25
verses.text: The descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Benjamin rallied after Abner, and they became as one fighting group and stood on the top of a certain hill.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:26
verses.text: Then Abner called to Joab and said, “Will <transChange type="added">the</transChange> sword devour forever? Do you not know that <transChange type="added">there</transChange> will be bitterness in the end? <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞How long⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And up to when”</note> will you not tell the people to turn <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞away from pursuing⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from after”</note> their brothers?”

verses.name: II Samuel 2:27
verses.text: Joab said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞As God lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “The life of God”</note> for if you had not spoken, the people would surely have gone up in the morning, each one of them <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from following after⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from after”</note> his brother.”

verses.name: II Samuel 2:28
verses.text: Then Joab blew on the trumpet and all the people stopped, and they no longer pursued after Israel, and they did not fight with them again.  <div eID="gen2451" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 2:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1771"/><div sID="gen2452" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1771"/>Then Abner and his men went through the Arabah all that night, and they crossed over the Jordan. They went all the forenoon and came to Mahanaim.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:30
verses.text: After Joab returned from <transChange type="added">pursuing</transChange><note placement="foot">Hebrew “after”</note> Abner, he gathered all the people; nineteen of the servants of David <transChange type="added">were</transChange> missing <transChange type="added">along</transChange> with Asahel.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:31
verses.text: The servants of David had killed some of the Benjaminites among the men of Abner; three hundred and sixty men had died.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:32
verses.text: Then they picked up Asahel and buried him in the grave of his father, which <transChange type="added">was at</transChange> Bethlehem. Joab and his men went all that night <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞<transChange type="added">arriving</transChange> in Hebron at first light⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “it became light for them in Hebron”</note>  <chapter eID="2Sam.2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 3:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1772"/><title type="x-s">The House of David Grows Stronger</title> <div sID="gen2453" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1772"/>The battle <transChange type="added">was</transChange> prolonged between the house of Saul and the house of David, but David <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞<transChange type="added">was</transChange> growing stronger and stronger⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “was going and strong”</note> while the house of Saul <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞was becoming weaker and weaker⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “was going and weak”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 3:2
verses.text: And sons <transChange type="added">were</transChange> born to David in Hebron; his firstborn <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Amnon by Ahinoam <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from Jezreel⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the Jezreelitess”</note>.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:3
verses.text: His second <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Kileab by Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite; the third <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Absalom the son of Maacah, <transChange type="added">who was</transChange> the daughter of Talmai the king of Geshur.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:4
verses.text: The fourth <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Adonijah the son of Haggith; the fifth <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Shephatiah the son of Abital.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:5
verses.text: The sixth <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Ithream by Eglah the wife of David. These <transChange type="added">were</transChange> born to David in Hebron.  <div eID="gen2453" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 3:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1773"/><div sID="gen2454" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1773"/>As the war between the house of Saul and the house of David was <transChange type="added">continuing</transChange>, Abner was strengthening himself in the house of Saul.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:7
verses.text: Saul had had a concubine, and her name <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Rizpah the daughter of Aiah. Then <transChange type="added">Ish-Bosheth</transChange><note placement="foot">Supported by some Hebrew and Greek manuscripts</note> said to Abner, “Why <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞did you have sex with⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “have you gone into”</note> my father’s concubine?”

verses.name: II Samuel 3:8
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Abner became very angry⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it became hot for Abner very”</note> at the words of Ish-Bosheth, and he said, “Am I the head of a dog which is for Judah today? Do I not continue to show loyal love with the house of Saul your father, to his brothers, and to his friends? I have not let you fall into the hands of David, yet you have <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞accused me of sin with this woman⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “you have called me into account with the guilt of the woman”</note> today.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:9
verses.text: Thus <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞may God punish Abner⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “may God do to Abner, and thus may he add to it”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞if I do not accomplish what Yahweh has sworn to David⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “for as that Yahweh has sworn to David, so I will accomplish for him”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 3:10
verses.text: <transChange type="added">specifically,</transChange> to transfer the kingdom from the house of Saul and to establish the throne of David over Israel and over Judah from Dan to Beersheba!”

verses.name: II Samuel 3:11
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">Ish-Bosheth</transChange> was no longer able to <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞answer⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “return a word to”</note> Abner <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞because he feared him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “because of his fearing him”</note>  <div eID="gen2454" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 3:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1774"/><title type="x-s">Abner Pledges Support for David</title> <div sID="gen2455" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1774"/>Abner sent messengers to David <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞where he was⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “under him”</note> saying, “To whom does the land belong? <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Make your covenant with me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!<note placement="foot">Literally “cut your covenant with me”</note> Look, my hand <transChange type="added">is</transChange> with you to bring all of Israel over to you!”

verses.name: II Samuel 3:13
verses.text: He<note placement="foot">David</note> said, “Good. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I will make a covenant with you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “I will cut a covenant with you”</note> I am asking only one thing from you: You shall not see my face unless you bring Michal the daughter of Saul when you come to see <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “my face”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 3:14
verses.text: Then David sent messengers to Ish-Bosheth the son of Saul, saying, “Give <transChange type="added">me</transChange> my wife Michal whom I betrothed to myself<note placement="foot">Hebrew “me”</note> for a hundred foreskins of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines.”

verses.name: II Samuel 3:15
verses.text: So Ish-Bosheth sent and took her from <transChange type="added">her</transChange> husband, from Paltiel the son of Laish.<note placement="foot">The Hebrew Masoretic text (<hi type="italic">Kethib</hi>) reads “Lush”; <hi type="italic">Qere</hi> reads “Laish”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 3:16
verses.text: But her husband went with her, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞weeping all along⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “going and weeping”</note> after her as far as Bahurim. Then Abner said to him, “Go <transChange type="added">and</transChange> return.” So he returned.  <div eID="gen2455" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 3:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1775"/><div sID="gen2456" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1775"/>The word of Abner <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞came to⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “was with”</note> the elders of Israel, saying, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞For quite some time⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Both yesterday and the day before”</note> you were seeking David as king over you.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:18
verses.text: So then, bring it about, because Yahweh had said to David, “Through the hand of David my servant <transChange type="added">I am about</transChange> to save my people Israel from the hand of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines and from the hand of all their enemies.”

verses.name: II Samuel 3:19
verses.text: Abner also spoke <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞privately to Benjamin⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “in the ears of Benjamin”</note> Abner also went <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to speak to David⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to speak in the ears of David”</note> in Hebron, all that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> good in the eyes of Israel and in the eyes of all the house of Benjamin.  <div eID="gen2456" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 3:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1776"/><div sID="gen2457" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1776"/>Then Abner came to David in Hebron and with him <transChange type="added">were</transChange> twenty men. David had prepared a feast for Abner and for the men who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:21
verses.text: And Abner said to David, “Let me get up and go and gather all of Israel to my lord the king, that they may <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞make a covenant⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “cut a covenant”</note> with you so you can reign over all which your soul desires.” So David dismissed Abner, and he left in peace.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:22
verses.text: And look, the servants of David and Joab came from the raid, and they brought much plunder with them. But Abner was not with David at Hebron, for he<note placement="foot">David</note> had dismissed him, and he had gone in peace.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:23
verses.text: When Joab and all the army that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> with him came, they told Joab, “Abner the son of Ner came to the king, and he sent him away, and he left in peace.”  <div eID="gen2457" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 3:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1777"/><title type="x-s">Joab Assassinates Abner</title> <div sID="gen2458" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1777"/>Then Joab came to the king and said, “What have you done? Abner came here to you? Why have you dismissed him that he <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞actually went away⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?<note placement="foot">Literally “and he went going”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 3:25
verses.text: You know that Abner the son of Ner came to deceive you. He came to learn about your going out and coming <transChange type="added">in</transChange> and to know all which you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> doing.”

verses.name: II Samuel 3:26
verses.text: Then Joab went out from David, and he sent messengers after Abner, and they brought him back from Bor Hasirah, but David did not know <transChange type="added">it</transChange>.  <div eID="gen2458" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 3:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1778"/><div sID="gen2459" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1778"/>When Abner returned to Hebron, Joab took him aside to the middle of the gate to speak with him in private. Then he struck him in the stomach there and he died, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞for he had shed the blood of Asahel his brother⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “for the blood of Asahel his brother.” See Num 35:16–25</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 3:28
verses.text: When David heard this afterwards, he said: “I and my kingdom <transChange type="added">are</transChange> innocent <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before Yahweh⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from with Yahweh”</note> forever <transChange type="added">for</transChange> the blood of Abner the son of Ner.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:29
verses.text: May <transChange type="added">the blood</transChange> come down on the head of Joab and all the house of his father. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞May the house of Joab never lack⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “May there not be cut off from the house of Joab”</note> <transChange type="added">one with</transChange> a bodily discharge or <transChange type="added">one with</transChange> leprosy or <transChange type="added">one who</transChange> grasps the distaff or <transChange type="added">one who</transChange> falls by the sword or <transChange type="added">one who is</transChange> lacking food.”  <div eID="gen2459" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 3:30
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1779"/><div sID="gen2460" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1779"/>So Joab and Abishai, his brother, killed Abner because he had killed Asahel, their brother, at Gibeon in the battle.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:31
verses.text: David said to Joab and to all the people who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him, “Tear your clothing and put on sackcloth and mourn before Abner.” Now King David <transChange type="added">was</transChange> following after the bier.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:32
verses.text: And they buried Abner at Hebron. And the king lifted up his voice and wept at the grave of Abner, and all the people wept.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:33
verses.text: The king sang a lament for Abner and said, “Should Abner have died the death of a fool?

verses.name: II Samuel 3:34
verses.text: Your hands <transChange type="added">were</transChange> not tied and your feet <transChange type="added">were</transChange> not in contact with bronze fetters. You have fallen as one who falls before sons of wickedness.” Then <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞all the people wept over him again⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “and all the people did again to weep over him”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 3:35
verses.text: Then all the people came to give David food. Still on that day, David swore, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞May God punish me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Thus may God do to me and thus may he add”</note> if I taste food or anything before the sun goes down.”

verses.name: II Samuel 3:36
verses.text: All the people noticed, and it <transChange type="added">was</transChange> good in their eyes, as everything that the king did <transChange type="added">was</transChange> good in the eyes of all the people.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:37
verses.text: Then all the people and all of Israel realized on that day that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the king had not desired⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “that it was not from the king”</note> to kill Abner the son of Ner.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:38
verses.text: Then the king said to his servants, “Did you not realize that a prince and a great man has fallen today in Israel?

verses.name: II Samuel 3:39
verses.text: I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> weak today even though anointed king, and these men, the sons of Zeruiah, <transChange type="added">are</transChange> crueler than I <transChange type="added">am</transChange>. May Yahweh pay them back for doing wickedness according to their <transChange type="added">own</transChange> wickedness.”  <chapter eID="2Sam.3"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 4:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1780"/><title type="x-s">Ish-Bosheth is Assassinated</title> <div sID="gen2461" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1780"/>When the son of Saul heard that Abner had died in Hebron, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his courage failed⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “his hands hung limp”</note> and all of Israel <transChange type="added">was</transChange> horrified.

verses.name: II Samuel 4:2
verses.text: Two of the men, commanders of the raiding bands, were <transChange type="added">for</transChange> the son of Saul. The name of one <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Baanah, and the name of the other <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Recab, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite from the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Benjamin; also, Beeroth <transChange type="added">was</transChange> regarded <transChange type="added">as belonging</transChange> to Benjamin.

verses.name: II Samuel 4:3
verses.text: The Beerothites fled to Gittaim, and they are resident aliens there until this day.

verses.name: II Samuel 4:4
verses.text: (Now Jonathan the son of Saul had a son who <transChange type="added">was</transChange> crippled in the feet. He <transChange type="added">was</transChange> five years old when the message of Saul and Jonathan came from Jezreel, and his nurse had picked him up and fled. It happened that as she <transChange type="added">was</transChange> hurrying away to flee, he fell and became crippled. His name <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Mephibosheth.)

verses.name: II Samuel 4:5
verses.text: When the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Recab and Baanah, set out, they came at the heat of the day to the house of Ish-Bosheth while <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> taking a noontime rest⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “he was lying with the bed at noon”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 4:6
verses.text: They came as far as the middle of the house <transChange type="added">as if</transChange> takers of wheat, and they struck him in the stomach. Then Recab and Baanah his brother escaped.

verses.name: II Samuel 4:7
verses.text: When they had come <transChange type="added">into</transChange> the house, he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> lying on his couch <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in his bedchamber⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “in the room of his lying”</note> and they attacked him and killed him. Then they <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞beheaded him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “they took away his head”</note> and they took his head and went on the way of the Arabah all night.

verses.name: II Samuel 4:8
verses.text: They brought the head of Ish-Bosheth to David at Hebron, and they said to the king, “Here <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the head of Ish-Bosheth, the son of Saul your enemy, who sought your life. Yahweh has given to my lord the king vengeance this day on Saul and on his offspring.”

verses.name: II Samuel 4:9
verses.text: Then David answered Recab and Baanah his brother, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and he said to them, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞As Yahweh lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “The life of Yahweh”</note> who redeemed my soul from all trouble,

verses.name: II Samuel 4:10
verses.text: when the <transChange type="added">one</transChange> who told me, “Look, Saul <transChange type="added">is</transChange> dead,” <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞thought that he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> bringing good news⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “and he was as one bringing good news in his eyes”</note> I seized him and killed him at Ziklag, which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> as my giving the news <transChange type="added">back</transChange> to him.

verses.name: II Samuel 4:11
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞How much more⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Also”</note> when wicked men kill a righteous man in his house, on his bed! So then, shall I not seek his lifeblood from your hand, so that I may destroy you from the earth?”

verses.name: II Samuel 4:12
verses.text: Then David commanded the young men, and they killed them, and they cut off their hands and their feet, and they hung <transChange type="added">them</transChange> at the pool at Hebron, but the head of Ish-Bosheth they took and buried in the grave of Abner at Hebron.  <chapter eID="2Sam.4"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 5:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1781"/><title type="x-s">David Anointed as King over All of Israel</title> <div sID="gen2462" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1781"/>So all the tribes of Israel came to David at Hebron, and they said, “Here we <transChange type="added">are</transChange>, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞we are your flesh and blood⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “We are your bone and your flesh”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 5:2
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞For some time⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “Both yesterday and three days before”</note> when Saul was king over us, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you were leading Israel in and out⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “you were going out and coming in, Israel.” (So <hi type="italic">Kethib</hi>; <hi type="italic">Qere</hi> reads “bringing out and bringing in Israel”)</note> Yahweh had said to you, ‘You shall be the shepherd of my people Israel, and you will be the leader over Israel.’ ”

verses.name: II Samuel 5:3
verses.text: All the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, and King David <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞made a covenant⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “cut a covenant”</note> with them at Hebron in the presence of Yahweh; then they anointed David as king over Israel.

verses.name: II Samuel 5:4
verses.text: David <transChange type="added">was</transChange> thirty years old when he began to reign; he reigned forty years.

verses.name: II Samuel 5:5
verses.text: He reigned over Judah at Hebron <transChange type="added">for</transChange> seven years and six months; and he reigned over all Israel and Judah at Jerusalem <transChange type="added">for</transChange> thirty-three years.  <div eID="gen2462" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 5:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1782"/><title type="x-s">The Capture and Growth of Jerusalem</title> <div sID="gen2463" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1782"/>The king and his men went to Jerusalem, to the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land. They said to David, “You will not come here, for even the blind and the lame can turn you back, saying, ‘David cannot come here.’ ”

verses.name: II Samuel 5:7
verses.text: David captured the fortress of Zion, the city of David.

verses.name: II Samuel 5:8
verses.text: David had said, “On that day <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞when we attack the Jebusites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “in all of the striking down the Jebusites”</note> one must attack the lame and the blind, <transChange type="added">those</transChange> who hate the soul of David, by <transChange type="added">means of</transChange> the water supply.” For thus the blind and the lame would say, “He cannot come into the house.”

verses.name: II Samuel 5:9
verses.text: David occupied the fortress and called it the city of David. And David built all around <transChange type="added">it</transChange> from the Millo and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞inward⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “to the house”</note>  <div eID="gen2463" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 5:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1783"/><div sID="gen2464" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1783"/>David <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞continued growing stronger and stronger⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “went going and great”</note> and Yahweh the God of hosts <transChange type="added">was</transChange> with him.

verses.name: II Samuel 5:11
verses.text: So Hiram, the king of Tyre, sent messengers to David, <transChange type="added">along with</transChange> cedar trees and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞craftsmen skilled in wood and in stone masonry⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “skilled craftsmen of wood and skilled craftsmen of stone wall”</note> and they built a house for David.

verses.name: II Samuel 5:12
verses.text: David realized that Yahweh had established him as king over Israel and that he had exalted his kingdom because of his people Israel.

verses.name: II Samuel 5:13
verses.text: David took more concubines and wives from Jerusalem after he came from Hebron, and more sons and daughters <transChange type="added">were</transChange> born to him.

verses.name: II Samuel 5:14
verses.text: These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the names of the ones born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua and Shobab and Nathan and Solomon;

verses.name: II Samuel 5:15
verses.text: Ibhar and Elishua and Nepheg and Japhia;

verses.name: II Samuel 5:16
verses.text: Elishama and Eliada and Eliphelet.  <div eID="gen2464" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 5:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1784"/><title type="x-s">War with the Philistines</title> <div sID="gen2465" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1784"/>When <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines heard that they had anointed David as king over Israel, all <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines went up to seek David, but David heard and went down to the stronghold.<note placement="foot">Thought by many to be the stronghold of Masada</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 5:18
verses.text: Now <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines had come, and they spread out in the Valley of Rephaim.

verses.name: II Samuel 5:19
verses.text: And David inquired of Yahweh, saying, “Shall I go up to the Philistines? Will you give them into my hands?” Yahweh said to David, “Go up, for <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I will certainly give⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “giving I will give”</note> <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines into your hand.”

verses.name: II Samuel 5:20
verses.text: So David came to Baal Perazim and defeated them there; and David said, “Yahweh has burst through my enemies before me like the bursting of water.” Therefore he called the name of that place Baal Perazim.<note placement="foot">Baal Perazim may mean “the master of the bursting through”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 5:21
verses.text: They had left their idols there, so David and his men carried them away.  <div eID="gen2465" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 5:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1785"/><div sID="gen2466" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1785"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Once again⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And they again did again”</note> <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines came up and spread out in the Valley of Rephaim.

verses.name: II Samuel 5:23
verses.text: So David inquired of Yahweh, but he said, “You shall not go up. <transChange type="added">Rather,</transChange> go around to their rear and come to them from opposite the balsam trees.

verses.name: II Samuel 5:24
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And it shall be⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it shall happen”</note> that when you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, then pay attention, for then Yahweh has gone out before you to strike down the army of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines.”

verses.name: II Samuel 5:25
verses.text: So David did thus, just as Yahweh had commanded him, and he struck down <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines from Geba <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞all the way⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “as you go up”</note> to Gezer.  <chapter eID="2Sam.5"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 6:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1786"/><title type="x-s">David Brings the Ark of Yahweh to Jerusalem</title> <div sID="gen2467" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1786"/>David again gathered all the chosen men in Israel, thirty thousand.

verses.name: II Samuel 6:2
verses.text: David got up and went and all the people who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him, from Baale-judah to bring up from there the ark of God which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> called the name, the name of Yahweh of hosts, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞upon which the cherubim sit⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the cherubim are sitting on him”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 6:3
verses.text: They loaded the ark of God on a new utility cart, and they carried it from the house of Abinadab, which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> on the hill. Now Uzza and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, <transChange type="added">were</transChange> driving the new utility cart along.

verses.name: II Samuel 6:4
verses.text: So they brought it out from the house of Abinadab, which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> on the hill with the ark of God, and Ahio <transChange type="added">was</transChange> going before the ark.

verses.name: II Samuel 6:5
verses.text: Now David and all the house of Israel <transChange type="added">were</transChange> dancing before Yahweh, with all kinds of <transChange type="added">musical instruments made from</transChange> ash trees, and with zithers, harps, tambourines, sistrums, and cymbals.

verses.name: II Samuel 6:6
verses.text: When they came to the threshing floor of Nakon, Uzza reached out to the ark of God and took hold of <transChange type="added">it</transChange>, because the oxen had stumbled.

verses.name: II Samuel 6:7
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Then the anger of Yahweh was kindled⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Then the nose of Yahweh became hot”</note> against Uzza, and God struck him down there because of the indiscretion,<note placement="foot">Legal regulations offered by Moses did not permit an Israelite to handle the ark of the covenant in this manner (compare Exod 25:12–16)</note> and he died there beside the ark of God.

verses.name: II Samuel 6:8
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞David was angry⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “It was hot for David”</note> because Yahweh had burst out against Uzza, and he called that place Perez-Uzza until this day.

verses.name: II Samuel 6:9
verses.text: But David feared Yahweh on that day and said, “How can the ark of Yahweh come to me?”

verses.name: II Samuel 6:10
verses.text: However, David <transChange type="added">was</transChange> not willing to bring the ark of Yahweh to himself, to the city of David, so David caused it to turn <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite.

verses.name: II Samuel 6:11
verses.text: So the ark of Yahweh remained <transChange type="added">in</transChange> the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite <transChange type="added">for</transChange> three months, and Yahweh blessed Obed-Edom and all his household.  <div eID="gen2467" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 6:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1787"/><div sID="gen2468" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1787"/>It <transChange type="added">was</transChange> told to King David, “Yahweh has blessed the household of Obed-Edom and all that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> his because of the ark of God.” So David went and brought up the ark of God from the house of Obed-Edom to the city of David with jubilation.

verses.name: II Samuel 6:13
verses.text: It happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> when the carriers of the ark of Yahweh had marched six steps that he sacrificed an ox and a fatling.

verses.name: II Samuel 6:14
verses.text: Now David <transChange type="added">was</transChange> dancing with all <transChange type="added">his</transChange> might before Yahweh, and David <transChange type="added">was</transChange> wearing<note placement="foot">Hebrew “girded with”</note> a linen ephod.

verses.name: II Samuel 6:15
verses.text: So David and all the house of Israel <transChange type="added">were</transChange> bringing up the ark of Yahweh with shouts of joyful acclaim and with the sound of the trumpet.

verses.name: II Samuel 6:16
verses.text: It happened that when the ark of Yahweh came <transChange type="added">into</transChange> the city of David, Michal the daughter of Saul looked down through the window and saw King David leaping and dancing before Yahweh, and she despised him in her heart.  <div eID="gen2468" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 6:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1788"/><div sID="gen2469" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1788"/>They brought the ark of Yahweh and set it in its place in the middle of the tent which David had pitched for it. Then David offered up burnt offerings and fellowship offerings in the presence of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Samuel 6:18
verses.text: When David had finished from the sacrificing of the burnt offerings and the fellowship offerings, he blessed the people in the name of Yahweh of hosts.

verses.name: II Samuel 6:19
verses.text: Then he distributed to all the people, to all the multitude of Israel, from man to woman, to each: one ring-shaped piece of bread, one cake of dates, and one cake of raisins; and all the people went each to his house.  <div eID="gen2469" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 6:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1789"/><div sID="gen2470" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1789"/>When David returned to bless his household, Michal the daughter of Saul came out to meet David. She said, “How the king of Israel honored himself today <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞by uncovering himself⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “who has uncovered himself”</note> before the eyes of the maids of his servants, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as the total exposure of a worthless one⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “as the total uncovering of one of the worthless”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 6:21
verses.text: So David said to Michal, “<transChange type="added">In the</transChange> presence of Yahweh who chose me <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞over⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “more than”</note> your father and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞over⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “more than”</note> his household, to appoint me <transChange type="added">as</transChange> leader over the people of Yahweh, over Israel, I have celebrated before Yahweh.

verses.name: II Samuel 6:22
verses.text: I will demean myself again more than this, and I will be abased in my eyes, but with the maids whom you mentioned, with them I will be honored.”

verses.name: II Samuel 6:23
verses.text: So for Michal the daughter of Saul, she had no child until the day of her death.  <chapter eID="2Sam.6"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 7:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1790"/><title type="x-s">Yahweh Makes a Covenant with David</title> <div sID="gen2471" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1790"/>It happened that the king settled in his house. (Now Yahweh had given rest to him from all his enemies all around.)

verses.name: II Samuel 7:2
verses.text: And the king said to Nathan the prophet, “Look, please, I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> living in a house of cedar, but the ark of God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> staying in the middle of the tent.”

verses.name: II Samuel 7:3
verses.text: Nathan said to the king, “Go and do all that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in your heart, for Yahweh <transChange type="added">is</transChange> with you.”

verses.name: II Samuel 7:4
verses.text: But it happened <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞that night⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “in the night the that”</note> the word of Yahweh came<note placement="foot">Hebrew “was”</note> to Nathan, saying,

verses.name: II Samuel 7:5
verses.text: “Go and tell my servant David, ‘Thus says Yahweh: “<transChange type="added">Are</transChange> you the one to build for me a house for my dwelling?

verses.name: II Samuel 7:6
verses.text: For I have not dwelt in a house from the day I brought up the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> from Egypt until this day; <transChange type="added">rather,</transChange> I <transChange type="added">was</transChange> going about in a tent and in a tabernacle.

verses.name: II Samuel 7:7
verses.text: In all of my going about among all the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> did I speak a word with one of the tribes of Israel whom I commanded to shepherd my people Israel, saying, ‘Why did you not build me a cedar house?’ ” ’

verses.name: II Samuel 7:8
verses.text: So then, thus you shall say to my servant David, ‘Thus says Yahweh of hosts, “I took you from the pasture <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from following⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from behind”</note> the sheep to be a leader over my people, over Israel,

verses.name: II Samuel 7:9
verses.text: and I have been with you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞everywhere you went⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “in all that you went”</note> I have cut off all of your enemies from in front of you, and I will make a great name for you, as the name of the great <transChange type="added">ones</transChange> who <transChange type="added">are</transChange> on the earth.

verses.name: II Samuel 7:10
verses.text: I will make a place for my people Israel, and I will plant them<note placement="foot">Hebrew “him”</note> so that they<note placement="foot">Hebrew “he”</note> can dwell <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in their own place⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “under him”</note> They will not tremble <transChange type="added">any</transChange> longer, and the children of wickedness will not afflict them again, as in the former days.

verses.name: II Samuel 7:11
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞In the manner that⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And as far as” or “And from the day”</note> I appointed judges over my people Israel, I will give you rest from all your enemies. And Yahweh declares to you that Yahweh will build a house for you.

verses.name: II Samuel 7:12
verses.text: When your days <transChange type="added">are</transChange> full and you lie down with your ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> I will raise up your offspring after you who will go out from your body, and I will establish his kingdom.

verses.name: II Samuel 7:13
verses.text: He will build a house for my name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever.

verses.name: II Samuel 7:14
verses.text: I will be a father to him, and he will be a son for me, whom I will punish when he does wrong, with a rod of men and with blows of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞human beings⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “children of men”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 7:15
verses.text: But my loyal love shall not depart from him as I took <transChange type="added">it</transChange> from Saul, whom I removed from before you.

verses.name: II Samuel 7:16
verses.text: Your house and your kingdom shall endure forever before you; your throne shall be established forever.” ’ ”  <div eID="gen2471" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 7:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1791"/><title type="x-s">David Responds to Yahweh’s Covenant</title> <div sID="gen2472" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1791"/>According to all these words and according to all this vision, this Nathan spoke to David.

verses.name: II Samuel 7:18
verses.text: Then King David went and sat before Yahweh and said, “Who <transChange type="added">am</transChange> I, my lord Yahweh, and what <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my house that you have brought me up to <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞this place⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?<note placement="foot">Literally “here”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 7:19
verses.text: Still, this <transChange type="added">was</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞insignificant⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “small”</note> in your eyes, my lord Yahweh, and also you have spoken about the house of your servant from afar, and this <transChange type="added">may be</transChange> the teaching of humans, my lord Yahweh.

verses.name: II Samuel 7:20
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞What more can David say to you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?<note placement="foot">Literally “And what can David still add to say”</note> You know your servant, my lord Yahweh.

verses.name: II Samuel 7:21
verses.text: Because of your word and according to your heart, you have done all of this great thing, <transChange type="added">in order</transChange> to let your servant know.

verses.name: II Samuel 7:22
verses.text: Therefore you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> great, my lord Yahweh, for there is no one like you, and there <transChange type="added">is</transChange> no god except you, in all that we have heard with our ears.

verses.name: II Samuel 7:23
verses.text: Who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> like your people, like Israel? <transChange type="added">Israel is</transChange> the one nation on earth whose God <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞led them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “went”; LXX reads “led”</note> in order to redeem a people for himself, and to make a name for himself, and to do for you<note placement="foot">David switches pronouns from the third person to the second person</note> the great and awesome things for your land in the presence of your people whom he redeemed for himself from Egypt, <transChange type="added">from the</transChange> nations and their gods.

verses.name: II Samuel 7:24
verses.text: You have established your people Israel for yourself as a people forever, and you, O Yahweh, have become their God.

verses.name: II Samuel 7:25
verses.text: So then, Yahweh God, the word that you have spoken concerning your servant and concerning his house, confirm it forever, and do just as you have promised.

verses.name: II Samuel 7:26
verses.text: Your name shall be great forever, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞and they will say⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “saying”</note> ‘Yahweh of hosts <transChange type="added">is</transChange> God over Israel’; and the house of your servant David shall be established before you.

verses.name: II Samuel 7:27
verses.text: For you, O Yahweh of hosts, <transChange type="added">are</transChange> God of Israel! You have revealed to the ear of your servant, ‘I will build a house for you’; therefore your servant <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞has found courage⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “has found his heart”</note> to pray this prayer to you.

verses.name: II Samuel 7:28
verses.text: Now, my Lord Yahweh, you alone <transChange type="added">are</transChange> God, and your words <transChange type="added">are</transChange><note placement="foot">Hebrew “will be”</note> true. You have promised this good to your servant.

verses.name: II Samuel 7:29
verses.text: So then, be content and bless the house of your servant to be forever in your presence, for you, my Lord Yahweh, have spoken, and because of your blessing, may the house of your servant be blessed forever.”  <chapter eID="2Sam.7"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 8:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1792"/><title type="x-s">David’s Military Victories Continue</title> <div sID="gen2473" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1792"/>It happened afterwards <transChange type="added">that</transChange> David attacked <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines and subdued them, and he took Metheg Ammah from the hands of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines.

verses.name: II Samuel 8:2
verses.text: When he defeated Moab, he measured them with the cord, making them lie on the ground. He measured two cords to kill and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the third cord⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the filling of a cord”</note> to let live.<note placement="foot">This method of selection must have been well known to the reader, but the exact procedure has been obscured over the millennia. It may be that one out of three lived through the process, only to become subservient</note> So Moab became servants of David, bringing tribute.

verses.name: II Samuel 8:3
verses.text: Then David struck down Hadadezer the son of Rehob, king of Zobah, when he went to restore his monument<note placement="foot">Hebrew “hand”</note> at the Euphrates River.

verses.name: II Samuel 8:4
verses.text: David captured from him one thousand and seven hundred horsemen and twenty thousand <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞foot soldiers⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “men of infantry”</note> David hamstrung all the chariot horses, but <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from him”</note> he spared a hundred chariot horses.

verses.name: II Samuel 8:5
verses.text: When Aram of Damascus came to help Hadadezer, the king of Zobah, David killed twenty-two thousand men of Aram.

verses.name: II Samuel 8:6
verses.text: David placed garrisons in Aram of Damascus, so Aram became servants of David, bringing tribute. Yahweh protected David everywhere he went.  <div eID="gen2473" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 8:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1793"/><div sID="gen2474" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1793"/>David took the small round gold shields which had <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞belonged⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “been”</note> to the servants of Hadadezer, and he brought them <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Samuel 8:8
verses.text: From Betah and from Berothai, the towns of Hadadezer, King David took very many bronze <transChange type="added">items</transChange>.  <div eID="gen2474" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 8:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1794"/><div sID="gen2475" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1794"/>When Toi, the king of Hamath, heard that David had defeated all the army of Hadadezer,

verses.name: II Samuel 8:10
verses.text: Toi sent Joram his son to King David <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to greet him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to ask peace for himself”</note> and to congratulate him because he had fought against Hadadezer and defeated him; <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞for Hadadezer had often been at war with Toi⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “for Hadadezer was a man of wars with Toi”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞He brought with him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “In his hand were”</note> objects of silver and objects of gold and objects of bronze.

verses.name: II Samuel 8:11
verses.text: King David dedicated them also to Yahweh <transChange type="added">along</transChange> with the silver and the gold that he had dedicated from all of the nations which he had subdued;

verses.name: II Samuel 8:12
verses.text: from Aram and from Moab and from the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> and from <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines and from Amalek and from the plunder of Hadadezer the son of Rehob, the king of Zobah.

verses.name: II Samuel 8:13
verses.text: So David made a name for himself when he returned from defeating Aram in the Valley of Salt, eighteen thousand.

verses.name: II Samuel 8:14
verses.text: He put garrisons in Edom; all over Edom he put garrisons, and all of Edom became servants of David. Yahweh protected David wherever he went.  <div eID="gen2475" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 8:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1795"/><div sID="gen2476" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1795"/>David reigned over all of Israel, and he<note placement="foot">Hebrew “David”</note> was administering justice and righteousness for all his people.

verses.name: II Samuel 8:16
verses.text: Joab the son of Zeruiah <transChange type="added">was</transChange> over the army, and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud <transChange type="added">was</transChange> secretary.

verses.name: II Samuel 8:17
verses.text: Zadok the son of Ahitub and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar <transChange type="added">were</transChange> priests and Seraiah <transChange type="added">was</transChange> scribe.

verses.name: II Samuel 8:18
verses.text: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada <transChange type="added">was over</transChange> the Kerethites and the Pelethites, and the sons of David <transChange type="added">were</transChange> priests.  <chapter eID="2Sam.8"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 9:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1796"/><title type="x-s">David Cares for Mephibosheth</title> <div sID="gen2477" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1796"/>Then David said, “<transChange type="added">Is</transChange> there still anyone who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> left for the house of Saul that I may show loyal love to him for the sake of Jonathan?”

verses.name: II Samuel 9:2
verses.text: Now Saul’s household had a servant whose name <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Ziba, so they summoned him to David, and the king asked him, “<transChange type="added">Are</transChange> you Ziba?” He said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞At your service⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!”<note placement="foot">Literally “Your servant”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 9:3
verses.text: Then the king said, “But <transChange type="added">is</transChange> there still anyone of Saul’s household that I may show the loyal love of God with him?” And Ziba said to the king, “There <transChange type="added">is</transChange> still a son of Jonathan <transChange type="added">who is</transChange> lame in the feet.”

verses.name: II Samuel 9:4
verses.text: The king said to him, “Where <transChange type="added">is</transChange> he?” And Ziba said to the king, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞He <transChange type="added">is</transChange> here⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Look, he”</note> in the house of Makir the son of Ammiel in Lo Debar.”

verses.name: II Samuel 9:5
verses.text: So King David sent and brought him from the house of Makir the son of Ammiel from Lo Debar.

verses.name: II Samuel 9:6
verses.text: So Mephibosheth the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, came to David. And he fell on his face and did obeisance. David said, “Mephibosheth,” and he said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I am ready to serve you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “Here is your servant”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 9:7
verses.text: Then David said to him, “Don’t be afraid, for <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I will certainly show⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “doing I will do” or “showing I will show”</note> loyal love to you for the sake of Jonathan your father, and I will restore to you all the lands of Saul your father. And you shall always eat food at my table.”

verses.name: II Samuel 9:8
verses.text: Then he<note placement="foot">Mephibosheth</note> did obeisance and said, “What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> your servant that you have paid attention to the dead dog like me?”  <div eID="gen2477" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 9:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1797"/><div sID="gen2478" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1797"/>David summoned Ziba the servant of Saul and said to him, “All that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Saul’s and all his household I have given to the son of your master.

verses.name: II Samuel 9:10
verses.text: You shall till the land for him, you and your sons and your servants; you shall bring <transChange type="added">in the produce</transChange> and it shall be food for the son of your master that he may eat. But Mephibosheth the son of your master may always eat food at my table.” (Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty slaves.)

verses.name: II Samuel 9:11
verses.text: Ziba said to the king, “According to all that my master the king commands his servant, so your servant will do.” So Mephibosheth <transChange type="added">was</transChange> eating at his table as one of the sons of the king.

verses.name: II Samuel 9:12
verses.text: Now Mephibosheth had a young son whose name <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Micah, and all of the dwelling of the household of Ziba <transChange type="added">became</transChange> servants for Mephibosheth.

verses.name: II Samuel 9:13
verses.text: And Mephibosheth <transChange type="added">was</transChange> living in Jerusalem, because he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> continually eating at the table of the king, <transChange type="added">even though</transChange> he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> lame in both of his feet.  <chapter eID="2Sam.9"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 10:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1798"/><title type="x-s">The Ammonites Refuse David’s Loyal Love</title> <div sID="gen2479" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1798"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Afterwards the king of the Ammonites died⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “And it happened afterwards that the king of the sons of Ammon died”</note> and his son Hanun ruled in his place.

verses.name: II Samuel 10:2
verses.text: David said, “I will show loyal love with Hanun, the son of Nahash, as his father showed loyal love with me.” So David sent to console him concerning his father, by the hand of his servants. And the servants of David came to the land of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 10:3
verses.text: But the commanders of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> said to Hanun their master, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞In your opinion⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “In your eyes”</note> <transChange type="added">is</transChange> David honoring your father because he has sent condolences to you? <transChange type="added">Is</transChange> it not in order to search the city, to spy it out, and to overthrow it <transChange type="added">that</transChange> David sent his servants to you?”

verses.name: II Samuel 10:4
verses.text: Then Hanun took the servants of David, and he shaved off half of their beards and cut their garments off in the middle up to their buttocks, then sent them away.

verses.name: II Samuel 10:5
verses.text: When they told David, he sent to meet them, for the men were greatly ashamed. And the king said, “Remain in Jericho until your beards have grown, and then you can return.”  <div eID="gen2479" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 10:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1799"/><title type="x-s">Israel Fights Ammon and Aram</title> <div sID="gen2480" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1799"/>When the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> saw that they had become odious to David, the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> sent <transChange type="added">word</transChange> and hired Aram Beth-Rehob and Aram-Zobah, twenty thousand infantry; and <transChange type="added">they also hired</transChange> the king of Maacah, a thousand men, and the men of Tob, twelve thousand men.

verses.name: II Samuel 10:7
verses.text: When David heard, he sent Joab and all the army of mighty warriors.

verses.name: II Samuel 10:8
verses.text: The <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> came out and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞drew up a battle formation⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “drew up battle”</note> at the entrance of the gate, but Aram-Zobah and Rehob and the men of Tob and Maacah <transChange type="added">were</transChange> alone in the open field.

verses.name: II Samuel 10:9
verses.text: When Joab saw that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the battle was to be fought on two fronts⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the face of the battle was against him in front and in the rear”</note> he chose from all the members of the elite troops of Israel and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞lined them up for battle⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “arrayed”</note> to meet Aram.

verses.name: II Samuel 10:10
verses.text: The rest of the army he placed into the hand of his brother Abishai, who <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞arranged them in battle lines⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “arrayed”</note> to meet the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 10:11
verses.text: Then he said, “If Aram <transChange type="added">is</transChange> stronger than I <transChange type="added">am</transChange>, you must become my deliverer; but if the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> <transChange type="added">are</transChange> too strong for you, then I will come to rescue you.

verses.name: II Samuel 10:12
verses.text: Be strong, and let us strengthen ourselves for the sake of the people and for the sake of the cities of our God. May Yahweh do <transChange type="added">what is</transChange> good in his eyes.

verses.name: II Samuel 10:13
verses.text: Joab and all the people who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him moved forward into the battle against Aram, and they fled from before him.

verses.name: II Samuel 10:14
verses.text: When the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> saw that Aram had fled, they fled from before Abishai and entered the city. Then Joab returned from fighting against the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> and came to Jerusalem.  <div eID="gen2480" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 10:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1800"/><title type="x-s">The Arameans Regroup for Attack</title> <div sID="gen2481" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1800"/>When the Arameans saw that they <transChange type="added">were</transChange> defeated before Israel, they gathered themselves together.

verses.name: II Samuel 10:16
verses.text: Then Hadadezer sent and brought out the Arameans who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> beyond the Euphrates, and they came to Helam. Now Shobach, the commander of the army of Hadadezer, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞was at their head⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “before the face of them”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 10:17
verses.text: David <transChange type="added">was</transChange> told, so he gathered all Israel and crossed over the Jordan and came to Helam. Aram <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞arranged themselves in battle lines⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “arrayed”</note> to meet David, and they fought with him.

verses.name: II Samuel 10:18
verses.text: And Aram fled before Israel, and David killed from <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Arameans seven hundred chariot teams and forty thousand horsemen. He struck down Shobach, the commander of his army, and he died there.

verses.name: II Samuel 10:19
verses.text: When all the kings, the servants of Hadadezer, saw that he had been defeated before Israel, they made peace with Israel and served them, and Aram <transChange type="added">was</transChange> afraid to help the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> any longer.  <chapter eID="2Sam.10"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 11:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1801"/><title type="x-s">David Commits Adultery with Bathsheba</title> <div sID="gen2482" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1801"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞It came about in the spring⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “And it happened at the turn of the year”</note> at the time <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞kings⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">According to the reading tradition (<hi type="italic">Qere)</hi>; <hi type="italic">Kethib</hi> has “angels” or “messengers”</note> go out, David sent Joab and his servants with him and all of Israel. They ravaged all of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> and besieged Rabbah, but David <transChange type="added">was</transChange> remaining in Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Samuel 11:2
verses.text: It happened <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞late one afternoon⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “at the time of the evening”</note> that David got up from his bed and walked about on the roof of the king’s house, and he saw a woman bathing on her<note placement="foot">Hebrew “the”</note> roof. Now the woman <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞was very beautiful⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “very good of appearance”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 11:3
verses.text: David sent and inquired about the woman, and <transChange type="added">someone</transChange> said, “<transChange type="added">Is</transChange> this not Bathsheba the daughter of Eliam, the wife of Uriah the Hittite?”

verses.name: II Samuel 11:4
verses.text: Then David sent messengers and took her, and she came to him, and he slept with her. (Now she had been purifying herself from her uncleanness.) And she returned to her house.

verses.name: II Samuel 11:5
verses.text: The woman became pregnant, and she sent and told David, and she said, “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> pregnant.”

verses.name: II Samuel 11:6
verses.text: So David sent to Joab, “Send Uriah the Hittite to me.” So Joab sent Uriah to David.

verses.name: II Samuel 11:7
verses.text: Uriah came to him, and David asked <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞how Joab and the army fared and how the war was going⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “as far as the peace of Joab, as far as the peace of the army, and as far as the peace of the battle”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 11:8
verses.text: David said to Uriah, “Go down to your house, and wash your feet.” So Uriah went out from the king’s house, and a gift from the king went out after him.

verses.name: II Samuel 11:9
verses.text: But Uriah slept <transChange type="added">at</transChange> the entrance of the king’s house with all the servants of his master and did not go down to his house.

verses.name: II Samuel 11:10
verses.text: They told David, “Uriah did not go down to his house.” David said to Uriah, “<transChange type="added">Are</transChange> you not coming from a journey? Why did you not go down to your house?”

verses.name: II Samuel 11:11
verses.text: Uriah said to David, “The ark and Israel and Judah <transChange type="added">are</transChange> living in the booths; and my lord Joab and the servants of my lord <transChange type="added">are</transChange> camping on the surface of the open field; and I, shall I go to my house to eat and to drink and to sleep with my wife? <transChange type="added">By</transChange> your life and the life of your soul, I surely will not do this thing.”

verses.name: II Samuel 11:12
verses.text: David said to Uriah, “Remain here <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞today⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “also the day”</note> and tomorrow I will send you away.” So Uriah remained in Jerusalem on that day and the next.

verses.name: II Samuel 11:13
verses.text: David invited him, and he ate and drank in his presence <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞so that he became drunk⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “and he made him drunk”</note> and he went out in the evening to lie on his bed with the servants of his lord, but he did not go down to his house.

verses.name: II Samuel 11:14
verses.text: And it happened in the morning, David wrote a letter to Joab, and he sent it by the hand of Uriah.

verses.name: II Samuel 11:15
verses.text: He had written in the letter, “Put Uriah in the front, in the face of the fiercest fighting, then draw back from behind him so that he may be struck down and die.”  <div eID="gen2482" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 11:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1802"/><div sID="gen2483" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1802"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞When Joab was besieging⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it happened at the besieging of Joab”</note> the city, he put Uriah toward the place which he knew <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞there were valiant warriors⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “there were men of ability”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 11:17
verses.text: The men of the city came out and fought with Joab. Some from the army from the servants of David fell; Uriah the Hittite also died.

verses.name: II Samuel 11:18
verses.text: Joab sent and told David all of the news of the battle.

verses.name: II Samuel 11:19
verses.text: He instructed the messenger, saying, “As you are finishing to speak all the news of the battle to the king,

verses.name: II Samuel 11:20
verses.text: if the anger of the king rises and he says to you, ‘Why did you go near the city to fight? Did you not know that they would shoot from <transChange type="added">atop</transChange> the wall?

verses.name: II Samuel 11:21
verses.text: Who killed Abimelech the son of Jerub-bosheth,<note placement="foot">In putting words in David’s mouth, Joab alludes to the story of Abimelech the son of Gideon from Judg 9:52–55. Though Gideon was also known as Jerub-ba’al, Joab conventionally substitutes <hi type="italic">bosheth</hi> (shame) for Ba’al to avoid naming the Canaanite deity</note> if not a woman who threw an upper millstone on him from <transChange type="added">atop</transChange> the wall and he died at Thebez? Why did you go near the wall?’ Then you shall say, ‘Your servant Uriah the Hittite also died.’ ”

verses.name: II Samuel 11:22
verses.text: Then the messenger left, and he came and told David all that Joab had sent him <transChange type="added">to say</transChange>.

verses.name: II Samuel 11:23
verses.text: The messenger said to David, “Because <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the men overpowered us⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the men were superior over us”</note> the men came out to us in the field, but <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞we forced them back⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “we were upon them”</note> to the entrance of the gate.

verses.name: II Samuel 11:24
verses.text: The archers shot at your servant from <transChange type="added">atop</transChange> the wall, and some of the servants of the king died; your servant Uriah the Hittite also died.”

verses.name: II Samuel 11:25
verses.text: Then David said to the messenger, “Thus you shall say to Joab, ‘<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Do not feel badly about this matter⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “Do not let his matter be evil in your eyes”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞now one and then another⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for as this and as this”</note> the sword will devour. Intensify your attack on the city and overthrow it.’ ” And he encouraged him.

verses.name: II Samuel 11:26
verses.text: When the wife of Uriah heard that Uriah her husband <transChange type="added">was</transChange> dead, she mourned over her husband.

verses.name: II Samuel 11:27
verses.text: When the mourning <transChange type="added">was</transChange> over, David sent and brought her to his household, and she became his wife and bore him a son. But the thing which David had done <transChange type="added">was</transChange> evil in the eyes of Yahweh.  <chapter eID="2Sam.11"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 12:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1803"/><title type="x-s">Nathan Reproves David</title> <div sID="gen2484" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1803"/>So Yahweh sent Nathan to David, and he came to him and said, “Two men were in a certain city; one <transChange type="added">was</transChange> rich and the other <transChange type="added">was</transChange> poor.

verses.name: II Samuel 12:2
verses.text: The rich <transChange type="added">man</transChange> had very many flocks and herds,

verses.name: II Samuel 12:3
verses.text: but the poor <transChange type="added">man</transChange> had nothing except for one small ewe lamb which he had bought. He had nurtured her, and she grew up with him and with his children together. She used to eat from his morsel and drink from his cup, and she used to lie in his lap and became like a daughter for him.

verses.name: II Samuel 12:4
verses.text: And a visitor came to the rich man, but he <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞was reluctant⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “felt sorry”</note> to take from his flocks or from his herds to prepare a meal for the traveler when he came to him. So he took the ewe lamb of the poor man and prepared it for the man who had come to him.”

verses.name: II Samuel 12:5
verses.text: Then <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the anger of David was kindled⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the nose of David became very hot”</note> against the man, and he said to Nathan, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞As Yahweh lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “The life of Yahweh”</note> the man who has done this <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞deserves to die⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!<note placement="foot">Literally “is a son of death”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 12:6
verses.text: He shall restore the ewe lamb fourfold because he has done this thing, and because he had no pity.”

verses.name: II Samuel 12:7
verses.text: Then Nathan said to him, “You <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the man! Thus says Yahweh the God of Israel: ‘I anointed you as king over Israel, and I delivered you from the hand of Saul.

verses.name: II Samuel 12:8
verses.text: I gave you the household of your master and the women of your master into your lap. I also gave you the house of Israel and Judah; if <transChange type="added">that had been too</transChange> little, I would have added to you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞much more⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “as here and as here”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 12:9
verses.text: Why have you despised the word of Yahweh by doing evil in his eyes?<note placement="foot">Thus <hi type="italic">Kethib</hi>; the reading tradition (<hi type="italic">Qere)</hi> reads “my eyes”</note> Uriah the Hittite you have struck down with the sword, and his wife you have taken to yourself as wife! You have killed him with the sword of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 12:10
verses.text: So then, a sword will not turn away from your house forever, because you have despised me and have taken the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be your wife!’

verses.name: II Samuel 12:11
verses.text: Thus says Yahweh, ‘Look, I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> going to raise up evil against you from <transChange type="added">within</transChange> your house, and I will take your women before your eyes, and I will give them to your neighbor, and he shall sleep with your wives <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in broad daylight⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “before the eyes of this sun”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 12:12
