verses.text: Though you did this in secret, I will do this thing before all of Israel <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in broad daylight⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!’ ”<note placement="foot">Literally “before the sun”</note>  <div eID="gen2484" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 12:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1804"/><title type="x-s">David Repents, But the Child Dies</title> <div sID="gen2485" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1804"/>Then David said to Nathan, “I have sinned against Yahweh!”<note placement="foot">See Pss 32:1–5; 51:1–13</note> Nathan said to David, “Yahweh has also forgiven your sin; you shall not die.

verses.name: II Samuel 12:14
verses.text: But because you have <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞utterly scorned⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “scorning you have scorned.” The term “enemies of” in the MT is likely a textual corruption and is deleted here</note> Yahweh in this matter, the son born for you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞will certainly die⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “dying will die” (compare Gen 2:17)</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 12:15
verses.text: Then Nathan went to his house, and Yahweh struck the child that the wife of Uriah bore for David, and he became ill.

verses.name: II Samuel 12:16
verses.text: David pleaded <transChange type="added">with</transChange> God on behalf of the boy and David fasted. He went to spend the night and lay upon the ground.

verses.name: II Samuel 12:17
verses.text: The elders of his household stood over him to lift him up from the ground, but he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> not willing, and he did not eat <transChange type="added">any</transChange> food with them.

verses.name: II Samuel 12:18
verses.text: It happened on the seventh day that the child died, and the servants of David <transChange type="added">were</transChange> afraid to tell him that the child <transChange type="added">was</transChange> dead, for they said, “Look, when the child <transChange type="added">was</transChange> alive, we spoke to him, but he would not listen to our voice. How can we tell him, ‘The child <transChange type="added">is</transChange> dead’? He may do <transChange type="added">something</transChange> evil.”

verses.name: II Samuel 12:19
verses.text: When David saw that his servants <transChange type="added">were</transChange> whispering together, he realized that the child <transChange type="added">was</transChange> dead. Then David said to his servants, “<transChange type="added">Is</transChange> the child dead?” And they said, “He <transChange type="added">is</transChange> dead.”

verses.name: II Samuel 12:20
verses.text: David stood up from the ground and washed and anointed himself and changed his clothing. Then he went <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the house of Yahweh and worshiped, and he went to his <transChange type="added">own</transChange> house. He asked, so they served him food, and he ate.

verses.name: II Samuel 12:21
verses.text: Then his servants said to him, “What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> this thing that you have done? While the child <transChange type="added">was</transChange> alive, you fasted and wept; <transChange type="added">now</transChange> that the child has died, you get up and eat food!”

verses.name: II Samuel 12:22
verses.text: He said, “When the child <transChange type="added">was</transChange> still alive, I fasted and I wept because I thought, ‘Who knows? Yahweh may have mercy on me that the child will live.’

verses.name: II Samuel 12:23
verses.text: But now he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> dead. Why <transChange type="added">should I be</transChange> fasting? <transChange type="added">Am</transChange> I able to return him again? I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> going to him, but he cannot return to me.”

verses.name: II Samuel 12:24
verses.text: David consoled Bathsheba his wife, and he went to her and slept with her. She bore a son, and he called<note placement="foot">So <hi type="italic">Kethib</hi>; <hi type="italic">Qere</hi> reads “she called”</note> him Solomon, and Yahweh loved him.

verses.name: II Samuel 12:25
verses.text: He sent <transChange type="added">word</transChange> by the hand of Nathan the prophet, so he called him Jedidiah<note placement="foot">Jedidiah means “beloved of Yahweh”</note> because of Yahweh.  <div eID="gen2485" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 12:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1805"/><title type="x-s">Battle with the Ammonites</title> <div sID="gen2486" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1805"/>And Joab fought against Rabbah of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> and he captured <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the royal city⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “city of the kingship”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 12:27
verses.text: Then Joab sent messengers to David and said, “We have fought against Rabbah, and we captured the city of the waters.

verses.name: II Samuel 12:28
verses.text: So then, gather the remainder of the army and encamp against the city and capture it, lest I capture the city and my name be proclaimed over it.”

verses.name: II Samuel 12:29
verses.text: So David gathered all of the army, and he went to Rabbah and fought against it and captured it.

verses.name: II Samuel 12:30
verses.text: He took the crown of their king from his head. (Now its weight <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a talent of gold, and there <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a precious stone <transChange type="added">in it</transChange> and it <transChange type="added">was</transChange> put on David’s head.) He brought out the plunder of the city <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in great abundance⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “very many”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 12:31
verses.text: He also brought out the people who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in it and put them to the saws and to the iron picks and to the iron axes, and he sent them to the place of the brickmakers. Thus he used to do to all the cities of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> and he and all of the army returned to Jerusalem.  <chapter eID="2Sam.12"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 13:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1806"/><title type="x-s">Amnon Assaults His Sister Tamar</title> <div sID="gen2487" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1806"/>It happened afterwards that Absalom the son of David had a beautiful sister whose name <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Tamar, and Amnon the son of David fell in love with her.

verses.name: II Samuel 13:2
verses.text: And Amnon <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞was so frustrated that he felt ill⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “was distressed to the point of sickness”</note> because of Tamar his sister, because she <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a virgin, and it <transChange type="added">was</transChange> too difficult in Amnon’s eyes to do anything with her.

verses.name: II Samuel 13:3
verses.text: Now Amnon had a friend whose name <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Jonadab the son of Shimeah, the brother of David. (Now Jonadab <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a very crafty man.)

verses.name: II Samuel 13:4
verses.text: And he said to him, “Why <transChange type="added">are</transChange> you so sullen <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞every morning⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “in the morning, in the morning”</note> O son of the king? Will you not tell me?” And Amnon said to him, “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> in love with Tamar, the sister of my brother Absalom.”

verses.name: II Samuel 13:5
verses.text: Then Jonadab said to him, “Lie down on your bed and appear ill. If your father comes to see you, you shall say to him, ‘Please let Tamar my sister come and give me food to eat, and let her prepare the food before my eyes, in order that I may see it and eat from her hand.’ ”

verses.name: II Samuel 13:6
verses.text: So Amnon lay down and pretended to be ill, and the king came to see him. Amnon said to the king, “Please let Tamar my sister come, and let her bake two cakes before my eyes that I may eat from her hand.”

verses.name: II Samuel 13:7
verses.text: So David sent to the house for Tamar, saying, “Please go to the house of Amnon your brother and prepare food for him.”

verses.name: II Samuel 13:8
verses.text: Tamar went to the house of Amnon her brother. Now he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> lying down, and she took the dough and kneaded <transChange type="added">it</transChange> and made cakes before his eyes, and she baked the cakes.

verses.name: II Samuel 13:9
verses.text: Then she took the pan and poured it out before him, but he refused to eat. Then Amnon said, “Let all <transChange type="added">the</transChange> men go out from me.” So all <transChange type="added">the</transChange> men went out from him.

verses.name: II Samuel 13:10
verses.text: Then Amnon said to Tamar, “Bring the food <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the private room that I may eat from your hand.” So Tamar took the cakes which she had made and brought them to Amnon her brother in<note placement="foot">Hebrew “to”</note> the private room.

verses.name: II Samuel 13:11
verses.text: When she brought them near to him to eat, he took hold of her and said to her, “Come, lie with me, my sister!”

verses.name: II Samuel 13:12
verses.text: Then Tamar said to him, “No, my brother! Do not force me, for such a thing has not been done in Israel. Do not do this disgraceful thing!

verses.name: II Samuel 13:13
verses.text: As for me, where should I take my disgrace? You will be as one of the fools in Israel. So please, speak to the king, for he will not withhold me from you.”

verses.name: II Samuel 13:14
verses.text: But he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> not willing to listen to her voice. He <transChange type="added">was</transChange> stronger than she, and he forced her and lay with her.  <div eID="gen2487" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 13:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1807"/><div sID="gen2488" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1807"/>Then Amnon hated her <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞very deeply⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “with a great hatred”</note> for the hatred with which he hated her <transChange type="added">was</transChange> greater than <transChange type="added">the</transChange> love with which he had loved her. So Amnon said to her, “Get up <transChange type="added">and</transChange> go.”

verses.name: II Samuel 13:16
verses.text: She said to him, “No, because this evil in sending me away <transChange type="added">is</transChange> greater than the other you have done to me.” But he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> not willing to listen to her.

verses.name: II Samuel 13:17
verses.text: Then he called his young man who <transChange type="added">was</transChange> serving him and said, “Please send this woman from me to the outside, and bolt the door behind her!”

verses.name: II Samuel 13:18
verses.text: Now there <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a long-sleeved robe on her, for so they clothed the daughters of the king who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> virgins, in robes. His servant put her outside, and he bolted the door behind her.

verses.name: II Samuel 13:19
verses.text: Tamar put ashes on her head, and she tore the long-sleeved robe which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> on her. She put her hand on her head, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞she went away, crying out as she went⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “she went, going and crying aloud”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 13:20
verses.text: Absalom her brother said to her, “<transChange type="added">Was</transChange> Amnon your brother with you? But now, my sister, be quiet; he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> your brother. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Do not take this matter to heart⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “Do not place/set your heart to this matter”</note> So Tamar remained a desolate woman in the house of Absalom her brother.  <div eID="gen2488" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 13:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1808"/><title type="x-s">Absalom Kills Amnon</title> <div sID="gen2489" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1808"/>Now King David heard all these things, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he became very angry⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “it became very hot for him”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 13:22
verses.text: Absalom did not speak with Amnon <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞either bad or good⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “as far as from bad and up to good”</note> for Absalom hated Amnon <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞over the matter when⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “because of the thing that”</note> he raped Tamar his sister.

verses.name: II Samuel 13:23
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞About two full years later⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “And it happened at two years of days”</note> Absalom’s shearers were in Baal Hazor, which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> near Ephraim, and Absalom summoned all the sons of the king.

verses.name: II Samuel 13:24
verses.text: Then Absalom went to the king and said, “Look, here <transChange type="added">are</transChange> your servant’s shearers; please let the king and his servants go with your servant.

verses.name: II Samuel 13:25
verses.text: The king said to Absalom, “No my son, not all of us shall go, so that we not be a burden to you.” And he urged him, but he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> not willing to go, but he blessed him.

verses.name: II Samuel 13:26
verses.text: So Absalom said, “But <transChange type="added">will you</transChange> not let Amnon my brother go with us?” And the king said to him, “Why should he go with you?”

verses.name: II Samuel 13:27
verses.text: But Absalom pressed him, so he sent Amnon with him and all of the sons of the king.

verses.name: II Samuel 13:28
verses.text: Absalom commanded his servants, saying, “Please watch. At the moment the heart of Amnon <transChange type="added">is</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞tipsy⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “good”</note> with wine, then I shall say to you, ‘Strike Amnon down,’ and you shall kill him! Don’t be afraid. Is it not I myself who has commanded you? Be courageous and be <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞valiant!⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “as sons of ability”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 13:29
verses.text: So Absalom’s servants did to Amnon just as Absalom commanded, and all the sons of the king got up, and each mounted his mule and fled.  <div eID="gen2489" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 13:30
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1809"/><div sID="gen2490" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1809"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞While they were on the way⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “And it happened they were on the way”</note> the message came to David, “Absalom has killed all the sons of the king, and not one of them <transChange type="added">was</transChange> left.”

verses.name: II Samuel 13:31
verses.text: Then the king rose and tore his garments, and he lay on the ground, and all his servants standing by <transChange type="added">were</transChange> tearing their garments.

verses.name: II Samuel 13:32
verses.text: Then Jonadab the son of Shimeah, the brother of David, responded and said, “My lord should not think that all the young men, the sons of the king, <transChange type="added">are</transChange> dead, because only Amnon <transChange type="added">is</transChange> dead. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Absalom was talking about it⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “For it was on the mouth of Absalom”</note> as it was being determined from the day he<note placement="foot">Amnon</note> raped Tamar his sister.

verses.name: II Samuel 13:33
verses.text: So then, let not my lord the king set his heart on this matter, thinking, ‘All the sons of the king <transChange type="added">are</transChange> dead,’ for only Amnon alone <transChange type="added">is</transChange> dead.”  <div eID="gen2490" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 13:34
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1810"/><title type="x-s">Absalom Flees</title> <div sID="gen2491" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1810"/>So Absalom fled, and the young man who <transChange type="added">was</transChange> keeping watch lifted up his eyes and saw, and there were many people coming from the road behind him from the side of the mountain.

verses.name: II Samuel 13:35
verses.text: Jonadab said to the king, “Look, the sons of the king have come. According to the word of your servant, so it has come about.”

verses.name: II Samuel 13:36
verses.text: When he finished speaking, look, the sons of the king came and they lifted up their voice and wept. Also, the king and all his servants wept a very great weeping.

verses.name: II Samuel 13:37
verses.text: Absalom fled and went to Talmai the son of Ammihur, the king of Geshur. <transChange type="added">David</transChange> mourned over his son <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞day after day⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “all the days”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 13:38
verses.text: But Absalom had fled and went <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Geshur, and he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> there three years.

verses.name: II Samuel 13:39
verses.text: King David longed to go out to Absalom, for he was consoled that Amnon had died.  <chapter eID="2Sam.13"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 14:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1811"/><title type="x-s">Joab Plots to Reconcile David with Absalom</title> <div sID="gen2492" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1811"/>Joab the son of Zeruiah realized that the mind of the king <transChange type="added">was</transChange> on Absalom.

verses.name: II Samuel 14:2
verses.text: So Joab sent to Tekoa and took from there a wise woman, and he said to her, “Please pretend to mourn and put on garments of mourning. You should not anoint yourself <transChange type="added">with</transChange> oil, and you must act like this woman who has been mourning over the dead for <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a long time⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “many days”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 14:3
verses.text: Then you must go to the king and speak to him according to this word.” <transChange type="added">Thus</transChange> Joab put the words in her mouth.  <div eID="gen2492" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 14:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1812"/><div sID="gen2493" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1812"/>So the Tekoite woman spoke to the king, and she fell on her face to the ground and did obeisance. She said, “Help me, O king!”

verses.name: II Samuel 14:5
verses.text: Then the king asked her, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞What do you want⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?”<note placement="foot">Literally “What is for you”</note> And she said, “Truly I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> a widow, and my husband <transChange type="added">is</transChange> dead.

verses.name: II Samuel 14:6
verses.text: Your servant had two sons, and they both fought in the open field, and there <transChange type="added">was</transChange> no one <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to part them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “to save between them”</note> One struck the other and killed him.

verses.name: II Samuel 14:7
verses.text: And look, all of the family has risen up against your servant, and they said, ‘Give up the one who struck his brother, that we may kill him in exchange for the life of his brother whom he murdered. We will also wipe out the heir,’ and so they would put out my embers which remain, by not preserving for my husband a name and a remnant on the face of the earth.”  <div eID="gen2493" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 14:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1813"/><div sID="gen2494" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1813"/>Then the king said to the woman, “Go to your house, and I myself will give the command concerning you.”

verses.name: II Samuel 14:9
verses.text: The Tekoite woman said to the king, “On me, my lord the king, <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the guilt, and on the house of my father, but the king on<note placement="foot">Hebrew “and”</note> his throne <transChange type="added">is</transChange> innocent.”

verses.name: II Samuel 14:10
verses.text: The king said, “<transChange type="added">Whoever</transChange> has spoken to you, bring him to me, and he will not touch you again.”

verses.name: II Samuel 14:11
verses.text: Then she said, “Please may the king remember Yahweh your God, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to prevent the increase of blood avengers who kill⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “from making numerous the avenger of blood to kill”</note> so that they not wipe out my son.” He said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞As Yahweh lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “The life of Yahweh”</note> surely not one hair shall fall from your son to the ground.”

verses.name: II Samuel 14:12
verses.text: The woman said, “Please let your servant speak a word to my lord the king.” And he said, “Speak.”

verses.name: II Samuel 14:13
verses.text: The woman said, “But why have you plotted like this against the people of God? By speaking this word, he is guilty not to bring back his banished one.

verses.name: II Samuel 14:14
verses.text: For <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞we must certainly die⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “dying we must die”</note> and <transChange type="added">we are</transChange> as the waters spilled to the ground which cannot be gathered. God will not take a life but devises plans for a banished person not to be cast out from him.

verses.name: II Samuel 14:15
verses.text: Now I have come to speak this word to my lord the king, because the people made me afraid, and your servant thought, ‘I will speak to the king, perhaps the king will grant<note placement="foot">Hebrew “do/make”</note> the request of his servant.

verses.name: II Samuel 14:16
verses.text: For the king will listen, to deliver his servant from the hand of the man <transChange type="added">who seeks</transChange> to destroy me and my son together from the inheritance of God.’

verses.name: II Samuel 14:17
verses.text: Your servant also thought, ‘May the word of my lord the king <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞bring rest⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “become a rest”</note> for as an angel of God, so is my lord the king, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to sense what is good and what is bad⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.’<note placement="foot">Literally “to hear the good and the bad”</note> May Yahweh your God be with you.”

verses.name: II Samuel 14:18
verses.text: The king answered and said to the woman, “Please do not withhold from me a thing which I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> about to ask you.” The woman said, “Please let my lord the king speak.”

verses.name: II Samuel 14:19
verses.text: The king asked, “<transChange type="added">Was</transChange> the hand of Joab with you in all of this?” The woman answered and said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞As your soul lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “The life of your soul”</note> my lord the king, surely <transChange type="added">one cannot</transChange> go to the right or to the left from all that my lord the king has spoken. Yes, your servant Joab himself commanded me, and he put all of these words in the mouth of your servant.

verses.name: II Samuel 14:20
verses.text: In order <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to change the situation⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to turn the face of the thing”</note> your servant Joab did this thing. But my lord <transChange type="added">has</transChange> wisdom, as the wisdom of an angel of God, to know all that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> on the earth.”

verses.name: II Samuel 14:21
verses.text: Then the king said to Joab, “Look, please, I will grant this thing. Go and bring back the young man Absalom.”

verses.name: II Samuel 14:22
verses.text: Joab fell with his face to the ground and did obeisance. And he blessed the king, and he<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Joab”</note> said, “Today your servant knows that I have found favor in your eyes, my lord the king, <transChange type="added">in</transChange> that the king has granted the request of his servant.”  <div eID="gen2494" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 14:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1814"/><title type="x-s">Absalom Returns to Jerusalem</title> <div sID="gen2495" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1814"/>Then Joab got up and went to Geshur and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Samuel 14:24
verses.text: The king said, “Let him go over to his house, and he may not see my face.” So Absalom went over to his house, and did not see the face of the king.

verses.name: II Samuel 14:25
verses.text: As far as Absalom, there was not a more handsome man in all of Israel to admire so much; from the sole of his foot up to his crown, there was no physical defect on him.

verses.name: II Samuel 14:26
verses.text: When he shaved his head, it would happen <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞every year⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “from the end of days for the days”</note> which he did because it was heavy on him, he would shave it off and weigh the hair of his head: two hundred shekels <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞by the king’s weight⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “by the stone of the king”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 14:27
verses.text: Three sons <transChange type="added">were</transChange> born to Absalom and one daughter, whose name <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Tamar. She <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a woman beautiful of appearance.

verses.name: II Samuel 14:28
verses.text: Absalom lived in Jerusalem <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞two full years⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “two years of days”</note> but he did not see the face of the king.

verses.name: II Samuel 14:29
verses.text: So Absalom sent for Joab, <transChange type="added">in order that he</transChange> send him to the king, but he was not willing to go to him. He sent again a second <transChange type="added">time</transChange>, but he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> not willing to go.

verses.name: II Samuel 14:30
verses.text: So he said to his servants, “Look at the tract of land of Joab <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞next to mine⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “toward my hand”</note> for he has barley plants there. Go, set it ablaze with fire.” So the servants of Absalom set the tract of land ablaze with fire.

verses.name: II Samuel 14:31
verses.text: Then Joab got up and went to Absalom, to the house, and said to him, “Why have your servants set my tract of land ablaze with fire?”

verses.name: II Samuel 14:32
verses.text: Absalom said to Joab, “Look, I have sent to you, saying, ‘Come here that I may send you to the king to say, “Why have I come from Geshur? It would be better for me if I <transChange type="added">were</transChange> still there.” ’ So then, let me see the face of the king; if there <transChange type="added">is</transChange> guilt in me, then let him kill me.”

verses.name: II Samuel 14:33
verses.text: So Joab went to the king and he told him. Then he summoned Absalom, and he came to the king, and he bowed down to him with his face to the ground before the king. Then the king kissed Absalom.  <chapter eID="2Sam.14"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 15:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1815"/><title type="x-s">Absalom Leads a Rebellion</title> <div sID="gen2496" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1815"/>It happened afterward that Absalom made himself a chariot with horses and fifty men running before him.

verses.name: II Samuel 15:2
verses.text: Absalom used to rise early in the morning, and he stood <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞beside⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “on hand of”</note> the road at the gate; <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞anyone⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “every man”</note> who had a legal dispute to bring to the king for judgment Absalom would call to him and say, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Where are you from?⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>”<note placement="foot">Literally “Where from this city are you?”</note> And he would say, “Your servant <transChange type="added">is</transChange> from one of the tribes of Israel.”

verses.name: II Samuel 15:3
verses.text: Then Absalom would say to him, “Look, your case <transChange type="added">is</transChange> good and right, but for you there is no hearing with the king.”

verses.name: II Samuel 15:4
verses.text: Then Absalom would say, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Oh, that someone would⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Who will …?”</note> appoint me as judge in the land, that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞anyone⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “every man”</note> might come to me who had a legal dispute or a case, and I would give him justice.”

verses.name: II Samuel 15:5
verses.text: It happened whenever anyone drew near to do obeisance to him, that he would stretch his hand and take hold of him and kiss him.

verses.name: II Samuel 15:6
verses.text: Absalom did like this to all of Israel who came to the king for judgment; so Absalom stole the hearts<note placement="foot">Hebrew “heart”</note> of the people of Israel.  <div eID="gen2496" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 15:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1816"/><div sID="gen2497" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1816"/>It happened at the end of four<note placement="foot">So LXX, followed by Syriac and Vulgate; MT has “forty”</note> years <transChange type="added">that</transChange> Absalom said to the king, “Please let me go and pay my vow which I have made to Yahweh in Hebron,

verses.name: II Samuel 15:8
verses.text: for your servant made a vow while I <transChange type="added">was</transChange> staying in Geshur in Aram, saying, ‘<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞If Yahweh will indeed let me return⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally (following <hi type="italic">Qere</hi>) “If returning Yahweh will return me”</note> to Jerusalem, then I will worship Yahweh.’ ”

verses.name: II Samuel 15:9
verses.text: Then the king said to him, “Go in peace.” So he got up and went to Hebron.

verses.name: II Samuel 15:10
verses.text: Then Absalom sent scouts throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, “When you hear the sound of the trumpet, you shall shout ‘Absalom has become king in Hebron!’ ”

verses.name: II Samuel 15:11
verses.text: Two hundred men from Jerusalem went with Absalom as invited guests, going in their innocence as they did not know anything.

verses.name: II Samuel 15:12
verses.text: Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, the advisor of David, from his city Giloh, while he offered the sacrifices. The conspiracy <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞grew in strength⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “became strong”</note> and the people were going and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞increasing⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “many”</note> with Absalom.  <div eID="gen2497" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 15:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1817"/><title type="x-s">David Flees from Jerusalem</title> <div sID="gen2498" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1817"/>Then the messenger came to David, saying, “The hearts<note placement="foot">Hebrew “heart”</note> of the men of Israel have gone after Absalom.”

verses.name: II Samuel 15:14
verses.text: Then David said to all his servants who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him in Jerusalem, “Get up and let us flee, for there will be no escape for us from Absalom! Hurry to go, otherwise he will come quickly and overtake us! And he will bring disaster on us and evil! He will attack the city with the edge of the sword!”

verses.name: II Samuel 15:15
verses.text: Then the servants of the king said to the king, “According to all that my lord the king chooses, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞your servants are ready to act⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!”<note placement="foot">Literally “here are your servants”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 15:16
verses.text: The king went out with<note placement="foot">Hebrew “and”</note> all his household <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞following him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “at his feet”</note> but the king left behind ten concubines to look after the house.

verses.name: II Samuel 15:17
verses.text: So the king went out with<note placement="foot">Hebrew “and”</note> all the people <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞following him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “at his feet”</note> and they stopped <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞at the last house⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “at the house of the distance”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 15:18
verses.text: All his servants <transChange type="added">were</transChange> passing <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞by him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>:<note placement="foot">Literally “on his hand”</note> all of the Kerethites and all of the Pelethites and all of the Gittites—six hundred men <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who had followed him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “who had come at his feet”</note> from Gath—passing <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before the king⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “on the face of the king”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 15:19
verses.text: The king said to Ittai the Gittite, “Why <transChange type="added">are</transChange> you also coming with us? Return and stay with the king, for you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> a foreigner; moreover, you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> an exile. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞You <transChange type="added">are</transChange> far from your place⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “You as far as your place”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 15:20
verses.text: Yesterday when you came and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞today⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the day”</note> I have caused you to wander by going with us. Now I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> going to where I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> going; return and let your brothers return. <transChange type="added">May</transChange> loyal love and faithfulness <transChange type="added">be</transChange> with you.”

verses.name: II Samuel 15:21
verses.text: But Ittai answered the king and said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞As Yahweh lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “The life of Yahweh”</note> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞my lord the king lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the life of my lord the king”</note> surely in the place wherever my lord the king shall be, if for death or if for life, surely there your servant will be.”

verses.name: II Samuel 15:22
verses.text: Then David said to Ittai, “Go and pass over.” So Ittai the Gittite passed over and all his men and all of the little children who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him.

verses.name: II Samuel 15:23
verses.text: All of the land <transChange type="added">was</transChange> weeping <transChange type="added">with</transChange> a loud voice as all the people <transChange type="added">were</transChange> passing by and the king <transChange type="added">was</transChange> crossing through the Wadi Kidron, and all the people <transChange type="added">were</transChange> passing <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞on the road to the wilderness⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “on the face of the road with the wilderness”</note>  <div eID="gen2498" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 15:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1818"/><title type="x-s">The Priests Offer Sacrifices for David</title> <div sID="gen2499" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1818"/>Suddenly Zadok <transChange type="added">was</transChange> there, and all of the Levites with him, carrying the ark of the covenant of God. They set the ark of God down, and Abiathar offered sacrifices until all the people passed out of the city.

verses.name: II Samuel 15:25
verses.text: The king said to Zadok, “Let the ark of God return to the city. If I find favor in the eyes of Yawheh, he will let me return and let me see him in his dwelling place.

verses.name: II Samuel 15:26
verses.text: But if he says, ‘I take no pleasure in you,’ then <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I am ready⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “here I am”</note> Let him do to me that which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> good in his eyes.

verses.name: II Samuel 15:27
verses.text: Then the king said to Zadok the priest, “<transChange type="added">Are</transChange> you a seer? Return to the city in peace, <transChange type="added">with</transChange> Ahimaaz your son and Jonathan the son of Abiathar, your two sons with you.

verses.name: II Samuel 15:28
verses.text: See, I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> waiting at the fords of the wilderness until a word comes from you all to inform me.”

verses.name: II Samuel 15:29
verses.text: So Zadok and Abiathar returned the ark of God to Jerusalem and they remained there.  <div eID="gen2499" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 15:30
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1819"/><title type="x-s">Hushai Offers to Serve King David</title> <div sID="gen2500" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1819"/>Now David <transChange type="added">was</transChange> going up on the Ascent of the Olives, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞weeping as he went⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “going up and weeping”</note> with his head covered and going barefoot. All the people who were with him each covered their head <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞and wept as they went⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “going up and weeping”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 15:31
verses.text: Now David <transChange type="added">was</transChange> told, “Ahithophel <transChange type="added">was</transChange> among the conspirators with Absalom.” Then David said, “Please frustrate the counsel of Ahithophel, O Yahweh.”

verses.name: II Samuel 15:32
verses.text: It happened that as David <transChange type="added">was</transChange> coming up to the summit where he used to worship God, suddenly Hushai the Arkite <transChange type="added">was</transChange> there to meet him. His coat <transChange type="added">was</transChange> torn and dirt <transChange type="added">was</transChange> on his head.

verses.name: II Samuel 15:33
verses.text: David said to him, “If you move on with me, you will be a burden to me,

verses.name: II Samuel 15:34
verses.text: but if you want to return to the city and say to Absalom, ‘I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> your servant, O king. I used to be a servant of your father, but from then and now I <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> your servant,’ then you can frustrate the counsel of Ahithophel for me.

verses.name: II Samuel 15:35
verses.text: <transChange type="added">Will</transChange> not Zadok and Abiathar the priests <transChange type="added">be</transChange> with you there? It shall be that all the words you hear from the house of the king you shall tell Zadok and Abiathar the priests.

verses.name: II Samuel 15:36
verses.text: Look, there with them <transChange type="added">are</transChange> their two sons, Ahimaaz of Zadok and Jonathan of Abiathar. You shall send to me <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞by means of them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by their hand”</note> all the words that you hear.”

verses.name: II Samuel 15:37
verses.text: So Hushai the friend of David came to the city <transChange type="added">as</transChange> Absalom was entering Jerusalem.  <chapter eID="2Sam.15"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 16:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1820"/><title type="x-s">Ziba Brings Provisions</title> <div sID="gen2501" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1820"/>Now David passed a little from beyond the summit, and suddenly Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth <transChange type="added">was</transChange> there to meet him <transChange type="added">with</transChange> a pair of saddled donkeys; on them <transChange type="added">were</transChange> two hundred loaves of bread and a hundred raisin cakes, <transChange type="added">with</transChange> a hundred summer fruits and a skin of wine.

verses.name: II Samuel 16:2
verses.text: The king said to Ziba, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞What do you want to accomplish by bringing these⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?”<note placement="foot">Literally “What are these to you?”</note> And Ziba said, “The donkeys <transChange type="added">are</transChange> for the king’s household to ride <transChange type="added">on</transChange>; the bread and the summer fruit <transChange type="added">are</transChange> for the young men to eat, and the wine <transChange type="added">is</transChange> for the faint in the wilderness to drink.

verses.name: II Samuel 16:3
verses.text: Then the king said, “Where <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the son of your lord?” And Ziba said to the king, “He <transChange type="added">is</transChange> living in Jerusalem for he said, ‘Today the house of Israel shall return the kingdom of my father to me.’ ”

verses.name: II Samuel 16:4
verses.text: The king said to Ziba, “Look, all that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Mephibosheth’s is yours.” Ziba said, “I hereby do obeisance; may I find favor in your eyes, my lord the king.”  <div eID="gen2501" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 16:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1821"/><title type="x-s">Shimei Curses David</title> <div sID="gen2502" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1821"/>King David came up to Bahurim and suddenly a man from there <transChange type="added">was</transChange> coming out from the family of the house of Saul, and his name <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Shimei the son of Gera. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞He was cursing as he came out⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “He was coming out, coming out and cursing”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 16:6
verses.text: And he threw stones at David and at all the servants of King David and at all the people and at all the mighty warriors on his right and on his left.

verses.name: II Samuel 16:7
verses.text: Shimei said while cursing him, “Go out, go out, <transChange type="added">you</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞man of bloodshed⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “man of bloods”</note> you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞man of wickedness⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “and man of the wickedness”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 16:8
verses.text: Yahweh has returned on you all the blood of the household of Saul <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞whom you have supplanted as king⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “who you have reigned in place of him”</note> and Yahweh has given the kingship into the hand of Absalom your son. Look, you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> in disaster for you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> a man of blood.”

verses.name: II Samuel 16:9
verses.text: Then Abishai the son of Zeruiah said to the king, “Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? Please let me go over and take off his head.”

verses.name: II Samuel 16:10
verses.text: The king said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞What do we have in common⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “What is for me and what is for you”</note> sons of Zeruiah? If<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Because”</note> he curses because Yahweh has said to him ‘Curse David,’ who can say, “Why have you done this?”

verses.name: II Samuel 16:11
verses.text: David said to Abishai and to all his servants, “Look, my son who came out of my loins<note placement="foot">Hebrew “intestines”</note> is seeking my life. Now <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as far as⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and even that now”</note> <transChange type="added">this</transChange> Benjaminite, leave him alone and let him curse, for Yahweh has spoken to him.

verses.name: II Samuel 16:12
verses.text: Perhaps Yahweh will look <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in my eye⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">According to the reading tradition (<hi type="italic">Qere)</hi>; <hi type="italic">Kethib</hi> has “at my guilt”</note> and repay good for me in place of his curse this day.

verses.name: II Samuel 16:13
verses.text: Then David and his men went on the road, with Shimei going on the side of the hill beside him, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞cursing as he went⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “going and cursing”</note> He threw stones beside him and threw<note placement="foot">Hebrew “flung”</note> dust in the air.

verses.name: II Samuel 16:14
verses.text: When the king and all of the people who were with him arrived, he was weary, so he recovered there.  <div eID="gen2502" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 16:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1822"/><title type="x-s">Hushai Comes to Absalom</title> <div sID="gen2503" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1822"/>Now Absalom and all the people, the men of Israel, had come to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel <transChange type="added">was</transChange> with him.

verses.name: II Samuel 16:16
verses.text: When Hushai the Arkite the friend of David came to Absalom, Hushai said to Absalom, “<transChange type="added">Long</transChange> live the king, <transChange type="added">long</transChange> live the king!”

verses.name: II Samuel 16:17
verses.text: Absalom said to Hushai, “This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> your loyal love with your friend? Why did you not go with your friend?”

verses.name: II Samuel 16:18
verses.text: Then Hushai said to Absalom, “No, rather, whom Yahweh and this people and all the men of Israel have chosen, to him<note placement="foot">According to the reading tradition (<hi type="italic">Qere</hi>); <hi type="italic">Kethib</hi> has “no”</note> I will be, and with him I will remain.

verses.name: II Samuel 16:19
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Furthermore⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “And the second thing”</note> for whom have I served? Is it not in the presence of his son that I have served before your father? <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞So shall I serve you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!”<note placement="foot">Literally “So shall I be in your presence”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 16:20
verses.text: Then Absalom said to Ahithophel, “Give your advice. What shall we do?”

verses.name: II Samuel 16:21
verses.text: And Ahithophel said to Absalom, “Go to the concubines of your father whom he left behind to watch over the house, then all of Israel will hear that you made yourself odious to your father, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞all of your followers will be motivated⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!”<note placement="foot">Literally “the hands of all who are with you will be strengthened”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 16:22
verses.text: Then they pitched a tent for Absalom on the roof, and he went <transChange type="added">in</transChange> to the concubines of his father before the eyes of all Israel.

verses.name: II Samuel 16:23
verses.text: The counsel that Ahithophel gave in those days <transChange type="added">was</transChange> regarded as when a man<note placement="foot"><hi type="italic">Qere</hi> reads “a man inquired”; <hi type="italic">Kethib</hi> omits “a man”</note> inquired of the word of God, so all the counsel of Ahithophel <transChange type="added">was esteemed</transChange> both by David and by Absalom.  <chapter eID="2Sam.16"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 17:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1823"/><title type="x-s">Hushai Frustrates the Counsel of Ahithophel</title> <div sID="gen2504" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1823"/>Then Ahithophel said to Absalom, “Please let me choose twelve thousand men, and I will set out and pursue after David <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞tonight⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the night”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 17:2
verses.text: I will come upon him while he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> weary and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞weak⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “slack of hands”</note> I will startle him, and all of the people who <transChange type="added">are</transChange> with him will flee. Then I will strike down the king <transChange type="added">while</transChange> he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> alone.

verses.name: II Samuel 17:3
verses.text: Then I will return all the people to you; when all have returned, the man whom you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> seeking <transChange type="added">will be dead</transChange>,<note placement="foot">According to the MT; the LXX has “and I will return all the people to you the way a bride returns to her husband, except the life of the one man whom you are seeking”</note> but all the people will be safe.”

verses.name: II Samuel 17:4
verses.text: The word <transChange type="added">was</transChange> right in the eyes of Absalom and in the eyes of all the elders of Israel.

verses.name: II Samuel 17:5
verses.text: Then Absalom said, “Please call also for Hushai the Arkite, and let us hear <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞what he has to say⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “what is in his mouth”</note> also.”

verses.name: II Samuel 17:6
verses.text: So Hushai came to Absalom, who said to him, “Shall we do according to this word <transChange type="added">that</transChange> Ahithophel has spoken? If not, then you tell <transChange type="added">us</transChange>.”

verses.name: II Samuel 17:7
verses.text: Then Hushai said to Absalom, “The counsel that Ahithophel gave <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not good <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞at this time⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “at this occurrence”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 17:8
verses.text: Hushai continued, “You know your father and his men, that they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> mighty warriors and they <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞are enraged⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “are bitter of soul”</note> as a bear robbed of <transChange type="added">her</transChange> offspring in the field. Your father <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a man of war, so he will not spend the night with the troops.

verses.name: II Samuel 17:9
verses.text: Now he has hidden himself in one of the caves or in one of the places. At the moment he falls on them<note placement="foot">I.e., Absalom’s troops</note> the first time, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞whoever hears⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and the one who hears hears”</note> the report will say, ‘There has been a defeat among the people who follow after Absalom.’

verses.name: II Samuel 17:10
verses.text: And he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> also a <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞valiant warrior⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “son of ability”</note> whose heart is like the heart of the lion. He<note placement="foot">i.e., one of Absalom’s troops</note> will <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞certainly melt⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “melting he will melt”</note> with fear, for all Israel knows that your father is a mighty warrior and those who are with him are <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞valiant warriors⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “son of ability”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 17:11
verses.text: I give the advice that all of Israel from Dan to Beersheba should be completely gathered to you, as the sand which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> on the seashore for abundance, with <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you personally⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “your face”</note> going into the battle.

verses.name: II Samuel 17:12
verses.text: Then we will come to him in one of the places where he may be found, and we shall come upon him as the dew falls on the ground. He and all the men who are with him will not survive, <transChange type="added">not</transChange> even one!

verses.name: II Samuel 17:13
verses.text: <transChange type="added">Even</transChange> if he withdraws to a city, all Israel will bring up ropes to that city, and they will drag him away to the valley until there <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not even a pebble to be found.”

verses.name: II Samuel 17:14
verses.text: Then Absalom and all the men of Israel said, “The advice of Hushai the Arkite <transChange type="added">is</transChange> better than the advice of Ahithophel.” (Now Yahweh had ordained to frustrate the good counsel of Ahithophel in order for Yahweh to bring misery upon Absalom).  <div eID="gen2504" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 17:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1824"/><title type="x-s">Hushai Sends Word to David</title> <div sID="gen2505" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1824"/>Hushai said to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Thus and so⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “so this and so this”</note> Ahithophel advised Absalom and the elders of Israel, but <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞thus and so⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “so this and so this”</note> I have advised.

verses.name: II Samuel 17:16
verses.text: So then, send quickly and tell David, ‘Don’t spend the night at the fords of the wilderness! Moreover, by all means cross over lest the king and all the people who <transChange type="added">are</transChange> with him be swallowed up.’ ”

verses.name: II Samuel 17:17
verses.text: Now Jonathan and Ahimaaz <transChange type="added">were</transChange> staying at En Rogel, so a servant girl used to go and tell them, then they would go and tell King David, for they <transChange type="added">were</transChange> not able to be seen coming to the city.

verses.name: II Samuel 17:18
verses.text: But a young man saw them and told Absalom, so both of them went quickly and came to the house of a man at Bahurim. Now he had a well in his courtyard, so they went down there.

verses.name: II Samuel 17:19
verses.text: Then the woman took and spread a covering over the opening of the well; then she spread out dried grain on it, so nothing was discovered.

verses.name: II Samuel 17:20
verses.text: When the servants of Absalom came to the woman <transChange type="added">at</transChange> the house, they said, “Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?” And she said to them, “They crossed over the brook of water.” So they searched but could not find them, so they returned to Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Samuel 17:21
verses.text: After they left, they came up from the well and went and told King David. They said to David, “Set out and cross over the water quickly, for thus Ahithophel has advised against you.”

verses.name: II Samuel 17:22
verses.text: So David and all the people who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him set out, and they crossed over the Jordan until morning light until <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞there was no one⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “until one was not missing”</note> missing who had not crossed over the Jordan.

verses.name: II Samuel 17:23
verses.text: When Ahithophel saw that his advice <transChange type="added">was</transChange> not followed, he saddled the donkey, and he set out and went up to his house in his city. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞After he set his house in order⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “And he commanded to his household”</note> he hanged himself, and he died and was buried in the tomb of his ancestors.<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note>  <div eID="gen2505" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 17:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1825"/><div sID="gen2506" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1825"/>Now David had come to Mahanaim, and Absalom had crossed over the Jordan, he and all the men of Israel with him.

verses.name: II Samuel 17:25
verses.text: Absalom had appointed Amasa in place of Joab over the army. Now Amasa <transChange type="added">was</transChange> the son of a man whose name <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Ithra the Israelite, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who had married⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “who went to”</note> Abigail the daughter of Nahash the sister of Zeruiah, the mother of Joab.

verses.name: II Samuel 17:26
verses.text: Israel and Absalom camped <transChange type="added">in</transChange> the land of Gilead.

verses.name: II Samuel 17:27
verses.text: Just as David had arrived in Mahanaim, Shobi the son of Nahash from Rabbah of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> and Makir the son of Ammiel from Lo Debar and Barzillai the Gileadite from Rogelim

verses.name: II Samuel 17:28
verses.text: brought beds and basins and objects of pottery, as well as wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain, beans, lentils,

verses.name: II Samuel 17:29
verses.text: honey, curds, sheep, cheese, and cattle for David and for the people who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him to eat. For they had thought, “The troops <transChange type="added">are</transChange> hungry and weary and thirsty in the wilderness.”  <chapter eID="2Sam.17"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 18:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1826"/><title type="x-s">Absalom Dies in Battle</title> <div sID="gen2507" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1826"/>Then David mustered the people who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him, and he appointed over them commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds.

verses.name: II Samuel 18:2
verses.text: David sent forth a third of the troops <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞under the command of Joab⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “in the hand of Joab”</note> and a third <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞under the command of Abishai⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “in the hand of Abishai”</note> the brother of Joab, the son of Zeruiah, and the remaining third <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞under the command of Ittai⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in the hand of Ittai”</note> the Gittite. And the king said to the troops, “I, even I, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞will certainly go out⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “going out I will go out”</note> with you.”

verses.name: II Samuel 18:3
verses.text: Then the troops said, “You will not go out, for <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞if we must flee⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “fleeing we must flee”</note> then <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they will not care about us⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “they will not set heart toward us”</note> even if half of us die, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they will not care about us⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “they will not set heart toward us”</note> but now, you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> like ten thousand of us. And so then, <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> better for us that you be in the city to help.”

verses.name: II Samuel 18:4
verses.text: The king said to them, “I will do what seems good in your eyes.” So the king stood at the side of the gate <transChange type="added">while</transChange> all of the troops went out by hundreds and by thousands.

verses.name: II Samuel 18:5
verses.text: The king ordered Joab, Abishai, and Ittai, “With respect to the young man Absalom, <transChange type="added">deal</transChange> gently for me.” And all the troops heard when the king ordered all of the commanders concerning the matter of Absalom.  <div eID="gen2507" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 18:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1827"/><div sID="gen2508" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1827"/>The army went out to the field to meet Israel, and the battle was <transChange type="added">fought</transChange> in the forest of Ephraim.

verses.name: II Samuel 18:7
verses.text: The army of Israel <transChange type="added">was</transChange> defeated there before the servants of David, and the defeat there was great on that day: twenty thousand.

verses.name: II Samuel 18:8
verses.text: The battle there was spreading over the surface of all the land, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the forest devoured more among the army than⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the forest made numerous to eat among the army more than”</note> the sword <transChange type="added">did</transChange> on that day.

verses.name: II Samuel 18:9
verses.text: Absalom was found in the presence of the servants of David <transChange type="added">as he was</transChange> riding on the mule. The mule went under the thicket of the great oak tree, and his head <transChange type="added">was</transChange> caught in the tree. He <transChange type="added">was</transChange> left hanging between heaven and earth, and the mule which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> under him went on.

verses.name: II Samuel 18:10
verses.text: When a certain man saw <transChange type="added">it</transChange>, he told Joab, and he said, “Look, I saw Absalom hanging in the oak tree!”

verses.name: II Samuel 18:11
verses.text: Then Joab said to the man who <transChange type="added">was</transChange> telling him, “Look, <transChange type="added">if</transChange> you saw, why did you not strike him down to the ground there? <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I would have gladly given you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And upon me to give to you”</note> ten pieces of silver and a leather belt.”

verses.name: II Samuel 18:12
verses.text: The man said to Joab, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Even if I felt the weight⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “I am not weighing out on my palms”</note> of a thousand pieces of silver in my palms, I would not have sent my hand against the son of the king, for in our ears the king commanded you and Abishai and Ittai, ‘Whoever you may be, protect the young man Absalom.’

verses.name: II Samuel 18:13
verses.text: If I had dealt treacherously against his life, and <transChange type="added">there is</transChange> not any matter hidden from the king, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you would have presented yourself aloof⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “you would have presented yourself from before”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 18:14
verses.text: Joab said, “No longer will I wait in your presence.” Then he took three spears in his hand and thrust them into the heart of Absalom while he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> still alive in the oak tree.

verses.name: II Samuel 18:15
verses.text: Then ten of the young men who bore the weapons of Joab surrounded <transChange type="added">him</transChange> and struck and killed Absalom.

verses.name: II Samuel 18:16
verses.text: Then Joab blew on the trumpet and the troops returned from pursuing after Israel, for Joab kept back the troops.

verses.name: II Samuel 18:17
verses.text: They took Absalom and they threw him into the large pit in the forest and raised a very great heap of stones over him. Then all of Israel fled, each to his tent.  <div eID="gen2508" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 18:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1828"/><div sID="gen2509" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1828"/>(Now Absalom had taken and set up for himself in his lifetime a stone pillar that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in the valley of the king, because he said, “I have no son in order to remember my name,” and he called the stone pillar by his name. It <transChange type="added">is</transChange> called the monument of Absalom until this day).

verses.name: II Samuel 18:19
verses.text: Now Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said, “Please let me run and bring the good news to the king that Yahweh has vindicated him from the hand of his enemies.”

verses.name: II Samuel 18:20
verses.text: Joab said to him, “You <transChange type="added">will</transChange> not <transChange type="added">be</transChange> a man <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞bringing⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for upon”</note> good news this day! You may bring good news on another day, but today you will not be bringing good news because the king’s son is dead.”

verses.name: II Samuel 18:21
verses.text: Then Joab said to the Cushite, “Go, tell the king what you have seen”; then the Cushite bowed down to Joab and ran <transChange type="added">off</transChange>.

verses.name: II Samuel 18:22
verses.text: Then Ahimaaz the son of Zadok again said to Joab, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Come what may⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “And let it happen what”</note> please let me also run after the Cushite.” Joab asked, “Why are you wanting to run, my son, when for you there is no <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞messenger’s reward⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?”<note placement="foot">Literally “and for you there is no good news finding”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 18:23
verses.text: “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Come what may⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “And let it happen what”</note> I want to run.” He said to him, “Run,” so Ahimaaz ran on the road on the plain, and he passed the Cushite.  <div eID="gen2509" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 18:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1829"/><div sID="gen2510" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1829"/>Now David <transChange type="added">was</transChange> sitting between the two gates, and the sentinel went up to the roof of the gate by the wall and he lifted up his eyes and watched, and look, a man <transChange type="added">was</transChange> running by himself.

verses.name: II Samuel 18:25
verses.text: The sentry called and told the king, and the king said, “If he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> alone, good news is in his mouth.” <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞He kept coming closer⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “And he came, coming and near”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 18:26
verses.text: Then the sentinel saw another man running, so the sentinel called to the gatekeeper and said, “Look, a man running alone.” The king said, “This one also <transChange type="added">is</transChange> bringing good news.”

verses.name: II Samuel 18:27
verses.text: The sentinel said, “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> seeing <transChange type="added">that</transChange> the running of the first <transChange type="added">is</transChange> like the running of Ahimaaz the son of Zakok.” The king said, “He <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a good man; he will come, for good news.”

verses.name: II Samuel 18:28
verses.text: Then Ahimaaz called and said to the king, “Peace.” He bowed down to the king with his face to the ground, and he said, “May Yahweh your God be blessed, who has delivered the men who raised their hand against my lord the king.”

verses.name: II Samuel 18:29
verses.text: The king said, “<transChange type="added">Is</transChange> it peace for the young man Absalom?” Ahimaaz said, “I saw the great commotion when Joab the servant of the king sent your servant, but I do not know what <transChange type="added">it was all about</transChange>.”

verses.name: II Samuel 18:30
verses.text: Then the king said, “Turn aside, take your place here,” so he turned aside and waited.

verses.name: II Samuel 18:31
verses.text: Suddenly the Cushite arrived and said, “May my lord the king receive the good news, for Yahweh has vindicated you today from the power of all who stood up against you.”

verses.name: II Samuel 18:32
verses.text: The king said to the Cushite, “<transChange type="added">Is</transChange> it peace for the young man Absalom?” Then the Cushite answered, “May the enemies of my lord the king and all who rise up against you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to harm you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for evil”</note> be like the young man!”

verses.name: II Samuel 18:33
verses.text: <note placement="foot">2 Samuel 18:33–19:43 in the English Bible is 19:1–44 in the Hebrew Bible</note> The king was upset, and he went up to the upper room of the gate and wept. He said as he went, “My son, Absalom, my son, my son, Absalom. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞If only⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Who would grant my dying in place of you”</note> I had died instead of you, Absalom, my son, my son.”  <chapter eID="2Sam.18"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 19:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1830"/><title type="x-s">King David Weeps for Absalom</title> <div sID="gen2511" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1830"/>And it was told to Joab that the king <transChange type="added">was</transChange> weeping and he mourned over Absalom,

verses.name: II Samuel 19:2
verses.text: so the victory turned to mourning on that day for all the army, because they had heard that day, “The king is grieving over his son.”

verses.name: II Samuel 19:3
verses.text: The army <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞came secretly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “stole secretly to come”</note> into the city on that day because the army was disgraced when they fled in the battle,

verses.name: II Samuel 19:4
verses.text: and because the king had covered his face and cried with a loud voice, “My son, Absalom, Absalom, my son, my son.”  <div eID="gen2511" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 19:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1831"/><div sID="gen2512" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1831"/>Then Joab came to the king’s house and said, “Today you have humiliated the faces of all of your servants who have saved your life this day, and the life of your sons and your daughters, the life of your wives, and the life of your concubines,

verses.name: II Samuel 19:6
verses.text: by loving those who hate you and hating those who love you. Indeed, you have made clear this day that you have no <transChange type="added">regard for your</transChange> commanders or officers, for I have realized today that <transChange type="added">were</transChange> Absalom alive, and all of us were dead, then <transChange type="added">that would</transChange> have been right in your eyes!

verses.name: II Samuel 19:7
verses.text: So then, get up and go out and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞speak kindly to your servants⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “speak to the heart of your servants”</note> for I swear by Yahweh, if you do not go out, no man will lodge this night with you, and this disaster <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> greater for you than any disaster that has come upon you from your childhood until now!”

verses.name: II Samuel 19:8
verses.text: So the king got up and he sat in the gate, and they told all the army, “Look, the king <transChange type="added">is</transChange> sitting in the gate.” Then all the army came before the king; <transChange type="added">whereas</transChange> all of Israel had fled, each to his tent.  <div eID="gen2512" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 19:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1832"/><title type="x-s">David Returns from Exile</title> <div sID="gen2513" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1832"/>Then it happened that all the people <transChange type="added">were</transChange> disputing among all the tribes of Israel, saying, “The king delivered us from the hand of our enemies, and he saved us from the hand of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines, but now he has fled from the land because of Absalom.

verses.name: II Samuel 19:10
verses.text: Now Absalom whom we anointed <transChange type="added">as king</transChange> over us has died in the battle; so then, why <transChange type="added">are</transChange> you taking no action to restore the king?”

verses.name: II Samuel 19:11
verses.text: Then King David sent to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, saying, “Speak to the elders of Judah: ‘Why <transChange type="added">are</transChange> you last to bring back the king to his house? The talk of all Israel has come to the king in his house.

verses.name: II Samuel 19:12
verses.text: My brothers, you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> my bones and you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> my flesh. Why should you be the last to bring back the king?’

verses.name: II Samuel 19:13
verses.text: To Amasa you shall say: ‘<transChange type="added">Are</transChange> you not my bones and my flesh? <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞May God punish me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Thus may God do to me and thus may he add”</note> if you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> not the commander of my army before me forever, in place of Joab.’ ”

verses.name: II Samuel 19:14
verses.text: So he turned the heart of all the men of Judah as one man, and they sent <transChange type="added">word</transChange> to the king, “Return, you and all your servants.”  <div eID="gen2513" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 19:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1833"/><div sID="gen2514" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1833"/>Then the king returned and he came to the Jordan; Judah had come to Gilgal to come to meet the king, to bring the king over the Jordan.

verses.name: II Samuel 19:16
verses.text: Then Shimei the son of Gera, the son of the Benjaminite, who <transChange type="added">was</transChange> from Bahurim quickly came down with the men of Judah to meet King David,

verses.name: II Samuel 19:17
verses.text: and a thousand men <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him from Benjamin. Too, Ziba the servant of the household of Saul and fifteen of his sons and twenty of his servants <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him, and they rushed to the Jordan before the king.

verses.name: II Samuel 19:18
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞The crossing took place⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And the ford crossed”</note> to bring the household of the king over and to do good in his eyes. Then Shimei the son of Gera fell before the king when he crossed over the Jordan,

verses.name: II Samuel 19:19
verses.text: and he said to the king, “May not my lord hold me guilty, and may you not remember how your servant did wrong on the day that my lord the king went out from Jerusalem, by taking it to heart!

verses.name: II Samuel 19:20
verses.text: For your servant knows that I have sinned; look, I have come this day <transChange type="added">as the first</transChange> of all the house of Joseph to come down to meet my lord the king.”

verses.name: II Samuel 19:21
