verses.text: Then Abishai the son of Zeruiah responded and said, “Because of this, should not Shimei be put to death, for he cursed the anointed one of Yahweh?”

verses.name: II Samuel 19:22
verses.text: Then David said, “What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> it to me or to you, sons of Zeruiah, that you should be an adversary today? <transChange type="added">Should</transChange> anyone be put to death in Israel? Do I not know today that I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> king over Israel?”

verses.name: II Samuel 19:23
verses.text: Then the king said to Shimei, “You shall not die,” and <transChange type="added">so</transChange> the king swore to him.  <div eID="gen2514" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 19:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1834"/><div sID="gen2515" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1834"/>Now, Mephibosheth the son of Saul came down to meet the king; he had not taken care of his feet nor trimmed his moustache nor washed his clothes from the day the king left until the day he came back in peace.

verses.name: II Samuel 19:25
verses.text: It happened that when he came to Jerusalem to meet the king, the king said to him, “Why did you not come with me, Mephibosheth?”

verses.name: II Samuel 19:26
verses.text: Then he said, “My lord the king, my servant deceived me, for your servant had said, ‘Let me saddle the donkey that I may ride on her and go with the king,’ for your servant <transChange type="added">is</transChange> lame.

verses.name: II Samuel 19:27
verses.text: But he slandered against your servant to my lord the king. My lord the king <transChange type="added">is</transChange> like the angel of God; <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞do as you see fit.⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “do the good in your eyes”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 19:28
verses.text: For there <transChange type="added">was no one</transChange> in all the house of my father <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who were not doomed to death⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “except men of death”</note> before my lord the king, but you set your servant among those who eat at your table. Do I have any righteousness any longer except to cry out to the king?”

verses.name: II Samuel 19:29
verses.text: Then the king said to him, “Why should you speak any more <transChange type="added">about</transChange> the matter? I have decided: you and Ziba shall divide the land.”

verses.name: II Samuel 19:30
verses.text: Then Mephibosheth said to the king, “Let him take the whole <transChange type="added">thing</transChange>, since my lord the king has come <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞safely⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in peace”</note> to his house.”  <div eID="gen2515" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 19:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1835"/><div sID="gen2516" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1835"/>Then Barzillai the Gileadite came down from Rogelim and crossed with the king over the Jordan to escort him through the Jordan.

verses.name: II Samuel 19:32
verses.text: Now Barzillai <transChange type="added">was</transChange> very old, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞eighty years old⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “a son of eighty years”</note> Now he had provided the king <transChange type="added">with food</transChange> while he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> staying at Mahanaim, for he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a very wealthy man.

verses.name: II Samuel 19:33
verses.text: The king said to Barzillai, “You cross over with me, and I will provide for you <transChange type="added">to dwell</transChange> with me in Jerusalem.”

verses.name: II Samuel 19:34
verses.text: Then Barzillai said to the king, “What <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the days of the years of my life, that I should go with the king to Jerusalem?

verses.name: II Samuel 19:35
verses.text: I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> eighty years old today. Can I discern between good and bad? Or can your servant taste what I eat or what I drink? Or can I still hear the voice of singing men and women? Why should your servant be a burden any longer to my lord the king?

verses.name: II Samuel 19:36
verses.text: Your servant shall go over the Jordan with the king a little way, but why should the king recompense me with this reward?

verses.name: II Samuel 19:37
verses.text: Please let your servant return, and let me die in my city in the tomb of my father and my mother. Here <transChange type="added">is</transChange> your servant Kimham; let him cross over with my lord the king, and do for him that which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> good in your eyes.”

verses.name: II Samuel 19:38
verses.text: The king said, “Let Kimham go over with me, and I will do for him the good in your eyes, and all that you desire of me I will do for you.”  <div eID="gen2516" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 19:39
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1836"/><div sID="gen2517" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1836"/>Then all the people crossed over the Jordan, and the king crossed and kissed Barzillai and blessed him; then he returned to his place.

verses.name: II Samuel 19:40
verses.text: The king went over to Gilgal, and Kimham went over with him. All the people of Judah went over with the king, and half of the people of Israel too.

verses.name: II Samuel 19:41
verses.text: Suddenly, all the men of Israel <transChange type="added">were</transChange> coming to the king. They said to the king, “Why have our brothers the men of Judah stolen away and brought the king and his household over the Jordan, with all the men of David?”

verses.name: II Samuel 19:42
verses.text: Then all the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, “Because the king <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my close relative! Why <transChange type="added">are</transChange> you this angry over this matter? <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Have we by any means eaten <transChange type="added">anything</transChange> from the king? Did we take by any means anything that was not ours⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?”<note placement="foot">Literally “By any means did we eat from the king or by any means was it dragged away for us?”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 19:43
verses.text: Then the people of Israel answered the men of Judah and said, “I have <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞ten times as much⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “ten hands”</note> in the king, moreover in David I have more than you. Why did you treat me with contempt <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞by not giving me first chance⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and my word was not the first”</note> to bring back my king?” But the words of the men of Judah <transChange type="added">were</transChange> fiercer than the word of the men of Israel.  <chapter eID="2Sam.19"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 20:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1837"/><title type="x-s">Sheba Leads a Revolt</title> <div sID="gen2518" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1837"/>Now a man of wickedness was found there whose name <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Sheba the son of Bichri, a Benjaminite. He blew the horn and said, “There is no share for us in David, and there <transChange type="added">is</transChange> no inheritance for us in the son of Jesse; each to his tents, O Israel!”

verses.name: II Samuel 20:2
verses.text: Then all the men of Israel went up from <transChange type="added">following</transChange> after David, <transChange type="added">following instead</transChange> after Sheba the son of Bicri, but the men of Judah stuck to their king from the Jordan up to Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Samuel 20:3
verses.text: David went up to his house in Jerusalem, then the king took the ten concubines whom he had left to look after the house, and he put them <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞under confinement⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “a house of guard”</note> However, he provided for them, but <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he did not sleep with them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “he did not come into them”</note> So they were confined until the day of their death, like a lifetime of widowhood.  <div eID="gen2518" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 20:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1838"/><title type="x-s">Joab Assassinates Amasa</title> <div sID="gen2519" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1838"/>Then the king said to Amasa, “Summon for me the men of Judah <transChange type="added">within</transChange> three days, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞and be here yourself⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “and you stand here”</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 20:5
verses.text: So Amasa went to summon Judah, but he tarried more than the appointed time which he had set for him.

verses.name: II Samuel 20:6
verses.text: Then David said to Abishai, “Now Sheba the son of Bicri will do us more harm than Absalom. You take the servants of your lord and pursue after him, lest he find fortified cities for himself and escape from us.”

verses.name: II Samuel 20:7
verses.text: Then the men of Joab, the Kerethites and the Pelethites, and all the mighty warriors went out after him; they went out from Jerusalem to pursue after Sheba the son of Bicri.

verses.name: II Samuel 20:8
verses.text: They <transChange type="added">were</transChange> near the big rock that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in Gibeon, and Amasa came before them. Joab <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞was dressed in his military clothing⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “was dressed his garment his clothing”</note> <transChange type="added">with</transChange> a utility belt on him and a sword strapped to his waist in its scabbard. Now he went out, and it fell out.

verses.name: II Samuel 20:9
verses.text: Then Joab said to Amasa, “Is it peace, O you my brother?” Then the right hand of Joab took hold of the beard of Amasa <transChange type="added">as if</transChange> to kiss him.

verses.name: II Samuel 20:10
verses.text: Now Amasa was not on his guard against the sword that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in Joab’s hand, and he struck him with it into the stomach, and his entrails poured out to the ground. He did not strike him again, and he died. Then Joab and Abishai his brother pursued after Sheba the son of Bicri.

verses.name: II Samuel 20:11
verses.text: A young man stood over him, from the young men of Joab, and he said, “Whoever takes delight in Joab and whoever <transChange type="added">is</transChange> for David, <transChange type="added">follow</transChange> after Joab.”

verses.name: II Samuel 20:12
verses.text: Now Amasa <transChange type="added">was</transChange> wallowing in the blood in the middle of the highway; when the man saw that all the people stood <transChange type="added">there</transChange>, he turned Amasa over from the highway into the field, and he threw a garment over him because he had seen that all who had come by him had stopped.

verses.name: II Samuel 20:13
verses.text: After he was removed from the highway, all the men passed by after Joab to pursue after Sheba the son of Bicri.  <div eID="gen2519" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 20:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1839"/><title type="x-s">Wisdom from a Woman under Siege</title> <div sID="gen2520" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1839"/>(He<note placement="foot">i.e., “Sheba”</note> had passed through all the tribes of Israel to Abel and Beth Maacah; now all of the Berites had been treated badly, so they also followed after him.)

verses.name: II Samuel 20:15
verses.text: And they came and besieged him in Abel Beth Maacah. They threw up a siege ramp against the city, and they stood against the ramparts. And all the army who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with Joab <transChange type="added">were</transChange> battering to cause the wall to fall.

verses.name: II Samuel 20:16
verses.text: Then a wise woman from the city called out, “Listen, listen! Please speak to Joab <transChange type="added">to</transChange> come near here so that I may speak to you.”

verses.name: II Samuel 20:17
verses.text: Then he came near to her, and the woman asked, “<transChange type="added">Are</transChange> you Joab?” And he said, “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange>.” Then she said to him, “Listen to the words of your servant.” He said, “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> listening.”

verses.name: II Samuel 20:18
verses.text: Then she said, “In former times, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they would always say⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “speaking they would speak”</note> ‘By all means, let them inquire in Abel,’ and so they settled things.

verses.name: II Samuel 20:19
verses.text: I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> one of the faithful representatives of Israel. You <transChange type="added">are</transChange> seeking to destroy a city and a mother in Israel. Why do you want to swallow the inheritance of Yahweh?”

verses.name: II Samuel 20:20
verses.text: Then Joab answered and said, “Far be it, far be it from me that I should swallow or I should destroy.

verses.name: II Samuel 20:21
verses.text: That is not the matter. But a man from the mountains of Ephraim, whose name <transChange type="added">is</transChange> Sheba the son Bicri, has lifted up his hand against the king, against David. Give only him to us, and I will depart from the city.” The woman said to Joab, “Look, his head <transChange type="added">is</transChange> being thrown down to you over the wall.”

verses.name: II Samuel 20:22
verses.text: The woman went to all of the people with her wise plan, so they cut off the head of Sheba the son of Bicri and threw <transChange type="added">it</transChange> to Joab. Then he blew the horn and dispersed from the city, each to his tent. Then Joab returned to Jerusalem to the king.

verses.name: II Samuel 20:23
verses.text: Now Joab <transChange type="added">was</transChange> over all the army of Israel and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada <transChange type="added">was</transChange> over the Carites and over the Pelethites.

verses.name: II Samuel 20:24
verses.text: Adoram <transChange type="added">was</transChange> over the forced labor, and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud <transChange type="added">was</transChange> the recorder.

verses.name: II Samuel 20:25
verses.text: Shiya <transChange type="added">was</transChange> secretary, and Zadok and Abiathar <transChange type="added">were</transChange> priests.

verses.name: II Samuel 20:26
verses.text: Also Ira the Jairite <transChange type="added">was</transChange> priest for David.  <chapter eID="2Sam.20"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 21:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1840"/><title type="x-s">The Famine Brings Justice</title> <div sID="gen2521" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1840"/>There <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a famine in the days of David <transChange type="added">for</transChange> three years, year after year. And David <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞inquired of Yahweh⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sought the face of Yahweh”</note> and Yahweh said, “The bloodguilt <transChange type="added">is</transChange> on Saul and on his household, because he killed the Gibeonites.”

verses.name: II Samuel 21:2
verses.text: So the king called the Gibeonites and spoke to them. Now the Gibeonites <transChange type="added">were</transChange> not from the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> they were from the remainder of the Amorites. Now the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> had sworn to them,<note placement="foot">The treaty between Israel and the Gibeonites is found in Josh 9</note> but Saul tried to wipe them out in his zeal for the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> and Judah.

verses.name: II Samuel 21:3
verses.text: So David asked the Gibeonites, “What can I do for you, and with what can I make amends that you may bless the inheritance of Yahweh?”

verses.name: II Samuel 21:4
verses.text: Then the Gibeonites said to him, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞It is not a matter for us of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “There is not for me (<hi type="italic">Qere</hi> ‘us’)”</note> silver or gold with Saul or with his household. It is not for us to put to death anyone in Israel.” He asked, “What <transChange type="added">are</transChange> you saying <transChange type="added">that</transChange> I should do for you all?”

verses.name: II Samuel 21:5
verses.text: Then they said to the king, “The man who consumed us and who plotted against us <transChange type="added">so that</transChange> we were destroyed from existing in all of the territory of Israel,

verses.name: II Samuel 21:6
verses.text: let seven men from his sons be given over to us, and we will execute them before Yahweh in Gibeah of Saul, the chosen one of Yahweh.” Then the king said, “I will give them over.”

verses.name: II Samuel 21:7
verses.text: But the king spared Mephibosheth the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, because of the sworn oath of Yahweh which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> between them, between David and Jonathan the son of Saul.

verses.name: II Samuel 21:8
verses.text: So the king took two of the sons of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, whom she bore to Saul, namely Armoni and Mephibosheth, and five of the sons of Michal the daughter of Saul whom she had borne to Adriel the son of Barzillai the Meholathite.

verses.name: II Samuel 21:9
verses.text: He gave them into the hands of the Gibeonites, and they executed them on the mountain in the presence of Yahweh, and the seven fell together. Now they were put to death in the days of the harvest, at the beginning of the harvest of barley.  <div eID="gen2521" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 21:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1841"/><div sID="gen2522" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1841"/>Rizpah the daughter of Aiah took the sackcloth, and she spread it for herself on the rock at the beginning of the harvest until water gushed forth on them from heaven, but she did not allow the birds of heaven to rest on them by day nor the animals of the field by night.

verses.name: II Samuel 21:11
verses.text: David <transChange type="added">was</transChange> told about what Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, the concubine of Saul, had done.

verses.name: II Samuel 21:12
verses.text: So David left and took the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son from the rulers of Jabesh Gilead, who had stolen them from the public square of Beth Shan, where <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines hung them <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞when⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “on the day”</note> <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines killed Saul on Gilboa.

verses.name: II Samuel 21:13
verses.text: He brought up the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son from there, and they gathered the bones of the executed.

verses.name: II Samuel 21:14
verses.text: And they buried the bones of Saul and Jonathan his son in the land of Benjamin at Zela, in the tomb of Kish his father. They did all that the king had commanded, and afterward God was entreated for the land.  <div eID="gen2522" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 21:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1842"/><title type="x-s">Battles with the Philistines Recounted</title> <div sID="gen2523" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1842"/>There <transChange type="added">was</transChange> war again for <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines with Israel, and David and his servants with him went down, and they fought <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines, and David grew weary.

verses.name: II Samuel 21:16
verses.text: Now Yishbi in Nob, who <transChange type="added">was</transChange> among the descendents of Raphah<note placement="foot">The descendants of Raphah (i.e., the Rephaim) were thought to be giants</note> (now the weight of his spearhead <transChange type="added">was</transChange> three hundredweight of bronze, and he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> newly armed), said that he would kill David.

verses.name: II Samuel 21:17
verses.text: But Abishai the son of Zeruiah helped him, and he attacked the Philistine and killed him. Then the men of David swore to him, saying, “You shall not go out with us any longer to the battle, so that you do not quench the lamp of Israel.”  <div eID="gen2523" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 21:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1843"/><div sID="gen2524" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1843"/>It happened afterward that there <transChange type="added">was</transChange> again battle at Gob with <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines. Then Sibbecai the Hushathite killed Saph who <transChange type="added">was</transChange> among the descendants of the Raphah.  <div eID="gen2524" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 21:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1844"/><div sID="gen2525" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1844"/>There <transChange type="added">was</transChange> again a battle with <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines at Gob. And Elhanan the son of Jaare-Oregim, the Bethlehemite, killed Goliath<note placement="foot">In view of the account of David and Goliath in 1 Sam 17, it is likely that Elhanan actually killed the brother of Goliath, Lahmi, in 1 Chr 20:5</note> the Gittite, the shaft of whose spear <transChange type="added">was</transChange> like the beam of a weaver.  <div eID="gen2525" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 21:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1845"/><div sID="gen2526" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1845"/>Once again there <transChange type="added">was</transChange> battle at Gath, and there <transChange type="added">was</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a man of great size⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “a man of measurement”</note> The fingers of his hand and the toes of his feet <transChange type="added">were</transChange> six and six, twenty-four in number. He <transChange type="added">was</transChange> also born to the Raphah.

verses.name: II Samuel 21:21
verses.text: He taunted Israel but Jonathan the son of Shimei, the brother of David, killed him.

verses.name: II Samuel 21:22
verses.text: These four <transChange type="added">were</transChange> born for the Raphah in Gath, and they fell by the hand of David and by the hand of his servants.  <chapter eID="2Sam.21"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1846"/><title type="x-s">The Victory Song of David</title> <div sID="gen2527" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1846"/>Then David spoke to Yahweh the words of this song,<note placement="foot">This same song is recorded in Psa 18, with minor differences</note> on the day Yahweh delivered him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul.  <div eID="gen2527" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1847"/><lg sID="gen2528"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2529"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1847"/>And he said:<l eID="gen2529" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2530"/>“Yahweh <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my rock, my fortress, and my deliverer. <l eID="gen2530" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1848"/><l level="1" sID="gen2531"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1848"/>I take refuge in God, my rock,<note placement="foot">So many LXX mss, Targum, Vulgate, and Psa 18:3. MT has “the God of my rock”</note> my shield, and the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞strength⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “horn”</note> of my salvation.<l eID="gen2531" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2532"/>My stronghold and my refuge, O my savior, you will save me from violence! <l eID="gen2532" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1849"/><l level="1" sID="gen2533"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1849"/>I call <transChange type="added">upon</transChange> Yahweh who is praiseworthy,<l eID="gen2533" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2534"/>and I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> saved from those who hate me. <l eID="gen2534" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1850"/><l level="1" sID="gen2535"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1850"/>For the breaker waves of death engulfed me;<l eID="gen2535" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2536"/>the currents of chaos overwhelmed me. <l eID="gen2536" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1851"/><l level="1" sID="gen2537"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1851"/>The ropes of Sheol entangled me;<l eID="gen2537" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2538"/>the snares of death confronted me. <l eID="gen2538" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1852"/><l level="1" sID="gen2539"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1852"/>In my distress I called <transChange type="added">upon</transChange> Yahweh, and to my God I called.<l eID="gen2539" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2540"/>He heard my voice from his temple,<l eID="gen2540" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2541"/>and my cry for help <transChange type="added">was</transChange> to his ears. <l eID="gen2541" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1853"/><l level="1" sID="gen2542"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1853"/>The earth heaved and shook,<l eID="gen2542" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2543"/>the foundations of heaven trembled and heaved<l eID="gen2543" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2544"/>because <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he was angry⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “it was hot for him”</note> <l eID="gen2544" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1854"/><l level="1" sID="gen2545"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1854"/>Smoke went up from his nostrils and fire from his mouth.<l eID="gen2545" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2546"/>Burning coals devoured, they burned from him. <l eID="gen2546" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1855"/><l level="1" sID="gen2547"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1855"/>He bowed the heavens and came down;<l eID="gen2547" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2548"/>a very thick cloud <transChange type="added">was</transChange> under his feet. <l eID="gen2548" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1856"/><l level="1" sID="gen2549"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1856"/>He rode upon a cherub and flew;<l eID="gen2549" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2550"/>he was seen on the wings of the wind. <l eID="gen2550" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1857"/><l level="1" sID="gen2551"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1857"/>He put darkness <transChange type="added">as</transChange> a canopy all around him,<l eID="gen2551" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2552"/>a collection of <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞thick rain clouds⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “clouds of thick clouds”</note> <l eID="gen2552" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1858"/><l level="1" sID="gen2553"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1858"/>From the brightness before him<l eID="gen2553" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2554"/>flamed burning coals of fire. <l eID="gen2554" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1859"/><l level="1" sID="gen2555"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1859"/>Yahweh thundered from heaven,<l eID="gen2555" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2556"/>and the Most High <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞uttered his voice⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “gave his voice”</note> <l eID="gen2556" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1860"/><l level="1" sID="gen2557"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1860"/>He sent arrows and he scattered them,<l eID="gen2557" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2558"/>lightning, and he directed them. <l eID="gen2558" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1861"/><l level="1" sID="gen2559"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1861"/>Then the channels of water of the sea were exposed,<l eID="gen2559" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2560"/>the foundations of the world,<l eID="gen2560" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2561"/>at the rebuke of Yawheh,<l eID="gen2561" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2562"/>from the blast of the breath of his nostrils. <l eID="gen2562" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1862"/><l level="1" sID="gen2563"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1862"/>He sent from a high position <transChange type="added">and</transChange> took me;<l eID="gen2563" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2564"/>he drew me from mighty waters. <l eID="gen2564" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1863"/><l level="1" sID="gen2565"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1863"/>He delivered me from my strong enemies,<l eID="gen2565" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2566"/>from those who hate me, for they <transChange type="added">were</transChange> mightier than I. <l eID="gen2566" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1864"/><l level="1" sID="gen2567"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1864"/>They approached me on the day of my disaster,<l eID="gen2567" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2568"/>but Yahweh <transChange type="added">was</transChange> my support. <l eID="gen2568" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1865"/><l level="1" sID="gen2569"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1865"/>He brought me out to a spacious place.<l eID="gen2569" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2570"/>He delivered me because he delighted in me. <l eID="gen2570" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1866"/><l level="1" sID="gen2571"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1866"/>Yahweh rewarded me according to my righteousness,<l eID="gen2571" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2572"/>according to the cleanness of my hands he recompensed me. <l eID="gen2572" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1867"/><l level="1" sID="gen2573"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1867"/>For I have kept the ways of Yahweh;<l eID="gen2573" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2574"/>I have not acted wickedly against my God. <l eID="gen2574" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1868"/><l level="1" sID="gen2575"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1868"/>For all of his ordinances <transChange type="added">were</transChange> before me,<l eID="gen2575" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2576"/>and I did not turn aside from his statutes. <l eID="gen2576" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1869"/><l level="1" sID="gen2577"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1869"/>I was blameless before him,<l eID="gen2577" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2578"/>and I kept myself from my iniquity. <l eID="gen2578" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1870"/><l level="1" sID="gen2579"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1870"/>Yahweh has recompensed me according to my righteousness,<l eID="gen2579" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2580"/>according to my cleanness before his eyes. <l eID="gen2580" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1871"/><l level="1" sID="gen2581"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1871"/>With the loyal, you act as loyal,<l eID="gen2581" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2582"/>and with the blameless, you show yourself blameless. <l eID="gen2582" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1872"/><l level="1" sID="gen2583"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1872"/>With the pure, you show yourself pure,<l eID="gen2583" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2584"/>but with the crooked, you appear as a fool. <l eID="gen2584" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1873"/><l level="1" sID="gen2585"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1873"/>Humble people you will deliver,<l eID="gen2585" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2586"/>but your eyes <transChange type="added">are</transChange> on the haughty, <transChange type="added">whom</transChange> you bring down. <l eID="gen2586" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1874"/><l level="1" sID="gen2587"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1874"/>For you, O Yahweh <transChange type="added">are</transChange> my lamp,<l eID="gen2587" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2588"/>and Yahweh lightens my darkness. <l eID="gen2588" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:30
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1875"/><l level="1" sID="gen2589"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1875"/>For by you I can run a raid;<l eID="gen2589" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2590"/>by my God I can leap over a wall. <l eID="gen2590" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1876"/><l level="1" sID="gen2591"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1876"/>This God, his way <transChange type="added">is</transChange> blameless;<l eID="gen2591" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2592"/>the promise of Yahweh <transChange type="added">is</transChange> flawless.<l eID="gen2592" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2593"/>He <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a shield to all who take refuge in him. <l eID="gen2593" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1877"/><l level="1" sID="gen2594"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1877"/>For who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> God apart from Yahweh?<l eID="gen2594" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2595"/>And who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a rock apart from our God? <l eID="gen2595" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:33
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1878"/><l level="1" sID="gen2596"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1878"/>God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my strong refuge,<l eID="gen2596" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2597"/>he has fully opened my way.<note placement="foot">Thus <hi type="italic">Qere</hi>; <hi type="italic">Kethib</hi> has “his way”</note> <l eID="gen2597" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:34
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1879"/><l level="1" sID="gen2598"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1879"/>He makes my feet<note placement="foot">Thus <hi type="italic">Qere</hi>; <hi type="italic">Kethib</hi> has “his feet”</note> like a doe deer,<l eID="gen2598" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2599"/>and on my high places he has set me. <l eID="gen2599" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:35
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1880"/><l level="1" sID="gen2600"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1880"/>He trains my hands for the war,<l eID="gen2600" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2601"/>so that my arms can bend a bow of bronze. <l eID="gen2601" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:36
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1881"/><l level="1" sID="gen2602"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1881"/>You have given me the shield of your salvation;<l eID="gen2602" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2603"/>your willingness to help has made me great. <l eID="gen2603" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:37
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1882"/><l level="1" sID="gen2604"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1882"/>You have broadened my steps beneath me;<l eID="gen2604" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2605"/>my ankles have not wobbled. <l eID="gen2605" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:38
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1883"/><l level="1" sID="gen2606"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1883"/>I pursued those who hate me, and I destroyed them.<l eID="gen2606" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2607"/>I did not turn back until finishing them. <l eID="gen2607" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:39
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1884"/><l level="1" sID="gen2608"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1884"/>I wiped them out and I smashed them;<l eID="gen2608" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2609"/>they did not get up; they fell under my feet. <l eID="gen2609" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:40
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1885"/><l level="1" sID="gen2610"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1885"/>You have girded me with physical strength for the battle;<l eID="gen2610" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2611"/>you caused those who rose up against me to kneel under me. <l eID="gen2611" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:41
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1886"/><l level="1" sID="gen2612"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1886"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞My enemies you cause to retreat from me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “Those who hate me you give to me back”</note><l eID="gen2612" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2613"/>I destroy those who hate me. <l eID="gen2613" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:42
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1887"/><l level="1" sID="gen2614"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1887"/>They looked out, but there was no deliverer,<l eID="gen2614" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2615"/><transChange type="added">even</transChange> to Yahweh, but he did not answer them. <l eID="gen2615" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:43
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1888"/><l level="1" sID="gen2616"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1888"/>I beat them fine, like the dust of the earth;<l eID="gen2616" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2617"/>like the mire of the streets, I crushed them, I stamped them down. <l eID="gen2617" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:44
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1889"/><l level="1" sID="gen2618"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1889"/>You delivered me from the strife of my people;<l eID="gen2618" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2619"/>you preserved me as the head of the nations.<l eID="gen2619" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2620"/>A people I had not known served me. <l eID="gen2620" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:45
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1890"/><l level="1" sID="gen2621"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1890"/>Children of a foreign land came cringing to me;<l eID="gen2621" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2622"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞when they heard of me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “at the hearing of an ear”</note> they became obedient to me. <l eID="gen2622" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:46
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1891"/><l level="1" sID="gen2623"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1891"/>Children of a foreign land lost heart<l eID="gen2623" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2624"/>and came trembling from their strongholds. <l eID="gen2624" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:47
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1892"/><l level="1" sID="gen2625"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1892"/>Yahweh lives! Blessed be my rock!<l eID="gen2625" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2626"/>May God, the rock of my salvation, be exalted! <l eID="gen2626" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:48
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1893"/><l level="1" sID="gen2627"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1893"/>God does vengeance for me,<l eID="gen2627" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2628"/>bringing down peoples under me. <l eID="gen2628" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:49
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1894"/><l level="1" sID="gen2629"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1894"/>He brings me out from my enemies,<l eID="gen2629" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2630"/>and from those who rose up against me you lift me up,<l eID="gen2630" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2631"/>and from men of violence you rescue me. <l eID="gen2631" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:50
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1895"/><l level="1" sID="gen2632"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1895"/>Therefore I will extol you, Yahweh, among the nations!<l eID="gen2632" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2633"/>I will sing praises to your name! <l eID="gen2633" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 22:51
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1896"/><l level="1" sID="gen2634"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1896"/>He makes great salvation <transChange type="added">for</transChange> his king<l eID="gen2634" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2635"/>and shows loyal love to his anointed one, David<l eID="gen2635" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2636"/>and to his descendants forever.” <l eID="gen2636" level="2"/><lg eID="gen2528"/> <chapter eID="2Sam.22"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 23:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1897"/><title type="x-s">David Extols Yahweh</title> <div sID="gen2637" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1897"/>These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the last words of David, the declaration of David the son of Jesse, and the declaration of the man exalted <transChange type="added">by</transChange> the Most High, the anointed one of the God of Jacob and the darling of the songs of Israel.

verses.name: II Samuel 23:2
verses.text: “The spirit of Yahweh speaks through me, and his word <transChange type="added">is</transChange> upon my tongue.

verses.name: II Samuel 23:3
verses.text: The God of Israel said to me, the rock of Israel has spoken; ‘He who rules over mankind rules righteously, in the fear of God.

verses.name: II Samuel 23:4
verses.text: Like the light of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> morning when the sun rises, shining with no clouds, <transChange type="added">bringing</transChange> vegetation from the earth apart from rain.’<note placement="foot">In other words, even men who rule rightly pass like the dew of the morning</note>

verses.name: II Samuel 23:5
verses.text: Yet not so <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my house with God, for he made an everlasting covenant for me, arranging everything. He has secured all my deliverance, and all my desire he will cause to happen.

verses.name: II Samuel 23:6
verses.text: But evil persons <transChange type="added">are</transChange> like thorns cast aside; all of them, because they cannot be picked up in the hand.

verses.name: II Samuel 23:7
verses.text: And if a man wants to touch them, he must use an iron instrument or the shaft of a spear; then they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> consumed entirely with fire on the spot.”  <div eID="gen2637" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 23:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1898"/><title type="x-s">David’s Faithful Soldiers</title> <div sID="gen2638" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1898"/>These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the names of the mighty warriors who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> David’s: Josheb-Basshebeth a Tahkemonite <transChange type="added">was</transChange> chief of three officers; first Adino, whose spear <transChange type="added">was</transChange> against eight hundred slain on one occurrence.

verses.name: II Samuel 23:9
verses.text: Next to him Eleazar, the son of Dodo the son of an Ahohite, <transChange type="added">was</transChange> among the three mighty warriors with David when they defied the Philistines and they gathered there for the battle and the men of Israel withdrew.

verses.name: II Samuel 23:10
verses.text: He stood up and struck down the Philistines until his hand grew tired and his hand clung to the sword, and Yahweh brought about a great victory on that day. Then the army returned back to him only for stripping <transChange type="added">the dead</transChange>.

verses.name: II Samuel 23:11
verses.text: Next to him <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Shamma, the son of Agee the Hararite. When <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines assembled at Lehi, a plot of the field was there filled with lentils, and the army fled there from the presence of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines.

verses.name: II Samuel 23:12
verses.text: But he took a stand in the middle of the plot of land and defended it. He killed <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines, and Yahweh brought about a great victory.

verses.name: II Samuel 23:13
verses.text: Then three<note placement="foot">So <hi type="italic">Qere</hi>; <hi type="italic">Kethib</hi> reads “thirty”</note> of the thirty leaders went down and came to David <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞at the time of the harvest⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the harvest”</note> to the cave of Adullam, while a group of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines <transChange type="added">were</transChange> camping in the valley of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Rephaim.

verses.name: II Samuel 23:14
verses.text: Now at that time, David <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in the stronghold, and a garrison of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in Bethlehem at that <transChange type="added">same</transChange> time.

verses.name: II Samuel 23:15
verses.text: David <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞said longingly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “desired and said”</note> “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Oh that someone would bring me a drink⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Who will let me drink …?”</note> of water from the well of Bethlehem that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> at the gate.”

verses.name: II Samuel 23:16
verses.text: So three of the mighty warriors broke into the camp of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines, and they drew water from the well of Bethlehem that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> at the gate, and they carried <transChange type="added">it</transChange> and brought <transChange type="added">it</transChange> to David. But he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> not willing to drink it, but poured it out to Yahweh.

verses.name: II Samuel 23:17
verses.text: He said, “Far be it from me before Yahweh that I should do this. <transChange type="added">Is this not</transChange> the blood of the men who went at the risk of their lives?” So he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> not willing to drink it. These things the three mighty warriors did.

verses.name: II Samuel 23:18
verses.text: Now Abishai the brother of Joab the son of Zeruiah <transChange type="added">was</transChange> himself the leader of the thirty. He <transChange type="added">was</transChange> wielding his spear against three hundred slain and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞gained a name⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and to him a name”</note> among the thirty.

verses.name: II Samuel 23:19
verses.text: Among the thirty, is it not that he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> honored and became a commander for them? But he did not come up to the three.

verses.name: II Samuel 23:20
verses.text: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, the son of Ish-Hai, <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a great <transChange type="added">man</transChange> of deeds from Kabzeel. He struck down two sons of Ariel of Moab, and he went down and killed a lion in the middle of a pit on a snowy day.

verses.name: II Samuel 23:21
verses.text: He also killed a good-looking Egyptian man, in whose hand <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a spear. He went down against him with the staff and snatched the spear from the hand of the Egyptian and killed him with his spear.

verses.name: II Samuel 23:22
verses.text: These things Benaiah the son of Jehoiada did and gained a name for himself among the three mighty warriors.

verses.name: II Samuel 23:23
verses.text: He <transChange type="added">was</transChange> honored more than the thirty, but he did not come up to the three. David appointed him in charge of his bodyguard.  <div eID="gen2638" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 23:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1899"/><title type="x-s">The Mighty Men of David</title> <div sID="gen2639" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1899"/>Among the thirty <transChange type="added">were</transChange> Asahel the brother of Joab, Elhanan the son of Dodo of Bethlehem,

verses.name: II Samuel 23:25
verses.text: Shammah the Harodite, Elika the Harodite,

verses.name: II Samuel 23:26
verses.text: Helez the Paltite, Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite,

verses.name: II Samuel 23:27
verses.text: Abiezer the Anathothite, Mebunnai the Hushathite,

verses.name: II Samuel 23:28
verses.text: Zalmon the Ahohite, Maharai the Netophathite,

verses.name: II Samuel 23:29
verses.text: Heleb the son of Baanah the Netophathite, Ittai the son of Ribai from Gibeah of the sons of Benjamin,

verses.name: II Samuel 23:30
verses.text: Benaiah <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Pirathonite, Hiddai from the wadis of Gaash,

verses.name: II Samuel 23:31
verses.text: Abi-Albon the Arbathite, Azmaveth the Barhumite,

verses.name: II Samuel 23:32
verses.text: Eliahba the Shaalbonite, the sons of Jashen, Jonathan

verses.name: II Samuel 23:33
verses.text: <transChange type="added">the son</transChange> of Shammah the Hararite, Ahiam the son of Sharar the Ararite,

verses.name: II Samuel 23:34
verses.text: Eliphelet the son of Ahasbai the son of the Maacathite, Eliam the son of Ahithophel the Gilonite,

verses.name: II Samuel 23:35
verses.text: Hezro the Carmelite, Paarai the Arbite,

verses.name: II Samuel 23:36
verses.text: Igal the son of Nathan from Zobah, Bani the Gadite,

verses.name: II Samuel 23:37
verses.text: Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Beerothite, the carriers of the weapons of Joab the son of Zeruiah,

verses.name: II Samuel 23:38
verses.text: Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite,

verses.name: II Samuel 23:39
verses.text: Uriah the Hittite; in all, thirty-seven.  <chapter eID="2Sam.23"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 24:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1900"/><title type="x-s">David and the Census of the People</title> <div sID="gen2640" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1900"/>Again Yahweh <transChange type="added">was</transChange> angry with Israel, and he<note placement="foot">The parallel passage in 1 Chr 21 names the “he” as Satan</note> incited David against them, saying, “Go count Israel and Judah.”

verses.name: II Samuel 24:2
verses.text: The king said to Joab, the commander of the army who <transChange type="added">was</transChange> with him: “Please go about through all the tribes of Israel from Dan to Beersheba, and count the people that I may know the number of the people.”

verses.name: II Samuel 24:3
verses.text: Then Joab said to the king, “May Yahweh your God increase the people a hundred times <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞what they are⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “as them and as them”</note> as the eyes of my lord the king are seeing. But my lord the king, why does he desire this thing?”

verses.name: II Samuel 24:4
verses.text: But the word of the king prevailed over Joab and over the commanders of the army, so Joab and the commanders of the army went out from before the king to count the people of Israel.

verses.name: II Samuel 24:5
verses.text: They crossed over the Jordan and camped at Aroer to the south of the city, which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in the middle of the wadi of Gad, and up to Jazer.

verses.name: II Samuel 24:6
verses.text: Then they went to Gilead and to the land of Tahtim Hodshi. They came to Dan Jaan and around to Sidon

verses.name: II Samuel 24:7
verses.text: and came to the fortress of Tyre and all the cities of the Hivites and the Canaanites. Then they went out to the Negev of Judah at Beersheba.

verses.name: II Samuel 24:8
verses.text: They went about through all the land, and they came to Jerusalem at the end of nine months and twenty days.  <div eID="gen2640" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 24:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1901"/><div sID="gen2641" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1901"/>Then Joab gave the number of the counting of the people to the king. Israel <transChange type="added">was</transChange> eight hundred thousand <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞valiant warriors⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “men of ability”</note> wielding the sword, and the men of Judah <transChange type="added">were</transChange> five hundred thousand.

verses.name: II Samuel 24:10
verses.text: The heart of David struck him after he had counted the people, and David said to Yahweh, “I have sinned greatly in what I have done! So then, O Yahweh, please forgive the guilt of your servant because I have acted very foolishly.”

verses.name: II Samuel 24:11
verses.text: When David got up in the morning, the word of Yahweh came to Gad the prophet, the seer of David, saying,

verses.name: II Samuel 24:12
verses.text: “Go and speak to David, ‘Thus says Yahweh, three things I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> laying on you; choose for yourself one of them and I will do it to you.’ ”

verses.name: II Samuel 24:13
verses.text: Then Gad came to David, and he told him and said to him, “Shall seven years of famine in the land come to you? Or three months of your fleeing from your enemies while he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> pursuing you? Or should there be three days of pestilence in your land? Now consider and decide what I must return to the one who sent me a word.”

verses.name: II Samuel 24:14
verses.text: Then David said to Gad, “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> greatly distressed. Please let us fall into the hand of Yahweh, because he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> great in his compassion; but into the hand of man don’t let me fall.”

verses.name: II Samuel 24:15
verses.text: Then Yahweh sent a plague into Israel from the morning <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞until the agreed time⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “until the time of agreed time”</note> and from the people from Dan to Beersheba, seventy thousand men died.  <div eID="gen2641" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 24:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1902"/><div sID="gen2642" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1902"/>When the angel stretched out his hand to destroy Jerusalem, Yahweh regretted about the evil, and he said to the angel who brought destruction among the people, “Enough, now relax your hand.” Now the angel of Yahweh <transChange type="added">was</transChange> at the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.

verses.name: II Samuel 24:17
verses.text: David spoke to Yahweh when he saw the angel destroying among the people, and he said, “Look, I have sinned and I have done wrong, but these sheep, what did they do? Please let your hand be against me and against the house of my father.”

verses.name: II Samuel 24:18
verses.text: Then Gad came to David on that same day and said to him, “Go up and erect an altar to Yahweh at the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.”

verses.name: II Samuel 24:19
verses.text: So David went up according to the word of Gad, as Yahweh had commanded.

verses.name: II Samuel 24:20
verses.text: Araunah looked down and saw the king and his servants coming over to him, so Araunah went out and bowed down before the king with his face to the ground.

verses.name: II Samuel 24:21
verses.text: Then Araunah said, “Why has my lord the king come to his servant?” David said, “To buy from you the threshing floor, to build an altar to Yahweh who brought a halt to the plague on the people.”

verses.name: II Samuel 24:22
verses.text: Araunah said to David, “Let my lord the king take and offer what <transChange type="added">is</transChange> good in his eyes. Look, here <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the cattle for the burnt offering and the threshing sledge and the yokes of the oxen for the firewood.

verses.name: II Samuel 24:23
verses.text: All of this Araunah hereby gives to the king.” Then Araunah said to the king, “May Yahweh your God respond favorably for you.”

verses.name: II Samuel 24:24
verses.text: Then the king said to Araunah, “No, but <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I will certainly buy⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “buying I will buy”</note> it from you for a price; I don’t want to offer to Yahweh my God burnt offerings that cost me nothing.” So David bought the threshing floor and the cattle for fifty shekels of silver.

verses.name: II Samuel 24:25
verses.text: David built an altar to Yahweh there, and he offered burnt offerings and fellowship offerings. Then Yahweh responded to <transChange type="added">his</transChange> prayer for the land and brought the plague to a halt from upon Israel.  <chapter eID="2Sam.24"/> <div eID="gen2642" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen2419" osisID="2Sam" type="book"/>

verses.name: I Kings 1:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1903"/><title type="x-s">David’s Last Days</title> <div sID="gen2644" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1903"/>Now King David had become old, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞advanced in years⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “he went in the days”</note> and they covered him with garments, but he was not warm.

verses.name: I Kings 1:2
verses.text: His servants said to him, “Let them search for a young virgin for my lord the king, and let her stand before the king. Let her be of use for him, and let her lie in your lap that my lord the king may be warm.”

verses.name: I Kings 1:3
verses.text: So they sought a beautiful young woman in all the territory of Israel, and they found Abishag the Shunnamite and brought her to the king.

verses.name: I Kings 1:4
verses.text: Now the young woman was very beautiful; she was of use for the king, and she served him, but the king did not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞have sexual relations with her⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “know her”</note>  <div eID="gen2644" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 1:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1904"/><title type="x-s">Adonijah Seeks David’s Throne</title> <div sID="gen2645" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1904"/>Now Adonijah the son of Haggith was exalting himself, saying, “I will be king,” so he prepared for himself a chariot and horsemen and fifty men running before him.

verses.name: I Kings 1:6
verses.text: His father did not rebuke him <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞at any time⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from his days”</note> by saying, “Why did you do so?” Now he was also very handsome of appearance; she had borne him after Absalom.<note placement="foot">“She” refers to Haggith bearing Adonijah; Absalom’s mother was Maacah</note>

verses.name: I Kings 1:7
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞He conferred⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And there were his words”</note> with Joab the son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they supported Adonijah⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “they helped after Adonijah”</note>

verses.name: I Kings 1:8
verses.text: But Zadok the priest, Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and the mighty warriors were David’s; they were not with Adonijah.  <div eID="gen2645" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 1:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1905"/><div sID="gen2646" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1905"/>And Adonijah sacrificed sheep, oxen, and fattened animals near the stone of Zoheleth, which is beside En Rogel. He invited all of his brothers, the sons of the king, and all the men of Judah, the servants of the king.

verses.name: I Kings 1:10
verses.text: But he did not invite Nathan the prophet or Benaiah or the mighty warriors or Solomon his brother.  <div eID="gen2646" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 1:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1906"/><title type="x-s">Solomon’s Intercessors</title> <div sID="gen2647" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1906"/>Then Nathan said to Bathsheba the mother of Solomon, “Have you not heard that Adonijah the son of Haggith has become king, but our lord David does not know?

verses.name: I Kings 1:12
verses.text: So then, come, let me advise you please, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞that you may save⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and save”</note> your life and the life of your son, Solomon.

verses.name: I Kings 1:13
verses.text: Come, go to King David and say to him, ‘Have you not, my lord the king, sworn to your servant, “Surely Solomon your son shall become king after me. And he will sit on my throne”? But why is Adonijah king?’

verses.name: I Kings 1:14
verses.text: While you are still there speaking with the king, I will enter after you, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I will confirm your words⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “I will make full your words”</note>  <div eID="gen2647" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 1:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1907"/><div sID="gen2648" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1907"/>So Bathsheba went to the king in the private room. Now the king was very old, and Abishag the Shunnamite was attending the king.

verses.name: I Kings 1:16
verses.text: Bathsheba knelt and bowed down before the king, and the king asked, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞What do you want⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?”<note placement="foot">Literally “What is for you”</note>

verses.name: I Kings 1:17
verses.text: She said to him, “My lord, you swore by Yahweh your God to your servant, ‘Solomon your son surely shall become king after me, and he will sit upon my throne!’

verses.name: I Kings 1:18
verses.text: But now, look! Adonijah has become king! And now, my lord the king, you do not know!

verses.name: I Kings 1:19
verses.text: He has sacrificed oxen and sheep and fattened animals <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in abundance⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “as far as the many”</note> and he has invited all the sons of the king, Abiathar the priest, Joab the commander of the army, but Solomon your servant he did not invite.

verses.name: I Kings 1:20
verses.text: But as for you, my lord the king, the eyes of all of Israel are on you, to tell them who shall sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.

verses.name: I Kings 1:21
verses.text: It shall be that when my lord the king sleeps with his ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> I and my son Solomon will be <transChange type="added">considered as</transChange> sinners.”  <div eID="gen2648" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 1:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1908"/><div sID="gen2649" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1908"/>While she was still speaking with the king, Nathan the prophet came <transChange type="added">in</transChange>.

verses.name: I Kings 1:23
verses.text: They told the king, “Nathan the prophet is here.” He came into the presence of the king and bowed down before the king with his face to the ground.

verses.name: I Kings 1:24
verses.text: Nathan said, “My lord the king, have you said, ‘Adonijah shall be king after me and he shall sit on my throne’?  <div eID="gen2649" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 1:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1909"/><div sID="gen2650" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1909"/>“For he went down today and sacrificed oxen, sheep, and fattened animals <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in abundance⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “as far as the many”</note> He invited all the sons of the king, the commanders of the army, and Abiathar the priest, and look, they are eating and drinking before him. They have also said, “Long live King Adonijah!

verses.name: I Kings 1:26
verses.text: But me, your servant, Zadok the priest, Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and Solomon your servant he did not invite.

verses.name: I Kings 1:27
verses.text: If it was from my lord the king that this thing has happened, <transChange type="added">then all is well,</transChange> but if not, you must let your servants know who shall sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.”

verses.name: I Kings 1:28
verses.text: Then King David answered and said, “Summon Bathsheba for me.” Then she came before the king and stood in his presence.<note placement="foot">Following the corrected LXX and Vulgate</note>

verses.name: I Kings 1:29
verses.text: Then the king swore and said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞As Yahweh lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “The life of Yahweh”</note> who has saved my life from all trouble,

verses.name: I Kings 1:30
verses.text: surely as I swore to you by Yahweh the God of Israel, saying, ‘Solomon your son shall surely be king after me, and he shall sit on my throne in my place,’ surely I shall do so this <transChange type="added">very</transChange> day.”

verses.name: I Kings 1:31
verses.text: Then Bathsheba knelt with her face to the ground and did obeisance to the king, and she said, “May my lord, King David, live forever.”  <div eID="gen2650" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 1:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1910"/><title type="x-s">Solomon Is Crowned King</title> <div sID="gen2651" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1910"/>Then King David said, “Summon Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada,” and they came before the king.

verses.name: I Kings 1:33
verses.text: The king said to them, “Take with you all the servants of your lord, and let them make Solomon my son ride on my mule, and bring him down to Gihon.

verses.name: I Kings 1:34
verses.text: Let Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anoint him there as king over Israel. Blow on the trumpet and say, ‘Long live King Solomon!’

verses.name: I Kings 1:35
verses.text: Then you shall go up after him, and let him come and sit on my throne; he shall be king in my place. I have appointed him to be leader over Israel and Judah.”

verses.name: I Kings 1:36
verses.text: Then Benaiah the son of Jehoiada answered the king and said, “Amen! So may Yahweh, the God of my lord the king, confirm it!

verses.name: I Kings 1:37
verses.text: As Yahweh was with my lord the king, so may he be with Solomon and make his throne greater than the throne of my lord King David.”

verses.name: I Kings 1:38
verses.text: Then Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, the Kerethites, and the Pelethites went down, and they let Solomon ride on the mule of King David, and they brought him to Gihon.

verses.name: I Kings 1:39
verses.text: Then Zadok the priest took the horn of oil from the tent, and he anointed Solomon. They blew on the trumpet, and all the people said, “Long live King Solomon!”

verses.name: I Kings 1:40
verses.text: All the people went up after him, and the people were playing on the flutes and rejoicing <transChange type="added">with</transChange> great joy, and the earth shook with their noise.  <div eID="gen2651" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 1:41
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1911"/><title type="x-s">Adonijah’s Response to the Coronation of Solomon</title> <div sID="gen2652" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1911"/>And Adonijah and all the invited guests who were with him heard <transChange type="added">it</transChange>. Now they were finished eating when Joab heard the sound of the trumpet and said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Why is there such a noise in the city?⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>”<note placement="foot">Literally “Why is the sound of the city noisy?”</note>

verses.name: I Kings 1:42
verses.text: While he was still speaking, suddenly Jonathan the son of Abiathar the priest came. Adonijah said, “Come, for you are a man of valor, and you bring good news.”

verses.name: I Kings 1:43
verses.text: Jonathan answered and said to Adonijah, “But our lord King David has made Solomon king!

verses.name: I Kings 1:44
verses.text: He sent Zadok the priest with the king, and Nathan the prophet, Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, the Kerethites, and the Pelethites; they made him ride on the king’s mule.

verses.name: I Kings 1:45
verses.text: Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anointed him as king at Gihon, and they have gone up from there rejoicing. The city has gone wild; this <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the sound which you heard.

verses.name: I Kings 1:46
verses.text: And also, Solomon sits on the throne of the kingdom!

verses.name: I Kings 1:47
verses.text: The servants of the king also came to congratulate our lord King David, saying, ‘Your God has made the name of Solomon better than your name and his throne greater than your throne!’ So the king worshiped on the bed.

verses.name: I Kings 1:48
verses.text: What is more, the king said, ‘May Yahweh the God of Israel be blessed, who has given this day one sitting on my throne, and my eyes are seeing <transChange type="added">it</transChange>!’ ”  <div eID="gen2652" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 1:49
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1912"/><div sID="gen2653" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1912"/>Then all the invited guests who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> for Adonijah trembled and got up and went, each on his way.

verses.name: I Kings 1:50
verses.text: Adonijah was afraid because of Solomon, and he got up and went and grasped the horns of the altar.

verses.name: I Kings 1:51
verses.text: Solomon was told, “Look, Adonijah is afraid of King Solomon, and he has grasped the horns of the altar, saying, ‘Let King Solomon swear to me <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞first⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “as the day”</note> that he will surely not kill his servant with the sword!’ ”

verses.name: I Kings 1:52
verses.text: Solomon said, “If he is a son of noble character, not a hair of his <transChange type="added">head</transChange> will fall to the ground, but if evil is found in him, then he will die.”

verses.name: I Kings 1:53
verses.text: Then King Solomon sent and brought him down from upon the altar. He came and did obeisance to King Solomon. Solomon said to him, “Go to your house.”  <chapter eID="1Kgs.1"/>

verses.name: I Kings 2:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1913"/><title type="x-s">David’s Instructions for Solomon</title> <div sID="gen2654" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1913"/>The days of David came near <transChange type="added">for him</transChange> to die, and he charged Solomon his son, saying,

verses.name: I Kings 2:2
verses.text: “I <transChange type="added">am about to</transChange> go the way of all the world. Be strong and be <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞courageous⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “as a man”</note>

verses.name: I Kings 2:3
verses.text: You shall keep the charge of Yahweh your God, to walk in his ways, to keep his statutes, his commandments, his judgments, and his testimonies, as are written in the law of Moses, so that you may prosper in all that you do and everywhere you turn,

verses.name: I Kings 2:4
verses.text: so that Yahweh may establish his word which he spoke concerning me, saying, ‘If your sons take heed of their way, to walk before me in faithfulness, with all their heart and with all their soul, no man of yours will be cut off from the throne of Israel.’ ”  <div eID="gen2654" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 2:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1914"/><div sID="gen2655" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1914"/>“Moreover, you also know what Joab the son of Zeruiah did to me when he dealt with the two commanders of the armies of Israel, to Abner son of Ner and to Amasa son of Jether, and he murdered them and put the blood of war in <transChange type="added">a time of</transChange> peace. He put the blood of war on the leather belt that was on his waist and on the sandals which were on his feet.

verses.name: I Kings 2:6
verses.text: You must act according to your wisdom, but you must not let his gray hair go down to Sheol in peace.

verses.name: I Kings 2:7
verses.text: Regarding the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite, you shall do loyal love and let them be among those who eat at your table, because they met me when I fled from Absalom your brother.

verses.name: I Kings 2:8
verses.text: And look, Shimei the son of Gera the son of the Benjaminite from Bahurim is with you. Now he <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞cursed me severely⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “cursed me with a curse”</note> when I went to Mahanaim, but he came down to meet me at the Jordan, so I swore to him by Yahweh, ‘I surely will not kill you with the sword.’

verses.name: I Kings 2:9
verses.text: So then, do not leave him unpunished, for you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> a wise man, and you will know what you must do to him. You must bring his grey hair down to Sheol with blood.”  <div eID="gen2655" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 2:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1915"/><div sID="gen2656" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1915"/>Then David slept with his ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and was buried in the city of David.

verses.name: I Kings 2:11
verses.text: The days that David reigned over Israel <transChange type="added">were</transChange> forty years; he reigned seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem.

verses.name: I Kings 2:12
verses.text: Then Solomon sat on the throne of David his father, and his kingdom was firmly established.  <div eID="gen2656" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 2:13
