verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1916"/><title type="x-s">Adonijah’s Persistence</title> <div sID="gen2657" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1916"/>Adonijah the son of Haggith came to Bathsheba the mother of Solomon, and she said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Are you coming in peace⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?”<note placement="foot">Literally “Is peace your coming?”</note> He said, “Peace.”

verses.name: I Kings 2:14
verses.text: Then he said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞May I have a word with you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?”<note placement="foot">Literally “A word is for me to you”</note> Then she said, “Go on.”

verses.name: I Kings 2:15
verses.text: He said, “You know that the kingship was mine and that all Israel had set their face toward me as king, but the kingship turned around and became my brother’s, for it was from Yahweh for him <transChange type="added">to have it</transChange>.

verses.name: I Kings 2:16
verses.text: Now one request I am asking from you, and you must <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞not refuse me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “not turn my face”</note> Then she said to him, “Go on.”

verses.name: I Kings 2:17
verses.text: He said, “Please speak to King Solomon, for he will not refuse you, so that he will give to me Abishag the Shunnamite as wife.”

verses.name: I Kings 2:18
verses.text: Then Bathsheba said, “Very well, I will speak to the king concerning you.”  <div eID="gen2657" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 2:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1917"/><title type="x-s">Solomon’s Responses to Adonijah, Joab, and Shimei</title> <div sID="gen2658" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1917"/>Bathsheba came to King Solomon to speak to him concerning Adonijah, and the king got up to meet her, bowed down to her, and then sat on his throne. Then he set up a throne for the king’s mother, and she sat on his right.

verses.name: I Kings 2:20
verses.text: She said, “I have one small request I am asking from you. Do <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞not refuse me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “not turn my face”</note> The king said to her, “Ask, my mother, for I will <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞not refuse you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “not turn your face”</note>

verses.name: I Kings 2:21
verses.text: Then she said, “Let Abishag the Shunnamite be given to Adonijah your brother as wife.”

verses.name: I Kings 2:22
verses.text: King Solomon answered and said to his mother, “Why are you asking Abishag the Shunnamite for Adonijah? Ask for him also the kingdom, for he is my brother, older than I; and <transChange type="added">ask</transChange> for him also Abiathar the priest, and for Joab the son of Zeruiah.”

verses.name: I Kings 2:23
verses.text: Then King Solomon swore by Yahweh, saying, “Thus may God do to me and thus may he add, if Adonijah hasn’t spoken this thing at the expense of his life.

verses.name: I Kings 2:24
verses.text: So then, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as Yahweh lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the life of Yahweh”</note> who has established me and seated me on the throne of my father David and who has established for me a dynasty as he promised, then surely Adonijah will be put to death today.”

verses.name: I Kings 2:25
verses.text: King Solomon sent through the hand of Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, so he struck him, and he died.  <div eID="gen2658" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 2:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1918"/><div sID="gen2659" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1918"/>To Abiathar the priest, the king said, “Go to Anathoth, to your field, for <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you deserve to die⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “you are a man of death”</note> but on this day I will not kill you, for you carried the ark of the Lord Yahweh before David my father, and because you endured hardship in all the hardship that my father endured.”

verses.name: I Kings 2:27
verses.text: So Solomon banished Abiathar from being priest to Yahweh, thus fulfilling the word which Yahweh had spoken concerning the house of Eli in Shiloh.  <div eID="gen2659" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 2:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1919"/><div sID="gen2660" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1919"/>When the message came to Joab (now Joab <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞had supported⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “had turned after”</note> Adonijah but <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞had not supported⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “had not turned after”</note> Absalom), he fled to the tent of Yahweh and grasped the horns of the altar.

verses.name: I Kings 2:29
verses.text: It was told to King Solomon that Joab had fled to the tent of Yahweh and was beside the altar. So Solomon sent <transChange type="added">word</transChange> to Benaiah son of Jehoiada, saying, “Go and fall upon him.”

verses.name: I Kings 2:30
verses.text: So Benaiah went to the tent of Yahweh, and he said to him, “Thus says the king: ‘Come out.’ ” And he said, “No, for I want to die here.” So Benaiah returned a word to the king, saying, “Thus Joab spoke, and thus he answered me.”

verses.name: I Kings 2:31
verses.text: Then the king said to him, “Do as he spoke; fall upon him and bury him, and so you shall remove the innocent blood that Joab shed from on me and from on the house of my father.

verses.name: I Kings 2:32
verses.text: Yahweh will return his blood on his head, because he fell upon two men, more righteous and better than he, and he killed them with the sword, even though my father did not know it; <transChange type="added">namely</transChange> Abner son of Ner, commander of the army of Israel, and Amasa son of Jether, commander of the army of Judah.

verses.name: I Kings 2:33
verses.text: And their blood will return on the head of Joab and on the head of his descendants forever, but for David and his descendants and for his house and his throne, <transChange type="added">there</transChange> will be peace forever from Yahweh.”

verses.name: I Kings 2:34
verses.text: So Benaiah son of Jehoiada went up, and he fell on him and killed him, and he was buried in his house in the wilderness.

verses.name: I Kings 2:35
verses.text: Then the king appointed Benaiah the son of Jehoiada in his place over the army, and the king appointed Zadok the priest in place of Abiathar.  <div eID="gen2660" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 2:36
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1920"/><div sID="gen2661" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1920"/>Then the king sent and summoned Shimei, and he said to him, “Build yourself a house in Jerusalem and live there, but you must not go out <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞anywhere whatsoever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “where and where”</note> from there.

verses.name: I Kings 2:37
verses.text: It shall happen that on the day you go out and cross over the Wadi<note placement="foot">A valley that is dry most of the year, but contains a stream during the rainy season</note> Kidron, know for certain that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you will surely die⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “dying you will die”</note> Your blood will be on your head.”

verses.name: I Kings 2:38
verses.text: Shimei said to the king, “The word is good that my lord the king has spoken to me; thus will your servant do.” So Shimei lived in Jerusalem many days.  <div eID="gen2661" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 2:39
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1921"/><div sID="gen2662" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1921"/>It happened that at the end of three years, two of Shimei’s slaves fled to Achish, son of Maacah, the king of Gath. They told Shimei, saying, “Your slaves <transChange type="added">are</transChange> here in Gath.”

verses.name: I Kings 2:40
verses.text: So Shimei got up and saddled his donkey, and he went to Gath, to Achish, to search for his slaves. So Shimei went and brought his slaves from Gath.

verses.name: I Kings 2:41
verses.text: When Solomon was told that Shimei had gone from Jerusalem to Gath and had returned,

verses.name: I Kings 2:42
verses.text: the king sent and summoned Shimei, and he said to him, “Did I not make you swear by Yahweh? I warned you, saying, ‘On the day you go out and you go <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞anywhere whatsoever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “where and where”</note> know for certain that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you will surely die⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.’<note placement="foot">Literally “dying you will die”</note> And you said to me, ‘The word is good; I accept.’

verses.name: I Kings 2:43
verses.text: Why have you not kept the oath of Yahweh and the command which I commanded you?”

verses.name: I Kings 2:44
verses.text: Then the king said to Shimei, “You know all the evil which your heart knows, what you did to David my father. Now Yahweh will return the evil on your head,

verses.name: I Kings 2:45
verses.text: but King Solomon will be blessed and the throne of David will be established before Yahweh forever.”

verses.name: I Kings 2:46
verses.text: Then the king commanded Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he went out and fell upon him, and he died. So the kingdom was established in the hand of Solomon.  <chapter eID="1Kgs.2"/>

verses.name: I Kings 3:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1922"/><title type="x-s">Solomon’s Walk with Yahweh</title> <div sID="gen2663" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1922"/>Solomon intermarried with Pharaoh the king of Egypt, and he took the daughter of Pharaoh and brought her to the city of David until he finished building his house, the house of Yahweh, and the walls of Jerusalem all around.

verses.name: I Kings 3:2
verses.text: But the people <transChange type="added">were</transChange> sacrificing on the high places, for the house for the name of Yahweh had not <transChange type="added">yet</transChange> been built in those days.

verses.name: I Kings 3:3
verses.text: Solomon loved Yahweh, by walking in the statutes of David his father; only he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> sacrificing and offering incense on the high places.

verses.name: I Kings 3:4
verses.text: So the king went to Gibeon to sacrifice, for the great high place <transChange type="added">was</transChange> there. Solomon used to offer a thousand burnt offerings on that altar.  <div eID="gen2663" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 3:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1923"/><title type="x-s">Solomon’s Request for Wisdom</title> <div sID="gen2664" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1923"/>Yahweh appeared to Solomon at Gibeon in a dream at night, and God said, “Ask what I should give to you.”

verses.name: I Kings 3:6
verses.text: Then Solomon said, “You have shown great loyal love with your servant David my father, as he walked before you in faithfulness and in righteousness and in uprightness of heart with you. You have shown for him this great loyal love, and you have given a son to him who is sitting on his throne as <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> this day.

verses.name: I Kings 3:7
verses.text: So then, O Yahweh, you are my God. You have made your servant king in place of David my father <transChange type="added">though</transChange> I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> a young boy. I do not know going out or coming in.

verses.name: I Kings 3:8
verses.text: Your servant <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in the middle of your people whom you have chosen; a great people who cannot be counted or numbered because of abundance.

verses.name: I Kings 3:9
verses.text: Give to your servant a listening heart to judge your people, to discern between good and bad, because who is able to judge this, your difficult people?”  <div eID="gen2664" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 3:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1924"/><div sID="gen2665" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1924"/>The word was good in the eyes of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Lord that Solomon had asked this thing.

verses.name: I Kings 3:11
verses.text: And God said to him, “Because you have asked this thing and you did not ask for yourself <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a long life⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “many days”</note> and you did not ask riches for yourself and you did not ask for the life of your enemies, but you have asked for yourself <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the ability to make wise judgments⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “understanding to hear judgment”</note>

verses.name: I Kings 3:12
verses.text: behold, I do hereby do according to your word. I hereby give you a wise and discerning heart; there was no one like you before you, nor afterwards will one like you arise.

verses.name: I Kings 3:13
verses.text: Too, what you have not asked I give to you: both riches and honor, <transChange type="added">so that</transChange> no man among the kings will be like you all of your days.

verses.name: I Kings 3:14
verses.text: If you will walk in my ways by keeping my statutes and my commandments, as David your father walked, then I will lengthen your days.”

verses.name: I Kings 3:15
verses.text: Then Solomon awoke, and look, <transChange type="added">it was</transChange> a dream, and he came <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Jerusalem and stood before the ark of the covenant of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Lord, and he offered burnt offerings and presented fellowship offerings, and he held a feast for all of his servants.  <div eID="gen2665" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 3:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1925"/><title type="x-s">Solomon’s Wisdom Tested: The Two Prostitutes</title> <div sID="gen2666" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1925"/>Then two prostitutes came to the king, and they stood before him.

verses.name: I Kings 3:17
verses.text: The one woman said, “Please my lord, I and this woman are living in one house, and I gave birth, with her in the house.

verses.name: I Kings 3:18
verses.text: It happened on the third day <transChange type="added">after</transChange> my giving birth, this woman also gave birth, and we <transChange type="added">were</transChange> together. There was not anyone with us in the house, only the two of us <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in the house.

verses.name: I Kings 3:19
verses.text: Then the son of this woman died <transChange type="added">in the</transChange> night because she laid on him.

verses.name: I Kings 3:20
verses.text: So she got up in the middle of the night, and she took my son from beside me while your servant was asleep, and she put him in her lap, and she put her dead son in my lap.

verses.name: I Kings 3:21
verses.text: When I got up in the morning to nurse my son, behold, he was dead! When I looked closely at him in the morning, behold, it was not my son whom I had borne.”

verses.name: I Kings 3:22
verses.text: Then the other woman said, “No, for my son <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the living one, and your son <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the dead one.” The other kept on saying, “No, for your son <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the dead one, and my son <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the living one,” and so they argued in front of the king.

verses.name: I Kings 3:23
verses.text: Then the king said, “This one <transChange type="added">is</transChange> saying, ‘This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my son, the living one, but your son <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the dead one,’ and the other one keeps saying, ‘But no! Your son <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the dead one, and my son <transChange type="added">is</transChange> living!’ ”

verses.name: I Kings 3:24
verses.text: So the king said, “Bring me a sword,” and they brought the sword before the king.

verses.name: I Kings 3:25
verses.text: Then the king said, “Divide the living child into two, and give half to the one and half to the other.”

verses.name: I Kings 3:26
verses.text: Then the woman whose son <transChange type="added">was</transChange> the living one spoke to the king because her compassion was aroused for her son, and she said, “Please, my lord, give her the living child, but certainly do not kill him!” The other one <transChange type="added">was</transChange> saying, “As for me, so for you! Divide <transChange type="added">him</transChange>!”

verses.name: I Kings 3:27
verses.text: Then the king answered and said, “Give the living child to her, and do not kill him; she <transChange type="added">is</transChange> his mother.”

verses.name: I Kings 3:28
verses.text: When all of Israel heard the judgment that the king had rendered, they <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞stood in awe⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “feared the face”</note> of the king, because they realized that the wisdom of God was in him to execute justice.  <chapter eID="1Kgs.3"/>

verses.name: I Kings 4:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1926"/><title type="x-s">Solomon’s Wisdom: Political Administration</title> <div sID="gen2667" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1926"/>King Solomon was king over all Israel.

verses.name: I Kings 4:2
verses.text: Now these are the officials who were his: Azariah the son of Zadok <transChange type="added">was</transChange> the priest.

verses.name: I Kings 4:3
verses.text: Elihoreph and Ahijah, the sons of Shisha, <transChange type="added">were</transChange> the secretaries; Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud <transChange type="added">was</transChange> the recorder.

verses.name: I Kings 4:4
verses.text: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada <transChange type="added">was</transChange> over the army, and Zadok and Abiathar were priests.

verses.name: I Kings 4:5
verses.text: Azariah the son of Nathan <transChange type="added">was</transChange> over the governors, and Zabud the son of Nathan was a priest, an advisor to the king.

verses.name: I Kings 4:6
verses.text: Ahishar <transChange type="added">was</transChange> over the palace, and Adoniram the son of Abda <transChange type="added">was</transChange> over the forced labor.

verses.name: I Kings 4:7
verses.text: Solomon had twelve governors over all Israel, and they sustained the king and his palace, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞each one was to sustain for each month of the year⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “a month in the year he was over one to sustain”</note>

verses.name: I Kings 4:8
verses.text: These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> their names: Ben-Hur <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in the hill country of Ephraim.

verses.name: I Kings 4:9
verses.text: Ben-Deker <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in Makaz and in Shaalbim and in Beth-Shemesh and Elon of Beth-Hanan.

verses.name: I Kings 4:10
verses.text: Ben-Hesed <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in the Arubbot; Socoh and all the land of Hepher <transChange type="added">were</transChange> his.

verses.name: I Kings 4:11
verses.text: Ben-Abinadab <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in all of Naphat of Dor; Taphath the daughter of Solomon was his wife.

verses.name: I Kings 4:12
verses.text: Baanah the son of Ahilud <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in Taanach and Megiddo and all Beth-Shean which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> beside Zarethan below Jezreel, of Beth-Shean up to Abel-Meholah up to the other side of Jokmeam.

verses.name: I Kings 4:13
verses.text: Ben-Geber <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in Ramoth-Gilead; the villages of Jair, the son of Manasseh which are in the Gilead <transChange type="added">were</transChange> his, and the region of Argob which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in the Bashan, sixty great cities, with walls <transChange type="added">having</transChange> crossbars of bronze, <transChange type="added">were</transChange> his.

verses.name: I Kings 4:14
verses.text: Ahinadab the son of Iddo <transChange type="added">was in</transChange> Mahanaim.

verses.name: I Kings 4:15
verses.text: Ahimaaz <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in Naphtali; he moreover also had taken Basemath the daughter of Solomon as wife.

verses.name: I Kings 4:16
verses.text: Baanah the son of Hushai <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in Asher and Bealoth.

verses.name: I Kings 4:17
verses.text: Jehoshaphat the son of Paruah <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in Issachar.

verses.name: I Kings 4:18
verses.text: Shimei the son of Ela <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in Benjamin.

verses.name: I Kings 4:19
verses.text: Geber the son of Uri <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in the land of Gilead, the land of Sihon, the king of the Amorites, and of Og, the king of Bashan; one governor which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> over the land.

verses.name: I Kings 4:20
verses.text: Judah and Israel <transChange type="added">were</transChange> as many as the sand which is on the seashore in abundance, eating and drinking and rejoicing!  <div eID="gen2667" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 4:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1927"/><title type="x-s">Solomon’s Wisdom: Prosperity</title> <div sID="gen2668" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1927"/><note placement="foot"><reference osisRef="1Kgs.4.21-1Kgs.5.18">1 Kings 4:21–5:18 </reference>in the English Bible is 5:1–32 in the Hebrew Bible</note> Now Solomon was ruling over all the kingdoms from the River<note placement="foot">That is, the Euphrates</note> <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the land of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines, and up to the border of Egypt, who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> bringing tribute and <transChange type="added">were</transChange> serving Solomon all the days of his life.

verses.name: I Kings 4:22
verses.text: The food of Solomon for one day was thirty dry measures of choice meal and sixty dry measures of flour;

verses.name: I Kings 4:23
verses.text: ten stall-fed oxen and twenty pasture-fed oxen and a hundred sheep, besides deer and buck gazelles and roebucks and well-fed fowls.

verses.name: I Kings 4:24
verses.text: For he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> ruling over all the west of the River<note placement="foot">That is, the Euphrates</note> from Tiphsah up to Gaza, over all the kings west of the River;<note placement="foot">That is, the Euphrates</note> and he had peace from every side all around.

verses.name: I Kings 4:25
verses.text: Judah and Israel lived in security, each man under his vine and under his fig tree, from Dan as far as Beersheba, all the days of Solomon.  <div eID="gen2668" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 4:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1928"/><div sID="gen2669" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1928"/>Now Solomon had forty thousand stalls of horses for his war chariots and twelve thousand horsemen.

verses.name: I Kings 4:27
verses.text: These governors sustained King Solomon and all who came near to the table of King Solomon, each <transChange type="added">in</transChange> his month; they did not omit anything.

verses.name: I Kings 4:28
verses.text: The barley and the straw for the horses and for packhorses they brought to the place where they were, each according to his share.  <div eID="gen2669" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 4:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1929"/><title type="x-s">Solomon’s Wisdom: Literature, Zoology, Biology, Dendrology</title> <div sID="gen2670" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1929"/>God gave wisdom to Solomon and very great discernment, as well as <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞breadth of understanding⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “width of heart”</note> as the sand which is on the edge of the seashore.

verses.name: I Kings 4:30
verses.text: The wisdom of Solomon was greater than the wisdom of all the people<note placement="foot">Or “sons/children”</note> of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> east and more than all the wisdom of Egypt.

verses.name: I Kings 4:31
verses.text: He was wiser than all the men: Ethan the Ezrahite; Heman, Calcol, and Darda the children of Mahol; and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he was very well known⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “his name was among all the peoples around”</note>

verses.name: I Kings 4:32
verses.text: He spoke three thousand proverbs, and his songs were one thousand and five.

verses.name: I Kings 4:33
verses.text: He spoke concerning the trees, from the cedar which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in Lebanon up to the hyssop which grows on the wall; he also spoke concerning the animals, concerning the birds, concerning the creeping things, and concerning the fish.

verses.name: I Kings 4:34
verses.text: They came from all the nations to hear the wisdom of Solomon; from all the kings of the earth who had heard <transChange type="added">of</transChange> his wisdom.  <chapter eID="1Kgs.4"/>

verses.name: I Kings 5:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1930"/><title type="x-s">Solomon’s Wisdom: Architecture</title> <div sID="gen2671" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1930"/>Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants to Solomon when he heard that they had anointed him as king in place of his father, for Hiram had always been a friend for David.

verses.name: I Kings 5:2
verses.text: Then Solomon sent to Hiram, saying,

verses.name: I Kings 5:3
verses.text: “You knew David my father, that he was not able to build a house for the name of Yahweh his God, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in view of the warfare⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “because of the face of the warfare”</note> which surrounded him, until Yahweh placed them<note placement="foot">That is, David’s enemies</note> under the soles of his feet.

verses.name: I Kings 5:4
verses.text: But now Yahweh my God has given me rest all around me. There is no adversary, and there is no bad occurrence.

verses.name: I Kings 5:5
verses.text: Here I am, intending to build a house for the name of Yahweh my God, as Yahweh promised to my father David, saying, ‘Your son, whom I will set in your place on your throne, shall build the house for my name.’

verses.name: I Kings 5:6
verses.text: So then, command that they may cut cedars for me from Lebanon, and let my servants be with your servants. The wage of your servants I will give to you according to all that you say, for you know that there is no one among us who knows <transChange type="added">how</transChange> to cut timber like the Sidonians.”

verses.name: I Kings 5:7
verses.text: When Hiram heard the words of Solomon, he rejoiced greatly, and he said, “Blessed be Yahweh this day, who has given to David a wise son over this great people.”

verses.name: I Kings 5:8
verses.text: Hiram sent to Solomon, saying, “I have heard what you have sent to me; I will do all of your desire concerning the timber of cedars and concerning the timber of cypresses.

verses.name: I Kings 5:9
verses.text: My servants will bring <transChange type="added">them</transChange> down from Lebanon to the sea, and I will make them <transChange type="added">into</transChange> rafts in the sea <transChange type="added">to float to</transChange> the place which you indicated to me. Then I shall break them up there, and you may carry <transChange type="added">them further</transChange>, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you shall meet my needs⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “you shall do my desire”</note> by giving food for my house.”

verses.name: I Kings 5:10
verses.text: So Hiram was giving to Solomon the cedar timbers and the cypress timbers, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞everything he needed⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “all of his desire”</note>

verses.name: I Kings 5:11
verses.text: Then Solomon gave to Hiram twenty thousand dry measures of wheat <transChange type="added">as</transChange> food for his household, and twenty dry measures of <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞specially prepared olive oil⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “beaten olive oil”</note> thus Solomon gave to Hiram year by year.

verses.name: I Kings 5:12
verses.text: Yahweh gave wisdom to Solomon as he promised to him, and there was peace between Hiram and Solomon, and the two of them <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞made⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “cut”</note> a covenant.  <div eID="gen2671" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 5:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1931"/><div sID="gen2672" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1931"/>Then King Solomon conscripted a forced labor from all Israel, and the forced labor <transChange type="added">numbered</transChange> thirty thousand men.

verses.name: I Kings 5:14
verses.text: He sent them to Lebanon, ten thousand <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞every month⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “in the month”</note> the work groups were a month in Lebanon and two months at home; now Adoniram was over the forced labor.

verses.name: I Kings 5:15
verses.text: Solomon had seventy thousand <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞common laborers⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “carrying burden”</note> and eighty thousand stone craftsmen in the hill country.

verses.name: I Kings 5:16
verses.text: Besides the chiefs of the officers Solomon had, there were three thousand three hundred having charge over the people who were doing the work.

verses.name: I Kings 5:17
verses.text: When the king commanded, they quarried great stones <transChange type="added">and</transChange> precious stones to lay <transChange type="added">the</transChange> foundation of the house <transChange type="added">with</transChange> hewn stones.

verses.name: I Kings 5:18
verses.text: So Solomon’s builders and Hiram’s builders and the Gebalites hewed <transChange type="added">stones</transChange>, and they prepared the timber and the stone to build the house.  <chapter eID="1Kgs.5"/>

verses.name: I Kings 6:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1932"/><title type="x-s">Solomon Builds the Temple for Yahweh</title> <div sID="gen2673" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1932"/>It happened in the four hundred and eightieth year <transChange type="added">after</transChange> the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> went out from the land of Egypt, in the fourth year <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞of Solomon’s rule⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Solomon to rule”</note> over Israel, the month of Ziv (that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the second month), that he began to build the house for Yahweh.

verses.name: I Kings 6:2
verses.text: Now the house that King Solomon built for Yahweh <transChange type="added">was</transChange> sixty cubits <transChange type="added">in</transChange> its length and twenty cubits <transChange type="added">in</transChange> its width and thirty cubits <transChange type="added">in</transChange> its height.

verses.name: I Kings 6:3
verses.text: The vestibule on the face of the main hall of the temple<note placement="foot">Or “house”</note> was twenty cubits in its length, and the width of the temple<note placement="foot">Or “house”</note> was ten cubits wide on the face of the temple.<note placement="foot">Or “house”</note>

verses.name: I Kings 6:4
verses.text: And he made for the temple<note placement="foot">Or “house”</note> specially designed framed windows,

verses.name: I Kings 6:5
verses.text: and he built a structure against the wall of the temple<note placement="foot">Or “house”</note> <transChange type="added">running</transChange> all along the walls of the house, for the outer sanctuary and for the inner sanctuary, and made side rooms all around.

verses.name: I Kings 6:6
verses.text: The lower structure <transChange type="added">was</transChange> five cubits in its width and the middle <transChange type="added">was</transChange> six cubits in its width and the third <transChange type="added">was</transChange> seven cubits in its width, for he made niches for the temple<note placement="foot">Or “house”</note> all around to the outside, so that beams would not attach to the walls of the temple.<note placement="foot">Or “house”</note>

verses.name: I Kings 6:7
verses.text: Now while the temple<note placement="foot">Or “house”</note> was being built, it was built with stones finished at the quarry, so that no hammer or stone shaping tool or any instrument of iron was heard in the temple<note placement="foot">Or “house”</note> as it was being built.

verses.name: I Kings 6:8
verses.text: The doorway of the side room in the middle of the side of the temple<note placement="foot">Or “house”</note> <transChange type="added">was</transChange> on the south; they went up with a stairway to the middle and from the middle to the third <transChange type="added">floor</transChange>.

verses.name: I Kings 6:9
verses.text: So he built the house and finished it. He covered the temple<note placement="foot">Or “house”</note> <transChange type="added">with</transChange> rafters and wood planks and with the cedars.

verses.name: I Kings 6:10
verses.text: He also built the structure against all of the temple<note placement="foot">Or “house”</note> five cubits in height and fastened it to the temple<note placement="foot">Or “house”</note> with beams of cedar.  <div eID="gen2673" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 6:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1933"/><div sID="gen2674" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1933"/>Then the word of Yahweh came to Solomon, saying,

verses.name: I Kings 6:12
verses.text: “<transChange type="added">Regarding</transChange> this temple<note placement="foot">Or “house”</note> that you are building: if you walk in my ordinances and if you do my judgments and you keep all my commandments to walk in them, then I will establish my promise with you which I made to David your father.

verses.name: I Kings 6:13
verses.text: And I will dwell <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞among⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in the middle of”</note> the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> and I will not forsake my people Israel.”  <div eID="gen2674" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 6:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1934"/><div sID="gen2675" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1934"/>So Solomon built the temple<note placement="foot">Or “house”</note> and finished it.

verses.name: I Kings 6:15
verses.text: He lined the walls <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞of the inside of the house⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the house from house”</note> with boards of cedar; from the floor of the temple<note placement="foot">Or “house”</note> up to the rafters of the ceiling he covered them with wood <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞on the inside⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “from house”</note> He also covered the floor of the temple<note placement="foot">Or “house”</note> with cypress boards.

verses.name: I Kings 6:16
verses.text: He built twenty cubits from the rear of the house with boards of cedar from the floor up to the ceiling, and he built for it an inner sanctuary on the inside, as the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞most holy place⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “as the holy place of the holy places.” Often referred to as the Holy of Holies</note>

verses.name: I Kings 6:17
verses.text: The main hall of the temple<note placement="foot">Or “house”</note> was forty cubits <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in front of the inner sanctuary⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">So LXX supported by the Vulgate. MT has “before me”</note>

verses.name: I Kings 6:18
verses.text: with the cedar within the inner house <transChange type="added">having</transChange> carvings of gourds and buds of flowers. It <transChange type="added">was</transChange> entirely of cedar; there was not a stone visible.

verses.name: I Kings 6:19
verses.text: Now <transChange type="added">in</transChange> the inner sanctuary in the middle of the temple<note placement="foot">Or “house”</note> he prepared the inside to place the ark of the covenant of Yahweh there.

verses.name: I Kings 6:20
verses.text: In front, the inner sanctuary <transChange type="added">was</transChange> twenty cubits long and twenty cubits wide and twenty cubits high, and he overlaid it <transChange type="added">with</transChange> pure gold and covered the altar <transChange type="added">with</transChange> cedar.

verses.name: I Kings 6:21
verses.text: Solomon overlaid the temple<note placement="foot">Or “house”</note> on the inside <transChange type="added">with</transChange> pure gold, and he drew across it with golden chains in front of the inner sanctuary, which he overlaid with gold.  <div eID="gen2675" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 6:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1935"/><div sID="gen2676" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1935"/>All of the temple<note placement="foot">Or “house”</note> he overlaid with gold until all of the temple<note placement="foot">Or “house”</note> <transChange type="added">was</transChange> finished; all of the altar which belonged to the inner sanctuary he overlaid with gold.

verses.name: I Kings 6:23
verses.text: He made two cherubim of olive wood for the inner sanctuary, ten cubits high.

verses.name: I Kings 6:24
verses.text: Five cubits <transChange type="added">was</transChange> the first wing of the cherub, and five cubits the second wing of the cherub, from the tip of his <transChange type="added">one</transChange> wing up to the tip of his <transChange type="added">other</transChange> wing.

verses.name: I Kings 6:25
verses.text: The second cherub <transChange type="added">was</transChange> ten cubits <transChange type="added">according to</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the same⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “one”</note> measurement, and <transChange type="added">there</transChange> was one shape for the two cherubim.

verses.name: I Kings 6:26
verses.text: The height of the first cherub <transChange type="added">was</transChange> ten cubits and so <transChange type="added">was</transChange> the second cherub.  <div eID="gen2676" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 6:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1936"/><div sID="gen2677" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1936"/>He placed the cherubim in the middle of the inner house, and they spread out the wings of the cherubim; the wing of the first cherub touched against the wall and the wing of the second cherub <transChange type="added">was</transChange> touching against the second wall; their wings <transChange type="added">spread</transChange> to the middle of the house <transChange type="added">and were</transChange> touching wing to wing.

verses.name: I Kings 6:28
verses.text: He also overlaid the cherubim with gold.  <div eID="gen2677" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 6:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1937"/><div sID="gen2678" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1937"/>On all of the walls around the house, he carved engravings of cherubim and palm tree images and budding flowers both inside and out.

verses.name: I Kings 6:30
verses.text: He overlaid the floor of the house with gold both inside and out.

verses.name: I Kings 6:31
verses.text: He made doors of olive wood for the doorway of the inner sanctuary, <transChange type="added">as well as for</transChange> the doorpost of the fifth doorframe.

verses.name: I Kings 6:32
verses.text: <transChange type="added">On</transChange> the two doors of olive wood he made carvings of cherubim and palm tree images and budding flowers, and he overlaid them with gold <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞by beating⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and he beat out”</note> out the gold on the cherubim and the palm tree images.

verses.name: I Kings 6:33
verses.text: Thus he made doorframes of olive wood on four sides for the doorway of the main hall

verses.name: I Kings 6:34
verses.text: and two doors of cypress wood; one door <transChange type="added">with</transChange> two folding panels and the second door <transChange type="added">with</transChange> two folding panels.

verses.name: I Kings 6:35
verses.text: He carved cherubim and palm tree images and budding flowers and overlaid them with gold evenly applied on the carved work.

verses.name: I Kings 6:36
verses.text: Then he built the inner courtyard <transChange type="added">with</transChange> three rows of dressed stone and a row of cedar beams.

verses.name: I Kings 6:37
verses.text: In the fourth year,<note placement="foot">That is, the fourth year of Solomon’s reign</note> the house of Yahweh was founded in the month of Ziv.

verses.name: I Kings 6:38
verses.text: In the eleventh year in the month of Bul, that is, the eighth month, the house was finished <transChange type="added">according</transChange> to all his specifications and <transChange type="added">according</transChange> to all his plans. He had built it in seven years.  <chapter eID="1Kgs.6"/>

verses.name: I Kings 7:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1938"/><title type="x-s">Solomon Continues to Build</title> <div sID="gen2679" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1938"/>Solomon built his house <transChange type="added">over</transChange> thirteen years, and he finished all of his house.  <div eID="gen2679" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 7:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1939"/><div sID="gen2680" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1939"/>He built the House of the Forest of Lebanon; one hundred cubits its length, fifty cubits its width, and thirty cubits its height, on four rows of cedar pillars and cedar beams atop the pillars.

verses.name: I Kings 7:3
verses.text: It was covered with cedar above, and the supporting beams which <transChange type="added">were</transChange> on the forty-five pillars, fifteen <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the row.

verses.name: I Kings 7:4
verses.text: <transChange type="added">There were</transChange> three rows of specially designed windows; <transChange type="added">with</transChange> window to window three times.

verses.name: I Kings 7:5
verses.text: All of the doorways and the doorframes <transChange type="added">had</transChange> four-sided casings, with opening to opposite opening three times.  <div eID="gen2680" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 7:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1940"/><div sID="gen2681" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1940"/>The hall of pillars he made fifty cubits <transChange type="added">in</transChange> its length and thirty cubits <transChange type="added">in</transChange> its width, and a porch <transChange type="added">was</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in front of them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “on their face”</note> with pillars and an overhang <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in front of them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “on their face”</note>

verses.name: I Kings 7:7
verses.text: He made the hall of the throne where he <transChange type="added">would</transChange> pronounce judgment, the hall of justice, and <transChange type="added">it was</transChange> covered with cedar from the floor to the rafters.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “floor,” but other ancient versions have “rafters”</note>

verses.name: I Kings 7:8
verses.text: His house where he would live in the next courtyard on the inside of the porch was like this work, and he would make a house like this porch for the daughter of Pharaoh whom Solomon had taken <transChange type="added">as wife</transChange>.

verses.name: I Kings 7:9
verses.text: All of these <transChange type="added">were</transChange> of precious stones, according to the measurement of dressed stone, sawn with a saw <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞on all sides⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “on the inside and on the outside”</note> from <transChange type="added">the</transChange> foundation up to the eaves and from <transChange type="added">the</transChange> outside up to the great courtyard.

verses.name: I Kings 7:10
verses.text: <transChange type="added">The</transChange> foundation <transChange type="added">was of</transChange> precious stones, <transChange type="added">and</transChange> large stones of ten cubits and stones of eight cubits

verses.name: I Kings 7:11
verses.text: with precious stones above, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞just the right size⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “according to the measurement of dressed stones”</note> and cedar.

verses.name: I Kings 7:12
verses.text: The great courtyard all around had three rows of dressed stones and a row of cedar beams; for <transChange type="added">both</transChange> the courtyard of the inner house<note placement="foot">Or “temple”</note> of Yahweh and for the porch of the house.  <div eID="gen2681" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 7:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1941"/><div sID="gen2682" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1941"/>King Solomon invited and received Hiram from Tyre.

verses.name: I Kings 7:14
verses.text: He <transChange type="added">was</transChange> the son of a widow woman from the tribe of Naphtali, and his father <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a man of Tyre, an artisan of bronze. He was filled with wisdom and with ability and with the knowledge to do all the work with the bronze. And he came to King Solomon, and he did all of his work.

verses.name: I Kings 7:15
verses.text: He cast the two pillars <transChange type="added">out of</transChange> bronze; eighteen cubits <transChange type="added">was</transChange> the height of the first, and a cord of twelve cubits would encircle the second pillar.

verses.name: I Kings 7:16
verses.text: He made two capitals to place on the tops of the pillars <transChange type="added">out of</transChange> molten bronze; the first capital <transChange type="added">was</transChange> five cubits <transChange type="added">in</transChange> height, and the second capital <transChange type="added">was</transChange> five cubits <transChange type="added">in</transChange> height.

verses.name: I Kings 7:17
verses.text: A network of latticework <transChange type="added">and</transChange> wreaths of chainwork with small chains <transChange type="added">were</transChange> for the capitals which <transChange type="added">were</transChange> on top of the pillars; seven for the first capital and seven for the second capital.

verses.name: I Kings 7:18
verses.text: He also made the pillars with two rows around on the lattice, each to cover the capitals which <transChange type="added">were</transChange> on top, <transChange type="added">out of</transChange> the pomegranate-shaped ornaments, and thus he did for the second capital <transChange type="added">as well</transChange>.

verses.name: I Kings 7:19
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">on</transChange> the capitals which <transChange type="added">were</transChange> on top of the pillars in the porch <transChange type="added">were</transChange> works of lilies four cubits <transChange type="added">high</transChange>.

verses.name: I Kings 7:20
verses.text: And capitals <transChange type="added">were</transChange> on the two pillars above near the bulging section which was beside the lattice, and two hundred pomegranate-shaped ornaments <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in rows all around on the second capital.

verses.name: I Kings 7:21
verses.text: He set up the pillars for the porch of the main hall; he erected the pillar on the right and called its name Jakin, and he set up the pillar on the left and called its name Boaz.

verses.name: I Kings 7:22
verses.text: On the top of the pillars <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a work of lilies; and so the work of the pillars <transChange type="added">was</transChange> finished.  <div eID="gen2682" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 7:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1942"/><div sID="gen2683" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1942"/>He also made the molten<note placement="foot">That is, cast from molten bronze</note> sea, ten cubits <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in diameter⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “from its edge up to its edge, round all around”</note> and five cubits <transChange type="added">was</transChange> its height. A measuring line of thirty cubits would encircle it all around.

verses.name: I Kings 7:24
verses.text: Gourds <transChange type="added">were</transChange> under its rim surrounding it all around; ten to the cubit, surrounding the sea all around with two rows of gourds, <transChange type="added">which</transChange> were cast when he cast the metal.

verses.name: I Kings 7:25
verses.text: <transChange type="added">The sea</transChange> was standing on twelve oxen, with three facing to the north, three facing to the west, three facing to the south, and three facing to the east. The sea <transChange type="added">was</transChange> on top of them, with all of their hindquarters <transChange type="added">turned</transChange> to the inside.

verses.name: I Kings 7:26
verses.text: Its thickness <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a handbreadth, but its rim <transChange type="added">was</transChange> as the work on the brim of a cup, <transChange type="added">like the</transChange> bud of a lily; it held two thousand baths.  <div eID="gen2683" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 7:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1943"/><div sID="gen2684" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1943"/>He made the ten stands of bronze; each stand <transChange type="added">was</transChange> four cubits long, four cubits wide, and three cubits in height.

verses.name: I Kings 7:28
verses.text: Now this <transChange type="added">was</transChange> the construction of the stands: there <transChange type="added">were</transChange> frames for them and frames between the crossbars,

verses.name: I Kings 7:29
verses.text: and on the frames which <transChange type="added">were</transChange> between the crossbars <transChange type="added">were</transChange> lions, oxen, and cherubim. On the crossbars both above and beneath the lions and oxen <transChange type="added">were</transChange> works of cascading wreaths.

verses.name: I Kings 7:30
verses.text: <transChange type="added">There were</transChange> four bronze wheels for each of the stands, with bronze axles; the four support pedestals for these <transChange type="added">were</transChange> under the basin, and the supports <transChange type="added">were</transChange> decorated on each side <transChange type="added">with</transChange> wreaths.

verses.name: I Kings 7:31
verses.text: Its opening from <transChange type="added">the</transChange> inside of the capital and above <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a cubit; its pedestal <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a round work of a cubit and a half; moreover, on its opening <transChange type="added">were</transChange> the carvings with four-sided frames, not circular.

verses.name: I Kings 7:32
verses.text: Four of the wheels <transChange type="added">were</transChange> underneath the frames, and the axles of the wheels <transChange type="added">were</transChange> on the stands. The height of each wheel <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a cubit and a half.

verses.name: I Kings 7:33
verses.text: The construction of the wheel <transChange type="added">was</transChange> like the construction of the wheel of the chariot; their axles, their rims, their spokes, and their naves <transChange type="added">were</transChange> all cast.

verses.name: I Kings 7:34
verses.text: The four supports <transChange type="added">were</transChange> the four corners of each stand, with the stand supporting it.

verses.name: I Kings 7:35
verses.text: On top of the stand <transChange type="added">was</transChange> half a cubit deep, circular all around, and on the top of the stand <transChange type="added">were</transChange> its supports and its frames.

verses.name: I Kings 7:36
verses.text: He engraved on the plates, on its supports, and on its frame cherubim, lions and images of a palm tree, according to the space for each, with wreaths all around.

verses.name: I Kings 7:37
verses.text: He made the ten stands like this in one cast, with the same measurement and shape for each of them.  <div eID="gen2684" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 7:38
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1944"/><div sID="gen2685" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1944"/>He also made ten bronze basins, <transChange type="added">each</transChange> holding forty baths; each basin <transChange type="added">was</transChange> four cubits, one basin on each of the ten stands.

verses.name: I Kings 7:39
verses.text: He placed five of the stands on the south side of the house and five on the north side of the house, and the sea he set on the southeast side of the house.  <div eID="gen2685" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 7:40
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1945"/><div sID="gen2686" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1945"/>Hiram also made the basins and the shovels and the bowls for drinking wine; and so Hiram finished doing all of the work <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞that he was to do⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “that he did”</note> for King Solomon in the house of Yahweh:

verses.name: I Kings 7:41
verses.text: the two pillars and the bowls of the capitals which <transChange type="added">were</transChange> atop the two pillars, and the two lattice works to cover the two bowls of the capitals which <transChange type="added">were</transChange> atop the pillars;

verses.name: I Kings 7:42
verses.text: and the four hundred pomegranate-shaped ornaments for the two lattice works, the two rows of pomegranate-shaped ornaments for each latticework to cover the two bowls of the capitals which <transChange type="added">were</transChange> on the surface of the pillars;

verses.name: I Kings 7:43
verses.text: and the ten stands and the ten basins on the stands;

verses.name: I Kings 7:44
verses.text: and the one sea and the twelve oxen under the sea;

verses.name: I Kings 7:45
verses.text: and the pots, the shovels, and the bowls for drinking wine. All the vessels of the tent which Hiram had made for King Solomon <transChange type="added">for</transChange> the house of Yahweh <transChange type="added">were</transChange> polished bronze.

verses.name: I Kings 7:46
verses.text: The king had cast them in the plain of the Jordan with the casting mold <transChange type="added">set in</transChange> the ground between Succoth and Zarethan.

verses.name: I Kings 7:47
verses.text: Solomon left all of the vessels <transChange type="added">unweighed</transChange> because of their very great abundance, so the weight of the bronze could not be determined.  <div eID="gen2686" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 7:48
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1946"/><div sID="gen2687" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1946"/>Solomon also made all of the vessels which <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in the house of Yahweh: the golden altar and the golden table on which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> the bread of the presence;

verses.name: I Kings 7:49
verses.text: as well as the five lampstands of beaten gold at the south and five lampstands at the north before the presence of the inner sanctuary, with the flower-shaped ornaments, the lamps, and the pair of tongs <transChange type="added">all of gold</transChange>.

verses.name: I Kings 7:50
verses.text: The cups, the snuffers, the bowls for drinking wine, the bowls for the incense, and the firepans <transChange type="added">were made from</transChange> beaten gold; the facades for the doors of the inner house, for the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞most holy place⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “holy of the holiest”</note> for the doors of the main hall of the temple <transChange type="added">were of</transChange> gold.

verses.name: I Kings 7:51
verses.text: <transChange type="added">When</transChange> all of the work which king Solomon did on the house of Yahweh was completed, Solomon brought out the holy objects of his father David, the silver and the gold and the vessels, <transChange type="added">which</transChange> he put in the treasury rooms of the house of Yahweh.  <chapter eID="1Kgs.7"/>

verses.name: I Kings 8:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1947"/><title type="x-s">The Dedication of the Temple</title> <div sID="gen2688" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1947"/>At that time, Solomon assembled the elders of Israel, all the heads of the tribes, and the leaders of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞families⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “fathers”</note> of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> before King Solomon, in order to bring up the ark of the covenant of Yahweh from the city of David, that is, Zion.

verses.name: I Kings 8:2
verses.text: All the men of Israel assembled before King Solomon at the festival in the month of Ethnaim, that is, the seventh month.

verses.name: I Kings 8:3
verses.text: All the elders of Israel came, and the priests carried the ark.

verses.name: I Kings 8:4
verses.text: So they brought up the ark of Yahweh and the tent of assembly<note placement="foot">Or “meeting”</note> and all of the holy vessels that <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in the tent; the priests and the Levites brought them up.

verses.name: I Kings 8:5
verses.text: King Solomon and all the assembly of Israel who were assembling with him in the presence of the ark <transChange type="added">were</transChange> sacrificing sheep and oxen that could not be counted nor numbered because of abundance.

verses.name: I Kings 8:6
verses.text: The priests brought the ark of the covenant of Yahweh to its place in the inner sanctuary of the house, to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞most holy place⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “holy of the holiest”</note> under the wings of the cherubim,

verses.name: I Kings 8:7
verses.text: for the cherubim <transChange type="added">were</transChange> spreading their wings over the place of the ark. The cherubim overshadowed the ark and its poles from above.

verses.name: I Kings 8:8
verses.text: The poles <transChange type="added">were</transChange> long, and the ends of the poles could be seen from the holy place <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in front of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “on the face of”</note> the inner sanctuary, but they could not be seen <transChange type="added">from</transChange> the outside, and they are there until this day.

verses.name: I Kings 8:9
verses.text: There was not <transChange type="added">anything</transChange> in the ark <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞except⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Hebrew “only”</note> the two tablets of stone which Moses had placed there at Horeb, where Yahweh <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞made⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “cut”</note> a covenant with the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> after they went out from the land of Egypt.

verses.name: I Kings 8:10
verses.text: When the priests went out from the holy place, the cloud filled the house of Yahweh.

verses.name: I Kings 8:11
verses.text: The priests <transChange type="added">were</transChange> not able to stand to minister <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞because of the presence of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from the face of”</note> the cloud, for the glory of Yahweh filled the house of Yahweh.  <div eID="gen2688" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 8:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1948"/><title type="x-s">Solomon’s Proclamation to the Assembly of Israel</title> <div sID="gen2689" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1948"/>Then Solomon said, “Yahweh has said that <transChange type="added">he</transChange> would dwell in the very thick cloud.

verses.name: I Kings 8:13
verses.text: I have certainly built a lofty house for you, a place for you to live forever.”

verses.name: I Kings 8:14
verses.text: <transChange type="added">Then</transChange> the king turned his face around, and he blessed all of the assembly of Israel. (Now all the assembly of Israel was standing).

verses.name: I Kings 8:15
verses.text: Then he said, “Blessed be Yahweh the God of Israel who has promised with his mouth <transChange type="added">to</transChange> David my father and fulfilled <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞by his oath⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “by his hand”</note> saying,

verses.name: I Kings 8:16
verses.text: ‘From the day that I brought out my people Israel from Egypt I have not chosen a city from all the tribes of Israel to build a house where my name might be, but I have chosen David to be over my people Israel.’

verses.name: I Kings 8:17
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞David my father desired⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “It had been within the heart of David my father”</note> to build a house for the name of Yahweh the God of Israel,

verses.name: I Kings 8:18
verses.text: but Yahweh said to David my father, ‘Because <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you desired⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “it was within your heart”</note> to build a house for my name, you did well in that it was within your heart.

verses.name: I Kings 8:19
verses.text: However, you will not build the house, but your son who has come from your loins, he shall build the house for my name.’

verses.name: I Kings 8:20
verses.text: Yahweh has carried out his promise which he had made; I have risen in place of David my father, and I sit on the throne of Israel as Yahweh promised, and I have built the house for the name of Yahweh the God of Israel.

verses.name: I Kings 8:21
verses.text: I have provided a place there for the ark, in which is the covenant which Yahweh made with our ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> when He brought them out of the land of Egypt.”  <div eID="gen2689" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 8:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1949"/><title type="x-s">Solomon’s Prayer to Yahweh</title> <div sID="gen2690" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1949"/>Then Solomon stood before the altar of Yahweh in the presence of all of the assembly of Israel, and he spread out his hands <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the heavens,

verses.name: I Kings 8:23
verses.text: and he said, “O Yahweh, God of Israel, there is no god like you in the heavens above or on the earth beneath, keeping the covenant and the loyal love for your servants who are walking before you with all their heart.

verses.name: I Kings 8:24
verses.text: You have kept for your servant David my father what you promised to him, and you have spoken with your mouth, and with your hand you have fulfilled <transChange type="added">it</transChange> this very day.

verses.name: I Kings 8:25
verses.text: So then, O Yahweh, God of Israel, keep for your servant David my father what you promised to him, saying, ‘For you, no man will be cut off from before me who <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> sitting on the throne of Israel, if only your sons keep their ways to walk before me just as you have walked before me.’

verses.name: I Kings 8:26
verses.text: So then, O God of Israel, please let your word be confirmed which you have promised<note placement="foot">Or “spoken”</note> to your servant David my father.

verses.name: I Kings 8:27
verses.text: For will God really dwell on the earth? Behold, the heavens and the heaven of heavens could not contain you! <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞How could⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Even that”</note> this house that I have built?

verses.name: I Kings 8:28
verses.text: You must regard the prayer of your servant and his plea! O Yahweh my God, listen to the pleading and to the prayer that your servant <transChange type="added">is</transChange> praying before you this day,

verses.name: I Kings 8:29
verses.text: so that your eyes <transChange type="added">will</transChange> be open to this house night and day, to the place which you said, ‘My name will be there,’ to hear the prayer that your servant prays toward this place.

verses.name: I Kings 8:30
verses.text: You must listen to the plea of your servant and your people Israel which they pray <transChange type="added">toward</transChange> this place; and you must hear from the place where you live, from heaven you must hear and you must forgive.

verses.name: I Kings 8:31
verses.text: <transChange type="added">If</transChange> a man sins against his neighbor and he pronounces an oath against him to curse him, and the curse comes before your altar in this house,

verses.name: I Kings 8:32
verses.text: then you shall hear in heaven and you shall act and you shall judge your servant, to declare the wicked guilty by bringing his way upon his head and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to declare the righteous innocent⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to declare righteous the righteous”</note> by rewarding him according to his righteousness.

verses.name: I Kings 8:33
verses.text: When your people Israel are defeated before the enemy <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞because⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “who”</note> they sinned against you, and <transChange type="added">when</transChange> they turn to you and confess your name and pray and beg for mercy from you in this house,

verses.name: I Kings 8:34
verses.text: then you shall hear in heaven and forgive the sin of your people Israel, and you shall bring them back to the ground which you gave to their ancestors.<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note>

verses.name: I Kings 8:35
verses.text: When you shut up the heavens so there is no rain because they have sinned against you, then they pray to this place and they confess your name and they return from their sin because you punished them,

verses.name: I Kings 8:36
verses.text: then you shall hear in heaven and forgive the sin of your servants and your people Israel, for you will teach them the good way in which they should go, and you will give rain upon your land which you have given to your people as an inheritance.

verses.name: I Kings 8:37
verses.text: If there should be in the land famine or disease, if there should be blight or mildew or locust or caterpillars, if it happens that his enemy lays siege against him in the land of his gates, if any plague or any disease,

verses.name: I Kings 8:38
verses.text: any prayer or any plea which is <transChange type="added">offered</transChange> by any person for all of your people Israel, who each knows the infestation of his <transChange type="added">own</transChange> heart and spreads out his palms to this house,

verses.name: I Kings 8:39
verses.text: then you shall hear in heaven the place of your dwelling, and you shall forgive and act and give to the man whose heart you know, according to all his ways, for you alone know the heart of all the sons of man.

verses.name: I Kings 8:40
verses.text: <transChange type="added">Do these things</transChange> so that they may fear you all the days that they live on the face of the land that you gave to our ancestors.<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note>

verses.name: I Kings 8:41
verses.text: Also for the foreigner who is not from your people Israel, and he comes from a distant land because of your name,

verses.name: I Kings 8:42
verses.text: (for they shall hear of your great name and your powerful hand and your outstretched arm), and he shall come and pray toward this house,

verses.name: I Kings 8:43
verses.text: you shall hear in heaven, the place of your dwelling, and act according to all that the foreigner calls to you, so that all the peoples of the earth may know your name, to fear you as your people Israel, and to know that your name has been invoked over this house that I have built.

verses.name: I Kings 8:44
verses.text: If your people go out to battle against his enemy in the way that you shall send them and they pray to Yahweh, toward the city which you have chosen and the house which I have built for your name,

verses.name: I Kings 8:45
verses.text: then you shall hear in heaven their prayer and their plea, and you shall <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞vindicate⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “their judgment”</note> them.  <div eID="gen2690" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 8:46
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1950"/><div sID="gen2691" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1950"/>“If they sin against you (for there is not a person who does not sin) and you are angry with them and you give them to an enemy and they take them captive to the land of the enemy far or near,

verses.name: I Kings 8:47
verses.text: and then they return their heart in the land where they have been taken captive and they return and plead to you in the land of their captivity, saying, ‘We have sinned and we did wrong. We acted wickedly,’

verses.name: I Kings 8:48
verses.text: if they return to you with all of their heart and with all of their soul in the land of their enemies who took them captive and they pray to you toward their land which you gave to their ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> the city that you have chosen and the house that you<note placement="foot">The Hebrew Masoretic text (<hi type="italic">Kethib</hi>) reads “you have built”;<hi type="italic">Qere</hi> reads “I have built”</note> built for your name,

verses.name: I Kings 8:49
verses.text: then you shall hear in heaven, the place of your dwelling, their prayer and their plea, and you shall <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞vindicate them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “and you shall do their justice”</note>

verses.name: I Kings 8:50
verses.text: You shall forgive your people who sinned against you, <transChange type="added">even</transChange> for all their transgressions which they committed against you. You shall give them compassion before their captors so that they may have compassion on them,

verses.name: I Kings 8:51
verses.text: for they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> your people and your inheritance whom you brought from Egypt from the middle of the smelter of iron.

verses.name: I Kings 8:52
verses.text: <transChange type="added">O,</transChange> that your eyes <transChange type="added">may</transChange> be open to the plea of your servant and to the plea of your people Israel, to listen to them in all things <transChange type="added">when</transChange> they call to you.

verses.name: I Kings 8:53
verses.text: For you have separated them for yourself as an inheritance from all the peoples of the earth, as you promised through the hand of Moses your servant when you brought out our ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> from Egypt, my Lord Yahweh!”  <div eID="gen2691" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 8:54
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1951"/><title type="x-s">Solomon Charges the People Israel</title> <div sID="gen2692" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1951"/>It happened that when Solomon finished praying to Yahweh all of the prayer and this plea, he got up from before the altar of Yahweh, from kneeling down on his knees with his palms outstretched to heaven.

verses.name: I Kings 8:55
verses.text: He stood and blessed all of the assembly of Israel with a loud voice, saying,

verses.name: I Kings 8:56
verses.text: “Blessed be Yahweh who gave a resting place to his people Israel. According to all that he promised, not one word has fallen from all of his promises <transChange type="added">concerning</transChange> the good which he spoke through the hand of Moses his servant.

verses.name: I Kings 8:57
verses.text: May Yahweh our God be with us as he was with our ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and may he not leave us or abandon us,

verses.name: I Kings 8:58
verses.text: to incline our hearts toward him, to walk in all his ways and to keep his commandments, his statutes, and his judgments which he commanded our ancestors.<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note>

verses.name: I Kings 8:59
verses.text: Let these my words which I pleaded before Yahweh <transChange type="added">be</transChange> near to Yahweh our God, by day and by night, to maintain the justice of his servant and the justice of his people Israel <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as each day requires⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the word of the day on its day”</note>

verses.name: I Kings 8:60
verses.text: so that all of the people of the earth may know that Yahweh, he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> God; there is none other.

verses.name: I Kings 8:61
verses.text: Let your heart be completely with Yahweh our God by walking in his statutes, by keeping his commands as this day.”  <div eID="gen2692" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 8:62
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1952"/><title type="x-s">The Great Confirming Sacrifice</title> <div sID="gen2693" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1952"/>Then the king and all of Israel with him offered a sacrifice in the presence of Yahweh.

verses.name: I Kings 8:63
verses.text: Solomon sacrificed the fellowship offerings which he offered to Yahweh: twenty-two thousand oxen and one hundred and twenty thousand sheep; and the king and all of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> dedicated the house of Yahweh.

verses.name: I Kings 8:64
verses.text: On that day the king consecrated the middle of the courtyard before the house of Yahweh because he offered there the burnt offerings, the grain offerings, and the fat of the fellowship offerings because the bronze altar that was in the presence of Yahweh was too small to hold the burnt offerings and the grain offerings and the fat of the fellowship offerings.

verses.name: I Kings 8:65
verses.text: Solomon held the festival at that time and all of Israel with him, a great assembly from Lebo Hamath up to the wadi<note placement="foot">A valley that is dry most of the year, but contains a stream during the rainy season</note> of Egypt before Yahweh our God, for seven days <transChange type="added">and</transChange> seven days, <transChange type="added">a total of</transChange> fourteen days.

verses.name: I Kings 8:66
verses.text: On the eighth day, he sent the people away, and they blessed the king, and they went to their tents rejoicing and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in good spirits⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and good of heart”</note> because of all the goodness that Yahweh had shown to David his servant and to Israel his people.  <chapter eID="1Kgs.8"/>

verses.name: I Kings 9:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1953"/><title type="x-s">Yahweh’s Challenge to Solomon</title> <div sID="gen2694" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1953"/>It happened that as Solomon finished the building of the house of Yahweh, the king’s house, and all the things Solomon desired to do,

verses.name: I Kings 9:2
verses.text: Yahweh appeared to Solomon a second time, as he had appeared to him in Gibeon.

verses.name: I Kings 9:3
verses.text: Yahweh said to him, “I have heard your prayer and your plea which you have made before me. I have consecrated this house which you have built, by putting my name there forever. My eyes and my heart will always be there.

verses.name: I Kings 9:4
