verses.text: As for you, if you walk before me as David your father walked, with <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞integrity of heart⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in blamelessness of heart”</note> and with uprightness, to do according to all that I have commanded you, <transChange type="added">and if</transChange> you keep my ordinances and my judgments,

verses.name: I Kings 9:5
verses.text: then I will establish the throne of your kingdom over Israel forever, as I promised David your father, saying, ‘A man will not be cut off for you from upon the throne of Israel.’  <div eID="gen2694" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 9:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1954"/><div sID="gen2695" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1954"/>“If ever you or any of your descendants<note placement="foot">Or “children”</note> turn from <transChange type="added">following</transChange> me and do not keep my commandments <transChange type="added">and</transChange> my ordinances that I have set before you and you go and serve other gods and bow down to them,

verses.name: I Kings 9:7
verses.text: then I will cut Israel off from the face of the land that I have given to them, <transChange type="added">even</transChange> the house which I have consecrated for my name I will cast away from my face; and Israel shall become a proverb and an object of taunting among all the peoples.

verses.name: I Kings 9:8
verses.text: This house shall become a heap of ruins; all those passing by will be appalled by it and hiss, and they will say, ‘On what account did Yahweh do this to this land and to this house?’

verses.name: I Kings 9:9
verses.text: And they will say, ‘Because they have forsaken Yahweh their God who brought their ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> out from the land of Egypt and they embraced other gods and bowed down to them and served them. Therefore, Yahweh brought on them all of this disaster.’ ”  <div eID="gen2695" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 9:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1955"/><title type="x-s">Solomon and Hiram Complete Their Agreement</title> <div sID="gen2696" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1955"/>It happened at the end of twenty years <transChange type="added">in</transChange> which Solomon had built the two houses, the house of Yahweh and the house of the king,

verses.name: I Kings 9:11
verses.text: <transChange type="added">since</transChange> Hiram king of Tyre had supplied Solomon with wood of cedar and with wood of cypresses and with the gold according to all his desire, then King Solomon gave twenty cities in the land of the Galilee to Hiram.

verses.name: I Kings 9:12
verses.text: So Hiram went out from Tyre to see the cities that Solomon had given him, but they were not right in his eyes.

verses.name: I Kings 9:13
verses.text: So he said, “What <transChange type="added">are</transChange> these cities that you have given to me, my brother?” <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞So they are called the land of Cabul until this day⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “So he called them the land of Cabul up to this day”</note>

verses.name: I Kings 9:14
verses.text: Then Hiram sent to the king a hundred and twenty talents of gold.  <div eID="gen2696" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 9:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1956"/><title type="x-s">Solomon’s Accomplishments</title> <div sID="gen2697" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1956"/>This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the account of the forced labor that King Solomon conscripted to build the house of Yahweh and his house, the Millo, the walls of Jerusalem, Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer.

verses.name: I Kings 9:16
verses.text: Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, had gone up and captured Gezer and burnt it with fire. He had also killed the Canaanites who were living in the city and had given it as a dowry to his daughter, the wife of Solomon.

verses.name: I Kings 9:17
verses.text: Solomon rebuilt Gezer and Lower Beth-Horon,

verses.name: I Kings 9:18
verses.text: <transChange type="added">as well as</transChange> Baalath and Tamar in the wilderness in the land;

verses.name: I Kings 9:19
verses.text: and <transChange type="added">he also built</transChange> all of the storage cities which were Solomon’s, the cities <transChange type="added">for</transChange> the chariots, the cities <transChange type="added">for</transChange> the cavalry, and all of Solomon’s desire that he wanted<note placement="foot">Or “desired”</note> to build in Jerusalem and in Lebanon and in all the land of his dominion.  <div eID="gen2697" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 9:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1957"/><div sID="gen2698" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1957"/>All of the people who were remaining from the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> not of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note>

verses.name: I Kings 9:21
verses.text: their children who remained after them in the land, whom the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> were not able to completely destroy, Solomon conscripted them for forced labor, until this very day.

verses.name: I Kings 9:22
verses.text: But from the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> Solomon did not make a slave, but they <transChange type="added">were</transChange> the men of war, his officers, his commanders, his captains, and the commanders of his chariots and his cavalry.

verses.name: I Kings 9:23
verses.text: These <transChange type="added">were</transChange> the commanders of the overseers who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> over the work for Solomon, five hundred and fifty, ruling over the people doing the work.  <div eID="gen2698" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 9:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1958"/><div sID="gen2699" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1958"/>As soon as the daughter of Pharaoh went up from the city of David to her house which he<note placement="foot">That is, Solomon</note> built for her, then he built the Millo.  <div eID="gen2699" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 9:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1959"/><div sID="gen2700" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1959"/>Solomon sacrificed three times a year: burnt offerings and fellowship offerings on the altar that he had built to Yahweh, and he offered incense with it before Yahweh; and so he completed the house.  <div eID="gen2700" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 9:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1960"/><div sID="gen2701" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1960"/>King Solomon also built a fleet of ships at Ezion-Geber which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> near Elath on the shore of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Red Sea⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sea of reed”</note> in the land of Edom.

verses.name: I Kings 9:27
verses.text: Hiram sent his servants with the fleet of ships, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞sailors⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “men of ships”</note> who knew the sea, with the servants of Solomon.

verses.name: I Kings 9:28
verses.text: They went to Ophir and imported from there four hundred and twenty talents of gold, and they brought it to King Solomon.  <chapter eID="1Kgs.9"/>

verses.name: I Kings 10:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1961"/><title type="x-s">The Visit of the Queen of Sheba</title> <div sID="gen2702" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1961"/>Now the queen of Sheba had heard of the fame of Solomon regarding the name of Yahweh, and she came to test him with hard questions.

verses.name: I Kings 10:2
verses.text: So she came to Jerusalem with very great wealth; <transChange type="added">with</transChange> camels carrying spices, very much gold, and precious stones. She came to Solomon, and she spoke to him all that was on her heart.

verses.name: I Kings 10:3
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Solomon answered all of her questions⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “Solomon told her all of her words”</note> there was not a thing hidden from the king which he could not explain to her.

verses.name: I Kings 10:4
verses.text: When the queen of Sheba observed all the wisdom of Solomon and the house which he had built,

verses.name: I Kings 10:5
verses.text: the food of his table, the seat of his servants, the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞manner⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “service”</note> of his servants and their clothing, his cupbearers, and his burnt offerings which he offered in the house of Yahweh, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞she was breathless⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “and there was not in her spirit/breath any longer”</note>

verses.name: I Kings 10:6
verses.text: Then she said to the king, “The report which I heard in my land was true concerning your accomplishments and your wisdom.

verses.name: I Kings 10:7
verses.text: I had not believed the report to be true until I came and my eyes had seen, and behold! The half had not been told to me. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Your wisdom and prosperity surpass⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “You have added wisdom and prosperity to”</note> the report that I had heard.

verses.name: I Kings 10:8
verses.text: Happy <transChange type="added">are</transChange> your men and happy <transChange type="added">are</transChange> these your servants who stand before you continually hearing your wisdom.

verses.name: I Kings 10:9
verses.text: May Yahweh your God be blessed, who has delighted in you to set you on the throne of Israel, because of the love of Yahweh for Israel forever, and he has made you king to execute justice and righteousness.”

verses.name: I Kings 10:10
verses.text: Then she gave the king a hundred and twenty talents of gold, abundant spices, and precious stones. Spices as these did not come again in such abundance <transChange type="added">as that which</transChange> the queen of Sheba brought to King Solomon.  <div eID="gen2702" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 10:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1962"/><div sID="gen2703" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1962"/>Moreover, the fleet of ships of Hiram which carried the gold from Ophir <transChange type="added">also</transChange> brought from Ophir abundant amounts of almug wood and precious stones.

verses.name: I Kings 10:12
verses.text: The king made a raised structure for the house of Yahweh and for the house of the king out of the almug wood, as well as lyres and harps for the singers. <transChange type="added">This much</transChange> almug wood has not come nor been seen <transChange type="added">again</transChange> up to this day.

verses.name: I Kings 10:13
verses.text: King Solomon gave to the queen of Sheba all of her desire that she asked, besides that which <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞King Solomon freely offered her⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “according to the hand of King Solomon”</note> Then she turned and went to her land with her servants.  <div eID="gen2703" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 10:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1963"/><div sID="gen2704" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1963"/>The weight of the gold that came to Solomon in one year <transChange type="added">was</transChange> six hundred and sixty-six talents of gold,

verses.name: I Kings 10:15
verses.text: apart from <transChange type="added">that of</transChange> the men of the traders and the profits of the traders, and all the kings of the Arabs and the governors of the land.

verses.name: I Kings 10:16
verses.text: King Solomon made two hundred shields of hammered gold; six hundred <transChange type="added">measures of</transChange> gold went up over each shield.

verses.name: I Kings 10:17
verses.text: Also <transChange type="added">he made</transChange> three hundred small shields of hammered gold; three minas of gold went up over each of the small shields; and the king put them <transChange type="added">into</transChange> the House of the Forest of Lebanon.

verses.name: I Kings 10:18
verses.text: The king also made a large ivory throne, and he overlaid it <transChange type="added">with</transChange> fine gold.

verses.name: I Kings 10:19
verses.text: Six steps <transChange type="added">led up</transChange> to the throne, and <transChange type="added">there was</transChange> a circular top to the throne behind it, and armrests were <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞on each side of the seat⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “from this and from this”</note> with two lions standing beside the armrests.

verses.name: I Kings 10:20
verses.text: Twelve lions <transChange type="added">were</transChange> standing there, six on each of the six steps <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞on either side⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “from this and from this”</note> nothing like this was made for any of the kingdoms.

verses.name: I Kings 10:21
verses.text: All of the drinking vessels of King Solomon <transChange type="added">were</transChange> gold, and all the vessels for the House of the Forest of Lebanon were pure gold. There was no silver; <transChange type="added">it was</transChange> not considered as something valuable in the days of Solomon.

verses.name: I Kings 10:22
verses.text: For the fleet of Tarshish belonged to the king <transChange type="added">and was</transChange> on the sea with the fleet of Hiram; once every three years the fleet of Tarshish used to come carrying gold and silver, ivory, apes, and baboons.  <div eID="gen2704" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 10:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1964"/><div sID="gen2705" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1964"/>King Solomon was greater than all the kings of the earth with respect to wealth and wisdom.

verses.name: I Kings 10:24
verses.text: All of the earth <transChange type="added">was</transChange> seeking the presence of Solomon, to hear his wisdom which God had put in his heart.

verses.name: I Kings 10:25
verses.text: They <transChange type="added">were</transChange> each bringing his gift; objects of silver and objects of gold, clothing, weapons, spices, horses, and mules. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞This used to happen year after year⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “A thing of year to year”</note>  <div eID="gen2705" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 10:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1965"/><div sID="gen2706" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1965"/>Solomon gathered chariots and horses; he had fourteen hundred chariots and twelve thousand horses. He stationed them in the cities of the chariots and with the king in Jerusalem.

verses.name: I Kings 10:27
verses.text: The king made the silver in Jerusalem as the stones, and the cedars he made as the sycamore fig trees which are in the Shephelah in abundance.

verses.name: I Kings 10:28
verses.text: The import of the horses which were Solomon’s <transChange type="added">was</transChange> from Egypt and from Kue; the traders of the king received <transChange type="added">horses</transChange> from Kue at a price.

verses.name: I Kings 10:29
verses.text: A chariot went up and went out from Egypt at six hundred silver <transChange type="added">shekels</transChange> and a horse at a hundred and fifty. So it was for all the kings of the Hittites and for the kings of Aram; by their hand they were exported.  <chapter eID="1Kgs.10"/>

verses.name: I Kings 11:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1966"/><title type="x-s">Solomon’s Foreign Wives</title> <div sID="gen2707" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1966"/>King Solomon loved many foreign women: the daughter of Pharaoh, Moabite, Ammonite, Edomite, Sidonian, Hittite;

verses.name: I Kings 11:2
verses.text: from the nations which Yahweh had said to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> “You shall not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞marry them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “go into them”</note> and they shall not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞marry you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “go into you”</note> They will certainly turn your heart after other gods.” But Solomon clung to them to love.

verses.name: I Kings 11:3
verses.text: He had seven hundred princesses and three hundred concubines, and his wives turned his heart.  <div eID="gen2707" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 11:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1967"/><title type="x-s">Solomon’s Apostasy</title> <div sID="gen2708" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1967"/>It happened at the time of Solomon’s old age that his wives guided his heart after other gods, and his heart was not fully with Yahweh his God as the heart of David his father <transChange type="added">had been</transChange>.

verses.name: I Kings 11:5
verses.text: Solomon went after Ashtoreth the god of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Sidonians and after Molech the abhorrence of the Ammonites.

verses.name: I Kings 11:6
verses.text: So Solomon did evil in the eyes of Yahweh and did not fully <transChange type="added">follow</transChange> after Yahweh as David his father.

verses.name: I Kings 11:7
verses.text: At that time, Solomon built a high place for Chemosh, the abomination of Moab, on the mountain which <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞faces⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “was on the face of”</note> Jerusalem and for Molech, the abomination of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note>

verses.name: I Kings 11:8
verses.text: Thus he did for all of his foreign wives, offering incense and sacrificing to their gods.  <div eID="gen2708" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 11:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1968"/><title type="x-s">Yahweh’s Judgment on Solomon</title> <div sID="gen2709" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1968"/>Yahweh was angry with Solomon, for he had turned his heart from Yahweh, the God of Israel who had appeared to him twice.

verses.name: I Kings 11:10
verses.text: And he had commanded him concerning this matter not to go after other gods, but he did not keep that which Yahweh commanded.

verses.name: I Kings 11:11
verses.text: So Yahweh said to Solomon, “Because this was with you, and you did not keep my covenant and my ordinances which I have commanded you, I will certainly tear the kingdom from you, and I will give it to your servant.

verses.name: I Kings 11:12
verses.text: However, I will not do it in your days, for the sake of David your father; from the hand of your son I will tear it <transChange type="added">away</transChange>.

verses.name: I Kings 11:13
verses.text: Yet all of the kingdom I will not tear <transChange type="added">away</transChange>. I will give one tribe to your son for the sake of my servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem which I have chosen.”  <div eID="gen2709" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 11:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1969"/><div sID="gen2710" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1969"/>Then Yahweh raised an adversary against Solomon, Hadad the Edomite, from the descendants of that king in Edom.

verses.name: I Kings 11:15
verses.text: It had happened that when David was at Edom, Joab the commander of the army went up to bury the slain, and he killed every male in Edom.

verses.name: I Kings 11:16
verses.text: For Joab and all Israel had stayed there six months until he exterminated every male in Edom.

verses.name: I Kings 11:17
verses.text: But Hadad himself had fled, and some Edomite men from the servants of his father with him, to go to Egypt, when Hadad <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a young boy.

verses.name: I Kings 11:18
verses.text: They had set out from Midian until they came to Paran where they took men from Paran with them and came <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Egypt, <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Pharaoh king of Egypt. He gave to him a house and assigned food for him and gave him land.

verses.name: I Kings 11:19
verses.text: Hadad found great favor in the eyes of Pharaoh, and he gave him the sister of his wife, the sister of Tahpenes the queen, as wife.

verses.name: I Kings 11:20
verses.text: The sister of Tahpenes bore Genubath his son for him, and Tahpenes weaned him in the middle of the house of Pharaoh. Genubath was <transChange type="added">in</transChange> the house of Pharaoh in the midst of the children<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Pharaoh.

verses.name: I Kings 11:21
verses.text: Now Hadad heard in Egypt that David had slept with his ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and that Joab the commander of the army was dead. Then Hadad said to Pharaoh, “Send me away that I may go to my land.”

verses.name: I Kings 11:22
verses.text: Pharaoh said to him, “What do you lack with me that you now <transChange type="added">are</transChange> seeking to go to your land?” He said, “No, but you must surely send me away.”  <div eID="gen2710" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 11:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1970"/><div sID="gen2711" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1970"/>God had <transChange type="added">also</transChange> raised Rezon the son of Eliada as an adversary against him, who had fled from Hadadezer the king of Zobah, his master.

verses.name: I Kings 11:24
verses.text: He gathered men around him and he became the commander of bandits. When David killed <transChange type="added">some of</transChange> them, they went to Damascus and settled <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞there⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “in it”</note> and they reigned in Damascus.

verses.name: I Kings 11:25
verses.text: He was an adversary for Israel all the days of Solomon, and <transChange type="added">along with</transChange> the evil that Hadad <transChange type="added">did</transChange>, he detested Israel <transChange type="added">while</transChange> he reigned over Aram.  <div eID="gen2711" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 11:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1971"/><title type="x-s">Yahweh Raises Up Jeroboam</title> <div sID="gen2712" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1971"/>Now Jeroboam the son of Nebat, an Ephraimite from Zeredah (now the name of his mother <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Zeruah, a widow woman), a servant of Solomon <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞rebelled against the king⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “raised a hand against the king”</note>

verses.name: I Kings 11:27
verses.text: This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the reason that he rebelled against the king: <transChange type="added">when</transChange> Solomon built the Millo, he closed the gap of the city of David his father.

verses.name: I Kings 11:28
verses.text: Now the man Jeroboam <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a man of ability, and Solomon saw that the young man <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞was a diligent worker⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “was a doer of work he”</note> so he appointed him over all of the forced labor for the house of Joseph.

verses.name: I Kings 11:29
verses.text: It happened at that time that Jeroboam went out from Jerusalem, and he accidentally met Ahijah the Shilonite the prophet on the way. Now he had clothed himself with new clothing. While the two of them <transChange type="added">were</transChange> alone in the field,

verses.name: I Kings 11:30
verses.text: Ahijah took hold of the new cloak which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> on him and tore it into twelve pieces.

verses.name: I Kings 11:31
verses.text: Then he said to Jeroboam, “Take for yourself ten pieces, for thus says Yahweh, the God of Israel: ‘Behold, I <transChange type="added">am about</transChange> to tear the kingdom from the hand of Solomon, and I will give to you ten tribes,

verses.name: I Kings 11:32
verses.text: but one tribe shall be for him, for the sake of my servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem, the city which I have chosen from all the tribes of Israel;

verses.name: I Kings 11:33
verses.text: because he has forsaken me, and they bowed down to Ashtoreth, the god of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Sidonians, to Chemosh, the god of Moab, and to Molech, the god of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> They did not walk in my ways to do right in my eyes, my ordinances, or my judgments, as <transChange type="added">did</transChange> David his father.

verses.name: I Kings 11:34
verses.text: But I will not take all of the kingdom from his hand, but I will make him a leader all the days of his life for the sake of David my servant whom I chose, who kept my commandments and my ordinances.

verses.name: I Kings 11:35
verses.text: But I will take the kingship from the hand of his son, and I will give ten tribes to you.

verses.name: I Kings 11:36
verses.text: To his son I will give one tribe in order to be a lamp for my servant David, always before my face, in Jerusalem the city in which I have chosen to place my name.

verses.name: I Kings 11:37
verses.text: You I will take, and you shall reign over all your soul desires, and you shall be king over Israel.

verses.name: I Kings 11:38
verses.text: It shall be that if you listen to all that I command you and you walk in my ways and you do right in my eyes by keeping my statutes and my commandments, as David my servant did, then I will be with you, and I will build an enduring house for you as I built for David, and I will give Israel to you.

verses.name: I Kings 11:39
verses.text: I will punish the offspring of David on account of this; however, not always.’ ”

verses.name: I Kings 11:40
verses.text: Then Solomon sought to kill Jeroboam, but Jeroboam got up and fled to Egypt, to Shishak the king of Egypt, and he remained in Egypt until the death of Solomon.  <div eID="gen2712" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 11:41
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1972"/><div sID="gen2713" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1972"/>Now the rest of the acts of Solomon and all that he did and his wisdom; <transChange type="added">are</transChange> they not written on the scroll of the acts of Solomon?

verses.name: I Kings 11:42
verses.text: All the days that Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all of Israel <transChange type="added">were</transChange> forty years.

verses.name: I Kings 11:43
verses.text: Then Solomon slept with his ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and they buried him in the city of David his father, and Rehoboam his son became king in his place.  <chapter eID="1Kgs.11"/>

verses.name: I Kings 12:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1973"/><title type="x-s">Israel’s Appeal to Rehoboam</title> <div sID="gen2714" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1973"/>Then Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all of Israel had come to Shechem to make him king.

verses.name: I Kings 12:2
verses.text: It happened that Jeroboam the son of Nebat heard <transChange type="added">of it</transChange> while he was still in Egypt where he had fled from the face of King Solomon, and Jeroboam had lived in Egypt.

verses.name: I Kings 12:3
verses.text: So they sent and summoned him, and Jeroboam and all the assembly of Israel came. <transChange type="added">Then</transChange> they spoke to Rehoboam, saying,

verses.name: I Kings 12:4
verses.text: “Your father made our yoke heavy; now lighten the hard labor of your father and the heavy yoke which he placed on us, and we will serve you.”

verses.name: I Kings 12:5
verses.text: He said, “Go up for three days and then return to me”; so the people went away.  <div eID="gen2714" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 12:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1974"/><title type="x-s">Rehoboam Seeks Counsel to Respond</title> <div sID="gen2715" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1974"/>Then King Rehoboam consulted with the old men who had been <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞serving⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “standing”</note> before Solomon his father when he was alive, saying, “How are you advising me <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to answer this people⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?”<note placement="foot">Literally “to return a word to this people”</note>

verses.name: I Kings 12:7
verses.text: They said to him, “If you will be a servant today to this people, then you will serve them; and if you answer them and speak good words to them, they will always be your servants.”

verses.name: I Kings 12:8
verses.text: But he rejected the advice of the old men, which they gave him, and he consulted with the youngsters who had grown up with him, who were <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞serving⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “standing”</note> before him.

verses.name: I Kings 12:9
verses.text: He said to them, “What <transChange type="added">are</transChange> you advising that we should reply to this people who spoke to me by saying, ‘Lighten the yoke your father put on us.’ ”

verses.name: I Kings 12:10
verses.text: Then the youngsters who had grown up with him spoke to him, saying, “Thus you shall say to this people who spoke to you: ‘Your father made our yoke heavy, but you lighten <transChange type="added">it</transChange> for us,’ you shall say to them, ‘My little finger is thicker than my father’s loins.

verses.name: I Kings 12:11
verses.text: So then, my father loaded a heavy yoke on all of you, but I will add to your yoke; my father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions!’ ”  <div eID="gen2715" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 12:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1975"/><title type="x-s">Rehoboam Responds Unwisely with Disastrous Results</title> <div sID="gen2716" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1975"/>Jeroboam and all of the people came to Rehoboam on the third day, as the king had spoken: “Return to me on the third day.”

verses.name: I Kings 12:13
verses.text: Then the king answered all the people harshly, <transChange type="added">as</transChange> he had rejected the advice of the old men that they had offered.

verses.name: I Kings 12:14
verses.text: He spoke to them according to the advice of the youngsters, saying, “My father made your yoke heavy, but I will add onto your yoke; my father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions.”

verses.name: I Kings 12:15
verses.text: So the king did not listen to the people, for it was a turning of events from Yahweh in order to fulfill his word which Yahweh had spoken through the hand of Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam the son of Nebat.

verses.name: I Kings 12:16
verses.text: When all of Israel saw that the king would not listen to them, the people answered the king, saying, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞What share do we have in David⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?<note placement="foot">Literally “What is for us a share in David”</note> There is no inheritance in the son of Jesse. To your tents, Israel! Now look to your house, David!” Then Israel went to their<note placement="foot">Hebrew “his”</note> tents.  <div eID="gen2716" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 12:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1976"/><div sID="gen2717" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1976"/>The <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> were living in the cities of Judah, and Rehoboam was reigning over them.

verses.name: I Kings 12:18
verses.text: King Rehoboam sent Adoram who <transChange type="added">was</transChange> over the forced labor, and all of Israel cast stones at him and he died, but King Rehoboam managed to get up on the chariot to flee <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Jerusalem.

verses.name: I Kings 12:19
verses.text: So Israel rebelled against the house of David until this day.  <div eID="gen2717" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 12:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1977"/><title type="x-s">Civil War Averted</title> <div sID="gen2718" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1977"/>It happened that just when all of Israel heard that Jeroboam had returned, they sent and called him to the assembly and made him king over all of Israel. Not one <transChange type="added">followed</transChange> after the house of David except the tribe of Judah alone.

verses.name: I Kings 12:21
verses.text: When Rehoboam came to Jerusalem, he assembled all of the house of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin, a hundred and eighty thousand <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞choice troops⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “chosen makers of war”</note> to fight with the house of Israel, to restore the kingship to Rehoboam the son of Solomon.

verses.name: I Kings 12:22
verses.text: Then the word of God came to Shemaiah the man of God, saying,

verses.name: I Kings 12:23
verses.text: “Say to Rehoboam the son of Solomon the king of Judah and to all the house of Judah and Benjamin and the remainder of the people, saying,

verses.name: I Kings 12:24
verses.text: ‘Thus says Yahweh: “You shall not go up and you shall not fight with your brothers the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> Return each of you to his house, for this thing was from me.” ’ ” So they heeded the word of Yahweh, and they returned to go home according to the word of Yahweh.  <div eID="gen2718" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 12:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1978"/><title type="x-s">Jeroboam Becomes King over Israel</title> <div sID="gen2719" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1978"/>Then Jeroboam built Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim, and he resided in it. Then he went out from there and built Penuel.

verses.name: I Kings 12:26
verses.text: Then Jeroboam <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞said to himself⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “said to his heart”</note> “Now the kingdom will return to the house of David

verses.name: I Kings 12:27
verses.text: if this people go up to offer sacrifices in the house<note placement="foot">Or “temple”</note> of Yahweh in Jerusalem. The heart of this people will return to their master Rehoboam the king of Judah, and they shall kill me and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞return to him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Hebrew “return to Rehoboam the king of Judah”</note>  <div eID="gen2719" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 12:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1979"/><div sID="gen2720" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1979"/>And the king had decided, so he made two golden calves and he said to them,<note placement="foot">That is, the people</note> “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞You have been going up to Jerusalem long enough⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “enough for you from going up to Jerusalem”</note> here are your gods, O Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt.”

verses.name: I Kings 12:29
verses.text: He put one in Bethel, and the other he put in Dan.

verses.name: I Kings 12:30
verses.text: This thing became a sin, and the people walked before the one as far as Dan.

verses.name: I Kings 12:31
verses.text: Then he built the houses on the high places, and he appointed priests <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from all walks of life⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from the fringes of the people”</note> who were not from the sons of Levi.

verses.name: I Kings 12:32
verses.text: Jeroboam also inaugurated a religious feast in the eighth month on the fifteenth day of the month, like the religious feast which was in Judah, and he offered <transChange type="added">sacrifices</transChange> on the altar. Thus he did in Bethel, by sacrificing to the calves that he had made; and he placed in Bethel the priests of the high places which he had made.

verses.name: I Kings 12:33
verses.text: He offered <transChange type="added">sacrifices</transChange> on the altar which he had made in Bethel on the fifteenth day of the eighth month which his heart had devised. He inaugurated a religious feast for the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> and he went up to the altar to offer incense.  <chapter eID="1Kgs.12"/>

verses.name: I Kings 13:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1980"/><title type="x-s">A Man of God Proclaims Judgment against the False Altar</title> <div sID="gen2721" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1980"/>Suddenly a man of God from Judah came to Bethel, by the word of Yahweh, while Jeroboam <transChange type="added">was</transChange> standing at the altar to offer incense.

verses.name: I Kings 13:2
verses.text: Then he proclaimed against the altar by the word of Yahweh and said, “O altar, altar, thus says Yahweh: ‘Look, a son will be born to the house of David, Josiah by name, and he shall sacrifice on you the priests of the high places who burn incense on you, and human bones shall burn on you.’ ”  <div eID="gen2721" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 13:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1981"/><div sID="gen2722" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1981"/>He gave a sign on that day, saying, “This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the sign that Yahweh has predetermined: Look, <transChange type="added">this</transChange> altar will be torn <transChange type="added">apart</transChange>, and the ashes that <transChange type="added">are</transChange> on it will be poured out.”  <div eID="gen2722" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 13:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1982"/><div sID="gen2723" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1982"/>It happened at the moment the king heard the word of the man of God that he cried out against the altar in Bethel, Jeroboam stretched out his hand from the altar, saying, “Seize him!” But his hand which he stretched out to him was paralyzed, and he was not able to draw it back to himself.

verses.name: I Kings 13:5
verses.text: Then the altar was torn <transChange type="added">apart</transChange> and the ashes from the altar poured out according to the sign which the man of God had announced by the word of Yahweh.

verses.name: I Kings 13:6
verses.text: Then the king responded and said to the man of God, “Please entreat the favor of Yahweh your God, and pray for me that my hand may return to me.” So the man of God entreated the face of Yahweh, and the hand of the king returned to him, as it was in the beginning.

verses.name: I Kings 13:7
verses.text: Then the king spoke to the man of God, “Come with me to the house and refresh yourself, that I may give you a gift.”

verses.name: I Kings 13:8
verses.text: Then the man of God said to the king, “Even if you give to me half of your house I will not come with you, nor will I eat bread or drink water in this place,

verses.name: I Kings 13:9
verses.text: for the word of Yahweh has commanded me, saying, ‘You shall not eat bread nor drink water, and you shall not return on the way that you came.’ ”

verses.name: I Kings 13:10
verses.text: So he went another way, and he did not return by the way on which he had come to Bethel.  <div eID="gen2723" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 13:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1983"/><title type="x-s">The Man of God Disobeys</title> <div sID="gen2724" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1983"/>Now a certain older prophet was living in Bethel, and his son came and recounted to him all of the things that the man of God had done that day in Bethel <transChange type="added">and</transChange> the words he had spoken to the king, and they told them to their father.

verses.name: I Kings 13:12
verses.text: Then their father asked them, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Which way did he go⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?”<note placement="foot">Literally “Where is this way he went?”</note> His sons had seen the way which the man of God who had come from Judah had taken.

verses.name: I Kings 13:13
verses.text: Then he said to his sons, “Saddle the donkey for me.” So they saddled the donkey for him, and he mounted it

verses.name: I Kings 13:14
verses.text: and went after the man of God. He found him sitting under the oak and said to him, “Are you the man of God who came from Judah?” He said, “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange>.”

verses.name: I Kings 13:15
verses.text: Then he said to him, “Come with me to the house and eat <transChange type="added">some</transChange> food.”

verses.name: I Kings 13:16
verses.text: Then he said, “I am not able to return with you or to go with you. I will not eat food nor will I drink water with you in this place.

verses.name: I Kings 13:17
verses.text: For a word <transChange type="added">came</transChange> to me by the word of Yahweh, ‘You shall not eat food, nor shall you drink water there. You shall not return to go by the way that you came.’ ”  <div eID="gen2724" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 13:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1984"/><div sID="gen2725" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1984"/>Then he said, “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> also a prophet like you. An angel spoke to me by the word of Yahweh, saying, ‘Let him return with you to your house that he may eat food and drink water.’ ” He lied to him.

verses.name: I Kings 13:19
verses.text: So he returned with him and ate food in his house and drank water.  <div eID="gen2725" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 13:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1985"/><div sID="gen2726" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1985"/>Now it happened that they <transChange type="added">were</transChange> sitting at the table, and the word of Yahweh came to the prophet who brought him back.

verses.name: I Kings 13:21
verses.text: He proclaimed to the man of God who came from Judah, saying, “Thus says Yahweh: ‘Because you have disobeyed the word of Yahweh and have not kept the command which Yahweh your God commanded you,

verses.name: I Kings 13:22
verses.text: but you have returned and have eaten food and drank water in the place which he ordered you not to eat food nor to drink water, then your dead body shall not return to the tomb of your ancestors.’ ”<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note>  <div eID="gen2726" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 13:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1986"/><title type="x-s">The Disobedient Man of God Dies</title> <div sID="gen2727" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1986"/>It happened after he ate food and drank water that he saddled the donkey for the prophet whom he had brought back.

verses.name: I Kings 13:24
verses.text: When he left, a lion found him on the road and killed him, and his dead body <transChange type="added">was</transChange> thrown on the road with the donkey standing beside it, and the lion <transChange type="added">was</transChange> standing by the dead body.

verses.name: I Kings 13:25
verses.text: As men <transChange type="added">were</transChange> passing by and they saw the dead body thrown in the road and the lion standing beside the dead body, they came and told it in the city where the old prophet <transChange type="added">was</transChange> living.

verses.name: I Kings 13:26
verses.text: When the prophet who had brought him back from the way heard, he said, “It <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the man of God who disobeyed the mouth of Yahweh, and Yahweh has given him to the lion. He tore him in pieces and killed him according to the word of Yahweh which he had spoken to him.”

verses.name: I Kings 13:27
verses.text: Then he spoke to his sons, saying, “Saddle the donkey for me.” So they saddled it.

verses.name: I Kings 13:28
verses.text: He went and found his dead body thrown in the road and a donkey with the lion standing beside it, but the lion had not eaten the corpse nor attacked the donkey.

verses.name: I Kings 13:29
verses.text: So the prophet lifted up the corpse of the man of God and put it on the donkey and brought it back. He came to the city of the old prophet to mourn him and to bury him.

verses.name: I Kings 13:30
verses.text: He put his corpse in his tomb, and they mourned over him, “Alas, my brother!”

verses.name: I Kings 13:31
verses.text: It happened after he buried him that he said to his sons, “When I die, you shall bury me in the tomb where the man of God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> buried; you shall lay my bones beside his bones.

verses.name: I Kings 13:32
verses.text: For surely, the thing which he proclaimed by the word of Yahweh against the altar which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in Bethel will happen, <transChange type="added">as it will</transChange> against all the houses of the high places which <transChange type="added">are</transChange> in the cities of Samaria.”  <div eID="gen2727" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 13:33
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1987"/><title type="x-s">Jeroboam Continues in His Sin</title> <div sID="gen2728" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1987"/>After this event, Jeroboam did not turn from his evil way, but he returned and <transChange type="added">again</transChange> made priests for the high places of people from <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞all walks of life⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “from the fringes of the people”</note> He filled his hand with all <transChange type="added">his</transChange> desire and became <transChange type="added">one of</transChange> the priests of the high places <transChange type="added">himself</transChange>.

verses.name: I Kings 13:34
verses.text: This matter became sin in the house of Jeroboam, to make it disappear and to destroy <transChange type="added">it</transChange> from the surface of the earth.  <chapter eID="1Kgs.13"/>

verses.name: I Kings 14:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1988"/><title type="x-s">Judgment for Jeroboam Continues</title> <div sID="gen2729" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1988"/>At that time, Abijah son of Jeroboam became ill.

verses.name: I Kings 14:2
verses.text: Jeroboam said to his wife, “Please get up and disguise yourself so that they will not know that you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the wife of Jeroboam, and go <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Shiloh. Look, Ahijah the prophet is there, and he spoke concerning me <transChange type="added">before I became</transChange> king over this people.

verses.name: I Kings 14:3
verses.text: You must take ten loaves of bread in your hand and cakes and a jar of honey, and you must go to him. He shall tell you what will happen to the boy.”

verses.name: I Kings 14:4
verses.text: The wife of Jeroboam did so. She got up, went <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Shiloh, and came <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the house of Ahijah. Now Ahijah was not able to see, for <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his eyes were fixed⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “his eyes stood”</note> because of his old age.

verses.name: I Kings 14:5
verses.text: Then Yahweh said to Ahijah, “Look, the wife of Jeroboam <transChange type="added">is</transChange> coming to seek a word from you about her son, for he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> ill. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Thus and so⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “As this and as this”</note> you shall say to her. When she comes, she <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> disguising herself.”

verses.name: I Kings 14:6
verses.text: It happened at the moment Ahijah heard the sound of her footsteps coming through the doorway, he said, “Come <transChange type="added">in</transChange>, wife of Jeroboam. Why <transChange type="added">are</transChange> you making yourself unrecognizable? I have been sent a hard <transChange type="added">message</transChange> for you:

verses.name: I Kings 14:7
verses.text: Go, tell Jeroboam, ‘Thus says Yahweh the God of Israel: “Because I raised you from the midst of the people and I made you leader over my people Israel,

verses.name: I Kings 14:8
verses.text: I tore the kingdom from the house of David and I gave it to you. But you were not like my servant David who kept my commandments, and who went after me with all his heart, to do only <transChange type="added">what is</transChange> right in my eyes.

verses.name: I Kings 14:9
verses.text: But you did more evil than all who were before you. You have gone and made for yourself other gods and molten idols to provoke me, but me you have <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞completely disregarded⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “hurled behind your back”</note>

verses.name: I Kings 14:10
verses.text: Therefore, look, I am about to bring disaster upon the house of Jeroboam, and I will cut off <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞males⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “those who urinate against a wall”</note> from Jeroboam, bond or free, in Israel. I will burn after the house of Jeroboam as one burns after the manure, until it is finished.

verses.name: I Kings 14:11
verses.text: He who dies for Jeroboam in the city, the dogs will eat. He who dies in the open field, the birds from the heavens will eat, for Yahweh has spoken <transChange type="added">it</transChange>.” ’

verses.name: I Kings 14:12
verses.text: As for you, get up. Go to your house. When your feet enter the city, the child will die.

verses.name: I Kings 14:13
verses.text: All of Israel will mourn for him, and they will bury him. This one alone will come to a tomb for Jeroboam, because a good thing has been found in him by Yahweh the God of Israel in the house of Israel.

verses.name: I Kings 14:14
verses.text: Yahweh will raise up a king for himself over Israel who will even now cut off the house of Jeroboam this day.

verses.name: I Kings 14:15
verses.text: Yahweh will strike Israel as one shakes the reed plant in the water, and he will root Israel up from this good land that he gave to their ancestors.<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> He will scatter them beyond the River<note placement="foot">That is, the Euphrates</note> because they have made their sacred poles <transChange type="added">which are</transChange> provoking Yahweh.

verses.name: I Kings 14:16
verses.text: He will give up Israel because of the sin of Jeroboam which he sinned and which he caused Israel to sin.”  <div eID="gen2729" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 14:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1989"/><div sID="gen2730" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1989"/>Then the wife of Jeroboam got up, went, and came to Tirzah. <transChange type="added">As</transChange> she <transChange type="added">was</transChange> coming to the threshold of the house, the boy died.

verses.name: I Kings 14:18
verses.text: They buried him and all of Israel mourned for him, according to the word of Yahweh which he had spoken by the hand of his servant Ahijah the prophet.

verses.name: I Kings 14:19
verses.text: The remainder of the acts of Jeroboam, how he fought and how he reigned, behold, they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> written in the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Israel.

verses.name: I Kings 14:20
verses.text: The days which Jeroboam reigned were twenty-two years, and he slept with his ancestors.<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> Then Nadab his son became king in place of him.  <div eID="gen2730" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 14:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1990"/><title type="x-s">Rehoboam Reigns in Judah</title> <div sID="gen2731" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1990"/>Now Rehoboam the son of Solomon reigned in Judah. He was forty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city which, from all of the tribes of Israel, Yahweh chose to place his name. And the name of his mother <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Naamah the Ammonitess.

verses.name: I Kings 14:22
verses.text: But Judah did evil in the eyes of Yahweh, and they annoyed him more than their fathers<note placement="foot">Or “ancestors”</note> did with their sins that they had committed.

verses.name: I Kings 14:23
verses.text: They also built for themselves high places and stone pillars and sacred poles on every high hill and under every green tree.

verses.name: I Kings 14:24
verses.text: There were also male shrine prostitutes in the land, and they did according to all the abominations of the nations which Yahweh had driven out from before the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note>  <div eID="gen2731" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 14:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1991"/><title type="x-s">Pharaoh Shishak of Egypt Raids Jerusalem</title> <div sID="gen2732" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1991"/>It happened in the fifth year of King Rehoboam that Shishak the king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem,

verses.name: I Kings 14:26
verses.text: and he took the treasures of the house of Yahweh, and he took all the treasures of the king’s house. He took the small gold shields that Solomon had made,

verses.name: I Kings 14:27
verses.text: so King Rehoboam made small copper shields in place of them and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞entrusted them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “he assigned on the hand”</note> to the commanders of the royal guard who keep the doorway of the king’s house.

verses.name: I Kings 14:28
verses.text: Whenever the king came <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the house of Yahweh, the royal guard carried them and brought them back to the alcove room of the royal guard.

verses.name: I Kings 14:29
verses.text: The remainder of the acts of Rehoboam and all that he did, are they not written on the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Judah?

verses.name: I Kings 14:30
verses.text: There was always war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam.

verses.name: I Kings 14:31
verses.text: Then Rehoboam slept with his ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and he was buried with his ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> in the city of David. The name of his mother <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Naamah the Ammonitess. Abijam his son became king in his place.  <chapter eID="1Kgs.14"/>

verses.name: I Kings 15:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1992"/><title type="x-s">The Reign of Abijam in Judah</title> <div sID="gen2733" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1992"/>In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam the son of Nebat, Abijam began to reign over Judah.

verses.name: I Kings 15:2
verses.text: Three years he reigned in Jerusalem. The name of his mother <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Maacah the daughter of Abishalom.

verses.name: I Kings 15:3
verses.text: He walked in all the sins of his father that he had done before him, and his heart was not fully with Yahweh his God as the heart of David his father.

verses.name: I Kings 15:4
verses.text: For the sake of David, Yahweh his God gave him a lamp in Jerusalem, by establishing his son after him and by causing Jerusalem to exist;

verses.name: I Kings 15:5
verses.text: because David did right in the eyes of Yahweh and he didn’t turn aside from all that he commanded him all the days of his life, except in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.  <div eID="gen2733" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 15:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1993"/><div sID="gen2734" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1993"/>There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the days of his life.

verses.name: I Kings 15:7
verses.text: The remainder of the acts of Abijam and all that he did, are they not written in the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Judah? There was also war between Abijam and Jeroboam.

verses.name: I Kings 15:8
verses.text: Abijam slept with his ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and they buried him in the city of David, and Asa his son became king in his place.  <div eID="gen2734" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 15:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1994"/><title type="x-s">The Reign of Asa in Judah</title> <div sID="gen2735" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1994"/>In the twentieth year of Jeroboam the king of Israel, Asa became the king of Judah.

verses.name: I Kings 15:10
verses.text: He reigned forty-one years in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Maacah the daughter of Abishalom.

verses.name: I Kings 15:11
verses.text: Asa did right in the eyes of Yahweh, like David his ancestor.<note placement="foot">Or “father”</note>

verses.name: I Kings 15:12
verses.text: He put away the male shrine prostitutes from the land, and he removed all of the idols that his ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> made.

verses.name: I Kings 15:13
verses.text: Also, he had Maacah his mother removed from the office of queen mother, <transChange type="added">as</transChange> she had made a repulsive image for the Asherah. Asa also cut down her repulsive image and burned it in the Wadi<note placement="foot">Or “valley”; a wadi is a valley that is dry most of the year, but contains a stream during the rainy season</note> Kidron.

verses.name: I Kings 15:14
verses.text: But the high places he did not remove. Nevertheless, the heart of Asa was completely with Yahweh all of his days.

verses.name: I Kings 15:15
verses.text: He brought the holy objects of his father and his <transChange type="added">own</transChange> holy objects to the house of Yahweh, silver and gold and utensils.  <div eID="gen2735" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 15:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1995"/><div sID="gen2736" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1995"/>There was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all of their days.

verses.name: I Kings 15:17
verses.text: Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah, and he built Ramah <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to hinder the coming and going of anyone to Asa⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to not give going and coming to Asa”</note> king of Judah.

verses.name: I Kings 15:18
verses.text: Asa took all of the silver and gold remaining in the storerooms of the house of Yahweh and in the treasury rooms of the house of the king, and he gave them into the hand of his servants; so King Asa sent them to Ben-Hadad the son of Tabrimmon the son of Hezion, the king of Aram, who lived in Damascus, saying,

verses.name: I Kings 15:19
verses.text: “<transChange type="added">Let there be</transChange> a covenant between me and you, between my father and your father. Look, I have sent you a gift of silver and gold. Go, break your covenant with Baasha king of Israel that he may go up <transChange type="added">away</transChange> from me.”

verses.name: I Kings 15:20
verses.text: Ben-Hadad listened to King Asa, and he sent the commanders of his armies against the cities of Israel and he attacked Ijon, Dan, Abel-Beth-Maacah, and all of Kinnereth, in addition to all the land of Naphtali.

verses.name: I Kings 15:21
verses.text: When Baasha heard, he stopped building Ramah, and he lived in Tirzah.

verses.name: I Kings 15:22
verses.text: Then King Asa proclaimed among all of Israel that there was no one free from obligation, so they carried the stones of Ramah and its wood with which Baasha had built, and King Asa rebuilt Geba in Benjamin with them, and the Mizpah.

verses.name: I Kings 15:23
verses.text: The remainder of the acts of Asa, all of his achievements, all that he did, and the cities which he built, are they not written in the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Judah? But at the time of his old age, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he developed a foot disease⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “he became ill in his feet”</note>

verses.name: I Kings 15:24
verses.text: Asa slept with his ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and was buried with his ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> in the city of David his ancestor;<note placement="foot">Or “father”</note> Jehoshaphat his son became king in his place.  <div eID="gen2736" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 15:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1996"/><title type="x-s">The Reign of Nadab in Israel</title> <div sID="gen2737" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1996"/>Nadab the son of Jeroboam began to reign over Israel in the second year of Asa king of Judah, and he reigned over Israel two years.

verses.name: I Kings 15:26
verses.text: He did evil in the eyes of Yahweh, and he walked in the way of his father and in his sin that he caused Israel to commit.

verses.name: I Kings 15:27
verses.text: Baasha son of Ahijah of the house of Issachar conspired against him, and Baasha struck him down at Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines. Now Nadab and all of Israel <transChange type="added">were</transChange> laying siege to Gibbethon,

verses.name: I Kings 15:28
verses.text: and Baasha killed him in the third year of Asa the king of Judah, and he reigned in his place.

verses.name: I Kings 15:29
verses.text: It happened that as soon as he became king, he killed all of the house of Jeroboam. There was no one left of Jeroboam who breathed, until he had destroyed him according to the word of Yahweh that he had spoken by the hand of his servant, Ahijah the Shilonite,

verses.name: I Kings 15:30
verses.text: because of the sins of Jeroboam that he had committed and that he had caused Israel to commit <transChange type="added">and</transChange> because of his anger <transChange type="added">with</transChange> which he had provoked Yahweh the God of Israel.

verses.name: I Kings 15:31
verses.text: Now the remainder of the acts of Nadab and all that he did, <transChange type="added">are</transChange> they not written on the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Israel?  <div eID="gen2737" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 15:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1997"/><title type="x-s">The Reign of Baasha in Israel</title> <div sID="gen2738" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1997"/>There was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.

verses.name: I Kings 15:33
verses.text: In the third year of Asa king of Judah, Baasha son of Ahijah had become king over all of Israel; <transChange type="added">he lived</transChange> in Tirzah twenty-four years.

verses.name: I Kings 15:34
verses.text: He did evil in the eyes of Yahweh, and he walked in the way of Jeroboam and in his sin that he caused Israel to commit.  <chapter eID="1Kgs.15"/> <div eID="gen2738" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 16:1
verses.text: The word of Yahweh came to Jehu the son of Hanani against Baasha, saying,

verses.name: I Kings 16:2
verses.text: “Because I exalted you from the dust and I made you a leader over my people Israel, but you have walked in the way of Jeroboam and you caused my people Israel to sin, to provoke me with their sins,

verses.name: I Kings 16:3
verses.text: I am now <transChange type="added">about to</transChange> consume Baasha and his house. I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat.

verses.name: I Kings 16:4
verses.text: Those who die for Baasha in the city, the dogs will eat; those who die for him in the field, the birds of the heavens will eat.”  <div eID="gen2739" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 16:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1998"/><div sID="gen2740" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1998"/>The remainder of the acts of Baasha, what he did, and his powerful deeds, are they not written on the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Israel?

verses.name: I Kings 16:6
verses.text: Baasha slept with his ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and was buried in Tirzah, and Elah his son became king in his place.

verses.name: I Kings 16:7
verses.text: Moreover, the word of Yahweh came to Baasha and to his house by the hand of Jehu the son of Hanani the prophet, because of all the evil that he did in the eyes of Yahweh by provoking him with the work of his hands, by being like the house of Jeroboam; and he destroyed him.  <div eID="gen2740" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 16:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1999"/><title type="x-s">The Reign of Elah in Israel</title> <div sID="gen2741" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1999"/>In the twenty-sixth year of Asa king of Judah, Elah the son of Baasha became king over Israel for two years.

verses.name: I Kings 16:9
verses.text: His servant Zimri the commander of half of the chariots conspired against him. Now he had been in Tirzah drinking <transChange type="added">himself</transChange> drunk in the house of Arza who was over the palace in Tirzah.

verses.name: I Kings 16:10
verses.text: Zimri came and struck him down and killed him in the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah and became king in his place.

verses.name: I Kings 16:11
verses.text: It happened that as soon as he became king, at the moment he sat on his throne, he killed all of the house of Baasha. He left <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞no males⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “no one for him who urinated against a wall”</note> <transChange type="added">among</transChange> his kindred or <transChange type="added">any of</transChange> his friends.  <div eID="gen2741" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 16:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2000"/><div sID="gen2742" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2000"/>So Zimri destroyed all of the house of Baasha according to the word of Yahweh which he spoke against Baasha by the hand of Jehu the prophet

verses.name: I Kings 16:13
verses.text: because of all the sins of Baasha and the sins of Elah his son which they committed and which they caused Israel to sin by provoking Yahweh the God of Israel with their idols.

verses.name: I Kings 16:14
verses.text: The remainder of the acts of Elah and all that he did, are they not written in the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Israel?  <div eID="gen2742" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 16:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2001"/><title type="x-s">The Very Brief Reign of Zimri in Israel</title> <div sID="gen2743" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2001"/>In the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, Zimri reigned seven days in Tirzah. Now the army was encamping against Gibbethon which belonged to the Philistines.

verses.name: I Kings 16:16
verses.text: The encamping army heard that Zimri had conspired and moreover had killed the king,<note placement="foot">That is, Elah</note> so they made Omri the commander of the army of Israel king over all Israel in the camp on that day.

verses.name: I Kings 16:17
verses.text: Then Omri went up and all Israel with him from Gibbethon, and they besieged Tirzah.

verses.name: I Kings 16:18
verses.text: It happened that when Zimri saw that the city was taken, he went to the citadel fortress of the house of the king, and he burnt the house of the king over him with fire so that he died.

verses.name: I Kings 16:19
verses.text: <transChange type="added">This happened</transChange> because of his sin which he committed by doing evil in the eyes of Yahweh, by going the way of Jeroboam and in his sin which he did by causing Israel to sin.

verses.name: I Kings 16:20
verses.text: The remainder of the acts of Zimri and his conspiracy which he made, <transChange type="added">are</transChange> they not written on the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Israel?  <div eID="gen2743" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 16:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2002"/><title type="x-s">The Reign of Omri in Israel</title> <div sID="gen2744" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2002"/>At that time, the people of Israel were divided into two parts: half of the people went after Tibni the son of Ginath to make him king, and the other half went after Omri.

verses.name: I Kings 16:22
verses.text: The people who went after Omri overcame the people who went after Tibni the son of Ginath, so that he died and Omri became king.  <div eID="gen2744" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 16:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2003"/><div sID="gen2745" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2003"/>In the thirty-first year of Asa king of Judah, Omri became king over Israel <transChange type="added">for</transChange> twelve years. He reigned in Tirzah six years,

verses.name: I Kings 16:24
verses.text: then bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver, fortified the hill, and called the name of the city Samaria that he built after Shemer, the owner of the hill.

verses.name: I Kings 16:25
verses.text: But Omri did evil in the eyes of Yahweh more than all who were before him.

verses.name: I Kings 16:26
verses.text: He went in all the way of Jeroboam the son of Nebat and in his sins that he caused Israel to sin by provoking Yahweh the God of Israel with their idols.

verses.name: I Kings 16:27
verses.text: The remainder of the acts of Omri that he did and his powerful deeds, are they not written in the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Israel?

verses.name: I Kings 16:28
verses.text: Omri slept with his ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and he was buried in Samaria, and Ahab his son became king in his place.  <div eID="gen2745" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 16:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2004"/><title type="x-s">The Reign of Ahab in Israel</title> <div sID="gen2746" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2004"/>Now Ahab son of Omri became king over Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Asa king of Judah. Ahab son of Omri reigned over Israel in Samaria twenty-two years.

verses.name: I Kings 16:30
verses.text: But Ahab son of Omri did evil in the eyes of Yahweh more than all who were before him.

verses.name: I Kings 16:31
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞If it wasn’t enough that he went⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “It happened that it was trivial his going”</note> after the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, he also took as wife Jezebel the daughter of Ethbaal the king of the Sidonians. He went and served Baal and bowed down to him.

verses.name: I Kings 16:32
verses.text: And he built an altar to Baal in the house of Baal which he had built in Samaria.

verses.name: I Kings 16:33
verses.text: Ahab also made the sacred pole, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he continued to provoke⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Ahab added to make to provoke”</note> Yahweh the God of Israel more than all the kings of Israel who were before him.

verses.name: I Kings 16:34
verses.text: In his days, Hiel the Bethelite rebuilt Jericho; at the cost of Abiram his firstborn he laid its foundation, and at the cost of Segub his younger sibling, he set up its gates, according to the word of Yahweh which he spoke by the hand of Joshua the son of Nun.  <chapter eID="1Kgs.16"/>

verses.name: I Kings 17:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2005"/><title type="x-s">The Prophet Elijah Arises</title> <div sID="gen2747" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2005"/>Elijah the Tishbite from Tishbe of Gilead said to Ahab, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞As Yahweh lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “The life of Yahweh”</note> the God of Israel before whom I stand, there shall surely not be dew nor rain these years <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞except by my command⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “except at the word of my mouth”</note>

verses.name: I Kings 17:2
verses.text: Then the word of Yahweh came to him, saying,

verses.name: I Kings 17:3
verses.text: “Go from this place and turn to the east; you must hide yourself in the Wadi<note placement="foot">A valley that is dry most of the year, but contains a stream during the rainy season</note> Kerith <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞which faces the Jordan⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “on the face of the Jordan”</note>

verses.name: I Kings 17:4
verses.text: It shall be that you shall drink from the wadi,<note placement="foot">A valley that is dry most of the year, but contains a stream during the rainy season</note> and I have commanded the crows to sustain you there.”

verses.name: I Kings 17:5
verses.text: So he went and did according to the word of Yahweh. He went and stayed in the Wadi<note placement="foot">A valley that is dry most of the year, but contains a stream during the rainy season</note> Kerith <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞which faces the Jordan⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “on the face of the Jordan”</note>

verses.name: I Kings 17:6
verses.text: The crows <transChange type="added">were</transChange> bringing bread and meat in the morning for him and bread and meat in the evening, and he drank from the wadi.<note placement="foot">A valley that is dry most of the year, but contains a stream during the rainy season</note>

verses.name: I Kings 17:7
verses.text: It happened <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞after a while⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from the end of days”</note> that the wadi<note placement="foot">A seasonal stream that is often dry</note> dried up, because there was no rain in the land.  <div eID="gen2747" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 17:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2006"/><div sID="gen2748" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2006"/>Then the word of Yahweh came to him, saying,

verses.name: I Kings 17:9
verses.text: “Get up and go to Zarephath which belongs to Sidon and stay there. Look, I have commanded a woman there, a widow, to sustain you.”

verses.name: I Kings 17:10
verses.text: So he arose and went to Zarephath and came to the gate of the city. There <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a widow woman gathering wood, so he called to her, and he said, “Please bring a little water for me in a vessel so that I can drink.”

verses.name: I Kings 17:11
verses.text: She went to fetch <transChange type="added">it</transChange>, and he called to her and said, “Please bring me a morsel of bread in your hand.”

verses.name: I Kings 17:12
verses.text: She said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞As Yahweh your God lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “The life of Yahweh your God”</note> surely I do not have a cake, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞but only a handful of flour⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “except that which fills a hand with flour”</note> in the jar and a little olive oil in the jug. Here I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> gathering a few pieces of wood, and I will go and prepare it for me and my son, that we might eat it and die.”

verses.name: I Kings 17:13
verses.text: Elijah said to her, “Don’t be afraid. Go and do according to your word; only make for me a small bread cake from it first, and bring it out to me. Make it for yourself and for your son afterward.

verses.name: I Kings 17:14
