verses.text: For thus says Yahweh, the God of Israel: ‘The jar of flour will not be emptied and the jug of olive oil will not run out until the day Yahweh gives rain on the surface of the earth.’ ”

verses.name: I Kings 17:15
verses.text: So she went and did according to the word of Elijah; then <transChange type="added">both</transChange> she and he ate with her household for many days.

verses.name: I Kings 17:16
verses.text: The jar of flour was not emptied and the jug of olive oil did not run out, according to the word of Yahweh which he spoke by the hand of Elijah.  <div eID="gen2748" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 17:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2007"/><div sID="gen2749" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2007"/>It happened after these things that the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, became ill; and his illness was very severe until there was no breath left in him.

verses.name: I Kings 17:18
verses.text: She said to Elijah, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞What do you have against me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “What for me and for you”</note> O man of God, <transChange type="added">that</transChange> you have come to me to make known my guilt and to cause my son to die?”

verses.name: I Kings 17:19
verses.text: Then he said to her, “Give me your son.” He took him from her lap and carried him up to the upper room where he was staying, and he laid him on his bed.

verses.name: I Kings 17:20
verses.text: Then he called to Yahweh and said, “O Yahweh my God, are you also causing evil to come upon the widow with whom I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> dwelling as an alien by causing her son to die?”

verses.name: I Kings 17:21
verses.text: He stretched himself out on the child three times and called to Yahweh and said, “O Yahweh my God, please let the life of this child return within him.”

verses.name: I Kings 17:22
verses.text: Yahweh listened to the voice of Elijah, and the life of the child returned within him, and he lived.

verses.name: I Kings 17:23
verses.text: Elijah then took the child and brought him down from the upper room to the house and gave him to his mother. Elijah said, “Look, your son <transChange type="added">is</transChange> alive.”

verses.name: I Kings 17:24
verses.text: Then the woman said to Elijah, “Now this I know, that you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> a man of God and the word of Yahweh in your mouth <transChange type="added">is</transChange> truth.”  <chapter eID="1Kgs.17"/>

verses.name: I Kings 18:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2008"/><title type="x-s">War between Elijah and the Prophets of Baal</title> <div sID="gen2750" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2008"/>It happened many days <transChange type="added">later</transChange> that the word of Yahweh came to Elijah in the third year, saying, “Go, present yourself to Ahab so that I may give rain on the surface of the earth.”

verses.name: I Kings 18:2
verses.text: So Elijah went to present himself to Ahab. Now the famine <transChange type="added">was</transChange> severe in Samaria.

verses.name: I Kings 18:3
verses.text: Ahab summoned Obadiah who <transChange type="added">was</transChange> over the house. (Now Obadiah was fearing Yahweh greatly.

verses.name: I Kings 18:4
verses.text: It had happened that when Jezebel killed the prophets of Yahweh, Obadiah took a hundred prophets and hid them <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞by fifties⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “fifty men”</note> in the cave and sustained them <transChange type="added">with</transChange> food and water.)

verses.name: I Kings 18:5
verses.text: Ahab said to Obadiah, “Go through the land to all the springs of water and to all the wadis.<note placement="foot">A valley that is dry most of the year, but contains a stream during the rainy season</note> Perhaps we may find green grass that we may keep horses and mules alive and that we might not lose any of the animals.”

verses.name: I Kings 18:6
verses.text: So they divided the land for themselves in order to pass through it; Ahab went one way by himself, and Obadiah went another way by himself.  <div eID="gen2750" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 18:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2009"/><div sID="gen2751" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2009"/>It happened that Obadiah <transChange type="added">was</transChange> on the way, and suddenly Elijah was there to meet him. When he recognized him, he fell on his face and said, “<transChange type="added">Is</transChange> this you, my lord Elijah?”

verses.name: I Kings 18:8
verses.text: He said to him, “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange>. Go, say to your lord, ‘Elijah <transChange type="added">is</transChange> here.’ ”

verses.name: I Kings 18:9
verses.text: He said, “How have I sinned that you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> giving your servant into the hand of Ahab to kill me?

verses.name: I Kings 18:10
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞As Yahweh your God lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “The life of Yahweh your God”</note> surely there is not a nation or a kingdom to which my lord has not sent me to seek you. <transChange type="added">If</transChange> they would say, ‘He is not here,’ then he would make the kingdom or the nation swear that it could not find you.

verses.name: I Kings 18:11
verses.text: Now you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> saying, ‘Go, say to your lord: “Elijah <transChange type="added">is</transChange> here.” ’

verses.name: I Kings 18:12
verses.text: And it will happen that I will go from you and the Spirit of Yahweh will carry you up to where I do not know. Then I will come to tell Ahab, but he will not find you, and then he will kill me, <transChange type="added">even though</transChange> your servant has feared Yahweh from my youth.

verses.name: I Kings 18:13
verses.text: Has it not been told to my lord what I did when Jezebel killed the prophets of Yahweh? I hid a hundred men of the prophets of Yahweh <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞by fifties⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “fifty fifty men”</note> in the cave, and I sustained them <transChange type="added">with</transChange> food and water.

verses.name: I Kings 18:14
verses.text: Now you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> saying, ‘Go, say to your lord: “Elijah <transChange type="added">is</transChange> here,” ’ and he will kill me.”

verses.name: I Kings 18:15
verses.text: Elijah said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞As Yahweh of hosts lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “The life of Yahweh of hosts”</note> before whom I stand, I will certainly show myself to him today.”  <div eID="gen2751" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 18:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2010"/><div sID="gen2752" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2010"/>So Obadiah went to meet Ahab, and he told him, so Ahab went to meet Elijah.

verses.name: I Kings 18:17
verses.text: When Ahab saw Elijah, Ahab said to him, “<transChange type="added">Is</transChange> this you <transChange type="added">who</transChange> throws Israel into confusion?”

verses.name: I Kings 18:18
verses.text: He said, “I did not throw Israel into confusion; rather you and the house of your father <transChange type="added">have</transChange> by forsaking the commands of Yahweh when you went after the Baals!

verses.name: I Kings 18:19
verses.text: So then, send <transChange type="added">word</transChange> and assemble all of Israel to me on Mount Carmel, with the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal and the four hundred prophets of Asherah, who eat at the table of Jezebel.”  <div eID="gen2752" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 18:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2011"/><div sID="gen2753" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2011"/>So Ahab sent <transChange type="added">word</transChange> among the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> and he assembled the prophets to Mount Carmel.

verses.name: I Kings 18:21
verses.text: Elijah approached to all the people and said, “How long <transChange type="added">will</transChange> you <transChange type="added">go</transChange> limping over two opinions? If Yahweh <transChange type="added">is</transChange> God, go after him; but if Baal, go after him.” But the people did not answer him a word.

verses.name: I Kings 18:22
verses.text: Then Elijah said to the people, “I alone <transChange type="added">am</transChange> left a prophet of Yahweh, but the prophets of Baal <transChange type="added">are</transChange> four hundred and fifty men.

verses.name: I Kings 18:23
verses.text: Let them give us two bulls, and let them choose for themselves one bull, cut him in pieces, and put it on the wood, but don’t let them start a fire on it. I will prepare the other bull and set it on the wood, but I will put no fire <transChange type="added">on it</transChange>.

verses.name: I Kings 18:24
verses.text: Then you call on the name of your god, and I will call on the name of Yahweh, and it shall be that the god who answers by fire, he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> God.”<note placement="foot">Baal is known in Canaanite texts as being the god in control of lightning and fire</note> Then all the people answered and said, “The word <transChange type="added">is</transChange> good!”  <div eID="gen2753" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 18:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2012"/><div sID="gen2754" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2012"/>Then Elijah said to the prophets of Baal, “Choose for yourselves one bull and prepare it first, for you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the majority, and call on the name of your god, but don’t set fire <transChange type="added">under it</transChange>.”

verses.name: I Kings 18:26
verses.text: So they took the bull that he allowed to them, prepared it, and called upon the name of Baal from morning until noon, saying, “O Baal, answer us!” But there was no voice and there was no answer, so they limped<note placement="foot">That is, moved about the altar in a cultic dance step</note> about the altar which they had made.

verses.name: I Kings 18:27
verses.text: It happened at noon that Elijah mocked them and said, “Call out with a loud voice, for he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a god! Perhaps he is meditating, or <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞is using the bathroom⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “has backed off for himself”</note> or <transChange type="added">is</transChange> on a journey. Perhaps he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> asleep and must wake up!”

verses.name: I Kings 18:28
verses.text: So they called out with a loud voice, and they cut themselves with swords and with spears as was their custom, until the blood poured out over them.

verses.name: I Kings 18:29
verses.text: It happened as noon passed, they raged until the <transChange type="added">time of</transChange> the evening offering, but there was no voice, there was no answer, and no <transChange type="added">one</transChange> paid attention.  <div eID="gen2754" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 18:30
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2013"/><div sID="gen2755" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2013"/>Then Elijah said to all the people, “Come near to me,” so all the people came closer to him. He repaired the altar of Yahweh <transChange type="added">that had been</transChange> destroyed.

verses.name: I Kings 18:31
verses.text: Elijah took twelve stones according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Jacob, to whom the word of God came, saying, “Israel shall be your name.”

verses.name: I Kings 18:32
verses.text: With them, he built an altar in the name of Yahweh, and he made a trench <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞which would have held⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “as the house of”</note> about two seahs of seed, all around the altar.

verses.name: I Kings 18:33
verses.text: And he arranged the wood, cut the bull into pieces, and placed <transChange type="added">it</transChange> on the wood.<note placement="foot">in the Hebrew Bible, <reference osisRef="1Kgs.18.34">1 Kings 18:34 </reference>begins here</note> Then he said, “Fill four jars <transChange type="added">with</transChange> water, and pour it on the burnt offering and on the wood.”

verses.name: I Kings 18:34
verses.text: He said, “Do <transChange type="added">it</transChange> again!” They did <transChange type="added">it</transChange> again. He said, “Do <transChange type="added">it</transChange> a third time!” So they did <transChange type="added">it</transChange> a third time.

verses.name: I Kings 18:35
verses.text: The water went all around the altar, and the trench also was filled <transChange type="added">with</transChange> water.  <div eID="gen2755" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 18:36
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2014"/><div sID="gen2756" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2014"/>It happened at the offering of the <transChange type="added">evening</transChange> oblation, Elijah the prophet went near, and he said, “O Yahweh, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel; let it be known today that you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> God in Israel and <transChange type="added">that</transChange> I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> your servant and <transChange type="added">that</transChange> I have done all of these things by your words.

verses.name: I Kings 18:37
verses.text: Answer me, O Yahweh, answer me; that this people may know that you, O Yahweh, <transChange type="added">are</transChange> God and that you have turned their hearts back again.”

verses.name: I Kings 18:38
verses.text: Then the fire of Yahweh fell, and it consumed the burnt offering, and the wood, and the stones, and the dust; and the water which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in the trench it licked up!

verses.name: I Kings 18:39
verses.text: When all the people saw, they fell on their faces and said, “Yahweh, he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> God! Yahweh, he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> God!”

verses.name: I Kings 18:40
verses.text: Then Elijah said to them, “Seize the prophets of Baal; don’t let any man of them escape!” So they seized them, and Elijah brought them down to the wadi<note placement="foot">A valley that is dry most of the year, but contains a stream during the rainy season</note> of Kishon and killed them there.  <div eID="gen2756" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 18:41
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2015"/><div sID="gen2757" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2015"/>Then Elijah said to Ahab, “Go up, eat and drink, for <transChange type="added">there is</transChange> the sound of the noise of rain.”

verses.name: I Kings 18:42
verses.text: So Ahab went up to eat and to drink while Elijah went to the top of Carmel, bent down to the earth, and put his face between his knees.

verses.name: I Kings 18:43
verses.text: Then he said to his servant, “Please go <transChange type="added">and</transChange> look in the direction of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> sea.” So he went up and looked; then he said, “There is nothing.” Then he said, “Go back,” seven times.

verses.name: I Kings 18:44
verses.text: It happened that at the seventh time, he said, “Look, there is a small cloud, as <transChange type="added">the</transChange> hand of a man, coming up from the sea.” Then <transChange type="added">Elijah</transChange> said, “Go up, say to Ahab, ‘Harness <transChange type="added">your horses</transChange> and go down, lest the rain stop you.’ ”

verses.name: I Kings 18:45
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞In no time⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Until here and until here”</note> the heavens grew black <transChange type="added">with</transChange> clouds and wind, and there was heavy rain. Ahab rode and he went to Jezreel,

verses.name: I Kings 18:46
verses.text: but the hand of Yahweh was on Elijah; he girded up his loins and ran before Ahab as one comes to Jezreel.  <chapter eID="1Kgs.18"/>

verses.name: I Kings 19:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2016"/><title type="x-s">Elijah Flees to Horeb</title> <div sID="gen2758" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2016"/>Then Ahab told Jezebel all that Elijah had done and how he had killed all the prophets with the sword.

verses.name: I Kings 19:2
verses.text: Then Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah, saying, “Thus may the gods do <transChange type="added">to me</transChange>, and may they add <transChange type="added">to it</transChange>, surely at this time tomorrow I will make your life as the life of one of them!”

verses.name: I Kings 19:3
verses.text: Then he became afraid,<note placement="foot">According to Greek, Syriac, and Latin manuscripts. Hebrew reads “he saw”</note> got up, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞fled for his life⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “he went to his life”</note> He came <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Beersheba which belongs to Judah, and he left his servant there.

verses.name: I Kings 19:4
verses.text: Then he went into the wilderness one day’s journey, and he went and sat under a certain broom tree. Then <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he asked Yahweh that he might die⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “he asked his life to die”</note> and he said, “It is enough now, Yahweh; take my life, for I am no better than my ancestors.”<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note>

verses.name: I Kings 19:5
verses.text: He lay down and fell asleep under a certain broom tree, and suddenly this angel <transChange type="added">was</transChange> touching him and said to him, “Get up, eat!”

verses.name: I Kings 19:6
verses.text: He looked, and behold, a bread cake on hot coals <transChange type="added">was</transChange> near his head and a jar of water, so he ate and drank. Then he did it again and lay down.

verses.name: I Kings 19:7
verses.text: The angel of Yahweh appeared a second <transChange type="added">time</transChange> and touched him and said, “Get up, eat, for the journey is greater than you.”

verses.name: I Kings 19:8
verses.text: So he got up, ate, drank, and went in the strength of that food forty days and forty nights up to Horeb, the mountain of God.  <div eID="gen2758" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 19:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2017"/><title type="x-s">Elijah Encounters Yahweh at Horeb</title> <div sID="gen2759" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2017"/>He came to the cave there and spent the night there. Suddenly the <transChange type="added">word</transChange> of Yahweh came to him and asked him, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Elijah, what are you doing here⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?”<note placement="foot">Literally “What is for you here, Elijah”</note>

verses.name: I Kings 19:10
verses.text: Then he said, “I have been very zealous for Yahweh the God of hosts, for the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> have forsaken your covenant. They have demolished your altars, and they have killed your prophets with the sword. I alone am left over, and they seek to take my life.

verses.name: I Kings 19:11
verses.text: He<note placement="foot">That is, Yahweh</note> said, “Go out and stand on the mountain before Yahweh.” Suddenly Yahweh was passing by, with a great and strong wind ripping the mountains and crushing rocks before Yahweh; <transChange type="added">but</transChange> Yahweh <transChange type="added">was</transChange> not in the wind. After the wind, <transChange type="added">there was</transChange> an earthquake; <transChange type="added">but</transChange> Yahweh was not in the earthquake.

verses.name: I Kings 19:12
verses.text: After the earthquake <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a fire, <transChange type="added">but</transChange> Yahweh was not in the fire. After the fire <transChange type="added">there was</transChange> the sound of a gentle whisper.

verses.name: I Kings 19:13
verses.text: It happened at the moment Elijah heard, he covered his face with his cloak and went out and stood <transChange type="added">at</transChange> the entrance of the cave. Suddenly a voice <transChange type="added">came</transChange> to him and said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Elijah, why are you here⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?”<note placement="foot">Literally “What is for you here, Elijah”</note>

verses.name: I Kings 19:14
verses.text: He said, “I have been very zealous for Yahweh the God of Hosts, for the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> have forsaken your covenant, demolished your altars, and killed your prophets with the sword; I alone am left, and they seek to take my life!”

verses.name: I Kings 19:15
verses.text: Then Yahweh said to him, “Go, return on your way to the wilderness of Damascus. Go and anoint Hazael as king over Aram;

verses.name: I Kings 19:16
verses.text: and Jehu son of Nimshi you shall anoint as king over Israel. You shall also anoint Elisha son of Shaphat from Abel-Meholah as prophet in your place.

verses.name: I Kings 19:17
verses.text: It shall be that the <transChange type="added">one</transChange> who escapes from the sword of Hazael, Jehu will kill; the one who escapes from the sword of Jehu, Elisha shall kill.

verses.name: I Kings 19:18
verses.text: I will leave in Israel seven thousand, all of the knees that have not bowed down to Baal and all of the mouths that have not kissed him.”  <div eID="gen2759" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 19:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2018"/><div sID="gen2760" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2018"/>So he went from there and found Elisha son of Shaphat while he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> plowing <transChange type="added">with</transChange> twelve pairs of oxen before him. When he and the twelve passed Elijah, he threw his cloak on him.

verses.name: I Kings 19:20
verses.text: Then he left the oxen and ran after Elijah and said, “Please let me kiss my father and my mother, and then I will go after you.” Then he said, “Go, return, for what I have done to you?”

verses.name: I Kings 19:21
verses.text: So he returned from after him, and he took a pair of oxen and slaughtered them, and with the yoke of the oxen he boiled the flesh and gave it to the people and they ate. Then he arose and went after Elijah and served him.  <chapter eID="1Kgs.19"/>

verses.name: I Kings 20:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2019"/><title type="x-s">Syrian-Israeli Conflicts: Ben-Hadad vs. Ahab of Israel</title> <div sID="gen2761" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2019"/>Ben-Hadad king of Aram gathered all of his army, and thirty-two kings <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him, and horses and chariots. He went up and laid siege against Samaria and fought with it.

verses.name: I Kings 20:2
verses.text: He sent messengers to the city to Ahab king of Israel.

verses.name: I Kings 20:3
verses.text: He said to him, “Thus says Ben-Hadad: ‘Your silver and your gold are mine, and your women and your best sons are mine.’ ”

verses.name: I Kings 20:4
verses.text: Then the king of Israel answered and said, “As your word, my master the king; I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> yours, and all that is mine <transChange type="added">is yours</transChange>.”

verses.name: I Kings 20:5
verses.text: The messengers returned and said, “Thus says Ben-Hadad, saying, ‘I sent to you saying, “Your silver and gold are mine, and your women and your best sons you must give to me.”

verses.name: I Kings 20:6
verses.text: So <transChange type="added">at this</transChange> time tomorrow, I will send my servants to you that they might search your house and the houses of your servants. All the desire of your eyes <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they will lay hands on⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “they will put in their hands”</note> and take it away.’ ”  <div eID="gen2761" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 20:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2020"/><div sID="gen2762" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2020"/>Then the king of Israel called all the elders of the land and said, “Please know and realize that this <transChange type="added">man is</transChange> seeking trouble, for he sent to me for my women, my sons, my silver, and my gold, and I did not withhold <transChange type="added">anything</transChange> from him.”

verses.name: I Kings 20:8
verses.text: All of the elders and all of the people said to him, “Do not listen and do not consent.”

verses.name: I Kings 20:9
verses.text: So he said to the messengers of Ben-Hadad, “Say to my lord the king, ‘All that you demanded from your servant at the first, I will do, but this thing I am not able to do.’ ” Then the messengers went and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞made a report to him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “returned him a word”</note>

verses.name: I Kings 20:10
verses.text: Then Ben-Hadad sent to him and said, “Thus may the gods do to me and thus may they add if the dust of Samaria is sufficient for the hollow of a hand for all of the people who are at my feet.”

verses.name: I Kings 20:11
verses.text: The king of Israel answered and said, “Tell <transChange type="added">him</transChange>, ‘Let not him who girds on his armor boast as one who takes off his armor.’ ”

verses.name: I Kings 20:12
verses.text: It happened at the moment he heard this word, he and the kings <transChange type="added">were</transChange> drinking in the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞tents⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “booths”</note> He said to his servants, “Get ready <transChange type="added">to attack</transChange>.” So they got ready <transChange type="added">to attack</transChange> the city.  <div eID="gen2762" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 20:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2021"/><div sID="gen2763" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2021"/>Suddenly a certain prophet approached Ahab king of Israel and said, “Thus says Yahweh: ‘Have you seen all this great crowd? Behold, I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> giving it into your hand today, that you may know that I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> Yahweh.’ ”

verses.name: I Kings 20:14
verses.text: Ahab said, “By whom?” And he said, “Thus says Yahweh: ‘By the servants of the commanders of the provinces.’ ” He asked, “Who will begin the battle?” And he said, “You.”

verses.name: I Kings 20:15
verses.text: So he mustered the servants of the commanders of the provinces, and there were two hundred and thirty-two. After them he mustered all of the army, all the sons of Israel, seven thousand.  <div eID="gen2763" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 20:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2022"/><div sID="gen2764" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2022"/>They went out at noon while Ben-Hadad <transChange type="added">was</transChange> drinking <transChange type="added">himself</transChange> drunk in the tents, he and the thirty-two kings helping him.

verses.name: I Kings 20:17
verses.text: Then the servants of the commanders of the provinces went out first, and Ben-Hadad sent, and they reported to him, saying, “Men have come out from Samaria.”

verses.name: I Kings 20:18
verses.text: Then he said, “If they have come out for peace, seize them alive; and if they have come out for war, seize them alive.”

verses.name: I Kings 20:19
verses.text: But these had come out from the city, the servants of the commanders of the provinces, and the army that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> after them.

verses.name: I Kings 20:20
verses.text: Each man killed his man, and the Arameans fled, so Israel pursued them, but Ben-Hadad king of Aram escaped on a horse with cavalry.

verses.name: I Kings 20:21
verses.text: The king of Israel went out and attacked the horses and the chariots and defeated Aram with a great blow.  <div eID="gen2764" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 20:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2023"/><div sID="gen2765" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2023"/>Then the prophet came near to the king of Israel, and he said to him, “Go, strengthen yourself; <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞consider well⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “know and see”</note> what you should do, for the king of Aram is coming against you at the turn of the year.”  <div eID="gen2765" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 20:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2024"/><div sID="gen2766" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2024"/>The servants of the king of Aram said to him, “Their gods <transChange type="added">are</transChange> gods of the mountains, therefore they were stronger than we.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “he”</note> Let us fight with them in the plain; surely we will be stronger than they.

verses.name: I Kings 20:24
verses.text: Do this thing: remove the kings each from his post, and put a governor in their place.

verses.name: I Kings 20:25
verses.text: You must muster an army for yourself as the army <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you have lost⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “as the army which fell from with you”</note> and horses and chariots as the horses and chariots <transChange type="added">you lost</transChange>, then we will fight them in the plain. Surely we will be stronger than they.” So he listened to their voice and did so.  <div eID="gen2766" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 20:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2025"/><div sID="gen2767" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2025"/>It happened at the turning of the year that Ben-Hadad mustered Aram and went up to Aphek for the war with Israel.

verses.name: I Kings 20:27
verses.text: The <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> had been mustered and provisioned, and they went to engage them. The <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> encamped opposite them as two flocks of goats, but the Arameans filled the land.

verses.name: I Kings 20:28
verses.text: Then the man of God approached, and he spoke to the king of Israel, and he said, “Thus says Yahweh: ‘Because Aram has said, “Yahweh <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a god of the mountains and not a god of the valleys,” ’ I will give all this great crowd into your hand that you may know that I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> Yahweh.”

verses.name: I Kings 20:29
verses.text: These encamped opposite for seven days, and it happened on the seventh day that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the battle began⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the battle drew near”</note> and the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> killed the Arameans, one hundred thousand infantry in one day.

verses.name: I Kings 20:30
verses.text: Then those who remained fled to Aphek, to the city, and the wall fell on twenty-seven thousand men who had remained, so Ben-Hadad fled and went to the innermost rooms of the city.  <div eID="gen2767" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 20:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2026"/><div sID="gen2768" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2026"/>Then his servants said to him, “Please now, we have heard that the kings of the house of Israel are kings of mercy. Let us now put sackcloth on around our waists and ropes on our heads. Then let us go out to the king of Israel. Perhaps <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he will let you live⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “he may let your life live”</note>

verses.name: I Kings 20:32
verses.text: So they tied sackcloth around their waists and ropes on their heads. Then they went to the king of Israel and said, “Your servant Ben-Hadad says, ‘Please let me live.’ ” And he said, “<transChange type="added">Is</transChange> my brother still alive?”

verses.name: I Kings 20:33
verses.text: The men took this as a good omen and they quickly accepted <transChange type="added">it</transChange> as true from him, and they said, “Your brother Ben-Hadad <transChange type="added">lives</transChange>.” So he said, “Go, get him.” Ben-Hadad came out to him, and <transChange type="added">Ahab</transChange> pulled him up on the chariot.

verses.name: I Kings 20:34
verses.text: <transChange type="added">Ben-Hadad</transChange> said to him, “The cities which my father took from your father I shall return. You may set up streets with stalls for yourself in Damascus just as my father set up in Samaria.” <transChange type="added">Then Ahab said</transChange>, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞On these terms⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “In covenant”</note> I will let you go,” So he made a covenant with him and let him go.  <div eID="gen2768" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 20:35
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2027"/><div sID="gen2769" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2027"/>A certain man from the sons of the prophets said to his fellow countryman, “By the word of Yahweh, please strike me.” But the man refused to strike him.  <div eID="gen2769" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 20:36
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2028"/><div sID="gen2770" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2028"/>He said to him, “Because you have not obeyed the voice of Yahweh, look, as you now are going from me, a lion will kill you.” When he went from beside him, the lion found him and killed him.

verses.name: I Kings 20:37
verses.text: Then he found another man and said, “Strike me, please,” so the man struck him sharply and wounded him.

verses.name: I Kings 20:38
verses.text: Then the prophet went and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞waited⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “stood”</note> for the king along the road and disguised himself with a<note placement="foot">Hebrew “the”</note> headband over his eyes.

verses.name: I Kings 20:39
verses.text: As the king <transChange type="added">was</transChange> passing by, he called to the king and said, “Your servant went out in the thick of the battle, and suddenly a man turned and brought a man to me and said, ‘Guard this man. If by any means he should be missed, it will be your life in his place, or you shall pay a talent of silver.’

verses.name: I Kings 20:40
verses.text: It happened that your servant <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞was busy here and there⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “was doing here and here”</note> and he <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞disappeared⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “and he was not”</note> Then the king said to him, “Your own judgment has been determined.”

verses.name: I Kings 20:41
verses.text: He quickly removed the headband from his eyes, and the king of Israel recognized him, that he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> from the prophets.

verses.name: I Kings 20:42
verses.text: He said to him, “Thus says Yahweh: ‘Because you have let the man I devoted for destruction go from <transChange type="added">your</transChange> hand, your life shall be in place of his life and your people in place of his people.’ ”

verses.name: I Kings 20:43
verses.text: Then the king of Israel went to his house, sullen and angry, and he came to Samaria.  <chapter eID="1Kgs.20"/>

verses.name: I Kings 21:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2029"/><title type="x-s">The Vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite</title> <div sID="gen2771" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2029"/>It happened after these things that Naboth the Jezreelite had a vineyard which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in Jezreel beside the palace of Ahab king of Samaria.

verses.name: I Kings 21:2
verses.text: Ahab spoke to Naboth, saying, “Give me your vineyard that it may be mine for a garden of vegetable plants, because it is near, beside my house, and I will give to you a better vineyard in place of it. If it is better in your eyes, I will give you the money of its price.”

verses.name: I Kings 21:3
verses.text: Naboth said to Ahab, “Far be it from me from Yahweh that I should give the inheritance of my ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> to you.”

verses.name: I Kings 21:4
verses.text: Then Ahab went to his house, sullen and angry because of the word that Naboth the Jezreelite had spoken to him <transChange type="added">when</transChange> he had said, “I will not give to you the inheritance of my ancestors.”<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> So he lay on his bed, turned away his face, and would not eat <transChange type="added">any</transChange> food.  <div eID="gen2771" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 21:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2030"/><div sID="gen2772" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2030"/>Then Jezebel his wife came to him, and she said to him, “What is this, that your spirit is sullen and you are not eating food?”

verses.name: I Kings 21:6
verses.text: Then he said to her, “When I spoke to Naboth the Jezreelite and asked him, ‘Give me your vineyard for money, or it you prefer, I will give you a vineyard in place of it,’ he said, ‘I will not give you my vineyard.’ ”

verses.name: I Kings 21:7
verses.text: Jezebel his wife said to him, “Now, you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞rule⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “do kingship”</note> over Israel. Get up, eat food, and let your heart be <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞cheerful⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “good”</note> I myself will give you the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite.”  <div eID="gen2772" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 21:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2031"/><div sID="gen2773" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2031"/>So she wrote letters in the name of Ahab and sealed them with his seal. She sent the letters to the elders and the nobles who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> dwelling with Naboth in his city.

verses.name: I Kings 21:9
verses.text: She had written in the letters, saying, “Call a fast and seat Naboth at the head of the people.

verses.name: I Kings 21:10
verses.text: Seat two men, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞scoundrels⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons of wickedness”</note> opposite him. Let them witness against him saying, ‘You cursed God and the king.’ Then you shall bring him out and stone him so that he dies.”

verses.name: I Kings 21:11
verses.text: The men of his city and the elders and nobles who were living in his city did according to what Jezebel had sent to them, as <transChange type="added">was</transChange> written in the letters which she had sent to them.

verses.name: I Kings 21:12
verses.text: They called a fast, and they seated Naboth at the head of the people.

verses.name: I Kings 21:13
verses.text: Then the two men, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞scoundrels⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons of wickedness”</note> came, sat opposite him, and the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞scoundrels⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “men of wickedness”</note> witnessed against Naboth before the people, saying, “Naboth cursed God and the king,” so they brought him outside of the city and stoned him with stones, and he died.  <div eID="gen2773" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 21:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2032"/><div sID="gen2774" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2032"/>They sent to Jezebel saying, “Naboth has been stoned, and he is dead.”

verses.name: I Kings 21:15
verses.text: It happened at the moment Jezebel heard that Naboth had been stoned and died, Jezebel said to Ahab, “Get up, take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite which he had refused to give to you for money, for Naboth is not alive, but dead.”

verses.name: I Kings 21:16
verses.text: When Ahab heard that Naboth was dead, he got up to go down to the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite to take possession of it.  <div eID="gen2774" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 21:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2033"/><title type="x-s">Elijah Responds to Ahab</title> <div sID="gen2775" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2033"/>The word of Yahweh came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,

verses.name: I Kings 21:18
verses.text: “Arise, go down to meet Ahab the king of Israel who is in Samaria. Look in the vineyard of Naboth, where he has gone to take possession of it.

verses.name: I Kings 21:19
verses.text: You shall say to him, ‘Thus says Yahweh: “Have you committed murder and also taken possession?” ’ You shall also say to him, ‘Thus says Yahweh: “In the place where the dogs licked the blood of Naboth, the dogs will also lick your blood.” ’ ”  <div eID="gen2775" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 21:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2034"/><div sID="gen2776" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2034"/>Then Ahab said to Elijah, “Have you found me, my enemy?” He said, “I have found you because you have sold yourself to do evil in the eyes of Yahweh.

verses.name: I Kings 21:21
verses.text: ‘Look, I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> bringing disaster on you, and I will sweep away after you. I will cut off for Ahab <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞every male⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">“Literally “the one who urinates against the wall”</note> in Israel, bond or free.

verses.name: I Kings 21:22
verses.text: I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat and like the house of Baasha the son of Ahijah, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞because you made me angry⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for the provocation which you have provoked”</note> and have caused Israel to sin.’

verses.name: I Kings 21:23
verses.text: Moreover, concerning Jezebel, Yahweh has said, ‘The dogs will eat Jezebel in the outer rampart of Jezreel.’

verses.name: I Kings 21:24
verses.text: The one who dies for Ahab in the city, the dogs will eat; the one who dies in the open country, the birds of heaven will eat.”  <div eID="gen2776" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 21:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2035"/><div sID="gen2777" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2035"/>Truly, there was no one like Ahab who had sold himself by doing evil in the eyes of Yahweh, whose wife Jezebel urged him on.

verses.name: I Kings 21:26
verses.text: Also, he acted very abominably by going after idols like all the Amorites had done whom Yahweh had driven out from before the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note>  <div eID="gen2777" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 21:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2036"/><div sID="gen2778" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2036"/>When Ahab heard these words, he tore his clothes and put sackcloth over his flesh, fasted, lay in the sackcloth, and went about dejectedly.

verses.name: I Kings 21:28
verses.text: Then the word of Yahweh came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,

verses.name: I Kings 21:29
verses.text: “Have you seen how Ahab has humbled himself before me? Because he has humbled himself before me, I will not bring disaster in his days. I will bring the disaster on his house in the days of his son.”  <chapter eID="1Kgs.21"/>

verses.name: I Kings 22:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2037"/><title type="x-s">Jehoshaphat of Judah Allies with Ahab of Israel</title> <div sID="gen2779" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2037"/>They lived three years, and there was no war between Aram and Israel.

verses.name: I Kings 22:2
verses.text: It happened in the third year, Jehoshaphat king of Judah went down to the king of Israel,

verses.name: I Kings 22:3
verses.text: and the king of Israel said to his servants, “Do you know Ramoth-Gilead belongs to us, and we <transChange type="added">are</transChange> doing nothing about taking it from the hand of the king of Aram?”

verses.name: I Kings 22:4
verses.text: Then he said to Jehoshaphat, “Will you go with me to the battle for Ramoth-Gilead?” Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I am like you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “Like I am, like you are”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞my people are like your people⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “like my people, like your people”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞my horses are like your horses⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “like my horses, like your horses”</note>  <div eID="gen2779" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 22:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2038"/><div sID="gen2780" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2038"/>Jehoshaphat also said to the king of Israel, “Please inquire for the word of Yahweh today.”

verses.name: I Kings 22:6
verses.text: Then the king of Israel assembled the prophets, about four hundred men, and he said to them, “Shall I go against Ramoth-Gilead for the battle, or should I refrain?” Then they said, “Go up, for the Lord will give it into the hand of the king.”

verses.name: I Kings 22:7
verses.text: So Jehoshaphat said, “Is there no prophet of Yahweh here that we might still inquire from him?”

verses.name: I Kings 22:8
verses.text: Then the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “<transChange type="added">There is</transChange> still one man to inquire from Yahweh, but I despise him, for he never prophesies <transChange type="added">anything</transChange> good concerning me, but only bad: Micaiah the son of Imlah.” Then Jehoshaphat said, “The king should not say so.”

verses.name: I Kings 22:9
verses.text: The king of Israel summoned a certain court official, and he said, “Quickly fetch Micaiah son of Imlah.”

verses.name: I Kings 22:10
verses.text: The king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah <transChange type="added">were</transChange> each sitting on his throne, dressed <transChange type="added">in their</transChange> robes, at the threshing floor at the entrance of the gate of Samaria, <transChange type="added">with</transChange> all the prophets prophesying before them.

verses.name: I Kings 22:11
verses.text: Zedekiah son of Kenaanah made horns of iron for himself and said, “Thus says Yahweh: ‘With these you shall gore the Arameans until finishing them.’ ”

verses.name: I Kings 22:12
verses.text: All of the prophets <transChange type="added">were</transChange> likewise prophesying, saying, “Go up <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Ramoth-Gilead and triumph, and Yahweh will give it into the hand of the king.”  <div eID="gen2780" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 22:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2039"/><div sID="gen2781" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2039"/>Then the messenger who had gone to summon Micaiah said to him, “Please now, the words of the prophet are <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞unanimously⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “one mouth”</note> favorable to the king. Please let your words be as one word with them, and speak favorably.”

verses.name: I Kings 22:14
verses.text: Then Micaiah said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞As Yahweh lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “The life of Yahweh”</note> surely only as Yahweh speaks to me, that will I speak.”

verses.name: I Kings 22:15
verses.text: When he came to the king, the king asked him, “Micaiah, shall we go to Ramoth-Gilead to the battle, or shall we refrain?” He said to him, “Go up and triumph, and Yahweh will give <transChange type="added">it</transChange> into the hand of the king.”

verses.name: I Kings 22:16
verses.text: Then the king said to him, “How many times must I make you swear that you shall not tell me <transChange type="added">anything</transChange> but truth in the name of Yahweh?”

verses.name: I Kings 22:17
verses.text: So he said, “I saw all of Israel scattering to the mountains, like the sheep without a shepherd. Yahweh also said, ‘There are no masters for these, let them return in peace, each to his house.’ ”

verses.name: I Kings 22:18
verses.text: Then the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “Did I not say to you that he would not prophesy good concerning me, but disaster?”  <div eID="gen2781" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 22:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2040"/><div sID="gen2782" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2040"/>And he<note placement="foot">That is, Micaiah</note> said, “Therefore, hear the word of Yahweh. I saw Yahweh sitting on his throne with all the hosts of heaven standing beside him from his right hand and from his left <transChange type="added">hand</transChange>.

verses.name: I Kings 22:20
verses.text: And Yahweh said, ‘Who will entice Ahab so that he will go up and fall at Ramoth-Gilead?’ Then <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞this one was saying one thing and the other one was saying another⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “this one said in thus and this one was saying in thus”</note>

verses.name: I Kings 22:21
verses.text: Then a spirit came out and stood before Yahweh and said, ‘I will entice him,’ and Yahweh said to him, ‘How?’

verses.name: I Kings 22:22
verses.text: He said, ‘I will go out and I will be a false spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.’ And he<note placement="foot">That is, Yahweh</note> said, ‘You shall entice and succeed, go out and do so.’

verses.name: I Kings 22:23
verses.text: So then, see that Yahweh has placed a false spirit in the mouth of all of these your prophets, and Yahweh has spoken disaster concerning you.”  <div eID="gen2782" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 22:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2041"/><div sID="gen2783" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2041"/>Then Zedekiah son of Kenaanah came near and slapped Micaiah on the cheek and said, “When did the Spirit of Yahweh pass from me to speak with you?”

verses.name: I Kings 22:25
verses.text: Then Micaiah said, “Behold, you <transChange type="added">are about to</transChange> see on that day when you go <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from room to room⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “private room in private room”</note> to hide.”

verses.name: I Kings 22:26
verses.text: The king of Israel said, “Take Micaiah and return him to Amon the commander of the city and to Jehoash the son of the king;

verses.name: I Kings 22:27
verses.text: and say, ‘Thus says the king: “Put this <transChange type="added">fellow in</transChange> the house of imprisonment and feed him reduced rations of food and water until I come in peace.” ’ ”

verses.name: I Kings 22:28
verses.text: Then Micaiah said, “If you indeed return in peace, then Yahweh has not spoken with me.” Then he said, “Let all the peoples hear!”  <div eID="gen2783" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 22:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2042"/><div sID="gen2784" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2042"/>Then the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Ramoth-Gilead.

verses.name: I Kings 22:30
verses.text: Then the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “<transChange type="added">I will</transChange> disguise myself and go into the battle, but you wear your robes.” So the king of Israel disguised himself, and he went into the battle.

verses.name: I Kings 22:31
verses.text: The king of Aram commanded his thirty-two chariot commanders, saying, “You shall not fight with small or great, but only against the king of Israel, him alone!”

verses.name: I Kings 22:32
verses.text: When the chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat, they said, “Surely he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the king of Israel,” and they turned to fight against him, so Jehoshaphat called out.

verses.name: I Kings 22:33
verses.text: When the chariot commanders saw that it <transChange type="added">was</transChange> not the king of Israel, they turned away from him.

verses.name: I Kings 22:34
verses.text: But another man drew his bow fully and struck the king of Israel between the armor scales and the breastplate; so he said to his chariot driver, “Turn <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the chariot⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “your hand”</note> and bring me out from the camp, for I am wounded.”  <div eID="gen2784" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 22:35
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2043"/><div sID="gen2785" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2043"/>The battle intensified on that day, and the king was being propped up in the chariot opposite Aram, but he died in the evening, and the blood of the wound ran out to the floor of the chariot.

verses.name: I Kings 22:36
verses.text: Then the shout passed through the camp about sunset, saying, “Each man to his city and each to his land!”

verses.name: I Kings 22:37
verses.text: So the king died, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they brought him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and he went”</note> to Samaria, and they buried the king in Samaria.

verses.name: I Kings 22:38
verses.text: They washed the chariot by the pool of Samaria, and the dogs licked his blood (now, the prostitutes washed themselves <transChange type="added">there</transChange>) according to the word of Yahweh which he had spoken.

verses.name: I Kings 22:39
verses.text: The remainder of the acts of Ahab and all that he did, and the ivory palace and all the cities that he built, <transChange type="added">are</transChange> they not written in the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Israel?

verses.name: I Kings 22:40
verses.text: So Ahab slept with his ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and Ahaziah his son became king in his place.  <div eID="gen2785" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 22:41
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2044"/><title type="x-s">King Jehoshaphat of Judah</title> <div sID="gen2786" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2044"/>Jehoshaphat the son of Asa became king over Judah in the fourth year of Ahab king of Israel.

verses.name: I Kings 22:42
verses.text: Jehoshaphat was thirty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem. The name of his mother was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.

verses.name: I Kings 22:43
verses.text: He walked in all of the way of Asa his father, and he did not turn aside from it, doing right in the eyes of Yahweh.<note placement="foot"><reference osisRef="1Kgs.22.44">1 Kings 22:44 </reference>begins here in the Hebrew Bible</note> Only he did not remove the high places; the people <transChange type="added">were</transChange> still sacrificing and burning incense on the high places.

verses.name: I Kings 22:44
verses.text: <note placement="foot"><reference osisRef="1Kgs.22.44-1Kgs.22.53">1 Kings 22:44– 53 </reference>in the English Bible is 22:45–54 in the Hebrew Bible</note> But, Jehoshaphat made peace with the king of Israel.

verses.name: I Kings 22:45
verses.text: The remainder of the acts of Jehoshaphat, his powerful <transChange type="added">deeds</transChange> he did, and how he fought, are they not written in the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Judah?

verses.name: I Kings 22:46
verses.text: The remainder of the male shrine prostitutes who were left over in the days of Asa his father he exterminated from the land.

verses.name: I Kings 22:47
verses.text: There was not a king in Edom; a governor <transChange type="added">served</transChange> as king.

verses.name: I Kings 22:48
verses.text: Jehoshaphat built<note placement="foot">According to the reading tradition(<hi type="italic">Qere</hi>); what is written (<hi type="italic">Kethib</hi>) is “ten”</note> ships of the Tarshish <transChange type="added">type</transChange> to go to Ophir for the gold; but he did not go because the ships were destroyed at Ezion-Geber.

verses.name: I Kings 22:49
verses.text: Then Ahaziah son of Ahab said to Jehoshaphat, “Let my servants go with your servants in the ships,” but Jehoshaphat was not willing.

verses.name: I Kings 22:50
verses.text: And Jehoshaphat slept with his ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and was buried with his ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> in the city of David his ancestor,<note placement="foot">Or “father”</note> and Joram his son became king in his place.  <div eID="gen2786" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 22:51
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2045"/><title type="x-s">King Ahaziah of Israel</title> <div sID="gen2787" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2045"/>Ahaziah son of Ahab became king over Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he reigned over Israel two years.

verses.name: I Kings 22:52
verses.text: He did evil in the eyes of Yahweh, and he went in the way of his father and his mother and in the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat who caused Israel to sin.

verses.name: I Kings 22:53
verses.text: He served Baal and bowed down to him; and he provoked Yahweh the God of Israel according to all that his father did.  <chapter eID="1Kgs.22"/> <div eID="gen2787" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen2643" osisID="1Kgs" type="book"/>

verses.name: II Kings 1:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2046"/><title type="x-s">Elijah and the Messengers of Ahaziah</title> <div sID="gen2789" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2046"/>Moab rebelled against Israel after the death of Ahab.

verses.name: II Kings 1:2
verses.text: Ahaziah had fallen through the lattice in his upper room, which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in Samaria, and he was injured. So he sent messengers, and he said to them, “Go, inquire of Baal-Zebub, the god of Ekron, if I will survive this injury.”  <div eID="gen2789" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 1:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2047"/><div sID="gen2790" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2047"/>Then the angel of Yahweh spoke to Elijah the Tishbite, “Get up, go up to meet the messengers of the king of Samaria and speak to them, ‘Is it because there is no God in Israel that you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> going to inquire of Baal-Zebub, the god of Ekron?’

verses.name: II Kings 1:4
verses.text: Therefore, thus says Yahweh, ‘The bed upon which you have gone, you will not come down from it, but you shall surely die.’ ” So Elijah went.  <div eID="gen2790" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 1:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2048"/><div sID="gen2791" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2048"/>When the messengers returned to him, he asked them, “Why have you returned?”

verses.name: II Kings 1:6
verses.text: Then they said to him, “A man came up to meet us, and he said to us, ‘Go, return to the king who sent you and speak to him, “Thus says Yahweh, ‘Is it because there is no God in Israel that you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> sending to inquire of Baal-Zebub the god of Ekron? Therefore the bed upon which you have gone, you will not come down from it, for you will surely die.’ ” ’ ”

verses.name: II Kings 1:7
verses.text: Then he spoke to them, “What <transChange type="added">was</transChange> the manner of the man who came up to meet you and spoke to you all these things?”

verses.name: II Kings 1:8
verses.text: They answered him, “A <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞hairy man⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “an owner of hair”</note> with a leather belt girded around his waist.” And he said, “It <transChange type="added">is</transChange> Elijah the Tishbite.”  <div eID="gen2791" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 1:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2049"/><div sID="gen2792" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2049"/>So <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ahaziah⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “he”</note> sent to him the commander of fifty with his fifty <transChange type="added">men</transChange>, and he went up to him while he was sitting on the top of the hill. He said to him, “<transChange type="added">O</transChange> man of God, the king says, ‘Come down.’ ”

verses.name: II Kings 1:10
verses.text: Then Elijah answered and said to the commander of the fifty, “If I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty!” Then fire came down from heaven and consumed him and his fifty.  <div eID="gen2792" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 1:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2050"/><div sID="gen2793" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2050"/>So he <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞again sent⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “returned and sent”</note> another commander of fifty and his fifty <transChange type="added">men</transChange>. He answered and said to him, “<transChange type="added">O</transChange> man of God, thus says the king, ‘Come down quickly!’ ”

verses.name: II Kings 1:12
verses.text: Then Elijah answered and said to them, “If I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> a man of God, then let fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty!” Then the fire of God came down from heaven and consumed him and his fifty.  <div eID="gen2793" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 1:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2051"/><div sID="gen2794" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2051"/>So he <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞again sent⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “returned and sent”</note> a third <transChange type="added">time</transChange> a commander of fifty and his fifty, and the commander of the third fifty went up and came and knelt down on his knees before Elijah and entreated him. He said to him, “<transChange type="added">O</transChange> man of God, please let my life and the lives of your servants, these fifty, be precious in your eyes.

verses.name: II Kings 1:14
verses.text: Behold, fire from heaven came down and consumed the first two commanders of fifty and their fifties, so then let my life be precious in your eyes.”

verses.name: II Kings 1:15
verses.text: Then the angel of Yahweh spoke to Elijah, “Go down with him. Do not be afraid because of him.” So he got up and went down with him to the king,

verses.name: II Kings 1:16
verses.text: and he said to him, “Thus says Yahweh, ‘Because you have sent messengers to inquire of Baal-Zebub, the god of Ekron—is it because there is no God in Israel <transChange type="added">from whom</transChange> to inquire his word?—therefore the bed upon which you went, you shall not come down from it, for you shall surely die.’ ”  <div eID="gen2794" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 1:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2052"/><title type="x-s">Epitaph for Ahaziah</title> <div sID="gen2795" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2052"/>So he died, according to the word of Yahweh which Elijah had spoken, and Joram became king in his place in the second year of Joram the son of Jehoshaphat, the king of Judah, because he had no son.

verses.name: II Kings 1:18
verses.text: The remainder of the acts of Ahaziah which he did, <transChange type="added">are</transChange> they not written in the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Israel?  <chapter eID="2Kgs.1"/>

verses.name: II Kings 2:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2053"/><title type="x-s">Elijah Taken Away from Elisha</title> <div sID="gen2796" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2053"/>When Yahweh was about to take Elijah up in the storm <transChange type="added">to</transChange> heaven, Elijah and Elisha went from Gilgal.

verses.name: II Kings 2:2
verses.text: Elijah said to Elisha, “Please stay here, for Yahweh has sent me up to Bethel.” Elisha said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞As Yahweh lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “The life of Yahweh”</note> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as your soul lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “life of your soul”</note> I will certainly not leave you!” So they went down <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Bethel.

verses.name: II Kings 2:3
verses.text: Then the sons of the prophets who <transChange type="added">were in</transChange> Bethel came out to Elisha, and they said to him, “Do you know that Yahweh <transChange type="added">is</transChange> going to take your master <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from over your head”</note> today?” He said, “I also know; be quiet!”  <div eID="gen2796" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 2:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2054"/><div sID="gen2797" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2054"/>Elijah said to him, “Elisha, please stay here because Yahweh has sent me to Jericho.” And he said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞As Yahweh lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “The life of Yahweh”</note> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as your soul lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “life of your soul”</note> I will certainly not leave you!” So they came to Jericho.

verses.name: II Kings 2:5
verses.text: Then the sons of the prophets who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in Jericho came near to Elisha, and they said to him, “Do you know that Yahweh <transChange type="added">is</transChange> going to take your master <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from over your head”</note> today?” He said, “I also know; be quiet!”  <div eID="gen2797" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 2:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2055"/><div sID="gen2798" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2055"/>Then Elijah said to him, “Please stay here, because Yahweh has sent me to the Jordan.” He said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞As Yahweh lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “The life of Yahweh”</note> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as your soul lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “life of your soul”</note> I will certainly not leave you!” So the two of them went on.

verses.name: II Kings 2:7
verses.text: Then fifty men from the sons of the prophets went and stood opposite <transChange type="added">them</transChange> at a distance while the two of them stood by the Jordan.

verses.name: II Kings 2:8
verses.text: Elijah took his cloak, rolled it up, and struck the water. It divided <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in two⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “here and here”</note> and the two of them crossed over on dry land.  <div eID="gen2798" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 2:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2056"/><div sID="gen2799" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2056"/>After they crossed over, Elijah said to Elisha, “Ask what I may do for you before I am taken away from you.” Then Elisha said, “Please let there come to me a double portion of your spirit.”

verses.name: II Kings 2:10
verses.text: He said, “What you ask is difficult. If you see me being taken from you, it will be so for you, but if not, it will not happen.”

verses.name: II Kings 2:11
verses.text: Then they <transChange type="added">were</transChange> walking, talking as they went. Suddenly a fiery chariot with horses of fire <transChange type="added">appeared</transChange> and separated between the two of them. Elijah went up in the storm <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the heavens

verses.name: II Kings 2:12
verses.text: while Elisha <transChange type="added">was</transChange> watching and crying out, “My father, my father; the chariot of Israel and its horsemen!” But he could not see him any longer, and he grasped his clothes and tore them in two pieces.  <div eID="gen2799" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 2:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2057"/><div sID="gen2800" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2057"/>Then he picked up Elijah’s cloak that had fallen off of him, and he returned and stood on the bank of the Jordan.

verses.name: II Kings 2:14
verses.text: He took Elijah’s cloak that had fallen from upon him and struck the water. Then he said, “Where is Yahweh, the God of Elijah?” So he also struck the water, and it divided <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in two⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “here and here”</note> and Elisha crossed over.  <div eID="gen2800" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 2:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2058"/><title type="x-s">Elisha Begins His Ministry</title> <div sID="gen2801" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2058"/>When the sons of the prophets who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> at Jericho saw him from <transChange type="added">the</transChange> other side, they declared, “The spirit of Elijah rests upon Elisha,” and they came to meet him and bowed down to him to the ground.

verses.name: II Kings 2:16
verses.text: Then they said to him, “Look, there are with your servants fifty able men. Please let them go and look for your master, lest the Spirit of Yahweh has lifted him up and thrown him on one of the mountains or into one of the valleys,” but he said, “You must not send them.”

verses.name: II Kings 2:17
verses.text: But they urged him until embarrassing <transChange type="added">him</transChange>, so he said, “Send them.” So they sent fifty men, and they looked for three days, but they could not find him.

verses.name: II Kings 2:18
verses.text: Then they returned to him while he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> staying in Jericho. He said to them, “Did I not tell you not to go?”  <div eID="gen2801" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 2:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2059"/><div sID="gen2802" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2059"/>The men of the city said to Elisha, “Please now, the location of the city <transChange type="added">is</transChange> good, as my master can see, but the water <transChange type="added">is</transChange> bad and the land unproductive.”

verses.name: II Kings 2:20
verses.text: So he said, “Bring me a new bowl and put salt in it.” So they brought it to him.

verses.name: II Kings 2:21
verses.text: Then he went out to the spring of waters and threw the salt <transChange type="added">into it</transChange> there and said, “Thus says Yahweh, ‘I hereby purify these waters; let there be no longer any death or unproductiveness from it.’ ”

verses.name: II Kings 2:22
verses.text: Then the waters were purified until this very day according to the word of Elisha that he spoke.  <div eID="gen2802" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 2:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2060"/><div sID="gen2803" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2060"/>Then he went up from there <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Bethel; as he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> going up along the way, young boys came out from the city and mocked at him and said to him, “Go up, baldhead; go up, baldhead!”

verses.name: II Kings 2:24
verses.text: When he turned around and saw them, he cursed them in the name of Yahweh. Then two bears came out of the forest and mauled forty-two boys among them.

verses.name: II Kings 2:25
verses.text: Then he went from there to Mount Carmel and from there he returned <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Samaria.  <chapter eID="2Kgs.2"/>

verses.name: II Kings 3:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2061"/><title type="x-s">Joram Meets Moab in Battle</title> <div sID="gen2804" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2061"/>Now Joram the son of Ahab had become king over Israel in Samaria in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah. He reigned twelve years

verses.name: II Kings 3:2
verses.text: and did evil in the eyes of Yahweh, yet not as his father or his mother, as he removed the stone pillars of Baal that his father had made.

verses.name: II Kings 3:3
verses.text: But he did cling to the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat who caused Israel to sin, and he did not depart from it.  <div eID="gen2804" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 3:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2062"/><div sID="gen2805" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2062"/>Now Mesha king of Moab was a sheep breeder, and he used to deliver to the king of Israel a hundred thousand male lambs and a hundred thousand wool rams.

verses.name: II Kings 3:5
verses.text: It happened that when Ahab died, Mesha king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel.

verses.name: II Kings 3:6
verses.text: So King Joram went out on that day from Samaria, and he mustered all of Israel.

verses.name: II Kings 3:7
verses.text: He went and sent <transChange type="added">a message</transChange> to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, saying, “The king of Moab has rebelled against me. Will you go with me against Moab for the battle?” And he said, “I will go up. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I am like you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “Like I am, like you are”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞my people are like your people⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “like my people, like your people”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞my horses are like your horses⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “like my horses, like your horses”</note>

verses.name: II Kings 3:8
verses.text: Then he said, “Which way shall we go up?” And he answered, “By way of the wilderness of Edom.”  <div eID="gen2805" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 3:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2063"/><div sID="gen2806" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2063"/>So the king of Israel and the king of Judah and the king of Edom went around, a way of seven days, but there was no water for the army or for the animals which <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞were with them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “were at their feet”</note>

verses.name: II Kings 3:10
verses.text: Then the king of Israel said, “Aha, Yahweh has called for these three kings to give them into the hand of Moab.”

verses.name: II Kings 3:11
verses.text: Then Jehoshaphat asked, “Is there no prophet of Yahweh here that we might inquire <transChange type="added">guidance</transChange> from Yahweh?” One of the servants of the king of Israel answered and said, “Elisha the son of Shaphat is here, who poured water on the hands of Elijah.”<note placement="foot">That is, Elisha had served Elijah</note>

verses.name: II Kings 3:12
verses.text: Jehoshaphat said, “The word of Yahweh is with him.” So the king of Israel, Jehoshaphat, and the king of Edom went down to him.  <div eID="gen2806" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 3:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2064"/><div sID="gen2807" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2064"/>Then Elisha said to the king of Israel, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞What do we have in common⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?<note placement="foot">Literally “What to me and what for you”</note> Go to the prophets of your father and to the prophets of your mother.” Then the king of Israel said to him, “No, for Yahweh has called for these three kings to give them into the hand of Moab.”
