verses.name: II Kings 3:14
verses.text: Then Elisha said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞As Yahweh of hosts lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “The life of Yahweh of hosts”</note> before whom I stand, surely if I was not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞regarding the face⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Or “lifting the face”</note> of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, I would have not looked at you nor even glanced at you.

verses.name: II Kings 3:15
verses.text: But now, bring me a musician.” It happened that at the moment the musician played, the hand of Yahweh came upon him.

verses.name: II Kings 3:16
verses.text: He said, “Thus says Yahweh, ‘Make this wadi <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞full of cisterns⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,’<note placement="foot">Literally “cisterns, cisterns”</note>

verses.name: II Kings 3:17
verses.text: for thus says Yahweh, ‘You will see neither wind nor rain, yet this wadi will be full of water; and you and all of your livestock and your animals shall drink.’

verses.name: II Kings 3:18
verses.text: And since this is too trivial in the eyes of Yahweh, he will also give Moab into your hand,

verses.name: II Kings 3:19
verses.text: and you shall defeat every fortified city, every choice city, and you shall fell every good tree. All of the springs of water you shall stop up, and every tract of good land you shall ruin with the stones.”

verses.name: II Kings 3:20
verses.text: It happened in the morning about the time of the <transChange type="added">morning</transChange> offering, that water was suddenly coming from the direction of Edom and the land was filled with water.  <div eID="gen2807" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 3:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2065"/><div sID="gen2808" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2065"/>Now all of Moab had heard that the kings had come up to fight against them, and all <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who were fighting age and up⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “who girded on a belt and above”</note> were called up, and they stood at the border.

verses.name: II Kings 3:22
verses.text: When they arose early in the morning, the sun shone on the waters, and Moab saw the waters from the opposite <transChange type="added">side</transChange> as red as blood.

verses.name: II Kings 3:23
verses.text: Then they said, “This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> blood! Certainly the kings have fought one another, and each has killed his neighbor. Now, to the war booty, O Moab!”

verses.name: II Kings 3:24
verses.text: But when they came to the camp of Israel, Israel stood up and killed Moab, so that they fled from before them. They came at her and defeated Moab.

verses.name: II Kings 3:25
verses.text: The cities they tore down, <transChange type="added">on</transChange> every good tract of land they threw stones until it was filled up, every spring of water they stopped up, and every good tree they felled. They let the stone walls at Kir Hareseth remain, but the slingers surrounded and attacked it.

verses.name: II Kings 3:26
verses.text: When the king of Moab saw that the battle was too heavy for him, he took with him seven hundred men who drew the sword to break through to the king of Edom, but they were not able.

verses.name: II Kings 3:27
verses.text: He took his firstborn son who was to become king in his place and offered him <transChange type="added">as</transChange> a burnt offering on the wall. Great wrath came upon Israel, and they withdrew from him and returned to the land.  <chapter eID="2Kgs.3"/>

verses.name: II Kings 4:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2066"/><title type="x-s">Elisha Answers a Widow’s Request</title> <div sID="gen2809" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2066"/>A certain woman from the wives of the sons of the prophets cried out to Elisha, saying, “Your servant my husband is dead. Now you know that your servant was a fearer of Yahweh, but the creditor came to take two of my children for himself as slaves.

verses.name: II Kings 4:2
verses.text: Elisha asked her, “What shall I do for you? Tell me, what do you have in the house?” Then she said, “Your servant has nothing in the house except a jar of olive oil.”

verses.name: II Kings 4:3
verses.text: Then he said to her, “Go, ask for yourself <transChange type="added">some</transChange> containers from the streets, from all your neighbors. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞You must collect as many empty containers as you can⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!<note placement="foot">Literally “You must not collect only a few empty containers”</note>

verses.name: II Kings 4:4
verses.text: You must also go and shut the door behind you and your children, and you must pour out <transChange type="added">oil</transChange> into all of these containers and set the filled <transChange type="added">ones</transChange> aside.”

verses.name: II Kings 4:5
verses.text: So she went from him, and she shut the door behind her and her children. They <transChange type="added">were</transChange> bringing <transChange type="added">containers</transChange> to her, and she <transChange type="added">kept</transChange> pouring.

verses.name: II Kings 4:6
verses.text: It happened that when the containers were full, she said to her son, “Bring near me another container,” but he said to her, “There is not another container.” Then the olive oil stopped flowing.

verses.name: II Kings 4:7
verses.text: So she came and told the man of God, and he said, “Go, sell the olive oil and repay your debt. You and your sons can live on what is left over.”  <div eID="gen2809" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 4:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2067"/><title type="x-s">Elisha at Shunem</title> <div sID="gen2810" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2067"/>It happened one day that Elisha passed through to Shunem where there <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a wealthy woman, and she urged him to eat bread; so it happened each time he passed through, he would stop there to eat.

verses.name: II Kings 4:9
verses.text: She said to her husband, “Please now, I know that he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a holy man of God who is passing <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞our way⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “upon us”</note> regularly;

verses.name: II Kings 4:10
verses.text: let us make a small enclosed room <transChange type="added">upstairs</transChange> and put a bed, table, chair, and lampstand there for him, so that when he comes to us, he can turn and stay there.

verses.name: II Kings 4:11
verses.text: One day it happened that he came there and went to the upper room and lay down there.

verses.name: II Kings 4:12
verses.text: He said to Gehazi his servant, “Call to this Shunammite,” so he called to her, and she stood before him.

verses.name: II Kings 4:13
verses.text: He said to him, “Please say to her, ‘Look, you took all this trouble, showing care for us; what is there <transChange type="added">for me</transChange> to do for you? To speak for you to the king or to the commander of the army?’ ” She said, “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> living among my people.”

verses.name: II Kings 4:14
verses.text: Then he said, “What may be done for her?” Gehazi said, “Well, she has no son, and her husband is old.”

verses.name: II Kings 4:15
verses.text: And he said, “Call for her,” so he called for her and she stood in the doorway.

verses.name: II Kings 4:16
verses.text: And he said, “At this time <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞next spring⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “about that season as the time of life”</note> you <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> embracing a son.” She said, “No, my lord, <transChange type="added">O</transChange> man of God! You must not tell a lie to your servant!”

verses.name: II Kings 4:17
verses.text: But the woman conceived, and she bore a son <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in the spring⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “about that season as the time of life”</note> which Elisha had promised to her.  <div eID="gen2810" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 4:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2068"/><title type="x-s">Elisha Restores the Shunammite’s Son</title> <div sID="gen2811" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2068"/>The child grew older, and it happened one day that he went out to his father <transChange type="added">and</transChange> to the reapers.

verses.name: II Kings 4:19
verses.text: Then he said to his father, “My head, my head!” So he said to the servant, “Carry him to his mother.”

verses.name: II Kings 4:20
verses.text: So they carried him and brought him to his mother; he sat on her lap until noon and then died.

verses.name: II Kings 4:21
verses.text: She went up, laid him on the bed of the man of God, closed <transChange type="added">the door</transChange>, and went out behind it.

verses.name: II Kings 4:22
verses.text: She called to her husband and said, “Please send one of the servants and one of the female donkeys for me, so that I can go quickly up to the man of God and return.”

verses.name: II Kings 4:23
verses.text: And he said, “Why are you going to him today? <transChange type="added">It is</transChange> neither the new moon nor the Sabbath!” And she said, “Peace.”

verses.name: II Kings 4:24
verses.text: She saddled the female donkey, and she said to her servant, “Drive along and go; you must not hold me back from riding, unless I tell you.”

verses.name: II Kings 4:25
verses.text: So she went and came to the man of God by Mount Carmel. It happened when the man of God saw her <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞at a distance⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “from opposite”</note> he said to Gehazi his servant, “There is this Shunammite.

verses.name: II Kings 4:26
verses.text: Now, please run to meet her and ask her, ‘Is it peace for you? Is it peace for your husband? Is it peace for the boy?’ ” She said, “Peace.”

verses.name: II Kings 4:27
verses.text: So she came to the man of God at the mountain, and she caught hold of his feet. Then Gehazi came near to push her away, but the man of God said, “Let her alone, for her soul is bitter, and Yahweh has hidden it from me and has not told me.”

verses.name: II Kings 4:28
verses.text: Then she said, “Did I ask for a son from my lord? Did I not say that you must not mislead me?”  <div eID="gen2811" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 4:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2069"/><div sID="gen2812" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2069"/>Then he said to Gehazi, “Gird up your loins and take my staff in your hand and go. If you meet anyone, you must not greet them; if anyone greets you, you must not answer them. You must put my staff on the face of the boy.”

verses.name: II Kings 4:30
verses.text: Then the mother of the boy said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞As Yahweh lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “The life of Yahweh”</note> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as your soul lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “life of your soul”</note> I will surely not leave you.” So he got up and went after her.

verses.name: II Kings 4:31
verses.text: Gehazi crossed over before them, and he put the staff on the face of the boy; but there was no sound, and there was no sign of life, so he returned to meet him. He told him, saying, “The boy did not wake up.”  <div eID="gen2812" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 4:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2070"/><div sID="gen2813" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2070"/>When Elisha came to the house, here <transChange type="added">was</transChange> the boy dead, lying on his bed.

verses.name: II Kings 4:33
verses.text: He went and closed the door behind the two of them and prayed to Yahweh.

verses.name: II Kings 4:34
verses.text: Then he went up and lay upon the child and put his mouth on his mouth, his eyes on his eyes, and his palms on his palms. As he bent down over him, the flesh of the boy became warm.

verses.name: II Kings 4:35
verses.text: He returned and went <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to and fro⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “here first and here”</note> in the house one time, then he went up and bent over him. Then the boy sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.

verses.name: II Kings 4:36
verses.text: <transChange type="added">Elisha</transChange> called to Gehazi and said, “Call this Shunammite.” So he called her and she came to him; then he said, “Pick up your son.”

verses.name: II Kings 4:37
verses.text: She came and fell at his feet and bowed down to the ground; then she picked up her son and went out.  <div eID="gen2813" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 4:38
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2071"/><title type="x-s">Elisha Secures the Food</title> <div sID="gen2814" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2071"/>So Elisha returned to Gilgal. Now the famine <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in the land, and the sons of the prophets were sitting before him. He said to his servant, put on the large pot and cook a stew for the sons of the prophets.

verses.name: II Kings 4:39
verses.text: One went out to the field to gather herbs, and he found a <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞wild vine⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a vine of the field”</note> and gathered wild gourds from it <transChange type="added">and</transChange> filled his cloak. Then he came and cut them into the pot of stew, but they did not know <transChange type="added">what they were</transChange>.

verses.name: II Kings 4:40
verses.text: They served the men to eat, but when they ate from the stew, they cried out and said, “There <transChange type="added">is</transChange> death in the pot, <transChange type="added">O</transChange> man of God!” They were not able to eat <transChange type="added">it</transChange>.

verses.name: II Kings 4:41
verses.text: Then he said, “Bring <transChange type="added">some</transChange> flour,” and he threw it into the pot. He then said, “Serve the people and let them eat.” There was nothing harmful in the pot.  <div eID="gen2814" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 4:42
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2072"/><div sID="gen2815" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2072"/>A man came from Baal-Shalishah and brought food to the man of God: firstfruits and twenty loaves of barley bread, with ripe grain in his sack. He said, “Give <transChange type="added">it</transChange> to the people and let them eat.”

verses.name: II Kings 4:43
verses.text: Then his servant said, “How can I set this before a hundred men?” He said, “Give it to the people and let them eat, for thus Yahweh says, ‘They shall eat and have some left over.’ ”

verses.name: II Kings 4:44
verses.text: So he set it before them, and they ate and had some left over, according to the word of Yahweh.  <chapter eID="2Kgs.4"/>

verses.name: II Kings 5:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2073"/><title type="x-s">The Healing of Naaman the Syrian</title> <div sID="gen2816" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2073"/>Now Naaman was the commander of the army of the king of Aram. He was a great man before his master and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞highly regarded⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “faces were being lifted up ”</note> for by him Yahweh had given victory to Aram. Now the man was a mighty warrior, <transChange type="added">but he was</transChange> afflicted with a skin disease.

verses.name: II Kings 5:2
verses.text: When the Arameans went <transChange type="added">on</transChange> a raid, they brought back a young girl from the land of Israel, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞she came into the service of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “she became before”</note> the wife of Naaman.

verses.name: II Kings 5:3
verses.text: She said to her mistress, “If only my lord would <transChange type="added">come</transChange> before the prophet who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in Samaria; then <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he would cure his skin disease⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “he would withdraw him from his skin disease”</note>

verses.name: II Kings 5:4
verses.text: He came and told his master, saying, “Thus and so the girl who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> from the land of Israel said.”

verses.name: II Kings 5:5
verses.text: So the king of Aram said, “Go, I will send a letter to the king of Israel.” He went and took <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞with him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in his hand”</note> ten talents of silver, six thousand <transChange type="added">shekels of</transChange> gold, and ten sets of clothing.  <div eID="gen2816" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 5:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2074"/><div sID="gen2817" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2074"/>So he brought the letter of the king to Israel, saying, “Now, when this letter comes to you, I have just sent Naaman my servant to you that you may cure him from his skin disease.”

verses.name: II Kings 5:7
verses.text: It happened that when the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his clothes and said, “Am I God to cause death or to give life? This man <transChange type="added">is</transChange> sending a man to me to cure his disease. Indeed! But know and see that he seeks an opportunity against me.”  <div eID="gen2817" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 5:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2075"/><div sID="gen2818" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2075"/>It happened that as soon as Elisha the man of God heard that the king of Israel had torn his clothes, he sent to the king, saying, “Why did you tear your clothes? Please may he come to me, that he might know that there is a prophet in Israel.”

verses.name: II Kings 5:9
verses.text: Then Naaman came with his horses and his chariots, and he stopped <transChange type="added">at</transChange> the doorway of the house of Elisha.

verses.name: II Kings 5:10
verses.text: Elisha sent a messenger to him, saying, “Go, you must wash seven times in the Jordan, then your flesh shall return to you, and you shall be clean.”

verses.name: II Kings 5:11
verses.text: But Naaman became angry and he went and said, “Look, I said to myself, ‘Surely he will come out, stand, call upon the name of Yahweh his God, and wave his hands over the spot; then he would take away the skin disease.’

verses.name: II Kings 5:12
verses.text: Are not the Abana and the Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all of the waters of Israel? Could I not wash in them that I may be clean?” Then he turned and left in anger.

verses.name: II Kings 5:13
verses.text: But his servants came near and spoke to him and said, “My father, <transChange type="added">if</transChange> the prophet had spoken a difficult thing to you to do, would you not have done <transChange type="added">it</transChange>? <transChange type="added">Why not</transChange> even when he says to you, ‘Wash and you shall be clean’?”

verses.name: II Kings 5:14
verses.text: So he went down and plunged into the Jordan seven times, according to the word of the man of God, and his flesh returned as the flesh of a small boy, and he was clean.  <div eID="gen2818" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 5:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2076"/><title type="x-s">Elisha’s Greedy Servant Gehazi</title> <div sID="gen2819" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2076"/>When he returned to the man of God, he and all of his army, he came and stood before him and said, “Please now, I know that there is no God in all of the world except in Israel. So then, please take a gift from your servant.”

verses.name: II Kings 5:16
verses.text: And he said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞As Yahweh lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “The life of Yahweh”</note> before whom I stand, I surely will not take <transChange type="added">it</transChange>.” <transChange type="added">Still</transChange> he urged him to take <transChange type="added">it</transChange>, but he refused.

verses.name: II Kings 5:17
verses.text: Then Naaman said, “If not, then please let a load of soil on a pair of mules be given to your servants, for your servant will never again bring a burnt offering and sacrifice to other gods, <transChange type="added">but</transChange> only to Yahweh.

verses.name: II Kings 5:18
verses.text: As far as this matter, may Yahweh pardon your servant when my master goes <transChange type="added">into</transChange> the house of Rimmon to worship there, and he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> leaning himself on my arm, that I also bow down <transChange type="added">in</transChange> the house of Rimmon: when I bow down <transChange type="added">in</transChange> the house of Rimmon, may Yahweh please pardon your servant in this matter.”

verses.name: II Kings 5:19
verses.text: He said to him, “Go in peace,” so he went from him <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a short distance⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “a stretch of land”</note>  <div eID="gen2819" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 5:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2077"/><div sID="gen2820" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2077"/>But Gehazi the servant of Elisha, the man of God, thought, “Look, my master has refrained from taking what this Aramean Naaman brought from his hand. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞As Yahweh lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “The life of Yahweh”</note> I will certainly run after him, and I will accept something from him.”

verses.name: II Kings 5:21
verses.text: So Gehazi pursued after Naaman. When Naaman saw <transChange type="added">someone</transChange> running after him, he jumped off his chariot to meet him and asked him, “<transChange type="added">Is it</transChange> peace?”

verses.name: II Kings 5:22
verses.text: He said, “Peace. My master has sent me saying, ‘Look, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞just now⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “now this”</note> two servants from the hill country of Ephraim came to me, from the sons of the prophets. Please give them a talent of silver and two sets of clothing.’ ”

verses.name: II Kings 5:23
verses.text: Then Naaman said, “Be prepared to accept two talents.” So he urged him and tied up two talents of silver in two bags, with two sets of clothing and gave it to two of his servants and they carried it before him.

verses.name: II Kings 5:24
verses.text: When he came to the citadel, he took them from their hand and put them in the house, then sent away the men so that they went.

verses.name: II Kings 5:25
verses.text: When he went and stood by his master, Elisha asked him, “From where have you come, Gehazi?” And he said, “Your servant has not gone <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞anywhere⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “where to where”</note>  <div eID="gen2820" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 5:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2078"/><div sID="gen2821" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2078"/>Then he said to him, “Did not my heart go <transChange type="added">with you</transChange> as the man turned from on his chariot to meet you? <transChange type="added">Is</transChange> it time to take silver, clothes, olive orchards, vineyards, sheep, oxen, male slaves, and female slaves?

verses.name: II Kings 5:27
verses.text: The skin disease of Naaman shall cling to you and to your offspring forever.” Then he went out from before him having a skin disease like the snow.  <chapter eID="2Kgs.5"/>

verses.name: II Kings 6:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2079"/><title type="x-s">Elisha Recovers a Lost Axe Head</title> <div sID="gen2822" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2079"/>Then the sons of the prophets said to Elisha, “Please look; the place where we are living before you <transChange type="added">is</transChange> too cramped for us.

verses.name: II Kings 6:2
verses.text: Let us please go to the Jordan and each bring from there one log that we might make a place there for us to live.” Then he said, “Do so.”

verses.name: II Kings 6:3
verses.text: Then a certain one said, “Please be prepared and go with your servants,” and he said, “I will go.”

verses.name: II Kings 6:4
verses.text: He went with them, and they went to the Jordan, and they cut down the trees.

verses.name: II Kings 6:5
verses.text: It happened as the one <transChange type="added">was</transChange> felling the log, that the iron ax fell into the water. He called out and said, “Oh, no! My master, it was borrowed!”

verses.name: II Kings 6:6
verses.text: Then the man of God said, “Where did it fall?” So he showed him the place, and then he cut off a stick and threw <transChange type="added">it</transChange> there and made the iron ax float.

verses.name: II Kings 6:7
verses.text: Then he said, “Pick <transChange type="added">it</transChange> up for yourself,” so he stretched out his hand and took it.  <div eID="gen2822" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 6:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2080"/><title type="x-s">Arameans Plot to Take Elisha</title> <div sID="gen2823" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2080"/>The king of Aram was fighting with Israel, so he consulted with his officers, saying, “My camp is <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞at such and such a place⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “to a place a certain someone”</note>

verses.name: II Kings 6:9
verses.text: Then the man of God sent to the king of Israel, saying, “Take care while crossing over to this place, because <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Arameans <transChange type="added">are</transChange> descending there.”

verses.name: II Kings 6:10
verses.text: So the king of Israel sent to the place which the man of God said to him and warned him, so he was on guard there <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞continually⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “not once or twice”</note>  <div eID="gen2823" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 6:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2081"/><div sID="gen2824" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2081"/>Then the heart of the king of Aram was stormy because of this matter, so he called his servants and said to them, “Can you not tell me <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who among us sides with the king of Israel⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?”<note placement="foot">Literally “who from of us to the king of Israel”</note>

verses.name: II Kings 6:12
verses.text: Then one of his servants said, “No, my lord the king, but Elisha the prophet who is <transChange type="added">in</transChange> Israel tells the king of Israel things which you speak <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in your own bedchamber⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “in the private room of your bed”</note>

verses.name: II Kings 6:13
verses.text: Then he said, “Go and see where he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> so that I can send and capture him.” Then he was told to him, “Look, <transChange type="added">he is</transChange> in Dothan.”

verses.name: II Kings 6:14
verses.text: So he sent horses, chariots, and an oppressing army there. They arrived at night and surrounded the town.

verses.name: II Kings 6:15
verses.text: The attendant of the man of God arose early and went out, and look, the army <transChange type="added">was</transChange> surrounding the city with horses and chariots. His servant said to him, “Oh no, my master! What shall we do?”

verses.name: II Kings 6:16
verses.text: And he said, “Don’t be afraid, for more <transChange type="added">are</transChange> with us than are with them.”

verses.name: II Kings 6:17
verses.text: Then Elisha prayed and said, “O Yahweh, please open his eyes that he may see,” and Yahweh opened the eyes of the servant, and he saw, and look, the mountain <transChange type="added">was</transChange> full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha.

verses.name: II Kings 6:18
verses.text: They came down to him, and Elisha prayed to Yahweh and said, “Please strike this people with blindness,” so he struck them with blindness as <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Elisha had spoken⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “according to the word of Elisha”</note>

verses.name: II Kings 6:19
verses.text: Then Elisha said to them, “This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not the way and this <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not the city. Come after me, and I will bring you to the man whom you seek.” Then he brought them to Samaria.  <div eID="gen2824" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 6:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2082"/><div sID="gen2825" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2082"/>It happened at the moment they came to Samaria, Elisha said, “O Yahweh, open the eyes of these that they may see,” so Yahweh opened their eyes, and they saw, and look, the middle of Samaria!

verses.name: II Kings 6:21
verses.text: Then the king of Israel said to Elisha when he saw them, “Shall I kill them? Shall I kill, my father?”

verses.name: II Kings 6:22
verses.text: And he said, “You shall not kill. Would you kill <transChange type="added">those</transChange> whom you took captive with the sword or with the bow? Put food and water before them that they may eat and drink and then go to their master.”

verses.name: II Kings 6:23
verses.text: So he made a great feast for them, and they ate and drank; then he sent them, and they went to their master. And the bands of the Arameans did not come again into the land of Israel.  <div eID="gen2825" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 6:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2083"/><title type="x-s">Besieged Samaria Resorts to Cannibalism</title> <div sID="gen2826" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2083"/>It happened after this that Ben-Hadad king of Aram assembled all of his army and marched up and laid siege against Samaria.

verses.name: II Kings 6:25
verses.text: There was a great famine in Samaria, and behold, a siege <transChange type="added">was</transChange> against it, until the head of a donkey <transChange type="added">went</transChange> for eighty shekels of silver, and one fourth of the measure of the dung of doves <transChange type="added">went</transChange> for five shekels of silver.

verses.name: II Kings 6:26
verses.text: It happened that the king of Israel <transChange type="added">was</transChange> crossing over on the wall, and a woman called out to him, saying, “Help, my lord the king!”

verses.name: II Kings 6:27
verses.text: He said, “No, let Yahweh help you. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞How⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “From where”</note> can I save you? From the threshing floor or from the wine press?”

verses.name: II Kings 6:28
verses.text: The king said to her, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞What is the problem⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?”<note placement="foot">Literally “What is for you”</note> Then the woman said, “This woman said to me, ‘Give me your son, and let us eat him today, then tomorrow we will eat my son.’

verses.name: II Kings 6:29
verses.text: So we cooked my son and ate him, and I said to her the next day, ‘Give your son that we may eat him.’ But she had hidden her son.”

verses.name: II Kings 6:30
verses.text: It happened that when the king heard the words of the woman, he tore his clothes. Now he had been walking on the wall, and the people saw, and behold, sackcloth was over his flesh underneath.

verses.name: II Kings 6:31
verses.text: Then he said, “May God do to me and thus may he add, if the head of Elisha the son of Shaphat remains on him today!”

verses.name: II Kings 6:32
verses.text: Now Elisha <transChange type="added">was</transChange> sitting in his house and the elders <transChange type="added">were</transChange> sitting with him, and <transChange type="added">the king</transChange> dispatched a man from before him, but before the messenger came to him, he said to the elders, “Did you see that this son of a murderer has sent to remove my head? Look, when the messenger comes, close the door; and you must <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞hold the door closed against him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “hold him close against the door”</note> <transChange type="added">Is</transChange> not the sound of the feet of his master behind him?”

verses.name: II Kings 6:33
verses.text: While he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> still speaking with them, suddenly the messenger <transChange type="added">was</transChange> coming down to him, and he said, “Look this trouble <transChange type="added">is</transChange> from Yahweh. Why should I wait for Yahweh any longer?”  <chapter eID="2Kgs.6"/>

verses.name: II Kings 7:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2084"/><title type="x-s">Elisha Prophesies Hope for Relief</title> <div sID="gen2827" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2084"/>Elisha said, “Hear the word of Yahweh: ‘Thus says Yahweh, “At this time tomorrow a seah of wheat bread flour <transChange type="added">will sell</transChange> for a shekel, and two seahs of barley for a shekel in the gate of Samaria.’ ”

verses.name: II Kings 7:2
verses.text: Then the officer <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞on whom the king relied⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “whom the king was leaning on his hand”</note> answered the man of God and said, “Look, <transChange type="added">even if</transChange> Yahweh <transChange type="added">is</transChange> making windows in heaven, could this thing happen?” And he said, “Look, you <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> seeing <transChange type="added">it</transChange> with your eyes, but you shall not eat from it there.”  <div eID="gen2827" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 7:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2085"/><title type="x-s">Four Lepers Report the Departure of the Arameans</title> <div sID="gen2828" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2085"/>Now four men who had a skin disease were <transChange type="added">at</transChange> the entrance of the gate, and they said <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to each other⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “each to his friend”</note> “Why <transChange type="added">are</transChange> we sitting here until we die?

verses.name: II Kings 7:4
verses.text: If we say, ‘Let us go <transChange type="added">into</transChange> the city,’ the famine <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in the city, and we shall die there; but if we sit here, we shall die. So then, come, let us fall into the camp of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Arameans. If they let us live, we shall live; but if they kill us, then we shall die.”

verses.name: II Kings 7:5
verses.text: So they got up at dusk to go to the camp of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Arameans. They went up to the edge of the camp of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Arameans, and look, there was no man there!

verses.name: II Kings 7:6
verses.text: Now the Lord had caused the camp of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Arameans to hear the sound of chariots, the sound of horses, and the sound of a great army. So they said <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to one another⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “each to his brother”</note> “Look, the king of Israel has hired the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Egypt to come against us!”

verses.name: II Kings 7:7
verses.text: So they got up and fled at dusk and left their tents, their horses, their donkeys, and the camp as it was, and they fled for their lives.

verses.name: II Kings 7:8
verses.text: When these who had the skin disease came to the edge of the camp, they went into a certain tent and they ate, drank, and took from there silver and gold and clothes. Then they went and hid <transChange type="added">them</transChange>, then returned and came to another tent, and they took from there and went and hid <transChange type="added">them</transChange>.  <div eID="gen2828" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 7:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2086"/><div sID="gen2829" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2086"/>Then they said <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to one another⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “each to his friend”</note> “We are not doing right. This day is a day of good news! If we are silent and wait until the light of morning, they will find us and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞we will be punished⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “guiltiness”</note> So then, come, let us go and tell the house of the king.”

verses.name: II Kings 7:10
verses.text: When they came, they called to the gatekeepers of the city and told them, saying, “We came to the camp of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Arameans, and behold, there was no man or the voice of a man there! Only the horses and the donkeys were tied up, and the tents <transChange type="added">were left</transChange> as they <transChange type="added">were</transChange>.”

verses.name: II Kings 7:11
verses.text: Then the gatekeepers called and told <transChange type="added">it</transChange> inside the house of the king.

verses.name: II Kings 7:12
verses.text: The king got up in the night and said to his servants, “Please let me tell you what <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Arameans have done to us. <transChange type="added">The</transChange> Arameans know that we <transChange type="added">are</transChange> hungry, so they went out from the camp to hide in the field, saying, ‘When they go out from the city, we shall seize them alive and go into the city.’ ”

verses.name: II Kings 7:13
verses.text: Then one of his servants replied and said, “Please let them take five of the remaining horses which remain in <transChange type="added">the city</transChange>; behold, they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> like all of the multitude of Israel that remain in it; they are like all the multitude of Israel who have perished. Let us send and see.”

verses.name: II Kings 7:14
verses.text: So he took two charioteer horsemen, and the king sent after the camp of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Arameans, saying, “Go, find out,”

verses.name: II Kings 7:15
verses.text: and they went after them to the Jordan. Look, all of the way <transChange type="added">was</transChange> littered with clothes and equipment which <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Arameans had thrown away in their haste. Then the messengers returned and told the king.  <div eID="gen2829" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 7:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2087"/><title type="x-s">Prophecy Fulfilled</title> <div sID="gen2830" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2087"/>So the people went out and plundered the camp of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Arameans. A seah of wheat flour <transChange type="added">went</transChange> for a shekel and two seahs of barley <transChange type="added">went</transChange> for a shekel according to the word of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Kings 7:17
verses.text: Then the king appointed the officer he was depending on over the gate, but the people trampled him and he died, according to that which the man of God had said which he spoke when the king came down to him.

verses.name: II Kings 7:18
verses.text: It happened as the man of God spoke to the king, saying, “Two seahs of barley <transChange type="added">shall be sold</transChange> for a shekel and a seah of wheat flour for a shekel at this time tomorrow in the gate of Samaria.”

verses.name: II Kings 7:19
verses.text: Then the officer had replied to the man of God and said, “Look, even if Yahweh is opening the windows in heaven, could this thing happen?” And he had said, “Look you <transChange type="added">are about to</transChange> see it with your eyes, but you will not eat from it.”

verses.name: II Kings 7:20
verses.text: So it had happened to him; the people trampled him in the gate and he died.  <chapter eID="2Kgs.7"/>

verses.name: II Kings 8:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2088"/><title type="x-s">Joram Restores the Shunammite’s Land</title> <div sID="gen2831" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2088"/>Elisha spoke to the woman whose son he had restored to life, saying, “Get up and go, you and your household, and dwell as an alien wherever you can, for Yahweh has called for a famine, and it will come to the land <transChange type="added">for</transChange> seven years.”

verses.name: II Kings 8:2
verses.text: So the woman got up and did according to the word of the man of God. She and her household went and dwelt as an alien in the land of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines for seven years.

verses.name: II Kings 8:3
verses.text: It happened at the end of seven years that the woman returned from the land of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines and went out to appeal to the king for her household and for her <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞properties⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “fields”</note>

verses.name: II Kings 8:4
verses.text: Now the king <transChange type="added">was</transChange> speaking to Gehazi the servant of the man of God, saying, “Please tell me all of the great things which Elisha has done.”

verses.name: II Kings 8:5
verses.text: It happened that as he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> telling the king how he had restored the dead to life, suddenly the woman whose son he had restored to life <transChange type="added">was</transChange> crying out to the king about her household and about her field. Then Gehazi said, “My lord the king, this <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the woman and this is her son whom Elisha restored to life!”

verses.name: II Kings 8:6
verses.text: So the king asked the woman, and she told him. So the king appointed for her a certain court official, saying, “Restore all that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> hers and all the yield of the field from <transChange type="added">the</transChange> day she left the land up to now.”  <div eID="gen2831" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 8:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2089"/><div sID="gen2832" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2089"/>Elisha came <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Damascus. Now Ben-Hadad king of Aram <transChange type="added">was</transChange> ill, and he was told, “The man of God has come up here.”

verses.name: II Kings 8:8
verses.text: Then the king said to Hazael, “Take a gift in your hand and go meet the man of God. Inquire of Yahweh from him, saying, ‘Shall I recover from this illness?’ ”

verses.name: II Kings 8:9
verses.text: So Hazael went to meet him and took a gift in his hand of all of the good things of Damascus, a load <transChange type="added">on each</transChange> of forty camels, and he came and stood before him. Then he said, “Your son Ben-Hadad king of Aram has sent me to you, saying, ‘Shall I recover from this illness?’ ”

verses.name: II Kings 8:10
verses.text: Elisha said to him, “Go; say to him, ‘You shall certainly recover,’ but Yahweh has shown me that he certainly will die.”

verses.name: II Kings 8:11
verses.text: Then the man <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞fixed his gaze and stared at him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “caused his face to stand and set it”</note> until he was ashamed and the man of God cried.

verses.name: II Kings 8:12
verses.text: Then Hazael asked, “Why <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my lord crying?” He said, “Because I know what evil you will do to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> You will <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞set their fortifications on fire⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “you will send their fortifications with the fire”</note> and you will kill their young men with the sword. Their little ones you will dash to pieces, and their pregnant women you will rip open!”

verses.name: II Kings 8:13
verses.text: Then Hazael said, “But how could your servant, who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> like a dog, do this great thing?” Elisha said, “Yahweh has shown me <transChange type="added">that</transChange> you <transChange type="added">are to be</transChange> king over Aram.”

verses.name: II Kings 8:14
verses.text: So he departed from Elisha and came to his master. He asked him, “What did Elisha say to you.” So he said, “He said to me that you will certainly recover.”

verses.name: II Kings 8:15
verses.text: On the next day, he took the bed cover, dipped <transChange type="added">it</transChange> in the water, and spread <transChange type="added">it</transChange> over his face so that he died. Then Hazael became king in his place.  <div eID="gen2832" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 8:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2090"/><title type="x-s">Joram Reigns in Judah</title> <div sID="gen2833" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2090"/>Now in the fifth year of Joram son of Ahab, king of Israel, and Jehoshaphat king of Judah, Joram son of Jehoshaphat became the king of Judah.<note placement="foot">This likely indicates a coregency in Judah at the time.</note>

verses.name: II Kings 8:17
verses.text: He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Kings 8:18
verses.text: He walked in the way of the kings of Israel as the house of Ahab had done, for the daughter of Ahab became his wife, and he did evil in the eyes of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Kings 8:19
verses.text: Yet Yahweh was not willing to destroy Judah, for the sake of David his servant, as he had promised to give him a lamp for his sons always.  <div eID="gen2833" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 8:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2091"/><div sID="gen2834" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2091"/>In his days, Edom rebelled <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞against the rule⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from under the hand”</note> of Judah, and they set up a king over them.

verses.name: II Kings 8:21
verses.text: So Joram crossed over to Zair and all the chariots with him. It happened that he arose <transChange type="added">by</transChange> night and attacked Edom who had surrounded him and the commanders of the chariots; but the army fled to their tents.

verses.name: II Kings 8:22
verses.text: So Edom has rebelled <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞against the rule⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from under the hand”</note> of Judah until this day; then Libnah <transChange type="added">also</transChange> rebelled at that time.

verses.name: II Kings 8:23
verses.text: The remainder of the acts of Joram and all that he did, <transChange type="added">are</transChange> they not written in the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Judah?

verses.name: II Kings 8:24
verses.text: So Joram slept with his ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and he was buried with his ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> in the city of David, and Ahaziah his son became king in place of him.  <div eID="gen2834" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 8:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2092"/><title type="x-s">Ahaziah Succeeds Joram in Judah</title> <div sID="gen2835" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2092"/>In the twelfth year of Joram the son of Ahab, king of Israel, Ahaziah the son of Joram became king of Judah.

verses.name: II Kings 8:26
verses.text: Ahaziah <transChange type="added">was</transChange> twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. The name of his mother <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Athaliah daughter of Omri, king of Israel.

verses.name: II Kings 8:27
verses.text: He walked in the way of the house of Ahab and did evil in the eyes of Yahweh, as the house of Ahab; for he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> the son-in-law of the house of Ahab.  <div eID="gen2835" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 8:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2093"/><div sID="gen2836" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2093"/>He went with Joram the son of Ahab for the battle against Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth-Gilead, and the Arameans wounded Joram.

verses.name: II Kings 8:29
verses.text: Joram the king returned to Jezreel to heal from the wounds which the Arameans had inflicted at Ramah when Hazael king of Aram fought him. Ahaziah the son of Joram, king of Judah, went down to see Joram the son of Ahab in Jezreel, for he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> ill.  <chapter eID="2Kgs.8"/>

verses.name: II Kings 9:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2094"/><title type="x-s">Jehu Anointed Prophetically to Rule in Place of Joram of Israel</title> <div sID="gen2837" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2094"/>Now Elisha the prophet called for one of the sons of the prophets, and he said to him, “Gird your loins, and take this flask of olive oil in your hand, and go to Ramoth-Gilead.

verses.name: II Kings 9:2
verses.text: Go there and look there for Jehu the son of Jehoshaphat the son of Nimshi. Go, for you must cause him to arise from among his brothers, and you must bring him into an <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞inner room⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “inner room of the inner room”</note>

verses.name: II Kings 9:3
verses.text: You must take the flask of olive oil and pour it out on his head. You must say, ‘Thus says Yahweh, “I hereby anoint you as king over Israel.” ’ Then you must open the door and flee; do not linger!”  <div eID="gen2837" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 9:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2095"/><div sID="gen2838" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2095"/>So the young man, servant of the prophet, went <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Ramoth-Gilead.

verses.name: II Kings 9:5
verses.text: He came, and look, the commanders of the army <transChange type="added">were</transChange> sitting <transChange type="added">there</transChange>. He said, “I have a word for you, O commander!” Jehu said, “For whom? For all of us?” And he said, “For you, O commander!”

verses.name: II Kings 9:6
verses.text: He got up and went to the house, and poured the olive oil on his head and said to him, “Thus says Yahweh, the God of Israel: ‘I hereby anoint you as king over the people of Yahweh, over Israel.

verses.name: II Kings 9:7
verses.text: You will destroy the house of Ahab your master, and you will avenge the blood of my servants the prophets and the blood of all of the servants of Yahweh, from the hand of Jezebel.

verses.name: II Kings 9:8
verses.text: All of the house of Ahab will perish, and I shall cut off <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞all males⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the one who urinates against a wall”</note> from Ahab, both bond and free.

verses.name: II Kings 9:9
verses.text: I will make the house of Ahab like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat and like the house of Baasha the son of Ahijah.

verses.name: II Kings 9:10
verses.text: The dogs will eat Jezebel in the territory of Jezreel, and there shall not be <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞anyone to bury her⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.’ ”<note placement="foot">Literally “burying”</note> Then he opened the door and fled.  <div eID="gen2838" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 9:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2096"/><title type="x-s">Jehu Assassinates Joram</title> <div sID="gen2839" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2096"/>Then Jehu came out to the officers of his master, and they said to him, “Peace? Why did this madman come to you?” And he said to them, “You know the man and his foolish talk.”

verses.name: II Kings 9:12
verses.text: Then they said, “Liar. Please tell us.” He said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Thus and so⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “As this and as this”</note> he said to me, saying, ‘Thus says Yahweh, “I hereby anoint you as king over Israel.” ’ ”

verses.name: II Kings 9:13
verses.text: So they hastened each one to take his cloak, and they spread <transChange type="added">them</transChange> under him on the bare steps, blew on the trumpet, and said, “Jehu is king!”  <div eID="gen2839" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 9:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2097"/><div sID="gen2840" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2097"/>So Jehu the son of Jehoshaphat the son of Nimshi conspired against Joram. Now Joram was keeping guard in Ramoth-Gilead, he and all of Israel, because of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞threat⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from the face/presence of”</note> of Hazael king of Aram.

verses.name: II Kings 9:15
verses.text: But Joram the king had returned to heal in Jezreel from the wound which the Arameans had inflicted on him when he fought with Hazael king of Aram. Jehu said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞If this is what you want⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “If there is your soul”</note> do not let him go out as a fugitive from the city to go to make it known in Jezreel.”

verses.name: II Kings 9:16
verses.text: Jehu mounted his chariot and went to Jezreel, for Joram <transChange type="added">was</transChange> lying there, and Ahaziah king of Judah had gone down to visit Joram.

verses.name: II Kings 9:17
verses.text: Now the watchman <transChange type="added">was</transChange> standing on the tower in Jezreel, and he saw the company of Jehu when he came, and he said, “I see a company.” Joram said, “Take a horseman and send <transChange type="added">him</transChange> to meet them.” And he said, “Is it peace?”

verses.name: II Kings 9:18
verses.text: So the rider of the horse went out to meet him, and he said, “Thus the king asks, ‘Is it peace?’ ” Then Jehu said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞What do you have to do with peace⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?<note placement="foot">Literally “What is for you and for peace”</note> Turn after me.” Then the watchman reported, saying, “The messenger went up to them, but he did not return.”

verses.name: II Kings 9:19
verses.text: Then he sent out a second horseman, and he came to them and said, “Thus the king asks, ‘Is it peace?’ ” Then Jehu said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞What do you have to do with peace⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?<note placement="foot">Literally “What is for you and for peace”</note> Turn after me.”

verses.name: II Kings 9:20
verses.text: So the sentinel reported, saying, “He went up to them, but he did not return, and the driving <transChange type="added">is</transChange> like the driving of Jehu the son of Nimshi, for he drives with madness.”  <div eID="gen2840" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 9:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2098"/><div sID="gen2841" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2098"/>Then Joram said, “Get ready,” so he got his chariot ready. Joram king of Israel went out, and Ahaziah king of Judah, each with his chariot. They went out to meet Jehu, and they found him at the tract of land of Naboth the Jezreelite.

verses.name: II Kings 9:22
verses.text: When Joram saw Jehu, he asked, “<transChange type="added">Is it</transChange> peace?” And he said, “What peace <transChange type="added">is there</transChange> while the prostitutions of your mother Jezebel and her sorceries are numerous?”

verses.name: II Kings 9:23
verses.text: Joram turned his <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞chariot⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “hand”</note> and fled and said to Ahaziah, “It’s treason, Ahaziah!”

verses.name: II Kings 9:24
verses.text: Then Jehu <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞drew his bow⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “filled his hand with the bow”</note> and shot Joram between his shoulders so that the arrow went out from his heart, and he slumped down in his chariot.

verses.name: II Kings 9:25
verses.text: He said to Bidkar his third <transChange type="added">servant</transChange>, “Lift <transChange type="added">him</transChange> out and throw him on the plot of the field of Naboth the Jezreelite, for remember, you and I <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with the pair <transChange type="added">of chariots</transChange> behind Ahab his father when Yahweh pronounced this oracle against him:

verses.name: II Kings 9:26
verses.text: ‘ “Since I saw the blood of Naboth and the blood of his children yesterday,” declares Yahweh, “I will requite it for you in this tract of land,” declares Yahweh.’ So then lift him out and throw him on the tract of land according to the word of Yahweh.”  <div eID="gen2841" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 9:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2099"/><title type="x-s">Jehu Orders the Assassination of Ahaziah</title> <div sID="gen2842" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2099"/>When Ahaziah king of Judah saw, he fled the way of Beth-Haggen. Jehu pursued after him and said, “Shoot him also, in the chariot.” <transChange type="added">They shot him</transChange> at the ascent of Gur which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in Ibleam, and he fled <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Megiddo, but he died there.

verses.name: II Kings 9:28
verses.text: Then his officers carried him to Jerusalem, and they buried him in his tomb with his ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> in the city of David.

verses.name: II Kings 9:29
verses.text: In the eleventh year of Joram the son of Ahab, Ahaziah had become king over Judah.  <div eID="gen2842" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 9:30
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2100"/><title type="x-s">Jezebel Loses Her High Position</title> <div sID="gen2843" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2100"/>When Jehu came to Jezreel, Jezebel heard <transChange type="added">of it</transChange>, so she painted her eyes with black eye paint and adorned her head and looked through the window.

verses.name: II Kings 9:31
verses.text: Now Jehu had come in the gate, so she said, “<transChange type="added">Is it</transChange> peace, O Zimri, murderer of his master?”

verses.name: II Kings 9:32
verses.text: When he lifted up his face to the window, he asked, “Who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> with me?” Two or three eunuchs looked down to him.

verses.name: II Kings 9:33
verses.text: So he said, “Throw her down.” So they threw her down, and her blood spattered on the wall and on the horses, and they trampled her.

verses.name: II Kings 9:34
verses.text: Then he came and ate and drank, and said, “Please take care of this cursed one and bury her, for she is the daughter of a king.”

verses.name: II Kings 9:35
verses.text: When they went to bury her, they could not find her, except the skull, the feet, and the palms of the hands.

verses.name: II Kings 9:36
verses.text: They returned and told him, and he said, “This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the word of Yahweh which he spoke by the hand of his servant Elijah the Tishbite, saying, ‘On the plot of ground of Jezreel, the dogs shall eat the flesh of Jezebel.’ ”

verses.name: II Kings 9:37
verses.text: So the dead body of Jezebel became dung on the surface <transChange type="added">spread</transChange> on the field in the plot of ground of Jezreel, so one cannot say, “This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> Jezebel.”  <chapter eID="2Kgs.9"/>

verses.name: II Kings 10:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2101"/><title type="x-s">Jehu Continues Purging the House of Ahab</title> <div sID="gen2844" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2101"/>Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria, and Jehu wrote letters, and he sent them to Samaria to the officials of Jezreel, to the elders and to the guardians of Ahab, saying,

verses.name: II Kings 10:2
verses.text: “Now, when this letter comes to you and your master’s sons <transChange type="added">are</transChange> with you, the chariots <transChange type="added">are</transChange> with you, the horses, a fortified city, and weapons,

verses.name: II Kings 10:3
verses.text: then you must select the best and the most suitable from the sons of your master, and you must place <transChange type="added">him</transChange> on the throne of his father, and they must fight for the house of your masters.”

verses.name: II Kings 10:4
verses.text: But they were very afraid, and they said, “Look, two kings could not stand before him; how can we stand?”

verses.name: II Kings 10:5
verses.text: So whoever was over the house, and whoever was over the city, and the elders and the guardians sent to Jehu, saying, “We <transChange type="added">are</transChange> your servants; all that you say to us, we shall do. We shall not make anyone a king. Do <transChange type="added">what</transChange> is good in your eyes.”  <div eID="gen2844" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 10:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2102"/><div sID="gen2845" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2102"/>Then he wrote to them a second letter, saying, “If you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> for me, and you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> listening to my voice, take the heads of the men of the sons of your master and come to me at <transChange type="added">this</transChange> time tomorrow at Jezreel.” Now the sons of the king, seventy men, <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with the leaders of the city who were raising them.

verses.name: II Kings 10:7
verses.text: When the letter came to them, they took the sons of the king, and they killed seventy men. Then they put their heads in baskets and sent them to him at Jezreel.

verses.name: II Kings 10:8
verses.text: Then the messenger came and told him, saying, “They have brought the heads of the king’s sons,” and he said, “Put them <transChange type="added">in</transChange> two piles <transChange type="added">at</transChange> the entrance of the gate until morning.”

verses.name: II Kings 10:9
verses.text: It happened in the morning that he went out, stood, and said to all of the people, “You <transChange type="added">are</transChange> righteous. Look, I conspired against my master and killed him. But who killed all of these?

verses.name: II Kings 10:10
verses.text: Know then that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the word of Yahweh will not fail⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “it shall not fall from the word of Yahweh to the ground”</note> which Yahweh spoke concerning the house of Ahab; Yahweh has done what he spoke by the hand of his servant Elijah.

verses.name: II Kings 10:11
verses.text: Then Jehu killed all of the remainder of the house of Ahab in Jezreel, all of his leaders, his close friends, and his priests, until there was no survivor left for him.  <div eID="gen2845" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 10:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2103"/><div sID="gen2846" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2103"/>Then he arose and went and came to Samaria. On the way, he was <transChange type="added">at</transChange> Beth-Eked of the shepherds,

verses.name: II Kings 10:13
verses.text: and Jehu met the brothers of Ahaziah king of Judah. He asked, “Who <transChange type="added">are</transChange> you?” They said, “We <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the brothers of Ahaziah; we came down for the peace of the king’s children and the children of the queen.”

verses.name: II Kings 10:14
verses.text: Then he said, “Seize them alive!” So they seized them alive but then slaughtered them at the cistern of Beth-Eked, forty-two men. He did not allow any of them to survive.  <div eID="gen2846" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 10:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2104"/><div sID="gen2847" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2104"/>Next he went from there and found Jehonadab the son of Recab to meet him. He greeted him and asked him, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Is your heart right with me as my heart is with you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?”<note placement="foot">Literally “Is there uprightness with your heart as that of my heart with your heart”</note> Then Jehonadab said, “Yes, it is. Give your hand!” And he gave his hand and took him up to him on the chariot.

verses.name: II Kings 10:16
verses.text: Then he said, “Come with me! Look at my zeal for Yahweh!” So he let him ride in his chariot.

verses.name: II Kings 10:17
verses.text: Then he came to Samaria and killed all who remained to Ahab in Samaria until he wiped them out according to the word of Yahweh which he had spoken to Elijah.  <div eID="gen2847" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 10:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2105"/><title type="x-s">Jehu Purges the Baal Worshipers</title> <div sID="gen2848" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2105"/>Then Jehu assembled all of the people and said to them, “Ahab served Baal a little, but Jehu will worship him greatly.

verses.name: II Kings 10:19
verses.text: So then, summon to me all of the prophets of Baal and all of his servants and his priests; no man should fail to come, for I have a great sacrifice for Baal. Anyone who fails to come shall not live!” Now Jehu was acting with cunning in order to destroy the servants of Baal.

verses.name: II Kings 10:20
verses.text: Then Jehu said, “Sanctify a <transChange type="added">solemn</transChange> assembly for Baal!” So they proclaimed <transChange type="added">it</transChange>.

verses.name: II Kings 10:21
verses.text: Jehu sent <transChange type="added">word</transChange> through all of Israel, and all of the servants of Baal came; there did not remain a man who did not come. They came to the house of Baal so that the house of Baal was filled from <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞wall to wall⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “edge to edge”</note>

verses.name: II Kings 10:22
verses.text: He said to the one who <transChange type="added">was</transChange> over the wardrobe, “Bring out clothing for all of the servants of Baal.” So he brought the clothing out for them.

verses.name: II Kings 10:23
verses.text: Then Jehu and Jehonadab the son of Recab came <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the temple of Baal, and he said to the servants of Baal, “Search and see that there is none of the servants of Yahweh here with you; only those who serve Baal.”

verses.name: II Kings 10:24
verses.text: They came to offer sacrifices and burnt offerings. Now Jehu had stationed for himself eighty men outside, and he said, “The man who lets <transChange type="added">anyone</transChange> escape from the men who I am <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞entrusting to you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “bringing upon your hand”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he will pay with his life⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!”<note placement="foot">Literally “his life in place of his life”</note>  <div eID="gen2848" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 10:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2106"/><div sID="gen2849" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2106"/>It happened that when he finished offering the burnt offering, Jehu said to the royal guard and to the officers, “Come and kill them; let no man go free!” So <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they put them to the sword⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “they struck them with the edge of the sword”</note> and the royal guard and the officers threw them out, then they went up to the citadel of the temple of Baal.

verses.name: II Kings 10:26
verses.text: They brought out the stone pillars of the temple of Baal and burned <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “it”</note>

verses.name: II Kings 10:27
verses.text: So they broke down the stone pillars of Baal and destroyed the temple of Baal and made it into a latrine until this day.

verses.name: II Kings 10:28
verses.text: So Jehu wiped out Baal from Israel.  <div eID="gen2849" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 10:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2107"/><div sID="gen2850" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2107"/>Only Jehu did not turn aside from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat <transChange type="added">by</transChange> which he caused Israel to sin; <transChange type="added">namely,</transChange> the calf-shaped idols of gold which <transChange type="added">were in</transChange> Bethel and Dan.

verses.name: II Kings 10:30
verses.text: Yahweh said to Jehu, “Because you have done well by doing right in my eyes and you have done to the house of Ahab according to all that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in my heart; <transChange type="added">therefore,</transChange> sons of the fourth generation will sit for you on the throne of Israel.”

verses.name: II Kings 10:31
verses.text: But Jehu was not careful to walk in the law of Yahweh God of Israel with all his heart; he did not turn from the sins of Jeroboam <transChange type="added">by</transChange> which he caused Israel to sin.  <div eID="gen2850" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 10:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2108"/><div sID="gen2851" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2108"/>In those days, Yahweh began to reduce Israel, so Hazael defeated them in every territory of Israel,

verses.name: II Kings 10:33
verses.text: from the Jordan eastward: all of the land of Gilead, the Gadites, the Reubenites, and the Manassites, from Aroer which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> on the Wadi Arnon and Gilead and Bashan.

verses.name: II Kings 10:34
verses.text: Now the remainder of the acts of Jehu and all that he did and all of his powerful <transChange type="added">deeds, are</transChange> they not written in the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Israel?

verses.name: II Kings 10:35
verses.text: So Jehu slept with his ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and they buried him in Samaria, and Jehoahaz his son became king in his place.

verses.name: II Kings 10:36
verses.text: Now the days which Jehu had reigned over Israel <transChange type="added">were</transChange> twenty-eight years in Samaria.  <chapter eID="2Kgs.10"/>

verses.name: II Kings 11:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2109"/><title type="x-s">Athaliah Usurps the Throne in Judah</title> <div sID="gen2852" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2109"/>Now Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, so she prepared to destroy all of the offspring of the royal family.

verses.name: II Kings 11:2
verses.text: But Jehosheba the daughter of King Joram and sister of Ahaziah took Jehoash the son of Ahaziah, and she stole him from among the sons of the king who were being put to death, <transChange type="added">putting</transChange> him and his nurse in the inner bedroom. So they hid him from the presence of Athaliah, and he was not killed.

verses.name: II Kings 11:3
verses.text: He remained with her in the temple of Yahweh, hidden for six years <transChange type="added">while</transChange> Athaliah was reigning over the land.  <div eID="gen2852" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 11:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2110"/><div sID="gen2853" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2110"/>But in the seventh year Jehoiada sent and took the commanders of the hundreds of the Carites and the runners, and he brought them to himself to the temple of Yahweh. Then he <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞made⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “cut”</note> a covenant with them and made them swear in the house of Yahweh and showed them the son of the king.

verses.name: II Kings 11:5
verses.text: He commanded them, saying, “This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the thing which you must do: one third of you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who go off duty on the Sabbath⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “who go on the Sabbath”</note> the keepers of the guard in the house of the king,

verses.name: II Kings 11:6
verses.text: and another third at the gate of Sur, and a third at the gate behind the runners, shall guard the post of the palace alternately.

verses.name: II Kings 11:7
verses.text: Two of the units among you, all <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who go on duty on the Sabbath⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the going out of the Sabbath”</note> guard the post of the temple of Yahweh for the king.

verses.name: II Kings 11:8
verses.text: You must surround the king all about, each with his weapon in his hand; whoever comes to the ranks must be killed. Be with the king <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞wherever he goes⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “when he goes out and when he comes”</note>  <div eID="gen2853" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 11:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2111"/><div sID="gen2854" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2111"/>So the commanders of hundreds did according to all that Jehoiada the priest commanded, and each took his men <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who went off duty on the Sabbath⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the coming of the Sabbath”</note> and those <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who came on duty on the Sabbath⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the going out of the Sabbath”</note> and they came to Jehoiada the priest.

verses.name: II Kings 11:10
verses.text: Then the priest gave to the commanders of the hundreds spears and small round shields which <transChange type="added">were</transChange> King David’s, which <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in the temple of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Kings 11:11
verses.text: So the royal runners stood, each <transChange type="added">with</transChange> his weapons in his hand, from the side of the temple to the south up to the side of the temple on the north, around the altar and around the temple, about the king all around.

verses.name: II Kings 11:12
verses.text: Then he brought out the son of the king, put the crown on him with the testimony, and they made him king, anointed him, clapped <transChange type="added">their</transChange> hands, and said, “<transChange type="added">Long</transChange> live the king!”  <div eID="gen2854" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 11:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2112"/><div sID="gen2855" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2112"/>When Athaliah heard the sound of the runners of the people, she came to the people at the temple of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Kings 11:14
verses.text: She looked, and there was the king standing by the pillar according to the custom. The commanders and the trumpeters <transChange type="added">were</transChange> by the king, and all of the people of the land were rejoicing and blowing on the trumpets. Athaliah tore her clothes and she called, “Treason, treason!”

verses.name: II Kings 11:15
verses.text: Then Jehoiada the priest commanded the commanders of the hundreds, the appointed of the army, and he said to them, “Bring her out to the house of the ranks! The one coming after her <transChange type="added">should</transChange> kill her with the sword,” for the priest had said, “Let her not be killed in the temple of Yahweh.”

verses.name: II Kings 11:16
verses.text: So <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they grabbed her⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “they put hands to her”</note> as she went <transChange type="added">by</transChange> the entranceway of the horses to the palace of the king, and she was killed there.

verses.name: II Kings 11:17
verses.text: Then Jehoiada <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞made⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “cut”</note> a covenant between Yahweh and the king and the people, that the people should be as a people for Yahweh, and <transChange type="added">also a covenant</transChange> between the king and the people.

verses.name: II Kings 11:18
