verses.text: Then all the people of the land went to the temple of Baal and tore it down, and its altars and its images they broke completely into pieces. Mattan the priest of Baal they killed in front of the altars. Then the priest put guards over the house of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Kings 11:19
verses.text: He took the commanders of the hundreds and the Carites and the runners and all the people of the land, and they brought the king down from the temple of Yahweh. And they marched by the way of the runner’s gate <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the palace of the king, and he sat on the throne of the kings.

verses.name: II Kings 11:20
verses.text: All the people of the land rejoiced, and the city rested; <transChange type="added">for</transChange> Athaliah had been killed with the sword in the palace of the king.  <div eID="gen2855" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 11:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2113"/><div sID="gen2856" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2113"/><note placement="foot">2 Kings 11:21–12:21 in the English Bible is 2 Kings 12:1–22 in the Hebrew Bible</note> Jehoash was <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞seven years old⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a son of seven years”</note> when he began to reign.  <chapter eID="2Kgs.11"/>

verses.name: II Kings 12:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2114"/><title type="x-s">Jehoash/Joash Reigns in Judah</title> <div sID="gen2857" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2114"/>In the seventh year of Jehu, Jehoash became king. He reigned in Jerusalem forty years, and the name of his mother <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Zibiah from Beersheba.

verses.name: II Kings 12:2
verses.text: Jehoash did right in the eyes of Yahweh all of his days, because Jehoiada the priest instructed him.

verses.name: II Kings 12:3
verses.text: Only the high places were not removed; the people <transChange type="added">were</transChange> still making sacrifices and offering incense on the high places.  <div eID="gen2857" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 12:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2115"/><title type="x-s">Temple Repairs Planned</title> <div sID="gen2858" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2115"/>Jehoash said to the priests, “All of the money for the sacred things that is brought to the temple of Yahweh, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the money taxed at its proper value for each person⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “money passing over a man, the money of persons his proper value”</note> <transChange type="added">and</transChange> all of the money which comes upon the heart of a man to bring to the temple of Yahweh,

verses.name: II Kings 12:5
verses.text: let the priests take for themselves, each from his treasurers, and let them repair the breach of the temple for every place where damage is found.”  <div eID="gen2858" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 12:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2116"/><div sID="gen2859" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2116"/>It happened in the twenty-third year of King Jehoash that the priests had not repaired the damage in the temple.

verses.name: II Kings 12:7
verses.text: So King Jehoash summoned Jehoiada the priest and the priests, and he said to them, “Why are you not repairing the damage in the temple? Now, you shall not take money from your treasurers for the damage in the temple. You must provide it.”

verses.name: II Kings 12:8
verses.text: So the priests agreed not to take money from the people and not to repair the damage to the temple.  <div eID="gen2859" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 12:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2117"/><div sID="gen2860" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2117"/>Then Jehoiada the priest took a certain chest and bored a hole in its lid, and he put it beside the altar to the right as a man enters into the temple of Yahweh; then the priests who were keepers of the threshold would put there all of the money brought into the temple.

verses.name: II Kings 12:10
verses.text: It happened that when they saw a great deal of money in the chest, the secretary of the king and the high priest would come up, put the money in bags, then count the money found in the temple of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Kings 12:11
verses.text: They placed the money, <transChange type="added">which was</transChange> weighed out, into the hands of the workers who were appointed over the temple of Yahweh, and they paid <transChange type="added">it to</transChange> the skilled craftsmen of wood and <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the builders working on the temple of Yahweh

verses.name: II Kings 12:12
verses.text: and to the masons and the stonecutters, to buy timber and stones for hewing, in order to repair the damage of the temple of Yahweh, and for all who went to the temple to repair it.

verses.name: II Kings 12:13
verses.text: Only, for the temple of Yahweh, there were not any silver basins, snuffers, bowls for drinking wine, trumpets, or any vessel of gold or silver from the money being brought <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the temple of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Kings 12:14
verses.text: For they gave that to all the workers, and they repaired the temple<note placement="foot">Or “house”</note> of Yahweh with it.

verses.name: II Kings 12:15
verses.text: They did not <transChange type="added">have to</transChange> settle accounts with the men into whose hands they placed the money to give to the workers, for they <transChange type="added">were</transChange> dealing honestly.

verses.name: II Kings 12:16
verses.text: <transChange type="added">The</transChange> money of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> guilt offering and <transChange type="added">the</transChange> money of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> sin offering was not brought into the temple<note placement="foot">Or “house”</note> of Yahweh, but were <transChange type="added">each</transChange> for the priests.  <div eID="gen2860" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 12:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2118"/><title type="x-s">Hazael Threatens Judah</title> <div sID="gen2861" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2118"/>At that time, Hazael king of Aram went up and fought against Gath and captured it; then Hazael set his face to go up against Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Kings 12:18
verses.text: Jehoash king of Judah took all of the holy objects that Jehoshaphat, Joram, and Ahaziah his ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> the kings of Judah, had devoted, and all his holy objects and all of the gold found in the treasuries of the temple of Yahweh, and <transChange type="added">in</transChange> the palace of the king, and he sent them to Hazael king of Aram, so that he went up from Jerusalem.  <div eID="gen2861" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 12:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2119"/><div sID="gen2862" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2119"/>Now the remainder of the acts of Joash and all that he did, are they not written in the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Judah?

verses.name: II Kings 12:20
verses.text: Then his servants arose and conspired and killed Joash <transChange type="added">in</transChange> the house of the Millo as he was going down toward Silla.

verses.name: II Kings 12:21
verses.text: Jozabad<note placement="foot">A number of Hebrew manuscripts read “Jozakar” here, a reading followed by many English versions. The Hebrew letters for K and B are very similar, as are the letters for R and D. Scribal error may account for the variant reading.</note> the son of Shimeath and Jehozabad the son of Shomer, his servants, struck him and killed him, so they buried him with his ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> in the city of David. Then Amaziah his son became king in his place.  <chapter eID="2Kgs.12"/>

verses.name: II Kings 13:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2120"/><title type="x-s">Jehoahaz and Jehoash in Israel</title> <div sID="gen2863" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2120"/>In the twenty-third year of Joash the son of Ahaziah, king of Judah, Jehoahaz the son of Jehu became king over Israel in Samaria, <transChange type="added">reigning</transChange> seventeen years.

verses.name: II Kings 13:2
verses.text: But he did evil in the eyes of Yahweh, and he went after the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat with which he had caused Israel to sin, and he did not depart from it.

verses.name: II Kings 13:3
verses.text: So the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞anger of Yahweh was kindled⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the nose of Yahweh became hot”</note> against Israel, and he gave them into the hand of Hazael king of Aram and into the hand of Ben-Hadad the son of Hazael <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞repeatedly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “all the days”</note>

verses.name: II Kings 13:4
verses.text: Then Jehoahaz entreated Yahweh, and Yahweh listened to him, for he saw the oppression of Israel, because the king of Aram oppressed them.

verses.name: II Kings 13:5
verses.text: Yahweh gave Israel a savior, and they went out from under the hand of Aram. So the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> lived in their tents as <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞formerly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “as yesterday and the day before”</note>

verses.name: II Kings 13:6
verses.text: Yet they did not depart from the sins of the house of Jeroboam which he caused Israel to sin, but walked in it; and also, the pole of the Asherah worship was <transChange type="added">still</transChange> standing in Samaria.

verses.name: II Kings 13:7
verses.text: For there was no army left over for Jehoahaz except for fifty horsemen, ten chariots, and ten thousand infantry, for the king of Aram had destroyed them and made them as the dust at threshing.

verses.name: II Kings 13:8
verses.text: Now the remainder of the acts of Jehoahaz and all that he did and his powerful <transChange type="added">deeds, are</transChange> they not written in the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Israel?

verses.name: II Kings 13:9
verses.text: Then Jehoahaz slept with his ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and they buried him in Samaria, and Jehoash his son became king in his place.  <div eID="gen2863" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 13:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2121"/><div sID="gen2864" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2121"/>In the thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah, Jehoash the son of Jehoahaz became king over Israel in Samaria, <transChange type="added">reigning</transChange> sixteen years.

verses.name: II Kings 13:11
verses.text: He did evil in the eyes of Yahweh; he did not depart from all of the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat which he caused Israel to sin, <transChange type="added">but</transChange> walked in it.

verses.name: II Kings 13:12
verses.text: The remainder of the acts of Joash<note placement="foot">That is, the king of Israel rather than the king of Judah; “Jehoash” and “Joash” are variant spellings of one another</note> and all that he did, his powerful <transChange type="added">deeds</transChange>, and how he fought with Amaziah king of Judah, <transChange type="added">are</transChange> they not written in the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Israel?

verses.name: II Kings 13:13
verses.text: Then Joash slept with his ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and Jeroboam sat on his throne. Joash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.  <div eID="gen2864" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 13:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2122"/><title type="x-s">Elisha Passes Away</title> <div sID="gen2865" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2122"/>Elisha became ill with the illness with which he would die, so Jehoash king of Israel went down to him and wept before him, and said, “My father, my father; the chariot of Israel and its horsemen!”

verses.name: II Kings 13:15
verses.text: Elisha said to him, “Take a bow and arrows,” so he took him a bow and arrows.

verses.name: II Kings 13:16
verses.text: He said to the king of Israel, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Lay your hand on the bow⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,”<note placement="foot">Literally “Let your hand climb upon the bow”</note> so he lay hold <transChange type="added">of it</transChange>; then Elisha put his hand on the hands of the king.

verses.name: II Kings 13:17
verses.text: Then he said, “Open the window to the east,” so he opened <transChange type="added">it</transChange>. Elisha said, “Shoot,” and he shot. Then he said, “An arrow of victory for Yahweh, and an arrow of victory against Aram; you shall fight the Arameans in Aphek until finishing <transChange type="added">them</transChange>.”

verses.name: II Kings 13:18
verses.text: Then he said, “Take the arrows,” so he took <transChange type="added">them</transChange>. He said to the king of Israel, “Strike the ground,” so he struck three times and stopped.

verses.name: II Kings 13:19
verses.text: <transChange type="added">Yet</transChange> the man of God became angry against him and said, “For striking five or six times, then you would have defeated Aram until finishing <transChange type="added">them</transChange>, but now you will defeat Aram <transChange type="added">only</transChange> three times.”  <div eID="gen2865" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 13:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2123"/><div sID="gen2866" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2123"/>Elisha died and they buried him. Now the raiding parties of Moab came <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in the spring⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “coming year”</note>

verses.name: II Kings 13:21
verses.text: And it happened that they <transChange type="added">were</transChange> burying a man; suddenly they saw the marauding band, so they threw the man in the grave of Elisha. <transChange type="added">As he</transChange> went <transChange type="added">in</transChange>, the man touched the bones of Elisha, and became alive and got up on his feet!  <div eID="gen2866" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 13:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2124"/><div sID="gen2867" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2124"/>Hazael king of Aram oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz.

verses.name: II Kings 13:23
verses.text: But Yahweh had mercy on them and showed compassion to them and turned to them because of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. He was not willing to destroy them nor cast them from his presence up to now.  <div eID="gen2867" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 13:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2125"/><div sID="gen2868" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2125"/>When Hazael king of Aram died, his son Ben-Hadad became king in his place.

verses.name: II Kings 13:25
verses.text: Jehoash the son of Jehoahaz returned and took the cities from the hand of Ben-Hadad the son of Hazael which he had taken from the hand of Jehoahaz his father in the war. Three times Jehoash defeated him and recovered the towns of Israel.  <chapter eID="2Kgs.13"/>

verses.name: II Kings 14:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2126"/><title type="x-s">Amaziah Reigns in Judah; Jeroboam II in Israel</title> <div sID="gen2869" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2126"/>In the second year of Jehoash the son of Jehoahaz king of Israel, Amaziah the son of Jehoash king of Judah began to reign.

verses.name: II Kings 14:2
verses.text: He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem; and the name of his mother <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Jehoaddin from Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Kings 14:3
verses.text: He did right in the eyes of Yahweh, only not as David his ancestor;<note placement="foot">Or “father”</note> as all which Jehoash his father had done, he did.

verses.name: II Kings 14:4
verses.text: Only the high places were not removed; the people <transChange type="added">were</transChange> still sacrificing and offering incense on the high places.  <div eID="gen2869" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 14:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2127"/><div sID="gen2870" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2127"/>It happened that when the kingdom was firmly in his hand, he killed his servants who had killed his father the king.

verses.name: II Kings 14:6
verses.text: But the sons of the killers he did not kill, as it is written in the scroll of the law of Moses which Yahweh had commanded, saying, “Fathers should not be killed because of children, and children should not be killed because of fathers; but a man should die because of his <transChange type="added">own</transChange> sin.”

verses.name: II Kings 14:7
verses.text: He also killed ten thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt, and he seized Sela in the battle, and he called its name Jokteel, until this day.  <div eID="gen2870" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 14:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2128"/><div sID="gen2871" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2128"/>Then Amaziah sent messengers to Jehoash the son of Jehoahaz the son of Jehu king of Israel, saying, “Come let us meet <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞face-to-face⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “faces”</note>

verses.name: II Kings 14:9
verses.text: So Jehoash the king of Israel sent to Amaziah, saying, “The thornbush which is in Lebanon sent to the cedar which is in Lebanon, saying, ‘Give your daughter to my son as wife,’ but an animal of the field which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in Lebanon passed by and trampled the thornbush.

verses.name: II Kings 14:10
verses.text: You have indeed defeated Edom and your heart is lifted up; enjoy the honor and stay home. Why should you provoke trouble so that you fall and Judah with you?”  <div eID="gen2871" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 14:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2129"/><div sID="gen2872" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2129"/>But Amaziah would not listen, so Jehoash king of Israel went up and they met face-to-face, he and Amaziah king of Judah, at Beth-Shemesh which belongs to Judah.

verses.name: II Kings 14:12
verses.text: Judah was defeated before Israel and they fled, each to this tent.

verses.name: II Kings 14:13
verses.text: Jehoash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, the son of Jehoash, the son of Ahaziah, at Beth-Shemesh. Then they came <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Jerusalem, and he broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the Gate of Ephraim up to the Corner Gate, four hundred cubits!

verses.name: II Kings 14:14
verses.text: He also took all of the gold and silver and all the vessels found <transChange type="added">in</transChange> the temple of Yahweh and in the treasury rooms of the palace of the king, as well as the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞hostages⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “sons of the pledges”</note> then he returned to Samaria.  <div eID="gen2872" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 14:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2130"/><div sID="gen2873" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2130"/>Now the remainder of the acts of Jehoash which he did, and his powerful <transChange type="added">deeds</transChange>, and how he fought with Amaziah king of Judah, <transChange type="added">are</transChange> they not written on the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Israel?

verses.name: II Kings 14:16
verses.text: Then Jehoash slept with his ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel, and Jeroboam his son reigned in his place.  <div eID="gen2873" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 14:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2131"/><title type="x-s">Azariah Succeeds Amaziah in Jerusalem; Zechariah Succeeds Jeroboam II in Samaria</title> <div sID="gen2874" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2131"/>Amaziah the son of Jehoash king of Judah lived fifteen years after the death of Jehoash the son of Jehoahaz king of Israel.

verses.name: II Kings 14:18
verses.text: The remainder of the acts of Amaziah, <transChange type="added">are</transChange> they not written on the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Judah?

verses.name: II Kings 14:19
verses.text: They conspired against him in Jerusalem, so he fled to Lachish. But they sent <transChange type="added">men</transChange> after him to Lachish, and they killed him there.

verses.name: II Kings 14:20
verses.text: Then they carried him on the horses, and he was buried with his ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> in the city of David.

verses.name: II Kings 14:21
verses.text: All of the people of Judah took sixteen-year-old Azariah and made him king in place of this father Amaziah.

verses.name: II Kings 14:22
verses.text: He rebuilt Elath and restored it to Judah after the king slept with his ancestors.<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note>  <div eID="gen2874" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 14:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2132"/><div sID="gen2875" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2132"/>In the fifteenth year of Amaziah the son of Jehoash king of Judah, Jeroboam the son of Jehoash king of Israel began to reign in Samaria, <transChange type="added">reigning</transChange> forty-one years.

verses.name: II Kings 14:24
verses.text: But he did evil in the eyes of Yahweh; he did not depart from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat which he caused Israel to sin.

verses.name: II Kings 14:25
verses.text: He restored the boundary of Israel from Lebo-Hamath up to the sea of the Arabah, according to the word of Yahweh which he spoke by the hand of his servant Jonah the son of Amittai the prophet, who was from Gath-Hepher.

verses.name: II Kings 14:26
verses.text: For Yahweh saw that the misery of Israel was very bitter, whether bond or free, but there was no helper for Israel.

verses.name: II Kings 14:27
verses.text: Yahweh did not decree to blot out the name of Israel from under the heavens, so he saved them by the hand of Jeroboam the son of Jehoash.  <div eID="gen2875" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 14:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2133"/><div sID="gen2876" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2133"/>Now the remainder of the acts of Jeroboam, all that he did, his powerful <transChange type="added">deeds</transChange>, how he fought, and how he restored Damascus and Hamath of Judah to Israel, <transChange type="added">are</transChange> they not written on the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Israel?

verses.name: II Kings 14:29
verses.text: So Jeroboam slept with his ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> the kings of Israel, and his son Zechariah became king in his place.  <chapter eID="2Kgs.14"/>

verses.name: II Kings 15:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2134"/><title type="x-s">The Acts of Azariah (Uzziah) in Judah</title> <div sID="gen2877" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2134"/>In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Azariah the son of Amaziah king of Judah began to reign.

verses.name: II Kings 15:2
verses.text: He was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem. The name of his mother <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Jecoliah of Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Kings 15:3
verses.text: He did right in the eyes of Yahweh, according to all that Amaziah his father had done.

verses.name: II Kings 15:4
verses.text: Only he did not remove the high places; the people <transChange type="added">were</transChange> still sacrificing and burning incense on the high places.

verses.name: II Kings 15:5
verses.text: Yahweh struck the king, and he was infected with a skin disease until the day of his death. He lived in a separate house, <transChange type="added">while</transChange> Jotham the son of the king <transChange type="added">was</transChange> over the house, governing the people of the land.

verses.name: II Kings 15:6
verses.text: The remainder of the acts of Azariah, and all that he did, <transChange type="added">are</transChange> they not written on the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Judah?

verses.name: II Kings 15:7
verses.text: So Azariah slept with his ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and they buried him with his ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> in the city of David, and Jotham his son became king in his place.  <div eID="gen2877" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 15:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2135"/><title type="x-s">Zechariah in Israel</title> <div sID="gen2878" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2135"/>In the thirty-eighth year of Azariah king of Judah, Zechariah the son of Jeroboam reigned over Israel in Samaria for six months.

verses.name: II Kings 15:9
verses.text: He did evil in the eyes of Yahweh as his ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> had done. He did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat which he caused Israel to sin.

verses.name: II Kings 15:10
verses.text: Shallum the son of Jabesh conspired against him, struck him in front of the people, killed him, and reigned in his place.

verses.name: II Kings 15:11
verses.text: Now the remainder of the acts of Zechariah, look, they are written on the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Israel.

verses.name: II Kings 15:12
verses.text: This is the word of Yahweh which he spoke to Jehu, saying, “Sons of a fourth <transChange type="added">generation</transChange> shall sit for you on the throne of Israel,” and it was so.  <div eID="gen2878" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 15:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2136"/><title type="x-s">Shallum Reigns only a Month in Israel</title> <div sID="gen2879" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2136"/>Shallum the son of Jabesh began to reign in the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah king of Judah, and he reigned <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a full month⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a month of days”</note> in Samaria.

verses.name: II Kings 15:14
verses.text: Then Menahem the son of Gadi came up from Tirzah, and he came <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Samaria and struck down Shallum the son of Jabesh in Samaria and killed him. Then he became king in place of him.

verses.name: II Kings 15:15
verses.text: Now the remainder of the acts of Shallum, and his conspiracy which he conspired; look, they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> written on the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Israel.

verses.name: II Kings 15:16
verses.text: At that time Menahem destroyed Tiphsah, all who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in it, and all its territory from Tirzah, because <transChange type="added">it</transChange> had not opened <transChange type="added">to him</transChange>, so he destroyed it and ripped open all of its pregnant women.  <div eID="gen2879" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 15:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2137"/><title type="x-s">Menahem Reigns in Israel</title> <div sID="gen2880" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2137"/>In the thirty-ninth year of Azariah king of Judah, Menahem the son of Gadi began to reign over Israel <transChange type="added">for</transChange> ten years in Samaria.

verses.name: II Kings 15:18
verses.text: But he did evil in the eyes of Yahweh. He did not depart all of his days from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat which he caused Israel to sin.  <div eID="gen2880" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 15:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2138"/><div sID="gen2881" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2138"/>Pul the king of Assyria came against the land, so Menahem gave a thousand talents of silver to Pul so that his hand would be with him <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to strengthen his hold on the kingdom⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “to strengthen the kingship in his hand”</note>

verses.name: II Kings 15:20
verses.text: Menahem exacted the money from Israel, from all <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the very rich⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the mighty of the wealth”</note> to give to the king of Assyria fifty shekels of silver for each one. Then the king of Assyria returned and did not stay there in the land.

verses.name: II Kings 15:21
verses.text: Now the rest of the acts of Menahem, and all that he did, <transChange type="added">are</transChange> they not written in the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Israel?

verses.name: II Kings 15:22
verses.text: So Menahem slept with his ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and Pekahiah his son became king in his place.  <div eID="gen2881" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 15:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2139"/><title type="x-s">Pekahiah Reigns in Israel</title> <div sID="gen2882" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2139"/>In the fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekahiah the son of Menahem began to reign over Israel in Samaria <transChange type="added">for</transChange> two years.

verses.name: II Kings 15:24
verses.text: But he did evil in the eyes of Yahweh. He did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat which he caused Israel to sin.

verses.name: II Kings 15:25
verses.text: Pekah the son of Remaliah, his captain, conspired against him, so he attacked him in Samaria in the citadel fortress of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> palace of the king, with Argob and Arieh. With him <transChange type="added">also were</transChange> fifty men from the children of the Gileadites, and he killed him and became king in his place.

verses.name: II Kings 15:26
verses.text: Now the remainder of the acts of Pekahiah and all that he did, look, they are written in the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Israel.  <div eID="gen2882" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 15:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2140"/><title type="x-s">Pekah Reigns in Israel</title> <div sID="gen2883" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2140"/>In the fifty-second year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekah the son of Remaliah began to reign over Israel in Samaria <transChange type="added">for</transChange> twenty years.

verses.name: II Kings 15:28
verses.text: He did evil in the eyes of Yahweh. He did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat which he caused Israel to sin.  <div eID="gen2883" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 15:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2141"/><div sID="gen2884" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2141"/>In the days of Pekah king of Israel, Tiglath-Pileser the king of Assyria came and took Ijon, Abel-Beth-Maacah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, the Gilead, the Galilee, and all the land of Naphtali; then he deported them to Assyria.

verses.name: II Kings 15:30
verses.text: Hoshea the son of Elah conspired against Pekah the son of Remaliah, and he attacked and killed him. He reigned in place of him in the twentieth year of Jotham the son of Uzziah.

verses.name: II Kings 15:31
verses.text: Now the remainder of the acts of Pekah and all that he did, look, they are written in the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Israel.  <div eID="gen2884" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 15:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2142"/><title type="x-s">Jotham Reigns in Judah</title> <div sID="gen2885" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2142"/>In the second year of Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, Jotham the son of Uzziah king of Judah began to reign.

verses.name: II Kings 15:33
verses.text: He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother was Jerusha the daughter of Zadok.

verses.name: II Kings 15:34
verses.text: He did what was right in the eyes of Yahweh, according to all that Uzziah his father had done.

verses.name: II Kings 15:35
verses.text: Only the high places were not removed; the people still <transChange type="added">were</transChange> sacrificing and offering incense on the high places. He built the upper gate of the temple of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Kings 15:36
verses.text: Now the remainder of the acts of Jotham which he did, <transChange type="added">are</transChange> they not written on the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Judah?

verses.name: II Kings 15:37
verses.text: (Now, in those days, Yahweh began to send Rezin the king of Aram and Pekah the son of Remaliah against Judah.)

verses.name: II Kings 15:38
verses.text: So Jotham slept with his ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and was buried with his ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> in the city of David his ancestor,<note placement="foot">Or “father”</note> and his son Ahaz became king in his place.  <chapter eID="2Kgs.15"/>

verses.name: II Kings 16:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2143"/><title type="x-s">Ahaz Reigns in Judah and Seeks Help against the Assyrians</title> <div sID="gen2886" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2143"/>In the seventeenth year of Pekah the son of Remaliah, Ahaz the son of Jotham king of Judah began to reign.

verses.name: II Kings 16:2
verses.text: Ahaz was twenty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. He did not do right in the eyes of Yahweh his God as David his ancestor.<note placement="foot">Or “father”</note>

verses.name: II Kings 16:3
verses.text: He walked in the way of the kings of Israel; he even let his son pass through the fire according to the detestable things of the nations which Yahweh drove out from before the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note>

verses.name: II Kings 16:4
verses.text: He sacrificed and offered incense on the high places, on the hills, and under every green tree.

verses.name: II Kings 16:5
verses.text: Then Rezin the king of Aram went up <transChange type="added">with</transChange> Pekah the son of Remaliah king of Israel against Jerusalem for battle, and they besieged Ahaz but were not able to <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞defeat⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “fight”</note> him.

verses.name: II Kings 16:6
verses.text: At that time, Rezin king of Aram recovered Elath for Aram and drove out the Judeans from Elath. The Arameans came to Elath and have lived there until this day.  <div eID="gen2886" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 16:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2144"/><div sID="gen2887" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2144"/>Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-Pileser king of Assyria, saying, “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> your servant and your son. Come up and rescue me from the hand of the king of Aram and from the hand of the king of Israel who are rising up against me.”

verses.name: II Kings 16:8
verses.text: Ahaz took the silver and gold found in the house of Yahweh and in the treasury rooms of the palace of the king, and he sent a gift to the king of Assyria.

verses.name: II Kings 16:9
verses.text: So the king of Assyria listened to him and he went up to Damascus and captured it and deported them to Kir. He also killed Rezin.  <div eID="gen2887" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 16:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2145"/><title type="x-s">Damascus Falls to the Assyrians</title> <div sID="gen2888" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2145"/>So King Ahaz went to meet Tiglath-Pileser the king of Assyria <transChange type="added">in</transChange> Damascus, and he saw the altar which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in Damascus, so King Ahaz sent to Uriah the priest the builder’s plan of the altar and the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞exact model of how it had been made⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “and its model according to all its work”</note>

verses.name: II Kings 16:11
verses.text: So Uriah the priest built the altar according to all that King Ahaz had sent from Damascus; thus Uriah the priest did before King Ahaz came from Damascus.

verses.name: II Kings 16:12
verses.text: When the king came from Damascus, the king saw the altar, so he went near to the altar and went up on it.

verses.name: II Kings 16:13
verses.text: Then he offered his burnt offerings and his grain offerings, he poured his libations and dashed the blood of his fellowship offerings against the altar.

verses.name: II Kings 16:14
verses.text: Now the bronze altar which was before Yahweh, he brought over from the front of the temple, from between <transChange type="added">his</transChange> altar and the temple of Yahweh, and he placed it at the side of <transChange type="added">his</transChange> altar to the north.

verses.name: II Kings 16:15
verses.text: Then King Ahaz commanded Uriah the priest, saying, “On the great altar burn the morning burnt offering and the grain offering of the evening, the burnt offering of the king and his grain offering, the burnt offering of all of the people of the land, their offerings, their libations, and all of the blood of the burnt offerings, the blood of the sacrifices you must dash on it. But the bronze altar shall be for me to inquire <transChange type="added">by</transChange>.”

verses.name: II Kings 16:16
verses.text: So Uriah the priest did according to all that King Ahaz commanded.

verses.name: II Kings 16:17
verses.text: Then King Ahaz cut off the side panels of the water carts and removed from upon them the basin, and the sea he took down from the bronze oxen that were under it and put it on a stone base.

verses.name: II Kings 16:18
verses.text: The covering for the Sabbath which they had built in the palace and in the entrance of the king to the outside, he removed <transChange type="added">from</transChange> the temple of Yahweh because of the presence of the king of Assyria.

verses.name: II Kings 16:19
verses.text: Now the remainder of the acts of Ahaz which he did, <transChange type="added">are</transChange> they not written in the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Judah?

verses.name: II Kings 16:20
verses.text: So Ahaz slept with his ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and was buried with his ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> in the city of David, and Hezekiah his son reigned in his place.  <chapter eID="2Kgs.16"/>

verses.name: II Kings 17:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2146"/><title type="x-s">Hoshea Reigns in Israel</title> <div sID="gen2889" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2146"/>In the twelfth year of Ahaz the king of Judah, Hoshea the son of Elah began to reign over Israel in Samaria, <transChange type="added">reigning</transChange> nine years.

verses.name: II Kings 17:2
verses.text: He did evil in the eyes of Yahweh, only not as the kings of Israel who were before him.

verses.name: II Kings 17:3
verses.text: Shalmaneser the king of Assyria<note placement="foot">This would have been Shalmaneser V of Assyria (ruled ca. 727–722 <sc>bc</sc>)</note> came up against him, and Hoshea became his vassal and paid tribute to him.

verses.name: II Kings 17:4
verses.text: But the king of Assyria found treachery in Hoshea, for he had sent messengers to So king of Egypt, and he did not offer tribute to the king of Assyria as <transChange type="added">he had</transChange> year after year; so the king of Assyria arrested him, and confined him <transChange type="added">in</transChange> a house of imprisonment.

verses.name: II Kings 17:5
verses.text: So the king of Assyria went up in all the land, then he went up <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Samaria and besieged it <transChange type="added">for</transChange> three years.  <div eID="gen2889" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 17:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2147"/><title type="x-s">Israel Deported to Assyria and the Reasons It Fell</title> <div sID="gen2890" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2147"/>In the ninth year of Hoshea, the king of Assyria captured Samaria and deported Israel to Assyria. He placed them in Halah, in Habor, <transChange type="added">in</transChange> the river <transChange type="added">regions</transChange> of Gozan, and <transChange type="added">in</transChange> the cities of the Medes.

verses.name: II Kings 17:7
verses.text: Now <transChange type="added">this</transChange> happened because the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> had sinned against Yahweh their God when he brought them up from the land of Egypt from under the hand of Pharaoh the king of Egypt and they feared other gods.

verses.name: II Kings 17:8
verses.text: They walked in the statutes of the nations whom Yahweh had driven out from before the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> which the kings of Israel had introduced.

verses.name: II Kings 17:9
verses.text: The <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> secretly did things which <transChange type="added">were</transChange> not right, against Yahweh their God; they built high places for themselves in all their towns, from the watchtower up to the fortified city.

verses.name: II Kings 17:10
verses.text: They set up for themselves stone pillars and poles of Asherah worship on every high hill and under every green tree.

verses.name: II Kings 17:11
verses.text: They burned incense there on all the high places, like the nations which Yahweh deported before them, and they did evil things to provoke Yahweh.

verses.name: II Kings 17:12
verses.text: They served idols which Yahweh had said to them, “You shall not do this thing!”

verses.name: II Kings 17:13
verses.text: Yahweh warned Israel and Judah by the hand of his every prophet, <transChange type="added">with</transChange> every seer saying, “Turn from all of your evil ways, and keep my commandments and my ordinances, according to all the law which I commanded your ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> which I sent to you by the hand of my servants the prophets.”

verses.name: II Kings 17:14
verses.text: But they did not listen and they stiffened their necks, like the necks of their ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers</note> who did not believe in Yahweh their God.

verses.name: II Kings 17:15
verses.text: They rejected his statutes, his covenant which he <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞made⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “cut”</note> with their ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and his warnings which he gave to them; and they went after the idols, became vain, and <transChange type="added">went</transChange> after all the nations which <transChange type="added">were</transChange> all around them, which Yahweh had commanded them not to do as they <transChange type="added">did</transChange>.

verses.name: II Kings 17:16
verses.text: They abandoned all the commands of Yahweh their God and made for themselves two molten calf-shaped idols; they made a pole of Asherah worship and bowed down to the army of the heavens and served Baal.

verses.name: II Kings 17:17
verses.text: They made their sons and their daughters pass through the fire, they practiced divination and read omens, and they sold themselves to do evil in the eyes of Yahweh to provoke him.

verses.name: II Kings 17:18
verses.text: So Yahweh was very angry with Israel and he removed them from his presence; none remained except the tribe of Judah alone.  <div eID="gen2890" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 17:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2148"/><div sID="gen2891" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2148"/>Even Judah did not keep the commands of Yahweh their God, and they walked in the customs of Israel which they introduced,

verses.name: II Kings 17:20
verses.text: so Yahweh rejected all the offspring of Israel and punished them, and he gave them into the hand of the plunderers until he banished them from his presence.

verses.name: II Kings 17:21
verses.text: For he had torn Israel from the house of David, and they made Jeroboam the son of Nebat king, but Jeroboam detached Israel from following Yahweh, and he made them sin a great sin.

verses.name: II Kings 17:22
verses.text: The <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> walked in all the sins of Jeroboam which he committed, and they did not depart from it,

verses.name: II Kings 17:23
verses.text: until Yahweh removed Israel from his presence as he had foretold by the hand of all his servants, the prophets. And so he deported Israel from upon his land to Assyria until this day.  <div eID="gen2891" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 17:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2149"/><title type="x-s">Israel Repopulated with Foreign Captives</title> <div sID="gen2892" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2149"/>The king of Assyria brought from Babylonia, from Cush, from Arva, from Hamath, and Sepharvaim, and he settled <transChange type="added">them</transChange> in the cities of Samaria in place of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> so they took possession of Samaria and lived in her cities.

verses.name: II Kings 17:25
verses.text: It happened that when they began living there, they did not fear Yahweh, so Yahweh sent lions among them, and they were killing them.<note placement="foot">Leviticus 26:22 warns that non-belief will result in attacks from wild animals.</note>

verses.name: II Kings 17:26
verses.text: So they said to the king of Assyria, “The nations whom you deported and settled in the cities of Samaria do not know the customs of the God of the land, so he sent lions among them, and now they are killing them because they do not know the customs of the God of the land.”

verses.name: II Kings 17:27
verses.text: Then the king of Assyria commanded, saying, “Release one of the priests whom you deported from there, and let him go and settle there. Let him teach them the customs of the God of the land.”

verses.name: II Kings 17:28
verses.text: So one of the priests went, whom they had deported from Samaria, and he settled in Bethel and was teaching them how they should fear Yahweh.  <div eID="gen2892" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 17:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2150"/><div sID="gen2893" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2150"/>Yet every nation was making their<note placement="foot">Hebrew “his”</note> gods, and they put them in the shrine of the high places that the Samaritans had made, every nation in their cities in which they <transChange type="added">were</transChange> living.

verses.name: II Kings 17:30
verses.text: The men of Babylonia made Succoth Benoth; the men of Cush made Nergal; the men of Hamath made Ashima.

verses.name: II Kings 17:31
verses.text: The Arvites made Nibhaz and Tartak; the Sepharvites were burning their children in the fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech the gods of Sepharvaim.

verses.name: II Kings 17:32
verses.text: Those who were fearing Yahweh made priests of the high places <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from among themselves⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “for them from their ends”</note> and they were sacrificing for them in the shrines of the high places.

verses.name: II Kings 17:33
verses.text: Yahweh they were fearing, but their gods they were serving, according to the customs of the nations from which they were deported.  <div eID="gen2893" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 17:34
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2151"/><div sID="gen2894" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2151"/>Until this day they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> doing according to their former customs; none of them <transChange type="added">are</transChange> fearing Yahweh, and none of them <transChange type="added">are</transChange> doing according to their statutes, to their decisions, to the law, or to the commands that Yahweh commanded the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Jacob <transChange type="added">to</transChange> which he had given the name Israel.

verses.name: II Kings 17:35
verses.text: Yahweh had <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞made⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “cut”</note> a covenant with them and commanded them, “You shall not fear other gods, nor shall you bow down to them, nor shall you serve them, nor shall you sacrifice to them.

verses.name: II Kings 17:36
verses.text: Rather, Yahweh, who brought you out from the land of Egypt with great strength and with an outstretched arm—him you shall fear, and to him you shall bow down, and to him you shall sacrifice.

verses.name: II Kings 17:37
verses.text: The statutes, the decisions, the law, and the commands that he wrote to you, you shall observe to do always, and you shall not fear other gods.

verses.name: II Kings 17:38
verses.text: The covenant that I have <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞made⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “cut”</note> with you, you shall not forget, and you shall not fear other gods.

verses.name: II Kings 17:39
verses.text: But Yahweh your God you shall fear, and he will deliver you from the hand of all of your enemies.”

verses.name: II Kings 17:40
verses.text: They did not listen but kept on doing according to their former customs.

verses.name: II Kings 17:41
verses.text: So these nations were fearing Yahweh, but they were serving their idols, as were their children and their children’s children; as their ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> did, they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> doing until this day.  <chapter eID="2Kgs.17"/>

verses.name: II Kings 18:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2152"/><title type="x-s">Hezekiah Reigns in Judah</title> <div sID="gen2895" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2152"/>It happened in the third year of Hoshea the son of Elah king of Israel, that Hezekiah the son of Ahaz king of Judah became king.

verses.name: II Kings 18:2
verses.text: He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. The name of his mother was Abi, the daughter of Zechariah.

verses.name: II Kings 18:3
verses.text: He did right in the eyes of Yahweh according to all that David his ancestor<note placement="foot">Or “father”</note> had done.

verses.name: II Kings 18:4
verses.text: He removed the high places, and he smashed the stone pillars; he cut down the poles of Asherah worship and demolished the bronze serpent which Moses had made, for up to those days the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> were offering incense to it and called it Nehushtan.

verses.name: II Kings 18:5
verses.text: He trusted in Yahweh the God of Israel; there was no one like him, before or after, among all the kings of Judah.

verses.name: II Kings 18:6
verses.text: He held on to Yahweh; he did not depart from following him, and he kept his commands that Yahweh had commanded Moses.

verses.name: II Kings 18:7
verses.text: Yahweh was with him; everywhere he went, he succeeded. He rebelled against the king of Assyria and did not serve him.

verses.name: II Kings 18:8
verses.text: He attacked <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Philistines up to Gaza and its territory from the watchtower up to the fortified city.  <div eID="gen2895" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 18:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2153"/><div sID="gen2896" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2153"/>It happened in the fourth year of King Hezekiah, that <transChange type="added">is,</transChange> the seventh year of Hoshea the son of Elah king of Israel, Shalmaneser king of Assyria came against Samaria and laid siege against her.

verses.name: II Kings 18:10
verses.text: At the end of three years, he captured it in the sixth year of Hezekiah, that <transChange type="added">is,</transChange> the ninth year of Hoshea king of Israel; Samaria was captured.

verses.name: II Kings 18:11
verses.text: Then the king of Assyria deported Israel to Assyria and settled them in Halah, in Habor, <transChange type="added">in</transChange> the river <transChange type="added">regions</transChange> of Gozan, and <transChange type="added">in</transChange> the cities of the Medes,

verses.name: II Kings 18:12
verses.text: because they did not listen to the voice of Yahweh their God, and they transgressed his covenant; all that he had commanded Moses, the servant of Yahweh, they did not listen <transChange type="added">to</transChange> nor did they obey.  <div eID="gen2896" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 18:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2154"/><title type="x-s">Sennacherib of Assyria Invades Judah</title> <div sID="gen2897" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2154"/>In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against all of the fortified cities of Judah and captured them.

verses.name: II Kings 18:14
verses.text: So Hezekiah king of Judah sent <transChange type="added">word</transChange> to the king of Assyria at Lachish, saying, “I have done wrong. Withdraw from me. What you impose on me I will bear.” So the king of Assyria imposed on Hezekiah king of Judah three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.

verses.name: II Kings 18:15
verses.text: Then Hezekiah gave all of the silver found <transChange type="added">in</transChange> the temple of Yahweh and in the storerooms of the house of the king.

verses.name: II Kings 18:16
verses.text: At that time, Hezekiah cut off the doors of the temple of Yahweh and the doorposts which Hezekiah king of Judah had overlaid, and he gave them to the king of Assyria.

verses.name: II Kings 18:17
verses.text: So the king of Assyria sent the commander in chief, the chief eunuch, and the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞chief advisor⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Traditionally “Rabshekah”</note> from Lachish to King Hezekiah at Jerusalem with a heavy army. They went up and came to Jerusalem, then they went up and came and stood at the aqueduct of the upper pool which is on the main road of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞washer’s⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Or “fuller’s”</note> field.

verses.name: II Kings 18:18
verses.text: Then they called to the king, so Eliakim the son of Hilkiah who <transChange type="added">was</transChange> over the palace, Shebna the secretary, and Joah the son of Asaph the recorder, came out to them.  <div eID="gen2897" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 18:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2155"/><title type="x-s">Assyrians Advise against Trust in Yahweh</title> <div sID="gen2898" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2155"/>Then the chief advisor said to them, “Please say to Hezekiah: ‘Thus says the great king, the king of Assyria: “What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> this confidence that you trust?

verses.name: II Kings 18:20
verses.text: You think only a word of lips, ‘<transChange type="added">I have</transChange> advice and power for the war.’ Now, on whom do you trust that you have rebelled against me?

verses.name: II Kings 18:21
verses.text: Now, look! You <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞rely⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “trust for yourself”</note> on the staff of this broken reed, on Egypt, which <transChange type="added">when</transChange> a man leans on it, it goes into his hand and pierces it! So <transChange type="added">is</transChange> Pharaoh the king of Egypt for all who are trusting on him!

verses.name: II Kings 18:22
verses.text: But if you say to me, ‘On Yahweh our God we trust,’ <transChange type="added">is</transChange> it not he whose high places and altars Hezekiah removed, and he had said to Judah and to Jerusalem, ‘In the presence of this altar you shall bow down <transChange type="added">only</transChange> in Jerusalem?’

verses.name: II Kings 18:23
verses.text: So then, please make a wager with my lord, with the king of Assyria, and I will give to you a thousand horses <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞if you are able on your part to put riders on them.⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “if you are able to give for yourself riders upon them”</note>

verses.name: II Kings 18:24
verses.text: How <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞can you repulse a single captain among the least of the servants of my master⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “can you return the face of the governor one of the servants of my master”</note>? <transChange type="added">Yet</transChange> you rely for yourself on Egypt for chariots and horsemen!

verses.name: II Kings 18:25
verses.text: Have I now come up against this place without Yahweh to destroy it? Yahweh has said to me, ‘Go up against this land and destroy it!’ ” ’ ”  <div eID="gen2898" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 18:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2156"/><div sID="gen2899" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2156"/>Then Eliakim the son of Hilkiah and Shebna and Joah said to the chief commander, “Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, for we <transChange type="added">are</transChange> understanding, but you must not speak Judean with us in the ears of the people who <transChange type="added">are</transChange> on the wall.”

verses.name: II Kings 18:27
verses.text: The chief commander said to them, “Is it <transChange type="added">solely</transChange> to your master and to you my master has sent me to speak these words? <transChange type="added">Is</transChange> it not for the men who sit on the wall to eat their feces and to drink their urine with you?”  <div eID="gen2899" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 18:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2157"/><div sID="gen2900" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2157"/>Then the chief commander stood and called with a great voice in Judean, and he spoke and said, “Hear the word of the king, the great king of Assyria!

verses.name: II Kings 18:29
verses.text: Thus says the king, ‘Do not let Hezekiah deceive you, for he will not be able to rescue you from my<note placement="foot">Hebrew “his”</note> hand.

verses.name: II Kings 18:30
verses.text: Do not let Hezekiah <transChange type="added">make you</transChange> trust in Yahweh, saying, “Certainly Yahweh will rescue us, and this city shall not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria!” ’

verses.name: II Kings 18:31
verses.text: Do not listen to Hezekiah; for thus says the king of Assyria, ‘Make with me a treaty of peace and come out to me that each <transChange type="added">may</transChange> eat <transChange type="added">from</transChange> his vine and each <transChange type="added">from</transChange> his fig tree, and each <transChange type="added">may</transChange> drink water <transChange type="added">from</transChange> his cistern!

verses.name: II Kings 18:32
verses.text: Until I come and take you to a land like your land, a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards, a land of olive trees, olive oil, and honey, that <transChange type="added">you may</transChange> live and not die! You must not listen to Hezekiah, for he has misled you <transChange type="added">by</transChange> saying, “Yahweh will deliver us!”

verses.name: II Kings 18:33
verses.text: Did the gods of each of the nations ever rescue the land from the hand of the king of Assyria?

verses.name: II Kings 18:34
verses.text: Where <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah? For did they rescue Samaria from my hand?

verses.name: II Kings 18:35
verses.text: Who among all of the gods of the countries have rescued their countries from my hand that Yahweh should rescue Jerusalem from my hand?’ ”  <div eID="gen2900" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 18:36
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2158"/><div sID="gen2901" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2158"/>The people were silent, and they did not answer him a word, for the command of that king was saying, “You shall not answer him.”

verses.name: II Kings 18:37
verses.text: Eliakim the son of Hilkiah who was over the palace, and Shebna the secretary, and Joah the son of Asaph the recorder came to Hezekiah <transChange type="added">with</transChange> torn clothes, and they told him the words of the chief commander.  <chapter eID="2Kgs.18"/>

verses.name: II Kings 19:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2159"/><title type="x-s">Isaiah Sends Encouragement to Hezekiah</title> <div sID="gen2902" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2159"/>It happened that when King Hezekiah heard, he tore his clothes and covered himself with sackcloth and went <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the temple of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Kings 19:2
verses.text: He sent Eliakim who <transChange type="added">was</transChange> over the palace, Shebna the secretary, the elders, and the priests, <transChange type="added">all</transChange> clothed in sackcloth, to Isaiah the prophet the son of Amoz.

verses.name: II Kings 19:3
verses.text: They said to him, “Thus says Hezekiah, ‘A day of distress, rebuke, and disgrace is this day, for the children <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞are about to be born⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “came up to the outer vagina”</note> but there is no strength to bear them.

verses.name: II Kings 19:4
verses.text: Perhaps Yahweh your God will hear all of the words of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> chief commander whom his master the king of Assyria has sent to insult <transChange type="added">the</transChange> living God, and he will rebuke the words which Yahweh your God has heard. Therefore lift up a prayer for the remainder who are left.’ ”

verses.name: II Kings 19:5
verses.text: So the servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah,

verses.name: II Kings 19:6
verses.text: and Isaiah said to them, “Thus you must say to your master, ‘Thus says Yahweh, “You must not be afraid because the face of the words which you have heard, <transChange type="added">with</transChange> which the servants of the king of Assyria have reviled me.

verses.name: II Kings 19:7
verses.text: Look, I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> putting in him a spirit. He will hear a rumor and return to his land. Then I will cause him to fall by the sword in his land.” ’ ”  <div eID="gen2902" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 19:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2160"/><title type="x-s">The Assyrians Defy God</title> <div sID="gen2903" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2160"/>When <transChange type="added">the</transChange> chief commander returned, he found the king of Assyria fighting against Libnah, for he had heard that he had departed from Lachish.

verses.name: II Kings 19:9
verses.text: He heard about Tirhakah, the king of Cush, saying, “Look, he has set out to fight with you,” so he again sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying,

verses.name: II Kings 19:10
verses.text: “Thus you shall say to Hezekiah the king of Judah, ‘Let not your God whom you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> trusting deceive you, by his saying, “Jerusalem shall not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria!”

verses.name: II Kings 19:11
verses.text: Look, you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the lands, by utterly destroying them, and shall you be delivered?

verses.name: II Kings 19:12
verses.text: Did the gods of the nations that my <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞predecessors⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “fathers”</note> destroyed deliver them? <transChange type="added">Not</transChange> Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, <transChange type="added">nor</transChange> the children of Eden who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in Tel Assar.

verses.name: II Kings 19:13
verses.text: Where are the king of Hamath, the king of Arpad, the king of the city of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah?’ ”  <div eID="gen2903" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 19:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2161"/><title type="x-s">Hezekiah Prays to Yahweh</title> <div sID="gen2904" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2161"/>Hezekiah took the letters from the hand of the messengers and read them. <transChange type="added">Then</transChange> he went up to the temple of Yahweh, and Hezekiah spread them out before the presence of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Kings 19:15
verses.text: Then Hezekiah prayed before the face of Yahweh and said, “O Yahweh, God of Israel who lives <transChange type="added">above</transChange> the cherubim. You <transChange type="added">are</transChange> God, you alone, of all the kingdoms of the world; you have made the heavens and the earth.

verses.name: II Kings 19:16
verses.text: Incline your ears and hear; open, O Yahweh, your eyes and see and hear the words of Sennacherib which he has sent to insult the living God.

verses.name: II Kings 19:17
verses.text: Truly, O Yahweh, the kings of Assyria have utterly destroyed the nations and their land.

verses.name: II Kings 19:18
verses.text: He has hurled their gods in the fire because they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> not gods, but the work of the hands of a human <transChange type="added">made of</transChange> wood and stone, so they destroyed them.

verses.name: II Kings 19:19
verses.text: So then, O Yahweh our God, rescue us, please, from his hand, that all of the kingdoms of the earth may know that you, O Yahweh, you alone are God!”  <div eID="gen2904" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 19:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2162"/><title type="x-s">Isaiah Brings a Prophetic Response</title> <div sID="gen2905" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2162"/>Then Isaiah the son of Amoz sent to Hezekiah, saying, “Thus says Yahweh the God of Israel, ‘What you have prayed to me about Sennacherib king of Assyria I have heard.

verses.name: II Kings 19:21
verses.text: This is the word that Yahweh has spoken concerning him: <div eID="gen2905" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen2906"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2907"/>She despises you, she scorns you,<l eID="gen2907" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2908"/>the virgin daughter of Zion.<l eID="gen2908" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2909"/>Behind you the daughter of Jerusalem<l eID="gen2909" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2910"/>shakes <transChange type="added">her</transChange> head. <l eID="gen2910" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Kings 19:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2163"/><l level="1" sID="gen2911"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2163"/>Whom have you mocked and reviled?<l eID="gen2911" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2912"/>And against whom have you have raised <transChange type="added">your</transChange> voice<l eID="gen2912" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2913"/>and have haughtily lifted your eyes?<l eID="gen2913" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2914"/>Against the Holy One of Israel! <l eID="gen2914" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Kings 19:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2164"/><l level="1" sID="gen2915"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2164"/>By the hand of your messengers you have mocked the Lord,<l eID="gen2915" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2916"/>and you have said,<l eID="gen2916" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2917"/>‘With my many chariots I have gone up<l eID="gen2917" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2918"/><transChange type="added">to</transChange> the height of the mountains.<l eID="gen2918" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2919"/><transChange type="added">To</transChange> the remote areas of Lebanon,<l eID="gen2919" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2920"/>I have felled the tallest of its cedars,<l eID="gen2920" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2921"/>the choicest of its cypresses.<l eID="gen2921" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2922"/>I have entered the place of overnight lodging.<l eID="gen2922" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2923"/>Even <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the edge of forest of its fertile land. <l eID="gen2923" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Kings 19:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2165"/><l level="1" sID="gen2924"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2165"/>I dug <transChange type="added">wells</transChange> and I drank foreign water,<l eID="gen2924" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2925"/>and I dried up with the sole of my steps<l eID="gen2925" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2926"/>all the canals of Egypt.’ <l eID="gen2926" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Kings 19:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2166"/><l level="1" sID="gen2927"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2166"/>Have you not heard?<l eID="gen2927" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2928"/>From long ago I have determined it,<l eID="gen2928" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2929"/>from the days of old I have planned it,<l eID="gen2929" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2930"/>and now I am bringing it to pass.<l eID="gen2930" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2931"/>It shall be turned into a pile of rocks;<l eID="gen2931" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2932"/>fortified cities are ruined. <l eID="gen2932" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Kings 19:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2167"/><l level="1" sID="gen2933"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2167"/>Their inhabitants, short of hand, shall be dismayed;<l eID="gen2933" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2934"/>and they shall be ashamed.<l eID="gen2934" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2935"/>They have become green plants of the open field,<l eID="gen2935" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2936"/>and tender grass,<l eID="gen2936" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2937"/>green grass of the roof<l eID="gen2937" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2938"/>and blight before the standing grain. <l eID="gen2938" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Kings 19:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2168"/><l level="1" sID="gen2939"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2168"/>Your sitting, your going out, and your coming <transChange type="added">in</transChange> I know,<l eID="gen2939" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2940"/>and your raging against me. <l eID="gen2940" level="2"/>

verses.name: II Kings 19:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2169"/><l level="1" sID="gen2941"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2169"/>Because you are raging against me,<l eID="gen2941" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2942"/>and your arrogance has come up in my ears,<l eID="gen2942" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2943"/>I will put my nose ring in your nose<l eID="gen2943" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2944"/>and my bridle in your mouth.<l eID="gen2944" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen2945"/>And I will turn you back<l eID="gen2945" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen2946"/>on the way that you have come. <l eID="gen2946" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen2906"/>

verses.name: II Kings 19:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2170"/><div sID="gen2947" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2170"/>“ ‘This will be the sign for you: Eat the volunteer plants for the year, and in the second year, the volunteer plants that spring up from that. But <transChange type="added">in</transChange> the third year, sow and reap, plant vineyards and eat their fruit.

verses.name: II Kings 19:30
verses.text: The remainder of the house of Judah which survives will again <transChange type="added">take</transChange> root below and bear fruit above.

verses.name: II Kings 19:31
verses.text: For from Jerusalem a remnant shall go out and survivors from Mount Zion; the zeal of Yahweh will do this.  <div eID="gen2947" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 19:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2171"/><div sID="gen2948" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2171"/>“ ‘Therefore thus says Yahweh to the king of Assyria, “He shall not come to this city, nor shall he shoot an arrow there, nor shall he bring a small shield near her, nor shall he cast a siege ramp against her.

verses.name: II Kings 19:33
verses.text: By the way that he came to her he shall return; but to this city, he shall not come,” declares Yahweh.

verses.name: II Kings 19:34
verses.text: And I will defend this city to save her for my sake and for the sake of David my servant.’ ”  <div eID="gen2948" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 19:35
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2172"/><title type="x-s">An Angel Neutralizes the Assyrian Army</title> <div sID="gen2949" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2172"/>It happened in that night that an angel of Yahweh went out, and he struck down one hundred and eighty-five thousand in the camp of Assyria. When they got up early in the morning, look! All of them <transChange type="added">were</transChange> dead corpses.

verses.name: II Kings 19:36
verses.text: Then Sennacherib king of Assyria set out and went and returned and lived in Nineveh.

verses.name: II Kings 19:37
verses.text: It happened that he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> worshiping in the temple of Nisroch his god, and Adrammelech and Sharezer<note placement="foot">So <hi type="italic">Kethib</hi>; <hi type="italic">Qere</hi> adds “his sons”</note> struck him with the sword. Then they escaped <transChange type="added">into</transChange> the land of Ararat, and Esarhaddon his son became king in his place.  <chapter eID="2Kgs.19"/>

verses.name: II Kings 20:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2173"/><title type="x-s">Hezekiah Loses Health and Regains It through Prayer</title> <div sID="gen2950" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2173"/>In those days Hezekiah became <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞deathly ill⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “ill to die”</note> and Isaiah the son of Amoz the prophet came to him and said to him, “Thus says Yahweh, ‘Command your house, for you <transChange type="added">are about</transChange> to die; you will not recover.’ ”

verses.name: II Kings 20:2
verses.text: Then he turned his face to the wall and prayed to Yahweh, saying,

verses.name: II Kings 20:3
verses.text: “O Yahweh, please remember how I went about before you in faithfulness and with a whole heart, and <transChange type="added">remember</transChange> the good that I have done in your eyes.” Then Hezekiah <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞wept bitterly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “wept a great weeping”</note>

verses.name: II Kings 20:4
verses.text: Isaiah had not gone out from the middle of the city when the word of Yahweh came to him, saying,

verses.name: II Kings 20:5
verses.text: “Return; you must say to Hezekiah, the leader of my people, ‘Thus says Yahweh the God of David your ancestor,<note placement="foot">Or “father”</note> “I have heard your prayer and I have seen your tears. Look, I <transChange type="added">am about to</transChange> heal you. On the third day you shall go up <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the temple of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Kings 20:6
verses.text: I will add to your days fifteen years, and from the hand of the king of Assyria I will deliver you and this city. I will defend this city for my sake and for the sake of David my servant.” ’ ”

verses.name: II Kings 20:7
verses.text: Then Isaiah said, “Bring a lump of figs,” so they took and put it on the skin sores, and he lived.  <div eID="gen2950" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 20:8
