verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2174"/><div sID="gen2951" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2174"/>Hezekiah said to Isaiah, “What is the sign that Yahweh will heal me that I shall go up on the third day <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the temple of Yahweh?”

verses.name: II Kings 20:9
verses.text: Isaiah said, “This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the sign for you from Yahweh that Yahweh will do the thing that he has promised: Shall the shadow advance ten steps or shall it return ten steps?”

verses.name: II Kings 20:10
verses.text: Hezekiah answered, “It is easy for the shadow to lengthen ten steps. No, but let the shadow return backwards ten steps.”

verses.name: II Kings 20:11
verses.text: Isaiah the prophet called to Yahweh, and he brought back the shadow on the steps where it had gone down on the steps of Ahaz, backwards ten steps.  <div eID="gen2951" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 20:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2175"/><title type="x-s">Hezekiah Reveals Too Much to a Babylonian Envoy</title> <div sID="gen2952" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2175"/>At that time, Berodak-Baladan the son of Baladan king of <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Babylon⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Or “Babel.” Babel was the ancient name for Babylon, the capital of Babylonia. See also Genesis 11:9</note> sent letters and a gift to Hezekiah, for he had heard that Hezekiah had been ill.

verses.name: II Kings 20:13
verses.text: Hezekiah heard about them and showed them all of the house of his treasure, both the silver and the gold, the spices, the good olive oil, the room of his weapons, and all that could be found in his treasuries. There was nothing that he did not show them in his palace and in all of his kingdom.

verses.name: II Kings 20:14
verses.text: Then Isaiah the prophet came to King Hezekiah and said to him, “What did these men say, and from where have they come to you?” Hezekiah said, “From a far land; they have come from Babylon.”

verses.name: II Kings 20:15
verses.text: Then he asked, “What did they see in your palace?” And Hezekiah said, “All that is in my palace they have seen; there is nothing that I did not show them in my treasuries.”  <div eID="gen2952" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 20:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2176"/><div sID="gen2953" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2176"/>Then Isaiah said to Hezekiah, “Hear the word of Yahweh!

verses.name: II Kings 20:17
verses.text: ‘Look, days <transChange type="added">are</transChange> coming when all that is in your palace will be carried off; <transChange type="added">even</transChange> all that your ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> have stored up until this day, to Babylon; nothing shall be left,’ says Yahweh.

verses.name: II Kings 20:18
verses.text: ‘Your sons who went out from you, whom you brought forth, will be taken, and they shall be eunuchs in the temple of the king of Babylon.’ ”

verses.name: II Kings 20:19
verses.text: Then Hezekiah said to Isaiah, “The word of Yahweh which you have spoken <transChange type="added">is</transChange> good,” and he thought, “Is it not that peace and security shall be in my days?”

verses.name: II Kings 20:20
verses.text: Now the remainder of the acts of Hezekiah, all of his powerful <transChange type="added">deeds</transChange>, and how he made the pool and the conduit and brought the water into the city, are they not written in the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Judah?

verses.name: II Kings 20:21
verses.text: Then Hezekiah slept with his ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and Manasseh his son became king in his place.  <chapter eID="2Kgs.20"/>

verses.name: II Kings 21:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2177"/><title type="x-s">Evil Manasseh Reigns after Godly Hezekiah</title> <div sID="gen2954" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2177"/>Manasseh was twelve years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem. The name of his mother <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Hephzibah.

verses.name: II Kings 21:2
verses.text: He did evil in the eyes of Yahweh, according to the detestable things of the nations that Yahweh had driven out from the presence of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note>

verses.name: II Kings 21:3
verses.text: He returned and rebuilt the high places which Hezekiah his father had destroyed. He erected altars for Baal and made a pole of Asherah worship just as Ahab king of Israel had made, and he bowed down to all of the host of heaven and served them.

verses.name: II Kings 21:4
verses.text: He built altars in the temple of Yahweh <transChange type="added">about</transChange> which Yahweh had said, “I will put my name in Jerusalem.”

verses.name: II Kings 21:5
verses.text: He built an altar to all of the host of heaven in the two courtyards of the temple of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Kings 21:6
verses.text: He made his son pass through the fire, practiced soothsaying and divination, and dealt with mediums and spiritists. He increased the doing of evil in the eyes of Yahweh to provoke him.

verses.name: II Kings 21:7
verses.text: He put the image of the Asherah that he had made in the temple which Yahweh had said to David and to Solomon his son, “In this temple and in Jerusalem which I have chosen from all of the tribes of Israel, I will put my name forever.

verses.name: II Kings 21:8
verses.text: I will not again make the feet of Israel wander from the land which I have given to their ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> if they only observe to do according to all that I have commanded them, as far as the law that Moses my servant commanded them.”

verses.name: II Kings 21:9
verses.text: But Manasseh did not listen and tempted them to do evil more than the nations that Yahweh destroyed before the presence of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note>  <div eID="gen2954" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 21:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2178"/><title type="x-s">Yahweh Sends a Rebuke to Manasseh</title> <div sID="gen2955" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2178"/>So Yahweh spoke by the hand of his servants the prophets, saying,

verses.name: II Kings 21:11
verses.text: “Because Manasseh the king of Judah committed these detestable things <transChange type="added">and</transChange> did evil more than the Amorites did who were before him and caused even Judah to sin with his idols,

verses.name: II Kings 21:12
verses.text: therefore, thus says Yahweh the God of Israel, ‘Look, I am bringing disaster upon Jerusalem and Judah about which the two ears of all who hear it will tingle.

verses.name: II Kings 21:13
verses.text: I will stretch out over Jerusalem the measuring line of Samaria and the plumb line of the house of Ahab, and I will wipe Jerusalem as one wipes the dish; he wipes it and turns it on its face.

verses.name: II Kings 21:14
verses.text: I will give up the remainder of my inheritance, and I will give them into the hand of their enemies. They shall become as prey and as spoil for all their enemies,

verses.name: II Kings 21:15
verses.text: because they have done evil in my eyes and were provoking me from the day that their ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> came out from Egypt up to this day.’ ”  <div eID="gen2955" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 21:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2179"/><div sID="gen2956" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2179"/>Moreover, Manasseh shed very much innocent blood until he filled Jerusalem <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from one end to another⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “end to end”</note> apart from his sin which he caused Judah to sin by doing evil in the eyes of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Kings 21:17
verses.text: The remainder of the acts of Manasseh and all that he did and his sin that he committed, <transChange type="added">are</transChange> they not written on the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Judah?

verses.name: II Kings 21:18
verses.text: Then Manasseh slept with his ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and was buried in the garden of his palace, in the garden of Uzza. Amon his son became king in his place.  <div eID="gen2956" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 21:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2180"/><title type="x-s">Amon Reigns in Judah Only Two Years</title> <div sID="gen2957" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2180"/>Amon was twenty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem. The name of his mother <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Meshullemeth the daughter of Haruz from Jotbah.

verses.name: II Kings 21:20
verses.text: He did evil in the eyes of Yahweh as Manasseh his father had done.

verses.name: II Kings 21:21
verses.text: He walked in all of the way which his father had walked, and he served the idols which his father had served and bowed down to them.

verses.name: II Kings 21:22
verses.text: He abandoned Yahweh the God of his ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and did not walk in the way of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Kings 21:23
verses.text: The servants of Amon conspired against him and killed the king in his palace.

verses.name: II Kings 21:24
verses.text: But the people of the land killed all who conspired against the king and made Josiah his son king in his place.

verses.name: II Kings 21:25
verses.text: The remainder of the acts of Amon that he did, <transChange type="added">are</transChange> they not written on the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Judah?

verses.name: II Kings 21:26
verses.text: They buried him in his tomb in the garden of Uzza, and Josiah his son became king in place of him.  <chapter eID="2Kgs.21"/>

verses.name: II Kings 22:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2181"/><title type="x-s">Josiah Becomes King in Judah</title> <div sID="gen2958" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2181"/>Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem. The name of his mother <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Jedidah the daughter of Adaiah from Bozkath.

verses.name: II Kings 22:2
verses.text: He did right in the eyes of Yahweh, and he walked in all of the way of David his ancestor<note placement="foot">Or “father”</note> and did not turn aside to the right or to the left.  <div eID="gen2958" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 22:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2182"/><div sID="gen2959" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2182"/>It happened in the eighteenth year of King Josiah, the king sent <transChange type="added">word to</transChange> Shaphan the son of Azaliah the son of Meshullam, the secretary of the temple of Yahweh, saying,

verses.name: II Kings 22:4
verses.text: “Go up to Hilkiah the high priest, and let them count the money being brought to the temple of Yahweh which the keepers of the threshold have collected from the people,

verses.name: II Kings 22:5
verses.text: and let them give it into the hand of those appointed doers of the work at the temple of Yahweh. Let them give it to the doers of the work who <transChange type="added">are</transChange> at the temple of Yahweh to repair the breach of the temple:

verses.name: II Kings 22:6
verses.text: to the skilled craftsmen, to the builders, to the masons, and to buy timber and hewing stones to repair the temple.

verses.name: II Kings 22:7
verses.text: Only the money being given to them is not to be accounted for by them, for they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> dealing with honesty.”  <div eID="gen2959" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 22:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2183"/><title type="x-s">A Scroll of the Torah Discovered in the Temple</title> <div sID="gen2960" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2183"/>Then Hilkiah the high priest said to Shaphan the secretary, “I have found the scroll of the Torah in the temple of Yahweh,” and Hilkiah gave the scroll to Shaphan and he read it.

verses.name: II Kings 22:9
verses.text: Shaphan the secretary came to the king and returned the king a word, and he said, “Your servant poured out the money found in the temple, and they have given it into the hand of the doers of the work appointed <transChange type="added">over</transChange> the temple of Yahweh.”

verses.name: II Kings 22:10
verses.text: Then Shaphan the secretary informed the king saying, “Hilkiah the priest has given me a scroll.” Then Shaphan read before the king.  <div eID="gen2960" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 22:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2184"/><div sID="gen2961" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2184"/>When the king heard the words of the scroll of the Torah, he tore his clothes.

verses.name: II Kings 22:12
verses.text: Then the king commanded Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam the son of Shaphan, Acbor the son of Micaiah, Shaphan the secretary, and Asaiah the servant of the king, saying,

verses.name: II Kings 22:13
verses.text: “Go, inquire of Yahweh for me and for the people and for all of Judah concerning the words of this scroll <transChange type="added">that was</transChange> found. For the wrath of Yahweh that is kindled against us <transChange type="added">is</transChange> great because our ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> did not listen to the words of this scroll to do according to all that is written concerning us!”  <div eID="gen2961" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 22:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2185"/><title type="x-s">The Prophetess Huldah Predicts Doom for Judah</title> <div sID="gen2962" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2185"/>So Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam, Acbor, Shaphan, and Asaiah went to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum the son of Tikvah the son of Harhas, the keeper of the robes. Now she <transChange type="added">was</transChange> living in Jerusalem in the second district. Then they spoke to her,

verses.name: II Kings 22:15
verses.text: and she said to them, “Thus says Yahweh the God of Israel, ‘Say to the man who sent you to me,

verses.name: II Kings 22:16
verses.text: “Thus says Yahweh, ‘Look I am bringing evil to this place and upon its inhabitants, <transChange type="added">according to</transChange> all of the words of that scroll that the king of Judah has read

verses.name: II Kings 22:17
verses.text: because they have abandoned me and they have burned incense to other gods, provoking me to anger with all of the works of their hands. My wrath shall be kindled against this place and not be quenched.’ ”

verses.name: II Kings 22:18
verses.text: And to the king of Judah who sent all of you to inquire of Yahweh, thus you shall say to him, “Thus says Yahweh the God of Israel, ‘<transChange type="added">Concerning</transChange> the words that you have heard,

verses.name: II Kings 22:19
verses.text: because you have a responsive heart, and you humbled yourself before Yahweh when you heard how I spoke against this place and against its inhabitants to become a desolation and a curse, and you have torn your clothes and wept before my face, I have also heard, declares Yahweh.

verses.name: II Kings 22:20
verses.text: Therefore look, I am gathering you to your ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and you shall be gathered to your tombs in peace. Your eyes will not see all of the disaster that I am bringing onto this place.’ ” ’ ” Then they <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞reported the word⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “they returned a word”</note> to the king.  <chapter eID="2Kgs.22"/>

verses.name: II Kings 23:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2186"/><title type="x-s">Josiah’s Covenantal Reforms</title> <div sID="gen2963" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2186"/>So the king sent <transChange type="added">word</transChange>, and all of the elders of Judah and Jerusalem gathered to him.

verses.name: II Kings 23:2
verses.text: Then the king went up <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the temple of Yahweh, and all of the men of Judah and all of the inhabitants of Jerusalem <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him, <transChange type="added">including</transChange> the priests, the prophets, and all of the people from smallest to greatest; and in their <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞hearing⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “ears”</note> he read all of the words of the scroll of the covenant that had been found in the temple of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Kings 23:3
verses.text: Then the king stood by the pillar, and he <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞made⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “cut”</note> a covenant before Yahweh, to go after Yahweh and to keep his commands and his warnings and his statutes, with all of his heart and with his all of his soul, to keep the words of this covenant written on this scroll. Then all of the people <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞joined⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “stood”</note> in the covenant.  <div eID="gen2963" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 23:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2187"/><div sID="gen2964" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2187"/>Then the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞king⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">That is, Josiah</note> commanded Hilkiah the high priest, the second priests, and the keepers of the threshold, to bring out of the temple of Yahweh all of the objects made for Baal and for the Asherah and for all the host of heaven, and he burned them outside of Jerusalem in the fields of the Kidron, and then he carried their ashes to Bethel.

verses.name: II Kings 23:5
verses.text: He removed the priests whom the kings of Judah had ordained <transChange type="added">to</transChange> burn incense on the high places at the cities of Judah and around Jerusalem and who offered incense to, to the sun, to the moon, to the constellations, and to all the host of heaven.

verses.name: II Kings 23:6
verses.text: He brought out the Asherah image from the temple of Yahweh outside of Jerusalem to the Wadi of the Kidron and burnt it <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞there⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “at the wadi of the Kidron”</note> then he pulverized <transChange type="added">it</transChange> to dust and threw its dust upon the tombs of the children of the people.

verses.name: II Kings 23:7
verses.text: He tore down the shrines of the male shrine prostitutes which were in the temple of Yahweh, where the women were weaving shrines for the Asherah.

verses.name: II Kings 23:8
verses.text: Then he brought all of the priests from the cities of Judah and defiled the high places where the priests from Geba up to Beersheba burned incense. He tore down the high places of the gates which were at the entrance of the gate of Joshua, the governor of the city, which were on the left of each gate of the city.

verses.name: II Kings 23:9
verses.text: However, the priests of the high places did not come up to the altar of Yahweh in Jerusalem, but they ate unleavened bread in the midst of their relatives.

verses.name: II Kings 23:10
verses.text: He defiled the Topheth which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in the Valley of Ben-Hinnom, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to prevent⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “so that not”</note> anyone causing his sons or his daughters to pass through the fire for Molech.

verses.name: II Kings 23:11
verses.text: He kept the horses that the kings of Judah had dedicated to the sun from coming to the temple of Yawheh at the side room of Nathan-Melech the eunuch, which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in the court; and the chariots of the sun he burned with fire.

verses.name: II Kings 23:12
verses.text: The altars which <transChange type="added">were</transChange> on the roof of the upper room of Ahaz, which the kings of Judah had made, and the altars which Manasseh had made in the two courtyards of the temple of Yahweh, the king tore down and ran from there and threw their ashes into the Wadi Kidron.

verses.name: II Kings 23:13
verses.text: The high places which <transChange type="added">were</transChange> east of Jerusalem, which <transChange type="added">were</transChange> on the south of the Mountain of Destruction which Solomon king of Israel had built for Ashtoreth the abomination of the Sidonians and for Chemosh the abomination of Moab and for Molech the detestable thing of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> the king defiled.

verses.name: II Kings 23:14
verses.text: He also broke into pieces the stone pillars and cut down the Asherah poles and covered their sites <transChange type="added">with</transChange> human bones.  <div eID="gen2964" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 23:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2188"/><div sID="gen2965" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2188"/>Moreover, the altar which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in Bethel, the high place which Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who had caused Israel to sin, had built, even that altar and the high place, <transChange type="added">Josiah</transChange> tore down. Then he burned down the high place and crushed <transChange type="added">the</transChange> pole of Asherah worship to dust and burned it with fire.

verses.name: II Kings 23:16
verses.text: When Josiah turned and saw the tombs which <transChange type="added">were</transChange> there on the hill, he sent and took the bones from the tombs and burned <transChange type="added">them</transChange> on the altar. <transChange type="added">Thus</transChange> he defiled them according to the word of Yahweh that the man of God had proclaimed who had proclaimed these things.

verses.name: II Kings 23:17
verses.text: Then he said, “What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> this gravestone that I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> seeing?” The men of the city said to him, “<transChange type="added">This is the</transChange> tomb of the man of God who came from Judah and proclaimed these things which you have done against the altar of Bethel.”

verses.name: II Kings 23:18
verses.text: So Josiah said, “Let him rest and let no man move his bones.” So they left his bones undisturbed with the bones of the prophet who had come from Samaria.

verses.name: II Kings 23:19
verses.text: Moreover, all of the shrines of the high places which <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in the towns of Samaria which the kings of Israel had made to provoke <transChange type="added">Yahweh</transChange>, Josiah removed, and he did to them like all of the deeds he had done in Bethel.

verses.name: II Kings 23:20
verses.text: Then he slaughtered all of the priests of the high places who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> there, on the altars, and he burned the bones of the humans on them. Then he returned <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Jerusalem.  <div eID="gen2965" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 23:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2189"/><title type="x-s">Passover Renewed</title> <div sID="gen2966" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2189"/>Then the king commanded all of the people, saying, “Keep the Passover to Yahweh your God, as has been written on the scroll of this covenant.”

verses.name: II Kings 23:22
verses.text: For they had not kept this Passover from the days of the judges who had judged over Israel <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞or⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> <transChange type="added">during</transChange> the days of the kings of Israel and the kings of Judah.

verses.name: II Kings 23:23
verses.text: But in the eighteenth year of King Josiah, this Passover was kept for Yahweh in Jerusalem.  <div eID="gen2966" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 23:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2190"/><div sID="gen2967" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2190"/>Moreover, the mediums and the spiritists, the household gods and the idols, and all of the abominations that were seen in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem, Josiah removed in order to establish the words of the law written on the scroll that Hilkiah the priest had found <transChange type="added">in</transChange> the temple of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Kings 23:25
verses.text: There was not a king like him before him, who turned to Yahweh with all of his heart and with all of his soul and with all of his might according to the law<note placement="foot">Or “Torah”</note> of Moses, nor did one arise like him afterwards.  <div eID="gen2967" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 23:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2191"/><div sID="gen2968" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2191"/>However, Yahweh did not turn from the fierceness of his great anger which was kindled against Judah because of all of the provocations <transChange type="added">with</transChange> which Manasseh had provoked him.

verses.name: II Kings 23:27
verses.text: Yahweh had said, “Even Judah I will remove from my face, as I have removed Israel; I will reject this city that I have chosen, even Jerusalem and the house <transChange type="added">of</transChange> which I said, ‘My name shall be there’!”  <div eID="gen2968" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 23:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2192"/><div sID="gen2969" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2192"/>The remainder of the acts of Josiah and all that he did, <transChange type="added">are</transChange> they not written on the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Judah?

verses.name: II Kings 23:29
verses.text: In his days, Pharaoh Neco, king of Egypt, went up against the king of Assyria at the Euphrates River. King Josiah went to meet him, and he<note placement="foot">That is, Neco</note> killed him at Megiddo as soon as he saw him.

verses.name: II Kings 23:30
verses.text: So his servants drove him dead in a chariot from Megiddo, and they brought him to Jerusalem and buried him in his tomb. Then the people of the land took Jehoahaz the son of Josiah and anointed him and made him king in place of his father.  <div eID="gen2969" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 23:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2193"/><title type="x-s">Jehoahaz Reigns in Judah</title> <div sID="gen2970" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2193"/>Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. The name of his mother <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah.

verses.name: II Kings 23:32
verses.text: He did evil in the eyes of Yahweh according to all his ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> had done.

verses.name: II Kings 23:33
verses.text: Then Pharaoh Neco confined him at Riblah in the land of Hamath, from reigning in Jerusalem, and imposed a levy on the land of a hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.  <div eID="gen2970" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 23:34
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2194"/><title type="x-s">Jehoiakim Replaces Jehoahaz</title> <div sID="gen2971" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2194"/>Then Pharaoh Neco made Eliakim the son of Josiah king in place of Josiah his father, and he changed his name to Jehoiakim. Then he took Jehoahaz and brought <transChange type="added">him</transChange> to Egypt, and he died there.

verses.name: II Kings 23:35
verses.text: The silver and the gold Jehoiakim gave to Pharaoh; however, he taxed the land to give the silver <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to meet the demands of Pharaoh⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “on the hunger of Pharaoh”</note> Each according to assessment, he exacted <transChange type="added">payment</transChange> of the silver and the gold from the people of the land to give to Pharaoh Neco.  <div eID="gen2971" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 23:36
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2195"/><div sID="gen2972" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2195"/>Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. The name of his mother <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Zebudah,<note placement="foot">According to the reading tradition (<hi type="italic">Qere)</hi>; <hi type="italic">Kethib</hi> reads “Zebidah”</note> the daughter of Pedaiah from Rumah.

verses.name: II Kings 23:37
verses.text: He did evil in the eyes of Yahweh according to all that his ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> had done.  <chapter eID="2Kgs.23"/>

verses.name: II Kings 24:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2196"/><title type="x-s">First Invasion of Nebuchadnezzar; Jehoiakim Submits</title> <div sID="gen2973" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2196"/>In his days, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up <transChange type="added">because</transChange> Jehoiakim had become his servant <transChange type="added">for</transChange> three years; then he turned and rebelled against him.

verses.name: II Kings 24:2
verses.text: So Yahweh sent against him raiding bands of Chaldeans, raiding bands of Aram, raiding bands of Moab, and raiding bands of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> He had sent them against Judah to destroy it, according to the word of Yahweh that he had spoken by the hand of his servants the prophets.

verses.name: II Kings 24:3
verses.text: Surely, it was <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞on the command⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “on the mouth”</note> of Yahweh against Judah to remove them from his sight because of the sins of Manasseh, according to all that he had done.

verses.name: II Kings 24:4
verses.text: Also, <transChange type="added">for</transChange> the blood of the innocent that he had shed—and he filled Jerusalem <transChange type="added">with</transChange> innocent blood—Yahweh was not willing to forgive.

verses.name: II Kings 24:5
verses.text: The remainder of the acts of Jehoiakim and all that he did, <transChange type="added">are</transChange> they not written on the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Judah?

verses.name: II Kings 24:6
verses.text: So Jehoiakim slept with his ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and Jehoiachin his son became king in his place.

verses.name: II Kings 24:7
verses.text: The king of Egypt did not again come out from his land, for the king of Babylon had taken <transChange type="added">territory</transChange> from the Wadi of Egypt to the Euphrates River.  <div eID="gen2973" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 24:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2197"/><title type="x-s">Jehoichin Succeeds Jehoiakim</title> <div sID="gen2974" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2197"/>Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. The name of his mother <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Nehushta daughter of Elnathan from Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Kings 24:9
verses.text: He did evil in the eyes of Yahweh according to all that his father had done.  <div eID="gen2974" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 24:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2198"/><title type="x-s">Second Invasion of Nebuchadnezzar</title> <div sID="gen2975" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2198"/>At that time, the servants of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Jerusalem, and the city came under the siege.

verses.name: II Kings 24:11
verses.text: Then Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came against the city <transChange type="added">while</transChange> his servants were besieging it.

verses.name: II Kings 24:12
verses.text: Jehoiachin king of Judah went out to the king of Babylon, he, his mother, his servants, his commanders, and his court officials. The king of Babylon took him in the eighth year of his reign.

verses.name: II Kings 24:13
verses.text: Then he took from there all of the treasures of the temple of Yahweh and the treasures of the palace of the king. He cut up all of the vessels of gold which Solomon the king of Israel had made in the temple of Yahweh, as Yahweh had foretold.

verses.name: II Kings 24:14
verses.text: He deported all of Jerusalem: all of the commanders, ten thousand of the skilled warriors, and the artisans; no one was left over except the poorest of the people of the land.

verses.name: II Kings 24:15
verses.text: He deported Jehoiachin to Babylon; the mother of the king, the wives of the king, his court officials, and the citizenry of the land he caused to go into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon:

verses.name: II Kings 24:16
verses.text: of all of the skilled men, seven thousand, and <transChange type="added">of</transChange> the skilled craftsmen and the artisans, one thousand. All of the mighty warriors <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞fit for war⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “doers of war”</note> the king of Babylon brought captive to Babylon.

verses.name: II Kings 24:17
verses.text: Then the king of Babylon made Mattaniah his uncle king in his place and changed his name <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Zedekiah.  <div eID="gen2975" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 24:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2199"/><title type="x-s">Zedekiah Replaces Jehoiachin</title> <div sID="gen2976" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2199"/>Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. The name of his mother <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah.

verses.name: II Kings 24:19
verses.text: He did evil in the eyes of Yahweh <transChange type="added">just</transChange> like all that Jehoiakim had done.

verses.name: II Kings 24:20
verses.text: For it happened because of the anger of Yahweh, in Jerusalem and in Judah, until they were cast out from his presence. Then Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.  <chapter eID="2Kgs.24"/>

verses.name: II Kings 25:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2200"/><title type="x-s">The Final Invasion of Nebuchadnezzar</title> <div sID="gen2977" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2200"/>It happened that in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth of the month, Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon came, he and his army, against Jerusalem. He encamped against it and built siege works against it all around.

verses.name: II Kings 25:2
verses.text: So the city came under siege until the eleventh year of the king.

verses.name: II Kings 25:3
verses.text: In the ninth month, the famine became severe in the city, and there was no food for the people of the land.

verses.name: II Kings 25:4
verses.text: Then the city was breached, and all of the men of war <transChange type="added">entered</transChange> by night by way of the gate between the wall which was by the garden of the king, and the Chaldeans <transChange type="added">were</transChange> against the city all around, so he<note placement="foot">That is, Zedekiah</note> left by the way of the Arabah.

verses.name: II Kings 25:5
verses.text: But the army of the Chaldeans pursued the king, and they overtook him in the Arabah of Jericho, and all of his army scattered from him.

verses.name: II Kings 25:6
verses.text: So they captured the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they passed sentence on him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “they spoke justice with him”</note>

verses.name: II Kings 25:7
verses.text: They slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes; then they blinded the eyes of Zedekiah and bound him in bronze fetters and brought him <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Babylon.  <div eID="gen2977" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 25:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2201"/><title type="x-s">Jerusalem Is Sacked and the Temple Burned</title> <div sID="gen2978" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2201"/>In the fifth month, on the seventh of the month, that is, the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon, Nebuzaradan, a commander of the imperial guard, a servant of the king of Babylon, came <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Kings 25:9
verses.text: He burned the temple of Yahweh, the palace of the king, and all of the houses of Jerusalem; every large house he burned with fire.

verses.name: II Kings 25:10
verses.text: He and all the army of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Chaldeans who <transChange type="added">were with</transChange> the imperial guard tore down the wall of Jerusalem all around.

verses.name: II Kings 25:11
verses.text: The remainder of the people left in the city, the deserters who had deserted to the king of Babylon, and the remainder of the multitude, Nebuzaradan the commander of the imperial guard deported.  <div eID="gen2978" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 25:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2202"/><div sID="gen2979" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2202"/>But the poor of the land the commander of the imperial guard left for the vineyards and for tilling.  <div eID="gen2979" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 25:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2203"/><title type="x-s">Plunder Taken by the Chaldeans</title> <div sID="gen2980" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2203"/>The bronze pillars which <transChange type="added">were in</transChange> the temple<note placement="foot">Or “house”</note> of Yahweh, the water carts, and the bronze sea that was in the temple of Yahweh, the Chaldeans broke into pieces and carried their bronze to Babylon.

verses.name: II Kings 25:14
verses.text: The pots, the shovels, the snuffers, the dishes, and the vessels of bronze with which they served there, they took.

verses.name: II Kings 25:15
verses.text: The firepans and the basins, whatever was gold, the commander of the imperial guard took <transChange type="added">for</transChange> the gold and whatever was silver, <transChange type="added">for</transChange> the silver.

verses.name: II Kings 25:16
verses.text: The two pillars, the one sea, and the water cart which Solomon had made for the temple of Yahweh, there was no weighing to the bronze of all of these vessels.

verses.name: II Kings 25:17
verses.text: The height of the one pillar <transChange type="added">was</transChange> eighteen cubits; a bronze capital was on it, with the height of the capital <transChange type="added">being</transChange> three cubits. The latticework and pomegranates on the capital all around were bronze, and likewise on the latticework for the second pillar.  <div eID="gen2980" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 25:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2204"/><div sID="gen2981" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2204"/>Then the commander of the imperial guard took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and three of the threshold keepers.

verses.name: II Kings 25:19
verses.text: From the city he took one court official who <transChange type="added">was</transChange> chief officer over the men of war, five men <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from the king’s council⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from those who saw the face of the king”</note> who were found in the city, the secretary of the commander of the army who mustered the people of the land, and sixty men from the people of the land being found in the city.

verses.name: II Kings 25:20
verses.text: Nebuzaradan commander of the imperial guard took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.

verses.name: II Kings 25:21
verses.text: Then the king of Babylon struck them down and killed them at Riblah in the land of Hamath; thus Judah was removed from its land.  <div eID="gen2981" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 25:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2205"/><title type="x-s">Gedaliah Appointed Governor</title> <div sID="gen2982" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2205"/>Now <transChange type="added">as far as</transChange> the people left in Judah whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon left behind, he appointed Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan over them.

verses.name: II Kings 25:23
verses.text: When all of the commanders of the troops heard, they and the men, that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah, they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah, <transChange type="added">even</transChange> Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, Johanan the son of Kareah, Seriah the son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, Jaazaniah the son of the Maacathite, they and their men.

verses.name: II Kings 25:24
verses.text: Gedaliah swore to them and to their men, and he said to them, “You must not be afraid because of the Chaldeans. Settle in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and may it go well with you.”

verses.name: II Kings 25:25
verses.text: But it happened in the seventh month that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah the son of Elishama from the offspring of the kingship came, and ten men with him, and they struck down Gedaliah so that he died with the Judeans and with the Chaldeans who were with him at Mizpah.

verses.name: II Kings 25:26
verses.text: Then all the people, from youngest to oldest, and the commanders of the troops, went <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Egypt, for they were afraid of the presence of the Chaldeans.  <div eID="gen2982" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 25:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2206"/><title type="x-s">Elderly Jehoiachin Cared for in Babylon</title> <div sID="gen2983" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2206"/>It happened in the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month on the twenty-seventh of the month, lifted Evil-Merodach king of Babylon in the year that he became king, the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah from the house of imprisonment.

verses.name: II Kings 25:28
verses.text: He spoke <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞kindly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “good things”</note> to him, and he gave him a better seat than the seat of the kings who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him in Babylon.

verses.name: II Kings 25:29
verses.text: So he changed the clothes of his imprisonment, and he ate food continually in his presence all the days of his life.

verses.name: II Kings 25:30
verses.text: His allowance was continually given to him from the king, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a portion every day⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a thing of day on his day”</note> all the days of his life.  <chapter eID="2Kgs.25"/> <div eID="gen2983" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen2788" osisID="2Kgs" type="book"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2207"/><title type="x-s">From Adam to Abraham</title> <div sID="gen2985" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2207"/>Adam, Seth, Enosh;

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:2
verses.text: Kenan, Mahalalel, Jared;

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:3
verses.text: Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech;

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:4
verses.text: Noah, Shem, Ham, and Japheth.  <div eID="gen2985" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2208"/><div sID="gen2986" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2208"/>The sons of Japheth: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:6
verses.text: The sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, Diphath, and Togarmah.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:7
verses.text: The sons of Javan: Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Rhodanim.  <div eID="gen2986" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2209"/><div sID="gen2987" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2209"/>The sons of Ham: Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:9
verses.text: The sons of Cush: Seba, Havilah, Sabta, Raamah, and Sabteca. And the sons of Raamah: Sheba and Dedan.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:10
verses.text: And Cush fathered Nimrod; he himself began to be mighty on earth.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:11
verses.text: And Mizraim fathered the Ludim, the Anamim, the Lehabim, the Naphtuhim,

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:12
verses.text: the Pathrusim, the Casluhim (from whence the Philistines descended), and the Caphtorim.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:13
verses.text: And Canaan fathered Zidon his firstborn, and Heth,

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:14
verses.text: and the Jebusites, the Amorites, the Girgashites,

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:15
verses.text: the Hivites, the Arkites, the Sinites,

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:16
verses.text: the Arvadites, the Zemarites, and the Hamathites.  <div eID="gen2987" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2210"/><div sID="gen2988" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2210"/>The sons of Shem: Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud, Aram, Uz, Hul, Gether, and Meshech.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:18
verses.text: And Arphaxad fathered Shelah; and Shelah fathered Eber.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:19
verses.text: And two sons were born to Eber: the name of the one <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Peleg (for in his days the earth was divided), and the name of his brother <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Joktan.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:20
verses.text: And Joktan fathered Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:21
verses.text: Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah,

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:22
verses.text: Ebal,<note placement="foot">Spelled “Obal” in <reference osisRef="Gen.10.28">Genesis 10:28</reference></note> Abimael, Sheba,

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:23
verses.text: Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab; all these were the sons of Joktan.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:24
verses.text: Shem, Arphaxad, Shelah;

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:25
verses.text: Eber, Peleg, Reu;

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:26
verses.text: Serug, Nahor, Terah;

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:27
verses.text: Abram, that is, Abraham.  <div eID="gen2988" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2211"/><div sID="gen2989" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2211"/>The sons of Abraham: Isaac and Ishmael.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:29
verses.text: These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> their generations: the firstborn of Ishmael, Nebaioth, and Kedar, Abdeel, Mibsam,

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:30
verses.text: Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad, Tema,

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:31
verses.text: Jetur, Naphish, and Kedmah. These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the sons of Ishmael.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:32
verses.text: And the sons of Keturah, Abraham’s concubine: she gave birth to Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. And the sons of Jokshan: Sheba and Dedan.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:33
verses.text: And the sons of Midian: Ephah, Epher, Enoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these <transChange type="added">were</transChange> the sons of Keturah.  <div eID="gen2989" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:34
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2212"/><div sID="gen2990" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2212"/>Abraham fathered Isaac. The sons of Isaac: Esau and Israel.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:35
verses.text: The sons of Esau: Eliphaz, Reuel, Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:36
verses.text: The sons of Eliphaz: Teman, Omar, Zephi,<note placement="foot">Spelled “Zepho” in <reference osisRef="Gen.36.11">Genesis 36:11</reference></note> Gatam, Kenaz, Timna, and Amalek.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:37
verses.text: The sons of Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:38
verses.text: And the sons of Seir: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:39
verses.text: And the sons of Lotan: Hori and Homam; and the sister of Lotan <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Timna.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:40
verses.text: The sons of Shobal: Alian, Manahath, Ebal, Shephi, and Onam. And the sons of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:41
verses.text: The sons of Anah: Dishon. And the sons of Dishon: Hamran, Eshban, Ithran, and Keran.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:42
verses.text: The sons of Ezer: Bilhan, Zaavan, and Jaakan. The sons of Dishan: Uz and Aran.  <div eID="gen2990" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:43
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2213"/><div sID="gen2991" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2213"/>These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the kings who reigned in the land of Edom before any king reigned over the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>:<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> Bela son of Beor, and the name of his city <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Dinhabah.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:44
verses.text: When Bela died, Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah reigned in his place.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:45
verses.text: When Jobab died, Husham from the land of the Temanites reigned in his place.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:46
verses.text: When Husham died, Hadad son of Bedad, who defeated the Midianites in the country of Moab, reigned in his place. And the name of his city was Avith.<note placement="foot">According to the reading tradition (<hi type="italic">Qere)</hi>; <hi type="italic">Kethib</hi> has “Avuth”</note>

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:47
verses.text: When Hadad died, Samlah from Masrekah reigned in his place.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:48
verses.text: When Samlah died, Shaul from Rehoboth-by-the-River reigned in his place.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:49
verses.text: When Shaul died, Baal-Hanan son of Achbor reigned in his place.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:50
verses.text: When Baal-Hanan died, Hadad reigned in his place, and the name of his city <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Pai.<note placement="foot">Spelled “Pau” in <reference osisRef="Gen.36.39">Genesis 36:39</reference></note> And the name of his wife <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Mehetabel, daughter of Matred, daughter of Me-Zahab.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:51
verses.text: And Hadad died. And the chiefs of Edom were: chiefs Timna, Aliah, Jetheth,

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:52
verses.text: Oholibamah, Elah, Pinon,

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:53
verses.text: Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar,

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:54
verses.text: Magdiel, and Iram. These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the chiefs of Edom.  <chapter eID="1Chr.1"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2214"/><title type="x-s">The Genealogy of David</title> <div sID="gen2992" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2214"/>These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the sons of Israel: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun,

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:2
verses.text: Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:3
verses.text: The sons of Judah: Er, Onan and Shelah; <transChange type="added">these</transChange> three were born to him from Bathshua the Canaanite. Now Er, Judah’s firstborn, <transChange type="added">was</transChange> evil in the sight of Yahweh, and he put him to death.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:4
verses.text: And Tamar his daughter-in-law bore Perez and Zerah to him. The sons of Judah <transChange type="added">were</transChange> five in all.  <div eID="gen2992" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2215"/><div sID="gen2993" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2215"/>The sons of Perez: Hezron and Hamul.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:6
verses.text: The sons of Zerah: Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol, and Dara, five in all.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:7
verses.text: The son of Carmi: Achar, the troubler of Israel, who acted unfaithfully in the matter of the devoted thing.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:8
verses.text: And the son of Ethan <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Azariah.  <div eID="gen2993" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2216"/><div sID="gen2994" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2216"/>The sons of Hezron who were born to him: Jerahmeel, Ram, and Caleb.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:10
verses.text: And Ram fathered Amminadab, and Amminadab fathered Nahshon, prince of the sons of Judah.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:11
verses.text: And Nahshon fathered Salma, and Salma fathered Boaz.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:12
verses.text: And Boaz fathered Obed, and Obed fathered Jesse.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:13
verses.text: And Jesse fathered Eliab his firstborn, Abinadab the second, Shimea the third,

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:14
verses.text: Nethanel the fourth, Raddai the fifth,

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:15
verses.text: Ozem the sixth, David the seventh.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:16
verses.text: And their sisters <transChange type="added">were</transChange> Zeruiah and Abigail. The sons of Zeruiah: Abishai, Joab, and Asahel, three.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:17
verses.text: And Abigail bore Amasa, and the father of Amasa <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Jether the Ishmaelite.  <div eID="gen2994" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2217"/><div sID="gen2995" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2217"/>And Caleb the son of Hezron fathered children by Azubah his wife and by Jerioth. And these <transChange type="added">were</transChange> her sons: Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:19
verses.text: And when Azubah died, Caleb married<note placement="foot">Or “took”</note> Ephrathah, and she bore Hur to him.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:20
verses.text: And Hur fathered Uri, and Uri fathered Bezalel.  <div eID="gen2995" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2218"/><div sID="gen2996" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2218"/>And afterward Hezron went in to the daughter of Makir the father of Gilead. And he married<note placement="foot">Or “took”</note> her when he was sixty years old. And she bore Segub to him.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:22
verses.text: And Segub fathered Jair, and he had twenty-three cities in the land of Gilead.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:23
verses.text: And Geshur and Aram took Havvoth-Jair from them, Kenath and its villages, sixty cities. All these <transChange type="added">were</transChange> the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞descendants⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons”</note> of Makir, the father of Gilead.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:24
verses.text: And after the death of Hezron in Caleb-Ephrathah, Abijah the wife of Hezron bore to him Ashhur, the father of Tekoa.  <div eID="gen2996" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2219"/><div sID="gen2997" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2219"/>And the sons of Jerahmeel the firstborn of Hezron were Ram his firstborn, Bunah, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:26
verses.text: And Jerahmeel had another wife, and her name <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Atarah. She <transChange type="added">was</transChange> the mother of Onam.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:27
verses.text: The sons of Ram the firstborn of Jerahmeel were Maaz, Jamin, and Eker.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:28
verses.text: And the sons of Onam were Shammai and Jada. And the sons of Shammai <transChange type="added">were</transChange> Nadab and Abishur.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:29
verses.text: And the name of the wife of Abishur <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Abihail, and she bore to him Ahban and Molid.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:30
verses.text: And the sons of Nadab <transChange type="added">were</transChange> Seled and Appaim. And Seled died without children.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:31
verses.text: And the sons of Appaim: Ishi. The sons of Ishi: Sheshan. The sons of Sheshan: Ahlai.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:32
verses.text: And the sons of Jada the brother of Shammai: Jether and Jonathan. And Jether died without children.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:33
verses.text: And the sons of Jonathan: Peleth and Zaza. These were the children of Jerahmeel.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:34
verses.text: And Sheshan had no sons, only daughters, but Sheshan had an Egyptian slave, and his name <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Jarha.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:35
verses.text: So Sheshan gave his daughter to Jarha his slave for a wife, and she bore to him Attai.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:36
verses.text: And Attai fathered Nathan, and Nathan fathered Zabad.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:37
verses.text: And Zabad fathered Ephlal, and Ephlal fathered Obed.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:38
verses.text: And Obed fathered Jehu, and Jehu fathered Azariah.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:39
verses.text: And Azariah fathered Helez, and Helez fathered Eleasah.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:40
verses.text: And Eleasah fathered Sismai, and Sismai fathered Shallum.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:41
verses.text: And Shallum fathered Jekamiah, and Jekamiah fathered Elishama.  <div eID="gen2997" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:42
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2220"/><div sID="gen2998" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2220"/>And the sons of Caleb the brother of Jerahmeel were Mesha his firstborn; he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> the father of Ziph. The sons of Mareshah: Hebron.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:43
verses.text: And the sons of Hebron <transChange type="added">were</transChange> Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:44
verses.text: And Shema fathered Raham, the father of Jorkeam. And Rekem fathered Shammai.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:45
verses.text: And the son of Shammai <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Maon, and Maon <transChange type="added">was</transChange> the father of Beth-Zur.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:46
verses.text: And Ephah, the concubine of Caleb, gave birth to Haran, Moza, and Gazez. And Haran fathered Gazez.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:47
verses.text: And the sons of Jahdai <transChange type="added">were</transChange> Regem, Jotham, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah, and Shaaph.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:48
verses.text: Maacah, the concubine of Caleb, gave birth to Sheber and Tirhanah.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:49
verses.text: She also gave birth to Shaaph the father of Madmannah, Sheva the father of Machbenah and the father of Gibea; and the daughter of Caleb <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Acsah.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:50
verses.text: These were the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞descendants⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons”</note> of Caleb. <div eID="gen2998" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2999" type="x-p"/> The sons of Hur the firstborn of Ephrathah: Shobal the father of Kiriath-Jearim,

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:51
verses.text: Salma the father of Bethlehem, <transChange type="added">and</transChange> Hareph the father of Beth-Gader.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:52
verses.text: And Shobal the father of Kiriath-Jearim had <transChange type="added">other</transChange> sons: Haroeh, half of the Menuhoth.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:53
verses.text: And the families of Kiriath-Jearim: the Ithrites, the Puthites, the Shumathites, and the Mishraites. From these descended the Zorathites and the Eshtaolites.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:54
verses.text: The sons of Salma: Bethlehem, the Netophathites, Ataroth-Beth-Joab, and half of the Manahathites, the Zorites.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:55
verses.text: And the families of the scribes who lived <transChange type="added">at</transChange> Jabez: the Tirathites, the Shimeathites, and the Sucathites. These <transChange type="added">were</transChange> the Kenites who came from Hammath, the father of the house of Recab.  <chapter eID="1Chr.2"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 3:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2221"/><title type="x-s">The Descendants of David</title> <div sID="gen3000" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2221"/>These were the sons of David who were born to him in Hebron: the firstborn, Amnon, by Ahinoam the Jezreelite; the second, Daniel, by Abigail the Carmelite;

verses.name: I Chronicles 3:2
verses.text: the third, Absalom, the son of Maacah the daughter of Talmai, king of Geshur; the fourth, Adonijah, the son of Haggith;

verses.name: I Chronicles 3:3
verses.text: the fifth, Shephatiah, by Abital; the sixth, Ithream, by his wife Eglah.

verses.name: I Chronicles 3:4
verses.text: Six were born to him in Hebron. And he reigned there seven years and six months. And he reigned thirty-three years in Jerusalem.

verses.name: I Chronicles 3:5
verses.text: And these were born to him in Jerusalem: Shimea, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon, four by Bathshua the daughter of Ammiel;

verses.name: I Chronicles 3:6
verses.text: then Ibhar, Elishama, Eliphelet,

verses.name: I Chronicles 3:7
verses.text: Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia,

verses.name: I Chronicles 3:8
verses.text: Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet, nine.

verses.name: I Chronicles 3:9
verses.text: All these <transChange type="added">were</transChange> the sons of David, besides the sons of the concubines. And Tamar was their sister.  <div eID="gen3000" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 3:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2222"/><div sID="gen3001" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2222"/>Now the son of Solomon <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Rehoboam; Abijah <transChange type="added">was</transChange> his son, Asa <transChange type="added">was</transChange> his son, Jehoshaphat <transChange type="added">was</transChange> his son,

verses.name: I Chronicles 3:11
verses.text: Joram <transChange type="added">was</transChange> his son, Ahaziah <transChange type="added">was</transChange> his son, Joash <transChange type="added">was</transChange> his son,

verses.name: I Chronicles 3:12
verses.text: Amaziah <transChange type="added">was</transChange> his son, Azariah <transChange type="added">was</transChange> his son, Jotham <transChange type="added">was</transChange> his son,

verses.name: I Chronicles 3:13
verses.text: Ahaz <transChange type="added">was</transChange> his son, Hezekiah <transChange type="added">was</transChange> his son, Manasseh <transChange type="added">was</transChange> his son,

verses.name: I Chronicles 3:14
verses.text: Amon <transChange type="added">was</transChange> his son, Josiah <transChange type="added">was</transChange> his son.  <div eID="gen3001" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 3:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2223"/><div sID="gen3002" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2223"/>And the sons of Josiah: Johanan the firstborn, the second Jehoiakim, the third Zedekiah, the fourth Shallum.

verses.name: I Chronicles 3:16
verses.text: And the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞descendants⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons”</note> of Jehoiakim: Jeconiah his son, Zedekiah his son.

verses.name: I Chronicles 3:17
verses.text: And the sons of Jeconiah, the captive: Shealtiel his son,

verses.name: I Chronicles 3:18
verses.text: Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah.

verses.name: I Chronicles 3:19
verses.text: And the sons of Pedaiah: Zerubbabel and Shimei. And the sons of Zerubbabel: Meshullam and Hananiah, and Shelomith their sister,

verses.name: I Chronicles 3:20
verses.text: and Hashubah, Ohel, Berekiah, Hasadiah, and Jushab-Hesed, five.

verses.name: I Chronicles 3:21
verses.text: And the sons of Hananiah: Pelatiah and Jeshaiah. The sons of Rephaiah, the sons of Arnan, the sons of Obadiah, the sons of Shecaniah.

verses.name: I Chronicles 3:22
verses.text: And the sons of Shecaniah: Shemaiah. And the sons of Shemaiah: Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat, six.

verses.name: I Chronicles 3:23
verses.text: And the sons of Neariah: Elioenai, Hezekiah, and Azrikam, three.

verses.name: I Chronicles 3:24
verses.text: And the sons of Elioenai: Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah, and Anani, seven.  <chapter eID="1Chr.3"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2224"/><title type="x-s">The Descendants of David</title> <div sID="gen3003" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2224"/>The sons of Judah: Perez, Hezron, Carmi, Hur, and Shobal.

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:2
verses.text: And Reaiah the son of Shobal fathered Jahath, and Jahath fathered Ahumai and Lahad. These <transChange type="added">were</transChange> the clans of the Zorathites.

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:3
verses.text: And these <transChange type="added">were</transChange> the sons of Etam: Jezreel, Ishma, and Idbash. And the name of their sister <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Hazzelelponi,

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:4
verses.text: and Penuel <transChange type="added">was</transChange> the father of Gedor, and Ezer <transChange type="added">was</transChange> the father of Hushah. These <transChange type="added">were</transChange> the sons of Hur, the firstborn of Ephrathah, the father of Bethlehem.

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:5
verses.text: And Ashhur, the father of Tekoa, had two wives: Helah and Naarah.

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:6
verses.text: And Naarah bore him Ahuzzam, Hepher, Temeni, and Haahashtari. These <transChange type="added">were</transChange> the sons of Naarah.

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:7
verses.text: The sons of Helah: Zereth, Izhar, and Ethnan.

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:8
verses.text: And Koz fathered Anub, Zobebah, and the clans of Aharhel, the son of Harum.

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:9
verses.text: And Jabez was more honorable than his brothers. And his mother called his name Jabez, saying, “Because I bore him in pain.”

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:10
verses.text: And Jabez called upon the God of Israel, saying, “Oh that you would surely bless me and enlarge my border. And may your hand be with me, that you would keep me from evil so that it might not harm me!” And God granted what he asked.

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:11
verses.text: Chelub, the brother of Shuhah, fathered Mehir. He <transChange type="added">was</transChange> the father of Eshton.

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:12
verses.text: And Eshton fathered Beth-Rapha, Paseah, and Tehinnah, the father of the city of Nahash. These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the men of Recah.

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:13
verses.text: The sons of Kenaz: Othniel and Seraiah. And the sons of Othniel: Hathath.

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:14
verses.text: And Meonothai fathered Ophrah; and Seraiah fathered Joab, the father of Ge-Harashim, because they <transChange type="added">were</transChange> craftsmen.

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:15
verses.text: The sons of Caleb, the son of Jephunneh: Iru, Elah, and Naam. And the sons of Elah: Kenaz.

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:16
verses.text: The sons of Jehallelel: Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria, and Asarel.

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:17
verses.text: The sons of Ezrah: Jether, Mered, Epher, and Jalon. And she became pregnant with Miriam, Shammai, and Ishbah, the father of Eshtemoa.

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:18
verses.text: And his Judahite wife bore Jered the father of Gedor, Heber the father of Soco, and Jekuthiel the father of Zanoah. And these <transChange type="added">were</transChange> the sons of Bithiah daughter of Pharaoh, whom Mered married.

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:19
verses.text: The sons of the wife of Hodiah, the sister of Naham, <transChange type="added">were</transChange> the fathers of Keilah the Garmite and Eshtemoa the Maacathite.

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:20
verses.text: The sons of Shimon: Amnon, Rinnah, Ben-Hanan, and Tolon. The sons of Ishi: Zoheth and Ben-Zoheth.

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:21
verses.text: The sons of Shelah, the son of Judah: Er the father of Lecah, Laadah the father of Mareshah, and the families of the house of linen workers at Beth Ashbea;

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:22
verses.text: and Jokim, and the men of Cozeba, and Joash, and Saraph, who ruled in Moab and returned to Lehem. (Now the records are ancient).

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:23
verses.text: These <transChange type="added">were</transChange> the potters and inhabitants of Netaim and Gederah. They lived there with the king in his service.  <div eID="gen3003" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2225"/><title type="x-s">Descendants of Simeon</title> <div sID="gen3004" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2225"/>The sons of Simeon: Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, Shaul.

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:25
verses.text: Shallum his son, Mibsam his son, Mishma his son.

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:26
verses.text: The sons of Mishma: Hammuel his son, Zaccur his son, Shimei his son.

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:27
verses.text: Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters, but his brothers did not have many children. But all their families did not multiply like the men of Judah.

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:28
verses.text: And they lived in Beersheba, Moladah, Hazar Shual,

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:29
verses.text: Bilhah, Ezem, Tolad,

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:30
verses.text: Bethuel, Hormah, Ziklag,

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:31
verses.text: Beth-Marcaboth, Hazar-Susim, Beth-Biri, and Shaaraim. These <transChange type="added">were</transChange> their cities until David reigned.

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:32
verses.text: And their villages <transChange type="added">were</transChange> Etam, Ain, Rimmon, Token, and Ashan, five cities

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:33
verses.text: and all their villages that surrounding these cities as far as Baal. These <transChange type="added">were</transChange> their settlements, and they kept a genealogical record for them.  <div eID="gen3004" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:34
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2226"/><div sID="gen3005" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2226"/>Meshobab, Jamlech, and Joshah the son of Amaziah,

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:35
verses.text: Joel, and Jehu the son of Joshibiah, son of Seraiah, son of Asiel.

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:36
verses.text: And Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Jesimiel, Benaiah,

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:37
verses.text: and Ziza the son of Shiphi, son of Allon, son of Jedaiah, son of Shimri, son of Shemaiah.

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:38
verses.text: These <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞mentioned by name⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “coming in the names”</note> <transChange type="added">were</transChange> leaders in their families, and their fathers’ households increased greatly.

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:39
verses.text: And they went to the entrance of Gedor, up to the east side of the valley, to seek pasture for their flocks.

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:40
verses.text: And they found fertile and good pasture, and the land <transChange type="added">was</transChange> very broad, quiet, and at ease, for the former inhabitants there <transChange type="added">were</transChange> from Ham.

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:41
verses.text: These, mentioned by name, came in the days of Hezekiah, king of Judah, and attacked their tents and the Meunites who were found there. And they devoted them to destruction to this day, and they settled among them because <transChange type="added">there was</transChange> pasture there for their flocks.

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:42
verses.text: And some of them from the Simeonites went to Mount Seir, five hundred men. And Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel, the sons of Ishi, <transChange type="added">were</transChange> under their leadership.

verses.name: I Chronicles 4:43
verses.text: And they destroyed the remainder of the Amalekites who had escaped, and they have lived there to this day.  <chapter eID="1Chr.4"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 5:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2227"/><title type="x-s">The Descendants of Reuben</title> <div sID="gen3006" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2227"/>The sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel (for he was the firstborn, but when he defiled the couch of his father, his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph, the son of Israel, so that he was not enrolled in the genealogy as the firstborn,

verses.name: I Chronicles 5:2
verses.text: though Judah became strong among his brothers and a chief <transChange type="added">came</transChange> from him, but the birthright belonged to Joseph).

verses.name: I Chronicles 5:3
verses.text: The sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel: Enoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.

verses.name: I Chronicles 5:4
verses.text: The sons of Joel: Shemaiah his son, Gog his son, Shimei his son,

verses.name: I Chronicles 5:5
verses.text: Micah his son, Reaiah his son, Baal his son,

verses.name: I Chronicles 5:6
verses.text: Beerah his son, a leader of the Reubenites, whom Tiglath-Pilneser king of Assyria deported into exile.

verses.name: I Chronicles 5:7
verses.text: And his kinsmen by their families, when their generations were recorded in <transChange type="added">the</transChange> genealogy: the chief, Jeiel, and Zechariah,

verses.name: I Chronicles 5:8
verses.text: and Bela son of Azaz, son of Shema, son of Joel, who lived in Aroer, as far as Nebo and Baal-Meon.

verses.name: I Chronicles 5:9
verses.text: He also lived to the east up to the entrance of the desert <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞this side of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Or “from”</note> the River Euphrates, for their livestock had multiplied in the land of Gilead.

verses.name: I Chronicles 5:10
verses.text: And in the days of Saul they made war against the Hagrites, and they<note placement="foot">That is, the Hagrites</note> fell into their hand. And they lived in their tents in all the region east of Gilead.  <div eID="gen3006" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 5:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2228"/><title type="x-s">The Descendants of Gad</title> <div sID="gen3007" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2228"/>And the sons of Gad lived near to them in the land of Bashan as far as Salecah:

verses.name: I Chronicles 5:12
verses.text: Joel the chief, Shapham the second, Janai, and Shaphat in Bashan.

verses.name: I Chronicles 5:13
verses.text: And their kinsmen according to their fathers’ households: Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia, and Eber, seven.

verses.name: I Chronicles 5:14
verses.text: These <transChange type="added">were</transChange> the sons of Abihail the son of Huri, son of Jaroah, son of Gilead, son of Michael, son of Jeshishai, son of Jahdo, son of Buz.

verses.name: I Chronicles 5:15
verses.text: Ahi son of Abdiel, son of Guni, <transChange type="added">was</transChange> chief in their fathers’ households.

verses.name: I Chronicles 5:16
verses.text: And they lived in Gilead, in Bashan, and in <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞its towns⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “her daughters”</note> and in all the pasturelands of Sharon to their limits.

verses.name: I Chronicles 5:17
verses.text: All of them were enrolled in <transChange type="added">the</transChange> genealogy in the days of Jotham, king of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam, king of Israel.  <div eID="gen3007" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 5:18
