verses.text: And his brothers, sons of ability, <transChange type="added">were</transChange> two thousand seven hundred heads of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞families⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “fathers”</note> and King David appointed them over the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, for every matter of God and matter of the king.  <chapter eID="1Chr.26"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 27:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2333"/><title type="x-s">Military Divisions</title> <div sID="gen3155" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2333"/>And as for the number of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> the heads of <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞families⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “fathers”</note> the commanders of thousands and hundreds, and their officials who serve the king in all matters of the working groups that came and went, month by month, throughout all the months of the year, each working group: twenty-four thousand.  <div eID="gen3155" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 27:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2334"/><div sID="gen3156" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2334"/>Over the first working group for the first month: Jashobeam the son of Zabdiel. And <transChange type="added">he was</transChange> over his working group <transChange type="added">of</transChange> twenty-four thousand.

verses.name: I Chronicles 27:3
verses.text: From the sons of Perez <transChange type="added">who was</transChange> the chief of the commanders of the armies for the first month.

verses.name: I Chronicles 27:4
verses.text: And over the working groups of the second month: Dodai the Ahohite and his working group, and Mikloth the commander. And <transChange type="added">he was</transChange> over his working group <transChange type="added">of</transChange> twenty-four thousand.

verses.name: I Chronicles 27:5
verses.text: The third commander of the army for the third month <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Benaiah son of Jehoiada the chief priest. And <transChange type="added">he was</transChange> over his working group <transChange type="added">of</transChange> twenty-four thousand.

verses.name: I Chronicles 27:6
verses.text: This <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Benaiah <transChange type="added">who was</transChange> a mighty warrior of thirty, and over the thirty and his working group <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Ammizabad his son.

verses.name: I Chronicles 27:7
verses.text: The fourth, for the fourth month, <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Asahel the brother of Joab and his son Zebadiah after him. And <transChange type="added">he was</transChange> over his working group <transChange type="added">of</transChange> twenty-four thousand.

verses.name: I Chronicles 27:8
verses.text: The fifth, for the fifth month, the commander <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Shamhuth the Izrahite. And <transChange type="added">he was</transChange> over his working group <transChange type="added">of</transChange> twenty-four thousand.

verses.name: I Chronicles 27:9
verses.text: The sixth, for the sixth month, <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite. And <transChange type="added">he was</transChange> over his working group <transChange type="added">of</transChange> twenty-four thousand.

verses.name: I Chronicles 27:10
verses.text: The seventh, for the seventh month, <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Helez the Pelonite, from the sons of Ephraim. And <transChange type="added">he was</transChange> over his working group <transChange type="added">of</transChange> twenty-four thousand.

verses.name: I Chronicles 27:11
verses.text: The eighth, for the eighth month, <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Sibbecai the Hushathite of the Zerahites. And <transChange type="added">he was</transChange> over his working group <transChange type="added">of</transChange> twenty-four thousand.

verses.name: I Chronicles 27:12
verses.text: The ninth, for the ninth month, <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Abiezer the Anathothite of the Benjamites. And <transChange type="added">he was</transChange> over his working group <transChange type="added">of</transChange> twenty-four thousand.

verses.name: I Chronicles 27:13
verses.text: The tenth, for the tenth month, <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Maharai the Netophathite of the Zerahites. And <transChange type="added">he was</transChange> over his working group <transChange type="added">of</transChange> twenty-four thousand.

verses.name: I Chronicles 27:14
verses.text: The eleventh, for the eleventh month, <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Benaiah the Pirathonite from the sons of Ephraim. And <transChange type="added">he was</transChange> over his working group <transChange type="added">of</transChange> twenty-four thousand.

verses.name: I Chronicles 27:15
verses.text: The twelfth, for the twelfth month, <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Heldai the Netophathite, of Othniel. And <transChange type="added">he was</transChange> over his working group <transChange type="added">of</transChange> twenty-four thousand.  <div eID="gen3156" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 27:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2335"/><title type="x-s">Leaders of the Tribes and Other High Ranking Officials</title> <div sID="gen3157" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2335"/>And over the tribes of Israel, for the Reubenites: the commander <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Eliezer the son of Zikri. For the Simeonites: Shephatiah the son of Maacah.

verses.name: I Chronicles 27:17
verses.text: For Levi: Hashabiah the son of Kemuel. For Aaron, Zadok.

verses.name: I Chronicles 27:18
verses.text: For Judah: Elihu, from the brothers of David. For Issachar: Omri the son of Michael.

verses.name: I Chronicles 27:19
verses.text: For Zebulun: Ishmaiah the son of Obadiah. For Naphtali: Jerimoth the son of Azriel.

verses.name: I Chronicles 27:20
verses.text: For the Ephraimites: Hoshea the son of Azaziah. For the half-tribe of Manasseh: Joel the son of Pedaiah.

verses.name: I Chronicles 27:21
verses.text: For the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead: Iddo the son of Zechariah. For Benjamin: Jaasiel son of Abner.

verses.name: I Chronicles 27:22
verses.text: For Dan: Azarel the son of Jeroham. These <transChange type="added">were</transChange> the commanders of the tribes of Israel.

verses.name: I Chronicles 27:23
verses.text: And David did not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞take a census of those twenty years old or under⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “take up their count from a son of twenty years and to less”</note> because Yahweh promised<note placement="foot">Or “said”</note> to make Israel more numerous than the stars of heaven.

verses.name: I Chronicles 27:24
verses.text: Joab the son of Zeruiah began to count, but he did not finish. But wrath came upon Israel concerning this, and the number was not included in <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the chronicles⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in the numbering of the words of the days”</note> of King David.  <div eID="gen3157" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 27:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2336"/><div sID="gen3158" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2336"/>And over the treasury rooms of the king <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Azmaveth the son of Adiel. And over the treasuries in the country, in the cities, in the unwalled villages, and in the towers <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Jonathan the son of Uzziah.

verses.name: I Chronicles 27:26
verses.text: And over those who did the work in the field to till the soil <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Ezri the son of Kelub.

verses.name: I Chronicles 27:27
verses.text: And over the vineyards <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Shemei the Ramathite. And over the produce in the vineyards for the storehouses of the wine <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Zabdi the Shiphmite.

verses.name: I Chronicles 27:28
verses.text: And over the olive trees and the sycamore trees that <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in the Shephelah <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Baal-Hanan the Gederite. And over the treasury houses of olive oil <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Joash.

verses.name: I Chronicles 27:29
verses.text: And over the cattle pastured in the Sharon <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Shitrai the Sharonite. And over the cattle in the valley <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Shaphat the son of Adlai.

verses.name: I Chronicles 27:30
verses.text: And over the camels <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Obil the Ishmaelite. And over the female donkeys <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Jehdeiah the Meronothite.<note placement="foot"><reference osisRef="1Chr.27.31">1 Chronicles 27:31 </reference>begins here in the Hebrew Bible</note> And over the sheep <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Jaziz the Hagrite.

verses.name: I Chronicles 27:31
verses.text: All of these <transChange type="added">were</transChange> officials of the property of King David.  <div eID="gen3158" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 27:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2337"/><div sID="gen3159" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2337"/>And Jehonathan the uncle of David <transChange type="added">was</transChange> an adviser, a man of insight, and he was a scribe. And Jehiel the son of Hachmoni <transChange type="added">was</transChange> with the sons of the king.

verses.name: I Chronicles 27:33
verses.text: And Ahithophel <transChange type="added">was</transChange> an adviser to the king, and Hushai the Arkite <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a friend of the king.  <div eID="gen3159" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 27:34
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2338"/><div sID="gen3160" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2338"/>And after Ahithophel <transChange type="added">came</transChange> Jehoiada, the son of Benaiah, and Abiathar. And Joab <transChange type="added">was</transChange> the commander of the king’s army.  <chapter eID="1Chr.27"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 28:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2339"/><title type="x-s">David’s Charge to Israel</title> <div sID="gen3161" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2339"/>Then David assembled all the commanders of Israel, the commanders of the tribes and the commanders of working groups who served the king, and the commanders of thousands, the commanders of hundreds, and the commanders over all the property of the king and his sons, with the court officials and mighty warriors, and all the mighty warriors of ability, at Jerusalem.

verses.name: I Chronicles 28:2
verses.text: And King David rose to his feet and said, “Listen to me, my brothers and my people. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I myself wanted⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “I myself with my heart”</note> to build a house of rest for the ark of the covenant of Yahweh and the footstool of our God, and I prepared to build.

verses.name: I Chronicles 28:3
verses.text: But God said to me, ‘You may not build a house for my name because you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> a man of war, and you have shed blood.’

verses.name: I Chronicles 28:4
verses.text: But Yahweh the God of Israel chose me from all of the house of my father to be king over Israel forever, for he chose Judah as leader, and in the house of Judah, the house of my father, and among the sons of my father he took pleasure in me to reign over all Israel.

verses.name: I Chronicles 28:5
verses.text: And from all my sons—for Yahweh has given many sons to me—he has chosen Solomon my son to sit on the throne of the kingdom of Yahweh over Israel.

verses.name: I Chronicles 28:6
verses.text: And he said to me, ‘Solomon your son, he himself shall build my house and my courts, for I have chosen him as a son to myself, and I myself will be as a father to him,

verses.name: I Chronicles 28:7
verses.text: and I will establish his kingdom forever if <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he firmly performs⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “if he is strong to do”</note> my commandments and my judgments as <transChange type="added">he has to</transChange> this day.’

verses.name: I Chronicles 28:8
verses.text: So now in the sight of all Israel, the assembly of Yahweh, and in the hearing of our God, observe and seek all the commandments of Yahweh your God so that you may take possession of this good land and bestow <transChange type="added">it</transChange> as an inheritance to your children after you forever.”  <div eID="gen3161" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 28:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2340"/><title type="x-s">David’s Charge to Solomon</title> <div sID="gen3162" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2340"/>“And you, Solomon my son, know the God of your father and serve him with a whole heart and a willing mind, for Yahweh searches all hearts and understands every plan and <transChange type="added">all</transChange> thoughts. If you seek him, he will be found by you, but if you abandon him, he will reject you forever.

verses.name: I Chronicles 28:10
verses.text: Look now, for Yahweh has chosen you to build a house for the sanctuary; be strong and do it!”  <div eID="gen3162" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 28:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2341"/><div sID="gen3163" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2341"/>Then David gave to Solomon his son the plan of the vestibule and of its houses, its treasuries, its upper rooms, its inner chambers, and of the house of the lid of the ark,

verses.name: I Chronicles 28:12
verses.text: and the plan of all <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞that he had in mind⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “that was in the spirit with him”</note> for the courtyards of the house of Yahweh and for all the surrounding storage rooms, the treasuries of the house of God, and the treasuries for sanctified objects,

verses.name: I Chronicles 28:13
verses.text: and for the working groups of the priests and the Levites, and for all the work of the service of the house of Yahweh, and for all the vessels for the service of the house of Yahweh,

verses.name: I Chronicles 28:14
verses.text: <transChange type="added">and</transChange> for the gold, according to the weight of the gold for all the vessels of the service, and the service of all the vessels of silver according to the weight of all the vessels <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞for every kind of service⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “service and service”</note>

verses.name: I Chronicles 28:15
verses.text: And the weight of the golden lampstands and the golden lamps, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the weight of each lampstand and each lamp⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “by weight of lampstand and lampstand, with its lamp and to the lamps”</note> and the silver according to the weight of a lampstand and its lamp, according to the use of <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞each lampstand⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “lampstand and lampstand”</note>

verses.name: I Chronicles 28:16
verses.text: and the weight of gold for the tables of the arranged <transChange type="added">bread</transChange>, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞each table⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to table and table”</note> and silver for the tables of silver,

verses.name: I Chronicles 28:17
verses.text: and pure gold <transChange type="added">for</transChange> the three-pronged meat forks, and the bowls and the pitchers, and for the golden bowls, by weight for <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞each bowl⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “for bowl and bowl”</note> and for the silver bowls, by weight for <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞each bowl⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “for bowl and bowl”</note>

verses.name: I Chronicles 28:18
verses.text: and for the altar of incense <transChange type="added">made of</transChange> refined gold, by weight, and gold for the plan for the chariot—the cherubim with outspread and covering wings over the ark of the covenant of Yahweh.

verses.name: I Chronicles 28:19
verses.text: “All this <transChange type="added">I give you</transChange> in writing; from the hand of Yahweh he instructed me <transChange type="added">about</transChange> all the workings of this plan.”  <div eID="gen3163" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 28:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2342"/><div sID="gen3164" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2342"/>Then David said to Solomon his son, “Be strong and courageous, and do <transChange type="added">this</transChange>! Do not be afraid and do not be dismayed, for Yahweh God, my God, <transChange type="added">is</transChange> with you. He will not fail you and will not forsake you until all the work of the service of the house of Yahweh is finished.

verses.name: I Chronicles 28:21
verses.text: And behold, the working groups of the priests and the Levites for all the service of the house of God; and with you in all the work for all <transChange type="added">those</transChange> willing with the skill for every service, and the commanders and all the people for all your commands.”  <chapter eID="1Chr.28"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 29:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2343"/><title type="x-s">Offerings for the Temple</title> <div sID="gen3165" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2343"/>Then David the king said to all the assembly, “God has chosen Solomon my son alone, a young man and inexperienced, and the work <transChange type="added">is</transChange> great, for the citadel <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not for humankind, but for Yahweh God.

verses.name: I Chronicles 29:2
verses.text: So I have provided for the house of my God according to all my strength, the gold for the things of gold, the silver for the things of silver, the bronze for the things of bronze, the iron for the things of iron, and the wood for the things of wood, <transChange type="added">along with</transChange> an abundance of onyx stones, stones for settings, stones of turquoise, and variegated stones, and all <transChange type="added">kinds of</transChange> precious stones and alabaster stones.

verses.name: I Chronicles 29:3
verses.text: And moreover, with respect to my provisions for the house of my God I have a treasure of gold and silver that I have given to the house of my God above all that I have provided for the holy house:

verses.name: I Chronicles 29:4
verses.text: three thousand talents of gold from the gold of Ophir and seven thousand talents of refined silver to overlay the walls of the houses,

verses.name: I Chronicles 29:5
verses.text: gold for the golden things and silver for the silver things, for all the work by the hand of skilled craftsmen. Now who will offer willingly, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞consecrating himself⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to consecrate his hand”</note> today to Yahweh?”  <div eID="gen3165" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 29:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2344"/><div sID="gen3166" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2344"/>Then the commanders of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞families⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “fathers”</note> the commanders of the tribes of Israel, and the commanders of thousands and hundreds, and the commanders of the work of the king offered themselves willingly.

verses.name: I Chronicles 29:7
verses.text: And they gave for the service of the house of God five thousand talents and ten thousand darics of gold, ten thousand talents of silver, eighteen thousand talents of bronze, and one hundred thousand talents of iron.

verses.name: I Chronicles 29:8
verses.text: And whoever had <transChange type="added">precious</transChange> stones gave <transChange type="added">them</transChange> to the treasury of the house of Yahweh under the authority<note placement="foot">Or “hand”</note> of Jehiel the Gershonite.

verses.name: I Chronicles 29:9
verses.text: And the people rejoiced over their freewill offering, for with a whole heart they had willingly offered to Yahweh, and King David also rejoiced with great joy.  <div eID="gen3166" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 29:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2345"/><div sID="gen3167" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2345"/>Then David blessed Yahweh in the sight of all the assembly, and David said, “Blessed <transChange type="added">are</transChange> you, O Yahweh, God of Israel, our father forever and ever!

verses.name: I Chronicles 29:11
verses.text: To you, O Yahweh, <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the greatness and the power and the splendor and the glory and the strength, for everything in the heavens and in the earth. Yours, O Yahweh, <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the kingdom and exaltation over all as head!

verses.name: I Chronicles 29:12
verses.text: And wealth and glory <transChange type="added">are</transChange> from you, and you rule over all. And in your hand <transChange type="added">is</transChange> power and might. And in your hand <transChange type="added">is power</transChange> to make great and to give strength to all.

verses.name: I Chronicles 29:13
verses.text: And now, our God, we give thanks to you and offer praise to the name of your splendor.

verses.name: I Chronicles 29:14
verses.text: And indeed, who <transChange type="added">am</transChange> I, and who <transChange type="added">are</transChange> my people that we retain power to offer according to these <transChange type="added">offerings</transChange> willingly? For everything <transChange type="added">is</transChange> from you, and from your hand we have given to you.

verses.name: I Chronicles 29:15
verses.text: For we <transChange type="added">are</transChange> strangers before you and sojourners like all our ancestors.<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> Our days <transChange type="added">are</transChange> like the shadow upon earth, and there is no hope <transChange type="added">of abiding</transChange>.

verses.name: I Chronicles 29:16
verses.text: O Yahweh our God, all this abundance that we have provided to build for you a house for your holy name is from your hand, and all <transChange type="added">of it</transChange> is yours.

verses.name: I Chronicles 29:17
verses.text: And I know, my God, that you yourself test the heart and are pleased with uprightness. I, in the uprightness of my heart, have willingly offered all these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, and now I have seen your people who are found here willingly offer to you.

verses.name: I Chronicles 29:18
verses.text: O Yahweh, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, our ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> keep this forever as a plan <transChange type="added">and</transChange> thoughts of the heart of your people, and establish their heart toward you.

verses.name: I Chronicles 29:19
verses.text: Grant to Solomon my son a heart of peace to keep your commands, your statutes, and your regulations to do everything, and to build the citadel for which I have provided.”

verses.name: I Chronicles 29:20
verses.text: And David said to all the assembly, “Bless Yahweh your God!” And all the assembly blessed Yahweh, the God of their ancestors.<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> And they bowed down and prostrated themselves before Yahweh and the king.  <div eID="gen3167" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 29:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2346"/><title type="x-s">Solomon’s Coronation</title> <div sID="gen3168" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2346"/>And they offered sacrifices to Yahweh, and on that next day they offered burnt offerings to Yahweh: one thousand bulls, one thousand rams, one thousand lambs, with their libations and sacrifices in abundance for all Israel.

verses.name: I Chronicles 29:22
verses.text: And they ate and drank before Yahweh on that day with great joy. And they made Solomon the son of David king the second time, and they anointed <transChange type="added">him</transChange> commander for Yahweh, and Zadok the priest.  <div eID="gen3168" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 29:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2347"/><div sID="gen3169" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2347"/>Then Solomon sat upon the throne of Yahweh as king in place of David his father. And he prospered, and all Israel obeyed him.

verses.name: I Chronicles 29:24
verses.text: And all the officials and mighty warriors, and also all the sons of King David, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞pledged allegiance to⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “placed a hand under”</note> King Solomon.

verses.name: I Chronicles 29:25
verses.text: And Yahweh made Solomon exceedingly great in the sight of all Israel, and he bestowed upon him royal splendor that was not <transChange type="added">bestowed</transChange> upon any king before him in Israel.  <div eID="gen3169" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 29:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2348"/><title type="x-s">The Death of King David</title> <div sID="gen3170" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2348"/>And David the son of Jesse reigned over all Israel.

verses.name: I Chronicles 29:27
verses.text: And the days that he reigned over Israel <transChange type="added">were</transChange> forty years. In Hebron he reigned seven years, and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty-three years.

verses.name: I Chronicles 29:28
verses.text: And he died in a good old age, full of days, wealth, and honor. And Solomon his son reigned in his place.

verses.name: I Chronicles 29:29
verses.text: Now the words of King David, <transChange type="added">from</transChange> the first to the last, see, they are written among the words of Samuel the seer, and among the words of Nathan the prophet, and among the words of Gad the seer,

verses.name: I Chronicles 29:30
verses.text: with all <transChange type="added">the accounts of</transChange> his kingdom, his power, and the times that came upon him, and upon Israel, and upon all the kingdoms of the earth.  <chapter eID="1Chr.29"/> <div eID="gen3170" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen2984" osisID="1Chr" type="book"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 1:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2349"/><title type="x-s">Solomon Worships at Gibeon</title> <div sID="gen3172" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2349"/>And Solomon the son of David strengthened himself concerning his kingdom, and Yahweh his God <transChange type="added">was</transChange> with him and made him exceedingly great.

verses.name: II Chronicles 1:2
verses.text: And Solomon spoke to all Israel, to the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and to the judges, and to all the leaders for all Israel, the heads of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞families⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “fathers”</note>

verses.name: II Chronicles 1:3
verses.text: And Solomon and the whole assembly with him went to the high place that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> at Gibeon, for the tent of assembly<note placement="foot">Or “meeting”</note> of God that Moses the servant of Yahweh had made in the desert was there.

verses.name: II Chronicles 1:4
verses.text: (But the ark of God David had brought up from Kiriath-Jearim to <transChange type="added">the place</transChange> David had prepared for it, for David had pitched a tent for it in Jerusalem.)

verses.name: II Chronicles 1:5
verses.text: And the bronze altar that Bezalel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, had made <transChange type="added">was</transChange> there before the tabernacle of Yahweh. And Solomon and the assembly sought it out.

verses.name: II Chronicles 1:6
verses.text: And Solomon went up there to the bronze altar before Yahweh, which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> at the tent of assembly,<note placement="foot">Or “meeting”</note> and he offered upon it a thousand burnt offerings.  <div eID="gen3172" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 1:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2350"/><title type="x-s">Solomon’s Prayer for Wisdom</title> <div sID="gen3173" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2350"/>On that night God appeared to Solomon and said to him, “Ask what I shall give to you.”

verses.name: II Chronicles 1:8
verses.text: Then Solomon said to God, “You yourself have shown steadfast<note placement="foot">Or “great”</note> loyal love to David my father and have made me king in his place.

verses.name: II Chronicles 1:9
verses.text: Now, O Yahweh God, let your word to David my father be fulfilled, for you yourself have made me king over a people as numerous as the dust of the earth.

verses.name: II Chronicles 1:10
verses.text: Now, give to me wisdom and knowledge that I may go out and come in before this people, for who can judge this, your great people?”  <div eID="gen3173" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 1:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2351"/><div sID="gen3174" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2351"/>Then God said to Solomon, “Because this was with your heart and you did not ask for wealth, possessions, honor, and the lives of your enemies, and also did not ask for <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞long life⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “many days”</note> but have asked for wisdom and knowledge that you might judge my people over whom I have made you king,

verses.name: II Chronicles 1:12
verses.text: wisdom and knowledge is given to you. And I will <transChange type="added">also</transChange> give to you wealth, possessions, and honor, the like of which was not had by the kings who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> before you, nor will there be the like after you.”

verses.name: II Chronicles 1:13
verses.text: So Solomon went from the high place which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> at Gibeon <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Jerusalem before the tent of assembly.<note placement="foot">Or “meeting”</note> And he reigned over Israel.  <div eID="gen3174" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 1:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2352"/><title type="x-s">Solomon’s Wealth</title> <div sID="gen3175" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2352"/>And Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen. And he had one thousand four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, and he placed them in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 1:15
verses.text: And the king made silver and gold in Jerusalem like the stones. And he made cedar as abundant as the sycamore fig trees that <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in the Shephelah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 1:16
verses.text: And Solomon’s horses <transChange type="added">were</transChange> imported from Egypt and from Kue. The traders of the king received <transChange type="added">them</transChange> from Kue at a price.

verses.name: II Chronicles 1:17
verses.text: They went up and exported a chariot from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver and a horse for one hundred and fifty <transChange type="added">shekels</transChange>. And <transChange type="added">these were</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞likewise exported⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “likewise through their hand”</note> to all the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Aram.<note placement="foot">Or “Syria”</note>  <chapter eID="2Chr.1"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 2:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2353"/><title type="x-s">Solomon Petitions the King of Tyre</title> <div sID="gen3176" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2353"/><note placement="foot"><reference osisRef="2Chr.2.1-2Chr.2.18">2 Chronicles 2:1–18 </reference>in the English Bible is 1:18–2:17 in the Hebrew Bible</note> And Solomon planned to build a house for the name of Yahweh and a <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞royal palace for himself⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “house for his kingdom”</note>

verses.name: II Chronicles 2:2
verses.text: And Solomon assigned seventy thousand men <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to bear burdens⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “carriers”</note> and eighty thousand <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞quarriers⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “stone craftsmen”</note> in the hill country, and three thousand six hundred <transChange type="added">men</transChange> to supervise them.

verses.name: II Chronicles 2:3
verses.text: And Solomon sent <transChange type="added">word</transChange> to Huram<note placement="foot">This is the spelling in Hebrew, though many translations have “Hiram”</note> king of Tyre, saying, “As you have dealt with David my father and sent cedar to him to build for himself a house in which to live, <transChange type="added">please deal with me</transChange>.

verses.name: II Chronicles 2:4
verses.text: Look, I am building a house for the name of Yahweh my God to dedicate to him, to offer sweet spices of incense before him, and <transChange type="added">for</transChange> the regular rows <transChange type="added">of bread</transChange>, and burnt offerings for mornings, evenings, Sabbaths, and new moon festivals, and for appointed feasts of Yahweh our God which <transChange type="added">are</transChange> everlasting for Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 2:5
verses.text: And the house that I am building <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> great, for our God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> greater than all gods.

verses.name: II Chronicles 2:6
verses.text: Now who indeed has adequate strength to build a house for him? For the heavens and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the highest heavens⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the heavens of the heavens”</note> are not able to contain him. Now who <transChange type="added">am</transChange> I that I would build a house for him, except to burn incense before him?

verses.name: II Chronicles 2:7
verses.text: So then, send to me skilled men to work with gold, silver, bronze, and iron, and with purple, crimson, and blue fabric, knowledgeable in engraving, with the skilled men who <transChange type="added">are</transChange> with me in Judah and in Jerusalem, whom David my father has established.

verses.name: II Chronicles 2:8
verses.text: Send me trees of cedar, cypress, and algum from Lebanon, for I myself know that your servants <transChange type="added">are</transChange> knowledgeable in cutting the trees of Lebanon. Now see, my servants <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> with your servants

verses.name: II Chronicles 2:9
verses.text: to prepare trees in abundance for me, for the house that I am building <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> great and wonderful.

verses.name: II Chronicles 2:10
verses.text: Now see, I will provide twenty thousand dry measures of crushed wheat, twenty thousand dry measures of barley, twenty thousand baths of wine, and twenty thousand baths of oil to the woodcarvers and those who cut timber.”  <div eID="gen3176" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 2:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2354"/><div sID="gen3177" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2354"/>Then Huram<note placement="foot">This is the spelling in Hebrew, though many translations have “Hiram”</note> king of Tyre answered in a letter, and he sent <transChange type="added">word</transChange> to Solomon: “Because Yahweh loves his people, he has made you king over them.”

verses.name: II Chronicles 2:12
verses.text: Then Huram<note placement="foot">This is the spelling in Hebrew, though many translations have “Hiram”</note> said, “Blessed be Yahweh, the God of Israel, who has made the heavens and the earth, who has given to King David a wise son knowing discretion and understanding, who will build for Yahweh a house and a royal palace for himself.

verses.name: II Chronicles 2:13
verses.text: So now I have sent a skilled man, knowledgeable <transChange type="added">and with</transChange> understanding: my master<note placement="foot">Or “my father”</note> Huram,

verses.name: II Chronicles 2:14
verses.text: a son of a woman from the daughters of Dan, and his father <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a man of Tyre, knowledgeable for working with gold, silver, bronze, iron, stone, and wood, and with purple, blue, and crimson fabric, and with fine linen, for engraving any engraving and devising any plan that is given to him, with your skilled men and the skilled men of my lord David your father.

verses.name: II Chronicles 2:15
verses.text: Now as for the wheat, barley, oil, and wine that my lord mentioned, let him send <transChange type="added">that</transChange> to his servants.

verses.name: II Chronicles 2:16
verses.text: And we ourselves will cut trees from Lebanon according to all your need, and we will bring them to you on rafts over the sea to Joppa, so that you may bring them up to Jerusalem.”  <div eID="gen3177" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 2:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2355"/><div sID="gen3178" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2355"/>Then Solomon counted all the resident alien men who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in the land of Israel after the census that David his father had taken of them. And there were found one hundred and fifty-three thousand.

verses.name: II Chronicles 2:18
verses.text: And he appointed from them seventy thousand <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to bear burdens⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “carriers”</note> eighty thousand <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to quarry⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “stone craftsmen”</note> in the hill country, and three thousand six hundred overseers to make the people work.  <chapter eID="2Chr.2"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 3:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2356"/><title type="x-s">Solomon Builds the Temple</title> <div sID="gen3179" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2356"/>Then Solomon began to build the house of Yahweh in Jerusalem, on Mount Moriah, where Yahweh had appeared to David his father, at the place that David had established, on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.

verses.name: II Chronicles 3:2
verses.text: And he began to build in the second month of the fourth year of his reign.  <div eID="gen3179" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 3:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2357"/><div sID="gen3180" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2357"/>Now these <transChange type="added">were</transChange> the measurements of Solomon for building the house of God: the length in cubits by the former measurement <transChange type="added">was</transChange> sixty cubits, and the width <transChange type="added">was</transChange> twenty cubits.

verses.name: II Chronicles 3:4
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞The length of the portico that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in front was the same as the front of the width of the house⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>:<note placement="foot">Literally “The length at the front of the portico the front of the width of the house”</note> twenty cubits. And its height <transChange type="added">was</transChange> one hundred and twenty cubits. And he overlaid it on the inside with pure gold.

verses.name: II Chronicles 3:5
verses.text: And the great house <transChange type="added">itself</transChange> he covered with cypress wood, then he overlaid it with pure gold. And he put on it palm tree <transChange type="added">images</transChange> and <transChange type="added">ornate</transChange> chains.

verses.name: II Chronicles 3:6
verses.text: Then he overlaid the house with precious stone as decoration. (Now the gold <transChange type="added">was</transChange> the gold of Parvaim.)

verses.name: II Chronicles 3:7
verses.text: And he overlaid the house with gold—the beams, the thresholds, the walls, and the doors. And he carved cherubim upon the walls.

verses.name: II Chronicles 3:8
verses.text: Then he made <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the most holy place⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the house of the holy of the holies”</note> Its length <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞was equal to⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “at the front of”</note> the width of the house: twenty cubits. And its breadth <transChange type="added">was</transChange> twenty cubits. And he overlaid it with six hundred talents of fine gold.

verses.name: II Chronicles 3:9
verses.text: And the weight for the nails <transChange type="added">was</transChange> fifty shekels of gold. And he overlaid its upper rooms with gold.

verses.name: II Chronicles 3:10
verses.text: And he made two sculpted wood cherubim in <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the most holy place⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the house of the holy of the holies”</note> and he overlaid them with gold.

verses.name: II Chronicles 3:11
verses.text: The length of the <transChange type="added">outstretched</transChange> wings of the cherubim <transChange type="added">were</transChange> twenty cubits; one wing of five cubits touched the wall of the house, and the other wing of five cubits <transChange type="added">was</transChange> touching the <transChange type="added">outstretched</transChange> wing of the other cherub.

verses.name: II Chronicles 3:12
verses.text: And the wing of five cubits of the other cherub <transChange type="added">was</transChange> touching the wall of the house, and its other wing five cubits long touching the wing of the first<note placement="foot">Or “other”</note> cherub.

verses.name: II Chronicles 3:13
verses.text: The wings of these cherubim extended twenty cubits, and they were standing on their feet, their faces toward the house.

verses.name: II Chronicles 3:14
verses.text: And he made the curtain of blue and purple and crimson and fine linen, and put cherubim on it.

verses.name: II Chronicles 3:15
verses.text: And at the front of the house he made two columns, thirty-five cubits high, and the capital on their top was five cubits.

verses.name: II Chronicles 3:16
verses.text: And he made <transChange type="added">decorative</transChange> chains in the inner sanctuary and put <transChange type="added">them</transChange> on top of the columns. And he made one hundred pomegranate <transChange type="added">ornaments</transChange>, and put them on the chains.

verses.name: II Chronicles 3:17
verses.text: And he erected the columns in front of the temple, one on the south and one on the north. He called the name of the southern one Jakin, and the name of the northern one Boaz.  <chapter eID="2Chr.3"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 4:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2358"/><title type="x-s">The Furnishings of Solomon’s Temple</title> <div sID="gen3181" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2358"/>And he made an altar of bronze, twenty cubits <transChange type="added">was</transChange> its length, and twenty cubits <transChange type="added">was</transChange> its width, and ten cubits <transChange type="added">was</transChange> its height.

verses.name: II Chronicles 4:2
verses.text: Then he made the sea of molten metal, from brim to brim <transChange type="added">it was</transChange> ten cubits, completely round. And <transChange type="added">it was</transChange> five cubits in height, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞its circumference measured⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and it measured a line all around it”</note> thirty cubits.

verses.name: II Chronicles 4:3
verses.text: Under it <transChange type="added">were</transChange> figures of oxen all around it, ten cubits <transChange type="added">high</transChange>, encircling the sea all around. The oxen <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in two rows <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞cast as one piece with it⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “molten with its casting”</note>

verses.name: II Chronicles 4:4
verses.text: <transChange type="added">It was</transChange> standing upon twelve oxen, three facing north, and three facing west, and three facing south, and three facing east. The sea <transChange type="added">was set</transChange> upon them from above, and all their hindquarters <transChange type="added">faced</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞inward⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “into the house”</note>

verses.name: II Chronicles 4:5
verses.text: And its thickness <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a handbreadth, and its brim <transChange type="added">was</transChange> like the working of the lip of a cup, the blossom of a lily. And it held three thousand baths.

verses.name: II Chronicles 4:6
verses.text: And he made ten basins. And he set five on the south and five on the north in which to wash; they washed off the work of the burnt offering in them, but the sea <transChange type="added">was</transChange> for the priests to wash therein.

verses.name: II Chronicles 4:7
verses.text: And he made ten golden lampstands according to their custom, and he set <transChange type="added">them</transChange> in the temple, five on the south and five on the north.

verses.name: II Chronicles 4:8
verses.text: And he made ten tables and placed them in the temple, five on the south and five on the north. And he made a hundred drinking bowls of gold.

verses.name: II Chronicles 4:9
verses.text: And he made the courtyard of the priests and the great outer courtyard and the doors for the outer court. And he overlaid their doors with bronze.

verses.name: II Chronicles 4:10
verses.text: And he set the sea at the southeast <transChange type="added">corner of the temple</transChange>.

verses.name: II Chronicles 4:11
verses.text: And Huram<note placement="foot">This is the spelling in Hebrew, though many translations have “Hiram”</note> made the pots, the shovels, and the drinking bowls. So Hiram<note placement="foot">The spelling (“Hiram”) is different here than in the previous occurrences</note> finished making the work that he made on the house of God for King Solomon:

verses.name: II Chronicles 4:12
verses.text: the two columns, the bowls, and the two capitals on top of the columns, and the two latticeworks to cover the two bowls of the capitals that <transChange type="added">were</transChange> on top of the columns,

verses.name: II Chronicles 4:13
verses.text: and the four hundred pomegranates for the two latticeworks, two rows of pomegranates for the latticework, to cover the two bowls of the capitals that <transChange type="added">were</transChange> before the columns.

verses.name: II Chronicles 4:14
verses.text: And he made the water carts, and he made the basins on the water carts,

verses.name: II Chronicles 4:15
verses.text: and the one sea and the twelve oxen underneath it.  <div eID="gen3181" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 4:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2359"/><div sID="gen3182" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2359"/>And Huram-abi made for King Solomon the pots, the shovels, the three-pronged meat forks, and all the utensils of polished bronze for the house of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Chronicles 4:17
verses.text: The king cast them in the plain of the Jordan, in the clay soil between Succoth and Zeredah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 4:18
verses.text: Solomon made all these utensils in great abundance, for the weight of the bronze could not be determined.

verses.name: II Chronicles 4:19
verses.text: So Solomon made all the objects that <transChange type="added">were in</transChange> the house of God: the altar of gold; the tables upon which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> the bread of the presence;

verses.name: II Chronicles 4:20
verses.text: the lampstands, and the lamps for burning according to the custom before the inner sanctuary, of solid gold;

verses.name: II Chronicles 4:21
verses.text: and the blossoms, the lamps, and the tongs that <transChange type="added">were</transChange> of solid gold;

verses.name: II Chronicles 4:22
verses.text: and the snuffers, the drinking bowls, the dishes, and the firepans, of solid gold; and the entrance to the house, the inner doors to <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the most holy place⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>, and the doors to the house of the temple <transChange type="added">were</transChange> of gold.  <chapter eID="2Chr.4"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 5:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2360"/><title type="x-s">The Ark Installed in the Temple</title> <div sID="gen3183" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2360"/>When all the work that Solomon did for the house of Yahweh was finished, Solomon brought the holy objects of David his father: the silver, the gold, and all the objects he had put into the storehouses of the house of God.

verses.name: II Chronicles 5:2
verses.text: Then Solomon assembled all the elders of Israel and all the heads of the tribes, the leaders of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞families⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “fathers”</note> for the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> to Jerusalem in order to bring up the ark of the covenant of Yahweh from the city of David, which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> Zion.

verses.name: II Chronicles 5:3
verses.text: And all the men of Israel assembled before the king at the feast that <transChange type="added">is in</transChange> the seventh month.

verses.name: II Chronicles 5:4
verses.text: And all the elders of Israel came, and the Levites took up the ark.

verses.name: II Chronicles 5:5
verses.text: And they brought up the ark, the tent of assembly,<note placement="foot">Or “meeting”</note> and all the holy objects that <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in the tent; the Levitical priests brought them up.

verses.name: II Chronicles 5:6
verses.text: And King Solomon and the whole community of Israel that was assembled before him <transChange type="added">were</transChange> before the ark, sacrificing sheep and cattle that could not be counted nor numbered for abundance.

verses.name: II Chronicles 5:7
verses.text: Then the priests brought up the ark of the covenant of Yahweh to its place in the inner sanctuary of the house, into <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the most holy place⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>, underneath the wings of the cherubim.

verses.name: II Chronicles 5:8
verses.text: The cherubim were spreading <transChange type="added">their</transChange> wings over the place of the ark, so that the cherubim were covering the ark and over its poles <transChange type="added">from</transChange> above.

verses.name: II Chronicles 5:9
verses.text: But the poles were <transChange type="added">so</transChange> long that the ends of the poles from the ark were seen from before the inner sanctuary, but they could not be seen from the outside. And they are there until this day.

verses.name: II Chronicles 5:10
verses.text: There was nothing in the ark but the two stone tablets that Moses had put <transChange type="added">inside</transChange> at Horeb <transChange type="added">on</transChange> which Yahweh had <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞made⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “cut”</note> a covenant with the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> when they went out from Egypt.

verses.name: II Chronicles 5:11
verses.text: And when the priests came out of the sanctuary (for all the priests who were present<note placement="foot">Or “who were found”</note> sanctified themselves without keeping their divisions)

verses.name: II Chronicles 5:12
verses.text: and all the Levitical singers—Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun, their sons, their brothers, dressed <transChange type="added">in</transChange> fine linen, with cymbals, harps, and stringed instruments—<transChange type="added">they</transChange> were standing to the east of the altar. And with them outside <transChange type="added">were</transChange> one hundred and twenty priests <transChange type="added">who were</transChange> trumpet blowers.

verses.name: II Chronicles 5:13
verses.text: And it was the primary <transChange type="added">duty</transChange> of the trumpeters and singers to make themselves heard <transChange type="added">with</transChange> one voice, to praise and give thanks to Yahweh. And when a sound from the trumpets, cymbals, and other instruments of song was raised to Yahweh—for he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> good, because his loyal love <transChange type="added">is</transChange> everlasting—then the house, the house of Yahweh, was filled with a cloud.

verses.name: II Chronicles 5:14
verses.text: And the priests were not able to stand to minister because of the cloud, for the glory of Yahweh filled the house of God.  <chapter eID="2Chr.5"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2361"/><title type="x-s">Solomon Blesses the People</title> <div sID="gen3184" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2361"/>Then Solomon said, “Yahweh has decided<note placement="foot">Or “said”</note> to dwell in the deep gloom.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:2
verses.text: But I have built for you an exalted house, even a place for you to dwell in forever.”

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:3
verses.text: Then the king turned around<note placement="foot">Or “turned his face”</note> and blessed all the assembly of Israel, and all the assembly of Israel were standing.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:4
verses.text: And he said, “Blessed be Yahweh, the God of Israel, who spoke with his mouth with David my father, and with his hands he has fulfilled <transChange type="added">it</transChange>, saying,

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:5
verses.text: ‘From the day that I brought my people out of the land of Egypt I did not choose a city among all the tribes of Israel to build a house in order for my name <transChange type="added">to be</transChange> there. Nor did I choose a man to be leader over my people Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:6
verses.text: But I have chosen my name to be there in Jerusalem, and I have chosen David to be over my people Israel.’

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:7
verses.text: Now, it was in the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of Yahweh, the God of Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:8
verses.text: But Yahweh said to David my father, ‘Because it was in your heart to build a house for my name, you did well that it was in your heart,

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:9
verses.text: but you yourself will not build the house, but your son who will proceed from your loins; he himself will build the house for my name.’

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:10
verses.text: Now Yahweh has fulfilled his word that he spoke. I have risen in the place of David my father and am seated on the throne of Israel as Yahweh has spoken. I have built the house for the name of Yahweh, the God of Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:11
verses.text: And I have there the ark <transChange type="added">in</transChange> which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the covenant of Yahweh that he <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞made⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “cut”</note> with the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note>  <div eID="gen3184" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2362"/><title type="x-s">Solomon’s Prayer to Dedicate the Temple</title> <div sID="gen3185" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2362"/>Then Solomon stood before the altar of Yahweh before all the assembly of Israel and spread out his hands.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:13
verses.text: (For Solomon had made a platform of bronze five cubits long and five cubits wide and three cubits high, and placed it in the midst of the outer court.) And he stood upon it, then knelt down on his knees before the whole assembly of Israel and spread out his hands to heaven.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:14
verses.text: And he said, “O Yahweh, God of Israel, there is none like you, a God in the heavens and on the earth, keeping the covenant and loyal love with your servants who walk before you with all their heart,

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:15
verses.text: that you have kept for your servant David my father what you spoke to him. You spoke with your mouth, and by your hand you have fulfilled <transChange type="added">it</transChange> on this day.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:16
verses.text: And now, O Yahweh, God of Israel, keep for your servant David, my father, what you have spoken to him, saying, ‘<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞You shall not lack⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “There shall not be cut off”</note> a man to sit on the throne of Israel before me, if only your sons keep their way, to walk in my law as you have walked before me.’

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:17
verses.text: And now, O Yahweh, God of Israel, let your word that you have spoken to your servant David be confirmed.  <div eID="gen3185" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2363"/><div sID="gen3186" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2363"/>“But will God indeed dwell with humankind upon the earth? Look, the heavens and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the highest heavens⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the heavens of the heavens”</note> cannot contain you! Surely then this house that I have built <transChange type="added">will not contain you!</transChange>

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:19
verses.text: But turn to the prayer of your servant and to his plea, O Yahweh my God, to hearken to the pleading and to the prayer that your servant is praying before you,

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:20
verses.text: that your eyes may be open day and night to this house, to the place that you have promised to place your name there, that you may hear the prayer that your servant has prayed to this place.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:21
verses.text: And listen to the pleas of your servant and your people Israel when they pray toward this place, that you yourself might hear from the place of your dwelling, from the heavens, that you might hear and forgive.  <div eID="gen3186" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2364"/><div sID="gen3187" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2364"/>“If a man sins against his neighbor and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞makes him swear an oath⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “places upon him an oath to swear an oath”</note> and comes <transChange type="added">with</transChange> an oath before your altar in this house,

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:23
verses.text: then may you yourself hear from the heavens and act and judge your servants, to repay the guilty by bringing his way upon his head and to vindicate the righteous by giving to him according to his righteousness.  <div eID="gen3187" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2365"/><div sID="gen3188" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2365"/>“And if your people Israel are defeated before an enemy because they have sinned against you and they repent and confess your name and pray and plead before you in this house,

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:25
verses.text: then may you yourself hear from the heavens and forgive the sin of your people Israel and again bring them back to the land that you gave to them and to their ancestors.<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note>  <div eID="gen3188" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2366"/><div sID="gen3189" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2366"/>“When the heavens are stopped up and there is no rain because they have sinned against you and they pray to this place and confess your name and turn back from their sin when you humble them,

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:27
verses.text: then may you yourself hear from the heavens and forgive the sin of your servants and your people Israel, when you teach them the good way in which they should walk, and give rain upon your land that you have given to your people as an inheritance.  <div eID="gen3189" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2367"/><div sID="gen3190" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2367"/>“If there is a famine in the land; if there is disease, blight, mildew, locust, and caterpillar; if it happens that his enemy lays siege to him in the land <transChange type="added">and</transChange> his gates; any kind of plague, any kind of disease,

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:29
verses.text: <transChange type="added">then</transChange> any prayer, any plea that is <transChange type="added">made</transChange> by any person and by all your people Israel, each one who knows his own affliction and his own anguish and <transChange type="added">who</transChange> spreads out his hands to this house,

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:30
verses.text: then may you yourself hear from the heavens, your dwelling place, and forgive and give to each according to all his ways, since you know the heart of the children of humankind,

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:31
verses.text: that they may fear you <transChange type="added">and</transChange> walk in your ways all the days that they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> alive upon the face of the land that you have given to our ancestors.<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note>  <div eID="gen3190" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2368"/><div sID="gen3191" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2368"/>“And also, with respect to the foreigner, he who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not of your people Israel, but comes from a distant land, for the sake of your great name and your powerful hand and outstretched arm, when he comes and prays to this house,

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:33
verses.text: then may you yourself hear from the heavens, from your dwelling place, and do according to all that the foreigner asks of you, so that all peoples of earth will know of your name and fear you, as <transChange type="added">do</transChange> your people Israel, and that they may know that your name <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞possesses⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “is called over”</note> this house that I have built.  <div eID="gen3191" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:34
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2369"/><div sID="gen3192" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2369"/>“When your people go out to battle against their enemy according to the way that you have sent them, and they pray to you toward this city that you have chosen and the house that I have built for your name,

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:35
verses.text: then may you hear their prayer and their pleas from the heavens and uphold their case.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:36
verses.text: When they sin against you—for there is no person who does not sin—and you become angry with them and place them before their enemy that they carry them away as captives to a land far or near,

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:37
verses.text: but <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞if they repent⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “if they turn back to their heart”</note> in the land where they were taken captive and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞repent⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “turn back”</note> and beg you for mercy in the land of their captivity, saying, ‘We have sinned and acted perversely and done wickedly,

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:38
verses.text: and we return to you,’ with their whole heart and with all their inmost being in the land of their captivity where they took them captive, and <transChange type="added">if</transChange> they pray toward their land that you have given to their ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and the city that you have chosen and to the house that I have built for your name,

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:39
verses.text: then may you hear their prayer and their pleas from the heavens, from your dwelling place, and uphold their case and forgive your people who sinned against you.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:40
verses.text: Now, O my God, please let your eyes be open and your ears attentive to the prayer of this place!  <div eID="gen3192" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:41
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2370"/><div sID="gen3193" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2370"/>“And now arise, O Yahweh God, to your resting place, you and the ark of your strength! O Yahweh God, let the priests be clothed with salvation, and let your holy ones rejoice in your goodness!

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:42
verses.text: O Yahweh God, do not turn away the face of your anointed one! Remember the loyal love of your servant, David!”  <chapter eID="2Chr.6"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2371"/><title type="x-s">God Answers with Fire from Heaven</title> <div sID="gen3194" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2371"/>And when Solomon finished praying, then fire came down from heaven and consumed the burnt offering and the sacrifices, and the glory of Yahweh filled the house.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:2
verses.text: And the priests were not able to go into the house of Yahweh, for the glory of Yahweh had filled the house.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:3
verses.text: When all the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> saw the fire come down and the glory of Yahweh upon the house, they knelt down <transChange type="added">with their</transChange> faces to the ground on the pavement and worshiped and gave thanks to Yahweh, for <transChange type="added">he is</transChange> good, for his loyal love <transChange type="added">is</transChange> everlasting.  <div eID="gen3194" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2372"/><title type="x-s">The Temple Dedication</title> <div sID="gen3195" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2372"/>Then the king and all the people were offering a sacrifice before Yahweh.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:5
verses.text: And King Solomon offered a sacrifice of twenty-two thousand cattle and one hundred and twenty thousand sheep. So the king and all the people dedicated the house of God.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:6
verses.text: And the priests stood at their posts with the Levites, with the instruments of the song of Yahweh that King David had made to give thanks to Yahweh—for his loyal love <transChange type="added">is</transChange> everlasting—whenever David offered praise by their hand. Now the priests sounded trumpets <transChange type="added">standing</transChange> opposite them, and all Israel stood.  <div eID="gen3195" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2373"/><div sID="gen3196" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2373"/>And Solomon consecrated the middle of the courtyard that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> before the house of Yahweh, for there he had made the burnt offerings and the fat of the fellowship offerings, for the bronze altar that Solomon had made was not able to hold the burnt offerings, cereal offerings, and the fat.  <div eID="gen3196" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2374"/><div sID="gen3197" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2374"/>And Solomon held<note placement="foot">Or “made”</note> a feast at that time <transChange type="added">of</transChange> seven days. And all Israel <transChange type="added">was</transChange> with him, a very great assembly, from Lebo-Hamath to the river of Egypt.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:9
verses.text: And on the eighth day they made a solemn assembly, for they held<note placement="foot">Or “made”</note> the dedication of the altar seven days and the feast seven days.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:10
verses.text: And on the twenty-third day of the seventh month he sent the people away to their tents rejoicing and festive of heart on account of the goodness that Yahweh had done for David, Solomon, and Israel his people.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:11
verses.text: And Solomon finished the house of Yahweh and the house of the king. And all that came into the heart of Solomon to do with respect to the house of Yahweh and his own house he accomplished.  <div eID="gen3197" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2375"/><title type="x-s">God’s Charge to Solomon</title> <div sID="gen3198" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2375"/>Then Yahweh appeared to Solomon at night and said to him, “I have heard your prayer and have chosen this place for myself as a house of sacrifice.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:13
verses.text: When I hold back the heavens so that there is not rain, and when I command the locust to devour the earth, and if I send disease among my people,

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:14
verses.text: <transChange type="added">then if</transChange> my people who are called by my name will humble themselves and will pray and will seek my face and will turn from their evil ways, then I myself shall hear from the heavens and will forgive their sins and heal their land.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:15
verses.text: Now my eyes will be open and my ears attentive to the prayer of this place.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:16
verses.text: And now I have chosen and consecrated this house for my name to be there forever. My eyes and my heart will be there <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞for all time⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “all the days”</note>

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:17
verses.text: Now <transChange type="added">as for</transChange> you, if you will walk before me as David your father walked and do according to all that I have commanded you and will keep my ordinances and judgments,

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:18
verses.text: then I will establish the throne of your kingdom as I promised<note placement="foot">Or “covenanted”</note> to David your father, saying, ‘A man shall not be cut off for you <transChange type="added">from</transChange> ruling over Israel.’  <div eID="gen3198" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2376"/><div sID="gen3199" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2376"/>“But if you turn yourselves away and forsake my ordinances and my commandments which I have given before you <transChange type="added">all</transChange> and will go and serve other gods and bow down to them,

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:20
verses.text: then I will uproot them from upon my land that I have given to them, and this house that I have consecrated for my name I will send away from before my face, and I will make it a proverb and a taunt among all the nations.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:21
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">as for</transChange> this house, which was exalted, all who pass by it will be appalled and will say, ‘Why has Yahweh done thus to this land and to this house?’

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:22
verses.text: Then they will say, ‘Because they forsook Yahweh, the God of their ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> who brought them out from the land of Egypt, and <transChange type="added">they</transChange> laid hold of other gods and worshiped them and served them. Therefore he has brought upon them all this evil.’ ”  <chapter eID="2Chr.7"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2377"/><title type="x-s">Solomon’s Accomplishments and Deeds</title> <div sID="gen3200" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2377"/>And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> at the end of twenty years <transChange type="added">in</transChange> which Solomon had built the house of Yahweh and his own house,

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:2
verses.text: Solomon also built the cities that Huram<note placement="foot">This is the spelling in Hebrew, though many translations have “Hiram”</note> had given to him, and he settled the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> in them.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:3
verses.text: And Solomon went to Hamath-Zobah and laid siege upon it.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:4
verses.text: And he built Tadmor in the desert, and he built all the storage cities in Hamath.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:5
verses.text: He also built Upper Beth-Horon and Lower Beth-Horon, fortified cities <transChange type="added">with</transChange> walls, gates, and bars;

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:6
verses.text: Baalath and all the storage cities that belonged to Solomon; all the cities for chariots<note placement="foot">Hebrew “chariot”</note> and cities for horses; and any desire of Solomon that he desired to build in Jerusalem, in Lebanon, and in all the land of his dominion.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:7
verses.text: All the people who remained from the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites who were not from Israel,

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:8
verses.text: from the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons/children”</note> who were left over after them in the land, whom the Israelites had not destroyed, Solomon conscripted them as forced labor until this day.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:9
verses.text: But from the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> Solomon did not give as servants for his work, but they were men of war, his commanders of his officers, and commanders of his chariots<note placement="foot">Hebrew “chariot”</note> and his horses.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:10
verses.text: And these <transChange type="added">were</transChange> the commanders of the garrisons that belonged to King Solomon, two hundred and fifty who exercised authority over the people.  <div eID="gen3200" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2378"/><div sID="gen3201" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2378"/>And Solomon brought up the daughter of Pharaoh from the city of David to the house that he had built for her, for he said, “My wife shall not dwell in the house of David, king of Israel, for those <transChange type="added">places</transChange> to which the ark of Yahweh has come <transChange type="added">are</transChange> holy.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:12
verses.text: Then Solomon offered burnt offerings to Yahweh on the altar of Yahweh that he had built before the portico,

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:13
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as was the daily requirement⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “with respect to the word of the day, by day”</note> to offer up according to the commandments of Moses for Sabbaths, new moon festivals, and the three <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞annual⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “occurrences in the year”</note> feasts: the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the Feast of Weeks, and the Feast of Booths.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:14
