verses.text: And in accord with the ordinance of David his father he appointed working groups of priests for their service, Levites for their responsibilities for praise and cultic service before the priests <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞according to the daily requirement⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “according to the word of the day, by day”</note> and the gatekeepers in their working groups, gate by gate. For thus David the man of God had commanded.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:15
verses.text: And they did not turn aside from the commandment of the king concerning the priests and the Levites concerning anything, and concerning the treasury rooms.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:16
verses.text: And Solomon accomplished all the work from the day the foundation stone <transChange type="added">was laid for</transChange> the house of Yahweh until its completion, and the house of Yahweh was finished.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:17
verses.text: Then Solomon went to Ezion-Geber, and to Elath, on the edge of the sea in the land of Edom.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:18
verses.text: And Huram<note placement="foot">This is the spelling in Hebrew, though many translations have “Hiram”</note> sent to him, by the hand of his servants, ships and servants knowledgeable of the sea. And they went with the servants of Solomon to Ophir, and from there they collected four hundred and fifty talents of gold and brought it to King Solomon.  <chapter eID="2Chr.8"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2379"/><title type="x-s">Solomon and the Queen of Sheba</title> <div sID="gen3202" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2379"/>Now the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon, and she came to Jerusalem to test Solomon with hard questions, with much wealth and camels, bearing spices and much gold and precious stones. And she came to Solomon and told him all that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞on her mind⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “in her heart”</note>

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:2
verses.text: And Solomon <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞answered all her questions⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “made known to her all her words”</note> Not a word was hidden from Solomon that he did not answer for her.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:3
verses.text: When the queen of Sheba saw the wisdom of Solomon and the house he had built,

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:4
verses.text: and the food of his table, and the position of his officers, the duty of his servants and their clothing, his cupbearers and their clothing, and his burnt offerings that he offered at the house of Yahweh, there was no longer any breath<note placement="foot">Or “spirit”</note> in her.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:5
verses.text: And she said to the king, “The word which I heard in my land concerning your words and your wisdom <transChange type="added">is</transChange> true,

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:6
verses.text: but I did not believe their words until I came and saw with my own eyes. And behold, half the greatness of your wisdom was not reported to me; you surpass the rumors that I had heard.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:7
verses.text: Blessed <transChange type="added">are</transChange> your men, and blessed <transChange type="added">are</transChange> these your servants who stand before you regularly and hear your wisdom!

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:8
verses.text: Blessed be Yahweh your God who took delight in you, to put you on his throne as king for Yahweh your God! Because your God loved Israel, he established him forever and has put you over them as king to do justice and righteousness!”

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:9
verses.text: And she gave to the king one hundred and twenty talents of gold and a very great amount of spices and precious stones. And there were no spices such as those that the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.  <div eID="gen3202" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2380"/><div sID="gen3203" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2380"/>Moreover the servants of Hiram and the servants of Solomon who brought gold from Ophir brought algum wood and precious stones.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:11
verses.text: And the king made steps for the house of Yahweh and the house of the king, and lyres and harps for the singers <transChange type="added">from</transChange> the algum wood. And there was not seen <transChange type="added">anything</transChange> like them before in the land of Judah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:12
verses.text: Now King Solomon gave to the queen of Sheba every desired thing she asked, besides what she had brought to the king. Then she turned and went to her land, she and her servants.  <div eID="gen3203" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2381"/><title type="x-s">Solomon’s Great Wealth</title> <div sID="gen3204" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2381"/>And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> the weight of the gold that came to Solomon in one year <transChange type="added">was</transChange> six hundred and sixty-six talents of gold,

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:14
verses.text: besides the gold and silver the traders and merchants brought, and all the kings of Arabia and the governors of the land brought.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:15
verses.text: And King Solomon made two hundred shields of beaten gold; six hundred <transChange type="added">shekels</transChange> of beaten gold went into each shield.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:16
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">he made</transChange> three hundred small shields of beaten gold; three hundred <transChange type="added">shekels</transChange> went into each small shield. And the king put them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:17
verses.text: And the king made a large ivory throne and overlaid it with pure gold.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:18
verses.text: And the throne had six steps, and a footstool of gold <transChange type="added">was</transChange> attached to the throne. And <transChange type="added">there were</transChange> armrests <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞on each side⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “from this and from that”</note> And by <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the seat⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the place of sitting”</note> <transChange type="added">were</transChange> two lions standing beside the armrests.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:19
verses.text: And twelve lions were standing there on <transChange type="added">each</transChange> of the six steps <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞on each end⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “from this and from that”</note> And there was nothing like <transChange type="added">it</transChange> made in all the kingdom.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:20
verses.text: And all the drinking vessels of King Solomon <transChange type="added">were</transChange> of gold, and all the vessels of the House of the Forest of Lebanon <transChange type="added">were</transChange> of pure gold. Silver was not valued as anything in the days of Solomon.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:21
verses.text: For the ships of the king went to Tarshish with the servants of Huram.<note placement="foot">This is the spelling in Hebrew, though many translations have “Hiram”</note> Once <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞every three years⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for three years”</note> the ships of Tarshish came carrying gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.  <div eID="gen3204" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2382"/><div sID="gen3205" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2382"/>Thus King Solomon was greater than all the kings of the earth in wealth and wisdom.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:23
verses.text: And all the kings of the earth sought the face of Solomon to hear his wisdom that God put in his heart.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:24
verses.text: And each of them brought his gifts, objects of silver, objects of gold, cloaks, myrrh, spices, horses, and mules, <transChange type="added">as</transChange> an amount year by year.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:25
verses.text: And Solomon had four thousand stalls for horses and chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen. And he stationed them in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:26
verses.text: And he ruled over all the kings from the River<note placement="foot">That is, the Euphrates</note> to the land of the Philistines, to the boundary of Egypt.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:27
verses.text: And the king made silver in Jerusalem as stones, and he made cedar as the sycamore trees that <transChange type="added">are</transChange> in the Shephelah for abundance.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:28
verses.text: And the horses <transChange type="added">were</transChange> imported from Egypt and from all lands for Solomon.  <div eID="gen3205" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2383"/><title type="x-s">The Death of Solomon</title> <div sID="gen3206" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2383"/>As for the remainder of the words of Solomon <transChange type="added">from</transChange> the first to the last, are they not written in the chronicles<note placement="foot">Or “words”</note> of Nathan the prophet and in the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and in the visions of Iddo the seer, concerning Jeroboam the son of Nebat?

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:30
verses.text: And Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel forty years.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:31
verses.text: And Solomon slept with his ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and they buried him in the city of David his father. And Rehoboam his son reigned in his place.  <chapter eID="2Chr.9"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2384"/><title type="x-s">Rehoboam’s Debacle</title> <div sID="gen3207" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2384"/>Then Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel had come <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Shechem to make him king.

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:2
verses.text: And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> when Jeroboam the son of Nebat heard <transChange type="added">it</transChange>—now he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in Egypt, where he had fled from the presence of King Solomon—Jeroboam returned from Egypt.

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:3
verses.text: And they sent and called him. Then Jeroboam and all Israel went, and they spoke to Rehoboam, saying,

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:4
verses.text: “Your father made our yoke heavy. Now, therefore, lighten the hard service of your father and his heavy yoke which he put upon us, and we will serve you.”

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:5
verses.text: And he said to them, “In three days return to me again.” And the people went away.  <div eID="gen3207" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2385"/><div sID="gen3208" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2385"/>Then King Rehoboam took counsel with the elders who had been <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞serving⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “standing”</note> before Solomon his father when he was alive, saying, “What word do you advise to answer this people?”

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:7
verses.text: And they said to him, “If you will be good to this people and please them, then speak good words to them. Then they will be your servants <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “all the days”</note>

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:8
verses.text: But he forsook the advice of the elders that advised him and took counsel of the young men who had grown up with him who were <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞serving⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “standing”</note> before him.

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:9
verses.text: And he said to them, “What do you advise that we should say in return to this people, who said to me, ‘Lighten the yoke that your father has put upon us’?”

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:10
verses.text: Then the young men who had grown up with him said to him, “Thus you should say to this people who have said to you, ‘Your father made our yoke heavy, so you yourself should lighten <transChange type="added">it</transChange> for us.’ Thus you should say to them, ‘My little finger <transChange type="added">is</transChange> thicker than the loins of my father.

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:11
verses.text: So now, my father laid upon you a heavy yoke, but I myself will add to the yoke. My father disciplined you with whips, but I myself <transChange type="added">will do so</transChange> with scorpions.’ ”  <div eID="gen3208" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2386"/><div sID="gen3209" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2386"/>Then Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day as the king had spoken, saying, “Return to me on the third day.”

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:13
verses.text: And the king answered them harshly, and King Rehoboam forsook the advice of the elders.

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:14
verses.text: And he spoke to them according to the advice of the young men, saying, “I will make your yoke heavy, and I myself will add to it. My father disciplined you with whips, but I <transChange type="added">will do so</transChange> with scorpions.”

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:15
verses.text: So the king did not listen to the people, for it was a turning <transChange type="added">of events</transChange> from God, so that Yahweh might fulfill his word that he had spoken by the hand of Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam son of Nebat.

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:16
verses.text: So all Israel <transChange type="added">saw</transChange> that the king would not listen to them, and the people answered the king, saying, “What portion <transChange type="added">is there</transChange> for us in David? <transChange type="added">We have</transChange> no inheritance in the son of Jesse. Each to your tents, O Israel! Now look to your own house, David!” And all Israel went to their own tents.

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:17
verses.text: But as for the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> who were living in the cities of Judah, Rehoboam ruled over them.

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:18
verses.text: Then King Rehoboam sent Hadoram, who was <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in charge of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “over”</note> the forced labor, but the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> stoned him with stones, and he died. Then King Rehoboam hastily went up into the chariot to flee to Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:19
verses.text: So Israel has rebelled against the house of David until this day.  <chapter eID="2Chr.10"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2387"/><title type="x-s">Rehoboam’s Kingdom</title> <div sID="gen3210" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2387"/>When Rehoboam came to Jerusalem he assembled the house of Judah and Benjamin, one hundred and eighty thousand <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞chosen warriors⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “chosen makers of war”</note> to fight against Israel to restore the kingdom to Rehoboam.

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:2
verses.text: But the word of Yahweh came to Shemaiah, the man of God, saying,

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:3
verses.text: “Say to Rehoboam, son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all Israel in Judah and Benjamin,

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:4
verses.text: ‘Thus says Yahweh: “Do not go up, and do not fight against your brothers. Return, each man to his house, for this matter has come from me.” ’ ” So they obeyed the words of Yahweh and turned back from going against Jeroboam.  <div eID="gen3210" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2388"/><div sID="gen3211" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2388"/>And Rehoboam lived in Jerusalem, and he built cities as strongholds in Judah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:6
verses.text: He built Bethlehem, Etah, Tekoa,

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:7
verses.text: Beth-Zur, Socoh, Adullam,

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:8
verses.text: Gath, Mareshah, Ziph,

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:9
verses.text: Adoraim, Lachish, Azekah,

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:10
verses.text: Zorah, Aijalon, and Hebron, fortified cities that <transChange type="added">are</transChange> in Judah and in Benjamin.

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:11
verses.text: And he strengthened the fortifications and put commanders in them, <transChange type="added">along with</transChange> stores of food, olive oil, and wine.

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:12
verses.text: And in all the cities <transChange type="added">he put</transChange> shields and spears, and he greatly strengthened them. So he had Judah and Benjamin.  <div eID="gen3211" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2389"/><title type="x-s">The Priests and Levites Come to Jerusalem</title> <div sID="gen3212" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2389"/>Now the priests and the Levites who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> throughout all Israel took their stand with him<note placement="foot">That is, Rehoboam</note> from all their territories.

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:14
verses.text: For the Levites left their pasturelands and their property and came to Judah and to Jerusalem, for Jeroboam and his sons had rejected them from serving as priests to Yahweh.

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:15
verses.text: And he appointed his own priests for the high places and for the goat idols and for the bull calves that he had made.

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:16
verses.text: Then after them, from all the tribes of Israel, those who set their heart to seek Yahweh, the God of Israel, came to Jerusalem to offer to Yahweh, the God of their ancestors.<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note>

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:17
verses.text: And they strengthened the kingdom of Judah and made Rehoboam, the son of Solomon, secure for three years, for they walked in the way of David and Solomon for three years.  <div eID="gen3212" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2390"/><title type="x-s">Rehoboam’s Harem and Family</title> <div sID="gen3213" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2390"/>Then Rehoboam took to himself as a wife Mahalath, the daughter<note placement="foot">This follows the reading tradition (<hi type="italic">Qere)</hi>; the <hi type="italic">Kethib</hi> reading has “son”</note> of Yerimot son of David, and of Abihail the daughter of Eliab the son of Jesse.

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:19
verses.text: And she bore to him sons: Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham.

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:20
verses.text: And after her he took Maacah the daughter of Absalom, who bore to him Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith.

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:21
verses.text: And Rehoboam loved Maacah the daughter of Absalom more than all his wives and concubines (for he took eighteen wives and sixty concubines, and he fathered twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters).

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:22
verses.text: And Rehoboam appointed Abijah the son of Maacah as chief and crown prince over his brothers, in order to make him king.

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:23
verses.text: And he dealt wisely and distributed some of his sons throughout all the land of Judah and Benjamin, through all the fortified cities, and gave abundant provisions to them and obtained many wives <transChange type="added">for them</transChange>.  <chapter eID="2Chr.11"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2391"/><title type="x-s">Shishak of Egypt Invades Jerusalem</title> <div sID="gen3214" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2391"/>And when the kingdom of Rehoboam was established and when he was strengthened, he forsook the law of Yahweh, and all Israel with him.

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:2
verses.text: And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> in the fifth year of King Rehoboam (for they had acted unfaithfully against Yahweh), Shishak the king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:3
verses.text: with one thousand two hundred chariots and sixty thousand horsemen. And there was no number to the people who came up with him from Egypt—Libyans, Sukkites, and Cushites.

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:4
verses.text: And he took the fortified cities that belonged to Judah, and he came up to Jerusalem.  <div eID="gen3214" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2392"/><div sID="gen3215" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2392"/>Then Shemaiah the prophet came to Rehoboam and the princes of Judah who had gathered at Jerusalem from before Shishak. And he said to them, “Thus says Yahweh: ‘You yourselves have abandoned me, and I myself have surely abandoned you into the hand of Shishak.’ ”

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:6
verses.text: Then the princes of Israel and the king humbled themselves and said, “Yahweh <transChange type="added">is</transChange> righteous.”

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:7
verses.text: And when Yahweh saw that they humbled themselves, the word of Yahweh came to Shemaiah, saying, “They have humbled themselves; I will not destroy. I will give to them some way of escape, that my anger not be poured out against Jerusalem by the hand of Shishak.

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:8
verses.text: However, they shall be his servants, that they might know my service and the service of the kingdoms of <transChange type="added">other</transChange> countries.”  <div eID="gen3215" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2393"/><div sID="gen3216" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2393"/>Then Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, and he took the treasures out of the house of Yahweh and the treasures out of the king’s house. He took everything. He also took the small shields of gold that Solomon had made.

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:10
verses.text: And King Rehoboam made small shields of bronze in their place and committed them into the hand of the commanders of the guards who were keeping the entrance of the house of the king.

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:11
verses.text: And whenever the king went into the house of Yahweh, the guards came and carried them, and then they returned them to the alcove of the guards.

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:12
verses.text: And when he humbled himself, the anger of Yahweh was turned away from him, so that he did not destroy <transChange type="added">the city</transChange> completely. Moreover, matters were well in Judah.  <div eID="gen3216" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2394"/><title type="x-s">The Death of Rehoboam</title> <div sID="gen3217" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2394"/>So King Rehoboam was strengthened in Jerusalem, and he reigned <transChange type="added">there</transChange>. Now, Rehoboam <transChange type="added">was</transChange> forty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city where Yahweh had chosen to put his name out of all the tribes of Israel. And the name of his mother <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Naamah the Ammonite.

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:14
verses.text: And he did evil, for he did not set his heart to seek Yahweh.  <div eID="gen3217" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2395"/><div sID="gen3218" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2395"/>Now the words of Rehoboam <transChange type="added">from</transChange> the first to the last, are they not written in the chronicles<note placement="foot">Or “words”</note> of Shemaiah the prophet and Iddo the seer as a record? And there were battles between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all their<note placement="foot">Or “the”</note> days.

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:16
verses.text: And Rehoboam slept with his ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and he was buried in the city of David, and Abijah his son reigned in his place.  <chapter eID="2Chr.12"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2396"/><title type="x-s">Abijah and Civil War</title> <div sID="gen3219" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2396"/>In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam, Abijah reigned over Judah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:2
verses.text: He reigned for three years in Jerusalem. And the name of his mother <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Micaiah the daughter of Uriel from Gibeah. <div eID="gen3219" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3220" type="x-p"/> Now there was war between Abijah and between Jeroboam.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:3
verses.text: And Abijah joined in the battle with an army of four hundred thousand <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞battle-hardened warriors⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “mighty warriors of battle”</note> chosen men, and Jeroboam put the battle in order against him with eight hundred thousand chosen men, an army of mighty warriors.  <div eID="gen3220" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2397"/><div sID="gen3221" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2397"/>Then Abijah stood up on top of Mount Zemaraim that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in the hill country of Ephraim and said, “Hear me, O Jeroboam and all Israel!

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:5
verses.text: Do you not all know that Yahweh the God of Israel gave the kingdom to David over Israel forever, to him and to his sons <transChange type="added">by</transChange> a covenant of salt?

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:6
verses.text: But Jeroboam the son of Nebat, a servant of Solomon the son of David, rose up and rebelled against his master,

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:7
verses.text: and worthless men, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞sons of wickedness⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons of Belial”</note> were gathered about him and became hostile against Rehoboam the son of Solomon, when Rehoboam was a boy and gentle of heart and was not strong enough <transChange type="added">to stand</transChange> before them.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:8
verses.text: So now you yourselves are considering <transChange type="added">that you are</transChange> strong before the kingdom of Yahweh <transChange type="added">which is</transChange> in the hand the sons of David, since you yourselves are a great multitude and you have bull calves of gold that Jeroboam has made for idols.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:9
verses.text: Did you not drive out the priests of Yahweh, the sons of Aaron, the Levites? Have you <transChange type="added">not</transChange> made for yourselves priests like all the peoples of the lands? All who come <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to be consecrated for priestly service⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to fill his hand” (a Hebrew idiom for ordination)</note> with a young bull or seven rams becomes a priest of <transChange type="added">what is</transChange> not a god.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:10
verses.text: But as for us, Yahweh <transChange type="added">is</transChange> our God, and we have not forsaken him. The priests serving Yahweh <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the sons of Aaron, the Levites, according to their service.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:11
verses.text: They offer burnt offerings to Yahweh <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞every morning⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in the morning, in the morning”</note> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞every evening⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “in the evening, in the evening”</note> sweet spices of incense, and the rows of bread upon the pure table. And the golden lampstand with its lamps they keep kindled <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞every evening⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “in the evening, in the evening”</note> for we are keeping the requirement of Yahweh our God, but you yourselves have forsaken him.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:12
verses.text: And look, God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> with us at the head, and his priests <transChange type="added">have</transChange> the trumpets for sounding blasts against you, O sons of Israel. Do not fight against Yahweh, the God of your ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> for you will not succeed.”  <div eID="gen3221" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2398"/><div sID="gen3222" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2398"/>Then Jeroboam sent around an ambush to come behind them. So they were in front of Judah, but the ambush <transChange type="added">was</transChange> behind them.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:14
verses.text: When Judah turned, then behold, the battle against them <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in front and behind, and they cried to Yahweh, and the priests blew on the trumpets.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:15
verses.text: Then the men of Judah shouted, and it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> when the men of Judah were shouting, then God defeated Jeroboam and all Israel before Abijah and Judah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:16
verses.text: And the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> fled from before Judah, and God gave them into their hand.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:17
verses.text: And Abijah and his people struck a great blow against them, and the dead from Israel <transChange type="added">that</transChange> fell <transChange type="added">were</transChange> five hundred thousand chosen men.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:18
verses.text: And the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> were subdued at that time, and the people<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Judah were victorious, for they relied upon Yahweh the God of their ancestors.<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note>  <div eID="gen3222" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2399"/><div sID="gen3223" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2399"/>And Abijah pursued after Jeroboam and took cities from him: Bethel with its villages, Jeshanah with its villages, and Ephron with its villages.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:20
verses.text: And Jeroboam did not regain strength again in the days of Abijah. And Yahweh plagued him and he died.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:21
verses.text: But Abijah became strong, and he took to himself fourteen wives and fathered twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:22
verses.text: Now the rest of the words of Abijah and his ways and his words are written in the story of the prophet Iddo.  <chapter eID="2Chr.13"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2400"/><title type="x-s">The Reign of Asa in Judah</title> <div sID="gen3224" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2400"/><note placement="foot"><reference osisRef="2Chr.14.1-2Chr.14.15">2 Chronicles 14:1–15 </reference>in the English Bible is 13:23–14:14 in the Hebrew Bible</note> And Abijah slept with his ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and they buried him in the city of David. And Asa his son became king in his place. In his days the land was at rest ten years.

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:2
verses.text: Asa did that which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> good and right in the eyes of Yahweh his God.

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:3
verses.text: He removed the foreign altars and high places, broke down the stone pillars, and cut down the Asherahs.

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:4
verses.text: And he commanded Judah to seek Yahweh, the God of their ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and to keep the law and the commandment.

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:5
verses.text: And he removed the high places and the incense stands from all the cities of Judah, and the kingdom had rest under<note placement="foot">Or “before”</note> him.

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:6
verses.text: And he built fortified cities in Judah, for the land was at rest. Under<note placement="foot">Or “With”</note> him there was no war in those years, for Yahweh had given rest to him.

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:7
verses.text: And he said to Judah, “Let us build these cities and surround <transChange type="added">them with</transChange> walls, towers, gates, and bars while the land <transChange type="added">is</transChange> before us, because we have sought Yahweh our God. We have sought and he has given rest to us on every side.” So they built and had success.

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:8
verses.text: And Asa had an army <transChange type="added">of</transChange> three hundred thousand from Judah, bearing shields and spears, and two hundred and eighty thousand from Benjamin <transChange type="added">who</transChange> carried shields and drew bows. All of these <transChange type="added">were</transChange> mighty warriors of strength.  <div eID="gen3224" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2401"/><div sID="gen3225" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2401"/>Zerah the Cushite came out against them with an army of a thousand thousands and three hundred chariots. And he came to Mareshah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:10
verses.text: And Asa went out before him, and a battle was put in order in the valley of Zepah at Mareshah.  <div eID="gen3225" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2402"/><div sID="gen3226" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2402"/>Then Asa cried out to Yahweh his God. And he said, “O Yahweh, there is none with you to help between the great and the powerless. Help us, O Yahweh our God, for we rely upon you, and in your name we have come against this multitude. O Yahweh, you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> our God! Let no man prevail against you!”  <div eID="gen3226" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2403"/><div sID="gen3227" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2403"/>So Yahweh defeated the Cushites before Asa and before Judah, and the Cushites fled.

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:13
verses.text: Then Asa and the army<note placement="foot">Or “people”</note> with him pursued them to Gerar. And <transChange type="added">many</transChange> from the Cushites fell, for they had no deliverance, for they were shattered before Yahweh and before his army. And they carried away much war booty.

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:14
verses.text: And they struck all the cities around Gerar, for the fear of Yahweh was upon them. And they plundered all the cities, for there was much plunder in them.

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:15
verses.text: And they also struck the tents of the herdsmen and carried away many sheep and camels. Then they returned to Jerusalem.  <chapter eID="2Chr.14"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2404"/><title type="x-s">Asa’s Religious Reforms</title> <div sID="gen3228" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2404"/>Now Azariah the son of Oded—the Spirit of God came upon him.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:2
verses.text: And he went out before Asa and said to him, “Hear me, O Asa and all of Judah and Benjamin! Yahweh <transChange type="added">is</transChange> with you while you are with him. And if you will seek him he will be found by you. But if you forsake him he will forsake you.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:3
verses.text: Now Israel <transChange type="added">has been</transChange> without the true God many days, and without a teaching priest, and without law,

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:4
verses.text: but at its trouble he returned to Yahweh, the God of Israel. They sought him, and he was found by them.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:5
verses.text: And in those times there was no peace for the one going out and the one coming in, for great tumults <transChange type="added">were</transChange> upon all the inhabitants of the lands.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:6
verses.text: Nation was crushed by nation, and city <transChange type="added">was</transChange> against city, for God threw them into confusion by all <transChange type="added">sorts of</transChange> trouble.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:7
verses.text: But as for you, be strong and let not your hands be weak, for there is reward for your labor.”  <div eID="gen3228" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2405"/><div sID="gen3229" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2405"/>And when Asa heard these words, the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he took courage and removed the vile idols from all the lands of Judah and Benjamin, and from the cities that he had taken in the hill country of Ephraim, and he repaired the altar of Yahweh that was in front of the portico of Yahweh.  <div eID="gen3229" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2406"/><div sID="gen3230" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2406"/>And he gathered all Judah and Benjamin and those sojourning with them, from Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon, for many had deserted to him from Israel when they saw that Yahweh his God <transChange type="added">was</transChange> with him.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:10
verses.text: And they were gathered <transChange type="added">at</transChange> Jerusalem in the third month of the fifteenth year of the reign of Asa.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:11
verses.text: And they sacrificed to Yahweh on that day from the war booty they brought back: seven hundred oxen and seven thousand sheep.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:12
verses.text: And they entered into a covenant to seek Yahweh, the God of their ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> with all their heart and with all their inmost being,<note placement="foot">Or “soul”</note>

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:13
verses.text: but all who will not seek Yahweh the God of Israel should be killed, from young to old, from men to women.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:14
verses.text: And they took an oath to Yahweh with a great voice, with shouting, with trumpets, and with horns.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:15
verses.text: And all Judah rejoiced over the oath, for they swore with all their heart. And they sought him with their whole desire, and he was found by them, and Yahweh gave rest to them all around.  <div eID="gen3230" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2407"/><div sID="gen3231" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2407"/>And also Maacah, the mother of Asa, the king removed her from <transChange type="added">being</transChange> queen, because she had made a repulsive image for Asherah. And Asa cut down her repulsive image, and he crushed and burned <transChange type="added">it</transChange> at the Wadi<note placement="foot">Or “valley”; a wadi is a valley that is dry most of the year, but contains a stream during the rainy season</note> Kidron.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:17
verses.text: But the high places were not removed from Israel. Nevertheless, the heart of Asa was fully devoted all his days.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:18
verses.text: And he brought the holy objects of his father and his own holy objects <transChange type="added">into</transChange> the house of God—silver and gold and vessels.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:19
verses.text: And there was no war until the thirty-fifth year of the reign of Asa.  <chapter eID="2Chr.15"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2408"/><title type="x-s">The End of Asa’s Reign</title> <div sID="gen3232" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2408"/>In the thirty-sixth year of the reign of Asa, Baasha the king of Israel went up against Judah. And he built Ramah in order not to allow <transChange type="added">anyone</transChange> to go out or come in to Asa, king of Judah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:2
verses.text: Then Asa brought out silver and gold from the storehouses of the house of Yahweh and the house of the king, and he sent <transChange type="added">them</transChange> to Ben-Hadad, king of Aram,<note placement="foot">Or “Syria”</note> who lived in Damascus, saying,

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:3
verses.text: “<transChange type="added">There is</transChange> a covenant between me and you, <transChange type="added">as there was</transChange> between my father and your father. Look, I am sending you silver and gold. Go, break your covenant with Baasha, king of Israel, that he might withdraw from me.”  <div eID="gen3232" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2409"/><div sID="gen3233" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2409"/>And Ben-Hadad listened to King Asa, and he sent commanders of his troops that <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him against the cities of Israel. And they struck Ijon, Dan, Abel-Maim, and all the storage cities of Naphtali.

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:5
verses.text: And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> when Baasha heard <transChange type="added">this</transChange>, he stopped building Ramah and ceased his work.

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:6
verses.text: Then King Asa took all of Judah, and they carried away the stones of Ramah and its timber with which Baasha had been building, and he built Geba and Mizpah with them.  <div eID="gen3233" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2410"/><div sID="gen3234" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2410"/>And at that time Hanani the seer came to Asa king of Judah and said to him, “On account of your reliance upon the king of Aram,<note placement="foot">Or “Syria”</note> and since you did not rely on Yahweh your God, therefore the troops of the king of Aram<note placement="foot">Or “Syria”</note> escaped from your hand.

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:8
verses.text: Were not the Cushites and Libyans a mighty army with very abundant chariots and horsemen? And because of your reliance on Yahweh he gave them into your hand.

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:9
verses.text: For the eyes of Yahweh roam throughout all the earth to strengthen those whose heart is fully devoted to him. You have been foolish in this, for from now on you will have wars.”  <div eID="gen3234" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2411"/><div sID="gen3235" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2411"/>Then Asa was angry with the seer and put him in <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the prison⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the house of the stocks”</note> for he was enraged with him concerning this. And Asa oppressed some of the people at that time.  <div eID="gen3235" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2412"/><div sID="gen3236" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2412"/>Now behold, the words of Asa <transChange type="added">from</transChange> the first to the last, behold, they are written in the scroll of the kings of Judah and Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:12
verses.text: And in the thirty-ninth year of his reign, he fell <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞severely⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “until his illness unto severity”</note> ill in his feet. But even in his illness he did not seek Yahweh, but <transChange type="added">only</transChange> among the healers.

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:13
verses.text: And Asa slept with his ancestors.<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> And he died in the forty-first year of his reign.

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:14
verses.text: And they buried him in his burial site, which had been cut out for him in the city of David. And they laid him on the bier which they had filled with all kinds of spices made <transChange type="added">by</transChange> the perfumers as a fragment ointment. And they made a great fire in his honor.  <chapter eID="2Chr.16"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2413"/><title type="x-s">Jehoshaphat Reigns in Judah</title> <div sID="gen3237" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2413"/>And Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his place, and he strengthened himself against Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:2
verses.text: And he put troops in all the fortified cities of Judah, and put garrisons in the land of Judah and in the cities of Ephraim that Asa his father had taken.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:3
verses.text: And Yahweh was with Jehoshaphat, because he walked in the former ways of David his father and did not seek after the Baals,

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:4
verses.text: but he sought after the God of his ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and walked in his commandments and not according to the works of Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:5
verses.text: So Yahweh established the kingdom in his hand. And all Judah gave tribute to Jehoshaphat, and he had much wealth and honor.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:6
verses.text: And his heart was courageous in the ways of Yahweh. Moreover, he removed the high places and the Asherahs from Judah.  <div eID="gen3237" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2414"/><div sID="gen3238" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2414"/>In the third year of his reign he sent his officials, Ben-Hail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel, and Micaiah, to teach in the cities of Judah;

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:8
verses.text: and with them the Levites Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah, and Tob-Adonijah; and with them the priests Elisham and Joram.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:9
verses.text: And they taught in Judah, and the scroll of the law of Yahweh <transChange type="added">was</transChange> with them when they went around in all the cities of Judah, and they taught the people.  <div eID="gen3238" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2415"/><div sID="gen3239" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2415"/>And the fear of Yahweh was upon all the kingdoms of the lands surrounding Judah, and they did not make war against Jehoshaphat.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:11
verses.text: And some of the Philistines brought a gift and silver to Jehoshaphat <transChange type="added">as</transChange> tribute. The Arabians also brought him seven thousand seven hundred sheep and seven thousand seven hundred goats.  <div eID="gen3239" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2416"/><div sID="gen3240" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2416"/>And Jehoshaphat <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞grew greater and greater⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “was going and becoming great to the height”</note> and he built fortresses and storage cities in Judah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:13
verses.text: And he had many supplies in the cities of Judah and mighty warriors for battle in Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:14
verses.text: Now these <transChange type="added">were</transChange> their enrollment by the house of their ancestors:<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> of Judah, the commanders of thousands: Adnah, the commander, and with him <transChange type="added">were</transChange> three hundred thousand mighty armed warriors;

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:15
verses.text: and at his side,<note placement="foot">Or “hand”</note> Jehohanan the commander, and with him <transChange type="added">were</transChange> two hundred and eighty thousand;

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:16
verses.text: and at his side,<note placement="foot">Or “hand”</note> Amasiah the son of Zicri, who had made a freewill offering to Yahweh, and with him <transChange type="added">were</transChange> two hundred thousand mighty armed warriors.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:17
verses.text: And from Benjamin: Eliada, a powerful mighty warrior, and with him <transChange type="added">were</transChange> two hundred thousand armed with bow and shield;

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:18
verses.text: and at his side,<note placement="foot">Or “hand”</note> Jehozabad, and with him <transChange type="added">were</transChange> one hundred and eighty thousand armed for war.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:19
verses.text: These were serving the king, besides <transChange type="added">those</transChange> whom the king had placed in the fortified cities throughout all Judah.  <chapter eID="2Chr.17"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2417"/><title type="x-s">Jehoshaphat’s Alliance with Ahab</title> <div sID="gen3241" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2417"/>Now Jehoshaphat had much wealth and honor, and he became son-in-law to Ahab.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:2
verses.text: And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞after some years⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “at the end of years”</note> he went down to Ahab in Samaria. And Ahab slaughtered many sheep and cattle for him and for the people who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him, and urged him to go up against Ramoth-Gilead.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:3
verses.text: And Ahab the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, “Will you go up with me to Ramoth-Gilead?” And he answered him, “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> as you <transChange type="added">are</transChange>, and my people <transChange type="added">are</transChange> as your people with you in war.”  <div eID="gen3241" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2418"/><div sID="gen3242" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2418"/>Then Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, “Seek <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞first of all⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “as the day”</note> the word of Yahweh.”

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:5
verses.text: Then the king of Israel gathered the prophets, four hundred men. And he said to them, “Shall we go to Ramoth-Gilead to battle, or shall we cease?” And they said, “Go up, since God will give <transChange type="added">it</transChange> into the hand of the king.”

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:6
verses.text: Then Jehoshaphat said, “Is there not here another prophet of Yahweh that we might inquire of him?”

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:7
verses.text: Then the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “<transChange type="added">There is</transChange> yet one man by whom to seek Yahweh, but I hate him, because he never prophesies good concerning me, but <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞always⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “all his days”</note> disaster. He <transChange type="added">is</transChange> Micaiah the son of Imlah.” Then Jehoshaphat said, “Let not the king say thus.”

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:8
verses.text: Then the king of Israel called to a eunuch and said, “Quickly bring Micaiah the son of Imlah.”  <div eID="gen3242" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2419"/><div sID="gen3243" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2419"/>Now the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat the king of Judah were each sitting on his throne, clothed in robes. And they were sitting at the threshing floor at the entrance of the gate of Samaria, and all the prophets were prophesying before them.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:10
verses.text: And Zedekiah the son of Kenaanah made for himself horns of iron, and he said, “Thus says Yahweh: ‘With these you will gore Aram<note placement="foot">Or “Syria”</note> to their destruction.’ ”

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:11
verses.text: And all the prophets prophesied thus, saying, “Go up to Ramoth-Gilead and triumph! Yahweh will give it into the hand of the king.”  <div eID="gen3243" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2420"/><div sID="gen3244" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2420"/>Then the messenger who went to call Micaiah said to him, “Behold, the words of the prophets <transChange type="added">are</transChange> good with one voice to the king. Please let your word be as one with them and speak good.”

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:13
verses.text: But Micaiah said, “As Yahweh lives, only what my God has said, that will I speak.”  <div eID="gen3244" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2421"/><div sID="gen3245" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2421"/>And when he had come to the king, the king said to him, “Micaiah, shall we go to Ramoth-Gilead to war or shall I cease?” And he said, “Go up and triumph! They shall be given into your hand.”

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:15
verses.text: But the king said to him, “How many times shall I make you swear that you speak nothing except the truth in the name of Yahweh?”

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:16
verses.text: Then he said, “I saw all Israel scattered upon the mountains like sheep that had no shepherd. And Yahweh said, ‘These have no masters; let them return to his own house in peace.’ ”

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:17
verses.text: Then the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “Did I not say to you he would not prophesy good concerning me, but only disaster?”

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:18
verses.text: Then Micaiah said, “Therefore hear the word of Yahweh: I saw Yahweh sitting upon his throne with all the host of heaven standing on his right and on his left.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:19
verses.text: And Yahweh said, ‘Who will entice Ahab the king of Israel that he would go up and fall at Ramoth-Gilead?’ And one said this, and another said that.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:20
verses.text: Then a spirit came forth and stood before Yahweh and said, ‘I will entice him.’ Then Yahweh said to him, ‘By what means?’

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:21
verses.text: Then he said, ‘I will go forth and will be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.’ And he said, ‘You will entice him and will also succeed. Go out and do so.’

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:22
verses.text: So now, behold, Yahweh has put a spirit of deception into the mouths of these your prophets. Yahweh has spoken disaster against you.”  <div eID="gen3245" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2422"/><div sID="gen3246" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2422"/>Then Zedekiah the son of Kenaanah came near and struck Micaiah on the cheek and said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Which way⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Where is this the way”</note> did the Spirit of Yahweh come from me to speak to you?”

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:24
verses.text: Then Micaiah said, “Behold, you will see on that day when you go into a private room to hide yourself.”

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:25
verses.text: Then the king of Israel said, “Take Micaiah and return him to Amon the commander of the city and to Jehoash the son of the king,

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:26
verses.text: and say, ‘Thus says the king: “Put this one into the prison house, and let him eat <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a meager ration of bread and water⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “bread a short ration and water a short ration”</note> until I return in peace.” ’ ”

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:27
verses.text: And Micaiah said, “If you surely return in peace Yahweh has not spoken with me.” Then he said, “Hear, peoples, all of them!”  <div eID="gen3246" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2423"/><title type="x-s">The Death of Ahab</title> <div sID="gen3247" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2423"/>Then the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up to Ramoth-Gilead.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:29
verses.text: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “I will disguise myself and go into battle, but you, wear your garments.” So the king of Israel disguised himself, and they went to war.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:30
verses.text: Now the king of Aram<note placement="foot">Or “Syria”</note> had commanded the commanders of his chariots,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “chariot”</note> saying, “Do not fight with the small <transChange type="added">or</transChange> the great, but only with the king of Israel.”

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:31
verses.text: And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> when the commanders of the chariots<note placement="foot">Hebrew “chariot”</note> saw Jehoshaphat, then they said, “It <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the king of Israel!” And they turned against him to fight. Then Jehoshaphat cried out and Yahweh helped him. God drove them away from him.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:32
verses.text: And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> when the commanders of the chariots<note placement="foot">Hebrew “chariot”</note> saw that it was not the king of Israel, they turned back from following him.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:33
verses.text: Now a certain man drew the bow <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞at random⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in his innocence”</note> and struck the king of Israel between the soldering of his breastplate armor. Then he said to the chariot driver, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Turn around⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “Turn away your hand”</note> get me away from the <transChange type="added">war</transChange> camp, for I am wounded.”

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:34
verses.text: And the battle went on that day, and the king of Israel was propped up in the chariot facing Aram<note placement="foot">Or “Syria”</note> until the evening. And he died at the time of the going down of the sun.  <chapter eID="2Chr.18"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 19:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2424"/><title type="x-s">Jehoshaphat’s Reforms</title> <div sID="gen3248" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2424"/>Then Jehoshaphat king of Judah returned to his house in peace to Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 19:2
verses.text: And Jehu son of Hanani the seer went out to meet him. And he said to King Jehoshaphat, “Should you <transChange type="added">be</transChange> a help to the wicked and love those who hate Yahweh? On account of this, wrath <transChange type="added">has come</transChange> against you from Yahweh.

verses.name: II Chronicles 19:3
verses.text: Nevertheless some good things have been found in regard to you, for you burned the Asherahs out of the land and set your heart to seek God.”  <div eID="gen3248" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 19:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2425"/><div sID="gen3249" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2425"/>And Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem and returned and went out among the people from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim and brought them back to Yahweh, the God of their ancestors.<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note>

verses.name: II Chronicles 19:5
verses.text: And he appointed judges in the land and in all the fortified cities of Judah, city by city.

verses.name: II Chronicles 19:6
verses.text: And he said to the judges, “Consider what you are doing, for you are not judging for a man but for Yahweh. Now <transChange type="added">he is</transChange> with you in speaking justice.

verses.name: II Chronicles 19:7
verses.text: So now, let the fear of Yahweh be upon you all. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Be careful what you do⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “Keep and do”</note> for there is neither wickedness nor <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞showing partiality⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “lifting faces”</note> and taking bribes with Yahweh our God.”  <div eID="gen3249" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 19:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2426"/><div sID="gen3250" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2426"/>Moreover, Jehoshaphat appointed in Jerusalem some of the Levites and the priests and heads of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞families⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “fathers”</note> of Israel as judges and to decide legal disputes for Yahweh. And they sat<note placement="foot">Or “lived”</note> <transChange type="added">in</transChange> Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 19:9
verses.text: And he commanded them, saying, “Thus you must do in the fear of Yahweh in faithfulness and with a whole heart.

verses.name: II Chronicles 19:10
verses.text: Any legal dispute that comes before you from your brothers who live in their cities concerning bloodguilt, law, commandment, statutes, and justice, you must warn them, so that they do not incur guilt before Yahweh, and that wrath may not come upon you and your brothers. Thus you must do that you do not incur guilt.

verses.name: II Chronicles 19:11
verses.text: And behold, Amariah the chief priest <transChange type="added">is</transChange> over you in all matters of the word of Yahweh, and Zebadiah the son of Ishmael, the governor of the house of Judah, in all matters of the king, and the Levites <transChange type="added">shall be</transChange> before you <transChange type="added">as</transChange> officials. Be strong and do <transChange type="added">well</transChange>! May Yahweh be with the upright.”  <chapter eID="2Chr.19"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2427"/><title type="x-s">The Prayer of Jehoshaphat</title> <div sID="gen3251" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2427"/>And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> afterward, the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Moabites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Moab”</note> the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> and some of the Meunites<note placement="foot">The Hebrew term is difficult; it may also mean “Ammonim”</note> came against Jehoshaphat for war.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:2
verses.text: And they came and reported <transChange type="added">it</transChange> to Jehoshaphat, saying, “A great multitude from beyond the sea, from Aram,<note placement="foot">Or “Syria”</note> is coming against you. Now behold, <transChange type="added">they are</transChange> in Hazazon Tamar” (that <transChange type="added">is</transChange>, En Gedi).

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:3
verses.text: Then Jehoshaphat was afraid and set his face to seek Yahweh. And he called for a fast through all Judah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:4
verses.text: And Judah assembled to seek after Yahweh; even from all the cities of Judah they came to seek Yahweh.  <div eID="gen3251" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2428"/><div sID="gen3252" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2428"/>Then Jehoshaphat stood in the assembly of Judah and Jerusalem in the house of Yahweh before the new courtyard.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:6
verses.text: And he said, “O Yahweh, God of our ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> are you not God in heaven? Now you rule in all the kingdoms of the nations, and in your hand <transChange type="added">are</transChange> power and might, and there is none <transChange type="added">who can</transChange> resist against you.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:7
verses.text: O, our God, did you yourself not drive out the inhabitants of this land before your people Israel and give it to the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “seed”</note> of Abraham your friend forever?

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:8
verses.text: And they lived in it and built for you a sanctuary for your name in it, saying,

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:9
verses.text: ‘If disaster, a sword, punishment, disease, or famine come upon us, we shall stand before this house and before you—for your name <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in this house—and cry out to you out of our trouble, then you will hear and save <transChange type="added">us</transChange>.’

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:10
verses.text: And now, look, the people<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Moab and Ammon and Mount Seir whom you did not allow Israel to come against when they came from Egypt, from whom they turned aside and did not destroy,

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:11
verses.text: now behold, they are rewarding us by coming to dispossess us from your possession which you gave us as an inheritance.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:12
verses.text: O our God, will you not judge them, for there is no power in us before this great multitude that is coming against us. Now we do not know what we shall do, for our eyes <transChange type="added">are</transChange> upon you.”  <div eID="gen3252" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2429"/><div sID="gen3253" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2429"/>And all Judah was standing before Yahweh, <transChange type="added">and</transChange> also their little children, their wives, and their children.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:14
verses.text: Then the Spirit of Yahweh came upon Jahaziel, the son of Zechariah, the son of Benaiah, the son of Jeiel, the son of Mattaniah, the Levite from the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Asaph, in the midst of the assembly.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:15
verses.text: And he said, “Listen, all Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem and King Jehoshaphat, thus says Yahweh to you: ‘Do not be afraid and do not be dismayed before this great multitude, for the battle is not yours, but God’s.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:16
verses.text: Tomorrow go down against them. Behold, they are coming up the ascent of Ziz. And you will find them at the end of the valley facing the desert of Jeruel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:17
verses.text: <transChange type="added">There will be</transChange> no <transChange type="added">need</transChange> for you to fight in this <transChange type="added">battle</transChange>. Take your stand! Stand and see the deliverance of Yahweh among you, O Judah and Jerusalem! Do not fear and do not be dismayed. Tomorrow go out before them and Yahweh <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> with you.’ ”

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:18
verses.text: Then Jehoshaphat bowed his face<note placement="foot">Literally “nostrils”</note> down to the ground, and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem fell before Yahweh to worship Yahweh.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:19
verses.text: Then the Levites, from the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Kohathites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons of the Kohathites”</note> and from the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Korahites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons of the Korahites”</note> stood up to praise Yahweh the God of Israel with an exceedingly<note placement="foot">Literally “above”</note> loud voice.  <div eID="gen3253" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2430"/><title type="x-s">God Delivers Judah and Jerusalem</title> <div sID="gen3254" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2430"/>And they rose up early in the morning and went out to the desert of Tekoa. And when they went out, Jehoshaphat stood and said, “Hear me, O Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem! Believe in Yahweh your God, and you shall be established! Believe in his prophets, and you shall succeed!”

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:21
verses.text: And when he had taken counsel with the people, he appointed singers to Yahweh <transChange type="added">who were</transChange> giving praise to the splendor of <transChange type="added">his</transChange> holiness when they went out before the army. And they said, “Give thanks to Yahweh, for his loyal love <transChange type="added">is</transChange> everlasting!”  <div eID="gen3254" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2431"/><div sID="gen3255" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2431"/>And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞when⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Or “on time” or “at the time”</note> they began with singing and praise, Yahweh set ambushes against the people<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir who were coming against Judah. And they were defeated

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:23
verses.text: when the people<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Ammon and Moab rose up against the inhabitants of Mount Seir to destroy and demolish <transChange type="added">them</transChange>. And when the inhabitants of Seir had made an end of them, each helped to destroy his comrade.  <div eID="gen3255" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2432"/><div sID="gen3256" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2432"/>And Judah came against the watchtower of the wilderness. And they looked at the crowd, and behold, corpses were lying on the ground. There was none <transChange type="added">who had</transChange> escaped.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:25
verses.text: When Jehoshaphat came with his people to plunder their booty, they found among them in abundance possessions, corpses, and precious items. And they took plunder for themselves <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞until they could carry no more⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “until not carrying”</note> And they were three days in plundering the booty, for it <transChange type="added">was</transChange> abundant.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:26
verses.text: And on the fourth day, they assembled in the Valley of Berakah, for there they blessed Yahweh. Therefore the name of that place is called the Valley of Berakah up to this day.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:27
verses.text: And all the men of Judah and Jerusalem returned, and Jehoshaphat <transChange type="added">was</transChange> at their head in returning to Jerusalem with joy, for Yahweh caused them to rejoice over their enemies.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:28
verses.text: And they came to Jerusalem with harps, stringed instruments, and trumpets to the house of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:29
verses.text: And the fear of God came upon all the kingdoms of the earth when they heard that Yahweh had fought against the enemies of Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:30
verses.text: So the kingdom of Jehoshaphat was at rest, since his God gave rest to him all around.  <div eID="gen3256" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2433"/><title type="x-s">The End of Jehoshaphat’s Reign</title> <div sID="gen3257" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2433"/>So Jehoshaphat reigned over Judah. <transChange type="added">He was</transChange> thirty-five years old when he began to reign. And he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem. The name of his mother <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Azubah, the daughter of Shilhi.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:32
verses.text: And he walked in the way of his father Asa and did not turn aside from it, to do what was right in the eyes of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:33
verses.text: Only the high places were not removed. The people still had not yet set their heart on the God of their ancestors.<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note>

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:34
verses.text: Now the rest of the words of Jehoshaphat, <transChange type="added">from</transChange> the first to the last, behold, they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> written in the chronicles<note placement="foot">Or “words”</note> of Jehu the son of Hanani, which <transChange type="added">are</transChange> recorded in the scroll of the kings of Israel.  <div eID="gen3257" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:35
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2434"/><div sID="gen3258" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2434"/>And afterward Jehoshaphat the king of Judah joined with Ahaziah the king of Israel, who acted wickedly.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:36
verses.text: He joined with him to build ships to go to Tarshish. And they built the ships in Ezion Geber.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:37
verses.text: Then Eliezer the son of Dodavahu of Mareshah prophesied against Jehoshaphat, saying, “Because of your joining with Ahaziah, Yahweh will break down your works.” And the ships were destroyed and were not able to go to Tarshish.  <chapter eID="2Chr.20"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2435"/><title type="x-s">The Reign of Jehoram</title> <div sID="gen3259" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2435"/>And Jehoshaphat slept with his ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and was buried with his ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> in the city of David, and Jehoram his son reigned in his place.

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:2
verses.text: Now he had brothers, the sons of Jehoshaphat: Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariah, Michael, and Shephatiah. All these <transChange type="added">were</transChange> the sons of Jehoshaphat, king of Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:3
verses.text: And their father gave to them many gifts of silver, gold, and valuables, with fortified cities in Judah, but he gave the kingdom to Jehoram, for he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> the firstborn.

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:4
verses.text: When Jehoram ascended to the kingdom of his father, he strengthened himself and murdered all his brothers with the sword, and even some of the princes of Israel.  <div eID="gen3259" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2436"/><div sID="gen3260" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2436"/>Jehoram <transChange type="added">was</transChange> thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:6
verses.text: And he walked in the way of the kings of Israel as the house of Ahab had done, for the daughter of Ahab was his wife. And he did evil in the sight of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:7
