verses.text: But Yahweh was not willing to destroy the house of David on account of the covenant that he had <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞made⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “cut”</note> with David and since he had promised<note placement="foot">Or “said”</note> to give a lamp to him and to his descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “all the days”</note>  <div eID="gen3260" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2437"/><div sID="gen3261" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2437"/>In his days Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah, and they set up a king of their own.

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:9
verses.text: Then Jehoram passed over with his commanders and all the chariots with him, and when night came he struck Edom who <transChange type="added">was</transChange> all around him and the commanders of his chariots.

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:10
verses.text: So Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah until this day. Then Libnah <transChange type="added">also</transChange> revolted at that time from under his hand, because he had forsaken Yahweh, the God of his ancestors.<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note>  <div eID="gen3261" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2438"/><div sID="gen3262" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2438"/>Moreover, he made high places in the hill country of Judah, and he enticed the inhabitants of Jerusalem to be unfaithful, and he led Judah astray.

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:12
verses.text: And a letter from Elijah the prophet came to him, saying, “Thus says Yahweh, the God of David your father: ‘Because you have not walked in the ways of Jehoshaphat your father or in the ways of Asa, the king of Judah,

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:13
verses.text: but have walked in the way of the kings of Israel and have enticed Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to be unfaithful like the unfaithfulness of the house of Ahab, and have also murdered your brothers of the house of your father who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> better than you,

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:14
verses.text: behold, Yahweh is inflicting a great plague on your people, your children, your wives, and all your possessions,

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:15
verses.text: and you yourself <transChange type="added">will be afflicted</transChange> with great illness, with sickness in your bowels, until your bowels come out on account of the illness, day by day.’ ”  <div eID="gen3262" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2439"/><div sID="gen3263" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2439"/>And Yahweh stirred up the spirit of the Philistines and the Arabs who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞near⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “at the hand of”</note> the Cushites against Jehoram.

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:17
verses.text: And they came up against Judah and invaded it and carried away all the possessions found in the house of the king, and also his sons and his wives, so that no son was left to him except Jehoahaz his youngest son.  <div eID="gen3263" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2440"/><div sID="gen3264" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2440"/>And after all this Yahweh afflicted him in his bowels with an illness for <transChange type="added">which there was</transChange> no cure.

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:19
verses.text: And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞after many days, at the end of two years⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “for days from days and as the time went out to the end for two days”</note> his bowels came out because of his illness, and he died in terrible agony. And his people did not make a fire for him like the fire for his ancestors.<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note>

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:20
verses.text: He was thirty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem. And he departed<note placement="foot">Or “went”</note> with no <transChange type="added">one’s</transChange> regret. And they buried him in the city of David, but not in the burial sites of the kings.  <chapter eID="2Chr.21"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 22:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2441"/><title type="x-s">The Reign of Ahaziah</title> <div sID="gen3265" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2441"/>And the inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah his youngest son king in his place, for the band of men who had come with the Arabs to the camp had murdered all the older sons. And Ahaziah the son of Jehoram, the king of Judah, reigned.

verses.name: II Chronicles 22:2
verses.text: Ahaziah <transChange type="added">was</transChange> forty-two<note placement="foot">The Septuagint reads “twenty-two” here</note> years old when he became king, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. And the name of his mother was Athaliah, the daughter<note placement="foot">Some translations render the term “granddaughter”</note> of Omri.

verses.name: II Chronicles 22:3
verses.text: He also walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, for his mother was his counselor for doing wickedness.

verses.name: II Chronicles 22:4
verses.text: And he did evil in the eyes of Yahweh as the house of Ahab <transChange type="added">had done</transChange>, for they were his counselors to his destruction after the death of his father.

verses.name: II Chronicles 22:5
verses.text: He also walked in their counsel and went with Jehoram the son of Ahab, king of Israel, to war against Hazael king of Aram<note placement="foot">Or “Syria”</note> at Ramoth-Gilead. And the Arameans wounded Joram.

verses.name: II Chronicles 22:6
verses.text: And he returned to be healed in Jezreel because of the wounds he had suffered at Ramah, when he made war against Hazael king of Aram.<note placement="foot">Or “Syria”</note> And Azariah the son of Jehoram, king of Judah, went down to see Jehoram son of Ahab in Jezreel for he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> sick.  <div eID="gen3265" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 22:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2442"/><div sID="gen3266" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2442"/>But the downfall of Ahaziah was from God, <transChange type="added">and intended</transChange> to come to Joram. And when he came, he went out with Jehoram to Jehu the son of Nimshi, whom Yahweh had anointed to destroy the house of Ahab.

verses.name: II Chronicles 22:8
verses.text: And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> when Jehu was judging the house of Ahab, he found the princes of Judah and the sons of the brothers of Ahaziah who ministered to Ahaziah, and he killed them.

verses.name: II Chronicles 22:9
verses.text: And he searched for Ahaziah and captured him. And he was hiding in Samaria. And they brought him to Jehu and put him to death. And they buried him, for they said, “He <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the descendant<note placement="foot">Or “son”; Ahaziah was Jehoshaphat’s grandson</note> of Jehoshaphat, who sought Yahweh with his whole heart.” And the house of Ahab had no one to exercise power over the kingdom.  <div eID="gen3266" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 22:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2443"/><title type="x-s">The Reign of Athaliah</title> <div sID="gen3267" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2443"/>Now <transChange type="added">when</transChange> Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son <transChange type="added">was</transChange> dead, she arose and murdered all the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞royal descendants⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “seed of the kingdom”</note> of the house of Judah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 22:11
verses.text: But Jehosheba the daughter of the king took Joash, the son of Ahaziah, and kidnapped him away from the sons of the king who were to be put to death. And she put him and his nurse in a private bedroom. So Jehosheba the daughter of King Jehoram, the wife of Jehoiada the priest, because she was a sister of Ahaziah, hid him from before Athaliah so that she did not put him to death.

verses.name: II Chronicles 22:12
verses.text: And he was hidden with them in the house of God six years, but Athaliah reigned over the land.  <chapter eID="2Chr.22"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2444"/><title type="x-s">Joash Is Made King</title> <div sID="gen3268" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2444"/>And in the seventh year Jehoiada strengthened himself and took with him into a covenant <transChange type="added">relationship</transChange> the commanders of hundreds: Azariah the son of Jeroham, Ishmael the son of Jehohanan, Azariah the son of Obed, Maaseiah the son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat the son of Zicri.

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:2
verses.text: And they went around in Judah and gathered the Levites from all the cities of Judah, and the heads of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞families⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “fathers”</note> of Israel, and they came to Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:3
verses.text: And all the assembly <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞made⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “cut”</note> a covenant with the king in the house of God. And he said to them, “Behold, the son of the king shall reign as Yahweh has spoken concerning the sons of David.

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:4
verses.text: This is the thing that you must do: one third of you priests and Levites <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞coming off duty on the Sabbath⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “coming the Sabbath”</note> <transChange type="added">shall be</transChange> gatekeepers at the entrances,

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:5
verses.text: and one third at the house of the king, and one third at the Gate of the Foundation. And all the people <transChange type="added">shall be</transChange> in the courtyards of the house of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:6
verses.text: Let no one enter into the house of Yahweh except the priests and the ministering Levites. They themselves may enter, for they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> holy, but all the people shall keep the requirements of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:7
verses.text: And the Levites shall surround the king all around, each with his weapons in his hand. And whoever comes into the house shall be put to death. You shall be with the king when he comes in and when he goes out.”  <div eID="gen3268" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2445"/><div sID="gen3269" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2445"/>And the Levites and all Judah did according to all that Jehoiada the priest commanded. And they each took his men <transChange type="added">who were</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞coming off duty on the Sabbath⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “coming the Sabbath”</note> with <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the ones going out to duty on the Sabbath⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “going out the Sabbath”</note> for Jehoiada the priest did not dismiss the working groups.

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:9
verses.text: And Jehoiada the priest gave the spears and small shields that had belonged to King David that <transChange type="added">were in</transChange> the house of God to the commanders of hundreds.

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:10
verses.text: And he appointed all the people, each <transChange type="added">with</transChange> his weapon in his hand from the south side of the house to the north side of the house around the altar and the house.

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:11
verses.text: Then they brought out the son of the king and set upon him the crown and <transChange type="added">gave him</transChange> the statute and made him king. And Jehoiada and his sons anointed him and said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Long live the king⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!”<note placement="foot">Or “May the king live!”</note>  <div eID="gen3269" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2446"/><div sID="gen3270" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2446"/>When Athaliah heard the sound of the people running and praising the king, she came to the people <transChange type="added">at</transChange> the house of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:13
verses.text: And she looked and, behold, the king was standing by his column at the entrance, and the commanders and trumpeters beside the king, along with all the people of the land, rejoicing and blowing with trumpets, and the singers with the instruments of song leading the praise. And Athaliah tore her garments and cried, “Conspiracy! Conspiracy!”

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:14
verses.text: Then Jehoiada the priest brought out the commanders of the hundreds appointed over the troops, and he said to them, “Bring her out between the ranks, and whoever goes after her shall be put to death with the sword.” For the priest had said, “You must not kill her in the house of Yahweh.”

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:15
verses.text: And they laid hands on her, and she went into the entrance of the Horse Gate of the house of the king, and they killed her there.  <div eID="gen3270" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2447"/><div sID="gen3271" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2447"/>And Jehoiada <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞made⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “cut”</note> a covenant between himself and all the people and the king, that they should be Yahweh’s people.

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:17
verses.text: Then all the people went to the house of Baal and broke it down. And they smashed his altars and his images, and they killed Mattan the priest of Baal before the altars.

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:18
verses.text: And Jehoiada placed appointees <transChange type="added">at</transChange> the house of Yahweh under the hand of the Levitical priests whom David had allotted to the house of Yahweh to offer burnt offerings to Yahweh as was written in the law of Moses, with joy and with song, according to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞order of David⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “hands of David”</note>

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:19
verses.text: And he set the gatekeepers at the gates of the house of Yahweh so that no person unclean with respect to any matter could enter.

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:20
verses.text: And he took the commanders of hundreds, the noblemen, the governors over the people, and all the people of the land, and they brought the king down from the house of Yahweh. And they came through the upper gate <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the house of the king, and they set the king upon the throne of the kingdom.

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:21
verses.text: So all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet <transChange type="added">after</transChange> Athaliah had been killed with the sword.  <chapter eID="2Chr.23"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2448"/><title type="x-s">Joash Repairs the Temple</title> <div sID="gen3272" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2448"/>Joash <transChange type="added">was</transChange> seven years old when he became king, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. And the name of his mother <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Zibiah from Beersheba.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:2
verses.text: And Joash did what was right in the eyes of Yahweh all the days of Jehoiada the priest.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:3
verses.text: And Jehoiada took two wives for him, and he fathered sons and daughters.  <div eID="gen3272" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2449"/><div sID="gen3273" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2449"/>And afterward it was in the heart of Joash to repair the house of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:5
verses.text: So he gathered the priests and the Levites and said to them, “Go out to the cities of Judah and gather money from all Israel to strengthen the house of your God sufficiently year by year. Now you yourselves must hasten to the matter.” But the Levites did not act with haste.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:6
verses.text: So the king called Jehoiada the chief, and he said to him, “Why have you not required the Levites to bring from Judah and Jerusalem the tax of Moses, the servant of Yahweh, and <transChange type="added">of</transChange> the assembly of Israel for the tent of the testimony?”

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:7
verses.text: For the sons of the wicked Athaliah had broken into the house of God and had used all the holy vessels of the house of Yahweh for the Baals.  <div eID="gen3273" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2450"/><div sID="gen3274" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2450"/>Then the king commanded, and they made a chest and put it at the gate outside the house of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:9
verses.text: And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they issued a proclamation⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “they gave a voice”</note> in Judah and in Jerusalem to bring to Yahweh the tax <transChange type="added">that</transChange> Moses the servant of God <transChange type="added">had levied</transChange> upon Israel in the wilderness.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:10
verses.text: And all the princes and all the people rejoiced, and they brought <transChange type="added">their tax</transChange> and threw <transChange type="added">it</transChange> into the chest until <transChange type="added">it was</transChange> finished.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:11
verses.text: And whenever he brought the chest to the appointee of the king by the hand of the Levites, and when they saw that <transChange type="added">there was</transChange> much money <transChange type="added">in it</transChange>, then the secretary of the king and the officer of the chief priest came and emptied the chest, then they took it and returned it to its place. Thus they did day by day and gathered money in abundance.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:12
verses.text: And the king and Jehoiada gave it to those who did the work of the service of the house of Yahweh. And they hired stonemasons and skilled craftsmen to restore the house of Yahweh, and also workers in iron and bronze to repair the house of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:13
verses.text: So those doing the work labored, and the restoration for the work made progress under their hand. And they restored the house of God to its position and strengthened it.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:14
verses.text: And when they had finished, they brought the remainder of the money before the king and Jehoiada, and they used it <transChange type="added">for</transChange> objects for the house of Yahweh, objects for the service and the burnt offerings, dishes, and objects of gold and silver. And they were offering burnt offerings in the house of Yahweh regularly, all the days of Jehoiada.  <div eID="gen3274" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2451"/><div sID="gen3275" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2451"/>And Jehoiada grew old and full of days, and he died; <transChange type="added">he was</transChange> one hundred and thirty years old at his death.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:16
verses.text: And they buried him in the city of David with the kings, for he did good in Israel and with respect to God and his house.  <div eID="gen3275" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2452"/><div sID="gen3276" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2452"/>Now after the death of Jehoiada, the princes of Judah came and bowed down to the king. Then the king listened to them.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:18
verses.text: And they forsook the house of Yahweh, the God of their ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and served the Asherahs and the idols. And wrath came upon Judah and Jerusalem on account of this guilt.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:19
verses.text: But he sent prophets among them, to bring them back to Yahweh. And they testified against them, and they did not obey.  <div eID="gen3276" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2453"/><div sID="gen3277" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2453"/>Then the Spirit of God clothed Zechariah the son of Jehoiada the priest, and he stood above the people and said to them, “Thus says God: ‘Why are you transgressing the commandments of Yahweh so that you will not succeed? For you have forsaken Yahweh, so he will forsake you.’ ”

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:21
verses.text: Then they conspired against him and stoned him <transChange type="added">with</transChange> stones at the command of the king in the courtyard of the house of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:22
verses.text: So King Joash did not remember the loyal love that Jehoiada had shown to him, and he killed his son. And as he was dying he said, “May Yahweh see and avenge!”  <div eID="gen3277" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2454"/><title type="x-s">The Death of Joash</title> <div sID="gen3278" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2454"/>And it happened at the turn of the year <transChange type="added">that</transChange> the army of Aram<note placement="foot">Or “Syria”</note> went up against him, and they came to Judah and Jerusalem and destroyed all the commanders of the people from among the people, and all the war booty they sent to the king of Damascus.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:24
verses.text: Though the army of Aram<note placement="foot">Or “Syria”</note> came with few men, Yahweh gave a very large army into their hand, for they had forsaken Yahweh, the God of their ancestors.<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> And they inflicted punishment on Joash.  <div eID="gen3278" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2455"/><div sID="gen3279" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2455"/>And when they were going away from him (for they had left him with many wounds), his servants conspired against him on account of the blood of the sons<note placement="foot">The Septuagint reads “son”</note> of Jehoiada the priest. So they killed him on his bed and he died. And they buried him in the city of David, but they did not bury him at the burial sites of the kings.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:26
verses.text: Now these <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the ones who conspired against him: Zabad the son of Shimeath, the Ammonite, and Jehozabad the son of Shimrith, the Moabite.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:27
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">as for</transChange> his sons, the many oracles against him, and <transChange type="added">his repair of</transChange> the foundation of the house of God, behold, they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> written in the story of the scroll of the kings. And Amaziah his son reigned in his place.  <chapter eID="2Chr.24"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2456"/><title type="x-s">The Reign of Amaziah</title> <div sID="gen3280" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2456"/>Amaziah was twenty-five years old <transChange type="added">when</transChange> he became king. And he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Jehoaddan from Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:2
verses.text: And he did what was right in the eyes of Yahweh, only not with a fully-devoted heart.

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:3
verses.text: And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> as his reign was strengthened, he killed his servants who had killed his father the king.

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:4
verses.text: But he did not put their children to death, according to <transChange type="added">what</transChange> is written in the law, in the scroll of Moses, where Yahweh commanded, saying, “Fathers shall not be put to death on account of the sons, and the sons shall not be put to death on account of the fathers, but each shall be put to death for his own sin.”  <div eID="gen3280" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2457"/><div sID="gen3281" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2457"/>Then Amaziah assembled <transChange type="added">the men of</transChange> Judah and set them by <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞families⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the house of the fathers”</note> under commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds for all Judah and Benjamin. And he counted them from twenty years old and upward, and found them <transChange type="added">to be</transChange> three hundred thousand chosen for going out to battle, able <transChange type="added">with</transChange> spear and shield.

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:6
verses.text: And he hired from Israel one hundred thousand strong, mighty warriors for one hundred talents.  <div eID="gen3281" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2458"/><div sID="gen3282" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2458"/>But a man of God came to him, saying, “O king, do not let the army of Israel go with you, for Yahweh is not with Israel, all the Ephraimites.

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:8
verses.text: But even still, you yourself go, do! Be strong for the battle <transChange type="added">else</transChange> God will make you stumble before the enemy! For there is power with God to help and to cause stumbling.”

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:9
verses.text: And Amaziah said to the man of God, “Now what <transChange type="added">should I</transChange> do with the one hundred talents that I have given to the troops of Israel?” And the man of God said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Yahweh is able to give⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “There is to Yahweh to give”</note> to you more than this.”

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:10
verses.text: Then Amaziah dismissed the troops that came to him from Ephraim to go to their home.<note placement="foot">Or “their place”</note> And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they became very angry⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “their noses became very hot”</note> with Judah, and they returned to their home <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in great anger⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “in hotness of nose”</note>  <div eID="gen3282" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2459"/><div sID="gen3283" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2459"/>Then Amaziah strengthened himself, and leading his army, he went <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the Valley of Salt. And he struck <transChange type="added">down</transChange> ten thousand men<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Seir.

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:12
verses.text: Now the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞troops⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the sons of the troop”</note> captured ten thousand <transChange type="added">others</transChange> alive, and they brought them to the top of the rock and threw them from the top of the rock. So all of them were smashed <transChange type="added">to pieces</transChange>.  <div eID="gen3283" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2460"/><div sID="gen3284" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2460"/>As for the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞troops⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons of the troop”</note> Amaziah had sent back from going with him to war, they raided the cities of Judah from Samaria to Beth-Horon. And they struck <transChange type="added">down</transChange> three thousand of them and plundered much booty.  <div eID="gen3284" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2461"/><div sID="gen3285" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2461"/>And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> after Amaziah came <transChange type="added">back</transChange> from killing the Edomites, he brought the gods of the sons of Seir, and he stood them up to himself as gods and bowed down before them and make smoke offerings for them.

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:15
verses.text: So <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Yahweh became very angry⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Yahweh’s nose became very hot”</note> with Amaziah and sent a prophet to him, and he said to him, “Why have you sought the gods of the people who could not deliver their own people from your hand?”

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:16
verses.text: And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> while he was speaking to him, he said to him, “Have we appointed you as a counselor to the king? Stop—<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞why should you be killed⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?”<note placement="foot">Literally “why shall he strike you?”</note> So the prophet stopped and said, “I know that God has determined to destroy you, because you have done this and have not listened to my advice.”  <div eID="gen3285" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2462"/><div sID="gen3286" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2462"/>Then Amaziah king of Judah took counsel, and he sent to Joash the son of Jehoahaz the son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, “Come,<note placement="foot">This translation follows the <hi type="italic">Qere</hi> reading</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞let us face one another⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “let us look at faces”</note>

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:18
verses.text: And Joash the king of Israel sent to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, “The thorn bush that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in Lebanon has sent to the cedar which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in Lebanon, saying, ‘Give your daughter to my son as wife.’ But a wild animal of the field that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in Lebanon passed by and trampled the thorn bush.

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:19
verses.text: Look, you say <transChange type="added">that</transChange> you have struck Edom, and your heart has lifted you up to boast. Now remain at your home. Why stir up disaster that you fall, you and Judah with you?”  <div eID="gen3286" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2463"/><div sID="gen3287" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2463"/>But Amaziah did not listen, for it <transChange type="added">was</transChange> from God that he might give them into the hand <transChange type="added">of enemies</transChange>, because they sought the gods of Edom.

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:21
verses.text: So Joash the king of Israel went up, and he and Amaziah the king of Judah <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞faced one another⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “looked at one another’s faces”</note> at Beth-Shemesh, which belongs to Judah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:22
verses.text: And Judah was defeated before Israel, and each <transChange type="added">man</transChange> fled to his tent.

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:23
verses.text: And Joash the king of Israel captured Amaziah the king of Judah, the son of Joash, the son of Jehoahaz, at Beth-Shemesh. And they brought him <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Jerusalem and broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the Gate of Ephraim to the Corner Gate, four hundred cubits.

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:24
verses.text: Then with all the gold and silver, all the objects found in the house of God with Obed-Edom, the storehouses of the house of the king, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the hostages⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the sons of the pledges”</note> he returned to Samaria.  <div eID="gen3287" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2464"/><div sID="gen3288" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2464"/>And Amaziah the son of Joash, king of Judah, lived after the death of Joash the son of Jehoahaz, the king of Israel, fifteen years.

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:26
verses.text: Now the remainder of the words of Amaziah, <transChange type="added">from</transChange> the first <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the last, behold, are they not written in the scroll of the kings of Judah and Israel?

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:27
verses.text: And from the time that Amaziah turned away from Yahweh, they had plotted a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem. And he fled to Lachish, but they sent after him to Lachish and killed him there.

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:28
verses.text: And they carried him on the horses and buried him with his ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> in the city of Judah.  <chapter eID="2Chr.25"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2465"/><title type="x-s">The Reign of Uzziah</title> <div sID="gen3289" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2465"/>Then all the people of Judah took Uzziah (now he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> sixteen years old) and made him king in the place of his father Amaziah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:2
verses.text: He built Elath and returned it to Judah after the king slept with his ancestors.<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note>

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:3
verses.text: Uzziah <transChange type="added">was</transChange> sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem fifty-two years. And the name of his mother <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Yecoliah of Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:4
verses.text: And he did what <transChange type="added">was</transChange> right in the eyes of Yahweh, according to all that Amaziah his father had done.

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:5
verses.text: And he began to seek<note placement="foot">Or “was seeking”</note> God in the days of Zechariah who was teaching in visions of God. And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞whenever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in the days”</note> he sought Yahweh God made him have success.  <div eID="gen3289" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2466"/><div sID="gen3290" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2466"/>And he went out and made war against the Philistines, and he broke down the wall of Gath and the wall of Jabneh and the wall of Ashdod, and he built cities in Ashdod and among the Philistines.

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:7
verses.text: And God helped him against the Philistines and against the Arabs who were living in Gur-Baal and Meunim.

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:8
verses.text: And the Ammonites gave tribute to Uzziah, and his fame<note placement="foot">Or “name”</note> went out to the boundary<note placement="foot">Literally “to coming in”</note> of Egypt, for he became <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞very strong⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “to above”</note>

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:9
verses.text: And Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem at the Corner Gate, at the Valley Gate, and at the Angle, and he strengthened them.

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:10
verses.text: And he built towers in the desert and hewed many cisterns, for he had much livestock, both in the Shephelah and on the plain, <transChange type="added">along with</transChange> farmers and vinedressers in the hills and in the fertile lands, for he loved the soil.

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:11
verses.text: And Uzziah had troops <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞trained and ready for war⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “making war, going out to fight”</note> in divisions according to the number of their enrollment at the hand of Jeuel the scribe and Maaseiah the officer, under the hand of Hananiah of the king’s commanders.

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:12
verses.text: The whole number of the heads of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞families⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “fathers”</note> for mighty warriors of strength <transChange type="added">was</transChange> two thousand six hundred.

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:13
verses.text: And under their hand <transChange type="added">were</transChange> army troops <transChange type="added">numbering</transChange> three hundred and seven thousand five hundred who could make war with power and strength to help the king against an enemy.

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:14
verses.text: And Uzziah prepared small shields, spears, helmets, breastplates, bows, and slingstones for the whole army.

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:15
verses.text: And he made siege machines in Jerusalem designed <transChange type="added">by</transChange> skillful men to be <transChange type="added">set</transChange> upon the towers and upon the corners to shoot arrows and large slingstones. And his fame<note placement="foot">Or “name”</note> went out far, for he helped marvelously, for he was strong.  <div eID="gen3290" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2467"/><div sID="gen3291" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2467"/>But on account of his strength his heart grew proud unto destruction. And he acted unfaithfully against Yahweh his God and went into the temple of Yahweh to offer an incense offering on the altar.

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:17
verses.text: And Azariah the priest, along with eighty strong priests with him, went in after him.

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:18
verses.text: And they stood against King Uzziah and said to him, “It is not for you, Uzziah, to burn incense to Yahweh, but <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> for the priests, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Aaron, who are consecrated to burn incense. Go out of the sanctuary, for you have acted unfaithfully. There will be no honor for you from Yahweh God.”

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:19
verses.text: Then Uzziah, his censer in hand to burn incense, became angry. And when he became angry with the priests, then leprosy appeared on his forehead in front of the priests in the house of Yahweh at the altar of incense.

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:20
verses.text: When Azariah the chief priest and all the priests turned to him, behold, he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> leprous in the forehead. So they rushed him away from there, and he also hastened to go out, for Yahweh had smitten him.

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:21
verses.text: So King Uzziah was leprous until the day of his death, and he lived in a separate house as a leper, for he was cut off from the house of Yahweh. And Jotham his son <transChange type="added">was</transChange> over the house of the king, judging the people of the land.  <div eID="gen3291" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2468"/><div sID="gen3292" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2468"/>Now the remainder of the words of Uzziah, <transChange type="added">from</transChange> the first <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the last, Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, wrote <transChange type="added">them</transChange>.

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:23
verses.text: And Uzziah slept with his ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and they buried him with his ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> in the burial field which belonged to the kings, because, they said, “He <transChange type="added">was</transChange> leprous.” And Jotham his son reigned in his place.  <chapter eID="2Chr.26"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 27:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2469"/><title type="x-s">The Reign of Jotham</title> <div sID="gen3293" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2469"/>Jotham <transChange type="added">was</transChange> twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. And the name of his mother <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Jerusha the daughter of Zadok.

verses.name: II Chronicles 27:2
verses.text: And he did what was right in the eyes of Yahweh, according to all that his father Uzziah had done—only he did not go into the temple of Yahweh. But the people still acted corruptly.

verses.name: II Chronicles 27:3
verses.text: He built the upper gate of the house of Yahweh, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he did much restoration⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “he built much”</note> on the wall of Ophel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 27:4
verses.text: And he built cities in the hill country of Judah, and he built forts and towers in the wooded places.

verses.name: II Chronicles 27:5
verses.text: Now he fought with the king of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> and prevailed against them. And the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> gave to him in that year one hundred talents of silver and ten thousand measures of wheat and ten thousand measures of barley. This is what the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Ammon”</note> rendered to him, as well as in the second and third year.

verses.name: II Chronicles 27:6
verses.text: And Jotham strengthened himself, for he established his ways before Yahweh his God.  <div eID="gen3293" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 27:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2470"/><div sID="gen3294" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2470"/>Now the remainder of the words of Jotham and all his wars and his ways, behold, they are written upon the scroll of the kings of Israel and Judah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 27:8
verses.text: He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 27:9
verses.text: And Jotham slept with his ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and they buried him in the city of David. And his son Ahaz became king in his place.  <chapter eID="2Chr.27"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2471"/><title type="x-s">The Reign of Ahaz</title> <div sID="gen3295" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2471"/>Ahaz <transChange type="added">was</transChange> twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. And he did not do what is right in the eyes of Yahweh like David his ancestor.<note placement="foot">Or “father”</note>

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:2
verses.text: But he walked in the ways of the kings of Israel and also made molten idols for the Baals.

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:3
verses.text: And he himself burned incense in the valley of Ben-Hinnom and burned his sons in the fire, according to the detestable <transChange type="added">practices</transChange> of the nations whom Yahweh drove out before the Israelites.

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:4
verses.text: And he sacrificed and burned incense at the high places, on the hilltops, and under every flourishing tree.  <div eID="gen3295" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2472"/><div sID="gen3296" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2472"/>Then Yahweh his God gave him into the hand of the king of Aram<note placement="foot">Or “Syria”</note> who defeated him and captured many captives from him and brought <transChange type="added">them to</transChange> Damascus. Moreover, he was also given into the hand of the king of Israel, and he defeated him by a great attack.

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:6
verses.text: And Pekah, the son of Remaliah, killed in one day one hundred and twenty thousand in Judah, all men of strength, because they forsook Yahweh the God of their ancestors.<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note>

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:7
verses.text: And Zikri, a mighty warrior of Ephraim, killed Maaseiah the son of the king, Azrikam the commander of the house, and Elkanah the second to the king.

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:8
verses.text: And the Israelites captured two hundred thousand of their brothers, women, sons, and daughters. And they also plundered much booty from them and brought the booty to Samaria.  <div eID="gen3296" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2473"/><div sID="gen3297" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2473"/>Now a prophet of Yahweh was there; Oded <transChange type="added">was</transChange> his name. And he went out before the army that was coming to Samaria and said to them, “Look, <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> on account of the anger of Yahweh, the God of your ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> against Judah <transChange type="added">that</transChange> he gave them into your hands, and you killed them in a rage reaching to the heavens.

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:10
verses.text: So now, you yourselves plan to subdue people of Judah and Jerusalem as slaves and female servants for yourselves. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Is there not also guilt on your part⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Is there not only you with yourselves guilt?”</note> against Yahweh your God?

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:11
verses.text: So now, listen to me and return the captives of your brothers whom you have taken captive, for the fierce anger of Yahweh <transChange type="added">is</transChange> against you.”  <div eID="gen3297" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2474"/><div sID="gen3298" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2474"/>Then men from the heads of Ephraim—Azariah the son of Jehohanan, Berekiah the son of Meshillemoth, Hezekiah the son of Shallum, and Amasa the son of Hadlai—stood against those returning from the fight.

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:13
verses.text: And they said to them, “You shall not bring the captives here, for <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> as guilt <transChange type="added">against</transChange> Yahweh upon us. You yourselves plan to add to our sins and to our guilt, but our guilt is very great, and <transChange type="added">there is</transChange> great anger against Israel.”

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:14
verses.text: So the soldiers left the captives and the plunder before the commanders and all the assembly.

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:15
verses.text: Then the men designated by name arose and took the captives and from the plunder clothed all their nakedness. So they clothed them, gave them sandals, gave them food to eat, gave them water to drink, anointed them, and guided them with the donkeys <transChange type="added">provided</transChange> for all those who stumbled, and brought them to Jericho, the city of the palm trees, next to their brothers. Then they returned to Samaria.  <div eID="gen3298" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2475"/><div sID="gen3299" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2475"/>At that time King Ahaz sent to the king of Assyria to help him,

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:17
verses.text: since again the Edomites came and struck against Judah and took captives.

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:18
verses.text: And the Philistines sent raids into the cities of the Shephelah and the Negeb of Judah. And they captured Beth-Shemesh, Aijalon, Gederoth, Socoh with its villages, Timnah with its villages, and Gimzo with its villages. And they settled there.

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:19
verses.text: For Yahweh subdued Judah for the sake of Ahaz, king of Israel, for he created disorder in Judah and acted unfaithfully against Yahweh.

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:20
verses.text: Then Tiglath-Pileser<note placement="foot">The Hebrew reads “Tilgath-Pilneser”</note> the king of Assyria came against him and brought trouble for him, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞instead of helping him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “and did not strengthen him”</note>

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:21
verses.text: for Ahaz took a portion <transChange type="added">from</transChange> the house of Yahweh and the house of the king and the princes, and he gave <transChange type="added">it</transChange> to the king of Assyria, but it was no help to him.  <div eID="gen3299" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2476"/><div sID="gen3300" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2476"/>And in the time of his distress, King Ahaz continued to act unfaithfully against Yahweh.

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:23
verses.text: He sacrificed to the gods of Damascus that had defeated him and said, “Because the gods of the king of Aram<note placement="foot">Or “Syria”</note> helped them, I will sacrifice to them so that they will help me.” But they were <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a disaster⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a cause of stumbling”</note> to him and to all Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:24
verses.text: Then Ahaz gathered the objects of the house of God, and he cut the objects of the house of God to pieces. And he shut the doors of the house of Yahweh and made for himself altars in every corner of Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:25
verses.text: And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in every city⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in all city and city”</note> of Judah he made high places to burn incense to other gods, and he provoked Yahweh, the God of his ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> to anger.  <div eID="gen3300" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2477"/><div sID="gen3301" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2477"/>Now the remainder of his words and all his ways, <transChange type="added">from</transChange> the first <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the last, behold, they are written upon the scroll of the kings of Judah and Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:27
verses.text: And Ahaz slept with his ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and they buried him in the city, in Jerusalem, for they did not bring him to the burial site of the kings of Israel. And Hezekiah his son became king in his place.  <chapter eID="2Chr.28"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2478"/><title type="x-s">The Reign of Hezekiah</title> <div sID="gen3302" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2478"/>Hezekiah became king when he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> twenty-five years old, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. And the name of his mother <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Abijah the daughter of Zechariah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:2
verses.text: And he did that which was right in the eyes of Yahweh, according to all that David his father had done.  <div eID="gen3302" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2479"/><div sID="gen3303" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2479"/>In the first year of his kingship, in the first month, he opened the doors of the house of Yahweh and strengthened them.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:4
verses.text: And he brought in the priests and the Levites, and he gathered them into the eastern square.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:5
verses.text: And he said to them, “Hear me, O Levites! Sanctify yourselves now, and sanctify the house of Yahweh, the God of your ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and bring out the defilement from the sanctuary.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:6
verses.text: For our ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> acted unfaithfully and did evil in the sight of Yahweh our God, and have forsaken him and turned away their faces from the dwelling place of Yahweh. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞They have turned their backs⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And they have given back”</note> <transChange type="added">on it</transChange>.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:7
verses.text: They also shut the doors of the portico and extinguished the lamps. And they did not burn incense or offer burnt offerings in the sanctuary to the God of Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:8
verses.text: And the wrath of Yahweh was upon Judah and Jerusalem. And he made them as an abhorrence, as a desolation and an object of scorn, as you see with your own eyes.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:9
verses.text: Now behold, our fathers have fallen by the sword, and our sons and our daughters and our wives <transChange type="added">are</transChange> in captivity on account of this.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:10
verses.text: Now <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞it is in my heart⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “with my heart”</note> to <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞make⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “cut”</note> a covenant with Yahweh, the God of Israel, so that his fierce anger might turn away from him.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:11
verses.text: Now, my sons, do not be negligent, for Yahweh has chosen you to stand before him to serve him and to be his servants and incense burners.”  <div eID="gen3303" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2480"/><div sID="gen3304" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2480"/>Then the Levites arose—Mahath the son of Amasai and Joel the son of Azariah, from the Kohathites; and Kish the son of Abdi and Azariah the son of Jehallelel from the Merarites; and Joah son of Zimmah and Eden son of Joah, from the Gershonites.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:13
verses.text: And from the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Elizaphan: Shimri and Jeiel; and from the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Asaph: Zechariah and Mattaniah;

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:14
verses.text: and from the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Heman: Jeiel and Shimei; and from the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Jeduthun: Shemaiah and Uzziel—

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:15
verses.text: and they gathered their brothers and sanctified themselves, and they went in according to the command of the king because of the words of Yahweh, to purify the house of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:16
verses.text: And the priests went into the inner <transChange type="added">part</transChange> of the house of Yahweh to purify <transChange type="added">it</transChange>. And they brought out all the impurity that they found in the temple of Yahweh <transChange type="added">out</transChange> to the courtyard of the house of Yahweh. And the Levites took <transChange type="added">them</transChange> to bring <transChange type="added">them</transChange> outside to the Wadi<note placement="foot">Or “valley”; a wadi is a valley that is dry most of the year, but contains a stream during the rainy season</note> Kidron.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:17
verses.text: And they began to sanctify themselves on the first day of the first month. And on the eighth day of the month they came to the portico of Yahweh. And they sanctified the house of Yahweh for eight days, and on the sixteenth day of the first month they finished.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:18
verses.text: And they went into the inner <transChange type="added">part</transChange> to King Hezekiah and said, “We have cleansed all the house of Yahweh: the altar of burnt offering, all its objects, the table of the rows <transChange type="added">of bread</transChange> and all its objects,

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:19
verses.text: and all the objects that King Ahaz discarded in his reign when he sinned, we have prepared and sanctified. Look, they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> before the altar of Yahweh.”  <div eID="gen3304" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2481"/><div sID="gen3305" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2481"/>Then King Hezekiah rose early and gathered the officials of the city, and he went up to the house of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:21
verses.text: And they brought seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven male goats as a purification offering for the kingdom, for the sanctuary, and for Judah. And he commanded the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Aaron, the priests, to offer <transChange type="added">them</transChange> on the altar of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:22
verses.text: And they slaughtered the cattle, and the priests received the blood and threw it toward the altar. Then they slaughtered the rams and threw the blood toward the altar, and then they slaughtered the lambs and threw the blood toward the altar.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:23
verses.text: Then they brought the goats of the sin offering before the king and the assembly, and they laid hands upon them.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:24
verses.text: And the priest killed them and offered their blood against the altar to make atonement for all Israel, for the king had commanded the burnt offering and the sin offering for all Israel.  <div eID="gen3305" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2482"/><div sID="gen3306" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2482"/>And he stood the Levites <transChange type="added">in</transChange> the house of Yahweh with cymbals, harps, and lyres, according to the command of David and Gad, the seer of the king, and Nathan the prophet, for the command <transChange type="added">was</transChange> by the hand of Yahweh by the hand of his prophets.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:26
verses.text: When the Levites stood with the objects of David and the priests with the trumpets,

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:27
verses.text: Hezekiah commanded to offer the burnt offering upon the altar. And at the time the burnt offering began, the song of Yahweh began, and also the trumpets, at the hands of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> instruments of David king of Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:28
verses.text: Then all the assembly bowed down, and the song was sung, and the trumpeters trumpeted—all <transChange type="added">together</transChange> until the end of the burnt offering.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:29
verses.text: And when the offering was finished, the king and all who were found with him knelt down and bowed themselves.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:30
verses.text: Then King Hezekiah and the princes commanded the Levites to praise Yahweh with the words of David and Asaph the seer. So they offered praise with joy, and they bowed down and worshiped.  <div eID="gen3306" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2483"/><div sID="gen3307" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2483"/>Then Hezekiah answered and said, “Now <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you have consecrated yourselves⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “you have filled your hands”</note> to Yahweh. Come near and bring sacrifices and thank offerings to the house of Yahweh!” And the assembly brought sacrifices and thank offerings, and all <transChange type="added">who were</transChange> willing in heart <transChange type="added">brought</transChange> burnt offerings.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:32
verses.text: And the number of burnt offerings that the assembly brought was seventy cattle, one hundred rams, two hundred lambs—all these <transChange type="added">were</transChange> to offer to Yahweh.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:33
verses.text: And the consecrated offerings of cattle <transChange type="added">were</transChange> six hundred cattle and three thousand sheep.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:34
verses.text: But the priests were too few, and they were not able to offer all the burnt offerings, so their brothers, the Levites, strengthened them to finish the work, and until the <transChange type="added">rest of</transChange> the priests consecrated themselves. (For the Levites <transChange type="added">were</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞more conscientious⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “more upright of heart”</note> to sanctify themselves than the priests.)

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:35
verses.text: And beside the many burnt offerings <transChange type="added">was</transChange> the fat of the peace offerings and the libations for the burnt offerings. So the service of the house of Yahweh was established.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:36
verses.text: And Hezekiah and all the people rejoiced over what God had established with the people, for the matter happened suddenly.  <chapter eID="2Chr.29"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2484"/><title type="x-s">Hezekiah Celebrates Passover</title> <div sID="gen3308" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2484"/>Then Hezekiah sent to all Israel and Judah, and he also wrote letters to Ephraim and Manasseh, to come to the house of Yahweh in Jerusalem to make a Passover feast to Yahweh the God of Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:2
verses.text: Now the king and his princes, and all the assembly in Jerusalem had taken counsel to make the Passover feast in the second month—

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:3
verses.text: but they were not able to make it at that time, for the priests had not consecrated themselves <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in sufficient numbers⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “for enough”</note> and the people had not been assembled in Jerusalem—

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:4
verses.text: and the plan seemed right in the eyes of the king and in the eyes of all the assembly.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:5
verses.text: So they let the decree stand, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to make a proclamation⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to spread a voice”</note> throughout all Israel, from Beersheba to Dan, to come to make a Passover feast to Yahweh the God of Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:6
verses.text: And the runners went with the letter from the hand of the king and his princes throughout all Israel and Judah according to the command of the king, saying, “O sons of Israel, return to Yahweh, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, that he may turn again to the remnant of you who escaped from the hand of the kings of Assyria.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:7
verses.text: Do not be like your fathers and like your brothers, who acted unfaithfully before Yahweh, the God of their ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> so that he made them as a desolation, as you see.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:8
verses.text: Now, do not stiffen your neck as your fathers,<note placement="foot">Or “ancestors”</note> but give a hand to Yahweh and come to his sanctuary, which he has consecrated forever, and serve Yahweh your God that his fierce anger may turn away from you.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:9
verses.text: For when you return to Yahweh, your brothers and your children <transChange type="added">will find</transChange> compassion before their captors and return to this land, for Yahweh your God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> gracious and compassionate, and he will not turn away his face from you if you return to him.”  <div eID="gen3308" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2485"/><div sID="gen3309" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2485"/>And it happened <transChange type="added">that</transChange> the runners were passing from city to city in the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, and up to Zebulun, but they were laughing at them and mocking them.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:11
verses.text: Only men from Asher, Manasseh, and Zebulun humbled themselves and came to Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:12
verses.text: The hand of God was also upon Judah, to give them one heart to obey the command of the king and the princes concerning the word of Yahweh.  <div eID="gen3309" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2486"/><div sID="gen3310" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2486"/>So many people gathered in Jerusalem to hold the Feast of Unleavened Bread in the second month; <transChange type="added">it was</transChange> a very great assembly.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:14
verses.text: And they rose up and removed the altars that <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in Jerusalem. And they removed all the incense altars and threw <transChange type="added">them</transChange> away in the Wadi<note placement="foot">Or “valley”; a wadi is a valley that is dry most of the year, but contains a stream during the rainy season</note> Kidron.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:15
verses.text: And they slaughtered the Passover lamb on the fourteenth day of the second month. And the priests and the Levites were disgraced, so they consecrated themselves and brought burnt offerings into the house of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:16
verses.text: Then they stood at their positions according to custom, according to the law of Moses the man of God. The priests were sprinkling the blood from the hand of the Levites.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:17
verses.text: For <transChange type="added">there were</transChange> many in the assembly who did not consecrate themselves, so the Levites <transChange type="added">were</transChange> over the killing of the Passover sacrifices for all who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> not clean, to consecrate <transChange type="added">them</transChange> to Yahweh.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:18
verses.text: For a majority of the people, many from Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun, had not cleansed themselves. But they ate the Passover sacrifice <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞otherwise than prescribed⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “in not as it is written”</note> but Hezekiah had prayed for them, saying, “May the good Yahweh make atonement unto

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:19
verses.text: everyone whose heart is set to seek God, Yahweh the God of his ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> though not according to the cleansing for the sanctuary.”

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:20
verses.text: And Yahweh listened to Hezekiah, and he healed the people.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:21
verses.text: And the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> who were found in Jerusalem kept the Feast of Unleavened Bread seven days with great joy. And the Levites and the priests were offering praise to Yahweh day by day, with powerful instruments to Yahweh.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:22
verses.text: And Hezekiah spoke to the heart of all the Levites <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who were skilled at service⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “who were showing good understanding”</note> to Yahweh. So they ate the feast seven days, offering peace offerings and giving thanks to Yahweh, the God of their ancestors.<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note>  <div eID="gen3310" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2487"/><div sID="gen3311" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2487"/>Then the whole assembly decided to make seven more days <transChange type="added">of feasting</transChange>, so they made seven <transChange type="added">more</transChange> days with joy,

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:24
verses.text: for Hezekiah the king of Judah had <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞provided⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “lifted up”</note> one thousand bulls and seven thousand sheep for the assembly, and the princes <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞provided⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “lifted up”</note> one thousand bulls and ten thousand sheep for the assembly. And many priests consecrated themselves.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:25
verses.text: And the whole assembly of Judah, the priests and the Levites, all the assembly who had come from the land of Israel, and those living in Judah rejoiced.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:26
verses.text: And there was great joy in Jerusalem, for from the days of Solomon the son of David, king of Israel, there was nothing such as this in Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:27
verses.text: Then the priests and the Levites arose and blessed the people, and their voice was heard, and their prayer came to his holy dwelling place in the heavens.  <chapter eID="2Chr.30"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2488"/><title type="x-s">Hezekiah Organizes the Priesthood</title> <div sID="gen3312" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2488"/>And when all this was finished, all Israel who were found in the cities of Judah went out and shattered the stone pillars, cut down the Asherahs, and destroyed the high places and the altars from all Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to the very last one⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “until finishing”</note> Then all the Israelites returned, each to his own property <transChange type="added">and</transChange> to their cities.  <div eID="gen3312" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2489"/><div sID="gen3313" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2489"/>And Hezekiah appointed working groups of the priests and the Levites, each according to their divisions, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞according to the service for priests and Levites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “according to the mouth of his service, for priests and Levites”</note> for burnt offerings, for peace offerings, to serve, to give thanks, and to praise in the gates of the camps of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:3
verses.text: And the gift of the king <transChange type="added">was</transChange> out of his own possessions for the burnt offerings—the burnt offerings for the morning and the evening and for Sabbaths, new moon festivals, and appointed feasts, as is written in the law of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:4
verses.text: Then he said to the people, to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, to give a gift for the priests and the Levites, so that they might be strong in the law of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:5
verses.text: And the word spread. The Israelites gave abundantly <transChange type="added">from</transChange> the firstfruits of grain, new wine, olive oil, honey, and all <transChange type="added">kinds of</transChange> grains from the field. And they brought tithes of everything in abundance.

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:6
verses.text: Then the people of Israel and Judah who were living in the cities of Judah, they also brought a tithe of cattle and sheep and a tithe of consecrated objects to Yahweh their God. And they gave heaps <transChange type="added">upon</transChange> heaps.

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:7
verses.text: In the third month the heaps began to pile up, and in the seventh month they ceased.

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:8
verses.text: When Hezekiah and the princes came and saw the heaps, they blessed Yahweh and his people Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:9
verses.text: And Hezekiah questioned<note placement="foot">Or “sought”</note> the priests and the Levites concerning the heaps.

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:10
verses.text: And Azariah the chief priest of the house of Zadok answered him, saying, “Since the offerings began to be brought to the house of Yahweh, <transChange type="added">we have</transChange> eaten and been satisfied, and have much to spare, for Yahweh has blessed his people. Now <transChange type="added">see</transChange> this abundant remainder!”  <div eID="gen3313" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2490"/><div sID="gen3314" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2490"/>And Hezekiah commanded to prepare chambers in the house of Yahweh, and they were prepared.

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:12
verses.text: Then they brought the offerings and tithes and holy objects faithfully. And over them <transChange type="added">as</transChange> leader <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Conaniah the Levite. And Shimei his brother <transChange type="added">was</transChange> second <transChange type="added">in rank</transChange>.

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:13
verses.text: And Jehiel, Azaziah, Nathan, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Benaiah <transChange type="added">were</transChange> chief officers under the hand of Conaniah and Shimei, his brother, by appointment of King Hezekiah. And Azaraiah <transChange type="added">was</transChange> leader of the house of God.

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:14
verses.text: Now Kore the son of Imlah, the Levite, the gatekeeper of the east gate <transChange type="added">was</transChange> over the freewill offerings of God, to give offerings to Yahweh and the most holy things.

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:15
verses.text: And at his hand <transChange type="added">were</transChange> Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah in the cities of the priests <transChange type="added">and</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞entrusted⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in faithfulness”</note> to give to their brothers by working groups, according to the eldest <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the youngest,

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:16
verses.text: besides their enrollment by genealogy, to males from three years old and upward, to all who came into the house of Yahweh, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as each day required⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for the word of the day by his day”</note> for their service in their posts according to their working groups.

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:17
verses.text: And the enrollment of the priests <transChange type="added">was</transChange> according to the house of their fathers, and the Levites, from twenty years old and upward, according to their posts by their working groups.

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:18
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">they were</transChange> enrolled with all their little ones, their wives, their sons, and their daughters for the whole assembly because of their faithfulness. And they sanctified themselves in holiness.

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:19
