verses.text: And for the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Aaron, the priests, who were in the fields of the pasturelands of their cities, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in each and every one of their cities⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in every city and the city”</note> <transChange type="added">were</transChange> men who were designated by name to give shares to every male among the priests and to everyone enrolled among the Levites.  <div eID="gen3314" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2491"/><div sID="gen3315" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2491"/>And Hezekiah did according to this throughout all Judah. And he did what <transChange type="added">is</transChange> good and what <transChange type="added">is</transChange> right and what <transChange type="added">is</transChange> faithful before Yahweh his God.

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:21
verses.text: And in every work that he began in the service of the house of God or with respect to the law and the commandment to seek his God, he did with all his heart, and he prospered.  <chapter eID="2Chr.31"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2492"/><title type="x-s">Sennacherib’s Invasion of Judah</title> <div sID="gen3316" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2492"/>After these things and these <transChange type="added">acts of</transChange> faithfulness, Sennacherib the king of Assyria came, and he came against Judah. And he encamped against the fortified cities and planned to break them down for himself.

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:2
verses.text: When Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had come and <transChange type="added">that</transChange> his face <transChange type="added">was set</transChange> for battle against Jerusalem,

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:3
verses.text: he took counsel with his commanders and his mighty warriors to block off the waters of the springs that <transChange type="added">came</transChange> from outside the city, and they helped him.

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:4
verses.text: Then many people were gathered, and they blocked off all the springs and the river that flowed through the midst of the land, saying, “Why should the kings of Assyria come and find much water?”

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:5
verses.text: Then he strengthened himself and built up all the walls that were broken down, and raised towers upon <transChange type="added">them</transChange> and another wall <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞outside⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “toward the street”</note> And he strengthened the Millo of the city of David and made much weaponry and small shields.

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:6
verses.text: And he appointed commanders for battle over the people and gathered them to himself into the public square of the gate of the city. And he spoke to their hearts, saying,

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:7
verses.text: “Be strong! Be courageous! Do not fear and do not be dismayed before the king of Assyria and before all the crowd that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> with him, for <transChange type="added">there are</transChange> more with us than with him.

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:8
verses.text: With him <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the arm of flesh, and with us <transChange type="added">is</transChange> Yahweh our God, to help us and to fight our battles.” And the people took confidence with the words of Hezekiah, king of Judah.  <div eID="gen3316" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2493"/><div sID="gen3317" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2493"/>After this Sennacherib the king of Assyria sent his servants to Jerusalem (now he and all his armies with him <transChange type="added">were</transChange> against Lachish) to Hezekiah king of Judah and to all of Judah that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in Jerusalem, saying,

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:10
verses.text: “Thus says Sennacherib the king of Assyria: ‘On what <transChange type="added">are</transChange> you relying that <transChange type="added">you are</transChange> dwelling in siege works in Jerusalem?

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:11
verses.text: Is not Hezekiah urging you to give you <transChange type="added">up</transChange> to die by starvation and thirst, saying, “Yahweh our God will save us from the hand of the king of Assyria”?

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:12
verses.text: Has not Hezekiah himself removed his high places and his altars and said to Judah and to Jerusalem, saying, “You must bow down before one altar and upon it you must make offerings”?

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:13
verses.text: Do you not know what I have done, I and my ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> to all the peoples of the lands? Were the gods of the nations of all the lands at all able to save their land from my hand?

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:14
verses.text: Who among all the gods of those nations whom my ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> utterly destroyed was able to save his people from my hand, that your God will be able to save you from my hand?

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:15
verses.text: So now, do not let Hezekiah deceive you. Do not let him urge you according to this. Do not put trust in him, for no god of any nation and kingdom has been able to save his people from my hand and from the hand of my ancestors.<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> Surely then your God will not save you from my hand!’ ”  <div eID="gen3317" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2494"/><div sID="gen3318" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2494"/>And still more his servants said against Yahweh God and against Hezekiah his servant.

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:17
verses.text: And he wrote letters to treat Yahweh the God of Israel with contempt and spoke against him, saying, “As the gods of the nations of the earth who did not save their people from my hand, so likewise the God of Hezekiah will not save his people from my hand.”

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:18
verses.text: Then they called with a great voice in Judean to the people of Jerusalem who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> upon the wall to frighten them and terrify them, so that they could take the city captive.

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:19
verses.text: And they spoke about the God of Jerusalem as about the gods of the peoples of the earth, the works of the hands of humankind.  <div eID="gen3318" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2495"/><title type="x-s">Yahweh’s Deliverance of Jerusalem</title> <div sID="gen3319" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2495"/>Then King Hezekiah and Isaiah the son of Amoz, the prophet, prayed concerning this. And they cried to the heavens.

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:21
verses.text: Then Yahweh sent an angel, and he destroyed every mighty warrior of strength, commander, and officer in the camp of the king of Assyria. And he returned with shamed face to his land and went into the house of his god. And some of the offspring of his loins fell upon him there with the sword.

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:22
verses.text: So Yahweh saved Hezekiah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem from the hand of Sennacherib, king of Assyria, and from the all <transChange type="added">their enemies</transChange>, and gave them rest all around.

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:23
verses.text: And many brought tribute to Yahweh, to Jerusalem, and precious things to Hezekiah king of Judah, so that he was exalted in the eyes of all the nations thereafter.  <div eID="gen3319" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2496"/><title type="x-s">The Rest of Hezekiah’s Reign</title> <div sID="gen3320" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2496"/>In those days Hezekiah fell ill unto death, and he prayed to Yahweh. And he answered him and gave him a sign.

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:25
verses.text: But Hezekiah did not reciprocate according to the benefit <transChange type="added">placed</transChange> upon him, because his heart became proud. So wrath was upon him and upon Judah and Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:26
verses.text: But Hezekiah humbled himself with respect to the arrogance of his heart, he and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so that the wrath of Yahweh did not come upon them in the days of Hezekiah.  <div eID="gen3320" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2497"/><div sID="gen3321" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2497"/>And Hezekiah had very much wealth and honor, and he made storehouses for himself for silver, gold, precious stones, spices, small shields, and all <transChange type="added">sorts of</transChange> desirable objects;

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:28
verses.text: and storage buildings for the yield of grain, new wine, and olive oil; and animal stalls for all <transChange type="added">kinds of</transChange> animals, and animals and herds for animal stalls.

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:29
verses.text: And he made cities for himself, and livestock of sheep and abundant cattle, for God had given to him very abundant possessions.

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:30
verses.text: And this same Hezekiah blocked off the flow of the waters of the upper Gihon, and directed them down the west <transChange type="added">side</transChange> of the city of David. And Hezekiah prospered in all his works.

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:31
verses.text: And thus <transChange type="added">in the matter of</transChange> the envoys of the commanders of Babylon who had been sent to him to seek the sign that had happened in the land, God forsook him, to test him <transChange type="added">and</transChange> to know all <transChange type="added">that was</transChange> in his heart.  <div eID="gen3321" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2498"/><div sID="gen3322" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2498"/>Now the remainder of the words of Hezekiah and his loyal love, behold, they are written in the visions of Isaiah the son of Amoz, the prophet, upon the scroll of the kings of Judah and Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:33
verses.text: And Hezekiah slept with his ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and they buried him in the upper part of the burial sites of the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of David. And all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem did him honor at his death. And Manasseh his son became king in his place.  <chapter eID="2Chr.32"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2499"/><title type="x-s">The Reign of Manasseh</title> <div sID="gen3323" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2499"/>Manasseh <transChange type="added">was</transChange> twelve years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:2
verses.text: And he did evil in the eyes of Yahweh according to the detestable things of the nations whom Yahweh drove out before the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note>

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:3
verses.text: And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he rebuilt⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “returned and built”</note> the high places that Hezekiah his father broke down, and he set up altars for the Baals, made Asherahs, and bowed down to the host of heaven and served them.

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:4
verses.text: And he built altars in the house of Yahweh, <transChange type="added">of</transChange> which Yahweh had said, “In Jerusalem my name shall be forever.”

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:5
verses.text: And he built altars to all the host of heaven in the two courtyards of the house of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:6
verses.text: And he himself burned his sons in the fire in the Valley of Ben-Hinnom. And he practiced sorcery and divination, and he engaged in witchcraft and dealt with mediums and spiritists. And he did much evil in the eyes of Yahweh, to provoke him to anger.

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:7
verses.text: And he placed the carved image of the idol that he had made in the house of God, <transChange type="added">of</transChange> which God had said to David and to Solomon his son, “In this house and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen from all the tribes of Israel, I will put my name forever.

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:8
verses.text: And I will <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞never⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “not continue to”</note> remove the foot of Israel from upon the land that I appointed to your ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> if only you will take care to do all that I have commanded them, all the law, the regulations, and the judgments by the hand of Moses.”

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:9
verses.text: And Manasseh seduced Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to do evil more than the nations that Yahweh destroyed before the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note>  <div eID="gen3323" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2500"/><title type="x-s">Manasseh’s Repentance</title> <div sID="gen3324" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2500"/>And Yahweh spoke to Manasseh and to his people, but they would not listen.

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:11
verses.text: So Yahweh brought the commanders of the army of the king of Assyria upon them, and they took Manasseh captive with hooks, and they bound him with bronze fetters and brought him to Babylon.

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:12
verses.text: And when he was in distress he entreated Yahweh his God and greatly humbled himself before the God of his ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note>

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:13
verses.text: and prayed to him. And God responded to him and heard his plea and let him return to Jerusalem to his kingdom. And Manasseh knew that Yahweh was God.  <div eID="gen3324" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2501"/><div sID="gen3325" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2501"/>Then afterward he built an outer wall for the city of David west of the Gihon in the valley, and for the entrance into the Gate of the Fishes. And it encircled the Ophel and raised it very high. Then he placed strong commanders in all the fortified cities of Judah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:15
verses.text: And he removed the foreign gods and the carved image from the house of Yahweh and all the altars which he built on the mountain of the house of Yahweh and in Jerusalem, and he threw them outside the city.

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:16
verses.text: And he restored the altar of Yahweh and offered sacrifices of peace offerings and thank offerings upon it. And he commanded Judah to serve Yahweh, the God of Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:17
verses.text: Nevertheless, the people offered at the high places, but only to Yahweh their God.  <div eID="gen3325" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2502"/><div sID="gen3326" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2502"/>Now the remainder of the words of Manasseh and his prayer to his God and the words of the seers who spoke to him in the name of Yahweh, the God of Israel, behold, they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> in the words of the kings of Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:19
verses.text: And his prayer, and <transChange type="added">how</transChange> he<note placement="foot">That is, God</note> responded to him, all his sin and his unfaithful acts, and the places where he built the high places and set up Asherahs and idols before he humbled himself, behold, they are written in the words of the seers.  <div eID="gen3326" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2503"/><title type="x-s">Amon’s Reign</title> <div sID="gen3327" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2503"/>And Manasseh slept with his ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and they buried him in his house. And Amon his son became king in his place.

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:21
verses.text: Amon <transChange type="added">was</transChange> twenty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:22
verses.text: And he did what <transChange type="added">was</transChange> evil in the eyes of Yahweh as Manasseh his father had done. And Amon sacrificed to all the idols that Manasseh his father had made, and he served them.

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:23
verses.text: And he did not humble himself before Yahweh, as Manasseh his father humbled himself, but Amon himself multiplied <transChange type="added">his</transChange> guilt.

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:24
verses.text: And his servants conspired against him and killed him in his house.

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:25
verses.text: But the people of the land struck down all who conspired against King Amon. And the people of the land made his son Josiah king in his place.  <chapter eID="2Chr.33"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2504"/><title type="x-s">The Reign of Josiah</title> <div sID="gen3328" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2504"/>Josiah <transChange type="added">was</transChange> eight years old when he became king, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:2
verses.text: And he did what was right in the eyes of Yahweh, and he walked in the ways of David his ancestor<note placement="foot">Or “father”</note> and did not deviate <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the right or <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the left.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:3
verses.text: In the eighth year of his reign, while he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> still a boy, he began to seek the God of David his ancestor.<note placement="foot">Or “father”</note> And in the twelfth year he began to cleanse Judah and Jerusalem of the high places, the Asherahs, the idols, and the images.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:4
verses.text: And he destroyed before him the altars for the Baals, and he cut down the incense stands above them. And the Asherahs, the idols, and the images he smashed. And he ground <transChange type="added">them</transChange> to powder and sprinkled <transChange type="added">the dust</transChange> over the burial sites of those who sacrificed to them.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:5
verses.text: And he burned the bones of the priests on the altars and cleansed Judah and Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:6
verses.text: And in the cities of Manasseh, Ephraim, Simeon, and as far as Naphtali, in their ruins all around,

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:7
verses.text: he broke down the altars and the Asherahs and crushed the idols, grinding <transChange type="added">them</transChange> to dust, and he cut down all the incense stands in all the land of Israel. Then he returned to Jerusalem.  <div eID="gen3328" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2505"/><title type="x-s">The Scroll of the Law Discovered</title> <div sID="gen3329" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2505"/>Now in the eighteenth year of his reign <transChange type="added">after</transChange> he purged the land and the house, he sent Shaphan the son of Azaliah, Maaseiah the commander of the city, and Joah the son of Joahaz, the recorder, to repair the house of Yahweh his God.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:9
verses.text: And they came to Hilkiah the high priest and gave the money that was brought for the house of God, which the Levites, the guardians of the threshold, had gathered from the hand of Manasseh, Ephraim, and from the whole remnant of Israel, and from all Judah and Benjamin and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:10
verses.text: And they delivered <transChange type="added">it</transChange> into the hand of the workmen who were appointed in the house of Yahweh, and they <transChange type="added">in turn</transChange> gave it to those doing the work who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> at work in the house of Yahweh, to repair <transChange type="added">and</transChange> restore the house.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:11
verses.text: And they dispensed<note placement="foot">Or “gave”</note> <transChange type="added">it</transChange> to the skilled craftsmen and the builders to buy stone <transChange type="added">for</transChange> hewing and timber for the seams and for binding the houses that the kings of Judah had destroyed.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:12
verses.text: And the men did the work faithfully. Over them as supervisors <transChange type="added">were</transChange> appointed Jahath and Obadiah, the Levites from the Merarites, and Zechariah and Meshullam from the Kohathites. And <transChange type="added">other</transChange> Levites, all who were skilled in instruments of song,

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:13
verses.text: <transChange type="added">were</transChange> over the porters and were directing all who worked <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞on each task⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “for service and service”</note> And some of the Levites <transChange type="added">were</transChange> scribes, officials, and gatekeepers.  <div eID="gen3329" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2506"/><div sID="gen3330" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2506"/>And when they brought out the money that had been brought <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the house of Yahweh, Hilkiah the priest found a scroll of the law of Yahweh by the hand of Moses.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:15
verses.text: And Hilkiah answered and said to Shaphan the scribe, “I have found a scroll of the law in the house of Yahweh!” Then Hilkiah gave the scroll to Shaphan.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:16
verses.text: And Shaphan brought the scroll to the king and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞also informed⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “returned again a word to”</note> the king, saying, “All that was put into the hand of your servants they are doing.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:17
verses.text: They have dispensed<note placement="foot">Or “emptied out”</note> the money which was found in the house of Yahweh and have put it into the hand of the overseers and those doing the work.”

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:18
verses.text: Then Shaphan the scribe reported to the king, “Hilkiah the priest gave to me a scroll.” Then Shaphan read from it before the king.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:19
verses.text: And when the king heard the words of the law, he tore his garments,

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:20
verses.text: and the king commanded Hilkiah, Ahikam the son of Shaphan, Abdon the son of Micah, Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah the servant of the king, saying,

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:21
verses.text: “Go! Seek Yahweh on my behalf and on behalf of those remaining in Israel and Judah concerning the words of the scroll that was found, for the anger of Yahweh that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> poured out on us <transChange type="added">is</transChange> great, because our ancestors<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> have not kept the word of Yahweh, to do all that is written in this scroll.”  <div eID="gen3330" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2507"/><div sID="gen3331" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2507"/>Then Hilkiah and those whom the king <transChange type="added">had sent</transChange> went to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum, son of Tikvath, son of Hasrah, keeper of the garments. (Now she was living in Jerusalem in the second district.) And they spoke to her concerning this.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:23
verses.text: And she said to them, “Thus says Yahweh, the God of Israel: ‘Say to the man who sent you all to me:

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:24
verses.text: “Thus says Yahweh: ‘Behold, I am bringing disaster upon this place and upon its inhabitants—all the curses written in the scroll that were read before the king of Judah—

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:25
verses.text: because they have abandoned me and burned incense to other gods so as to provoke me to anger with all the works of their hands. And my wrath will be poured out on this place and it will not be quenched.’

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:26
verses.text: But to the king of Judah who sent you to seek Yahweh, thus shall you say to him: ‘Thus says Yahweh, the God of Israel: <transChange type="added">As for</transChange> the words which you heard,

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:27
verses.text: because your heart was responsive and you humbled yourself before God when you heard his words against this place and against its inhabitants and you humbled yourself before me and tore your garments and wept before me, now I also have heard,’ <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞declares⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “declaration of”</note> Yahweh.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:28
verses.text: ‘Behold, I will gather you to your ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and you will be gathered to your grave in peace. Your eyes will not see any of the disaster that I am bringing upon this place.’ ” ’ ”  <div eID="gen3331" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2508"/><div sID="gen3332" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2508"/>Then they sent <transChange type="added">word</transChange> to the king, and he gathered all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:30
verses.text: And the king went up to the house of Yahweh with all the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, with the priests and the Levites—all the people from great to small—and they read in their ears all the words of the scroll of the covenant that was found in the house of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:31
verses.text: And the king stood at his position. And he made the covenant before Yahweh, to walk after Yahweh and to keep his commands and statutes and regulations with all his heart and with all his soul, to do the words of the covenant that <transChange type="added">were</transChange> written on this scroll.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:32
verses.text: Then he obligated<note placement="foot">Or “stood”</note> all who were found in Jerusalem and in Benjamin, that the inhabitants of Jerusalem would do according to the covenant of God, the God of their ancestors.<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note>

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:33
verses.text: And Josiah removed all the detestable things from the whole land that belonged to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> and obligated<note placement="foot">Or “made”</note> all who were found in Israel to serve Yahweh their God. All his days they did not turn aside from following<note placement="foot">Or “after”</note> Yahweh, the God of their ancestors.<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note>  <chapter eID="2Chr.34"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 35:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2509"/><title type="x-s">Josiah Observes the Passover</title> <div sID="gen3333" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2509"/>Josiah kept<note placement="foot">Or “made”</note> the Passover to Yahweh in Jerusalem. And they slaughtered the Passover <transChange type="added">sacrifice</transChange> on the fourteenth day of the first month.

verses.name: II Chronicles 35:2
verses.text: And he set the priests at their posts and encouraged them in the service of the house of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Chronicles 35:3
verses.text: And he said to the Levites who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> teaching all Israel, who were sanctified to Yahweh, “Put the holy ark in the house which Solomon the son of David, king of Israel, built. There is no <transChange type="added">need</transChange> to carry it on <transChange type="added">your</transChange> shoulders. Now serve Yahweh your God and his people Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 35:4
verses.text: And prepare yourselves according to <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞your families⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the house of your fathers”</note> according to your working groups, according to the decree<note placement="foot">Or “writing”</note> of David king of Israel and according to the decree<note placement="foot">Or “writing”</note> of Solomon his son.

verses.name: II Chronicles 35:5
verses.text: And stand in the sanctuary according to the clans of <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞your families⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the house of your fathers”</note> for your brothers, the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞lay people⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons of the people”</note> and a part of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞family⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “house of the father”</note> of the Levites.

verses.name: II Chronicles 35:6
verses.text: And slaughter the Passover <transChange type="added">lamb</transChange> and consecrate yourself and prepare for your brothers to do according to the word of Yahweh by the hand of Moses.  <div eID="gen3333" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 35:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2510"/><div sID="gen3334" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2510"/>Then Josiah provided for the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞lay people⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons of the people”</note> sheep, lambs, and young goats, all for the Passover for all who were found <transChange type="added">there</transChange>, to the sum of thirty thousand, along with three thousand bulls. These <transChange type="added">were</transChange> the possession of the king.

verses.name: II Chronicles 35:8
verses.text: And his officials contributed a freewill offering to the people, to the priests, and to the Levites. Hilkiah, Zechariah, and Jehiel, commanders of the house of God, gave to the priests two thousand six hundred Passover <transChange type="added">lambs</transChange> and three hundred bulls.

verses.name: II Chronicles 35:9
verses.text: Conaniah also, and Shemaiah and Nethanel his brothers, and Hashabiah and Jeiel and Jehozabad, commanders of the Levites, contributed to the Levites five thousand Passover <transChange type="added">lambs</transChange> and five hundred bulls.  <div eID="gen3334" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 35:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2511"/><div sID="gen3335" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2511"/>And when the work had been completed, the priests stood at their positions and the Levites in their working groups according to the command of the king.

verses.name: II Chronicles 35:11
verses.text: And they slaughtered the Passover <transChange type="added">lamb</transChange>, and the priests sprinkled <transChange type="added">the blood</transChange> from their hand, and the Levites flayed <transChange type="added">the sacrifices</transChange>.

verses.name: II Chronicles 35:12
verses.text: And they set aside the burnt offerings to give them to the clans of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞families⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “house of the fathers”</note> for the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞lay people⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons of the people”</note> to offer to Yahweh according to what is written in the scroll of Moses. And thus they did with the bulls.

verses.name: II Chronicles 35:13
verses.text: Then they roasted the Passover <transChange type="added">lamb</transChange> in the fire according to the ordinance. And they boiled the holy offerings in pots, in kettles, and in dishes and brought it quickly to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞lay people⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons of the people”</note>

verses.name: II Chronicles 35:14
verses.text: And afterward they prepared for themselves and for the priests, since the priests, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Aaron, were busy with offering the burnt offerings and the fat until night. So the Levites prepared for themselves and for the priests, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Aaron.

verses.name: II Chronicles 35:15
verses.text: And the singers, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Asaph, were at their stations according to the decree<note placement="foot">Or “command”</note> of David and Asaph and Heman and Jeduthun, the seer of the king. And the gatekeepers were at <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞each gate⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “gate to gate”</note> They did not need to depart from their service, for their brothers the Levites had made preparations for them.  <div eID="gen3335" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 35:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2512"/><div sID="gen3336" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2512"/>So all the service of Yahweh was prepared on that day to keep<note placement="foot">Or “make”</note> the Passover and to sacrifice burnt offerings on the altar of Yahweh, according to the command of King Josiah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 35:17
verses.text: And the Israelites who were present kept<note placement="foot">Or “made”</note> the Passover at that time, and the Feast of Unleavened Bread seven days.

verses.name: II Chronicles 35:18
verses.text: And there was no Passover like it kept<note placement="foot">Or “made”</note> in Israel since the days of Samuel the prophet. And none of the kings of Israel kept<note placement="foot">Or “made”</note> a Passover like that which Josiah and the priests and the Levites, and all of Judah and Israel who were present, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, kept.<note placement="foot">Or “made”</note>

verses.name: II Chronicles 35:19
verses.text: In the eighteenth year of the reign of Josiah this Passover was kept.<note placement="foot">Or “made”</note>  <div eID="gen3336" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 35:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2513"/><title type="x-s">The Death of Josiah</title> <div sID="gen3337" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2513"/>After all of this that Josiah had prepared <transChange type="added">for</transChange> the temple,<note placement="foot">Or “house”</note> Neco the king of Egypt went up to make war at Carchemish on the Euphrates, and Josiah went up to meet him.

verses.name: II Chronicles 35:21
verses.text: And he<note placement="foot">That is, Neco</note> sent messengers to him, saying, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞What is there between us⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “What to me and to you”</note> O king of Judah? <transChange type="added">I am</transChange> not against you yourself this day, but against the house making war against me. And God has commanded me to make haste. Stop <transChange type="added">opposing</transChange> God, who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> with me that he will not destroy you.”

verses.name: II Chronicles 35:22
verses.text: But Josiah did not turn his face from him, but he disguised himself to fight with him. He did not listen to the words of Neco from the mouth of God, and he went out to fight in the plain of Megiddo.

verses.name: II Chronicles 35:23
verses.text: And the archers shot King Josiah, and the king said to his servants, “Take me away, for I am badly wounded.”

verses.name: II Chronicles 35:24
verses.text: So his servants took him out of the chariot and transported him in his second chariot and brought him to Jerusalem. And he died and was buried in the burial sites of his ancestors.<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> And all Judah and Jerusalem mourned over Josiah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 35:25
verses.text: And Jeremiah uttered a lament for Josiah, and all the male and female singers have spoken in their laments about Josiah to this day. And they made them a requirement in Israel, and behold, they are written in the laments.  <div eID="gen3337" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 35:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2514"/><div sID="gen3338" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2514"/>Now the remainder of the words of Josiah and his loyal love <transChange type="added">for</transChange> what is written in the law of Yahweh

verses.name: II Chronicles 35:27
verses.text: and his words, <transChange type="added">from</transChange> the first <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the last, behold, they are written in the scroll of the kings of Israel and Judah.  <chapter eID="2Chr.35"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 36:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2515"/><title type="x-s">The Decline of Judah</title> <div sID="gen3339" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2515"/>And the people of the land took Jehoahaz the son of Josiah and made him king in place of his father in Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 36:2
verses.text: Jehoahaz <transChange type="added">was</transChange> twenty-three years old when he began to reign, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 36:3
verses.text: Then the king of Egypt deposed him in Jerusalem and laid a tribute upon the land <transChange type="added">of</transChange> one hundred talents of silver and one talent of gold.

verses.name: II Chronicles 36:4
verses.text: And the king of Egypt made Eliakim his brother king over Judah and Jerusalem, and he changed his name to Jehoiakim. But Neco took Jehoahaz his brother and brought him to Egypt.  <div eID="gen3339" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 36:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2516"/><div sID="gen3340" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2516"/>Jehoiakim <transChange type="added">was</transChange> twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. And he did evil in the eyes of Yahweh his God.

verses.name: II Chronicles 36:6
verses.text: Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon went up against him, and he bound him with bronze fetters to bring him to Babylon.

verses.name: II Chronicles 36:7
verses.text: And Nebuchadnezzar brought to Babylon the objects of the house of Yahweh and put them into the temple in Babylon.

verses.name: II Chronicles 36:8
verses.text: Now the remainder of the words of Jehoiakim and the detestable things that he did and what was found against him, behold, they are written in the scroll of the kings of Israel and Judah. And Jehoiachin his son reigned in his place.  <div eID="gen3340" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 36:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2517"/><div sID="gen3341" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2517"/>Jehoiachin <transChange type="added">was</transChange> eighteen years old when he became king, and he reigned three months and ten days in Jerusalem. And he did evil in the eyes of Yahweh.

verses.name: II Chronicles 36:10
verses.text: And at the turn of the year King Nebuchadnezzar sent and brought him to Babylon, with objects of the treasure of the house of Yahweh. And he made Zedekiah his brother king in Judah and Jerusalem.  <div eID="gen3341" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 36:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2518"/><div sID="gen3342" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2518"/>Zedekiah <transChange type="added">was</transChange> twenty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 36:12
verses.text: And he did evil in the eyes of Yahweh his God. He did not humble himself before Jeremiah the prophet <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who spoke for⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from the mouth of”</note> Yahweh.

verses.name: II Chronicles 36:13
verses.text: And he also rebelled against King Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear by God. He stiffened his neck and hardened his heart against turning to Yahweh, the God of Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 36:14
verses.text: All the leaders of the priests and the people likewise increased in unfaithfulness according to all the detestable things of the nations. And they polluted the house of Yahweh that he had consecrated in Jerusalem.  <div eID="gen3342" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 36:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2519"/><div sID="gen3343" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2519"/>And Yahweh, the God of their ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> had repeatedly and persistently sent to them by the hand of his messengers, because he had compassion on his people and on his dwelling place.

verses.name: II Chronicles 36:16
verses.text: But they were mocking the messengers of God and despising his words and scoffing at his prophets until the wrath of Yahweh rose against his people until there was no remedy.  <div eID="gen3343" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 36:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2520"/><title type="x-s">The Destruction of Jerusalem</title> <div sID="gen3344" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2520"/>Therefore he brought against them the king of the Chaldeans, and he killed their young men with the sword in the house of their sanctuary. He showed no mercy on a young man, a virgin, <transChange type="added">the</transChange> elderly, or decrepit. He delivered all into his hand.

verses.name: II Chronicles 36:18
verses.text: And all the vessels of the house of God, the great and the small, the storehouses of the house of Yahweh, and the storehouses of the king and his princes, these all he brought to Babylon.

verses.name: II Chronicles 36:19
verses.text: And they burned the house of God. And they shattered the walls of Jerusalem and burned its citadels with fire and destroyed all the vessels of its treasuries.

verses.name: II Chronicles 36:20
verses.text: And he took <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞those who escaped the sword⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the remainder from the sword”</note> to Babylon. And they became servants to him and to his sons until the rule of the kingdom of Persia,

verses.name: II Chronicles 36:21
verses.text: to fulfill the word of Yahweh by the mouth of Jeremiah, until the land has enjoyed its Sabbaths. All the days of desolation it kept Sabbath, to fulfill seventy years.  <div eID="gen3344" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 36:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2521"/><title type="x-s">The Decree of Cyrus</title> <div sID="gen3345" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2521"/>And in the first year of Cyrus, the king of Persia, in order to fulfill the word of Yahweh by the mouth of Jeremiah, Yahweh stirred up the spirit of Cyrus, king of Persia, so that he <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞made a proclamation⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “extended a voice”</note> throughout all his kingdom and also in writing, saying:

verses.name: II Chronicles 36:23
verses.text: “Thus says Cyrus, king of Persia: ‘Yahweh the God of heaven has given to me all the kingdoms of the earth, and he has appointed me to build a house for him at Jerusalem, which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in Judah. Whoever <transChange type="added">is</transChange> among you from all his people, may Yahweh his God go up with him.’ ”  <chapter eID="2Chr.36"/> <div eID="gen3345" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen3171" osisID="2Chr" type="book"/>

verses.name: Ezra 1:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2522"/><title type="x-s">The Decree of Cyrus</title> <div sID="gen3347" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2522"/>In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, in order to accomplish the word of Yahweh by the mouth of Jeremiah, Yahweh stirred the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia and he sent a message to all of his kingdom and also <transChange type="added">put the message</transChange> in writing:  <div eID="gen3347" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ezra 1:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2523"/><div sID="gen3348" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2523"/>“Thus says Cyrus king of Persia: Yahweh, the God of the heavens, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth. And he himself has appointed me to build a house for him in Jerusalem, which is in Judah.

verses.name: Ezra 1:3
verses.text: Whoever among you <transChange type="added">who is</transChange> from all of his people, may his God be with him and may he go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judah, and may he build the house of Yahweh, the God of Israel. He is the God who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in Jerusalem.

verses.name: Ezra 1:4
verses.text: And let every survivor, from wherever he <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞resides⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “resides as a foreigner”</note> be assisted by the men of that place with silver and gold, with possessions and domestic animals, and with the freewill offering for the house of God which is in Jerusalem.”  <div eID="gen3348" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ezra 1:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2524"/><div sID="gen3349" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2524"/>So the heads of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞families⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “fathers”</note> for Judah and Benjamin, and the priests and the Levites—to all whose spirit God had stirred—<transChange type="added">prepared</transChange> to go up and build the house of Yahweh which is in Jerusalem.

verses.name: Ezra 1:6
verses.text: And all of their neighbors <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞helped them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “helped with their hands”</note> with objects of silver, gold, possessions, domestic animal<transChange type="added">s</transChange>, and with valuable gifts—besides all of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> freewill offering.

verses.name: Ezra 1:7
verses.text: And Cyrus the king brought out the objects of the house of Yahweh that Nebuchadnezzar had brought from Jerusalem and placed in the house of his gods.

verses.name: Ezra 1:8
verses.text: Cyrus the king of Persia let them go out by the hand of Mithredath the treasurer, and he counted them out to Sheshbazzar the prince of Judah.

verses.name: Ezra 1:9
verses.text: Now these were the inventories: thirty gold metal dishes, one thousand silver metal dishes, twenty-nine vessels,

verses.name: Ezra 1:10
verses.text: thirty bowls of gold, four hundred and ten matching silver metal bowls, and one thousand other objects.

verses.name: Ezra 1:11
verses.text: All of the objects of gold and silver metal <transChange type="added">were</transChange> five thousand four hundred. All this Sheshbazzar brought up along with the exiles from Babylonia to Jerusalem.  <chapter eID="Ezra.1"/>

verses.name: Ezra 2:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2525"/><title type="x-s">The List of Returned Exiles</title> <div sID="gen3350" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2525"/>Now these were the people<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of the province who came up from the captivity of the exile whom Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon carried captive to Babylonia. They returned to Jerusalem and Judah, each to his <transChange type="added">own</transChange> city.

verses.name: Ezra 2:2
verses.text: They came with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah, Reelaiah, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispar, Bigvai, Rehum, and Baanah. <div eID="gen3350" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3351" type="x-p"/> The number of the men of the people of Israel:

verses.name: Ezra 2:3
verses.text: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Parosh, two thousand one hundred and seventy-two;

verses.name: Ezra 2:4
verses.text: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Shephatiah, three hundred and seventy-two;

verses.name: Ezra 2:5
verses.text: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Arah, seven hundred and seventy-five;

verses.name: Ezra 2:6
verses.text: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Pahath-moab, particularly the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Jeshua and Joab, two thousand eight hundred and twelve;

verses.name: Ezra 2:7
verses.text: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Elam, one thousand two hundred and fifty-four;

verses.name: Ezra 2:8
verses.text: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Zattu, nine hundred and forty-five;

verses.name: Ezra 2:9
verses.text: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Zaccai, seven hundred and sixty;

verses.name: Ezra 2:10
verses.text: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Bani, six hundred and forty-two;

verses.name: Ezra 2:11
verses.text: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Bebai, six hundred and twenty-three;

verses.name: Ezra 2:12
verses.text: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Azgad, one thousand two hundred and twenty-two;

verses.name: Ezra 2:13
verses.text: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Adonikam, six hundred and sixty-six;

verses.name: Ezra 2:14
verses.text: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Bigvai, two thousand fifty-six;

verses.name: Ezra 2:15
verses.text: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Adin, four hundred and fifty-four;

verses.name: Ezra 2:16
verses.text: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Ater, <transChange type="added">particularly</transChange> of Hezekiah, ninety-eight;

verses.name: Ezra 2:17
verses.text: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Bezai, three hundred and twenty-three;

verses.name: Ezra 2:18
verses.text: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Jorah, one hundred and twelve;

verses.name: Ezra 2:19
verses.text: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Hashum, two hundred and twenty-three;

verses.name: Ezra 2:20
verses.text: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Gibbar, ninety-five;

verses.name: Ezra 2:21
verses.text: the people<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Bethlehem, one hundred and twenty-three;

verses.name: Ezra 2:22
verses.text: the men of Netophah, fifty-six;

verses.name: Ezra 2:23
verses.text: the men of Anathoth, one hundred and twenty-eight;

verses.name: Ezra 2:24
verses.text: the people<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Azmaveth, forty-two;

verses.name: Ezra 2:25
verses.text: the people<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Kiriath Αrim, Kephirah, and Beeroth, seven hundred and forty-three;

verses.name: Ezra 2:26
verses.text: the people<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Ramah and Geba, six hundred and twenty-one;

verses.name: Ezra 2:27
verses.text: the men of Micmash, one hundred and twenty-two;

verses.name: Ezra 2:28
verses.text: the men of Bethel and Ai, two hundred and twenty-three;

verses.name: Ezra 2:29
verses.text: the people<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Nebo, fifty-two;

verses.name: Ezra 2:30
verses.text: the people<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Magbish, one hundred and fifty-six;

verses.name: Ezra 2:31
verses.text: the people<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of the other Elam, one thousand two hundred and fifty-four;

verses.name: Ezra 2:32
verses.text: the people<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Harim, three hundred and twenty;

verses.name: Ezra 2:33
verses.text: the people<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Lod, Hadid, and Ono, seven hundred and twenty-five;

verses.name: Ezra 2:34
verses.text: the people<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Jericho, three hundred and forty-five;

verses.name: Ezra 2:35
verses.text: the people<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Senaah, three thousand six hundred and thirty.  <div eID="gen3351" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ezra 2:36
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2526"/><div sID="gen3352" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2526"/>The priests: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua, nine hundred and seventy-three;

verses.name: Ezra 2:37
verses.text: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Immer, one thousand fifty-two;

verses.name: Ezra 2:38
verses.text: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Pashhur, one thousand two hundred and forty-seven;

verses.name: Ezra 2:39
verses.text: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Harim, one thousand seventeen.  <div eID="gen3352" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ezra 2:40
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2527"/><div sID="gen3353" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2527"/>The Levites: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Jeshua and Kadmiel, of the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Hodaviah, seventy-four.  <div eID="gen3353" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ezra 2:41
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2528"/><div sID="gen3354" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2528"/>The singers: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Asaph, one hundred and twenty-eight.  <div eID="gen3354" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ezra 2:42
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2529"/><div sID="gen3355" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2529"/>The descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of the gatekeepers: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Shallum, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Ater, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Talmon, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Akkub, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Hatita, and the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Shobai; in total one hundred and thirty-nine.  <div eID="gen3355" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ezra 2:43
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2530"/><div sID="gen3356" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2530"/>The temple servants: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Ziha, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Hasupha, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Tabbaoth,

verses.name: Ezra 2:44
verses.text: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Keros, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Siaha, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Padon,

verses.name: Ezra 2:45
verses.text: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Lebanah, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Hagabah, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Akkub,

verses.name: Ezra 2:46
verses.text: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Hagab, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Shamlai, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Hanan,

verses.name: Ezra 2:47
verses.text: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Giddel, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Gahar, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Reaiah,

verses.name: Ezra 2:48
verses.text: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Rezin, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Nekoda, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Gazzam,

verses.name: Ezra 2:49
verses.text: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Uzza, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Paseah, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Besai,

verses.name: Ezra 2:50
verses.text: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Asnah, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Meunim, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Nephisim,

verses.name: Ezra 2:51
verses.text: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Bakbuk, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Hakupha, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Harhur,

verses.name: Ezra 2:52
verses.text: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Bazluth, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Mehida, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Harsha,

verses.name: Ezra 2:53
verses.text: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Barkos, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Sisera, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Temah,

verses.name: Ezra 2:54
verses.text: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Neziah, and the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Hatipha.  <div eID="gen3356" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ezra 2:55
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2531"/><div sID="gen3357" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2531"/>The descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Solomon’s servants: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Sotai, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Hassophereth, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Peruda,

verses.name: Ezra 2:56
verses.text: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Jaalah, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Darkon, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Giddel,

verses.name: Ezra 2:57
verses.text: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Shephatiah, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Hattil, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Pochereth-hazzebaim, and the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Ami.  <div eID="gen3357" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ezra 2:58
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2532"/><div sID="gen3358" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2532"/>All the temple servants and the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Solomon’s servants were three hundred and ninety-two.  <div eID="gen3358" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ezra 2:59
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2533"/><div sID="gen3359" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2533"/>Now these were the ones who came up from Tel-melah, Tel-harsha, Cherub, Addan, and Immer, but they were not able to prove their fathers’ household and their descent, if they were from Israel:

verses.name: Ezra 2:60
verses.text: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Delaiah, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Tobiah, and the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Nekoda, six hundred and fifty-two.

verses.name: Ezra 2:61
verses.text: And from the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of the priests: the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Habaiah, the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Hakkoz, and the descendants<note placement="foot">Or “sons”</note> of Barzillai (who took a wife from the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called by their name).

verses.name: Ezra 2:62
verses.text: These sought their record in the genealogy <transChange type="added">records</transChange>, but they were not found, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞were excluded from the priesthood as unclean⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “they were unclean from the priesthood”</note>

verses.name: Ezra 2:63
verses.text: The governor said to them that they could not eat from the holy food of the sanctuary<note placement="foot">Or “most holy things”</note> until there was present a priest for the Urim and Thummim.  <div eID="gen3359" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ezra 2:64
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2534"/><div sID="gen3360" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2534"/>The whole assembly together was forty-two thousand three hundred and sixty,

verses.name: Ezra 2:65
verses.text: apart from their male and female servants, of whom were seven thousand three hundred and thirty-seven; and they had two hundred male and female singers.

verses.name: Ezra 2:66
verses.text: Their horses <transChange type="added">numbered</transChange> seven hundred and thirty-six, their mules <transChange type="added">numbered</transChange> two hundred and forty-five,

verses.name: Ezra 2:67
verses.text: their camels <transChange type="added">numbered</transChange> four hundred and thirty-five, their donkeys <transChange type="added">numbered</transChange> six thousand seven hundred and twenty.  <div eID="gen3360" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ezra 2:68
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2535"/><title type="x-s">Gifts Given for Temple Work</title> <div sID="gen3361" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2535"/>When <transChange type="added">some</transChange> of the heads of <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞families⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the fathers”</note> came to the house of Yahweh that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in Jerusalem, they gave freewill offerings for the house of God to erect it on its place.

verses.name: Ezra 2:69
verses.text: According to their ability they gave to the treasury room for the work sixty-one thousand darics of gold, five thousand minas of silver, and one hundred priestly tunics.  <div eID="gen3361" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ezra 2:70
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2536"/><div sID="gen3362" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2536"/>The priests, the Levites, and some of the people lived <transChange type="added">in Jerusalem</transChange>, and the singers, the gatekeepers, and the temple servants <transChange type="added">lived</transChange> in their cities, and all Israel in their cities.  <chapter eID="Ezra.2"/>

verses.name: Ezra 3:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2537"/><title type="x-s">Worship in Jerusalem Restored</title> <div sID="gen3363" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2537"/>Now the seventh month drew near and the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Israelites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons/children of Israel”</note> were in the cities, so the people gathered as <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞one⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “one man”</note> in Jerusalem.

verses.name: Ezra 3:2
verses.text: And Jeshua son of Jehozadak and his brothers the priests stood up, and Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel and his brothers built the altar of the God of Israel, in order to offer burnt offerings on it, as it is written in the law of Moses, the man of God.

verses.name: Ezra 3:3
verses.text: They set up the altar on its foundations, because <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they were in terror⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in terror before them”</note> because of the peoples of the lands. And they offered burnt offerings on it for Yahweh, burnt offerings for the morning and the evening.

verses.name: Ezra 3:4
verses.text: And they kept the feast of booths, as it is written, and <transChange type="added">offered</transChange> burnt offerings day by day in number according to the ordinance <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as described for each day⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the daily word on its day”</note>

verses.name: Ezra 3:5
verses.text: After <transChange type="added">this, they presented</transChange> the daily sacrifice of burnt offerings, <transChange type="added">the offerings</transChange> for the New Moon Festival, and for all of the appointed times consecrated for Yahweh and for all who gave a freewill offering to Yahweh.

verses.name: Ezra 3:6
verses.text: From the first day of the seventh month they began to offer burnt offerings to Yahweh. But the temple of Yahweh was not yet founded.

verses.name: Ezra 3:7
verses.text: So they gave money to the stone craftsmen and skilled craftsmen, and food, drink, and olive oil to the Sidonians and Tyrians, to bring cedar trees from Lebanon to the sea of Joppa, according to the authorization over them of Cyrus king of Persia.  <div eID="gen3363" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ezra 3:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2538"/><title type="x-s">Foundation of the Temple is Laid</title> <div sID="gen3364" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2538"/>In the second year after their coming to the house of God at Jerusalem, in the second month, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jehozadak began <transChange type="added">their work</transChange>, and the remainder of their brothers the priests and the Levites and all who came from the captivity to Jerusalem. They appointed the Levites <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from twenty years and older⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a son of twenty years and above”</note> to direct the work of the house of Yahweh.

verses.name: Ezra 3:9
verses.text: And Jeshua <transChange type="added">with</transChange> his sons and brothers, and Kadmiel and his sons—the sons of Judah—together directed the workers in the house of God, <transChange type="added">along with</transChange> the sons of Henadad and their sons and brothers the Levites.  <div eID="gen3364" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ezra 3:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2539"/><div sID="gen3365" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2539"/>And the builders laid the foundation of the temple of Yahweh, and the priests <transChange type="added">in their</transChange> apparel with the trumpets, and the Levites, the sons of Asaph, with the cymbals, were positioned to praise Yahweh, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as described by⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by the hands of”</note> King David of Israel.

verses.name: Ezra 3:11
verses.text: And they <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞sang responsively⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “they answered”</note> with praising and thanksgiving to Yahweh <transChange type="added">saying</transChange>, “For he is good, for his loyal love is everlasting for Israel.” <div eID="gen3365" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3366" type="x-p"/> And all of the people responded with a great shout of joyful acclaim in praise to Yahweh because the house of Yahweh was laid.

verses.name: Ezra 3:12
verses.text: But many of the elderly priests, Levites, and heads of the families who had seen the first temple, wept with a loud voice when they saw the foundation of this house, but many <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞shouted aloud with joy⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “exalted with voice in joy with a shout”</note>

verses.name: Ezra 3:13
verses.text: No person could distinguish the sound of joyful acclaim from the sound of people weeping, for the people shouted with great joyful acclaim and the sound was heard from afar.  <chapter eID="Ezra.3"/>

verses.name: Ezra 4:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2540"/><title type="x-s">Resistance to Rebuilding the House of God</title> <div sID="gen3367" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2540"/>Now the enemies of Judah and Benjamin heard that the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞returned exiles⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the sons of the exile”</note> <transChange type="added">were</transChange> building a temple for Yahweh the God of Israel.

verses.name: Ezra 4:2
verses.text: And they approached Zerubbabel and the heads of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞families⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “fathers”</note> and they said to them, “Let us build with you. Like you, we seek your God and have been sacrificing <transChange type="added">to him</transChange> from the days of Esarhaddon the king of Assyria who brought us up here.

verses.name: Ezra 4:3
verses.text: But Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and the rest of the heads of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞families⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “fathers”</note> of Israel said to them, “<transChange type="added">It is</transChange> not for you but for us to build a house for our God. For we ourselves alone will build <transChange type="added">it</transChange> for Yahweh the God of Israel, just as Cyrus the king of Persia has commanded us.”  <div eID="gen3367" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ezra 4:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2541"/><div sID="gen3368" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2541"/>Then the people of the land discouraged <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the people of Judah⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the hands of the people of Judah”</note> and made them afraid to build

verses.name: Ezra 4:5
verses.text: and bribed officials against them to frustrate their plan for all the days of Cyrus king of Persia until the reign of Darius king of Persia.  <div eID="gen3368" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ezra 4:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2542"/><title type="x-s">Resistance to Rebuilding Jerusalem</title> <div sID="gen3369" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2542"/>In the reign of Ahasuerus, at the beginning of his reign, they wrote an accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem.

verses.name: Ezra 4:7
verses.text: And in the days of Artaxerxes, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and the rest of their colleagues wrote to Artaxerxes king of Persia. The letter was written in Aramaic and translated from Aramaic.

verses.name: Ezra 4:8
verses.text: Rehum the royal officer and Shimshai the scribe wrote a letter against Jerusalem to King Artaxerxes as follows

verses.name: Ezra 4:9
verses.text: (then Rehum the royal officer, Shimshai the scribe, and the rest of their associates, the judges, the envoys, the officials, the Persians, the Erechs, the Babylonians, the Susians (that is the Elamites)

verses.name: Ezra 4:10
verses.text: and the rest of the nations whom the great and noble Osnappar deported and settled in the cities of Samaria and the rest of <transChange type="added">the province</transChange> Beyond the River) and now

verses.name: Ezra 4:11
verses.text: this is the copy of the letter which they sent to him: <div eID="gen3369" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3370" type="x-p"/> “To King Artaxerxes <transChange type="added">from</transChange> your servants, the men of <transChange type="added">the province</transChange> Beyond the River. And now,

verses.name: Ezra 4:12
verses.text: be it known to the king that the Jews who have come up from near you to us have gone to Jerusalem. They are building the rebellious and wicked city. They are finishing the wall and repairing the foundation.

verses.name: Ezra 4:13
verses.text: Now be it known to the king that if this city is built and the walls are finished, they will not pay tribute and toll, and the royal revenue will be reduced.

verses.name: Ezra 4:14
verses.text: Now since we eat the salt of the palace and the dishonor of the king is not proper for us to see, we send and make <transChange type="added">this</transChange> known to the king,

verses.name: Ezra 4:15
verses.text: so that it may be investigated in the book of records of your ancestors.<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> You will find in the book of records and learn that this city is a rebellious city, hurtful to kings and provinces, and they have rebelled in its midst from ancient times. Because of that this city was destroyed.

verses.name: Ezra 4:16
verses.text: We make known to the king that if this city is built and the walls are finished, you will have nothing in <transChange type="added">the province</transChange> Beyond the River.”  <div eID="gen3370" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ezra 4:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2543"/><div sID="gen3371" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2543"/>The king sent a reply: “To Rehum the royal officer, Shimshai the scribe, and the rest of their associates who live in Samaria and the rest <transChange type="added">of the province</transChange> Beyond the River, greetings. And now

verses.name: Ezra 4:18
verses.text: the letter that you sent to us has been translated <transChange type="added">and</transChange> read before me.

verses.name: Ezra 4:19
verses.text: And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I issued⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by my means made”</note> a decree, and they searched and found that this city from ancient days revolted against kings, and rebellion and sedition has been made in it.

verses.name: Ezra 4:20
verses.text: Mighty kings have ruled over Jerusalem, <transChange type="added">governing</transChange> all <transChange type="added">the province</transChange> Beyond the River, to whom tribute, duty, and tax has been given.

verses.name: Ezra 4:21
verses.text: So now, issue forth a decree that these men stop and this city not be built, until a decree is issued from me.

verses.name: Ezra 4:22
verses.text: And be careful not to be negligent on this matter. Why should damage grow to hurt kings?”  <div eID="gen3371" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ezra 4:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2544"/><div sID="gen3372" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2544"/>Then when a copy of the letter of King Artaxerxes was read before Rehum, Shimshai the scribe, and their associates they returned in a hurry to Jerusalem against the Jews and they stopped them by force and power.

verses.name: Ezra 4:24
verses.text: Then the work on the house of God in Jerusalem stopped, and was discontinued until the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia.  <chapter eID="Ezra.4"/>

verses.name: Ezra 5:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2545"/><title type="x-s">Temple Restoration Resumed</title> <div sID="gen3373" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2545"/>Now the prophets, Haggai and Zechariah the son of Iddo, prophesied to the Jews who were in <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Judah⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Jehud”</note> and in Jerusalem, in the name of the God of Israel who was over them.

verses.name: Ezra 5:2
verses.text: Then Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel and Jeshua the son of Jozadak set out and began to build the house of God that is in Jerusalem. And with them the prophets of God <transChange type="added">were</transChange> helping them.  <div eID="gen3373" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ezra 5:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2546"/><div sID="gen3374" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2546"/>At the same time Tattenai, governor of <transChange type="added">the province</transChange> Beyond the River, and Shethar-bozenai, and their associates came to them and spoke to them thus: “Who issued you all a decree to build this house and to finish this structure?”

verses.name: Ezra 5:4
verses.text: Then we<note placement="foot">Hebrew is first person plural</note> asked them this: “What are the names of the men who are building this building?”

verses.name: Ezra 5:5
verses.text: And the eye of their God was on the elders of the Jews, and they did not stop them until the report came to Darius, and then <transChange type="added">answer</transChange> was received.  <div eID="gen3374" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ezra 5:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2547"/><div sID="gen3375" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2547"/>The copy of the letter that Tattenai, the governor of <transChange type="added">the province</transChange> Beyond the River, and Shethar-bozenai and his associates the envoys who were in <transChange type="added">the province</transChange> Beyond the River sent to Darius the king.
