verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2665"/><title type="x-s">A Plot Against the King</title> <div sID="gen3499" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2665"/>When <transChange type="added">the</transChange> virgins were gathered a second time, Mordecai <transChange type="added">was</transChange> sitting at the gate of the king.

verses.name: Esther 2:20
verses.text: Esther had not made known her family and her people, just as Mordecai had instructed her; for Esther <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞did what Mordecai told her⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “did the word of Mordecai”</note> just as when she was brought up by him.

verses.name: Esther 2:21
verses.text: In those days Mordecai <transChange type="added">was</transChange> sitting at the gate of the king. Bigthana and Teresh, two of the king’s eunuchs from the keepers of the threshold, became angry and they conspired <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to assassinate⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to send a hand against”</note> King Ahasuerus.

verses.name: Esther 2:22
verses.text: And the matter became known to Mordecai and he told <transChange type="added">it</transChange> to Queen Esther, and Esther told <transChange type="added">it</transChange> to the king in the name of Mordecai.

verses.name: Esther 2:23
verses.text: And the matter was investigated and found <transChange type="added">to be so</transChange>; and the two of them were hanged on <transChange type="added">the</transChange> gallows, and it was written in the scroll of the events of the days before the presence of the king.  <chapter eID="Esth.2"/>

verses.name: Esther 3:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2666"/><title type="x-s">Haman is Promoted</title> <div sID="gen3500" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2666"/>After these things King Ahasuerus promoted Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, and he exalted him and set <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his position⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “his throne”</note> above all the officials who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him.

verses.name: Esther 3:2
verses.text: And all of the king’s servants who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> at the gate of the king <transChange type="added">were</transChange> kneeling and bowing down to Haman; for so the king had commanded concerning him, but Mordecai did not kneel and bow down.

verses.name: Esther 3:3
verses.text: And the king’s servants who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> at the gate of the king said to Mordecai, “Why <transChange type="added">are</transChange> you transgressing the command of the king?”

verses.name: Esther 3:4
verses.text: They spoke to him day after day, but he did not listen to them, and they informed Haman to see if <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Mordecai’s resolve would prevail⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “the word’s of Mordecai would stand”</note> for he had told them that he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a Jew.

verses.name: Esther 3:5
verses.text: And Haman saw that Mordecai was not kneeling and bowing down to him, and he was filled <transChange type="added">with</transChange> anger.

verses.name: Esther 3:6
verses.text: But <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he considered it beneath him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “he despised it in his eyes”</note> to lay hands on Mordecai only, for they told him of Mordecai’s people, and Haman sought to destroy all the Jews, the people of Mordecai, who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in the kingdom of Ahasuerus.  <div eID="gen3500" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Esther 3:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2667"/><div sID="gen3501" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2667"/>In the first month, that <transChange type="added">is</transChange>, the month of Nisan, in the twelfth year of King Ahasurus, he cast pur—that <transChange type="added">is</transChange>, the lot—before the presence of Haman <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞for the day and for the month⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “from day to day and from month to month”</note> until<note placement="foot">The Septuagint adds, “and the lot fell on the thirteenth day of”</note> the twelfth month, that <transChange type="added">is</transChange>, the month of Adar.

verses.name: Esther 3:8
verses.text: And Haman said to King Ahasuerus, “There is a certain people scattered and separated among the peoples in all of the provinces of your kingdom; their laws <transChange type="added">are</transChange> different from every <transChange type="added">other</transChange> people, and they do not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞observe⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “do”</note> the laws of the king; it is not appropriate for the king to tolerate them.

verses.name: Esther 3:9
verses.text: If it pleases the king, let a <transChange type="added">decree</transChange> be issued to destroy them, and I will pay<note placement="foot">Or “I will weigh”</note> ten thousand talents<note placement="foot">Hebrew “talent”</note> of silver to those who do the job, to bring to the treasury of the king.”

verses.name: Esther 3:10
verses.text: So the king removed his signet ring from his hand and gave it to Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the enemy of the Jews.

verses.name: Esther 3:11
verses.text: And the king said to Haman, “The money <transChange type="added">is</transChange> given to you and to the people to do with it <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as you see fit⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “as the good is in your eyes”</note>  <div eID="gen3501" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Esther 3:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2668"/><div sID="gen3502" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2668"/>And the king’s secretaries were called in the first month on the thirteenth day, and <transChange type="added">a decree</transChange> was issued, according to all that Haman commanded, to the satraps of the king and to the governors who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> over all the provinces, and to <transChange type="added">the</transChange> officials of all the people, to each province according to <transChange type="added">its own</transChange> script and to all people according to their own language; <transChange type="added">it was</transChange> written in the name of King Ahasuerus and <transChange type="added">was</transChange> sealed with the king’s ring.

verses.name: Esther 3:13
verses.text: Letters <transChange type="added">were</transChange> sent by couriers<note placement="foot">Or “by runners”</note> to all the provinces of the king to destroy, to kill, and to annihilate all the Jews, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞both young and old⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “from young to old”</note> women and children, on one day, the thirteenth day of the month, that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> Adar, and to plunder their goods.

verses.name: Esther 3:14
verses.text: A copy of the edict <transChange type="added">was</transChange> presented <transChange type="added">as</transChange> law in every province making <transChange type="added">it</transChange> known to all the people to be ready for that day.

verses.name: Esther 3:15
verses.text: The couriers went out quickly by order of the king, and the law was issued in the citadel of Susa. The king and Haman sat down to drink; and the city of Susa was bewildered.<note placement="foot">Or “disturbed”</note>  <chapter eID="Esth.3"/>

verses.name: Esther 4:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2669"/><title type="x-s">Mordecai Tells Esther of Haman’s Plot</title> <div sID="gen3503" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2669"/>Mordecai learned all that had been done and he tore his clothes and put on sackcloth and ashes. And he went through the middle of the city and cried out a loud and bitter cry;

verses.name: Esther 4:2
verses.text: he went up to the entrance of the gate of the king, for he could not go to the gate of the king in sackcloth.

verses.name: Esther 4:3
verses.text: In every province <transChange type="added">each</transChange> place where the king’s edict and his law came, there <transChange type="added">was</transChange> great mourning for the Jews with fasting, crying, wailing, <transChange type="added">and</transChange> sackcloth; and ashes were spread out as a bed for them.  <div eID="gen3503" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Esther 4:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2670"/><div sID="gen3504" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2670"/>And Esther’s maids and her eunuchs came and they told her, and the queen was deeply distressed; she sent garments to clothe Mordecai so that he might remove his sackcloth—but he did not accept <transChange type="added">them</transChange>.

verses.name: Esther 4:5
verses.text: Then Esther called Hathach from the king’s eunuchs <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who regularly attended to her⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “who stood before her presence”</note> and she ordered him <transChange type="added">to go</transChange> to Mordecai to learn what was happening and why.

verses.name: Esther 4:6
verses.text: So Hathach went out to Mordecai, to the public square of the city, which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in front of the gate of the king,

verses.name: Esther 4:7
verses.text: and Mordecai told him all that had happened to him, and the exact amount of money that Haman has promised to pay to the treasury of the king for the destruction of the Jews.

verses.name: Esther 4:8
verses.text: And he gave him a copy of the edict of the law that had been issued in Susa for their destruction to show Esther, and to inform her, and to charge her to go to the king and make supplication to him and entreat before him for her people.  <div eID="gen3504" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Esther 4:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2671"/><div sID="gen3505" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2671"/>And Hathach went <transChange type="added">back</transChange> and told Esther the words of Mordecai.

verses.name: Esther 4:10
verses.text: And Esther spoke to Hathach and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞she gave him a message for Mordecai⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>:<note placement="foot">Literally “she charged him to Mordecai”</note>

verses.name: Esther 4:11
verses.text: “All the king’s servants and the people of the king’s provinces know that <transChange type="added">if</transChange> any man or woman who goes to the king to the inner courtyard, who is not called, he has one law, to be killed, except if the king extends to him the gold scepter so that he may live. I have not been called to come to the king <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞for thirty days⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “these thirty days”</note>

verses.name: Esther 4:12
verses.text: And they told Mordecai the words of Esther.

verses.name: Esther 4:13
verses.text: Then Mordecai told <transChange type="added">them</transChange> to reply to Esther: “Do not think that your life will be saved <transChange type="added">in</transChange> the palace of the king more than all the Jews.

verses.name: Esther 4:14
verses.text: For if indeed you keep silent at this time, relief and deliverance will arise for the Jews from another place, and you and the family of your father will perish. Who knows? <transChange type="added">Perhaps</transChange> you have come to a royal position for a time such as this.”

verses.name: Esther 4:15
verses.text: Esther replied to Mordecai:

verses.name: Esther 4:16
verses.text: “Go, gather all the Jews that are found in Susa and fast for me; do not eat or drink <transChange type="added">for</transChange> three days, both night and day. I and my young girls will fast likewise, and then I will go to the king, which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not according to the law; if I perish, I perish.

verses.name: Esther 4:17
verses.text: And Mordecai went away and he did everything that Esther commanded him.  <chapter eID="Esth.4"/>

verses.name: Esther 5:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2672"/><title type="x-s">Esther’s Banquet</title> <div sID="gen3506" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2672"/>And it happened, on the third day, and Esther put on royal clothes, and she stood in the inner courtyard of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞king’s palace⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “house of the king”</note> opposite the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞king’s palace⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “house of the king”</note> the king was sitting on his royal throne in the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞throne room⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “house of the reign” or “house of the kingdom”</note> opposite the doorway of the palace.

verses.name: Esther 5:2
verses.text: When the king saw Queen Esther standing in the courtyard she found favor in his eyes, and the king held out the gold scepter that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in his hand to Esther, and Esther approached and touched the top of the scepter.

verses.name: Esther 5:3
verses.text: And the king said to her, “What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> it, Queen Esther? What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> your request? It will be given to you—even half the kingdom.”

verses.name: Esther 5:4
verses.text: And Esther said, “If it is good to the king, let the king and Haman come today to the banquet that I have prepared for him.”

verses.name: Esther 5:5
verses.text: And the king said, “Bring Haman quickly <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to fulfill⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to do”</note> the request of Esther.” So the king and Haman came to the banquet that Esther had prepared.

verses.name: Esther 5:6
verses.text: And the king said to Esther <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞while they were drinking wine⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “at the meal of wine”</note> “What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> your petition? It will be given to you. What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> your request? Even half the kingdom, it will done.

verses.name: Esther 5:7
verses.text: And Esther answered and said, “<transChange type="added">This is</transChange> my petition and my request.

verses.name: Esther 5:8
verses.text: If I have found favor in the eyes of the king,<note placement="foot">Or “I have won the favor of the king</note> and if it is good to the king to grant my petition and fulfill my request, let the king and Haman come to the banquet that I will prepare for them tomorrow, and I will do according to the word of the king.  <div eID="gen3506" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Esther 5:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2673"/><div sID="gen3507" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2673"/>And Haman went out on that day rejoicing and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞feeling good⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “good of heart”</note> But when Haman saw Mordecai at the gate of the king, and he did not rise or tremble before him, Haman was filled <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞with rage toward⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “rage to”</note> Mordecai.

verses.name: Esther 5:10
verses.text: But Haman controlled himself and went to his house, and he sent <transChange type="added">for</transChange> and brought his friends and Zeresh his wife.

verses.name: Esther 5:11
verses.text: And Haman recounted to them the splendor of his wealth and the number of his sons and all <transChange type="added">the ways</transChange> that the king had honored him and promoted him above the officials and king’s servants.

verses.name: Esther 5:12
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And Haman added⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “And Haman said also”</note> “Esther the Queen did not let <transChange type="added">just anyone</transChange> come to the banquet that she prepared with the king except me, and I am also invited tomorrow to her <transChange type="added">banquet</transChange> with the king.

verses.name: Esther 5:13
verses.text: But all this <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞fails to satisfy me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “it is not sufficient for me”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞when⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “at every time”</note> I see Mordecai the Jew setting at the gate of the king.”

verses.name: Esther 5:14
verses.text: And Zeresh his wife and all of his friends said to him, “Let them make a gallows fifty cubits<note placement="foot">Hebrew “cubit”</note> high, and in the morning tell the king, “Let them hang Mordecai on it; then go with the king to the banquet happily.” The advice pleased Haman, so he had the gallows made.  <chapter eID="Esth.5"/>

verses.name: Esther 6:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2674"/><title type="x-s">Mordecai is Honored</title> <div sID="gen3508" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2674"/>During that night the king’s sleep escaped <transChange type="added">him</transChange>, and he gave orders to bring the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞scroll of records and chronicles⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the scroll of remembrance and the events of the days”</note> and they were read before the king.

verses.name: Esther 6:2
verses.text: And it was found written how Mordecai had reported concerning Bigthana and Teresh, two of the king’s eunuchs from the keepers of the threshold who had conspired <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to assassinate⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to send a hand against”</note> King Ahasuerus.

verses.name: Esther 6:3
verses.text: And the king asked, “What has been done to bestow honor to Mordecai for this?” And the king’s servants who attended him said, “Nothing has been done for him.”

verses.name: Esther 6:4
verses.text: And the king asked, “Who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in the courtyard?” Haman had just come to the courtyard of the king’s outer palace to tell the king to hang Mordecai on the gallows that he had prepared for him.

verses.name: Esther 6:5
verses.text: And the king’s servants said to him, “Look! Haman <transChange type="added">is</transChange> standing in the courtyard.” And the king said, “Let him come.”

verses.name: Esther 6:6
verses.text: And Haman came, and the king said to him, “What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> to be done for the man whom the king wishes to honor?” And Haman thought to himself, “Whom would the king wish to honor more than me?”

verses.name: Esther 6:7
verses.text: So Haman said to the king, “For a man whom the king wishes to honor,

verses.name: Esther 6:8
verses.text: let them bring <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞royal clothing⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “clothing of the kingdom”</note> with which the king has clothed himself, and a horse that the king has ridden, and on whose head a royal head-dress has been given.

verses.name: Esther 6:9
verses.text: And let the clothing and the horse be given <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to the man⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the hand of the man”</note> by the officials of the king’s nobles; let them cloth the man whom the king wishes to honor, and let him ride on his horse through the public square of the city, and let them proclaim before him, ‘Thus, it will be done for the man whom the king wishes to honor.’ ”

verses.name: Esther 6:10
verses.text: Then the king said to Haman, “Quickly, take the clothing and the horse, just as you have said, and do so to Mordecai the Jew who sits at the gate of the king; you must not leave out anything from what you have said.”

verses.name: Esther 6:11
verses.text: So Haman took the clothing and the horse, and he clothed Mordecai and let him ride through the public square of the city; and he proclaimed before him, “Thus, it is done to the man whom the king wishes to honor.”  <div eID="gen3508" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Esther 6:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2675"/><div sID="gen3509" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2675"/>Then Mordecai returned to the gate of the king, and Haman rushed to his house mournful and with his head covered.

verses.name: Esther 6:13
verses.text: And Haman told Zeresh his wife and all his friends all that had happened to him. And his advisers and Zeresh his wife said to him, “If Mordecai, before whom you have begun to fall, <transChange type="added">is</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from the descendants of the Jews⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “from seed of the Jews”</note> you will not prevail against him, but will certainly fall before him.”

verses.name: Esther 6:14
verses.text: As they <transChange type="added">were</transChange> still speaking with him the king’s eunuchs arrived and hurried to bring Haman to the banquet that Esther had prepared.  <chapter eID="Esth.6"/>

verses.name: Esther 7:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2676"/><title type="x-s">Esther’s Banquet</title> <div sID="gen3510" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2676"/>So the king and Haman went <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to dine⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to drink”</note> with Queen Esther.

verses.name: Esther 7:2
verses.text: And the king again said to Esther, on the second day <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞while they were drinking⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “at the meal of wine”</note> “What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> your petition, Queen Esther? It will be given to you. What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> your request? It will be given <transChange type="added">to you</transChange>—even half the kingdom.”

verses.name: Esther 7:3
verses.text: Then Queen Esther answered, and she said, “If I have found favor in your eyes,<note placement="foot">Or “If I have won your favor”</note> O king, and if it is good to the king, let my life be given to me at my petition and my people at my request;

verses.name: Esther 7:4
verses.text: I and my people have been sold to be destroyed and killed, to be annihilated. If we had been sold as male and female slaves I would have kept quiet, because this<note placement="foot">Hebrew “there”</note> is not a need sufficient to trouble the king.”<note placement="foot">See HALOT 1437, s.v. NRSV translates, “but no enemy can compensate for this damage to the king”</note>

verses.name: Esther 7:5
verses.text: And King Ahasuerus said to Queen Esther, “Who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> he, and where <transChange type="added">is</transChange> he, who <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞gave himself the right to do this⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?”<note placement="foot">Literally “has filled his heart to do so”</note>

verses.name: Esther 7:6
verses.text: And Esther said, “The adversary and enemy <transChange type="added">is</transChange> this evil Haman!” And Haman was terrified before the king and queen.  <div eID="gen3510" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Esther 7:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2677"/><title type="x-s">Haman is Hanged</title> <div sID="gen3511" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2677"/>The king rose in his anger <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from the banquet⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from the banquet of wine”</note> and went to the palace garden, and Haman stood to beg for his life from Queen Esther, for <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he realized that the king was determined to make an end to his life⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “that evil had been determined for him from the king”</note>

verses.name: Esther 7:8
verses.text: And the king returned from the palace garden to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞banquet hall⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “house of the meal of wine”</note> where Haman was lying prostrate on the couch that Esther was on, and the king said, “Will he also molest the queen with me in the house?” As the words<note placement="foot">Hebrew “word”</note> went from the king’s mouth they covered Haman’s face.

verses.name: Esther 7:9
verses.text: And Habrona, one of the eunuchs in the presence of the king, said, “Look, the same gallows that Haman had prepared for Mordecai who spoke good <transChange type="added">for the sake</transChange> of the king stands at Haman’s house, fifty cubits high.” And the king said, “Hang him on it.”

verses.name: Esther 7:10
verses.text: And they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai, and the anger of the king was abated.  <chapter eID="Esth.7"/>

verses.name: Esther 8:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2678"/><title type="x-s">Mordecai is Promoted</title> <div sID="gen3512" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2678"/>On that day King Ahasuerus gave Queen Esther the house of Haman, the enemy of the Jews; and Mordecai came before the king, for Esther had told what he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> to her.

verses.name: Esther 8:2
verses.text: And the king removed his signet ring that he had taken away from Haman, and he gave it to Mordecai. So Esther set Mordecai over the house of Haman.  <div eID="gen3512" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Esther 8:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2679"/><div sID="gen3513" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2679"/>And Esther again spoke before the king, and she fell before his feet and wept, pleading for his grace to avert Haman the Agagite’s evil <transChange type="added">plan</transChange> and the plot that he devised against the Jews.

verses.name: Esther 8:4
verses.text: And the king held out to Esther the scepter of gold, and Esther rose and stood before the king,

verses.name: Esther 8:5
verses.text: and she said, “If it is good to the king, and if I have found favor before him,<note placement="foot">Or “if I have won his favor”</note> and if the king is pleased with this matter, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I have his approval⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “I am good in his eyes”</note> let <transChange type="added">an edict</transChange> be written to revoke the letters of the plans of Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, which he wrote to destroy the Jews that <transChange type="added">are</transChange> in all the provinces of the king.

verses.name: Esther 8:6
verses.text: For <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞how can I bear⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “how am I able”</note> to look on the disaster that will find my people, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞how can I bear⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “how am I able”</note> to look on the destruction of my family?”

verses.name: Esther 8:7
verses.text: And King Ahasuerus said to Queen Esther and to Mordecai the Jew, “Look, I have given Haman’s house to Esther, and they have hanged him on the gallows because he <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞plotted against⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sent his hand against”</note> the Jews.

verses.name: Esther 8:8
verses.text: Write <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as you see fit⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “as it is good in your eyes”</note> concerning the Jews in the name of the king, and seal <transChange type="added">it</transChange> with the king’s signet ring; for a decree that is written in the name of the king and sealed with the king’s signet ring cannot be revoked.”  <div eID="gen3513" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Esther 8:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2680"/><div sID="gen3514" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2680"/>And the secretaries of the king were summoned<note placement="foot">Or “called”</note> at that time, in the third month, which is in the month of Sivan on the twenty-third day, and an edict was written according to all that Mordecai commanded, to the Jews and to the governors and satraps and officials of the provinces from India to Cush<note placement="foot">That is, “Ethiopia”</note>—one hundred and twenty-seven provinces<note placement="foot">Hebrew “province”</note>—each province according to its own script and to every people in their own <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞language⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “tongue”</note> and to the Jews in their own script and language.

verses.name: Esther 8:10
verses.text: And he wrote in the name of King Ahasuerus, and he sealed <transChange type="added">the letters</transChange> with the king’s signet ring and sent them<note placement="foot">Hebrew “the letters”</note> by couriers on horses, riding on royal horses <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞bred by⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons of”</note> racing mares.<note placement="foot">See HALOT 1244 s.v.</note>

verses.name: Esther 8:11
verses.text: <transChange type="added">In them</transChange> the king allowed the Jews who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in every city to assemble and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞defend their lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to stand for their lives”</note> to destroy and kill and annihilate any army of any people or province attacking them, including women and children, and to plunder their spoil,

verses.name: Esther 8:12
verses.text: in one day in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus, on the thirteenth <transChange type="added">day</transChange> of the twelfth month, which is the month of Adar.

verses.name: Esther 8:13
verses.text: A copy of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞edict⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “writing”</note> was to be given as law in each province to inform all the people, so that the Jews would be ready<note placement="foot">See HALOT 902 s.v.</note> on that day to avenge themselves from their enemies.

verses.name: Esther 8:14
verses.text: The mounted couriers on the royal horses went out without delay, urged by the king’s word. The law was given in the citadel of Susa.  <div eID="gen3514" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Esther 8:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2681"/><div sID="gen3515" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2681"/>Mordecai went out from the presence of the king in <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞royal clothing⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “clothing of the kingdom”</note> of blue cloth and white linen, and a great crown of gold and a robe of fine white linen and purple, and the city of Susa was shouting and rejoicing.

verses.name: Esther 8:16
verses.text: For the Jews, there was light and gladness, joy and honor.

verses.name: Esther 8:17
verses.text: In every province and city, wherever the king’s edict and his law came, there was gladness and joy for the Jews, a banquet and a <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞holiday⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “day of good”</note> and many of the people from the country <transChange type="added">were</transChange> posing as Jews because the fear of the Jews had fallen on them.  <chapter eID="Esth.8"/>

verses.name: Esther 9:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2682"/><title type="x-s">The Jews Destroy Their Enemies</title> <div sID="gen3516" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2682"/>In the twelfth month, that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the month of Adar, on the thirteenth day, on which the edict of the king arrived and his law was enacted, on the day in which the enemies of the Jews had hoped to gain power over them but was overturned, <transChange type="added">and</transChange> the Jews gained power against their enemies,

verses.name: Esther 9:2
verses.text: the Jews gathered in their cities in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to strike against⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to send a hand against”</note> those who sought their destruction, and no one could withstand them,<note placement="foot">Or “stand in their presence”</note> as the fear of them fell on all the people.

verses.name: Esther 9:3
verses.text: All the officials of the provinces, the satraps, governors, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞those who did the work of the king⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the doers of the work who were for the king”</note> <transChange type="added">were</transChange> supporting the Jews, because the fear of Mordecai had fallen on them.

verses.name: Esther 9:4
verses.text: For Mordecai <transChange type="added">was</transChange> high-ranking in the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞king’s palace⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “house of the king”</note> and his fame spread throughout all the provinces as <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Mordecai grew more and more powerful⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the man Mordecai was going and becoming great”</note>

verses.name: Esther 9:5
verses.text: The Jews struck down all their enemies with <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the sword⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the striking of the sword”</note> killing and destroying <transChange type="added">them</transChange>; and they did as they pleased with those that hated them.

verses.name: Esther 9:6
verses.text: And in the citadel of Susa the Jews killed and destroyed five hundred men,

verses.name: Esther 9:7
verses.text: and Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha,

verses.name: Esther 9:8
verses.text: Portha, Adalia, Aridatha,

verses.name: Esther 9:9
verses.text: Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai, and Vaizatha,

verses.name: Esther 9:10
verses.text: the ten sons of Haman, the son of Hammedatha, the enemy of the Jews; but they did not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞touch⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “send their hand to”</note> the plunder.  <div eID="gen3516" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Esther 9:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2683"/><div sID="gen3517" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2683"/>On that day the number of those being killed in the citadel of Susa <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞was reported to⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “came before”</note> the king.

verses.name: Esther 9:12
verses.text: And the king said to Queen Esther, “In the citadel of Susa the Jews killed and destroyed five hundred men and the ten sons of Haman. What have they done in the rest of the king’s provinces? What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> your petition? It will be granted to you. And what further <transChange type="added">is</transChange> your request? It will be done.”

verses.name: Esther 9:13
verses.text: Esther replied, “If it is good to the king, let tomorrow also be granted to the Jews who <transChange type="added">are</transChange> in Susa to do according to the edict of today; and let them hang Haman’s ten sons on the gallows.”

verses.name: Esther 9:14
verses.text: And the king said to do so. And a decree was issued in Susa and Haman’s ten sons were hanged.

verses.name: Esther 9:15
verses.text: And the Jews were gathered who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in Susa, and on the fourteenth day of the month of Adar and they killed in Susa three hundred men, but they did not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞touch⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “send their hand to”</note> the plunder.  <div eID="gen3517" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Esther 9:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2684"/><div sID="gen3518" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2684"/>The rest of the Jews who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in the king’s provinces gathered and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞defended their lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to stand for their lives”</note> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞found repose⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “rested”</note> from their enemies. And they killed seventy-five thousand of those that hated them, but they did not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞touch⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “send their hand to”</note> the plunder.

verses.name: Esther 9:17
verses.text: <transChange type="added">This was</transChange> on the thirteenth day of the month of Adar. <transChange type="added">They</transChange> rested on the fourteenth <transChange type="added">day</transChange> and made it a day of feasting and joy.

verses.name: Esther 9:18
verses.text: But the Jews who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in Susa gathered on the thirteenth and on the fourteenth day, and rested on the fifteenth day. And they made it a day of feasting and joy.

verses.name: Esther 9:19
verses.text: Therefore the Jews in the rural <transChange type="added">areas</transChange>, living in the rural towns, made the fourteenth month of Adar a day of joy and feasting, a festive day of giving gifts to each other.  <div eID="gen3518" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Esther 9:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2685"/><title type="x-s">The Feast of Purim</title> <div sID="gen3519" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2685"/>Mordecai wrote down these things and he sent letters to all the Jews who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in all <transChange type="added">of</transChange> the provinces of King Ahasuerus, <transChange type="added">both</transChange> near and far,

verses.name: Esther 9:21
verses.text: to impose on them to keep the fourteenth day of the month of Adar, and the fifteenth <transChange type="added">day</transChange>, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞every year⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “and every year and year”</note>

verses.name: Esther 9:22
verses.text: as the day that the Jews <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞found relief⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “rested”</note> from their enemies, and the month which changed for them from sorrow to joy, and from a mourning ceremony to a <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞festive day⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “a day of good”</note> to make them days of feasting and joy, and giving gifts to each other and to the poor.

verses.name: Esther 9:23
verses.text: And the Jews adopted what they had begun to do and what Mordecai had written to them.  <div eID="gen3519" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Esther 9:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2686"/><div sID="gen3520" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2686"/>For Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews had plotted against the Jews to destroy them, and he had cast pur, that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the lot, to rout them out and destroy them.

verses.name: Esther 9:25
verses.text: But when it came<note placement="foot">Or “she came”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to the attention of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “before”</note> the king, he <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞gave orders in writing⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “said with a scroll”</note> <transChange type="added">that</transChange> his evil plot that he had devised against the Jews should return on his head, and they hung him and his sons on the gallows.

verses.name: Esther 9:26
verses.text: Therefore they called these days Purim, because of the name Pur. Thus because of all the words of this letter, and of what they faced concerning this, and of what had happened to them,

verses.name: Esther 9:27
verses.text: the Jews established and adopted <transChange type="added">it</transChange> for themselves and for their offspring, and for all who joined them. They did not neglect <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to observe⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to be doing”</note> these two days every year as it was written and appointed to them.

verses.name: Esther 9:28
verses.text: These days <transChange type="added">are</transChange> to be remembered and <transChange type="added">are</transChange> to be kept in every generation, and in family, province, and city; and these days of Purim are not <transChange type="added">to be</transChange> neglected among the Jews, and their memory shall not come to an end among their offspring.  <div eID="gen3520" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Esther 9:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2687"/><div sID="gen3521" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2687"/>So Queen Esther the daughter of Abihail and Mordecai the Jew wrote in full authority to confirm this second letter of Purim.

verses.name: Esther 9:30
verses.text: He sent letters of words of peace and truth to all the Jews, to the one hundred and twenty-seven provinces<note placement="foot">Hebrew “province”</note> of Ahasuerus’ kingdom,

verses.name: Esther 9:31
verses.text: to establish these days of Purim at their appointed times, just as Mordecai the Jew and Queen Esther had imposed, and just as they had imposed on themselves and their offspring regulations of the fast and their lament.

verses.name: Esther 9:32
verses.text: And the command of Esther established these practices of Purim, and <transChange type="added">it was</transChange> written on the scroll.  <chapter eID="Esth.9"/>

verses.name: Esther 10:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2688"/><title type="x-s">Title</title> <div sID="gen3522" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2688"/>King Ahasuerus imposed forced labor on the land and islands of the sea.

verses.name: Esther 10:2
verses.text: All the work of his authority and his <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞powerful deeds⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “power”</note> and the full accounting of the greatness of Mordecai, to which the king advanced him, are they not written on the scroll of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞chronicles⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the events of the days”</note> of the kings of Media and Persia?

verses.name: Esther 10:3
verses.text: For Mordecai the Jew <transChange type="added">was</transChange> second-in-command to King Ahasuerus. <transChange type="added">He was</transChange> great for the Jews and popular with many of his brothers, for he sought good for his people, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞interceding for the welfare of all his descendants⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “spoke peace for all his offspring”</note>  <chapter eID="Esth.10"/> <div eID="gen3522" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen3489" osisID="Esth" type="book"/>

verses.name: Job 1:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2689"/><title type="x-s">Job’s Character and Greatness</title> <div sID="gen3524" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2689"/><transChange type="added">There</transChange> was a man in the land of Uz whose<note placement="foot">Hebrew “his”</note> name was Job. That<note placement="foot">Hebrew “And that”</note> man was blameless and upright and God-fearing and turning away from evil.

verses.name: Job 1:2
verses.text: And seven sons and three daughters were born to him.

verses.name: Job 1:3
verses.text: Then<note placement="foot">Hebrew “And”</note> his livestock came to be seven thousand sheep and goats and three thousand camels and five hundred pairs<note placement="foot">Hebrew “pair”</note> of oxen and five hundred female donkeys, and he had very many slaves, and that man was greater than all the people of the east.

verses.name: Job 1:4
verses.text: And his sons used to go and hold a feast <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞at each other’s house⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “at the house of a man,” or “at the house of each”</note> on his day, and they would send, and they would invite their three sisters to eat and to drink with them.

verses.name: Job 1:5
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Then when⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it would happen that,” or “And it would happen when”</note> the days of the feast had run their course, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Job would send⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “and Job would send”</note> and he would sanctify them. Thus<note placement="foot">Hebrew “And”</note> he would arise early in the morning and offer burnt offerings according to the number of all of them, because Job thought,<note placement="foot">Or “said”</note> “Perhaps my children have sinned and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞cursed⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “blessed”— negative meaning by context</note> God in their heart.” This is what Job used to do <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞all the time⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Or “always”; literally “all the days”</note>  <div eID="gen3524" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 1:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2690"/><div sID="gen3525" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2690"/>And it happened <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞one day⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the day”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞that⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and”</note> the sons of God<note placement="foot">Or “the heavenly beings,” or “the angels”</note> came to present themselves before Yahweh, and Satan<note placement="foot">Hebrew “the accuser,” or “the adversary”</note> also came into their midst.

verses.name: Job 1:7
verses.text: So<note placement="foot">Hebrew “And”</note> Yahweh said to Satan,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “the accuser,” or “the adversary”</note> “From where have you come?” <div eID="gen3525" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3526" type="x-p"/> Then<note placement="foot">Hebrew “And”</note> Satan<note placement="foot">Hebrew “the accuser,” or “the adversary”</note> answered Yahweh and said, “From roaming on the earth and from walking about in it.”  <div eID="gen3526" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 1:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2691"/><div sID="gen3527" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2691"/>So<note placement="foot">Hebrew “And”</note> Yahweh said to Satan,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “the accuser,” or “the adversary”</note> “Have you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞considered⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “set your heart”</note> my servant Job? Indeed,<note placement="foot">Or “For,” or “Because”</note> there is no one like him on the earth—a blameless man and upright and God-fearing and turning away from evil.”  <div eID="gen3527" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 1:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2692"/><div sID="gen3528" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2692"/>Then<note placement="foot">Hebrew “And”</note> Satan<note placement="foot">Hebrew “the accuser,” or “the adversary”</note> answered Yahweh and said, “Does Job fear God for nothing?

verses.name: Job 1:10
verses.text: Have you<note placement="foot">Emphatic personal pronoun could be translated “you yourself”</note> not put a fence around him and his household and around <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞all that belongs to him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “all that is his”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞on every side⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?<note placement="foot">Literally “from around”</note> You have blessed the work of his hands, and his livestock<note placement="foot">Or “possessions”</note> has increased in the land.

verses.name: Job 1:11
verses.text: But,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “And”</note> on the other hand, stretch out<note placement="foot">Or “please”</note> your hand and touch <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞all that belongs to him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “all that is his”</note> and see <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞whether⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “if not”</note> he will <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞curse⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “bless”— negative meaning by context</note> you to your face.”  <div eID="gen3528" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 1:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2693"/><div sID="gen3529" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2693"/>So<note placement="foot">Hebrew “And”</note> Yahweh said to Satan,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “the accuser,” or “the adversary”</note> “Look, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞all that belongs to him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “all that is his”</note> is in your <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞power⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “hand”</note> Only do not stretch out your hand <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞against⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to,” or “unto”</note> him.” So<note placement="foot">Hebrew “And”</note> Satan<note placement="foot">Hebrew “the accuser,” or “the adversary”</note> went out from Yahweh’s <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞presence⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “faces of”</note>  <div eID="gen3529" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 1:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2694"/><title type="x-s">The Adversary’s Attack on Job’s Possessions</title> <div sID="gen3530" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2694"/>And then <transChange type="added">there</transChange> was one day when<note placement="foot">Hebrew “and”</note> his sons and his daughters were eating and drinking wine in their firstborn brother’s house.

verses.name: Job 1:14
verses.text: And a messenger came to Job and said, “The oxen were plowing, and the female donkeys were feeding <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞beside them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “on their hands”</note>

verses.name: Job 1:15
verses.text: Then<note placement="foot">Hebrew “And”</note> the Sabeans <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞attacked⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “fell upon them”</note> and they took them, and they slew the servants <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞by the edge of the sword⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “with the mouth of the sword”</note> But<note placement="foot">Hebrew “And”</note> I escaped, <transChange type="added">even</transChange> I alone, to tell you.”  <div eID="gen3530" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 1:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2695"/><div sID="gen3531" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2695"/>While this one was still speaking, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞another⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “this”</note> came and said, “The fire of God fell from the heavens, and it blazed up against the sheep and goats and against the servants, and it consumed them. But I escaped, <transChange type="added">even</transChange> I alone, to tell you.”  <div eID="gen3531" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 1:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2696"/><div sID="gen3532" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2696"/>While this one was still speaking, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞another⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “this”</note> came and said, “The Chaldeans formed three divisions, and they made a raid on the camels, and they carried them away, and they struck your servants <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞by the edge of the sword⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “with the mouth of the sword”</note> but I escaped, <transChange type="added">even</transChange> I alone, to tell you.”  <div eID="gen3532" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 1:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2697"/><div sID="gen3533" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2697"/>At the time<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Until”</note> this one was speaking, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞another⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “this”</note> came and said, “Your sons and your daughters were eating and drinking wine in their firstborn brother’s house.

verses.name: Job 1:19
verses.text: And behold,<note placement="foot">Or “Look”</note> a great wind came from across the desert, and it struck the four corners of the house <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞so that⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and”</note> it fell upon the young people, and they died. But I escaped, <transChange type="added">even</transChange> I alone, to tell you.”  <div eID="gen3533" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 1:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2698"/><div sID="gen3534" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2698"/>Then<note placement="foot">Hebrew “And”</note> Job arose and tore his outer garment<note placement="foot">Or “robe”</note> and shaved his head; <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Hebrew “and”</note> he fell upon the ground and he worshiped.

verses.name: Job 1:21
verses.text: Then<note placement="foot">Hebrew “And”</note> he said, “Naked I came out from my mother’s womb, and naked I will return there. Yahweh gives, and Yahweh takes. Let Yahweh’s name be blessed.”

verses.name: Job 1:22
verses.text: In all this, Job did not sin and did not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞charge God with wrongdoing⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “give unseemliness to God”</note>  <chapter eID="Job.1"/>

verses.name: Job 2:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2699"/><title type="x-s">The Adversary’s Attack on Job’s Person</title> <div sID="gen3535" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2699"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it came to be,” or “and it happened”</note> one day the sons of God<note placement="foot">Or “the heavenly beings,” or “the angels”</note> came to present themselves before Yahweh, and Satan<note placement="foot">Hebrew “the accuser,” or “the adversary”</note> also came into their midst to present himself before Yahweh.

verses.name: Job 2:2
verses.text: So<note placement="foot">Hebrew “And”</note> Yahweh <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞asked⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “said to”</note> Satan,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “the accuser,” or “the adversary”</note> “From where have you come?” <div eID="gen3535" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3536" type="x-p"/> And Satan<note placement="foot">Hebrew “the accuser,” or “the adversary”</note> answered Yahweh and said, “From roaming on the earth and from walking about in it.”  <div eID="gen3536" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 2:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2700"/><div sID="gen3537" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2700"/>So<note placement="foot">Hebrew “And”</note> Yahweh <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞asked⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “said to”</note> Satan,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “the accuser,” or “the adversary”</note> “Have you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞considered⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “set your heart”</note> my servant Job? Indeed,<note placement="foot">Or “For” or “Because”</note> there is no one like him on the earth—a blameless man and upright and God-fearing and turning away from evil. And still he persists in his blamelessness <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞even though⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Hebrew “and”</note> you incited me against him to destroy him for nothing.”  <div eID="gen3537" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 2:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2701"/><div sID="gen3538" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2701"/>Then<note placement="foot">Hebrew “And”</note> Satan<note placement="foot">Hebrew “the accuser,” or “the adversary”</note> answered him and said, “Skin for skin! All that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞that⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the”</note> man has he will give for his life.

verses.name: Job 2:5
verses.text: But stretch out<note placement="foot">Or “please”</note> your hand and touch his bones and his flesh, and see <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞whether⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “if not”</note> he will <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞curse⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “bless”—negative meaning by context</note> you to your face.”<note placement="foot">Hebrew “your faces”</note>  <div eID="gen3538" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 2:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2702"/><div sID="gen3539" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2702"/>So<note placement="foot">Literally “And it happened the/one day”</note> Yahweh said to Satan,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “the accuser,” or “the adversary”</note> “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞All right⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “Look”</note> he is in your <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞power⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “hand”</note> Only spare his life.”  <div eID="gen3539" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 2:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2703"/><title type="x-s">Job’s Blameless Behavior</title> <div sID="gen3540" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2703"/>So<note placement="foot">Hebrew “And”</note> Satan<note placement="foot">Hebrew “the accuser,” or “the adversary”</note> went out from <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Yahweh’s presence⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the faces of Yahweh”</note> and he inflicted Job with loathsome skin sores from the sole of his foot up to the crown of his head.

verses.name: Job 2:8
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞So⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Hebrew “And”</note> he took for himself a potsherd with which to scrape himself, and he sat in the midst of the ashes.  <div eID="gen3540" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 2:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2704"/><div sID="gen3541" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2704"/>Then<note placement="foot">Hebrew “And”</note> his wife said to him, “Are you still persisting in your blamelessness? <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Curse⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Bless”—negative meaning by context</note> God and die.”  <div eID="gen3541" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 2:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2705"/><div sID="gen3542" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2705"/>So<note placement="foot">Hebrew “And”</note> he said to her, “You speak like one of the foolish women speaks. Indeed, should we receive the good from God, but<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> not receive the evil?” In all this, Job did not sin with his lips.  <div eID="gen3542" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 2:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2706"/><div sID="gen3543" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2706"/>Thus<note placement="foot">Hebrew “And”</note> Job’s three friends heard of this calamity that had come upon him. So<note placement="foot">Hebrew “And”</note> each set out from his own place: Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite. And they met<note placement="foot">Or “they agreed”</note> together to come to console him and to comfort him.  <div eID="gen3543" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 2:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2707"/><div sID="gen3544" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2707"/>Thus<note placement="foot">Hebrew “And”</note> they lifted up their eyes<note placement="foot">Or “they gazed”</note> from afar, but<note placement="foot">Hebrew “and”</note> they did not recognize him, so<note placement="foot">Hebrew “and”</note> they raised their voice, and they wept, and each man tore his outer garment<note placement="foot">Or “robe”</note> and threw dust on their heads <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞toward the sky⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Or “in the air”; literally “to the heavens”</note>

verses.name: Job 2:13
verses.text: Then<note placement="foot">Hebrew “And”</note> they sat with him on the ground for seven days and seven nights, but<note placement="foot">Hebrew “and”</note> no one spoke<note placement="foot">Or “there was no speaking”</note> a word to him because they saw that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the”</note> suffering was very great.  <chapter eID="Job.2"/>

verses.name: Job 3:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2708"/><title type="x-s">Job Regrets His Birth</title> <div sID="gen3545" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2708"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Afterward⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “After thus”</note> Job opened his mouth and cursed<note placement="foot">A different term than that employed in 1:5, 11; 2:5, 9</note> his day.

verses.name: Job 3:2
verses.text: Thus<note placement="foot">Hebrew “And”</note> Job <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞spoke up⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “answered”</note> and said,  <div eID="gen3545" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 3:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2709"/><lg sID="gen3546"/> <l level="1" sID="gen3547"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2709"/>“Let <transChange type="added">the</transChange> day perish on which I was born,<l eID="gen3547" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen3548"/>and the night that said, ‘A man-child is conceived.’ <l eID="gen3548" level="1"/>

verses.name: Job 3:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2710"/><l level="1" sID="gen3549"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2710"/>Let that day become<note placement="foot">Or “be”</note> darkness;<l eID="gen3549" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen3550"/>may God not seek it from above,<l eID="gen3550" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen3551"/>nor may daylight shine on it. <l eID="gen3551" level="1"/>

verses.name: Job 3:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2711"/><l level="1" sID="gen3552"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2711"/>Let darkness and deep shadow claim it;<l eID="gen3552" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen3553"/>let clouds<note placement="foot">Literally “cloud”</note> settle on it;<l eID="gen3553" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen3554"/>let them<note placement="foot">Masculine plural referring to all three entities mentioned in this verse</note> terrify it with the blackness<note placement="foot">Literally “blacknesses”</note> of day. <l eID="gen3554" level="1"/>

verses.name: Job 3:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2712"/><l level="1" sID="gen3555"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2712"/>Let darkness seize that night;<note placement="foot">Literally “That night, let darkness seize it”</note><l eID="gen3555" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen3556"/>let it not rejoice among <transChange type="added">the</transChange> days of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> year;<l eID="gen3556" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen3557"/>let it not enter among <transChange type="added">the</transChange> number of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> months. <l eID="gen3557" level="1"/>

verses.name: Job 3:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2713"/><l level="1" sID="gen3558"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2713"/>Look, let that night become<note placement="foot">Or “be”</note> barren;<l eID="gen3558" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen3559"/>let a joyful song not enter it. <l eID="gen3559" level="1"/>

verses.name: Job 3:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2714"/><l level="1" sID="gen3560"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2714"/>Let those who curse the day curse it,<l eID="gen3560" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen3561"/>those who are skilled at rousing Leviathan. <l eID="gen3561" level="1"/>

verses.name: Job 3:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2715"/><l level="1" sID="gen3562"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2715"/>Let the stars of its dawn be dark;<l eID="gen3562" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen3563"/>let it hope for light but<note placement="foot">Hebrew “and”</note> there be none,<l eID="gen3563" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen3564"/>and let it not see <transChange type="added">the</transChange> eyelids of dawn <l eID="gen3564" level="1"/>

verses.name: Job 3:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2716"/><l level="1" sID="gen3565"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2716"/>because it did not shut the doors of my <transChange type="added">mother’s</transChange> womb,<l eID="gen3565" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen3566"/>nor<note placement="foot">Hebrew “And”</note> did it hide trouble from my eyes.<l eID="gen3566" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen3546"/> <title type="x-s">Job Wishes He Had Died</title> <div sID="gen3567" type="x-p"/>  <div eID="gen3567" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 3:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2717"/><lg sID="gen3568"/> <l level="1" sID="gen3569"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2717"/>“Why did I not die at<note placement="foot">Literally “from”</note> birth?<l eID="gen3569" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen3570"/><transChange type="added">Why</transChange> did I <transChange type="added">not</transChange> come forth from <transChange type="added">the</transChange> womb and expire? <l eID="gen3570" level="1"/>

verses.name: Job 3:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2718"/><l level="1" sID="gen3571"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2718"/>Why did <transChange type="added">the</transChange> knees receive me<l eID="gen3571" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen3572"/>and the breasts, that I could suck? <l eID="gen3572" level="1"/>

verses.name: Job 3:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2719"/><l level="1" sID="gen3573"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2719"/>For now I would lie down, and I would be at peace;<l eID="gen3573" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen3574"/>I would be asleep; then <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I would be at rest⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “it would be at rest for me”</note> <l eID="gen3574" level="1"/>

verses.name: Job 3:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2720"/><l level="1" sID="gen3575"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2720"/>with kings and counselors of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> earth,<l eID="gen3575" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen3576"/>who <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞rebuild⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “build”</note> ruins for themselves, <l eID="gen3576" level="1"/>

verses.name: Job 3:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2721"/><l level="1" sID="gen3577"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2721"/>or with high officials <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who have gold⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “gold is for them”</note><l eID="gen3577" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen3578"/>who fill up their houses <transChange type="added">with</transChange> silver. <l eID="gen3578" level="1"/>

verses.name: Job 3:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2722"/><l level="1" sID="gen3579"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2722"/>Or <transChange type="added">why</transChange> was I not hidden like a miscarriage,<l eID="gen3579" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen3580"/>like infants <transChange type="added">who</transChange> did not see <transChange type="added">the</transChange> light? <l eID="gen3580" level="1"/>

verses.name: Job 3:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2723"/><l level="1" sID="gen3581"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2723"/>There <transChange type="added">the</transChange> wicked cease from troubling,<l eID="gen3581" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen3582"/>and there <transChange type="added">the</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞weary⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “weary of strength”</note> are at rest; <l eID="gen3582" level="1"/>

verses.name: Job 3:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2724"/><l level="1" sID="gen3583"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2724"/><transChange type="added">the</transChange> prisoners are at ease together;<l eID="gen3583" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen3584"/>they do not hear <transChange type="added">the</transChange> oppressor’s voice. <l eID="gen3584" level="1"/>

verses.name: Job 3:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2725"/><l level="1" sID="gen3585"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2725"/><transChange type="added">The</transChange> small and <transChange type="added">the</transChange> great <transChange type="added">are</transChange> there,<l eID="gen3585" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen3586"/>and <transChange type="added">the</transChange> slave <transChange type="added">is</transChange> free from his masters.<note placement="foot">Or “master”</note><l eID="gen3586" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen3568"/> <title type="x-s">Job Wishes He Might Die</title> <div sID="gen3587" type="x-p"/>  <div eID="gen3587" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 3:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2726"/><lg sID="gen3588"/> <l level="1" sID="gen3589"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2726"/>“Why does he<note placement="foot">Most likely God</note> give light to one in misery<l eID="gen3589" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen3590"/>and life to <transChange type="added">those</transChange> bitter of soul, <l eID="gen3590" level="1"/>

verses.name: Job 3:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2727"/><l level="1" sID="gen3591"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2727"/>who wait for death, but<note placement="foot">Hebrew “and”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞it does not come⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “it is not”</note><l eID="gen3591" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen3592"/>and search<note placement="foot">Or “dig”</note> <transChange type="added">for</transChange> it more than <transChange type="added">for</transChange> treasures, <l eID="gen3592" level="1"/>

verses.name: Job 3:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2728"/><l level="1" sID="gen3593"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2728"/>who rejoice <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞exceedingly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “unto rejoicing”</note><l eID="gen3593" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen3594"/><transChange type="added">and</transChange> they are glad when they find <transChange type="added">the</transChange> grave? <l eID="gen3594" level="1"/>

verses.name: Job 3:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2729"/><l level="1" sID="gen3595"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2729"/><transChange type="added">Why does he<note placement="foot">Most likely God</note> give light</transChange> to a man whose way is hidden,<l eID="gen3595" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen3596"/>and God has fenced him in <transChange type="added">all</transChange> around? <l eID="gen3596" level="1"/>

verses.name: Job 3:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2730"/><l level="1" sID="gen3597"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2730"/>For<note placement="foot">Or perhaps emphatic, “Indeed”</note> my sighing comes <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Or “in place of” (NET); literally “to the faces of”</note> my bread,<note placement="foot">Or “food”</note><l eID="gen3597" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen3598"/>and my groanings gush forth like water <l eID="gen3598" level="1"/>

verses.name: Job 3:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2731"/><l level="1" sID="gen3599"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2731"/>because the dread that I <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞feel⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “dread”</note> has come upon me,<l eID="gen3599" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen3600"/>and what I feared befalls me. <l eID="gen3600" level="1"/>

verses.name: Job 3:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2732"/><l level="1" sID="gen3601"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2732"/>I am not at ease, and I am not at peace,<l eID="gen3601" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen3602"/>and I do not have rest, thus<note placement="foot">Hebrew “and”</note> turmoil has come.” <l eID="gen3602" level="1"/><lg eID="gen3588"/> <chapter eID="Job.3"/>

verses.name: Job 4:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2733"/><title type="x-s">Eliphaz’s First Response to Job</title> <div sID="gen3603" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2733"/>Then<note placement="foot">Hebrew “And”</note> Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said,  <div eID="gen3603" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 4:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2734"/><lg sID="gen3604"/> <l level="1" sID="gen3605"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2734"/>“<transChange type="added">If</transChange> someone would test a word with you, would you be offended?<l eID="gen3605" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen3606"/>But<note placement="foot">Hebrew “And”</note> who can refrain from speaking? <l eID="gen3606" level="1"/>

verses.name: Job 4:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2735"/><l level="1" sID="gen3607"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2735"/>Look, you have instructed many,<l eID="gen3607" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen3608"/>and you have strengthened weak hands. <l eID="gen3608" level="1"/>

verses.name: Job 4:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2736"/><l level="1" sID="gen3609"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2736"/>Your words have raised up <transChange type="added">the one who</transChange> stumbles,<l eID="gen3609" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen3610"/>and you have strengthened knees giving way. <l eID="gen3610" level="1"/>

verses.name: Job 4:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2737"/><l level="1" sID="gen3611"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2737"/>But now it has come to you, and you are worn out;<l eID="gen3611" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen3612"/>it touches you, and you are horrified. <l eID="gen3612" level="1"/>

verses.name: Job 4:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2738"/><l level="1" sID="gen3613"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2738"/><transChange type="added">Is</transChange> not your fear <transChange type="added">in God</transChange> your confidence?<l eID="gen3613" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen3614"/><transChange type="added">Is not</transChange> your hope even<note placement="foot">Hebrew “and”</note> the integrity of your ways? <l eID="gen3614" level="1"/>

verses.name: Job 4:7
