verses.text: And beautiful women were not found in all the land like Job’s daughters, and their father gave to them an inheritance in the midst of their brothers.  <div eID="gen5719" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 42:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3727"/><div sID="gen5720" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3727"/>And Job lived after this one hundred and forty years, and he saw his sons and his <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞grandsons⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the sons of his sons”</note> <transChange type="added">for</transChange> four generations.

verses.name: Job 42:17
verses.text: Then<note placement="foot">Hebrew “And”</note> Job died old and full of days.  <chapter eID="Job.42"/> <div eID="gen5720" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen3523" osisID="Job" type="book"/>

verses.name: Psalms 1:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3728"/><title type="x-s">The Ways of the Righteous and the Wicked</title> <div sID="gen5722" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen5722" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen5723"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5724"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3728"/>Blessed is the man who does not walk in the advice of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> wicked;<l eID="gen5724" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5725"/>nor does he stand in <transChange type="added">the</transChange> way of sinners;<l eID="gen5725" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5726"/>nor does he sit in <transChange type="added">the</transChange> assembly of mockers. <l eID="gen5726" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 1:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3729"/><l level="1" sID="gen5727"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3729"/>Instead, in the law of Yahweh <transChange type="added">is</transChange> his delight,<l eID="gen5727" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5728"/>and on his law he meditates day and night. <l eID="gen5728" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 1:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3730"/><l level="1" sID="gen5729"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3730"/>And so, he is like a tree planted by streams of water<l eID="gen5729" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5730"/>that gives its fruit in its season;<l eID="gen5730" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5731"/>its leaf also does not wither.<l eID="gen5731" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5732"/>Therefore all that he does prospers. <l eID="gen5732" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 1:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3731"/><l level="1" sID="gen5733"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3731"/>Not so the wicked.<l eID="gen5733" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5734"/>Instead, <transChange type="added">they are</transChange> like the chaff that <transChange type="added">the</transChange> wind scatters. <l eID="gen5734" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 1:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3732"/><l level="1" sID="gen5735"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3732"/>Therefore <transChange type="added">the</transChange> wicked will not stand in the judgment,<l eID="gen5735" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5736"/>nor sinners in the congregation of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> righteous; <l eID="gen5736" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 1:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3733"/><l level="1" sID="gen5737"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3733"/>for Yahweh knows <transChange type="added">the</transChange> way of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> righteous,<note placement="foot">Plural</note><l eID="gen5737" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5738"/>but <transChange type="added">the</transChange> way of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> wicked will perish. <l eID="gen5738" level="1"/><lg eID="gen5723"/> <chapter eID="Ps.1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 2:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3734"/><title type="x-s">The Messiah’s Reign</title> <div sID="gen5739" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen5739" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen5740"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5741"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3734"/>Why are nations in tumult,<l eID="gen5741" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5742"/>and countries plotting<note placement="foot">Or “muttering”</note> in vain?<note placement="foot">Or “an empty thing”</note> <l eID="gen5742" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 2:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3735"/><l level="1" sID="gen5743"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3735"/><transChange type="added">The</transChange> kings of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> earth establish themselves,<l eID="gen5743" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5744"/>and the rulers conspire<note placement="foot">Or “make themselves firm”</note> together<l eID="gen5744" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5745"/>against Yahweh and his anointed: <l eID="gen5745" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 2:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3736"/><l level="1" sID="gen5746"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3736"/>“Let us tear off their bonds,<l eID="gen5746" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5747"/>and cast their cords from us!” <l eID="gen5747" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 2:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3737"/><l level="1" sID="gen5748"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3737"/><transChange type="added">He who</transChange> sits <transChange type="added">enthroned</transChange> in the heavens laughs.<l eID="gen5748" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5749"/>The Lord derides them. <l eID="gen5749" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 2:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3738"/><l level="1" sID="gen5750"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3738"/>Then he speaks to them in his wrath,<l eID="gen5750" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5751"/>and in his fury he terrifies them: <l eID="gen5751" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 2:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3739"/><l level="1" sID="gen5752"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3739"/>“But as for me, I have set my king<l eID="gen5752" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5753"/>on Zion, my holy mountain.” <l eID="gen5753" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 2:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3740"/><l level="1" sID="gen5754"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3740"/>I will tell the decree;<l eID="gen5754" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5755"/>Yahweh said to me:<l eID="gen5755" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5756"/>“You are my son;<l eID="gen5756" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5757"/>today I have begotten you. <l eID="gen5757" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 2:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3741"/><l level="1" sID="gen5758"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3741"/>Ask from me and I will make <transChange type="added">the</transChange> nations your heritage,<l eID="gen5758" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5759"/>and your possession <transChange type="added">the</transChange> ends of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> earth. <l eID="gen5759" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 2:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3742"/><l level="1" sID="gen5760"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3742"/>You will break them with an iron rod.<l eID="gen5760" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5761"/>Like a potter’s vessel you will shatter them.” <l eID="gen5761" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 2:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3743"/><l level="1" sID="gen5762"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3743"/>So then, O kings, be wise.<l eID="gen5762" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5763"/>Be warned, O rulers of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> earth. <l eID="gen5763" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 2:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3744"/><l level="1" sID="gen5764"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3744"/>Serve Yahweh with fear,<l eID="gen5764" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5765"/>and rejoice with trembling. <l eID="gen5765" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 2:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3745"/><l level="1" sID="gen5766"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3745"/>Kiss the Son<l eID="gen5766" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5767"/>lest he be angry and you perish <transChange type="added">on the</transChange> way,<l eID="gen5767" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5768"/>for his anger burns quickly.<l eID="gen5768" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5769"/>Blessed are all <transChange type="added">who</transChange> take refuge in him. <l eID="gen5769" level="1"/><lg eID="gen5740"/> <chapter eID="Ps.2"/>

verses.name: Psalms 3:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3746"/><title type="x-s">A Call to Yahweh in Distress</title> <div sID="gen5770" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen5770" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen5771"/> <lg eID="gen5771"/> <title canonical="true" type="psalm">A psalm of David at his fleeing from the presence of Absalom, his son.<note placement="foot">The Hebrew Bible counts the superscription as the first verse of the psalm; the English verse number is reduced by one</note></title> <lg sID="gen5772"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5773"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3746"/>Yahweh, how many are my enemies;<l eID="gen5773" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5774"/>many <transChange type="added">are</transChange> rising against me. <l eID="gen5774" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 3:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3747"/><l level="1" sID="gen5775"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3747"/>Many <transChange type="added">are</transChange> saying about my soul,<l eID="gen5775" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5776"/>“There is no deliverance for him from<note placement="foot">Or “in”</note> God. <hi type="italic">Selah</hi><note placement="foot">Meaning uncertain; probably a musical or liturgical direction</note> <l eID="gen5776" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 3:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3748"/><l level="1" sID="gen5777"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3748"/>But<note placement="foot">Or “And”</note> you, Yahweh, <transChange type="added">are</transChange> a shield around me,<l eID="gen5777" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5778"/>my glory and the one who lifts up my head. <l eID="gen5778" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 3:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3749"/><l level="1" sID="gen5779"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3749"/><transChange type="added">With</transChange> my voice I call to Yahweh<l eID="gen5779" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5780"/>and he answers me from <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his holy hill⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the hill of his holiness”</note> <hi type="italic">Selah</hi> <l eID="gen5780" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 3:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3750"/><l level="1" sID="gen5781"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3750"/>I lay down and slept;<l eID="gen5781" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5782"/>I woke up because Yahweh sustains me. <l eID="gen5782" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 3:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3751"/><l level="1" sID="gen5783"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3751"/>I am not afraid of the ten thousands of people<l eID="gen5783" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5784"/>who all around have set themselves against me. <l eID="gen5784" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 3:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3752"/><l level="1" sID="gen5785"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3752"/>Rise up, O Yahweh; deliver me, O my God;<l eID="gen5785" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5786"/>for you strike all my enemies <transChange type="added">on the</transChange> cheek.<l eID="gen5786" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5787"/><transChange type="added">The</transChange> teeth of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> wicked you break. <l eID="gen5787" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 3:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3753"/><l level="1" sID="gen5788"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3753"/>To Yahweh belongs deliverance;<l eID="gen5788" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5789"/><transChange type="added">may</transChange> your blessing <transChange type="added">be</transChange> over your people. <hi type="italic">Selah</hi> <l eID="gen5789" level="1"/><lg eID="gen5772"/> <chapter eID="Ps.3"/>

verses.name: Psalms 4:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3754"/><title type="x-s">Safety in Yahweh</title> <div sID="gen5790" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen5790" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen5791"/> <lg eID="gen5791"/> <title canonical="true" type="psalm">For the <transChange type="added">music</transChange> director; with stringed instruments. A psalm of David.<note placement="foot">The Hebrew Bible counts the superscription as the first verse of the psalm; the English verse number is reduced by one</note></title> <lg sID="gen5792"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5793"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3754"/>When I call, answer me, O God of my righteousness.<note placement="foot">Or “vindication”</note><l eID="gen5793" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5794"/>In trouble <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞deliver me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “make wide for me”</note><l eID="gen5794" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5795"/>Be gracious to me and hear my prayer. <l eID="gen5795" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 4:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3755"/><l level="1" sID="gen5796"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3755"/>O sons of man, how long will my honor<note placement="foot">Or “glory”</note> be a disgrace?<l eID="gen5796" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5797"/><transChange type="added">How long</transChange> will you love vanity?<l eID="gen5797" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5798"/><transChange type="added">How long</transChange> will you seek lies?<note placement="foot">Or “falsehood”</note> <hi type="italic">Selah</hi> <l eID="gen5798" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 4:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3756"/><l level="1" sID="gen5799"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3756"/>But know that Yahweh has set apart<note placement="foot">Or “treated specially”</note> for himself the faithful one.<note placement="foot">Or “pious, godly one”</note><l eID="gen5799" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5800"/>Yahweh hears when I call to him. <l eID="gen5800" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 4:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3757"/><l level="1" sID="gen5801"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3757"/>Be disturbed but do not sin.<l eID="gen5801" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5802"/>Commune in your heart<note placement="foot">That is, “think it over”</note> on your bed and be silent. <hi type="italic">Selah</hi> <l eID="gen5802" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 4:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3758"/><l level="1" sID="gen5803"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3758"/>Offer correct sacrifices,<note placement="foot">Or “right sacrifices”</note><l eID="gen5803" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5804"/>and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞trust in⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “trust to”</note> Yahweh. <l eID="gen5804" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 4:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3759"/><l level="1" sID="gen5805"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3759"/>Many are saying, “Who will show us <transChange type="added">something</transChange> good?”<l eID="gen5805" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5806"/>Lift up over<note placement="foot">Or “upon”</note> us the light of your face, O Yahweh. <l eID="gen5806" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 4:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3760"/><l level="1" sID="gen5807"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3760"/>You have put gladness in my heart<l eID="gen5807" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5808"/>more than <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞when⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the time of”</note> their grain and their wine abound. <l eID="gen5808" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 4:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3761"/><l level="1" sID="gen5809"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3761"/>In peace I will lie down and sleep <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞at once⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “together”</note><l eID="gen5809" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5810"/>for you alone, O Yahweh, make me dwell safely. <l eID="gen5810" level="1"/><lg eID="gen5792"/> <chapter eID="Ps.4"/>

verses.name: Psalms 5:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3762"/><title type="x-s">A Prayer for Guidance and Protection</title> <div sID="gen5811" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen5811" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen5812"/> <lg eID="gen5812"/> <title canonical="true" type="psalm">For the <transChange type="added">music</transChange> director; with the flutes. A psalm of David.<note placement="foot">The Hebrew Bible counts the superscription as the first verse of the psalm; the English verse number is reduced by one</note></title> <lg sID="gen5813"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5814"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3762"/>Hear my words, O Yahweh.<l eID="gen5814" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5815"/>Give heed to my sighing.<note placement="foot">Or “murmuring”</note> <l eID="gen5815" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 5:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3763"/><l level="1" sID="gen5816"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3763"/>Listen to the sound of my pleading,<note placement="foot">Or “cry for help”</note> my king and my God,<l eID="gen5816" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5817"/>for to you I pray. <l eID="gen5817" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 5:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3764"/><l level="1" sID="gen5818"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3764"/>O Yahweh, in <transChange type="added">the</transChange> morning you will hear my voice.<l eID="gen5818" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5819"/>In <transChange type="added">the</transChange> morning I will set forth<note placement="foot">Or “present”</note> my case to you and I will watch.<note placement="foot">Or “look expectantly”</note> <l eID="gen5819" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 5:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3765"/><l level="1" sID="gen5820"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3765"/>For you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> not a God <transChange type="added">who</transChange> desires<note placement="foot">Or “takes delight in”</note> wickedness.<l eID="gen5820" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5821"/>Evil cannot dwell with you. <l eID="gen5821" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 5:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3766"/><l level="1" sID="gen5822"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3766"/>The boastful do not stand before<note placement="foot">Or “in front of”</note> your eyes.<l eID="gen5822" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5823"/>You hate all evildoers. <l eID="gen5823" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 5:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3767"/><l level="1" sID="gen5824"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3767"/>You destroy speakers of lies.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “lie”</note><l eID="gen5824" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5825"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞A man of bloodshed⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a man of bloods”</note> and deceit Yahweh abhors. <l eID="gen5825" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 5:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3768"/><l level="1" sID="gen5826"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3768"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞But as for me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “And I”</note> through the abundance of your steadfast love<note placement="foot">Or “covenant love”</note><l eID="gen5826" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5827"/>I will enter your house.<note placement="foot">Or “temple”</note><l eID="gen5827" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5828"/>I will bow down<note placement="foot">Or “I will worship”</note> toward <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞your holy temple⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the temple of your holiness”</note> in awe <transChange type="added">of</transChange> you. <l eID="gen5828" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 5:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3769"/><l level="1" sID="gen5829"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3769"/>O Yahweh, lead me in your righteousness because of my enemies;<l eID="gen5829" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5830"/>make straight before me your way. <l eID="gen5830" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 5:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3770"/><l level="1" sID="gen5831"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3770"/>For there is not <transChange type="added">anything</transChange> reliable in his mouth;<l eID="gen5831" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5832"/>their inner part <transChange type="added">is</transChange> destruction.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “destructions”</note><l eID="gen5832" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5833"/>Their throat is an open grave;<l eID="gen5833" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5834"/><transChange type="added">with</transChange> their tongue they speak deceit.<note placement="foot">Or “flattery; smooth words”</note> <l eID="gen5834" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 5:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3771"/><l level="1" sID="gen5835"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3771"/>Treat them as guilty, O God;<l eID="gen5835" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5836"/>let them fall because of their plans.<l eID="gen5836" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5837"/>Because of the abundance of their transgressions cast them out,<l eID="gen5837" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5838"/>for they have rebelled against you. <l eID="gen5838" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 5:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3772"/><l level="1" sID="gen5839"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3772"/>But let all who take shelter in you rejoice.<l eID="gen5839" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5840"/>Let them ever<note placement="foot">Or “perpetually”</note> sing for joy,<l eID="gen5840" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5841"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞because⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and”</note> you spread protection over them;<l eID="gen5841" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5842"/>And let those<note placement="foot">Or “So that those”</note> <transChange type="added">who</transChange> love your name exult in you. <l eID="gen5842" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 5:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3773"/><l level="1" sID="gen5843"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3773"/>For you bless <transChange type="added">the</transChange> righteous.<l eID="gen5843" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5844"/>O Yahweh, like a<note placement="foot">Hebrew “the”</note> shield you surround him <transChange type="added">with</transChange> good favor. <l eID="gen5844" level="1"/><lg eID="gen5813"/> <chapter eID="Ps.5"/>

verses.name: Psalms 6:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3774"/><title type="x-s">An Appeal for Forgiveness and Deliverance</title> <div sID="gen5845" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen5845" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen5846"/> <lg eID="gen5846"/> <title canonical="true" type="psalm">For the <transChange type="added">music</transChange> director; with stringed instruments, on the Sheminith.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “upon the eighth”; meaning uncertain</note></title> <lg sID="gen5847"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5848"/>A psalm of David.<note placement="foot">The Hebrew Bible counts the superscription as the first verse of the psalm; the English verse number is reduced by one</note><l eID="gen5848" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5849"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3774"/>O Yahweh, do not rebuke me in your anger,<l eID="gen5849" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5850"/>and do not discipline me in your wrath. <l eID="gen5850" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 6:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3775"/><l level="1" sID="gen5851"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3775"/>Be gracious to me, O Yahweh, because I am feeble.<l eID="gen5851" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5852"/>Heal me, O Yahweh, for my bones are terrified. <l eID="gen5852" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 6:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3776"/><l level="1" sID="gen5853"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3776"/>My soul is also very terrified.<l eID="gen5853" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5854"/>But you, O Yahweh, how long? <l eID="gen5854" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 6:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3777"/><l level="1" sID="gen5855"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3777"/>Turn, O Yahweh; deliver my life.<note placement="foot">Or “my soul”; same word as in v. <reference osisRef="Ps.6.3">3</reference></note><l eID="gen5855" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5856"/>Save me for the sake of your steadfast love.<note placement="foot">Or “loyal love”</note> <l eID="gen5856" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 6:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3778"/><l level="1" sID="gen5857"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3778"/>For there is no remembrance of you in death.<l eID="gen5857" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5858"/>In Sheol, who will give thanks to you? <l eID="gen5858" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 6:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3779"/><l level="1" sID="gen5859"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3779"/>I am weary with my groaning;<l eID="gen5859" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5860"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I flood⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “I make my bed float”</note> my bed every night.<l eID="gen5860" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5861"/>With my tears <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I drench⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “I cause to melt”</note> my couch. <l eID="gen5861" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 6:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3780"/><l level="1" sID="gen5862"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3780"/>My eye wastes away because of vexation;<l eID="gen5862" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5863"/>it grows old because of all my oppressors. <l eID="gen5863" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 6:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3781"/><l level="1" sID="gen5864"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3781"/>Depart from me, all workers of evil,<l eID="gen5864" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5865"/>for Yahweh has heard the sound of my weeping. <l eID="gen5865" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 6:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3782"/><l level="1" sID="gen5866"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3782"/>Yahweh has heard my plea;<l eID="gen5866" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5867"/>Yahweh has accepted my prayer. <l eID="gen5867" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 6:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3783"/><l level="1" sID="gen5868"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3783"/>All my enemies shall be ashamed and shall be very terrified.<l eID="gen5868" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5869"/>They shall turn back; they shall suddenly be ashamed. <l eID="gen5869" level="1"/><lg eID="gen5847"/> <chapter eID="Ps.6"/>

verses.name: Psalms 7:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3784"/><title type="x-s">Prayer for Deliverance from Enemies</title> <div sID="gen5870" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen5870" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen5871"/> <lg eID="gen5871"/> <title canonical="true" type="psalm">A Shiggaion<note placement="foot">Meaning uncertain; perhaps a lamentation</note> of David which he sang to Yahweh</title> <lg sID="gen5872"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5873"/>on account of Cush, a Benjaminite.<note placement="foot">The Hebrew Bible counts the superscription as the first verse of the psalm; the English verse number is reduced by one</note><l eID="gen5873" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5874"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3784"/>O Yahweh, my God, in you I have taken refuge.<l eID="gen5874" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5875"/>Save me from all <transChange type="added">who</transChange> pursue me, and deliver me. <l eID="gen5875" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 7:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3785"/><l level="1" sID="gen5876"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3785"/>Or else he will tear me apart like a lion,<l eID="gen5876" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5877"/>ripping to pieces, with none <transChange type="added">to</transChange> deliver. <l eID="gen5877" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 7:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3786"/><l level="1" sID="gen5878"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3786"/>O Yahweh, my God, if I have done this,<l eID="gen5878" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5879"/>if there is wrong in my hands, <l eID="gen5879" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 7:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3787"/><l level="1" sID="gen5880"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3787"/>if I have repaid <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞my ally⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “one being at peace with me”</note> <transChange type="added">with</transChange> harm,<l eID="gen5880" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5881"/>or <transChange type="added">if</transChange> I have plundered my enemy without cause, <l eID="gen5881" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 7:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3788"/><l level="1" sID="gen5882"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3788"/>let the enemy of my soul pursue,<l eID="gen5882" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5883"/>and overtake and trample my life into the ground,<l eID="gen5883" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5884"/>and lay my honor in the dust. <hi type="italic">Selah</hi> <l eID="gen5884" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 7:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3789"/><l level="1" sID="gen5885"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3789"/>Rise up, O Yahweh, in your anger,<l eID="gen5885" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5886"/>and lift yourself up against the wrath<note placement="foot">Or “outbursts”</note> of my oppressors,<l eID="gen5886" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5887"/>and awake for me,<l eID="gen5887" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5888"/>since you have commanded judgment. <l eID="gen5888" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 7:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3790"/><l level="1" sID="gen5889"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3790"/>And let <transChange type="added">the</transChange> assembly of peoples surround you,<l eID="gen5889" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5890"/>and over it return on high. <l eID="gen5890" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 7:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3791"/><l level="1" sID="gen5891"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3791"/>Yahweh judges the nations.<l eID="gen5891" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5892"/>O Yahweh, vindicate me<l eID="gen5892" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5893"/>according to my innocence<note placement="foot">Or “righteousness”</note> and according to my integrity within me. <l eID="gen5893" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 7:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3792"/><l level="1" sID="gen5894"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3792"/>Let the evil of the wicked come to an end,<l eID="gen5894" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5895"/>but establish <transChange type="added">the</transChange> righteous,<l eID="gen5895" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5896"/>and test the hearts and innermost being, O righteous God. <l eID="gen5896" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 7:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3793"/><l level="1" sID="gen5897"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3793"/>My shield <transChange type="added">is</transChange> with God<l eID="gen5897" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5898"/>who saves the upright of heart. <l eID="gen5898" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 7:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3794"/><l level="1" sID="gen5899"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3794"/>God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a righteous judge,<l eID="gen5899" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5900"/>and a God who has indignation every day. <l eID="gen5900" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 7:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3795"/><l level="1" sID="gen5901"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3795"/>If he<note placement="foot">That is, a person</note> does not repent, he<note placement="foot">That is, God</note> will sharpen his sword.<l eID="gen5901" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5902"/>He has bent his bow and he has <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞strung⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “prepared”</note> it. <l eID="gen5902" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 7:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3796"/><l level="1" sID="gen5903"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3796"/>And he has prepared for him weapons of death.<l eID="gen5903" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5904"/>He has made his arrows fiery shafts. <l eID="gen5904" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 7:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3797"/><l level="1" sID="gen5905"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3797"/>See, he<note placement="foot">That is, the wicked</note> travails with<note placement="foot">Or “conceives”</note> evil.<l eID="gen5905" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5906"/>He is pregnant with trouble,<l eID="gen5906" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5907"/>and he gives birth to deception. <l eID="gen5907" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 7:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3798"/><l level="1" sID="gen5908"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3798"/>He makes a pit and digs it out,<l eID="gen5908" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5909"/>then falls in <transChange type="added">the</transChange> trap he has made. <l eID="gen5909" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 7:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3799"/><l level="1" sID="gen5910"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3799"/>His trouble comes back on his head,<l eID="gen5910" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5911"/>and his violence comes down on his skull. <l eID="gen5911" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 7:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3800"/><l level="1" sID="gen5912"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3800"/>I will thank Yahweh according to his righteousness,<l eID="gen5912" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5913"/>and I will sing praise to the name of Yahweh, <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Most High. <l eID="gen5913" level="1"/><lg eID="gen5872"/> <chapter eID="Ps.7"/>

verses.name: Psalms 8:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3801"/><title type="x-s">Yahweh’s Glory in Creation</title> <div sID="gen5914" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen5914" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen5915"/> <lg eID="gen5915"/> <title canonical="true" type="psalm">For the <transChange type="added">music</transChange> director, on the Gittith.<note placement="foot">Meaning uncertain</note> A psalm of David.<note placement="foot">The Hebrew Bible counts the superscription as the first verse of the psalm; the English verse number is reduced by one</note></title> <lg sID="gen5916"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5917"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3801"/>Yahweh, our Lord, how majestic <transChange type="added">is</transChange> your name in all the earth,<l eID="gen5917" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5918"/>who put your splendor above the heavens. <l eID="gen5918" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 8:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3802"/><l level="1" sID="gen5919"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3802"/>From the mouth of children and infants you have founded<note placement="foot">Or “ordained”</note> strength<l eID="gen5919" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5920"/>on account of your enemies,<l eID="gen5920" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5921"/>to silence <transChange type="added">the</transChange> enemy and <transChange type="added">the</transChange> avenger. <l eID="gen5921" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 8:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3803"/><l level="1" sID="gen5922"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3803"/>When I look at your heavens, the work of your fingers,<l eID="gen5922" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5923"/><transChange type="added">the</transChange> moon and <transChange type="added">the</transChange> stars which you set in place— <l eID="gen5923" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 8:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3804"/><l level="1" sID="gen5924"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3804"/>what <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a human being that you think of him?<l eID="gen5924" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5925"/>and a child of humankind that you care for him? <l eID="gen5925" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 8:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3805"/><l level="1" sID="gen5926"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3805"/>And you made him a little lower than heavenly beings,<note placement="foot">Or “than God”</note><l eID="gen5926" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5927"/>and <transChange type="added">with</transChange> glory and <transChange type="added">with</transChange> majesty you crowned him. <l eID="gen5927" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 8:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3806"/><l level="1" sID="gen5928"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3806"/>You make him over the works of your hands;<l eID="gen5928" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5929"/>all <transChange type="added">things</transChange> you have placed under his feet: <l eID="gen5929" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 8:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3807"/><l level="1" sID="gen5930"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3807"/>sheep and cattle, all of them,<l eID="gen5930" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5931"/>and also <transChange type="added">the</transChange> wild animals of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> field, <l eID="gen5931" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 8:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3808"/><l level="1" sID="gen5932"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3808"/><transChange type="added">the</transChange> birds of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> sky and the fish of the sea,<l eID="gen5932" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5933"/><transChange type="added">everything</transChange> that passes along the paths of seas. <l eID="gen5933" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 8:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3809"/><l level="1" sID="gen5934"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3809"/>Yahweh, our Lord,<l eID="gen5934" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5935"/>how majestic <transChange type="added">is</transChange> your name in all of the earth! <l eID="gen5935" level="1"/><lg eID="gen5916"/> <chapter eID="Ps.8"/>

verses.name: Psalms 9:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3810"/><title type="x-s">Praise for Yahweh’s Justice</title> <div sID="gen5936" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen5936" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen5937"/> <lg eID="gen5937"/> <title canonical="true" type="psalm">For the <transChange type="added">music</transChange> director, according to Muth-labben.<note placement="foot">Meaning uncertain</note> A psalm of David.<note placement="foot">The Hebrew Bible counts the superscription as the first verse of the psalm; the English verse number is reduced by one</note></title> <lg sID="gen5938"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5939"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3810"/>I will thank Yahweh with all my heart.<l eID="gen5939" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5940"/>I will tell of all your wonderful deeds. <l eID="gen5940" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 9:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3811"/><l level="1" sID="gen5941"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3811"/>I will be glad and rejoice in you.<l eID="gen5941" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5942"/>I will sing <transChange type="added">the praise of</transChange> your name, O Most High. <l eID="gen5942" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 9:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3812"/><l level="1" sID="gen5943"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3812"/>When my enemies turn back,<l eID="gen5943" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5944"/>they will stumble and perish because of your presence. <l eID="gen5944" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 9:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3813"/><l level="1" sID="gen5945"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3813"/>For you have maintained my just cause;<l eID="gen5945" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5946"/>you have sat on <transChange type="added">the</transChange> throne judging correctly. <l eID="gen5946" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 9:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3814"/><l level="1" sID="gen5947"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3814"/>You have rebuked <transChange type="added">the</transChange> nations;<l eID="gen5947" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5948"/>you have destroyed <transChange type="added">the</transChange> wicked.<l eID="gen5948" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5949"/>Their name you have blotted out<l eID="gen5949" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5950"/>forever and ever. <l eID="gen5950" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 9:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3815"/><l level="1" sID="gen5951"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3815"/>The enemies are destroyed <transChange type="added">in</transChange> ruins forever,<l eID="gen5951" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5952"/>and you have uprooted <transChange type="added">their</transChange> cities;<l eID="gen5952" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5953"/>their very memory has perished. <l eID="gen5953" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 9:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3816"/><l level="1" sID="gen5954"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3816"/>But Yahweh sits <transChange type="added">enthroned</transChange> forever.<l eID="gen5954" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5955"/>He has established his throne for judgment. <l eID="gen5955" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 9:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3817"/><l level="1" sID="gen5956"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3817"/>And he will judge <transChange type="added">the</transChange> world with righteousness.<l eID="gen5956" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5957"/>He will judge <transChange type="added">the</transChange> peoples with equity. <l eID="gen5957" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 9:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3818"/><l level="1" sID="gen5958"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3818"/>And Yahweh will be a stronghold for the oppressed,<l eID="gen5958" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5959"/>a stronghold in times of distress. <l eID="gen5959" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 9:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3819"/><l level="1" sID="gen5960"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3819"/>And those who know your name will trust in you,<l eID="gen5960" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5961"/>for you do not forsake those <transChange type="added">who</transChange> seek you, O Yahweh. <l eID="gen5961" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 9:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3820"/><l level="1" sID="gen5962"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3820"/>Sing <transChange type="added">praises</transChange> to Yahweh <transChange type="added">who</transChange> sits <transChange type="added">enthroned</transChange><note placement="foot">Or “who dwells”</note> in Zion.<l eID="gen5962" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5963"/>Tell his deeds among the peoples, <l eID="gen5963" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 9:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3821"/><l level="1" sID="gen5964"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3821"/>for he <transChange type="added">who</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞avenges bloodshed⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “seeks bloods”</note> remembers them.<l eID="gen5964" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5965"/>He does not forget the distressed cry of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> afflicted. <l eID="gen5965" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 9:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3822"/><l level="1" sID="gen5966"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3822"/>Be gracious to me, O Yahweh.<l eID="gen5966" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5967"/>See my suffering from <transChange type="added">those who</transChange> hate me,<l eID="gen5967" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5968"/><transChange type="added">you who</transChange> lift me up from the gates of death, <l eID="gen5968" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 9:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3823"/><l level="1" sID="gen5969"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3823"/>so that I may tell of all your praises.<l eID="gen5969" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5970"/>In the gates of the daughter of Zion<l eID="gen5970" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5971"/>let me rejoice in your salvation. <l eID="gen5971" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 9:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3824"/><l level="1" sID="gen5972"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3824"/><transChange type="added">The</transChange> nations have fallen in <transChange type="added">the</transChange> pit <transChange type="added">that</transChange> they made;<l eID="gen5972" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5973"/>their foot is caught in <transChange type="added">the</transChange> net that they hid. <l eID="gen5973" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 9:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3825"/><l level="1" sID="gen5974"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3825"/>Yahweh has made himself known;<l eID="gen5974" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5975"/>he has executed judgment.<l eID="gen5975" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5976"/>The wicked is snared by the work of his hands. <hi type="italic">Higgaion</hi><note placement="foot">Hebrew musical term</note> <hi type="italic">Selah</hi> <l eID="gen5976" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 9:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3826"/><l level="1" sID="gen5977"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3826"/><transChange type="added">The</transChange> wicked shall turn back to Sheol,<l eID="gen5977" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5978"/>all <transChange type="added">the</transChange> nations forgetting God, <l eID="gen5978" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 9:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3827"/><l level="1" sID="gen5979"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3827"/>for <transChange type="added">the</transChange> needy shall not always be forgotten;<l eID="gen5979" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5980"/>the hope of the poor shall never perish. <l eID="gen5980" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 9:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3828"/><l level="1" sID="gen5981"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3828"/>Rise up, O Yahweh, let not humans<note placement="foot">Hebrew “human”</note> prevail;<l eID="gen5981" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5982"/>let <transChange type="added">the</transChange> nations be judged before you. <l eID="gen5982" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 9:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3829"/><l level="1" sID="gen5983"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3829"/>O Yahweh, put them in fear.<l eID="gen5983" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5984"/>Let <transChange type="added">the</transChange> nations know they <transChange type="added">are merely</transChange> human. <hi type="italic">Selah</hi> <l eID="gen5984" level="1"/><lg eID="gen5938"/> <chapter eID="Ps.9"/>

verses.name: Psalms 10:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3830"/><title type="x-s">A Prayer for God to Throw down the Wicked</title> <div sID="gen5985" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen5985" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen5986"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5987"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3830"/>Why, O Yahweh, do you stand far off?<l eID="gen5987" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5988"/><transChange type="added">Why</transChange> do you hide<note placement="foot">Or “shut your eyes”</note> during times of distress? <l eID="gen5988" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 10:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3831"/><l level="1" sID="gen5989"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3831"/>In arrogance <transChange type="added">the</transChange> wicked persecutes<note placement="foot">Or “pursues”</note> <transChange type="added">the</transChange> poor.<l eID="gen5989" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5990"/>Let them be caught in <transChange type="added">the</transChange> schemes that they devised, <l eID="gen5990" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 10:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3832"/><l level="1" sID="gen5991"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3832"/>for <transChange type="added">the</transChange> wicked boasts about the desire of his <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞heart⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “soul”</note><l eID="gen5991" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5992"/>and <transChange type="added">the</transChange> one greedy for gain curses <transChange type="added">and</transChange> treats Yahweh with contempt. <l eID="gen5992" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 10:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3833"/><l level="1" sID="gen5993"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3833"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞With bald-faced pride⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “According to the height of his nose”</note> <transChange type="added">the</transChange> wicked will not seek <transChange type="added">God</transChange>.<l eID="gen5993" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5994"/>There is no God in any of his thoughts. <l eID="gen5994" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 10:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3834"/><l level="1" sID="gen5995"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3834"/>His ways<note placement="foot">According to the reading tradition (<hi type="italic">Qere</hi>)</note> endure at all times.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “time”</note><l eID="gen5995" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5996"/>Your judgments are aloof from him.<l eID="gen5996" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5997"/><transChange type="added">As for</transChange> all his enemies, he scoffs at them. <l eID="gen5997" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 10:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3835"/><l level="1" sID="gen5998"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3835"/>He says in his heart, “I shall not be moved<l eID="gen5998" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen5999"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞throughout all generations⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “for a generation and a generation”</note> <transChange type="added">during</transChange> which <transChange type="added">I will have</transChange> no trouble.” <l eID="gen5999" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 10:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3836"/><l level="1" sID="gen6000"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3836"/>His mouth is filled with cursing,<l eID="gen6000" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6001"/>with deceits and oppression;<l eID="gen6001" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6002"/>under his tongue are trouble and evil. <l eID="gen6002" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 10:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3837"/><l level="1" sID="gen6003"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3837"/>He sits in ambush in villages;<l eID="gen6003" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6004"/>in the hiding places he kills <transChange type="added">the</transChange> innocent.<l eID="gen6004" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6005"/>His eyes <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞lurk⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “lie hid”</note> for <transChange type="added">the</transChange> helpless. <l eID="gen6005" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 10:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3838"/><l level="1" sID="gen6006"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3838"/>He lies in ambush <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞secretly,⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in the secret places”</note> like a lion in a thicket.<l eID="gen6006" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6007"/>He lies in ambush to seize <transChange type="added">the</transChange> poor;<l eID="gen6007" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6008"/>he seizes <transChange type="added">the</transChange> poor by catching him in his net. <l eID="gen6008" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 10:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3839"/><l level="1" sID="gen6009"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3839"/>He is crushed;<note placement="foot">Or “and he the wicked stoops”</note> he is bowed down;<note placement="foot">Or “he the wicked crouches”</note><l eID="gen6009" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6010"/>so<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> the helpless host<note placement="foot">According to the reading tradition (<hi type="italic">Qere</hi>)</note> falls by his <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞might⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “mighty ones”</note> <l eID="gen6010" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 10:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3840"/><l level="1" sID="gen6011"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3840"/>He says in his heart, “God has forgotten.<l eID="gen6011" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6012"/>He has hidden his face.<l eID="gen6012" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6013"/>He never sees.” <l eID="gen6013" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 10:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3841"/><l level="1" sID="gen6014"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3841"/>Rise up, O Yahweh;<l eID="gen6014" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6015"/>O God, lift up your hand.<l eID="gen6015" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6016"/>Do not forget <transChange type="added">the</transChange> afflicted. <l eID="gen6016" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 10:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3842"/><l level="1" sID="gen6017"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3842"/>Why does the wicked treat God with contempt?<l eID="gen6017" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6018"/>He says in his heart, “You will not call <transChange type="added">me</transChange> to account.” <l eID="gen6018" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 10:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3843"/><l level="1" sID="gen6019"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3843"/><transChange type="added">But</transChange> you have seen; indeed you have noted trouble and grief<l eID="gen6019" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6020"/>to take <transChange type="added">it</transChange> into your hand.<l eID="gen6020" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6021"/>The helpless abandons <transChange type="added">himself</transChange> upon you;<l eID="gen6021" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6022"/>you have been <transChange type="added">the</transChange> helper <transChange type="added">for the</transChange> orphan. <l eID="gen6022" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 10:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3844"/><l level="1" sID="gen6023"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3844"/>Break <transChange type="added">the</transChange> arm of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> wicked,<l eID="gen6023" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6024"/>and <transChange type="added">as for the</transChange> evil <transChange type="added">man</transChange>—<l eID="gen6024" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6025"/>seek out his wickedness <transChange type="added">until</transChange> you find none. <l eID="gen6025" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 10:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3845"/><l level="1" sID="gen6026"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3845"/>Yahweh <transChange type="added">is</transChange> king forever and ever;<l eID="gen6026" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6027"/>the nations have perished from his land. <l eID="gen6027" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 10:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3846"/><l level="1" sID="gen6028"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3846"/><transChange type="added">The</transChange> longing of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> afflicted you have heard, O Yahweh.<l eID="gen6028" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6029"/>You will make their heart secure. You will <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞listen attentively⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “cause your ear to hear”</note> <l eID="gen6029" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 10:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3847"/><l level="1" sID="gen6030"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3847"/>to render judgment <transChange type="added">for the</transChange> fatherless and <transChange type="added">the</transChange> oppressed<l eID="gen6030" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6031"/><transChange type="added">so that</transChange> a <transChange type="added">mere</transChange> mortal from the earth will no longer cause terror. <l eID="gen6031" level="1"/><lg eID="gen5986"/> <chapter eID="Ps.10"/>

verses.name: Psalms 11:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3848"/><title type="x-s">Confidence in Yahweh’s Righteousness</title> <div sID="gen6032" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen6032" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen6033"/> <lg eID="gen6033"/> <title canonical="true" type="psalm">For the <transChange type="added">music</transChange> director. Of David.<note placement="foot">The Hebrew Bible counts the superscription as the first verse of the psalm</note></title> <lg sID="gen6034"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6035"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3848"/>In Yahweh I have taken refuge;<l eID="gen6035" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6036"/>how can you say to my soul,<l eID="gen6036" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6037"/>“Flee to your mountain <transChange type="added">like</transChange> a bird”? <l eID="gen6037" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 11:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3849"/><l level="1" sID="gen6038"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3849"/>For look: The wicked <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞string the bow⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “tread the bow,” that is, placing the foot on the bow to bend and string it</note><l eID="gen6038" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6039"/>They have fitted their arrow to <transChange type="added">the</transChange> string,<l eID="gen6039" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6040"/>to shoot from <transChange type="added">the</transChange> darkness<l eID="gen6040" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6041"/>at the upright of heart. <l eID="gen6041" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 11:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3850"/><l level="1" sID="gen6042"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3850"/>When the foundations are destroyed<l eID="gen6042" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6043"/>what can <transChange type="added">the</transChange> righteous do?<note placement="foot">Or “what has the righteous done”</note> <l eID="gen6043" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 11:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3851"/><l level="1" sID="gen6044"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3851"/>Yahweh <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in his holy temple;<l eID="gen6044" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6045"/>Yahweh <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in the heavens <transChange type="added">on</transChange> his throne.<l eID="gen6045" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6046"/>His eyelids see;<l eID="gen6046" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6047"/>they test <transChange type="added">the</transChange> children of humankind. <l eID="gen6047" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 11:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3852"/><l level="1" sID="gen6048"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3852"/>Yahweh tests <transChange type="added">the</transChange> righteous,<l eID="gen6048" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6049"/>but <transChange type="added">the</transChange> wicked and <transChange type="added">the</transChange> lover of violence<l eID="gen6049" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6050"/>his soul hates. <l eID="gen6050" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 11:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3853"/><l level="1" sID="gen6051"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3853"/>He will rain coals<note placement="foot">According to Symmachus (compare also <hi type="italic">Targum Psalms</hi>) a form slightly different from the MT’s “snares”</note> on <transChange type="added">the</transChange> wicked.<l eID="gen6051" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6052"/>Burning sulfur and scorching wind<l eID="gen6052" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6053"/><transChange type="added">will be</transChange> the portion of their cup. <l eID="gen6053" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 11:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3854"/><l level="1" sID="gen6054"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3854"/>For Yahweh <transChange type="added">is</transChange> righteous;<l eID="gen6054" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6055"/>he loves righteous deeds.<l eID="gen6055" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6056"/><transChange type="added">The</transChange> upright shall see his face. <l eID="gen6056" level="1"/><lg eID="gen6034"/> <chapter eID="Ps.11"/>

verses.name: Psalms 12:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3855"/><title type="x-s">Human Faithlessness and God’s Faithfulness</title> <div sID="gen6057" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen6057" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen6058"/> <lg eID="gen6058"/> <title canonical="true" type="psalm">For the <transChange type="added">music</transChange> director; on the Sheminith.<note placement="foot">Meaning uncertain</note> A psalm of David.<note placement="foot">The Hebrew Bible counts the superscription as the first verse of the psalm; the English verse number is reduced by one</note></title> <lg sID="gen6059"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6060"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3855"/>Save, O Yahweh, for <transChange type="added">the</transChange> pious have ceased <transChange type="added">to be</transChange>;<l eID="gen6060" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6061"/>for <transChange type="added">the</transChange> faithful have vanished<l eID="gen6061" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6062"/>from <transChange type="added">among the</transChange> children of humankind. <l eID="gen6062" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 12:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3856"/><l level="1" sID="gen6063"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3856"/>They speak falseness <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to each other⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “each with his companion”</note><l eID="gen6063" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6064"/><transChange type="added">With</transChange> flattering lips,<l eID="gen6064" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6065"/><transChange type="added">with</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a double heart⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a heart and a heart”</note> they speak. <l eID="gen6065" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 12:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3857"/><l level="1" sID="gen6066"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3857"/>May Yahweh cut off all flattering lips,<l eID="gen6066" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6067"/><transChange type="added">the</transChange> tongue speaking great boasts— <l eID="gen6067" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 12:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3858"/><l level="1" sID="gen6068"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3858"/><transChange type="added">those</transChange> who say, “With our tongue we will prevail.<l eID="gen6068" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6069"/>Our lips <transChange type="added">are</transChange> on our side.<l eID="gen6069" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6070"/>Who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> master over us?” <l eID="gen6070" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 12:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3859"/><l level="1" sID="gen6071"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3859"/>“Because of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> oppression of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> afflicted,<l eID="gen6071" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6072"/>because of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> groaning of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> poor,<l eID="gen6072" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6073"/>now I will rise up,” Yahweh says.<l eID="gen6073" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6074"/>“I shall put <transChange type="added">them</transChange> in <transChange type="added">the</transChange> safety <transChange type="added">for which</transChange> they<note placement="foot">Hebrew “he”</note> long.” <l eID="gen6074" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 12:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3860"/><l level="1" sID="gen6075"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3860"/>The words of Yahweh <transChange type="added">are</transChange> pure words<l eID="gen6075" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6076"/><transChange type="added">like</transChange> silver refined in the crucible on the ground,<l eID="gen6076" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6077"/>refined seven times. <l eID="gen6077" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 12:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3861"/><l level="1" sID="gen6078"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3861"/>You, O Yahweh, will protect them.<l eID="gen6078" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6079"/>You will preserve him<note placement="foot">Or “us”</note><l eID="gen6079" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6080"/>from this generation always. <l eID="gen6080" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 12:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3862"/><l level="1" sID="gen6081"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3862"/><transChange type="added">The</transChange> wicked prowl about<l eID="gen6081" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6082"/>when vileness <transChange type="added">is</transChange> exalted among <transChange type="added">the</transChange> children of humankind. <l eID="gen6082" level="1"/><lg eID="gen6059"/> <chapter eID="Ps.12"/>

verses.name: Psalms 13:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3863"/><title type="x-s">Trust in the Salvation of Yahweh</title> <div sID="gen6083" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen6083" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen6084"/> <lg eID="gen6084"/> <title canonical="true" type="psalm">For the <transChange type="added">music</transChange> director. A psalm of David.<note placement="foot">The Hebrew Bible counts the superscription as the first verse of the psalm; the English verse number is reduced by one</note></title> <lg sID="gen6085"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6086"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3863"/>How long, O Yahweh? Will you forget me forever?<l eID="gen6086" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6087"/>How long will you hide your face from me? <l eID="gen6087" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 13:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3864"/><l level="1" sID="gen6088"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3864"/>How long must I take counsel<note placement="foot">Hebrew pl.; with a slight modification of the Hebrew this reads “set pains”</note> in my soul,<l eID="gen6088" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6089"/><transChange type="added">and</transChange> sorrow in my heart <transChange type="added">all the</transChange> day?<l eID="gen6089" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6090"/>How long will my enemy be exalted over me? <l eID="gen6090" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 13:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3865"/><l level="1" sID="gen6091"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3865"/>Consider<note placement="foot">Literally “Look”</note> <transChange type="added">and</transChange> answer me, O Yahweh my God.<l eID="gen6091" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6092"/>Give light to my eyes<l eID="gen6092" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6093"/>lest I sleep <transChange type="added">the sleep of</transChange> death, <l eID="gen6093" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 13:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3866"/><l level="1" sID="gen6094"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3866"/><transChange type="added">and</transChange> lest my enemy should say, “I have overcome him,”<l eID="gen6094" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6095"/><transChange type="added">lest</transChange> my enemies rejoice because I am shaken. <l eID="gen6095" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 13:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3867"/><l level="1" sID="gen6096"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3867"/>But as for me, I have trusted in your steadfast love.<note placement="foot">Or, “loyal love”</note><l eID="gen6096" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6097"/>My heart will rejoice in your deliverance. <l eID="gen6097" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 13:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3868"/><l level="1" sID="gen6098"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3868"/><note placement="foot">In the Hebrew Bible, the previous verse continues</note> I will sing to Yahweh<l eID="gen6098" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6099"/>because he has dealt bountifully with me. <l eID="gen6099" level="1"/><lg eID="gen6085"/> <chapter eID="Ps.13"/>

verses.name: Psalms 14:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3869"/><title type="x-s">The Folly of the Godless and God’s Final Triumph</title> <div sID="gen6100" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen6100" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen6101"/> <lg eID="gen6101"/> <title canonical="true" type="psalm">For the <transChange type="added">music</transChange> director. Of David.<note placement="foot">The Hebrew Bible counts the superscription as the first verse of the psalm</note></title> <lg sID="gen6102"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6103"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3869"/><transChange type="added">The</transChange> fool says in his heart, “There is no God.”<l eID="gen6103" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6104"/>They are corrupt.<l eID="gen6104" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6105"/>They do abominable deeds.<l eID="gen6105" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6106"/>There is none who does good. <l eID="gen6106" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 14:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3870"/><l level="1" sID="gen6107"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3870"/>Yahweh looks down from heaven upon the children of humankind<l eID="gen6107" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6108"/>to see whether there is one who has insight,<l eID="gen6108" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6109"/>one who cares about God. <l eID="gen6109" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 14:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3871"/><l level="1" sID="gen6110"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3871"/>All have gone astray;<l eID="gen6110" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6111"/>they are altogether corrupt.<l eID="gen6111" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6112"/>There is not one who does good;<l eID="gen6112" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6113"/>there is not even one. <l eID="gen6113" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 14:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3872"/><l level="1" sID="gen6114"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3872"/>All who do evil—do they not know,<l eID="gen6114" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6115"/><transChange type="added">they</transChange> who eat my people <transChange type="added">as though</transChange> they were eating bread?<l eID="gen6115" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6116"/>They do not call on Yahweh. <l eID="gen6116" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 14:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3873"/><l level="1" sID="gen6117"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3873"/>There <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they are very fearful⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “they feared a fear”</note><l eID="gen6117" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6118"/>because God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> with <transChange type="added">the</transChange> generation of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> righteous. <l eID="gen6118" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 14:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3874"/><l level="1" sID="gen6119"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3874"/>You would put to shame <transChange type="added">the</transChange> plan of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> poor,<l eID="gen6119" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6120"/>because<note placement="foot">Or “but”</note> Yahweh <transChange type="added">is</transChange> his refuge. <l eID="gen6120" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 14:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3875"/><l level="1" sID="gen6121"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3875"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Oh that from Zion⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Who will give that from Zion”</note> <transChange type="added">would come</transChange> salvation <transChange type="added">for</transChange> Israel!<l eID="gen6121" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6122"/>When Yahweh returns the fortunes of his people,<l eID="gen6122" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6123"/>Jacob will rejoice; Israel will be happy. <l eID="gen6123" level="1"/><lg eID="gen6102"/> <chapter eID="Ps.14"/>

verses.name: Psalms 15:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3876"/><title type="x-s">A Description of Those Who May Dwell with Yahweh</title> <div sID="gen6124" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen6124" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen6125"/> <lg eID="gen6125"/> <title canonical="true" type="psalm">A psalm of David.<note placement="foot">The Hebrew Bible counts the superscription as the first verse of the psalm</note></title> <lg sID="gen6126"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6127"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3876"/>O Yahweh, who may reside in your tent?<l eID="gen6127" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6128"/>Who may dwell on your holy mountain? <l eID="gen6128" level="1"/>

verses.name: Psalms 15:2
