verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7089"/><l level="1" sID="gen13927"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7089"/>The sun rises, and the sun goes down;<l eID="gen13927" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen13928"/>to its place it hurries,<note placement="foot">The MT reads “it gasps for breath,” which is supported by LXX “to draw breath”; the BHS editors suggest “it returns again”</note> and there it rises again. <l eID="gen13928" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7090"/><l level="1" sID="gen13929"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7090"/>The wind goes to the south and goes around to the north;<l eID="gen13929" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen13930"/>around and around it goes, and on its circuit the wind returns. <l eID="gen13930" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7091"/><l level="1" sID="gen13931"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7091"/>All the streams flow to the sea,<l eID="gen13931" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen13932"/>but the sea is never full;<l eID="gen13932" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen13933"/>to the place where the streams flow,<l eID="gen13933" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen13934"/>there they continue to flow. <l eID="gen13934" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7092"/><l level="1" sID="gen13935"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7092"/>All things toil continuously;<note placement="foot">Or “are wearisome”</note><l eID="gen13935" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen13936"/>no one can ever finish describing this.<note placement="foot">The MT reads “no one is able to speak.” The BHS editors suggest “no one can finish speaking.” On the basis of internal evidence, the latter is adopted in the translation, since it makes better sense in the light of the immediate context</note><l eID="gen13936" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen13937"/>The eye is never<note placement="foot">Or “not”</note> satisfied with seeing,<l eID="gen13937" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen13938"/>and the ear is never<note placement="foot">Or “not”</note> filled with hearing. <l eID="gen13938" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7093"/><l level="1" sID="gen13939"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7093"/>What has been—it is what will be;<l eID="gen13939" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen13940"/>what has been done—it is what will be done;<l eID="gen13940" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen13941"/>there is nothing new under the sun. <l eID="gen13941" level="3"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7094"/><l level="1" sID="gen13942"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7094"/>There is a thing <transChange type="added">of</transChange> which it is said, “Look at this! This is new!”<l eID="gen13942" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen13943"/><transChange type="added">But</transChange> it already existed in ages past before us. <l eID="gen13943" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7095"/><l level="1" sID="gen13944"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7095"/>There is neither remembrance of former generations,<l eID="gen13944" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen13945"/>nor will there be remembrance of future generations. <l eID="gen13945" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen13922"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7096"/><title type="x-s">Qohelet Introduces His Quest</title> <div sID="gen13946" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7096"/>I, the Teacher,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Qohelet”</note> <transChange type="added">was</transChange> king over Israel in Jerusalem.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:13
verses.text: I applied my mind to seek and to search by wisdom all that is done under the heavens.<note placement="foot">MT reads “under the heavens,” which is supported by LXX; however, several versions (Syriac Peshitta, Aramaic Targum, Latin Vulgate) as well as the Cairo Geniza manuscript read, “under the sun,” cf. 1:3, 9, etc.</note> It is a grievous task God has given to <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞humans⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the sons of the man”</note>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:14
verses.text: I saw all the works that are done under the sun. Look! Everything <transChange type="added">is</transChange> vanity and chasing wind.  <div eID="gen13946" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7097"/><lg sID="gen13947"/> <l level="1" sID="gen13948"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7097"/>What is twisted cannot be straightened,<note placement="foot">The MT reads the active “to be straight”; however, the BHS editors suggest the passive “to be straightened,” which is supported by LXX, which reflects a passive form</note><l eID="gen13948" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen13949"/>and what is lacking cannot be counted.<note placement="foot">The MT reads “to be numbered”; however, the BHS editors suggest “to be supplied,” comparing 1:15b with similar wording in the Babylonian Talmud: “May the Almighty replenish your loss” (<hi type="italic">b. Berachot</hi> 16b)</note> <l eID="gen13949" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen13947"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7098"/><div sID="gen13950" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7098"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I said to myself⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “I myself said to my heart”</note> “Look! I have become great and have increased in wisdom more than anyone who <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞has preceded⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “before me”</note> me over Jerusalem. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I have acquired a great deal of wisdom and knowledge⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “And my mind has seen much wisdom and knowledge”</note>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:17
verses.text: So <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I dedicated myself⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “<reference osisRef="Song.1.1">So I </reference>gave my heart”</note> to learn about wisdom and to learn about delusion and folly. However, I discovered<note placement="foot">Or “I knew”</note> that this also <transChange type="added">is</transChange> chasing wind.  <div eID="gen13950" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7099"/><lg sID="gen13951"/> <l level="1" sID="gen13952"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7099"/>For in much wisdom <transChange type="added">is</transChange> much frustration,<note placement="foot">Or “vexation”</note><l eID="gen13952" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen13953"/>and whoever increases knowledge increases sorrow. <l eID="gen13953" level="2"/><lg eID="gen13951"/> <chapter eID="Eccl.1"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7100"/><title type="x-s">Qohelet’s Investigation of Self-Indulgence</title> <div sID="gen13954" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7100"/>I said <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to myself⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to my heart”</note> “Come! I will test<note placement="foot">The MT reads “I will test you,” but the BHS editors propose “I will test …” Whether or not one adopts MT, Qohelet is speaking to himself</note> pleasure <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to see whether it is worthwhile⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “and look at goodness”; this idiom refers to the enjoyment of life</note> But look, “This also <transChange type="added">is</transChange> vanity!”

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:2
verses.text: I said of laughter, “<transChange type="added">It is</transChange> folly!” and of pleasure, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞What does it accomplish?⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>”<note placement="foot">Literally “What does it give?”</note>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:3
verses.text: I also <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞explored⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “I searched in my mind”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the effects of indulging my flesh⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to cheer my flesh”</note> with wine. My mind guiding me with wisdom, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I investigated⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “laid hold of”</note> folly so that I might discover what is good under heaven<note placement="foot">Follows MT; two medieval Hebrew manuscripts, LXX, Peshitta read, “under the sun,” cf. 1:3, 9, etc.</note> for <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞humans⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the sons of the man”</note> to do <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞during the days of their lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the number of the days of their lives”</note>  <div eID="gen13954" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7101"/><title type="x-s">Qohelet’s Investigation of Personal Accomplishment</title> <div sID="gen13955" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7101"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I accomplished great things⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “I made great my works”</note> I built for myself houses; I planted for myself vineyards.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:5
verses.text: I made for myself gardens and parks, and I planted all <transChange type="added">sorts of</transChange> fruit trees in them.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:6
verses.text: I made for myself pools of water from which to irrigate a grove of flourishing trees.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:7
verses.text: I acquired male slaves and female slaves, as well as children <transChange type="added">born in my</transChange> house. I also had livestock, cattle, and flocks more than anyone who <transChange type="added">was</transChange> before me in Jerusalem.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:8
verses.text: I also gathered to myself silver and gold—the royal and provincial treasuries. I acquired for myself male and female singers, as well as the delight of <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞men⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the sons of the man”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞voluptuous concubines⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “a breast and breasts,” as a synecdoche for beautiful women in the king’s harem</note>  <div eID="gen13955" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7102"/><div sID="gen13956" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7102"/>Thus, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I accomplished far more⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “I became great and I surpassed”</note> than anyone who <transChange type="added">was</transChange> before me in Jerusalem—indeed, my wisdom stood by me.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:10
verses.text: I neither withheld anything from my eyes that they desired, nor did I deprive any pleasure from my heart. My heart rejoiced in all my toil, for this was my reward from all my toil.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:11
verses.text: Yet when I considered<note placement="foot">Or “turned to”</note> all the effort which I expended and the toil with which I toiled to do, then behold, “Everything <transChange type="added">is</transChange> vanity and chasing wind! There is nothing profitable under the sun!”  <div eID="gen13956" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7103"/><title type="x-s">The Living Must Abandon the Work of their Hands to Others at Death</title> <div sID="gen13957" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7103"/>Next, I considered wisdom, as well as delusion and folly. What can anyone <transChange type="added">do</transChange> who will come after the king that has not already been done?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:13
verses.text: I realized that wisdom has an advantage over folly, just as light has an advantage over darkness.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:14
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞The wise man can see where he is walking⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “The eyes of the wise are in his head”</note> but the fool walks in darkness. Yet I also realized that both of them suffer the same fate.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:15
verses.text: So I said <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to myself⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “in my heart”</note> “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞If I also suffer the same fate as the fool⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “Just as the fate of the fool—so it will happen to me!”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞what advantage is my great wisdom⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?”<note placement="foot">Literally “why have I been so exceedingly wise?”</note> So I said <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to myself⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “in my heart”</note> “This also <transChange type="added">is</transChange> vanity!”  <div eID="gen13957" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7104"/><div sID="gen13958" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7104"/>Certainly no one will remember the wise man or the fool in <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞future generations⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the futures”</note> When <transChange type="added">future</transChange> days come, both will have been forgotten already. How <transChange type="added">is it that</transChange> the wise man dies the same as the fool?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:17
verses.text: So I hated life because the work done under the sun <transChange type="added">is</transChange> grievous to me. For everything <transChange type="added">is</transChange> vanity and chasing wind!  <div eID="gen13958" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7105"/><div sID="gen13959" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7105"/>So I hated all my toil with which I have toiled under the sun, for I must leave it behind to someone who will be after me.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:19
verses.text: And who knows <transChange type="added">whether</transChange> he will be wise or foolish? Yet he will exercise control of all <transChange type="added">the fruit of</transChange> my toil with which I toiled wisely under the sun. This also <transChange type="added">is</transChange> vanity!  <div eID="gen13959" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7106"/><div sID="gen13960" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7106"/>So <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I began to despair⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “I myself turned to cause my heart to despair”</note> of all the toil with which I toiled under the sun.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:21
verses.text: For although a person may toil with great wisdom and skill, he must leave his reward to someone who has not toiled for it. This also <transChange type="added">is</transChange> vanity and a great calamity.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:22
verses.text: For what does a person receive for all his toil and in the longing of his heart with which he toils under the sun?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:23
verses.text: All his days <transChange type="added">are</transChange> painful, his labor <transChange type="added">brings</transChange> grief, and his heart cannot rest at night. This also <transChange type="added">is</transChange> vanity!  <div eID="gen13960" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7107"/><title type="x-s">It is Best to Simply Enjoy the Passing Pleasures of Life as Reward for Pleasing God</title> <div sID="gen13961" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7107"/>There is nothing better for a person than to eat and drink and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞find delight⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to see good”</note> in his toil. For I also realized that this <transChange type="added">is</transChange> from the hand of God!

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:25
verses.text: For who can eat <transChange type="added">and drink</transChange>, and who can enjoy <transChange type="added">life</transChange> apart from him?<note placement="foot">The MT reads “more than me,” which is supported by Aramaic Targum and Latin Vulgate, but several medieval Hebrew manuscripts read “from him”</note>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:26
verses.text: For to the person who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> good in his eyes, he gives wisdom, knowledge, and joy; but to the sinner he gives the task of gathering and heaping up only to give <transChange type="added">it</transChange> to <transChange type="added">him who is</transChange> pleasing to him. This also <transChange type="added">is</transChange> vanity and chasing wind!  <chapter eID="Eccl.2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7108"/><title type="x-s">God Has Ordained the Ebb and Flow of Human Activities</title> <div sID="gen13962" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7108"/>For everything there <transChange type="added">is</transChange> an appointed time, a time for every matter under heaven:  <div eID="gen13962" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7109"/><lg sID="gen13963"/> <l level="1" sID="gen13964"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7109"/>a time to bear<note placement="foot">Or “a time to be born”; MT reads the active form “to bear children”</note> and a time to die;<l eID="gen13964" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen13965"/>a time to plant and a time to root up <transChange type="added">what is</transChange> planted; <l eID="gen13965" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7110"/><l level="1" sID="gen13966"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7110"/>a time to kill and a time to heal;<l eID="gen13966" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen13967"/>a time to break down and a time to build up; <l eID="gen13967" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7111"/><l level="1" sID="gen13968"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7111"/>a time to weep and a time to laugh;<l eID="gen13968" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen13969"/>a time to mourn and a time to dance; <l eID="gen13969" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7112"/><l level="1" sID="gen13970"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7112"/>a time to throw away stones and a time to gather stones;<l eID="gen13970" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen13971"/>a time to embrace and a time to refrain from embracing; <l eID="gen13971" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7113"/><l level="1" sID="gen13972"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7113"/>a time to seek and a time to lose;<l eID="gen13972" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen13973"/>a time to keep and a time to throw away; <l eID="gen13973" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7114"/><l level="1" sID="gen13974"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7114"/>a time to tear and a time to sew;<l eID="gen13974" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen13975"/>a time to be silent and a time to speak; <l eID="gen13975" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7115"/><l level="1" sID="gen13976"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7115"/>a time to love and a time to hate;<l eID="gen13976" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen13977"/>a time <transChange type="added">for</transChange> war and a time <transChange type="added">for</transChange> peace. <l eID="gen13977" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen13963"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7116"/><div sID="gen13978" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7116"/>What does the worker gain in his toil?  <div eID="gen13978" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7117"/><title type="x-s">No One Understands God’s Mysterious Plan</title> <div sID="gen13979" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7117"/>I have seen the busyness God gives to <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞humans⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the sons of the man”</note> to preoccupy<note placement="foot">Or “to be busy”</note> them.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:11
verses.text: He has made everything suitable in its time. He also has put <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the past⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “eternity”</note> in their hearts, yet no one can grasp what God does from the beginning to the end.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:12
verses.text: So I realized that there is <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞nothing better⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “no good”</note> for them than to <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞rejoice and enjoy themselves⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to rejoice and to do good”</note> during their lives.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:13
verses.text: And for anyone to eat and drink, that is, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to enjoy the fruit of all his toil⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to see good in all his toil”</note> this also is a gift of God.  <div eID="gen13979" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7118"/><lg sID="gen13980"/> <l level="1" sID="gen13981"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7118"/>I know everything God does endures forever;<l eID="gen13981" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen13982"/>nothing can be added to it, and nothing can be taken from it,<l eID="gen13982" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen13983"/>for God so acts that humans<note placement="foot">Or “they”</note> might stand in awe before him. <l eID="gen13983" level="3"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7119"/><l level="1" sID="gen13984"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7119"/>What is—it already was,<l eID="gen13984" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen13985"/>and what will be—it already is,<l eID="gen13985" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen13986"/>for <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞God will do what he has done.⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “God seeks what is pursued”</note> <l eID="gen13986" level="3"/> <lg eID="gen13980"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7120"/><title type="x-s">God’s Mysterious Plan Allows Injustice to Exist in the World</title> <div sID="gen13987" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7120"/>I saw something else under the sun: instead of justice <transChange type="added">there was</transChange> evil; instead of righteousness <transChange type="added">there was</transChange> wickedness.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:17
verses.text: So I said <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to myself⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “in my heart”</note> “God will surely judge the righteous and the wicked, for he has appointed<note placement="foot">The MT reads שָׁם “there,” but repointing to שָׂם, “he has appointed,” makes better sense</note> a time <transChange type="added">of judgment</transChange> for every deed and every work.”  <div eID="gen13987" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7121"/><div sID="gen13988" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7121"/>I said to myself concerning <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞humans⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the sons of the man”</note> “God sifts<note placement="foot">Or “tests”</note> them in order to show<note placement="foot">The MT reads active “to see,” but causative “to show” is reflected by LXX, Syriac Peshitta, and Latin Vulgate</note> them that they are like beasts.”

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:19
verses.text: For the fate of <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞humans⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the sons of the man”</note> and the fate of the beast is <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the same⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “is one”</note> The death of the one is like the death of the other, for <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞both are mortal⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “and one breath is for all”</note> Man has no advantage over the beast, for both are fleeting.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:20
verses.text: Both go to one place—both came from dust and both return to dust.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:21
verses.text: For no one knows <transChange type="added">whether</transChange> the spirit of a human ascends <transChange type="added">to heaven</transChange> and <transChange type="added">whether</transChange> the spirit of the beast descends to the ground!  <div eID="gen13988" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7122"/><div sID="gen13989" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7122"/>So I concluded that there is nothing better for a person than to enjoy <transChange type="added">the fruit of</transChange> his labor, for this is his lot in life. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞For no one knows what will happen in the future.⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “For who can bring him to see in what will be after him?”</note>  <chapter eID="Eccl.3"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7123"/><title type="x-s">The Existence of Oppression in the World Makes Human Existence Miserable</title> <div sID="gen13990" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7123"/>I looked again, and I saw all the oppression that occurs under the sun. <div eID="gen13990" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen13991"/> <l level="1" sID="gen13992"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I saw the tears of the oppressed— <milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><l eID="gen13992" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen13993"/>no one comforts them!<l eID="gen13993" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen13994"/>Those who oppress them are powerful—<l eID="gen13994" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen13995"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>no one can comfort them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!<note placement="foot">Literally “And look! The tears of the oppressed, and there is no comforting for them, and from the hand of oppressors of them was power, and there is no comforting for them”</note> <l eID="gen13995" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7124"/><l level="1" sID="gen13996"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7124"/>So I deemed the dead who have already died<l eID="gen13996" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen13997"/>more <transChange type="added">fortunate</transChange> than the living who are still alive. <l eID="gen13997" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7125"/><l level="1" sID="gen13998"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7125"/>But better <transChange type="added">off</transChange> than both of them is the one who has not yet been born<l eID="gen13998" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen13999"/>and has not seen the evil deeds that are done under the sun. <l eID="gen13999" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen13991"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7126"/><title type="x-s">People Need Balance in Their Approach to Labor</title> <div sID="gen14000" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7126"/>I also realized that all <transChange type="added">of the</transChange> toil and all <transChange type="added">of</transChange> the skillful work that is done—it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> envy between one man and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞another⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “his friend”</note> This also <transChange type="added">is</transChange> vanity and chasing wind!  <div eID="gen14000" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7127"/><lg sID="gen14001"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14002"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7127"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞The fool refuses to work with his hands, <milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><l eID="gen14002" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14003"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>so he has nothing to eat except his own skin⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!<note placement="foot">Literally “The fool folds his hands and eats his flesh”</note> <l eID="gen14003" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7128"/><l level="1" sID="gen14004"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7128"/>Better <transChange type="added">is</transChange> one handful with peace<l eID="gen14004" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14005"/>than two fists full with toil and chasing wind. <l eID="gen14005" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen14001"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7129"/><title type="x-s">Wealth without Someone with Which to Enjoy It is Futile</title> <div sID="gen14006" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7129"/>I turned again and saw another vanity under the sun.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:8
verses.text: Sometimes a man is all alone with no companion; he also has neither son nor brother. Yet there is no end to all his toil, and his eye is not satisfied with wealth. <transChange type="added">He laments,</transChange> “For whom am I toiling and depriving <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞myself⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “his soul”</note> of pleasure?” This also <transChange type="added">is</transChange> vanity—it is an unhappy business!  <div eID="gen14006" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7130"/><title type="x-s">Friends and Family Can Help One Another in Life</title> <div sID="gen14007" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7130"/>Two <transChange type="added">are</transChange> better than the one, for they enjoy a better reward for their toil.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:10
verses.text: For if one falls, his companion may help him up. But pity the one who falls and there is <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞no one⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “there is not a second”</note> to help him up.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:11
verses.text: Also if two lie together, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they can keep each other warm⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “and it will be warm for them”</note> But how can one person be warm?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:12
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Although an assailant may overpower one person, two may withstand him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “And even though he will prevail against him, the one; the second, they will withstand opposite him”</note> A threefold cord <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞is not easily broken⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!<note placement="foot">Literally “will not be broken in haste”</note>  <div eID="gen14007" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7131"/><title type="x-s">One Must Be Willing to Listen to Counsel</title> <div sID="gen14008" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7131"/>A poor but wise youth <transChange type="added">is</transChange> better than an old but foolish king who no longer knows <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞how to receive advice⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “how to be warned”</note>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:14
verses.text: For he came out of the prison house to reign, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞since he was born poor in his kingdom⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “for all in his kingdom he was born poor”</note>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:15
verses.text: I saw all the living who move about under the sun with the youth; the second who will stand in his place.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:16
verses.text: There is no end to all the people, to all who were before him. Yet the later generation will not rejoice in him, for this also <transChange type="added">is</transChange> vanity and chasing wind!  <chapter eID="Eccl.4"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7132"/><title type="x-s">Listen to God Rather Than Uttering Rash Vows</title> <div sID="gen14009" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen14009" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen14010"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14011"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7132"/><note placement="foot"><reference osisRef="Eccl.5.1-Eccl.5.20">Ecclesiastes 5:1–20 </reference>in the English Bible is 4:17–5:19 in the Hebrew Bible</note> Guard your steps when you go to the house of God;<l eID="gen14011" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14012"/>draw near to listen <transChange type="added">rather</transChange> than to offer a sacrifice of fools,<l eID="gen14012" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen14013"/>for they do not know that they are doing evil. <l eID="gen14013" level="3"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7133"/><l level="1" sID="gen14014"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7133"/>Do not be rash with your mouth,<l eID="gen14014" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14015"/>and do not let your heart be quick to utter a word before God.<l eID="gen14015" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14016"/>For God is in heaven, and you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> on earth;<l eID="gen14016" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14017"/>therefore, let your words be few. <l eID="gen14017" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7134"/><l level="1" sID="gen14018"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7134"/>For a dream comes with many cares,<l eID="gen14018" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14019"/>and the voice of a fool with many words. <l eID="gen14019" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7135"/><l level="1" sID="gen14020"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7135"/>When you make a vow to God,<l eID="gen14020" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14021"/>do not delay in fulfilling it,<l eID="gen14021" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14022"/>for <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he takes no pleasure⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “there is no desire”</note> in fools.<l eID="gen14022" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14023"/>Fulfill what you vow! <l eID="gen14023" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7136"/><l level="1" sID="gen14024"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7136"/>It is better that you not vow<l eID="gen14024" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14025"/>than that you vow and not fulfill it. <l eID="gen14025" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7137"/><l level="1" sID="gen14026"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7137"/>Do not let your mouth lead your flesh into sin,<l eID="gen14026" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14027"/>and do not tell the messenger that it <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a mistake.<l eID="gen14027" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14028"/>Why anger God at your words,<l eID="gen14028" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14029"/>so that he destroys the work of your hands? <l eID="gen14029" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7138"/><l level="1" sID="gen14030"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7138"/>For with many dreams <transChange type="added">come</transChange> vanities and numerous words.<l eID="gen14030" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14031"/>Therefore, fear God!<l eID="gen14031" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen14010"/> <title type="x-s">Powerful Bureaucrats Exploit the Helpless Poor</title> <div sID="gen14032" type="x-p"/>  <div eID="gen14032" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7139"/><lg sID="gen14033"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14034"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7139"/>Do not be surprised if you see the poor being oppressed with violence<l eID="gen14034" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14035"/>or <transChange type="added">do not see</transChange> justice and righteousness in the province.<l eID="gen14035" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14036"/>For one official is watched by a higher official,<l eID="gen14036" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14037"/>and <transChange type="added">there are</transChange> even higher officials over them! <l eID="gen14037" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7140"/><l level="1" sID="gen14038"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7140"/>The produce of the land is exploited by everyone;<l eID="gen14038" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14039"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞even the king profits from the field <transChange type="added">of the poor</transChange>⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!<note placement="foot">Literally “for the field is even worked for the king”</note><l eID="gen14039" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen14033"/> <title type="x-s">There is Never Enough Money to Satisfy</title> <div sID="gen14040" type="x-p"/>  <div eID="gen14040" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7141"/><lg sID="gen14041"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14042"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7141"/>Whoever loves money is not satisfied <transChange type="added">with</transChange> money,<l eID="gen14042" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14043"/>and whoever loves wealth <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not <transChange type="added">satisfied with</transChange> profit.<l eID="gen14043" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14044"/>This also <transChange type="added">is</transChange> vanity! <l eID="gen14044" level="1"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7142"/><l level="1" sID="gen14045"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7142"/>When prosperity increases,<l eID="gen14045" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14046"/>those who consume it increase.<l eID="gen14046" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14047"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞So its owner gains nothing, <milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><l eID="gen14047" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14048"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>except to see his wealth before it is spent⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “And what gain has its owner but to see it with his eyes?”</note> <l eID="gen14048" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7143"/><l level="1" sID="gen14049"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7143"/>The sleep of the laborer <transChange type="added">is</transChange> pleasant, whether he eats little or much,<l eID="gen14049" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14050"/>but the wealth of the rich man does not allow him to rest. <l eID="gen14050" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen14041"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7144"/><title type="x-s">Hoarding Wealth Can Backfire</title> <div sID="gen14051" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7144"/>There is a grievous evil which I have seen under the sun: wealth <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞hoarded⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “kept ”</note> by its owner to his harm.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:14
verses.text: That wealth was lost in a bad venture. Although he has borne a child, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he has nothing to leave to him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “he has nothing in his hand”</note>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:15
verses.text: Just as he came from his mother’s womb naked, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he will depart⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “return to go”</note> just as he came; he will take nothing with him for his toil.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:16
verses.text: This also <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a grievous illness. Exactly as he came, so he will go. What profit <transChange type="added">does</transChange> he gain for all his toil for the wind?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:17
verses.text: Also, he eats in darkness all his days; he is frustrated <transChange type="added">in</transChange> much sickness and resentment.  <div eID="gen14051" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7145"/><title type="x-s">If You Have Wealth, Enjoy It as God Enables</title> <div sID="gen14052" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7145"/>Look! I have discovered what is good and fitting: to eat and to drink and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to enjoy⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to see goodness”</note> all the fruit of the toil with which one toils under the sun during the number of the days of his life that God gives to him—for this is his lot.<note placement="foot">Or “fate”</note>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:19
verses.text: This indeed is a gift of God: everyone to whom God gives wealth and possessions, he also empowers him <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to enjoy them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to eat from it”</note> to accept his lot, and to rejoice in <transChange type="added">the fruit of</transChange> his toil.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:20
verses.text: For he does not remember the <transChange type="added">brief</transChange> days of his life, for God keeps his heart preoccupied with enjoyment <transChange type="added">of life</transChange>.  <chapter eID="Eccl.5"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 6:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7146"/><title type="x-s">Those Who Have Wealth but Do Not Enjoy It Are Pitiful</title> <div sID="gen14053" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7146"/>Here is another misfortune that I have seen under the sun, and it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> prevalent among humankind.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 6:2
verses.text: God gives a man wealth, possessions, and honor, so that he lacks nothing his heart desires; yet God does not enable him to enjoy it—instead someone else ends up enjoying it. This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> vanity—indeed, it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a grievous ill!  <div eID="gen14053" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 6:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7147"/><div sID="gen14054" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7147"/>Even if a man fathers a hundred <transChange type="added">children</transChange> and lives many years so that the days of his years are many, if his heart<note placement="foot">Or “his soul”</note> is not satisfied with <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his prosperity⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the good”</note> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he does not receive a proper burial⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “and also there is no burial for him”</note> I deem the stillborn better than him.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 6:4
verses.text: For he comes into vanity and departs into darkness, and his name is shrouded in darkness.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 6:5
verses.text: He has neither seen nor known the sun, yet he has more rest than him.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 6:6
verses.text: Even if a man<note placement="foot">Hebrew “he”</note> lives a thousand years twice, if he<note placement="foot">Hebrew “and”</note> does not enjoy <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞prosperity⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “good”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞both suffer the same fate⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!<note placement="foot">Literally “are not the all going to the same place?”</note> <div eID="gen14054" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">One Must Learn to Be Content with What One Has</title> <div sID="gen14055" type="x-p"/>  <div eID="gen14055" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 6:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7148"/><lg sID="gen14056"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14057"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7148"/>All of a man’s toil <transChange type="added">is</transChange> for his mouth—<l eID="gen14057" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14058"/>yet his appetite is never satisfied. <l eID="gen14058" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 6:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7149"/><l level="1" sID="gen14059"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7149"/>So do the wise <transChange type="added">really</transChange> have an advantage over fools?<l eID="gen14059" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14060"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Can the poor <transChange type="added">really</transChange> gain anything by knowing how to act in front of others⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?<note placement="foot">Literally “What is there for the poor knowing how to conduct themselves before the living?”</note> <l eID="gen14060" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 6:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7150"/><l level="1" sID="gen14061"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7150"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Better to be content with what your eyes see <milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><l eID="gen14061" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14062"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>than for your soul to constantly crave more⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “Sight of the eyes is better than wandering of desire”</note><l eID="gen14062" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14063"/>This also <transChange type="added">is</transChange> vanity and chasing wind!<l eID="gen14063" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen14056"/> <title type="x-s">It is Futile for Humans to Complain about God’s Irresistible Will</title> <div sID="gen14064" type="x-p"/>  <div eID="gen14064" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 6:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7151"/><lg sID="gen14065"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14066"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7151"/>Whatever is—it was already determined,<l eID="gen14066" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14067"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞what will be—it has already been decided⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “and his name is known what he is man”</note><l eID="gen14067" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14068"/>As for man, he cannot argue<l eID="gen14068" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14069"/>against what is more powerful than him. <l eID="gen14069" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 6:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7152"/><l level="1" sID="gen14070"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7152"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Increasing words only multiplies futility⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “Where there are numerous words, it makes numerous vanity”</note><l eID="gen14070" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14071"/>how does that profit anyone? <l eID="gen14071" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen14065"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 6:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7153"/><title type="x-s">The Future is Inscrutable to Humans</title> <div sID="gen14072" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7153"/>For who knows what <transChange type="added">is</transChange> good for a man in his life during the few days of his fleeting life, which are fleeting as a shadow? For who can tell anyone what will happen <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in the future⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “after him”</note> under the sun?  <chapter eID="Eccl.6"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7154"/><title type="x-s">People Generally Do Not Know What is Best for Them</title> <div sID="gen14073" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen14073" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen14074"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14075"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7154"/>A good name <transChange type="added">is</transChange> better than precious ointment,<l eID="gen14075" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14076"/>and the day of death <transChange type="added">is better</transChange> than the day of one’s birth. <l eID="gen14076" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7155"/><l level="1" sID="gen14077"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7155"/>Better to go to the house of mourning<l eID="gen14077" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14078"/>than to go to the house of feasting,<l eID="gen14078" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14079"/>for <transChange type="added">death is</transChange> the end of every person,<l eID="gen14079" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14080"/>and the living should take <transChange type="added">it</transChange> to his heart. <l eID="gen14080" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7156"/><l level="1" sID="gen14081"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7156"/>Sorrow <transChange type="added">is</transChange> better than laughter,<l eID="gen14081" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14082"/>for by sadness of countenance the heart is made good. <l eID="gen14082" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7157"/><l level="1" sID="gen14083"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7157"/>The heart of the wise <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in the house of mourning,<l eID="gen14083" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14084"/>but the heart of fools <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in the house of mirth. <l eID="gen14084" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7158"/><l level="1" sID="gen14085"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7158"/>Better to listen to <transChange type="added">the</transChange> rebuke of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> wise<l eID="gen14085" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14086"/>than for a man to listen to <transChange type="added">the</transChange> song of fools. <l eID="gen14086" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7159"/><l level="1" sID="gen14087"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7159"/>Like the sound of thorns under a pot,<l eID="gen14087" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14088"/>so also the laughter of fools.<l eID="gen14088" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14089"/>This also <transChange type="added">is</transChange> vanity!<l eID="gen14089" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen14074"/> <title type="x-s">Wisdom—Although Vulnerable—is Beneficial</title> <div sID="gen14090" type="x-p"/>  <div eID="gen14090" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7160"/><lg sID="gen14091"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14092"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7160"/>Surely oppression makes a fool of the wise,<l eID="gen14092" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14093"/>and a bribe corrupts the heart. <l eID="gen14093" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7161"/><l level="1" sID="gen14094"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7161"/>The end of a matter <transChange type="added">is</transChange> better than its beginning;<l eID="gen14094" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14095"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞better to be slow to anger than hot-headed⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “one who is long of spirit is better than one who is high of spirit”</note> <l eID="gen14095" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7162"/><l level="1" sID="gen14096"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7162"/>Do not be quick in your spirit to anger,<l eID="gen14096" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14097"/>for anger lodges in the bosom of fools. <l eID="gen14097" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7163"/><l level="1" sID="gen14098"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7163"/>Do not say, “Why were the former days better than these?”<l eID="gen14098" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14099"/>For <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> not from wisdom <transChange type="added">that</transChange> you ask this. <l eID="gen14099" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7164"/><l level="1" sID="gen14100"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7164"/>Wisdom <transChange type="added">is</transChange> good with an inheritance;<l eID="gen14100" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14101"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞it benefits the living⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “to those who see the sun”</note> <l eID="gen14101" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7165"/><l level="1" sID="gen14102"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7165"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞For wisdom offers protection like money offers protection⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “For in the shade of wisdom is the shade of money”</note><l eID="gen14102" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14103"/>But knowledge <transChange type="added">has</transChange> an advantage—wisdom restores life to its possessor.<l eID="gen14103" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen14091"/> <title type="x-s">Humans Must Accept God’s Will and Make the Best of It</title> <div sID="gen14104" type="x-p"/>  <div eID="gen14104" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7166"/><lg sID="gen14105"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14106"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7166"/>Consider the work of God.<l eID="gen14106" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14107"/>For who is able to make straight what he made crooked? <l eID="gen14107" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7167"/><l level="1" sID="gen14108"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7167"/>In the day of prosperity, rejoice!<l eID="gen14108" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14109"/>But in the day of adversity, consider!<l eID="gen14109" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14110"/>For God made one in place of another<l eID="gen14110" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14111"/>so that mortals cannot find out what will happen <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in the future⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “after him”</note><l eID="gen14111" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen14105"/> <title type="x-s">The Law of Retribution Does Not Always Work—but It Does Sometimes</title> <div sID="gen14112" type="x-p"/>  <div eID="gen14112" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7168"/><lg sID="gen14113"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14114"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7168"/>I have seen all these things in my vain life:<l eID="gen14114" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14115"/>Sometimes a righteous man perishes in <transChange type="added">spite of</transChange> his righteousness,<l eID="gen14115" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen14116"/>and sometimes a wicked man lives a long life in <transChange type="added">spite of</transChange> his evil. <l eID="gen14116" level="3"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7169"/><l level="1" sID="gen14117"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7169"/>Do not be excessively<note placement="foot">Or “abundantly”</note> righteous,<l eID="gen14117" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14118"/>and do not act excessively wise, lest you destroy yourself. <l eID="gen14118" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7170"/><l level="1" sID="gen14119"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7170"/>Do not act excessively wicked,<l eID="gen14119" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14120"/>and do not be a fool, lest you die before your time. <l eID="gen14120" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7171"/><l level="1" sID="gen14121"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7171"/><transChange type="added">It is</transChange> good to take hold of the one and also must not let go of the other;<l eID="gen14121" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14122"/>for whoever fears God will hold both of them secure.<l eID="gen14122" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen14113"/> <title type="x-s">Wisdom is Valuable, but No One is Completely Righteous</title> <div sID="gen14123" type="x-p"/>  <div eID="gen14123" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7172"/><lg sID="gen14124"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14125"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7172"/>Wisdom gives more strength to the wise<l eID="gen14125" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14126"/>than ten rulers who are in the city. <l eID="gen14126" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7173"/><l level="1" sID="gen14127"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7173"/>Surely there is no one righteous on the earth<l eID="gen14127" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14128"/>who <transChange type="added">continually</transChange> does good and never sins. <l eID="gen14128" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7174"/><l level="1" sID="gen14129"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7174"/>Do not pay attention to everything people say,<l eID="gen14129" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14130"/>lest you hear your own servant curse you. <l eID="gen14130" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7175"/><l level="1" sID="gen14131"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7175"/>For your heart knows<l eID="gen14131" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14132"/>that you also have cursed others many times. <l eID="gen14132" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen14124"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7176"/><title type="x-s">Absolute Wisdom is Unattainable</title> <div sID="gen14133" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7176"/>All this I have tested with wisdom. I said, “I will be wise!” but <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞it was beyond my grasp⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “it was far from me”</note>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:24
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Whatever is—it is far beyond comprehension⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “That which is—it is far and deep deep”</note> Who can discover it?  <div eID="gen14133" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7177"/><div sID="gen14134" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7177"/>I set my mind to try to seek wisdom and the plan, and to know that wickedness <transChange type="added">is</transChange> foolishness and that folly <transChange type="added">is</transChange> delusion.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:26
verses.text: I myself found <transChange type="added">that</transChange> more bitter than death <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the woman who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a trap, whose heart <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a snare, and whose hands <transChange type="added">are</transChange> bonds. The one who pleases God escapes from her, but the sinner is caught by her.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:27
verses.text: “Look! I found this,” said the Teacher,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Qohelet”</note> “while trying to find how the plan fits together.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:28
verses.text: What my heart sought, I did not find. Although I found one righteous man among one thousand, I did not find one <transChange type="added">upright</transChange> woman among all these.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:29
verses.text: Look! This alone I found: God made mankind upright, but they have devised many schemes.”  <chapter eID="Eccl.7"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7178"/><title type="x-s">Wisdom is Valuable</title> <div sID="gen14135" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen14135" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen14136"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14137"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7178"/>Who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> like the sage?<l eID="gen14137" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14138"/>Who knows <transChange type="added">the</transChange> interpretation of a thing?<l eID="gen14138" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14139"/>A man’s wisdom makes his face shine,<l eID="gen14139" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14140"/>and the hardness of his face is changed. <l eID="gen14140" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7179"/><l level="1" sID="gen14141"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7179"/>Keep <transChange type="added">the</transChange> command of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> king<note placement="foot">While MT reads “I said, ‘Keep the mouth of the king,’ ” the versions read “Keep the mouth of the king,” which is adopted in the translation</note><l eID="gen14141" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14142"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞because of your oath to God⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “because of the oath of God”</note> <l eID="gen14142" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7180"/><l level="1" sID="gen14143"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7180"/>Do not be terrified of his presence!<l eID="gen14143" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14144"/>Go at once and do not delay when a matter <transChange type="added">is</transChange> unpleasant,<l eID="gen14144" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14145"/>for he can do anything that he desires. <l eID="gen14145" level="1"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7181"/><l level="1" sID="gen14146"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7181"/>Since the word of the king <transChange type="added">is</transChange> supreme,<l eID="gen14146" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14147"/>no one can say to him, “What are you doing?” <l eID="gen14147" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7182"/><l level="1" sID="gen14148"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7182"/>Whoever obeys <transChange type="added">his</transChange> command will not suffer disaster.<l eID="gen14148" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14149"/>The wise mind knows the <transChange type="added">proper</transChange> time and the right <transChange type="added">procedure</transChange>. <l eID="gen14149" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7183"/><l level="1" sID="gen14150"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7183"/>For there is a <transChange type="added">proper</transChange> time and right <transChange type="added">procedure</transChange> for every matter,<l eID="gen14150" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14151"/>even though the trouble of man <transChange type="added">weighs</transChange> heavy upon him.<l eID="gen14151" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen14136"/> <title type="x-s">No One Knows the Future</title> <div sID="gen14152" type="x-p"/>  <div eID="gen14152" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7184"/><lg sID="gen14153"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14154"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7184"/>Surely no one knows what will be,<l eID="gen14154" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14155"/>so who can tell anyone what will happen? <l eID="gen14155" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7185"/><l level="1" sID="gen14156"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7185"/>Just as no one can control the wind to restrain the wind,<l eID="gen14156" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14157"/>so also no one can control the day of his death.<l eID="gen14157" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14158"/>Just as no one is discharged in time of war,<l eID="gen14158" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14159"/>so wickedness will not deliver the wicked. <l eID="gen14159" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen14153"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7186"/><title type="x-s">The World Marred by Oppression and Injustice</title> <div sID="gen14160" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7186"/>I saw all this as I applied my heart to all the deeds done under the sun: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞sometimes those in authority harm others⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sometimes one man domineers another man to his harm”</note>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:10
verses.text: Meanwhile, I saw the wicked being <transChange type="added">honorably</transChange> buried, but those who came and went from the holy place were forgotten in the city, even though they had done so. This also <transChange type="added">is</transChange> vanity!  <div eID="gen14160" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7187"/><title type="x-s">Although Evil is Not Punished Swiftly, God Does Eventually Punish Sinners</title> <div sID="gen14161" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7187"/>Because sentence against an evil deed is not carried out quickly, the heart of <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞humans⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the sons of the man”</note> fills up within them to do evil.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:12
verses.text: Although the sinner does evil a hundred times and prolongs his life, yet I also know that it will be good for those who fear God—because they fear <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his presence⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “from before his face”</note>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:13
verses.text: But it will not go well with the wicked, and they will not prolong <transChange type="added">their</transChange> days, like the shadow; because there is no fearing <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞God’s presence⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “from before the face of God”</note>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:14
verses.text: There <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a vanity that happens on earth: sometimes the righteous suffer what the wicked deserve, and sometimes the wicked receive what the righteous deserve. I said, “This also <transChange type="added">is</transChange> vanity!”  <div eID="gen14161" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7188"/><title type="x-s">Humans Should Enjoy the Life That God Gives to Them</title> <div sID="gen14162" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7188"/>So I recommend enjoyment. For there <transChange type="added">is</transChange> nothing better for man under the sun than to eat and to drink and to rejoice. This will accompany him in his toil the days of his life that God gives to him under the sun.  <div eID="gen14162" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7189"/><title type="x-s">No One Can Discover the Rhyme and Reason for Things</title> <div sID="gen14163" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7189"/>I applied my mind to know wisdom and to understand the business that is done on earth—how neither day nor night one’s eyes see sleep.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:17
verses.text: Then I saw all the work of God—man <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not able to discover the work that is done under the sun. Although man may toil in seeking, he cannot find it. Even if a wise man claims <transChange type="added">that he</transChange> knows it, he cannot find it.  <chapter eID="Eccl.8"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7190"/><title type="x-s">The Same Fate—Death—Awaits Everyone</title> <div sID="gen14164" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7190"/>So all this I laid to my heart, and I concluded<note placement="foot">Or “examined”</note> that the righteous and the wise, as well as their deeds, <transChange type="added">are</transChange> in the hand of God. So no one knows anything that will <transChange type="added">come</transChange> to them, whether <transChange type="added">it will be</transChange> love or hatred.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:2
verses.text: The same fate <transChange type="added">comes</transChange> to everyone: <div eID="gen14164" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen14165"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14166"/>to the righteous and to the wicked,<l eID="gen14166" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14167"/>to the good and to the wicked,<note placement="foot">Several versions (Greek, Syriac, Latin) insert “and to the bad”</note><l eID="gen14167" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14168"/>to the clean and to the unclean,<l eID="gen14168" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14169"/>to those who sacrifice and to those who do not sacrifice.<l eID="gen14169" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14170"/>As <transChange type="added">with</transChange> the good <transChange type="added">man</transChange>, so also to the sinner;<l eID="gen14170" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14171"/><transChange type="added">as with</transChange> those who swear an oath, so <transChange type="added">also</transChange> those who fear oaths. <l eID="gen14171" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7191"/><l level="1" sID="gen14172"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7191"/>This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞injustice⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “evil”</note> that is done under the sun:<l eID="gen14172" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14173"/>the same fate <transChange type="added">comes</transChange> to everyone.<l eID="gen14173" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14174"/>Also the hearts of <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞humans⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the sons of the man”</note> are full <transChange type="added">of</transChange> evil;<l eID="gen14174" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14175"/>delusion <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in their hearts during their lives, and then they die. <l eID="gen14175" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen14165"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7192"/><title type="x-s">Death Deprives Humans of Everything in Life</title> <div sID="gen14176" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7192"/>Whoever is joined<note placement="foot">The <hi type="italic">Kethib</hi> reads “chosen,” but the <hi type="italic">Qere</hi> as well as all the versions and numerous medieval Hebrew manuscripts read “joined”</note> to all the living has hope. After all, even a live dog is better than a dead lion!

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:5
verses.text: For the living know that they will die, but the dead do not know anything. They no longer have a reward, and even the memory of them is forgotten.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:6
verses.text: What they loved and hated, as well as what they desired, has already perished. They no longer have any share in what is done under the sun.  <div eID="gen14176" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7193"/><title type="x-s">Enjoy Life While It Lasts</title> <div sID="gen14177" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7193"/>Go—eat your food with joy, and drink your wine with a merry heart! For God already has approved your deeds.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:8
verses.text: Always be clothed in white garments, and never let your head lack oil!

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:9
verses.text: Enjoy life with the wife whom you love all the days of your vain life which he gives you under the sun, because this <transChange type="added">is</transChange> your lot in life and in the toil with which you toil under the sun.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:10
verses.text: Whatever your hand finds to do—do <transChange type="added">it</transChange> with <transChange type="added">all</transChange> your might; for in Sheol—where you are going—no one works, plans, knows, or thinks about anything.  <div eID="gen14177" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7194"/><title type="x-s">The Injustice of Time and Chance</title> <div sID="gen14178" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7194"/>I looked again and saw under the sun that the race <transChange type="added">does</transChange> not <transChange type="added">belong</transChange> to the swift, the battle <transChange type="added">does</transChange> not <transChange type="added">belong</transChange> to the mighty, food <transChange type="added">does</transChange> not <transChange type="added">belong</transChange> to the wise, wealth <transChange type="added">does</transChange> not <transChange type="added">belong</transChange> to the intelligent, and success<note placement="foot">Or “favor”</note> <transChange type="added">does</transChange> not <transChange type="added">belong</transChange> to the skillful, for time and chance befalls all of them.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:12
verses.text: For man does not know his time. Just as fish are caught in a cruel net and like birds who are seized in a snare, so also <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞humans⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the sons of the man”</note> are ensnared at a cruel time when it falls suddenly upon them.  <div eID="gen14178" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7195"/><title type="x-s">Wisdom—Although Vulnerable—is Superior to Power</title> <div sID="gen14179" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7195"/>I have also seen this <transChange type="added">example of</transChange> wisdom under the sun, and it <transChange type="added">seemed</transChange> great to me.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:14
verses.text: <transChange type="added">There was</transChange> a small city with few people in it. A great king came and besieged it, building great siege works against it.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:15
verses.text: Now, a poor wise man was found in it, and he delivered the city by his wisdom.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:16
