verses.text: So I concluded that wisdom <transChange type="added">is</transChange> better than might, yet the wisdom of the poor is despised, and his words are not heard. <div eID="gen14179" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">Wisdom—Although Vulnerable—is Superior to Folly</title> <div sID="gen14180" type="x-p"/>  <div eID="gen14180" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7196"/><lg sID="gen14181"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14182"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7196"/>The words of the wise are heard in peace<l eID="gen14182" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14183"/><transChange type="added">more</transChange> than the shouting of a ruler <transChange type="added">is heard</transChange> among the fools. <l eID="gen14183" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7197"/><l level="1" sID="gen14184"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7197"/>Wisdom <transChange type="added">is</transChange> better than weapons of war,<l eID="gen14184" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14185"/>but one sinner destroys much good. <l eID="gen14185" level="2"/><lg eID="gen14181"/> <chapter eID="Eccl.9"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:1
verses.text: Dead flies cause a bad smell <transChange type="added">and</transChange> ruin<note placement="foot">Or “spew”</note> the ointment of the perfumer.<l eID="gen14188" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14189"/>So also a little folly outweighs wisdom and honor. <l eID="gen14189" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7198"/><l level="1" sID="gen14190"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7198"/>The heart of the wise <transChange type="added">inclines</transChange> to his right,<l eID="gen14190" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14191"/>but the heart of the fool <transChange type="added">inclines</transChange> to his left. <l eID="gen14191" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7199"/><l level="1" sID="gen14192"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7199"/>Even when the fool walks along the road, he lacks sense;<l eID="gen14192" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14193"/>he tells everyone <transChange type="added">that</transChange> he is a fool. <l eID="gen14193" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7200"/><l level="1" sID="gen14194"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7200"/>If the anger of the ruler rises against you,<l eID="gen14194" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14195"/>do not leave your post,<l eID="gen14195" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14196"/>for calmness can undo great offenses. <l eID="gen14196" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7201"/><l level="1" sID="gen14197"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7201"/>There is an evil I have seen under the sun—<l eID="gen14197" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14198"/><transChange type="added">it is</transChange> an error that proceeds from a ruler! <l eID="gen14198" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7202"/><l level="1" sID="gen14199"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7202"/>The fool is set in many high places,<l eID="gen14199" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14200"/>but the rich sit in lowly places. <l eID="gen14200" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7203"/><l level="1" sID="gen14201"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7203"/>I have even seen slaves <transChange type="added">riding</transChange> on horses<l eID="gen14201" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14202"/>and princes walking like slaves on the earth!<l eID="gen14202" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen14187"/> <title type="x-s">Accidents Happen—Even to Professionals</title> <div sID="gen14203" type="x-p"/>  <div eID="gen14203" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7204"/><lg sID="gen14204"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14205"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7204"/>Whoever digs a pit will fall into it.<l eID="gen14205" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14206"/>Whoever breaks through a wall, a snake will bite him. <l eID="gen14206" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7205"/><l level="1" sID="gen14207"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7205"/>Whoever <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞quarries⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “breaks out”</note> stones will be wounded by them.<l eID="gen14207" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14208"/>Whoever splits logs will be endangered by them.<l eID="gen14208" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen14204"/> <title type="x-s">Hard Work and Skill Alone Cannot Succeed—Wisdom is Necessary</title> <div sID="gen14209" type="x-p"/>  <div eID="gen14209" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7206"/><lg sID="gen14210"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14211"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7206"/>If the ax is blunt but one does not sharpen its edge,<l eID="gen14211" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14212"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he must exert more effort⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “he must be more strength”</note><l eID="gen14212" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14213"/>but the advantage of wisdom <transChange type="added">is</transChange> it brings success. <l eID="gen14213" level="1"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7207"/><l level="1" sID="gen14214"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7207"/>If the snake bites before the charming,<l eID="gen14214" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14215"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the snake charmer will not succeed⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “there is no advantage to the owner of the charm”</note><l eID="gen14215" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen14210"/> <title type="x-s">The Consequences of Foolishness</title> <div sID="gen14216" type="x-p"/>  <div eID="gen14216" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7208"/><lg sID="gen14217"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14218"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7208"/>The wise man <transChange type="added">wins</transChange> favor by the words of his mouth,<l eID="gen14218" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14219"/>but the fool is devoured by his own lips. <l eID="gen14219" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7209"/><l level="1" sID="gen14220"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7209"/>He begins by saying what is foolish<l eID="gen14220" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14221"/>and ends by uttering what is wicked delusion. <l eID="gen14221" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7210"/><l level="1" sID="gen14222"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7210"/>The fool <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞talks too much⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “increases words”</note><l eID="gen14222" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14223"/>for no one knows what will be.<l eID="gen14223" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen14224"/>Who can tell anyone what will happen <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in the future⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?<note placement="foot">Literally “after him”</note> <l eID="gen14224" level="3"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7211"/><l level="1" sID="gen14225"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7211"/>The fool is so worn out by a hard day’s work<l eID="gen14225" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14226"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he cannot even find his way home at night⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Or “for he knows not to go to a city”</note> <l eID="gen14226" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7212"/><l level="1" sID="gen14227"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7212"/>Woe to you, O land, when your king is a youth<l eID="gen14227" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14228"/>and your princes feast in the morning. <l eID="gen14228" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7213"/><l level="1" sID="gen14229"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7213"/>Blessed are you, O land, when your king is a son of nobility<l eID="gen14229" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14230"/>and your princes feast at the proper time—<l eID="gen14230" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen14231"/>to gain strength and not to get drunk. <l eID="gen14231" level="3"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7214"/><l level="1" sID="gen14232"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7214"/>Through sloth the roof sinks in,<l eID="gen14232" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14233"/>and through idleness of hands the house leaks. <l eID="gen14233" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7215"/><l level="1" sID="gen14234"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7215"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Feasts are held for celebration⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “They make bread for laughter”</note><l eID="gen14234" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14235"/>wine cheers the living,<l eID="gen14235" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen14236"/>and money answers everything. <l eID="gen14236" level="3"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7216"/><l level="1" sID="gen14237"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7216"/>Do not curse the king even in your thoughts,<l eID="gen14237" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14238"/>and do not curse the rich even in your own bedroom,<l eID="gen14238" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14239"/>for a bird of the sky may carry your voice;<l eID="gen14239" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14240"/>a winged messenger may repeat your words. <l eID="gen14240" level="2"/><lg eID="gen14217"/> <chapter eID="Eccl.10"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 11:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7217"/><title type="x-s">Living in the Light of the Limits of Human Knowledge</title> <div sID="gen14241" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen14241" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen14242"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14243"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7217"/>Send out your bread on the water,<l eID="gen14243" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14244"/>for in many days you will find it. <l eID="gen14244" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 11:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7218"/><l level="1" sID="gen14245"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7218"/>Divide your share in seven or in eight,<l eID="gen14245" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14246"/>for you do not know what disaster will happen on the earth. <l eID="gen14246" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 11:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7219"/><l level="1" sID="gen14247"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7219"/>When the clouds are full,<l eID="gen14247" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14248"/>they empty rain on the earth.<l eID="gen14248" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14249"/>Whether a tree falls to the south or whether it falls to the north,<l eID="gen14249" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14250"/>the place where the tree falls—there it will be. <l eID="gen14250" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 11:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7220"/><l level="1" sID="gen14251"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7220"/>Whoever watches the wind will not sow;<l eID="gen14251" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14252"/>whoever watches the clouds will not reap. <l eID="gen14252" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 11:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7221"/><l level="1" sID="gen14253"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7221"/>Just as you do not know how the path of the wind<note placement="foot">Or “the breath”</note> <transChange type="added">goes</transChange>,<l eID="gen14253" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14254"/>nor how the bones <transChange type="added">of a fetus</transChange> form in a mother’s womb,<l eID="gen14254" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14255"/>so you do not know the work of God who makes everything. <l eID="gen14255" level="1"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 11:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7222"/><l level="1" sID="gen14256"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7222"/>Sow your seed in the morning,<l eID="gen14256" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14257"/>and do not let your hands rest in the evening,<l eID="gen14257" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14258"/>for you do not know what will prosper—<l eID="gen14258" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14259"/>whether this or that, or whether both of them alike will succeed.<l eID="gen14259" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen14242"/> <title type="x-s">Enjoy Life to the Fullest within the Auspices of the Fear of God</title> <div sID="gen14260" type="x-p"/>  <div eID="gen14260" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 11:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7223"/><lg sID="gen14261"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14262"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7223"/>The light is sweet,<l eID="gen14262" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14263"/>and it <transChange type="added">is</transChange> pleasant for the eyes to see the sun. <l eID="gen14263" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 11:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7224"/><l level="1" sID="gen14264"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7224"/>For if a man lives many years,<l eID="gen14264" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14265"/>let him rejoice in all of them!<l eID="gen14265" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14266"/>Let him remember that the days of the darkness will be many—<l eID="gen14266" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14267"/>all that is coming <transChange type="added">is</transChange> vanity! <l eID="gen14267" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 11:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7225"/><l level="1" sID="gen14268"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7225"/>Rejoice, O young man, in your youth,<l eID="gen14268" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14269"/>and let your heart cheer you in the days of your youth!<l eID="gen14269" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14270"/>Follow the ways of your heart and the sight of your eyes—<l eID="gen14270" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14271"/>but know that God will bring you into judgment for all these things. <l eID="gen14271" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 11:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7226"/><l level="1" sID="gen14272"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7226"/>Banish anxiety from your heart,<l eID="gen14272" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14273"/>and put away pain from your body,<l eID="gen14273" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14274"/>for youth and vigor <transChange type="added">are</transChange> vanity. <l eID="gen14274" level="1"/><lg eID="gen14261"/> <chapter eID="Eccl.11"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7227"/><title type="x-s">Advice to the Young: Life is Short and Then You Die</title> <div sID="gen14275" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen14275" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen14276"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14277"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7227"/>Remember your Creator in the days of your youth—<l eID="gen14277" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14278"/>before the days of trouble come<l eID="gen14278" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14279"/>and the years draw near when you will say,<l eID="gen14279" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14280"/>“I find no pleasure in them!” <l eID="gen14280" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7228"/><l level="1" sID="gen14281"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7228"/>Before the sun, the light, the moon, and the stars darken<l eID="gen14281" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14282"/>and the clouds return after the rain. <l eID="gen14282" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7229"/><l level="1" sID="gen14283"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7229"/>When the guards of the house tremble,<l eID="gen14283" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14284"/>and the men of strength are bent;<l eID="gen14284" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14285"/>the grinders cease because they are few,<l eID="gen14285" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14286"/>and those looking through the windows see dimly. <l eID="gen14286" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7230"/><l level="1" sID="gen14287"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7230"/>When the doors on the street are shut,<l eID="gen14287" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14288"/>when the sound of the grinding mill is low;<l eID="gen14288" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14289"/>one rises up to the sound of the bird,<l eID="gen14289" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14290"/>and all the daughters of song are brought low. <l eID="gen14290" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7231"/><l level="1" sID="gen14291"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7231"/>They are afraid of heights,<l eID="gen14291" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14292"/>and terrors <transChange type="added">are</transChange> on the road.<l eID="gen14292" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14293"/>The almond tree blossoms,<l eID="gen14293" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14294"/>and the grasshopper draws itself along, and desire fails<l eID="gen14294" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14295"/>because man goes to his eternal home,<l eID="gen14295" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14296"/>and the mourners go about in the streets. <l eID="gen14296" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7232"/><l level="1" sID="gen14297"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7232"/>Before the silver cord is snapped<l eID="gen14297" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14298"/>and the golden bowl is broken;<l eID="gen14298" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14299"/>and the jar at the foundation is broken,<l eID="gen14299" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14300"/>and the wheel at the cistern is broken. <l eID="gen14300" level="2"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7233"/><l level="1" sID="gen14301"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7233"/>And the dust returns to the earth as it was,<l eID="gen14301" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14302"/>and the breath returns to God who gave it.<l eID="gen14302" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen14276"/> <title type="x-s">Motto Restated</title> <div sID="gen14303" type="x-p"/>  <div eID="gen14303" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7234"/><lg sID="gen14304"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14305"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7234"/>“Vanity of vanity!” says the Teacher.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Qohelet”</note><l eID="gen14305" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14306"/>“Everything <transChange type="added">is</transChange> vanity!” <l eID="gen14306" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen14304"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7235"/><title type="x-s">Epilogue</title> <div sID="gen14307" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7235"/>The Teacher<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Qohelet”</note> was full of wisdom, and he taught the people with knowledge. He carefully considered many proverbs and carefully arranged them.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:10
verses.text: The Teacher<note placement="foot">Hebrew “Qohelet”</note> sought to find delightful words,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “words of delight”</note> and he wrote<note placement="foot">The MT reads the term passively, “what is written,” but an alternate textual tradition reads, “and he wrote”</note> what is upright—truthful words.  <div eID="gen14307" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7236"/><div sID="gen14308" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7236"/>The words of the wise <transChange type="added">are</transChange> like cattle goads; the collections of the sages <transChange type="added">are</transChange> like pricks inflicted by one shepherd.<note placement="foot">Or “The owner of collections are given by one shepherd”</note>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:12
verses.text: My son, be careful <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞about anything beyond these things⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “but from more than them”</note> For the writing of books is endless, and too much study <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞is wearisome⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “increases weariness of flesh”</note>  <div eID="gen14308" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7237"/><lg sID="gen14309"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14310"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7237"/>Now that all has been heard, here is the final conclusion:<l eID="gen14310" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14311"/>Fear God and obey his commandments,<l eID="gen14311" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen14312"/>for this <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the whole <transChange type="added">duty</transChange> of man. <l eID="gen14312" level="3"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7238"/><l level="1" sID="gen14313"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7238"/>For God will bring every deed into judgment,<l eID="gen14313" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14314"/>including every secret thing, whether good or evil. <l eID="gen14314" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen14309"/> <chapter eID="Eccl.12"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen13915" osisID="Eccl" type="book"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7239"/><title type="x-s">Title</title> <div sID="gen14316" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen14316" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen14317"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14318"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7239"/>The Song of Songs,<note placement="foot">This construction conveys a superlative connotation, e.g., “The most exquisite song”</note> which is for<note placement="foot">Or “by Solomon” or “about/concerning Solomon”</note> Solomon.<l eID="gen14318" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen14317"/> <title type="x-s">Maiden’s Soliloquy</title> <div sID="gen14319" type="x-p"/>  <div eID="gen14319" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7240"/><lg sID="gen14320"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14321"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7240"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞May<note placement="foot">In the maiden’s soliloquy, she thinks about her beloved in her thoughts (“May he kiss me!”), then poetically speaks to him as if he were in her presence (“for your love is better than wine”). To avoid confusion, the translation uses the second-person form throughout vv. <reference osisRef="Song.1.2-Song.1.4">2–4</reference></note> you kiss me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “May he kiss me”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞passionately with your lips⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “with the kisses of his mouth”</note><l eID="gen14321" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14322"/>for your love <transChange type="added">is</transChange> better than wine.<note placement="foot">The shift from the third person “he … his” to the second person “you … your” in vv. <reference osisRef="Song.1.2-Song.1.4">2–4</reference> should not be interpreted as suggesting two different referents, that is, one male whom the maiden is addressing as “you,” and another to whom she refers as “he.” Rather, this shift is a poetic device (called “grammatical differentiation”) that is not uncommon in Hebrew poetry (e.g., <reference osisRef="Gen.49.4">Gen 49:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="Deut.32.15">Deut 32:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.23.2-Ps.23.5">Psa 23:2–5</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.1.29">Isa 1:29</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.42.20">42:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.54.1">54:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.22.24">Jer 22:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="Amos.4.1">Amos 4:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Mic.7.19">Mic 7:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="Lam.3.1">Lam 3:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Song.4.2">Song 4:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Song.6.6">6:6</reference>). This shift is characteristic of a soliloquy, a dramatic or literary form in which a character reveals her thoughts without addressing a listener who is actually present (e.g., <reference osisRef="2Sam.19.4">2 Sam 19:4</reference>). In this case, the maiden’s private thoughts about her beloved (v. <reference osisRef="Song.1.2a">2a</reference>) shift to an imaginary address to her beloved (vv. <reference osisRef="Song.1.2b-Song.1.4a">2b–4a</reference>)</note> <l eID="gen14322" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7241"/><l level="1" sID="gen14323"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7241"/>As fragrance, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞your perfumes⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “your oil lotions”</note> are <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞delightful⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “good”</note><l eID="gen14323" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14324"/>your name is poured out <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞perfume⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “oil lotion”</note><l eID="gen14324" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen14325"/>therefore young women love you. <l eID="gen14325" level="3"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7242"/><l level="1" sID="gen14326"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7242"/>Draw me after you, let us run!<l eID="gen14326" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14327"/>May the king bring me into his chambers!<note placement="foot">Or “The king has brought me into his chambers”</note><l eID="gen14327" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14328"/>Let us be joyful and let us rejoice in you;<l eID="gen14328" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14329"/>let us extol your love more than wine.<l eID="gen14329" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen14330"/>Rightly do they love you!<l eID="gen14330" level="3"/> <lg eID="gen14320"/> <title type="x-s">Maiden’s Self-Description</title> <div sID="gen14331" type="x-p"/>  <div eID="gen14331" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7243"/><lg sID="gen14332"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14333"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7243"/>I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> black but beautiful,<note placement="foot">Or “black and beautiful”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞O maidens of Jerusalem⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “O daughters of Jerusalem”</note><l eID="gen14333" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14334"/>like the tents of Kedar, like the curtains of Solomon. <l eID="gen14334" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7244"/><l level="1" sID="gen14335"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7244"/>Do not gaze at me because I am black,<note placement="foot">This is figurative for the maiden’s physical appearance; her skin was darkly tanned</note><l eID="gen14335" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14336"/>because the sun has stared <transChange type="added">at</transChange> me.<l eID="gen14336" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14337"/>The sons of my mother were angry with me;<l eID="gen14337" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14338"/>they made me keeper of the vineyards,<l eID="gen14338" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen14339"/><transChange type="added">but</transChange> my own “vineyard”<note placement="foot">Literally “my vineyard that for me”</note> I did not keep.<l eID="gen14339" level="3"/> <lg eID="gen14332"/> <title type="x-s">Dialogue between Shepherdess and Shepherd</title> <div sID="gen14340" type="x-p"/>  <div eID="gen14340" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7245"/><lg sID="gen14341"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14342"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7245"/>Tell me, <transChange type="added">you</transChange> whom my <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞heart⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “soul”</note> loves,<l eID="gen14342" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14343"/>where do you pasture your flock,<l eID="gen14343" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen14344"/>where do your sheep lie down at the noon?<l eID="gen14344" level="3"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14345"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞For why should I be like⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “For to what will I be like”</note> one who is veiled<note placement="foot">The reading of the MT (“like one who is veiled”) is supported by the LXX. However, several ancient versions (Syriac Peshitta, Latin Vulgate, Symmachus) reflect an alternate Hebrew textual tradition in which two letters are transposed, resulting in the reading “like one who wanders about.” This makes good sense contextually, since the maiden does not know where her beloved would be at noon</note><l eID="gen14345" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14346"/>beside the flocks of your companions? <l eID="gen14346" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7246"/><l level="1" sID="gen14347"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7246"/>If you do not know, O fairest among women,<l eID="gen14347" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14348"/>follow <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the tracks⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in the tracks”</note> of the flock,<l eID="gen14348" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen14349"/>and pasture your little lambs<note placement="foot">Or “your kids”</note> beside the tents of the shepherds.<l eID="gen14349" level="3"/> <lg eID="gen14341"/> <title type="x-s">Man’s Poetic Praise of His Beloved</title> <div sID="gen14350" type="x-p"/>  <div eID="gen14350" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7247"/><lg sID="gen14351"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14352"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7247"/>To a mare<note placement="foot">Or “my mare”</note> among the chariots<note placement="foot">Or “chariot horses”</note> of Pharaoh,<l eID="gen14352" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14353"/>I compare you, my beloved. <l eID="gen14353" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7248"/><l level="1" sID="gen14354"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7248"/>Your cheeks are beautiful with ornaments,<l eID="gen14354" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14355"/>your neck with strings of jewels. <l eID="gen14355" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7249"/><l level="1" sID="gen14356"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7249"/>We will make ornaments of gold for you<l eID="gen14356" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14357"/>with studs<note placement="foot">Or “droplets”</note> of silver.<l eID="gen14357" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen14351"/> <title type="x-s">Maiden’s Poetic Praise of Her Beloved</title> <div sID="gen14358" type="x-p"/>  <div eID="gen14358" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7250"/><lg sID="gen14359"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14360"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7250"/>While the king <transChange type="added">was</transChange> on his couch,<l eID="gen14360" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14361"/>my nard gave its fragrance. <l eID="gen14361" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7251"/><l level="1" sID="gen14362"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7251"/>My beloved <transChange type="added">is</transChange> to me <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a pouch⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the bag”</note> of myrrh,<l eID="gen14362" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14363"/>he spends the night<note placement="foot">Or “he lays”</note> between my breasts. <l eID="gen14363" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7252"/><l level="1" sID="gen14364"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7252"/>My beloved <transChange type="added">is</transChange> to me a cluster of blossoms of henna<l eID="gen14364" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14365"/>in the vineyards of En Gedi.<l eID="gen14365" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen14359"/> <title type="x-s">Mutual Admiration</title> <div sID="gen14366" type="x-p"/>  <div eID="gen14366" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7253"/><lg sID="gen14367"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14368"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7253"/>Look! You <transChange type="added">are</transChange> beautiful, my beloved.<l eID="gen14368" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14369"/>Look! You <transChange type="added">are</transChange> beautiful;<l eID="gen14369" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen14370"/>your eyes <transChange type="added">are</transChange> doves. <l eID="gen14370" level="3"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7254"/><l level="1" sID="gen14371"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7254"/>Look! You <transChange type="added">are</transChange> beautiful, my beloved,<l eID="gen14371" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14372"/>truly pleasant.<l eID="gen14372" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14373"/>Truly our couch <transChange type="added">is</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞verdant⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “green”</note> <l eID="gen14373" level="1"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7255"/><l level="2" sID="gen14374"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7255"/>the beams of our house <transChange type="added">are</transChange> cedar;<l eID="gen14374" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen14375"/>our rafter <transChange type="added">is</transChange> cypress. <l eID="gen14375" level="3"/><lg eID="gen14367"/> <chapter eID="Song.1"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7256"/><title type="x-s">Dialogue between Maiden and Her Beloved</title> <div sID="gen14376" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen14376" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen14377"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14378"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7256"/>I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> a rose<note placement="foot">More likely “meadow saffron” or “crocus.” Hebrew scholars and botanists suggest the term refers to <hi type="italic">Ashodelos</hi> (lily family), <hi type="italic">Narcissus tazetta</hi> (narcissus or daffodil), or <hi type="italic">Colchicum autumnale</hi> (meadow saffron or crocus) (e.g., <reference osisRef="Isa.35.1">Isa 35:1</reference>). The location of this flower in Sharon suggests a common wild flower rather than a rose. The maiden compares herself to a simple, common flower of the field</note> of Sharon,<l eID="gen14378" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14379"/>a lily of the valleys. <l eID="gen14379" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7257"/><l level="1" sID="gen14380"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7257"/>Like a lily among the thorns,<note placement="foot">Or “brambles”</note><l eID="gen14380" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14381"/>so <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my love among the maidens. <l eID="gen14381" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7258"/><l level="1" sID="gen14382"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7258"/>As an apple tree among the trees of the forest,<l eID="gen14382" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14383"/>so <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my beloved among the young men.<l eID="gen14383" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14384"/>In his shade <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I sat down with delight⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “I sat down and I delighted”</note><l eID="gen14384" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14385"/>and his fruit <transChange type="added">was</transChange> sweet to my palate.<l eID="gen14385" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen14377"/> <title type="x-s">Banquet Hall of Love</title> <div sID="gen14386" type="x-p"/>  <div eID="gen14386" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7259"/><lg sID="gen14387"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14388"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7259"/>He brought me to the house of the wine,<l eID="gen14388" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14389"/>and his intention <transChange type="added">was</transChange> love toward me. <l eID="gen14389" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7260"/><l level="1" sID="gen14390"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7260"/>Sustain me with the raisins,<l eID="gen14390" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14391"/>refresh me with the apples,<l eID="gen14391" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14392"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞for I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> lovesick⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “for I myself am sick with love”</note><l eID="gen14392" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen14387"/> <title type="x-s">Double Refrain: Embrace and Adjuration</title> <div sID="gen14393" type="x-p"/>  <div eID="gen14393" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7261"/><lg sID="gen14394"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14395"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7261"/>His left <transChange type="added">hand</transChange> <transChange type="added">is</transChange> under my head,<l eID="gen14395" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14396"/>and his right <transChange type="added">hand</transChange> embraces<note placement="foot">Or “would embrace me”</note> me. <l eID="gen14396" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7262"/><l level="1" sID="gen14397"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7262"/>I adjure you, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞O maidens of Jerusalem⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “O daughters of Jerusalem”</note><l eID="gen14397" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14398"/>by the gazelles or by the does of the field,<l eID="gen14398" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14399"/>do not arouse or awaken love until it pleases!<note placement="foot">Or “Do not stir up or awaken the love until it is willing,” or “Do not disturb or interrupt our lovemaking until it is satisfied”</note><l eID="gen14399" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen14394"/> <title type="x-s">Rendezvous in the Countryside</title> <div sID="gen14400" type="x-p"/>  <div eID="gen14400" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7263"/><lg sID="gen14401"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14402"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7263"/>The voice of my beloved!<l eID="gen14402" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14403"/>Look! Here <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “this one”</note> comes leaping upon the mountains,<l eID="gen14403" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen14404"/>bounding over the hills! <l eID="gen14404" level="3"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7264"/><l level="1" sID="gen14405"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7264"/>My beloved is like a gazelle or <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a young stag⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the fawn of the stag”</note><l eID="gen14405" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14406"/>Look! <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞He is⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “This is he”</note> standing behind our wall,<l eID="gen14406" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14407"/>gazing <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞through⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from”</note> the window,<l eID="gen14407" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14408"/>looking <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞through⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from”</note> the lattice. <l eID="gen14408" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7265"/><l level="1" sID="gen14409"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7265"/>My beloved answered and said to me,<l eID="gen14409" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14410"/>“<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Arise⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “Arise, you”</note> my beloved! <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Come, my beauty⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!<note placement="foot">Literally “And come, you”</note> <l eID="gen14410" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7266"/><l level="1" sID="gen14411"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7266"/>For look! The winter is over;<l eID="gen14411" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14412"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the rainy season⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the rain”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞has turned and gone away⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “is over; it is gone”</note> <l eID="gen14412" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7267"/><l level="1" sID="gen14413"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7267"/>The blossoms <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞appear⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “is seen”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in the land⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “on the earth”</note><l eID="gen14413" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14414"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the time of singing<note placement="foot">Most likely, a subtle word play occurs here since there are two different words in Hebrew spelled the same way: “pruning” and “singing.” The former plays upon the first line and the latter upon the third line</note> has arrived⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “the time of the song arrived”</note><l eID="gen14414" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14415"/>the voice of the turtledove is heard in our land. <l eID="gen14415" level="1"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7268"/><l level="1" sID="gen14416"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7268"/>The fig tree puts forth her figs,<l eID="gen14416" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14417"/>and the vines <transChange type="added">are in</transChange> blossom; they give fragrance.<l eID="gen14417" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14418"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Arise⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “Arise, to you!”</note> my beloved! <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Come, my beauty⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!”<note placement="foot">Literally “My beauty, come, you”</note> <l eID="gen14418" level="1"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7269"/><l level="1" sID="gen14419"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7269"/>My dove, in the clefts of the rock,<l eID="gen14419" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14420"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in the secluded place⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in the secret place”</note><note placement="foot">Or “in the covering”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in the mountain⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “foothold in the rock”</note><note placement="foot">Or “cliff”</note><l eID="gen14420" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14421"/>Let me see your face,<l eID="gen14421" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14422"/>let me hear your voice;<l eID="gen14422" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14423"/>for your voice <transChange type="added">is</transChange> sweet and your face <transChange type="added">is</transChange> lovely. <l eID="gen14423" level="1"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7270"/><l level="1" sID="gen14424"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7270"/>Catch for us the foxes,<l eID="gen14424" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14425"/>the little foxes destroying vineyards,<l eID="gen14425" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14426"/>for<note placement="foot">Or “while”</note> our vineyards <transChange type="added">are in</transChange> blossom!<l eID="gen14426" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen14401"/> <title type="x-s">Poetic Refrain(s)</title> <div sID="gen14427" type="x-p"/>  <div eID="gen14427" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7271"/><lg sID="gen14428"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14429"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7271"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞My beloved belongs to me and I belong to him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “My beloved for me and I for him”</note><l eID="gen14429" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14430"/>he pastures his flock among the lilies. <l eID="gen14430" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7272"/><l level="1" sID="gen14431"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7272"/>Until the day breathes and the shadows flee,<l eID="gen14431" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14432"/>turn, my beloved!<l eID="gen14432" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen14433"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Be like⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Be like for you”</note> a gazelle<note placement="foot">Or “a buck gazelle”</note> or <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞young stag⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the fawn of the stag”</note> on the cleft mountains.<note placement="foot">Or “the mountains of Bether”</note> <l eID="gen14433" level="3"/><lg eID="gen14428"/> <chapter eID="Song.2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 3:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7273"/><title type="x-s">Maiden’s Dream (?): Seeking and Finding</title> <div sID="gen14434" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen14434" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen14435"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14436"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7273"/>On my bed in the night,<l eID="gen14436" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14437"/>I sought<note placement="foot">Or “I seek”</note> him whom my <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞heart⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “soul”</note> loves.<l eID="gen14437" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14438"/>I sought him, but I did not find him. <l eID="gen14438" level="1"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 3:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7274"/><l level="1" sID="gen14439"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7274"/>Now I will arise, and I will go about in the city,<l eID="gen14439" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14440"/>in the streets and in the squares;<l eID="gen14440" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14441"/>I will seek him whom my <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞heart⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “soul”</note> loves.<l eID="gen14441" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14442"/>I sought him, but I did not find him. <l eID="gen14442" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 3:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7275"/><l level="1" sID="gen14443"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7275"/>The sentinels who go about in the city found me.<l eID="gen14443" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14444"/>“Have you seen the one whom my <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞heart⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “soul”</note> loves?” <l eID="gen14444" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 3:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7276"/><l level="1" sID="gen14445"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7276"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Scarcely had I passed⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “As little that I passed”</note> by them<l eID="gen14445" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14446"/>when I found him whom my <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞heart⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “soul”</note> loves.<l eID="gen14446" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14447"/>I held him and I would not let him go<l eID="gen14447" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14448"/>until I brought him to the house of my mother,<l eID="gen14448" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen14449"/>into the bedroom chamber of she who conceived me.<l eID="gen14449" level="3"/> <lg eID="gen14435"/> <title type="x-s">Adjuration Refrain</title> <div sID="gen14450" type="x-p"/>  <div eID="gen14450" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 3:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7277"/><lg sID="gen14451"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14452"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7277"/>I adjure you, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞O maidens of Jerusalem⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “O daughters of Jerusalem”</note><l eID="gen14452" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14453"/>by the gazelles or by the does of the field,<l eID="gen14453" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14454"/>do not arouse or awaken love until it pleases!<note placement="foot">Or “Do not stir up or awaken the love until it is willing,” or “Do not disturb or interrupt our love-making until it is satisfied”</note><l eID="gen14454" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen14451"/> <title type="x-s">Royal Wedding Procession</title> <div sID="gen14455" type="x-p"/>  <div eID="gen14455" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 3:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7278"/><lg sID="gen14456"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14457"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7278"/>What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> this coming up from the desert<l eID="gen14457" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14458"/>like a column of smoke,<l eID="gen14458" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14459"/>perfumed with myrrh and frankincense<l eID="gen14459" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14460"/>from all the fragrant powders of the merchant? <l eID="gen14460" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 3:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7279"/><l level="1" sID="gen14461"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7279"/>Look! <transChange type="added">It is</transChange> Solomon’s <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞portable couch⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!<note placement="foot">Literally “couch” or “portable sedan chair”</note><l eID="gen14461" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14462"/>Sixty mighty men surround <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞it⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “her”</note><l eID="gen14462" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen14463"/>the mighty men of Israel. <l eID="gen14463" level="3"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 3:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7280"/><l level="1" sID="gen14464"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7280"/>All of them <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞wield swords⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “holders of sword”</note><l eID="gen14464" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14465"/><transChange type="added">they are</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞trained in warfare⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “learnt of war”</note><l eID="gen14465" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14466"/>each with his sword at his thigh<l eID="gen14466" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14467"/><transChange type="added">to guard</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞against terror⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “because of the fear”</note> in the night. <l eID="gen14467" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 3:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7281"/><l level="1" sID="gen14468"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7281"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞King Solomon⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “The king, Solomon”</note> made for himself a sedan chair<l eID="gen14468" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14469"/>from the wood of Lebanon. <l eID="gen14469" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 3:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7282"/><l level="1" sID="gen14470"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7282"/>He made its column of silver, its back<note placement="foot">Or “its support,” “its base,” “its headrest,” “its litter,” “its cover”</note> of gold, its seat of purple;<l eID="gen14470" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14471"/>its interior is inlaid <transChange type="added">with</transChange> leather<note placement="foot">Or “love.” The Hebrew term here translated “leather” is spelled the same as the term for “love.” Most likely this is an example of a word play that puns on the intentional ambiguity: “Its interior was inlaid with leather<lb type="x-optional"/>love by the maidens of Jerusalem”</note> by <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the maidens of Jerusalem⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “by the daughters of Jerusalem”</note> <l eID="gen14471" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 3:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7283"/><l level="1" sID="gen14472"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7283"/>Come out and look, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞O maidens of Zion⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “O daughters of Zion”</note> at <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞King Solomon⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the king, Solomon”</note><l eID="gen14472" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14473"/>at the crown with which his mother crowned him<l eID="gen14473" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14474"/>on the day of his wedding,<l eID="gen14474" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14475"/>on the day of the joy of his heart! <l eID="gen14475" level="2"/><lg eID="gen14456"/> <chapter eID="Song.3"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7284"/><title type="x-s">Groom’s Praise of His Bride</title> <div sID="gen14476" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen14476" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen14477"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14478"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7284"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Oh my⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!<note placement="foot">Literally “Behold!” Or “Look!”</note> You <transChange type="added">are</transChange> beautiful, my beloved!<l eID="gen14478" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14479"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Oh my⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!<note placement="foot">Literally “Behold!” Or “Look!”</note> You <transChange type="added">are</transChange> beautiful!<l eID="gen14479" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14480"/>Your eyes <transChange type="added">are</transChange> doves<l eID="gen14480" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14481"/>from behind your veil.<l eID="gen14481" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14482"/>Your hair <transChange type="added">is</transChange> like a flock of goats<l eID="gen14482" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14483"/>that move down from the mountains of Gilead. <l eID="gen14483" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7285"/><l level="1" sID="gen14484"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7285"/>Your teeth <transChange type="added">are</transChange> like a flock of shorn ewes<l eID="gen14484" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14485"/>that came up from the washing,<l eID="gen14485" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14486"/>all of them bearing twins,<l eID="gen14486" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14487"/>and there is none bereaved among them. <l eID="gen14487" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7286"/><l level="1" sID="gen14488"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7286"/>Your lips <transChange type="added">are</transChange> like a thread of crimson,<l eID="gen14488" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14489"/>and your mouth <transChange type="added">is</transChange> lovely.<l eID="gen14489" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14490"/>Your temple <transChange type="added">is</transChange> like pomegranate<l eID="gen14490" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14491"/>from behind your veil. <l eID="gen14491" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7287"/><l level="1" sID="gen14492"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7287"/>Your neck <transChange type="added">is</transChange> like the tower of David,<l eID="gen14492" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14493"/>built in courses;<l eID="gen14493" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14494"/>a thousand <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞ornaments⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “shields”</note> are hung on it,<l eID="gen14494" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14495"/>all the shields of the warriors. <l eID="gen14495" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7288"/><l level="1" sID="gen14496"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7288"/>Your two breasts <transChange type="added">are</transChange> like two fawns,<l eID="gen14496" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14497"/>twins of a gazelle that feed among the lilies. <l eID="gen14497" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7289"/><l level="1" sID="gen14498"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7289"/>Until the day breathes and the shadows flee,<l eID="gen14498" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14499"/>I will go to the mountain of the myrrh,<l eID="gen14499" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen14500"/>to the hill of the frankincense. <l eID="gen14500" level="3"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7290"/><l level="1" sID="gen14501"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7290"/>You <transChange type="added">are</transChange> completely beautiful, my beloved!<l eID="gen14501" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14502"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞You are flawless⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!<note placement="foot">Literally “There is no flaw in you!”</note><l eID="gen14502" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen14477"/> <title type="x-s">The Mountains and Fragrance of Lebanon</title> <div sID="gen14503" type="x-p"/>  <div eID="gen14503" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7291"/><lg sID="gen14504"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14505"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7291"/>Come<note placement="foot">Or “You must come”</note> with me from Lebanon, my bride!<l eID="gen14505" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14506"/>Come with me<note placement="foot">Or “With me”</note> from Lebanon!<l eID="gen14506" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14507"/>Look from the top of Amana,<l eID="gen14507" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14508"/>from the top of Senir and Hermon,<l eID="gen14508" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14509"/>from the dwelling places of the lions,<l eID="gen14509" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14510"/>from the mountains of leopard. <l eID="gen14510" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7292"/><l level="1" sID="gen14511"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7292"/>You have stolen (my) heart, my sister bride!<l eID="gen14511" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14512"/>You have stolen <transChange type="added">my</transChange> heart with one <transChange type="added">glance</transChange> from your eyes,<l eID="gen14512" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen14513"/>with one ornament from your necklaces. <l eID="gen14513" level="3"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7293"/><l level="1" sID="gen14514"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7293"/>How beautiful is your love, my sister bride!<l eID="gen14514" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14515"/>How better is your love than wine,<l eID="gen14515" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen14516"/>and the fragrance of your oils than any spice! <l eID="gen14516" level="3"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7294"/><l level="1" sID="gen14517"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7294"/>Your lips drip nectar, <transChange type="added">my</transChange> bride;<l eID="gen14517" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14518"/>honey and milk <transChange type="added">are</transChange> under your lips;<l eID="gen14518" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen14519"/>the scent of your garments <transChange type="added">is</transChange> like the scent of Lebanon.<l eID="gen14519" level="3"/> <lg eID="gen14504"/> <title type="x-s">The Locked Garden of Delights Is Unlocked</title> <div sID="gen14520" type="x-p"/>  <div eID="gen14520" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7295"/><lg sID="gen14521"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14522"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7295"/>A garden locked <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my sister bride,<l eID="gen14522" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14523"/>a spring enclosed,<note placement="foot">Or “a source locked”</note> a fountain sealed. <l eID="gen14523" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7296"/><l level="1" sID="gen14524"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7296"/>Your shoots<note placement="foot">Or “your channel”</note> are an orchard of pomegranates with <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞choice fruit⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “fruit of choice things”</note><l eID="gen14524" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14525"/>henna with nard; <l eID="gen14525" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7297"/><l level="1" sID="gen14526"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7297"/>nard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon spice with all trees of frankincense,<l eID="gen14526" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14527"/>myrrh and aloes with all chief spices. <l eID="gen14527" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7298"/><l level="1" sID="gen14528"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7298"/>A garden fountain, a well of living water,<l eID="gen14528" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14529"/>flowing (streams) from Lebanon. <l eID="gen14529" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7299"/><l level="1" sID="gen14530"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7299"/>Awake, O north wind! Come, O south wind!<l eID="gen14530" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14531"/>Blow upon my garden! Let its fragrances<note placement="foot">Or “perfumes”</note> waft forth!<note placement="foot">Or “His perfumes can waft down”</note><l eID="gen14531" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14532"/>Let my beloved come to his garden,<l eID="gen14532" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14533"/>let him eat his choice fruit! <l eID="gen14533" level="2"/><lg eID="gen14521"/> <chapter eID="Song.4"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:1
verses.text: I have come to my garden, my sister bride,<l eID="gen14536" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14537"/>I have gathered my myrrh with my spice,<l eID="gen14537" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14538"/>I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey,<l eID="gen14538" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14539"/>I have drunk my wine with my milk!<l eID="gen14539" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14540"/>Eat, O friends! <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Drink and become drunk <transChange type="added">with</transChange> love⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!<note placement="foot">Or “Drink and become drunk, O lovers!”</note><l eID="gen14540" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen14535"/> <title type="x-s">Maiden’s Dream: Seeking and Not Finding</title> <div sID="gen14541" type="x-p"/>  <div eID="gen14541" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7300"/><lg sID="gen14542"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14543"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7300"/>I <transChange type="added">was</transChange> asleep but<note placement="foot">Or “and”</note> my heart was awake.<l eID="gen14543" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14544"/>A sound! My beloved knocking!<note placement="foot">Or “The sound of my beloved knocking!”</note><l eID="gen14544" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14545"/>“Open to me, my sister, my beloved,<l eID="gen14545" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14546"/>my dove, my perfect one!<l eID="gen14546" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14547"/>For my head is full of dew,<l eID="gen14547" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14548"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞my hair drenched from the moist night air⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “my locks with drops of night”</note> <l eID="gen14548" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7301"/><l level="1" sID="gen14549"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7301"/>I have taken off my tunic, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞must I put it on⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?<note placement="foot">Literally “How will I put it on?”</note><l eID="gen14549" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14550"/>I have bathed my feet, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞must I soil them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?<note placement="foot">Literally “How will I soil them?”</note> <l eID="gen14550" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7302"/><l level="1" sID="gen14551"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7302"/>My beloved thrust his hand into the opening,<l eID="gen14551" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14552"/>and my inmost yearned for him. <l eID="gen14552" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7303"/><l level="1" sID="gen14553"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7303"/>I myself arose to open to my beloved;<l eID="gen14553" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14554"/>my hands dripped with myrrh,<l eID="gen14554" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14555"/>my fingers with liquid myrrh<l eID="gen14555" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14556"/>upon the handles of the bolt. <l eID="gen14556" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7304"/><l level="1" sID="gen14557"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7304"/>I opened myself to my beloved,<l eID="gen14557" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14558"/>but my beloved had turned and gone;<note placement="foot">Or “my beloved had left; he was gone”</note><l eID="gen14558" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14559"/>my heart sank<note placement="foot">Or “my soul left”</note> when he turned away.<note placement="foot">Or “when he was speaking.” Translations equivocate on how to translate this verb, since there are two terms in Hebrew spelled identically: “to speak” and “to turn aside” (HALOT 1:210). The context suggests the latter</note><l eID="gen14559" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14560"/>I sought him, but I did not find him;<l eID="gen14560" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14561"/>I called him, but he did not answer me. <l eID="gen14561" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7305"/><l level="1" sID="gen14562"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7305"/>The sentinels making rounds in the city found me;<l eID="gen14562" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14563"/>they beat me, they wounded me;<l eID="gen14563" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14564"/>they took my cloak<note placement="foot">Or “mantle”</note> away from me—<l eID="gen14564" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14565"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞those sentinels on the walls⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!<note placement="foot">Literally “the sentinels of the walls”</note><l eID="gen14565" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen14542"/> <title type="x-s">Adjuration Refrain</title> <div sID="gen14566" type="x-p"/>  <div eID="gen14566" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7306"/><lg sID="gen14567"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14568"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7306"/>I adjure you, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞O maidens of Jerusalem⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “O daughters of Jerusalem”</note><l eID="gen14568" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14569"/>if you find my beloved, what will you tell him?<l eID="gen14569" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14570"/><transChange type="added">Tell him</transChange> that I am <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞lovesick⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!<note placement="foot">Literally “sick with love”</note><l eID="gen14570" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen14567"/> <title type="x-s">Maiden’s Praise of Her Beloved</title> <div sID="gen14571" type="x-p"/>  <div eID="gen14571" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7307"/><lg sID="gen14572"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14573"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7307"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞How is your beloved better than another lover⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “What is your beloved more than another beloved …?”</note><l eID="gen14573" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14574"/>O most beautiful among women?<l eID="gen14574" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14575"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞How is your beloved better than another lover⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “What is your beloved more than another beloved …?”</note><l eID="gen14575" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14576"/>that you adjure us thus? <l eID="gen14576" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7308"/><l level="1" sID="gen14577"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7308"/>My beloved <transChange type="added">is</transChange> radiant and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞ruddy⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “red”</note><l eID="gen14577" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14578"/>distinguished <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞among⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “more than”</note> ten thousand. <l eID="gen14578" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7309"/><l level="1" sID="gen14579"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7309"/>His head <transChange type="added">is</transChange> gold, refined gold;<l eID="gen14579" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14580"/>his locks <transChange type="added">are</transChange> wavy, black as a raven. <l eID="gen14580" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7310"/><l level="1" sID="gen14581"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7310"/>His eyes <transChange type="added">are</transChange> like doves beside springs<note placement="foot">Or “streams”</note> of water,<l eID="gen14581" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14582"/>bathed in milk, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞set like mounted jewels⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “dwelling in a setting”</note><note placement="foot">Or “seated at a suitable mounting”</note> <l eID="gen14582" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7311"/><l level="1" sID="gen14583"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7311"/>His cheeks <transChange type="added">are</transChange> like beds of spice, a tower of fragrances;<l eID="gen14583" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14584"/>his lips <transChange type="added">are</transChange> lilies dripping liquid myrrh. <l eID="gen14584" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7312"/><l level="1" sID="gen14585"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7312"/>His arms <transChange type="added">are</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞rods⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “cylinders”</note><note placement="foot">Or “rings”</note> of gold <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞engraved with⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “filled with”</note> jewels;<l eID="gen14585" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14586"/>his belly<note placement="foot">Or “body”</note> is polished ivory covered with sapphires.<note placement="foot">Or “works of ivory set with sapphire”</note> <l eID="gen14586" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7313"/><l level="1" sID="gen14587"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7313"/>His legs <transChange type="added">are</transChange> columns of alabaster,<note placement="foot">Or “marble”</note> set on bases of gold;<l eID="gen14587" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14588"/>his appearance <transChange type="added">is</transChange> like Lebanon, choice as <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞its cedars⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the cedars”</note> <l eID="gen14588" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7314"/><l level="1" sID="gen14589"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7314"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞His mouth⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Or “his palate”</note> <transChange type="added">is</transChange> sweet,<l eID="gen14589" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14590"/>and he is altogether desirable.<l eID="gen14590" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14591"/>This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my beloved;<l eID="gen14591" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14592"/>this <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my friend, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞O young women of Jerusalem⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “O daughters of Jerusalem”</note> <l eID="gen14592" level="2"/><lg eID="gen14572"/> <chapter eID="Song.5"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 6:1
verses.text: Where has your beloved gone,<l eID="gen14595" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14596"/>O most beautiful among women?<l eID="gen14596" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen14597"/>Where has your beloved turned<l eID="gen14597" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen14598"/>that we may seek him with you? <l eID="gen14598" level="2"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 6:2
