verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9053"/><div sID="gen20953" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9053"/>Then Jeremiah called Baruch the son of Neriah, and Baruch wrote from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of Yahweh that he had spoken to him on <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a scroll⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “a scroll of a scroll”</note>

verses.name: Jeremiah 36:5
verses.text: And Jeremiah instructed Baruch, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to say”</note> “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> held back, I am not able to enter the temple of Yahweh.

verses.name: Jeremiah 36:6
verses.text: So you must go and you shall read aloud from the scroll that you have written from my mouth the words of Yahweh in the hearing of the people <transChange type="added">in</transChange> the temple of Yahweh on a day of fast, and also you shall read aloud in the hearing of all those of Judah who came from their towns.

verses.name: Jeremiah 36:7
verses.text: Perhaps their plea will fall <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the face of”</note> Yahweh and each one will turn away from his evil way, for great <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the anger and wrath that Yahweh pronounced against this people.”

verses.name: Jeremiah 36:8
verses.text: And Baruch the son of Neriah did all that Jeremiah the prophet instructed him, to read aloud from the scroll the words of Yahweh <transChange type="added">in</transChange> the temple of Yahweh.  <div eID="gen20953" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 36:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9054"/><div sID="gen20954" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9054"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it was”</note> in the fifth year of Jehoiakim, the son of Josiah, the king of Judah, in the ninth month, all the people in Jerusalem and all the people who came from the towns of Judah to Jerusalem proclaimed a fast <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the face of”</note> Yahweh.

verses.name: Jeremiah 36:10
verses.text: Then Baruch read aloud from the scroll the words of Jeremiah <transChange type="added">in</transChange> the temple of Yahweh, in the chamber of Gemariah, the son of Shaphan, the secretary, in the upper courtyard <transChange type="added">at</transChange> the entrance of the New Gate of the temple of Yahweh in the hearing of all the people.  <div eID="gen20954" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 36:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9055"/><div sID="gen20955" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9055"/>When Micaiah, the son of Gemariah, the son of Shaphan, heard all the words of Yahweh from the scroll,

verses.name: Jeremiah 36:12
verses.text: he went down <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the house of the king, to the chamber of the secretary, and look, all the officials <transChange type="added">were</transChange> sitting there: Elishama the secretary, and Delaiah, the son of Shemaiah, and Elnathan, the son of Achbor, and Gemariah, the son of Shaphan, and Zedekiah, the son of Hananiah, and all the <transChange type="added">other</transChange> officials.

verses.name: Jeremiah 36:13
verses.text: And Micaiah told them all the words that he had heard at the reading aloud of Baruch from the scroll in the hearing of the people.  <div eID="gen20955" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 36:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9056"/><div sID="gen20956" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9056"/>Then all the officials sent Jehudi, the son of Nethaniah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Cushi, to Baruch, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to say”</note> “The scroll that you read aloud from in the hearing of the people, take it in your hand and come.” And Baruch the son of Neriah took the scroll in his hand and he came to them.

verses.name: Jeremiah 36:15
verses.text: And they said to him, “Sit please and read it aloud in our hearing.” So Baruch read aloud in their hearing.

verses.name: Jeremiah 36:16
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “And it was”</note> the moment of their hearing all the words, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they turned to one another in alarm⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “they approached in trepidation each one to his neighbor”</note> and they said to Baruch, “We must certainly report all these words to the king!”

verses.name: Jeremiah 36:17
verses.text: Then they asked Baruch, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to say”</note> “Tell us please, how did you write all these words, from his mouth?”

verses.name: Jeremiah 36:18
verses.text: And Baruch said to them, “From his mouth. He dictated to me all these words and I <transChange type="added">was</transChange> writing on the scroll with the ink.”

verses.name: Jeremiah 36:19
verses.text: Then the officials said to Baruch, “Go, hide yourself, you and Jeremiah, and let not a man know where you <transChange type="added">are</transChange>.”  <div eID="gen20956" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 36:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9057"/><div sID="gen20957" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9057"/>And they went to the king, <transChange type="added">to the</transChange> courtyard, and they <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞put⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “gave”</note> the scroll for safe-keeping in the chamber of Elishama the secretary, and they reported all the words in the hearing of the king.

verses.name: Jeremiah 36:21
verses.text: Then the king sent Jehudi to take the scroll, and he took it from the chamber of Elishama the secretary, and Jehudi read it aloud in the hearing of the king, and in the hearing of all the officials who stood next to the king.

verses.name: Jeremiah 36:22
verses.text: Now the king <transChange type="added">was</transChange> sitting <transChange type="added">in</transChange> the quarters of the winter in the ninth month, and a fire-pot <transChange type="added">was</transChange> burning <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the face of”</note> him.

verses.name: Jeremiah 36:23
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “and it was”</note> as Jehudi read three or four columns, he would cut it up in pieces with the knife of the scribe, and he would throw it<note placement="foot">Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> into the fire that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in the fire-pot until the whole of the scroll <transChange type="added">was</transChange> consumed in the fire that was in the fire-pot.

verses.name: Jeremiah 36:24
verses.text: And the king and any of his servants who heard all these words were not startled, and they did not tear their garments.

verses.name: Jeremiah 36:25
verses.text: And even <transChange type="added">when</transChange> Elnathan, and Delaiah, and Gemariah urged the king not to burn the scroll, he would not listen to them.

verses.name: Jeremiah 36:26
verses.text: And the king commanded Jerahmeel, the son of the king, and Seraiah, the son of Azriel, and Shelemiah, the son of Abdeel, to arrest Baruch the secretary and Jeremiah the prophet, but Yahweh hid them.  <div eID="gen20957" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 36:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9058"/><div sID="gen20958" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9058"/>And the word of Yahweh came to Jeremiah after the king burned the scroll and the words that Baruch wrote from the mouth of Jeremiah, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to say”</note>

verses.name: Jeremiah 36:28
verses.text: “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Take again⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Turn back take”</note> for yourself another scroll and write on it all the former words that were in the first scroll which Jehoiakim, the king of Judah, has burned.

verses.name: Jeremiah 36:29
verses.text: And concerning Jehoiakim, the king of Judah, you shall say, ‘Thus says Yahweh, “You have burned this scroll, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to say”</note> ‘Why have you written in it, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to say”</note> “The king of Babylon will certainly come and he will destroy this land, and he will cause to disappear from it humankind and animals”?’ ”<note placement="foot">Hebrew “animal”</note>

verses.name: Jeremiah 36:30
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Therefore⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “To thus”</note> thus says Yahweh concerning Jehoiakim, the king of Judah, “There will not be for him <transChange type="added">one who</transChange> sits on the throne of David. And his dead body will be thrown out to the heat in the day and to the frost in the night.

verses.name: Jeremiah 36:31
verses.text: And I will punish him, and his offspring, and his servants for their guilt, and I will bring on them, and on the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and on the people of Judah all the disaster with which I have threatened them, but they would not listen.” ’ ”

verses.name: Jeremiah 36:32
verses.text: Then Jeremiah took another scroll and gave it to Baruch the son of Neriah, the secretary, and he wrote on it from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the scroll that Jehoiakim, the king of Judah, had burned in the fire, and furthermore was added to them many words like these.  <chapter eID="Jer.36"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 37:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9059"/><title type="x-s">The Babylonians Withdraw to Meet a Threat from Egypt</title> <div sID="gen20959" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9059"/>And king Zedekiah, the son of Josiah, whom Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon, had made king, reigned as king in the land of Judah in place of Coniah, the son of Jehoiakim.

verses.name: Jeremiah 37:2
verses.text: But he and his servants and the people of the land did not listen to the words of Yahweh that he spoke by the hand of Jeremiah the prophet.

verses.name: Jeremiah 37:3
verses.text: And king Zedekiah sent Jehucal the son of Shelemiah, and Zephaniah the son of Maaseiah, the priest, to Jeremiah the prophet, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to say”</note> “Please pray for us to Yahweh our God.”

verses.name: Jeremiah 37:4
verses.text: Now Jeremiah <transChange type="added">was</transChange> coming and going out in the midst of the people and they had not put him <transChange type="added">in</transChange> the house of imprisonment.

verses.name: Jeremiah 37:5
verses.text: And the army of Pharaoh had come out from Egypt, and the Chaldeans, who were laying siege to Jerusalem, heard their report and they withdrew from Jerusalem.  <div eID="gen20959" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 37:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9060"/><div sID="gen20960" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9060"/>And the word of Yahweh came to Jeremiah the prophet, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to say”</note>

verses.name: Jeremiah 37:7
verses.text: “Thus says Yahweh, the God of Israel, ‘This is what you shall say to the king of Judah, who sent you to me to inquire <transChange type="added">of</transChange> me, “Look, the army of Pharaoh, which set out to help you, <transChange type="added">is</transChange> going to return to his land Egypt.

verses.name: Jeremiah 37:8
verses.text: And the Chaldeans will return, and they will fight against this city, and they will capture it, and they will burn it with fire.” ’

verses.name: Jeremiah 37:9
verses.text: Thus says Yahweh: ‘You must not deceive yourselves, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to say”</note> “Surely the Chaldeans will go from us,” for they will not go.

verses.name: Jeremiah 37:10
verses.text: For <transChange type="added">even</transChange> if you struck the whole army of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Chaldeans who are fighting against you, and <transChange type="added">only</transChange> men pierced through remained among them, each one in his tent, they would rise up and they would burn this city with fire.’ ”  <div eID="gen20960" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 37:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9061"/><title type="x-s">Jeremiah is Arrested and Put in Prison</title> <div sID="gen20961" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9061"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “And it will happen”</note> at the withdrawing of the army of the Chaldeans from Jerusalem <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from the face of”</note> the army of Pharaoh,

verses.name: Jeremiah 37:12
verses.text: Jeremiah set out from Jerusalem to go <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the land of Benjamin to receive a portion from there in the midst of the people.

verses.name: Jeremiah 37:13
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And when⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it was”</note> he was at the Gate of Benjamin, there was <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a sentry on duty⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “an owner of supervision”</note> whose name was Irijah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Hananiah, and he seized Jeremiah the prophet, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to say”</note> “You <transChange type="added">are</transChange> deserting to the Chaldeans!”

verses.name: Jeremiah 37:14
verses.text: And Jeremiah said, “<transChange type="added">That is</transChange> a lie! I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> not deserting to the Chaldeans.” But he would not listen to him. So Irijah seized Jeremiah and brought him to the officials.

verses.name: Jeremiah 37:15
verses.text: And the officials were angry at Jeremiah and they struck him. And they put him <transChange type="added">in</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞prison⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the house of the fetters”</note> in the house of Jonathan the secretary, for they had converted it to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞prison⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “house of the imprisonment”</note>.

verses.name: Jeremiah 37:16
verses.text: So Jeremiah came to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞dungeon⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “house of the cistern”</note>, even to the vaulted cells, and Jeremiah stayed there many days.  <div eID="gen20961" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 37:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9062"/><div sID="gen20962" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9062"/>Then King Zedekiah sent and fetched him. And the king questioned him in secrecy in his house, and he said, “Is there a word from Yahweh?” And Jeremiah said, “There is.” And he said, “You will be given into the hand of the king of Babylon.”  <div eID="gen20962" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 37:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9063"/><div sID="gen20963" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9063"/>Then Jeremiah said to King Zedekiah, “What did I do wrong to you, or to your servants, or to this people, that you have put me in <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞prison⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?<note placement="foot">Literally “the house of the imprisonment”</note>

verses.name: Jeremiah 37:19
verses.text: And where <transChange type="added">are</transChange> your prophets who prophesied to you, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to say”</note> ‘The king of Babylon will not come against you and against this land’?

verses.name: Jeremiah 37:20
verses.text: Now then, my lord the king, please let my plea fall <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “to the face of you”</note> You must not send me back <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the house of Jonathan the secretary, so that I will not die there.”

verses.name: Jeremiah 37:21
verses.text: So King Zedekiah commanded, and they handed Jeremiah over in the courtyard of the guard, and they gave to him a round loaf of bread from the street of the bakers <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞every day⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for the day”</note> until the finishing of all the bread from the city. And Jeremiah stayed in the courtyard of the guard.  <chapter eID="Jer.37"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 38:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9064"/><title type="x-s">Jeremiah is Thrown into the Pit of Malchiah</title> <div sID="gen20964" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9064"/>Now Shephatiah the son of Mattan, and Gedaliah the son of Pashhur, and Jehucal the son of Shelemiah, and Pashhur the son of Malchiah heard the words that Jeremiah <transChange type="added">was</transChange> saying to all the people, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to say”</note>

verses.name: Jeremiah 38:2
verses.text: “Thus says Yahweh, ‘The <transChange type="added">one who</transChange> stays in this city will die by the sword, by the famine, and by the plague. But the <transChange type="added">one who</transChange> goes out to the Chaldeans will live. And his life will be for him as booty, and he will live.’

verses.name: Jeremiah 38:3
verses.text: Thus says Yahweh, ‘Surely this city will be given into the hand of the army of the king of Babylon, and he will capture it.’ ”  <div eID="gen20964" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 38:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9065"/><div sID="gen20965" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9065"/>Then the officials said to the king, “Please, this man must be killed, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞because⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “unto thus”</note> he is making slack the hands of <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the soldiers⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the men of the war”</note> who are left in this city, and the hands of all the people, by speaking to them words like these, for this man is not seeking for welfare<note placement="foot">Or “peace”</note> to this people, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞but only⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “but if”</note> for harm.”

verses.name: Jeremiah 38:5
verses.text: And Zedekiah the king said, “Look, he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in your hand, for the king is not able <transChange type="added">to do</transChange> a thing against you.”

verses.name: Jeremiah 38:6
verses.text: So they took Jeremiah and threw him into the pit<note placement="foot">Or “cistern”</note> of Malchiah, the son of the king, which was in the courtyard of the guard. And they let Jeremiah down by ropes. Now in the pit<note placement="foot">Or “cistern”</note> there was no water,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “waters”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞but only⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “but if”</note> mud, and Jeremiah sank in the mud.  <div eID="gen20965" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 38:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9066"/><div sID="gen20966" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9066"/>When Ebed-melech the Cushite, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a eunuch⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a man of a eunuch”</note> who was in the house of the king, heard that they had put Jeremiah into the pit<note placement="foot">Or “cistern”</note>—now the king <transChange type="added">was</transChange> sitting at the Gate of Benjamin—

verses.name: Jeremiah 38:8
verses.text: Ebed-melech went out from the house of the king and spoke to the king, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to say”</note>

verses.name: Jeremiah 38:9
verses.text: “My lord the king, these men have done evil <transChange type="added">in</transChange> all that they have done to Jeremiah the prophet, <transChange type="added">in</transChange> that they have thrown <transChange type="added">him</transChange> into the pit,<note placement="foot">Or “cistern”</note> and he will die <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞there⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in it”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞because of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from the face of”</note> starvation, for there is no longer any bread in the city.”

verses.name: Jeremiah 38:10
verses.text: Then the king commanded Ebed-melech the Cushite, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to say”</note> “Take <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞with you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in your hand”</note> these thirty men and pull Jeremiah the prophet up from the pit<note placement="foot">Or “cistern”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “at not yet”</note> he dies.”  <div eID="gen20966" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 38:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9067"/><div sID="gen20967" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9067"/>So Ebed-melech took the men <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞with him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in his hand”</note> and went to the palace of the king, to a place beneath the storehouse, and he took from there <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞rags⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the rags of rags”</note> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞worn-out clothes⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “rags of ragged clothes”</note> And he let them down into the pit<note placement="foot">Or “cistern”</note> by ropes to Jeremiah.

verses.name: Jeremiah 38:12
verses.text: Then Ebed-melech the Cushite said to Jeremiah, “Please put <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the rags⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “rags of the rags”</note> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞worn-out clothes⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “ragged clothes”</note> under the joints of your arms under the ropes,” and Jeremiah did so.

verses.name: Jeremiah 38:13
verses.text: And they pulled Jeremiah by the ropes and brought him up from the pit.<note placement="foot">Or “cistern”</note> And Jeremiah stayed in the courtyard of the guard.  <div eID="gen20967" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 38:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9068"/><div sID="gen20968" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9068"/>And Zedekiah the king sent and made someone bring Jeremiah the prophet to him, to <transChange type="added">the</transChange> third entrance that <transChange type="added">was</transChange> at the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞temple⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “house”</note> of Yahweh. And the king said to Jeremiah, “I am asking you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞something⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “a thing”</note> you must not hide <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞anything⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a thing”</note> from me.”

verses.name: Jeremiah 38:15
verses.text: And Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, “If I tell you, will you not surely kill me? <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Besides⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “And”</note> if I advise you, you will not listen to me.

verses.name: Jeremiah 38:16
verses.text: So Zedekiah the king swore to Jeremiah in secret, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to say”</note> “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞As Yahweh lives⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “Life of Yahweh”</note> who has made for us this life, I will not kill you and I will not give you into the hand of these men who are seeking your life.”  <div eID="gen20968" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 38:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9069"/><div sID="gen20969" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9069"/>Then Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, “Thus says Yahweh, the God of hosts, the God of Israel, ‘If only you will go surrender to the officials of the king of Babylon, then <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “your life” or “your soul”</note> will live, and this city will not be burned with fire, and you will live, you and your house.

verses.name: Jeremiah 38:18
verses.text: But if you <transChange type="added">do</transChange> not go surrender to the officials of the king of Babylon, then this city will be given into the hand of the Chaldeans, and they will burn it with fire, and you will not escape from their hand.’ ”  <div eID="gen20969" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 38:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9070"/><div sID="gen20970" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9070"/>And Zedekiah the king said to Jeremiah, “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> afraid of the Judeans who have deserted to the Chaldeans, lest they give me into their hand and they abuse me.”

verses.name: Jeremiah 38:20
verses.text: And Jeremiah said, “They will not give <transChange type="added">you over</transChange>. Please obey the voice of Yahweh with regard to what I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> saying to you, and it will go well with you, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “your life” or “your soul”</note> will live.

verses.name: Jeremiah 38:21
verses.text: But if you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> refusing to surrender, this <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the thing that Yahweh has shown me.

verses.name: Jeremiah 38:22
verses.text: Now look, all the women who remain in the house of the king of Judah <transChange type="added">are</transChange> being led out to the officials of the king of Babylon. And look, <transChange type="added">they are</transChange> saying, <div eID="gen20970" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen20971"/> <l level="1" sID="gen20972"/>‘<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Your trusted friends⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “The men of your peace”</note> have misled you,<l eID="gen20972" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen20973"/>and they have prevailed against you.<l eID="gen20973" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen20974"/>Your feet are stuck in the mud,<l eID="gen20974" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen20975"/><transChange type="added">so</transChange> they turned backward.’ <l eID="gen20975" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen20971"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 38:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9071"/><div sID="gen20976" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9071"/>And all your wives and your children <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> led out to the Chaldeans, and you will not escape from their hand, but by the hand of the king of Babylon you will be seized, and this city will burn with fire.”  <div eID="gen20976" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 38:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9072"/><div sID="gen20977" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9072"/>And Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, “No man must know about these words so that you will not die.

verses.name: Jeremiah 38:25
verses.text: And if the officials hear that I have spoken with you, and they come to you and say to you, ‘Please tell us what you said to the king. You must not conceal <transChange type="added">it</transChange> from us so that we will not kill you. And what did the king say to you?’

verses.name: Jeremiah 38:26
verses.text: Then you shall say to them, ‘I <transChange type="added">was</transChange> presenting my plea <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the face of”</note> the king, to not cause me to return <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the house of Jonathan to die there.’ ”

verses.name: Jeremiah 38:27
verses.text: And all the officials came to Jeremiah and questioned him, and he informed them like all these words that the king commanded. So they fell silent, for the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞conversation⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “word”</note> was not heard.

verses.name: Jeremiah 38:28
verses.text: And Jeremiah stayed in the courtyard of the guard until <transChange type="added">the</transChange> day that Jerusalem was captured. And it happened that Jerusalem was captured.<note placement="foot"><reference osisRef="Jer.38.28b">Jeremiah 38:28b </reference>in the Hebrew Bible is 39:1a in the English Bible</note>  <chapter eID="Jer.38"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 39:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9073"/><title type="x-s">The Fall of Jerusalem</title> <div sID="gen20978" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9073"/>In the ninth year of Zedekiah, the king of Judah, in the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon and all his army came against Jerusalem and laid siege to it.

verses.name: Jeremiah 39:2
verses.text: In the eleventh year of Zedekiah, in the fourth month, on <transChange type="added">the</transChange> ninth <transChange type="added">day</transChange> of the month, the city was taken by assault.

verses.name: Jeremiah 39:3
verses.text: And all the officials of the king of Babylon came and sat in the Middle Gate: Nergal-sharezer, Samgar-nebo, Sarsechim <transChange type="added">the</transChange> chief officer, Nergal-sharezer <transChange type="added">the</transChange> high official, with all the rest of the officials of the king of Babylon.

verses.name: Jeremiah 39:4
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it was”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞when⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “as that”</note> Zedekiah the king of Judah saw them, and all <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the soldiers⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the men of the war”</note> <transChange type="added">with him</transChange>, they fled and went out <transChange type="added">at</transChange> night from the city <transChange type="added">by</transChange> the way of the garden of the king through <transChange type="added">the</transChange> gate between the walls. And they went out toward the Jordan Valley.

verses.name: Jeremiah 39:5
verses.text: But the army of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Chaldeans pursued after them and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho. And they took him and brought him up to Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon <transChange type="added">at</transChange> Riblah in the land of Hamath. And he pronounced <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞sentence⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “judgments”</note> on him.

verses.name: Jeremiah 39:6
verses.text: And the king of Babylon slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah at Riblah before his eyes. The king of Babylon also slaughtered all the nobles of Judah.

verses.name: Jeremiah 39:7
verses.text: Then he blinded the eyes of Zedekiah and tied him up with bronze fetters to bring him <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Babylon.

verses.name: Jeremiah 39:8
verses.text: And the Chaldeans burned the palace<note placement="foot">Or “house”</note> of the king and the houses<note placement="foot">Hebrew “house”</note> of the people with fire and broke down the walls of Jerusalem.  <div eID="gen20978" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 39:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9074"/><div sID="gen20979" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9074"/>Then the rest of the people who were left in the city, and those deserting who had deserted to him, and the rest of the people who remained, Nebuzaradan, <transChange type="added">the</transChange> captain of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> guard,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “guards”</note> deported <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Babylon.

verses.name: Jeremiah 39:10
verses.text: And some of the poor people, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who had nothing⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “who there was not for them something”</note> Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “guards”</note> left in the land of Judah. And he gave them vineyards and fields on that day.  <div eID="gen20979" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 39:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9075"/><div sID="gen20980" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9075"/>And Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon commanded concerning Jeremiah <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞through⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in the hand of”</note> Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “guards”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to say”</note>

verses.name: Jeremiah 39:12
verses.text: “Take him and set your eyes on him. And you must not do something bad to him, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞but only⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “but if”</note> that which he speaks to you, so do with him.”

verses.name: Jeremiah 39:13
verses.text: So Nebuzaradan, <transChange type="added">the</transChange> captain of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> guard,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “guards”</note> sent word, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞along with⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and”</note> Nebushazban <transChange type="added">the</transChange> chief officer, and Nergal-sharezer <transChange type="added">the</transChange> high official, and all the chief officers of the king of Babylon.

verses.name: Jeremiah 39:14
verses.text: And they sent and took Jeremiah from the courtyard of the guard and gave him to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, to take him to the house, so he stayed in the midst of the people.  <div eID="gen20980" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 39:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9076"/><title type="x-s">Ebed-melech is Rewarded for His Faith</title> <div sID="gen20981" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9076"/>And the word of Yahweh came to Jeremiah at his confinement in the courtyard of the guard, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to say”</note>

verses.name: Jeremiah 39:16
verses.text: “Go and say to Ebed-melech the Cushite, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to say”</note> ‘Thus says Yahweh of hosts, the God of Israel: “Look, I am about to bring my words to pass against this city for evil and not for good. And they will be <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the face of you”</note> on that day.

verses.name: Jeremiah 39:17
verses.text: But I will rescue you on that day,” <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞declares⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a declaration of”</note> Yahweh, “and you will not be given into the hand of the men <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞of whom you are frightened⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “who you are frightened from the face of them”</note>

verses.name: Jeremiah 39:18
verses.text: For surely I will save you, and you will not fall by the sword. But your life will be for you as booty because you have trusted in me,” <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞declares⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a declaration of”</note> Yahweh.’ ”  <chapter eID="Jer.39"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 40:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9077"/><title type="x-s">Jeremiah Decides to Remain in the Land</title> <div sID="gen20982" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9077"/>The word that came to Jeremiah from Yahweh after Nebuzaradan, <transChange type="added">the</transChange> captain of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> guard,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “guards”</note> had let him go from Ramah, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞where he had been taken⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “at his taking him</note> bound in chains in the midst of all the exiles<note placement="foot">Hebrew “exile”</note> of Jerusalem and Judah who were being deported <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Babylon.

verses.name: Jeremiah 40:2
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">the</transChange> captain of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> guard<note placement="foot">Hebrew “guards”</note> took Jeremiah and said to him, “Yahweh your God threatened this disaster to this place,

verses.name: Jeremiah 40:3
verses.text: and <transChange type="added">now</transChange> he has brought <transChange type="added">it about</transChange>,<note placement="foot">Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and Yahweh has done <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞just as⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “as that”</note> he threatened. Because you sinned against Yahweh and did not listen to his voice, so this thing <transChange type="added">has</transChange> happened to you.

verses.name: Jeremiah 40:4
verses.text: And so then look, I have released you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞today⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the day”</note> from the chains that were on your hands.<note placement="foot">Hebrew “hand”</note> If it is good in your eyes to come with me to Babylon, then come, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I will take care of you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “I will place my eye on you”</note> But if it is bad in your eyes to come with me to Babylon, then refrain. Look, the whole land is <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “to the face of you”</note> To <transChange type="added">wherever it is</transChange> good and right in your eyes to go, <transChange type="added">then</transChange> go there.”

verses.name: Jeremiah 40:5
verses.text: While he still had not turned back, <transChange type="added">Nebuzaradan</transChange> added, “Return to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon has appointed <transChange type="added">in an official position</transChange> over the towns of Judah, and stay with him in the midst of the people. Or to <transChange type="added">wherever it is</transChange> right in your eyes to go, <transChange type="added">then</transChange> go <transChange type="added">there</transChange>.”<note placement="foot">Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> Then the captain of the guard<note placement="foot">Hebrew “guards”</note> gave him an allowance of provisions and a present, and let him go.

verses.name: Jeremiah 40:6
verses.text: So Jeremiah went to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, <transChange type="added">at</transChange> Mizpah and stayed with him in the midst of the people who were left in the land.  <div eID="gen20982" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 40:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9078"/><title type="x-s">The Assassination of Gedaliah</title> <div sID="gen20983" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9078"/>When all the commanders of the armies who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in the open country and their men heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah the son of Ahikam <transChange type="added">in an official position</transChange> in the land, and that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he had put him in charge of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “he had appointed to him”</note> men, and women, and little children, and of the poor of the land, of <transChange type="added">all those</transChange> who had not been deported <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Babylon,

verses.name: Jeremiah 40:8
verses.text: then they went to Gedaliah <transChange type="added">at</transChange> Mizpah—Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and Johanan, and Jehonathan the son of Kareah, and Seraiah the son of Tanhumeth, and the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jezaniah the son of the Maacathite, they and their men.

verses.name: Jeremiah 40:9
verses.text: And Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, swore to them and to their men, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to say”</note> “You must not be afraid of serving the Chaldeans. Stay in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will go well with you.

verses.name: Jeremiah 40:10
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞As for me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “And I”</note> look, I am staying at Mizpah to represent you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the face of”</note> the Chaldeans who come to us. But you, gather wine and summer fruit and oil, and put <transChange type="added">them</transChange> in your vessels, and live in your towns that you have seized.”

verses.name: Jeremiah 40:11
verses.text: And also all the Judeans who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in Moab, and among the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons of Ammon”</note> and in Edom, and who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in all the lands, <transChange type="added">when</transChange> they heard that the king of Babylon had given a remnant to Judah and that he had appointed Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, <transChange type="added">in an official position</transChange> over them,

verses.name: Jeremiah 40:12
verses.text: then all the Judeans returned from all the places <transChange type="added">to</transChange> which they were scattered. And they came <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the land of Judah, to Gedaliah <transChange type="added">at</transChange> Mizpah, and they gathered wine and summer fruit that yielded <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in great abundance⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “very numerous”</note>  <div eID="gen20983" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 40:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9079"/><div sID="gen20984" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9079"/>And Johanan the son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in the open country came to Gedaliah <transChange type="added">at</transChange> Mizpah

verses.name: Jeremiah 40:14
verses.text: and said to him, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Are you at all aware⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “know you know”</note> that Baalis, the king of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “sons of Ammon”</note> has sent Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, to kill you?” But Gedaliah the son of Ahikam would not believe them.

verses.name: Jeremiah 40:15
verses.text: Then Johanan the son of Kareah said to Gedaliah in secrecy at Mizpah, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to say”</note> “Please let me go and kill Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞nobody⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “not a man”</note> will know. Why should he kill you, so that all of Judah who are gathered to you will be scattered, and the remnant of Judah will perish?”

verses.name: Jeremiah 40:16
verses.text: But Gedaliah the son of Ahikam said to Johanan the son of Kareah, “You must not do this thing, for you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> telling a lie about Ishmael.”  <chapter eID="Jer.40"/> <div eID="gen20984" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 41:1
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it was”</note> in the seventh month Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, the son of Elishama, from the offspring of the kingship, and one of the chief officers of the king, came to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam at Mizpah, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞along with⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and”</note> ten men. And they ate bread together there at Mizpah.

verses.name: Jeremiah 41:2
verses.text: And Ishmael the son of Nethaniah got up, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞along with⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and”</note> the ten men who were with him, and they struck Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, with the sword and killed him whom the king of Babylon had appointed <transChange type="added">in an official position</transChange> over the land.

verses.name: Jeremiah 41:3
verses.text: Then Ishmael killed all the Judeans who were with Gedaliah at Mizpah, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞along with⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and”</note> the Chaldeans who were found there, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the soldiers⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the men of the war”</note>  <div eID="gen20985" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 41:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9080"/><title type="x-s">The Massacre of the Mourners</title> <div sID="gen20986" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9080"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it was”</note> on the second day of the killing of Gedaliah—and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞no one⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “not a man”</note> knew—

verses.name: Jeremiah 41:5
verses.text: then men came from Shechem, from Shiloh, and from Samaria, eighty men <transChange type="added">with</transChange> shaven beards<note placement="foot">Hebrew “beard”</note> and torn garments, who had cut themselves with blades, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞having⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and”</note> grain offerings<note placement="foot">Hebrew “grain offering”</note> and frankincense in their hands<note placement="foot">Hebrew “hand”</note> to bring to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞temple⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “house”</note> of Yahweh.

verses.name: Jeremiah 41:6
verses.text: And Ishmael the son of Nethaniah came out to meet them from Mizpah, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞weeping as he came⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “coming he came and weeping”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it was”</note> as <transChange type="added">he was</transChange> meeting them, he said to them, “Come to Gedaliah, the son of Ahikam.”

verses.name: Jeremiah 41:7
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “And it was”</note> the moment of their coming to the middle of the city, then Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞along with⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and”</note> the men who were with him, slaughtered<note placement="foot">The Hebrew verb is singular</note> them and threw them to the middle of the pit.<note placement="foot">Or “cistern”</note>

verses.name: Jeremiah 41:8
verses.text: But ten men were found among them, and they said to Ishmael, “You must not kill us, for <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞we have⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “there is to us”</note> hidden treasures in the field, wheat, and barley, and oil, and honey. So he refrained and he did not kill them in the midst of their fellow countrymen.

verses.name: Jeremiah 41:9
verses.text: Now the pit<note placement="foot">Or “cistern”</note> into which Ishmael threw all the corpses of the men whom he had killed <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞along with⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by the hand of”</note> Gedaliah <transChange type="added">was the same one</transChange> that King Asa had made because of Baasha the king of Israel, <transChange type="added">who was</transChange> against him. Ishmael the son of Nethaniah filled <transChange type="added">it with</transChange> the slain ones.  <div eID="gen20986" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 41:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9081"/><div sID="gen20987" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9081"/>Then Ishmael took captive all the rest of the people who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in Mizpah, the daughters of the king and all the people who were left at Mizpah, <transChange type="added">over</transChange> whom Nebuzaradan, <transChange type="added">the</transChange> captain of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> guard,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “guards”</note> had appointed Gedaliah the son of Ahikam. And Ishmael took them captive and set out to cross over to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons of Ammon”</note>  <div eID="gen20987" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 41:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9082"/><div sID="gen20988" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9082"/>When Johanan the son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him, heard<note placement="foot">The Hebrew verb is singular</note> all the evil that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah had done,

verses.name: Jeremiah 41:12
verses.text: then they took all the men and went to fight against Ishmael the son of Nethaniah. And they met him at <transChange type="added">the</transChange> great pool that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in Gibeon.

verses.name: Jeremiah 41:13
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “And it was”</note> the moment that all the people who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with Ishmael saw Johanan the son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him, they were glad.

verses.name: Jeremiah 41:14
verses.text: So all the people whom Ishmael had taken captive from Mizpah turned around and returned and went to Johanan the son of Kareah.

verses.name: Jeremiah 41:15
verses.text: But Ishmael the son of Nethaniah escaped with eight men <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from the face of”</note> Johanan, and they went to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Ammonites⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “sons of Ammon”</note>  <div eID="gen20988" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 41:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9083"/><div sID="gen20989" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9083"/>Then Johanan the son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him took from Mizpah all the rest of the people whom he had recovered from Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, after he had killed Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, strong men, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞soldiers⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the men of the war”</note> and women, and little children, and eunuchs whom he brought back from Gibeon.

verses.name: Jeremiah 41:17
verses.text: And they set out and stayed at the lodging place of Chimham that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> near Bethlehem, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞intending⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “going”</note> to go <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Egypt

verses.name: Jeremiah 41:18
verses.text: because of the Chaldeans. For they were afraid <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞of them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “from the face of them”</note> because Ishmael the son of Nethaniah had killed Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had appointed <transChange type="added">in an official position</transChange> over the land.  <chapter eID="Jer.41"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 42:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9084"/><title type="x-s">The Remnant Asks Jeremiah to Pray to Yahweh for Direction</title> <div sID="gen20990" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9084"/>Then all the commanders of the armies, and Johanan the son of Kareah, and Jezaniah the son of Hoshaiah, and all the people from <transChange type="added">the</transChange> smallest to <transChange type="added">the</transChange> greatest, approached

verses.name: Jeremiah 42:2
verses.text: and said to Jeremiah the prophet, “May our plea please fall <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to the face of you”</note> and pray for us to Yahweh your God, for all this remnant, for we are left <transChange type="added">but</transChange> a few of many, as your eyes <transChange type="added">are</transChange> seeing us.

verses.name: Jeremiah 42:3
verses.text: And let Yahweh your God inform us the way in which we should go and the thing that we should do.”

verses.name: Jeremiah 42:4
verses.text: And Jeremiah the prophet said to them, “I have heard. Look, I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> going to pray to Yahweh your God according to your words, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞and then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and it will happen”</note> all the words<note placement="foot">Hebrew “word”</note> that Yahweh answers you I will tell you; I will not withhold from you a word.”

verses.name: Jeremiah 42:5
verses.text: Then they said to Jeremiah, “May Yahweh be against us as <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a true and faithful witness⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a witness of faithfulness and trustworthy”</note> if we do not do according to all the words<note placement="foot">Hebrew “word”</note> that Yahweh sends you for us.

verses.name: Jeremiah 42:6
verses.text: Whether good or bad, we will listen to the voice of Yahweh our God, <transChange type="added">to</transChange> whom we <transChange type="added">are</transChange> sending you, so that it may go well with us when we listen to the voice of Yahweh our God.”  <div eID="gen20990" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 42:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9085"/><title type="x-s">The Remnant Rejects the Word of Yahweh</title> <div sID="gen20991" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9085"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “And it was”</note> at <transChange type="added">the</transChange> end of ten days the word of Yahweh came to Jeremiah.

verses.name: Jeremiah 42:8
verses.text: And he summoned Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the commanders of the armies who <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him, and all the people from <transChange type="added">the</transChange> smallest to <transChange type="added">the</transChange> greatest,

verses.name: Jeremiah 42:9
verses.text: and said to them, “Thus says Yahweh, the God of Israel, to whom you sent me to cause your plea to fall <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>:<note placement="foot">Literally “to the face of him”</note>

verses.name: Jeremiah 42:10
verses.text: ‘If only you will stay in this land, then I will build you and I will not tear <transChange type="added">you</transChange> down, and I will plant you and I will not pluck <transChange type="added">you</transChange> up, for I relent of the disaster that I have brought to you.

verses.name: Jeremiah 42:11
verses.text: You must not be afraid <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from the face of”</note> the king of Babylon whom you are <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞afraid of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “in fear from the presence of him”</note> You must not be afraid of him,’ <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞declares⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a declaration of”</note> Yahweh, ‘for I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> with you to save you and to deliver you from his hand.

verses.name: Jeremiah 42:12
verses.text: And I will show you compassion, and he will have compassion on you and will restore you to your soil.  <div eID="gen20991" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 42:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9086"/><div sID="gen20992" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9086"/>But if you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> saying, “We will not stay in this land,” <transChange type="added">so as to</transChange> not listen to the voice of Yahweh your God,

verses.name: Jeremiah 42:14
verses.text: saying, “No, for we will go <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the land of Egypt where we will not see war, and we will not hear <transChange type="added">the</transChange> sound of a horn, and we will not be hungry for bread, and there we will stay,”

verses.name: Jeremiah 42:15
verses.text: then <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞therefore⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to thus”</note> hear the word of Yahweh, O remnant of Judah. Thus says Yahweh of hosts, the God of Israel: “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞If you are determined⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “If you indeed set your face”</note> to go <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Egypt, and you go to dwell as aliens there,

verses.name: Jeremiah 42:16
verses.text: then it will be <transChange type="added">that</transChange> the sword that you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> in fear of will overtake you there in the land of Egypt, and the famine that you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> anxious of will pursue after you there <transChange type="added">into</transChange> Egypt, and there you will die.

verses.name: Jeremiah 42:17
verses.text: So all the people who <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞are determined⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “have set their faces”</note> to go <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Egypt to dwell as aliens there will die by the sword, by the famine, and by the plague, and there will not be for them an escapee or a survivor from the disaster that I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> bringing upon them.”

verses.name: Jeremiah 42:18
verses.text: For thus says Yahweh of hosts, the God of Israel: “As my anger and my wrath were poured out on the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so my wrath will pour out on you at your going <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Egypt, and you will become a curse, and a horror, and a curse <transChange type="added">formula</transChange>, and a disgrace, and you will no longer see this place.” ’  <div eID="gen20992" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 42:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9087"/><div sID="gen20993" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9087"/>Yahweh has spoken to you, O remnant of Judah, ‘You must not go <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Egypt.’ You must certainly know that I have warned you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞today⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the day”</note>

verses.name: Jeremiah 42:20
verses.text: that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you have made a fatal mistake⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “you have caused them to err for your lives”</note> for you sent me to Yahweh your God, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to say”</note> ‘Pray for us to Yahweh our God, and all that Yahweh our God says, so tell us and we will do it.’<note placement="foot">Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Jeremiah 42:21
verses.text: So I have told you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞today⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the day”</note> and you have not listened to the voice of Yahweh your God, or of <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞anything⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “all”</note> that he sent me for you.

verses.name: Jeremiah 42:22
verses.text: Now then, certainly you must know that by the sword, by the famine, and by the plague you will die in the place where you desire to go, to dwell as aliens there.”  <chapter eID="Jer.42"/> <div eID="gen20993" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 43:1
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And then⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “And it was”</note> when Jeremiah had finished speaking to all the people all the words of Yahweh their God, for which Yahweh their God had sent him to them with all these words,

verses.name: Jeremiah 43:2
verses.text: Azariah the son of Hoshaiah, and Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the insolent men spoke,<note placement="foot">The Hebrew verb is singular</note> saying to Jeremiah, “You are telling a lie! Yahweh our God did not send you, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to say”</note> ‘You must not go <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Egypt to dwell as aliens there.’

verses.name: Jeremiah 43:3
verses.text: But Baruch the son of Neriah <transChange type="added">is</transChange> inciting you against us in order to give us into the hand of the Chaldeans, to kill us and to deport us <transChange type="added">to</transChange> Babylon.”  <div eID="gen20994" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 43:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9088"/><div sID="gen20995" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9088"/>So Johanan the son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies, and all the people did not listen<note placement="foot">The Hebrew verb is singular</note> to the voice of Yahweh to stay in the land of Judah.

verses.name: Jeremiah 43:5
verses.text: But Johanan the son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies took<note placement="foot">The Hebrew verb is singular</note> all the remnant of Judah who had returned from all the nations <transChange type="added">to</transChange> which they had been scattered to dwell as aliens in the land of Judah—

verses.name: Jeremiah 43:6
verses.text: the men, and the women, and the little children, and the daughters of the king, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞everyone⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “all of the person”</note> whom Nebuzaradan the captain of the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞guard⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Hebrew “guards”</note> had left with Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, and Jeremiah the prophet, and Baruch the son of Neriah—

verses.name: Jeremiah 43:7
verses.text: and they came <transChange type="added">into</transChange> the land of Egypt, for they did not listen to the voice of Yahweh. And they came up to Tahpanhes.  <div eID="gen20995" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 43:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9089"/><title type="x-s">The Throne of Nebuchadnezzar Will be Set Up at Tahpanhes</title> <div sID="gen20996" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9089"/>And the word of Yahweh came to Jeremiah in Tahpanhes, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,

verses.name: Jeremiah 43:9
verses.text: “Take in your hands<note placement="foot">Hebrew “hand”</note> large stones and bury them in the mortar in the clay floor that is at the entrance of the palace<note placement="foot">Or “house”</note> of Pharaoh in Tahpanhes before the eyes of the people<note placement="foot">Or “men”</note> of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> Judeans,

verses.name: Jeremiah 43:10
verses.text: and say to them, ‘Thus says Yahweh of hosts, the God of Israel: “Look, I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> going to send and take Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon, my servant, and I will set his throne above these stones that I have hidden. And he will spread out his canopy over them.

verses.name: Jeremiah 43:11
verses.text: And he will come and ravage the land of Egypt, <transChange type="added">and deliver those</transChange> who <transChange type="added">are appointed</transChange> for the plague, to the plague, and <transChange type="added">those</transChange> who <transChange type="added">are appointed</transChange> for the captivity, to the captivity, and <transChange type="added">those</transChange> who <transChange type="added">are appointed</transChange> for the sword, to the sword.

verses.name: Jeremiah 43:12
verses.text: Then he will kindle a fire in the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞temples⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “houses”</note> of the gods of Egypt, and he will burn them and take them captive. And he will wrap up the land of Egypt just as the shepherd wraps up his cloak. And he will go forth from there in peace.

verses.name: Jeremiah 43:13
verses.text: And he will break the stone pillars of Heliopolis, which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in the land of Egypt. And he will burn the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞temples⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “houses”</note> of the gods of Egypt with fire.” ’ ”  <chapter eID="Jer.43"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 44:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9090"/><title type="x-s">A Message of Rebuke for the Rebellious Remnant</title> <div sID="gen20997" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9090"/>The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the Judeans who were living in the land of Egypt, who were living at Migdol, and Tahpanhes, and Memphis, and in the land of Pathros, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to say”</note>

verses.name: Jeremiah 44:2
verses.text: “Thus says Yahweh of hosts, the God of Israel: ‘You yourselves have seen all the disaster that I have brought on Jerusalem, and on all the towns of Judah. And look, they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> a site of ruins this day, and there is not in them an inhabitant,

verses.name: Jeremiah 44:3
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞because of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from the face of”</note> their wickedness that they committed to provoke me to anger by going to make smoke offerings, serving other gods whom they had not known, neither they, you, or your ancestors.<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note>

verses.name: Jeremiah 44:4
verses.text: And I sent to you all my servants the prophets, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞sending over and over again⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “doing early and sending”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to say”</note> “Please, you must not do this detestable thing that I hate.”

verses.name: Jeremiah 44:5
verses.text: But they did not listen and they did not incline their ears<note placement="foot">Hebrew “ear”</note> to turn back from their wickedness, to not make smoke offerings to other gods.

verses.name: Jeremiah 44:6
verses.text: So my wrath and my anger were poured out<note placement="foot">The Hebrew verb is singular</note> and burned<note placement="foot">The Hebrew verb is singular</note> in the towns of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem, and they became as a site of ruins, as a desolation, as <transChange type="added">they are</transChange> this day.’  <div eID="gen20997" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 44:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9091"/><div sID="gen20998" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9091"/>So then, thus says Yahweh, the God of hosts, the God of Israel, ‘Why <transChange type="added">are</transChange> you doing great harm to <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞yourselves⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “your lives”</note> to cut off for yourselves man and woman, child and suckling, from the midst of Judah, to not leave over for yourselves a remnant,

verses.name: Jeremiah 44:8
verses.text: provoking me to anger with the works of your hands, to make smoke offerings to other gods in the land of Egypt where you <transChange type="added">have</transChange> come to dwell as aliens, so as to cut off yourselves, and so that you are becoming as a curse, and as a disgrace among all the nations of the earth?

verses.name: Jeremiah 44:9
verses.text: Have you forgotten the wicked things of your ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> and the wicked things of the kings of Judah, and the wicked things of their wives, and your wicked things, and the wicked things of your wives, which they committed in the land of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?

verses.name: Jeremiah 44:10
verses.text: They have not shown contrition up to this day, and they have not shown reverence, and they have not walked in my law and in my statutes that I set <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the face of you”</note> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the face of”</note> your ancestors.’<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note>  <div eID="gen20998" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 44:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9092"/><div sID="gen20999" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9092"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Therefore⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “To thus”</note> thus says Yahweh of hosts, the God of Israel: ‘Look, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I am determined to bring disaster on you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “I am setting my face against you for disaster”</note> even to exterminate all Judah.

verses.name: Jeremiah 44:12
verses.text: And I will take <transChange type="added">away</transChange> the remnant of Judah <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who are determined⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “who set their faces”</note> to come <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the land of Egypt to dwell as aliens there, and everyone will perish. They will fall in the land of Egypt by the sword; they will perish by the famine, from <transChange type="added">the</transChange> smallest to <transChange type="added">the</transChange> greatest. By the sword and by the famine they will die and become as a curse, as a horror, and as a curse, and as a disgrace.

verses.name: Jeremiah 44:13
verses.text: So I will punish those who live in the land of Egypt just as I have punished Jerusalem, with the sword, with the famine, and with the plague.

verses.name: Jeremiah 44:14
verses.text: And there will not be a survivor or an escapee of the remnant of Judah, those who have come to dwell as an alien there in the land of Egypt, to return <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the land of Judah where they <transChange type="added">are</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞longing⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “lifting up their soul”</note> to return to dwell there, for they will not turn back, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞but only⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “but if”</note> <transChange type="added">some</transChange> survivors.’ ”  <div eID="gen20999" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 44:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9093"/><div sID="gen21000" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9093"/>Then all the men who knew that their wives <transChange type="added">were</transChange> making smoke offerings to other gods, and all the women who stood <transChange type="added">by</transChange>, a great assembly, and all the people who lived in the land of Egypt in Pathros, answered Jeremiah, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to say”</note>

verses.name: Jeremiah 44:16
verses.text: “<transChange type="added">Concerning</transChange> the word that you have spoken to us in the name of Yahweh, we <transChange type="added">are</transChange> not going to listen to you!

verses.name: Jeremiah 44:17
verses.text: But certainly we will do <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞everything⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “all the word”</note> that went out from our mouths,<note placement="foot">Hebrew “mouth”</note> to make smoke offerings to the queen of heaven and to pour out to her libations just as we did, we, and our ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> our kings, and our officials, in the towns of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem, for then <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞we had enough to eat⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “we satisfied ourselves with food”</note> and we were well-off, and we did not see disaster.

verses.name: Jeremiah 44:18
verses.text: But <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞since⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from”</note> we stopped making smoke offerings to the queen of heaven and pouring out libations to her, we have lacked everything, and by the sword and by the famine we have perished.

verses.name: Jeremiah 44:19
verses.text: And indeed, <transChange type="added">when</transChange> we <transChange type="added">were</transChange> making smoke offerings to the queen of heaven and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞pouring out⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to pour out”</note> to her libations, was it not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞with the consent of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from apart from”</note> our husbands that we made for her sacrificial cakes <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞marked with her image⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to the copying of her”</note> and we poured out to her libations?”  <div eID="gen21000" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 44:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9094"/><div sID="gen21001" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9094"/>Then Jeremiah said to all the people, to the men and to the women, and to all the people who answered him a word, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞saying⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to say”</note>

verses.name: Jeremiah 44:21
verses.text: “The offering that you made, smoke offerings in the towns of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem, you, and your ancestors,<note placement="foot">Or “fathers”</note> your kings, and your officials, and the people of the land, did not Yahweh remember them, and did it not come to his <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞mind⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?<note placement="foot">Literally “heart”</note>

verses.name: Jeremiah 44:22
