verses.text: And he will bring back<note placement="foot">Or “And he will restore”</note> <transChange type="added">the</transChange> hearts of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> fathers to <transChange type="added">the</transChange> sons, and the hearts of <transChange type="added">the</transChange> sons to their fathers, so that I will not come and strike the land <transChange type="added">with</transChange> a ban.”  <chapter eID="Mal.4"/> <div eID="gen25652" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen25637" osisID="Mal" type="book"/>

verses.name: Matthew 1:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10500"/><title type="x-s">The Genealogy of Jesus Christ</title> <div sID="gen25654" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10500"/>The book of the genealogy of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham.  <div eID="gen25654" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 1:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10501"/><div sID="gen25655" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10501"/>Abraham became the father of Isaac, and Isaac became the father of Jacob, and Jacob became the father of Judah and his brothers,

verses.name: Matthew 1:3
verses.text: and Judah became the father of Perez and Zerah by Tamar, and Perez became the father of Hezron, and Hezron became the father of Aram,<note placement="foot">Although the Greek text reads “Aram,” many English versions substitute the Old Testament form of the name, “Ram” (cf. <reference osisRef="1Chr.2.9">1 Chr 2:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ruth.4.19">Ruth 4:19</reference>), here and in the following verse</note>

verses.name: Matthew 1:4
verses.text: and Aram became the father of Amminadab, and Amminadab became the father of Nahshon, and Nahshon became the father of Salmon,

verses.name: Matthew 1:5
verses.text: and Salmon became the father of Boaz by Rahab, and Boaz became the father of Obed by Ruth, and Obed became the father of Jesse,

verses.name: Matthew 1:6
verses.text: and Jesse became the father of David the king. <div eID="gen25655" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25656" type="x-p"/> And David became the father of Solomon by the <transChange type="added">wife</transChange><note placement="foot">*The word “wife” is not in the Greek text, but is implied idiomatically</note> of Uriah,

verses.name: Matthew 1:7
verses.text: and Solomon became the father of Rehoboam, and Rehoboam became the father of Abijah, and Abijah became the father of Asa,<note placement="foot">Greek “Asaph,” alternately spelled “Asa” in many English versions here and in the following verse (cf. <reference osisRef="1Chr.3.10">1 Chr 3:10</reference>)</note>

verses.name: Matthew 1:8
verses.text: and Asa became the father of Jehoshaphat,<note placement="foot">Greek “Josaphat”; alternately spelled “Jehoshaphat” in many English versions</note> and Jehoshaphat became the father of Joram, and Joram became the father of Uzziah,

verses.name: Matthew 1:9
verses.text: and Uzziah became the father of Jotham, and Jotham became the father of Ahaz, and Ahaz became the father of Hezekiah,

verses.name: Matthew 1:10
verses.text: and Hezekiah became the father of Manasseh, and Manasseh became the father of Amon,<note placement="foot">The earliest and best Greek manuscripts read “Amos,” but many English versions use the Old Testament form of the name here, “Amon” (cf. <reference osisRef="2Kgs.21.18">2 Kgs 21:18</reference>)</note> and Amon became the father of Josiah,

verses.name: Matthew 1:11
verses.text: and Josiah became the father of Jechoniah and his brothers, at the time of the deportation to Babylon.  <div eID="gen25656" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 1:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10502"/><div sID="gen25657" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10502"/>And after the deportation to Babylon, Jechoniah became the father of Shealtiel,<note placement="foot">Greek “Salathiel,” but many English versions use the Old Testament form of the name here, “Shealtiel” (cf. <reference osisRef="Ezra.3.2">Ezra 3:2</reference>)</note> and Shealtiel became the father of Zerubbabel,

verses.name: Matthew 1:13
verses.text: and Zerubbabel became the father of Abiud, and Abiud became the father of Eliakim, and Eliakim became the father of Azor,

verses.name: Matthew 1:14
verses.text: and Azor became the father of Zadok, and Zadok became the father of Achim, and Achim became the father of Eliud,

verses.name: Matthew 1:15
verses.text: and Eliud became the father of Eleazar, and Eleazar became the father of Matthan, and Matthan became the father of Jacob,

verses.name: Matthew 1:16
verses.text: and Jacob became the father of Joseph, the husband of Mary by whom<note placement="foot">The Greek relative pronoun is feminine gender and thus refers only to Mary, not Joseph</note> was born Jesus, who is called Christ.  <div eID="gen25657" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 1:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10503"/><div sID="gen25658" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10503"/>Therefore all the generations from Abraham to David <transChange type="added">are</transChange> fourteen generations, and from David to the deportation to Babylon <transChange type="added">are</transChange> fourteen generations, and from the deportation to Babylon to the Christ <transChange type="added">are</transChange> fourteen generations.  <div eID="gen25658" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 1:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10504"/><title type="x-s">The Birth of Jesus Christ</title> <div sID="gen25659" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10504"/>Now the birth of Jesus Christ occurred in this way. His mother Mary had been betrothed to Joseph, <transChange type="added">but</transChange> before they came together, she was found <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to be pregnant⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to have in the womb”</note> by the Holy Spirit.

verses.name: Matthew 1:19
verses.text: So Joseph her husband, being righteous and not wanting to disgrace her, intended to divorce her secretly.

verses.name: Matthew 1:20
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“considering”)</note> he was considering these things, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream, saying, “Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary <transChange type="added">as</transChange> your wife, for what has been conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit.

verses.name: Matthew 1:21
verses.text: And she will give birth to a son, and you will call his name ‘Jesus,’ because he will save his people from their sins.”

verses.name: Matthew 1:22
verses.text: Now all this happened in order that what was spoken by the Lord through the prophet would be fulfilled, saying,  <div eID="gen25659" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 1:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10505"/><lg sID="gen25660"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25661"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10505"/>“Behold, the virgin <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞will become pregnant⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “will have in the womb”</note> and will give birth to a son,<l eID="gen25661" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25662"/>and they will call his name Emmanuel,”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.7.14">Isa 7:14</reference></note><l eID="gen25662" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen25660"/> <div sID="gen25663" type="x-p"/> which is translated, “God with us.”<note placement="foot">An allusion to <reference osisRef="Isa.8.8">Isa 8:8</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.8.10">10 </reference>in the Greek OT (LXX)</note>

verses.name: Matthew 1:24
verses.text: And Joseph, <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“woke up”) which is understood as temporal</note> woke up from sleep, did as the angel of the Lord commanded him, and he took his wife

verses.name: Matthew 1:25
verses.text: and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞did not have sexual relations with⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “did not know”</note> her until she gave birth to a son. And he called his name Jesus.  <chapter eID="Matt.1"/>

verses.name: Matthew 2:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10506"/><title type="x-s">Wise Men Visit Jesus</title> <div sID="gen25664" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10506"/>Now <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was born”)</note> Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of Herod the king, behold, wise men from the east came to Jerusalem,

verses.name: Matthew 2:2
verses.text: saying, “Where is the one who has been born king of the Jews? For we have seen his star at its rising<note placement="foot">Or, “when it rose”; traditionally rendered “in the east” by many English versions</note> and have come to worship him.”

verses.name: Matthew 2:3
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> King Herod heard it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him,

verses.name: Matthew 2:4
verses.text: and <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“calling together”) which is understood as temporal</note> calling together all the chief priests and scribes of the people, he inquired from them where the Christ was to be born.

verses.name: Matthew 2:5
verses.text: So they said to him, “In Bethlehem of Judea, for thus it is written by the prophet,  <div eID="gen25664" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 2:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10507"/><lg sID="gen25665"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25666"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10507"/>‘And you, Bethlehem, land of Judah,<l eID="gen25666" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25667"/>are by no means least among the rulers of Judah,<l eID="gen25667" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25668"/>for from you will go out a ruler<l eID="gen25668" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25669"/>who will shepherd my people Israel.’ ”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Mic.5.2">Mic 5:2</reference></note> <l eID="gen25669" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen25665"/>

verses.name: Matthew 2:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10508"/><div sID="gen25670" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10508"/>Then Herod secretly summoned the wise men <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“summoned”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> determined precisely from them the time when<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“appeared”)</note> the star appeared.

verses.name: Matthew 2:8
verses.text: And he sent them to Bethlehem <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“sent”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “Go, inquire carefully concerning the child, and when you have found him, report to me so that I also may come and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“may come”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> worship him.”

verses.name: Matthew 2:9
verses.text: <transChange type="added">After</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“listened to”) which is understood as temporal</note> they listened to the king, they went out, and behold, the star which they had seen at its rising<note placement="foot">Or, “when it rose”; traditionally rendered “in the east” by many English versions</note> led them until it came and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> stood above <transChange type="added">the place</transChange> where the child was.

verses.name: Matthew 2:10
verses.text: Now <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw the star, they rejoiced <transChange type="added">with</transChange> very great joy.

verses.name: Matthew 2:11
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“came”) which is understood as temporal</note> came into the house, they saw the child with Mary his mother, and they fell down and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“fell down”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> worshiped him. And opening their treasure boxes, they offered him gifts of gold and frankincense and myrrh.

verses.name: Matthew 2:12
verses.text: And being warned in a dream not to return to Herod, they went back to their <transChange type="added">own</transChange> country by another route.  <div eID="gen25670" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 2:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10509"/><title type="x-s">Joseph, Mary, and Jesus Escape to Egypt</title> <div sID="gen25671" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10509"/>Now <transChange type="added">after</transChange> they had gone away, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph, saying, “Get up, take the child and his mother and flee to Egypt, and stay there until I tell you. For Herod is about to seek the child to destroy him.”

verses.name: Matthew 2:14
verses.text: So he got up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“got up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> took the child and his mother during the night and went away to Egypt.

verses.name: Matthew 2:15
verses.text: And he was there until the death of Herod, in order that what was said by the Lord through the prophet would be fulfilled, saying, <div eID="gen25671" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen25672"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25673"/>“Out of Egypt I called my son.” <l eID="gen25673" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen25672"/>

verses.name: Matthew 2:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10510"/><title type="x-s">Herod Has Innocent Children Murdered</title> <div sID="gen25674" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10510"/>Then Herod, <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw that he had been deceived by the wise men, became very angry, and he sent soldiers<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“sent”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> executed all the children in Bethlehem and in all the region <transChange type="added">around</transChange> it from <transChange type="added">the age of</transChange> two years old and under, according to the time which he had determined precisely from the wise men.

verses.name: Matthew 2:17
verses.text: Then what was spoken by the prophet Jeremiah was fulfilled, saying,  <div eID="gen25674" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 2:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10511"/><lg sID="gen25675"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25676"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10511"/>“A voice was heard in Ramah,<l eID="gen25676" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25677"/>weeping and great mourning,<l eID="gen25677" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25678"/>Rachel weeping <transChange type="added">for</transChange> her children,<l eID="gen25678" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25679"/>and she did not want to be comforted,<l eID="gen25679" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25680"/>because <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they exist no longer⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “they are not”</note>.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Jer.31.15">Jer 31:15</reference></note> <l eID="gen25680" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen25675"/>

verses.name: Matthew 2:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10512"/><title type="x-s">Joseph, Mary, and Jesus Return to Nazareth</title> <div sID="gen25681" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10512"/>Now <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“had died”)</note> Herod had died, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt,

verses.name: Matthew 2:20
verses.text: saying, “Get up, take the child and his mother and go to the land of Israel, for those who were seeking the life of the child are dead.”

verses.name: Matthew 2:21
verses.text: So he got up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“got up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> took the child and his mother and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞entered⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “entered into”</note> the land of Israel.

verses.name: Matthew 2:22
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard that Archelaus was reigning over Judea in place of his father Herod, he was afraid to go there, and being warned in a dream, he took refuge in the regions of Galilee.

verses.name: Matthew 2:23
verses.text: And he came <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> lived in a town called Nazareth, in order that what was said by the prophets would be fulfilled:<note placement="foot">Literally “that”; the conjunction could be understood (1) to introduce a direct quotation, serving a function similar to modern English quotation marks, and thus not translated; or (2) to introduce an indirect quotation, in which case it could be translated “that he would be called a Nazarene”</note> “He will be called a Nazarene.”  <chapter eID="Matt.2"/>

verses.name: Matthew 3:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10513"/><title type="x-s">John the Baptist Begins His Ministry</title> <div sID="gen25682" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10513"/>Now in those days John the Baptist came preaching in the Judean wilderness

verses.name: Matthew 3:2
verses.text: and saying, “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near!”

verses.name: Matthew 3:3
verses.text: For this is the one who was spoken about by the prophet Isaiah, saying, <div eID="gen25682" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen25683"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25684"/>“The voice of one crying out in the wilderness,<l eID="gen25684" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25685"/>‘Prepare the way of the Lord,<l eID="gen25685" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25686"/>make his paths straight.’ ”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.40.3">Isa 40:3</reference></note> <l eID="gen25686" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen25683"/>

verses.name: Matthew 3:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10514"/><div sID="gen25687" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10514"/>Now John himself had his clothing made from camel’s hair and a belt made of leather around his waist, and his food was locusts and wild honey.

verses.name: Matthew 3:5
verses.text: Then Jerusalem and all Judea and all the district around the Jordan were going out to him,

verses.name: Matthew 3:6
verses.text: and they were being baptized by him in the Jordan River <transChange type="added">as they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“confessed”) which is understood as temporal</note> confessed their sins.  <div eID="gen25687" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 3:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10515"/><div sID="gen25688" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10515"/>But <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming to his baptism, he said to them, “Offspring of vipers! Who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?

verses.name: Matthew 3:8
verses.text: Therefore produce fruit worthy of repentance!

verses.name: Matthew 3:9
verses.text: And do not think to say to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham <transChange type="added">as</transChange> father.’ For I say to you that God is able to raise up children for Abraham from these stones!

verses.name: Matthew 3:10
verses.text: Already now the ax is positioned at the root of the trees; therefore every tree not producing good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.

verses.name: Matthew 3:11
verses.text: I baptize you with water for repentance, but the one who comes after me is more powerful than I <transChange type="added">am</transChange>, whose sandals I am not worthy to carry. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.

verses.name: Matthew 3:12
verses.text: His winnowing shovel <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in his hand, and he will clean out his threshing floor and will gather his wheat into the storehouse, but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.”  <div eID="gen25688" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 3:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10516"/><title type="x-s">The Baptism of Jesus</title> <div sID="gen25689" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10516"/>Then Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan to John in order to be baptized by him.

verses.name: Matthew 3:14
verses.text: But John tried to prevent<note placement="foot">*The imperfect verb is understood as conative (“tried to”)</note> him, saying, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I need⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “I have need”</note> to be baptized by you, and do you come to me?”

verses.name: Matthew 3:15
verses.text: But Jesus answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to him, “Permit <transChange type="added">it</transChange> now, for in this way it is right for us to fulfill all righteousness.” Then he permitted him.

verses.name: Matthew 3:16
verses.text: Now <transChange type="added">after he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was baptized”) which is understood as temporal</note> was baptized, Jesus immediately went up from the water, and behold, the heavens opened<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “opened to him”</note> and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove coming<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “and coming”</note> upon him.

verses.name: Matthew 3:17
verses.text: And behold, <transChange type="added">there was</transChange><note placement="foot">The words “there was” are not in the Greek text, but are supplied to make a complete sentence in English</note> a voice from heaven saying, “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased.”  <chapter eID="Matt.3"/>

verses.name: Matthew 4:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10517"/><title type="x-s">The Temptation of Jesus</title> <div sID="gen25690" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10517"/>Then Jesus was led up into the wilderness by the Spirit to be tempted by the devil,

verses.name: Matthew 4:2
verses.text: and <transChange type="added">after he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had fasted”) which is understood as temporal</note> had fasted forty days and forty nights, then he was hungry.

verses.name: Matthew 4:3
verses.text: And the tempter approached <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“approached”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to him, “If you are the Son of God, order that these stones become bread.”

verses.name: Matthew 4:4
verses.text: But he answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “It is written, ‘Man will not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes out of the mouth of God.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Deut.8.3">Deut 8:3</reference></note>  <div eID="gen25690" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 4:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10518"/><div sID="gen25691" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10518"/>Then the devil took him to the holy city<note placement="foot">That is, Jerusalem</note> and placed him on the highest point of the temple

verses.name: Matthew 4:6
verses.text: and said to him, “If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down! For it is written, <div eID="gen25691" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen25692"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25693"/>‘He will command his angels concerning you,’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.91.11">Ps 91:11</reference></note><l eID="gen25693" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen25692"/> <div sID="gen25694" type="x-p"/> and <div eID="gen25694" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen25695"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25696"/>‘On <transChange type="added">their</transChange> hands they will lift you up,<l eID="gen25696" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25697"/>lest you strike your foot against a stone.’ ”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.91.12">Ps 91:12</reference></note> <l eID="gen25697" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen25695"/>

verses.name: Matthew 4:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10519"/><div sID="gen25698" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10519"/>Jesus said to him, “On the other hand it is written, ‘You are not to put the Lord your God to the test.’ ”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Deut.6.16">Deut 6:16</reference></note>  <div eID="gen25698" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 4:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10520"/><div sID="gen25699" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10520"/>Again the devil took him to a very high mountain and showed him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory,

verses.name: Matthew 4:9
verses.text: and he said to him, “I will give to you all these things, if you will fall down <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“will fall down”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> worship me.”

verses.name: Matthew 4:10
verses.text: Then Jesus said to him, “Go away, Satan, for it is written, ‘You shall worship the Lord your God and serve only him.’ ”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Deut.6.13">Deut 6:13</reference></note>

verses.name: Matthew 4:11
verses.text: Then the devil left him, and behold, angels came and began ministering to him.  <div eID="gen25699" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 4:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10521"/><title type="x-s">Public Ministry in Galilee</title> <div sID="gen25700" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10521"/>Now <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard that John <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞had been arrested⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “had been handed over”</note> he withdrew into Galilee.

verses.name: Matthew 4:13
verses.text: And leaving Nazareth, he went <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> lived in Capernaum by the sea, in the region of Zebulun and Naphtali,

verses.name: Matthew 4:14
verses.text: in order that what was spoken by the prophet Isaiah would be fulfilled, who said,  <div eID="gen25700" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 4:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10522"/><lg sID="gen25701"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25702"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10522"/>“Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali,<l eID="gen25702" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25703"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞toward the sea⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the way of the sea”</note> on the other side of the Jordan,<l eID="gen25703" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25704"/>Galilee of the Gentiles<note placement="foot">Or “nations”; the same Greek word can be translated “nations” or “Gentiles” depending on the context</note>— <l eID="gen25704" level="2"/>

verses.name: Matthew 4:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10523"/><l level="1" sID="gen25705"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10523"/>the people who sit in darkness<l eID="gen25705" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25706"/>have seen a great light,<l eID="gen25706" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25707"/>and the ones who sit in the land and shadow of death,<l eID="gen25707" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25708"/>a light has dawned on them.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.9.1">Isa 9:1</reference></note> <l eID="gen25708" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen25701"/>

verses.name: Matthew 4:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10524"/><div sID="gen25709" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10524"/>From that time <transChange type="added">on</transChange>, Jesus began to preach and to say, “Repent, because the kingdom of heaven is near.”  <div eID="gen25709" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 4:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10525"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Calls His First Disciples</title> <div sID="gen25710" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10525"/>Now <transChange type="added">as he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was walking”) which is understood as temporal</note> was walking beside the Sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers, Simon called Peter and his brother Andrew, throwing a casting net into the sea (for they were fishermen).

verses.name: Matthew 4:19
verses.text: And he said to them, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Follow me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “come behind me”</note> and I will make you fishers of people.”

verses.name: Matthew 4:20
verses.text: And immediately they left their nets <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“left”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> followed him.

verses.name: Matthew 4:21
verses.text: And going on from there, he saw two other brothers, James the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Zebedee and his brother John, in the boat with their father Zebedee, mending their nets, and he called them.

verses.name: Matthew 4:22
verses.text: And immediately they left the boat and their father <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“left”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> followed him.  <div eID="gen25710" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 4:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10526"/><title type="x-s">Teaching, Preaching, and Healing throughout Galilee</title> <div sID="gen25711" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10526"/>And he went around through all of Galilee, teaching in their synagogues and proclaiming the good news of the kingdom and healing every disease and every sickness among the people.

verses.name: Matthew 4:24
verses.text: And a report about him went out <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞throughout⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in the whole of”</note> Syria, and they brought to him all those <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who were sick⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “having badly”</note> with various diseases and afflicted by torments, demon-possessed<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “and demon-possessed”</note> and epileptics and paralytics, and he healed them.

verses.name: Matthew 4:25
verses.text: And large crowds followed him from Galilee, Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea, and from the other side of the Jordan.  <chapter eID="Matt.4"/>

verses.name: Matthew 5:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10527"/><title type="x-s">The Sermon on the Mount: The Beatitudes</title> <div sID="gen25712" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10527"/>Now <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw the crowds, he went up the mountain and after he<note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“sat down”) which is understood as temporal</note> sat down, his disciples approached him.

verses.name: Matthew 5:2
verses.text: And opening his mouth he began to teach them, saying,  <div eID="gen25712" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 5:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10528"/><lg sID="gen25713"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25714"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10528"/>“Blessed <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the poor in spirit,<l eID="gen25714" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25715"/>because theirs is the kingdom of heaven. <l eID="gen25715" level="2"/>

verses.name: Matthew 5:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10529"/><l level="1" sID="gen25716"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10529"/>Blessed <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the ones who mourn,<l eID="gen25716" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25717"/>because they will be comforted. <l eID="gen25717" level="2"/>

verses.name: Matthew 5:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10530"/><l level="1" sID="gen25718"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10530"/>Blessed <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the meek,<l eID="gen25718" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25719"/>because they will inherit the earth. <l eID="gen25719" level="2"/>

verses.name: Matthew 5:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10531"/><l level="1" sID="gen25720"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10531"/>Blessed <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the ones who hunger and thirst <transChange type="added">for</transChange> righteousness,<l eID="gen25720" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25721"/>because they will be satisfied. <l eID="gen25721" level="2"/>

verses.name: Matthew 5:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10532"/><l level="1" sID="gen25722"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10532"/>Blessed <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the merciful,<l eID="gen25722" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25723"/>because they will be shown mercy. <l eID="gen25723" level="2"/>

verses.name: Matthew 5:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10533"/><l level="1" sID="gen25724"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10533"/>Blessed <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the pure in heart,<l eID="gen25724" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25725"/>because they will see God. <l eID="gen25725" level="2"/>

verses.name: Matthew 5:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10534"/><l level="1" sID="gen25726"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10534"/>Blessed <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the peacemakers,<l eID="gen25726" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25727"/>because they will be called sons of God. <l eID="gen25727" level="2"/>

verses.name: Matthew 5:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10535"/><l level="1" sID="gen25728"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10535"/>Blessed <transChange type="added">are</transChange> those who are persecuted because of righteousness,<l eID="gen25728" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25729"/>because theirs is the kingdom of heaven. <l eID="gen25729" level="2"/>

verses.name: Matthew 5:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10536"/><l level="1" sID="gen25730"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10536"/>Blessed are you<l eID="gen25730" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25731"/>when they insult you and persecute <transChange type="added">you</transChange> and say all kinds of evil things against you, lying on account of me.

verses.name: Matthew 5:12
verses.text: Rejoice and be glad, because your reward <transChange type="added">is</transChange> great in heaven, for in the <transChange type="added">same</transChange> way they persecuted the prophets before you. <l eID="gen25731" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen25713"/>

verses.name: Matthew 5:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10537"/><title type="x-s">The Sermon on the Mount: Salt and Light</title> <div sID="gen25732" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10537"/>“You are the salt of the earth. But if salt becomes tasteless, by what will it be made salty? It is good for nothing any longer except to be thrown outside <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“thrown”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> trampled under foot by people.

verses.name: Matthew 5:14
verses.text: You are the light of the world. A city located on top of a hill cannot be hidden,

verses.name: Matthew 5:15
verses.text: nor do they light a lamp and place it under a basket, but on a lampstand, and it shines on all those in the house.

verses.name: Matthew 5:16
verses.text: In the <transChange type="added">same</transChange> way let your light shine before people, so that they can see your good works and glorify your Father who is in heaven.  <div eID="gen25732" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 5:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10538"/><title type="x-s">The Sermon on the Mount: The Law and the Prophets Fulfilled</title> <div sID="gen25733" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10538"/>“Do not think that I have come to destroy the law or the prophets. I have not come to destroy <transChange type="added">them</transChange> but to fulfill <transChange type="added">them</transChange>.

verses.name: Matthew 5:18
verses.text: For truly I say to you, until heaven and earth pass away, not one tiny letter or one stroke of a letter will pass away from the law until all takes place.

verses.name: Matthew 5:19
verses.text: Therefore whoever abolishes one of the least of these commandments and teaches people to do so will be called least in the kingdom of heaven, but whoever keeps <transChange type="added">them</transChange> and teaches <transChange type="added">them</transChange>, this person will be called great in the kingdom of heaven.

verses.name: Matthew 5:20
verses.text: For I say to you that unless your righteousness greatly surpasses <transChange type="added">that</transChange> of the scribes and Pharisees, you will never enter into the kingdom of heaven.  <div eID="gen25733" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 5:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10539"/><title type="x-s">The Sermon on the Mount: Anger Toward Others</title> <div sID="gen25734" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10539"/>“You have heard that it was said to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞people of old⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “ancients”</note> ‘Do not commit murder,’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Exod.20.13">Exod 20:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="Deut.5.17">Deut 5:17</reference></note> and ‘whoever commits murder will be subject to judgment.’

verses.name: Matthew 5:22
verses.text: But I say to you that everyone who is angry at his brother will be subject to judgment, and whoever says to his brother, ‘Stupid fool!’<note placement="foot">Greek “Raca,” a term of verbal abuse involving lack of intelligence</note> will be subject to the council, and whoever says, ‘Obstinate fool!’<note placement="foot">Perhaps with the idea of obstinate, godless foolishness; some take the word to be a Greek transliteration of the Hebrew word for “rebel” (<reference osisRef="Deut.21.18">Deut 21:18</reference>, <reference osisRef="Deut.21.20">20</reference>)</note> will be subject to fiery hell.

verses.name: Matthew 5:23
verses.text: Therefore if you present your gift at the altar and there remember that your brother has something against you,

verses.name: Matthew 5:24
verses.text: leave your gift there before the altar and first go be reconciled to your brother, and then come <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“come”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> present your gift.

verses.name: Matthew 5:25
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Settle the case quickly with your accuser⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “be making friends quickly with your accuser”</note> while you are with him on the way, lest your accuser hand you over to the judge, and the judge to the officer, and you be thrown into prison.

verses.name: Matthew 5:26
verses.text: Truly I say to you, you will never come out of there until you have paid back the last penny!  <div eID="gen25734" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 5:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10540"/><title type="x-s">The Sermon on the Mount: Adultery and Lust</title> <div sID="gen25735" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10540"/>“You have heard that it was said, ‘Do not commit adultery.’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Exod.20.14">Exod 20:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="Deut.5.17">Deut 5:17</reference></note>

verses.name: Matthew 5:28
verses.text: But I say to you that everyone who looks at a woman to lust for her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.

verses.name: Matthew 5:29
verses.text: And if your right eye causes you to sin, tear it out and throw <transChange type="added">it</transChange> from you! For it is better for you that one of your members be destroyed than your whole body be thrown into hell.

verses.name: Matthew 5:30
verses.text: And if your right hand causes you to sin, cut it off and throw <transChange type="added">it</transChange> from you! For it is better for you that one of your limbs be destroyed than your whole body go into hell.  <div eID="gen25735" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 5:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10541"/><title type="x-s">The Sermon on the Mount: Divorce</title> <div sID="gen25736" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10541"/>“And it was said, ‘Whoever divorces his wife must give her a certificate of divorce.’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Deut.24.1">Deut 24:1</reference></note>

verses.name: Matthew 5:32
verses.text: But I say to you that everyone who divorces his wife, except for a matter of sexual immorality, causes her to commit adultery, and whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery.  <div eID="gen25736" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 5:33
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10542"/><title type="x-s">The Sermon on the Mount: Taking Oaths</title> <div sID="gen25737" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10542"/>“Again you have heard that it was said to the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞people of old⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “ancients”</note> ‘Do not swear falsely,<note placement="foot">Or “do not break your oath”</note> but fulfill your oaths to the Lord.’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Lev.19.12">Lev 19:12</reference></note>

verses.name: Matthew 5:34
verses.text: But I say to you, do not swear at all, either by heaven, because it is the throne of God,

verses.name: Matthew 5:35
verses.text: or by the earth, because it is the footstool of his feet, or by Jerusalem, because it is the city of the great king.

verses.name: Matthew 5:36
verses.text: And do not swear by your head, because you are not able to make one hair white or black.

verses.name: Matthew 5:37
verses.text: But let your statement be ‘Yes, yes; no, no,’ and anything beyond these is from the evil one.<note placement="foot">Or “is of evil”</note>  <div eID="gen25737" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 5:38
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10543"/><title type="x-s">The Sermon on the Mount: Retaliation</title> <div sID="gen25738" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10543"/>“You have heard that it was said, ‘An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth.’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Exod.21.24">Exod 21:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="Lev.24.20">Lev 24:20</reference></note>

verses.name: Matthew 5:39
verses.text: But I say to you, do not resist the evildoer, but whoever strikes you on the right cheek,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “your right cheek”</note> turn the other to him also.

verses.name: Matthew 5:40
verses.text: And the one who wants to go to court with you and take your tunic, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞let him have⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “leave to him”</note> your outer garment also.

verses.name: Matthew 5:41
verses.text: And whoever forces you to go one mile,<note placement="foot">A Roman mile was originally a thousand paces, but was later fixed at eight stades (1,478.5 meters)</note> go with him two.

verses.name: Matthew 5:42
verses.text: Give to the one who asks you, and do not turn away from the one who wants to borrow from you.  <div eID="gen25738" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 5:43
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10544"/><title type="x-s">The Sermon on the Mount: Love for Enemies</title> <div sID="gen25739" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10544"/>“You have heard that it was said, ‘Love your neighbor’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Lev.19.18">Lev 19:18</reference></note> and ‘Hate your enemy.’<note placement="foot">An allusion to <reference osisRef="Deut.23.3-Deut.23.6">Deut 23:3–6</reference></note>

verses.name: Matthew 5:44
verses.text: But I say to you, love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you,

verses.name: Matthew 5:45
verses.text: in order that you may be sons of your Father who is in heaven, because he causes his sun to rise on the evil and the good, and he sends rain on the just and the unjust.

verses.name: Matthew 5:46
verses.text: For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Do not the tax collectors also do the same?

verses.name: Matthew 5:47
verses.text: And if you greet only your brothers, what are you doing that is remarkable? Do not the Gentiles also do the same?

verses.name: Matthew 5:48
verses.text: Therefore you be perfect as your heavenly Father is perfect.  <chapter eID="Matt.5"/>

verses.name: Matthew 6:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10545"/><title type="x-s">The Sermon on the Mount: Charitable Giving</title> <div sID="gen25740" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10545"/>“And take care not to practice your righteousness before people to be seen by them; <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞otherwise⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “but if not”</note> you have no reward from your Father who is in heaven.

verses.name: Matthew 6:2
verses.text: Therefore whenever you practice charitable giving, do not sound a trumpet in front of you, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, in order that they may be praised by people. Truly I say to you, they have received their reward in full!

verses.name: Matthew 6:3
verses.text: But you, <transChange type="added">when you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“practice”) which is understood as temporal</note> practice charitable giving, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,

verses.name: Matthew 6:4
verses.text: in order that your charitable giving may be in secret, and your Father who sees in secret will reward you.  <div eID="gen25740" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 6:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10546"/><title type="x-s">The Sermon on the Mount: How to Pray</title> <div sID="gen25741" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10546"/>And whenever you pray, do not be like the hypocrites, because they love to stand <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“stand”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> pray in the synagogues and on the corners of the streets, in order that they may be seen by people. Truly I say to you, they have received their reward in full!

verses.name: Matthew 6:6
verses.text: But whenever you pray, enter into your inner room and shut your door <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“shut”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> pray to your Father who is in secret, and your Father who sees in secret will reward you.  <div eID="gen25741" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 6:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10547"/><div sID="gen25742" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10547"/>“But <transChange type="added">when you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“pray”) which is understood as temporal</note> pray, do not babble repetitiously like the pagans, for they think that because of their many words they will be heard.

verses.name: Matthew 6:8
verses.text: Therefore do not be like them, for your Father knows <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞what you need⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “of what you have need”</note> before you ask him.

verses.name: Matthew 6:9
verses.text: Therefore you pray in this way: <div eID="gen25742" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen25743"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25744"/>“Our Father who is in heaven,<l eID="gen25744" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25745"/>may your name be treated as holy. <l eID="gen25745" level="1"/>

verses.name: Matthew 6:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10548"/><l level="1" sID="gen25746"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10548"/>May your kingdom come,<l eID="gen25746" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25747"/>may your will be done<l eID="gen25747" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25748"/>on earth as <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> in heaven. <l eID="gen25748" level="2"/>

verses.name: Matthew 6:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10549"/><l level="1" sID="gen25749"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10549"/>Give us today our daily bread, <l eID="gen25749" level="1"/>

verses.name: Matthew 6:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10550"/><l level="1" sID="gen25750"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10550"/>and forgive us our debts,<l eID="gen25750" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25751"/>as we also have forgiven our debtors. <l eID="gen25751" level="2"/>

verses.name: Matthew 6:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10551"/><l level="1" sID="gen25752"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10551"/>And do not bring us into temptation,<l eID="gen25752" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25753"/>but deliver us from the evil one.<note placement="foot">Or “evil”; most later Greek manuscripts add the phrase “for yours is the kingdom and the power and the glory forever, amen”</note> <l eID="gen25753" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen25743"/>

verses.name: Matthew 6:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10552"/><div sID="gen25754" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10552"/>For if you forgive people their sins, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.

verses.name: Matthew 6:15
verses.text: But if you do not forgive people, neither will your Father forgive your sins.  <div eID="gen25754" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 6:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10553"/><title type="x-s">The Sermon on the Mount: How to Fast</title> <div sID="gen25755" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10553"/>“Whenever you fast, do not be sullen like the hypocrites, for they make their faces unrecognizable in order that they may be seen fasting by people. Truly I say to you, they have received their reward in full!

verses.name: Matthew 6:17
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“fasting”) which is understood as temporal</note> you are fasting, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞put olive oil on your head⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “anoint your head”</note> and wash your face

verses.name: Matthew 6:18
verses.text: so that you will not be seen by people as fasting, but to your Father who is in secret, and your Father who sees in secret will reward you.  <div eID="gen25755" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 6:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10554"/><title type="x-s">The Sermon on the Mount: Treasure in Heaven</title> <div sID="gen25756" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10554"/>“Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moth and consuming <transChange type="added">insect</transChange><note placement="foot">Traditionally “rust,” but more likely in this context along with “moth” the term refers to “eating” by other types of insects or vermin</note> destroy and where thieves break in and steal,

verses.name: Matthew 6:20
verses.text: but store up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor consuming <transChange type="added">insect</transChange><note placement="foot">Traditionally “rust,” but more likely in this context along with “moth” the term refers to “eating” by other types of insects or vermin</note> destroy and where thieves do not break in or steal.

verses.name: Matthew 6:21
verses.text: For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.  <div eID="gen25756" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 6:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10555"/><div sID="gen25757" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10555"/>“The eye is the lamp of the body. Therefore if your eye is sincere, your whole body will be full of light.

verses.name: Matthew 6:23
verses.text: But if your eye is evil, your whole body will be dark. Therefore if the light in you is darkness, how great <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the darkness!  <div eID="gen25757" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 6:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10556"/><div sID="gen25758" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10556"/>“No one is able to serve two masters. For either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to one and despise the other. You are not able to serve God and money.<note placement="foot">Traditionally transliterated from the Greek as “mammon”</note>  <div eID="gen25758" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 6:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10557"/><title type="x-s">The Sermon on the Mount: Anxiety</title> <div sID="gen25759" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10557"/>“For this <transChange type="added">reason</transChange> I say to you, do not be anxious for your life, what you will eat,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts add “or what you will drink”; other later manuscripts add “and what you will drink”</note> and not for your body, what you will wear. Is your life not more than food and your body <transChange type="added">more than</transChange> clothing?

verses.name: Matthew 6:26
verses.text: Consider the birds of the sky, that they do not sow or reap or gather <transChange type="added">produce</transChange> into barns, and your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not worth more than they <transChange type="added">are</transChange>?

verses.name: Matthew 6:27
verses.text: And who among you, <transChange type="added">by</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“being anxious”) which is understood as means</note> being anxious, is able to add one hour<note placement="foot">Or “cubit”</note> to his life span?

verses.name: Matthew 6:28
verses.text: And why are you anxious about clothing? Observe the lilies of the field, how they grow: they do not toil or spin,

verses.name: Matthew 6:29
verses.text: but I say to you that not even Solomon in all his glory was dressed like one of these.

verses.name: Matthew 6:30
verses.text: But if God dresses the grass of the field in this way, <transChange type="added">although it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“is”) which is understood as concessive</note> is <transChange type="added">here</transChange> today and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, will he not <transChange type="added">do so</transChange> much more <transChange type="added">for</transChange> you, you of little faith?

verses.name: Matthew 6:31
verses.text: Therefore do not be anxious, saying, ‘What will we eat?’ or ‘What will we drink?’ or ‘What will we wear?,’

verses.name: Matthew 6:32
verses.text: for the pagans seek after all these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>. For your heavenly Father knows that you need all these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>.

verses.name: Matthew 6:33
verses.text: But seek first his kingdom and righteousness,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “the kingdom of God and his righteousness”</note> and all these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> will be added to you.

verses.name: Matthew 6:34
verses.text: Therefore do not be anxious for tomorrow, because tomorrow will be anxious for itself. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Each day has enough trouble of its own.⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sufficient for the day its trouble”</note>  <chapter eID="Matt.6"/>

verses.name: Matthew 7:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10558"/><title type="x-s">The Sermon on the Mount: On Judging Others</title> <div sID="gen25760" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10558"/>“Do not judge, so that you will not be judged.

verses.name: Matthew 7:2
verses.text: For by what judgment you judge, you will be judged, and by what measure you measure out, it will be measured out to you.

verses.name: Matthew 7:3
verses.text: And why do you see the speck <transChange type="added">that is</transChange> in your brother’s eye, but do not notice the beam of wood in your <transChange type="added">own</transChange> eye?

verses.name: Matthew 7:4
verses.text: Or how will you say to your brother, ‘Allow <transChange type="added">me</transChange> to remove the speck from your eye,’ and behold, the beam of wood <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in your <transChange type="added">own</transChange> eye?

verses.name: Matthew 7:5
verses.text: Hypocrite! First remove the beam of wood from your <transChange type="added">own</transChange> eye and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye!  <div eID="gen25760" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 7:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10559"/><div sID="gen25761" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10559"/>“Do not give what is holy to dogs, or throw your pearls in front of pigs, lest they trample them with their feet, and turn around <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“turn around”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> tear you to pieces.  <div eID="gen25761" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 7:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10560"/><title type="x-s">The Sermon on the Mount: Ask, Seek, Knock</title> <div sID="gen25762" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10560"/>“Ask and it will be given to you; seek and you will find; knock and it will be opened for you.

verses.name: Matthew 7:8
verses.text: For everyone who asks receives, and the one who seeks finds, and to the one who knocks it will be opened.

verses.name: Matthew 7:9
verses.text: Or what man is <transChange type="added">there</transChange> among you, <transChange type="added">if</transChange> his son will ask him <transChange type="added">for</transChange> bread, will give him a stone?

verses.name: Matthew 7:10
verses.text: Or also <transChange type="added">if</transChange> he will ask for a fish, will give him a snake?

verses.name: Matthew 7:11
verses.text: Therefore if you, <transChange type="added">although you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“are”) which is understood as concessive</note> are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father who is in heaven give good things to those who ask him?

verses.name: Matthew 7:12
verses.text: Therefore <transChange type="added">in</transChange> all <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, whatever you want that people should do to you, thus also you do to them. For this is the law and the prophets.  <div eID="gen25762" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 7:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10561"/><title type="x-s">The Sermon on the Mount: The Narrow Gate</title> <div sID="gen25763" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10561"/>“Enter through the narrow gate, because broad <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the gate and spacious <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the road that leads to destruction, and there are many who enter through it,

verses.name: Matthew 7:14
verses.text: because narrow<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “how narrow”</note> <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the gate and constricted <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the road that leads to life, and there are few who find it!  <div eID="gen25763" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 7:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10562"/><title type="x-s">The Sermon on the Mount: Recognizing False Prophets</title> <div sID="gen25764" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10562"/>“Beware of false prophets who come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inside are ravenous wolves.

verses.name: Matthew 7:16
verses.text: You will recognize them by their fruits: they do not gather grapes from thorn bushes or figs from thistles, <transChange type="added">do they</transChange>?<note placement="foot">The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here, indicated by “do they”</note>

verses.name: Matthew 7:17
verses.text: In the <transChange type="added">same</transChange> way, every good tree produces good fruit, but a bad tree produces bad fruit.

verses.name: Matthew 7:18
verses.text: A good tree is not able to produce bad fruit, nor a bad tree to produce good fruit.

verses.name: Matthew 7:19
verses.text: Every tree that does not produce good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.

verses.name: Matthew 7:20
verses.text: As a result, you will recognize them by their fruits.  <div eID="gen25764" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 7:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10563"/><title type="x-s">The Sermon on the Mount: False Followers</title> <div sID="gen25765" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10563"/>“Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter into the kingdom of heaven, but the one who does the will of my Father who is in heaven.

verses.name: Matthew 7:22
verses.text: On that day many will say to me, ‘Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name, and expel demons in your name, and perform many miracles in your name?’

verses.name: Matthew 7:23
verses.text: And then <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I will say to them plainly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “I will declare to them”</note> ‘I never knew you. Depart from me, you who practice lawlessness!’  <div eID="gen25765" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 7:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10564"/><title type="x-s">The Sermon on the Mount: Two Houses and Two Foundations</title> <div sID="gen25766" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10564"/>“Therefore everyone who hears these words of mine and does them will be like a wise man who built his house on the rock.

verses.name: Matthew 7:25
verses.text: And the rain came down and the rivers came and the winds blew and beat against that house, and it did not collapse, because its foundation was laid on the rock.

verses.name: Matthew 7:26
verses.text: And everyone who hears these words of mine and does not do them will be like a foolish man who built his house on the sand.

verses.name: Matthew 7:27
verses.text: And the rain came down and the rivers came and the winds blew and beat against that house, and it collapsed, and its fall was great.”  <div eID="gen25766" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 7:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10565"/><title type="x-s">The Sermon on the Mount: Response</title> <div sID="gen25767" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10565"/>And it happened when Jesus finished these words the crowds were amazed at his teaching,

verses.name: Matthew 7:29
verses.text: because he was teaching them like one who had authority, and not like their scribes.  <chapter eID="Matt.7"/>

verses.name: Matthew 8:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10566"/><title type="x-s">A Leper Cleansed</title> <div sID="gen25768" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10566"/>And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“came down”)</note> he came down from the mountain, large crowds followed him.

verses.name: Matthew 8:2
verses.text: And behold, a leper approached <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“approached”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> worshiped him, saying, “Lord, if you are willing, you are able to make me clean.”

verses.name: Matthew 8:3
verses.text: And extending his hand he touched him, saying, “I am willing, be clean.” And immediately his leprosy was cleansed.

verses.name: Matthew 8:4
verses.text: And Jesus said to him, “See that you tell no one, but go, show yourself to the priest and offer the gift that Moses commanded, for a testimony to them.”  <div eID="gen25768" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 8:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10567"/><title type="x-s">A Centurion’s Slave Healed</title> <div sID="gen25769" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10567"/>Now <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“entered”)</note> he entered Capernaum, a centurion approached him, appealing to him

verses.name: Matthew 8:6
verses.text: and saying, “Lord, my slave<note placement="foot">Traditionally “servant”; the Greek term here is one often used of a slave who was regarded with some degree of affection, possibly a personal servant (the parallel passage in <reference osisRef="Luke.7.7">Luke 7:7 </reference>uses the more common term for slave)</note> is lying paralyzed in my<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> house, terribly tormented!”

verses.name: Matthew 8:7
verses.text: And he said to him, “I will come <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“come”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> heal him.”

verses.name: Matthew 8:8
verses.text: And the centurion answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “Lord, I am not worthy that you should come in under my roof. But only say the word and my slave will be healed.

verses.name: Matthew 8:9
verses.text: For I also am a man under authority who has soldiers under me, and I say to this one, ‘Go!’ and he goes, and to another one, ‘Come!’ and he comes, and to my slave, ‘Do this!’ and he does <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation (see the parallel in <reference osisRef="Luke.7.8">Luke 7:8</reference>).</note>.”  <div eID="gen25769" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 8:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10568"/><div sID="gen25770" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10568"/>Now <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> Jesus heard this,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> he was astonished, and said to those who were following him,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> “Truly I say to you, I have found such great faith with no one in Israel.

verses.name: Matthew 8:11
verses.text: But I say to you that many will come from east and west and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞be seated at the banquet⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “recline at table”</note> with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven.

verses.name: Matthew 8:12
verses.text: But the sons of the kingdom will be thrown out into the outer darkness. In that place there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth!”

verses.name: Matthew 8:13
verses.text: And Jesus said to the centurion, “Go, as you have believed it will be done for you.” And the slave<note placement="foot">Many later manuscripts have “his slave”</note> was healed at that hour.  <div eID="gen25770" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 8:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10569"/><title type="x-s">Many at Capernaum Are Healed</title> <div sID="gen25771" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10569"/>And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“came”) which is understood as temporal</note> Jesus came into Peter’s house, he saw his mother-in-law lying down and suffering with a fever.

verses.name: Matthew 8:15
verses.text: And he touched her hand and the fever left her, and she got up and began to serve him.  <div eID="gen25771" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 8:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10570"/><div sID="gen25772" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10570"/>Now <transChange type="added">when it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was”)</note> was evening, they brought to him many who were demon-possessed, and he expelled the spirits with a word. And he healed all <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞those who were sick⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “those who were having badly”</note>

verses.name: Matthew 8:17
verses.text: in order that what was spoken through the prophet Isaiah would be fulfilled, who said, <div eID="gen25772" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen25773"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25774"/>“He himself took away our sicknesses,<l eID="gen25774" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25775"/>and carried away our diseases.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.53.4">Isa 53:4</reference></note> <l eID="gen25775" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen25773"/>

verses.name: Matthew 8:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10571"/><title type="x-s">Would-be Followers</title> <div sID="gen25776" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10571"/>Now <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> Jesus saw many crowds<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “a crowd”</note> around him, he gave orders to depart to the other side.<note placement="foot">That is, the other side of the Sea of Galilee</note>

verses.name: Matthew 8:19
verses.text: And a scribe approached <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“approached”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to him, “Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go!”

verses.name: Matthew 8:20
verses.text: And Jesus said to him, “Foxes have dens and birds of the sky <transChange type="added">have</transChange> nests, but the Son of Man has no place to lay his head.”

verses.name: Matthew 8:21
verses.text: And another of the disciples<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “of his disciples”</note> said to him, “Lord, allow me first to go and bury my father.”

verses.name: Matthew 8:22
verses.text: But Jesus said to him, “Follow me, and leave the dead to bury their own dead!”  <div eID="gen25776" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 8:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10572"/><title type="x-s">Calming of a Storm</title> <div sID="gen25777" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10572"/>And <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“got”) which is understood as temporal</note> he got into the boat, his disciples followed him.

verses.name: Matthew 8:24
verses.text: And behold, a great storm arose on the sea, so that the boat was being inundated by the waves, but he himself was asleep.

verses.name: Matthew 8:25
verses.text: And they came <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> woke him, saying, “Lord, save us!<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> We are perishing!”

verses.name: Matthew 8:26
verses.text: And he said to them, “Why are you fearful, <transChange type="added">you</transChange> of little faith?” Then he got up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“got up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> rebuked the winds and the sea and there was a great calm.

verses.name: Matthew 8:27
verses.text: And the men were astonished, saying, “What sort of <transChange type="added">man</transChange> is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him?”  <div eID="gen25777" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 8:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10573"/><title type="x-s">Demon-possessed Gadarenes Healed</title> <div sID="gen25778" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10573"/>And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“came”)</note> he came to the other side,<note placement="foot">That is, the other side of the Sea of Galilee</note> to the region of the Gadarenes,<note placement="foot">Many manuscripts read “Gergesenes”; others read “Gerasenes” (see <reference osisRef="Luke.8.26">Luke 8:26</reference>)</note> two demon-possessed men coming from among the tombs met him, very violent, so that no one was able to pass by along that road.

verses.name: Matthew 8:29
verses.text: And behold, they cried out, saying, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞What do you have to do with us⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “what to us and to you”</note> Son of God?
