Have you come here to torment us before the time?”<note placement="foot">That is, before the appointed time of judgment</note>

verses.name: Matthew 8:30
verses.text: Now a long way from them a large herd of pigs was feeding.

verses.name: Matthew 8:31
verses.text: So the demons implored him, saying, “If you are going to expel us, send us into the herd of pigs.”

verses.name: Matthew 8:32
verses.text: And he said to them, “Go!” So they departed <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“departed”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> went into the pigs, and behold, the whole herd rushed headlong down the steep slope into the sea and drowned in the water.

verses.name: Matthew 8:33
verses.text: Now the herdsmen fled and went into the town <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> reported everything, including the things concerning the demon-possessed men.

verses.name: Matthew 8:34
verses.text: And behold, the whole town came out to meet Jesus, and <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw him, they implored him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> that he would depart from their region.  <chapter eID="Matt.8"/>

verses.name: Matthew 9:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10574"/><title type="x-s">A Paralytic Healed</title> <div sID="gen25779" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10574"/>And getting into a boat, he crossed over and came to his own town.<note placement="foot">A reference to Capernaum</note>

verses.name: Matthew 9:2
verses.text: And behold, they brought to him a paralytic lying on a stretcher, and <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic, “Have courage, child, your sins are forgiven.”

verses.name: Matthew 9:3
verses.text: And behold, some of the scribes said to themselves, “This man is blaspheming!”

verses.name: Matthew 9:4
verses.text: And knowing<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “perceiving”</note> their thoughts, Jesus said, “Why do you think evil in your hearts?

verses.name: Matthew 9:5
verses.text: For which is easier to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up and walk’?

verses.name: Matthew 9:6
verses.text: But in order that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins,” then he said to the paralytic, “Get up, pick up your stretcher and go to your home.”

verses.name: Matthew 9:7
verses.text: And he got up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“got up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> went to his home.

verses.name: Matthew 9:8
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> the crowds saw this,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> they were afraid and glorified God who had given such authority to men.  <div eID="gen25779" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 9:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10575"/><title type="x-s">Matthew Called to Follow Jesus</title> <div sID="gen25780" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10575"/>And <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> Jesus was going away from there, he saw a man called Matthew sitting at the tax booth and said to him, “Follow me!” And he stood up and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“stood up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> followed him.  <div eID="gen25780" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 9:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10576"/><div sID="gen25781" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10576"/>And it happened <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was dining”)</note> he <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞was dining⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “was reclining at table”</note> in the house, behold, many tax collectors and sinners were coming and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“were coming”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞dining⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “reclining at table”</note> with Jesus and his disciples.

verses.name: Matthew 9:11
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> the Pharisees began to say to his disciples, “Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?”

verses.name: Matthew 9:12
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> he said, “Those who are healthy do not have need of a physician, but those <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who are sick⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “having badly”</note>

verses.name: Matthew 9:13
verses.text: But go <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“go”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> learn what it means, “I want mercy and not sacrifice.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Hos.6.6">Hos 6:6 </reference>(see also <reference osisRef="Matt.12.7">Matt 12:7</reference>)</note> For I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners.”  <div eID="gen25781" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 9:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10577"/><title type="x-s">On Fasting</title> <div sID="gen25782" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10577"/>Then the disciples of John<note placement="foot">That is, John the Baptist</note> approached him, saying, “Why do we and the Pharisees fast often, but your disciples do not fast?”

verses.name: Matthew 9:15
verses.text: And Jesus said to them, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞The bridegroom’s attendants⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the sons of the bridal chamber”</note> are not able to mourn as long as the bridegroom is with them. But days are coming when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they will fast.

verses.name: Matthew 9:16
verses.text: But no one puts a patch of unshrunken cloth on an old garment, for its patch pulls away from the garment, and the tear becomes worse.

verses.name: Matthew 9:17
verses.text: Nor do they put new wine into old wineskins. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Otherwise⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “but if not”</note> the wineskins burst and the wine is spilled, and the wineskins are destroyed. But they put new wine into new wineskins and both are preserved.”  <div eID="gen25782" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 9:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10578"/><title type="x-s">A Woman Healed and a Daughter Raised</title> <div sID="gen25783" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10578"/><transChange type="added">As</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was saying”)</note> he was saying these things to them, behold, one of the rulers came and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> knelt down before him, saying, “My daughter has just now died, but come, place your hand on her and she will live!”

verses.name: Matthew 9:19
verses.text: And Jesus and his disciples got up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“got up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> followed him.

verses.name: Matthew 9:20
verses.text: And behold, a woman who had been suffering with a hemorrhage twelve years approached from behind <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“approached”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> touched the edge<note placement="foot">Or “tassel”</note> of his cloak,

verses.name: Matthew 9:21
verses.text: for she said to herself, “If only I touch his cloak I will be healed.”

verses.name: Matthew 9:22
verses.text: But Jesus, turning around and seeing her, said, “Have courage, daughter! Your faith has healed you.” And the woman was healed from that hour.  <div eID="gen25783" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 9:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10579"/><div sID="gen25784" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10579"/>And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“came”) which is understood as temporal</note> Jesus came into the ruler’s house and saw the flute players and the disorderly crowd,

verses.name: Matthew 9:24
verses.text: he said, “Go away, because the girl is not dead, but is sleeping.” And they ridiculed him.

verses.name: Matthew 9:25
verses.text: But when the crowd had been sent out, he entered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“entered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> took her hand, and the girl got up.

verses.name: Matthew 9:26
verses.text: And this report went out into that whole region.  <div eID="gen25784" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 9:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10580"/><title type="x-s">Two Blind Men Healed</title> <div sID="gen25785" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10580"/>And <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“going away”) which is understood as temporal</note> Jesus was going away from there, two blind men followed him, crying out and saying, “Have mercy on us, Son of David!”

verses.name: Matthew 9:28
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“came”) which is understood as temporal</note> came into the house, the blind men approached him, and Jesus said to them, “Do you believe that I am able to do this?” They said to him, “Yes, Lord.”

verses.name: Matthew 9:29
verses.text: Then he touched their eyes, saying, “According to your faith let it be done for you.”

verses.name: Matthew 9:30
verses.text: And their eyes were opened, and Jesus sternly warned them, saying, “See <transChange type="added">that</transChange> no one finds out.”

verses.name: Matthew 9:31
verses.text: But they went out <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> spread the report about him in that whole region.  <div eID="gen25785" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 9:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10581"/><title type="x-s">A Demon Expelled</title> <div sID="gen25786" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10581"/>Now <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“were going away”)</note> they were going away, behold, they brought to him a demon-possessed man <transChange type="added">who was</transChange> unable to speak.

verses.name: Matthew 9:33
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“had been expelled”)</note> the demon had been expelled, the one who had been mute spoke, and the crowds were astonished, saying, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞This has never been seen before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “never has it been seen thus”</note> in Israel!”

verses.name: Matthew 9:34
verses.text: But the Pharisees were saying,<note placement="foot">Or “began to say”</note> “By the ruler of demons he expels the demons!”  <div eID="gen25786" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 9:35
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10582"/><title type="x-s">A Plentiful Harvest But Few Workers</title> <div sID="gen25787" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10582"/>And Jesus was going around all the towns and the villages, teaching in their synagogues and proclaiming the good news of the kingdom and healing every<note placement="foot">Or “every kind of”</note> disease and every<note placement="foot">Or “every kind of”</note> sickness.

verses.name: Matthew 9:36
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw the crowds, he had compassion for them, because they were weary and dejected, like sheep that did not have a shepherd.

verses.name: Matthew 9:37
verses.text: Then he said to his disciples, “The harvest <transChange type="added">is</transChange> plentiful, but the workers <transChange type="added">are</transChange> few.

verses.name: Matthew 9:38
verses.text: Therefore ask the Lord of the harvest that he send out workers into his harvest.”  <chapter eID="Matt.9"/>

verses.name: Matthew 10:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10583"/><title type="x-s">The Twelve Commissioned and Sent Out</title> <div sID="gen25788" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10583"/>And summoning his twelve disciples, he gave them authority over unclean spirits, so that they could expel <transChange type="added">them</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and could heal every<note placement="foot">Or “every kind of”</note> disease and every<note placement="foot">Or “every kind of”</note> sickness.

verses.name: Matthew 10:2
verses.text: Now these are the names of the twelve apostles: first Simon who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother, James<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “and James”</note> the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Zebedee, and John his brother,

verses.name: Matthew 10:3
verses.text: Philip, and Bartholomew, Thomas, and Matthew the tax collector, James the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus,

verses.name: Matthew 10:4
verses.text: Simon the Zealot,<note placement="foot">Literally “the Cananean,” but according to BDAG 507 s.v., this term has no relation at all to the geographical terms for Cana or Canaan, but is derived from the Aramaic term for “enthusiast, zealot” (see <reference osisRef="Luke.6.15">Luke 6:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="Acts.1.13">Acts 1:13</reference>)</note> and Judas Iscariot—the one who also betrayed him.  <div eID="gen25788" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 10:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10584"/><div sID="gen25789" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10584"/>Jesus sent out these twelve, instructing them saying, “Do not go on the road to the Gentiles, and do not enter into a city of the Samaritans,

verses.name: Matthew 10:6
verses.text: but go instead to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.

verses.name: Matthew 10:7
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">as you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“are going”) which is understood as temporal</note> are going, preach, saying, ‘The kingdom of heaven has come near!’

verses.name: Matthew 10:8
verses.text: Heal those who are sick, raise the dead, cleanse lepers, expel demons. Freely you have received; freely give.

verses.name: Matthew 10:9
verses.text: Do not procure gold or silver or copper for your belts.

verses.name: Matthew 10:10
verses.text: Do not <transChange type="added">take</transChange> a traveler’s bag for the road, or two tunics, or sandals, or a staff, for the worker <transChange type="added">is</transChange> deserving of his provisions.

verses.name: Matthew 10:11
verses.text: And into whatever town or village you enter, inquire who in it is worthy, and stay <transChange type="added">there</transChange> until you depart.

verses.name: Matthew 10:12
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“enter”) which is understood as temporal</note> enter into the house, greet it.

verses.name: Matthew 10:13
verses.text: And if the house is worthy, let your peace come upon it, but if it is not worthy, let your peace return to you.

verses.name: Matthew 10:14
verses.text: And whoever does not welcome you or listen to your words, shake off the dust from your feet <transChange type="added">as you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“are going”) which is understood as temporal</note> are going out of that house or that<note placement="foot">A repetition of “that” is supplied in English; the single Greek term is understood to modify both “house” and “town”</note> town.

verses.name: Matthew 10:15
verses.text: Truly I say to you, it will be more bearable for the region of Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgment than for that town!  <div eID="gen25789" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 10:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10585"/><title type="x-s">Persecution of Disciples Predicted</title> <div sID="gen25790" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10585"/>“Behold, I am sending you out like sheep in the midst of wolves. Therefore be wise as serpents and innocent as doves.

verses.name: Matthew 10:17
verses.text: But beware of people, because they will hand you over to councils, and they will flog you in their synagogues.

verses.name: Matthew 10:18
verses.text: And you will be brought before both governors and kings because of me, for a witness to them and to the Gentiles.

verses.name: Matthew 10:19
verses.text: But whenever they hand you over, do not be anxious how <transChange type="added">to speak</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “to speak” has been supplied for stylistic reasons, since “how to speak” is more natural in English than “how to say”; in Greek the same verb works with both expressions (“how or what you should say”) and also occurs again at the end of the verse</note> or what you should say, for what you should say will be given to you at that hour.

verses.name: Matthew 10:20
verses.text: For you are not the ones who are speaking, but the Spirit of your Father <transChange type="added">who is</transChange> speaking through you.  <div eID="gen25790" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 10:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10586"/><div sID="gen25791" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10586"/>“And brother will hand over brother to death, and a father <transChange type="added">his</transChange> children, and children will rise up against parents and have them put to death,

verses.name: Matthew 10:22
verses.text: and you will be hated by everyone because of my name. But the one who endures to the end—this one will be saved.

verses.name: Matthew 10:23
verses.text: And whenever they persecute you in this town, flee to another, for truly I say to you, you will never finish <transChange type="added">going through</transChange> the towns of Israel until the Son of Man comes.  <div eID="gen25791" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 10:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10587"/><div sID="gen25792" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10587"/>“A disciple is not superior to his teacher, nor a slave superior to his master.

verses.name: Matthew 10:25
verses.text: <transChange type="added">It is</transChange> enough for the disciple that he become like his teacher, and the slave like his master. If they have called the master of the house Beelzebul, how much more the members of his household?  <div eID="gen25792" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 10:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10588"/><title type="x-s">Fear God Rather Than People</title> <div sID="gen25793" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10588"/>“Therefore do not be afraid of them, because nothing is hidden that will not be revealed, and nothing secret that will not become known.

verses.name: Matthew 10:27
verses.text: What I say to you in the dark, tell in the light, and what you hear in your ear, proclaim on the housetops.

verses.name: Matthew 10:28
verses.text: And do not be afraid of those who kill the body but are not able to kill the soul, but instead be afraid of the one who is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.

verses.name: Matthew 10:29
verses.text: Are not two sparrows sold for a penny?<note placement="foot">Literally, “an assarion,” a Roman coin worth about 1/16 of a denarius</note> And one of them will not fall to the ground <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞without the knowledge and consent⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “without”; the phrase “the knowledge and consent” is implied when this term is used of God</note> of your Father.

verses.name: Matthew 10:30
verses.text: And even the hairs of your head are all numbered!

verses.name: Matthew 10:31
verses.text: Therefore do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows.  <div eID="gen25793" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 10:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10589"/><div sID="gen25794" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10589"/>“Therefore everyone who acknowledges me before people, I also will acknowledge him before my Father <transChange type="added">who is</transChange> in heaven.

verses.name: Matthew 10:33
verses.text: But whoever denies me before people, I also will deny him before my Father <transChange type="added">who is</transChange> in heaven.  <div eID="gen25794" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 10:34
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10590"/><title type="x-s">Not Peace, But a Sword of Divisiveness</title> <div sID="gen25795" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10590"/>“Do not think that I have come to bring peace on the earth! I have not come to bring peace, but a sword.

verses.name: Matthew 10:35
verses.text: For I have come to turn a man against his father, and a daughter against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.

verses.name: Matthew 10:36
verses.text: And the enemies of a man <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> the members of his household.<note placement="foot">An allusion to <reference osisRef="Mic.7.6">Mic 7:6</reference></note>

verses.name: Matthew 10:37
verses.text: The one who loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me, and the one who loves son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.

verses.name: Matthew 10:38
verses.text: And whoever does not take up his cross and follow me is not worthy of me.

verses.name: Matthew 10:39
verses.text: The one who finds his life will lose it, and the one who loses his life because of me will find it.  <div eID="gen25795" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 10:40
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10591"/><title type="x-s">On Rewards</title> <div sID="gen25796" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10591"/>“The one who receives you receives me, and the one who receives me receives the one who sent me.

verses.name: Matthew 10:41
verses.text: The one who receives a prophet in the name of a prophet will receive a prophet’s reward, and the one who receives a righteous person in the name of a righteous person will receive a righteous person’s reward.

verses.name: Matthew 10:42
verses.text: And whoever gives one of these little ones only a cup of cold water to drink in the name of a disciple, truly I say to you, he will never lose his reward.”  <chapter eID="Matt.10"/>

verses.name: Matthew 11:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10592"/><title type="x-s">A Question from John the Baptist</title> <div sID="gen25797" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10592"/>And it happened that when Jesus had finished giving orders to his twelve disciples, he went on from there to teach and to preach in their towns.

verses.name: Matthew 11:2
verses.text: Now <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> John<note placement="foot">That is, John the Baptist</note> heard in prison the deeds of Christ, he sent word<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> by his disciples

verses.name: Matthew 11:3
verses.text: <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“sent” in the previous verse) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to him, “Are you the one who is to come, or should we look for another?”

verses.name: Matthew 11:4
verses.text: And Jesus answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to them, “Go and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“go”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> tell John what you hear and see:

verses.name: Matthew 11:5
verses.text: the blind receive sight and the lame walk, lepers are cleansed and the deaf hear, and the dead are raised, and the poor have good news announced to <transChange type="added">them</transChange>.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Matthew 11:6
verses.text: And whoever is not offended by me is blessed.”  <div eID="gen25797" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 11:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10593"/><div sID="gen25798" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10593"/>Now <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“were going away”)</note> these were going away, Jesus began to speak to the crowds concerning John: “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?

verses.name: Matthew 11:8
verses.text: But what did you go out to see? A man dressed in soft clothing? Behold, those who wear soft clothing are in the houses of kings.

verses.name: Matthew 11:9
verses.text: But why did you go out? To see a prophet?<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “But what did you go out to see? A prophet?”</note> Yes, I tell you, and even more than a prophet!

verses.name: Matthew 11:10
verses.text: It is this man about whom it is written: <div eID="gen25798" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen25799"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25800"/>‘Behold, I am sending my messenger before your face,<l eID="gen25800" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25801"/>who will prepare your way before you.’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Mal.3.1">Mal 3:1; </reference>cf. <reference osisRef="Mark.1.2">Mark 1:2</reference></note> <l eID="gen25801" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen25799"/>

verses.name: Matthew 11:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10594"/><div sID="gen25802" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10594"/>Truly I say to you, among <transChange type="added">those</transChange> born of women there has not arisen <transChange type="added">one</transChange> greater than John the Baptist. But the one who is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.

verses.name: Matthew 11:12
verses.text: But from the days of John the Baptist until now, the kingdom of heaven is treated violently, and the violent claim<note placement="foot">Or “seize”</note> it.

verses.name: Matthew 11:13
verses.text: For all the prophets and the law prophesied until John,

verses.name: Matthew 11:14
verses.text: and if you are willing to accept <transChange type="added">it</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> he is Elijah, the one who is going to come.

verses.name: Matthew 11:15
verses.text: The one who has ears, let him hear!  <div eID="gen25802" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 11:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10595"/><div sID="gen25803" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10595"/>“But to what shall I compare this generation? It is like children sitting in the marketplaces who call out to one another,

verses.name: Matthew 11:17
verses.text: saying, <div eID="gen25803" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen25804"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25805"/>‘We played the flute for you and you did not dance;<l eID="gen25805" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25806"/>we sang a lament and you did not mourn.’ <l eID="gen25806" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen25804"/>

verses.name: Matthew 11:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10596"/><div sID="gen25807" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10596"/>For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, ‘He has a demon!’

verses.name: Matthew 11:19
verses.text: The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say, ‘Behold, a man <transChange type="added">who is</transChange> a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’ But wisdom is vindicated by her deeds.”<note placement="foot">Many Greek manuscripts, including most later ones, read “children”</note>  <div eID="gen25807" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 11:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10597"/><title type="x-s">Woes Pronounced on Unrepentant Towns</title> <div sID="gen25808" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10597"/>Then he began to reproach the towns in which the majority of his miracles had been done, because they did not repent:

verses.name: Matthew 11:21
verses.text: “Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the miracles done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.

verses.name: Matthew 11:22
verses.text: Nevertheless I tell you, it will be more bearable for Tyre and for Sidon on the day of judgment than for you!

verses.name: Matthew 11:23
verses.text: And you, Capernaum, will you be exalted to heaven? No, you will be brought down to Hades! For if the miracles done in you had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until today.

verses.name: Matthew 11:24
verses.text: Nevertheless I tell you that it will be more bearable for the region of Sodom on the day of judgment than for you!”  <div eID="gen25808" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 11:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10598"/><title type="x-s">A Yoke That Is Easy</title> <div sID="gen25809" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10598"/>At that time Jesus answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “I praise you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have hidden these things from the wise and intelligent, and have revealed them to young children.<note placement="foot">Or perhaps “to the childlike,” or “to the innocent”</note>

verses.name: Matthew 11:26
verses.text: Yes, Father, for <transChange type="added">to do</transChange> so <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞was your gracious will⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “was pleasing before you”</note>

verses.name: Matthew 11:27
verses.text: All <transChange type="added">things</transChange> have been handed over to me by my Father, and no one knows the Son except the Father, and no one knows the Father except the Son and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞anyone to whom⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to whomever”</note> the Son wants to reveal him.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Matthew 11:28
verses.text: Come to me, all <transChange type="added">of you</transChange> who labor and are burdened, and I will give you rest.

verses.name: Matthew 11:29
verses.text: Take my yoke on you and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls.

verses.name: Matthew 11:30
verses.text: For my yoke <transChange type="added">is</transChange> easy to carry and my burden is light.”  <chapter eID="Matt.11"/>

verses.name: Matthew 12:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10599"/><title type="x-s">Plucking Grain on the Sabbath</title> <div sID="gen25810" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10599"/>At that time Jesus went through the grain fields on the Sabbath. And his disciples were hungry, and they began to pluck off heads of grain and eat <transChange type="added">them</transChange>.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Matthew 12:2
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> the Pharisees saw it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> they said to him, “Behold, your disciples are doing what it is not permitted to do on the Sabbath!”

verses.name: Matthew 12:3
verses.text: So he said to them, “Have you not read what David did when he was hungry, and those with him,

verses.name: Matthew 12:4
verses.text: how he entered into the house of God and ate the bread of the presentation, which it was not permitted for him or for those with him to eat, but only for the priests?

verses.name: Matthew 12:5
verses.text: Or have you not read in the law that on the Sabbath the priests in the temple violate the sanctity of the Sabbath and are guiltless?

verses.name: Matthew 12:6
verses.text: But I tell you that <transChange type="added">something</transChange> greater than the temple is here!

verses.name: Matthew 12:7
verses.text: And if you had known what <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞it means⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “it is”</note> ‘I want mercy and not sacrifice,’ you would not have condemned the guiltless.

verses.name: Matthew 12:8
verses.text: For the Son of Man is lord of the Sabbath.”  <div eID="gen25810" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 12:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10600"/><title type="x-s">A Man with a Withered Hand Healed</title> <div sID="gen25811" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10600"/>And going on from there he came into their synagogue.

verses.name: Matthew 12:10
verses.text: And behold, <transChange type="added">there was</transChange> a man who had a withered hand, and they asked him, saying, “Is it permitted to heal on the Sabbath?” in order that they could accuse him.

verses.name: Matthew 12:11
verses.text: But he said to them, “What man will there be among you who will have one sheep and if this one fell into a pit on the Sabbath, will not take hold of it and lift <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> out?

verses.name: Matthew 12:12
verses.text: Then to what degree <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a man worth more than a sheep? So then, it is permitted to do good on the Sabbath.”  <div eID="gen25811" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 12:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10601"/><div sID="gen25812" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10601"/>Then he said to the man, “Stretch out your hand,” and he stretched <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> out, and it was restored <transChange type="added">as</transChange> healthy as the other <transChange type="added">one</transChange>.

verses.name: Matthew 12:14
verses.text: But the Pharisees went out <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞and plotted⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “taking counsel”</note> against him in order that they could destroy him.  <div eID="gen25812" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 12:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10602"/><title type="x-s">God’s Chosen Servant</title> <div sID="gen25813" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10602"/>Now Jesus, <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“learned”) which is understood as temporal</note> learned of it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> withdrew from there, and many<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “many crowds”</note> followed him, and he healed them all.

verses.name: Matthew 12:16
verses.text: And he warned them that they should not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞reveal his identity⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “make him known”</note>

verses.name: Matthew 12:17
verses.text: in order that what was spoken through the prophet Isaiah would be fulfilled, who said,  <div eID="gen25813" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 12:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10603"/><lg sID="gen25814"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25815"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10603"/>“Behold my servant whom I have chosen,<l eID="gen25815" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25816"/>my beloved in whom my soul is well pleased.<l eID="gen25816" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25817"/>I will put my Spirit on him,<l eID="gen25817" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25818"/>and he will proclaim justice to the Gentiles. <l eID="gen25818" level="2"/>

verses.name: Matthew 12:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10604"/><l level="1" sID="gen25819"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10604"/>He will not quarrel or cry out,<l eID="gen25819" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25820"/>nor will anyone hear his voice in the streets. <l eID="gen25820" level="2"/>

verses.name: Matthew 12:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10605"/><l level="1" sID="gen25821"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10605"/>A crushed reed he will not break,<l eID="gen25821" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25822"/>and a smoldering wick he will not extinguish,<l eID="gen25822" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25823"/>until he brings justice to victory. <l eID="gen25823" level="1"/>

verses.name: Matthew 12:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10606"/><l level="2" sID="gen25824"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10606"/>And in his name the Gentiles<note placement="foot">Or “the nations”; the same Greek word (in the plural) can be translated as “nations,” “Gentiles,” or “pagans”</note> will hope.<note placement="foot">Verses <reference osisRef="Matt.12.18-Matt.12.21">18–21</reference> are a quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.42.1-Isa.42.4">Isa 42:1–4</reference></note> <l eID="gen25824" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen25814"/>

verses.name: Matthew 12:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10607"/><title type="x-s">A House Divided Cannot Stand</title> <div sID="gen25825" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10607"/>Then a demon-possessed man <transChange type="added">who was</transChange> blind and mute was brought to him. And he healed him so that the <transChange type="added">man who was</transChange> mute could speak and see.

verses.name: Matthew 12:23
verses.text: And all the crowds were amazed and began saying, “Perhaps this one is the Son of David!”

verses.name: Matthew 12:24
verses.text: But the Pharisees, <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> said, “This man does not expel demons except by Beelzebul the ruler of demons!”

verses.name: Matthew 12:25
verses.text: But knowing their thoughts, he said to them, “Every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste, and every city or household divided against itself will not stand.

verses.name: Matthew 12:26
verses.text: And if Satan expels Satan, he is divided against himself. How then will his kingdom stand?

verses.name: Matthew 12:27
verses.text: And if I expel demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons expel <transChange type="added">them</transChange>?<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> For this <transChange type="added">reason</transChange> they will be your judges!

verses.name: Matthew 12:28
verses.text: But if I expel demons by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you!

verses.name: Matthew 12:29
verses.text: Or how can someone enter into the house of a strong <transChange type="added">man</transChange> and steal his property, unless he first ties up the strong <transChange type="added">man</transChange>? And then he can thoroughly plunder his house.

verses.name: Matthew 12:30
verses.text: The one who is not with me is against me, and the one who does not gather with me scatters.

verses.name: Matthew 12:31
verses.text: For this <transChange type="added">reason</transChange> I tell you, every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven people, but the blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven!

verses.name: Matthew 12:32
verses.text: And whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man, it will be forgiven him. But whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit, it will not be forgiven him either in this age or in the coming one!  <div eID="gen25825" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 12:33
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10608"/><title type="x-s">Good Trees and Good Fruit or Bad Trees and Bad Fruit</title> <div sID="gen25826" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10608"/>“Either make the tree good and its fruit <transChange type="added">is</transChange> good, or make the tree bad and its fruit <transChange type="added">is</transChange> bad, for the tree is known by its fruit.

verses.name: Matthew 12:34
verses.text: Offspring of vipers! How are you able to say good things <transChange type="added">when you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“are”) which is understood as temporal</note> are evil? For from the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks.

verses.name: Matthew 12:35
verses.text: The good person from his<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> good treasury brings out good things, and the evil person from his<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> evil treasury brings out evil <transChange type="added">things</transChange>.

verses.name: Matthew 12:36
verses.text: But I tell you that every worthless word that they speak, people will give an account for it on the day of judgment!

verses.name: Matthew 12:37
verses.text: For by your words you will be vindicated, and by your words you will be condemned.”  <div eID="gen25826" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 12:38
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10609"/><title type="x-s">The Sign of Jonah</title> <div sID="gen25827" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10609"/>Then some of the scribes and Pharisees answered him saying, “Teacher, we want to see a sign from you!”

verses.name: Matthew 12:39
verses.text: But he answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to them, “An evil and adulterous generation desires a sign, and no sign will be given to it except the sign of the prophet Jonah!

verses.name: Matthew 12:40
verses.text: For just as Jonah was in the belly of the huge fish three days and three nights, so the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth three days and three nights.

verses.name: Matthew 12:41
verses.text: The people of Nineveh will stand up at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they repented at the proclamation of Jonah, and behold, <transChange type="added">something</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “something” is supplied in the translation because the adjective is neuter gender</note> greater than Jonah <transChange type="added">is</transChange> here!

verses.name: Matthew 12:42
verses.text: The queen of the south will rise up at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and behold, <transChange type="added">something</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “something” is supplied in the translation because the adjective is neuter gender</note> greater than Solomon <transChange type="added">is</transChange> here!  <div eID="gen25827" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 12:43
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10610"/><title type="x-s">An Unclean Spirit Returns</title> <div sID="gen25828" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10610"/>“Now whenever an unclean spirit has gone out of a person, it travels through waterless places searching for rest, and does not find <transChange type="added">it</transChange>.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Matthew 12:44
verses.text: Then it says, ‘I will return to my house from which I came out.’ And <transChange type="added">when it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“arrives”) which is understood as temporal</note> arrives it finds the house<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> unoccupied and swept and put in order.

verses.name: Matthew 12:45
verses.text: Then it goes and brings along with itself seven other spirits more evil than itself, and <transChange type="added">they</transChange> go in <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“go in”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> live there. And the last <transChange type="added">state</transChange> of that person becomes worse than the first. So it will be for this evil generation also!”  <div eID="gen25828" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 12:46
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10611"/><title type="x-s">Jesus’ Mother and Brothers</title> <div sID="gen25829" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10611"/>And<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts omit “And”</note> while<note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“speaking”)</note> he was still speaking to the crowds, behold, his mother and brothers were standing there outside, desiring to speak to him.

verses.name: Matthew 12:47
verses.text: And someone told him, “Behold, your mother and your brothers are standing there outside desiring to speak to you.”

verses.name: Matthew 12:48
verses.text: But he answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to the one who told him, “Who is my mother, and who are my brothers?”

verses.name: Matthew 12:49
verses.text: And stretching out his hand toward his disciples, he said, “Behold my mother and my brothers!

verses.name: Matthew 12:50
verses.text: For whoever does the will of my Father <transChange type="added">who is</transChange> in heaven, he is my brother and sister and mother.”  <chapter eID="Matt.12"/>

verses.name: Matthew 13:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10612"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Sower</title> <div sID="gen25830" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10612"/>On that day Jesus went out of the house <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> was sitting by the sea.<note placement="foot">That is, the Sea of Galilee</note>

verses.name: Matthew 13:2
verses.text: And large crowds gathered close around him, so that he got into a boat to sit down, and all the crowd was standing on the shore.

verses.name: Matthew 13:3
verses.text: And he spoke many <transChange type="added">things</transChange> to them in parables, saying, “Behold, the sower went out to sow,

verses.name: Matthew 13:4
verses.text: and while he was sowing, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞some seed⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “some of which”</note> fell on the side of the path, and the birds came and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> devoured it.

verses.name: Matthew 13:5
verses.text: And other <transChange type="added">seed</transChange> fell on the rocky ground, where it did not have much soil, and it sprang up at once because it did not have <transChange type="added">any</transChange> depth of soil.

verses.name: Matthew 13:6
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“rose”)</note> the sun rose it was scorched, and because it did not have <transChange type="added">enough</transChange> root, it withered.

verses.name: Matthew 13:7
verses.text: And other <transChange type="added">seed</transChange> fell among the thorn plants, and the thorn plants came up and choked it.

verses.name: Matthew 13:8
verses.text: But other <transChange type="added">seed</transChange> fell on the good soil and produced grain,<note placement="foot">Literally “fruit,” describing here the grain harvested from the healthy plants; in contemporary English this would more naturally be expressed by terms like “grain” or “crop”</note> this one a hundred <transChange type="added">times as much</transChange> and this one sixty and this one thirty.

verses.name: Matthew 13:9
verses.text: The one who has ears, let him hear!”  <div eID="gen25830" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 13:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10613"/><title type="x-s">The Reason for the Parables</title> <div sID="gen25831" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10613"/>And the disciples came up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to him, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Why⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “because of what”</note> do you speak to them in parables?”

verses.name: Matthew 13:11
verses.text: And he answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to them, “To you it has been granted to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to those <transChange type="added">people</transChange> it has not been granted.

verses.name: Matthew 13:12
verses.text: For whoever has, to him <transChange type="added">more</transChange> will be given, and he will have an abundance. But whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.

verses.name: Matthew 13:13
verses.text: For this <transChange type="added">reason</transChange> I speak to them in parables, because seeing they do not see, and hearing they do not hear, nor do they understand,

verses.name: Matthew 13:14
verses.text: and with reference to them the prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled that says, <div eID="gen25831" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen25832"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25833"/>“<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞You will listen carefully⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “with hearing you will hear”</note> and will never understand,<l eID="gen25833" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25834"/>and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you will look closely⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “seeing you will see”</note> and will never perceive. <l eID="gen25834" level="2"/>

verses.name: Matthew 13:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10614"/><l level="1" sID="gen25835"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10614"/>For the heart of this people has become dull,<l eID="gen25835" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25836"/>and with their ears they hear with difficulty,<l eID="gen25836" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25837"/>and they have shut their eyes,<l eID="gen25837" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25838"/>so that they would not see with their eyes<l eID="gen25838" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25839"/>and hear with their ears<l eID="gen25839" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25840"/>and understand with their heart<l eID="gen25840" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25841"/>and turn, and I would heal them.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.6.9-Isa.6.10">Isa 6:9–10</reference></note> <l eID="gen25841" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen25832"/>

verses.name: Matthew 13:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10615"/><div sID="gen25842" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10615"/>But your eyes <transChange type="added">are</transChange> blessed because they see, and your ears because they hear.

verses.name: Matthew 13:17
verses.text: For truly I say to you that many prophets and righteous <transChange type="added">people</transChange> longed to see what you see, and did not see <transChange type="added">it</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and to hear what you hear, and did not hear it!<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>  <div eID="gen25842" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 13:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10616"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Sower Interpreted</title> <div sID="gen25843" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10616"/>“You, therefore, listen to the parable of the sower:

verses.name: Matthew 13:19
verses.text: <transChange type="added">When</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“hears”)</note> anyone hears the word about the kingdom and does not understand it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> the evil one comes and snatches away what was sown in his heart. This is what was sown on the side of the path.

verses.name: Matthew 13:20
verses.text: And what was sown on the rocky ground—this is the one who hears the word and immediately receives it with joy.

verses.name: Matthew 13:21
verses.text: But he does not have a root in himself, but <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞lasts only a little while⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “is temporary”</note> and when<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“happens”)</note> affliction or persecution happens because of the word, immediately he falls away.

verses.name: Matthew 13:22
verses.text: And what was sown into the thorn plants—this is the one who hears the word, and the anxiety of this world<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “of the world”</note> and the deceitfulness of wealth choke the word and it becomes unproductive.

verses.name: Matthew 13:23
verses.text: But what was sown on the good soil—this is the one who hears the word and understands <transChange type="added">it</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> who indeed bears fruit and produces, this one a hundred <transChange type="added">times as much</transChange>, and this one sixty, and this one thirty.”  <div eID="gen25843" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 13:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10617"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Weeds Among the Wheat</title> <div sID="gen25844" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10617"/>He put before them another parable, saying, “The kingdom of heaven may be compared to a man who sowed good seed in his field.

verses.name: Matthew 13:25
verses.text: But while his<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> people were sleeping, his enemy came and sowed darnel<note placement="foot">A weed that looks similar to wheat but has poisonous seeds</note> in the midst of the wheat and went away.

verses.name: Matthew 13:26
verses.text: So when the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞wheat⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “grass,” “hay,” but in this context referring to the good plants as opposed to the weeds</note> sprouted and yielded grain, then the darnel appeared also.

verses.name: Matthew 13:27
verses.text: So the slaves of the master of the house came <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to him, ‘Master, did you not sow good seed in your field? How then does it have darnel?’

verses.name: Matthew 13:28
verses.text: And he said to them, ‘An enemy has done this!’ So the slaves said to him, ‘Then do you want us to go <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“go”) has been translated as an English infinitive</note> gather them?’

verses.name: Matthew 13:29
verses.text: But he said, “No, lest <transChange type="added">when you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“gather”) which is understood as temporal</note> gather the darnel you uproot the wheat together with it.

verses.name: Matthew 13:30
verses.text: Let both grow together until the harvest, and at the season of the harvest I will tell the reapers, “First gather the darnel and tie it into bundles to burn them, but gather the wheat into my storehouse.” ’ ”  <div eID="gen25844" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 13:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10618"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Mustard Seed</title> <div sID="gen25845" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10618"/>He put before them another parable, saying, “The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed that a man took <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> sowed in his field.

verses.name: Matthew 13:32
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞It⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “which,” but a new sentence is started here in the English translation</note> is the smallest of all the seeds, but when it is grown it is larger than the garden herbs and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the sky come and nest in its branches.”  <div eID="gen25845" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 13:33
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10619"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Yeast</title> <div sID="gen25846" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10619"/>He told them another parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like yeast that a woman took <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> put into three measures of wheat flour until the whole <transChange type="added">batch</transChange> was leavened.”  <div eID="gen25846" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 13:34
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10620"/><title type="x-s">Parables Fulfill Prophecy</title> <div sID="gen25847" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10620"/>Jesus spoke all these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> to the crowds in parables, and he was saying nothing to them without a parable,

verses.name: Matthew 13:35
verses.text: in order that what was spoken through the prophet would be fulfilled, who said, <div eID="gen25847" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen25848"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25849"/>“I will open my mouth in parables;<l eID="gen25849" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25850"/>I will proclaim what has been hidden since the creation.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.78.2">Ps 78:2</reference></note><note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “since the creation of the world”</note> <l eID="gen25850" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen25848"/>

verses.name: Matthew 13:36
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10621"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Weeds Interpreted</title> <div sID="gen25851" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10621"/>Then he left the crowds <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“left”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> came into the house, and his disciples came to him saying, “Explain the parable of the darnel in the field to us.”

verses.name: Matthew 13:37
verses.text: So he answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “The one who sows the good seed is the Son of Man,

verses.name: Matthew 13:38
verses.text: and the field is the world. And the good seed—these are the sons of the kingdom, but the darnel are the sons of the evil one.

verses.name: Matthew 13:39
verses.text: And the enemy who sowed them is the devil, and the harvest is the end of the age, and the reapers are angels.

verses.name: Matthew 13:40
verses.text: Thus just as the darnel is gathered and burned<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “burned up”</note> with fire, so it will be at the end of the age.

verses.name: Matthew 13:41
verses.text: The Son of Man will send out his angels and they will gather out of his kingdom all the causes of sin and those who do lawless deeds,

verses.name: Matthew 13:42
verses.text: and throw them into the fiery furnace.<note placement="foot">An allusion to <reference osisRef="Dan.3.6">Dan 3:6</reference></note> In that place there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth!

verses.name: Matthew 13:43
verses.text: Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father.<note placement="foot">An allusion to <reference osisRef="Dan.12.3">Dan 12:3</reference></note> The one who has ears, let him hear!  <div eID="gen25851" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 13:44
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10622"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Treasure Hidden in a Field</title> <div sID="gen25852" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10622"/>“The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field, that a man found <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“found”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> concealed, and in his joy he goes and sells everything that he has and buys that field.  <div eID="gen25852" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 13:45
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10623"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Valuable Pearl</title> <div sID="gen25853" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10623"/>“Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant searching for fine pearls.

verses.name: Matthew 13:46
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“found”) which is understood as temporal</note> found one very valuable pearl, he went and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> sold everything that he possessed and purchased it.  <div eID="gen25853" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 13:47
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10624"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Dragnet</title> <div sID="gen25854" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10624"/>“Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a dragnet that was thrown into the sea and gathered <transChange type="added">fish</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> of every kind,

verses.name: Matthew 13:48
verses.text: which when it was filled they pulled to shore and sat down <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“sat down”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> collected the good fish<note placement="foot">*Here the word “fish” is not in the Greek text but is implied</note> into containers, but the bad they threw out.

verses.name: Matthew 13:49
verses.text: Thus it will be at the end of the age. The angels will go out and separate the evil from among the righteous

verses.name: Matthew 13:50
verses.text: and throw them into the fiery furnace.<note placement="foot">An allusion to <reference osisRef="Dan.3.6">Dan 3:6</reference></note> In that place there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth!  <div eID="gen25854" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 13:51
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10625"/><div sID="gen25855" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10625"/>“Have you understood all these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>?” They said to him, “Yes.”

verses.name: Matthew 13:52
verses.text: And he said to them, “For this <transChange type="added">reason</transChange> every scribe who has been trained for the kingdom of heaven is like the master of the house who brings out of his storeroom new <transChange type="added">things</transChange> and old <transChange type="added">things</transChange>.”  <div eID="gen25855" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 13:53
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10626"/><title type="x-s">Rejected at Nazareth</title> <div sID="gen25856" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10626"/>And it happened that when Jesus had finished these parables he went away from there.

verses.name: Matthew 13:54
verses.text: And he came to his hometown <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> began to teach<note placement="foot">The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to teach”)</note> them in their synagogue, so that they were amazed and said, “From where did this man <transChange type="added">get</transChange> this wisdom and these miracles?

verses.name: Matthew 13:55
verses.text: Is not this one the son of the carpenter? Is not his mother called Mary and his brothers James and Joseph and Simon and Judas?

verses.name: Matthew 13:56
verses.text: And are not all his sisters with us? From where then did this man <transChange type="added">get</transChange> all these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>?”

verses.name: Matthew 13:57
verses.text: And they were offended by him. But Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not without honor except in his <transChange type="added">own</transChange> hometown and in his <transChange type="added">own</transChange> household.”

verses.name: Matthew 13:58
verses.text: And he did not perform many miracles in that place because of their unbelief.  <chapter eID="Matt.13"/>

verses.name: Matthew 14:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10627"/><title type="x-s">Herod Kills John the Baptist</title> <div sID="gen25857" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10627"/>At that time Herod the tetrarch heard the report about Jesus

verses.name: Matthew 14:2
verses.text: and he said to his servants, “This is John the Baptist! He has been raised from the dead, and for this <transChange type="added">reason</transChange> miraculous powers are at work in him.”

verses.name: Matthew 14:3
verses.text: For Herod, <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“arresting”) which is understood as temporal</note> arresting John, bound him and put him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> in prison on account of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip,

verses.name: Matthew 14:4
verses.text: because John had been saying to him, “It is not permitted for you to have her.”

verses.name: Matthew 14:5
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">although he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“wanted”) which is understood as concessive</note> wanted to kill him, he feared the crowd, because they looked upon him as a prophet.  <div eID="gen25857" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 14:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10628"/><div sID="gen25858" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10628"/>But <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“took place”) which is understood as temporal</note> Herod’s birthday celebration took place, the daughter of Herodias danced in the midst <transChange type="added">of them</transChange> and pleased Herod.

verses.name: Matthew 14:7
verses.text: Therefore he promised with an oath to give her whatever she asked.

verses.name: Matthew 14:8
verses.text: And coached by her mother, she said, “Give me the head of John the Baptist here on a platter!”

verses.name: Matthew 14:9
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">although</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was distressed”) which is understood as concessive</note> the king was distressed, because of his oaths and his <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞dinner guests⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “those reclining at table with”</note> he commanded the request<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to be granted.

verses.name: Matthew 14:10
verses.text: And he sent <transChange type="added">orders</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“sent”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> had John beheaded in the prison,

verses.name: Matthew 14:11
verses.text: and his head was brought on a platter and given to the girl, and she brought <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to her mother.

verses.name: Matthew 14:12
verses.text: And his disciples came <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> took away the corpse and buried it, and went and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> told Jesus.  <div eID="gen25858" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 14:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10629"/><title type="x-s">The Feeding of Five Thousand</title> <div sID="gen25859" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10629"/>Now <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> Jesus heard it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> he withdrew from there in a boat to an isolated place by himself. And when<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> the crowds heard it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> they followed him by land from the towns.

verses.name: Matthew 14:14
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">as he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“got out”) which is understood as temporal</note> got out, he saw the large crowd and had compassion on them and healed their sick.

verses.name: Matthew 14:15
verses.text: Now <transChange type="added">when it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was”)</note> was evening, the disciples came to him saying, “The place is desolate and the hour <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞is late⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “has passed away”</note> Release the crowds so that they can go away into the villages and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“go away”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> purchase food for themselves.”

verses.name: Matthew 14:16
verses.text: But Jesus said to them, “They do not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞need⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “have need”</note> to go away. You give them something<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to eat.”

verses.name: Matthew 14:17
verses.text: And they said to him, “We do not have <transChange type="added">anything</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> here except five loaves and two fish.”

verses.name: Matthew 14:18
verses.text: So he said, “Bring them here to me.”

verses.name: Matthew 14:19
verses.text: And he commanded the crowds to recline for a meal on the grass. Taking the five loaves and the two fish <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” has been supplied in the English translation for stylistic reasons</note> looking up to heaven, he gave thanks. And after<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“breaking”) which is understood as temporal</note> breaking them,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> he gave the loaves to the disciples, and the disciples gave them<note placement="foot">*“gave them” is an implied repetition of the earlier verb</note> to the crowds.

verses.name: Matthew 14:20
verses.text: And they all ate and were satisfied, and they picked up what was left over of the broken pieces, twelve baskets full.

verses.name: Matthew 14:21
verses.text: Now those who ate were about five thousand men, in addition to women and children.  <div eID="gen25859" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 14:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10630"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Walks on the Water</title> <div sID="gen25860" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10630"/>And immediately he made the disciples get into the boat and go ahead of him to the other side, while he sent away the crowds.

verses.name: Matthew 14:23
