verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“sent away”) which is understood as temporal</note> sent away the crowds, he went up on the mountain by himself to pray. So when<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“came”)</note> evening came, he was there alone.

verses.name: Matthew 14:24
verses.text: But the boat was already many stadia distant from the land, being beaten by the waves, because the wind was against <transChange type="added">it</transChange>.

verses.name: Matthew 14:25
verses.text: And in the fourth watch of the night he came to them, walking on the sea.

verses.name: Matthew 14:26
verses.text: But the disciples, <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw him walking on the sea, were terrified, saying, “It is a ghost!” and they cried out in fear.

verses.name: Matthew 14:27
verses.text: But immediately Jesus spoke to them, saying, “Have courage, I am <transChange type="added">he</transChange>! Do not be afraid!”

verses.name: Matthew 14:28
verses.text: And Peter answered him <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “Lord, if <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞it is you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “you are” he</note> command me to come to you on the water!”

verses.name: Matthew 14:29
verses.text: So he said, “Come!” And getting out of the boat, Peter walked on the water and came toward Jesus.

verses.name: Matthew 14:30
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw the strong wind, he was afraid. And beginning to sink, he cried out, saying, “Lord, save me!”

verses.name: Matthew 14:31
verses.text: And immediately Jesus extended his<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> hand and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“extended”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> caught him and said to him, “<transChange type="added">You</transChange> of little faith! Why did you doubt?”

verses.name: Matthew 14:32
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“got”)</note> they got into the boat, the wind abated.

verses.name: Matthew 14:33
verses.text: So those in the boat worshiped him, saying, “Truly you are the Son of God!”  <div eID="gen25860" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 14:34
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10631"/><title type="x-s">Many Healed at Gennesaret</title> <div sID="gen25861" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10631"/>And <transChange type="added">after they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had crossed over”) which is understood as temporal</note> had crossed over, they came to land at Gennesaret.

verses.name: Matthew 14:35
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“recognized”) which is understood as temporal</note> the men of that place recognized him, they sent word into that whole surrounding region, and they brought to him all those <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who were sick⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “having badly”</note>

verses.name: Matthew 14:36
verses.text: And they were imploring him that they might only touch the edge<note placement="foot">Or “tassel”</note> of his cloak, and all those who touched it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> were cured.  <chapter eID="Matt.14"/>

verses.name: Matthew 15:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10632"/><title type="x-s">Human Traditions and God’s Commandments</title> <div sID="gen25862" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10632"/>Then Pharisees and scribes came to Jesus from Jerusalem, saying,

verses.name: Matthew 15:2
verses.text: “Why do your disciples break the tradition of the elders? For they do not wash their hands when they eat <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a meal⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “bread”</note>

verses.name: Matthew 15:3
verses.text: So he answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to them, “Why do you also break the commandment of God because of your tradition?

verses.name: Matthew 15:4
verses.text: For God said, ‘Honor your<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> father and your<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> mother,’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Exod.20.12">Exod 20:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="Deut.5.16">Deut 5:16</reference></note> and ‘The one who speaks evil of father or mother <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞must certainly die⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “let him die the death”</note>.’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Exod.21.17">Exod 21:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="Lev.20.9">Lev 20:9</reference></note>

verses.name: Matthew 15:5
verses.text: But you say, ‘Whoever says to his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> father or his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> mother, “Whatever <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞benefit you would have received⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “you would have been benefited”</note> from me <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a gift <transChange type="added">to God</transChange>,”

verses.name: Matthew 15:6
verses.text: need not honor his father,’<note placement="foot">Most later manuscripts add “or his mother”</note> and you make void the word of God for the sake of your tradition.

verses.name: Matthew 15:7
verses.text: Hypocrites! Isaiah correctly prophesied about you saying,  <div eID="gen25862" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 15:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10633"/><lg sID="gen25863"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25864"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10633"/>‘This people honors me with their<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> lips,<l eID="gen25864" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25865"/>but their heart is far, far away from me, <l eID="gen25865" level="2"/>

verses.name: Matthew 15:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10634"/><l level="1" sID="gen25866"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10634"/>and they worship me in vain,<l eID="gen25866" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25867"/>teaching <transChange type="added">as</transChange> doctrines the commandments of men.’ ”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.29.13">Isa 29:13</reference></note> <l eID="gen25867" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen25863"/>

verses.name: Matthew 15:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10635"/><title type="x-s">Defilement from Within</title> <div sID="gen25868" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10635"/>And summoning the crowd, he said to them, “Hear and understand:

verses.name: Matthew 15:11
verses.text: It is not what goes into the mouth that defiles a person, but what comes out of the mouth—this defiles a person.”

verses.name: Matthew 15:12
verses.text: Then the disciples came <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to him, “Do you know that the Pharisees were offended when they<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard this saying?”

verses.name: Matthew 15:13
verses.text: And he answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “Every plant that my heavenly Father did not plant will be uprooted.

verses.name: Matthew 15:14
verses.text: Let<note placement="foot">Or “Depart from”</note> them! They are blind guides of the blind. And if the blind guide the blind, both will fall into a pit.”

verses.name: Matthew 15:15
verses.text: But Peter answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to him, “Explain this parable to us.”

verses.name: Matthew 15:16
verses.text: But he said, “Are you also still without understanding?

verses.name: Matthew 15:17
verses.text: Do you not understand that everything that enters into the mouth goes into the stomach and is evacuated into the latrine?

verses.name: Matthew 15:18
verses.text: But the things that come out of the mouth come from the heart, and these defile the person.

verses.name: Matthew 15:19
verses.text: For from the heart come evil plans, murder, adultery, sexual immorality, theft, false witness, abusive speech.

verses.name: Matthew 15:20
verses.text: These are the things that defile a person. But eating with unwashed hands does not defile a person!”  <div eID="gen25868" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 15:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10636"/><title type="x-s">A Canaanite Woman’s Great Faith</title> <div sID="gen25869" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10636"/>And departing from there, Jesus went away to the region of Tyre and Sidon.

verses.name: Matthew 15:22
verses.text: And behold, a Canaanite woman from that district came <transChange type="added">and</transChange> cried out, saying, “Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David! My daughter <transChange type="added">is</transChange> severely possessed by a demon!”

verses.name: Matthew 15:23
verses.text: But he did not answer her a word. And his disciples came up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> asked him, saying, “Send her away, because she is crying out after us!”

verses.name: Matthew 15:24
verses.text: But he answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “I was not sent except to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”

verses.name: Matthew 15:25
verses.text: But she came <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> knelt down before him, saying, “Lord, help me!”

verses.name: Matthew 15:26
verses.text: And he answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “It is not right to take the children’s bread and throw it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to the dogs!”

verses.name: Matthew 15:27
verses.text: So she said, “Yes, Lord, for even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their master’s table.”

verses.name: Matthew 15:28
verses.text: Then Jesus answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange> said to her, “O woman, your faith <transChange type="added">is</transChange> great! Let it be done for you as you want.” And her daughter was healed from that hour.  <div eID="gen25869" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 15:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10637"/><title type="x-s">Many Others Healed in Galilee</title> <div sID="gen25870" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10637"/>And departing from there, Jesus went along the Sea of Galilee, and he went up on the mountain <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> was sitting there.

verses.name: Matthew 15:30
verses.text: And large crowds came to him, having with them <transChange type="added">the</transChange> mute, blind, lame, crippled,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “the lame, blind, crippled, mute”</note> and many others, and they put them down at his feet, and he healed them.

verses.name: Matthew 15:31
verses.text: So then the crowd was astonished <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw the mute speaking, the crippled healthy, and the lame walking, and the blind seeing, and they praised the God of Israel.  <div eID="gen25870" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 15:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10638"/><title type="x-s">The Feeding of Four Thousand</title> <div sID="gen25871" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10638"/>And Jesus summoned his disciples <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“summoned”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “I have compassion on the crowd, because they have remained with me three days already and do not have anything to eat, and I do not want to send them away hungry lest they give out on the way.”

verses.name: Matthew 15:33
verses.text: And the disciples said to him, “Where in <transChange type="added">this</transChange> desolate place <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞can we get⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for us”</note> so much bread that such a great crowd could be satisfied?”

verses.name: Matthew 15:34
verses.text: And Jesus said to them, “How many loaves do you have?” So they said, “Seven, and a few little fish.”

verses.name: Matthew 15:35
verses.text: And commanding the crowd to recline for a meal on the ground,

verses.name: Matthew 15:36
verses.text: he took the seven loaves and the fish and <transChange type="added">after he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had given thanks”) which is understood as temporal</note> had given thanks, he broke them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and began giving<note placement="foot">The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began giving”)</note> them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to the disciples, and the disciples <transChange type="added">gave them</transChange> to the crowds.

verses.name: Matthew 15:37
verses.text: And they all ate and were satisfied, and they picked up what was left over of the broken pieces, seven baskets full.

verses.name: Matthew 15:38
verses.text: Now those who ate were four thousand men, in addition to women and children.

verses.name: Matthew 15:39
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had given thanks”) which is understood as temporal</note> sent away the crowds, he got into the boat and went to the region of Magadan.  <chapter eID="Matt.15"/>

verses.name: Matthew 16:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10639"/><title type="x-s">The Signs of the Times</title> <div sID="gen25872" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10639"/>And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“came”) which is understood as temporal</note> the Pharisees and Sadducees came to test him,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> they asked him to show them a sign from heaven.

verses.name: Matthew 16:2
verses.text: So he answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to them, “When<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“comes”)</note> evening comes you say, ‘<transChange type="added">It will be</transChange> fair weather because the sky is red,’

verses.name: Matthew 16:3
verses.text: and early in the morning, ‘Today <transChange type="added">it will be</transChange> stormy weather, because the sky is red <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied in the translation because of English style</note> darkening.’ You know how to evaluate correctly the appearance of the sky, but you are not able to evaluate<note placement="foot">*Here “to evaluate” is an implied repetition of the verb earlier in the verse</note> the signs of the times.

verses.name: Matthew 16:4
verses.text: An evil and adulterous generation seeks for a sign, and a sign will not be given to it except the sign of Jonah!” And he left them <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“left”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> went away.  <div eID="gen25872" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 16:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10640"/><title type="x-s">Beware the Leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees</title> <div sID="gen25873" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10640"/>And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“arrived”) which is understood as temporal</note> the disciples arrived at the other side,<note placement="foot">That is, the other side of the Sea of Galilee</note> they had forgotten to take bread.

verses.name: Matthew 16:6
verses.text: And Jesus said to them, “Watch out for and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees!”

verses.name: Matthew 16:7
verses.text: So they were discussing <transChange type="added">this</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> among themselves, saying, “<transChange type="added">It is</transChange> because we did not take bread.”

verses.name: Matthew 16:8
verses.text: But knowing <transChange type="added">this</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> Jesus said, “Why are you discussing among yourselves that you did not take bread,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “you do not have bread”</note> <transChange type="added">you</transChange> of little faith?

verses.name: Matthew 16:9
verses.text: Do you not yet understand or do you not remember the five loaves for the five thousand, and how many baskets you took up?

verses.name: Matthew 16:10
verses.text: Or the seven loaves for the four thousand and how many baskets you took up?

verses.name: Matthew 16:11
verses.text: How do you not understand that I did not speak to you about bread? But beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees!”

verses.name: Matthew 16:12
verses.text: Then they understood that he did not say to beware of the leaven of bread, but of the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.  <div eID="gen25873" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 16:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10641"/><title type="x-s">Peter’s Confession at Caesarea Philippi</title> <div sID="gen25874" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10641"/>Now <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“came”) which is understood as temporal</note> Jesus came to the region of Caesarea <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Philippi⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “of Philip”</note> he began asking<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began asking”)</note> his disciples, saying, “Who do people say <transChange type="added">that</transChange> the Son of Man is?”

verses.name: Matthew 16:14
verses.text: And they said, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Some⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “those on the one hand”</note> <transChange type="added">say</transChange> John the Baptist, but others Elijah, and others Jeremiah or one of the prophets.”

verses.name: Matthew 16:15
verses.text: He said to them, “But who do you say <transChange type="added">that</transChange> I am?”

verses.name: Matthew 16:16
verses.text: And Simon Peter answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God!”

verses.name: Matthew 16:17
verses.text: And Jesus answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to him, “Blessed are you, Simon son of Jonah, because flesh and blood did not reveal this<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to you, but my Father <transChange type="added">who is</transChange> in heaven.

verses.name: Matthew 16:18
verses.text: And I also say to you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of Hades will not overpower it!

verses.name: Matthew 16:19
verses.text: I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven, and whatever you bind on earth will be bound<note placement="foot">Or “will have been bound”</note> in heaven, and whatever you release on earth will be released<note placement="foot">Or “will have been released”</note> in heaven.”

verses.name: Matthew 16:20
verses.text: Then he commanded the disciples that they should tell no one that he was the Christ.  <div eID="gen25874" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 16:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10642"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Predicts His Death and Resurrection</title> <div sID="gen25875" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10642"/>From that time <transChange type="added">on</transChange> Jesus began to show his disciples that he must go to Jerusalem and suffer many <transChange type="added">things</transChange> from the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and be raised on the third day.

verses.name: Matthew 16:22
verses.text: And Peter took him aside <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took … aside”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> began to rebuke him, saying, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞God forbid⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “merciful to you”</note> Lord! This will never happen to you!”

verses.name: Matthew 16:23
verses.text: But he turned around <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“turned around”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to Peter, “Get behind me, Satan! You are a cause for stumbling to me, because you are not intent on the things of God, but the things of people!”  <div eID="gen25875" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 16:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10643"/><title type="x-s">Taking Up One’s Cross to Follow Jesus</title> <div sID="gen25876" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10643"/>Then Jesus said to his disciples, “If anyone wants to come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross and follow me.

verses.name: Matthew 16:25
verses.text: For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life on account of me will find it.

verses.name: Matthew 16:26
verses.text: For what will a person be benefited if he gains the whole world but forfeits his life? Or what will a person give in exchange for his life?

verses.name: Matthew 16:27
verses.text: For the Son of Man is going to come in the glory of his Father with his angels, and at that time he will reward each one according to <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞what he has done⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “his activity”</note>

verses.name: Matthew 16:28
verses.text: Truly I say to you, that there are some of those standing here who will never experience death until they see the Son of Man coming in his kingdom.”  <chapter eID="Matt.16"/>

verses.name: Matthew 17:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10644"/><title type="x-s">The Transfiguration</title> <div sID="gen25877" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10644"/>And after six days Jesus took along Peter and James and John his brother, and led them up on a high mountain by themselves.

verses.name: Matthew 17:2
verses.text: And he was transfigured before them, and his face shone like the sun, and his clothing became bright as the light.

verses.name: Matthew 17:3
verses.text: And behold, Moses and Elijah appeared to them, talking with him.

verses.name: Matthew 17:4
verses.text: So Peter answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to Jesus, “Lord, it is good <transChange type="added">that</transChange> we are here! If you want, I will make here three shelters, one for you and one for Moses and one for Elijah.”

verses.name: Matthew 17:5
verses.text: <transChange type="added">While</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“speaking”)</note> he was still speaking, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them, and behold, a voice from the cloud said, “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased. Listen to him!”

verses.name: Matthew 17:6
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> the disciples heard this,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> they fell down on their faces and were extremely frightened.

verses.name: Matthew 17:7
verses.text: And Jesus came and touched them <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“touched”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “Get up and do not be afraid.”

verses.name: Matthew 17:8
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“lifted up”) which is understood as temporal</note> lifted up their eyes they saw no one except him—Jesus alone.  <div eID="gen25877" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 17:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10645"/><div sID="gen25878" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10645"/>And <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“were coming down”)</note> they were coming down from the mountain, Jesus commanded them saying, “Tell no one the vision until the Son of Man is raised from the dead.”

verses.name: Matthew 17:10
verses.text: And the disciples asked him, saying, “Then why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”

verses.name: Matthew 17:11
verses.text: And he answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “Elijah indeed is coming, and will restore all <transChange type="added">things</transChange>.

verses.name: Matthew 17:12
verses.text: But I say to you that Elijah has already come, and they did not recognize him, but did with him whatever they wanted. In the <transChange type="added">same</transChange> way also the Son of Man is going to suffer <transChange type="added">at</transChange> their hands.”

verses.name: Matthew 17:13
verses.text: Then the disciples understood that he had spoken to them about John the Baptist.  <div eID="gen25878" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 17:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10646"/><title type="x-s">A Demon-possessed Boy Healed</title> <div sID="gen25879" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10646"/>And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“came”)</note> came to the crowd, a man approached him, kneeling down before him

verses.name: Matthew 17:15
verses.text: and saying, “Lord, have mercy on my son, because he has seizures and suffers severely, for often he falls into the fire and often into the water.

verses.name: Matthew 17:16
verses.text: And I brought him to your disciples, and they were not able to heal him.”

verses.name: Matthew 17:17
verses.text: And Jesus answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “O unbelieving and perverse generation! <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞How long⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “until when”</note> will I be with you? <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞How long⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “until when”</note> must I put up with you? Bring him here to me!”

verses.name: Matthew 17:18
verses.text: And Jesus rebuked him, and the demon came out of him and the boy was healed from that hour.  <div eID="gen25879" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 17:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10647"/><div sID="gen25880" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10647"/>Then the disciples approached Jesus privately <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“approached”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Why⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for what”</note> were we not able to expel it?”

verses.name: Matthew 17:20
verses.text: And he said to them, “Because of your little faith. For truly I say to you, if you have faith like a mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, ‘Move from here <transChange type="added">to</transChange> there,’ and it will move, and nothing will be impossible for you.”<note placement="foot">Most later Greek manuscripts add v. <reference osisRef="Matt.17.21">21</reference>, “But this kind does not go out except by prayer and fasting.”</note>  <div eID="gen25880" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 17:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10648"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Predicts His Death and Resurrection a Second Time</title> <div sID="gen25881" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10648"/>Now <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“were gathering”)</note> they were gathering in Galilee, Jesus said to them, “The Son of Man is going to be betrayed into the hands of men,<note placement="foot">Or possibly “of people,” in a generic sense, although the reference here may be to the specific group responsible for Jesus’ arrest, where it is unlikely women were present</note>

verses.name: Matthew 17:23
verses.text: and they will kill him, and on the third day he will be raised.” And they were extremely distressed.  <div eID="gen25881" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 17:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10649"/><title type="x-s">Paying the Double Drachma Temple Tax</title> <div sID="gen25882" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10649"/>Now <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“arrived”)</note> they arrived in Capernaum, the ones who collected the double drachma tax<note placement="foot">This refers to the half-shekel annual tax paid by Jewish males to support the temple; over time the name of the coin commonly used to pay the tax came to be used for the tax itself</note> came up to Peter and said, “Does your teacher not pay the double drachma <transChange type="added">tax</transChange>?”

verses.name: Matthew 17:25
verses.text: He said, “Yes.” And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“came”) which is understood as temporal</note> came into the house, Jesus spoke to him first, saying, “What do you think, Simon? From whom do the kings of the earth collect tolls or taxes—from their own sons, or from foreigners?”

verses.name: Matthew 17:26
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“said”) which is understood as temporal</note> said, “From foreigners,” Jesus said to him, “Then the sons are free.

verses.name: Matthew 17:27
verses.text: But so that we do not give offense to them, go out to the sea, cast <transChange type="added">a line with</transChange><note placement="foot">*The words “a line with” are not in the Greek text but are implied</note> a hook, and take the first fish that comes up. And when you<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“open”) which is understood as temporal</note> open its mouth, you will find a four-drachma coin. Take that and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“take”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> give it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to them for me and you.”  <chapter eID="Matt.17"/>

verses.name: Matthew 18:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10650"/><title type="x-s">The Question About Who Is Greatest</title> <div sID="gen25883" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10650"/>At that time the disciples came up to Jesus, saying, “Who then is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?”

verses.name: Matthew 18:2
verses.text: And calling a child <transChange type="added">to himself</transChange>, he had him stand in their midst

verses.name: Matthew 18:3
verses.text: and said, “Truly I say to you, unless you turn around and become like young children, you will never enter into the kingdom of heaven!

verses.name: Matthew 18:4
verses.text: Therefore whoever humbles himself like this child, this person is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven,

verses.name: Matthew 18:5
verses.text: and whoever welcomes one child such as this in my name welcomes me.

verses.name: Matthew 18:6
verses.text: But whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to sin, it would be better for him that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a large millstone⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a millstone of a donkey”</note> be hung on<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “around”</note> his neck and he be drowned in the depths of the sea.

verses.name: Matthew 18:7
verses.text: Woe to the world because of causes for stumbling, for <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> a necessity <transChange type="added">that</transChange> causes for stumbling come; nevertheless, woe to the person through whom the cause for stumbling comes.

verses.name: Matthew 18:8
verses.text: And if your hand or your foot causes you to sin, cut it off and throw <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> from you! It is better for you to enter into life crippled or lame than, having two hands or two feet, to be thrown into the eternal fire!

verses.name: Matthew 18:9
verses.text: And if your eye causes you to sin, tear it out and throw <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> from you! It is better for you to enter into life one-eyed than, having two eyes, to be thrown into fiery hell!  <div eID="gen25883" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 18:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10651"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Lost Sheep</title> <div sID="gen25884" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10651"/>“See to it that you do not despise one of these little ones, for I tell you that their angels in heaven constantly see the face of my Father <transChange type="added">who is</transChange> in heaven.<note placement="foot">Many later Greek manuscripts include vs. <reference osisRef="Matt.18.11">11</reference>, “For the Son of Man came to save those who are lost.”</note>

verses.name: Matthew 18:12
verses.text: What do you think? If <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a certain man has⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “there are to a certain man”</note> a hundred sheep, and one of them wanders away, will he not leave the ninety-nine on the hills and go and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“go”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> look for the one that wandered away?

verses.name: Matthew 18:13
verses.text: And if he happens to find it, truly I say to you that he rejoices over it more than over the ninety-nine that did not wander away.

verses.name: Matthew 18:14
verses.text: In the <transChange type="added">same</transChange> way it is not the will <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in the presence of”</note> your Father <transChange type="added">who is</transChange> in heaven that one of these little ones perish.  <div eID="gen25884" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 18:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10652"/><title type="x-s">Confronting a Brother Who Sins Against You</title> <div sID="gen25885" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10652"/>“Now if your brother sins against you, go correct him between you and him alone. If he listens to you, you have gained your brother.

verses.name: Matthew 18:16
verses.text: But if he does not listen, take with you in addition one or two <transChange type="added">others</transChange>, so that by <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the testimony⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the mouth”</note> of two or three witnesses every matter may be established.

verses.name: Matthew 18:17
verses.text: And if he refuses to listen to them, tell <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to the church. But if he refuses to listen to the church also, let him be to you as a Gentile and a tax collector.  <div eID="gen25885" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 18:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10653"/><div sID="gen25886" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10653"/>“Truly I say to you, whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you release on earth will be released in heaven.

verses.name: Matthew 18:19
verses.text: Again, truly I say to you that if two of you agree on earth about any matter that they ask, it will be done for them from my Father <transChange type="added">who is</transChange> in heaven.

verses.name: Matthew 18:20
verses.text: For where two or three are gathered in my name, I am there in the midst of them.”  <div eID="gen25886" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 18:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10654"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Unforgiving Slave</title> <div sID="gen25887" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10654"/>Then Peter came up to him <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “Then Peter came up and said to him”</note> “Lord, how many times will my brother sin against me and I will forgive him? Up to seven times?”

verses.name: Matthew 18:22
verses.text: Jesus said to him, “I do not say to you up to seven times, but up to seventy times seven!<note placement="foot">Or “seventy-seven times”</note>  <div eID="gen25887" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 18:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10655"/><div sID="gen25888" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10655"/>“For this <transChange type="added">reason</transChange> the kingdom of heaven may be compared to a man—a king—who wanted to settle accounts with his slaves.

verses.name: Matthew 18:24
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“began”)</note> he began to settle them,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> someone was brought to him who owed ten thousand talents.

verses.name: Matthew 18:25
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">because</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“have”) which is understood as causal</note> he did not have enough<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to repay it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> the master ordered him to be sold, and his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> wife and his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> children and everything that he had, and to be repaid.

verses.name: Matthew 18:26
verses.text: Then the slave threw himself to the ground <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“threw himself to the ground”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> began to do obeisance to him, saying, ‘Be patient with me, and I will pay back everything to you!’

verses.name: Matthew 18:27
verses.text: So the master of that slave, <transChange type="added">because he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had compassion”) which is understood as causal</note> had compassion, released him and forgave him the loan.

verses.name: Matthew 18:28
verses.text: But that slave went out <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> found one of his fellow slaves who owed him a hundred denarii, and taking hold of him, he began to choke him,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> saying, ‘Pay back everything that you owe!’

verses.name: Matthew 18:29
verses.text: Then his fellow slave threw himself to the ground <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“threw himself to the ground”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> began to implore<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to implore”)</note> him, saying, ‘Be patient with me and I will repay you!’

verses.name: Matthew 18:30
verses.text: But he did not want to, but rather he went <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> threw him into prison until he would repay what was owed.

verses.name: Matthew 18:31
verses.text: So <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> his fellow slaves saw what had happened, they were extremely distressed, and went and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> reported to their master everything that had happened.

verses.name: Matthew 18:32
verses.text: Then his master summoned him <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“summoned”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to him, ‘Wicked slave! I forgave you all that debt because you implored me!

verses.name: Matthew 18:33
verses.text: Should you not also have shown mercy to your fellow slave as I also showed mercy to you?’

verses.name: Matthew 18:34
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">because he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was angry”) which is understood as causal</note> was angry, his master handed him over to the merciless jailers<note placement="foot">Or “torturers”</note> until he would repay everything that was owed.

verses.name: Matthew 18:35
verses.text: So also my heavenly Father will do to you, unless each of you forgives his brother from your hearts!”  <chapter eID="Matt.18"/>

verses.name: Matthew 19:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10656"/><title type="x-s">On Divorce</title> <div sID="gen25889" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10656"/>And it happened that when Jesus had finished these statements, he went away from Galilee and came into the region of Judea on the other side of the Jordan.

verses.name: Matthew 19:2
verses.text: And large crowds followed him, and he healed them there.

verses.name: Matthew 19:3
verses.text: And Pharisees came up to him <transChange type="added">in order to</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “in order to” is supplied as a component of the participle (“test”) which is understood as purpose</note> test him, and asked<note placement="foot">*Here the participle (“asked”) is translated as a finite verb because of English style</note> if it was permitted for a man to divorce his wife for any cause.

verses.name: Matthew 19:4
verses.text: And he answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “Have you not read that the one who created them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> from the beginning made them male and female

verses.name: Matthew 19:5
verses.text: and said, ‘On account of this a man will leave his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> father and his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> mother and will be joined to his wife, and the two will become one flesh’?<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Gen.2.24">Gen 2:24</reference></note>

verses.name: Matthew 19:6
verses.text: So then, they are no longer two but one flesh. Therefore what God has joined together, man must not separate.”

verses.name: Matthew 19:7
verses.text: They said to him, “Why then did Moses command <transChange type="added">us</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to give a document—a certificate of divorce—and to divorce her?”

verses.name: Matthew 19:8
verses.text: He said to them, “Moses, with reference to your hardness of heart, permitted you to divorce your wives, but from the beginning it was not like this.

verses.name: Matthew 19:9
verses.text: Now I say to you that whoever divorces his wife, except on the basis of sexual immorality, and marries another commits adultery, and whoever marries her who is divorced commits adultery.”<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts omit “and whoever marries her who is divorced commits adultery”</note>  <div eID="gen25889" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 19:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10657"/><div sID="gen25890" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10657"/>The disciples<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “His disciples”</note> said to him, “If this is the case of a man with his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> wife, it would be better not to marry!”

verses.name: Matthew 19:11
verses.text: But he said to them, “Not everyone can accept this saying but <transChange type="added">those</transChange> to whom it has been given.

verses.name: Matthew 19:12
verses.text: For there are eunuchs who were born as such from <transChange type="added">their</transChange> mother’s womb, and there are eunuchs who were made eunuchs by people, and there are eunuchs who have made themselves <transChange type="added">eunuchs</transChange><note placement="foot">An understood repetition of the term from earlier in the verse</note> for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. The one who is able to accept this,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> let him accept it.”<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>  <div eID="gen25890" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 19:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10658"/><title type="x-s">Little Children Brought to Jesus</title> <div sID="gen25891" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10658"/>Then children were brought to him so that he could lay his<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> hands on them and pray, but the disciples rebuked them.

verses.name: Matthew 19:14
verses.text: But Jesus said, “Allow the children, and do not forbid them to come to me, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞for to such belongs⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for of such is”</note> the kingdom of heaven.”

verses.name: Matthew 19:15
verses.text: And he laid his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> hands on them and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“laid”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> traveled on from there.  <div eID="gen25891" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 19:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10659"/><title type="x-s">A Rich Young Man</title> <div sID="gen25892" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10659"/>And behold, someone came up to him <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “Teacher, what good <transChange type="added">thing</transChange> must I do so that I will have eternal life?”

verses.name: Matthew 19:17
verses.text: And he said to him, “Why are you asking me about <transChange type="added">what is</transChange> good? There is one <transChange type="added">who is</transChange> good. But if you want to enter into life, keep the commandments!”

verses.name: Matthew 19:18
verses.text: He said to him, “Which <transChange type="added">ones</transChange>?” And Jesus said, “Do not commit murder, do not commit adultery, do not steal, do not give false testimony,

verses.name: Matthew 19:19
verses.text: honor your<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> father and your<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> mother, and love your neighbor as yourself.”

verses.name: Matthew 19:20
verses.text: The young man said to him, “All these I have observed. What do I still lack?”

verses.name: Matthew 19:21
verses.text: Jesus said to him, “If you want to be perfect, go, sell your possessions and give <transChange type="added">the proceeds</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to the poor—and you will have treasure in heaven—and come, follow me.”

verses.name: Matthew 19:22
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> the young man heard the statement, he went away sorrowful, because he was one who had many possessions.  <div eID="gen25892" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 19:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10660"/><div sID="gen25893" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10660"/>And Jesus said to his disciples, “Truly I say to you that with difficulty a rich person will enter into the kingdom of heaven!

verses.name: Matthew 19:24
verses.text: And again I say to you, it is easier <transChange type="added">for</transChange> a camel to go through the eye of a needle than a rich person into<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “to enter into”</note> the kingdom of God.”

verses.name: Matthew 19:25
verses.text: So <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> the disciples heard this,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> they were extremely amazed, saying, “Then who can be saved?”

verses.name: Matthew 19:26
verses.text: But Jesus looked at <transChange type="added">them</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“looked at”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to them, “With human beings this is impossible, but with God all <transChange type="added">things</transChange> <transChange type="added">are</transChange> possible.”

verses.name: Matthew 19:27
verses.text: Then Peter answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to him, “Behold, we have left everything and followed you. What then will there be for us?”

verses.name: Matthew 19:28
verses.text: And Jesus said to them, “Truly I say to you that in the renewal <transChange type="added">of the world</transChange>,<note placement="foot">The words “of the world” are supplied as a clarification of “renewal”</note> when the Son of Man sits on his glorious throne, you who have followed me—you also will sit on twelve thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

verses.name: Matthew 19:29
verses.text: And everyone who has left houses or brothers or sisters or father or mother or wife<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts omit “or wife”</note> or children or fields on account of my name will receive a hundred times as much, and will inherit eternal life.

verses.name: Matthew 19:30
verses.text: But many <transChange type="added">who are</transChange> first will be last, and the last first.  <chapter eID="Matt.19"/>

verses.name: Matthew 20:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10661"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Workers in the Vineyard</title> <div sID="gen25894" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10661"/>“For the kingdom of heaven is like a man—the master of the house—who went out early in the morning to hire workers for his vineyard.

verses.name: Matthew 20:2
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“coming to an agreement”) which is understood as temporal</note> coming to an agreement with the workers for a denarius per day, he sent them into his vineyard.

verses.name: Matthew 20:3
verses.text: And going out about the third hour, he saw others standing idle in the marketplace.

verses.name: Matthew 20:4
verses.text: And to those <transChange type="added">people</transChange> he said, ‘You also go into the vineyard, and I will give you whatever is right.’

verses.name: Matthew 20:5
verses.text: So they went. Going out<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “And going out”</note> again about the sixth and ninth hour he did the same <transChange type="added">thing</transChange>.

verses.name: Matthew 20:6
verses.text: And about the eleventh <transChange type="added">hour</transChange> he went out <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> found others standing <transChange type="added">there</transChange> and said to them, ‘Why are you standing here the whole day unemployed?’

verses.name: Matthew 20:7
verses.text: They said to him, ‘Because no one hired us.’ He said to them, ‘You go also into the vineyard.’

verses.name: Matthew 20:8
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“came”)</note> evening came, the owner of the vineyard said to his manager, ‘Call the workers and pay them their<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> wages, beginning from the last up to the first.’

verses.name: Matthew 20:9
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange> the ones <transChange type="added">hired</transChange> about the eleventh hour came, they received a denarius apiece.

verses.name: Matthew 20:10
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“came”) which is understood as temporal</note> the first came, they thought that they would receive more, and they also received a denarius apiece.

verses.name: Matthew 20:11
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“received”) which is understood as temporal</note> received it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> they began to complain<note placement="foot">The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to complain”)</note> against the master of the house,

verses.name: Matthew 20:12
verses.text: saying, ‘These last <transChange type="added">people</transChange> worked one hour and you made them equal to us who have endured the burden of the day and the burning heat!’

verses.name: Matthew 20:13
verses.text: But he answered one of them <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, ‘Friend, I am not doing you wrong. Did you not come to an agreement with me for a denarius?

verses.name: Matthew 20:14
verses.text: Take <transChange type="added">what is</transChange> yours and go! But I want to give to this last <transChange type="added">person</transChange> <transChange type="added">the same</transChange> as <transChange type="added">I gave</transChange><note placement="foot">The words “I gave” are an implied repetition from the verb earlier in the verse</note> to you also.

verses.name: Matthew 20:15
verses.text: Is it not<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “Or is it not”</note> permitted for me to do whatever I want with <transChange type="added">what is</transChange> mine? Or is your eye evil because I am generous?’

verses.name: Matthew 20:16
verses.text: Thus the last will be first and the first last.”  <div eID="gen25894" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 20:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10662"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Predicts His Death and Resurrection a Third Time</title> <div sID="gen25895" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10662"/>And <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was going up”) which is understood as temporal</note> Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, he took the twelve disciples by themselves and said to them on the way,

verses.name: Matthew 20:18
verses.text: “Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and scribes, and they will condemn him to death,

verses.name: Matthew 20:19
verses.text: and will hand him over to the Gentiles to mock <transChange type="added">him</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and flog him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and crucify him,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and on the third day he will be raised.”  <div eID="gen25895" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 20:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10663"/><title type="x-s">A Request by the Mother of James and John</title> <div sID="gen25896" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10663"/>Then the mother of the sons of Zebedee came up to him with her sons, <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the participle (“kneeling down”) has been translated as a finite verb in keeping with English style</note> kneeling down she asked<note placement="foot">*Here the participle (“asked”) is translated as a finite verb because of English style</note> something from him.

verses.name: Matthew 20:21
verses.text: And he said to her, “What do you want?” She said to him, “Say that these two sons of mine may sit one at your right hand and one at your left in your kingdom.”

verses.name: Matthew 20:22
verses.text: But Jesus answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “You do not know what you are asking! Are you able to drink the cup that I am about to drink?” They said to him, “We are able.”

verses.name: Matthew 20:23
verses.text: He said to them, “You will indeed drink my cup, but to sit at my right hand and at my left is not mine<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “this is not mine”</note> to grant, but <transChange type="added">is</transChange> for those for whom it has been prepared by my Father.”  <div eID="gen25896" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 20:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10664"/><div sID="gen25897" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10664"/>And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> the ten heard this,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> they were indignant concerning the two brothers.

verses.name: Matthew 20:25
verses.text: But Jesus called them to himself <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“called … to himself”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “You know that the rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and those in high positions exercise authority over them.

verses.name: Matthew 20:26
verses.text: It will not be like this among you! But whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant,

verses.name: Matthew 20:27
verses.text: and whoever wants to be most prominent among you must be your slave—

verses.name: Matthew 20:28
verses.text: just as the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life <transChange type="added">as</transChange> a ransom for many.”  <div eID="gen25897" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 20:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10665"/><title type="x-s">Two Blind Men Healed at Jericho</title> <div sID="gen25898" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10665"/>And <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“were going out”)</note> they were going out of Jericho, a large crowd followed him.

verses.name: Matthew 20:30
verses.text: And behold, <transChange type="added">there were</transChange> two blind men sitting beside the road. <transChange type="added">When they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard that Jesus was passing by, they called out, saying, “Lord, have mercy on us,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “Have mercy on us, Lord”</note> Son of David!”

verses.name: Matthew 20:31
verses.text: And the crowd rebuked them so that they would be quiet. But they called out all the more, saying, “Lord, have mercy on us,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “Have mercy on us, Lord”</note> Son of David!”

verses.name: Matthew 20:32
verses.text: And Jesus stopped,<note placement="foot">*Here the participle (“stopped”) is translated as a finite verb because of English style</note> called them, and said, “What do you want me to do for you?”

verses.name: Matthew 20:33
verses.text: They said to him, “Lord, that our eyes be opened!”

verses.name: Matthew 20:34
verses.text: And having compassion, Jesus touched their eyes, and immediately they received <transChange type="added">their</transChange> sight and followed him.  <chapter eID="Matt.20"/>

verses.name: Matthew 21:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10666"/><title type="x-s">The Triumphal Entry</title> <div sID="gen25899" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10666"/>And when they drew near to Jerusalem and came to Bethphage at the Mount of Olives, then Jesus sent two disciples,

verses.name: Matthew 21:2
verses.text: saying to them, “Go into the village before you, and right away you will find a donkey tied and a colt with her. Untie <transChange type="added">them</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“untie”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> bring them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to me.

verses.name: Matthew 21:3
verses.text: And if anyone says anything to you, you will say, ‘The Lord <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞needs them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,’<note placement="foot">Literally “has need of them”</note> and he will send them at once.”

verses.name: Matthew 21:4
verses.text: Now this took place so that what was spoken through the prophet would be fulfilled, saying,  <div eID="gen25899" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 21:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10667"/><lg sID="gen25900"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25901"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10667"/>“Say to the daughter of Zion,<l eID="gen25901" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25902"/>‘Behold, your king is coming to you,<l eID="gen25902" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25903"/>humble and mounted on a donkey,<l eID="gen25903" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25904"/>and<note placement="foot">Or “even”</note> on a colt, the foal of a pack animal.’ ”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Zech.9.9">Zech 9:9</reference></note> <l eID="gen25904" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen25900"/>

verses.name: Matthew 21:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10668"/><div sID="gen25905" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10668"/>So the disciples went<note placement="foot">*Here the participle (“went”) is translated as a finite verb because of English style</note> and did<note placement="foot">*Here the participle (“did”) is translated as a finite verb because of English style</note> just as Jesus directed them,

verses.name: Matthew 21:7
verses.text: <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participles (“went” and “did” in the previous verse) have been translated as finite verbs</note> brought the donkey and the colt and put their<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> cloaks on them, and he sat on them.

verses.name: Matthew 21:8
verses.text: And a very large crowd spread their cloaks on the road, and others were cutting branches from the trees and spreading <transChange type="added">them</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> on the road.

verses.name: Matthew 21:9
verses.text: And the crowds who went ahead of him and the ones who followed were shouting, saying, <div eID="gen25905" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen25906"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25907"/>“Hosanna to the Son of David!<l eID="gen25907" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25908"/>Blessed <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the one who comes in the name of the Lord!<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.118.25-Ps.118.26">Ps 118:25–26</reference></note><l eID="gen25908" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25909"/>Hosanna in the highest <transChange type="added">heaven</transChange>!”<note placement="foot">*Here “heaven” is understood</note> <l eID="gen25909" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen25906"/>

verses.name: Matthew 21:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10669"/><div sID="gen25910" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10669"/>And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“entered”)</note> he entered into Jerusalem, the whole city was stirred up, saying, “Who is this?”

verses.name: Matthew 21:11
verses.text: And the crowds were saying, “This is the prophet Jesus from Nazareth of Galilee!”  <div eID="gen25910" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 21:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10670"/><title type="x-s">The Cleansing of the Temple</title> <div sID="gen25911" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10670"/>And Jesus entered the temple <transChange type="added">courts</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> and drove out all those who were selling and buying in the temple, and overturned the tables of the money changers and the chairs of those who were selling doves.

verses.name: Matthew 21:13
verses.text: And he said to them, “It is written, ‘My house will be called a house of prayer,’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.56.7">Isa 56:7</reference></note> but you have made it a cave of robbers!”  <div eID="gen25911" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 21:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10671"/><div sID="gen25912" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10671"/>And the blind and the lame came up to him in the temple <transChange type="added">courts</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> and he healed them.

verses.name: Matthew 21:15
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> the chief priests and the scribes saw the wonderful things that he did, and the children shouting in the temple courts<note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> and saying, “Hosanna to the Son of David!” they were indignant.

verses.name: Matthew 21:16
verses.text: And they said to him, “Do you hear what these <transChange type="added">children</transChange><note placement="foot">*The word “children” is not in the Greek text but is implied</note> are saying?” So Jesus said to them, “Yes, have you never read, ‘Out of the mouths of children and nursing babies you have prepared for yourself praise’?”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.8.2">Ps 8:2</reference></note>

verses.name: Matthew 21:17
verses.text: And leaving them, he went outside of the city to Bethany and spent the night there.  <div eID="gen25912" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 21:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10672"/><title type="x-s">A Barren Fig Tree Cursed</title> <div sID="gen25913" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10672"/>Now early in the morning, <transChange type="added">as he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was returning”) which is understood as temporal</note> was returning to the city, he was hungry.

verses.name: Matthew 21:19
verses.text: And seeing a single fig tree by the road, he went to it and found nothing on it except leaves only. And he said to it, “May there be no more fruit from you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to the age”</note> and the fig tree withered at once.

verses.name: Matthew 21:20
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> the disciples were astonished, saying, “How did the fig tree wither at once?”

verses.name: Matthew 21:21
verses.text: And Jesus answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to them, “Truly I say to you, if you have faith and do not doubt, you will do not only <transChange type="added">what was done to</transChange> the fig tree, but even if you say to this mountain, ‘Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,” it will happen!

verses.name: Matthew 21:22
verses.text: And whatever you ask in prayer, <transChange type="added">if you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “if” is supplied as a component of the participle (“believe”) which is understood as conditional</note> believe, you will receive.”  <div eID="gen25913" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 21:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10673"/><title type="x-s">Jesus’ Authority Challenged</title> <div sID="gen25914" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10673"/>And <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“arrived”)</note> he arrived at the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people came up to him while he<note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was teaching”) which is understood as temporal</note> was teaching, saying, “By what authority are you doing these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>? And who gave you this authority?”

verses.name: Matthew 21:24
verses.text: And Jesus answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to them, “I also will ask you one question. If you tell the answer<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to me, I also will tell you by what authority I am doing these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>.

verses.name: Matthew 21:25
