verses.text: From where was the baptism of John—from heaven or from men?” And they began to discuss<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to discuss”)</note> this<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> among themselves, saying, “If we say ‘From heaven,’ he will say to us, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’

verses.name: Matthew 21:26
verses.text: But if we say, ‘From men,’ we are afraid of the crowd, because they all look upon John as a prophet.”

verses.name: Matthew 21:27
verses.text: And they answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to Jesus, “We do not know.” And he said to them, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I am doing these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>.  <div eID="gen25914" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 21:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10674"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Two Sons</title> <div sID="gen25915" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10674"/>“Now what do you think? A man had two sons. <transChange type="added">He</transChange> approached<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “And he approached”</note> the first and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“approached”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, ‘Son, go work in the vineyard today.’

verses.name: Matthew 21:29
verses.text: And he answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, ‘I do not want to!’ But later he changed his mind and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“changed his mind”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> went.

verses.name: Matthew 21:30
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">he</transChange> approached the second<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “the other”</note> and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“approached”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said the same thing. So he answered and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, ‘I <transChange type="added">will</transChange>, sir,’ and he did not go.

verses.name: Matthew 21:31
verses.text: Which of the two did the will of <transChange type="added">his</transChange><note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> father?” They said, “The first.” Jesus said to them, “Truly I say to you that the tax collectors and the prostitutes are going ahead of you into the kingdom of God!

verses.name: Matthew 21:32
verses.text: For John came to you in the way of righteousness and you did not believe him, but the tax collectors and the prostitutes did believe him. And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> you saw it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> you did not even change your minds later <transChange type="added">so as</transChange> to believe in him.  <div eID="gen25915" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 21:33
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10675"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Tenant Farmers in the Vineyard</title> <div sID="gen25916" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10675"/>“Listen to another parable: There was a man—a master of a house—who planted a vineyard, and put a fence <transChange type="added">around</transChange> it, and dug a winepress in it, and built a watchtower, and leased it to tenant farmers, and went on a journey.

verses.name: Matthew 21:34
verses.text: And when the season of fruit drew near, he sent his slaves to the tenant farmers to collect his fruit.

verses.name: Matthew 21:35
verses.text: And the tenant farmers seized his slaves, <transChange type="added">one of</transChange> whom they beat, and <transChange type="added">one of</transChange> whom they killed, and <transChange type="added">one of</transChange> whom they stoned.

verses.name: Matthew 21:36
verses.text: Again, he sent other slaves, more than the first <transChange type="added">ones</transChange>, and they did the same <transChange type="added">thing</transChange> to them.

verses.name: Matthew 21:37
verses.text: So finally he sent his son to them, saying, ‘They will respect my son.’

verses.name: Matthew 21:38
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> the tenant farmers saw the son, they said among themselves, ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him and have his inheritance!’

verses.name: Matthew 21:39
verses.text: And they seized him <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“seized”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> threw him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> out of the vineyard and killed him.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Matthew 21:40
verses.text: Now when the master of the vineyard arrives, what will he do to those tenant farmers?”

verses.name: Matthew 21:41
verses.text: They said to him, “He will destroy those evil <transChange type="added">men</transChange> completely and lease the vineyard to other tenant farmers who will give him the fruits in their season.”

verses.name: Matthew 21:42
verses.text: Jesus said to them, “Have you never read in the scriptures, <div eID="gen25916" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen25917"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25918"/>‘The stone which the builders rejected,<l eID="gen25918" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25919"/>this has become <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the cornerstone⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the head of the corner”</note><l eID="gen25919" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25920"/>This came about from the Lord,<l eID="gen25920" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25921"/>and it is marvelous in our eyes’?<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.118.22-Ps.118.23">Ps 118:22–23</reference></note> <l eID="gen25921" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen25917"/>

verses.name: Matthew 21:43
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10676"/><div sID="gen25922" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10676"/>For this <transChange type="added">reason</transChange>, I tell you that the kingdom of God will be taken away from you and will be given to a people<note placement="foot">Or “nation”</note> who produce its fruits.

verses.name: Matthew 21:44
verses.text: And the one who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces, and <transChange type="added">the one</transChange> on whom it falls—it will crush him!”

verses.name: Matthew 21:45
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> the chief priests and the Pharisees heard his parables, they knew that he was speaking about them,

verses.name: Matthew 21:46
verses.text: and <transChange type="added">although they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“wanted”) which is understood as concessive</note> wanted to arrest him, they were afraid of the crowds, because they looked upon him as a prophet.  <chapter eID="Matt.21"/>

verses.name: Matthew 22:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10677"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Wedding Celebration</title> <div sID="gen25923" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10677"/>And continuing, Jesus spoke to them again in parables, saying,

verses.name: Matthew 22:2
verses.text: “The kingdom of heaven may be compared to a man—a king—who gave a wedding celebration for his son.

verses.name: Matthew 22:3
verses.text: And he sent his slaves to summon those who had been invited to the wedding celebration, and they did not want to come.

verses.name: Matthew 22:4
verses.text: Again he sent other slaves, saying, ‘Tell those who have been invited, “Behold, I have prepared my dinner; my oxen and fattened <transChange type="added">cattle</transChange> have been slaughtered, and everything <transChange type="added">is</transChange> ready. Come to the wedding celebration!” ’

verses.name: Matthew 22:5
verses.text: But they paid no attention <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“paid no attention”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> went away—this one to his own field, that one to his business.

verses.name: Matthew 22:6
verses.text: And the others, seizing his slaves, mistreated <transChange type="added">them</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and killed them.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Matthew 22:7
verses.text: And the king was angry and sent his troops <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“sent”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> destroyed those murderers and burned their city.

verses.name: Matthew 22:8
verses.text: Then he said to his slaves, ‘The wedding celebration is ready, but those who had been invited were not worthy.

verses.name: Matthew 22:9
verses.text: Therefore, go out to the <transChange type="added">places where</transChange> the roads exit the city and invite to the wedding celebration as many <transChange type="added">people</transChange> as you find.’

verses.name: Matthew 22:10
verses.text: And those slaves went out into the roads <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> gathered everyone whom they found, both evil and good, and the wedding celebration was filled <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞with dinner guests⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “with those reclining at table”</note>

verses.name: Matthew 22:11
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“came in”) which is understood as temporal</note> the king came in to see the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞dinner guests⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “ones reclining at table”</note> he saw a man there not dressed <transChange type="added">in</transChange> wedding clothes.

verses.name: Matthew 22:12
verses.text: And he said to him, ‘Friend, how did you come in here, not having wedding clothes?’ But <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he could say nothing⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “he was silent”</note>

verses.name: Matthew 22:13
verses.text: Then the king said to the servants, ‘Tie him up <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞hand and foot⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “feet and hands”</note> and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“tie”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> throw him into the outer darkness. In that place there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth!’

verses.name: Matthew 22:14
verses.text: For many are called but few <transChange type="added">are</transChange> chosen.”  <div eID="gen25923" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 22:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10678"/><title type="x-s">Paying Taxes to Caesar</title> <div sID="gen25924" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10678"/>Then the Pharisees went <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞and consulted⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “took counsel”</note> so that they could entrap him with a statement.

verses.name: Matthew 22:16
verses.text: And they sent their disciples to him with the Herodians, saying, “Teacher, we know that you are truthful and teach the way of God in truth, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you do not care what anyone thinks⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “it is not a care to you concerning anyone”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞because you do not regard the opinion of people⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “because you do not look at the face of men”</note>

verses.name: Matthew 22:17
verses.text: Therefore tell us what you think. Is it permitted to pay taxes to Caesar or not?”

verses.name: Matthew 22:18
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">because he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“knew”) which is understood as causal</note> knew their maliciousness, Jesus said, “Hypocrites! Why are you testing me?

verses.name: Matthew 22:19
verses.text: Show me the coin for the tax!” So they brought him a denarius.

verses.name: Matthew 22:20
verses.text: And he said to them, “Whose image and inscription <transChange type="added">is</transChange> this?”

verses.name: Matthew 22:21
verses.text: They said to him, “Caesar’s.” Then he said to them, “Therefore give to Caesar the things of Caesar, and to God the things of God!”

verses.name: Matthew 22:22
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard this,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> they were astonished, and they left him and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“left”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> went away.  <div eID="gen25924" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 22:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10679"/><title type="x-s">A Question About Marriage and the Resurrection</title> <div sID="gen25925" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10679"/>On that day Sadducees—who say there is no resurrection—came up to him and asked him,

verses.name: Matthew 22:24
verses.text: saying, “Teacher, Moses said if someone dies without having children, his brother is to marry his wife and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞father⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “raise up”</note> descendants for his brother.

verses.name: Matthew 22:25
verses.text: Now there were seven brothers with us. And the first died <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“getting married”) which is understood as temporal</note> getting married, and because he<note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“have”) which is understood as causal</note> did not have descendants, he left his wife to his brother.

verses.name: Matthew 22:26
verses.text: So also the second and the third, up to the seventh.

verses.name: Matthew 22:27
verses.text: And last of all the woman died.

verses.name: Matthew 22:28
verses.text: In the resurrection, therefore, whose wife of the seven will she be? For they all had her <transChange type="added">as wife</transChange>.”<note placement="foot">*The words “as wife” are not in the Greek text but are implied</note>

verses.name: Matthew 22:29
verses.text: But Jesus answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to them, “You are mistaken, because<note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“know”) which is understood as causal</note> you do not know the scriptures or the power of God!

verses.name: Matthew 22:30
verses.text: For in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels of God<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts omit “of God”</note> in heaven.

verses.name: Matthew 22:31
verses.text: Now concerning the resurrection of the dead, have you not read what was spoken to you by God, who said,

verses.name: Matthew 22:32
verses.text: “I am the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob”?<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Exod.3.6">Exod 3:6</reference></note> He is not the God of the dead, but of the living!”

verses.name: Matthew 22:33
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> the crowds heard this,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> they were amazed at his teaching.  <div eID="gen25925" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 22:34
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10680"/><title type="x-s">The Greatest Commandment</title> <div sID="gen25926" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10680"/>Now <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> the Pharisees heard that he had silenced the Sadducees, they assembled at the same place.<note placement="foot">Or “they assembled together”</note>

verses.name: Matthew 22:35
verses.text: And one of them, a legal expert, put a question to <transChange type="added">him</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to test him:

verses.name: Matthew 22:36
verses.text: “Teacher, which commandment <transChange type="added">is</transChange> greatest in the law?”

verses.name: Matthew 22:37
verses.text: And he said to him, “ ‘You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Deut.6.5">Deut 6:5</reference></note>

verses.name: Matthew 22:38
verses.text: This is the greatest and first commandment.

verses.name: Matthew 22:39
verses.text: And the second <transChange type="added">is</transChange> like it: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Lev.19.18">Lev 19:18</reference></note>

verses.name: Matthew 22:40
verses.text: On these two commandments depend all the law and the prophets.”  <div eID="gen25926" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 22:41
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10681"/><title type="x-s">David’s Son and Lord</title> <div sID="gen25927" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10681"/>Now <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“assembled”)</note> the Pharisees were assembled, Jesus asked them,

verses.name: Matthew 22:42
verses.text: saying, “What do you think about the Christ? Whose son is he?” They said to him, “David’s.”

verses.name: Matthew 22:43
verses.text: He said to them, “How then does David, by the Spirit, call him ‘Lord,’ saying,  <div eID="gen25927" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 22:44
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10682"/><lg sID="gen25928"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25929"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10682"/>‘The Lord said to my Lord,<l eID="gen25929" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25930"/>“Sit at my right hand<l eID="gen25930" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25931"/>until I put your enemies<l eID="gen25931" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25932"/>under your feet” ’?<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.110.1">Ps 110:1</reference></note> <l eID="gen25932" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen25928"/>

verses.name: Matthew 22:45
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10683"/><div sID="gen25933" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10683"/>If then David calls him ‘Lord,’ how is he his son?”

verses.name: Matthew 22:46
verses.text: And no one was able to answer him a word, nor did anyone dare from that day <transChange type="added">on</transChange> to ask him any more <transChange type="added">questions</transChange>.<note placement="foot">*The word “questions” is not in the Greek text but is implied</note>  <chapter eID="Matt.22"/>

verses.name: Matthew 23:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10684"/><title type="x-s">Seven Woes Pronounced on the Scribes and Pharisees</title> <div sID="gen25934" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10684"/>Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and to his disciples,

verses.name: Matthew 23:2
verses.text: saying, “The scribes and the Pharisees sit on the seat of Moses.

verses.name: Matthew 23:3
verses.text: Therefore do and observe everything that they tell you, but do not do as <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they do⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “their deeds”</note> for they tell others to do something<note placement="foot">*The words “others to do something” are not in the Greek text but are implied</note> and do not do it themselves.<note placement="foot">*The words “it themselves” are not in the Greek text but are implied</note>

verses.name: Matthew 23:4
verses.text: And they tie up heavy burdens<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “burdens that are heavy and hard to bear”</note> and put them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> on people’s shoulders, but <transChange type="added">they</transChange> themselves are not willing with their finger to move them.

verses.name: Matthew 23:5
verses.text: And they do all their deeds in order to be seen by people, for they make their phylacteries broad and make their<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> tassels long.

verses.name: Matthew 23:6
verses.text: And they love the place of honor at banquets and the best seats in the synagogues

verses.name: Matthew 23:7
verses.text: and the greetings in the marketplaces and to be called ‘Rabbi’ by people.

verses.name: Matthew 23:8
verses.text: But you are not to be called ‘Rabbi,’ because one is your teacher, and you are all brothers,

verses.name: Matthew 23:9
verses.text: And do not call <transChange type="added">anyone</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> your father on earth, for one is your heavenly Father.

verses.name: Matthew 23:10
verses.text: And do not be called teachers, because one is your teacher, the Christ.

verses.name: Matthew 23:11
verses.text: And the greatest among you will be your servant.

verses.name: Matthew 23:12
verses.text: And whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.  <div eID="gen25934" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 23:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10685"/><div sID="gen25935" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10685"/>“But woe to you, scribes and Pharisees—hypocrites!—because you shut the kingdom of heaven before people! For you do not enter, nor permit those wanting to go in<note placement="foot">*Here the present tense has been translated as voluntative (“wanting to go in”)</note> to enter.<note placement="foot">The most important Greek manuscripts omit v. <reference osisRef="Matt.23.14">14</reference>, “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees—hypocrites!—because you devour widows’ houses and for show you pray long prayers! Therefore you will receive the greater condemnation.”</note>  <div eID="gen25935" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 23:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10686"/><div sID="gen25936" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10686"/>“Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees—hypocrites!—because you travel around the sea and the dry <transChange type="added">land</transChange> to make one convert, and when he becomes <transChange type="added">one</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> you make him twice as much a son of hell <transChange type="added">as</transChange> you <transChange type="added">are</transChange>!  <div eID="gen25936" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 23:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10687"/><div sID="gen25937" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10687"/>“Woe to you, blind guides, who say, ‘Whoever swears by the temple, it is nothing! But whoever swears by the gold of the temple is bound <transChange type="added">by his oath</transChange>.’<note placement="foot">The phrase “by his oath” is not in the Greek text but is implied</note>

verses.name: Matthew 23:17
verses.text: Fools and blind <transChange type="added">people</transChange>! For which is greater, the gold or the temple that makes the gold holy?

verses.name: Matthew 23:18
verses.text: And, ‘Whoever swears by the altar, it is nothing! But whoever swears by the gift <transChange type="added">that is</transChange> on it is bound <transChange type="added">by his oath</transChange>.’<note placement="foot">The phrase “by his oath” is not in the Greek text but is implied</note>

verses.name: Matthew 23:19
verses.text: Blind <transChange type="added">people</transChange>! For which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> greater, the gift or the altar that makes the gift holy?

verses.name: Matthew 23:20
verses.text: Therefore the one who swears by the altar swears by it and by everything <transChange type="added">that is</transChange> on it.

verses.name: Matthew 23:21
verses.text: And the one who swears by the temple swears by it and by the one who dwells <transChange type="added">in</transChange> it.

verses.name: Matthew 23:22
verses.text: And the one who swears by heaven swears by the throne of God and by the one who sits on it.  <div eID="gen25937" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 23:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10688"/><div sID="gen25938" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10688"/>“Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees—hypocrites!—because you pay a tenth of mint and dill and cumin, and neglect the more important <transChange type="added">matters</transChange> of the law—justice and mercy and faithfulness! It was necessary<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “But it was necessary”</note> to do these things <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞while not neglecting those⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “and those not to neglect”</note>

verses.name: Matthew 23:24
verses.text: Blind guides who filter out a gnat and swallow a camel!  <div eID="gen25938" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 23:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10689"/><div sID="gen25939" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10689"/>“Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees—hypocrites!—because you cleanse the outside of the cup and the dish, but inside they are full of greed and self-indulgence!

verses.name: Matthew 23:26
verses.text: Blind Pharisee! First clean the inside of the cup and the dish,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts omit “and the dish”</note> so that the outside of it may become clean also.  <div eID="gen25939" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 23:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10690"/><div sID="gen25940" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10690"/>“Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees—hypocrites!—because you are like whitewashed tombs which on the outside appear beautiful, but on the inside are full of the bones of the dead and of everything unclean!

verses.name: Matthew 23:28
verses.text: In the <transChange type="added">same</transChange> way, on the outside you also appear righteous to people, but inside you are full of hypocrisy and lawlessness.  <div eID="gen25940" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 23:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10691"/><div sID="gen25941" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10691"/>“Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees—hypocrites!—because you build the tombs of the prophets and decorate the graves of the righteous,

verses.name: Matthew 23:30
verses.text: and you say, ‘If we had lived in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partners with them in the blood of the prophets!’

verses.name: Matthew 23:31
verses.text: Thus you testify against yourselves that you are descendants of those who murdered the prophets!

verses.name: Matthew 23:32
verses.text: And you—fill up the measure of your fathers!

verses.name: Matthew 23:33
verses.text: Serpents! Offspring of vipers! How will you escape from the condemnation to hell?

verses.name: Matthew 23:34
verses.text: For this <transChange type="added">reason</transChange>, behold, I am sending to you prophets and wise men and scribes. <transChange type="added">Some</transChange> of them you will kill and crucify, and some of them you will flog in your synagogues and will pursue from town to town,

verses.name: Matthew 23:35
verses.text: so that upon you will come all the righteous blood shed on the earth from the blood of righteous Abel up to the blood of Zechariah son of Barachiah, whom you murdered between the temple and the altar.

verses.name: Matthew 23:36
verses.text: Truly I say to you, all these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> will come upon this generation!  <div eID="gen25941" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 23:37
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10692"/><title type="x-s">The Lament over Jerusalem</title> <div sID="gen25942" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10692"/>“Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those who are sent to her! How many times I wanted to gather your children together <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the way⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in the manner in which”</note> a hen gathers her young together under her<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> wings, and you were not willing!

verses.name: Matthew 23:38
verses.text: Behold, your house has been left to you desolate!

verses.name: Matthew 23:39
verses.text: For I tell you, you will never see me from now <transChange type="added">on</transChange> until you say, <div eID="gen25942" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen25943"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25944"/>‘Blessed <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the one who comes in the name of the Lord!’ ”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.118.26">Ps 118:26</reference></note> <l eID="gen25944" level="1"/><lg eID="gen25943"/> <chapter eID="Matt.23"/>

verses.name: Matthew 24:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10693"/><title type="x-s">The Destruction of the Temple Predicted</title> <div sID="gen25945" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10693"/>And <transChange type="added">as</transChange> Jesus went out of the temple <transChange type="added">courts</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> he was going along, and his disciples came up to point out to him the buildings of the temple.

verses.name: Matthew 24:2
verses.text: But he answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to them, “Do you not see all these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>? Truly I say to you, not <transChange type="added">one</transChange> stone will be left here on <transChange type="added">another</transChange> stone that will not be thrown down!”  <div eID="gen25945" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 24:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10694"/><title type="x-s">Signs of the End of the Age</title> <div sID="gen25946" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10694"/>And <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was sitting”)</note> he was sitting on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came up to him privately, saying, “Tell us, when will these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> happen, and what <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> the sign of your coming and of the end of the age?”

verses.name: Matthew 24:4
verses.text: And Jesus answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to them, “Watch out that no one deceives you!

verses.name: Matthew 24:5
verses.text: For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am the Christ,’ and they will deceive many.

verses.name: Matthew 24:6
verses.text: And you are going to hear about wars and rumors of wars. See to it that you are not alarmed, for this must happen, but the end is not yet.

verses.name: Matthew 24:7
verses.text: For nation will rise up against nation and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be famines and earthquakes in <transChange type="added">various</transChange> places.<note placement="foot">Or “in place after place”</note>

verses.name: Matthew 24:8
verses.text: But all these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the beginning of birth pains.  <div eID="gen25946" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 24:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10695"/><title type="x-s">Persecution of Disciples Predicted</title> <div sID="gen25947" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10695"/>“Then they will hand you over to persecution and will kill you, and you will be hated by all the nations<note placement="foot">Or “Gentiles”; the same Greek word can be translated “nations” or “Gentiles” depending on the context</note> because of my name.

verses.name: Matthew 24:10
verses.text: And then many will be led into sin and will betray one another and will hate one another,

verses.name: Matthew 24:11
verses.text: and many false prophets will appear and will deceive many,

verses.name: Matthew 24:12
verses.text: and because lawlessness will increase, the love of many will grow cold.

verses.name: Matthew 24:13
verses.text: But the one who endures to the end—this person will be saved.

verses.name: Matthew 24:14
verses.text: And this gospel of the kingdom will be proclaimed in the whole inhabited earth for a testimony to all the nations,<note placement="foot">Or “Gentiles”; the same Greek word can be translated “nations” or “Gentiles” depending on the context</note> and then the end will come.  <div eID="gen25947" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 24:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10696"/><title type="x-s">The Abomination of Desolation</title> <div sID="gen25948" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10696"/>“So when you see the abomination of desolation<note placement="foot">An allusion to <reference osisRef="Dan.9.27">Dan 9:27</reference></note> spoken about by the prophet Daniel standing in the holy place” (let the one who reads understand),

verses.name: Matthew 24:16
verses.text: “then those in Judea must flee to the mountains!

verses.name: Matthew 24:17
verses.text: The one who is on his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> housetop must not come down to take things out of his house,

verses.name: Matthew 24:18
verses.text: and the one who is in the field must not turn back to pick up his cloak.

verses.name: Matthew 24:19
verses.text: And woe to those <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who are pregnant⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “who have in the womb”</note> and to those who are nursing their babies<note placement="foot">*The words “their babies” are not in the Greek text but are supplied as a necessary clarification</note> in those days!

verses.name: Matthew 24:20
verses.text: But pray that your flight may not happen in winter or on a Sabbath.

verses.name: Matthew 24:21
verses.text: For at that time there will be great tribulation, such as has not happened from the beginning of the world until now, nor ever will happen.

verses.name: Matthew 24:22
verses.text: And unless those days had been shortened, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞no human being would be saved⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “every flesh would not be saved”</note> But for the sake of the elect, those days will be shortened.  <div eID="gen25948" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 24:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10697"/><div sID="gen25949" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10697"/>“At that time if anyone should say to you, ‘Behold, here <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the Christ,’ or ‘Here <transChange type="added">he is</transChange>,’ do not believe <transChange type="added">him</transChange>!<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Matthew 24:24
verses.text: For false messiahs and false prophets will appear, and will produce great signs and wonders in order to deceive, if possible, even the elect.

verses.name: Matthew 24:25
verses.text: Behold, I have told you ahead of time!

verses.name: Matthew 24:26
verses.text: Therefore if they say to you, ‘Behold, he is in the wilderness,’ do not go out, <transChange type="added">or</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “or” is supplied because of English style</note> ‘Behold, he is in the inner rooms,’ do not believe it!<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Matthew 24:27
verses.text: For just as the lightning comes from the east and flashes to the west, so the coming of the Son of Man will be.

verses.name: Matthew 24:28
verses.text: Wherever the corpse is, there the vultures will gather.  <div eID="gen25949" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 24:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10698"/><title type="x-s">The Arrival of the Son of Man</title> <div sID="gen25950" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10698"/>“And immediately after the tribulation of those days, <div eID="gen25950" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen25951"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25952"/>‘the sun will be darkened<l eID="gen25952" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25953"/>and the moon will not give its light,<l eID="gen25953" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25954"/>and the stars will fall from heaven,<l eID="gen25954" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25955"/>and the powers of heaven will be shaken.’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.13.10">Isa 13:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.34.4">34:4</reference></note> <l eID="gen25955" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen25951"/>

verses.name: Matthew 24:30
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10699"/><div sID="gen25956" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10699"/>And then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven,<note placement="foot">Or “the sky”</note> and then all the tribes of the earth will mourn, and they will see the Son of Man arriving on the clouds of heaven<note placement="foot">Or “the sky”</note> with power and great glory.

verses.name: Matthew 24:31
verses.text: And he will send out his angels with a loud trumpet call, and they will gather his elect together from the four winds, from <transChange type="added">one</transChange> end of heaven<note placement="foot">Or “of the sky”</note> to the <transChange type="added">other</transChange> end of it.  <div eID="gen25956" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 24:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10700"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Fig Tree</title> <div sID="gen25957" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10700"/>“Now learn the parable from the fig tree: Whenever its branch has already become tender and puts forth its<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> leaves, you know that summer <transChange type="added">is</transChange> near.

verses.name: Matthew 24:33
verses.text: So also you, when you see all these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, know<note placement="foot">Or “you know”</note> that he is near, at the door.

verses.name: Matthew 24:34
verses.text: Truly I say to you that this generation will never pass away until all these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> take place!

verses.name: Matthew 24:35
verses.text: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will never pass away.  <div eID="gen25957" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 24:36
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10701"/><title type="x-s">The Unknown Day and Hour</title> <div sID="gen25958" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10701"/>“But concerning that day and hour no one knows—not even the angels of heaven nor the Son—except the Father alone.

verses.name: Matthew 24:37
verses.text: For just as the days of Noah <transChange type="added">were</transChange>, so the coming of the Son of Man will be.

verses.name: Matthew 24:38
verses.text: For as in the days<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “those days”</note> before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day Noah entered into the ark.

verses.name: Matthew 24:39
verses.text: And they did not know <transChange type="added">anything</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> until the deluge came and swept them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> all away. So also the coming of the Son of Man will be.

verses.name: Matthew 24:40
verses.text: Then there will be two men in the field; one will be taken and one left.

verses.name: Matthew 24:41
verses.text: Two women will be grinding at the mill; one will be taken and one left.

verses.name: Matthew 24:42
verses.text: Therefore be on the alert, because you do not know what day your Lord is coming!

verses.name: Matthew 24:43
verses.text: But understand this: that if the master of the house had known what watch of the night the thief was coming, he would have stayed awake and would not have let his house be broken into.

verses.name: Matthew 24:44
verses.text: For this <transChange type="added">reason</transChange> you also must be ready, because the Son of Man is coming at an hour that you do not think <transChange type="added">he will come</transChange>.<note placement="foot">*The words “he will come” are not in the Greek text but are implied</note>  <div eID="gen25958" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 24:45
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10702"/><title type="x-s">A Faithful Slave and an Unfaithful Slave</title> <div sID="gen25959" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10702"/>“Who then is the faithful and wise slave whom the master has put in charge of his household slaves to give them their<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> food at the right time?

verses.name: Matthew 24:46
verses.text: Blessed <transChange type="added">is</transChange> that slave whom his master will find so doing <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“comes back”) which is understood as temporal</note> comes back.

verses.name: Matthew 24:47
verses.text: Truly I say to you that he will put him in charge of all his possessions.

verses.name: Matthew 24:48
verses.text: But if that evil slave should say <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to himself⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “in his heart”</note> ‘My master is staying away for a long time,’

verses.name: Matthew 24:49
verses.text: and he begins to beat his fellow slaves and eats and drinks with drunkards,

verses.name: Matthew 24:50
verses.text: the master of that slave will come on a day that he does not expect and at an hour that he does not know,

verses.name: Matthew 24:51
verses.text: and will cut him in two and assign his place with the hypocrites. In that place there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth!  <chapter eID="Matt.24"/>

verses.name: Matthew 25:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10703"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Ten Virgins</title> <div sID="gen25960" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10703"/>“Then the kingdom of heaven may be compared to ten virgins who took their lamps <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> went out to meet the bridegroom.

verses.name: Matthew 25:2
verses.text: Now five of them were foolish and five <transChange type="added">were</transChange> wise.

verses.name: Matthew 25:3
verses.text: For <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“took”) which is understood as temporal</note> the foolish ones took their lamps, they did not take olive oil with them.

verses.name: Matthew 25:4
verses.text: But the wise ones took olive oil in flasks with their lamps.

verses.name: Matthew 25:5
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was delayed”)</note> the bridegroom was delayed, they all became drowsy and fell asleep.<note placement="foot">The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to sleep”, “fell asleep”)</note>

verses.name: Matthew 25:6
verses.text: But in the middle of the night there was a shout, ‘Behold, the bridegroom! Come out to meet him!’

verses.name: Matthew 25:7
verses.text: Then all those virgins woke up and trimmed their lamps.

verses.name: Matthew 25:8
verses.text: And the foolish ones said to the wise ones, ‘Give us <transChange type="added">some</transChange> of your olive oil, because our lamps are going out!’

verses.name: Matthew 25:9
verses.text: But the wise ones answered saying, “Certainly there will never be enough for us and for you! Go instead to those who sell <transChange type="added">olive oil</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and buy some<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> for yourselves.’

verses.name: Matthew 25:10
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“had gone away”)</note> they had gone away to buy it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> the bridegroom arrived, and those who were ready went inside with him to the wedding celebration, and the door was shut.

verses.name: Matthew 25:11
verses.text: And later the other virgins came also, saying, ‘Lord, lord, open <transChange type="added">the door</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> for us!’

verses.name: Matthew 25:12
verses.text: But he answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, ‘Truly I say to you, I do not know you!’

verses.name: Matthew 25:13
verses.text: Therefore be on the alert, because you do not know the day or the hour!  <div eID="gen25960" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 25:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10704"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Talents</title> <div sID="gen25961" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10704"/>For <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> like a man going on a journey. He summoned his own slaves and handed over his property to them.

verses.name: Matthew 25:15
verses.text: And to one he gave five talents, and to another two, and to another one, to each one according to his own ability, and he went on a journey immediately.

verses.name: Matthew 25:16
verses.text: The one who had received the five talents went out <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> traded with them and gained five more.

verses.name: Matthew 25:17
verses.text: In the same way the one <transChange type="added">who had</transChange> the two gained two more.

verses.name: Matthew 25:18
verses.text: But the one who had received the one went away <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went away”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> dug up the ground and hid his master’s money.

verses.name: Matthew 25:19
verses.text: Now after a long time, the master of those slaves came and settled accounts with them.

verses.name: Matthew 25:20
verses.text: And the one who had received the five talents came up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> brought five more talents, saying, ‘Master, you handed over to me five talents. See, I have gained five more talents!’

verses.name: Matthew 25:21
verses.text: His master said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful slave! You were faithful over a few <transChange type="added">things</transChange>; I will put you <transChange type="added">in charge</transChange> over many <transChange type="added">things</transChange>. Enter into the joy of your master!’

verses.name: Matthew 25:22
verses.text: And the one <transChange type="added">who had</transChange> the two talents also came up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, ‘Master, you handed over to me two talents. See, I have gained two talents more!’

verses.name: Matthew 25:23
verses.text: His master said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful slave! You were faithful over a few <transChange type="added">things</transChange>; I will put you <transChange type="added">in charge</transChange> over many <transChange type="added">things</transChange>. Enter into the joy of your master!’

verses.name: Matthew 25:24
verses.text: And the one who had received the one talent came up also <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, ‘Master, because I<note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“knew”) which is understood as causal</note> knew you, that you are a hard man, reaping where you did not sow and gathering from where you did not scatter seed.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Matthew 25:25
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">because I</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was afraid”) which is understood as causal</note> was afraid, I went away and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went away”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> hid your talent in the ground. See, you have <transChange type="added">what is</transChange> yours!’

verses.name: Matthew 25:26
verses.text: But his master answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to him, ‘Evil and lazy slave! You knew that I reap where I did not sow and gather from where I did not scatter seed.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Matthew 25:27
verses.text: Then you ought to have deposited my money with the bankers, and <transChange type="added">when I</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“returned”) which is understood as temporal</note> returned I would have gotten back <transChange type="added">what was</transChange> mine with interest!

verses.name: Matthew 25:28
verses.text: Therefore take the talent from him and give <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to the one who has the ten talents.

verses.name: Matthew 25:29
verses.text: For to everyone who has, <transChange type="added">more</transChange> will be given, and he will have an abundance. But from the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.

verses.name: Matthew 25:30
verses.text: And throw the worthless slave into the outer darkness—in that place there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth!’  <div eID="gen25961" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 25:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10705"/><title type="x-s">The Judgment of the Sheep and the Goats</title> <div sID="gen25962" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10705"/>Now when the Son of Man comes in his glory and all the angels with him, then he will sit on his glorious throne.

verses.name: Matthew 25:32
verses.text: And all the nations will be gathered before him, and he will separate them from one another like a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.

verses.name: Matthew 25:33
verses.text: And he will place the sheep on his right and the goats on the left.

verses.name: Matthew 25:34
verses.text: Then the king will say to those on his right, ‘Come, <transChange type="added">you</transChange> who are blessed by my Father. Inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world!

verses.name: Matthew 25:35
verses.text: For I was hungry and you gave me <transChange type="added">something</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to eat, I was thirsty and you gave me something<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to drink, I was a stranger and you welcomed me as a guest,

verses.name: Matthew 25:36
verses.text: I was naked and you clothed me, I was sick and you cared for me, I was in prison and you came to me.’

verses.name: Matthew 25:37
verses.text: Then the righteous will answer him, saying, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed <transChange type="added">you</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> or thirsty and give you something<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to drink?

verses.name: Matthew 25:38
verses.text: And when did we see you a stranger and welcome <transChange type="added">you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> as a guest, or naked and clothe you?<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Matthew 25:39
verses.text: And when did we see you sick or in prison and come to you?’

verses.name: Matthew 25:40
verses.text: And the king will answer <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“will answer”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> say to them, ‘Truly I say to you, in as much as you did it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to one of the least of these brothers of mine, you did it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to me.’

verses.name: Matthew 25:41
verses.text: Then he will also say to those on <transChange type="added">his</transChange> left, ‘Depart from me, <transChange type="added">you</transChange> accursed ones, into the eternal fire that has been prepared for the devil and his angels!

verses.name: Matthew 25:42
verses.text: For I was hungry and you did not give me <transChange type="added">anything</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to eat, I was thirsty and you did not give me anything<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to drink,

verses.name: Matthew 25:43
verses.text: I was a stranger and you did not welcome me as a guest, naked and you did not clothe me, sick and in prison and you did not care for me.’

verses.name: Matthew 25:44
verses.text: Then they will also answer, saying, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison and not serve you?’

verses.name: Matthew 25:45
verses.text: Then he will answer them, saying, ‘Truly I say to you, in as much as you did not do <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to one of the least of these, you did not do it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to me.’

verses.name: Matthew 25:46
verses.text: And these will depart into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.”  <chapter eID="Matt.25"/>

verses.name: Matthew 26:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10706"/><title type="x-s">The Chief Priests and Elders Plot to Kill Jesus</title> <div sID="gen25963" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10706"/>And it happened that when Jesus had finished all these sayings, he said to his disciples,

verses.name: Matthew 26:2
verses.text: “You know that after two days the Passover takes place, and the Son of Man will be handed over<note placement="foot">Or “will be delivered up”</note> in order to be crucified.”  <div eID="gen25963" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 26:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10707"/><div sID="gen25964" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10707"/>Then the chief priests and the elders of the people assembled in the palace of the high priest, who was named Caiaphas,

verses.name: Matthew 26:4
verses.text: and plotted in order that they could arrest Jesus by stealth and kill <transChange type="added">him</transChange>.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Matthew 26:5
verses.text: But they were saying, “Not during the feast, so that there will not be an uproar among the people.”  <div eID="gen25964" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 26:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10708"/><title type="x-s">Jesus’ Anointing at Bethany</title> <div sID="gen25965" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10708"/>Now <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was”)</note> Jesus was at Bethany in the house of Simon the leper,

verses.name: Matthew 26:7
verses.text: a woman came up to him holding an alabaster flask of very expensive perfumed oil, and poured <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> out on his head while he<note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was reclining at table”)</note> was reclining at table.

verses.name: Matthew 26:8
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> the disciples saw it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> they were indignant, saying, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Why⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for what” reason</note> this waste?

verses.name: Matthew 26:9
verses.text: For this could have been sold for a large sum and given to the poor!”

verses.name: Matthew 26:10
verses.text: But Jesus, knowing <transChange type="added">this</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> said to them, “Why do you cause trouble for the woman? For she has done a good deed for me.

verses.name: Matthew 26:11
verses.text: For the poor you always have with you, but you do not always have me.

verses.name: Matthew 26:12
verses.text: For <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“poured”) which is understood as temporal</note> this woman poured this ointment on my body, she did it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> in order to prepare me for burial.

verses.name: Matthew 26:13
verses.text: Truly I say to you, wherever this gospel is proclaimed in the whole world, what this woman has done will also be told in memory of her.”  <div eID="gen25965" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 26:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10709"/><title type="x-s">Judas Arranges to Betray Jesus</title> <div sID="gen25966" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10709"/>Then one of the twelve, the one named Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests

verses.name: Matthew 26:15
verses.text: <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the participle in the previous verse (“went”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “What are you willing to give me if I in turn deliver him to you?” So they set out for him thirty silver coins.

verses.name: Matthew 26:16
verses.text: And from that time on, he began seeking a favorable opportunity in order that he could betray him.  <div eID="gen25966" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 26:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10710"/><title type="x-s">Jesus’ Final Passover with the Disciples</title> <div sID="gen25967" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10710"/>Now on the first <transChange type="added">day</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the word “day” is not in the Greek text but is implied</note> of the feast of Unleavened Bread the disciples came up to Jesus, saying, “Where do you want us to prepare for you to eat the Passover?”

verses.name: Matthew 26:18
verses.text: And he said, “Go into the city to a certain man and tell him, ‘The Teacher says, “My time is near. I am celebrating the Passover with you with my disciples.” ’

verses.name: Matthew 26:19
verses.text: And the disciples did as Jesus directed them, and they prepared the Passover.

verses.name: Matthew 26:20
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was”)</note> was evening, he was reclining at table with the twelve disciples.<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts omit “disciples”</note>

verses.name: Matthew 26:21
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“were eating”)</note> they were eating he said, “Truly I say to you, that one of you will betray me.”

verses.name: Matthew 26:22
verses.text: And greatly distressed, each one began to say to him, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Surely I am not he, am I⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “surely I am not”; the negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here, indicated in the translation by “am I”</note> Lord?”

verses.name: Matthew 26:23
verses.text: And he answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “The one who dips his<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> hand in the bowl with me—this one will betray me.

verses.name: Matthew 26:24
verses.text: The Son of Man is going just as it is written about him, but woe to that man by whom the Son of Man is betrayed! It would be better for him if that man had not been born.”

verses.name: Matthew 26:25
verses.text: And Judas, the one who was betraying him, answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Surely I am not he, am I⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “surely I am not”; the negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here, indicated in the translation by “am I”</note> Rabbi?” He said to him, “You have said it.”<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>  <div eID="gen25967" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 26:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10711"/><title type="x-s">The Lord’s Supper</title> <div sID="gen25968" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10711"/>Now <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“were eating”)</note> they were eating Jesus took bread and, after<note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“giving thanks”) which is understood as temporal</note> giving thanks, he broke it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and giving it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to the disciples, he said, “Take, eat, this is my body.”

verses.name: Matthew 26:27
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“taking”) which is understood as temporal</note> taking the cup and giving thanks he gave it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to them, saying, “Drink from it, all of you,

verses.name: Matthew 26:28
verses.text: for this is my blood of the covenant which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.

verses.name: Matthew 26:29
verses.text: But I tell you, from now <transChange type="added">on</transChange> I will never drink of this fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new with you in the kingdom of my Father.”

verses.name: Matthew 26:30
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had sung the hymn”) which is understood as temporal</note> had sung the hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.  <div eID="gen25968" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 26:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10712"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Predicts Peter’s Denial</title> <div sID="gen25969" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10712"/>Then Jesus said to them, “You will all fall away because of me during this night, for it is written, <div eID="gen25969" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen25970"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25971"/>‘I will strike the shepherd<l eID="gen25971" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25972"/>and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Zech.13.7">Zech 13:7</reference></note> <l eID="gen25972" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen25970"/>

verses.name: Matthew 26:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10713"/><div sID="gen25973" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10713"/>But after I am raised, I will go ahead of you into Galilee.”

verses.name: Matthew 26:33
verses.text: But Peter answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to him, “If they all fall away because of you, I will never fall away!”

verses.name: Matthew 26:34
verses.text: Jesus said to him, “Truly I say to you that during this night, before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times!”

verses.name: Matthew 26:35
verses.text: Peter said to him, “Even if it is necessary for me to die with you, I will never deny you!” And all the disciples said the same <transChange type="added">thing</transChange>.  <div eID="gen25973" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 26:36
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10714"/><title type="x-s">The Prayer in Gethsemane</title> <div sID="gen25974" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10714"/>Then Jesus went with them to a place called Gethsemane, and he said to the disciples, “Sit here while I go over there <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“go”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> pray.”

verses.name: Matthew 26:37
verses.text: And taking along Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, he began to be distressed and troubled.

verses.name: Matthew 26:38
verses.text: Then he said to them, “My soul is deeply grieved, to the point of death. Remain here and stay awake with me.”

verses.name: Matthew 26:39
verses.text: And going forward a little he fell down on his face, praying and saying, “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me. Nevertheless, not as I will, but as you <transChange type="added">will</transChange>.”<note placement="foot">*Here the verb “will” is an understood repetition of the verb earlier in this verse</note>

verses.name: Matthew 26:40
verses.text: And he came to the disciples and found them sleeping, and he said to Peter, “So, were you not able to stay awake with me one hour?

verses.name: Matthew 26:41
verses.text: Stay awake and pray that you will not enter into temptation. The spirit <transChange type="added">is</transChange> willing, but the flesh <transChange type="added">is</transChange> weak!”

verses.name: Matthew 26:42
verses.text: Again for the second time he went away <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went away”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> prayed, saying, “My Father, if this cannot pass unless I drink it, your will must be done.”

verses.name: Matthew 26:43
verses.text: And he came again <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came again”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> found them sleeping, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞for they could not keep their eyes open⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “for their eyes were weighed down”</note>

verses.name: Matthew 26:44
verses.text: And leaving them again, he went away <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went away”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> prayed for the third <transChange type="added">time</transChange>, saying the same thing again.

verses.name: Matthew 26:45
verses.text: Then he came to the disciples and said to them, “Are you still sleeping and resting? Behold, the hour is near, and the Son of Man is being betrayed into the hands of sinners.

verses.name: Matthew 26:46
verses.text: Get up, let us go! Behold, the one who is betraying me is approaching!”  <div eID="gen25974" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 26:47
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10715"/><title type="x-s">The Betrayal and Arrest of Jesus</title> <div sID="gen25975" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10715"/>And <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was … speaking”)</note> he was still speaking, behold, Judas—one of the twelve—arrived, and with him a large crowd with swords and clubs, from the chief priests and elders of the people.

verses.name: Matthew 26:48
verses.text: Now the one who was betraying him had given them a sign, saying, “<transChange type="added">The one</transChange> whom I kiss—he is <transChange type="added">the one</transChange>.<note placement="foot">*Here the predicate nominative (“the one”) is implied</note> Arrest him!”

verses.name: Matthew 26:49
verses.text: And he came up to Jesus immediately <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “Greetings, Rabbi,” and kissed him.

verses.name: Matthew 26:50
verses.text: And Jesus said to him, “Friend, <transChange type="added">do that</transChange><note placement="foot">*The words “do that” are not in the Greek text but are implied</note> for which you have come.”<note placement="foot">The meaning of this phrase is disputed: (1) some take it as a declarative (as in the translation); (2) others understand it as some form of a question, often with supplied words: (a) “Friend, are you misusing the kiss for that purpose for which you are here?” (b) “Friend, in connection with that for which you have appeared do you kiss me?” (c) “Friend, are you here for this purpose?” (d) “Friend, what are you here for?”; this last option, though often suggested, is doubtful because of lack of evidence for the relative pronoun used as an interrogative in direct questions</note> Then they came up and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> laid hands on Jesus and arrested him.  <div eID="gen25975" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 26:51
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10716"/><div sID="gen25976" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10716"/>And behold, one of those with Jesus extended his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> hand and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“extended”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> drew his sword, and striking the slave of the high priest, cut off his ear.

verses.name: Matthew 26:52
verses.text: Then Jesus said to him, “Put your sword back into its place! For all who take up the sword will die by the sword.

verses.name: Matthew 26:53
verses.text: Or do you think that I cannot call upon my Father, and he would put at my disposal at once more than twelve legions of angels?

verses.name: Matthew 26:54
verses.text: How then would the scriptures be fulfilled that it must happen in this way?”  <div eID="gen25976" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 26:55
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10717"/><div sID="gen25977" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10717"/>At that time Jesus said to the crowds, “Have you come out with swords and clubs, as against a robber, to arrest me? Every day in the temple <transChange type="added">courts</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> I sat teaching, and you did not arrest me!

verses.name: Matthew 26:56
verses.text: But all this has happened in order that the scriptures of the prophets would be fulfilled.” Then the disciples all abandoned him <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“abandoned”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> fled.  <div eID="gen25977" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 26:57
