verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10718"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Before the Sanhedrin</title> <div sID="gen25978" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10718"/>Now those who had arrested Jesus led <transChange type="added">him</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> away to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and the elders had gathered.

verses.name: Matthew 26:58
verses.text: But Peter was following him from a distance, as far as the courtyard of the high priest. And he went inside <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> was sitting with the officers to see the outcome.

verses.name: Matthew 26:59
verses.text: Now the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin were looking for false testimony against Jesus in order that they could put him to death.

verses.name: Matthew 26:60
verses.text: And they did not find <transChange type="added">it</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> although<note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“came forward”) which is understood as concessive</note> many false witnesses came forward. And finally two came forward

verses.name: Matthew 26:61
verses.text: <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the participle in the previous verse (“came forward”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “This man said, ‘I am able to destroy the temple of God and rebuild it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> within three days.’ ”

verses.name: Matthew 26:62
verses.text: And the high priest stood up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“stood up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to him, “Do you reply nothing? What are these <transChange type="added">people</transChange> testifying against you?”

verses.name: Matthew 26:63
verses.text: But Jesus was silent. And the high priest said to him, “I put you under oath by the living God, that you tell us if you are the Christ, the Son of God!”

verses.name: Matthew 26:64
verses.text: Jesus said to him, “You have said <transChange type="added">it</transChange>.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> But I tell you, from now on you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of the Power<note placement="foot">An indirect way of referring to God</note> and coming on the clouds of heaven.”

verses.name: Matthew 26:65
verses.text: Then the high priest tore his robes, saying, “He has blasphemed! What further need do we have of witnesses? Behold, you have just now heard the blasphemy!

verses.name: Matthew 26:66
verses.text: What do you think?” And they answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞He deserves death⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!”<note placement="foot">Literally “he is deserving of death”</note>

verses.name: Matthew 26:67
verses.text: Then they spat in his face and struck him with their fists, and they slapped <transChange type="added">him</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Matthew 26:68
verses.text: saying, “Prophesy for us, <transChange type="added">you</transChange> Christ! Who is it who hit you?”  <div eID="gen25978" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 26:69
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10719"/><title type="x-s">Peter Denies Jesus Three Times</title> <div sID="gen25979" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10719"/>Now Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard, and a female slave came up to him <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “You also were with Jesus the Galilean.”

verses.name: Matthew 26:70
verses.text: But he denied <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> in the presence of <transChange type="added">them</transChange> all, saying, “I do not know what you mean!”

verses.name: Matthew 26:71
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“went out”) which is understood as temporal</note> went out to the gateway, another female slave<note placement="foot">The words “female slave” are not in the Greek text but are implied by the feminine singular form</note> saw him and said to those <transChange type="added">who were</transChange> there, “This man was with Jesus the Nazarene.”

verses.name: Matthew 26:72
verses.text: And again he denied <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> with an oath, “I do not know the man!”

verses.name: Matthew 26:73
verses.text: And after a little <transChange type="added">while</transChange> those who were standing there came up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to Peter, “You really are one of them also, because even your accent <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞reveals who you are⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “makes you evident”</note>

verses.name: Matthew 26:74
verses.text: Then he began to curse and to swear with an oath, “I do not know the man!” And immediately a rooster crowed.

verses.name: Matthew 26:75
verses.text: And Peter remembered the statement Jesus had said, “Before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times,” and he went outside <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> wept bitterly.  <chapter eID="Matt.26"/>

verses.name: Matthew 27:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10720"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Taken to Pilate</title> <div sID="gen25980" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10720"/>Now <transChange type="added">when it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was”)</note> was early morning, all the chief priests and the elders of the people took counsel against Jesus in order to put him to death.

verses.name: Matthew 27:2
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“tying”) which is understood as temporal</note> tying him up, they led him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> away and handed him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> over to Pilate the governor.  <div eID="gen25980" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 27:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10721"/><title type="x-s">The Suicide of Judas Iscariot</title> <div sID="gen25981" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10721"/>Then <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> Judas, the one who had betrayed him, saw that he had been condemned, he regretted what he had done<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“regretted”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> returned the thirty silver coins to the chief priests and elders,

verses.name: Matthew 27:4
verses.text: saying, “I have sinned <transChange type="added">by</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“betraying”) which is understood as means</note> betraying innocent blood!” But they said, “What is that to us? You see to it!”<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Matthew 27:5
verses.text: And throwing the silver coins into the temple he departed. And he went away <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went away”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> hanged himself.

verses.name: Matthew 27:6
verses.text: But the chief priests took the silver coins <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “It is not permitted to put them into the temple treasury, because it is <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞blood money⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “the price of blood”</note>

verses.name: Matthew 27:7
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“taking”) which is understood as temporal</note> taking counsel, they purchased <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞with⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for”</note> them the Potter’s Field, for a burial place for strangers.

verses.name: Matthew 27:8
verses.text: (For this reason that field has been called the Field of Blood until today.)

verses.name: Matthew 27:9
verses.text: Then what was spoken by the prophet Jeremiah was fulfilled, who said, “And they took the thirty silver coins, the price of the one who had been priced, <transChange type="added">on</transChange> whom a price had been set by the sons of Israel,

verses.name: Matthew 27:10
verses.text: and they gave them for the potter’s field, just as the Lord directed me.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from various passages in Jeremiah including <reference osisRef="Jer.18.2-Jer.18.6">18:2–6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.19.1-Jer.19.13">19:1–13</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.32.6-Jer.32.15">32:6–15</reference>; see also <reference osisRef="Zech.11.12-Zech.11.13">Zech 11:12–13</reference></note>  <div eID="gen25981" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 27:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10722"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Before Pilate</title> <div sID="gen25982" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10722"/>So Jesus stood before the governor, and the governor asked him, saying, “Are you the king of the Jews?” And Jesus said, “You say <transChange type="added">so</transChange>.”

verses.name: Matthew 27:12
verses.text: And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞when he was being accused⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in the him being accused”</note> by the chief priests and elders he answered nothing.

verses.name: Matthew 27:13
verses.text: Then Pilate said to him, “Do you not hear how many <transChange type="added">things</transChange> they are testifying against you?”

verses.name: Matthew 27:14
verses.text: And he did not reply to him, not even with reference to one statement, so that the governor was very astonished.  <div eID="gen25982" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 27:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10723"/><title type="x-s">Pilate Releases Barabbas</title> <div sID="gen25983" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10723"/>Now at each feast, the governor was accustomed to release one prisoner to the crowd—the one whom they wanted.

verses.name: Matthew 27:16
verses.text: And at that time they had a notorious prisoner named Jesus<note placement="foot">Although many manuscripts omit “Jesus” here, it is so hard to explain why a scribe would have added it that the reading is probably original</note> Barabbas.<note placement="foot">“Barabbas” means “son of the father” in Aramaic</note>

verses.name: Matthew 27:17
verses.text: So <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“had assembled”)</note> they had assembled, Pilate said to them, “Whom do you want me to release for you—Jesus<note placement="foot">Although many manuscripts omit “Jesus” here, it is so hard to explain why a scribe would have added it that the reading is probably original</note> Barabbas or Jesus who is called Christ?”

verses.name: Matthew 27:18
verses.text: (For he knew that they had handed him over because of envy.

verses.name: Matthew 27:19
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was sitting”)</note> he was sitting on the judgment seat, his wife sent a message<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to him, saying, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Have nothing to do with that righteous man⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “nothing to you and to that righteous man”</note> for I have suffered much as a result of a dream today because of him.”)

verses.name: Matthew 27:20
verses.text: But the chief priests and the elders persuaded the crowds that they should ask for Barabbas and put Jesus to death.

verses.name: Matthew 27:21
verses.text: So the governor answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to them, “Which of the two do you want me to release for you?” And they said, “Barabbas!”

verses.name: Matthew 27:22
verses.text: Pilate said to them, “What then should I do <transChange type="added">with</transChange> Jesus, the one who is called Christ?” They all said, “Let him be crucified!”

verses.name: Matthew 27:23
verses.text: And he said, “Why? What wrong has he done?” But they began to shout<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to shout”)</note> even louder, saying, “Let him be crucified!”  <div eID="gen25983" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 27:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10724"/><div sID="gen25984" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10724"/>So Pilate, <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw that he was accomplishing nothing, but instead an uproar was developing, took water and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> washed his<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> hands before the crowd, saying, “I am innocent of the blood of this man. You see to it!”<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Matthew 27:25
verses.text: And all the people answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “His blood <transChange type="added">be</transChange> on us and on our children!”

verses.name: Matthew 27:26
verses.text: Then he released Barabbas for them, but <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“flogged”) which is understood as temporal</note> he had Jesus flogged, he handed him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> over so that he could be crucified.  <div eID="gen25984" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 27:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10725"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Is Mocked</title> <div sID="gen25985" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10725"/>Then the soldiers of the governor took Jesus into the governor’s residence <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> gathered the whole cohort to him.

verses.name: Matthew 27:28
verses.text: And they stripped him <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“stripped”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> put a scarlet military cloak around him,

verses.name: Matthew 27:29
verses.text: and weaving a crown of thorns, they put <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> on his head, and put<note placement="foot">This is an understood repetition of the verb from earlier in the verse</note> a reed in his right hand. And kneeling down before him, they mocked him, saying, “Hail, king of the Jews!”

verses.name: Matthew 27:30
verses.text: And they spat on him <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“spat”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> took the reed and repeatedly struck<note placement="foot">The imperfect tense has been translated as iterative here (“repeatedly struck”)</note> him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> on his head.

verses.name: Matthew 27:31
verses.text: And when they had mocked him, they stripped him of the military cloak and put his <transChange type="added">own</transChange> clothes on him, and led him away in order to crucify <transChange type="added">him</transChange>.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>  <div eID="gen25985" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 27:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10726"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Is Crucified</title> <div sID="gen25986" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10726"/>And <transChange type="added">as they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“were going out”) which is understood as temporal</note> were going out, they found a man of Cyrene <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞named⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by name”</note> Simon. They forced this man to carry his cross.

verses.name: Matthew 27:33
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“came”) which is understood as temporal</note> came to a place called <hi type="italic">Golgotha</hi> (which <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞means Place of a Skull⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>),<note placement="foot">Literally “is called Place of a Skull”</note>

verses.name: Matthew 27:34
verses.text: they gave him wine mixed with gall to drink, and <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“tasted”) which is understood as temporal</note> tasted it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> he did not want to drink it.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Matthew 27:35
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had crucified”) which is understood as temporal</note> had crucified him, they divided his clothes among themselves<note placement="foot">*Here “among themselves” reflects the middle voice of the verb “divided”</note> by<note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“casting”) which is understood as means</note> casting lots.

verses.name: Matthew 27:36
verses.text: And they sat down <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“sat down”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> were watching over him there.

verses.name: Matthew 27:37
verses.text: And they put above his head the charge against him <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in writing⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>:<note placement="foot">Literally “written”</note> “This is Jesus, the king of the Jews.”

verses.name: Matthew 27:38
verses.text: Then two robbers were crucified with him, one on <transChange type="added">his</transChange> right and one on <transChange type="added">his</transChange> left.

verses.name: Matthew 27:39
verses.text: And those who passed by reviled him, shaking their heads

verses.name: Matthew 27:40
verses.text: and saying, “The one who would destroy the temple and rebuild <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> in three days, save yourself! If you are the Son of God, come down from the cross!”

verses.name: Matthew 27:41
verses.text: In the same way also the chief priests, along with the scribes and elders, were mocking <transChange type="added">him</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> saying,

verses.name: Matthew 27:42
verses.text: “He saved others; he is not able to save himself! He is the king of Israel! Let him come down now from the cross, and we will believe in him!

verses.name: Matthew 27:43
verses.text: He trusts in God; let him deliver him now if he wants to,<note placement="foot">Or “let him deliver him now if he wants him”</note> because he said, ‘I am the Son of God’!”

verses.name: Matthew 27:44
verses.text: And in the same <transChange type="added">way</transChange> even the robbers who were crucified with him were reviling him.  <div eID="gen25986" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 27:45
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10727"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Dies on the Cross</title> <div sID="gen25987" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10727"/>Now from the sixth hour, darkness came over all the land until the ninth hour.

verses.name: Matthew 27:46
verses.text: And about the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice, saying, “<hi type="italic">Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?</hi>” (that is, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”)<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.22.1">Ps 22:1</reference></note>

verses.name: Matthew 27:47
verses.text: And some of those who were standing there, <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> said, “This man is summoning Elijah!”

verses.name: Matthew 27:48
verses.text: And immediately one of them ran and took a sponge and filled <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> with sour wine and put it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> on a reed and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participles (“ran … took … filled … put”) have been translated as finite verbs</note> gave it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to him to drink.

verses.name: Matthew 27:49
verses.text: But the others said, “Leave <transChange type="added">him</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> alone! let us see if Elijah is coming to save him.”

verses.name: Matthew 27:50
verses.text: And Jesus cried out again with a loud voice <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“cried out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> gave up his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> spirit.

verses.name: Matthew 27:51
verses.text: And behold, the curtain of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom, and the earth shook and the rocks were split.

verses.name: Matthew 27:52
verses.text: And the tombs were opened, and many bodies of the saints who had fallen asleep were raised,

verses.name: Matthew 27:53
verses.text: and coming out of the tombs after his resurrection, they went into the holy city and appeared to many.  <div eID="gen25987" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 27:54
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10728"/><div sID="gen25988" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10728"/>Now the centurion and those with him who were guarding Jesus, <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw the earthquake and the things that took place, were extremely frightened, saying, “Truly this man was God’s Son!”

verses.name: Matthew 27:55
verses.text: And there were many women there, observing from a distance, who had followed Jesus from Galilee, serving him,

verses.name: Matthew 27:56
verses.text: among whom were Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.  <div eID="gen25988" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 27:57
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10729"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Is Buried</title> <div sID="gen25989" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10729"/>Now <transChange type="added">when it</transChange> was evening, a rich man from Arimathea named Joseph came, who also was a disciple of Jesus himself.

verses.name: Matthew 27:58
verses.text: This man approached Pilate <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“approached”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> asked for the body of Jesus. Then Pilate ordered it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to be given to him.<note placement="foot">*The words “to him” are not in the Greek text but are implied</note>

verses.name: Matthew 27:59
verses.text: And Joseph took the body <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> wrapped it in a clean linen cloth,

verses.name: Matthew 27:60
verses.text: and placed it in his <transChange type="added">own</transChange> new tomb that he had cut in the rock. And he rolled a large stone to the entrance of the tomb <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“rolled”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> went away.

verses.name: Matthew 27:61
verses.text: Now Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were there, sitting opposite the tomb.  <div eID="gen25989" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 27:62
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10730"/><title type="x-s">The Tomb Is Sealed and Guarded</title> <div sID="gen25990" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10730"/>Now <transChange type="added">on</transChange> the next day, which is after the day of preparation, the chief priests and the Pharisees assembled before Pilate,

verses.name: Matthew 27:63
verses.text: saying, “Sir, we remember that <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the participle (“alive”) which is understood as temporal</note> that deceiver was still alive he said, ‘After three days I will rise.’

verses.name: Matthew 27:64
verses.text: Therefore give orders that the tomb be made secure until the third day, lest his disciples come <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“come”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> steal him and tell the people, ‘He has been raised from the dead,’ and the last deception will be worse than the first.”

verses.name: Matthew 27:65
verses.text: Pilate said to them, “You have a guard of soldiers. Go, make <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> as secure as you know how.”

verses.name: Matthew 27:66
verses.text: So they went with the guard of soldiers <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> made the tomb secure by<note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“sealing”) which is understood as means</note> sealing the stone.  <chapter eID="Matt.27"/>

verses.name: Matthew 28:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10731"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Is Raised</title> <div sID="gen25991" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10731"/>Now after the Sabbath, at the dawning on the first <transChange type="added">day</transChange> of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to view the tomb.

verses.name: Matthew 28:2
verses.text: And behold, there was a great earthquake, for an angel of the Lord descended from heaven and came up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participles (“descended” and “came up”) have been translated as finite verbs</note> rolled away the stone and sat down<note placement="foot">Or “was sitting”; here “sat down” reflects an ingressive nuance (beginning of a process or entry into a state) in the translation of the imperfect verb</note> on it.

verses.name: Matthew 28:3
verses.text: Now his appearance was like lightning and his clothing white as snow.

verses.name: Matthew 28:4
verses.text: And the guards trembled from the fear of him and became like dead men.

verses.name: Matthew 28:5
verses.text: But the angel answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to the women, “Do not be afraid, for I know that you are looking for Jesus, who was crucified.

verses.name: Matthew 28:6
verses.text: He is not here, for he has been raised, just as he said. Come, see the place where he was lying.

verses.name: Matthew 28:7
verses.text: And go quickly, tell his disciples, ‘He has been raised from the dead, and behold, he is going ahead of you into Galilee. You will see him there.’ Behold, I have told you.”

verses.name: Matthew 28:8
verses.text: And they departed quickly from the tomb with fear and great joy, <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“departed”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> ran to tell his disciples.

verses.name: Matthew 28:9
verses.text: And behold, Jesus met them, saying, “Greetings!” And they came up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> took hold of his feet and worshiped him.

verses.name: Matthew 28:10
verses.text: Then Jesus said to them, “Do not be afraid! Go tell my brothers that they should go to Galilee, and there they will see me.”  <div eID="gen25991" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 28:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10732"/><title type="x-s">The Guards Report the Body Stolen</title> <div sID="gen25992" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10732"/>And <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“were going”)</note> they were going, behold, some of the guard of soldiers went into the city and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> reported to the chief priests everything that had happened.

verses.name: Matthew 28:12
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had assembled”) which is understood as temporal</note> had assembled with the elders and had taken counsel, they gave a rather large sum of money to the soldiers,

verses.name: Matthew 28:13
verses.text: telling <transChange type="added">them</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> “Say ‘His disciples came during the night and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> stole him while<note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“were sleeping”)</note> we were sleeping.’

verses.name: Matthew 28:14
verses.text: And if this <transChange type="added">matter</transChange> is heard before the governor, we will satisfy him and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞keep you out of trouble⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “make you free from care”</note>

verses.name: Matthew 28:15
verses.text: So they took the money <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> did as they were told, and spread abroad this report among the Jews until this very day.  <div eID="gen25992" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 28:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10733"/><title type="x-s">The Great Commission</title> <div sID="gen25993" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10733"/>So the eleven disciples proceeded to Galilee, to the mountain which Jesus had designated for them.

verses.name: Matthew 28:17
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw him, they worshiped him,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> but some doubted.

verses.name: Matthew 28:18
verses.text: And Jesus approached <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“approached”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> spoke to them, saying, “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me.

verses.name: Matthew 28:19
verses.text: Therefore, go<note placement="foot">*As a participle of attendant circumstance this participle carries imperatival force picked up from the main verb (“make disciples”)</note> and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“go”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,

verses.name: Matthew 28:20
verses.text: teaching them to observe everything I have commanded you, and behold, I am with you all the days until the end of the age.”  <chapter eID="Matt.28"/> <div eID="gen25993" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen25653" osisID="Matt" type="book"/>

verses.name: Mark 1:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10734"/><title type="x-s">John the Baptist Begins His Ministry</title> <div sID="gen25995" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10734"/>The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ.<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts add “the Son of God”</note>

verses.name: Mark 1:2
verses.text: Just as it is written in the prophet Isaiah, <div eID="gen25995" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen25996"/> <l level="1" sID="gen25997"/>“Behold, I am sending my messenger before your face,<l eID="gen25997" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen25998"/>who will prepare your way, <l eID="gen25998" level="2"/>

verses.name: Mark 1:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10735"/><l level="1" sID="gen25999"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10735"/>the voice of one shouting in the wilderness,<l eID="gen25999" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26000"/>‘Prepare the way of the Lord,<l eID="gen26000" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26001"/>make straight his paths!’ ”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.40.3">Isa 40:3</reference></note> <l eID="gen26001" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen25996"/>

verses.name: Mark 1:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10736"/><div sID="gen26002" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10736"/>John was there baptizing in the wilderness, proclaiming<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “and proclaiming”</note> a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.

verses.name: Mark 1:5
verses.text: And all the Judean region and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem went out to him and were being baptized by him in the Jordan River, confessing their sins.

verses.name: Mark 1:6
verses.text: And John was dressed in camel’s hair and a belt made of leather around his waist, and he ate locusts and wild honey.

verses.name: Mark 1:7
verses.text: And he was preaching, saying, “One <transChange type="added">who is</transChange> more powerful than I is coming after me, of whom I am not worthy to bend down <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“bend down”) has been translated as an infinitive</note> untie the strap of his sandals.

verses.name: Mark 1:8
verses.text: I baptized you with water, but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.”  <div eID="gen26002" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 1:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10737"/><title type="x-s">The Baptism of Jesus</title> <div sID="gen26003" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10737"/>And it happened that in those days Jesus came from Nazareth in Galilee and was baptized in the Jordan by John.

verses.name: Mark 1:10
verses.text: And immediately <transChange type="added">as he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was coming up”) which is understood as temporal</note> was coming up out of the water, he saw the heavens being split apart and the Spirit descending like a dove on him.

verses.name: Mark 1:11
verses.text: And a voice came from heaven, “You are my beloved Son; with you I am well pleased.”  <div eID="gen26003" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 1:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10738"/><title type="x-s">The Temptation of Jesus</title> <div sID="gen26004" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10738"/>And immediately the Spirit drove him out into the wilderness.

verses.name: Mark 1:13
verses.text: And he was in the wilderness forty days being tempted by Satan. And he was with the wild animals, and the angels were ministering to him.  <div eID="gen26004" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 1:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10739"/><title type="x-s">Public Ministry in Galilee</title> <div sID="gen26005" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10739"/>And after<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “Now after”</note> John <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞had been taken into custody⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “had been handed over”</note> Jesus went into Galilee proclaiming the gospel of God

verses.name: Mark 1:15
verses.text: and saying, “The time is fulfilled and the kingdom of God has come near. Repent and believe in the gospel!”  <div eID="gen26005" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 1:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10740"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Calls His First Disciples</title> <div sID="gen26006" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10740"/>And <transChange type="added">as he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was passing by”) which is understood as temporal</note> was passing by along the Sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and Andrew, Simon’s brother, casting a net<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> into the sea (for they were fishermen).

verses.name: Mark 1:17
verses.text: And Jesus said to them, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Follow⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “come after”</note> me and I will make you become fishers of people.”

verses.name: Mark 1:18
verses.text: And immediately they left their nets <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“left”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> followed him.

verses.name: Mark 1:19
verses.text: And going on a little <transChange type="added">farther</transChange>, he saw James the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Zebedee and his brother John, and they <transChange type="added">were</transChange> in the boat mending the nets.

verses.name: Mark 1:20
verses.text: And immediately he called them, and they left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired men <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“left”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> went away after him.

verses.name: Mark 1:21
verses.text: And they went into Capernaum and immediately on the Sabbath he began to teach in the synagogue.<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “he went into the synagogue and began to teach”</note>  <div eID="gen26006" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 1:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10741"/><title type="x-s">A Man with an Unclean Spirit Healed</title> <div sID="gen26007" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10741"/>And they were amazed at his teaching, because he was teaching them like one who had authority, and not like the scribes.

verses.name: Mark 1:23
verses.text: And so then there was a man in their synagogue with an unclean spirit, and he cried out,

verses.name: Mark 1:24
verses.text: saying, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Leave us alone⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “what to us and to you”</note> Jesus the Nazarene! Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are—the Holy One of God!”

verses.name: Mark 1:25
verses.text: And Jesus rebuked him, saying, “Be silent, and come out of him!”

verses.name: Mark 1:26
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“convulsing”) which is understood as temporal</note> convulsing him and crying out with a loud voice, the unclean spirit came out of him.

verses.name: Mark 1:27
verses.text: And they were all amazed, so that <transChange type="added">they began</transChange> to discuss with one another, saying, “What is this? A new teaching with authority! He even commands the unclean spirits and they obey him.”

verses.name: Mark 1:28
verses.text: And the report about him then went out everywhere in the whole surrounding region of Galilee.  <div eID="gen26007" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 1:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10742"/><title type="x-s">Many at Capernaum Are Healed</title> <div sID="gen26008" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10742"/>And so then he departed from the synagogue <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“departed”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> came into the house of Simon and Andrew with James and John.

verses.name: Mark 1:30
verses.text: Now Simon’s mother-in-law was lying down, suffering with a fever, and at once they told him about her.

verses.name: Mark 1:31
verses.text: And he came <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> raised her up by<note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“taking hold of”) which is understood as means</note> taking hold of her<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> hand, and the fever left her, and she began to serve them.  <div eID="gen26008" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 1:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10743"/><div sID="gen26009" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10743"/>Now <transChange type="added">when it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was”)</note> was evening, when the sun had set, they began bringing<note placement="foot">The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began bringing”)</note> to him all those <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who were sick⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “who were having badly”</note> and those who were demon-possessed.

verses.name: Mark 1:33
verses.text: And the whole town was gathered together at the door.

verses.name: Mark 1:34
verses.text: And he healed many <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who were sick⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “who were having badly”</note> with various diseases and expelled many demons. And he did not permit the demons to speak, because they knew him.  <div eID="gen26009" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 1:35
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10744"/><title type="x-s">Preaching Throughout Galilee</title> <div sID="gen26010" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10744"/>And getting up early in the morning <transChange type="added">while it was</transChange> very dark, he departed and went to a deserted place, and there he was praying.

verses.name: Mark 1:36
verses.text: And Simon and those <transChange type="added">who were</transChange> with him searched diligently for him.

verses.name: Mark 1:37
verses.text: And they found him and said to him, “Everyone is looking for you!”

verses.name: Mark 1:38
verses.text: And he said to them, “Let us go elsewhere, into the neighboring rural towns, so that I can preach there also, because I have come out for this <transChange type="added">very</transChange> reason.”

verses.name: Mark 1:39
verses.text: And he went into all Galilee preaching in their synagogues and expelling demons.  <div eID="gen26010" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 1:40
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10745"/><title type="x-s">A Leper Cleansed</title> <div sID="gen26011" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10745"/>And a leper came to him, entreating him and kneeling down, saying<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “and saying”</note> to him, “If you are willing, you are able to make me clean.”

verses.name: Mark 1:41
verses.text: And becoming angry,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “having compassion”</note> he stretched out his hand and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“stretched out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> touched him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>, and said to him, “I am willing; be made clean.”

verses.name: Mark 1:42
verses.text: And immediately the leprosy went away from him and he was made clean.

verses.name: Mark 1:43
verses.text: And warning him sternly, he sent him away at once.

verses.name: Mark 1:44
verses.text: And he said to him, “See to it that you say nothing to anyone, but go, show yourself to the priest and bring for your cleansing <transChange type="added">the things</transChange> which Moses commanded, for a testimony to them.

verses.name: Mark 1:45
verses.text: But he went out <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> began to proclaim it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> freely and to spread abroad the account, so that he was no longer able to enter publicly into a town. But he was staying outside in deserted places, and they were coming to him from all directions.  <chapter eID="Mark.1"/>

verses.name: Mark 2:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10746"/><title type="x-s">A Paralytic Healed</title> <div sID="gen26012" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10746"/>And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“entered”) which is understood as temporal</note> entered again into Capernaum after <transChange type="added">some</transChange> days, it became known that he was at home.

verses.name: Mark 2:2
verses.text: And many had gathered, so that <transChange type="added">there was</transChange> no longer room, not even at the door, and he was speaking the word to them.

verses.name: Mark 2:3
verses.text: And they came bringing to him a paralytic, carried by four <transChange type="added">of them</transChange>.

verses.name: Mark 2:4
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“able”) which is understood as temporal</note> they were not able to bring him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to him because of the crowd, they removed the roof where he was. And after<note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“digging through”) which is understood as temporal</note> digging through, they lowered the stretcher on which the paralytic was lying.

verses.name: Mark 2:5
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic, “Child, your sins are forgiven.”  <div eID="gen26012" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 2:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10747"/><div sID="gen26013" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10747"/>Now some of the scribes were sitting there and reasoning in their hearts,

verses.name: Mark 2:7
verses.text: “Why does this man speak like this? He is blaspheming! Who is able to forgive sins except God alone?”

verses.name: Mark 2:8
verses.text: And immediately Jesus, perceiving in his spirit that they were reasoning like this within themselves, said to them, “Why are you considering these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> in your hearts?

verses.name: Mark 2:9
verses.text: Which is easier to say to the paralytic, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say ‘Get up and pick up your stretcher and walk’?

verses.name: Mark 2:10
verses.text: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins,”—he said to the paralytic—

verses.name: Mark 2:11
verses.text: “I say to you, get up, pick up your stretcher, and go to your home.”

verses.name: Mark 2:12
verses.text: And he got up and immediately picked up his<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> stretcher and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“picked up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> went out in front of them all, so that they were all amazed and glorified God, saying, “We have never seen anything<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> like this!”  <div eID="gen26013" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 2:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10748"/><title type="x-s">Levi Called to Follow Jesus</title> <div sID="gen26014" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10748"/>And he went out again beside the sea,<note placement="foot">That is, the Sea of Galilee</note> and all the crowd was coming to him, and he began to teach<note placement="foot">The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to teach”)</note> them.

verses.name: Mark 2:14
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">as he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was passing by”) which is understood as temporal</note> was passing by, he saw Levi the son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax booth, and he said to him, “Follow me!” And he stood up and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“stood up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> followed him.  <div eID="gen26014" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 2:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10749"/><div sID="gen26015" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10749"/>And it happened that he <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞was dining⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “was reclining for a meal”</note> in his house, and many tax collectors and sinners <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞were dining with⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “were reclining at table with”</note> Jesus and his disciples, for there were many and they were following him.

verses.name: Mark 2:16
verses.text: And the scribes of the Pharisees, <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw that he was eating with sinners and tax collectors, began to say<note placement="foot">The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to say”)</note> to his disciples, “Why does he eat with tax collectors and sinners?”

verses.name: Mark 2:17
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> Jesus heard it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>, he said to them, “Those who are healthy do not have need of a physician, but those <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who are sick⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “having badly”</note> I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners.”  <div eID="gen26015" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 2:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10750"/><title type="x-s">On Fasting</title> <div sID="gen26016" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10750"/>And John’s disciples and the Pharisees were fasting, and they came and said to him, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Why⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for what” reason</note> do the disciples of John and the disciples of the Pharisees fast, but your disciples do not fast?”

verses.name: Mark 2:19
verses.text: And Jesus said to them, “The <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞bridegroom’s attendants⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the sons of the bridal chamber”</note> are not able to fast while the bridegroom is with them, are they?<note placement="foot">The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here, indicated in the translation by the phrase “are they”</note> As long a time <transChange type="added">as</transChange> they have the bridegroom with them, they are not able to fast.

verses.name: Mark 2:20
verses.text: But days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they will fast in that day.

verses.name: Mark 2:21
verses.text: No one sews a patch of unshrunken cloth on an old garment. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Otherwise⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “but if not”</note> the patch pulls away from it—the new from the old—and the tear becomes worse.

verses.name: Mark 2:22
verses.text: And no one puts new wine into old wineskins. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Otherwise⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “but if not”</note> the wine will burst the wineskins and the wine is destroyed and the wineskins <transChange type="added">too</transChange>. But new wine <transChange type="added">is put</transChange> into new wineskins.”  <div eID="gen26016" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 2:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10751"/><title type="x-s">Plucking Grain on the Sabbath</title> <div sID="gen26017" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10751"/>And it happened that he was going through the grain fields on the Sabbath, and his disciples began to make <transChange type="added">their</transChange> way <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the participle (“picking”) which is understood as temporal</note> plucking off the heads of grain.

verses.name: Mark 2:24
verses.text: And the Pharisees began to say<note placement="foot">The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to say”)</note> to him, “Behold, why are they doing what is not permitted on the Sabbath?”

verses.name: Mark 2:25
verses.text: And he said to them, “Have you never read what David did when he had need and he and those <transChange type="added">who were</transChange> with him were hungry—

verses.name: Mark 2:26
verses.text: how he entered into the house of God in the time of Abiathar the high priest and ate the bread of the presentation, which it is not permitted to eat (except the priests) and also gave <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to those who were with him?”

verses.name: Mark 2:27
verses.text: And he said to them, “The Sabbath was established for people, and not people for the Sabbath.

verses.name: Mark 2:28
verses.text: So then, the Son of Man is lord even of the Sabbath.”  <chapter eID="Mark.2"/>

verses.name: Mark 3:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10752"/><title type="x-s">A Man with a Withered Hand Healed</title> <div sID="gen26018" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10752"/>And he entered into the synagogue again, and a man who had a withered hand was there.

verses.name: Mark 3:2
verses.text: And they were watching him closely <transChange type="added">to see</transChange> if he would heal him on the Sabbath, in order that they could accuse him.

verses.name: Mark 3:3
verses.text: And he said to the man who had the withered hand, “Come into the middle.”

verses.name: Mark 3:4
verses.text: And he said to them, “Is it permitted on the Sabbath to do good or to do evil, to save life or to kill?” But they were silent.

verses.name: Mark 3:5
verses.text: And looking around at them with anger, grieved at the hardness of their hearts, he said to the man, “Stretch out your<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> hand.” And he stretched it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> out, and his hand was restored.

verses.name: Mark 3:6
verses.text: And the Pharisees went out immediately with the Herodians <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞and began to conspire⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “began to give counsel”; the imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive (“began to”)</note> against him with regard to how they could destroy him.  <div eID="gen26018" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 3:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10753"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Heals Crowds by the Sea</title> <div sID="gen26019" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10753"/>And Jesus went away with his disciples to the sea,<note placement="foot">That is, the Sea of Galilee</note> and a great crowd from Galilee followed him.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> And from Judea

verses.name: Mark 3:8
verses.text: and from Jerusalem and from Idumea and the other side of the Jordan and around Tyre and Sidon a great crowd came to him <transChange type="added">because they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as causal</note> heard all that he was doing.

verses.name: Mark 3:9
verses.text: And he told his disciples that a small boat should stand ready for him because of the crowd, so that they would not press upon him.

verses.name: Mark 3:10
verses.text: For he had healed many, so that all those who <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞were suffering from diseases⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “had suffering”</note> pressed about him in order that they could touch him.

verses.name: Mark 3:11
verses.text: And the unclean spirits, whenever they saw him, were falling down before him and crying out, saying, “You are the Son of God!”

verses.name: Mark 3:12
verses.text: And he warned them strictly that they should not make him known.  <div eID="gen26019" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 3:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10754"/><title type="x-s">The Selection of the Twelve Apostles</title> <div sID="gen26020" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10754"/>And he went up on the mountain and summoned <transChange type="added">those</transChange> whom he wanted, and they came to him.

verses.name: Mark 3:14
verses.text: And he appointed twelve,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts add “whom he also named apostles”</note> so that they would be with him and so that he could send them out to preach

verses.name: Mark 3:15
verses.text: and to have authority to expel demons.

verses.name: Mark 3:16
verses.text: And he appointed the twelve.<note placement="foot">Most Greek manuscripts omit the phrase “and he appointed the twelve”</note> And to Simon he gave the name Peter,

verses.name: Mark 3:17
verses.text: and James the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Zebedee and John the brother of James (and he gave to them the name Boanerges, that is, “Sons of Thunder”),

verses.name: Mark 3:18
verses.text: and Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus, and Simon the Zealot,<note placement="foot">Literally “the Cananean,” but according to BDAG 507 s.v., this term has no relation at all to the geographical terms for Cana or Canaan, but is derived from the Aramaic term for “enthusiast, zealot” (see <reference osisRef="Luke.6.15">Luke 6:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="Acts.1.13">Acts 1:13</reference>)</note>

verses.name: Mark 3:19
verses.text: and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.  <div eID="gen26020" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 3:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10755"/><title type="x-s">A House Divided Cannot Stand</title> <div sID="gen26021" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10755"/>And he went home, and the crowd gathered again, so that they were not even able to eat a meal.

verses.name: Mark 3:21
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his family⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally those “close to him”</note> heard this,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> they went out to restrain him, for they were saying, “He has lost his mind!”  <div eID="gen26021" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 3:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10756"/><div sID="gen26022" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10756"/>And the scribes who had come down from Jerusalem were saying, “He is possessed by Beelzebul!” and “By the ruler of the demons he expels the demons!”

verses.name: Mark 3:23
verses.text: And he called them to himself <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“called”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> was speaking to them in parables, “How can Satan expel Satan?

verses.name: Mark 3:24
verses.text: And if a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom is not able to stand.

verses.name: Mark 3:25
verses.text: And if a house is divided against itself, that house will not be able to stand.

verses.name: Mark 3:26
verses.text: And if Satan has risen up against himself and is divided, he is not able to stand, but is at an end!

verses.name: Mark 3:27
verses.text: But no one is able to enter into the house of a strong <transChange type="added">man</transChange> <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“enter”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> plunder his property unless he first ties up the strong <transChange type="added">man</transChange>, and then he can thoroughly plunder his house.  <div eID="gen26022" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 3:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10757"/><div sID="gen26023" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10757"/>“Truly I say to you that all the sins and the blasphemies will be forgiven the sons of men, however much they blaspheme.

verses.name: Mark 3:29
verses.text: But whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit does not have forgiveness <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “for the age”</note> but is guilty of <transChange type="added">an</transChange> eternal sin”—

verses.name: Mark 3:30
verses.text: because they were saying, “He has an unclean spirit.”  <div eID="gen26023" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 3:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10758"/><title type="x-s">Jesus’ Mother and Brothers</title> <div sID="gen26024" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10758"/>And his mother and his brothers arrived, and standing outside, they sent <transChange type="added">word</transChange> to him to summon him.

verses.name: Mark 3:32
verses.text: And a crowd was sitting around him, and they told him, “Behold, your mother and your brothers<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts add “and your sisters”</note> <transChange type="added">are</transChange> outside looking for you.”

verses.name: Mark 3:33
verses.text: And he answered them <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “Who is my mother or<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “and”</note> my brothers?”

verses.name: Mark 3:34
verses.text: And looking around at those who were sitting around him in a circle, he said, “Behold, my mother and my brothers!

verses.name: Mark 3:35
verses.text: For whoever does the will of God, this person is my brother and sister and mother.”  <chapter eID="Mark.3"/>

verses.name: Mark 4:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10759"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Sower</title> <div sID="gen26025" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10759"/>And again he began to teach beside the sea,<note placement="foot">That is, the Sea of Galilee</note> and a very large crowd was gathered to him, so that he got into a boat and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“got”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> sat on the sea, and the whole crowd was at the sea on the land.

verses.name: Mark 4:2
verses.text: And he began to teach<note placement="foot">The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to teach”)</note> them many <transChange type="added">things</transChange> in parables, and was saying to them in his teaching,

verses.name: Mark 4:3
verses.text: “Listen! Behold, the sower went out to sow.

verses.name: Mark 4:4
verses.text: And it happened that while <transChange type="added">he</transChange> was sowing, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞some seed⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “some of which”</note> fell on the side of the path, and the birds came and devoured it.

verses.name: Mark 4:5
verses.text: And other <transChange type="added">seed</transChange> fell on the rocky ground where it did not have much soil, and it sprang up at once, because it did not have <transChange type="added">any</transChange> depth of soil.

verses.name: Mark 4:6
verses.text: And when the sun rose it was scorched, and because it did not have <transChange type="added">enough</transChange> root, it withered.

verses.name: Mark 4:7
verses.text: And other <transChange type="added">seed</transChange> fell among the thorn plants, and the thorn plants came up and choked it, and it did not produce grain.<note placement="foot">Literally “fruit,” describing here the grain harvested from the healthy plants; in contemporary English this would more naturally be expressed by terms like “grain” or “crop”</note>

verses.name: Mark 4:8
verses.text: And other <transChange type="added">seed</transChange> fell on the good soil, and produced grain,<note placement="foot">Literally “fruit,” describing here the grain harvested from the healthy plants; in contemporary English this would more naturally be expressed by terms like “grain” or “crop”</note> coming up and increasing, and it bore a crop<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>—one thirty and one sixty and one a hundred times as much.<note placement="foot">The phrase “times as much” is not in the Greek text but is implied</note>

verses.name: Mark 4:9
verses.text: And he said, “Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear!”  <div eID="gen26025" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 4:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10760"/><title type="x-s">The Reason for the Parables</title> <div sID="gen26026" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10760"/>And when he was alone, those around him together with the twelve began asking<note placement="foot">The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began asking”)</note> him about the parables.

verses.name: Mark 4:11
verses.text: And he said to them, “To you has been granted the secret of the kingdom of God, but to those who are outside everything is in parables,

verses.name: Mark 4:12
verses.text: so that <div eID="gen26026" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen26027"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26028"/>‘<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they may look closely⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “seeing they may see”</note> and not perceive,<l eID="gen26028" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26029"/>and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they may listen carefully⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “hearing they may hear”</note> and not understand,<l eID="gen26029" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26030"/>lest they turn and it be forgiven them.’ ”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.6.9-Isa.6.10">Isa 6:9–10</reference></note> <l eID="gen26030" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen26027"/>

verses.name: Mark 4:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10761"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Sower Interpreted</title> <div sID="gen26031" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10761"/>And he said to them, “Do you not understand this parable? And how will you understand all the parables?

verses.name: Mark 4:14
verses.text: The sower sows the word.

verses.name: Mark 4:15
verses.text: And these are the ones beside the path where the word is sown, and whenever they hear <transChange type="added">it</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> immediately Satan comes and takes away the word that was sown in them.

verses.name: Mark 4:16
verses.text: And these are like<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts omit “like”</note> the ones sown on the rocky ground, who whenever they hear the word immediately receive it with joy.

verses.name: Mark 4:17
verses.text: And they have no root in themselves, but are temporary. Then <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“comes”)</note> affliction or persecution comes because of the word, immediately they fall away.

verses.name: Mark 4:18
verses.text: And others are the ones sown among the thorn plants—these are the ones who hear the word,

verses.name: Mark 4:19
verses.text: and the cares of the world and the deceitfulness of wealth and the desires for other <transChange type="added">things</transChange> come in <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“come in”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> choke the word and it becomes unproductive.

verses.name: Mark 4:20
verses.text: And those are the ones sown on the good soil, who hear the word and receive <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and bear fruit—one thirty and one sixty and one a hundred times as much.”<note placement="foot">The phrase “times as much” is not in the Greek text but is implied</note>  <div eID="gen26031" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 4:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10762"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Lamp</title> <div sID="gen26032" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10762"/>And he said to them, “Surely a lamp is not brought so that it may be put under a bushel basket or under a bed, <transChange type="added">is it</transChange>?<note placement="foot">The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here, indicated in the translation by the phrase “is it”</note> Is it not<note placement="foot">The negative construction in Greek anticipates a positive answer here</note> so that it may be put on a lampstand?

verses.name: Mark 4:22
verses.text: For nothing is secret except so that it may be revealed, nor has become hidden except so that it will come to light.

verses.name: Mark 4:23
verses.text: If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear!”

verses.name: Mark 4:24
verses.text: And he said to them, “Take care what you hear! With the measure by which you measure out, it will be measured out to you, and will be added to you.

verses.name: Mark 4:25
verses.text: For whoever has, <transChange type="added">more</transChange> will be given to him, and whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.”  <div eID="gen26032" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 4:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10763"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Seed that Grows by Itself</title> <div sID="gen26033" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10763"/>And he said, “The kingdom of God is like this: like a man scatters seed on the ground.

verses.name: Mark 4:27
verses.text: And he sleeps and gets up, night and day, and the seed sprouts and grows—<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he does not know how⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “in such a way as he does not know”</note>

verses.name: Mark 4:28
verses.text: By itself the soil produces a crop: first the grass, then the head of grain, then the full grain in the head.

verses.name: Mark 4:29
verses.text: But when the crop permits, he sends <transChange type="added">in</transChange> the sickle right away, because the harvest has come.”  <div eID="gen26033" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 4:30
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10764"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Mustard Seed</title> <div sID="gen26034" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10764"/>And he said, “With what can we compare the kingdom of God, or by what parable can we present it?

verses.name: Mark 4:31
