verses.text: <transChange type="added">It is</transChange> like a mustard seed that when sown on the ground, <transChange type="added">although it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“is”) which is understood as concessive</note> is the smallest of all the seeds that <transChange type="added">are</transChange> on the ground,

verses.name: Mark 4:32
verses.text: but when it is sown it grows up and becomes the largest of all the garden herbs, and sends out large branches so that the birds of the sky are able to nest in its shade.”

verses.name: Mark 4:33
verses.text: And with many parables such as these he was speaking the word to them, as they were able to hear <transChange type="added">it</transChange>.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Mark 4:34
verses.text: And he did not speak to them without a parable, but in private he explained everything to his own disciples.  <div eID="gen26034" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 4:35
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10765"/><title type="x-s">Calming of a Storm</title> <div sID="gen26035" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10765"/>And on that day, <transChange type="added">when it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was”)</note> was evening, he said to them, “Let us cross over to the other side.”

verses.name: Mark 4:36
verses.text: And leaving the crowd, they took him along, as he was, in the boat. And other boats were with him.

verses.name: Mark 4:37
verses.text: And a great storm of wind developed, and the waves were breaking into the boat, so that the boat was already being filled <transChange type="added">with water</transChange>.<note placement="foot">*The words “with water” are not in the Greek text but are implied</note>

verses.name: Mark 4:38
verses.text: And he was in the stern sleeping on the cushion, and they woke him up and said to him, “Teacher, is it not a concern to you that we are perishing?”

verses.name: Mark 4:39
verses.text: And he woke up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“woke up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, “Be quiet! Be silent!” And the wind abated and there was a great calm.

verses.name: Mark 4:40
verses.text: And he said to them, “Why are you fearful? Do you not yet have faith?”

verses.name: Mark 4:41
verses.text: And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they were terribly frightened⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “they feared a great fear”</note> and began to say<note placement="foot">The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to say”)</note> to one another, “Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?”  <chapter eID="Mark.4"/>

verses.name: Mark 5:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10766"/><title type="x-s">A Demon-possessed Gerasene Healed</title> <div sID="gen26036" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10766"/>And they came to the other side of the sea,<note placement="foot">That is, the Sea of Galilee</note> to the region of the Gerasenes.<note placement="foot">Most later manuscripts read “Gadarenes,” while other manuscripts read “Gergesenes” here</note>

verses.name: Mark 5:2
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was getting out”)</note> he was getting out of the boat, immediately from the tombs a man with an unclean spirit went to meet him,

verses.name: Mark 5:3
verses.text: who <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞lived⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “had his dwelling”</note> among the tombs. And no one was able to bind him any longer, not even with a chain,

verses.name: Mark 5:4
verses.text: because he had often been bound with shackles and chains, and the chains had been torn apart by him, and the shackles had been shattered. And no one was strong <transChange type="added">enough</transChange> to subdue him.

verses.name: Mark 5:5
verses.text: And during every night and day among the tombs and on the mountains he was crying out and cutting himself with stones.

verses.name: Mark 5:6
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw Jesus from a distance, he ran and knelt down before him.

verses.name: Mark 5:7
verses.text: And crying out with a loud voice he said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞What have I to do with you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “what to me and to you”</note>, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I implore you by God, do not torment me!”

verses.name: Mark 5:8
verses.text: (For he was saying to him, “Come out of the man, unclean spirit!”)

verses.name: Mark 5:9
verses.text: And he was asking him “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞What is your name⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?”<note placement="foot">Literally “what name to you”</note> And he said to him, “My name <transChange type="added">is</transChange> Legion, because we are many.”

verses.name: Mark 5:10
verses.text: And he was imploring him many <transChange type="added">times</transChange> that he would not send them out of the region.

verses.name: Mark 5:11
verses.text: Now a large herd of pigs was there at the hill feeding,

verses.name: Mark 5:12
verses.text: and they implored him, saying, “Send us to the pigs so that we may enter into them.”

verses.name: Mark 5:13
verses.text: And he permitted them. And the unclean spirits came out <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> entered into the pigs, and the herd—about two thousand—rushed headlong down the steep slope into the sea and were drowned in the sea.

verses.name: Mark 5:14
verses.text: And their herdsmen fled and reported <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> in the town and in the countryside, and they came to see what it was that had happened.

verses.name: Mark 5:15
verses.text: And they came to Jesus and saw the demon-possessed man sitting <transChange type="added">there</transChange> clothed and in his right mind—the one who had had the legion—and they were afraid.

verses.name: Mark 5:16
verses.text: And those who had seen <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> described to them what had happened to the demon-possessed man, and about the pigs.

verses.name: Mark 5:17
verses.text: And they began to urge him to depart from their region.

verses.name: Mark 5:18
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was getting”)</note> he was getting into the boat, the man who had been demon-possessed began to implore<note placement="foot">The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to implore”)</note> him that he could go with him.

verses.name: Mark 5:19
verses.text: And he did not permit him, but said to him, “Go to your home to your <transChange type="added">people</transChange> and tell them all that the Lord has done for you, and <transChange type="added">that</transChange> he has had mercy on you.”

verses.name: Mark 5:20
verses.text: And he went away and began to proclaim in the Decapolis all that Jesus had done for him, and they were all astonished.  <div eID="gen26036" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 5:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10767"/><title type="x-s">A Woman Healed and a Daughter Raised</title> <div sID="gen26037" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10767"/>And <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“had crossed over”)</note> Jesus had crossed over again in the boat to the other side, a large crowd gathered to him, and he was beside the sea.

verses.name: Mark 5:22
verses.text: And one of the rulers of the synagogue came—Jairus by name—and <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw him, he fell down at his feet.

verses.name: Mark 5:23
verses.text: And he was imploring him many <transChange type="added">times</transChange>, saying, “My little daughter <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞is at the point of death⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!<note placement="foot">Literally “has finally”</note> Come, lay your<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> hands on her, so that she will get well and will live.”

verses.name: Mark 5:24
verses.text: And he went with him, and a large crowd was following him and pressing around him.  <div eID="gen26037" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 5:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10768"/><div sID="gen26038" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10768"/>And <transChange type="added">there was</transChange> a woman who was <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞suffering from hemorrhages⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “with a flow of blood”</note> twelve years.

verses.name: Mark 5:26
verses.text: And she had endured many <transChange type="added">things</transChange> under many physicians, and had spent <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞all that she had⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “all with her”</note> and had received no help at all, but instead <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞became worse⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “came back for the worse”</note>

verses.name: Mark 5:27
verses.text: <transChange type="added">When she</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard about Jesus, she came up in the crowd behind him and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> touched his cloak,

verses.name: Mark 5:28
verses.text: for she was saying, “If I touch just his clothing, I will be healed!”

verses.name: Mark 5:29
verses.text: And immediately her <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞hemorrhage stopped⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “flow of blood was dried up”</note> and she realized in her<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> body that she was healed of her<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> suffering.

verses.name: Mark 5:30
verses.text: And immediately Jesus, perceiving in himself <transChange type="added">that</transChange> power had gone out from himself, turned around in the crowd <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“turned around”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “Who touched my clothing?”

verses.name: Mark 5:31
verses.text: And his disciples said to him, “You see the crowd pressing upon you, and you say ‘Who touched me?’ ”

verses.name: Mark 5:32
verses.text: And he was looking around to see the one who had done this.

verses.name: Mark 5:33
verses.text: So the woman, frightened and trembling, knowing what had happened to her, came and fell down before him and told him the whole truth.

verses.name: Mark 5:34
verses.text: But he said to her, “Daughter, your faith has healed you. Go in peace and be well from your suffering.”  <div eID="gen26038" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 5:35
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10769"/><div sID="gen26039" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10769"/><transChange type="added">While</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“speaking”)</note> he was still speaking, they came from the synagogue ruler’s house<note placement="foot">*Here “house” is implied since the synagogue ruler himself is directly addressed (and therefore present) in the remainder of this verse</note> saying, “Your daughter has died. Why trouble the Teacher further?”

verses.name: Mark 5:36
verses.text: But Jesus, ignoring<note placement="foot">Or “overhearing”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞what was said⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the report that was spoken”</note> told the ruler of the synagogue, “Do not be afraid—only believe!”

verses.name: Mark 5:37
verses.text: And he did not allow anyone to follow along with him except Peter and James and John, the brother of James.

verses.name: Mark 5:38
verses.text: And they came to the house of the ruler of the synagogue and saw a commotion, and <transChange type="added">people</transChange> weeping and wailing loudly.

verses.name: Mark 5:39
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“entered”) which is understood as temporal</note> entered, he said to them, “Why are you agitated and weeping? The child is not dead, but is sleeping.”

verses.name: Mark 5:40
verses.text: And they began laughing<note placement="foot">The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began laughing”)</note> at him. But he sent them all out and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“sent … out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> took along the father and mother of the child, and those <transChange type="added">who were</transChange> with him, and went in to where the child was.

verses.name: Mark 5:41
verses.text: And taking hold of the child’s hand, he said to her, “<hi type="italic">Talitha koum!</hi>” (which is translated, “Little girl, I say to you, get up!”),

verses.name: Mark 5:42
verses.text: and immediately the girl stood up and began walking around<note placement="foot">The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began walking around”)</note> (for she was twelve years old). And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞immediately they were utterly and completely astonished⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “immediately they were astonished with great astonishment”</note>

verses.name: Mark 5:43
verses.text: And he commanded them strictly that no one should learn of this, and said to give her <transChange type="added">something</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to eat.  <chapter eID="Mark.5"/>

verses.name: Mark 6:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10770"/><title type="x-s">Rejected at Nazareth</title> <div sID="gen26040" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10770"/>And he went out from there and came to his hometown, and his disciples followed him.

verses.name: Mark 6:2
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“came”)</note> the Sabbath came, he began to teach in the synagogue, and many who heard him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> were amazed, saying, “Where did this man <transChange type="added">get</transChange> these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>? And what <transChange type="added">is</transChange> this wisdom that has been granted to this man, and the miracles such as these performed through his hands?

verses.name: Mark 6:3
verses.text: Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary and brother of James and Joses and Judas and Simon? And are not his sisters here with us?” And they were offended by him.

verses.name: Mark 6:4
verses.text: And Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not without honor except in his hometown, and among his relatives, and in his <transChange type="added">own</transChange> household.”

verses.name: Mark 6:5
verses.text: And he was not able to do any miracle in that place except to lay his<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> hands on a few sick people and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“lay”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> heal them.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Mark 6:6
verses.text: And he was astonished because of their unbelief. <div eID="gen26040" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">The Twelve Commissioned and Sent Out</title> <div sID="gen26041" type="x-p"/> And he was going around among the villages teaching.

verses.name: Mark 6:7
verses.text: And he summoned the twelve and began to send them out two <transChange type="added">by</transChange> two, and gave them authority over the unclean spirits.

verses.name: Mark 6:8
verses.text: And he commanded them that they take along nothing for the journey except only a staff—no bread, no traveler’s bag, no money in their<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> belts—

verses.name: Mark 6:9
verses.text: but to put on sandals and not to wear two tunics.

verses.name: Mark 6:10
verses.text: And he said to them, “Whenever you enter into a house, stay there until you depart from there.

verses.name: Mark 6:11
verses.text: And whatever place does not welcome you or listen to you, <transChange type="added">as you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“go out”) which is understood as temporal</note> go out from there, shake off the dust that is on your feet for a testimony against them.”

verses.name: Mark 6:12
verses.text: And they went out <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> proclaimed that people<note placement="foot">*Here “people” is supplied as the subject because a third-person pronoun (“they”) would be ambiguous</note> should repent.

verses.name: Mark 6:13
verses.text: And they were expelling many demons and anointing many sick <transChange type="added">people</transChange> with olive oil and healing <transChange type="added">them</transChange>.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>  <div eID="gen26041" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 6:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10771"/><title type="x-s">Herod Kills John the Baptist</title> <div sID="gen26042" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10771"/>And King Herod heard <transChange type="added">it</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> because his name had become known. And they were saying, “John, the one who baptizes, has been raised from the dead, and because of this these miraculous powers are at work in him.”

verses.name: Mark 6:15
verses.text: But others were saying, “He is Elijah,” and others were saying, “<transChange type="added">He is</transChange> a prophet like one of the prophets.”

verses.name: Mark 6:16
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> Herod heard it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> he said, “John whom I beheaded—this one has been raised!”

verses.name: Mark 6:17
verses.text: For Herod himself had sent <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“had sent”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> arrested John and bound him in prison because of Herodias, the wife of Philip his brother, because he had married her.

verses.name: Mark 6:18
verses.text: For John had been saying to Herod, “It is not permitted for you to have your brother’s wife.”

verses.name: Mark 6:19
verses.text: So Herodias held a grudge against him and was wanting to kill him, and was not able <transChange type="added">to do so</transChange>.

verses.name: Mark 6:20
verses.text: For Herod was afraid of John, <transChange type="added">because he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“knew”) which is understood as causal</note> knew him to be a righteous and holy man and protected him. And when he<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participles (“came in” and “danced”) which are understood as temporal</note> listened to him, he was greatly perplexed, and <transChange type="added">yet</transChange> he listened to him gladly.

verses.name: Mark 6:21
verses.text: And a suitable day came when Herod, on his birthday, gave a banquet for his courtiers and military tribunes and the most prominent <transChange type="added">men</transChange> of Galilee.

verses.name: Mark 6:22
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“came in”)</note> the daughter of Herodias herself<note placement="foot">In place of “the daughter of Herodias herself” some manuscripts have “his daughter Herodias”</note> came in and danced and pleased<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “danced, she pleased”</note> Herod and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his dinner guests⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “those reclining at table with him”</note> the king said to the girl, “Ask me for whatever you want, and I will give it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to you.”

verses.name: Mark 6:23
verses.text: And he swore to her,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts add “at length”</note> “Anything whatever you ask me for I will give you, up to half my kingdom!”

verses.name: Mark 6:24
verses.text: And she went out <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to her mother, “What should I ask for?” And she said, “The head of John the baptizer.”

verses.name: Mark 6:25
verses.text: And she came in immediately with haste to the king <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came in”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> asked, saying, “I want you to give me the head of John the Baptist on a platter immediately.”

verses.name: Mark 6:26
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">although he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was”) which is understood as concessive</note> was deeply grieved, the king, because of his<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> oaths and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞dinner guests⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “those who were reclining at table”</note> did not want to refuse her.

verses.name: Mark 6:27
verses.text: And immediately the king sent an executioner <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“sent”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> ordered him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to bring his head. And he went and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> beheaded him in the prison.

verses.name: Mark 6:28
verses.text: And he brought his head on a platter and gave it to the girl, and the girl gave it to her mother.

verses.name: Mark 6:29
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> his disciples heard this,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> they came and took away his corpse and placed it in a tomb.  <div eID="gen26042" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 6:30
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10772"/><title type="x-s">The Feeding of Five Thousand</title> <div sID="gen26043" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10772"/>And the apostles regathered to Jesus and reported to him everything that they had done and that they had taught.

verses.name: Mark 6:31
verses.text: And he said to them, “You yourselves come privately to an isolated place and rest for a short time.” For those <transChange type="added">who were</transChange> coming and going were many, and they did not even have time to eat.

verses.name: Mark 6:32
verses.text: And they went away in the boat to an isolated place by themselves.

verses.name: Mark 6:33
verses.text: And many <transChange type="added">people</transChange> saw them leaving and recognized <transChange type="added">them</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and ran there together by land from all the towns, and arrived ahead of them.

verses.name: Mark 6:34
verses.text: And getting out <transChange type="added">of the boat</transChange><note placement="foot">*The words “of the boat” are not in the Greek text but are implied by this verb, which refers to disembarking from a boat or ship</note> he saw the large crowd and had compassion on them, because they were like sheep <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞without⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “not having”</note> a shepherd, and he began to teach them many <transChange type="added">things</transChange>.

verses.name: Mark 6:35
verses.text: And the hour had already become late <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“came up”) which is understood as temporal</note> his disciples came up to him, saying, “The place is desolate and the hour <transChange type="added">is</transChange> already late.

verses.name: Mark 6:36
verses.text: Send them away so that they can go into the surrounding farms and villages <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“go”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> purchase something to eat for themselves.”

verses.name: Mark 6:37
verses.text: But he answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to them, “You give them something<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to eat.” And they said to him, “Should we go and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“go”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> purchase bread for two hundred denarii and give it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to them to eat?”

verses.name: Mark 6:38
verses.text: And he said to them, “How many loaves do you have? Go look!” And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“found out”) which is understood as temporal</note> found out, they said, “Five, and two fish.”

verses.name: Mark 6:39
verses.text: And he ordered them all to recline in groups on the green grass.

verses.name: Mark 6:40
verses.text: And they reclined in groups, by hundreds and by fifties.

verses.name: Mark 6:41
verses.text: And taking the five loaves and the two fish <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied in the translation because of English style</note> looking up to heaven, he gave thanks and broke the loaves and gave them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to his disciples so that they could set them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> before them. And he distributed the two fish to <transChange type="added">them</transChange> all.

verses.name: Mark 6:42
verses.text: And they all ate and were satisfied.

verses.name: Mark 6:43
verses.text: And they picked up the broken pieces, twelve baskets full, and of the fish.

verses.name: Mark 6:44
verses.text: And those who ate the loaves were five thousand men.  <div eID="gen26043" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 6:45
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10773"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Walks on the Water</title> <div sID="gen26044" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10773"/>And immediately he made his disciples get into the boat and go on ahead to the other side, to Bethsaida, while he himself dismissed the crowd.

verses.name: Mark 6:46
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“went away”) which is understood as temporal</note> had said farewell to them, he went away to the mountain to pray.

verses.name: Mark 6:47
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“came”)</note> evening came, the boat was in the middle of the sea and he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> alone on the land.

verses.name: Mark 6:48
verses.text: And he saw them being beaten in their rowing<note placement="foot">Or “being held up in their progress”</note> because the wind was against them. Around the fourth watch of the night he came to them, walking on the sea, and he was wanting to pass by them.

verses.name: Mark 6:49
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> they saw him walking on the sea, they thought that it was a ghost, and they cried out.

verses.name: Mark 6:50
verses.text: For they all saw him and were terrified. But immediately he spoke with them and said to them, “Have courage, I am <transChange type="added">he</transChange>! Do not be afraid!”

verses.name: Mark 6:51
verses.text: And he went up with them into the boat, and the wind abated. And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they were extraordinarily⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “exceedingly extremely”</note> astounded within themselves,

verses.name: Mark 6:52
verses.text: because they did not understand concerning the loaves, but their hearts were hardened.  <div eID="gen26044" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 6:53
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10774"/><title type="x-s">Many Healed at Gennesaret</title> <div sID="gen26045" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10774"/>And <transChange type="added">after they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had crossed over”) which is understood as temporal</note> had crossed over, they came to land at Gennesaret and anchored <transChange type="added">there</transChange>.

verses.name: Mark 6:54
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">as</transChange> they were getting out of the boat, <transChange type="added">people</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “people” is supplied as the subject of the verb because the third person pronoun “they” could be confused with the disciples getting out of the boat earlier in this verse</note> recognized him immediately.

verses.name: Mark 6:55
verses.text: They ran about <transChange type="added">through</transChange> that whole region and began to carry around those <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who were sick⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “who were having badly”</note> on stretchers, wherever they heard that he was.

verses.name: Mark 6:56
verses.text: And wherever he would go, into villages or into towns or to farms, they would put those who were sick in the marketplaces and would implore him that if they could touch even the edge of his cloak. And all those who touched it were healed.  <chapter eID="Mark.6"/>

verses.name: Mark 7:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10775"/><title type="x-s">Human Traditions and God’s Commandments</title> <div sID="gen26046" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10775"/>And the Pharisees and some of the scribes who had come from Jerusalem gathered to him.

verses.name: Mark 7:2
verses.text: And they saw that some of his disciples were eating their<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> bread with unclean—that is, unwashed—hands.

verses.name: Mark 7:3
verses.text: (For the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they wash their hands <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞ritually⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “with the fist”; although the exact meaning of the phrase is uncertain, there is general agreement it has to do with the ritual or ceremonial nature of the handwashing</note> thus<note placement="foot">*Here “thus” is supplied as a component of the participle (“holding fast to”) which is understood as result</note> holding fast to the traditions of the elders.

verses.name: Mark 7:4
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when they come</transChange><note placement="foot">The phrase “when they come” is not in the Greek text but is implied</note> from the marketplace, they do not eat unless they wash. And there are many other traditions<note placement="foot">*The word “traditions” is not in the Greek text but is implied</note> which they have received and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“have received”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> hold fast to—for example,<note placement="foot">The phrase “for example” is not in the Greek text but is supplied as a clarification in the English translation</note> the washing of cups and pitchers and bronze kettles and dining couches.)<note placement="foot">Several important manuscripts omit “and dining couches”</note>

verses.name: Mark 7:5
verses.text: And the Pharisees and the scribes asked him, “Why do your disciples not live according to the tradition of the elders, but eat their<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> bread with unclean hands?”

verses.name: Mark 7:6
verses.text: So he said to them, “Isaiah prophesied correctly about you hypocrites, as it is written, <div eID="gen26046" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen26047"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26048"/>‘This people honors me with their<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> lips,<l eID="gen26048" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26049"/>but their heart is far, far away from me. <l eID="gen26049" level="2"/>

verses.name: Mark 7:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10776"/><l level="1" sID="gen26050"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10776"/>And they worship me in vain,<l eID="gen26050" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26051"/>teaching <transChange type="added">as</transChange> doctrines the commandments of men.’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.29.13">Isa 29:13</reference></note> <l eID="gen26051" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen26047"/>

verses.name: Mark 7:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10777"/><div sID="gen26052" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10777"/>Abandoning the commandment of God, you hold fast to the tradition of men.”  <div eID="gen26052" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 7:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10778"/><div sID="gen26053" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10778"/>And he said to them, “You splendidly ignore the commandment of God so that you can keep<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “you can maintain”</note> your tradition.

verses.name: Mark 7:10
verses.text: For Moses said, ‘Honor your father and your mother,’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Exod.20.12">Exod 20:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="Deut.5.16">Deut 5:16</reference></note> and, ‘The one who speaks evil of father or mother <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞must certainly die⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “let him die the death”</note>.’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Exod.21.17">Exod 21:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="Lev.20.9">Lev 20:9</reference></note>

verses.name: Mark 7:11
verses.text: But you say, ‘If a man says to his<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> father or to his<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> mother, “Whatever <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞benefit you would have received⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “you would have been benefited”</note> from me is <hi type="italic">corban</hi>”<note placement="foot">A Hebrew term referring to something consecrated as a gift to God and thus not available for ordinary use</note> (that is, a gift <transChange type="added">to God</transChange>),

verses.name: Mark 7:12
verses.text: you no longer permit him to do anything for his<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> father or his<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> mother,

verses.name: Mark 7:13
verses.text: <transChange type="added">thus</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “thus” is supplied as a component of the participle (“making void”) which is understood as result</note> making void the word of God by your tradition that you have handed down, and you do many similar <transChange type="added">things</transChange> such as this.”  <div eID="gen26053" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 7:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10779"/><title type="x-s">Defilement from Within</title> <div sID="gen26054" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10779"/>And summoning the crowd again, he said to them, “Listen to me, all <transChange type="added">of you</transChange>, and understand:

verses.name: Mark 7:15
verses.text: There is nothing outside of a person that is able to defile him <transChange type="added">by</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“going”) which is understood as means</note> going into him. But the things that go out of a person are the things that defile a person.”<note placement="foot">Most later manuscripts add v. <reference osisRef="Mark.7.16">16</reference>, “If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear.”</note>

verses.name: Mark 7:17
verses.text: And when he entered into the house away from the crowd, his disciples asked him about the parable.

verses.name: Mark 7:18
verses.text: And he said to them, “So are you also without understanding? Do you not understand that everything <transChange type="added">that is</transChange> outside that goes into a person <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not able to defile him?

verses.name: Mark 7:19
verses.text: For it does not enter into his heart but into his<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> stomach, and goes out into the latrine”—thus<note placement="foot">*Here “thus” is supplied as a component of the participle (“declaring”) which is understood as result</note> declaring all foods clean.

verses.name: Mark 7:20
verses.text: And he said, “What comes out of a person, that defiles a person.

verses.name: Mark 7:21
verses.text: For from within, from the heart of people, come evil plans, sexual immoralities, thefts, murders,

verses.name: Mark 7:22
verses.text: adulteries, <transChange type="added">acts of</transChange> greed, malicious <transChange type="added">deeds</transChange>, deceit, licentiousness, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞envy⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the evil eye”</note> abusive speech, pride, foolishness.

verses.name: Mark 7:23
verses.text: All these evil <transChange type="added">things</transChange> come from within and defile a person.”  <div eID="gen26054" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 7:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10780"/><title type="x-s">A Syrophoenician Woman’s Great Faith</title> <div sID="gen26055" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10780"/>And from there he set out <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“set out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> went to the region of Tyre. And when he<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“entered”) which is understood as temporal</note> entered into a house, he wanted no one to know, and <transChange type="added">yet</transChange> he was not able to escape notice.

verses.name: Mark 7:25
verses.text: But immediately a woman whose young daughter was possessed by an unclean spirit, <transChange type="added">when she</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard about him, came and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> fell down at his feet,

verses.name: Mark 7:26
verses.text: Now the woman was a Greek—a Syrophoenician by nationality—and she was asking him that he would expel the demon from her daughter.

verses.name: Mark 7:27
verses.text: And he said to her, “Let the children be satisfied first, for it is not right to take the children’s bread and throw <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to the dogs!”

verses.name: Mark 7:28
verses.text: But she answered and said to him, “Lord, even the dogs under the table eat the children’s crumbs.”

verses.name: Mark 7:29
verses.text: And he said to her, “Because of this statement, go! The demon has gone out of your daughter.”

verses.name: Mark 7:30
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when she</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“went”) which is understood as temporal</note> went to her home, she found the child lying on the bed and the demon gone.  <div eID="gen26055" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 7:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10781"/><title type="x-s">A Man Deaf and Unable to Speak Healed</title> <div sID="gen26056" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10781"/>And again he went away from the region of Tyre <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went away”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> came through Sidon to the Sea of Galilee, within the region of the Decapolis.

verses.name: Mark 7:32
verses.text: And they brought to him a man who was deaf and had difficulty speaking, and they were imploring him that he would place his<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> hand on him.

verses.name: Mark 7:33
verses.text: And he took him away from the crowd by himself <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took … away”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> put his fingers into his ears, and after<note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“spitting”) which is understood as temporal</note> spitting, he touched his tongue.

verses.name: Mark 7:34
verses.text: And looking up to heaven, he sighed and said to him, “<hi type="italic">Ephphatha!</hi>” (that is, “Be opened!”).

verses.name: Mark 7:35
verses.text: And<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “And immediately”</note> his ears were opened and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his difficulty in speaking was removed⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the bond of his tongue was loosened”</note> and he began to speak normally.

verses.name: Mark 7:36
verses.text: And he ordered them that they should say nothing, but as much as he ordered them <transChange type="added">not to</transChange>, they proclaimed <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> even more instead.

verses.name: Mark 7:37
verses.text: And they were amazed beyond all measure, saying, “He has done all <transChange type="added">things</transChange> well! He even makes the deaf hear and the mute speak!”  <chapter eID="Mark.7"/>

verses.name: Mark 8:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10782"/><title type="x-s">The Feeding of Four Thousand</title> <div sID="gen26057" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10782"/>In those days there was<note placement="foot">*Here the participle (“was”) is translated as a finite verb because of English style</note> again a large crowd, and they did not have<note placement="foot">*Here the participle (“have”) is translated as a finite verb because of English style</note> anything they could eat. Summoning the disciples, he said to them,

verses.name: Mark 8:2
verses.text: “I have compassion on the crowd, because they have remained with me three days already and do not have anything to eat.

verses.name: Mark 8:3
verses.text: And if I send them away hungry to their homes they will give out on the way, and some of them have come from far away.”

verses.name: Mark 8:4
verses.text: And his disciples answered him, “Where is anyone able to feed these <transChange type="added">people</transChange> with bread here in the desert?”

verses.name: Mark 8:5
verses.text: And he asked them, “How many loaves do you have?” So they said, “Seven.”

verses.name: Mark 8:6
verses.text: And he commanded the crowd to recline for a meal on the ground, and taking the seven loaves, <transChange type="added">after he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had given thanks”) which is understood as temporal</note> had given thanks he broke them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and began giving<note placement="foot">The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began giving”)</note> them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to his disciples so that they could set them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> before them.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> And they set them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> before the crowd.

verses.name: Mark 8:7
verses.text: And they had a few small fish, and <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“giving thanks”) which is understood as temporal</note> giving thanks for them, he said to set these <transChange type="added">before them</transChange> also.

verses.name: Mark 8:8
verses.text: And they ate and were satisfied, and they picked up the broken pieces that were left, seven baskets <transChange type="added">full</transChange>.

verses.name: Mark 8:9
verses.text: Now there were about four thousand. And he sent them away.

verses.name: Mark 8:10
verses.text: And immediately he got into the boat with his disciples <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“got”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> went to the district of Dalmanutha.  <div eID="gen26057" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 8:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10783"/><title type="x-s">Pharisees Demand a Sign</title> <div sID="gen26058" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10783"/>And the Pharisees came and began to argue with him, demanding from him a sign from heaven <transChange type="added">in order to</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “in order to” is supplied as a component of the participle (“test”) which is understood as purpose</note> test him.

verses.name: Mark 8:12
verses.text: And sighing deeply in his spirit, he said, “Why does this generation demand a sign? Truly I say to you, no sign will be given to this generation!”

verses.name: Mark 8:13
verses.text: And he left them, got into <transChange type="added">the boat</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the words “the boat” are not in the Greek text but must be supplied</note> again, and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participles (“left” and “got into”) have been translated as finite verbs</note> went to the other side.  <div eID="gen26058" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 8:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10784"/><title type="x-s">Beware the Leaven of the Pharisees and Herod</title> <div sID="gen26059" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10784"/>And they had forgotten to take bread, and except <transChange type="added">for</transChange> one loaf, they did not have <transChange type="added">any</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> with them in the boat.

verses.name: Mark 8:15
verses.text: And he ordered them, saying, “Watch out! Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and the leaven of Herod!”

verses.name: Mark 8:16
verses.text: And they began to discuss with one another that they had no bread.

verses.name: Mark 8:17
verses.text: And knowing <transChange type="added">this</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> he said to them, “Why are you discussing that you have no bread? Do you not yet perceive or understand? Have your hearts been hardened?

verses.name: Mark 8:18
verses.text: <transChange type="added">Although you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“have”) which is understood as concessive</note> have eyes, do you not see? And although you<note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“have”) which is understood as concessive</note> have ears, do you not hear? And do you not remember?

verses.name: Mark 8:19
verses.text: When I broke the five loaves for the five thousand how many baskets full of broken pieces did you pick up?” They said to him, “Twelve.”

verses.name: Mark 8:20
verses.text: “When <transChange type="added">I</transChange> also<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts omit “also”</note> broke<note placement="foot">*The words “I broke” are not in the Greek text, but are understood based on the previous verse</note> the seven loaves<note placement="foot">*The word “loaves” is not in the Greek text, but is understood based on the previous verse</note> for the four thousand, how many baskets full of broken pieces did you pick up?” And they said to him, “Seven.”

verses.name: Mark 8:21
verses.text: And he said to them, “Do you not yet understand?”  <div eID="gen26059" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 8:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10785"/><title type="x-s">A Blind Man Healed at Bethsaida</title> <div sID="gen26060" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10785"/>And they came to Bethsaida. And they brought to him a blind man and implored him that he would touch him.

verses.name: Mark 8:23
verses.text: And he took hold of the blind man’s hand <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took hold of”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> led him outside the village, and after<note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“spitting”) which is understood as temporal</note> spitting in his eyes, he placed his hands on him and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“placed”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> asked him, “Do you see anything?”

verses.name: Mark 8:24
verses.text: And looking up he said, “I see people, for I see <transChange type="added">them</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> like trees walking around.”

verses.name: Mark 8:25
verses.text: Then he placed his<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> hands on his eyes again, and he opened his eyes and was cured, and could see everything clearly.

verses.name: Mark 8:26
verses.text: And he sent him to his home, saying, “Do not even go into the village.”  <div eID="gen26060" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 8:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10786"/><title type="x-s">Peter’s Confession at Caesarea Philippi</title> <div sID="gen26061" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10786"/>And Jesus and his disciples went out to the villages of Caesarea Philippi, and on the way he asked his disciples, saying to them, “Who do people say <transChange type="added">that</transChange> I am?”

verses.name: Mark 8:28
verses.text: And they told him, saying, “John the Baptist, and others Elijah, and others that <transChange type="added">you are</transChange> one of the prophets.”

verses.name: Mark 8:29
verses.text: And he asked them, “But who do you say <transChange type="added">that</transChange> I am?” Peter answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to him, “You are the Christ!”

verses.name: Mark 8:30
verses.text: And he warned them that they should tell no one about him.  <div eID="gen26061" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 8:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10787"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Predicts His Death and Resurrection</title> <div sID="gen26062" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10787"/>And he began to teach them that it was necessary <transChange type="added">for</transChange> the Son of Man to suffer many <transChange type="added">things</transChange> and to be rejected by the elders and the chief priests and the scribes, and to be killed, and after three days to rise.

verses.name: Mark 8:32
verses.text: And he was speaking openly <transChange type="added">about</transChange> the subject, and Peter took him aside <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took … aside”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> began to rebuke him.

verses.name: Mark 8:33
verses.text: But turning around and seeing his disciples, he rebuked Peter and said, “Get behind me, Satan, because you are not setting your mind on the things of God, but the things of people!”  <div eID="gen26062" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 8:34
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10788"/><title type="x-s">Taking Up One’s Cross to Follow Jesus</title> <div sID="gen26063" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10788"/>And summoning the crowd together with his disciples, he said to them, “If anyone wants to come<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “to follow”</note> after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross and follow me.

verses.name: Mark 8:35
verses.text: For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life on account of me and of the gospel will save it.

verses.name: Mark 8:36
verses.text: For what does it benefit a person to gain the whole world and forfeit his life?

verses.name: Mark 8:37
verses.text: For what can a person give in exchange for his life?

verses.name: Mark 8:38
verses.text: For whoever is ashamed of me and my words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man will also be ashamed of him when he comes in the glory of his Father with the holy angels.”  <chapter eID="Mark.8"/> <div eID="gen26063" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 9:1
verses.text: And he said to them, “Truly I say to you, that there are some of those standing here who will never experience death until they see the kingdom of God having come with power.”  <div eID="gen26064" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 9:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10789"/><title type="x-s">The Transfiguration</title> <div sID="gen26065" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10789"/>And after six days, Jesus took along Peter and James and John, and led them to a high mountain by themselves alone. And he was transfigured before them,

verses.name: Mark 9:3
verses.text: and his clothing became radiant—extremely white, like no cloth refiner on earth can <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞make so white⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “make white like this”</note>

verses.name: Mark 9:4
verses.text: And Elijah appeared to them together with Moses, and they were talking with Jesus.

verses.name: Mark 9:5
verses.text: And Peter answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to Jesus, “Rabbi, it is good <transChange type="added">that</transChange> we are here! And let us make three shelters, one for you and one for Moses and one for Elijah.”

verses.name: Mark 9:6
verses.text: (For he did not know what he should answer, because they were terrified.)

verses.name: Mark 9:7
verses.text: And a cloud came, overshadowing them, and a voice came from the cloud, “This is my beloved Son. Listen to him!”

verses.name: Mark 9:8
verses.text: And suddenly, looking around, they no longer saw anyone with them but Jesus alone.  <div eID="gen26065" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 9:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10790"/><div sID="gen26066" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10790"/>And <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“were coming down”)</note> they were coming down from the mountain, he ordered them that they should tell no one <transChange type="added">the things</transChange> that they had seen, except when the Son of Man had risen from the dead.

verses.name: Mark 9:10
verses.text: And they kept the matter to themselves, discussing what this rising from the dead <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞meant⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “is”</note>

verses.name: Mark 9:11
verses.text: And they asked him, saying, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Why do⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “what is it that”</note> the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”

verses.name: Mark 9:12
verses.text: And he said to them, “Elijah indeed does come first <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“does come”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> restores all <transChange type="added">things</transChange>. And how is it written concerning the Son of Man that he should suffer many <transChange type="added">things</transChange> and be treated with contempt?

verses.name: Mark 9:13
verses.text: But I tell you that indeed Elijah has come, and they did to him whatever they wanted, just as it is written about him.”  <div eID="gen26066" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 9:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10791"/><title type="x-s">A Demon-possessed Boy Healed</title> <div sID="gen26067" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10791"/>And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“came”) which is understood as temporal</note> came to the disciples, they saw a large crowd around them and scribes arguing with them.

verses.name: Mark 9:15
verses.text: And immediately the whole crowd, <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw him, were amazed, and ran up to him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“ran up to”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> greeted him.

verses.name: Mark 9:16
verses.text: And he asked them, “What are you arguing <transChange type="added">about</transChange> with them?”

verses.name: Mark 9:17
verses.text: And one <transChange type="added">individual</transChange> from the crowd answered him, “Teacher, I brought to you my son who has <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a spirit that makes him mute⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “a mute spirit”</note>

verses.name: Mark 9:18
verses.text: And whenever it seizes him, it throws him down and he foams at the mouth and grinds his<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> teeth and becomes paralyzed. And I told your disciples that they should expel it, and they were not able to do so.<note placement="foot">*The words “to do so” are not in the Greek text but are implied</note>

verses.name: Mark 9:19
verses.text: And he answered them <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “O unbelieving generation! <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞How long⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “until when”</note> will I be with you? <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞How long⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “until when”</note> must I put up with you? Bring him to me!”

verses.name: Mark 9:20
verses.text: And they brought him to him. And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw him, the spirit immediately convulsed him, and falling on the ground, he began to roll around, foaming at the mouth.

verses.name: Mark 9:21
verses.text: And he asked his father how long it was since this had been happening to him. And he said, “From childhood.

verses.name: Mark 9:22
verses.text: And often it has thrown him both into fire and into water, in order that it could destroy him. But if you are able <transChange type="added">to do</transChange> anything, have compassion on us <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied and the following participle (“have compassion”) has been translated as a finite verb and placed before the verb “help” in keeping with English style</note> help us!”

verses.name: Mark 9:23
verses.text: But Jesus said to him, “If you are able! All <transChange type="added">things</transChange> <transChange type="added">are</transChange> possible for the one who believes!”

verses.name: Mark 9:24
verses.text: Immediately the father of the child cried out <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“cried out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “I believe! Help my unbelief!”

verses.name: Mark 9:25
verses.text: Now <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> Jesus saw that a crowd was running together, he rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to it, “Mute and deaf spirit, I command you, come out of him, and enter into him no more!”

verses.name: Mark 9:26
verses.text: And it came out, screaming and convulsing <transChange type="added">him</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> greatly, and he became as if <transChange type="added">he were</transChange> dead, so that most <transChange type="added">of them</transChange> said, “He has died!”

verses.name: Mark 9:27
verses.text: But Jesus took hold of his hand <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took hold of”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> raised him up, and he stood up.

verses.name: Mark 9:28
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“had entered”)</note> he had entered into the house, his disciples asked him privately, “Why were we not able to expel it?”

verses.name: Mark 9:29
verses.text: And he said to them, “This kind can come out by nothing except by prayer.”<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts add “and fasting”</note>  <div eID="gen26067" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 9:30
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10792"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Predicts His Death and Resurrection a Second Time</title> <div sID="gen26068" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10792"/>And from there they went out <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> passed through Galilee. And he did not want anyone to know,

verses.name: Mark 9:31
verses.text: for he was teaching his disciples and was telling them, “The Son of Man is being betrayed into the hands of men, and they will kill him. And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“is killed”) which is understood as temporal</note> is killed, after three days he will rise.”

verses.name: Mark 9:32
verses.text: But they did not understand the statement, and they were afraid to ask him.  <div eID="gen26068" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 9:33
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10793"/><title type="x-s">The Question About Who Is Greatest</title> <div sID="gen26069" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10793"/>And they came to Capernaum. And <transChange type="added">after he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was”) which is understood as temporal</note> was in the house, he asked them, “What were you discussing on the way?”

verses.name: Mark 9:34
verses.text: But they were silent, because they had argued with one another on the way <transChange type="added">about</transChange> who <transChange type="added">was</transChange> greatest.

verses.name: Mark 9:35
verses.text: And he sat down <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“sat down”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> called the twelve and said to them, “If anyone wants to be first, he will be last of all and servant of all.”

verses.name: Mark 9:36
verses.text: And he took a young child <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> had him stand <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞among them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “in the midst of them”</note> And taking him in his arms, he said to them,

verses.name: Mark 9:37
verses.text: “Whoever welcomes one of the young children such as these in my name welcomes me, and whoever welcomes me does not welcome me, but the one who sent me.”  <div eID="gen26069" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 9:38
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10794"/><title type="x-s">Whoever Is Not Against Us Is for Us</title> <div sID="gen26070" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10794"/>John said to him, “Teacher, we saw someone expelling demons in your name, and we tried to prevent him because he was not following us.”

verses.name: Mark 9:39
verses.text: But Jesus said, “Do not prevent him, because there is no one who does a miracle in my name and will be able soon afterward to speak evil of me.

verses.name: Mark 9:40
verses.text: For whoever is not against us is for us.

verses.name: Mark 9:41
verses.text: For whoever gives you a cup of water to drink in <transChange type="added">my</transChange> name because you are Christ’s, truly I say to you that he will never lose his reward.  <div eID="gen26070" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 9:42
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10795"/><title type="x-s">Temptations to Sin</title> <div sID="gen26071" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10795"/>“And whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to sin, it is better for him if instead <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a large millstone⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a millstone of a donkey”</note> is placed around his neck and he is thrown into the sea.

verses.name: Mark 9:43
verses.text: And if your hand causes you to sin, cut it off! It is better <transChange type="added">for</transChange> you to enter into life crippled than, having two hands, to go into hell—into the unquenchable fire!<note placement="foot">Most later Greek manuscripts add v. <reference osisRef="Mark.9.44">44</reference> after v. <reference osisRef="Mark.9.43">43</reference>, “where their worm does not die and the fire is not extinguished” (identical to v. <reference osisRef="Mark.9.48">48</reference>)</note>

verses.name: Mark 9:45
verses.text: And if your foot causes you to sin, cut it off! It is better <transChange type="added">for</transChange> you to enter into life lame than, having two feet, to be thrown into hell!<note placement="foot">Most later Greek manuscripts add v. <reference osisRef="Mark.9.46">46</reference> after v. <reference osisRef="Mark.9.45">45</reference>, “where their worm does not die and the fire is not extinguished” (identical to v. <reference osisRef="Mark.9.48">48</reference>)</note>

verses.name: Mark 9:47
verses.text: And if your eye causes you to sin, tear it out! It is better <transChange type="added">for</transChange> you to enter into the kingdom of God with one eye than, having two eyes, to be thrown into hell,

verses.name: Mark 9:48
verses.text: ‘where their worm does not die and the fire is not extinguished.’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.66.24">Isa 66:24</reference></note>

verses.name: Mark 9:49
verses.text: For everyone will be salted with fire.

verses.name: Mark 9:50
verses.text: Salt <transChange type="added">is</transChange> good, but if the salt becomes deprived of its salt content, by what can you make it salty? Have salt among yourselves, and be at peace with one another.”  <chapter eID="Mark.9"/>

verses.name: Mark 10:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10796"/><title type="x-s">On Divorce</title> <div sID="gen26072" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10796"/>And from there he set out <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“set out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> came to the region of Judea and the other side of the Jordan, and again crowds came together to him. And again, as he was accustomed to do,<note placement="foot">*The words “to do” are not in the Greek text but are implied</note> he began to teach<note placement="foot">The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to teach”)</note> them.

verses.name: Mark 10:2
verses.text: And they asked<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “And Pharisees came up and asked”</note> him if it was permitted for a man to divorce his<note placement="foot">The pronoun “his” is not in the Greek text but is implied</note> wife, in order to<note placement="foot">*Here “in order to” is supplied as a component of the participle (“test”) which is understood as purpose</note> test him.

verses.name: Mark 10:3
verses.text: And he answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to them, “What did Moses command you?”

verses.name: Mark 10:4
verses.text: So they said, “Moses permitted <transChange type="added">a man</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to write a certificate of divorce and to send her<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> away.”

verses.name: Mark 10:5
verses.text: But Jesus said to them, “He wrote this commandment for you because of your hardness of heart.

verses.name: Mark 10:6
verses.text: But from the beginning of creation ‘he made them male and female.<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Gen.1.27">Gen 1:27</reference>; <reference osisRef="Gen.5.2">5:2</reference></note>

verses.name: Mark 10:7
verses.text: Because of this a man will leave his father and mother and will be joined to his wife,<note placement="foot">The earliest and most important manuscripts do not contain the phrase “and be joined to his wife”</note>

verses.name: Mark 10:8
verses.text: and the two will become one flesh,’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Gen.2.24">Gen 2:24</reference></note> so that they are no longer two but one flesh.

verses.name: Mark 10:9
verses.text: Therefore what God has joined together, man must not separate.”  <div eID="gen26072" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 10:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10797"/><div sID="gen26073" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10797"/>And in the house again the disciples began to ask<note placement="foot">The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to ask”)</note> him about this.

verses.name: Mark 10:11
verses.text: And he said to them, “Whoever divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery against her.

verses.name: Mark 10:12
verses.text: And if she divorces her husband <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“divorces”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> marries another, she commits adultery.”  <div eID="gen26073" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 10:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10798"/><title type="x-s">Little Children Brought to Jesus</title> <div sID="gen26074" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10798"/>And they were bringing young children to him so that he could touch them, but the disciples rebuked them.

verses.name: Mark 10:14
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> Jesus saw it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> he was indignant, and said to them, “Let the young children come to me. Do not forbid them, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞for to such belongs⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for of such is”</note> the kingdom of God.

verses.name: Mark 10:15
verses.text: Truly I say to you, whoever does not welcome the kingdom of God like a young child will never enter into it.”

verses.name: Mark 10:16
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“taking … into his arms”) which is understood as temporal</note> taking them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> into his arms, he blessed them, placing his<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> hands on them.  <div eID="gen26074" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 10:17
