verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10799"/><title type="x-s">A Rich Young Man</title> <div sID="gen26075" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10799"/>And <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was setting out”)</note> he was setting out on his way, one individual ran up and knelt down before him and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the two previous participles (“ran up” and “knelt down before”) have been translated as finite verbs</note> asked him, “Good Teacher, what must I do so that I will inherit eternal life?”

verses.name: Mark 10:18
verses.text: So Jesus said to him, “Why do you call me good? No one <transChange type="added">is</transChange> good except God alone.

verses.name: Mark 10:19
verses.text: You know the commandments: ‘Do not murder, do not commit adultery, do not steal, do not give false testimony, do not defraud, honor your father and mother.’ ”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Exod.20.12-Exod.20.16">Exod 20:12–16</reference>; <reference osisRef="Deut.5.16-Deut.5.20">Deut 5:16–20</reference>, except for “do not defraud” which is an allusion to <reference osisRef="Deut.24.14">Deut 24:14</reference></note>

verses.name: Mark 10:20
verses.text: And he said to him, “Teacher, all these I have observed from my youth.”

verses.name: Mark 10:21
verses.text: And Jesus, looking at him, loved him, and said to him, “You lack one <transChange type="added">thing</transChange>: Go, sell all that you have, and give <transChange type="added">the proceeds</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to the poor—and you will have treasure in heaven—and come, follow me.”

verses.name: Mark 10:22
verses.text: But he looked gloomy at the statement <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“looked gloomy”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> went away sorrowful, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞because he had⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “because he was having”</note> many possessions.  <div eID="gen26075" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 10:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10800"/><div sID="gen26076" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10800"/>And Jesus looked around <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“looked around”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to his disciples, “How <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞difficult it is for⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “with difficulty”</note> those who possess wealth to enter into the kingdom of God!”

verses.name: Mark 10:24
verses.text: And the disciples were astounded at his words. But Jesus answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to them again, “Children, how difficult it is to enter into the kingdom of God!

verses.name: Mark 10:25
verses.text: It is easier <transChange type="added">for</transChange> a camel to go through the eye of a needle than <transChange type="added">for</transChange> a rich person to enter into the kingdom of God.”

verses.name: Mark 10:26
verses.text: And they were very astounded, saying to one another, “And who can be saved?”

verses.name: Mark 10:27
verses.text: Jesus looked at them <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“looked at”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “With human beings <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> impossible, but not with God. For all <transChange type="added">things</transChange> <transChange type="added">are</transChange> possible with God.”

verses.name: Mark 10:28
verses.text: Peter began to say to him, “Behold, we have left everything and followed you.”

verses.name: Mark 10:29
verses.text: Jesus said, “Truly I say to you, there is no one who has left house or brothers or sisters or mother or father or children or fields on account of me and on account of the gospel

verses.name: Mark 10:30
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who will not⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “unless he will not”</note> receive a hundred times as much now in this time—houses and brothers and sisters and mothers and children and fields, together with persecutions—and in the age to come, eternal life.

verses.name: Mark 10:31
verses.text: But many <transChange type="added">who are</transChange> first will be last, and the last first.”  <div eID="gen26076" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 10:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10801"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Predicts His Death and Resurrection a Third Time</title> <div sID="gen26077" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10801"/>Now they were on the road going up to Jerusalem, and Jesus was going on ahead of them. And they were astounded, but those who were following <transChange type="added">him</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> were afraid. And taking aside the twelve again, he began to tell them the things that were about to happen to him:

verses.name: Mark 10:33
verses.text: “Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes, and they will condemn him to death and will hand him over to the Gentiles.

verses.name: Mark 10:34
verses.text: And they will mock him and spit on him and flog him and kill <transChange type="added">him</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and after three days he will rise.”  <div eID="gen26077" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 10:35
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10802"/><title type="x-s">A Request by James and John</title> <div sID="gen26078" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10802"/>And James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came up to him <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the participle (“said”) has been translated as a finite verb in keeping with English style</note> said to him, “Teacher, we want you to do for us whatever we ask you.”

verses.name: Mark 10:36
verses.text: And he said to them, “What do you want that I do<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “do you want me to do”</note> for you?”

verses.name: Mark 10:37
verses.text: So they said to him, “Grant to us that we may sit one at your right hand and one at <transChange type="added">your</transChange> left in your glory.”

verses.name: Mark 10:38
verses.text: But Jesus said to them, “You do not know what you are asking! Are you able to drink the cup that I drink, or to be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with?”

verses.name: Mark 10:39
verses.text: And they said to him, “We are able.” So Jesus said to them, “You will drink the cup that I drink, and you will be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with,

verses.name: Mark 10:40
verses.text: but to sit at my right hand or at <transChange type="added">my</transChange> left is not mine to grant, but <transChange type="added">is</transChange> for those for whom it has been prepared.”

verses.name: Mark 10:41
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard this,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> the ten began to be indignant about James and John.

verses.name: Mark 10:42
verses.text: And Jesus called them to himself <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“called … to himself”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to them, “You know that those who are considered to rule over the Gentiles lord it over them, and their <transChange type="added">people</transChange> in high positions exercise authority over them.

verses.name: Mark 10:43
verses.text: But it is not like this among you! But whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant,

verses.name: Mark 10:44
verses.text: and whoever wants to be most prominent among you must be the slave of all.

verses.name: Mark 10:45
verses.text: For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life <transChange type="added">as</transChange> a ransom for many.”  <div eID="gen26078" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 10:46
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10803"/><title type="x-s">A Blind Man Healed at Jericho</title> <div sID="gen26079" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10803"/>And they came to Jericho. And <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was setting out”)</note> he was setting out from Jericho along with his disciples and a large crowd, a blind beggar, Bartimaeus the son of Timaeus, was sitting beside the road.

verses.name: Mark 10:47
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard that it was Jesus the Nazarene, he began to cry out and say, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”

verses.name: Mark 10:48
verses.text: And many <transChange type="added">people</transChange> warned him that he should be quiet. But he was crying out <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞even more loudly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “by much more”</note> “Son of David, have mercy on me!”

verses.name: Mark 10:49
verses.text: And Jesus stopped <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“stopped”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “Call him.” And they called the blind man and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“called”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to him, “Have courage! Get up! He is calling you.”

verses.name: Mark 10:50
verses.text: And he threw off his cloak, jumped up, <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the two previous participles (“threw off” and “jumped up”) have been translated as finite verbs</note> came to Jesus.

verses.name: Mark 10:51
verses.text: And Jesus answered him <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “What do you want <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞me to do⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “that I do”</note> for you?” And the blind man said to him, “<hi type="italic">Rabboni</hi>,<note placement="foot">The Aramaic term is an elevated form of Rabbi</note> that I may regain <transChange type="added">my</transChange> sight.”

verses.name: Mark 10:52
verses.text: And Jesus said to him, “Go, your faith has healed you.” And immediately he regained <transChange type="added">his</transChange> sight and began to follow<note placement="foot">The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to follow”)</note> him on the road.  <chapter eID="Mark.10"/>

verses.name: Mark 11:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10804"/><title type="x-s">The Triumphal Entry</title> <div sID="gen26080" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10804"/>And when they came near to Jerusalem, to Bethphage and Bethany at the Mount of Olives, he sent two of his disciples

verses.name: Mark 11:2
verses.text: and said to them, “Go into the village before you, and right away <transChange type="added">as you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“enter”) which is understood as temporal</note> enter into it you will find a colt tied, on which no one has ever sat. Untie it and bring it.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Mark 11:3
verses.text: And if anyone says to you, ‘Why are you doing this?’ say<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts omit “that” after “say” here; though understood to be present in the underlying Greek text, it introduces direct discourse here and is left untranslated, functioning much like English quotation marks</note> ‘The Lord has need of it, and will send it here again at once.’ ”

verses.name: Mark 11:4
verses.text: And they went away and found a colt tied at a door outside in the street, and they untied it.

verses.name: Mark 11:5
verses.text: And some of those who were standing there said to them, “What are you doing, untying the colt?”

verses.name: Mark 11:6
verses.text: So they told them, just as Jesus had said, and they allowed them <transChange type="added">to take it</transChange>.<note placement="foot">The phrase “to take it” is not in the Greek text, but is implied</note>

verses.name: Mark 11:7
verses.text: And they brought the colt to Jesus and threw their cloaks over it, and he sat on it.

verses.name: Mark 11:8
verses.text: And many <transChange type="added">people</transChange> spread their cloaks on the road, and others <transChange type="added">spread</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the verb “spread” is an understood repetition of the verb earlier in this verse</note> leafy branches they<note placement="foot">*Here the participle “had cut” has been translated as a finite verb; it agrees in number, gender, and case with “others,” so “they’ has been supplied to indicate this</note> had cut from the fields.

verses.name: Mark 11:9
verses.text: And those who went ahead and those who were following were shouting, <div eID="gen26080" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen26081"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26082"/>“Hosanna!<l eID="gen26082" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26083"/>Blessed <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the one who comes in the name of the Lord!<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.118.25-Ps.118.26">Ps 118:25–26</reference></note> <l eID="gen26083" level="1"/>

verses.name: Mark 11:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10805"/><l level="1" sID="gen26084"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10805"/>Blessed <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the coming kingdom of our father David!<l eID="gen26084" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26085"/>Hosanna in the highest <transChange type="added">heaven</transChange>!”<note placement="foot">*Here “heaven” is understood</note> <l eID="gen26085" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen26081"/>

verses.name: Mark 11:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10806"/><div sID="gen26086" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10806"/>And he went into Jerusalem to the temple, and <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“looking around”) which is understood as temporal</note> looking around at everything, because<note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was”) which is understood as causal</note> the hour was already late, he went out to Bethany with the twelve.  <div eID="gen26086" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 11:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10807"/><title type="x-s">A Barren Fig Tree Cursed</title> <div sID="gen26087" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10807"/>And on the next day <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“were departing”)</note> they were departing from Bethany, he was hungry.

verses.name: Mark 11:13
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw from a distance a fig tree that had leaves, he went to see if perhaps he would find anything on it. And when he<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“came up”) which is understood as temporal</note> came up to it he found nothing except leaves, because it was not the season for figs.

verses.name: Mark 11:14
verses.text: And he responded <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“responded”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to it, “Let no one eat fruit from you any more <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!”<note placement="foot">Literally “for the age”</note> And his disciples heard it.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>  <div eID="gen26087" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 11:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10808"/><title type="x-s">The Cleansing of the Temple</title> <div sID="gen26088" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10808"/>And they came to Jerusalem. And he entered into the temple <transChange type="added">courts</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“entered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> began to drive out those who were selling and those who were buying in the temple courts,<note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> and overturned the tables of the money changers and the chairs of those who were selling doves.

verses.name: Mark 11:16
verses.text: And he did not permit anyone to carry objects<note placement="foot">Or “merchandise”</note> through the temple courts.<note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note>

verses.name: Mark 11:17
verses.text: And he began to teach<note placement="foot">The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to teach”)</note> and was saying to them, “Is it not written, <div eID="gen26088" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen26089"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26090"/>‘My house will be called a house of prayer<l eID="gen26090" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26091"/>for all the nations,’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.56.7">Isa 56:7</reference></note><l eID="gen26091" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen26089"/> <div sID="gen26092" type="x-p"/> but you have made it a cave of robbers!”

verses.name: Mark 11:18
verses.text: And the chief priests and the scribes heard <transChange type="added">it</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and began considering<note placement="foot">The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began considering”)</note> how they could destroy him. For they were afraid of him because the whole crowd was astounded by his teaching.

verses.name: Mark 11:19
verses.text: And when evening came they went out of the city.  <div eID="gen26092" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 11:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10809"/><title type="x-s">The Barren Fig Tree Withered</title> <div sID="gen26093" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10809"/>And <transChange type="added">as they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“passed by”) which is understood as temporal</note> passed by early in the morning, they saw the fig tree withered from the roots.

verses.name: Mark 11:21
verses.text: And Peter remembered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“remembered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to him, “Rabbi, look! The fig tree that you cursed has withered!”

verses.name: Mark 11:22
verses.text: And Jesus answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to them, “Have faith in God!

verses.name: Mark 11:23
verses.text: Truly I say to you that whoever says to this mountain, ‘Be lifted up and thrown into the sea!’ and does not doubt in his heart, but believes that what he says will happen, it will be <transChange type="added">done</transChange> for him.

verses.name: Mark 11:24
verses.text: For this <transChange type="added">reason</transChange> I say to you, whatever you pray and ask for, believe that you have received <transChange type="added">it</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and it will be <transChange type="added">done</transChange> for you.

verses.name: Mark 11:25
verses.text: And whenever you stand praying, if you have anything against anyone, forgive <transChange type="added">him</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> so that your Father who is in heaven will also forgive you your sins.”<note placement="foot">Most later Greek manuscripts add v. <reference osisRef="Mark.11.26">26</reference> after v. <reference osisRef="Mark.11.25">25</reference>, “But if you do not forgive, neither will your Father in heaven forgive your sins”</note>  <div eID="gen26093" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 11:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10810"/><title type="x-s">Jesus’ Authority Challenged</title> <div sID="gen26094" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10810"/>And they came again to Jerusalem. And <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was walking”)</note> he was walking in the temple courts,<note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> the chief priests and the scribes and the elders came up to him

verses.name: Mark 11:28
verses.text: and said to him, “By what authority are you doing these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, or who gave you this authority that you do these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>?”

verses.name: Mark 11:29
verses.text: So Jesus said to them, “I will ask you one question. Answer me and I will tell you by what authority I am doing these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>.

verses.name: Mark 11:30
verses.text: The baptism of John—was <transChange type="added">it</transChange> from heaven or from men? Answer me!”

verses.name: Mark 11:31
verses.text: And they began to discuss<note placement="foot">The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to discuss”)</note> this<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> with one another, saying, “What should we say?<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts omit “What should we say?”</note> If we say ‘From heaven,’ he will say, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’

verses.name: Mark 11:32
verses.text: But if we say, ‘From men’ ”—they were afraid of the crowd, because they all looked upon John <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as truly a prophet⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “that he was truly a prophet”</note>

verses.name: Mark 11:33
verses.text: And they replied to Jesus saying, “We do not know.” And Jesus said to them, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I am doing these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>.”  <chapter eID="Mark.11"/>

verses.name: Mark 12:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10811"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Tenant Farmers in the Vineyard</title> <div sID="gen26095" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10811"/>And he began to speak to them in parables: “A man planted a vineyard, and put a fence <transChange type="added">around it</transChange>, and dug a trough for the winepress, and built a watchtower, and leased it to tenant farmers, and went on a journey.

verses.name: Mark 12:2
verses.text: And he sent a slave to the tenant farmers at the proper time, so that he could collect <transChange type="added">some</transChange> of the fruit of the vineyard from the tenant farmers.

verses.name: Mark 12:3
verses.text: And they seized him <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“seized”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> beat him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and sent him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> away empty-handed.

verses.name: Mark 12:4
verses.text: And again he sent to them another slave, and that one they struck on the head and dishonored.

verses.name: Mark 12:5
verses.text: And he sent another, and that one they killed. And <transChange type="added">he sent</transChange><note placement="foot">*The words “he sent” are not in the Greek text, but are an implied repetition from earlier in the verse</note> many others, <transChange type="added">some</transChange> of whom they beat and <transChange type="added">some</transChange> of whom they killed.

verses.name: Mark 12:6
verses.text: He had one more, a beloved son. Last <transChange type="added">of all</transChange> he sent him to them, saying, ‘They will respect my son.’

verses.name: Mark 12:7
verses.text: But those tenant farmers said to one another, ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him and the inheritance will be ours!’

verses.name: Mark 12:8
verses.text: And they seized <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“seized”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> killed him and threw him out of the vineyard.

verses.name: Mark 12:9
verses.text: What<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “What then”</note> will the owner of the vineyard do? He will come and destroy the tenant farmers and give the vineyard to others.

verses.name: Mark 12:10
verses.text: Have you not read this scripture: <div eID="gen26095" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen26096"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26097"/>‘The stone which the builders rejected,<l eID="gen26097" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26098"/>this has become <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the cornerstone⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the head of the corner”</note> <l eID="gen26098" level="2"/>

verses.name: Mark 12:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10812"/><l level="1" sID="gen26099"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10812"/>This came about from the Lord,<l eID="gen26099" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26100"/>and it is marvelous in our eyes’?”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.118.22-Ps.118.23">Ps 118:22–23</reference></note> <l eID="gen26100" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen26096"/>

verses.name: Mark 12:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10813"/><div sID="gen26101" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10813"/>And they were seeking to arrest him, and they were afraid of the crowd, because they knew that he had told the parable with reference to them. And they left him <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“left”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> went away.  <div eID="gen26101" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 12:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10814"/><title type="x-s">Paying Taxes to Caesar</title> <div sID="gen26102" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10814"/>And they sent some of the Pharisees and the Herodians to him so that they could catch him unawares in a statement.

verses.name: Mark 12:14
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“came”) which is understood as temporal</note> came, they said to him, “Teacher, we know that you are truthful and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you do not care what anyone thinks⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “it is not a care to you concerning anyone”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞because you do not regard the opinion of people⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “because you do not look at the face of men”</note> but teach the way of God in truth. Is it permitted to pay taxes to Caesar or not? Should we pay or should we not pay?”

verses.name: Mark 12:15
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">because he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“knew”) which is understood as causal</note> knew their hypocrisy, he said to them, “Why are you testing me? Bring me a denarius so that I can look at it!”<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Mark 12:16
verses.text: So they brought <transChange type="added">one</transChange>.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> And he said to them, “Whose image and inscription <transChange type="added">is</transChange> this?” And they said to him, “Caesar’s.”

verses.name: Mark 12:17
verses.text: And Jesus said to them, “Give to Caesar the things of Caesar, and to God the things of God!” And they were utterly amazed at him.  <div eID="gen26102" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 12:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10815"/><title type="x-s">A Question About Marriage and the Resurrection</title> <div sID="gen26103" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10815"/>And Sadducees—who say there is no resurrection—came up to him and began to ask<note placement="foot">The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to ask”)</note> him, saying,

verses.name: Mark 12:19
verses.text: “Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if someone’s brother dies and he leaves behind a wife and does not leave a child, that his brother should take the wife and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞father⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “raise up”</note> descendants for his brother.

verses.name: Mark 12:20
verses.text: There were seven brothers, and the first took a wife. And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“died”) which is understood as temporal</note> died, he did not leave descendants.

verses.name: Mark 12:21
verses.text: And the second took her, and he died without leaving descendants. And the third likewise.

verses.name: Mark 12:22
verses.text: And the seven did not leave descendants. Last of all the woman also died.

verses.name: Mark 12:23
verses.text: In the resurrection, when they rise, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞whose⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “who of them”</note> wife will she be? For the seven had her <transChange type="added">as</transChange> wife.

verses.name: Mark 12:24
verses.text: Jesus said to them, “Are you not deceived because of this, <transChange type="added">because you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“know”) which is understood as causal</note> do not know the scriptures or the power of God?

verses.name: Mark 12:25
verses.text: For when they rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in heaven.

verses.name: Mark 12:26
verses.text: Now concerning the dead, that they are raised, have you not read in the book of Moses <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in the passage about the bush⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “at the bush”</note> how God spoke to him, saying, ‘I am the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob’?<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Exod.3.6">Exod 3:6</reference></note>

verses.name: Mark 12:27
verses.text: He is not God of the dead, but of the living. You are very much mistaken!”  <div eID="gen26103" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 12:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10816"/><title type="x-s">The Greatest Commandment</title> <div sID="gen26104" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10816"/>And one of the scribes came up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> heard them debating. When he<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw that he answered them well, he asked him, “Which commandment is the most important of all?”

verses.name: Mark 12:29
verses.text: Jesus answered, “The most important is, ‘Listen, Israel! The Lord our God, the Lord is one.

verses.name: Mark 12:30
verses.text: And you shall love the Lord your God from your whole heart and from your whole soul and from your whole mind and from your whole strength.’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Deut.6.4-Deut.6.5">Deut 6:4–5</reference>; <reference osisRef="Josh.22.5">Josh 22:5</reference></note>

verses.name: Mark 12:31
verses.text: The second <transChange type="added">is</transChange> this: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Lev.19.18">Lev 19:18</reference></note> There is no other commandment greater than these.”

verses.name: Mark 12:32
verses.text: And the scribe said to him, “That is true, Teacher. You have said <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞correctly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in accordance with truth”</note> that he is one and there is no other except him.

verses.name: Mark 12:33
verses.text: And to love him from your<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> whole heart and from your<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> whole understanding and from your<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> whole strength, and to love your<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> neighbor as yourself, is much more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.”

verses.name: Mark 12:34
verses.text: And Jesus, <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw that he had answered thoughtfully, said to him, “You are not far from the kingdom of God.” And no one dared to put a question to him any longer.  <div eID="gen26104" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 12:35
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10817"/><title type="x-s">David’s Son and Lord</title> <div sID="gen26105" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10817"/>And continuing, Jesus said <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the participle (“teaching”) which is understood as temporal</note> teaching in the temple courts,<note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> “How can the scribes say that the Christ is David’s son?

verses.name: Mark 12:36
verses.text: David himself said by the Holy Spirit, <div eID="gen26105" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen26106"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26107"/>‘The Lord said to my Lord,<l eID="gen26107" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26108"/>“Sit at my right hand,<l eID="gen26108" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26109"/>until I put your enemies<l eID="gen26109" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26110"/>under your feet.” ’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.110.1">Ps 110:1</reference></note> <l eID="gen26110" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen26106"/>

verses.name: Mark 12:37
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10818"/><div sID="gen26111" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10818"/>David himself calls him ‘Lord,’ and how is he his son?” And the large crowd was listening to him gladly.  <div eID="gen26111" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 12:38
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10819"/><title type="x-s">Warning to Beware of the Scribes</title> <div sID="gen26112" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10819"/>And in his teaching he said, “Beware of the scribes, who like walking around in long robes and greetings in the marketplaces

verses.name: Mark 12:39
verses.text: and the best seats in the synagogues and the places of honor at banquets,

verses.name: Mark 12:40
verses.text: who devour the houses of widows and pray lengthy <transChange type="added">prayers</transChange> for the sake of appearance. These will receive more severe condemnation!”  <div eID="gen26112" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 12:41
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10820"/><title type="x-s">A Poor Widow’s Offering</title> <div sID="gen26113" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10820"/>And he sat down opposite the contribution box <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“sat down”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> was observing how the crowd was putting coins into the contribution box. And many rich people were putting in many coins.<note placement="foot">Although often translated “large sums,” the plural here suggests large numbers of individual coins, which would make an impressive noise</note>

verses.name: Mark 12:42
verses.text: And one poor widow came <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> put in two small copper coins<note placement="foot">This coin was the <hi type="italic">lepton</hi>, worth 1/128 of a denarius</note> (that is, a penny).<note placement="foot">This coin was the <hi type="italic">quadrans</hi>, the smallest Roman coin, worth 2 <hi type="italic">lepta</hi></note>

verses.name: Mark 12:43
verses.text: And summoning his disciples, he said to them, “Truly I say to you that this poor widow put in more than all those who put <transChange type="added">offerings</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> into the contribution box.

verses.name: Mark 12:44
verses.text: For they all <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞contributed⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “put in”</note> out of their abundance, but she out of her poverty put in everything she had, her whole means of subsistence.”  <chapter eID="Mark.12"/>

verses.name: Mark 13:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10821"/><title type="x-s">The Destruction of the Temple Predicted</title> <div sID="gen26114" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10821"/>And <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was going out”)</note> he was going out of the temple courts,<note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> one of his disciples said to him, “Teacher, look! What great stones and what wonderful buildings!”

verses.name: Mark 13:2
verses.text: And Jesus said to him, “Do you see these great buildings? Not <transChange type="added">one</transChange> stone will be left here on <transChange type="added">another</transChange> stone that will not be thrown down!”  <div eID="gen26114" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 13:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10822"/><title type="x-s">Signs of the End of the Age</title> <div sID="gen26115" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10822"/>And <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was sitting”)</note> he was sitting on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter and James and John and Andrew asked him privately,

verses.name: Mark 13:4
verses.text: “Tell us, when will these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> happen, and what <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> the sign when all these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> are about to be accomplished?”

verses.name: Mark 13:5
verses.text: So Jesus began to say to them, “Watch out that no one deceives you!

verses.name: Mark 13:6
verses.text: Many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am <transChange type="added">he</transChange>,’ and they will deceive many.

verses.name: Mark 13:7
verses.text: And when you hear about wars and rumors of wars, do not be alarmed. This must happen, but the end <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not yet.

verses.name: Mark 13:8
verses.text: For nation will rise up against nation and kingdom against kingdom. There will be earthquakes in <transChange type="added">various</transChange> places. There will be famines. These <transChange type="added">things</transChange> <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the beginning of birth pains.  <div eID="gen26115" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 13:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10823"/><title type="x-s">Persecution of Disciples Predicted</title> <div sID="gen26116" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10823"/>“But you, watch out for yourselves! They will hand you over to councils and you will be beaten in the synagogues and will have to stand before governors and kings because of me, for a witness to them.

verses.name: Mark 13:10
verses.text: And the gospel must first be proclaimed to all the nations.<note placement="foot">Or “Gentiles”; the same Greek word can be translated “nations” or “Gentiles” depending on the context</note>

verses.name: Mark 13:11
verses.text: And when they arrest you <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the participle (“hand you over”) has been translated as a finite verb in keeping with English style</note> hand you over, do not be anxious beforehand what you should say, but whatever is given to you at that hour, say this. For you are not the ones who are speaking, but the Holy Spirit.

verses.name: Mark 13:12
verses.text: And brother will hand over brother to death, and a father <transChange type="added">his</transChange><note placement="foot">*The word “his” is not in the Greek text but is implied</note> child, and children will rise up against parents and have them put to death.

verses.name: Mark 13:13
verses.text: And you will be hated by all because of my name. But the one who endures to the end—this one will be saved.  <div eID="gen26116" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 13:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10824"/><title type="x-s">The Abomination of Desolation</title> <div sID="gen26117" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10824"/>“But when you see the abomination of desolation standing where it should not be” (let the one who reads understand), “then those in Judea must flee to the mountains!

verses.name: Mark 13:15
verses.text: The one<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “And the one”</note> who is on his<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> housetop must not come down or go inside to take anything out of his house,

verses.name: Mark 13:16
verses.text: and the one who is in the field must not turn back to pick up his cloak.

verses.name: Mark 13:17
verses.text: And woe to those <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who are pregnant⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “who have in the womb”</note> and to those who are nursing their babies<note placement="foot">*The words “their babies” are not in the Greek text but are supplied as a necessary clarification</note> in those days!

verses.name: Mark 13:18
verses.text: But pray that it will not happen in winter.

verses.name: Mark 13:19
verses.text: For <transChange type="added">in</transChange> those days there will be tribulation of such a kind as has not happened from the beginning of the creation that God created until now, and never will happen.

verses.name: Mark 13:20
verses.text: And if the Lord had not shortened the days, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞no human being would be saved⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “every flesh would not be saved”</note> But for the sake of the elect, whom he chose, he has shortened the days.  <div eID="gen26117" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 13:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10825"/><div sID="gen26118" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10825"/>“And at that time if anyone should say to you, “Behold, here <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the Christ,’ ‘Behold, there <transChange type="added">he is</transChange>,’ do not believe <transChange type="added">him</transChange>!<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Mark 13:22
verses.text: For false messiahs and false prophets will appear, and will produce signs and wonders in order to mislead, if possible, the elect.

verses.name: Mark 13:23
verses.text: But you, watch out! I have told you everything ahead of time!  <div eID="gen26118" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 13:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10826"/><title type="x-s">The Arrival of the Son of Man</title> <div sID="gen26119" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10826"/>“But in those days, after that tribulation, <div eID="gen26119" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen26120"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26121"/>‘the sun will be darkened<l eID="gen26121" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26122"/>and the moon will not give its light, <l eID="gen26122" level="2"/>

verses.name: Mark 13:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10827"/><l level="1" sID="gen26123"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10827"/>and the stars will be falling from heaven,<l eID="gen26123" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26124"/>and the powers in the heavens will be shaken.’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.13.10">Isa 13:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.34.4">34:4</reference></note> <l eID="gen26124" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen26120"/>

verses.name: Mark 13:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10828"/><div sID="gen26125" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10828"/>And then they will see the Son of Man arriving in the clouds with great power and glory.

verses.name: Mark 13:27
verses.text: And then he will send out the angels, and will gather the<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “his”</note> elect together from the four winds, from the end of the earth to the end of heaven.  <div eID="gen26125" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 13:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10829"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Fig Tree</title> <div sID="gen26126" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10829"/>“Now learn the parable from the fig tree: Whenever its branch has already become tender and puts forth its<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> leaves, you know that summer is near.

verses.name: Mark 13:29
verses.text: So also you, when you see these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> happening, know<note placement="foot">Or “you know”</note> that he is near, at the door.

verses.name: Mark 13:30
verses.text: Truly I say to you that this generation will never pass away until all these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> take place!

verses.name: Mark 13:31
verses.text: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will never pass away.  <div eID="gen26126" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 13:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10830"/><title type="x-s">The Unknown Day and Hour</title> <div sID="gen26127" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10830"/>“But concerning that day or hour no one knows—not even the angels in heaven nor the Son—except the Father.

verses.name: Mark 13:33
verses.text: Watch out! Be alert, because you do not know when the time is!

verses.name: Mark 13:34
verses.text: It is like a man away on a journey, who left his house and gave his slaves authority—to each one his work—and to the doorkeeper he gave orders that he should be on the alert.

verses.name: Mark 13:35
verses.text: Therefore be on the alert, for you do not know when the master of the house is coming—whether in the evening, or at midnight, or when the rooster crows, or early in the morning—

verses.name: Mark 13:36
verses.text: lest he arrive suddenly <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“arrive”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> find you sleeping.

verses.name: Mark 13:37
verses.text: And what I say to you, I say to everyone: Be on the alert!”  <chapter eID="Mark.13"/>

verses.name: Mark 14:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10831"/><title type="x-s">The Chief Priests and Scribes Plot to Kill Jesus</title> <div sID="gen26128" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10831"/>Now after two days it was the Passover and the feast of Unleavened Bread, and the chief priests and the scribes were seeking how, <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“arresting”) which is understood as temporal</note> arresting him by stealth, they could kill him.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Mark 14:2
verses.text: For they said, “Not at the feast, lest there be an uproar by the people.”  <div eID="gen26128" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 14:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10832"/><title type="x-s">Jesus’ Anointing at Bethany</title> <div sID="gen26129" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10832"/>And <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was”)</note> he was at Bethany in the house of Simon the leper, as<note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was reclining for a meal”)</note> he was reclining for a meal, a woman came holding an alabaster flask of very costly perfumed oil of genuine nard. After<note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“breaking”) which is understood as temporal</note> breaking the alabaster flask, she poured it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> out on his head.

verses.name: Mark 14:4
verses.text: But some were expressing indignation to one another:<note placement="foot">Or perhaps “within themselves”</note> “Why has there been this waste of perfumed oil?

verses.name: Mark 14:5
verses.text: For this perfumed oil could have been sold for more than three hundred denarii and given to the poor!” And they began to scold<note placement="foot">The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to scold”)</note> her.

verses.name: Mark 14:6
verses.text: But Jesus said, “Leave her alone. Why do you cause trouble for her? She has done a good deed to me.

verses.name: Mark 14:7
verses.text: For the poor you always have with you, and you can do good for them whenever you want, but you do not always have me.

verses.name: Mark 14:8
verses.text: She has done what she could; <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞she has anointed my body beforehand⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “she has anticipated to anoint my body”</note> for burial.

verses.name: Mark 14:9
verses.text: And truly I say to you, wherever the gospel is proclaimed in the whole world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her.  <div eID="gen26129" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 14:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10833"/><title type="x-s">Judas Arranges to Betray Jesus</title> <div sID="gen26130" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10833"/>And Judas Iscariot, who <transChange type="added">was</transChange> one of the twelve, went to the chief priests in order to betray him to them.

verses.name: Mark 14:11
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> they heard this,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> they were delighted, and promised to give him money. And he began seeking<note placement="foot">The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began seeking”)</note> how he could betray him conveniently.  <div eID="gen26130" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 14:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10834"/><title type="x-s">Jesus’ Final Passover with the Disciples</title> <div sID="gen26131" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10834"/>And on the first day of the feast of Unleavened Bread, when they sacrificed the Passover lamb, his disciples said to him, “Where do you want us to go <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“go”) has been translated as an English infinitive</note> prepare, so that you can eat the Passover?”

verses.name: Mark 14:13
verses.text: And he sent two of his disciples and said to them, “Go into the city and a man carrying a jar of water will meet you. Follow him,

verses.name: Mark 14:14
verses.text: and wherever he enters, say to the master of the house, ‘The Teacher says, “Where is my guest room where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?” ’

verses.name: Mark 14:15
verses.text: And he will show you a large upstairs room furnished<note placement="foot">Or perhaps “paved” or “panelled”</note> and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied in the translation because of English style</note> ready, and prepare for us there.”

verses.name: Mark 14:16
verses.text: And the disciples went out and came into the city and found <transChange type="added">everything</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> just as he had told them, and they prepared the Passover.  <div eID="gen26131" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 14:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10835"/><div sID="gen26132" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10835"/>And <transChange type="added">when it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was”)</note> was evening, he arrived with the twelve.

verses.name: Mark 14:18
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“were reclining at table”)</note> they were reclining at table and eating, Jesus said, “Truly I say to you, that one of you who is eating with me will betray me.”

verses.name: Mark 14:19
verses.text: They began to be distressed and to say to him one by one, “Surely not I?”<note placement="foot">The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here</note>

verses.name: Mark 14:20
verses.text: But he said to them, “<transChange type="added">It is</transChange> one of the twelve—the one who is dipping <transChange type="added">bread</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> into the bowl with me.

verses.name: Mark 14:21
verses.text: For the Son of Man is going just as it is written about him, but woe to that man by whom the Son of Man is betrayed! <transChange type="added">It would be</transChange> better for him if that man had not been born.”  <div eID="gen26132" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 14:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10836"/><title type="x-s">The Lord’s Supper</title> <div sID="gen26133" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10836"/>And <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“were eating”)</note> they were eating, he took bread and,<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied in the translation because of English style</note> after<note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“giving thanks”) which is understood as temporal</note> giving thanks, he broke it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and gave it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to them and said, “Take it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> this is my body.”

verses.name: Mark 14:23
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“taking”) which is understood as temporal</note> taking the cup and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied in the translation because of English style</note> giving thanks, he gave it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to them, and they all drank from it.

verses.name: Mark 14:24
verses.text: And he said to them, “This is my blood of the covenant which is poured out for many.

verses.name: Mark 14:25
verses.text: Truly I say to you that I will never drink of the fruit of the vine any longer until that day when I drink it new in the kingdom of God.”

verses.name: Mark 14:26
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had sung the hymn”) which is understood as temporal</note> had sung the hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.  <div eID="gen26133" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 14:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10837"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Predicts Peter’s Denial</title> <div sID="gen26134" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10837"/>And Jesus said to them, “You will all fall away, because it is written, <div eID="gen26134" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen26135"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26136"/>‘I will strike the shepherd<l eID="gen26136" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26137"/>and the sheep will be scattered.’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Zech.13.7">Zech 13:7</reference></note> <l eID="gen26137" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen26135"/>

verses.name: Mark 14:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10838"/><div sID="gen26138" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10838"/>But after I am raised, I will go ahead of you into Galilee.”

verses.name: Mark 14:29
verses.text: But Peter said to him, “Even if they all fall away, certainly I will not!”

verses.name: Mark 14:30
verses.text: And Jesus said to him, “Truly I say to you that today—this night—before the rooster crows twice, you will deny me three times!”

verses.name: Mark 14:31
verses.text: But he kept saying emphatically, “If it is necessary for me to die with you, I will never deny you!” And they all were saying the same <transChange type="added">thing</transChange> also.  <div eID="gen26138" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 14:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10839"/><title type="x-s">The Prayer in Gethsemane</title> <div sID="gen26139" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10839"/>And they came to a place <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞named⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the name of which”</note> Gethsemane, and he said to his disciples, “Sit here while I pray.”

verses.name: Mark 14:33
verses.text: And he took along Peter and James and John with him, and he began to be distressed and troubled.

verses.name: Mark 14:34
verses.text: And he said to them, “My soul is deeply grieved, to the point of death. Remain here and stay awake.”

verses.name: Mark 14:35
verses.text: And going forward a little he fell to the ground and began to pray<note placement="foot">The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to pray”)</note> that, if it were possible, the hour would pass from him.

verses.name: Mark 14:36
verses.text: And he said, “Abba,<note placement="foot">The word “Abba” means “father” in Aramaic</note> Father, all things are possible for you! Take away this cup from me! Yet not what I will, but what you will.”<note placement="foot">*Here the verb “will” is an understood repetition of the verb earlier in this verse</note>

verses.name: Mark 14:37
verses.text: And he came and found them sleeping, and he said to Peter, “Simon, are you sleeping? Were you not able to stay awake one hour?

verses.name: Mark 14:38
verses.text: Stay awake and pray that you will not enter into temptation. The spirit <transChange type="added">is</transChange> willing, but the flesh <transChange type="added">is</transChange> weak!”

verses.name: Mark 14:39
verses.text: And again he went away <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went away”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> prayed, saying the same thing.

verses.name: Mark 14:40
verses.text: And again he came <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> found them sleeping, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞for they could not keep their eyes open⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “for their eyes were weighed down”</note> and they did not know what to reply to him.

verses.name: Mark 14:41
verses.text: And he came the third <transChange type="added">time</transChange> and said to them, “Are you still sleeping and resting? It is enough! The hour has come. Behold, the Son of Man is being betrayed into the hands of sinners.

verses.name: Mark 14:42
verses.text: Get up, let us go! Behold, the one who is betraying me is approaching!”  <div eID="gen26139" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 14:43
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10840"/><title type="x-s">The Betrayal and Arrest of Jesus</title> <div sID="gen26140" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10840"/>And immediately, <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was … speaking”)</note> he was still speaking, Judas—one of the twelve—arrived, and with him a crowd with swords and clubs, from the chief priests and the scribes and the elders.

verses.name: Mark 14:44
verses.text: Now the one who was betraying him had given them a sign, saying, “<transChange type="added">The one</transChange> whom I kiss—he is <transChange type="added">the one</transChange>.<note placement="foot">*Here the predicate nominative (“the one”) is implied</note> Arrest him and lead him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> away under guard!”

verses.name: Mark 14:45
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“arrived”) which is understood as temporal</note> arrived, he came up to him immediately and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “Rabbi,” and kissed him.

verses.name: Mark 14:46
verses.text: So they laid hands on him and arrested him.  <div eID="gen26140" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 14:47
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10841"/><div sID="gen26141" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10841"/>But a certain one of the bystanders, drawing <transChange type="added">his</transChange><note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> sword, struck the slave of the high priest and cut off his ear.

verses.name: Mark 14:48
verses.text: And Jesus answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to them, “Have you come out with swords and clubs, as against a robber, to arrest me?

verses.name: Mark 14:49
verses.text: Every day I was with you in the temple <transChange type="added">courts</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> teaching, and you did not arrest me! But this has happened<note placement="foot">The phrase “this has happened” is not in the Greek text, but is understood and must be supplied in the translation because of English style; cf. the parallel in <reference osisRef="Matt.26.56">Matt 26:56</reference></note> in order that the scriptures would be fulfilled.

verses.name: Mark 14:50
verses.text: And they all abandoned him <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“abandoned”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> fled.  <div eID="gen26141" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 14:51
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10842"/><div sID="gen26142" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10842"/>And a certain young man was following him, clothed <transChange type="added">only</transChange> in a linen cloth on <transChange type="added">his</transChange> naked body. And they attempted to seize<note placement="foot">*Here the present tense is translated as a conative present (“attempted to”)</note> him,

verses.name: Mark 14:52
verses.text: but he left behind the linen cloth <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“left behind”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> fled naked.  <div eID="gen26142" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 14:53
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10843"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Before the Sanhedrin</title> <div sID="gen26143" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10843"/>And they led Jesus away to the high priest, and all the chief priests and the elders and the scribes came together.

verses.name: Mark 14:54
verses.text: And Peter followed him from a distance, right inside, into the courtyard of the high priest. And he was sitting with the officers and warming himself by the fire.

verses.name: Mark 14:55
verses.text: Now the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin were looking for testimony against Jesus in order to put him to death, and they did not find <transChange type="added">it</transChange>.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Mark 14:56
verses.text: For many gave false testimony against him, and their<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> testimony was not consistent.

verses.name: Mark 14:57
verses.text: And some stood up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“stood up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> began to give false testimony<note placement="foot">The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to give false testimony”)</note> against him, saying,

verses.name: Mark 14:58
verses.text: “We heard him saying, ‘I will destroy this temple made by hands, and within three days I will build another not made by hands.”

verses.name: Mark 14:59
verses.text: And their testimony was not even consistent about this.

verses.name: Mark 14:60
verses.text: And the high priest stood up in the midst <transChange type="added">of them</transChange> <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“stood up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> asked Jesus, saying, “Do you not reply anything? What are these <transChange type="added">people</transChange> testifying against you?”

verses.name: Mark 14:61
verses.text: But he was silent and did not reply anything. Again the high priest asked him and said to him, “Are you the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?”

verses.name: Mark 14:62
verses.text: And Jesus said, “I am, and you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of the Power<note placement="foot">An indirect way of referring to God</note> and coming with the clouds of heaven.”

verses.name: Mark 14:63
verses.text: And the high priest tore his clothes <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“tore”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “What further need do we have of witnesses?

verses.name: Mark 14:64
verses.text: You have heard the blasphemy! What <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞do you think⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?”<note placement="foot">Literally “does it seem to you”</note> And they all condemned him <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as deserving death⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “to be deserving of death”</note>

verses.name: Mark 14:65
verses.text: And some began to spit on him and to cover his face and to strike him with their fists, and to say to him “Prophesy!” And the officers received him with slaps in the face.<note placement="foot">Or “with blows” (either meaning is possible here)</note>  <div eID="gen26143" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 14:66
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10844"/><title type="x-s">Peter Denies Jesus Three Times</title> <div sID="gen26144" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10844"/>And <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was”)</note> Peter was below in the courtyard, one of the female slaves of the high priest came up

verses.name: Mark 14:67
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> she saw Peter warming himself, she looked intently at him and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“looked intently at”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “You also were with the Nazarene, Jesus.”

verses.name: Mark 14:68
verses.text: But he denied <transChange type="added">it</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> saying, “I neither know nor understand what you mean!” And he went out into the gateway, and a rooster crowed.<note placement="foot">Several important and early manuscripts lack the words “and a rooster crowed”</note>

verses.name: Mark 14:69
verses.text: And the female slave, <transChange type="added">when she</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw him, began to say again to the bystanders, “This man is one of them!”

verses.name: Mark 14:70
verses.text: But he denied <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> again. And after a little while, again the bystanders began to say<note placement="foot">The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to say”)</note> to Peter, “You really are one of them, because you also are a Galilean, and your accent <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞shows it⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!”<note placement="foot">Literally “is like”</note><note placement="foot">Some manuscripts omit “and your accent shows it”</note>

verses.name: Mark 14:71
verses.text: And he began to curse and to swear with an oath, “I do not know this man whom you are talking about!”

verses.name: Mark 14:72
verses.text: And immediately a rooster crowed for the second time. And Peter remembered the statement, how Jesus had said to him, “Before the rooster crows twice, you will deny me three times,” and throwing himself down, he began to weep.<note placement="foot">The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to weep”)</note>  <chapter eID="Mark.14"/>

verses.name: Mark 15:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10845"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Taken to Pilate</title> <div sID="gen26145" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10845"/>And as soon as morning <transChange type="added">came</transChange>, <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“formulating”) which is understood as temporal</note> formulating a plan, the chief priests, with the elders and scribes and the whole Sanhedrin, tied up Jesus, led him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> away, and handed him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> over to Pilate.

verses.name: Mark 15:2
verses.text: And Pilate asked him, “Are you the king of the Jews?” And he answered him <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “You say <transChange type="added">so</transChange>.”

verses.name: Mark 15:3
verses.text: And the chief priests began to accuse<note placement="foot">The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to accuse”)</note> him <transChange type="added">of</transChange> many <transChange type="added">things</transChange>.

verses.name: Mark 15:4
verses.text: So Pilate asked him again, saying, “Do you not answer anything? See how many <transChange type="added">charges</transChange><note placement="foot">*The word “charges” is not in the Greek text but is implied</note> they are bringing against you!”

verses.name: Mark 15:5
verses.text: But Jesus did not answer anything further, so that Pilate was astonished.  <div eID="gen26145" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 15:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10846"/><title type="x-s">Pilate Releases Barabbas</title> <div sID="gen26146" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10846"/>Now at each feast he customarily released<note placement="foot">The imperfect tense has been translated as customary here (“customarily released”)</note> for them one prisoner whom they requested.

verses.name: Mark 15:7
verses.text: And the one named Barabbas<note placement="foot">“Barabbas” means “son of the father” in Aramaic</note> was imprisoned with the rebels who had committed murder in the rebellion.

verses.name: Mark 15:8
verses.text: And the crowd came up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> began to ask him to do as he customarily did<note placement="foot">The imperfect tense has been translated as customary here (“customarily did”)</note> for them.

verses.name: Mark 15:9
verses.text: So Pilate answered them, saying, “Do you want me to release for you the king of the Jews?”

verses.name: Mark 15:10
verses.text: (For he realized that the chief priests had handed him over because of envy.)

verses.name: Mark 15:11
verses.text: But the chief priests incited the crowd so that he would release for them Barabbas<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> instead.

verses.name: Mark 15:12
