verses.text: So Pilate answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange> said to them again, “Then what do you want me to do with <transChange type="added">the one</transChange> whom you call the king of the Jews?”

verses.name: Mark 15:13
verses.text: And they shouted again, “Crucify him!”

verses.name: Mark 15:14
verses.text: And Pilate said to them, “Why? What evil has he done?” But they shouted even louder, “Crucify him!”  <div eID="gen26146" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 15:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10847"/><div sID="gen26147" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10847"/>So Pilate, <transChange type="added">because he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“wanted”) which is understood as causal</note> wanted <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to satisfy⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to make sufficient”</note> the crowd, released for them Barabbas. And after<note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“flogged”) which is understood as temporal</note> he had Jesus flogged, he handed him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> over so that he could be crucified.  <div eID="gen26147" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 15:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10848"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Is Mocked</title> <div sID="gen26148" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10848"/>So the soldiers led him away into the palace (that is, the governor’s residence) and called together the whole cohort.

verses.name: Mark 15:17
verses.text: And they put a purple cloak on him, and <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“weaving”) which is understood as temporal</note> weaving a crown of thorns they placed it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> on him.

verses.name: Mark 15:18
verses.text: And they began to greet him, “Hail, king of the Jews!”

verses.name: Mark 15:19
verses.text: And they repeatedly struck<note placement="foot">The imperfect tense has been translated as iterative here (“repeatedly struck”)</note> him on the head with a reed, and were spitting on him, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they knelt down⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “bending the knees”</note> and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“knelt down”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> did obeisance to him.

verses.name: Mark 15:20
verses.text: And when they had mocked him, they stripped him of the purple cloak and put his own clothes<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “his clothes” in place of “his own clothes”</note> on him, and they led him out so that they could crucify him.  <div eID="gen26148" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 15:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10849"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Is Crucified</title> <div sID="gen26149" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10849"/>And they forced a certain man who was passing by, Simon of Cyrene (the father of Alexander and Rufus), who was coming from the country, to carry his cross.

verses.name: Mark 15:22
verses.text: And they brought him to the place <hi type="italic">Golgotha</hi> (which is translated “Place of a Skull”).

verses.name: Mark 15:23
verses.text: And they attempted to give<note placement="foot">*Here the imperfect tense is translated as a conative imperfect (“attempted to give”)</note> him wine mixed with myrrh, but he did not take it.

verses.name: Mark 15:24
verses.text: And they crucified him and divided his clothes among themselves<note placement="foot">*Here “among themselves” reflects the middle voice of the verb “divided”</note> by<note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“casting”) which is understood as means</note> casting lots for them <transChange type="added">to see</transChange> who should take what.

verses.name: Mark 15:25
verses.text: Now it was the third hour when they crucified him.

verses.name: Mark 15:26
verses.text: And the inscription of the charge against him was written, “The king of the Jews.”

verses.name: Mark 15:27
verses.text: And with him they crucified two robbers, one on <transChange type="added">his</transChange> right and one on <transChange type="added">his</transChange> left.<note placement="foot">Most later Greek manuscripts add v. <reference osisRef="Mark.15.28">28</reference> (a quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.53.12">Isa 53:12</reference>) after v. <reference osisRef="Mark.15.27">27</reference>, “And the scripture was fulfilled that says, ‘And he was counted with the lawless ones’ ”</note>

verses.name: Mark 15:29
verses.text: And those who passed by reviled him, shaking their heads and saying, “Aha! The one who would destroy the temple and rebuild <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> in three days,

verses.name: Mark 15:30
verses.text: save yourself <transChange type="added">by</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“coming down”) which is understood as means</note> coming down from the cross!”

verses.name: Mark 15:31
verses.text: In the same way also the chief priests, along with the scribes, were mocking <transChange type="added">him</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to one another, saying, “He saved others; he is not able to save himself!

verses.name: Mark 15:32
verses.text: Let the Christ, the king of Israel, come down now from the cross, so that we may see and believe! Even those who were crucified with him were reviling him.  <div eID="gen26149" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 15:33
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10850"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Dies on the Cross</title> <div sID="gen26150" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10850"/>And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“came”)</note> the sixth hour came, darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour.

verses.name: Mark 15:34
verses.text: And at the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice, “<hi type="italic">Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?</hi>” (which is translated, “My God, my God, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞why⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for what reason”</note> have you forsaken me?”)<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.22.1">Ps 22:1</reference></note>

verses.name: Mark 15:35
verses.text: And some of the bystanders, <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> said, “Behold, he is summoning Elijah!”

verses.name: Mark 15:36
verses.text: And someone ran and filled a sponge with sour wine, put <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> on a reed, and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the two previous participles (“ran” and “filled”) have been translated as finite verbs</note> gave it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to him to drink, saying, “Leave him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> alone! Let us see if Elijah is coming to take him down.”

verses.name: Mark 15:37
verses.text: But Jesus uttered a loud cry <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“uttered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> expired.

verses.name: Mark 15:38
verses.text: And the curtain of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.

verses.name: Mark 15:39
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> the centurion who was standing opposite him saw that he expired like this, he said, “Truly this man was God’s Son!”

verses.name: Mark 15:40
verses.text: And there were also women observing from a distance, among whom <transChange type="added">were</transChange> Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James the younger<note placement="foot">Or perhaps “the short,” referring to stature</note> and Joses,<note placement="foot">This name appears in <reference osisRef="Matt.27.56">Matt 27:56 </reference>as “Joseph”</note> and Salome,

verses.name: Mark 15:41
verses.text: who used to follow<note placement="foot">The imperfect tense has been translated as customary here (“used to follow”)</note> him and serve him when he was in Galilee, and many other <transChange type="added">women</transChange> who went up with him to Jerusalem.  <div eID="gen26150" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 15:42
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10851"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Is Buried</title> <div sID="gen26151" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10851"/>And <transChange type="added">when it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was”)</note> was already evening, since it was the day of preparation (that is, the day before the Sabbath),

verses.name: Mark 15:43
verses.text: Joseph of Arimathea, a prominent member of the council who was also himself looking forward to<note placement="foot">Or “waiting for”</note> the kingdom of God, came acting courageously and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> went in to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.

verses.name: Mark 15:44
verses.text: And Pilate was surprised that he was already dead, and summoning the centurion, asked him whether he had died already.

verses.name: Mark 15:45
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“learned of”) which is understood as temporal</note> learned of it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> from the centurion, he granted the corpse to Joseph.

verses.name: Mark 15:46
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“purchasing”) which is understood as temporal</note> purchasing a linen cloth and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the participle (“taking...down”) has been translated as a finite verb in keeping with English style</note> taking him down, he wrapped him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> in the linen cloth and placed him in a tomb that had been cut from the rock. And he rolled a stone over the entrance of the tomb.

verses.name: Mark 15:47
verses.text: Now Mary Magdalene and Mary the <transChange type="added">mother</transChange> of Joses saw where he was placed.  <chapter eID="Mark.15"/>

verses.name: Mark 16:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10852"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Is Raised</title> <div sID="gen26152" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10852"/>And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was over”)</note> the Sabbath was over, Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James, and Salome purchased fragrant spices so that they could go and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“go”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> anoint him.

verses.name: Mark 16:2
verses.text: And very early in the morning on the first <transChange type="added">day</transChange> of the week they came to the tomb <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“had risen”)</note> the sun had risen.

verses.name: Mark 16:3
verses.text: And they were saying to one another, “Who will roll away the stone for us from the entrance of the tomb?”

verses.name: Mark 16:4
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“looked up”) which is understood as temporal</note> looked up, they saw that the stone had been rolled away (for it was very large).

verses.name: Mark 16:5
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">as they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“going”) which is understood as temporal</note> were going into the tomb, they saw a young man dressed in a white robe sitting on the right side, and they were alarmed.

verses.name: Mark 16:6
verses.text: But he said to them, “Do not be alarmed. You are looking for Jesus the Nazarene who was crucified. He has been raised, he is not here! See the place where they laid him!

verses.name: Mark 16:7
verses.text: But go, tell his disciples and Peter that he is going ahead of you to Galilee. You will see him there, just as he told you.”

verses.name: Mark 16:8
verses.text: And they went out <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> fled from the tomb, because trembling and amazement had seized them. And they said nothing to anyone, because they were afraid.<note placement="foot">The Gospel of Mark ends at this point in some manuscripts, including two of the most important ones, while other manuscripts supply a shorter ending (sometimes included as part of v. <reference osisRef="Mark.16.8">8</reference>), others supply the traditional longer ending (vv. <reference osisRef="Mark.16.9-Mark.16.20">9–20</reference>), and still other manuscripts supply both the shorter ending and vv. <reference osisRef="Mark.16.9-Mark.16.20">9–20</reference>; due to significant questions about the authenticity of these alternative endings, many scholars regard 16:8 as the last verse of the Gospel of Mark</note> <div eID="gen26152" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">The Shorter Ending of Mark</title> <div sID="gen26153" type="x-p"/> 〚So they promptly reported all the <transChange type="added">things</transChange> they had been commanded to those around Peter. And after these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, Jesus himself also sent out through them from the east even as far as the west the holy and imperishable proclamation of eternal salvation. Amen.〛 <div eID="gen26153" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">The Longer Ending of Mark</title> <div sID="gen26154" type="x-p"/> 〚

verses.name: Mark 16:9
verses.text: Now early on the first <transChange type="added">day</transChange> of the week, <transChange type="added">after he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“rose”) which is understood as temporal</note> rose, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom he had expelled seven demons.

verses.name: Mark 16:10
verses.text: She went out <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> announced it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to those who were with him while they<note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the participle (“were”) which is understood as temporal</note> were mourning and weeping.

verses.name: Mark 16:11
verses.text: And those, <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard that he was alive and had been seen by her, refused to believe it.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Mark 16:12
verses.text: And after these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, he appeared in a different form to two of them <transChange type="added">as they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“were walking”) which is understood as temporal</note> were walking, while they<note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the participle (“were going out”) which is understood as temporal</note> were going out into the countryside.

verses.name: Mark 16:13
verses.text: And these went <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> reported it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to the others, and they did not believe them.

verses.name: Mark 16:14
verses.text: And later, <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the participle (“were reclining at table”) which is understood as temporal</note> they were reclining at table, he appeared to the eleven. And he reprimanded their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they did not believe those who had seen him after he<note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had been raised”) which is understood as temporal</note> had been raised.

verses.name: Mark 16:15
verses.text: And he said to them, “Go<note placement="foot">As a participle of attendant circumstance this participle carries imperatival force picked up from the main verb (“preach”)</note> into all the world and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“go”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> preach the gospel to all creation.

verses.name: Mark 16:16
verses.text: The one who believes and is baptized will be saved, but the one who refuses to believe will be condemned.

verses.name: Mark 16:17
verses.text: And these signs will accompany those who believe: in my name they will expel demons, they will speak in new tongues,

verses.name: Mark 16:18
verses.text: they will pick up<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “and they will pick up”</note> snakes.<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts add “with their hands”</note> And if they drink any deadly poison it will never hurt them; they will lay hands on the sick and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they will get⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “they will have”</note> well.”  <div eID="gen26154" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 16:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10853"/><div sID="gen26155" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10853"/>Then the Lord Jesus, after <transChange type="added">he</transChange> had spoken to them, was taken up into heaven and sat down at the right hand of God.

verses.name: Mark 16:20
verses.text: And they went out <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> proclaimed everywhere, while<note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was working together with”)</note> the Lord was working together with them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and confirming the message through the accompanying signs.〛  <chapter eID="Mark.16"/> <div eID="gen26155" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen25994" osisID="Mark" type="book"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10854"/><title type="x-s">The Preface to Luke’s Gospel</title> <div sID="gen26157" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10854"/>Since many have attempted to compile an account concerning the events that have been fulfilled among us,

verses.name: Luke 1:2
verses.text: just as those who were eyewitnesses and servants of the word from the beginning passed on to us,

verses.name: Luke 1:3
verses.text: it seemed best to me also—<transChange type="added">because I</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“have followed”) which is understood as causal</note> have followed all things carefully from the beginning—to write them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> down in orderly sequence for you, most excellent Theophilus,

verses.name: Luke 1:4
verses.text: so that you may know the certainty concerning the things about which you were taught.  <div eID="gen26157" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10855"/><title type="x-s">The Prediction of John the Baptist’s Birth</title> <div sID="gen26158" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10855"/>It happened that in the days of Herod, king of Judea, <transChange type="added">there was</transChange> a certain priest, Zechariah by name, of the division of Abijah. And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he had a wife⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a wife to him”</note> from the daughters of Aaron, and her name <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Elizabeth.

verses.name: Luke 1:6
verses.text: And they were both righteous in the sight of God, living blamelessly in all the commandments and regulations of the Lord.

verses.name: Luke 1:7
verses.text: And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they did not have⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “there was not to them”</note> a child, because Elizabeth was barren. And they were both advanced <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in years⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “in their days”</note>  <div eID="gen26158" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10856"/><div sID="gen26159" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10856"/>And it happened that <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal infinitive (“was serving as priest”)</note> he was serving as priest before God in the order of his division,

verses.name: Luke 1:9
verses.text: according to the custom of the priesthood he was chosen by lot to enter into the temple of the Lord to burn incense.

verses.name: Luke 1:10
verses.text: And the whole crowd of the people were praying outside at the hour of the incense offering.

verses.name: Luke 1:11
verses.text: And an angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing at the right side of the altar of incense.

verses.name: Luke 1:12
verses.text: And Zechariah was terrified <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw the angel,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and fear fell upon him.

verses.name: Luke 1:13
verses.text: But the angel said to him, <div eID="gen26159" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen26160"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26161"/>“Do not be afraid, Zechariah,<l eID="gen26161" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26162"/>because your prayer has been heard,<l eID="gen26162" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26163"/>and your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son,<l eID="gen26163" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26164"/>and you will call his name John. <l eID="gen26164" level="1"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10857"/><l level="1" sID="gen26165"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10857"/>And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you will experience joy and exultation⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “joy and exultation will be to you”</note><l eID="gen26165" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26166"/>and many will rejoice at his birth. <l eID="gen26166" level="1"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10858"/><l level="1" sID="gen26167"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10858"/>For he will be great in the sight of the Lord,<l eID="gen26167" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26168"/>and he must never drink wine or beer,<l eID="gen26168" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26169"/>and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit<l eID="gen26169" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26170"/><transChange type="added">while he is</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the phrase “while he is,” including the verb, is understood in Greek and is supplied in the translation</note> still in his mother’s womb. <l eID="gen26170" level="2"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10859"/><l level="1" sID="gen26171"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10859"/>And he will turn many of the sons of Israel<l eID="gen26171" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26172"/>to the Lord their God. <l eID="gen26172" level="2"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10860"/><l level="1" sID="gen26173"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10860"/>And he will go on before him<l eID="gen26173" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26174"/>in the spirit and power of Elijah,<l eID="gen26174" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26175"/>to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children,<l eID="gen26175" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26176"/>and the disobedient to the wisdom of the righteous,<l eID="gen26176" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26177"/>to prepare for the Lord a people made ready.” <l eID="gen26177" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen26160"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10861"/><div sID="gen26178" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10861"/>And Zechariah said to the angel, “By what will I know this? For I am an old man, and my wife is advanced <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in years⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!”<note placement="foot">Literally “in her days”</note>

verses.name: Luke 1:19
verses.text: And the angel answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to him, “I am Gabriel, who stands in the presence of God, and I was sent to speak to you and to announce to you this good news.

verses.name: Luke 1:20
verses.text: And behold, you will be silent and not able to speak until the day these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> take place, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞because⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in return for which”</note> you did not believe my words, which will be fulfilled in their time.”  <div eID="gen26178" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10862"/><div sID="gen26179" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10862"/>And the people were waiting for Zechariah, and began to wonder<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to wonder”)</note> when<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal infinitive (“was delayed”)</note> he was delayed in the temple.

verses.name: Luke 1:22
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“came out”) which is understood as temporal</note> came out he was not able to speak to them, and they realized that he had seen a vision in the temple. And he kept making signs to them, and remained unable to speak.

verses.name: Luke 1:23
verses.text: And it happened that when the days of his service came to an end, he went away to his home.  <div eID="gen26179" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10863"/><div sID="gen26180" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10863"/>Now after these days, his wife Elizabeth conceived, and she kept herself in seclusion <transChange type="added">for</transChange> five months, saying,

verses.name: Luke 1:25
verses.text: “Thus the Lord has done for me in the days in which he has concerned himself with <transChange type="added">me</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to take away my disgrace among people.”  <div eID="gen26180" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10864"/><title type="x-s">The Prediction of Jesus’ Birth</title> <div sID="gen26181" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10864"/>Now in the sixth month, the angel Gabriel was sent from God to a town of Galilee <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞named⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to which the name”</note> Nazareth,

verses.name: Luke 1:27
verses.text: to a virgin legally promised in marriage to a man <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞named⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to whom the name”</note> Joseph of the house of David. And the name of the virgin <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Mary.

verses.name: Luke 1:28
verses.text: And he came to her <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “Greetings, favored one! The Lord <transChange type="added">is</transChange> with you.”

verses.name: Luke 1:29
verses.text: But she was greatly perplexed at the statement, and was pondering what sort of greeting this might be.

verses.name: Luke 1:30
verses.text: And the angel said to her, <div eID="gen26181" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen26182"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26183"/>“Do not be afraid, Mary, for you have found favor with God. <l eID="gen26183" level="1"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10865"/><l level="1" sID="gen26184"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10865"/>And behold, you will conceive in the womb and will give birth to a son,<l eID="gen26184" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26185"/>and you will call his name Jesus. <l eID="gen26185" level="2"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10866"/><l level="1" sID="gen26186"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10866"/>This one will be great, and he will be called the Son of the Most High,<l eID="gen26186" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26187"/>and the Lord God will give him the throne of his father David. <l eID="gen26187" level="2"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:33
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10867"/><l level="1" sID="gen26188"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10867"/>And he will reign over the house of Jacob <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “for the ages”</note><l eID="gen26188" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26189"/>and of his kingdom there will be no end. <l eID="gen26189" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen26182"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:34
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10868"/><div sID="gen26190" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10868"/>And Mary said to the angel, “How will this be, since I have not had sexual relations with a man?”

verses.name: Luke 1:35
verses.text: And the angel answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to her, <div eID="gen26190" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen26191"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26192"/>“The Holy Spirit will come upon you,<l eID="gen26192" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26193"/>and the power of the Most High will overshadow you.<l eID="gen26193" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26194"/>Therefore also the one to be born will be called holy, the Son of God. <l eID="gen26194" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen26191"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:36
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10869"/><div sID="gen26195" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10869"/>And behold, your relative Elizabeth—she also has conceived a son in her old age, and this is the sixth month for her who was called barren.

verses.name: Luke 1:37
verses.text: For <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞nothing will be impossible with God⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “every thing will not be impossible with God”</note>  <div eID="gen26195" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:38
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10870"/><div sID="gen26196" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10870"/>So Mary said, “Behold, the Lord’s female slave! May it happen to me according to your word.” And the angel departed from her.  <div eID="gen26196" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:39
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10871"/><title type="x-s">Mary Visits Elizabeth</title> <div sID="gen26197" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10871"/>Now in those days Mary set out <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“set out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> traveled with haste into the hill country, to a town of Judah,

verses.name: Luke 1:40
verses.text: and entered into the house of Zechariah, and greeted Elizabeth.

verses.name: Luke 1:41
verses.text: And it happened that when Elizabeth heard the greeting of Mary, the baby in her womb leaped and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit.

verses.name: Luke 1:42
verses.text: And she cried out with a loud shout and said, <div eID="gen26197" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen26198"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26199"/>“Blessed <transChange type="added">are</transChange> you among women,<l eID="gen26199" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26200"/>and blessed <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the fruit of your womb! <l eID="gen26200" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen26198"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:43
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10872"/><div sID="gen26201" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10872"/>And why <transChange type="added">is</transChange> this <transChange type="added">granted</transChange> to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?

verses.name: Luke 1:44
verses.text: For behold, when the sound of your greeting came to my ears, the baby in my womb leaped for joy!

verses.name: Luke 1:45
verses.text: And blessed <transChange type="added">is</transChange> she who believed that <transChange type="added">there</transChange> will be a fulfillment to what was spoken to her from the Lord!”  <div eID="gen26201" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:46
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10873"/><title type="x-s">Mary’s Hymn of Praise to God</title> <div sID="gen26202" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10873"/>And Mary said, <div eID="gen26202" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen26203"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26204"/>“My soul exalts the Lord, <l eID="gen26204" level="1"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:47
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10874"/><l level="2" sID="gen26205"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10874"/>and my spirit has rejoiced greatly in God my Savior, <l eID="gen26205" level="2"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:48
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10875"/><l level="1" sID="gen26206"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10875"/>because he has looked upon the humble state of his female slave,<l eID="gen26206" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26207"/>for behold, from now on all generations will consider me blessed, <l eID="gen26207" level="2"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:49
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10876"/><l level="1" sID="gen26208"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10876"/>because the Mighty <transChange type="added">One</transChange> has done great <transChange type="added">things</transChange> for me,<l eID="gen26208" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26209"/>and holy <transChange type="added">is</transChange> his name. <l eID="gen26209" level="2"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:50
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10877"/><l level="1" sID="gen26210"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10877"/>And his mercy <transChange type="added">is</transChange> for generation after generation<l eID="gen26210" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26211"/>to those who fear him. <l eID="gen26211" level="2"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:51
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10878"/><l level="1" sID="gen26212"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10878"/>He has done a mighty deed with his arm;<l eID="gen26212" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26213"/>he has dispersed the proud in the thoughts of their hearts. <l eID="gen26213" level="2"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:52
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10879"/><l level="1" sID="gen26214"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10879"/>He has brought down rulers from <transChange type="added">their</transChange> thrones,<l eID="gen26214" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26215"/>and has exalted the lowly. <l eID="gen26215" level="2"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:53
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10880"/><l level="1" sID="gen26216"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10880"/>He has filled those who are hungry with good <transChange type="added">things</transChange>,<l eID="gen26216" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26217"/>and those who are rich he has sent away empty-handed. <l eID="gen26217" level="2"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:54
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10881"/><l level="1" sID="gen26218"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10881"/>He has helped Israel his servant,<l eID="gen26218" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26219"/>remembering <transChange type="added">his</transChange> mercy, <l eID="gen26219" level="2"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:55
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10882"/><l level="1" sID="gen26220"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10882"/>just as he spoke to our fathers,<l eID="gen26220" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26221"/>to Abraham and to his descendants <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “for the age”</note> <l eID="gen26221" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen26203"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:56
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10883"/><div sID="gen26222" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10883"/>And Mary stayed with her about three months, and returned to her home.  <div eID="gen26222" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:57
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10884"/><title type="x-s">The Birth of John the Baptist</title> <div sID="gen26223" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10884"/>Now the time came for Elizabeth that she should give birth, and she gave birth to a son.

verses.name: Luke 1:58
verses.text: And her neighbors and relatives heard that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the Lord had shown his great mercy to her⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the Lord had made great his mercy with her”</note> and they rejoiced with her.

verses.name: Luke 1:59
verses.text: And it happened that on the eighth day they came to circumcise the child, and they were wanting to name him <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞after⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in the name of”</note> his father Zechariah.

verses.name: Luke 1:60
verses.text: And his mother answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “No, but he will be named John.”

verses.name: Luke 1:61
verses.text: And they said to her, “There is no one of your relatives who is called by this name.”

verses.name: Luke 1:62
verses.text: So they made signs to his father <transChange type="added">asking</transChange> what he wanted him to be named,

verses.name: Luke 1:63
verses.text: and he asked for a writing tablet <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“asked for”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> wrote, saying, “John is his name.” And they were all astonished.

verses.name: Luke 1:64
verses.text: And his mouth and his tongue were opened immediately, and he began to speak,<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to speak”)</note> praising God.

verses.name: Luke 1:65
verses.text: And fear came on all those who lived near them, and in all the hill country of Judea all these events were discussed.

verses.name: Luke 1:66
verses.text: And all those who heard kept <transChange type="added">these things</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> in their hearts, saying, “What then will this child be? For indeed the hand of the Lord was with him!”  <div eID="gen26223" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:67
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10885"/><title type="x-s">The Praise and Prophecy of Zechariah</title> <div sID="gen26224" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10885"/>And his father Zechariah was filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesied, saying,  <div eID="gen26224" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:68
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10886"/><lg sID="gen26225"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26226"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10886"/>“Blessed <transChange type="added">be</transChange> the Lord, the God of Israel,<l eID="gen26226" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26227"/>because he has visited to help and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞has redeemed⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “has done redemption for”</note> his people, <l eID="gen26227" level="2"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:69
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10887"/><l level="1" sID="gen26228"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10887"/>and has raised up a horn of salvation for us<l eID="gen26228" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26229"/>in the house of his servant David, <l eID="gen26229" level="2"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:70
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10888"/><l level="1" sID="gen26230"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10888"/>just as he spoke through the mouth of his holy prophets from earliest times— <l eID="gen26230" level="1"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:71
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10889"/><l level="2" sID="gen26231"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10889"/>salvation from our enemies and from the hand of all those who hate us, <l eID="gen26231" level="2"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:72
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10890"/><l level="1" sID="gen26232"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10890"/>to show mercy to our fathers<l eID="gen26232" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26233"/>and to remember his holy covenant, <l eID="gen26233" level="2"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:73
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10891"/><l level="1" sID="gen26234"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10891"/>the oath that he swore to Abraham our father,<l eID="gen26234" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26235"/>to grant us

verses.name: Luke 1:74
verses.text: <transChange type="added">that</transChange> we, being rescued from the hand of <transChange type="added">our</transChange> enemies,<l eID="gen26235" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26236"/>could serve him without fear

verses.name: Luke 1:75
verses.text: in holiness and righteousness<l eID="gen26236" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26237"/>before him all our days. <l eID="gen26237" level="2"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:76
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10892"/><l level="1" sID="gen26238"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10892"/>And so you, child, will be called the prophet of the Most High,<l eID="gen26238" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26239"/>for you will go on before the Lord to prepare his ways, <l eID="gen26239" level="2"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:77
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10893"/><l level="1" sID="gen26240"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10893"/>to give knowledge of salvation to his people<l eID="gen26240" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26241"/>by the forgiveness of their sins, <l eID="gen26241" level="2"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:78
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10894"/><l level="1" sID="gen26242"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10894"/>because of the merciful compassion<note placement="foot">Or “heart”</note> of our God<l eID="gen26242" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26243"/>by which the dawn will visit to help us from on high, <l eID="gen26243" level="2"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:79
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10895"/><l level="1" sID="gen26244"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10895"/>to give light to those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death,<l eID="gen26244" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26245"/>to direct our feet into the way of peace.” <l eID="gen26245" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen26225"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:80
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10896"/><div sID="gen26246" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10896"/>And the child kept growing and becoming strong in spirit, and was in the wilderness until the day of his public appearance to Israel.  <chapter eID="Luke.1"/>

verses.name: Luke 2:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10897"/><title type="x-s">The Birth of Jesus Christ</title> <div sID="gen26247" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10897"/>Now it happened that in those days a decree went out from Caesar<note placement="foot">Or “the emperor”</note> Augustus to register all the empire.

verses.name: Luke 2:2
verses.text: (This first registration took place <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Or perhaps “before”; here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was governor”)</note> Quirinius was governor of Syria.)

verses.name: Luke 2:3
verses.text: And everyone went to be registered, each one to his own town.

verses.name: Luke 2:4
verses.text: So Joseph also went up from Galilee, from the town of Nazareth, to Judea, to the city of David which is called Bethlehem, because he was of the house and family line of David,

verses.name: Luke 2:5
verses.text: to be registered together with Mary, who was legally promised in marriage to him <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied in keeping with English style</note> was pregnant.

verses.name: Luke 2:6
verses.text: And it happened that while they were there, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the time came⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the days were completed”</note> for her to give birth.

verses.name: Luke 2:7
verses.text: And she gave birth to her firstborn son, and wrapped him in strips of cloth and laid him in a manger, because there was no place for them in the inn.  <div eID="gen26247" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 2:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10898"/><title type="x-s">The Shepherds and the Angels</title> <div sID="gen26248" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10898"/>And there were shepherds in the same region, living out of doors and keeping watch, guarding over their flock by night.

verses.name: Luke 2:9
verses.text: And an angel of the Lord stood near them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they were terribly frightened⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “they were afraid with great fear”</note>

verses.name: Luke 2:10
verses.text: And the angel said to them, “Do not be afraid, for behold, I bring good news to you of great joy which will be for all the people:

verses.name: Luke 2:11
verses.text: that today a Savior, who is Christ the Lord, was born for you in the city of David.

verses.name: Luke 2:12
verses.text: And this will be the sign for you: you will find the baby wrapped in strips of cloth and lying in a manger.”

verses.name: Luke 2:13
verses.text: And suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly army, praising God and saying,  <div eID="gen26248" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 2:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10899"/><lg sID="gen26249"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26250"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10899"/>“Glory to God in the highest,<l eID="gen26250" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26251"/>and on earth peace<l eID="gen26251" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26252"/>among people <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞with whom he is pleased⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!”<note placement="foot">Literally “of good pleasure”</note> <l eID="gen26252" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen26249"/>

verses.name: Luke 2:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10900"/><div sID="gen26253" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10900"/>And it happened that when the angels had departed from them into heaven, the shepherds began to say<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to say”)</note> to one another, “Let us go now to Bethlehem and see this thing that has happened, which the Lord has revealed to us!”

verses.name: Luke 2:16
verses.text: And they went hurrying and found both Mary and Joseph, and the baby who was lying in the manger.

verses.name: Luke 2:17
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> they made known the statement that had been told to them about this child.

verses.name: Luke 2:18
verses.text: And all who heard <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> were astonished concerning what had been said to them by the shepherds.

verses.name: Luke 2:19
verses.text: But Mary treasured up all these words, pondering <transChange type="added">them</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> in her heart.

verses.name: Luke 2:20
verses.text: And the shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all that they had heard and seen, just as it had been told to them.  <div eID="gen26253" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 2:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10901"/><div sID="gen26254" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10901"/>And when eight days were completed <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞so that he could be circumcised⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to circumcise him”</note> he was named Jesus, his name <transChange type="added">that</transChange> <transChange type="added">he</transChange> was called by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.  <div eID="gen26254" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 2:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10902"/><title type="x-s">The Presentation of Jesus at the Temple</title> <div sID="gen26255" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10902"/>And when the days of their purification were completed according to the law of Moses, they brought him up to Jerusalem to present <transChange type="added">him</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to the Lord

verses.name: Luke 2:23
verses.text: (just as it is written in the law of the Lord, “Every male that opens the womb will be called holy to the Lord”)<note placement="foot">An allusion to <reference osisRef="Exod.13.2">Exod 13:2</reference>, <reference osisRef="Exod.13.12">12</reference>, <reference osisRef="Exod.13.15">15</reference></note>

verses.name: Luke 2:24
verses.text: and to offer a sacrifice according to what was stated in the law of the Lord, “a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Lev.5.11">Lev 5:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="Lev.12.8">12:8</reference></note>  <div eID="gen26255" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 2:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10903"/><title type="x-s">The Prophecy of Simeon</title> <div sID="gen26256" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10903"/>And behold, there was a man in Jerusalem <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞whose name was⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to whom the name”</note> Simeon, and this man <transChange type="added">was</transChange> righteous and devout, looking forward to the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was upon him.

verses.name: Luke 2:26
verses.text: And it had been revealed to him by the Holy Spirit <transChange type="added">that he would</transChange> not see death before he would see the Lord’s Christ.<note placement="foot">Or “Messiah”</note>

verses.name: Luke 2:27
verses.text: And he came in the Spirit into the temple, and when the parents brought in the child Jesus so that they could do for him according to what was customary under the law,

verses.name: Luke 2:28
verses.text: he took him in <transChange type="added">his</transChange><note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> arms and praised God and said,  <div eID="gen26256" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 2:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10904"/><lg sID="gen26257"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26258"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10904"/>“Now dismiss your slave in peace, Lord,<l eID="gen26258" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26259"/>according to your word. <l eID="gen26259" level="2"/>

verses.name: Luke 2:30
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10905"/><l level="1" sID="gen26260"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10905"/>For my eyes have seen your salvation <l eID="gen26260" level="1"/>

verses.name: Luke 2:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10906"/><l level="2" sID="gen26261"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10906"/>that you have prepared in the presence of all the peoples, <l eID="gen26261" level="2"/>

verses.name: Luke 2:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10907"/><l level="1" sID="gen26262"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10907"/>a light for revelation to the Gentiles,<l eID="gen26262" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26263"/>and glory to your people Israel.” <l eID="gen26263" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen26257"/>

verses.name: Luke 2:33
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10908"/><div sID="gen26264" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10908"/>And his father and mother were astonished at what was said about him.

verses.name: Luke 2:34
verses.text: And Simeon blessed them and said to his mother Mary, “Behold, this child is appointed for the fall and rise of many in Israel, and for a sign that is opposed<note placement="foot">Or “rejected”</note>—

verses.name: Luke 2:35
verses.text: and a sword will pierce your own soul also, so that the thoughts of many hearts will be revealed!”  <div eID="gen26264" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 2:36
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10909"/><title type="x-s">The Testimony of Anna</title> <div sID="gen26265" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10909"/>And there was a prophetess, Anna the daughter of Phanuel of the tribe of Asher (she was advanced <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in years⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “with many days”</note> having lived with her husband seven years <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞after her marriage⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “from her virginity”</note>

verses.name: Luke 2:37
verses.text: and herself <transChange type="added">as</transChange> a widow up to eighty-four years)<note placement="foot">Or “eighty-four years as a widow”</note> who did not depart from the temple with fastings and prayers, serving night and day.

verses.name: Luke 2:38
verses.text: And at <transChange type="added">that</transChange> same hour she approached <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“approached”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> began to give thanks<note placement="foot">The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to give thanks”)</note> to God, and to speak about him to all those who were waiting for the redemption of Jerusalem.  <div eID="gen26265" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 2:39
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10910"/><div sID="gen26266" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10910"/>And when they had completed everything according to the law of the Lord, they returned to Galilee, to their own town of Nazareth.

verses.name: Luke 2:40
verses.text: And the child was growing and becoming strong, filled with wisdom, and the favor of God was upon him.  <div eID="gen26266" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 2:41
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10911"/><title type="x-s">Jesus in the Temple at Twelve Years Old</title> <div sID="gen26267" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10911"/>And his parents went every year to Jerusalem for the feast of the Passover.

verses.name: Luke 2:42
verses.text: And when he was twelve years <transChange type="added">old</transChange>, they went up according to the custom of the feast.

verses.name: Luke 2:43
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“were completed”) which is understood as temporal</note> the days were completed, while they were returning, the boy Jesus stayed behind in Jerusalem. And his parents did not know it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Luke 2:44
verses.text: but believing him to be in the group of travelers, they went a day’s journey. And they began searching for<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began searching for”)</note> him among their<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> relatives and their<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> acquaintances,

verses.name: Luke 2:45
verses.text: and <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“find”) which is understood as temporal</note> did not find him,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> they returned to Jerusalem to search for him.

verses.name: Luke 2:46
verses.text: And it happened that after three days they found him in the temple <transChange type="added">courts</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> sitting in the midst of the teachers and listening to them and asking them <transChange type="added">questions</transChange>.

verses.name: Luke 2:47
verses.text: And all who heard him were amazed at his insight and <transChange type="added">his</transChange><note placement="foot">*This is an understood repetition of “his” due to English style</note> answers.

verses.name: Luke 2:48
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw him, they were astounded and his mother said to him, “Child, why have you done this to us? Look, your father and I have been searching for you anxiously!”

verses.name: Luke 2:49
verses.text: And he said to them, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Why⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “what is it that”</note> were you searching for me? Did you not know that it was necessary for me to be in the house<note placement="foot">Or “things” (= business)</note> of my Father?”

verses.name: Luke 2:50
verses.text: And they did not understand the statement that he spoke to them.

verses.name: Luke 2:51
verses.text: And he went down with them and came to Nazareth, and was submitting to them. And his mother treasured all these things in her heart.  <div eID="gen26267" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 2:52
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10912"/><div sID="gen26268" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10912"/>And Jesus was advancing in wisdom and stature and in favor with God and <transChange type="added">with</transChange> people.  <chapter eID="Luke.2"/>

verses.name: Luke 3:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10913"/><title type="x-s">John the Baptist Begins His Ministry</title> <div sID="gen26269" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10913"/>Now in the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar,<note placement="foot">Or “the emperor Tiberius”</note> <transChange type="added">when</transChange> Pontius Pilate was governor of Judea, and Herod was tetrarch of Galilee, and his brother Philip was tetrarch of the region of Iturea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias was tetrarch of Abilene,

verses.name: Luke 3:2
verses.text: in the time of the high priest Annas and Caiaphas, the word of God came to John the son of Zechariah in the wilderness.

verses.name: Luke 3:3
verses.text: And he went into all the surrounding region of the Jordan, preaching a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins,

verses.name: Luke 3:4
verses.text: as it is written in the book of the words of the prophet Isaiah, <div eID="gen26269" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen26270"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26271"/>“The voice of one crying out in the wilderness,<l eID="gen26271" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26272"/>‘Prepare the way of the Lord,<l eID="gen26272" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26273"/>make his paths straight! <l eID="gen26273" level="2"/>

verses.name: Luke 3:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10914"/><l level="1" sID="gen26274"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10914"/>Every valley will be filled,<l eID="gen26274" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26275"/>and every mountain and hill will be leveled,<l eID="gen26275" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26276"/>and the crooked will become straight,<l eID="gen26276" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26277"/>and the rough road <transChange type="added">will become</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “will become” is an implied repetition of the verb earlier in the verse</note> smooth, <l eID="gen26277" level="2"/>

verses.name: Luke 3:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10915"/><l level="1" sID="gen26278"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10915"/>and all flesh will see the salvation of God.’ ”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.40.3-Isa.40.5">Isa 40:3–5</reference></note> <l eID="gen26278" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen26270"/>

verses.name: Luke 3:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10916"/><div sID="gen26279" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10916"/>Therefore he was saying to the crowds that came out to be baptized by him, “Offspring of vipers! Who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?

verses.name: Luke 3:8
verses.text: Therefore produce fruit worthy of repentance! And do not begin to say to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham <transChange type="added">as</transChange> father.’ For I say to you that God is able to raise up children for Abraham from these stones!

verses.name: Luke 3:9
verses.text: And even now the ax is positioned at the root of the trees; therefore every tree not producing good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.”  <div eID="gen26279" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 3:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10917"/><div sID="gen26280" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10917"/>And the crowds were asking him, saying, “What then should we do?”

verses.name: Luke 3:11
verses.text: And he answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to them, “The one who has two tunics must share with the one who does not have one,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and the one who has food must do likewise.”

verses.name: Luke 3:12
verses.text: And tax collectors also came to be baptized, and they said to him, “Teacher, what should we do?”

verses.name: Luke 3:13
verses.text: And he said to them, “Collect no more than <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞what you are ordered to⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “what is ordered to you”</note>

verses.name: Luke 3:14
verses.text: And those who served in the army were also asking him, saying, “What should we also do?” And he said to them, “Extort from no one, and do not blackmail <transChange type="added">anyone</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and be content with your pay.”  <div eID="gen26280" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 3:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10918"/><div sID="gen26281" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10918"/>And <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“were waiting expectantly”)</note> the people were waiting expectantly and all were pondering in their hearts concerning John, whether perhaps he might be the Christ,<note placement="foot">Or “Messiah”</note>

verses.name: Luke 3:16
verses.text: John answered them all, saying, “I baptize you with water, but the one who is more powerful than I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> is coming, of whom I am not worthy to untie the strap of his sandals. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.

verses.name: Luke 3:17
verses.text: His winnowing shovel <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in his hand, to clean out his threshing floor and to gather the wheat into his storehouse, but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.”  <div eID="gen26281" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 3:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10919"/><div sID="gen26282" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10919"/>So with many other exhortations also he proclaimed good news to the people.

verses.name: Luke 3:19
verses.text: But Herod the tetrarch, who had been reproved by him concerning Herodias, his brother’s wife, and concerning all the evil deeds that Herod had done,

verses.name: Luke 3:20
verses.text: added this also to them all: he also locked up John in prison.  <div eID="gen26282" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 3:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10920"/><title type="x-s">The Baptism of Jesus</title> <div sID="gen26283" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10920"/>Now it happened that when all the people were baptized, Jesus also was baptized, and <transChange type="added">while he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was praying”)</note> was praying, heaven was opened,

verses.name: Luke 3:22
verses.text: and the Holy Spirit descended on him in bodily form like a dove, and a voice came from heaven, “You are my beloved Son; with you I am well pleased.”  <div eID="gen26283" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 3:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10921"/><title type="x-s">The Genealogy of Jesus Christ</title> <div sID="gen26284" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10921"/>And Jesus, <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“began”) which is understood as temporal</note> began his ministry,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> was himself about thirty years <transChange type="added">old</transChange>, being the son (as it was believed) of Joseph the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Eli,

verses.name: Luke 3:24
verses.text: the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Matthat, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Levi, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Melchi, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Jannai, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Joseph,

verses.name: Luke 3:25
verses.text: the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Mattathias, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Amos, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Nahum, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Esli, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Naggai,

verses.name: Luke 3:26
verses.text: the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Maath, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Mattathias, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Semein, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Josech, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Joda,

verses.name: Luke 3:27
verses.text: the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Joanan, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Rhesa, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Zerubbabel, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Shealtiel, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Neri,

verses.name: Luke 3:28
verses.text: the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Melchi, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Addi, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Cosam, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Elmadam, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Er,

verses.name: Luke 3:29
verses.text: the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Joshua, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Eliezer, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Jorim, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Matthat, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Levi,

verses.name: Luke 3:30
verses.text: the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Simeon, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Judah, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Joseph, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Jonam, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Eliakim,

verses.name: Luke 3:31
verses.text: the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Melea, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Menna, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Mattatha, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Nathan, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of David,

verses.name: Luke 3:32
verses.text: the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Jesse, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Obed, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Boaz, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Sala, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Nahshon,

verses.name: Luke 3:33
verses.text: the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Amminadab, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Admin, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Arni, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Hezron, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Perez, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Judah,

verses.name: Luke 3:34
verses.text: the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Jacob, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Isaac, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Abraham, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Terah, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Nahor,

verses.name: Luke 3:35
verses.text: the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Serug, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Reu, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Peleg, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Eber, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Shelah,<note placement="foot">Greek “Sala”</note>

verses.name: Luke 3:36
verses.text: the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Cainan, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Arphaxad, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Shem, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Noah, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Lamech,

verses.name: Luke 3:37
verses.text: the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Methuselah, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Enoch, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Jared, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Mahalaleel, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Cainan,

verses.name: Luke 3:38
verses.text: the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Enosh, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Seth, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Adam, the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of God.  <chapter eID="Luke.3"/>

verses.name: Luke 4:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10922"/><title type="x-s">The Temptation of Jesus</title> <div sID="gen26285" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10922"/>And Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan and was led by the Spirit in the wilderness

verses.name: Luke 4:2
verses.text: forty days, being tempted by the devil. And he ate nothing during those days, and <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“were completed”)</note> they were completed, he was hungry.

verses.name: Luke 4:3
verses.text: So the devil said to him, “If you are the Son of God, order this stone that it become bread!”

verses.name: Luke 4:4
verses.text: And Jesus replied to him, “It is written, ‘Man will not live on bread alone.’ ”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Deut.8.3">Deut 8:3; </reference>most manuscripts add “but by every word of God” here</note>  <div eID="gen26285" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 4:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10923"/><div sID="gen26286" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10923"/>And he led him up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“led … up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> showed him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time.

verses.name: Luke 4:6
verses.text: And the devil said to him, “I will give you all this domain and their glory, because it has been handed over to me, and I can give it to whomever I want.

verses.name: Luke 4:7
verses.text: So if you will worship before me, all <transChange type="added">this</transChange> will be yours.”

verses.name: Luke 4:8
