verses.text: And Jesus answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to him, “It is written, ‘You shall worship the Lord your God, and serve only him.’ ”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Deut.6.13">Deut 6:13</reference></note>  <div eID="gen26286" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 4:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10924"/><div sID="gen26287" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10924"/>And he brought him to Jerusalem, and had him stand on the highest point of the temple and said to him, “If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down from here,

verses.name: Luke 4:10
verses.text: for it is written, <div eID="gen26287" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen26288"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26289"/>‘He will command his angels concerning you,<l eID="gen26289" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26290"/>to protect you,’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.91.11">Ps 91:11</reference></note> <l eID="gen26290" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen26288"/>

verses.name: Luke 4:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10925"/><div sID="gen26291" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10925"/>and <div eID="gen26291" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen26292"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26293"/>‘on <transChange type="added">their</transChange> hands they will lift you up,<l eID="gen26293" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26294"/>lest you strike your foot against a stone.’ ”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.91.12">Ps 91:12</reference></note> <l eID="gen26294" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen26292"/>

verses.name: Luke 4:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10926"/><div sID="gen26295" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10926"/>And Jesus answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to him, “It is said, ‘You are not to put to the test the Lord your God.’ ”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Deut.6.16">Deut 6:16</reference></note>

verses.name: Luke 4:13
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had completed”) which is understood as temporal</note> the devil had completed every temptation, he departed from him until a favorable time.<note placement="foot">Or “for a while”</note>  <div eID="gen26295" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 4:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10927"/><title type="x-s">Public Ministry in Galilee</title> <div sID="gen26296" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10927"/>And Jesus returned in the power of the Spirit to Galilee, and news about him went out throughout all the surrounding region.

verses.name: Luke 4:15
verses.text: And he began to teach<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to teach”)</note> in their synagogues, and<note placement="foot">*Here the participle (“was praised”) is translated as a finite verb because of English style</note> was praised by all.  <div eID="gen26296" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 4:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10928"/><title type="x-s">Rejected at Nazareth</title> <div sID="gen26297" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10928"/>And he came to Nazareth, where <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he had been brought up⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “he was having been brought up”</note> and according to <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his custom⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “what he was accustomed to for him”</note> he entered into the synagogue on the day of the Sabbath and stood up to read.

verses.name: Luke 4:17
verses.text: And the scroll of the prophet Isaiah was given to him, and unrolling the scroll he found the place where it was written,  <div eID="gen26297" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 4:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10929"/><lg sID="gen26298"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26299"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10929"/>“The Spirit of the Lord <transChange type="added">is</transChange> upon me,<l eID="gen26299" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26300"/>because of which he has anointed me<l eID="gen26300" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26301"/>to proclaim good news to the poor.<l eID="gen26301" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26302"/>He has sent me<l eID="gen26302" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26303"/>to proclaim release to the captives,<l eID="gen26303" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26304"/>and recovery of sight to the blind,<l eID="gen26304" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26305"/>to send out in freedom those who are oppressed, <l eID="gen26305" level="1"/>

verses.name: Luke 4:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10930"/><l level="2" sID="gen26306"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10930"/>to proclaim the favorable year of the Lord.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.61.1-Isa.61.2">Isa 61:1–2, </reference>with one line from <reference osisRef="Isa.58.6">Isa 58:6</reference></note> <l eID="gen26306" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen26298"/>

verses.name: Luke 4:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10931"/><div sID="gen26307" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10931"/>And he rolled up the scroll <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“rolled up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> gave it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> back to the attendant and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“gave … back”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> sat down. And the eyes of everyone in the synagogue were looking intently at him.

verses.name: Luke 4:21
verses.text: And he began to say to them, “Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.”

verses.name: Luke 4:22
verses.text: And they were all speaking well of him, and were astonished at the gracious words that were coming out of his mouth. And they were saying, “Is this man not the son of Joseph?”

verses.name: Luke 4:23
verses.text: And he said to them, “Doubtless you will tell me this parable: ‘Physician, heal yourself!’ Whatever we have heard that took place in Capernaum, do here in your hometown also!”

verses.name: Luke 4:24
verses.text: And he said, “Truly I say to you that no prophet is acceptable in his <transChange type="added">own</transChange> hometown.

verses.name: Luke 4:25
verses.text: But in truth I say to you, there were many widows in Israel in the days of Elijah, when the sky was shut for three years and six months while a great famine took place over all the land.

verses.name: Luke 4:26
verses.text: And Elijah was sent to none of them, but only to Zarephath <transChange type="added">in the region</transChange> of Sidon, to a woman <transChange type="added">who was</transChange> a widow.

verses.name: Luke 4:27
verses.text: And there were many lepers in Israel in the time of the prophet Elisha, and none of them was made clean except Naaman the Syrian.”

verses.name: Luke 4:28
verses.text: And all <transChange type="added">those</transChange> in the synagogue were filled with anger <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>.

verses.name: Luke 4:29
verses.text: And they stood up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“stood up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> forced him out of the town and brought him up to the edge of the hill on which their town was built, so that they could throw him down the cliff.

verses.name: Luke 4:30
verses.text: But he passed through their midst <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“passed”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> went on his way.  <div eID="gen26307" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 4:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10932"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Teaches and Heals Many in Capernaum</title> <div sID="gen26308" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10932"/>And he came down to Capernaum, a town of Galilee, and was teaching them on the Sabbath.

verses.name: Luke 4:32
verses.text: And they were astounded at his teaching, because <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he spoke⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “his word was”</note> with authority.  <div eID="gen26308" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 4:33
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10933"/><div sID="gen26309" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10933"/>And in the synagogue there was a man who had the spirit of an unclean demon,<note placement="foot">Or “an unclean demonic spirit”</note> and he cried out with a loud voice,

verses.name: Luke 4:34
verses.text: “Ha! <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Leave us alone⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “what to us and to you”</note> Jesus the Nazarene! Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are—the Holy One of God!”

verses.name: Luke 4:35
verses.text: And Jesus rebuked him, saying, “Be silent and come out of him!” And <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“throwing … down”) which is understood as temporal</note> throwing him down in their midst, the demon came out of him without hurting him at all.

verses.name: Luke 4:36
verses.text: And amazement came upon <transChange type="added">them</transChange> all, and they began to talk<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to talk”)</note> with one another, saying, “What word<note placement="foot">Or “command”</note> <transChange type="added">is</transChange> this? For he commands the unclean spirits with authority and power, and they come out!”

verses.name: Luke 4:37
verses.text: And news about him went out into every place of the surrounding region.  <div eID="gen26309" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 4:38
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10934"/><div sID="gen26310" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10934"/>And <transChange type="added">after he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“set out”) which is understood as temporal</note> set out from the synagogue, he went into Simon’s house. And Simon’s mother-in-law was afflicted with a high fever, and they asked him on behalf of her.

verses.name: Luke 4:39
verses.text: And he stood over her <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“stood”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> rebuked the fever, and it left her. And immediately she got up and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“got up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> began to serve<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to serve”)</note> them.  <div eID="gen26310" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 4:40
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10935"/><div sID="gen26311" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10935"/>Now <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was setting”)</note> the sun was setting, all who had those who were sick with various diseases brought them to him, and placing his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> hands on every one of them, he healed them.

verses.name: Luke 4:41
verses.text: And demons also were coming out of many, crying out and saying, “You are the Son of God!” And he rebuked <transChange type="added">them</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and did not permit them to speak, because they knew that he was the Christ.<note placement="foot">Or “Messiah”</note>  <div eID="gen26311" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 4:42
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10936"/><div sID="gen26312" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10936"/>And <transChange type="added">when it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was”)</note> was day, he departed and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“departed”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> went to an isolated place. And the crowds were seeking him, and came to him and were trying to prevent him from departing from them.

verses.name: Luke 4:43
verses.text: But he said to them, “It is necessary <transChange type="added">for</transChange> me to proclaim the good news <transChange type="added">of</transChange> the kingdom of God to the other towns also, because I was sent for this <transChange type="added">purpose</transChange>.

verses.name: Luke 4:44
verses.text: And he was preaching in the synagogues of Judea.  <chapter eID="Luke.4"/>

verses.name: Luke 5:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10937"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Calls His First Disciples</title> <div sID="gen26313" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10937"/>Now it happened that while the crowd was pressing around him and hearing the word of God, he was standing beside the lake of Gennesaret,<note placement="foot">Another name for the Sea of Galilee</note>

verses.name: Luke 5:2
verses.text: and he saw two boats there beside the lake, but the fishermen had gotten out of them <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“had gotten out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> were washing their nets.

verses.name: Luke 5:3
verses.text: And he got into one of the boats, which was Simon’s, <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“got”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> asked him to put out from the land a little. And he sat down and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“sat down”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> began to teach<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to teach”)</note> the crowds from the boat.

verses.name: Luke 5:4
verses.text: And when he stopped speaking, he said to Simon, “Put out into the deep water and let down your nets for a catch.”

verses.name: Luke 5:5
verses.text: And Simon answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “Master, although we<note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“worked hard”) which is understood as concessive</note> worked hard through the whole night, we caught nothing. But at your word I will let down the nets.”

verses.name: Luke 5:6
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“did”) which is understood as temporal</note> did this, they caught a very large number of fish, and their nets began to tear.<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to tear”)</note>

verses.name: Luke 5:7
verses.text: And they signaled to their partners in the other boat to come <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“come”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> help them, and they came and filled both the boats so that they began to sink.

verses.name: Luke 5:8
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> Simon Peter fell down at Jesus’ knees, saying, “Depart from me, Lord, because I am <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a sinful man⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!”<note placement="foot">Literally “a man, a sinner”</note>

verses.name: Luke 5:9
verses.text: For amazement had seized him and all those <transChange type="added">who were</transChange> with him at the catch of fish that they had caught,

verses.name: Luke 5:10
verses.text: and so also <transChange type="added">were</transChange> James and John, the sons of Zebedee, who were business partners with Simon. And Jesus said to Simon, “Do not be afraid! From now on you will be catching people!”

verses.name: Luke 5:11
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“brought”) which is understood as temporal</note> brought their<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> boats to the land, they left everything and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“left”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> followed him.  <div eID="gen26313" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 5:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10938"/><title type="x-s">A Leper Cleansed</title> <div sID="gen26314" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10938"/>And it happened that while he was in one of the towns, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞there was⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “behold”</note> a man <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞covered with leprosy⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “full of leprosy”</note> And when he<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw Jesus, he fell down on his face and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“fell down”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> begged him, saying, “Lord, if you are willing, you are able to make me clean.”

verses.name: Luke 5:13
verses.text: And extending <transChange type="added">his</transChange><note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> hand he touched him, saying, “I am willing; be clean.” And immediately the leprosy went away from him.

verses.name: Luke 5:14
verses.text: And he ordered him, “Tell no one, but go <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“go”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> show yourself to the priest and bring the offering<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> for your cleansing just as Moses commanded, for a testimony to them.

verses.name: Luke 5:15
verses.text: But the report about him spread even more, and large crowds were gathering to hear <transChange type="added">him</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and to be healed of their illnesses.

verses.name: Luke 5:16
verses.text: But he himself was withdrawing in the wilderness and praying.  <div eID="gen26314" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 5:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10939"/><title type="x-s">A Paralytic Healed</title> <div sID="gen26315" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10939"/>And it happened that on one of the days as he was teaching, Pharisees and teachers of the law were sitting <transChange type="added">there</transChange> who <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞had come⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “were having come”</note> from every village of Galilee and Judea and <transChange type="added">from</transChange> Jerusalem, and the power of the Lord was <transChange type="added">there</transChange> in order <transChange type="added">for</transChange> him to heal.

verses.name: Luke 5:18
verses.text: And behold, men <transChange type="added">came</transChange> carrying on a stretcher a man who was paralyzed, and they were seeking to bring him in and place <transChange type="added">him</transChange><note placement="foot">Some manuscripts Some manuscripts include the pronoun “him” after “place”</note><note placement="foot">Since Greek routinely omits direct objects when they are clear from context, the pronoun is not necessary here in the Greek text, but it must be supplied in the English translation</note> before him.

verses.name: Luke 5:19
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“find”) which is understood as temporal</note> did not find a way to bring him in because of the crowd, they went up on the roof and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> let him down through the roof tiles with the stretcher into the midst <transChange type="added">of them</transChange>, in front of Jesus.

verses.name: Luke 5:20
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw their faith, he said, “Friend, your sins are forgiven you.”

verses.name: Luke 5:21
verses.text: And the scribes and the Pharisees began to reason, saying, “Who is this man who speaks blasphemies? Who is able to forgive sins except God alone?”

verses.name: Luke 5:22
verses.text: But Jesus, perceiving their thoughts, answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to them, “Why are you reasoning in your hearts?

verses.name: Luke 5:23
verses.text: Which is easier to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven you,’ or to say, ‘Get up and walk?’

verses.name: Luke 5:24
verses.text: But in order that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins,” he said to the one who was paralyzed, “I say to you, ‘Get up and pick up your stretcher <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“pick up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> go to your home.’ ”

verses.name: Luke 5:25
verses.text: And immediately he stood up before them, picked up what he had been lying on, <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participles (“stood up” and “picked up”) have been translated as finite verbs</note> went away to his home, glorifying God.

verses.name: Luke 5:26
verses.text: And amazement seized <transChange type="added">them</transChange> all, and they began to glorify<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to glorify”)</note> God. And they were filled with fear, saying, “We have seen wonderful things today!”  <div eID="gen26315" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 5:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10940"/><title type="x-s">Levi Called to Follow Jesus</title> <div sID="gen26316" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10940"/>And after these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, he went out and saw a tax collector <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞named⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by name”</note> Levi sitting at the tax booth, and he said to him, “Follow me!”

verses.name: Luke 5:28
verses.text: And leaving everything behind, he got up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“got up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> began to follow<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to follow”)</note> him.  <div eID="gen26316" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 5:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10941"/><div sID="gen26317" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10941"/>And Levi gave a great banquet for him in his house, and there was a large crowd of tax collectors and others who were reclining for the meal with them.

verses.name: Luke 5:30
verses.text: And the Pharisees and their scribes began to complain<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to complain”)</note> to his disciples, saying, “Why do you eat and drink with the tax collectors and sinners?”

verses.name: Luke 5:31
verses.text: And Jesus answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to them, “Those who are healthy do not have need of a physician, but those <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who are sick⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “having badly”</note>

verses.name: Luke 5:32
verses.text: I have not come to call the righteous but sinners to repentance.”  <div eID="gen26317" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 5:33
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10942"/><title type="x-s">On Fasting</title> <div sID="gen26318" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10942"/>And they said to him, “The disciples of John fast often and make prayers—likewise also the <transChange type="added">disciples</transChange><note placement="foot">*The word “disciples” is not in the Greek text but is implied</note> of the Pharisees—but yours are eating and drinking!”

verses.name: Luke 5:34
verses.text: So he<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> said<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “So Jesus said”</note> to them, “You are not able to make the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞bridegroom’s attendants⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sons of the bridal chamber”</note> fast as long as the bridegroom is with them, are you?<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here, indicated in the translation by the phrase “are you”</note>

verses.name: Luke 5:35
verses.text: But days will come, and when the bridegroom is taken away from them, then they will fast in those days.”

verses.name: Luke 5:36
verses.text: And he also told a parable to them: “No one tears a patch from a new garment <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“tears”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> puts it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> on an old garment. Otherwise, he will have torn the new also, and the old will not match the patch <transChange type="added">that is</transChange> from the new.

verses.name: Luke 5:37
verses.text: And no one pours new wine into old wineskins. Otherwise, the new wine will burst the wineskins, and it will be spilled and the wineskins will be destroyed.

verses.name: Luke 5:38
verses.text: But new wine must be put into new wineskins.

verses.name: Luke 5:39
verses.text: And no one <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“drinking”) which is understood as temporal</note> drinking old wine<note placement="foot">*The word “wine” is not in the Greek text but is implied</note> wants new, because he says, ‘The old is <transChange type="added">just</transChange> fine!’ ”  <chapter eID="Luke.5"/>

verses.name: Luke 6:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10943"/><title type="x-s">Plucking Grain on the Sabbath</title> <div sID="gen26319" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10943"/>Now it happened that on a Sabbath he went through the grain fields, and his disciples were picking and eating the heads of grain, rubbing <transChange type="added">them</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> in their<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> hands.

verses.name: Luke 6:2
verses.text: But some of the Pharisees said, “Why are you doing what is not permitted on the Sabbath?

verses.name: Luke 6:3
verses.text: And Jesus answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to them, “Have you not read this, what David did when he and those <transChange type="added">who were</transChange> with him were hungry—

verses.name: Luke 6:4
verses.text: how he entered into the house of God and took the bread of the presentation, which it is not permitted to eat (except the priests alone), <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> ate it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and gave it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to those with him?”

verses.name: Luke 6:5
verses.text: And he said to them, “The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”  <div eID="gen26319" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 6:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10944"/><title type="x-s">A Man with a Withered Hand Healed</title> <div sID="gen26320" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10944"/>Now it happened that on another Sabbath he entered into the synagogue and was teaching, and a man was there, and his right hand was withered.

verses.name: Luke 6:7
verses.text: So the scribes and the Pharisees were watching closely<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “were watching him closely”</note> to see if he would heal on the Sabbath, in order that they could find a reason<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to accuse him.

verses.name: Luke 6:8
verses.text: But he knew their thoughts and said to the man who had the withered hand, “Get up and stand in the middle,” and he got up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“get up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> stood there.

verses.name: Luke 6:9
verses.text: And Jesus said to them, “I ask you whether it is permitted on the Sabbath to do good or to do evil, to save a life or to destroy <transChange type="added">it</transChange>?”<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Luke 6:10
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“looking around”) which is understood as temporal</note> looking around at them all, he said to him, “Stretch out your hand,” and he did, and his hand was restored.

verses.name: Luke 6:11
verses.text: But they were filled with fury, and began discussing<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began discussing”)</note> with one another what they might do to Jesus.  <div eID="gen26320" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 6:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10945"/><title type="x-s">The Selection of the Twelve Apostles</title> <div sID="gen26321" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10945"/>Now it happened that in these days he went away to the mountain to pray, and was spending the whole night in prayer to God.

verses.name: Luke 6:13
verses.text: And when day came, he summoned his disciples and chose from them twelve, whom he also named apostles:

verses.name: Luke 6:14
verses.text: Simon (whom he also named Peter) and his brother Andrew, and James, and John, and Philip, and Bartholomew,

verses.name: Luke 6:15
verses.text: and Matthew, and Thomas, and James the <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Alphaeus, and Simon who was called the Zealot,

verses.name: Luke 6:16
verses.text: and Judas <transChange type="added">the son</transChange> of James, and Judas Iscariot, who became a traitor.  <div eID="gen26321" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 6:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10946"/><title type="x-s">The Sermon on the Plain: The Beatitudes</title> <div sID="gen26322" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10946"/>And he came down with them <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came down”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> stood on a level place, and a large crowd of his disciples and a great multitude of people from all of Judea and Jerusalem and the seacoast district of Tyre and Sidon,

verses.name: Luke 6:18
verses.text: who came to hear him and to be healed of their diseases, and those who were troubled by unclean spirits were cured.

verses.name: Luke 6:19
verses.text: And the whole crowd was seeking to touch him, because power was going out from him and healing <transChange type="added">them</transChange> all.  <div eID="gen26322" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 6:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10947"/><div sID="gen26323" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10947"/>And he lifted up his eyes to his disciples <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“lifted up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, <div eID="gen26323" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen26324"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26325"/>“Blessed <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the poor,<l eID="gen26325" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26326"/>because yours is the kingdom of God. <l eID="gen26326" level="2"/>

verses.name: Luke 6:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10948"/><l level="1" sID="gen26327"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10948"/>Blessed <transChange type="added">are</transChange> those who are hungry now,<l eID="gen26327" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26328"/>because you will be satisfied.<l eID="gen26328" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26329"/>Blessed <transChange type="added">are</transChange> those who weep now,<l eID="gen26329" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26330"/>Because you will laugh. <l eID="gen26330" level="2"/>

verses.name: Luke 6:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10949"/><l level="1" sID="gen26331"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10949"/>Blessed are you when people hate you, and when they exclude you and revile <transChange type="added">you</transChange> and spurn your name as evil on account of the Son of Man.

verses.name: Luke 6:23
verses.text: Rejoice in that day, and leap for joy, for behold, your reward <transChange type="added">is</transChange> great in heaven. For their fathers used to do the same <transChange type="added">things</transChange> to the prophets.<l eID="gen26331" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen26324"/> <title type="x-s">The Sermon on the Plain: Woes</title> <div sID="gen26332" type="x-p"/>  <div eID="gen26332" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 6:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10950"/><lg sID="gen26333"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26334"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10950"/>“But woe to you who are rich,<l eID="gen26334" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26335"/>because you have received your comfort. <l eID="gen26335" level="2"/>

verses.name: Luke 6:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10951"/><l level="1" sID="gen26336"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10951"/>Woe to you who are satisfied now,<l eID="gen26336" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26337"/>because you will be hungry.<l eID="gen26337" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26338"/>Woe, you who laugh now,<l eID="gen26338" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26339"/>because you will mourn and weep. <l eID="gen26339" level="2"/>

verses.name: Luke 6:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10952"/><l level="1" sID="gen26340"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10952"/>Woe whenever all people speak well of you,<l eID="gen26340" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26341"/>for their fathers used to do the same <transChange type="added">things</transChange> to the false prophets. <l eID="gen26341" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen26333"/>

verses.name: Luke 6:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10953"/><title type="x-s">The Sermon on the Plain: Love for Enemies</title> <div sID="gen26342" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10953"/>“But to you who are listening I say: Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you,

verses.name: Luke 6:28
verses.text: bless those who curse you, pray for those who mistreat you.

verses.name: Luke 6:29
verses.text: To the one who strikes you on the cheek, offer the other also, and from the one who takes away your cloak, do not withhold your tunic also.

verses.name: Luke 6:30
verses.text: Give to everyone who asks you, and from the one who takes away your things, do not ask for <transChange type="added">them back</transChange>.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Luke 6:31
verses.text: And just as you want people <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to do⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “would do”</note> to you, do <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the same⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “likewise”</note> to them.  <div eID="gen26342" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 6:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10954"/><div sID="gen26343" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10954"/>“And if you love those who love you, what kind of credit is <transChange type="added">that</transChange> to you? For even sinners love those who love them!

verses.name: Luke 6:33
verses.text: And if<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “For even if”</note> you do good to those who do good to you, what kind of credit is <transChange type="added">that</transChange> to you? Even the sinners do the same!

verses.name: Luke 6:34
verses.text: And if you lend <transChange type="added">to those</transChange> from whom you expect to receive <transChange type="added">back</transChange>, what kind of credit is <transChange type="added">that</transChange> to you? Even sinners lend to sinners, so that they may get back an equal <transChange type="added">amount</transChange>!

verses.name: Luke 6:35
verses.text: But love your enemies, and do good, and lend expecting back nothing, and your reward will be great, and you will be sons of the Most High, because he is kind to the ungrateful and wicked.

verses.name: Luke 6:36
verses.text: Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful!<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “also is merciful”</note>  <div eID="gen26343" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 6:37
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10955"/><title type="x-s">The Sermon on the Plain: On Judging Others</title> <div sID="gen26344" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10955"/>“And do not judge, and you will never be judged. And do not condemn, and you will never be condemned. Pardon, and you will be pardoned.

verses.name: Luke 6:38
verses.text: Give, and it will be given to you, a good measure—pressed down, shaken, overflowing—they will pour out into your lap. For with the measure by which you measure out, it will be measured out to you in return.”  <div eID="gen26344" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 6:39
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10956"/><div sID="gen26345" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10956"/>And he also told them a parable: “Surely a blind person cannot lead the blind, <transChange type="added">can he</transChange>?<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here, indicated in the translation by the phrase “can he”</note> Will they not both fall into a pit?

verses.name: Luke 6:40
verses.text: A disciple is not superior to <transChange type="added">his</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> teacher, but everyone, when he<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“is fully trained”) which is understood as temporal</note> is fully trained, will be like his teacher.

verses.name: Luke 6:41
verses.text: And why do you see the speck <transChange type="added">that is</transChange> in your brother’s eye, but do not notice the beam of wood <transChange type="added">that is</transChange> in your own eye?

verses.name: Luke 6:42
verses.text: How are you able to say to your brother, “Brother, allow <transChange type="added">me</transChange> to remove the speck <transChange type="added">that is</transChange> in your eye,” <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the participle (“see”) which is understood as temporal</note> you yourself do not see the beam of wood in your <transChange type="added">own</transChange> eye? Hypocrite! First remove the beam of wood from your <transChange type="added">own</transChange> eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck <transChange type="added">that is</transChange> in your brother’s eye!  <div eID="gen26345" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 6:43
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10957"/><title type="x-s">The Sermon on the Plain: Trees and Their Fruit</title> <div sID="gen26346" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10957"/>“For there is no good tree that produces bad fruit, nor on the other hand a bad tree that produces good fruit,

verses.name: Luke 6:44
verses.text: for each tree is known by its own fruit. For figs are not gathered from thorn plants, nor are grapes harvested from thorn bushes.

verses.name: Luke 6:45
verses.text: The good person out of the good treasury of his heart brings forth good, and the evil person out of <transChange type="added">his</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> evil treasury<note placement="foot">*The word “treasury” here is an understood repetition from earlier in the verse</note> brings forth evil. For out of the abundance of the heart his mouth speaks.  <div eID="gen26346" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 6:46
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10958"/><div sID="gen26347" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10958"/>“And why do you call me ‘Lord, Lord,’ and do not do what I tell <transChange type="added">you</transChange>?<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>  <div eID="gen26347" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 6:47
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10959"/><title type="x-s">The Sermon on the Plain: Two Houses and Two Foundations</title> <div sID="gen26348" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10959"/>“Everyone who comes to me and listens to my words and does them—I will show you what he is like:

verses.name: Luke 6:48
verses.text: he is like a man building a house, who dug and went down deep and laid the foundation on the rock. And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“came”)</note> a flood came, the river burst against that house and was not able to shake it, because it had been built well.

verses.name: Luke 6:49
verses.text: But the one who hears <transChange type="added">my words</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and does not do them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> is like a man who built a house on the ground without a foundation, which the river burst against, and immediately it collapsed—and the collapse of that house was great!”  <chapter eID="Luke.6"/>

verses.name: Luke 7:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10960"/><title type="x-s">A Centurion’s Slave Healed</title> <div sID="gen26349" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10960"/>After he had finished all his statements in the hearing of the people, he entered into Capernaum.

verses.name: Luke 7:2
verses.text: Now a certain centurion’s slave, who was esteemed by him, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞was sick⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “was having badly”</note> and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“was having”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> was about to die.

verses.name: Luke 7:3
verses.text: So <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard about Jesus, he sent Jewish elders to him, asking him that he would come and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“come”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> cure his slave.

verses.name: Luke 7:4
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“came”) which is understood as temporal</note> came to Jesus, they began imploring<note placement="foot">The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began imploring”)</note> him earnestly, saying, “He is worthy <transChange type="added">that</transChange> you grant this for him,

verses.name: Luke 7:5
verses.text: because he loves our nation and he himself built the synagogue for us.”

verses.name: Luke 7:6
verses.text: So Jesus went with them. Now by this time he was not far away from the house, <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“away”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> the centurion sent friends, saying to him, “Lord, do not trouble yourself, for I am not worthy that you should come in under my roof.

verses.name: Luke 7:7
verses.text: For this reason neither did I consider myself worthy to come to you. But say the word and my slave must be healed.

verses.name: Luke 7:8
verses.text: For I also am a man placed under authority, who has soldiers under me, and I say to this one, ‘Go!’ and he goes, and to another one, ‘Come!’ and he comes, and to my slave, ‘Do this!’ and he does <transChange type="added">it</transChange>.”<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>  <div eID="gen26349" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 7:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10961"/><div sID="gen26350" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10961"/>And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> Jesus heard these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, he marveled at him, and turning around to the crowd that was following him, he said, “I tell you, not even in Israel have I found such great faith!”

verses.name: Luke 7:10
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“returned”) which is understood as temporal</note> returned to the house, those who had been sent found the slave healthy.  <div eID="gen26350" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 7:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10962"/><title type="x-s">A Widow’s Son Raised</title> <div sID="gen26351" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10962"/>And it happened that on the next <transChange type="added">day</transChange> he went to a town called Nain, and his disciples and a large crowd went with him.

verses.name: Luke 7:12
verses.text: And as he approached the gate of the town, behold, a man who had died was being carried out, his mother’s only son, and she was a widow. And a large crowd from the town was with her.

verses.name: Luke 7:13
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> the Lord saw her, he had compassion for her and said to her, “Do not weep!”

verses.name: Luke 7:14
verses.text: And he came up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> touched the bier, and those who were carrying it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> stopped. And he said, “Young man, I say to you, get up!”

verses.name: Luke 7:15
verses.text: And the dead man sat up and began to speak, and he gave him to his mother.

verses.name: Luke 7:16
verses.text: And fear seized <transChange type="added">them</transChange> all, and they began to glorify<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to glorify”)</note> God, saying, “A great prophet has appeared among us!” and “God has visited to help his people!”

verses.name: Luke 7:17
verses.text: And this report about him went out in the whole of Judea and in all the surrounding region.  <div eID="gen26351" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 7:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10963"/><title type="x-s">A Question from John the Baptist</title> <div sID="gen26352" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10963"/>And his disciples reported to John about all these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>. And summoning a certain two of his disciples, John

verses.name: Luke 7:19
verses.text: sent <transChange type="added">them</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to the Lord,<note placement="foot">A number of significant manuscripts read “Jesus”</note> saying, “Are you the one who is to come, or should we look for another?”

verses.name: Luke 7:20
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“came”) which is understood as temporal</note> the men came to him, they said, “John the Baptist sent us to you, saying, ‘Are you the one who is to come, or should we look for another?’ ”

verses.name: Luke 7:21
verses.text: In that hour he healed many <transChange type="added">people</transChange> of diseases and suffering and evil spirits, and he granted sight to many blind <transChange type="added">people</transChange>.

verses.name: Luke 7:22
verses.text: And he answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to them, “Go and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“go”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> tell John what you have seen and heard: the blind receive sight, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear;<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “and the deaf hear”</note> the dead are raised, the poor have good news announced to them.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Luke 7:23
verses.text: And whoever is not offended by me is blessed.”  <div eID="gen26352" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 7:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10964"/><div sID="gen26353" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10964"/>And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“had departed”)</note> the messengers of John had departed, he began to speak to the crowds concerning John: “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?

verses.name: Luke 7:25
verses.text: But what did you go out to see? A man dressed in soft clothing? Behold, those who are in splendid clothing and luxury are in the royal palaces.

verses.name: Luke 7:26
verses.text: But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and even more than a prophet!

verses.name: Luke 7:27
verses.text: It is this man about whom it is written: <div eID="gen26353" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen26354"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26355"/>‘Behold, I am sending my messenger before your face,<l eID="gen26355" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26356"/>who will prepare your way before you.’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Mal.3.1">Mal 3:1; </reference>cf. <reference osisRef="Mark.1.2">Mark 1:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Matt.11.10">Matt 11:10</reference></note> <l eID="gen26356" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen26354"/>

verses.name: Luke 7:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10965"/><div sID="gen26357" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10965"/>I tell you, there is no one greater among <transChange type="added">those</transChange> born of women than John, but the one who is least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.

verses.name: Luke 7:29
verses.text: (And all the people, <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard this<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>—even the tax collectors—affirmed the righteousness of God, because they<note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had been baptized”) which is understood as causal</note> had been baptized <transChange type="added">with</transChange> the baptism of John,

verses.name: Luke 7:30
verses.text: but the Pharisees and the legal experts rejected the purpose of God for themselves, <transChange type="added">because they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“been baptized”) which is understood as causal</note> had not been baptized by him.)  <div eID="gen26357" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 7:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10966"/><div sID="gen26358" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10966"/>“To what then shall I compare the people of this generation, and what are they like?

verses.name: Luke 7:32
verses.text: They are like children sitting in the marketplace and calling out to one another, who say, <div eID="gen26358" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen26359"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26360"/>‘We played the flute for you and you did not dance;<l eID="gen26360" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26361"/>we sang a lament and you did not weep.’ <l eID="gen26361" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen26359"/>

verses.name: Luke 7:33
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10967"/><div sID="gen26362" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10967"/>For John the Baptist has come not eating bread or drinking wine, and you say, ‘He has a demon!’

verses.name: Luke 7:34
verses.text: The Son of Man has come eating and drinking, and you say, ‘Behold, a man <transChange type="added">who is</transChange> a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’

verses.name: Luke 7:35
verses.text: And wisdom is vindicated by all her children.”  <div eID="gen26362" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 7:36
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10968"/><title type="x-s">A Sinful Woman Anoints Jesus’ Feet</title> <div sID="gen26363" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10968"/>Now one of the Pharisees asked him to eat with him, and he entered into the house of the Pharisee <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“entered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> reclined at the table.

verses.name: Luke 7:37
verses.text: And behold, a woman in the town who was a sinner, <transChange type="added">when she</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“learned”) which is understood as temporal</note> learned that he was dining in the Pharisee’s house, brought an alabaster flask of perfumed oil,

verses.name: Luke 7:38
verses.text: and standing behind <transChange type="added">him</transChange> at his feet weeping, she began to wet his feet with <transChange type="added">her</transChange> tears and was wiping <transChange type="added">them</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> with the hair of her head and was kissing his feet and anointing them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> with the perfumed oil.

verses.name: Luke 7:39
verses.text: Now <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> the Pharisee who invited him saw this,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> he spoke to himself, saying, “If this man were a prophet, he would have known who and what kind of woman <transChange type="added">this is</transChange> who is touching him, that she is a sinner.”

verses.name: Luke 7:40
verses.text: And Jesus answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to him, “Simon, I have something to say to you.” And he said, “Teacher, say it.”<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Luke 7:41
verses.text: “There were two debtors <transChange type="added">who owed</transChange> a certain creditor. One owed five hundred denarii and the other fifty.

verses.name: Luke 7:42
verses.text: <transChange type="added">When</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“able”)</note> they were not able to repay him,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> he forgave the debts<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> of both. Now which of them will love him more?”

verses.name: Luke 7:43
verses.text: Simon answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “I suppose that <transChange type="added">it is the one</transChange> to whom he forgave more.” And he said to him, “You have judged correctly.”

verses.name: Luke 7:44
verses.text: And turning toward the woman, he said to Simon, “Do you see this woman? I entered into your house. You did not give me water for <transChange type="added">my</transChange> feet, but she wet my feet with <transChange type="added">her</transChange> tears and wiped <transChange type="added">them</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> with her hair.

verses.name: Luke 7:45
verses.text: You did not give me a kiss, but from the time I entered, she has not stopped kissing my feet.

verses.name: Luke 7:46
verses.text: You did not anoint my head with olive oil, but she anointed my feet with perfumed oil.

verses.name: Luke 7:47
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞For this reason⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “on account of which”</note> I tell you, her sins—<transChange type="added">which were</transChange> many—have been forgiven, for she loved much. But <transChange type="added">the one</transChange> to whom little is forgiven loves little.”

verses.name: Luke 7:48
verses.text: And he said to her, “Your sins are forgiven.”

verses.name: Luke 7:49
verses.text: And those who were reclining at the table with <transChange type="added">him</transChange> began to say among themselves, “Who is this who even forgives sins?”

verses.name: Luke 7:50
verses.text: And he said to the woman, “Your faith has saved you. Go in peace.”  <chapter eID="Luke.7"/>

verses.name: Luke 8:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10969"/><title type="x-s">Some Women Accompany Jesus</title> <div sID="gen26364" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10969"/>And it happened that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞afterward⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in what follows”</note> also he was going about from <transChange type="added">one</transChange> town and village <transChange type="added">to another</transChange> preaching and proclaiming the good news concerning the kingdom of God, and the twelve <transChange type="added">were</transChange> with him,

verses.name: Luke 8:2
verses.text: and some women who had been healed of evil spirits and diseases: Mary (who was called Magdalene), from whom seven demons had gone out,

verses.name: Luke 8:3
verses.text: and Joanna the wife of Chuza (Herod’s household manager), and Susanna, and many others who were helping to support them from their possessions.  <div eID="gen26364" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 8:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10970"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Sower</title> <div sID="gen26365" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10970"/>And <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was gathering”)</note> a large crowd was gathering and <transChange type="added">they</transChange> were going to him from town <transChange type="added">after town</transChange>, he spoke by means of a parable:

verses.name: Luke 8:5
verses.text: “The sower went out to sow his seed, and while he was sowing, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞some seed⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “some of which”</note> fell on the side of the path and was trampled under foot, and the birds of the sky devoured it.

verses.name: Luke 8:6
verses.text: And other <transChange type="added">seed</transChange> fell on the rock, and <transChange type="added">when it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“came up”) which is understood as temporal</note> came up, it withered, because it did not have moisture.

verses.name: Luke 8:7
verses.text: And other <transChange type="added">seed</transChange> fell in the midst of the thorn plants, and the thorn plants grew up with <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“grew up with”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> choked it.

verses.name: Luke 8:8
verses.text: And other <transChange type="added">seed</transChange> fell on the good soil, and <transChange type="added">when it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“came up”) which is understood as temporal</note> came up, it produced a hundred times as much grain.” As he<note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“said”) which is understood as temporal</note> said these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, he called out, “The one who has ears to hear, let him hear!”  <div eID="gen26365" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 8:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10971"/><title type="x-s">The Reason for the Parables</title> <div sID="gen26366" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10971"/>And his disciples asked him what this parable meant.

verses.name: Luke 8:10
verses.text: And he said, “To you it has been given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of God, but to the rest <transChange type="added">they are</transChange> in parables, so that <div eID="gen26366" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen26367"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26368"/>‘Seeing they may not see,<l eID="gen26368" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26369"/>and hearing they may not understand.’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.6.9">Isa 6:9</reference></note> <l eID="gen26369" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen26367"/>

verses.name: Luke 8:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10972"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Sower Interpreted</title> <div sID="gen26370" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10972"/>Now the parable means this: the seed is the word of God,

verses.name: Luke 8:12
verses.text: and those beside the path are the ones who have heard. Then the devil comes and takes away the word from their heart, so that they may not believe <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“believe”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> be saved.

verses.name: Luke 8:13
verses.text: And those on the rock <transChange type="added">are those</transChange> who receive the word with joy when they hear <transChange type="added">it</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and these do not have <transChange type="added">enough</transChange> root, who believe for a time and in a time of testing fall away.

verses.name: Luke 8:14
verses.text: And the <transChange type="added">seed</transChange> that fell into the thorn plants—these are the ones who hear and <transChange type="added">as they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“go along”) which is understood as temporal</note> go along are choked by the worries and riches and pleasures of life, and they do not bear fruit to maturity.

verses.name: Luke 8:15
verses.text: But the <transChange type="added">seed</transChange> on the good soil—these are the ones who, <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“hearing”) which is understood as temporal</note> hearing the word, hold fast to it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> with a noble and good heart, and bear fruit with patient endurance.  <div eID="gen26370" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 8:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10973"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Lamp</title> <div sID="gen26371" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10973"/>“And no one, <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“lighting”) which is understood as temporal</note> lighting a lamp, covers it with a jar or puts it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> under a bed, but puts it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> on a lampstand, so that those who come in can see the light.

verses.name: Luke 8:17
verses.text: For nothing is secret that will not become evident, and nothing hidden that will never be known and come to light.

verses.name: Luke 8:18
verses.text: Therefore consider how you listen, for whoever has, to him <transChange type="added">more</transChange> will be given, and whoever does not have, even what he thinks <transChange type="added">that he</transChange> has will be taken away from him.”  <div eID="gen26371" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 8:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10974"/><title type="x-s">Jesus’ Mother and Brothers</title> <div sID="gen26372" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10974"/>Now his mother and brothers came to him, and they were not able to meet with him because of the crowd.

verses.name: Luke 8:20
verses.text: And it was reported to him, “Your mother and your brothers are standing outside wanting to see you.”

verses.name: Luke 8:21
verses.text: But he answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to them, “These are my mother and my brothers—the ones who hear the word of God and do it.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>  <div eID="gen26372" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 8:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10975"/><title type="x-s">Calming of a Storm</title> <div sID="gen26373" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10975"/>Now it happened that on one of the days both he and his disciples got into a boat, and he said to them, “Let us cross over to the other side of the lake.” And they set sail,

verses.name: Luke 8:23
verses.text: and <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“were sailing”)</note> they were sailing, he fell asleep. And a storm of wind came down on the lake, and they were being swamped and were in danger.

verses.name: Luke 8:24
verses.text: And they came <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> woke him up, saying, “Master, master! We are perishing!” So he got up and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“got up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> rebuked the wind and the billowing waves of water and they ceased, and it became calm.

verses.name: Luke 8:25
verses.text: And he said to them, “Where <transChange type="added">is</transChange> your faith?” But they were afraid <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“were afraid”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> were astonished, saying to one another, “Who then is this, that he commands even the winds and the water and they obey him?”  <div eID="gen26373" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 8:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10976"/><title type="x-s">A Demon-possessed Gerasene Healed</title> <div sID="gen26374" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10976"/>And they sailed to the region of the Gerasenes, which is opposite Galilee.

verses.name: Luke 8:27
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“got out”) which is understood as temporal</note> he got out on the land, a certain man from the town met him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> who had demons and for a considerable time had not worn clothes and did not live in a house, but among the tombs.

verses.name: Luke 8:28
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw Jesus, he cried out, fell down before him, and said with a loud voice, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞What do I have to do with you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “what to me and to you”</note> Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg you, do not torment me!”

verses.name: Luke 8:29
verses.text: For he had commanded the unclean spirit to come out of the man. (For it had seized him many times, and he was bound with chains and shackles <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“was bound”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> was guarded, and breaking the bonds he would be driven by the demon into the deserted places.)

verses.name: Luke 8:30
verses.text: So Jesus asked him, “What is your name?” And he said, “Legion,” because many demons had entered into him.

verses.name: Luke 8:31
verses.text: And they began imploring<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began imploring”)</note> him that he would not order them to depart into the abyss.

verses.name: Luke 8:32
verses.text: Now there was a large herd of pigs feeding there on the hill, and they implored him that he would permit them to enter into those <transChange type="added">pigs</transChange>. And he permitted them.

verses.name: Luke 8:33
verses.text: So the demons came out of the man <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> entered into the pigs, and the herd rushed headlong down the steep slope into the lake and were drowned.

verses.name: Luke 8:34
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> the herdsmen saw what had happened, they fled and reported it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> in the town and in the countryside.

verses.name: Luke 8:35
verses.text: So they went out to see what had happened, and they came to Jesus and found the man from whom the demons had gone out sitting <transChange type="added">there</transChange> clothed and in his right mind, at the feet of Jesus, and they were afraid.

verses.name: Luke 8:36
verses.text: And those who had seen <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> reported to them how the man who had been demon-possessed had been healed.

verses.name: Luke 8:37
verses.text: And all the people of the surrounding region of the Gerasenes asked him to depart from them, because they had been seized with great fear. So he got into the boat <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“got”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> returned.

verses.name: Luke 8:38
verses.text: And the man from who the demons had gone out was begging him to stay with him, but he sent him away, saying,

verses.name: Luke 8:39
verses.text: “Return to your home and tell all that God has done for you.” And he went away, proclaiming throughout the whole town all that Jesus had done for him.  <div eID="gen26374" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 8:40
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10977"/><title type="x-s">A Woman Healed and a Daughter Raised</title> <div sID="gen26375" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10977"/>Now when Jesus returned, the crowd welcomed him, because they were all waiting for him.

verses.name: Luke 8:41
verses.text: And behold, a man <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who was named⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to whom the name”</note> Jairus came, and this man was a ruler of the synagogue. And he fell down at the feet of Jesus and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“fell down”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> began imploring<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began imploring”)</note> him to come to his house,

verses.name: Luke 8:42
