verses.text: because <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he had⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “there was to him”</note> an only daughter, about twelve years <transChange type="added">old</transChange>, and she was dying. <div eID="gen26375" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen26376" type="x-p"/> Now as he was going, the crowds were pressing against him.

verses.name: Luke 8:43
verses.text: And a woman who was <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞suffering from hemorrhages⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally, “with a flow of blood”</note> for twelve years (who, although she<note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had spent”) which is understood as concessive</note> had spent all her<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> assets on physicians, was not able to be healed by anyone)

verses.name: Luke 8:44
verses.text: came up behind <transChange type="added">him</transChange> <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> touched the edge of his cloak, and immediately <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞her hemorrhaging⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the flow of her blood”</note> stopped.

verses.name: Luke 8:45
verses.text: And Jesus said, “Who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the one who touched me?” And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“denied”)</note> all denied it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> Peter said, “Master, the crowds are pressing you hard and crowding you!”<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Luke 8:46
verses.text: But Jesus said, “Someone touched me, because I know power has gone out from me.”

verses.name: Luke 8:47
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> the woman saw that she did not escape notice, she came trembling and falling down before him. In the presence of all the people, she told for what reason she had touched him, and that she was healed immediately.

verses.name: Luke 8:48
verses.text: And he said to her, “Daughter, your faith has saved you. Go in peace.”  <div eID="gen26376" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 8:49
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10978"/><div sID="gen26377" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10978"/><transChange type="added">While</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“speaking”)</note> he was still speaking, someone came from the synagogue ruler’s <transChange type="added">house</transChange>, saying, “Your daughter is dead! Trouble the Teacher no longer!”

verses.name: Luke 8:50
verses.text: But Jesus, <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard this,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> replied to him, “Do not be afraid! Only believe, and she will be healed.”

verses.name: Luke 8:51
verses.text: Now <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“came”) which is understood as temporal</note> came to the house, he did not allow anyone to enter with him except Peter and John and James and the father and mother of the child.

verses.name: Luke 8:52
verses.text: And they were all weeping and mourning for her, but he said, “Do not weep! For she is not dead, but is sleeping.”

verses.name: Luke 8:53
verses.text: And they began laughing<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began laughing”)</note> at him, because they<note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“knew”) which is understood as causal</note> knew that she was dead.

verses.name: Luke 8:54
verses.text: But he took her hand <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> called, saying, “Child, get up.”

verses.name: Luke 8:55
verses.text: And her spirit returned, and she got up immediately, and he ordered <transChange type="added">something</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to be given to her to eat.

verses.name: Luke 8:56
verses.text: And her parents were astonished, but he ordered them to tell no one what had happened.  <chapter eID="Luke.8"/>

verses.name: Luke 9:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10979"/><title type="x-s">The Twelve Commissioned and Sent Out</title> <div sID="gen26378" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10979"/>And summoning the twelve, he gave them power and authority over all the demons and to cure diseases,

verses.name: Luke 9:2
verses.text: and he sent them out to proclaim the kingdom of God and to heal the sick.

verses.name: Luke 9:3
verses.text: And he said to them, “Take along nothing for the journey—neither a staff, nor a traveler’s bag, nor bread, nor money, nor to have two tunics apiece.

verses.name: Luke 9:4
verses.text: And into whatever house you enter, stay there and depart from there.

verses.name: Luke 9:5
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">as for</transChange> all those who do not welcome you—<transChange type="added">when you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“depart”) which is understood as temporal</note> depart from that town, shake off the dust from your feet for a testimony against them.”

verses.name: Luke 9:6
verses.text: So they departed <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“departed”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> went throughout the villages, proclaiming the good news and healing everywhere.  <div eID="gen26378" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 9:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10980"/><title type="x-s">Herod Perplexed About Jesus</title> <div sID="gen26379" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10980"/>Now Herod the tetrarch heard about all that was happening, and he was greatly perplexed, because it was said by some that John has been raised from the dead,

verses.name: Luke 9:8
verses.text: and by some that Elijah had appeared, and others that some prophet of ancient times had risen.

verses.name: Luke 9:9
verses.text: And Herod said, “John I beheaded, but who is this about whom I hear such things?” And he was wanting to see him.  <div eID="gen26379" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 9:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10981"/><title type="x-s">The Feeding of Five Thousand</title> <div sID="gen26380" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10981"/>And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“returned”) which is understood as temporal</note> returned, the apostles described to him all that they had done. And he took them along and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took … along”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> withdrew privately to a town called Bethsaida.

verses.name: Luke 9:11
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“found out”) which is understood as temporal</note> the crowds found out, they followed him, and welcoming them, he began to speak<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to speak”)</note> to them about the kingdom of God, and he cured those who had need of healing.

verses.name: Luke 9:12
verses.text: Now the day began to be far spent, and the twelve came up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to him, “Send away the crowd so that they can go into the surrounding villages and farms to obtain lodging and find provisions, because we are here in a desolate place.

verses.name: Luke 9:13
verses.text: But he said to them, “You give them <transChange type="added">something</transChange> to eat!” And they said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞We have no⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “there is not to us”</note> more than five loaves and two fish, unless perhaps we go and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“go”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> purchase food for all these people.”

verses.name: Luke 9:14
verses.text: (For there were about five thousand men.) So he said to his disciples, “Have them sit down in groups of about fifty each.”

verses.name: Luke 9:15
verses.text: And they did so, and had <transChange type="added">them</transChange> all sit down.

verses.name: Luke 9:16
verses.text: And taking the five loaves and the two fish, <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied before the participle (“looking up”) in keeping with English style</note> looking up to heaven, he gave thanks and broke them and began giving<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began giving”)</note> them<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to speak”)</note> to the disciples to set before the crowd.

verses.name: Luke 9:17
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">they</transChange> all ate and were satisfied, and what was left over was picked up by them—twelve baskets of broken pieces.  <div eID="gen26380" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 9:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10982"/><title type="x-s">Peter’s Confession</title> <div sID="gen26381" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10982"/>And it happened that while he was praying alone, the disciples were with him. And he asked them, saying, “Who do the crowds say <transChange type="added">that</transChange> I am?”

verses.name: Luke 9:19
verses.text: And they answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “John the Baptist, but others, Elijah, and others, that one of the ancient prophets has risen.”

verses.name: Luke 9:20
verses.text: And he said to them, “But who do you say <transChange type="added">that</transChange> I am?” And Peter answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “The Christ of God.”  <div eID="gen26381" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 9:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10983"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Predicts His Death and Resurrection</title> <div sID="gen26382" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10983"/>But he warned <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“warned”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> commanded them to tell this to no one,

verses.name: Luke 9:22
verses.text: saying, “It is necessary <transChange type="added">for</transChange> the Son of Man to suffer many <transChange type="added">things</transChange> and to be rejected by the elders and chief priests and scribes, and to be killed, and to be raised on the third day.  <div eID="gen26382" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 9:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10984"/><title type="x-s">Taking Up One’s Cross to Follow Jesus</title> <div sID="gen26383" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10984"/>And he said to <transChange type="added">them</transChange> all, “If anyone wants to come after me, he must deny himself and take up his cross every day and follow me.

verses.name: Luke 9:24
verses.text: For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life on account of me, this person will save it.

verses.name: Luke 9:25
verses.text: For what is a person benefited <transChange type="added">if he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “if” is supplied as a component of the participle (“gains”) which is understood as conditional</note> gains the whole world but loses or forfeits himself?

verses.name: Luke 9:26
verses.text: For whoever is ashamed of me and my words, the Son of Man will be ashamed of this person when he comes in his glory and the <transChange type="added">glory</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “glory” is an understood repetition of the same word earlier in this verse</note> of the Father and of the holy angels.

verses.name: Luke 9:27
verses.text: But I tell you truly, there are some of those standing here who will never experience death until they see the kingdom of God.”  <div eID="gen26383" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 9:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10985"/><title type="x-s">The Transfiguration</title> <div sID="gen26384" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10985"/>Now it happened that about eight days after these words, he took along Peter and John and James <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took along”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> went up on the mountain to pray.

verses.name: Luke 9:29
verses.text: And as he was praying, the appearance of his face became different, and his clothing <transChange type="added">became</transChange> white, gleaming like lightning.<note placement="foot">Or “became brilliant as light”; or “became dazzling white”</note>

verses.name: Luke 9:30
verses.text: And behold, two men were talking with him, who were Moses and Elijah,

verses.name: Luke 9:31
verses.text: who appeared in glory <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“appeared”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> were speaking about his departure which he was about to fulfill<note placement="foot">Or “to accomplish”</note> in Jerusalem.  <div eID="gen26384" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 9:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10986"/><div sID="gen26385" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10986"/>Now Peter and those with him were <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞very sleepy⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “burdened with sleep”</note> but when they<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“became fully awake”) which is understood as temporal</note> became fully awake, they saw his glory and the two men who were standing with him.

verses.name: Luke 9:33
verses.text: And it happened that as they were going away from him, Peter said to Jesus, “Master, it is good <transChange type="added">for</transChange> us to be here. And let us make three shelters, one for you and one for Moses and one for Elijah,” not knowing what he was saying.

verses.name: Luke 9:34
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“saying”)</note> he was saying these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, a cloud came and overshadowed them, and they were afraid as they entered into the cloud.

verses.name: Luke 9:35
verses.text: And a voice came from the cloud, saying, “This is my Son, <transChange type="added">my</transChange> Chosen One. Listen to him!”

verses.name: Luke 9:36
verses.text: And after the voice had occurred, Jesus was found alone. And they kept silent and told no one in those days anything of what they had seen.  <div eID="gen26385" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 9:37
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10987"/><title type="x-s">A Demon-possessed Boy Healed</title> <div sID="gen26386" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10987"/>Now it happened that on the next day, <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“had come down”)</note> they had come down from the mountain, a large crowd met him.

verses.name: Luke 9:38
verses.text: And behold, a man from the crowd cried out, saying, “Teacher, I beg you to look with concern on my son, because he is my only <transChange type="added">son</transChange>!

verses.name: Luke 9:39
verses.text: And behold, a spirit seizes him and suddenly he screams, and it convulses him with foam and rarely withdraws from him, battering him severely.

verses.name: Luke 9:40
verses.text: And I begged your disciples that they would expel it, and they were not able <transChange type="added">to do so</transChange>.”

verses.name: Luke 9:41
verses.text: So Jesus answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “O unbelieving and perverted generation! <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞How long⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “until when”</note> will I be with you and put up with you? Bring your son here!”

verses.name: Luke 9:42
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“approaching”)</note> he was still approaching, the demon threw him down and convulsed him.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> But Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit and healed the boy, and gave him back to his father.

verses.name: Luke 9:43
verses.text: And they were all astounded at the impressiveness of God. <div eID="gen26386" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">Jesus Predicts His Suffering</title> <div sID="gen26387" type="x-p"/> But <transChange type="added">while they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“marveling”)</note> were all marveling at all <transChange type="added">the things</transChange> that he was doing, he said to his disciples,

verses.name: Luke 9:44
verses.text: “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞You take these words to heart⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “you put these words into your ears”</note> for the Son of Man is about to be betrayed into the hands of men.”

verses.name: Luke 9:45
verses.text: But they did not understand this statement, and it was concealed from them so that they could not understand it. And they were afraid to ask him about this statement.  <div eID="gen26387" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 9:46
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10988"/><title type="x-s">The Question About Who Is Greatest</title> <div sID="gen26388" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10988"/>And an argument developed among them as to who of them might be greatest.

verses.name: Luke 9:47
verses.text: But Jesus, <transChange type="added">because he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“knew”) which is understood as causal</note> knew the thoughts of their hearts, took hold of a child and had him stand beside him

verses.name: Luke 9:48
verses.text: and said to them, “Whoever welcomes this child in my name welcomes me, and whoever welcomes me welcomes the one who sent me. For the one who is least among you all—this one is great.”  <div eID="gen26388" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 9:49
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10989"/><title type="x-s">Whoever Is Not Against Us Is for Us</title> <div sID="gen26389" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10989"/>And John answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “Master, we saw someone expelling demons in your name, and we tried to prevent him, because he does not follow in company with us.”

verses.name: Luke 9:50
verses.text: But Jesus said to him, “Do not prevent <transChange type="added">him</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> because whoever is not against you is for you.”  <div eID="gen26389" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 9:51
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10990"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Rejected in a Samaritan Village</title> <div sID="gen26390" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10990"/>Now it happened that when the days were approaching <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞for him to be taken up⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “of his taking up”</note> he set his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> face to go to Jerusalem.

verses.name: Luke 9:52
verses.text: And he sent messengers before <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “his face”</note> and they went and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> entered into a village of the Samaritans in order to prepare for him.

verses.name: Luke 9:53
verses.text: And they did not welcome him because <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he was determined to go⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “his face was going”</note> to Jerusalem.

verses.name: Luke 9:54
verses.text: Now <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> the disciples James and John saw it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> they said, “Lord, do you want us to call fire to come down from heaven and consume them?”

verses.name: Luke 9:55
verses.text: But he turned around <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“turned around”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> rebuked them,

verses.name: Luke 9:56
verses.text: and they proceeded to another village.  <div eID="gen26390" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 9:57
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10991"/><title type="x-s">Would-be Followers</title> <div sID="gen26391" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10991"/>And <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“were going”)</note> they were traveling on the road, someone said to him, “I will follow you wherever you go!”

verses.name: Luke 9:58
verses.text: And Jesus said to him, “Foxes have dens and birds of the sky <transChange type="added">have</transChange> nests, but the Son of Man has no place to lay <transChange type="added">his</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> head.”

verses.name: Luke 9:59
verses.text: And he said to another, “Follow me!” But he said, “Lord, first allow me to go <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“go”) has been translated as an infinitive</note> bury my father.”

verses.name: Luke 9:60
verses.text: But he said to him, “Leave the dead to bury their own dead! But you go <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“go”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> proclaim the kingdom of God.”

verses.name: Luke 9:61
verses.text: And another <transChange type="added">person</transChange> also said, “I will follow you, Lord, but first allow me to say farewell to those in my house.”

verses.name: Luke 9:62
verses.text: But Jesus said,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “said to him”</note> “No one who puts his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> hand on the plow and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God!”  <chapter eID="Luke.9"/>

verses.name: Luke 10:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10992"/><title type="x-s">The Seventy-Two Appointed and Sent Out</title> <div sID="gen26392" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10992"/>And after these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, the Lord also<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts omit “also”</note> appointed seventy-two others and sent them out two by two before <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “his presence”</note> into every town and place where he was about to go.

verses.name: Luke 10:2
verses.text: And he said to them, “The harvest <transChange type="added">is</transChange> plentiful, but the workers <transChange type="added">are</transChange> few. Therefore ask the Lord of the harvest that he send out workers into his harvest.

verses.name: Luke 10:3
verses.text: Go! Behold, I am sending you out like lambs in the midst of wolves!

verses.name: Luke 10:4
verses.text: Do not carry a money bag or a traveler’s bag or sandals, and greet no one along the road.

verses.name: Luke 10:5
verses.text: And into whatever house you enter, first say, “Peace <transChange type="added">be</transChange> to this household!”

verses.name: Luke 10:6
verses.text: And if a son of peace is there, your peace will rest on him. But if not, it will return to you.

verses.name: Luke 10:7
verses.text: And remain in the same house, eating and drinking <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞whatever they provide⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the things from them”</note> for the worker <transChange type="added">is</transChange> worthy of his pay. Do not move from house to house.

verses.name: Luke 10:8
verses.text: And into whatever town you enter and they welcome you, eat <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞whatever is⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the things”</note> set before you,

verses.name: Luke 10:9
verses.text: and heal the sick in it, and say to them, “The kingdom of God has come near to you.”

verses.name: Luke 10:10
verses.text: But into whatever town you enter and they do not welcome you, go out into its streets <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“go out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> say,

verses.name: Luke 10:11
verses.text: “Even the dust of your town that clings to our feet we wipe off against you! Nevertheless know this: that the kingdom of God has come near!”<note placement="foot">Or “has come”</note>

verses.name: Luke 10:12
verses.text: I tell you that it will be more bearable on that day for Sodom than for that town!  <div eID="gen26392" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 10:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10993"/><div sID="gen26393" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10993"/>Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the miracles that were done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes!

verses.name: Luke 10:14
verses.text: But it will be more bearable for Tyre and for Sidon in the judgment than for you!

verses.name: Luke 10:15
verses.text: And you, Capernaum, will you be exalted to heaven? No! You will be brought down to Hades!

verses.name: Luke 10:16
verses.text: The one who listens to you listens to me, and the one who rejects you rejects me. But the one who rejects me rejects the one who sent me.”  <div eID="gen26393" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 10:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10994"/><div sID="gen26394" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10994"/>And the seventy-two returned with joy, saying, “Lord, even the demons are subject to us in your name!”

verses.name: Luke 10:18
verses.text: So he said to them, “I saw Satan falling like lightning from heaven.

verses.name: Luke 10:19
verses.text: Behold, I have given you the authority to tread on snakes and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing will ever harm you.

verses.name: Luke 10:20
verses.text: Nevertheless, do not rejoice in this, that the spirits are subject to you, but rejoice that your names are inscribed in heaven.”  <div eID="gen26394" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 10:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10995"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Rejoices and Prays</title> <div sID="gen26395" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10995"/>At <transChange type="added">that</transChange> same time he rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and said, “I praise you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that you have hidden these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> from the wise and intelligent and have revealed them to young children. Yes, Father, for this was pleasing before you.

verses.name: Luke 10:22
verses.text: All <transChange type="added">things</transChange> have been handed over to me by my Father, and no one knows who the Son is except the Father and who the Father is except the Son, and <transChange type="added">anyone</transChange> to whom the Son wants to reveal <transChange type="added">him</transChange>.”<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>  <div eID="gen26395" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 10:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10996"/><div sID="gen26396" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10996"/>And turning to the disciples, he said privately, “Blessed <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the eyes that see <transChange type="added">the things</transChange> which you see!

verses.name: Luke 10:24
verses.text: For I tell you that many prophets and kings desired to see <transChange type="added">the things</transChange> which you see, and did not see <transChange type="added">them</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and to hear the things which you hear, and did not hear them.”<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>  <div eID="gen26396" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 10:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10997"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Good Samaritan</title> <div sID="gen26397" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10997"/>And behold, a certain legal expert stood up to test him, saying, “Teacher, what must I do so that I will inherit eternal life?”

verses.name: Luke 10:26
verses.text: And he said to him, “What is written in the law? How do you read <transChange type="added">it</transChange>?”<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Luke 10:27
verses.text: And he answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “You shall love the Lord your God from all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your strength, and with all your mind,<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Deut.6.5">Deut 6:5</reference></note> and your neighbor as yourself.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Lev.19.18">Lev 19:18</reference></note>

verses.name: Luke 10:28
verses.text: And he said to him, “You have answered correctly. Do this and you will live.”  <div eID="gen26397" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 10:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10998"/><div sID="gen26398" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10998"/>But he, wanting to justify himself, said to Jesus, “And who is my neighbor?”

verses.name: Luke 10:30
verses.text: And<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts omit “and”</note> Jesus replied and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“replied”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and fell into the hands of robbers, who both stripped him and beat him.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> After<note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“inflicting blows on”) which is understood as temporal</note> inflicting blows on him,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> they went away, leaving him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> half dead.

verses.name: Luke 10:31
verses.text: Now by coincidence a certain priest was going down on that road, and <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw him, he passed by on the opposite side.

verses.name: Luke 10:32
verses.text: And in the same way also a Levite, <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“came”) which is understood as temporal</note> came down to the place<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “who happened by the place, when he came up to him”</note> and saw him,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> passed by on the opposite side.

verses.name: Luke 10:33
verses.text: But a certain Samaritan who was traveling came up to him and, <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw him,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> had compassion.

verses.name: Luke 10:34
verses.text: And he came up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> bandaged his wounds, pouring on olive oil and wine, and he put him on his own animal and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“put”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> brought him to an inn and took care of him.

verses.name: Luke 10:35
verses.text: And on the next day, he took out two denarii <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> gave them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note><note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “he took out and gave two denarii”</note> to the innkeeper, and said, “Take care of him, and whatever you spend in addition, I will repay to you when I return.

verses.name: Luke 10:36
verses.text: Which of these three do you suppose became a neighbor of the man who fell among the robbers?”

verses.name: Luke 10:37
verses.text: So he said, “The one who showed mercy to him.” And Jesus said to him, “You go and do likewise.”  <div eID="gen26398" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 10:38
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10999"/><title type="x-s">Martha and Mary</title> <div sID="gen26399" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10999"/>Now as they traveled along, he entered into a certain village. And a certain woman <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞named⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by name”</note> Martha welcomed him.<note placement="foot">Most manuscripts add some form of the location such as “into her house” but there is considerable variation in the exact wording, so the shorter reading is preferred</note>

verses.name: Luke 10:39
verses.text: And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞she had⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “this was”</note> a sister named Mary, who also sat at the feet of Jesus<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “of the Lord”</note> and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“sat”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> was listening to his teaching.

verses.name: Luke 10:40
verses.text: But Martha was distracted with much preparation, so she approached <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“approached”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “Lord, is it not a concern to you that my sister has left me alone to make preparations? Then tell her that she should help me!”

verses.name: Luke 10:41
verses.text: But the Lord answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to her, “Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many <transChange type="added">things</transChange>!

verses.name: Luke 10:42
verses.text: But few <transChange type="added">things</transChange> are necessary, or <transChange type="added">only</transChange> one <transChange type="added">thing</transChange>,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “But one thing is necessary”</note> for Mary has chosen the better part, which will not be taken away from her.”  <chapter eID="Luke.10"/>

verses.name: Luke 11:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11000"/><title type="x-s">How to Pray</title> <div sID="gen26400" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11000"/>And it happened that while he was in a certain place praying, when he stopped a certain one of his disciples said to him, “Lord, teach us to pray, just as John also taught his disciples.”

verses.name: Luke 11:2
verses.text: And he said to them, “When you pray, say, <div eID="gen26400" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen26401"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26402"/>“Father,<l eID="gen26402" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26403"/>may your name be treated as holy.<l eID="gen26403" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26404"/>May your kingdom come. <l eID="gen26404" level="1"/>

verses.name: Luke 11:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11001"/><l level="1" sID="gen26405"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11001"/>Give us each day our daily bread. <l eID="gen26405" level="1"/>

verses.name: Luke 11:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11002"/><l level="1" sID="gen26406"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11002"/>And forgive us our sins,<l eID="gen26406" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26407"/>for we ourselves also forgive everyone who is indebted to us.<l eID="gen26407" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26408"/>And do not lead us into temptation.” <l eID="gen26408" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen26401"/>

verses.name: Luke 11:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11003"/><title type="x-s">Ask, Seek, Knock</title> <div sID="gen26409" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11003"/>And he said to them, “Who of you will have a friend, and will go to him at midnight and say to him, ‘Friend, lend me three loaves,

verses.name: Luke 11:6
verses.text: because a friend of mine has come to me on a journey, and I do not have anything to set before him.’

verses.name: Luke 11:7
verses.text: And that one will answer from inside <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“will answer”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> say, ‘Do not cause me trouble! The door has already been shut and my children are with me in bed! I am not able to get up to give you anything.’<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Luke 11:8
verses.text: I tell you, even if he does not give him <transChange type="added">anything</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> after he<note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“gets up”) which is understood as temporal</note> gets up because he is his friend, at any rate because of his impudence<note placement="foot">Or “shamelessness”; some translate as “persistence” based on the context, though this is not the normal meaning of the word</note> he will get up and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“will get up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> give him whatever he needs.  <div eID="gen26409" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 11:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11004"/><div sID="gen26410" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11004"/>And I tell you, ask and it will be given to you; seek and you will find; knock and it will be opened for you.

verses.name: Luke 11:10
verses.text: For everyone who asks receives, and the one who seeks finds, and to the one who knocks it will be opened.

verses.name: Luke 11:11
verses.text: But what father from among you, <transChange type="added">if his</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> son will ask for a fish, instead of a fish will give him a snake?

verses.name: Luke 11:12
verses.text: Or also, <transChange type="added">if</transChange> he will ask for an egg, will give him a scorpion?

verses.name: Luke 11:13
verses.text: Therefore if you, <transChange type="added">although you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“are”) which is understood as concessive</note> are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will the Father from heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him?”  <div eID="gen26410" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 11:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11005"/><title type="x-s">A House Divided Cannot Stand</title> <div sID="gen26411" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11005"/>And he was expelling a mute demon.<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “a demon, and it was mute”</note> Now it happened that when<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“came out”)</note> the demon came out, the man who had been mute spoke, and the crowds were astonished.

verses.name: Luke 11:15
verses.text: But some of them said, “By Beelzebul the ruler of demons he expels demons!”

verses.name: Luke 11:16
verses.text: And others, <transChange type="added">in order to</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “in order to” is supplied as a component of the participle (“test”) which is understood as purpose</note> test him,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> were demanding from him a sign from heaven.

verses.name: Luke 11:17
verses.text: But he, knowing their thoughts, said to them, “Every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a divided household⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “house against house”</note> falls.

verses.name: Luke 11:18
verses.text: So if Satan also is divided against himself, how will his kingdom stand? For you say <transChange type="added">that</transChange> I expel demons by Beelzebul.

verses.name: Luke 11:19
verses.text: But if I expel demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons expel <transChange type="added">them</transChange>?<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> For this <transChange type="added">reason</transChange> they will be your judges!

verses.name: Luke 11:20
verses.text: But if I expel demons by the finger of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you!

verses.name: Luke 11:21
verses.text: When a strong man, fully armed, guards his own palace, his possessions are <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞safe⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “in peace”</note>

verses.name: Luke 11:22
verses.text: But when a stronger man attacks him <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“attacks”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> conquers him, he takes away his full armor in which he trusted and distributes his plunder.

verses.name: Luke 11:23
verses.text: The one who is not with me is against me, and the one who does not gather with me scatters.  <div eID="gen26411" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 11:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11006"/><title type="x-s">An Unclean Spirit Returns</title> <div sID="gen26412" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11006"/>“Whenever an unclean spirit has gone out of a person, it travels through waterless places searching for rest, and does not find <transChange type="added">it</transChange>.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> It says,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “Then it says”</note> ‘I will return to my house from which I came out.’

verses.name: Luke 11:25
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“arrives”) which is understood as temporal</note> arrives it finds the house<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> swept and put in order.

verses.name: Luke 11:26
verses.text: Then it goes and brings along seven other spirits more evil than itself, and <transChange type="added">they</transChange> go in <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“go in”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> live there. And the last <transChange type="added">state</transChange> of that person becomes worse than the first!”  <div eID="gen26412" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 11:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11007"/><div sID="gen26413" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11007"/>Now it happened that as he said these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, a certain woman from the crowd raised <transChange type="added">her</transChange> voice <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“raised”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to him, “Blessed <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the womb that bore you, and <transChange type="added">the</transChange> breasts <transChange type="added">at</transChange> which you nursed!”

verses.name: Luke 11:28
verses.text: But he said, “On the contrary, blessed <transChange type="added">are</transChange> those who hear the word of God and follow <transChange type="added">it</transChange>!”<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>  <div eID="gen26413" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 11:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11008"/><title type="x-s">The Sign of Jonah</title> <div sID="gen26414" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11008"/>And <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“were increasing”)</note> the crowds were increasing, he began to say, “This generation is an evil generation! It demands a sign, and no sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah!

verses.name: Luke 11:30
verses.text: For just as Jonah became a sign to the Ninevites, so also the Son of Man will be to this generation.

verses.name: Luke 11:31
verses.text: The queen of the south will rise up at the judgment with the people of this generation and condemn them, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and behold, <transChange type="added">something</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “something” is supplied in the translation because the adjective is neuter gender</note> greater than Solomon <transChange type="added">is</transChange> here!

verses.name: Luke 11:32
verses.text: The people of Nineveh will stand up at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they repented at the proclamation of Jonah, and behold, <transChange type="added">something</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “something” is supplied in the translation because the adjective is neuter gender</note> greater than Jonah <transChange type="added">is</transChange> here!  <div eID="gen26414" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 11:33
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11009"/><title type="x-s">Light and Darkness</title> <div sID="gen26415" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11009"/>“No one <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“lighting”) which is understood as temporal</note> lighting a lamp puts it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> in a cellar or under a bushel basket, but on a lampstand, so that those who come in can see the light.

verses.name: Luke 11:34
verses.text: Your eye is the lamp of the body. When your eye is sincere, your whole body is full of light also. But when it is evil, your body <transChange type="added">is</transChange> dark also.

verses.name: Luke 11:35
verses.text: Therefore pay careful attention <transChange type="added">that</transChange> the light in you is not darkness!

verses.name: Luke 11:36
verses.text: If therefore your whole body <transChange type="added">is</transChange> full of light, not having any part dark, it will be completely full of light, as when the lamp with <transChange type="added">its</transChange> light gives light to you.”  <div eID="gen26415" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 11:37
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11010"/><title type="x-s">Pharisees and Legal Experts Denounced</title> <div sID="gen26416" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11010"/>And as he was speaking, a Pharisee asked him <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to have a meal⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “that he would have a meal”</note> with him, and he went in and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went in”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> reclined at table.

verses.name: Luke 11:38
verses.text: And the Pharisee, <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> was astonished that he did not first wash before the meal.

verses.name: Luke 11:39
verses.text: But the Lord said to him, “Now you Pharisees cleanse the outside of the cup and of the dish, but your inside is full of greediness and wickedness.

verses.name: Luke 11:40
verses.text: Fools! Did not the one who made the outside make the inside also?

verses.name: Luke 11:41
verses.text: But give <transChange type="added">as</transChange> charitable giving the things that are within, and behold, everything is clean for you.  <div eID="gen26416" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 11:42
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11011"/><div sID="gen26417" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11011"/>“But woe to you, Pharisees, because you pay a tenth of mint and rue and every garden herb, and neglect justice and love for God! But it was necessary to do these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> without neglecting those things also.

verses.name: Luke 11:43
verses.text: Woe to you, Pharisees, because you love the best seat in the synagogues and the greetings in the marketplaces!

verses.name: Luke 11:44
verses.text: Woe to you, because you are like unmarked graves, and the people who walk over <transChange type="added">them</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> do not know it!<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>  <div eID="gen26417" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 11:45
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11012"/><div sID="gen26418" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11012"/>And one of the legal experts answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to him, “Teacher, when you<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“say”) which is understood as temporal</note> say these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, you insult us also!”

verses.name: Luke 11:46
verses.text: So he said, “Woe to you also, legal experts, because you load people <transChange type="added">with</transChange> burdens hard to bear, and <transChange type="added">you</transChange> yourselves do not touch the burdens with one of your fingers!

verses.name: Luke 11:47
verses.text: Woe to you, because you build the tombs of the prophets, and your fathers killed them!

verses.name: Luke 11:48
verses.text: As a result you are witnesses, and you approve of the deeds of your fathers, because they killed them and you build <transChange type="added">their tombs</transChange>!<note placement="foot">A large number of later manuscripts add the words “their tombs” here, with variations of wording; although the words are not likely to be original, it is necessary to supply them in keeping with English style</note>

verses.name: Luke 11:49
verses.text: For this <transChange type="added">reason</transChange> also the wisdom of God said, ‘I will send to them prophets and apostles, and <transChange type="added">some</transChange> of them they will kill and persecute,’

verses.name: Luke 11:50
verses.text: so that the blood of all the prophets that has been shed from the foundation of the world may be required of this generation,

verses.name: Luke 11:51
verses.text: from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah, who perished between the altar and the temple building.<note placement="foot">Literally “the house,” here a reference to the temple</note> Yes, I tell you, it will be required of this generation!

verses.name: Luke 11:52
verses.text: Woe to you, legal experts, because you have taken away the key to knowledge! You did not enter yourselves, and you hindered those who were entering!”  <div eID="gen26418" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 11:53
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11013"/><div sID="gen26419" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11013"/>And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“departed”)</note> he departed from there, the scribes and the Pharisees began to be terribly hostile, and to question him closely about many <transChange type="added">things</transChange>,

verses.name: Luke 11:54
verses.text: plotting to catch him with reference to something <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he might say⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “from his mouth”</note>  <chapter eID="Luke.11"/>

verses.name: Luke 12:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11014"/><title type="x-s">Warning Against Hypocrisy</title> <div sID="gen26420" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11014"/>During <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞this time⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “which time”</note> when<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“had gathered together”)</note> a crowd of many thousands had gathered together, so that they were trampling one another, he began to say to his disciples first, “Beware for yourselves of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.

verses.name: Luke 12:2
verses.text: But nothing is concealed that will not be revealed, and secret that will not be made known.

verses.name: Luke 12:3
verses.text: Therefore everything that you have said in the dark will be heard in the light, and what <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you have whispered⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “you have spoken to the ear”</note> in the inner rooms will be proclaimed on the housetops.  <div eID="gen26420" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 12:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11015"/><title type="x-s">Fear God Rather Than People</title> <div sID="gen26421" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11015"/>“And I tell you, my friends, do not be afraid of those who kill the body, and after these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> do not have anything more to do.

verses.name: Luke 12:5
verses.text: But I will show you whom you should fear: fear the one who has authority, after the killing, to throw <transChange type="added">you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> into hell! Yes, I tell you, fear this one!

verses.name: Luke 12:6
verses.text: Are not five sparrows sold for two pennies? And not one of them is forgotten in the sight of God.

verses.name: Luke 12:7
verses.text: But even the hairs of your head are all numbered! Do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows.  <div eID="gen26421" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 12:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11016"/><title type="x-s">Acknowledgement of Christ and Persecution of Disciples</title> <div sID="gen26422" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11016"/>“And I tell you, everyone who acknowledges me before people, the Son of Man also will acknowledge him before the angels of God,

verses.name: Luke 12:9
verses.text: but the one who denies me before people will be denied before the angels of God.

verses.name: Luke 12:10
verses.text: And everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man, it will be forgiven him, but to the one who blasphemes against the Holy Spirit, it will not be forgiven.

verses.name: Luke 12:11
verses.text: But when they bring you before the synagogues and the rulers and the authorities, do not be anxious how or what you should speak in your own defense or what you should say,

verses.name: Luke 12:12
verses.text: for the Holy Spirit will teach you in <transChange type="added">that</transChange> same hour what it is necessary to say.”  <div eID="gen26422" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 12:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11017"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Rich Landowner Who Was a Fool</title> <div sID="gen26423" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11017"/>Now someone from the crowd said to him, “Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me!”

verses.name: Luke 12:14
verses.text: But he said to him, “Man, who made me a judge or an arbitrator over you?”

verses.name: Luke 12:15
verses.text: And he said to them, “Watch out and guard yourselves from all greediness, because not <transChange type="added">even</transChange> when someone has an abundance <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞does⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “is”</note> his life <transChange type="added">consist</transChange> of his possessions.”

verses.name: Luke 12:16
verses.text: And he told a parable to them, saying, “The land of a certain rich man yielded an abundant harvest.

verses.name: Luke 12:17
verses.text: And he reasoned to himself, saying, ‘What should I do? For I do not have anywhere I can gather in my crops.’

verses.name: Luke 12:18
verses.text: And he said, ‘I will do this: I will tear down my barns and build larger ones, and I will gather in there all my grain and possessions.

verses.name: Luke 12:19
verses.text: And I will say to my soul, “Soul, you have many possessions stored up for many years. Relax, eat, drink, celebrate!” ’

verses.name: Luke 12:20
verses.text: But God said to him, ‘Fool! This night your life<note placement="foot">The same Greek word can be translated “soul” or “life” depending on the context</note> is demanded from you, and <transChange type="added">the things</transChange> which you have prepared—whose will they be?’

verses.name: Luke 12:21
verses.text: So <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the one who stores up treasure for himself, and who is not rich toward God!”  <div eID="gen26423" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 12:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11018"/><title type="x-s">Anxiety</title> <div sID="gen26424" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11018"/>And he said to his disciples, “For this <transChange type="added">reason</transChange> I tell you, do not be anxious for <transChange type="added">your</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> life, what you will eat, or for your<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> body, what you will wear.

verses.name: Luke 12:23
verses.text: For life is more than food, and the body <transChange type="added">more than</transChange> clothing.

verses.name: Luke 12:24
verses.text: Consider the ravens, that they neither sow nor reap; to them there is neither storeroom nor barn, and God feeds them. How much more are you worth than the birds?

verses.name: Luke 12:25
verses.text: And which of you <transChange type="added">by</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“being anxious”) which is understood as means</note> being anxious is able to add an hour<note placement="foot">Or “a cubit” (the literal meaning); most scholars understand this to refer figuratively to an “hour” of life here, though some take it as a literal measurement of height</note> to his life span?

verses.name: Luke 12:26
verses.text: If then you are not even able <transChange type="added">to do</transChange> a very little thing, why are you anxious about the rest?

verses.name: Luke 12:27
verses.text: Consider the lilies, how they grow: they do not toil or spin, but I say to you, not even Solomon in all his glory was dressed like one of these.

verses.name: Luke 12:28
verses.text: But if God clothes the grass in the field in this way, <transChange type="added">although it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“is”) which is understood as concessive</note> is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, how much more will he do so for<note placement="foot">*The phrase “will he do so for” is not in the Greek text but is implied</note> you, you of little faith?

verses.name: Luke 12:29
verses.text: And you, do not consider what you will eat and what you will drink, and do not be anxious.

verses.name: Luke 12:30
verses.text: For all the nations of the world seek after these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, and your Father knows that you need these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>.

verses.name: Luke 12:31
verses.text: But seek his kingdom and these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> will be added to you.  <div eID="gen26424" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 12:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11019"/><div sID="gen26425" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11019"/>“Do not be afraid, little flock, because your Father is well pleased to give you the kingdom.

verses.name: Luke 12:33
verses.text: Sell your possessions and give charitable gifts. Make for yourselves money bags that do not wear out, an inexhaustible treasure in heaven<note placement="foot">Or “in the heavens”</note> where thief does not approach or moth destroy.

verses.name: Luke 12:34
verses.text: For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.  <div eID="gen26425" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 12:35
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11020"/><title type="x-s">On the Alert for the Master’s Return</title> <div sID="gen26426" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11020"/>“<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞You must be prepared for action⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “your loins must be girded”</note> and your<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> lamps burning.

verses.name: Luke 12:36
verses.text: And you, <transChange type="added">be</transChange> like people who are waiting for their master when he returns from the wedding feast,<note placement="foot">Or perhaps simply “feast”</note> so that when he<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“comes back”)</note> comes back and knocks, they can open the door<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> for him immediately.

verses.name: Luke 12:37
verses.text: Blessed <transChange type="added">are</transChange> those slaves whom the master will find on the alert <transChange type="added">when he</transChange> returns! Truly I say to you that he will dress himself for service and have them recline at the table and will come by <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“will come by”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> serve them.

verses.name: Luke 12:38
verses.text: Even if he should come back in the second or in the third watch of the night and find <transChange type="added">them</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> like this, blessed are they!

verses.name: Luke 12:39
verses.text: But understand this, that if the master of the house had known what hour the thief was coming, he would not have left his house to be broken into.

verses.name: Luke 12:40
verses.text: You also must be ready, because the Son of Man is coming at an hour that you do not think <transChange type="added">he will come</transChange>.”<note placement="foot">*The words “he will come” are not in the Greek text but are implied</note>  <div eID="gen26426" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 12:41
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11021"/><title type="x-s">A Faithful Slave and an Unfaithful Slave</title> <div sID="gen26427" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11021"/>And Peter said, “Lord, are you telling this parable for us, or also for everyone?”

verses.name: Luke 12:42
verses.text: And the Lord said, “Who then is the faithful wise manager whom the master will put in charge over his servants to give <transChange type="added">them</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> their<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> food allowance at the right time?

verses.name: Luke 12:43
verses.text: Blessed <transChange type="added">is</transChange> that slave whom his master will find so doing <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“comes back”) which is understood as temporal</note> comes back.

verses.name: Luke 12:44
verses.text: Truly I say to you that he will put him in charge of all his possessions.

verses.name: Luke 12:45
verses.text: But if that slave should say <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to himself⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “in his heart”</note> ‘My master is taking a long time to return,’ and he begins to beat the male slaves and the female slaves and to eat and drink and get drunk,

verses.name: Luke 12:46
verses.text: the master of that slave will come on a day that he does not expect and at an hour that he does not know, and will cut him in two and assign his place with the unbelievers.

verses.name: Luke 12:47
verses.text: And that slave who knew the will of his master and did not prepare or do according to his will <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞will be given a severe beating⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “will be beaten much”</note>

verses.name: Luke 12:48
verses.text: But the one who did not know and did <transChange type="added">things</transChange> deserving blows <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞will be given a light beating⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “will be beaten a few times”</note> And from everyone to whom much has been given, much will be demanded, and from him to whom they entrusted much, they will ask him <transChange type="added">for</transChange> even more.  <div eID="gen26427" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 12:49
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11022"/><title type="x-s">Not Peace, But a Sword of Divisiveness</title> <div sID="gen26428" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11022"/>“I have come to bring fire on the earth, and how I wish that it had been kindled already!

verses.name: Luke 12:50
verses.text: But I have a baptism to be baptized with, and how I am distressed until it is accomplished!

verses.name: Luke 12:51
verses.text: Do you think that I have come to grant peace on the earth? No, I tell you, but rather division!

verses.name: Luke 12:52
verses.text: For from now on there will be five in one household, divided three against two and two against three.

verses.name: Luke 12:53
verses.text: They will be divided, father against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against mother-in-law.”  <div eID="gen26428" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 12:54
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11023"/><title type="x-s">The Signs of the Times</title> <div sID="gen26429" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11023"/>And he also said to the crowds, “When you see a cloud coming up in the west, you say at once, ‘A rainstorm is coming,’ and so it happens.

verses.name: Luke 12:55
verses.text: And when <transChange type="added">you see</transChange> the south wind blowing, you say, ‘There will be burning heat,’ and it happens.

verses.name: Luke 12:56
verses.text: Hypocrites! You know how to evaluate the appearance of the earth and the sky, but how <transChange type="added">is it</transChange> you do not know how to evaluate this present time?  <div eID="gen26429" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 12:57
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11024"/><title type="x-s">Settle Accounts Quickly</title> <div sID="gen26430" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11024"/>And why do you not also judge for yourselves <transChange type="added">what is</transChange> right?

verses.name: Luke 12:58
verses.text: For as you are going with your accuser before the magistrate, make an effort to come to a settlement with him on the way, so that he will not drag you to the judge, and the judge will hand you over to the bailiff, and the bailiff will throw you into prison.

verses.name: Luke 12:59
verses.text: I tell you, you will never get out of there until you have paid back even the last cent!”<note placement="foot">Literally “lepton,” a small copper coin worth 1/128 of a denarius</note>  <chapter eID="Luke.12"/>

verses.name: Luke 13:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11025"/><title type="x-s">Repent or Perish</title> <div sID="gen26431" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11025"/>Now at the same time some had come to tell him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.

verses.name: Luke 13:2
verses.text: And he answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to them, “Do you think that these Galileans were sinners worse than all the Galileans, because they suffered these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>?

verses.name: Luke 13:3
verses.text: No, I tell you, but unless you repent you will all perish as well!

verses.name: Luke 13:4
verses.text: Or those eighteen on whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them—do you think that they were sinners worse than all the people who live in Jerusalem?

verses.name: Luke 13:5
verses.text: No, I tell you, but unless you repent, you will all perish as well!”  <div eID="gen26431" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 13:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11026"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Barren Fig Tree</title> <div sID="gen26432" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11026"/>And he told this parable: “A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he came looking for fruit on it and did not find <transChange type="added">any</transChange>.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Luke 13:7
verses.text: So he said to the gardener, ‘Behold, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞for three years⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “three years from which”</note> I have come looking for fruit on this fig tree and did not find any.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> Cut it down!<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “Therefore cut it down!”</note> Why should it even exhaust the soil?’

verses.name: Luke 13:8
verses.text: But he answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to him, ‘Sir, leave it alone this year also, until I dig around it and put manure on it.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Luke 13:9
verses.text: And if indeed it produces fruit in the coming <transChange type="added">year</transChange>, <transChange type="added">so much the better</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*The phrase “so much the better” is not in the Greek text but is implied</note> but if not, you can cut it down.’ ”  <div eID="gen26432" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 13:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11027"/><title type="x-s">A Woman with a Disabling Spirit Healed</title> <div sID="gen26433" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11027"/>Now he was teaching in one of the synagogues on the Sabbath.

verses.name: Luke 13:11
verses.text: And behold, a woman <transChange type="added">was there</transChange><note placement="foot">*The phrase “was there” is not in the Greek text but is supplied in keeping with English style</note> who had a spirit <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞that had disabled her⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “of weakness”</note> for eighteen years, and she was bent over and not able to straighten herself up completely.<note placement="foot">Or “at all”</note>

verses.name: Luke 13:12
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw her, Jesus summoned her<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and said to her, “Woman, you are freed from your disability!”

verses.name: Luke 13:13
verses.text: And he placed <transChange type="added">his</transChange><note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> hands on her, and immediately she straightened up and glorified God.

verses.name: Luke 13:14
