verses.text: But the ruler of the synagogue, indignant because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath, answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to the crowd, “There are six days on which it is necessary to work. Therefore come and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“come”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> be healed on them, and not on the day of the Sabbath!”

verses.name: Luke 13:15
verses.text: But the Lord answered and said to him, “Hypocrites! Does not each one of you untie his ox or <transChange type="added">his</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> donkey from the feeding trough on the Sabbath and lead it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> away to water it?<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Luke 13:16
verses.text: And this woman, who is a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan bound <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞eighteen⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “ten and eight”</note> long years—is it not necessary that she be released from this bond on the day of the Sabbath?”

verses.name: Luke 13:17
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“said”)</note> he said these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, all those who opposed him were humiliated, and the whole crowd was rejoicing at all the splendid things that were being done by him.  <div eID="gen26433" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 13:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11028"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Mustard Seed</title> <div sID="gen26434" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11028"/>Therefore he said, “What is the kingdom of God like, and to what shall I compare it?

verses.name: Luke 13:19
verses.text: It is like a mustard seed that a man took <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> sowed in his own garden, and it grew and became a tree, and the birds of the sky nested in its branches.”  <div eID="gen26434" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 13:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11029"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Yeast</title> <div sID="gen26435" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11029"/>And again he said, “To what shall I compare the kingdom of God?

verses.name: Luke 13:21
verses.text: It is like yeast that a woman took <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> hid in<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “put into”</note> three measures of wheat flour until the whole <transChange type="added">batch</transChange> was leavened.”  <div eID="gen26435" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 13:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11030"/><title type="x-s">The Narrow Door</title> <div sID="gen26436" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11030"/>And he was going throughout towns and villages, teaching and making <transChange type="added">his</transChange> journey toward Jerusalem.

verses.name: Luke 13:23
verses.text: And someone said to him, “Lord, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞are there only⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “if”</note> a few who are saved?” And he said to them,

verses.name: Luke 13:24
verses.text: “Make every effort to enter through the narrow door, because many, I tell you, will seek to enter and will not be able to,

verses.name: Luke 13:25
verses.text: when once the master of the house has gotten up and shut the door, and you begin to stand outside and knock <transChange type="added">on</transChange> the door, saying, ‘Lord, open <transChange type="added">the door</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> for us!’ And he will answer and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answer”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> say to you, ‘I do not know where you are from!’

verses.name: Luke 13:26
verses.text: Then you will begin to say, ‘We ate and drank in your presence, and you taught in our streets!’

verses.name: Luke 13:27
verses.text: And he will reply, saying to you, ‘I do not know where you are from! Go away from me, all <transChange type="added">you</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞evildoers⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!’<note placement="foot">Literally “workers of unrighteousness”</note>

verses.name: Luke 13:28
verses.text: In that place there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when you see Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, but yourselves thrown outside!

verses.name: Luke 13:29
verses.text: And they will come from east and west, and from north and south, and will recline at the table in the kingdom of God.

verses.name: Luke 13:30
verses.text: And behold, <transChange type="added">some</transChange> are last who will be first, and <transChange type="added">some</transChange> are first who will be last.”  <div eID="gen26436" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 13:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11031"/><title type="x-s">The Lament over Jerusalem</title> <div sID="gen26437" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11031"/>At <transChange type="added">that</transChange> same hour some Pharisees came up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to him, “Go out and depart from here, because Herod wants to kill you!”

verses.name: Luke 13:32
verses.text: And he said to them, “Go <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“go”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> tell that fox, ‘Behold, I am expelling demons and performing healings today and tomorrow, and on the third day I will complete my work.’<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Luke 13:33
verses.text: Nevertheless, it is necessary <transChange type="added">for</transChange> me to be on the way today and tomorrow and on the next <transChange type="added">day</transChange>, because it is not possible <transChange type="added">for</transChange> a prophet to perish outside Jerusalem.  <div eID="gen26437" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 13:34
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11032"/><div sID="gen26438" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11032"/>“Jerusalem, Jerusalem, the one who kills the prophets and stones those who are sent to her! How many times I wanted to gather your children together <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the way⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in the manner in which”</note> a hen gathers<note placement="foot">*Here the term “gathers” is not in the Greek text but is implied</note> her own brood under her<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> wings, and you were not willing!

verses.name: Luke 13:35
verses.text: Behold, your house has been left to you! And I tell you, you will never see me until <transChange type="added">the time</transChange><note placement="foot">*The words “the time” are not in the Greek text but are implied</note> will come when you say, ‘Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord!’ ”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.118.26">Ps 118:26</reference></note>  <chapter eID="Luke.13"/>

verses.name: Luke 14:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11033"/><title type="x-s">A Man Suffering from Edema Healed</title> <div sID="gen26439" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11033"/>And it happened that when he came to the house of a certain one of the leaders of the Pharisees on a Sabbath to eat <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a meal⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “bread”</note> they were watching him closely.

verses.name: Luke 14:2
verses.text: And behold, a certain man was in front of him, suffering from edema.

verses.name: Luke 14:3
verses.text: And Jesus answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to the legal experts and Pharisees, saying, “Is it permitted to heal on the Sabbath, or not?”

verses.name: Luke 14:4
verses.text: But they remained silent. And he took hold of <transChange type="added">him</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took hold of”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> healed him, and sent him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> away.

verses.name: Luke 14:5
verses.text: And he said to them, “Who among you, <transChange type="added">if your</transChange><note placement="foot">*The words “if your” are not in the Greek text but are implied</note> son or your ox falls into a well<note placement="foot">Or “cistern”</note> on the day of the Sabbath, will not immediately pull him out?”

verses.name: Luke 14:6
verses.text: And they were not able to make a reply to these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>.  <div eID="gen26439" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 14:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11034"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Guests at the Wedding Feast</title> <div sID="gen26440" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11034"/>Now he told a parable to those who had been invited <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“noticed”) which is understood as temporal</note> noticed how they were choosing for themselves the places of honor, saying to them,

verses.name: Luke 14:8
verses.text: “When you are invited by someone to a wedding feast,<note placement="foot">Or perhaps simply “a feast”</note> do not recline at the table in the place of honor, lest <transChange type="added">someone</transChange> more distinguished than you has been invited by him,

verses.name: Luke 14:9
verses.text: and the one who invited you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞both⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and him”</note> will come and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“will come”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> say to you, ‘Give the place to this person,’ and then with shame you will begin to take the last place.

verses.name: Luke 14:10
verses.text: But when you are invited, go <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“go”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> recline at the table in the last place, so that when the one who invited you comes, he will say to you, ‘Friend, move up higher.’ Then it will be an honor to you in the presence of all those who are reclining at the table with you.

verses.name: Luke 14:11
verses.text: For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted.”  <div eID="gen26440" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 14:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11035"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Great Banquet</title> <div sID="gen26441" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11035"/>And he also said to the one who had invited him, “When you give a dinner or a banquet, do not invite your friends or your brothers or your relatives or wealthy neighbors, lest they also invite you <transChange type="added">in return</transChange>, and repayment come to you.

verses.name: Luke 14:13
verses.text: But whenever you give a banquet, invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, the blind,

verses.name: Luke 14:14
verses.text: and you will be blessed, because they are not able to repay you. For it will be paid back to you at the resurrection of the righteous.”  <div eID="gen26441" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 14:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11036"/><div sID="gen26442" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11036"/>Now <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> one of those reclining at the table with him heard these things, he said to him, “Blessed is <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞everyone who⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “whoever”</note> will eat bread in the kingdom of God!”

verses.name: Luke 14:16
verses.text: But he said to him, “A certain man was giving a large banquet and invited many.

verses.name: Luke 14:17
verses.text: And he sent his slave at the hour of the banquet to say to those who have been invited, ‘Come, because now it is ready!’

verses.name: Luke 14:18
verses.text: And they all <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞alike⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by one”</note> began to excuse themselves. The first said to him, ‘I have purchased a field, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I must⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “I have necessity”</note> go out to look at it. I ask you, consider me excused.’

verses.name: Luke 14:19
verses.text: And another said, ‘I have purchased five yoke of oxen, and I am going to examine them. I ask you, consider me excused.’

verses.name: Luke 14:20
verses.text: And another said, ‘I have married a wife, and for this <transChange type="added">reason</transChange> I am not able to come.’

verses.name: Luke 14:21
verses.text: And the slave came <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> reported these things to his master. Then the master of the house became angry and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“became angry”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to his slave, ‘Go out quickly into the streets and alleys of the city and bring in here the poor and crippled and blind and lame!’

verses.name: Luke 14:22
verses.text: And the slave said, ‘Sir, what you ordered has been done, and there is still room.’

verses.name: Luke 14:23
verses.text: And the master said to the slave, ‘Go out into the highways and hedges and press <transChange type="added">them</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to come in, so that my house will be filled!

verses.name: Luke 14:24
verses.text: For I say to you that none of those persons who were invited will taste my banquet!’ ”  <div eID="gen26442" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 14:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11037"/><title type="x-s">The Cost of Discipleship</title> <div sID="gen26443" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11037"/>Now large crowds were going along with him, and he turned around <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“turned around”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to them,

verses.name: Luke 14:26
verses.text: “If anyone comes to me and does not hate his own father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters, and furthermore, even his own life, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he cannot be⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “he is not able to be”</note> my disciple.

verses.name: Luke 14:27
verses.text: Whoever does not carry his own cross and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞follow⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “come after”</note> me <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞cannot be⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “is not able to be”</note> my disciple.

verses.name: Luke 14:28
verses.text: For which of you, wanting to build a tower, does not first sit down <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“sit down”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> calculate the cost to see if he has enough<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to complete it⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?<note placement="foot">Literally “for completion”</note>

verses.name: Luke 14:29
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Otherwise⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “so that lest”</note> after<note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“has laid”)</note> he has laid the foundation and is not able to finish it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> all who see it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> will begin to ridicule him,

verses.name: Luke 14:30
verses.text: saying, ‘This man began to build and was not able to finish!’

verses.name: Luke 14:31
verses.text: Or what king, going out to engage another king in battle, does not sit down first <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“sit down”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> deliberate whether he is able with ten thousand to oppose the one coming against him with twenty thousand.

verses.name: Luke 14:32
verses.text: But if not, <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“is”)</note> the other is still far away, he sends an ambassador and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“asks”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> asks <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞for terms of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the things with reference to”</note> peace.

verses.name: Luke 14:33
verses.text: In the <transChange type="added">same</transChange> way, therefore, every <transChange type="added">one</transChange> of you who does not renounce all his own possessions <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞cannot be⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “is not able to be”</note> my disciple.  <div eID="gen26443" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 14:34
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11038"/><div sID="gen26444" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11038"/>“Now salt <transChange type="added">is</transChange> good, but if salt becomes tasteless, with what will it be made salty?

verses.name: Luke 14:35
verses.text: It is usable neither for the soil nor for the manure pile; they throw it out. The one who has ears to hear, let him hear!”  <chapter eID="Luke.14"/>

verses.name: Luke 15:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11039"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Lost Sheep</title> <div sID="gen26445" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11039"/>Now all the tax collectors and the sinners were drawing near to hear him.

verses.name: Luke 15:2
verses.text: And both the Pharisees and the scribes were complaining, saying, “This man welcomes sinners and eats with them!”  <div eID="gen26445" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 15:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11040"/><div sID="gen26446" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11040"/>So he told them this parable, saying,

verses.name: Luke 15:4
verses.text: “What man of you, having a hundred sheep and losing one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the grassland and go after the one that was lost until he finds it?

verses.name: Luke 15:5
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“has found”) which is understood as temporal</note> has found it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> he places it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> on his shoulders, rejoicing.

verses.name: Luke 15:6
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“returns”) which is understood as temporal</note> returns to his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> home, he calls together his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> friends and neighbors, saying to them, ‘Rejoice with me, because I have found my sheep that was lost!’

verses.name: Luke 15:7
verses.text: I tell you that in the <transChange type="added">same</transChange> way, there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous people who have no need of repentance.  <div eID="gen26446" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 15:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11041"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Lost Coin</title> <div sID="gen26447" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11041"/>Or what woman who has ten drachmas, if she loses one drachma, does not light a lamp and sweep the house and search carefully until she finds <transChange type="added">it</transChange>?<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Luke 15:9
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when she</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“has found”) which is understood as temporal</note> has found it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> she calls together her<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> friends and neighbors, saying, ‘Rejoice with me, because I have found the drachma that I had lost!’

verses.name: Luke 15:10
verses.text: In the <transChange type="added">same</transChange> way, I tell you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner who repents.”  <div eID="gen26447" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 15:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11042"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Lost Son</title> <div sID="gen26448" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11042"/>And he said, “A certain man had two sons.

verses.name: Luke 15:12
verses.text: And the younger of them said to <transChange type="added">his</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> father, ‘Father, give me the share of the property that is coming to me.’ So he divided his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> assets between them.

verses.name: Luke 15:13
verses.text: And after not many days, the younger son gathered everything <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“gathered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> went on a journey to a distant country, and there he squandered his wealth by<note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the adverbial participle of manner (“living”)</note> living wastefully.

verses.name: Luke 15:14
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“had spent”)</note> he had spent everything, there was a severe famine throughout that country, and he began to be in need.

verses.name: Luke 15:15
verses.text: And he went <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> hired himself out to one of the citizens of that country, and he sent him into his fields to tend pigs.

verses.name: Luke 15:16
verses.text: And he was longing to fill his stomach with<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “to stuff himself with”</note> the carob pods that the pigs were eating, and no one was giving anything<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to him.  <div eID="gen26448" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 15:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11043"/><div sID="gen26449" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11043"/>“But <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“came”) which is understood as temporal</note> came to himself, he said, ‘How many of my father’s hired workers have an abundance <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞of food⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “of bread”</note> and I am dying here from hunger!

verses.name: Luke 15:18
verses.text: I will set out <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“set out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> go to my father and will say to him, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in your sight⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!<note placement="foot">Literally “in the sight of you”</note>

verses.name: Luke 15:19
verses.text: I am no longer worthy to be called your son! Make me like one of your hired workers.’

verses.name: Luke 15:20
verses.text: And he set out <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“set out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> came to his own father. But while<note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“away”)</note> he was still a long way away, his father saw him and had compassion, and ran <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞and embraced him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “fell on his neck”</note> and kissed him.

verses.name: Luke 15:21
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">his</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> son said to him, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in your sight⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!<note placement="foot">Literally “in the sight of you”</note> I am no longer worthy to be called your son!’

verses.name: Luke 15:22
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">his</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> father said to his slaves, ‘Quickly bring out the best robe and put it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> on him, and put a ring on his finger<note placement="foot">Literally “hand,” but this is a metonymy of whole (“hand”) for part (“finger”)</note> and sandals on his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> feet!

verses.name: Luke 15:23
verses.text: And bring the fattened calf—kill <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and let us eat and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“eat”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> celebrate,

verses.name: Luke 15:24
verses.text: because this son of mine was dead, and is alive again! He was lost and is found!’ And they began to celebrate.  <div eID="gen26449" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 15:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11044"/><div sID="gen26450" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11044"/>“Now his older son was in the field, and when he came <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> approached the house, he heard music and dancing.

verses.name: Luke 15:26
verses.text: And he summoned one of the slaves <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“summoned”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> asked what these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> meant.

verses.name: Luke 15:27
verses.text: And he said to him, ‘Your brother has come, and your father has killed the fattened calf because he has gotten him back healthy.’

verses.name: Luke 15:28
verses.text: But he became angry and did not want to go in. So his father came out <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> began to implore<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to implore”)</note> him.

verses.name: Luke 15:29
verses.text: But he answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to his father, ‘Behold, so many years I have served you, and have never disobeyed your command! And you never gave me a young goat so that I could celebrate with my friends!

verses.name: Luke 15:30
verses.text: But when this son of yours returned—who has consumed your assets with prostitutes—you killed the fattened calf for him!’

verses.name: Luke 15:31
verses.text: But he said to him, ‘Child, you are always with me, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞everything I have belongs to you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “all my things are yours”</note>

verses.name: Luke 15:32
verses.text: But it was necessary to celebrate and to rejoice, because this brother of yours was dead, and is alive, and was lost, and is found!’ ”  <chapter eID="Luke.15"/>

verses.name: Luke 16:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11045"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Dishonest Manager</title> <div sID="gen26451" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11045"/>And he also said to the disciples, “A certain man was rich, who had a manager. And charges were brought to him that this person was squandering his possessions.

verses.name: Luke 16:2
verses.text: And he summoned him <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“summoned”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to him, ‘What is this I hear about you? Give the account of your management, because you can no longer manage.’

verses.name: Luke 16:3
verses.text: And the manager said to himself, ‘What should I do, because my master is taking away the management from me? I am not strong enough to dig; I am ashamed to beg.

verses.name: Luke 16:4
verses.text: I know what I should do, so that when I am removed from the management they will welcome me into their homes!’

verses.name: Luke 16:5
verses.text: And he summoned each one of his own master’s debtors <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“summoned”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to the first, ‘How much do you owe my master?’

verses.name: Luke 16:6
verses.text: And he said, ‘A hundred measures of olive oil.’ So he said to him, ‘Take your promissory note and sit down quickly <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“sit down”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> write fifty.’

verses.name: Luke 16:7
verses.text: Then he said to another, ‘And how much do you owe?’ And he said, ‘A hundred measures of wheat.’ He said to him, ‘Take your promissory note and write eighty.’

verses.name: Luke 16:8
verses.text: And the master praised the dishonest manager, because he had acted shrewdly. For the sons of this age are shrewder than the sons of light with regard to their own generation.<note placement="foot">Or “kind”</note>

verses.name: Luke 16:9
verses.text: And I tell you, make friends for yourselves by means of unrighteous wealth, so that when it runs out they will welcome you into the eternal dwellings.  <div eID="gen26451" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 16:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11046"/><div sID="gen26452" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11046"/>“The one who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> faithful in very little is also faithful in much, and the one who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> dishonest in very little is also dishonest in much.

verses.name: Luke 16:11
verses.text: If then you have not been faithful with unrighteous wealth, who will entrust to you the true <transChange type="added">riches</transChange>?<note placement="foot">*The word “riches” is not in the Greek text but is implied</note>

verses.name: Luke 16:12
verses.text: And if you have not been faithful with what belongs to another, who will give you your own?

verses.name: Luke 16:13
verses.text: No domestic slave is able to serve two masters, for either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to one and will despise the other. You are not able to serve God and money.”  <div eID="gen26452" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 16:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11047"/><title type="x-s">Hypocrisy, Law, and the Kingdom of God</title> <div sID="gen26453" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11047"/>Now the Pharisees, who were lovers of money, heard all these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, and they ridiculed him.

verses.name: Luke 16:15
verses.text: And he said to them, “You are the ones who justify themselves in the sight of men, but God knows your hearts! For <transChange type="added">what is</transChange> <transChange type="added">considered</transChange> exalted among men <transChange type="added">is</transChange> an abomination in the sight of God.  <div eID="gen26453" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 16:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11048"/><div sID="gen26454" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11048"/>“The law and the prophets <transChange type="added">were</transChange> until John; from that time <transChange type="added">on</transChange> the kingdom of God has been proclaimed, and everyone is urgently pressed<note placement="foot">The verb is translated here as a passive; some English versions translate the verb as active (“forces their way into it”)</note> into it.

verses.name: Luke 16:17
verses.text: But it is easier <transChange type="added">for</transChange> heaven and earth to pass away than <transChange type="added">for</transChange> one stroke of a letter of the law to become invalid.  <div eID="gen26454" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 16:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11049"/><title type="x-s">On Divorce</title> <div sID="gen26455" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11049"/>“Everyone who divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery, and the one who marries a woman divorced from <transChange type="added">her</transChange> husband commits adultery.  <div eID="gen26455" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 16:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11050"/><title type="x-s">The Rich Man and Lazarus</title> <div sID="gen26456" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11050"/>“Now a certain man was rich, and dressed <transChange type="added">in</transChange> purple cloth and fine linen, feasting sumptuously every day.

verses.name: Luke 16:20
verses.text: And a certain poor man <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞named⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by name”</note> Lazarus, covered with sores, lay at his gate,

verses.name: Luke 16:21
verses.text: and was longing to be filled with what fell from the table of the rich man. But even the dogs came <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> licked his sores.

verses.name: Luke 16:22
verses.text: Now it happened that the poor man died, and he was carried away by the angels to <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Abraham’s side⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the bosom of Abraham”</note> And the rich man also died and was buried.

verses.name: Luke 16:23
verses.text: And in Hades he lifted up his eyes <transChange type="added">as he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was”) which is understood as temporal</note> was in torment and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“lifted up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> saw Abraham from a distance, and Lazarus <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞at his side⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “in his bosom”</note>

verses.name: Luke 16:24
verses.text: And he called out <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“called out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, ‘Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus so that he could dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue, because I am suffering pain in this flame!’

verses.name: Luke 16:25
verses.text: But Abraham said, ‘Child, remember that you received your good <transChange type="added">things</transChange> during your life, and Lazarus likewise bad <transChange type="added">things</transChange>. But now he is comforted here, but you are suffering pain.

verses.name: Luke 16:26
verses.text: And in <transChange type="added">addition to</transChange> all these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, a great chasm has been established between us and you, so that those who want to cross over from here to you are not able <transChange type="added">to do so</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*The words “to do so” are not in the Greek text but are implied</note> nor can they cross over from there to us.’

verses.name: Luke 16:27
verses.text: So he said, ‘Then I ask you, father, that you send him to my father’s house,

verses.name: Luke 16:28
verses.text: for I have five brothers, so that he could warn them, in order that they also should not come to this place of torment!’

verses.name: Luke 16:29
verses.text: But Abraham said, ‘They have Moses and the prophets; they must listen to them.’

verses.name: Luke 16:30
verses.text: And he said, ‘No, father Abraham, but if someone from the dead goes to them, they will repent!’

verses.name: Luke 16:31
verses.text: But he said to him, ‘If they do not listen to Moses and the prophets, neither will they be convinced if someone rises from the dead.’ ”  <chapter eID="Luke.16"/>

verses.name: Luke 17:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11051"/><title type="x-s">Sin, Forgiveness, Faith, and Service</title> <div sID="gen26457" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11051"/>And he said to his disciples, “It is impossible for causes for stumbling not to come, but woe <transChange type="added">to him</transChange> through whom they come!

verses.name: Luke 17:2
verses.text: It would be better for him if <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a millstone⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a stone belonging to a mill”</note> is placed around his neck and he is thrown into the sea than that he causes one of these little ones to sin.  <div eID="gen26457" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 17:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11052"/><div sID="gen26458" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11052"/>“Be concerned about yourselves! If your brother sins, rebuke him, and if he repents, forgive him.

verses.name: Luke 17:4
verses.text: And if he sins against you seven times in a day, and seven times he returns to you saying, ‘I repent,’ you must forgive him.”  <div eID="gen26458" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 17:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11053"/><div sID="gen26459" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11053"/>And the apostles said to the Lord, “Increase our faith!”

verses.name: Luke 17:6
verses.text: So the Lord said, “If you have faith like a mustard seed, you could say to this mulberry tree, ‘Be uprooted and planted in the sea,’ and it would obey you.  <div eID="gen26459" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 17:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11054"/><div sID="gen26460" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11054"/>“And which of you who has a slave plowing or shepherding <transChange type="added">sheep</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> who comes in from the field will say to him, ‘Come here at once and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“come here”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> recline at the table’?

verses.name: Luke 17:8
verses.text: Will he not rather say to him, ‘Prepare something that I may eat, and dress yourself to serve me while I eat and drink, and after these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> you will eat and drink.’

verses.name: Luke 17:9
verses.text: He will not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞be grateful⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “have gratitude”</note> to the slave because he did what was ordered, will he?<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here, indicated by “will he”</note>

verses.name: Luke 17:10
verses.text: Thus you also, when you have done all the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞things you were ordered to do⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “things that were ordered to you”</note> say, ‘We are unworthy slaves; we have done what we were obligated to do.’ ”  <div eID="gen26460" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 17:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11055"/><title type="x-s">Ten Lepers Cleansed</title> <div sID="gen26461" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11055"/>And it happened that while traveling toward Jerusalem, he was passing through <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the region between⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “through the midst”</note> Samaria and Galilee.

verses.name: Luke 17:12
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was entering”)</note> he was entering into a certain village, ten men met him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note><note placement="foot">Some manuscripts explicitly state “him”</note>—lepers, who stood at a distance.

verses.name: Luke 17:13
verses.text: And they raised <transChange type="added">their</transChange> voices, saying, “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!”

verses.name: Luke 17:14
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> he said to them, “Go and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“go”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> show yourselves to the priests.” And it happened that as they were going, they were cleansed.

verses.name: Luke 17:15
verses.text: But one of them, <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw that he was healed, turned back, praising God with a loud voice.

verses.name: Luke 17:16
verses.text: And he fell on <transChange type="added">his</transChange> face at his feet, giving thanks to him. And he was a Samaritan.

verses.name: Luke 17:17
verses.text: So Jesus answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “Were not ten cleansed? And where <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the nine?

verses.name: Luke 17:18
verses.text: Was no one found to turn back <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“turn back”) has been translated as an infinitive</note> give praise to God except this foreigner?”

verses.name: Luke 17:19
verses.text: And he said to him, “Get up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“get up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> go your way. Your faith has saved you.”  <div eID="gen26461" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 17:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11056"/><title type="x-s">The Coming of the Kingdom of God</title> <div sID="gen26462" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11056"/>Now <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was asked”) which is understood as temporal</note> was asked by the Pharisees when the kingdom of God would come, he answered them and said, “The kingdom of God does not come with <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞things that can be observed⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “observation”</note>

verses.name: Luke 17:21
verses.text: nor will they say, ‘Behold, here <transChange type="added">it is</transChange>!’ or ‘There!’ For behold, the kingdom of God is in your midst.”  <div eID="gen26462" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 17:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11057"/><title type="x-s">The Coming of the Son of Man</title> <div sID="gen26463" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11057"/>And he said to the disciples, “Days will come when you will desire to see one of the days of the Son of Man, and you will not see <transChange type="added">it</transChange>.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Luke 17:23
verses.text: And they will say to you, ‘Behold, there!’ ‘Behold, here!’<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “ ‘Behold, there!’ or ‘Behold, here!’ ”</note> Do not go out or run after them!<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Luke 17:24
verses.text: For just as the lightning shines forth, flashing from <transChange type="added">one place</transChange> under heaven to <transChange type="added">another place</transChange> under heaven, so the Son of Man will be in his day.

verses.name: Luke 17:25
verses.text: But first it is necessary <transChange type="added">for</transChange> him to suffer many <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, and to be rejected by this generation.

verses.name: Luke 17:26
verses.text: And just as it was in the days of Noah, so also it will be in the days of the Son of Man—

verses.name: Luke 17:27
verses.text: they were eating, they were drinking, they were marrying, they were being given in marriage, until the day Noah entered into the ark, and the flood came and destroyed <transChange type="added">them</transChange> all.

verses.name: Luke 17:28
verses.text: Likewise, just as it was in the days of Lot—they were eating, they were drinking, they were buying, they were selling, they were planting, they were building.

verses.name: Luke 17:29
verses.text: But on the day that Lot went out from Sodom, it rained fire and sulphur from heaven and destroyed <transChange type="added">them</transChange> all.

verses.name: Luke 17:30
verses.text: It will be <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞just the same⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “according to the same”</note> on the day that the Son of Man is revealed.

verses.name: Luke 17:31
verses.text: On that day, whoever is on the housetop and his goods <transChange type="added">are</transChange> in the house must not come down to take them away. And likewise the one who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in the field must not turn back

verses.name: Luke 17:32
verses.text: Remember Lot’s wife!

verses.name: Luke 17:33
verses.text: Whoever seeks to preserve his life will lose it, but whoever loses <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> will keep it.

verses.name: Luke 17:34
verses.text: I tell you that in that night there will be two in one bed; one will be taken and the other will be left.

verses.name: Luke 17:35
verses.text: There will be two <transChange type="added">women</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “women” is supplied because the form (“two”) is feminine gender in Greek</note> grinding at the same place; one will be taken and the other will be left.”<note placement="foot">A few manuscripts add v. <reference osisRef="Luke.17.36">36</reference> (with some variations): “There will be two in the field; one will be taken and the other will be left.”</note>  <div eID="gen26463" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 17:37
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11058"/><div sID="gen26464" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11058"/>And they answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to him, “Where, Lord?” So he said to them, “Where the dead body <transChange type="added">is</transChange>, there also the vultures will be gathered.”  <chapter eID="Luke.17"/>

verses.name: Luke 18:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11059"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Unjust Judge</title> <div sID="gen26465" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11059"/>And he told them a parable to <transChange type="added">show that</transChange> they must always pray and not be discouraged,

verses.name: Luke 18:2
verses.text: saying, “There was a certain judge in a certain town who did not fear God and did not respect people.

verses.name: Luke 18:3
verses.text: And there was a widow in that town, and she kept coming to him, saying, ‘Grant me justice against my adversary!’

verses.name: Luke 18:4
verses.text: And he was not willing for a time, but after these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> he said to himself, ‘Even if I do not fear God or respect people,

verses.name: Luke 18:5
verses.text: yet because this widow is causing trouble for me, I will grant her justice, so that she does not wear me down in the end <transChange type="added">by her</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“coming back”) which is understood as means</note> coming back!’ ”

verses.name: Luke 18:6
verses.text: And the Lord said, “Listen to what the unrighteous judge is saying!

verses.name: Luke 18:7
verses.text: And will not God surely <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞see to it that justice is done⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “carry out the giving of justice”</note> to his chosen ones who cry out to him day and night, and will he delay toward them?

verses.name: Luke 18:8
verses.text: I tell you that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he will see to it that justice is done⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “he will carry out the giving of justice”</note> for them soon! Nevertheless, when<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“comes”) which is understood as temporal</note> the Son of Man comes, then will he find faith on earth?”  <div eID="gen26465" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 18:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11060"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Pharisee and the Tax Collector</title> <div sID="gen26466" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11060"/>And he also told this parable to some who trusted in themselves that they were righteous, and looked down on <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞everyone else⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>:<note placement="foot">Literally “the rest”</note>

verses.name: Luke 18:10
verses.text: “Two men went up to the temple to pray, one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.

verses.name: Luke 18:11
verses.text: The Pharisee stood <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“stood”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> prayed these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> with reference to himself: ‘God, I give thanks to you that I am not like other people—swindlers, unrighteous <transChange type="added">people</transChange>, adulterers, or even like this tax collector!

verses.name: Luke 18:12
verses.text: I fast twice a week; I give a tenth of all that I get.’

verses.name: Luke 18:13
verses.text: But the tax collector, standing far away, did not want even to raise his eyes to heaven, but was beating his breast, saying, ‘God, be merciful to me, a sinner!’

verses.name: Luke 18:14
verses.text: I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than that one! For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but the one who humbles himself will be exalted.”  <div eID="gen26466" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 18:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11061"/><title type="x-s">Little Children Brought to Jesus</title> <div sID="gen26467" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11061"/>Now they were bringing even <transChange type="added">their</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> babies to him so that he could touch them. But when<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> the disciples saw it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> they rebuked them.

verses.name: Luke 18:16
verses.text: But Jesus called them to himself, saying, “Allow the children to come to me, and do not forbid them, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞for to such belongs⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for of such is”</note> the kingdom of God.

verses.name: Luke 18:17
verses.text: Truly I say to you, whoever does not welcome the kingdom of God like a young child will never enter into it.”  <div eID="gen26467" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 18:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11062"/><title type="x-s">A Rich Young Man</title> <div sID="gen26468" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11062"/>And a certain ruler asked him, saying, “Good Teacher, <transChange type="added">by</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“doing”) which is understood as means</note> doing what will I inherit eternal life?”

verses.name: Luke 18:19
verses.text: And Jesus said to him, “Why do you call me good? No one <transChange type="added">is</transChange> good except God alone.

verses.name: Luke 18:20
verses.text: You know the commandments: ‘Do not commit adultery, do not murder, do not steal, do not give false testimony, honor your father and mother.’ ”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Exod.20.12-Exod.20.16">Exod 20:12–16</reference>; <reference osisRef="Deut.5.16-Deut.5.20">Deut 5:16–20</reference></note>

verses.name: Luke 18:21
verses.text: And he said, “All these I have observed from my<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts omit “my”</note> youth.”

verses.name: Luke 18:22
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard this,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> Jesus said to him, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞You still lack one thing⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>:<note placement="foot">Literally “one still lacking to you”</note> Sell all that you have, and distribute the proceeds<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to the poor—and you will have treasure in heaven—and come, follow me.”

verses.name: Luke 18:23
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> he became very sad, because he was extremely wealthy.  <div eID="gen26468" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 18:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11063"/><div sID="gen26469" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11063"/>And Jesus took notice of him<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts add “becoming very sad”</note> and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took notice of”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “How <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞difficult it is for⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “with difficulty”</note> those who possess wealth to enter into the kingdom of God!

verses.name: Luke 18:25
verses.text: For it is easier <transChange type="added">for</transChange> a camel to go through the eye of a needle than <transChange type="added">for</transChange> a rich person to enter into the kingdom of God.

verses.name: Luke 18:26
verses.text: So those who heard <transChange type="added">this</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> said, “And who can be saved?”

verses.name: Luke 18:27
verses.text: But he said, “<transChange type="added">What is</transChange> impossible with men is possible with God.”  <div eID="gen26469" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 18:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11064"/><div sID="gen26470" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11064"/>And Peter said, “Behold, we have left <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞all that is ours⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “our own”</note> and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“have left”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> followed you.”

verses.name: Luke 18:29
verses.text: And he said to them, “Truly I say to you that there is no one who has left house or wife or brothers or parents or children on account of the kingdom of God,

verses.name: Luke 18:30
verses.text: who will not receive many times more in this time and in the age to come, eternal life.”  <div eID="gen26470" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 18:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11065"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Predicts His Death and Resurrection a Third Time</title> <div sID="gen26471" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11065"/>And taking aside the twelve, he said to them, “Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and all the things that are written by the prophets with reference to the Son of Man will be accomplished.

verses.name: Luke 18:32
verses.text: For he will be handed over to the Gentiles and will be mocked and mistreated and spit on,

verses.name: Luke 18:33
verses.text: and <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“flogging”) which is understood as temporal</note> flogging him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> they will kill him, and on the third day he will rise.”

verses.name: Luke 18:34
verses.text: And they understood none of these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, and this saying was concealed from them, and they did not comprehend the things that were said.  <div eID="gen26471" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 18:35
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11066"/><title type="x-s">A Blind Man Healed at Jericho</title> <div sID="gen26472" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11066"/>Now it happened that as he drew near to Jericho, a certain blind man was sitting on the side of the road begging.

verses.name: Luke 18:36
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard a crowd going by, he inquired what this meant.

verses.name: Luke 18:37
verses.text: And they told him, “Jesus the Nazarene is passing by.”

verses.name: Luke 18:38
verses.text: And he called out, saying, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”

verses.name: Luke 18:39
verses.text: And those who were in front rebuked him, that he should be silent, but he cried out <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞even more loudly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “by much more”</note> “Son of David, have mercy on me!”

verses.name: Luke 18:40
verses.text: So Jesus stopped <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“stopped”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> ordered him to be brought to him. And when<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“approached”)</note> he approached, he asked him,

verses.name: Luke 18:41
verses.text: “What do you want me to do for you?” And he said, “Lord, that I may regain <transChange type="added">my</transChange> sight.

verses.name: Luke 18:42
verses.text: And Jesus said to him, “Regain <transChange type="added">your</transChange> sight! Your faith has saved you.”

verses.name: Luke 18:43
verses.text: And immediately he regained <transChange type="added">his</transChange> sight and began to follow<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to follow”)</note> him, glorifying God. And all the people, when they<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> gave praise to God.  <chapter eID="Luke.18"/>

verses.name: Luke 19:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11067"/><title type="x-s">Jesus and Zacchaeus</title> <div sID="gen26473" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11067"/>And he entered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“entered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> traveled through Jericho.

verses.name: Luke 19:2
verses.text: And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞there was⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “behold”</note> a man <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞named⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “called by name”</note> Zacchaeus, and he was a chief tax collector, and he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> rich.

verses.name: Luke 19:3
verses.text: And he was seeking to see Jesus—who he was—and he was not able to as a result of the crowd, because he was short in stature.

verses.name: Luke 19:4
verses.text: And he ran on ahead <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“ran on”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> climbed up into a sycamore tree so that he could see him, because he was going to go through <transChange type="added">that way</transChange>.

verses.name: Luke 19:5
verses.text: And when he came to the place, Jesus looked up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“looked up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to him, “Zacchaeus, come down quickly, because it is necessary <transChange type="added">for</transChange> me to stay at your house today!”

verses.name: Luke 19:6
verses.text: And he came down quickly and welcomed him joyfully.

verses.name: Luke 19:7
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> they all began to complain,<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to complain”)</note> saying, “He has gone in to find lodging with a man who is a sinner!”

verses.name: Luke 19:8
verses.text: And Zacchaeus stopped <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“stopped”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to the Lord, “Behold, half of my possessions, Lord, I am giving to the poor, and if I have extorted anything from anyone, I am paying it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> back four times <transChange type="added">as much</transChange>!”

verses.name: Luke 19:9
verses.text: And Jesus said to him, “Today salvation has come to this house, because he too is a son of Abraham.

verses.name: Luke 19:10
verses.text: For the Son of Man came to seek and to save those who are lost.”  <div eID="gen26473" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 19:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11068"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Ten Minas</title> <div sID="gen26474" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11068"/>Now <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“were listening to”)</note> they were listening to these things, he went on and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went on”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> told a parable, because he was near Jerusalem and they thought that the kingdom of God was going to appear immediately.

verses.name: Luke 19:12
verses.text: Therefore he said, “A certain nobleman traveled to a distant country to receive for himself a kingdom and to return.

verses.name: Luke 19:13
verses.text: And summoning ten of his own slaves, he gave them ten minas<note placement="foot">A Greek monetary unit equal to 100 drachmas</note> and said to them, ‘Do business <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞until I come back⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.’<note placement="foot">Literally “in which time I am coming back”</note>

verses.name: Luke 19:14
verses.text: But his citizens hated him, and sent a delegation after him, saying, ‘We do not want this man to be king over us!’

verses.name: Luke 19:15
verses.text: And it happened that when he returned <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“receiving”) which is understood as temporal</note> receiving the kingdom, he ordered these slaves to whom he had given the money to be summoned to him, so that he could know what they had gained by trading.

verses.name: Luke 19:16
verses.text: So the first arrived, saying, ‘Sir, your mina has made ten minas more!’

verses.name: Luke 19:17
verses.text: And he said to him, ‘Well done, good slave! Because you have been faithful in a very small thing, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞have authority⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “be having authority”</note> over ten cities.’

verses.name: Luke 19:18
verses.text: And the second came, saying, ‘Sir, your mina has made five minas.’

verses.name: Luke 19:19
verses.text: So he said to this one also, ‘And you be over five cities.’

verses.name: Luke 19:20
verses.text: And another came, saying, ‘Sir, behold your mina, which I had put away for safekeeping in a piece of cloth.

verses.name: Luke 19:21
verses.text: For I was afraid of you, because you are a severe man—you withdraw what you did not deposit, and you reap what you did not sow!’

verses.name: Luke 19:22
verses.text: He said to him, ‘<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞By your own words⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from your own mouth”</note> I will judge you, wicked slave! You knew that I am a severe man, withdrawing what I did not deposit and reaping what I did not sow.

verses.name: Luke 19:23
verses.text: And why did you not give my money to the bank, and I, <transChange type="added">when I</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“returned”) which is understood as temporal</note> returned, would have collected it with interest?’

verses.name: Luke 19:24
verses.text: And to the bystanders he said, ‘Take away from him the mina and give <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to the one who has the ten minas!’

verses.name: Luke 19:25
verses.text: And they said to him, ‘Sir, he has ten minas.’

verses.name: Luke 19:26
verses.text: ‘I tell you that to everyone who has, <transChange type="added">more</transChange> will be given. But from the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away.

verses.name: Luke 19:27
verses.text: But these enemies of mine who did not want me to be king over them—bring <transChange type="added">them</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> here and slaughter them <transChange type="added">in</transChange> my presence!’ ”  <div eID="gen26474" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 19:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11069"/><title type="x-s">The Triumphal Entry</title> <div sID="gen26475" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11069"/>And <transChange type="added">after he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had said”) which is understood as temporal</note> had said these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, he traveled on ahead, going up to Jerusalem.

verses.name: Luke 19:29
verses.text: And it happened that when he drew near to Bethphage and Bethany, to the hill<note placement="foot">Or “mountain”</note> called <transChange type="added">the Mount</transChange> of Olives, he sent two of the disciples,

verses.name: Luke 19:30
verses.text: saying, ‘Go into the village in front of <transChange type="added">you</transChange>, in which <transChange type="added">as you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“enter”) which is understood as temporal</note> enter you will find a colt tied, on which <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞no person has ever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “no one of men ever”</note> sat, and untie it and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“untie”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> bring it.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Luke 19:31
verses.text: And if anyone asks you, ‘Why are you untying <transChange type="added">it</transChange>?’<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> you will say this: ‘The Lord has need of it.’ ”

verses.name: Luke 19:32
verses.text: So those who were sent went <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> found it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> just as he had told them.

verses.name: Luke 19:33
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“were untying”)</note> they were untying the colt, its owners said to them, ‘Why are you untying the colt?’

verses.name: Luke 19:34
verses.text: So they said, ‘The Lord has need of it.’

verses.name: Luke 19:35
verses.text: And they brought it to Jesus, and throwing their cloaks on the colt, they put Jesus <transChange type="added">on it</transChange>.

verses.name: Luke 19:36
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was going along”)</note> he was going along, they were spreading out their cloaks on the road.

verses.name: Luke 19:37
verses.text: Now <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was drawing near”)</note> he was drawing near by this time to the descent from the Mount of Olives, the whole crowd of the disciples began rejoicing to praise God with a loud voice for all the miracles that they had seen,

verses.name: Luke 19:38
verses.text: saying, <div eID="gen26475" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen26476"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26477"/>“Blessed <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the king,<l eID="gen26477" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26478"/>the one who comes in the name of the Lord!<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.118.26">Ps 118:26, </reference>with “the king” added as a clarification</note><l eID="gen26478" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26479"/>Peace in heaven<l eID="gen26479" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26480"/>and glory in the highest!” <l eID="gen26480" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen26476"/>

verses.name: Luke 19:39
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11070"/><div sID="gen26481" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11070"/>And some of the Pharisees from the crowd said to him, “Teacher, rebuke your disciples!”

verses.name: Luke 19:40
verses.text: And he answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “I tell you that<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts omit “that”</note> if these keep silent, the stones will cry out!”  <div eID="gen26481" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 19:41
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11071"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Weeps over Jerusalem</title> <div sID="gen26482" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11071"/>And when he approached <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“approached”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> saw the city, he wept over it,

verses.name: Luke 19:42
verses.text: saying, “If you had known on this day—even you—the things <transChange type="added">that make</transChange> for peace! But now they are hidden from your eyes.

verses.name: Luke 19:43
verses.text: For days will come upon you and your enemies will put up an embankment<note placement="foot">Or “a palisade” (the term can refer to either a wooden or an earthen barricade)</note> against you, and will surround you and press you hard from all directions.

verses.name: Luke 19:44
verses.text: And they will raze you to the ground, <transChange type="added">you</transChange> and your children within you, and will not leave a stone upon a stone within you, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞because⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in return for which”</note> you did not recognize the time of your visitation.”  <div eID="gen26482" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 19:45
