verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11072"/><title type="x-s">The Cleansing of the Temple</title> <div sID="gen26483" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11072"/>And he entered into the temple <transChange type="added">courts</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“entered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> began to drive out those who were selling,

verses.name: Luke 19:46
verses.text: saying to them, “It is written, ‘And my house will be a house of prayer,’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.56.7">Isa 56:7</reference></note> but you have made it a cave of robbers!”  <div eID="gen26483" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 19:47
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11073"/><div sID="gen26484" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11073"/>And he was teaching every day in the temple <transChange type="added">courts</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> and the chief priests and the scribes and the most prominent men of the people were seeking to destroy him.

verses.name: Luke 19:48
verses.text: And they did not find anything they could do, because all the people were paying close attention to <transChange type="added">what</transChange> they were hearing from him.  <chapter eID="Luke.19"/>

verses.name: Luke 20:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11074"/><title type="x-s">Jesus’ Authority Challenged</title> <div sID="gen26485" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11074"/>And it happened that on one of the days <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was teaching”)</note> he was teaching the people in the temple courts<note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> and proclaiming the gospel, the chief priests and the scribes approached together with the elders

verses.name: Luke 20:2
verses.text: and said, saying to him, “Tell us, by what authority you are doing these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, or who is the one who gave you this authority?

verses.name: Luke 20:3
verses.text: And he answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to them, “I also will ask you a question, and you tell me:

verses.name: Luke 20:4
verses.text: The baptism of John—was <transChange type="added">it</transChange> from heaven or from men?

verses.name: Luke 20:5
verses.text: And they discussed <transChange type="added">this</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> with one another, saying, “If we say ‘From heaven,’ he will say, ‘Why did you not believe him?’

verses.name: Luke 20:6
verses.text: But if we say, ‘From men,’ all the people will stone us to death, because they are convinced <transChange type="added">that</transChange> John was a prophet.”

verses.name: Luke 20:7
verses.text: And they replied <transChange type="added">that they</transChange> did not know where <transChange type="added">it was</transChange> from.

verses.name: Luke 20:8
verses.text: And Jesus said to them, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I am doing these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>.”  <div eID="gen26485" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 20:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11075"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Tenant Farmers in the Vineyard</title> <div sID="gen26486" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11075"/>And he began to tell the people this parable: “A man<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “A certain man”</note> planted a vineyard, and leased it to tenant farmers, and went on a journey for a long time.

verses.name: Luke 20:10
verses.text: And at the proper time he sent a slave to the tenant farmers, so that they would give him <transChange type="added">some</transChange> of the fruit of the vineyard. But the tenant farmers sent him away empty-handed <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“beating”) which is understood as temporal</note> beating him.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Luke 20:11
verses.text: And he proceeded to send another slave, but they beat and dishonored that one also, <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the two previous participles (“beat” and “dishonored”) have been translated as finite verbs</note> sent him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> away empty-handed.

verses.name: Luke 20:12
verses.text: And he proceeded to send a third, but they wounded <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“wounded”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> threw out this one also.

verses.name: Luke 20:13
verses.text: So the owner of the vineyard said, ‘What should I do? I will send my beloved son; perhaps they will respect him.’

verses.name: Luke 20:14
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> the tenant farmers saw him, they began to reason<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to reason”)</note> with one another, saying, ‘This is the heir. Let us kill him so that the inheritance will become ours!’

verses.name: Luke 20:15
verses.text: And they threw him out of the vineyard <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“threw”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> killed him.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> What then will the owner of the vineyard do to them?

verses.name: Luke 20:16
verses.text: He will come and destroy those tenant farmers and give the vineyard to others.” And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard this,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> they said, “<transChange type="added">May this</transChange> never happen!”

verses.name: Luke 20:17
verses.text: But he looked intently at them <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“looked intently at”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “What then is this that is written: <div eID="gen26486" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen26487"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26488"/>‘The stone which the builders rejected,<l eID="gen26488" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26489"/>this has become <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the cornerstone⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.’<note placement="foot">Literally “the head of the corner”</note> <l eID="gen26489" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen26487"/>

verses.name: Luke 20:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11076"/><div sID="gen26490" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11076"/>Everyone who falls on that stone will be broken to pieces, and <transChange type="added">the one</transChange> on whom it falls—it will crush him!”

verses.name: Luke 20:19
verses.text: And the scribes and the chief priests sought to lay <transChange type="added">their</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> hands on him at <transChange type="added">that</transChange> same hour, and they were afraid of the people, for they knew that he had told this parable with reference to them.  <div eID="gen26490" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 20:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11077"/><title type="x-s">Paying Taxes to Caesar</title> <div sID="gen26491" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11077"/>And they watched <transChange type="added">him</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> closely and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“watched closely”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> sent spies who pretended they were upright, in order that they could catch him in a statement, so that they could hand him over to the authority and the jurisdiction of the governor.

verses.name: Luke 20:21
verses.text: And they asked him, saying, “Teacher, we know that you speak and teach rightly, and do not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞show partiality⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “receive face”</note> but teach the way of God in truth.

verses.name: Luke 20:22
verses.text: Is it permitted <transChange type="added">for</transChange> us to pay taxes<note placement="foot">Or “the tribute tax”</note> to Caesar or not?”

verses.name: Luke 20:23
verses.text: But seeing through their craftiness, he said to them,

verses.name: Luke 20:24
verses.text: “Show me a denarius! Whose image and inscription does it have?” And they answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “And they said”</note> “Caesar’s.”

verses.name: Luke 20:25
verses.text: So he said to them, “Well then, give to Caesar the things of Caesar, and to God the things of God!”

verses.name: Luke 20:26
verses.text: And they were not able to catch <transChange type="added">him</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note><note placement="foot">Some manuscripts explicitly state “him”</note> in a statement in the sight of the people, and astonished at his answer, they became silent.  <div eID="gen26491" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 20:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11078"/><title type="x-s">A Question About Marriage and the Resurrection</title> <div sID="gen26492" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11078"/>Now some of the Sadducees—who deny <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞that there is a resurrection⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “resurrection not to exist”</note>—came up and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> asked him,

verses.name: Luke 20:28
verses.text: saying, “Teacher, Moses wrote for us if someone’s brother dies having a wife, and this man is childless, that his brother should take the wife and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞father⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “raise up”</note> descendants for his brother.

verses.name: Luke 20:29
verses.text: Now there were seven brothers, and the first took a wife <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> died childless,

verses.name: Luke 20:30
verses.text: and the second,

verses.name: Luke 20:31
verses.text: and the third took her, and likewise also the seven did not leave children and died.

verses.name: Luke 20:32
verses.text: Finally the woman also died.

verses.name: Luke 20:33
verses.text: Therefore in the resurrection, the woman—whose wife will she be? For the seven had her <transChange type="added">as</transChange> wife.”

verses.name: Luke 20:34
verses.text: And Jesus said to them, “The sons of this age marry and are given in marriage,

verses.name: Luke 20:35
verses.text: but those who are considered worthy to attain to that age and <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the resurrection from the dead neither marry nor are given in marriage,

verses.name: Luke 20:36
verses.text: for they are not even able to die any longer, because they are like the angels and are sons of God, <transChange type="added">because they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“are”) which is understood as causal</note> are sons of the resurrection.

verses.name: Luke 20:37
verses.text: But that the dead are raised, even Moses revealed in <transChange type="added">the passage about</transChange><note placement="foot">*The words “the passage about” are not in the Greek text but are implied; here a common form of rabbinic citation is being used to refer to an Old Testament passage</note> the bush, when he calls the Lord the God of Abraham and <transChange type="added">the</transChange> God of Isaac and <transChange type="added">the</transChange> God of Jacob.

verses.name: Luke 20:38
verses.text: Now he is not God of the dead, but of the living, for all live to him!”

verses.name: Luke 20:39
verses.text: And some of the scribes answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “Teacher, you have spoken well.”

verses.name: Luke 20:40
verses.text: For they no longer dared to ask him anything.  <div eID="gen26492" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 20:41
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11079"/><title type="x-s">David’s Son and Lord</title> <div sID="gen26493" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11079"/>But he said to them, “In what sense do they say <transChange type="added">that</transChange> the Christ is David’s son?

verses.name: Luke 20:42
verses.text: For David himself says in the book of Psalms, <div eID="gen26493" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen26494"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26495"/>‘The Lord said to my Lord,<l eID="gen26495" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26496"/>“Sit at my right hand, <l eID="gen26496" level="2"/>

verses.name: Luke 20:43
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11080"/><l level="1" sID="gen26497"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11080"/>until I make your enemies<l eID="gen26497" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26498"/>a footstool for your feet.” ’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.110.1">Ps 110:1</reference></note> <l eID="gen26498" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen26494"/>

verses.name: Luke 20:44
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11081"/><div sID="gen26499" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11081"/>David therefore calls him ‘Lord,’ and how is he his son?”  <div eID="gen26499" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 20:45
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11082"/><title type="x-s">Warning to Beware of the Scribes</title> <div sID="gen26500" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11082"/>And <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“were listening”)</note> all the people were listening, he said to the disciples,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “to his disciples”</note>

verses.name: Luke 20:46
verses.text: “Beware of the scribes, who like walking around in long robes and who love greetings in the marketplaces and the best seats in the synagogues and the places of honor at banquets,

verses.name: Luke 20:47
verses.text: who devour the houses of widows and pray lengthy <transChange type="added">prayers</transChange> for the sake of appearance. These will receive more severe condemnation!”  <chapter eID="Luke.20"/>

verses.name: Luke 21:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11083"/><title type="x-s">A Poor Widow’s Offering</title> <div sID="gen26501" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11083"/>And he looked up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“looked up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> saw the rich putting their gifts into the contribution box,

verses.name: Luke 21:2
verses.text: and he saw a certain poor widow putting in there two small copper coins.<note placement="foot">This coin was the <hi type="italic">lepton</hi>, worth 1/128 of a denarius</note>

verses.name: Luke 21:3
verses.text: And he said, “Truly I say to you that this poor widow put in more than all <transChange type="added">of them</transChange>.

verses.name: Luke 21:4
verses.text: For these all put <transChange type="added">gifts</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> into the offering out of their abundance, but this <transChange type="added">woman</transChange> out of her poverty put in all the means of subsistence that she had.”  <div eID="gen26501" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 21:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11084"/><title type="x-s">The Destruction of the Temple Predicted</title> <div sID="gen26502" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11084"/>And <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“were speaking”)</note> some were speaking about the temple, that it was adorned with precious stones and votive offerings, he said,

verses.name: Luke 21:6
verses.text: “<transChange type="added">As for</transChange> these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> that you see—days will come in which not <transChange type="added">one</transChange> stone will be left on <transChange type="added">another</transChange> stone that will not be thrown down!”  <div eID="gen26502" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 21:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11085"/><title type="x-s">Signs of the End of the Age</title> <div sID="gen26503" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11085"/>And they asked him, saying, “Teacher, when therefore will these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> happen, and what <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> the sign when these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> are about to take place?”

verses.name: Luke 21:8
verses.text: And he said, Watch out that you are not deceived! For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am <transChange type="added">he</transChange>,’ and ‘The time is near!’ Do not go after them!

verses.name: Luke 21:9
verses.text: And when you hear about wars and insurrections, do not be terrified, for these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> must happen first, but the end <transChange type="added">will</transChange> not <transChange type="added">be</transChange> at once.”

verses.name: Luke 21:10
verses.text: Then he said to them, “nation will rise up against nation and kingdom against kingdom.

verses.name: Luke 21:11
verses.text: There will be great earthquakes and famines and plagues in <transChange type="added">various</transChange> places. There will be terrible sights and great signs from heaven.  <div eID="gen26503" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 21:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11086"/><title type="x-s">Persecution of Disciples Predicted</title> <div sID="gen26504" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11086"/>“But before all these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, they will lay their hands on you and will persecute <transChange type="added">you</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> handing you<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> over to the synagogues and prisons. You will be brought before<note placement="foot">*Here the participle (“be brought before”) is translated as a finite verb because of English style</note> kings and governors because of my name.

verses.name: Luke 21:13
verses.text: This will turn out to you for a <transChange type="added">time of</transChange> witness.

verses.name: Luke 21:14
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Therefore make up your minds⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “therefore place in your hearts”</note> not to prepare in advance to speak in your own defense,

verses.name: Luke 21:15
verses.text: for I will give you a mouth and wisdom that all your opponents will not be able to resist or contradict.

verses.name: Luke 21:16
verses.text: And you will be handed over even by parents and brothers and relatives and friends, and they will put to death <transChange type="added">some</transChange> of you.

verses.name: Luke 21:17
verses.text: And you will be hated by all because of my name.

verses.name: Luke 21:18
verses.text: Even a hair of your head will never perish!

verses.name: Luke 21:19
verses.text: By your patient endurance you will gain your lives.  <div eID="gen26504" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 21:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11087"/><title type="x-s">The Desolation of Jerusalem</title> <div sID="gen26505" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11087"/>“But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that its desolation has come near.

verses.name: Luke 21:21
verses.text: Then those in Judea must flee to the mountains, and those <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞inside it⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in the midst of it”</note> must depart, and those in the fields must not enter into it,

verses.name: Luke 21:22
verses.text: because these are days of vengeance, <transChange type="added">so that</transChange> all the things that are written can be fulfilled.

verses.name: Luke 21:23
verses.text: Woe to those <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who are pregnant⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “who have in the womb”</note> and to those who are nursing their babies<note placement="foot">*The words “their babies” are not in the Greek text but are supplied as a necessary clarification</note> in those days! For there will be great distress on the earth and wrath against this people,

verses.name: Luke 21:24
verses.text: and they will fall by the edge of the sword, and will be led captive into all the nations,<note placement="foot">The same Greek word, occurring three times in this verse, can be translated “nations” or “Gentiles” depending on the context</note> and Jerusalem will be trampled down by the Gentiles until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled.  <div eID="gen26505" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 21:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11088"/><title type="x-s">The Arrival of the Son of Man</title> <div sID="gen26506" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11088"/>“And there will be signs in the sun and moon and stars, and on the earth distress of nations in perplexity from the noise of the sea and <transChange type="added">its</transChange> surging,

verses.name: Luke 21:26
verses.text: people fainting from fear and expectation of what is coming on the inhabited earth, for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.<note placement="foot">An allusion to <reference osisRef="Isa.34.4">Isa 34:4</reference></note>

verses.name: Luke 21:27
verses.text: And then they will see the Son of Man arriving in a cloud<note placement="foot">An allusion to <reference osisRef="Dan.7.13">Dan 7:13</reference></note> with power and great glory.

verses.name: Luke 21:28
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“begin”)</note> these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> begin to happen, stand up straight and raise your heads, because your redemption is drawing near!”  <div eID="gen26506" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 21:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11089"/><title type="x-s">The Parable of the Fig Tree</title> <div sID="gen26507" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11089"/>And he told them a parable: “Look at the fig tree and all the trees.

verses.name: Luke 21:30
verses.text: When they put out <transChange type="added">foliage</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> now you see for yourselves and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“see”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> know that by this time the summer is near.

verses.name: Luke 21:31
verses.text: So also you, when you see these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> happening, know<note placement="foot">Or “you know”</note> that the kingdom of God is near.

verses.name: Luke 21:32
verses.text: Truly I say to you that this generation will never pass away until all <transChange type="added">things</transChange> take place!

verses.name: Luke 21:33
verses.text: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will never pass away.  <div eID="gen26507" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 21:34
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11090"/><title type="x-s">Be Alert</title> <div sID="gen26508" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11090"/>“But take care for yourselves, lest your hearts are weighed down with dissipation and drunkenness and the worries of daily life, and that day come upon you suddenly

verses.name: Luke 21:35
verses.text: like a trap. For it will come upon all who reside on the face of the whole earth.

verses.name: Luke 21:36
verses.text: But be alert at all times, praying that you may have strength to escape all these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> <transChange type="added">that</transChange> are going to happen, and to stand before the Son of Man.”  <div eID="gen26508" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 21:37
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11091"/><div sID="gen26509" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11091"/>So <transChange type="added">throughout</transChange> the days he was teaching in the temple <transChange type="added">courts</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> and throughout the nights he was going out and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“was going out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> spending the night on the hill that is called <transChange type="added">the Mount</transChange> of Olives.

verses.name: Luke 21:38
verses.text: And all the people were getting up very early in the morning <transChange type="added">to come</transChange><note placement="foot">*The words “to come” are not in the Greek text but are implied</note> to him in the temple courts<note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> to listen to him.  <chapter eID="Luke.21"/>

verses.name: Luke 22:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11092"/><title type="x-s">The Chief Priests and Scribes Plot to Kill Jesus</title> <div sID="gen26510" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11092"/>Now the feast of Unleavened Bread (which is called Passover) was drawing near.

verses.name: Luke 22:2
verses.text: And the chief priests and the scribes were seeking how they could destroy him, because they were afraid of the people.  <div eID="gen26510" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 22:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11093"/><title type="x-s">Judas Arranges to Betray Jesus</title> <div sID="gen26511" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11093"/>And Satan entered into Judas, the one called Iscariot, who was of the number of the twelve.

verses.name: Luke 22:4
verses.text: And he went away <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went away”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> discussed with the chief priests and officers of the temple guard how he could betray him to them.

verses.name: Luke 22:5
verses.text: And they were delighted, and came to an agreement with him to give <transChange type="added">him</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> money.

verses.name: Luke 22:6
verses.text: And he agreed, and began looking<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began looking”)</note> for a favorable opportunity to betray him to them apart from the crowd.  <div eID="gen26511" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 22:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11094"/><title type="x-s">Jesus’ Final Passover with the Disciples</title> <div sID="gen26512" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11094"/>And the day of the feast of Unleavened Bread came, on which it was necessary <transChange type="added">for</transChange> the Passover lamb to be sacrificed.

verses.name: Luke 22:8
verses.text: And he sent Peter and John, saying, “Go <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“go”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> prepare the Passover for us, so that we may eat it.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Luke 22:9
verses.text: So they said to him, “Where do you want us to prepare <transChange type="added">it</transChange>?”<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Luke 22:10
verses.text: And he said to them, “Behold, <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“have entered”)</note> you have entered into the city, a man carrying a jar of water will meet you. Follow him into the house which he enters.

verses.name: Luke 22:11
verses.text: And you will say to the master of the house, ‘The Teacher says to you, “Where is the guest room where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?” ’

verses.name: Luke 22:12
verses.text: And he will show you a large furnished<note placement="foot">Or perhaps “paved” or “panelled”</note> upstairs room. Make preparations there.”

verses.name: Luke 22:13
verses.text: So they went <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> found everything<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> just as he had told them, and they prepared the Passover.  <div eID="gen26512" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 22:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11095"/><title type="x-s">The Lord’s Supper</title> <div sID="gen26513" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11095"/>And when the hour came, he reclined at the table, and the apostles with him.

verses.name: Luke 22:15
verses.text: And he said to them, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I have earnestly desired⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “I have desired with desire”</note> to eat this Passover with you before I suffer.

verses.name: Luke 22:16
verses.text: For I tell you that I will not eat it until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God.”

verses.name: Luke 22:17
verses.text: And he took in hand a cup, <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took in hand”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> after<note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the temporal participle (“giving thanks”)</note> giving thanks he said, “Take this and share it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> among yourselves.

verses.name: Luke 22:18
verses.text: For I tell you,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “I tell you that”</note> from now on I will not drink of the product of the vine until the kingdom of God comes.”  <div eID="gen26513" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 22:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11096"/><div sID="gen26514" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11096"/>And he took bread, <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> after<note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the temporal participle (“giving thanks”)</note> giving thanks, he broke it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and gave it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to them, saying, “This is my body which is given for you. Do this in remembrance of me.”

verses.name: Luke 22:20
verses.text: And in the same way the cup after <transChange type="added">they</transChange> had eaten, saying, “This cup <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the new covenant in my blood which is poured out for you.  <div eID="gen26514" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 22:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11097"/><div sID="gen26515" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11097"/>“But behold, the hand of the one who is betraying me <transChange type="added">is</transChange> with me on the table!

verses.name: Luke 22:22
verses.text: For the Son of Man is going according to what has been determined, but woe to that man by whom he is betrayed!”

verses.name: Luke 22:23
verses.text: And they began to debate with one another who then of them it could be who was going to do this.  <div eID="gen26515" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 22:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11098"/><title type="x-s">A Dispute About Who Is Greatest</title> <div sID="gen26516" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11098"/>And a dispute also occurred among them as to which of them was recognized as being greatest.

verses.name: Luke 22:25
verses.text: So he said to them, “The kings of the Gentiles<note placement="foot">The same Greek word can be translated “nations” or “Gentiles” depending on the context</note> lord it over them, and those who have authority over them are called benefactors.

verses.name: Luke 22:26
verses.text: But you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> not <transChange type="added">to be</transChange> like this! But the one who is greatest among you must become like the youngest, and the one who leads like the one who serves.

verses.name: Luke 22:27
verses.text: For who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> greater, the one who reclines at the table or the one who serves? <transChange type="added">Is it</transChange> not the one who reclines at the table? But I am in your midst as the one who serves.  <div eID="gen26516" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 22:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11099"/><div sID="gen26517" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11099"/>“And you are the ones who have remained<note placement="foot">Or “ones who have continued”</note> with me in my trials,

verses.name: Luke 22:29
verses.text: and I confer on you a kingdom, just as my Father conferred on me,

verses.name: Luke 22:30
verses.text: that you may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and you will sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.  <div eID="gen26517" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 22:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11100"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Predicts Peter’s Denial</title> <div sID="gen26518" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11100"/>“Simon, Simon, behold, Satan has demanded to sift you like wheat,

verses.name: Luke 22:32
verses.text: but I have prayed for you, that your faith may not fail. And you, <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“have turned back”) which is understood as temporal</note> once you have turned back,<note placement="foot">Or “have turned around”</note> strengthen your brothers.”

verses.name: Luke 22:33
verses.text: But he said to him, “Lord, I am ready to go with you both to prison and to death!”

verses.name: Luke 22:34
verses.text: And he said, “I tell you, Peter, the rooster will not crow today until you have denied three times <transChange type="added">that you</transChange> know me!”  <div eID="gen26518" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 22:35
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11101"/><title type="x-s">The Two Swords</title> <div sID="gen26519" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11101"/>And he said to them, “When I sent you out without a money bag and a traveler’s bag and sandals, you did not lack anything, <transChange type="added">did you</transChange>?”<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here, indicated in the translation by “did you”</note> And they said, “Nothing.”

verses.name: Luke 22:36
verses.text: And he said to them, “But now the one who has a money bag must take <transChange type="added">it</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and likewise a traveler’s bag. And the one who does not have a sword must sell his cloak and buy <transChange type="added">one</transChange>.

verses.name: Luke 22:37
verses.text: For I tell you that this that is written must be fulfilled in me: ‘And he was counted with the criminals.’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.53.12">Isa 53:12</reference></note> For indeed, what is written<note placement="foot">*The phrase “what is written” is not in the Greek text but is an understood repetition of the similar phrase at the beginning of the verse</note> about me <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞is being fulfilled⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “is having an end”</note>

verses.name: Luke 22:38
verses.text: So they said, “Lord, behold, here <transChange type="added">are</transChange> two swords!” And he said to them, “It is adequate.”  <div eID="gen26519" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 22:39
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11102"/><title type="x-s">The Prayer in Gethsemane</title> <div sID="gen26520" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11102"/>And he went away <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went away”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> proceeded, according to his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> custom, to the Mount of Olives, and the disciples also followed him.

verses.name: Luke 22:40
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“came”) which is understood as temporal</note> he came to the place, he said to them, “Pray that you will not enter into temptation.”

verses.name: Luke 22:41
verses.text: And he withdrew from them about a stone’s throw and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞knelt down⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “bent his knees”</note> and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“knelt down”; literally “bent his knees”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> began to pray,<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to pray”)</note>

verses.name: Luke 22:42
verses.text: saying, “Father, if you are willing, take away this cup from me. Nevertheless, not my will but yours be done.” 〚

verses.name: Luke 22:43
verses.text: And an angel from heaven appeared to him, strengthening him.

verses.name: Luke 22:44
verses.text: And being in anguish, he began praying<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began praying”)</note> more fervently and his sweat became like drops of blood falling down to the ground.〛<note placement="foot">A number of early and important Greek manuscripts lack verses 43 and 44</note>

verses.name: Luke 22:45
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“got up”) which is understood as temporal</note> got up from the prayer and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the participle (“came”) has been translated as a finite verb in keeping with English style</note> came to the disciples, he found them sleeping from sorrow,

verses.name: Luke 22:46
verses.text: and he said to them, “Why are you sleeping? Get up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“get up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> pray that you will not enter into temptation!”  <div eID="gen26520" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 22:47
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11103"/><title type="x-s">The Betrayal and Arrest of Jesus</title> <div sID="gen26521" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11103"/><transChange type="added">While</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“speaking”)</note> he was still speaking, behold, <transChange type="added">there came</transChange> a crowd, and the one named Judas, one of the twelve, leading them. And he approached Jesus to kiss him.

verses.name: Luke 22:48
verses.text: But Jesus said to him, “Judas, are you betraying the Son of Man with a kiss?”

verses.name: Luke 22:49
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> those around him saw what was about to happen, they said, “Lord, should we strike with the sword?”

verses.name: Luke 22:50
verses.text: And a certain one of them struck the slave of the high priest and cut off his right ear.

verses.name: Luke 22:51
verses.text: But Jesus answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Stop! No more of this!⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>”<note placement="foot">Literally “leave off to this”</note> And he touched his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> ear and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“touched”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> healed him.

verses.name: Luke 22:52
verses.text: And Jesus said to the chief priests and officers of the temple and elders who had come out against him, “Have you come out with swords and clubs, as against a robber?

verses.name: Luke 22:53
verses.text: Every day <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was”)</note> I was with you in the temple courts,<note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> you did not stretch out your<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> hands against me! But this is your hour and the domain of darkness!”  <div eID="gen26521" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 22:54
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11104"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Before the Sanhedrin</title> <div sID="gen26522" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11104"/>And they arrested him <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“arrested”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> led him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> away and brought him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> into the house of the high priest. But Peter was following at a distance.

verses.name: Luke 22:55
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had kindled”) which is understood as temporal</note> had kindled a fire in the middle of the courtyard and sat down together, Peter sat down among them.

verses.name: Luke 22:56
verses.text: And a certain female slave, seeing him sitting in the light and looking intently at him, said, “This man also was with him!”

verses.name: Luke 22:57
verses.text: But he denied <transChange type="added">it</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> saying, “Woman, I do not know him!”

verses.name: Luke 22:58
verses.text: And after a short time another person saw him <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“saw”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “You also are <transChange type="added">one</transChange> of them!” But Peter said, “Man, I am not!”

verses.name: Luke 22:59
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“had passed”)</note> about one hour had passed, someone else was insisting, saying, “In truth this man also was with him, because he is also a Galilean!”

verses.name: Luke 22:60
verses.text: But Peter said, “Man, I do not know what you are talking about!” And immediately, <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was speaking”)</note> he was still speaking, a rooster crowed.

verses.name: Luke 22:61
verses.text: And the Lord turned around <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“turned around”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> looked intently at Peter. And Peter remembered the word of the Lord,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “the Lord’s statement”</note> how he said to him, “Before the rooster crows today, you will deny me three times.”

verses.name: Luke 22:62
verses.text: And he went outside <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> wept bitterly.  <div eID="gen26522" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 22:63
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11105"/><div sID="gen26523" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11105"/>And the men who were guarding him began to mock<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to mock”)</note> him while<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“beat”) which is understood as temporal</note> they beat him,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Luke 22:64
verses.text: and <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“blindfolding”) which is understood as temporal</note> blindfolding him they repeatedly asked<note placement="foot">*This imperfect verb is translated as iterative (“repeatedly asked”)</note> him,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> saying, “Prophesy! Who is the one who struck you?”

verses.name: Luke 22:65
verses.text: And they were saying many other <transChange type="added">things</transChange> against him, reviling <transChange type="added">him</transChange>.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>  <div eID="gen26523" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 22:66
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11106"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Before the Sanhedrin</title> <div sID="gen26524" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11106"/>And when day came, the council of elders of the people gathered, both chief priests and scribes, and they led him away to their Sanhedrin,<note placement="foot">Or “council”</note>

verses.name: Luke 22:67
verses.text: saying, “If you are the Christ, tell us!” But he said to them, “If I tell you, you will never believe,

verses.name: Luke 22:68
verses.text: and if I ask <transChange type="added">you</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> you will never answer!

verses.name: Luke 22:69
verses.text: But from now on the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the power of God.”

verses.name: Luke 22:70
verses.text: So they all said, “Are you then the Son of God?” And he said to them, “You say that I am.”

verses.name: Luke 22:71
verses.text: And they said, “Why do we have need <transChange type="added">of</transChange> further testimony? For <transChange type="added">we</transChange> ourselves have heard <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> from his mouth!”  <chapter eID="Luke.22"/>

verses.name: Luke 23:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11107"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Brought Before Pilate</title> <div sID="gen26525" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11107"/>And the whole assembly of them rose up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“rose up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> brought him before Pilate.

verses.name: Luke 23:2
verses.text: And they began to accuse him, saying, “We have found this man misleading our nation and forbidding <transChange type="added">us</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to pay taxes to Caesar, and saying <transChange type="added">he</transChange> himself is Christ, a king!”

verses.name: Luke 23:3
verses.text: And Pilate asked him, saying, “Are you the king of the Jews?” And he answered him <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “You say <transChange type="added">so</transChange>.”

verses.name: Luke 23:4
verses.text: So Pilate said to the chief priests and the crowds, “I find no basis for an accusation against this man.”

verses.name: Luke 23:5
verses.text: But they insisted, saying, “He incites the people, teaching throughout the whole of Judea and beginning from Galilee as far as here.”  <div eID="gen26525" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 23:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11108"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Brought Before Herod</title> <div sID="gen26526" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11108"/>Now <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> Pilate heard this,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> he asked if the man was a Galilean.

verses.name: Luke 23:7
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“found out”) which is understood as temporal</note> found out that he was from the jurisdiction of Herod, he sent him over to Herod, who was also in Jerusalem in those days.

verses.name: Luke 23:8
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> Herod saw Jesus, he was very glad, for he had been wanting to see him for a long time, because he had heard about him and was hoping to see some miracle performed by him.

verses.name: Luke 23:9
verses.text: So he questioned him <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞at considerable length⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “with many words”</note> but he answered nothing to him.

verses.name: Luke 23:10
verses.text: And the chief priests and the scribes were standing there vehemently accusing him.

verses.name: Luke 23:11
verses.text: And Herod with his soldiers also treated him with contempt, and <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“mocking”) which is understood as temporal</note> mocking him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied to connect the two participles (“mocking” and “dressing”) in keeping with English style</note> dressing him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> <transChange type="added">in</transChange> glistening clothing, he sent him back to Pilate.

verses.name: Luke 23:12
verses.text: And both Herod and Pilate became friends with one another on <transChange type="added">that</transChange> same day, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞for they had previously been enemies of one another⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “for they had previously existed being at enmity with each other”</note>  <div eID="gen26526" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 23:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11109"/><title type="x-s">Pilate Releases Barabbas</title> <div sID="gen26527" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11109"/>So Pilate called together the chief priests and the rulers and the people

verses.name: Luke 23:14
verses.text: <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the participle in the previous verse (“called together”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to them, “You brought me this man as one who was misleading the people, and behold, when I<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“examined”) which is understood as temporal</note> examined him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> before you, I found nothing in this man as basis for the accusation which <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you are making⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “you are accusing”</note> against him.

verses.name: Luke 23:15
verses.text: But neither <transChange type="added">did</transChange> Herod, because he sent him back to us. And behold, nothing deserving death <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞has been done⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “is having been done”</note> by him.

verses.name: Luke 23:16
verses.text: Therefore I will punish him <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“punish”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> release him.”<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note><note placement="foot">Many of the most important Greek manuscripts lack v. <reference osisRef="Luke.23.17">17</reference>, “Now he was obligated to release for them at the feast one person.”</note>

verses.name: Luke 23:18
verses.text: But they all cried out in unison, saying, “Take this man away, and release for us Barabbas!”

verses.name: Luke 23:19
verses.text: (who had been thrown in prison because of a certain insurrection that had taken place in the city, and <transChange type="added">for</transChange> murder).

verses.name: Luke 23:20
verses.text: And Pilate, wanting to release Jesus, addressed <transChange type="added">them</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note><note placement="foot">Some manuscripts explicitly state “them”</note> again,

verses.name: Luke 23:21
verses.text: but they kept crying out, saying, “Crucify! Crucify him!”

verses.name: Luke 23:22
verses.text: So he said to them a third <transChange type="added">time</transChange>, “Why? What wrong has this man done? I found no basis for an accusation <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞deserving death⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “of death”</note> in him. Therefore I will punish him and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“punish”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> release him.”<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Luke 23:23
verses.text: But they were urgent, demanding with loud cries <transChange type="added">that</transChange> he be crucified. And their cries prevailed.

verses.name: Luke 23:24
verses.text: And Pilate decided <transChange type="added">that</transChange> their demand should be granted.

verses.name: Luke 23:25
verses.text: And he released the one who had been thrown into prison because of insurrection and murder, whom they were asking for, but Jesus he handed over to their will.  <div eID="gen26527" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 23:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11110"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Is Crucified</title> <div sID="gen26528" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11110"/>And as they led him away, they seized Simon, a certain <transChange type="added">man</transChange> of Cyrene, who was coming from the country, <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“seized”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> placed the cross on him, to carry it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> behind Jesus.

verses.name: Luke 23:27
verses.text: And a great crowd of the people were following him, and of women who were mourning and lamenting him.

verses.name: Luke 23:28
verses.text: But turning to them, Jesus said, “Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for me, but weep for yourselves and for your children!

verses.name: Luke 23:29
verses.text: For behold, days are coming in which they will say, ‘Blessed <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the barren, and the wombs that did not give birth, and <transChange type="added">the</transChange> breasts that did not nurse!’

verses.name: Luke 23:30
verses.text: Then they will begin to say to the mountains, ‘Fall on us!’ and to the hills, ‘Cover us!’

verses.name: Luke 23:31
verses.text: For if they do these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞when the wood is green⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “in the green wood”</note> what will happen <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞when it is dry⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?”<note placement="foot">Literally “in the dry”</note>  <div eID="gen26528" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 23:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11111"/><div sID="gen26529" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11111"/>And two other criminals were also led away to be executed with him.

verses.name: Luke 23:33
verses.text: And when they came to the place that is called “The Skull,” there they crucified him, and the criminals, the one on <transChange type="added">his</transChange> right and the other on <transChange type="added">his</transChange> left.

verses.name: Luke 23:34
verses.text: 〚But Jesus said, “Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing.”〛<note placement="foot">Many important manuscripts lack v. <reference osisRef="Luke.23.34a">34a</reference>, “But Jesus said, ‘Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing.’ ”</note> And they cast lots to divide his clothes.

verses.name: Luke 23:35
verses.text: And the people stood there watching, but the rulers also ridiculed <transChange type="added">him</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> saying, “He saved others; let him save himself, if this man is the Christ<note placement="foot">Or “Messiah”</note> of God, the Chosen One!”

verses.name: Luke 23:36
verses.text: And the soldiers also mocked him, coming up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied to connect the two participles (“coming up” and “offering”) in keeping with English style</note> offering him sour wine

verses.name: Luke 23:37
verses.text: and saying, “If you are the king of the Jews, save yourself!”

verses.name: Luke 23:38
verses.text: And there was also an inscription over him, “This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the king of the Jews.”  <div eID="gen26529" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 23:39
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11112"/><div sID="gen26530" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11112"/>And one of the criminals who were hanged there reviled him, saying, “Are you not the Christ? Save yourself—and us!”

verses.name: Luke 23:40
verses.text: But the other answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied to connect the two participles (“answered” and “rebuked”) in keeping with English style</note> rebuked him, saying, “Do you not even fear God, because you are undergoing the same condemnation?

verses.name: Luke 23:41
verses.text: And we indeed justly, for we are receiving <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞what we deserve⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “things worthy”</note> <transChange type="added">for</transChange> what we have done. But this man has done nothing wrong!”

verses.name: Luke 23:42
verses.text: And he said, “Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom!”

verses.name: Luke 23:43
verses.text: And he said to him, “Truly I say to you, today you will be with me in paradise.”  <div eID="gen26530" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 23:44
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11113"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Dies on the Cross</title> <div sID="gen26531" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11113"/>And by this time it was about the sixth hour, and darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour

verses.name: Luke 23:45
verses.text: <transChange type="added">because</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“failed”) which is understood as causal</note> <transChange type="added">the light</transChange> of the sun failed. And the curtain of the temple was torn apart <transChange type="added">down</transChange> the middle.

verses.name: Luke 23:46
verses.text: And Jesus, calling out with a loud voice, said, “Father, into your hands I entrust my spirit!”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.31.5">Ps 31:5</reference></note> And after he<note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“said”) which is understood as temporal</note> said this, he expired.  <div eID="gen26531" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 23:47
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11114"/><div sID="gen26532" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11114"/>Now <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> the centurion saw what had happened, he began to praise<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to praise”)</note> God, saying, “Certainly this man was righteous!”

verses.name: Luke 23:48
verses.text: And all the crowds that had come together for this spectacle, <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw the things that had happened, returned home<note placement="foot">*The word “home” is not in the Greek text, but is implied</note> beating their<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> breasts.

verses.name: Luke 23:49
verses.text: And all his acquaintances, and the women who had followed him from Galilee who saw these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, stood at a distance.  <div eID="gen26532" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 23:50
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11115"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Is Buried</title> <div sID="gen26533" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11115"/>And behold, a man <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞named⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by name”</note> Joseph, who was a member of the council,<note placement="foot">Or “a member of the Sanhedrin”</note> a good<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “and a good”</note> and righteous man

verses.name: Luke 23:51
verses.text: (this man was not consenting to their plan and deed), from Arimathea, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a Judean town⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “a town of the Jews”</note> who was looking forward to the kingdom of God.

verses.name: Luke 23:52
verses.text: This man approached Pilate <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“approached”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> asked for the body of Jesus.

verses.name: Luke 23:53
verses.text: And he took <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> down and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“wrapped”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> wrapped it in a linen cloth and placed him in a tomb cut into the rock where no one had ever been placed.

verses.name: Luke 23:54
verses.text: And it was the day of preparation, and the Sabbath was drawing near.

verses.name: Luke 23:55
verses.text: And the women who had been accompanying him from Galilee followed <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“followed”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> saw the tomb and how his body was placed.

verses.name: Luke 23:56
verses.text: And they returned <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“returned”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> prepared fragrant spices and perfumes, and on the Sabbath they rested according to the commandment.  <chapter eID="Luke.23"/>

verses.name: Luke 24:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11116"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Is Raised</title> <div sID="gen26534" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11116"/>Now on the first <transChange type="added">day</transChange> of the week, at very early dawn, they came back to the tomb bringing the fragrant spices which they had prepared.

verses.name: Luke 24:2
verses.text: And they found the stone had been rolled away from the tomb,

verses.name: Luke 24:3
verses.text: but <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“went in”) which is understood as temporal</note> went in, they did not find the body.<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts add “of the Lord Jesus”</note>

verses.name: Luke 24:4
verses.text: And it happened that while they were perplexed about this, behold, two men in gleaming clothing stood near them.

verses.name: Luke 24:5
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participles (“were” and “bowed”)</note> they were terrified and bowed their faces to the ground, they said to them, “Why are you looking for the living among the dead?

verses.name: Luke 24:6
verses.text: He is not here, but has been raised! Remember how he spoke to you <transChange type="added">while he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was”) which is understood as temporal</note> was still in Galilee,

verses.name: Luke 24:7
verses.text: saying that the Son of Man must be delivered into the hands of men <transChange type="added">who are</transChange> sinners, and be crucified, and on the third day rise?”

verses.name: Luke 24:8
verses.text: And they remembered his words,

verses.name: Luke 24:9
verses.text: and <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“returned”) which is understood as temporal</note> returned from the tomb, they reported all these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> to the eleven and to all the rest.

verses.name: Luke 24:10
verses.text: Now Mary Magdalene and Joanna and Mary the <transChange type="added">mother</transChange> of James and the others with them were telling these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> to the apostles.

verses.name: Luke 24:11
verses.text: And these words appeared to them as nonsense, and they refused to believe them.

verses.name: Luke 24:12
verses.text: But Peter got up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“got up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> ran to the tomb, and bending over to look, he saw only the strips of linen cloth, and he went away to his home<note placement="foot">Or “wondering to himself,” if the prepositional phrase modifies the following participle</note> wondering what had happened.  <div eID="gen26534" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 24:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11117"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Encountered on the Road to Emmaus</title> <div sID="gen26535" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11117"/>And behold, on <transChange type="added">that</transChange> same day, two of them were traveling to a village <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞named⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to which the name”</note> Emmaus that was sixty stadia<note placement="foot">A “stade” or “stadium” (plur. “stadia”) is about 607 ft (187 m)</note> distant from Jerusalem,

verses.name: Luke 24:14
verses.text: and they were conversing with one another about all these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> that had happened.

verses.name: Luke 24:15
verses.text: And it happened that while they were conversing, and discussing, Jesus himself also approached <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“approached”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> began to go along with<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to go along with”)</note> them,

verses.name: Luke 24:16
verses.text: but their eyes were prevented from recognizing him.

verses.name: Luke 24:17
verses.text: And he said to them, “What <transChange type="added">are</transChange> these matters that you are discussing with one another <transChange type="added">as you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“walking along”) which is understood as temporal</note> are walking along?” And they stood still, looking sad.

verses.name: Luke 24:18
verses.text: And one <transChange type="added">of them</transChange>, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞named⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by name”</note> Cleopas, answered and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to him, “<transChange type="added">Are</transChange> you the only one living near Jerusalem and not knowing the things that have happened in it in these days?”

verses.name: Luke 24:19
verses.text: And he said to them, “What <transChange type="added">things</transChange>?” So they said to him, “The things concerning Jesus the Nazarene, a man who was a prophet, powerful in deed and word before God and all the people,

verses.name: Luke 24:20
verses.text: and how our chief priests and rulers handed him over to a sentence of death, and crucified him.

verses.name: Luke 24:21
verses.text: But we were hoping that he was the one who was going to redeem Israel. But in addition to all these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, this <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the third day <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞since⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “he spends from which”</note> these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> took place.

verses.name: Luke 24:22
verses.text: But also some women from among us astonished us, who were at the tomb early in the morning,

verses.name: Luke 24:23
verses.text: and <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“find”) which is understood as temporal</note> did not find his body, they came back saying <transChange type="added">they</transChange> had seen even a vision of angels, who said <transChange type="added">that</transChange> he was alive!

verses.name: Luke 24:24
verses.text: And some of those with us went out to the tomb and found <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> like this, just as the women had also said, but him they did not see.”

verses.name: Luke 24:25
verses.text: And he said to them, “O foolish and slow in heart to believe in all that the prophets have spoken!

verses.name: Luke 24:26
verses.text: Was it not necessary <transChange type="added">that</transChange> the Christ suffer these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> and enter into his glory?”

verses.name: Luke 24:27
verses.text: And beginning from Moses and from all the prophets, he interpreted to them the things concerning himself in all the scriptures.

verses.name: Luke 24:28
verses.text: And they drew near to the village where they were going, and he acted as though he was going farther.

verses.name: Luke 24:29
verses.text: And they urged him strongly, saying, “Stay with us, because it is <transChange type="added">getting</transChange> toward evening, and by this time the day is far spent.” And he went in to stay with them.

verses.name: Luke 24:30
verses.text: And it happened that when he reclined at the table with them, he took the bread <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> gave thanks, and after<note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“breaking”) which is understood as temporal</note> breaking it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> he gave it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to them.

verses.name: Luke 24:31
verses.text: And their eyes were opened, and they recognized him, and he became invisible to them.

verses.name: Luke 24:32
verses.text: And they said to one another, “Were not our hearts burning within us while he was speaking with us on the road, while he was explaining the scriptures to us?”

verses.name: Luke 24:33
verses.text: And they got up <transChange type="added">that</transChange> same hour <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“got up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> returned to Jerusalem and found the eleven and those with them assembled,

verses.name: Luke 24:34
verses.text: saying, “The Lord has really been raised, and has appeared to Simon!”

verses.name: Luke 24:35
