verses.text: And they began describing<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began describing”)</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞what happened⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the things”</note> on the road, and how he was recognized by them in the breaking of the bread.  <div eID="gen26535" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 24:36
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11118"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Appears to His Disciples</title> <div sID="gen26536" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11118"/>And <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“were saying”)</note> they were saying these things, he himself stood there among them.<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts add “and said to them, ‘Peace to you!’ ”</note>

verses.name: Luke 24:37
verses.text: But they were startled and became terrified, <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the two previous participles (“startled” and “terrified”) have been translated as finite verbs</note> thought <transChange type="added">they</transChange> had seen a ghost.

verses.name: Luke 24:38
verses.text: And he said to them, “Why are you frightened? And for what <transChange type="added">reason</transChange> do doubts arise in your hearts?

verses.name: Luke 24:39
verses.text: Look at my hands and my feet, that I am I myself! Touch me and see, because a ghost does not have flesh and bones, as <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you see that I have⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “you see me having”</note>

verses.name: Luke 24:40
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had said”) which is understood as temporal</note> had said this, he showed them his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> hands and his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> feet.

verses.name: Luke 24:41
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“disbelieving”)</note> they were still disbelieving because of joy and were marveling, he said to them, “Do you have anything <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to eat⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “eatable”</note> here?”

verses.name: Luke 24:42
verses.text: So they gave him a piece of broiled fish,

verses.name: Luke 24:43
verses.text: and he took <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> ate it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> in front of them.  <div eID="gen26536" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 24:44
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11119"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Commissions His Disciples</title> <div sID="gen26537" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11119"/>And he said to them, “These <transChange type="added">are</transChange> my words that I spoke to you <transChange type="added">while I</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was”) which is understood as temporal</note> was still with you, that everything that is written about me in the law of Moses and the prophets and psalms must be fulfilled.”

verses.name: Luke 24:45
verses.text: Then he opened their minds to understand the scriptures,

verses.name: Luke 24:46
verses.text: and said to them, “Thus it is written <transChange type="added">that</transChange> the Christ would suffer and would rise from the dead on the third day,

verses.name: Luke 24:47
verses.text: and repentance and the forgiveness<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “repentance for the forgiveness”</note> of sins would be proclaimed in his name to all the nations,<note placement="foot">The same Greek word can be translated “nations” or “Gentiles” depending on the context</note> beginning from Jerusalem.

verses.name: Luke 24:48
verses.text: You are witnesses of these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>.

verses.name: Luke 24:49
verses.text: And behold, I am sending out<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “am sending”</note> what was promised by my Father upon you, but you stay in the city until you are clothed with power from on high.”  <div eID="gen26537" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Luke 24:50
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11120"/><title type="x-s">The Ascension</title> <div sID="gen26538" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11120"/>And he led them out as far as Bethany, and lifting up his hands, he blessed them.

verses.name: Luke 24:51
verses.text: And it happened that while he was blessing them, he parted from them and was taken up into heaven.

verses.name: Luke 24:52
verses.text: And they worshiped him <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“worshiped”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> returned to Jerusalem with great joy.

verses.name: Luke 24:53
verses.text: And they were <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞continually⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “through everything”</note> in the temple courts<note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> praising God.  <chapter eID="Luke.24"/> <div eID="gen26538" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen26156" osisID="Luke" type="book"/>

verses.name: John 1:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11121"/><title type="x-s">The Prologue to John’s Gospel</title> <div sID="gen26540" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11121"/>In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

verses.name: John 1:2
verses.text: This one was in the beginning with God.

verses.name: John 1:3
verses.text: All <transChange type="added">things</transChange> came into being through him, and apart from him not one <transChange type="added">thing</transChange> came into being that<note placement="foot">Or “came into being. What …,” beginning a new sentence connected with the following verse. A major punctuation problem is involved, since the earliest manuscripts have no punctuation, but some important later ones place the punctuation before this phrase, effectively connecting it to v. <reference osisRef="John.1.4">4</reference>: “What has come into being was life in him”</note> has come into being.

verses.name: John 1:4
verses.text: In him was life, and the life was the light of humanity.<note placement="foot">Or “humankind”</note>

verses.name: John 1:5
verses.text: And the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not overcome<note placement="foot">Or “comprehend” (if primarily referring to people in the world)</note> it.  <div eID="gen26540" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 1:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11122"/><div sID="gen26541" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11122"/>A man came, sent from God, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞whose name was⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the name to him”</note> John.

verses.name: John 1:7
verses.text: This one came for a witness, in order that he could testify about the light, so that all would believe through him.

verses.name: John 1:8
verses.text: That one was not the light, but <transChange type="added">came</transChange><note placement="foot">The verb is implied from the previous verse, and must be supplied in the English translation</note> in order that he could testify about the light.

verses.name: John 1:9
verses.text: The true light, who gives light to every person, was coming into the world.

verses.name: John 1:10
verses.text: He was in the world, and the world came into being through him, and the world did not recognize<note placement="foot">Or “acknowledge”</note> him.

verses.name: John 1:11
verses.text: He came to his own <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, and his own <transChange type="added">people</transChange> did not receive him.

verses.name: John 1:12
verses.text: But as many as received him—to those who believe in his name—he gave to them authority to become children of God,

verses.name: John 1:13
verses.text: who were born not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of a husband, but of God.  <div eID="gen26541" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 1:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11123"/><div sID="gen26542" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11123"/>And the Word became flesh and took up residence among us, and we saw his glory, glory as of the one and only from the Father, full of grace and truth.

verses.name: John 1:15
verses.text: John testified about him and cried out, saying, “This one was <transChange type="added">he about</transChange> whom I said, ‘The one who comes after me is ahead of me, because he existed before me.’ ”

verses.name: John 1:16
verses.text: For from his fullness we have all received, and grace after grace.

verses.name: John 1:17
verses.text: For the law was given through Moses; grace and truth came about through Jesus Christ.

verses.name: John 1:18
verses.text: No one has seen God at any time; the one and only, God, the one who is in the bosom of the Father—that one has made <transChange type="added">him</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> known.  <div eID="gen26542" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 1:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11124"/><title type="x-s">John the Baptist Testifies to Jesus</title> <div sID="gen26543" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11124"/>And this is the testimony of John, when the Jews sent<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “sent to him”</note> priests and Levites from Jerusalem so that they could ask him, “Who are you?”

verses.name: John 1:20
verses.text: And he confessed—and he did not deny, and confessed—“I am not the Christ!”

verses.name: John 1:21
verses.text: And they asked him, “Then who <transChange type="added">are</transChange> you? Are you Elijah?” And he said, “I am not!” “Are you the Prophet?”<note placement="foot">A reference to the “Prophet like Moses” of <reference osisRef="Deut.18.15">Deut 18:15 </reference>(see <reference osisRef="Acts.3.22">Acts 3:22</reference>)</note> And he answered, “No!”

verses.name: John 1:22
verses.text: Then they said to him, “Who are you, so that we can give an answer to those who sent us? What do you say about yourself?”  <div eID="gen26543" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 1:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11125"/><div sID="gen26544" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11125"/>He said, <div eID="gen26544" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen26545"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26546"/>“I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> ‘the voice of one crying out in the wilderness,<l eID="gen26546" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26547"/>“Make straight the way of the Lord,” ’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.40.3">Isa 40:3</reference></note><l eID="gen26547" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen26545"/> <div sID="gen26548" type="x-p"/> just as Isaiah the prophet said.”

verses.name: John 1:24
verses.text: (And they had been sent from the Pharisees.)

verses.name: John 1:25
verses.text: And they asked him and said to him, “Why then are you baptizing, if you are not the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the Prophet?”  <div eID="gen26548" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 1:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11126"/><div sID="gen26549" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11126"/>John answered them, saying, “I baptize with water. In your midst stands <transChange type="added">one</transChange> whom you do not know—

verses.name: John 1:27
verses.text: the one who comes after me, of whom I am not worthy <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to untie⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “that I might untie”</note> the strap of his sandal!”

verses.name: John 1:28
verses.text: These <transChange type="added">things</transChange> took place in Bethany on the other side of the Jordan, where John was baptizing.  <div eID="gen26549" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 1:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11127"/><div sID="gen26550" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11127"/>On the next day he saw Jesus coming to him and said, “Look! The Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!

verses.name: John 1:30
verses.text: This one is <transChange type="added">the one</transChange> about whom I said, ‘After me is coming a man who is ahead of me, because he existed before me.’

verses.name: John 1:31
verses.text: And I did not know him, but in order that he could be revealed to Israel, because of this I came baptizing with water.”  <div eID="gen26550" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 1:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11128"/><div sID="gen26551" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11128"/>And John testified, saying, “I have seen the Spirit descending like a dove from heaven and remaining upon him.

verses.name: John 1:33
verses.text: And I did not know him, but the one who sent me to baptize with water, that one said to me, ‘<transChange type="added">The one</transChange> upon whom you see the Spirit descending and remaining upon him—this one is the one who baptizes with the Holy Spirit.’

verses.name: John 1:34
verses.text: And I have seen and testify that this one is the Chosen One<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “the Son of God”</note> of God.  <div eID="gen26551" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 1:35
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11129"/><title type="x-s">Two of John’s Disciples Follow Jesus</title> <div sID="gen26552" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11129"/>On the next day again John was standing <transChange type="added">there</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*The word “there” is not in the Greek text but is implied</note> and two of his disciples,

verses.name: John 1:36
verses.text: and looking at Jesus <transChange type="added">as he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“walking by”) which is understood as temporal</note> was walking by, he said, “Look! The Lamb of God!”

verses.name: John 1:37
verses.text: And the two disciples heard him speaking, and they followed Jesus.

verses.name: John 1:38
verses.text: And Jesus, turning around and seeing them following <transChange type="added">him</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> said to them, “What do you seek?” And they said to him, “Rabbi” (which means when<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“translated”) which is understood as temporal</note> translated “Teacher”), “where are you staying?”

verses.name: John 1:39
verses.text: He said to them, “Come and you will see!” So they came and saw where he was staying, and they stayed with him that day (it was about the tenth hour).  <div eID="gen26552" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 1:40
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11130"/><title type="x-s">Andrew Declares Jesus to be the Messiah</title> <div sID="gen26553" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11130"/>Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, was one of the two who heard John and followed him.

verses.name: John 1:41
verses.text: This one first found his own brother Simon and said to him, “We have found the Messiah!” (which is translated “Christ”).

verses.name: John 1:42
verses.text: He brought him to Jesus. Looking at him, Jesus said, “You are Simon the son of John. You will be called Cephas” (which is interpreted “Peter”).  <div eID="gen26553" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 1:43
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11131"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Calls Philip and Nathanael</title> <div sID="gen26554" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11131"/>On the next day he wanted to depart for Galilee, and he found Philip. And Jesus said to him, “Follow me!”

verses.name: John 1:44
verses.text: (Now Philip was from Bethsaida, the town of Andrew and Peter.)

verses.name: John 1:45
verses.text: Philip found Nathanael and said to him, “We have found <transChange type="added">the one</transChange> whom Moses wrote <transChange type="added">about</transChange> in the law, and the prophets wrote <transChange type="added">about</transChange>—Jesus son of Joseph from Nazareth!”

verses.name: John 1:46
verses.text: And Nathanael said to him, “Can anything good come out of Nazareth?” Philip said to him, “Come and see!”  <div eID="gen26554" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 1:47
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11132"/><div sID="gen26555" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11132"/>Jesus saw Nathanael coming toward him and said about him, “Look! <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞A true Israelite⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “truly an Israelite”</note> in whom is no deceit!”

verses.name: John 1:48
verses.text: Nathanael said to him, “From where do you know me?” Jesus answered and said to him, “Before Philip called you, <transChange type="added">when you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“were”) which is understood as temporal</note> were under the fig tree, I saw you.”

verses.name: John 1:49
verses.text: Nathanael answered him, “Rabbi, you are the Son of God! You are the king of Israel!”

verses.name: John 1:50
verses.text: Jesus answered and said to him, “Because I said to you that I saw you under the fig tree, do you believe? You will see greater <transChange type="added">things</transChange> than these!”

verses.name: John 1:51
verses.text: And he said to him, “Truly, truly I say to all of you, you will see heaven opened and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man.”  <chapter eID="John.1"/>

verses.name: John 2:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11133"/><title type="x-s">The Wedding at Cana: Water Turned into Wine</title> <div sID="gen26556" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11133"/>And on the third day, there was a wedding at Cana in Galilee, and the mother of Jesus was there.

verses.name: John 2:2
verses.text: And both Jesus and his disciples were invited to the wedding.

verses.name: John 2:3
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when the</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“ran out”)</note> wine ran out, the mother of Jesus said to him, “They have no wine!”

verses.name: John 2:4
verses.text: And Jesus said to her, “What <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞does your concern have to do with me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to me and to you”</note> woman? My hour has not yet come.”

verses.name: John 2:5
verses.text: His mother said to the servants, “Whatever he says to you, do <transChange type="added">it</transChange>!”<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>  <div eID="gen26556" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 2:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11134"/><div sID="gen26557" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11134"/>Now six stone water jars were set there, in accordance with the ceremonial cleansing of the Jews, each holding two or three measures.<note placement="foot">A “measure” was about 9 gallons (40 liters)</note>

verses.name: John 2:7
verses.text: Jesus said to them, “Fill the water jars with water.” And they filled them to the brim.

verses.name: John 2:8
verses.text: And he said to them, “Now draw <transChange type="added">some</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> out and take it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to the head steward. So they took it.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: John 2:9
verses.text: Now when the head steward tasted the water which had become wine and did not know where it was from—but the servants who had drawn the water knew—the head steward summoned the bridegroom

verses.name: John 2:10
verses.text: and said to him, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Everyone⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “every man”</note> serves the good wine first, and whenever they are drunk, the inferior. You have kept the good wine until now!”

verses.name: John 2:11
verses.text: This beginning of signs Jesus performed at Cana in Galilee, and revealed his glory, and his disciples believed in him.  <div eID="gen26557" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 2:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11135"/><title type="x-s">Jesus’ First Journey to Jerusalem</title> <div sID="gen26558" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11135"/>After this he went down to Capernaum, and his mother and brothers<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “his brothers”</note> and his disciples, and they stayed there <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a few⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “not many”</note> days.

verses.name: John 2:13
verses.text: And the Passover of the Jews was near, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.  <div eID="gen26558" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 2:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11136"/><title type="x-s">The Cleansing of the Temple</title> <div sID="gen26559" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11136"/>And he found in the temple <transChange type="added">courts</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> those who were selling oxen and sheep and doves, and the money changers seated.

verses.name: John 2:15
verses.text: And he made a whip of cords <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“made”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> drove them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> all out of the temple courts,<note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> both the sheep and the oxen, and he poured out the coins of the money changers and overturned their<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> tables.

verses.name: John 2:16
verses.text: And to the ones selling the doves he said, “Take these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> away from here! Do not make my Father’s house <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a marketplace⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!”<note placement="foot">Literally “a market house”; or “a house of merchants” (an allusion to <reference osisRef="Zech.14.21">Zech 14:21</reference>)</note>

verses.name: John 2:17
verses.text: His disciples remembered that it is written, “Zeal for your house will consume me.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.69.9">Ps 69:9</reference></note>  <div eID="gen26559" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 2:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11137"/><div sID="gen26560" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11137"/>So the Jews answered and said to him, “What sign do you show to us, because you are doing these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>?”

verses.name: John 2:19
verses.text: Jesus answered and said to them, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up!”

verses.name: John 2:20
verses.text: Then the Jews said, “This temple has been under construction<note placement="foot">This translation of the aorist verb is based on a very close parallel in <reference osisRef="Ezra.5.16">Ezra 5:16 </reference>(LXX), where it is clear from the following verb that the construction had not yet been completed</note> forty-six years, and will you raise it up in three days?”

verses.name: John 2:21
verses.text: But he was speaking about the temple of his body.

verses.name: John 2:22
verses.text: So when he was raised from the dead, his disciples remembered that he had said this, and they believed the scripture and the saying that Jesus had spoken.  <div eID="gen26560" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 2:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11138"/><title type="x-s">Jesus at the Passover</title> <div sID="gen26561" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11138"/>Now while he was in Jerusalem at the Passover, during the feast, many believed in his name <transChange type="added">because they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as causal</note> saw his signs which he was doing.

verses.name: John 2:24
verses.text: But Jesus himself did not entrust himself to them, because he knew all <transChange type="added">people</transChange>,<note placement="foot">The Greek term is masculine and thus refers to “all people” rather than “all things” (which would be neuter)</note>

verses.name: John 2:25
verses.text: and because he did not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞need⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “have need that”</note> anyone <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to testify⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “should testify”</note> about man, for he himself knew what was in man.<note placement="foot">*Here “man” has been retained rather than the generic “people” to maintain the connection with the following verse</note>  <chapter eID="John.2"/>

verses.name: John 3:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11139"/><title type="x-s">A Meeting with Nicodemus</title> <div sID="gen26562" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11139"/>Now there was a man of the Pharisees <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞whose name was⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the name to him”</note> Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews.

verses.name: John 3:2
verses.text: This man came to him at night and said to him, “Rabbi, we know that <transChange type="added">you are</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here both the pronoun and verb are understood in Greek and are supplied in the translation</note> a teacher who has come from God, for no one is able to perform these signs that you are performing unless God were with him.”

verses.name: John 3:3
verses.text: Jesus answered and said to him, “Truly, truly I say to you, unless someone is born from above,<note placement="foot">The same Greek word can mean either “from above” or “again,” which allows for the misunderstanding by Nicodemus here; Jesus was speaking of new birth “from above,” while Nicodemus misunderstood him to mean a second physical birth</note> he is not able to see the kingdom of God.”

verses.name: John 3:4
verses.text: Nicodemus said to him, “How can a man be born <transChange type="added">when he</transChange> is an old man? He is not able to enter into his mother’s womb for the second time and be born, <transChange type="added">can he</transChange>?”<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here, indicated in the translation by the phrase “can he”</note>  <div eID="gen26562" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 3:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11140"/><div sID="gen26563" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11140"/>Jesus answered, “Truly, truly I say to you, unless someone is born of water and spirit, he is not able to enter into the kingdom of God.

verses.name: John 3:6
verses.text: What is born of the flesh is flesh, and what is born of the Spirit is spirit.

verses.name: John 3:7
verses.text: Do not be astonished that I said to you, ‘It is necessary for you to be born from above.’<note placement="foot">The same Greek word can mean either “from above” or “again” (see also v. <reference osisRef="John.3.3">3</reference>)</note>

verses.name: John 3:8
verses.text: The wind blows wherever it wishes, and you hear the sound of it, but you do not know where it comes from and where it is going. So is everyone who is born of the Spirit.”  <div eID="gen26563" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 3:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11141"/><div sID="gen26564" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11141"/>Nicodemus answered and said to him, “How can these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> be?”

verses.name: John 3:10
verses.text: Jesus answered and said to him, “Are you the teacher of Israel, and you do not understand these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>?

verses.name: John 3:11
verses.text: Truly, truly I say to you, we speak what we know, and we testify <transChange type="added">about</transChange> what we have seen, and you do not accept our testimony!

verses.name: John 3:12
verses.text: If I tell you earthly things and you do not believe, how will you believe if I tell you heavenly things?

verses.name: John 3:13
verses.text: And no one has ascended into heaven except the one who descended from heaven—the Son of Man.

verses.name: John 3:14
verses.text: And just as Moses lifted up the snake in the wilderness,<note placement="foot">An allusion to <reference osisRef="Num.21.5-Num.21.9">Num 21:5–9</reference></note> thus it is necessary <transChange type="added">that</transChange> the Son of Man be lifted up,

verses.name: John 3:15
verses.text: so that everyone who believes in him will have eternal life.”<note placement="foot">Some interpreters and Bible translations extend the quotation of Jesus’ words through v. <reference osisRef="John.3.21">21</reference></note>  <div eID="gen26564" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 3:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11142"/><title type="x-s">God’s Love for the World</title> <div sID="gen26565" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11142"/>For in this way God loved the world, so that he gave his one and only Son, in order that everyone who believes in him will not perish, but will have eternal life.

verses.name: John 3:17
verses.text: For God did not send his Son into the world in order that he should judge<note placement="foot">Or “he should condemn”</note> the world, but in order that the world should be saved through him.

verses.name: John 3:18
verses.text: The one who believes in him is not judged,<note placement="foot">Or “condemned”</note> but the one who does not believe has already been judged,<note placement="foot">Or “been condemned”</note> because he has not believed in the name of the one and only Son of God.

verses.name: John 3:19
verses.text: And this is the judgment: that the light has come into the world, and people loved the darkness rather than the light, because their deeds were evil.

verses.name: John 3:20
verses.text: For everyone who practices evil hates the light and does not come to the light, lest his deeds be exposed.

verses.name: John 3:21
verses.text: But the one who practices the truth comes to the light, in order that his deeds may be revealed, that they are done in God.  <div eID="gen26565" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 3:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11143"/><title type="x-s">Additional Testimony by John the Baptist About Jesus</title> <div sID="gen26566" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11143"/>After these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> Jesus and his disciples came into Judean territory, and there he spent time with them and was baptizing.

verses.name: John 3:23
verses.text: Now John was also baptizing at Aenon near Salim, because water was plentiful there, and they were coming and were being baptized.

verses.name: John 3:24
verses.text: (For John had not yet been thrown into prison.)  <div eID="gen26566" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 3:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11144"/><div sID="gen26567" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11144"/>So a dispute occurred on the part of John’s disciples with a Jew<note placement="foot">Some significant early manuscripts read “the Jews”</note> concerning purification.

verses.name: John 3:26
verses.text: And they came to John and said to him, “Rabbi, he who was with you on the other side of the Jordan, about whom you testified—look, this one is baptizing, and all are coming to him!”  <div eID="gen26567" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 3:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11145"/><div sID="gen26568" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11145"/>John answered and said, “A man can receive not one <transChange type="added">thing</transChange> unless it is granted to him from heaven!

verses.name: John 3:28
verses.text: You yourselves testify about me that I said, ‘I am not the Christ, but I am sent before that one.’

verses.name: John 3:29
verses.text: The one who has the bride is the bridegroom. But the friend of the bridegroom, who stands and hears him, rejoices <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞greatly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “with joy”</note> because of the bridegroom’s voice. So this joy of mine is complete.

verses.name: John 3:30
verses.text: It is necessary for that one to increase, but <transChange type="added">for</transChange> me to decrease.”  <div eID="gen26568" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 3:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11146"/><div sID="gen26569" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11146"/>The one who comes from above is over all. The one who is from the earth is from the earth and speaks from the earth; the one who comes from heaven is over all.

verses.name: John 3:32
verses.text: What he has seen and heard, this he testifies, and no one accepts his testimony.

verses.name: John 3:33
verses.text: The one who accepts his testimony has attested that God is true.

verses.name: John 3:34
verses.text: For <transChange type="added">the one</transChange> whom God sent speaks the words of God, for he does not give the Spirit by measure.

verses.name: John 3:35
verses.text: The Father loves the Son and has given all <transChange type="added">things</transChange> into his hand.

verses.name: John 3:36
verses.text: The one who believes in the Son has eternal life, but the one who disobeys the Son will not see life—but the wrath of God remains on him.<note placement="foot">Some interpreters and Bible translations extend the quotation of John the Baptist’s words through v. <reference osisRef="John.3.36">36</reference></note>  <chapter eID="John.3"/>

verses.name: John 4:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11147"/><title type="x-s">The Samaritan Woman at Jacob’s Well</title> <div sID="gen26570" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11147"/>Now when Jesus knew that the Pharisees had heard that Jesus was making and baptizing more disciples than John

verses.name: John 4:2
verses.text: (although Jesus himself was not baptizing, but his disciples),

verses.name: John 4:3
verses.text: he left Judea and departed again for Galilee.

verses.name: John 4:4
verses.text: And it was necessary <transChange type="added">for</transChange> him to go through Samaria.  <div eID="gen26570" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 4:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11148"/><div sID="gen26571" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11148"/>Now he came to a town of Samaria called Sychar, near the piece of land that Jacob had given to his son Joseph.

verses.name: John 4:6
verses.text: And Jacob’s well was there, so Jesus, <transChange type="added">because he</transChange> had become tired from the journey, simply sat down at the well. It was about the sixth hour.  <div eID="gen26571" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 4:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11149"/><div sID="gen26572" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11149"/>A woman of Samaria came to draw water. Jesus said to her, “Give me <transChange type="added">water</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “water” is supplied in the translation as the understood direct object of the verb “give”</note> to drink.”

verses.name: John 4:8
verses.text: (For his disciples had gone away into the town so that they could buy food.)

verses.name: John 4:9
verses.text: So the Samaritan woman said to him, “How do you, being a Jew, ask from me <transChange type="added">water</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “water” is supplied in the translation as the understood direct object of the verb “ask”</note> to drink, since I<note placement="foot">*Here “since” is supplied as a component of the participle (“am”) which is understood as causal</note> am a Samaritan woman?” (For Jews have no dealings with Samaritans.)  <div eID="gen26572" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 4:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11150"/><div sID="gen26573" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11150"/>Jesus answered and said to her, “If you had known the gift of God and who it is who says to you, ‘Give me <transChange type="added">water</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “water” is supplied in the translation as the understood direct object of the verb “give”</note> to drink,’ you would have asked him, and he would have given you living water.”

verses.name: John 4:11
verses.text: The woman said to him, “Sir, you have no bucket and the well is deep! From where then do you get this living water?

verses.name: John 4:12
verses.text: You are not greater than our father Jacob, <transChange type="added">are you</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here, indicated by the supplied phrase “are you” in the translation</note> who gave us the well and drank from it himself, and his sons and his livestock?”  <div eID="gen26573" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 4:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11151"/><div sID="gen26574" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11151"/>Jesus answered and said to her, “Everyone who drinks of this water will be thirsty again.

verses.name: John 4:14
verses.text: But whoever drinks of this water which I will give to him will never be thirsty for eternity, but the water which I will give to him will become in him a well of water springing up to eternal life.”

verses.name: John 4:15
verses.text: The woman said to him, “Sir, give me this water, so that I will not be thirsty or come here to draw <transChange type="added">water</transChange>!”<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: John 4:16
verses.text: He said to her, “Go, call your husband and come here.”

verses.name: John 4:17
verses.text: The woman answered and said to him, “I do not have a husband.” Jesus said to her, “You have said rightly, ‘I do not have a husband,’

verses.name: John 4:18
verses.text: for you have had five husbands, and <transChange type="added">the one</transChange> whom you have now is not your husband; this you have said truthfully!”  <div eID="gen26574" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 4:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11152"/><div sID="gen26575" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11152"/>The woman said to him, “Sir, I see that you are a prophet.

verses.name: John 4:20
verses.text: Our fathers worshiped on this mountain, and you <transChange type="added">people</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “people” is supplied in the translation because the Greek pronoun is plural</note> say that in Jerusalem is the place where it is necessary to worship.”

verses.name: John 4:21
verses.text: Jesus said to her, “Believe me, woman, that an hour is coming when neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem will you worship the Father.

verses.name: John 4:22
verses.text: You worship what you do not know. We worship what we know, because salvation is from the Jews.

verses.name: John 4:23
verses.text: But an hour is coming—and now is <transChange type="added">here</transChange><note placement="foot">*The word “here” is not in the Greek text but is implied</note>—when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth, for indeed the Father seeks such <transChange type="added">people</transChange> <transChange type="added">to be</transChange> his worshipers.

verses.name: John 4:24
verses.text: God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> spirit, and the ones who worship him must worship in spirit and truth.”

verses.name: John 4:25
verses.text: The woman said to him, “I know that Messiah is coming” (the one called Christ); “whenever that one comes, he will proclaim all <transChange type="added">things</transChange> to us.”

verses.name: John 4:26
verses.text: Jesus said to her, “I, the one speaking to you, am <transChange type="added">he</transChange>.<note placement="foot">*Here the predicate nominative is supplied from context in the English translation</note>  <div eID="gen26575" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 4:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11153"/><title type="x-s">The Disciples and the Harvest</title> <div sID="gen26576" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11153"/>And at this <transChange type="added">point</transChange><note placement="foot">*The word “point” is not in the Greek text but is implied</note> his disciples came, and they were astonished that he was speaking with a woman. However, no one said, “What do you seek?” or “Why are you speaking with her?”

verses.name: John 4:28
verses.text: So the woman left her water jar and went away into the town and said to the people,<note placement="foot">Assuming the term is used here in a generic sense to refer to persons of either gender, it should be translated “people”; if instead the term here refers only to the town leaders or elders who met at the town gate, then “men” would be appropriate</note>

verses.name: John 4:29
verses.text: “Come, see a man who told me everything I have ever done! Perhaps this one is the Christ?”

verses.name: John 4:30
verses.text: They went out from the town and were coming to him.  <div eID="gen26576" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 4:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11154"/><div sID="gen26577" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11154"/>In the meanwhile the disciples were asking him, saying, “Rabbi, eat <transChange type="added">something</transChange>!”<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: John 4:32
verses.text: But he said to them, “I have food to eat that you do not know about.”

verses.name: John 4:33
verses.text: So the disciples began to say<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to say”)</note> to one another, “No one brought him anything<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to eat, did they?”<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here, indicated by the supplied phrase “did they” in the translation</note>

verses.name: John 4:34
verses.text: Jesus said to them, “My food is that I do the will of the one who sent me and complete his work.

verses.name: John 4:35
verses.text: Do you not say, ‘There are yet four months and the harvest comes’? Behold, I say to you, lift up your eyes and look at the fields, that they are white for harvest already.<note placement="foot">Some interpreters and Bible translations place the word “already” at the beginning of the next verse: “Already the one who reaps receives wages …”</note>

verses.name: John 4:36
verses.text: The one who reaps receives wages and gathers fruit for eternal life, in order that the one who sows and the one who reaps can rejoice together.

verses.name: John 4:37
verses.text: For in this <transChange type="added">instance</transChange><note placement="foot">*The word “point” is not in the Greek text but is implied</note> the saying is true, ‘It is one who sows and another who reaps.’

verses.name: John 4:38
verses.text: I sent you to reap what you did not work for; others have worked, and you have entered into their work.”  <div eID="gen26577" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 4:39
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11155"/><title type="x-s">The Samaritans and the Savior of the World</title> <div sID="gen26578" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11155"/>Now from that town many of the Samaritans believed in him because of the word of the woman who testified, “He told me everything that I have done.”

verses.name: John 4:40
verses.text: So when the Samaritans came to him, they began asking<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began asking”)</note> him to stay with them. And he stayed there two days.

verses.name: John 4:41
verses.text: And many more believed because of his word,

verses.name: John 4:42
verses.text: And they were saying to the woman, “No longer because of <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞what you said⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “your speaking”</note> do we believe, for we ourselves have heard, and we know that this one is truly the Savior of the world!”  <div eID="gen26578" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 4:43
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11156"/><title type="x-s">Return to Galilee</title> <div sID="gen26579" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11156"/>And after the two days he departed from there into Galilee.

verses.name: John 4:44
verses.text: For Jesus himself testified that a prophet has no honor in his own homeland.

verses.name: John 4:45
verses.text: So when he came to Galilee, the Galileans welcomed him, <transChange type="added">because they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had seen”) which is understood as causal</note> had seen all <transChange type="added">the things</transChange> he had done in Jerusalem at the feast (for they themselves had also come to the feast).  <div eID="gen26579" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 4:46
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11157"/><title type="x-s">A Royal Official’s Son Is Healed</title> <div sID="gen26580" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11157"/>Now he came again to Cana in Galilee, where he had made the water wine. And <transChange type="added">there</transChange> was at Capernaum a certain royal official whose son was sick.

verses.name: John 4:47
verses.text: This man, <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard that Jesus had come from Judea into Galilee, went to him and asked that he come down and heal his son, for he was about to die.

verses.name: John 4:48
verses.text: So Jesus said to him, “Unless you <transChange type="added">people</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “people” is supplied in the translation because the Greek verb (“see”) is plural</note> see signs and wonders, you will never believe!”

verses.name: John 4:49
verses.text: The royal official said to him, “Sir, come down before my child dies!”

verses.name: John 4:50
verses.text: Jesus said to him, “Go, your son will live.” The man believed the word that Jesus spoke to him, and he departed.  <div eID="gen26580" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 4:51
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11158"/><div sID="gen26581" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11158"/>Now <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was going down”)</note> he was going down, his slaves met him, saying that his child was alive.

verses.name: John 4:52
verses.text: So he inquired from them the hour at which he had gotten better. Then they said to him, “Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him.”

verses.name: John 4:53
verses.text: So the father knew that <transChange type="added">it was</transChange> that<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “that it was at that same hour”</note> same hour at which Jesus said to him, “Your son will live,” and he himself believed, and his whole household.

verses.name: John 4:54
verses.text: Now this <transChange type="added">is</transChange> again a second sign Jesus performed <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“came”) which is understood as temporal</note> came from Judea into Galilee.  <chapter eID="John.4"/>

verses.name: John 5:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11159"/><title type="x-s">A Paralytic Is Healed</title> <div sID="gen26582" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11159"/>After these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> <transChange type="added">there</transChange> was a feast of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.

verses.name: John 5:2
verses.text: Now there is in Jerusalem near the Sheep Gate a pool called in Aramaic <hi type="italic">Bethzatha</hi>,<note placement="foot">The majority of later manuscripts read “Bethesda,” while other early manuscripts read “Bethsaida”</note> which has five porticoes.

verses.name: John 5:3
verses.text: In these were lying a large number of those who were sick, blind, lame, paralyzed.<note placement="foot">The majority of later manuscripts add the following words: “waiting for the moving of the water.

verses.name: John 5:4
verses.text: For an angel of the Lord from time to time went down in the pool and stirred up the water. So the one who went in first after the stirring of the water was healed of whatever disease he suffered.”</note>

verses.name: John 5:5
verses.text: And a certain man was there who had <transChange type="added">been</transChange> thirty-eight years in his sickness.

verses.name: John 5:6
verses.text: Jesus, <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw this one lying there and knew that he had been sick<note placement="foot">*The phrase “been sick” is not in the Greek text, but is supplied from the context</note> a long time already, said to him, “Do you want to become well?”

verses.name: John 5:7
verses.text: The one who was sick answered him, “Sir, I do not have anyone that, whenever the water is stirred up, could put me into the pool. But <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞while⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “during which time”</note> I am coming, another goes down before me.”

verses.name: John 5:8
verses.text: Jesus said to him, “Get up! Pick up your mat and walk!”

verses.name: John 5:9
verses.text: And immediately the man became well and picked up his mat and began to walk.<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to walk”)</note> (Now it was the Sabbath on that day.)  <div eID="gen26582" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 5:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11160"/><div sID="gen26583" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11160"/>So the Jews were saying to the one who had been healed, “It is the Sabbath, and it is not permitted for you to pick up the mat!”<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “your mat”</note>

verses.name: John 5:11
verses.text: But he answered them, “The one who made me well—that one said to me, ‘Pick up your mat and walk!’ ”

verses.name: John 5:12
verses.text: So they asked him,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “They asked him”</note> “Who is the man who said to you, ‘Pick up your mat<note placement="foot">*In Greek the direct object (“your mat”) is not in the Greek text but the repetition is implied from the previous verse</note> and walk?’ ”

verses.name: John 5:13
verses.text: But the one who was healed did not know who it was, for Jesus had withdrawn <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was”)</note> a crowd was in the place.  <div eID="gen26583" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 5:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11161"/><title type="x-s">Equal with God</title> <div sID="gen26584" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11161"/>After these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> Jesus found him at the temple and said to him, “Look, you have become well! Sin no longer, lest something worse happen to you.”

verses.name: John 5:15
verses.text: The man went and reported to the Jews that Jesus was the one who made him well.

verses.name: John 5:16
verses.text: And on account of this the Jews began to persecute<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to persecute”)</note> Jesus, because he was doing these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> on the Sabbath.

verses.name: John 5:17
verses.text: But he answered<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “Jesus answered”</note> them, “My Father is working until now, and I am working.”

verses.name: John 5:18
verses.text: So on account of this the Jews were seeking even more to kill him, because he not only was breaking the Sabbath, but also was calling God his own Father, <transChange type="added">thus</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “thus” is supplied as a component of the participle (“making”) which is understood as result</note> making himself equal with God.  <div eID="gen26584" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 5:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11162"/><title type="x-s">The Authority of the Son</title> <div sID="gen26585" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11162"/>So Jesus answered and said to them, “Truly, truly I say to you, the Son can do nothing from himself except what he sees the Father doing. For whatever that one does, these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> also the Son does likewise.

verses.name: John 5:20
verses.text: For the Father loves the Son and shows him everything that he himself is doing. And greater works than these he will show him, so that you will be astonished.

verses.name: John 5:21
verses.text: For just as the Father raises the dead and makes <transChange type="added">them</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> alive, thus also the Son makes alive whomever he wishes.

verses.name: John 5:22
verses.text: For the Father does not judge anyone, but he has given all judgment to the Son,

verses.name: John 5:23
verses.text: in order that all <transChange type="added">people</transChange><note placement="foot">*The word “people” is not in the Greek text but is implied</note> will honor the Son, just as they honor the Father. The one who does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent him.

verses.name: John 5:24
verses.text: Truly, truly I say to you that the one who hears my word and who believes the one who sent me has eternal life, and does not come into judgment, but has passed from death into life.  <div eID="gen26585" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 5:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11163"/><div sID="gen26586" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11163"/>“Truly, truly I say to you, that an hour is coming—and now is <transChange type="added">here</transChange>—when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and the ones who hear will live.

verses.name: John 5:26
verses.text: For just as the Father has life in himself, thus also he has granted to the Son to have life in himself.

verses.name: John 5:27
verses.text: And he has granted him authority to carry out judgment, because he is the Son of Man.  <div eID="gen26586" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 5:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11164"/><div sID="gen26587" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11164"/>“Do not be astonished <transChange type="added">at</transChange> this, because an hour is coming in which all those in the tombs will hear his voice

verses.name: John 5:29
verses.text: and they will come out—those who have done good <transChange type="added">things</transChange> to a resurrection of life, but those who have practiced evil <transChange type="added">things</transChange> to a resurrection of judgment.

verses.name: John 5:30
verses.text: I am able to do nothing from myself. Just as I hear, I judge, and my judgment is just, because I do not seek my <transChange type="added">own</transChange> will, but the will of the one who sent me.  <div eID="gen26587" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 5:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11165"/><title type="x-s">Further Testimony About the Son</title> <div sID="gen26588" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11165"/>“If I testify about myself, my testimony is not true.

verses.name: John 5:32
verses.text: There is another who testifies about me, and I know that the testimony which he testifies about me is true.

verses.name: John 5:33
verses.text: You have sent to John and he has testified to the truth.

verses.name: John 5:34
verses.text: (And I do not receive testimony from people, but I say these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> in order that you may be saved.)

verses.name: John 5:35
verses.text: That one was the lamp <transChange type="added">which was</transChange> burning and shining, and you wanted to rejoice for an hour in his light.  <div eID="gen26588" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 5:36
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11166"/><div sID="gen26589" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11166"/>“But I have a testimony greater than John’s, for the works which the Father has given to me that I should complete them—the very works which I am doing—<transChange type="added">these</transChange> testify about me, that the Father has sent me.

verses.name: John 5:37
verses.text: And the Father who sent me, that one has testified about me. You have neither heard his voice at any time nor seen his form.

verses.name: John 5:38
verses.text: And you do not have his word residing in yourselves, because the one whom that one sent, in this one you do not believe.

verses.name: John 5:39
verses.text: You search<note placement="foot">Or “Search” (an imperative)</note> the scriptures because you think that you have eternal life in them, and it is these that testify about me.

verses.name: John 5:40
verses.text: And you are not willing to come to me so that you may have life.  <div eID="gen26589" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 5:41
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11167"/><div sID="gen26590" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11167"/>“I do not accept glory<note placement="foot">Or “honor”</note> from people,

verses.name: John 5:42
verses.text: but I know you, that you do not have the love of God in yourselves.

verses.name: John 5:43
verses.text: I have come in my Father’s name, and you do not accept me. If another should come in his own name, you would accept that one!

verses.name: John 5:44
verses.text: How are you able to believe, <transChange type="added">if you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “if” is supplied as a component of the participle (“accept”) which is understood as conditional</note> accept glory from one another, and do not seek the glory <transChange type="added">which is</transChange> from the only God?

verses.name: John 5:45
verses.text: Do not think that I will accuse you before the Father! The one who accuses you is Moses, in whom you have put your hope!

verses.name: John 5:46
verses.text: For if you had believed Moses, you would believe me, for that one wrote about me.

verses.name: John 5:47
verses.text: But if you do not believe that one’s writings, how will you believe my words?”  <chapter eID="John.5"/>

verses.name: John 6:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11168"/><title type="x-s">The Feeding of Five Thousand</title> <div sID="gen26591" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11168"/>After these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> Jesus went away to the other side of the sea of Galilee (that is, Tiberias).

verses.name: John 6:2
verses.text: And a large crowd was following him because they were observing the signs that he was doing on those who were sick.

verses.name: John 6:3
verses.text: So Jesus went up on the mountain and sat down there with his disciples.

verses.name: John 6:4
verses.text: (Now the Passover, the feast of the Jews, was near.)

verses.name: John 6:5
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Then Jesus, when he looked up⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “then Jesus lifting up the eyes”</note><note placement="foot">*Here “when” in the translation is supplied as a component of the participle “lifting up” which is understood as temporal</note> and saw that a large crowd was coming to him, said to Philip, “Where can we buy bread so that these <transChange type="added">people</transChange> can eat?”

verses.name: John 6:6
verses.text: (Now he said this to test him, because he knew what he was going to do.)

verses.name: John 6:7
verses.text: Philip replied to him, “Two hundred denarii <transChange type="added">worth of</transChange> bread would not be enough for them, in order that each one could receive a little.”

verses.name: John 6:8
verses.text: One of his disciples, Andrew the brother of Simon Peter, said to him,

verses.name: John 6:9
verses.text: “Here is a boy who has five barley loaves and two fish, but what are these for so many <transChange type="added">people</transChange>?”

verses.name: John 6:10
verses.text: Jesus said, “Make the people recline.” (Now <transChange type="added">there</transChange> was a lot of grass in the place.) So the men reclined, approximately five thousand <transChange type="added">in</transChange> number.

verses.name: John 6:11
verses.text: Then Jesus took the bread, and <transChange type="added">after he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had given thanks”) which is understood as temporal</note> had given thanks, he distributed it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to those who were reclining—likewise also of the fish, as much as they wanted.

verses.name: John 6:12
verses.text: And when they were satisfied, he said to his disciples, “Gather the remaining fragments so that nothing is lost.”

verses.name: John 6:13
verses.text: So they gathered <transChange type="added">them</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and filled twelve baskets with fragments from the five barley loaves which were left over by those who had eaten.  <div eID="gen26591" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 6:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11169"/><div sID="gen26592" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11169"/>Now <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> the people saw the sign that he performed, they began to say,<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to say”)</note> “This one is truly the Prophet who is to come into the world!”

verses.name: John 6:15
verses.text: Then Jesus, <transChange type="added">because he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“knew”) which is understood as causal</note> knew that they were about to come and seize him in order to make him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> king, withdrew again up the mountain <transChange type="added">by</transChange> himself alone.  <div eID="gen26592" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 6:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11170"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Walks on the Water</title> <div sID="gen26593" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11170"/>Now when evening came, his disciples went down to the sea.

verses.name: John 6:17
verses.text: And getting into a boat, they began to go<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to go”)</note> to the other side of the sea, to Capernaum. And it had already become dark, and Jesus had not yet come to them.

verses.name: John 6:18
verses.text: And the sea began to be stirred up<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to be stirred up”)</note> because<note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was blowing”) which is understood as causal</note> a strong wind was blowing.

verses.name: John 6:19
verses.text: Then <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had rowed”) which is understood as temporal</note> had rowed about twenty-five or thirty stadia,<note placement="foot">A “stade” or “stadium” (plur. “stadia”) is about 607 ft (187 m), so this was around 3 miles (5 km)</note> they saw Jesus walking on the sea and coming near the boat, and they were afraid.

verses.name: John 6:20
verses.text: But he said to them, “<transChange type="added">It</transChange> is I! Do not be afraid!”

verses.name: John 6:21
verses.text: So they were wanting to take him into the boat, and immediately the boat came to the land to which they were going.  <div eID="gen26593" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 6:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11171"/><title type="x-s">Discourse About the Bread of Life</title> <div sID="gen26594" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11171"/>On the next day, the crowd that was on the other side of the sea saw that other boats were not there (except one), and that Jesus had not entered with his disciples into the boat, but his disciples had departed alone.

verses.name: John 6:23
verses.text: Other boats from Tiberias came near the place where they had eaten the bread <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“had given thanks”)</note> the Lord had given thanks.

verses.name: John 6:24
verses.text: So when the crowd saw that Jesus was not there, nor his disciples, they themselves got into the boats and came to Capernaum seeking Jesus.  <div eID="gen26594" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 6:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11172"/><div sID="gen26595" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11172"/>And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“found”) which is understood as temporal</note> found him on the other side of the sea, they said to him, “Rabbi, when did you get here?”

verses.name: John 6:26
verses.text: Jesus replied to them and said, “Truly, truly I say to you, you seek me not because you saw signs, but because you ate of the loaves and were satisfied!

verses.name: John 6:27
verses.text: Do not work for the food that perishes, but the food that remains to eternal life, which the Son of Man will give to you. For God the Father has set his seal on this one.”  <div eID="gen26595" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 6:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11173"/><div sID="gen26596" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11173"/>So they said to him, “What shall we do that we can accomplish the works of God?”

verses.name: John 6:29
verses.text: Jesus answered and said to them, “This is the work of God: that you believe in <transChange type="added">the one</transChange> whom that one sent.”

verses.name: John 6:30
verses.text: So they said to him, “Then what sign will you perform, so that we can see <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and believe you? What will you do?

verses.name: John 6:31
verses.text: Our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, just as it is written, ‘He gave them bread from heaven to eat.’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.78.24">Ps 78:24 </reference>which refers to the events of <reference osisRef="Exod.16.4-Exod.16.36">Exod 16:4–36</reference></note>  <div eID="gen26596" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 6:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11174"/><div sID="gen26597" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11174"/>Then Jesus said to them, “Truly, truly I say to you, Moses did not give you bread from heaven, but my Father is giving you the true bread from heaven!

verses.name: John 6:33
verses.text: For the bread of God is the one who comes down from heaven and gives life to the world.”

verses.name: John 6:34
verses.text: So they said to him, “Sir, always give us this bread!”  <div eID="gen26597" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 6:35
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11175"/><div sID="gen26598" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11175"/>Jesus said to them, “I am the bread of life. The one who comes to me will never be hungry, and the one who believes in me will never be thirsty again.

verses.name: John 6:36
verses.text: But I said to you that you have seen me and do not believe.

verses.name: John 6:37
verses.text: Everyone whom the Father gives to me will come to me, and the one who comes to me I will never throw out,

verses.name: John 6:38
verses.text: because I have come down from heaven not that I should do my will, but the will of the one who sent me.

verses.name: John 6:39
verses.text: Now this is the will of the one who sent me: that everyone whom he has given me, I would not lose <transChange type="added">any</transChange> of them,<note placement="foot">This pronoun is neuter singular in Greek, but is collective</note> but raise them<note placement="foot">This pronoun is neuter singular in Greek, but is collective</note> up on the last day.

verses.name: John 6:40
verses.text: For this is the will of my Father, that everyone who looks at the Son and believes in him would have eternal life, and I will raise him up on the last day.”  <div eID="gen26598" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 6:41
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11176"/><div sID="gen26599" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11176"/>Now the Jews began to grumble<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to grumble”)</note> about him because he said, “I am the bread that came down from heaven,”

verses.name: John 6:42
verses.text: and they were saying, “Is this one not Jesus the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? How does he now say, ‘I have come down from heaven’?”

verses.name: John 6:43
verses.text: Jesus answered and said to them, “Do not grumble <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞among yourselves⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!<note placement="foot">Literally “with one another”</note>

verses.name: John 6:44
verses.text: No one is able to come to me unless the Father who sent me draws him, and I will raise him up on the last day.

verses.name: John 6:45
verses.text: It is written in the prophets, ‘And they will all be taught by God.’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.54.13">Isa 54:13</reference></note> Everyone who hears from the Father and learns comes to me.

verses.name: John 6:46
verses.text: (Not that anyone has seen the Father except the one who is from God—this one has seen the Father.)<note placement="foot">The switch from first person in vv. <reference osisRef="John.6.44-John.6.45">44–45</reference> to third person here and back to first person in vv. <reference osisRef="John.6.47-John.6.51">47–51</reference> suggests that this verse is a parenthetical comment by the author rather than the words of Jesus</note>

verses.name: John 6:47
verses.text: Truly, truly I say to you, the one who believes has eternal life.

verses.name: John 6:48
verses.text: I am the bread of life.

verses.name: John 6:49
verses.text: Your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness and they died.

verses.name: John 6:50
verses.text: This is the bread that comes down from heaven so that someone may eat from it and not die.

verses.name: John 6:51
verses.text: I am the living bread that came down from heaven. If anyone eats from this bread, he will live <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “for the age”</note> And the bread that I will give for the life of the world is my flesh.”  <div eID="gen26599" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 6:52
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11177"/><div sID="gen26600" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11177"/>So the Jews began to quarrel<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to quarrel”)</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞among themselves⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “with one another”</note> saying, “How can this man give us his flesh to eat?”

verses.name: John 6:53
verses.text: Then Jesus said to them, “Truly, truly I say to you, unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you do not have life in yourselves!

verses.name: John 6:54
verses.text: The one who eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life, and I will raise him up on the last day.

verses.name: John 6:55
verses.text: For my flesh is true food, and my blood is true drink.

verses.name: John 6:56
verses.text: The one who eats<note placement="foot">*This term is somewhat graphic and typically used for animals feeding, but the distinction from other Greek verbs for eating is difficult to convey in English</note> my flesh and drinks my blood resides in me and I in him.

verses.name: John 6:57
verses.text: Just as the living Father sent me, and I live because of the Father, <transChange type="added">so</transChange> also the one who eats<note placement="foot">*This term is somewhat graphic and typically used for animals feeding, but the distinction from other Greek verbs for eating is difficult to convey in English</note> me—that one will live because of me.

verses.name: John 6:58
verses.text: This is the bread that came down from heaven, not as the fathers ate and died. The one who eats<note placement="foot">*This term is somewhat graphic and typically used for animals feeding, but the distinction from other Greek verbs for eating is difficult to convey in English</note> this bread will live <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “for the age”</note>  <div eID="gen26600" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 6:59
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11178"/><title type="x-s">Many of Jesus’ Disciples Offended by His Teaching</title> <div sID="gen26601" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11178"/>He said these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“teaching”) which is understood as temporal</note> teaching in the synagogue in Capernaum.

verses.name: John 6:60
verses.text: Thus many of his disciples, <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> said, “This saying is hard! Who can understand it?”

verses.name: John 6:61
verses.text: But Jesus, <transChange type="added">because he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“knew”) which is understood as causal</note> knew within himself that his disciples were grumbling about this, said to them, “Does this cause you to be offended?
