verses.name: John 6:62
verses.text: Then <transChange type="added">what</transChange> if you see the Son of Man ascending where he was before?

verses.name: John 6:63
verses.text: The Spirit is the one who gives life; the flesh profits nothing. The words that I have spoken to you are spirit and are life.

verses.name: John 6:64
verses.text: But there are some of you who do not believe.” (For Jesus knew from the beginning who they were who did not believe, and who it was who would betray him.)

verses.name: John 6:65
verses.text: And he said, “Because of this I said to you that no one can come to me unless it has been granted to him by the Father.”  <div eID="gen26601" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 6:66
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11179"/><title type="x-s">Peter’s Confession</title> <div sID="gen26602" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11179"/>For this <transChange type="added">reason</transChange> many of his disciples <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞drew back⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “went away to the things behind”</note> and were not walking with him any longer.

verses.name: John 6:67
verses.text: So Jesus said to the twelve, “You do not want to go away also, <transChange type="added">do you</transChange>?”<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here, indicated in the translation by the phrase “do you”</note>

verses.name: John 6:68
verses.text: Simon Peter answered him, “Lord, to whom would we go? You have the words of eternal life.

verses.name: John 6:69
verses.text: And we have believed, and have come to know, that you are the Holy One of God.”

verses.name: John 6:70
verses.text: Jesus replied to them, “Did I not choose you, the twelve, and one of you is the devil?”

verses.name: John 6:71
verses.text: (Now he was speaking about Judas <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Simon Iscariot, because this one—one of the twelve—was going to betray him.)  <chapter eID="John.6"/>

verses.name: John 7:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11180"/><title type="x-s">Jesus’ Brothers Do Not Believe in Him</title> <div sID="gen26603" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11180"/>And after these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> Jesus was going about in Galilee. For he did not want to go about in Judea, because the Jews were seeking to kill him.

verses.name: John 7:2
verses.text: Now the feast of the Jews—the <transChange type="added">feast of</transChange> Tabernacles—was near.

verses.name: John 7:3
verses.text: So his brothers said to him, “Depart from here and go to Judea, so that your disciples also can see your works that you are doing.

verses.name: John 7:4
verses.text: For no one does anything in secret and <transChange type="added">yet</transChange> he himself desires to be <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞publicly recognized⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “with openness”</note> If you are doing these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, reveal yourself to the world!”

verses.name: John 7:5
verses.text: (For not even his brothers believed in him.)  <div eID="gen26603" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 7:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11181"/><title type="x-s">Jesus at the Feast of Tabernacles</title> <div sID="gen26604" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11181"/>So Jesus said to them, “My time has not yet come, but your time is always ready.

verses.name: John 7:7
verses.text: The world cannot hate you, but it hates me, because I am testifying about it, that its deeds are evil.

verses.name: John 7:8
verses.text: You go up to the feast. I am not<note placement="foot">Most manuscripts read “not yet” here, but this is obviously an easier reading intended to reconcile the statement with Jesus’ later actions</note> going up to this feast, because my time is not yet completed.<note placement="foot">Or “fulfilled”</note>

verses.name: John 7:9
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had said”) which is understood as temporal</note> had said these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, he remained in Galilee.  <div eID="gen26604" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 7:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11182"/><div sID="gen26605" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11182"/>But when his brothers had gone up to the feast, then he also went up, not openly, but (as it were) in secret.

verses.name: John 7:11
verses.text: So the Jews were looking for him at the feast, and were saying, “Where is he?”

verses.name: John 7:12
verses.text: And there was a lot of grumbling concerning him among the crowds; some were saying, “He is a good <transChange type="added">man</transChange>,” but others were saying, “No, but he deceives the crowd.”

verses.name: John 7:13
verses.text: However, no one was speaking openly about him for fear of the Jews.  <div eID="gen26605" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 7:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11183"/><div sID="gen26606" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11183"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Now when the feast was already half over⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “now it being already in the middle of the feast”</note> Jesus went to the temple courts<note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> and began to teach.<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to teach”)</note>

verses.name: John 7:15
verses.text: Then the Jews were astonished, saying, “How does this man <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞possess knowledge⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “know letters”</note> because he<note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“been taught”) which is understood as causal</note> has not been taught?”

verses.name: John 7:16
verses.text: So Jesus answered them and said, “My teaching is not mine, but <transChange type="added">is</transChange> from the one who sent me.

verses.name: John 7:17
verses.text: If anyone wants to do his will, he will know about my<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> teaching, whether it is from God or I am speaking from myself.

verses.name: John 7:18
verses.text: The one who speaks from himself seeks his own glory. But the one who seeks the glory of the one who sent him—this one is true, and there is no unrighteousness in him.

verses.name: John 7:19
verses.text: Has not Moses given you the law, and none of you carries out the law? Why do you seek to kill me?”  <div eID="gen26606" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 7:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11184"/><div sID="gen26607" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11184"/>The crowd replied, “You have a demon! Who is seeking to kill you?”

verses.name: John 7:21
verses.text: Jesus answered and said to them, “I performed one work, and you are all astonished.

verses.name: John 7:22
verses.text: Because of this Moses has given you circumcision (not that it is from Moses, but from the fathers), and you circumcise a man on the Sabbath.

verses.name: John 7:23
verses.text: If a man receives circumcision on the Sabbath so that the law of Moses would not be broken, are you angry with me because I made a whole man well<note placement="foot">Or “a man entirely well”</note> on the Sabbath?

verses.name: John 7:24
verses.text: Do not judge according to outward appearance, but judge according to righteous judgment!”  <div eID="gen26607" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 7:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11185"/><title type="x-s">Is Jesus the Christ?</title> <div sID="gen26608" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11185"/>Then some of the inhabitants of Jerusalem began to say,<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to say”)</note> “Is this not <transChange type="added">the one</transChange> whom they are seeking to kill?

verses.name: John 7:26
verses.text: And behold, he is speaking openly and they are saying nothing to him! Can it be that the rulers truly know that this man is the Christ?

verses.name: John 7:27
verses.text: Yet we know where this man is from, but the Christ, whenever he comes—no one knows where he is from!”  <div eID="gen26608" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 7:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11186"/><div sID="gen26609" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11186"/>Then Jesus cried out in the temple <transChange type="added">courts</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> teaching and saying, “You both know me and you know where I am from! And I have not come from myself, but the one who sent me is true, whom you do not know.

verses.name: John 7:29
verses.text: I know him, because I am from him and he sent me.”  <div eID="gen26609" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 7:30
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11187"/><div sID="gen26610" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11187"/>So they were seeking to seize him, and no one laid a hand on him, because his hour had not yet come.

verses.name: John 7:31
verses.text: But from the crowd many believed in him and were saying, “Whenever the Christ comes, he will not perform more signs than this man has done, <transChange type="added">will he</transChange>?”<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here, indicated in the translation by the phrase “will he”</note>  <div eID="gen26610" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 7:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11188"/><div sID="gen26611" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11188"/>The Pharisees heard the crowd murmuring these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> about him, and the chief priests and the Pharisees sent officers in order <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to take him into custody ⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “that they could seize him”</note>

verses.name: John 7:33
verses.text: Then Jesus said, “Yet a little time I am with you, and I am going to the one who sent me.

verses.name: John 7:34
verses.text: You will seek me and will not find <transChange type="added">me</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note><note placement="foot">Some manuscripts explicitly state “me”</note> and where I am, you cannot come.”  <div eID="gen26611" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 7:35
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11189"/><div sID="gen26612" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11189"/>So the Jews said to one another, “Where <transChange type="added">is</transChange> this one going to go, that we will not find him? He is not going to go to the Dispersion among the Greeks and teach the Greeks, <transChange type="added">is he</transChange>?<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here, indicated in the translation by the phrase “is he”</note>

verses.name: John 7:36
verses.text: What is this saying that he said, ‘You will seek me and will not find <transChange type="added">me</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note><note placement="foot">Some manuscripts explicitly state “me”</note> and where I am, you cannot come’?”  <div eID="gen26612" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 7:37
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11190"/><title type="x-s">The Promise of the Spirit</title> <div sID="gen26613" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11190"/>Now on the last day of the feast—the great <transChange type="added">day</transChange>—Jesus stood and cried out, saying, “If anyone is thirsty, let him come to me, and let him drink,

verses.name: John 7:38
verses.text: the one who believes in me.<note placement="foot">An alternative punctuation of vv. <reference osisRef="John.7.37-John.7.38">37–38</reference> reads: “If anyone is thirsty, let him come to me and let him drink.  The one who believes in me, just as the scripture said, ‘Out of his belly will flow rivers of living water.’ ”</note> Just as the scripture said, ‘Out of his belly will flow rivers of living water.’ ”<note placement="foot">A quotation from the Old Testament of uncertain origin; texts most often suggested are <reference osisRef="Isa.44.3">Isa 44:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.55.1">55:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.58.11">58:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.14.8">Zech 14:8</reference></note>

verses.name: John 7:39
verses.text: Now he said this concerning the Spirit, whom those who believed in him were about to receive. For the Spirit was not yet <transChange type="added">given</transChange>,<note placement="foot">A few manuscripts supply the participle “given” here; while it is unlikely this represents the original reading, many English versions nevertheless supply “given” to avoid the impression that the Spirit did not exist prior to this point</note> because Jesus had not yet been glorified.)  <div eID="gen26613" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 7:40
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11191"/><title type="x-s">Different Opinions About Jesus</title> <div sID="gen26614" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11191"/>Then, <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard these words, some from the crowd began to say,<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to say”)</note> “This man is truly the Prophet!”

verses.name: John 7:41
verses.text: Others were saying, “This man is the Christ!” But others were saying, “No, for the Christ does not come from Galilee, <transChange type="added">does he</transChange>?<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here, indicated in the translation by the phrase “does he”</note>

verses.name: John 7:42
verses.text: Has not the scripture said that the Christ comes from the descendants of David, and from Bethlehem, the village where David was?”

verses.name: John 7:43
verses.text: So there was a division in the crowd because of him.

verses.name: John 7:44
verses.text: And some of them were wanting to seize him, but no one laid hands on him.  <div eID="gen26614" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 7:45
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11192"/><div sID="gen26615" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11192"/>So the officers came to the chief priests and Pharisees. And they said to them, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Why⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “because of what”</note> did you not bring him?”

verses.name: John 7:46
verses.text: The officers replied, “Never has a man spoken like this!”

verses.name: John 7:47
verses.text: Then the Pharisees replied to them, “You have not also been deceived, <transChange type="added">have you</transChange>?<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here, indicated in the translation by the phrase “have you”</note>

verses.name: John 7:48
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞None⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “not anyone”</note> of the rulers or of the Pharisees have believed in him, have they?<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here, indicated in the translation by the phrase “have they”</note>

verses.name: John 7:49
verses.text: But this crowd who does not know the law is accursed!”  <div eID="gen26615" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 7:50
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11193"/><div sID="gen26616" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11193"/>Nicodemus, the one who came to him previously—who was one of them—said to them,

verses.name: John 7:51
verses.text: “Our law does not condemn a man unless it first hears from him and knows what he is doing, <transChange type="added">does it</transChange>?”<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here, indicated in the translation by the phrase “does it”</note>

verses.name: John 7:52
verses.text: They answered and said to him, “You are not also from Galilee, <transChange type="added">are you</transChange>?<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here, indicated in the translation by the phrase “are you”</note> Investigate and see that a prophet does not arise from Galilee!” 〚

verses.name: John 7:53
verses.text: And each one went to his <transChange type="added">own</transChange> house.<note placement="foot"><reference osisRef="John.7.53-John.8.11">John 7:53–8:11 </reference>is not found in the earliest and best manuscripts and was almost certainly not an original part of the Gospel of John; one significant group of Greek manuscripts places it after <reference osisRef="Luke.21.38">Luke 21:38</reference></note>  <chapter eID="John.7"/>

verses.name: John 8:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11194"/><title type="x-s">A Woman Caught in Adultery</title> <div sID="gen26617" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11194"/>But Jesus went to the Mount of Olives.

verses.name: John 8:2
verses.text: Now early in the morning he came again to the temple <transChange type="added">courts</transChange>.<note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> And all the people were coming,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “were coming to him”</note> and he sat down and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“sat down”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> began to teach<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to teach”)</note> them.  <div eID="gen26617" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 8:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11195"/><div sID="gen26618" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11195"/>Now the scribes and the Pharisees brought to him a woman<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “brought a woman”</note> caught in adultery. And standing her in <transChange type="added">their</transChange> midst,

verses.name: John 8:4
verses.text: they said to him, testing <transChange type="added">him</transChange>,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts omit “testing him”</note> “Teacher, this woman was caught in the very act of committing adultery!

verses.name: John 8:5
verses.text: Now in the law, Moses commanded us to stone such women. So what do you say?”

verses.name: John 8:6
verses.text: (Now they were saying this to test him, so that they would have <transChange type="added">an occasion</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to bring charges against him.) But Jesus, bending down, began to write<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to write”)</note> with his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> finger on the ground, taking no notice.<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts omit “taking no notice”</note>

verses.name: John 8:7
verses.text: And when they persisted in asking him, straightening up he said<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “he straightened up and said”</note> to them, “The <transChange type="added">one</transChange> of you without sin, let him throw the first stone at her!”

verses.name: John 8:8
verses.text: And bending down again, he wrote on the ground.

verses.name: John 8:9
verses.text: Now <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> being convicted by their conscience,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts omit “being convicted by their conscience”</note> they began to depart,<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to depart”)</note> one by one, beginning with the older ones, and Jesus<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “he”</note> was left alone—and the woman who was in <transChange type="added">their</transChange> midst.

verses.name: John 8:10
verses.text: So Jesus, straightening up and seeing no one except the woman,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts omit “and seeing no one except the woman”</note> said to her, “Where are those accusers of yours?<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “said to her, ‘Woman, where are they?”</note> Does no one condemn you?”

verses.name: John 8:11
verses.text: And she said, “No one, Lord.” So Jesus said, “Neither do I condemn you. Go, and<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “and from now on”</note> sin no more.”〛<note placement="foot"><reference osisRef="John.7.53-John.8.11">John 7:53–8:11 </reference>is not found in the earliest and best manuscripts and was almost certainly not an original part of the Gospel of John; one significant group of Greek manuscripts places it after <reference osisRef="Luke.21.38">Luke 21:38</reference></note>  <div eID="gen26618" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 8:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11196"/><title type="x-s">Jesus, the Light of the World</title> <div sID="gen26619" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11196"/>Then Jesus spoke to them again, saying, “I am the light of the world! The one who follows me will never walk in darkness, but will have the light of life.”

verses.name: John 8:13
verses.text: So the Pharisees said to him, “You testify concerning yourself! Your testimony is not true.”

verses.name: John 8:14
verses.text: Jesus answered and said to them, “Even if I testify concerning myself, my testimony is true, because I know where I have come from and where I am going. But you do not know where I have come from or where I am going.

verses.name: John 8:15
verses.text: You judge according to externals; I do not judge anyone.

verses.name: John 8:16
verses.text: But even if I judge, my judgment is true, because I am not alone, but I and the Father who sent me.

verses.name: John 8:17
verses.text: And even in your law it is written that the testimony of two men is true.<note placement="foot">An allusion to <reference osisRef="Deut.17.6">Deut 17:6</reference></note>

verses.name: John 8:18
verses.text: I am the one who testifies concerning myself, and the Father who sent me testifies concerning me.”  <div eID="gen26619" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 8:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11197"/><div sID="gen26620" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11197"/>So they were saying to him, “Where is your father?” Jesus replied, “You know neither me nor my Father! If you had known me, you would have known my Father also.”

verses.name: John 8:20
verses.text: He spoke these words by the treasury <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the participle (“teaching”) which is understood as temporal</note> teaching in the temple courts,<note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> and no one seized him, because his hour had not yet come.  <div eID="gen26620" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 8:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11198"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Predicts His Death</title> <div sID="gen26621" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11198"/>So he said to them again, “I am going away, and you will seek me and will die in your sin. Where I am going you cannot come!”

verses.name: John 8:22
verses.text: Then the Jews began to say,<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to say”)</note> “Perhaps he will kill himself, because he is saying, ‘Where I am going you cannot come.’ ”

verses.name: John 8:23
verses.text: And he said to them, “You are from below; I am from above. You are from this world; I am not from this world.

verses.name: John 8:24
verses.text: Thus I said to you that you will die in your sins. For if you do not believe that I am <transChange type="added">he</transChange>, you will die in your sins.”  <div eID="gen26621" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 8:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11199"/><div sID="gen26622" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11199"/>So they began to say to him,<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to say”)</note> “Who are you?” Jesus said to them, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞What⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “that which”</note> I have been saying to you <transChange type="added">from</transChange> the beginning.

verses.name: John 8:26
verses.text: I have many <transChange type="added">things</transChange> to say and to judge concerning you, but the one who sent me is true, and <transChange type="added">the things</transChange> which I heard from him, these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> I say to the world.”

verses.name: John 8:27
verses.text: (They did not know that he was speaking to them about the Father.)  <div eID="gen26622" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 8:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11200"/><div sID="gen26623" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11200"/>Then Jesus said,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “said to them”</note> “When you lift up the Son of Man, then you will recognize that I am <transChange type="added">he</transChange>, and I do nothing from myself, but just as the Father taught me, I say these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>.

verses.name: John 8:29
verses.text: And the one who sent me is with me. He has not left me alone, because I always do the things that are pleasing to him.”

verses.name: John 8:30
verses.text: <transChange type="added">While</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was saying”)</note> he was saying these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, many believed in him.  <div eID="gen26623" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 8:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11201"/><title type="x-s">The Truth Will Set You Free</title> <div sID="gen26624" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11201"/>Then Jesus said to those Jews who had believed him, “If you continue in my word you are truly my disciples,

verses.name: John 8:32
verses.text: and you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.”

verses.name: John 8:33
verses.text: They replied to him, “We are descendants of Abraham and have not been enslaved to anyone at any time. How do you say, ‘You will become free’?”

verses.name: John 8:34
verses.text: Jesus replied to them, “Truly, truly I say to you, that everyone who commits sin is a slave of sin.

verses.name: John 8:35
verses.text: And the slave does not remain in the household <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “for the age”</note> the son remains <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “for the age”</note>

verses.name: John 8:36
verses.text: So if the son sets you free, you will be truly free.

verses.name: John 8:37
verses.text: I know that you are descendants of Abraham. But you are seeking to kill me, because my word makes no progress among you.

verses.name: John 8:38
verses.text: I speak <transChange type="added">the things</transChange> that I have seen with the Father; so also you do <transChange type="added">the things</transChange> that you have heard from the Father.”  <div eID="gen26624" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 8:39
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11202"/><title type="x-s">The Priority of Jesus Over Abraham</title> <div sID="gen26625" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11202"/>They answered and said to him, “Abraham is our father!” Jesus said to them, “If you are children of Abraham, do the deeds of Abraham!

verses.name: John 8:40
verses.text: But now you are seeking to kill me, a man who spoke to you the truth which I heard from God. This Abraham did not do.

verses.name: John 8:41
verses.text: You are doing the deeds of your father!” <div eID="gen26625" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen26626" type="x-p"/> They said<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “Then they said”</note> to him, “We were not born from sexual immorality! We have one father, God!”

verses.name: John 8:42
verses.text: Jesus said to them, “If God were your father, you would love me, for I have come forth from God and have come. For I have not come from myself, but that one sent me.

verses.name: John 8:43
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Why⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “because of what”</note> do you not understand my way of speaking? Because you are not able to listen to my message.

verses.name: John 8:44
verses.text: You are of your father the devil, and you want to do the desires of your father! That one was a murderer from the beginning, and does not stand firm in the truth, because truth is not in him. Whenever he speaks the lie, he speaks from his own <transChange type="added">nature</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*The word “nature” is not in the Greek text but is implied</note> because he is a liar and the father <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞of lies⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “of it”</note>

verses.name: John 8:45
verses.text: But because I am telling the truth, you do not believe me.

verses.name: John 8:46
verses.text: Who among you convicts me concerning sin? If I am telling the truth, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞why⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “because of what”</note> do you not believe me?

verses.name: John 8:47
verses.text: The one who is from God listens to the words of God. Because of this you do not listen—because you are not of God.”  <div eID="gen26626" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 8:48
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11203"/><div sID="gen26627" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11203"/>The Jews answered and said to him, “Do we not correctly say that you are a Samaritan and have a demon?”

verses.name: John 8:49
verses.text: Jesus replied, “I do not have a demon, but I honor my Father, and you dishonor me!

verses.name: John 8:50
verses.text: But I do not seek my <transChange type="added">own</transChange> glory. There is one who seeks and judges!

verses.name: John 8:51
verses.text: Truly, truly I say to you, if anyone keeps my word, he will never experience death <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “for the age”</note>  <div eID="gen26627" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 8:52
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11204"/><div sID="gen26628" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11204"/>The Jews<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “Then the Jews”</note> said to him, “Now we know that you have a demon! Abraham and the prophets died, and you say, ‘If anyone keeps my word, he will never taste death <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.’<note placement="foot">Literally “for the age”</note>

verses.name: John 8:53
verses.text: You are not greater than our father Abraham who died, <transChange type="added">are you</transChange>?<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here, indicated in the translation by the phrase “are you”</note> And the prophets died! Who do you make yourself <transChange type="added">to be</transChange>?”

verses.name: John 8:54
verses.text: Jesus replied, “If I glorify myself, my glory is nothing. The one who glorifies me is my Father, <transChange type="added">about</transChange> whom you say, ‘He is our God.’

verses.name: John 8:55
verses.text: And you have not known him, but I know him. And if I were to say that I do not know him, I would be a liar like you! But I know him and I keep his word.

verses.name: John 8:56
verses.text: Abraham your father rejoiced that he would see my day, and he saw <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and was glad.”  <div eID="gen26628" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 8:57
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11205"/><div sID="gen26629" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11205"/>So the Jews said to him, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞You are⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “you have”</note> not yet fifty years <transChange type="added">old</transChange>, and have you seen Abraham?”

verses.name: John 8:58
verses.text: Jesus said to them, “Truly, truly I say to you, before Abraham was, I am!”

verses.name: John 8:59
verses.text: Then they picked up stones in order to throw <transChange type="added">them</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> at him. But Jesus was hidden and went out of the temple courts.<note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note>  <chapter eID="John.8"/>

verses.name: John 9:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11206"/><title type="x-s">A Man Born Blind Is Given Sight</title> <div sID="gen26630" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11206"/>And <transChange type="added">as he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“went away”) which is understood as temporal</note> went away, he saw a man blind from birth.

verses.name: John 9:2
verses.text: And his disciples asked him, saying, “Rabbi, who sinned, this man or his parents, that he should be born blind?”

verses.name: John 9:3
verses.text: Jesus replied, “Neither this man sinned nor his parents, but <transChange type="added">it happened</transChange><note placement="foot">*The words “it happened” are not in the Greek text but are implied</note> so that the works of God could be revealed in him.

verses.name: John 9:4
verses.text: It is necessary <transChange type="added">for</transChange> us to do the deeds of the one who sent me while it is day; night is coming, when no one can work!

verses.name: John 9:5
verses.text: While I am in the world, I am the light of the world.”

verses.name: John 9:6
verses.text: <transChange type="added">When he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had said”) which is understood as temporal</note> had said these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, he spat on the ground and made clay with the saliva, and smeared the clay on his eyes.

verses.name: John 9:7
verses.text: And he said to him, “Go, wash in the pool of Siloam” (which is translated “sent”). So he went and washed and came back seeing.  <div eID="gen26630" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 9:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11207"/><div sID="gen26631" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11207"/>Then the neighbors and those who saw him previously (because he was a beggar) began to say,<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to say”)</note> “Is this man not the one who used to sit and beg?”

verses.name: John 9:9
verses.text: Others were saying, “It is this man”; others were saying, “No, but he is like him.” That one was saying, “I am <transChange type="added">he</transChange>!”

verses.name: John 9:10
verses.text: So they began to say<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to say”)</note> to him, “How<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “Then how”</note> were your eyes opened?”

verses.name: John 9:11
verses.text: He replied, “The man who is called Jesus made clay and smeared <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> on my eyes and said to me, ‘Go to Siloam and wash!’ So I went, and I washed, and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the two previous participles (“went” and “washed”) have been translated as finite verbs</note> I received sight.”

verses.name: John 9:12
verses.text: And they said to him, “Where is that man?” He said, “I do not know.”  <div eID="gen26631" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 9:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11208"/><title type="x-s">The Reaction of the Pharisees to the Healing</title> <div sID="gen26632" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11208"/>They brought him—the one formerly blind—to the Pharisees.

verses.name: John 9:14
verses.text: (Now the day on which Jesus made the clay and opened his eyes was the Sabbath.)

verses.name: John 9:15
verses.text: So the Pharisees also were asking him again how he received sight. And he said to them, “He put clay on my eyes, and I washed, and I see.”

verses.name: John 9:16
verses.text: So some of the Pharisees were saying, “This man is not from God, because he does not observe the Sabbath!” Others<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “But others”</note> were saying, “How can a man <transChange type="added">who is</transChange> a sinner perform such signs?” And there was a division among them.

verses.name: John 9:17
verses.text: So they said to the blind man again, “What do you say about him, because he opened your eyes?” And he said, “He is a prophet.”  <div eID="gen26632" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 9:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11209"/><div sID="gen26633" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11209"/>So the Jews did not believe concerning him that he had been blind and received sight, until they summoned the parents of the one<note placement="foot">Literally “of him”</note> who received sight.

verses.name: John 9:19
verses.text: And they asked them, saying, “Is this man your son, whom you say was born blind? Then how does he now see?”

verses.name: John 9:20
verses.text: So his parents answered and said, “We know that this man is our son, and that he was born blind.

verses.name: John 9:21
verses.text: But how he now sees we do not know, or who opened his eyes we do not know. Ask him! <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞He is a mature adult⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “he has maturity”</note> he will speak for himself!”

verses.name: John 9:22
verses.text: (His parents said these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> because they were afraid of the Jews, for the Jews had already decided that if anyone should confess him <transChange type="added">to be</transChange> Christ, he would be expelled from the synagogue.

verses.name: John 9:23
verses.text: Because of this his parents said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞He is a mature adult⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>;<note placement="foot">Literally “he has maturity”</note> ask him.”)  <div eID="gen26633" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 9:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11210"/><div sID="gen26634" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11210"/>So they summoned the man who had been blind for the second time and said to him, “Give glory to God! We know that this man is a sinner!”

verses.name: John 9:25
verses.text: Then that man replied, “Whether he is a sinner I do not know. One <transChange type="added">thing</transChange> I know—that <transChange type="added">although I</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was”) which is understood as concessive</note> was blind, now I see!”

verses.name: John 9:26
verses.text: So they said to him, “What did he do to you? How did he open your eyes?”

verses.name: John 9:27
verses.text: He replied to them, “I told you already and you did not listen! Why do you want to hear <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> again? You do not want to become his disciples also, do you?”<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here, indicated in the translation by the phrase “do you”</note>

verses.name: John 9:28
verses.text: They reviled<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “And they reviled”</note> him and said, “You are his disciple! But we are disciples of Moses!

verses.name: John 9:29
verses.text: We know that God has spoken to Moses, but we do not know where this man is from.”

verses.name: John 9:30
verses.text: The man answered and said to them, “For the remarkable thing is this, that you do not know where he is from, and he opened my eyes!

verses.name: John 9:31
verses.text: We know that God does not listen to sinners, but if someone is devout and does his will, he listens to this one.

verses.name: John 9:32
verses.text: From <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞time immemorial⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the age”</note> it has not been heard that someone opened the eyes of one born blind.

verses.name: John 9:33
verses.text: If this man were not from God, he would not be able to do anything!”

verses.name: John 9:34
verses.text: They answered and said to him, “You were born completely in sin, and are you attempting to teach<note placement="foot">*Here the present tense is translated as a conative present (“attempting to teach”)</note> us?” And they threw him out.  <div eID="gen26634" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 9:35
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11211"/><title type="x-s">Jesus as the Son of Man</title> <div sID="gen26635" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11211"/>Jesus heard that they had thrown him out, and finding him, he said, “Do you believe in the Son of Man?”

verses.name: John 9:36
verses.text: He answered and said, “And who is <transChange type="added">he</transChange>, sir, that I may believe in him?”

verses.name: John 9:37
verses.text: Jesus said to him, “You have both seen him, and he is the one who is speaking with you.” 〚

verses.name: John 9:38
verses.text: And he said, “I believe, Lord!” and he worshiped him.

verses.name: John 9:39
verses.text: And Jesus said,〛<note placement="foot">A number of important manuscripts lack v. <reference osisRef="John.9.38">38</reference> and the first part of v. <reference osisRef="John.9.39">39</reference> (“and Jesus said”)</note> “For judgment I have come into this world, so that those who do not see may see, and those who see may become blind!”

verses.name: John 9:40
verses.text: <transChange type="added">Some</transChange> of the Pharisees who were with him heard these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> and said to him, “We are not also blind, <transChange type="added">are we</transChange>?”<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here, indicated in the translation by the phrase “are we”</note>

verses.name: John 9:41
verses.text: Jesus said to them, “If you were blind, you would not have sin. But now you say, ‘We see,’ your sin remains.  <chapter eID="John.9"/>

verses.name: John 10:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11212"/><title type="x-s">Jesus as the Good Shepherd</title> <div sID="gen26636" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11212"/>“Truly, truly I say to you, the one who does not enter through the door into the fold of the sheep, but climbs up at some other place—that one is a thief and a robber.

verses.name: John 10:2
verses.text: But the one who enters through the door is the shepherd of the sheep.

verses.name: John 10:3
verses.text: For this one the doorkeeper opens, and the sheep hear his voice, and he calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.

verses.name: John 10:4
verses.text: Whenever he sends out all his own, he goes before them, and the sheep follow him because they know his voice.

verses.name: John 10:5
verses.text: And they will never follow a stranger, but will flee from him, because they do not know the voice of strangers.”

verses.name: John 10:6
verses.text: Jesus told them this parable, but they did not understand what it was that he was saying to them.  <div eID="gen26636" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 10:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11213"/><div sID="gen26637" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11213"/>Then Jesus said to them<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts omit “to them”</note> again, “Truly, truly, I say to you, I am the door of the sheep.

verses.name: John 10:8
verses.text: All those who came before me are thieves and robbers, but the sheep do not listen to them.

verses.name: John 10:9
verses.text: I am the door. If anyone enters through me, he will be saved, and will come in and will go out and will find pasture.

verses.name: John 10:10
verses.text: The thief <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞comes only⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “does not come except”</note> so that he can steal and kill and destroy; I have come so that they may have life, and have it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> abundantly.  <div eID="gen26637" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 10:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11214"/><div sID="gen26638" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11214"/>“I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.

verses.name: John 10:12
verses.text: The hired hand, who is not the shepherd, whose own the sheep are not, sees the wolf approaching and abandons the sheep and runs away—and the wolf seizes them and scatters <transChange type="added">them</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>—

verses.name: John 10:13
verses.text: because he is a hired hand and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he is not concerned⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “it is not a concern to him”</note> about the sheep.  <div eID="gen26638" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 10:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11215"/><div sID="gen26639" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11215"/>“I am the good shepherd, and I know my <transChange type="added">own</transChange>, and my <transChange type="added">own</transChange> know me,

verses.name: John 10:15
verses.text: just as the Father knows me and I know the Father, and I lay down my life for the sheep.

verses.name: John 10:16
verses.text: And I have other sheep which are not from this fold. I must bring these also, and they will hear my voice, and they will become one flock—one shepherd.

verses.name: John 10:17
verses.text: Because of this the Father loves me, because I lay down my life so that I may take possession of it again.

verses.name: John 10:18
verses.text: No one takes it from me, but I lay it down <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞voluntarily⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “from myself”</note> I have authority to lay it down, and I have authority to take possession of it again. This commandment I received from my Father.”  <div eID="gen26639" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 10:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11216"/><div sID="gen26640" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11216"/>Again there was a division among the Jews because of these words.

verses.name: John 10:20
verses.text: And many of them were saying, “He has a demon and is out of his mind! Why do you listen to him?”

verses.name: John 10:21
verses.text: Others were saying, “These are not the words of one who is possessed by a demon! A demon is not able to open the eyes of the blind, <transChange type="added">is it</transChange>?”<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here, indicated in the translation by the phrase “is it”</note>  <div eID="gen26640" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 10:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11217"/><title type="x-s">Jesus at the Feast of the Dedication</title> <div sID="gen26641" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11217"/>Then the feast of the Dedication took place in Jerusalem. It was winter,

verses.name: John 10:23
verses.text: and Jesus was walking in the temple in the Portico of Solomon.

verses.name: John 10:24
verses.text: So the Jews surrounded him and began to say<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to say”)</note> to him, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞How long will you keep us in suspense⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?<note placement="foot">Literally “until when will you take away our life”</note> If you are the Christ, tell us plainly!”

verses.name: John 10:25
verses.text: Jesus answered them, “I told you and you do not believe! The deeds that I do in the name of my Father, these testify about me.

verses.name: John 10:26
verses.text: But you do not believe, because you are not of my sheep!

verses.name: John 10:27
verses.text: My sheep listen to my voice, and I know them, and they follow me.

verses.name: John 10:28
verses.text: And I give them eternal life, and they will never perish <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “for the age”</note> and no one will seize them out of my hand.

verses.name: John 10:29
verses.text: My Father, who has given <transChange type="added">them</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to me, is greater than all, and no one can seize them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> from the Father’s hand.

verses.name: John 10:30
verses.text: The Father and I are one.”  <div eID="gen26641" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 10:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11218"/><div sID="gen26642" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11218"/>Then<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts omit “Then”</note> the Jews picked up stones again so that they could stone him.

verses.name: John 10:32
verses.text: Jesus answered them, “I have shown you many good deeds from the Father. For which one of them are you going to stone me?”

verses.name: John 10:33
verses.text: The Jews answered him, “We are not going to stone you concerning a good deed, but concerning blasphemy, and because you, <transChange type="added">although you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“are”) which is understood as concessive</note> are a man, make yourself <transChange type="added">to be</transChange> God!”

verses.name: John 10:34
verses.text: Jesus answered them, “Is it not written in your law, ‘I said, “You are gods” ’?<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.82.6">Ps 82:6 </reference>(in common usage “law” could refer to the entire Old Testament)</note>

verses.name: John 10:35
verses.text: If he called them ‘gods’ to whom the word of God came—and the scripture cannot be broken—

verses.name: John 10:36
verses.text: do you say about <transChange type="added">he</transChange> whom the Father set apart and sent into the world, ‘You are blaspheming,’ because I said, ‘I am the Son of God’?

verses.name: John 10:37
verses.text: If I do not do the deeds of my Father, do not believe me.

verses.name: John 10:38
verses.text: But if I am doing <transChange type="added">them</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> even if you do not believe me, believe the deeds, so that you may know and understand that the Father <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in me and I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> in the Father.”

verses.name: John 10:39
verses.text: So they were seeking again to seize him, and he departed out of their hand.  <div eID="gen26642" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 10:40
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11219"/><div sID="gen26643" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11219"/>And he went away again on the other side of the Jordan, to the place where John was baptizing at an earlier time, and he stayed there.

verses.name: John 10:41
verses.text: And many came to him and began to say,<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to say”)</note> “John performed no sign, but everything John said about this man was true!”

verses.name: John 10:42
verses.text: And many believed in him there.  <chapter eID="John.10"/>

verses.name: John 11:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11220"/><title type="x-s">Lazarus Dies</title> <div sID="gen26644" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11220"/>Now a certain man was sick, Lazarus from Bethany, the village of Mary and her sister Martha.

verses.name: John 11:2
verses.text: (Now it was Mary who anointed the Lord with perfumed oil and wiped his feet with her hair, whose brother Lazarus was sick.)

verses.name: John 11:3
verses.text: So the sisters sent <transChange type="added">word</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to him, saying, “Lord, behold, <transChange type="added">the one</transChange> whom you love is sick.”

verses.name: John 11:4
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> Jesus said, “This sickness is not to death, but for the glory of God, in order that the Son of God may be glorified through it.”

verses.name: John 11:5
verses.text: (Now Jesus loved Martha and her sister and Lazarus.)

verses.name: John 11:6
verses.text: So when he heard that he was sick, then he remained in the place <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞where⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in which”</note> he was two days.  <div eID="gen26644" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 11:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11221"/><div sID="gen26645" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11221"/>Then after this he said to the disciples, “Let us go to Judea again.”

verses.name: John 11:8
verses.text: The disciples said to him, “Rabbi, the Jews were seeking just now to stone you, and are you going there again?”

verses.name: John 11:9
verses.text: Jesus replied, Are <transChange type="added">there</transChange> not twelve hours in the day? If anyone walks around in the daylight, he does not stumble, because he sees the light of this world.

verses.name: John 11:10
verses.text: But if anyone walks around in the night, he stumbles, because the light is not in him.

verses.name: John 11:11
verses.text: He said these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, and after this he said to them, “Our friend Lazarus has fallen asleep, but I am going so that I can awaken him.”

verses.name: John 11:12
verses.text: So the disciples said to him, “Lord, if he has fallen asleep, he will get well.”

verses.name: John 11:13
verses.text: (Now Jesus had been speaking about his death, but they thought that he was speaking about <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞real sleep⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the sleep of slumber”</note>)

verses.name: John 11:14
verses.text: So Jesus then said to them plainly, “Lazarus has died,

verses.name: John 11:15
verses.text: and I am glad <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞for your sake⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for the sake of you”</note> that I was not there, so that you may believe. But let us go to him.”

verses.name: John 11:16
verses.text: Then Thomas (the one who is called Didymus)<note placement="foot">“Didymus” means “the twin” in Greek</note> said to his fellow disciples, “Let us go also, so that we may die with him.”  <div eID="gen26645" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 11:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11222"/><title type="x-s">Jesus the Resurrection and the Life</title> <div sID="gen26646" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11222"/>So <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“arrived”) which is understood as temporal</note> arrived, Jesus found he had already <transChange type="added">been</transChange> four days in the tomb.

verses.name: John 11:18
verses.text: (Now Bethany was near Jerusalem, about fifteen stadia.<note placement="foot">A “stade” or “stadium” (plur. “stadia”) is about 607 ft (187 m), so this was just under two miles (3 km)</note>

verses.name: John 11:19
verses.text: So many of the Jews came to Martha and Mary in order to console them concerning their<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> brother.)

verses.name: John 11:20
verses.text: Now Martha, when she heard that Jesus was coming, went to meet him, but Mary was sitting in the house.

verses.name: John 11:21
verses.text: So Martha said to Jesus, “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.

verses.name: John 11:22
verses.text: Even<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “But even”</note> now I know that whatever you ask God, God will grant you.”

verses.name: John 11:23
verses.text: Jesus said to her, “Your brother will rise again.”

verses.name: John 11:24
verses.text: Martha said to him, “I know that he will rise again in the resurrection at the last day.”

verses.name: John 11:25
verses.text: Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. The one who believes in me, even if he dies, will live,

verses.name: John 11:26
verses.text: and everyone who lives and believes in me will never die <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “for the age”</note> Do you believe this?”

verses.name: John 11:27
verses.text: She said to him, “Yes, Lord, I have believed that you are the Christ, the Son of God, who comes into the world.”  <div eID="gen26646" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 11:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11223"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Weeps</title> <div sID="gen26647" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11223"/>And <transChange type="added">when she</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had said”) which is understood as temporal</note> had said this, she went and called her sister Mary privately, saying, “The Teacher is here and is calling for you.”

verses.name: John 11:29
verses.text: So that one, when she heard <transChange type="added">it</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> got up quickly and went to him.

verses.name: John 11:30
verses.text: (Now Jesus has not yet come into the village, but was still in the place where Martha went to meet him.)

verses.name: John 11:31
verses.text: So the Jews who were with her in the house and were consoling her, <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw Mary—that she stood up quickly and went out—followed her, because they<note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“thought”) which is understood as causal</note> thought that she was going to the tomb in order to weep there.  <div eID="gen26647" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 11:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11224"/><div sID="gen26648" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11224"/>Then Mary, when she came where Jesus was <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the participle (“saw”) has been translated as a finite verb in keeping with English style</note> saw him, fell at his feet, saying to him, “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.”

verses.name: John 11:33
verses.text: Then Jesus, when he saw her weeping and the Jews who came with her weeping, was deeply moved in spirit and was troubled within himself.

verses.name: John 11:34
verses.text: And he said, “Where have you laid him?” They said to him, “Lord, come and see.”

verses.name: John 11:35
verses.text: Jesus wept.

verses.name: John 11:36
verses.text: So the Jews were saying, “See how he loved him!”

verses.name: John 11:37
verses.text: But some of them said, “Was not this man who opened the eyes of the blind able to do <transChange type="added">something</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> so that this man also would not have died?”  <div eID="gen26648" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 11:38
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11225"/><title type="x-s">Lazarus Is Raised</title> <div sID="gen26649" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11225"/>Then Jesus, deeply moved within himself again, came to the tomb. Now it was a cave, and a stone was lying on it.

verses.name: John 11:39
verses.text: Jesus said, “Take away the stone.” Martha, the sister of the one who had died, said to him, “Lord, he is stinking already, because it has been four days.”

verses.name: John 11:40
verses.text: Jesus said to her, “Did I not say to you that if you believed, you would see the glory of God?”

verses.name: John 11:41
verses.text: So they took away the stone. And Jesus lifted up his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> eyes above and said, “Father, I give thanks to you that you hear me.

verses.name: John 11:42
verses.text: And I know that you always hear me, but for the sake of the crowd standing around I said <transChange type="added">it</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> so that they may believe that you sent me.”

verses.name: John 11:43
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had said”) which is understood as temporal</note> had said these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, he cried out with a loud voice, “Lazarus, come out!”

verses.name: John 11:44
verses.text: The one who had died came out, his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> feet and his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> hands bound with strips of cloth, and his face wrapped with a facecloth. Jesus said to them, “Untie him and let him go.”  <div eID="gen26649" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 11:45
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11226"/><title type="x-s">The Jewish Leaders Plot to Kill Jesus</title> <div sID="gen26650" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11226"/>Then many of the Jews who had come with Mary and saw <transChange type="added">the things</transChange> which he did believed in him.

verses.name: John 11:46
verses.text: But some of them went to the Pharisees and told them <transChange type="added">the things</transChange> which Jesus had done.

verses.name: John 11:47
verses.text: So the chief priests and the Pharisees called together the Sanhedrin and said, “What are we doing? For this man is performing many signs!

verses.name: John 11:48
verses.text: If we allow him <transChange type="added">to go on</transChange> in this way, everyone will believe in him, and the Romans will come and take away both our place<note placement="foot">Generally understood to be a reference to the Jerusalem temple</note> and our<note placement="foot">Literally “both the place and the nation of us”; the possessive pronoun is repeated in the translation (rather than the article) in keeping with English style</note> nation.”  <div eID="gen26650" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 11:49
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11227"/><div sID="gen26651" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11227"/>But a certain one of them, Caiaphas (who was high priest in that year), said to them, “You do not know anything at all!

verses.name: John 11:50
verses.text: Nor do you consider that it is profitable for you that one man should die for the people, and the whole nation not perish.”

verses.name: John 11:51
verses.text: (Now he did not say this from himself, but being high priest in that year, he prophesied that Jesus was going to die for the nation,

verses.name: John 11:52
verses.text: and not for the nation only, but also that the children of God who are scattered would be gathered into one.)

verses.name: John 11:53
verses.text: So from that day they resolved that they should kill him.

verses.name: John 11:54
verses.text: So Jesus was no longer walking openly among the Jews, but went away from there to the region near the wilderness, to a city called Ephraim, and there he stayed with the disciples.  <div eID="gen26651" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 11:55
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11228"/><div sID="gen26652" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11228"/>Now the Passover of the Jews was near, and many went up to Jerusalem from the <transChange type="added">surrounding</transChange> country before the Passover, so that they could purify themselves.

verses.name: John 11:56
verses.text: So they were looking for Jesus, and were speaking with one another <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the participle (“standing”) which is understood as temporal</note> standing in the temple courts,<note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> “What do you think? That he will not come to the feast?”

verses.name: John 11:57
verses.text: (Now the chief priests and the Pharisees had given orders that if anyone knew where he was, they should report <transChange type="added">it</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> in order that they could arrest him.)  <chapter eID="John.11"/>

verses.name: John 12:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11229"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Is Anointed at Bethany</title> <div sID="gen26653" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11229"/>Then, six days before the Passover, Jesus came to Bethany, where Lazarus was, whom Jesus had raised from the dead.

verses.name: John 12:2
verses.text: So they made him a dinner there, and Martha was serving, but Lazarus was one of the ones reclining at table with him.

verses.name: John 12:3
verses.text: Then Mary took a pound<note placement="foot">The Greek term refers to a Roman pound, 327.45 grams (approximately 12 ounces)</note> of ointment of very valuable genuine nard and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> anointed the feet of Jesus, and wiped his feet with her hair. And the house was filled with the fragrance of the ointment.

verses.name: John 12:4
verses.text: But Judas Iscariot, one of his disciples (the one who was going to betray him) said,

verses.name: John 12:5
verses.text: “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Why⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “because of what”</note> was this ointment not sold for three hundred denarii and given to the poor?”

verses.name: John 12:6
verses.text: (Now he said this not because <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he was concerned⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “it was a concern to him”</note> about the poor, but because he was a thief, and having the money box, he used to steal what was put into it.)<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: John 12:7
verses.text: So Jesus said, “Leave her alone, so that she may keep it for the day of my preparation for burial.

verses.name: John 12:8
verses.text: For you have the poor with you always, but you do not always have me.”  <div eID="gen26653" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 12:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11230"/><title type="x-s">The Decision to Kill Lazarus</title> <div sID="gen26654" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11230"/>Now a large crowd<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “the large crowd”</note> of Jews found out that he was there, and they came, not only because of Jesus, but so that they could see Lazarus also, whom he raised from the dead.

verses.name: John 12:10
verses.text: So the chief priests decided that they would kill Lazarus also,

verses.name: John 12:11
verses.text: because on account of him many of the Jews were going and believing in Jesus.  <div eID="gen26654" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 12:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11231"/><title type="x-s">The Triumphal Entry</title> <div sID="gen26655" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11231"/>On the next day the large crowd who had come to the feast, <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem,

verses.name: John 12:13
verses.text: took the branches of palm trees and went out to meet him, and began crying out, <div eID="gen26655" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen26656"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26657"/>“Hosanna!<l eID="gen26657" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26658"/>Blessed <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the one who comes in the name of the Lord,<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.118.25-Ps.118.26">Ps 118:25–26</reference></note><l eID="gen26658" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26659"/>even the king of Israel!” <l eID="gen26659" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen26656"/>

verses.name: John 12:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11232"/><div sID="gen26660" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11232"/>So Jesus found a young donkey <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“found”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> sat on it, just as it is written,  <div eID="gen26660" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 12:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11233"/><lg sID="gen26661"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26662"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11233"/>“Do not be afraid, daughter of Zion!<l eID="gen26662" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26663"/>Behold, your king is coming,<l eID="gen26663" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26664"/>seated on the foal of a donkey!”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Zech.9.9">Zech 9:9</reference></note> <l eID="gen26664" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen26661"/>

verses.name: John 12:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11234"/><div sID="gen26665" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11234"/>(His disciples did not understand these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> at first, but when Jesus was glorified, then they remembered that these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> had been written about him and they did these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> to him.)

verses.name: John 12:17
verses.text: So the crowd who was with him when he called Lazarus out of the tomb and raised him from the dead were continuing to testify.

verses.name: John 12:18
verses.text: Because of this also the crowd went to meet him, for they had heard <transChange type="added">that</transChange> he had performed this sign.

verses.name: John 12:19
verses.text: So the Pharisees said to one another, “You see that you are accomplishing nothing! Behold, the world has gone after him.”  <div eID="gen26665" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 12:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11235"/><title type="x-s">Greeks Seeking Jesus</title> <div sID="gen26666" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11235"/>Now some Greeks were among those who had gone up in order to worship at the feast.

verses.name: John 12:21
verses.text: So these approached Philip, who was from Bethsaida in Galilee, and began asking him saying, “Sir, we want to see Jesus.”

verses.name: John 12:22
verses.text: Philip went and told Andrew. Andrew and Philip went and told Jesus.

verses.name: John 12:23
verses.text: And Jesus answered them, saying, “The hour has come that the Son of Man will be glorified.

verses.name: John 12:24
verses.text: Truly, truly I say to you, unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“falls”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> dies, it remains <transChange type="added">by</transChange> itself alone. But if it dies, it bears much fruit.

verses.name: John 12:25
verses.text: The one who loves his life loses it, and the one who hates his life in this world preserves it for eternal life.

verses.name: John 12:26
verses.text: If anyone serves me, he must follow me, and where I am, there my servant will be also. If anyone serves me, the Father will honor him.  <div eID="gen26666" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 12:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11236"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Predicts His Death</title> <div sID="gen26667" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11236"/>“Now my soul is troubled, and what shall I say? ‘Father, deliver me from this hour’? But for this <transChange type="added">reason</transChange> I have come to this hour!

verses.name: John 12:28
verses.text: Father, glorify your name!” Then a voice came from heaven, “I have both glorified <transChange type="added">it</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and I will glorify it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> again.”

verses.name: John 12:29
verses.text: Now the crowd that stood <transChange type="added">there</transChange> and heard <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> said <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞it had thundered⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “thunder had happened”</note> Others were saying, “An angel has spoken to him!”

verses.name: John 12:30
verses.text: Jesus answered and said, “This voice has not happened for my sake, but <transChange type="added">for</transChange> your sake.

verses.name: John 12:31
verses.text: Now is the judgment of this world! Now the ruler of this world will be thrown out!

verses.name: John 12:32
verses.text: And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all <transChange type="added">people</transChange> to myself.”

verses.name: John 12:33
verses.text: (Now he said this to indicate by what sort of death he was going to die.)  <div eID="gen26667" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 12:34
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11237"/><div sID="gen26668" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11237"/>Then the crowd replied to him, “We have heard from the law that the Christ remains <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!<note placement="foot">Literally “for the age”; probably an allusion to <reference osisRef="Ps.89.35-Ps.89.37">Ps 89:35–37 </reference>(in common usage “law” could refer to the entire Old Testament)</note> And how do you say that the Son of Man must be lifted up? Who is this Son of Man?”
