verses.name: John 12:35
verses.text: So Jesus said to them, “Yet a little time the light is with you! Walk while you have the light, so that the darkness does not overtake you! And the one who walks in the darkness does not know where he is going.

verses.name: John 12:36
verses.text: While you have the light, believe in the light, in order that you may become sons of light.” Jesus said these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, and <transChange type="added">then</transChange> he went away <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went away”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> was hidden from them.  <div eID="gen26668" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 12:37
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11238"/><title type="x-s">The People Still Refuse to Believe</title> <div sID="gen26669" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11238"/>But as many signs <transChange type="added">as</transChange> he had performed before them, they did not believe in him,

verses.name: John 12:38
verses.text: in order that the word of the prophet Isaiah would be fulfilled, who said, <div eID="gen26669" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen26670"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26671"/>“Lord, who has believed our message?<l eID="gen26671" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26672"/>And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.53.1">Isa 53:1</reference></note> <l eID="gen26672" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen26670"/>

verses.name: John 12:39
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11239"/><div sID="gen26673" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11239"/>For this <transChange type="added">reason</transChange> they were not able to believe, because again Isaiah said,  <div eID="gen26673" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 12:40
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11240"/><lg sID="gen26674"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26675"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11240"/>“He has blinded their eyes<l eID="gen26675" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26676"/>and hardened their hearts,<l eID="gen26676" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26677"/>lest they see with <transChange type="added">their</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> eyes<l eID="gen26677" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26678"/>and understand with <transChange type="added">their</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> hearts<l eID="gen26678" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26679"/>and turn, and I heal them.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.6.10">Isa 6:10</reference></note> <l eID="gen26679" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen26674"/>

verses.name: John 12:41
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11241"/><div sID="gen26680" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11241"/>Isaiah said these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> because he saw his glory, and he spoke about him.  <div eID="gen26680" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 12:42
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11242"/><div sID="gen26681" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11242"/>Yet despite that, even many of the rulers believed in him, but because of the Pharisees they did not confess <transChange type="added">it</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> so that they would not be expelled from the synagogue.

verses.name: John 12:43
verses.text: For they loved the praise of men more than praise from God.  <div eID="gen26681" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 12:44
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11243"/><title type="x-s">Jesus’ Final Public Appeal</title> <div sID="gen26682" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11243"/>But Jesus cried out and said, “The one who believes in me does not believe in me, but in the one who sent me,

verses.name: John 12:45
verses.text: and the one who sees me sees the one who sent me.

verses.name: John 12:46
verses.text: I have come <transChange type="added">as</transChange> a light into the world, in order that everyone who believes in me will not remain in the darkness.

verses.name: John 12:47
verses.text: And if anyone hears my words and does not observe <transChange type="added">them</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> I will not judge him. For I have not come to judge the world, but to save the world.

verses.name: John 12:48
verses.text: The one who rejects me and does not accept my words has one who judges him; the word that I have spoken will judge him on the last day.

verses.name: John 12:49
verses.text: For I have not spoken from myself, but the Father himself who sent me <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞has commanded me⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “has given me commandment”</note> what I should say and what I should speak.

verses.name: John 12:50
verses.text: And I know that his commandment is eternal life. So <transChange type="added">the things</transChange> that I say, just as the Father said to me, thus I say.”  <chapter eID="John.12"/>

verses.name: John 13:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11244"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Washes His Disciples’ Feet</title> <div sID="gen26683" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11244"/>Now before the feast of Passover, Jesus, knowing that his hour had come that he would depart from this world to the Father, <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied in keeping with English style</note> having loved his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> own in the world, loved them to the end.

verses.name: John 13:2
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was taking place”)</note> a dinner was taking place, when<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“put”)</note> the devil had already put into the heart of Judas <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Simon Iscariot that he should betray him,

verses.name: John 13:3
verses.text: <transChange type="added">because he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“knew”) which is understood as causal</note> knew that the Father had given him all things into his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> hands, and that he had come forth from God and was going away to God,

verses.name: John 13:4
verses.text: he got up from the dinner and took off <transChange type="added">his</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> outer clothing, and taking a towel, tied it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> around himself.

verses.name: John 13:5
verses.text: Then he poured water into the washbasin and began to wash the feet of the disciples, and to wipe <transChange type="added">them</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> dry with the towel <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞which he had tied around himself⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “with which he was girded”</note>  <div eID="gen26683" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 13:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11245"/><div sID="gen26684" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11245"/>Then he came to Simon Peter. He said to him, “Lord, are you going to wash my feet?”

verses.name: John 13:7
verses.text: Jesus answered and said to him, “What I am doing you do not understand now, but you will understand after these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>.”

verses.name: John 13:8
verses.text: Peter said to him, “You will never wash my feet <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!”<note placement="foot">Literally “for the age”</note> Jesus replied to him, “Unless I wash you, you do not have a share with me.”

verses.name: John 13:9
verses.text: Simon Peter said to him, “Lord, not my feet only, but also <transChange type="added">my</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> hands and my<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> head!”

verses.name: John 13:10
verses.text: Jesus said to him, “The one who has bathed <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞only needs⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “does not have need except”</note> to wash his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> feet, but is completely clean. And you are clean, but not all <transChange type="added">of you</transChange>.”

verses.name: John 13:11
verses.text: (For he knew the one who would betray him; because of this he said, “Not all <transChange type="added">of you</transChange> are clean.”)  <div eID="gen26684" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 13:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11246"/><div sID="gen26685" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11246"/>So when he had washed their feet and taken his outer clothing and reclined at table again, he said to them, “Do you understand what I have done for you?

verses.name: John 13:13
verses.text: You call me ‘Teacher’ and ‘Lord,’ and you speak correctly, for I am.

verses.name: John 13:14
verses.text: If then I—<transChange type="added">your</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> Lord and Teacher—wash your feet, you also ought to wash one another’s feet.

verses.name: John 13:15
verses.text: For I have given you an example, that just as I have done for you, you also do.

verses.name: John 13:16
verses.text: Truly, truly I say to you, a slave is not greater than his master, nor a messenger greater than the one who sent him.

verses.name: John 13:17
verses.text: If you understand these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, you are blessed if you do them.  <div eID="gen26685" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 13:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11247"/><div sID="gen26686" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11247"/>“I am not speaking about all of you. I know whom I have chosen, but in order that the scripture would be fulfilled, ‘The one who eats my bread has lifted up his heel against me.’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.41.9">Ps 41:9</reference></note>

verses.name: John 13:19
verses.text: From now <transChange type="added">on</transChange> I am telling you before <transChange type="added">it</transChange> happens, in order that when <transChange type="added">it</transChange> happens you may believe that I am <transChange type="added">he</transChange>.<note placement="foot">*Here the predicate nominative (“he”) is understood, but must be supplied in the translation</note>

verses.name: John 13:20
verses.text: Truly, truly I say to you, the one who receives anyone I send receives me, and the one who receives me receives the one who sent me.”  <div eID="gen26686" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 13:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11248"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Predicts Judas’ Betrayal</title> <div sID="gen26687" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11248"/><transChange type="added">When he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had said”) which is understood as temporal</note> had said these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, Jesus was troubled in spirit and testified and said, “Truly, truly I say to you that one of you will betray me.”

verses.name: John 13:22
verses.text: The disciples began looking<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began looking”)</note> at one another, uncertain about whom he was speaking.

verses.name: John 13:23
verses.text: One of his disciples—the one whom Jesus loved—was reclining <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞close beside⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in the bosom of” (a position dictated by ancient banqueting practice)</note> Jesus.

verses.name: John 13:24
verses.text: So Simon Peter gestured for this one to inquire who it was about whom he was speaking.

verses.name: John 13:25
verses.text: He leaned back<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “Then he leaned back”</note> accordingly against Jesus’ chest and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“leaned back”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to him, “Lord, who is it?”

verses.name: John 13:26
verses.text: Jesus replied, “It is he to whom I dip the piece of bread and give <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to him.” Then after<note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“dipping”) which is understood as temporal</note> dipping the piece of bread, he gave it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note><note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “after dipping the piece of bread, he took it and gave it”</note> to Judas <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Simon Iscariot.

verses.name: John 13:27
verses.text: And after the piece of bread, then Satan entered into him. Then Jesus said to him, “What you are doing, do quickly!”

verses.name: John 13:28
verses.text: (Now no one of those reclining at table knew for what <transChange type="added">reason</transChange> he said this to him.

verses.name: John 13:29
verses.text: For some were thinking because Judas had the money box, Jesus was telling him, “Purchase <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞what we need⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “of which we have need”</note> for the feast,” or that he should give something to the poor.)

verses.name: John 13:30
verses.text: So <transChange type="added">after he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had taken”) which is understood as temporal</note> had taken the piece of bread, he went out immediately. And it was night.  <div eID="gen26687" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 13:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11249"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Predicts Peter’s Denial</title> <div sID="gen26688" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11249"/>Then, when he had gone out, Jesus said, “Now the Son of Man is glorified, and God is glorified in him.

verses.name: John 13:32
verses.text: If God is glorified in him, God will also glorify him in himself, and will glorify him immediately.

verses.name: John 13:33
verses.text: Children, yet a little <transChange type="added">time</transChange> I am with you. You will seek me and just as I said to the Jews, “Where I am going you cannot come,” now I say also to you.  <div eID="gen26688" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 13:34
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11250"/><div sID="gen26689" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11250"/>“A new commandment I give to you: that you love one another—just as I have loved you, that you also love one another.

verses.name: John 13:35
verses.text: By this everyone will know that you are my disciples—if you have love for one another.”  <div eID="gen26689" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 13:36
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11251"/><div sID="gen26690" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11251"/>Simon Peter said to him, “Lord, where are you going?” Jesus replied,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “replied to him”</note> “Where I am going you cannot follow me now, but you will follow later.”

verses.name: John 13:37
verses.text: Peter said to him, “Lord, why am I not able to follow you now? I will lay down my life for you!”

verses.name: John 13:38
verses.text: Jesus replied, “Will you lay down your life for me? Truly, truly I say to you, the rooster will not crow until you have denied me three times!  <chapter eID="John.13"/>

verses.name: John 14:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11252"/><title type="x-s">Jesus’ Farewell Discourse</title> <div sID="gen26691" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11252"/>“Do not let your hearts be troubled. You believe<note placement="foot">Or simply “Believe”; the verb form can be either indicative (e.g., KJV, NAB, NLT) or imperative (e.g., NIV, NRSV, ESV)</note> in God; believe<note placement="foot">Like the previous verb “believe” this form could also be either indicative or imperative, though most English versions regard it as imperative</note> also in me.

verses.name: John 14:2
verses.text: In my Father’s house there are many dwelling places; but if not, I would have told you, because<note placement="foot">A large number of manuscripts, many of them later, lack “because”</note> I am going away to prepare a place for you.

verses.name: John 14:3
verses.text: And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again and receive you to myself, so that where I am, you may be also.

verses.name: John 14:4
verses.text: And you know the way where I am going.”  <div eID="gen26691" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 14:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11253"/><div sID="gen26692" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11253"/>Thomas said to him, “Lord, we do not know where you are going. How are we able to know the way?”

verses.name: John 14:6
verses.text: Jesus said to him, “I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.

verses.name: John 14:7
verses.text: If you had known me, you would have known<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “If you have known me, you will know”</note> my Father also. From now on<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “And from now on”</note> you know him and have seen him.”  <div eID="gen26692" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 14:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11254"/><div sID="gen26693" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11254"/>Philip said to him, “Lord, show us the Father, and it is enough for us.”

verses.name: John 14:9
verses.text: Jesus said to him, “Am I with you so long a time and you have not known me, Philip? The one who has seen me has seen the Father! How can you say, ‘Show us the Father?’

verses.name: John 14:10
verses.text: Do you not believe that I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> in the Father and the Father is in me? The words that I say to you I do not speak from myself, but the Father residing in me does his works.

verses.name: John 14:11
verses.text: Believe me that I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> in the Father and the Father <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in me; but if not, believe because of the works themselves.

verses.name: John 14:12
verses.text: Truly, truly I say to you, the one who believes in me, the works that I am doing he will do also, and he will do greater <transChange type="added">works</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> than these because I am going to the Father.

verses.name: John 14:13
verses.text: And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞whatever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “anything which”</note> you ask in my name, I will do this, in order that the Father may be glorified in the Son.

verses.name: John 14:14
verses.text: If you ask me anything in my name, I will do <transChange type="added">it</transChange>.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>  <div eID="gen26693" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 14:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11255"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Promises the Holy Spirit</title> <div sID="gen26694" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11255"/>“If you love me, you will keep my commandments.

verses.name: John 14:16
verses.text: And I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Advocate, in order that he may be with you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for the age”</note>—

verses.name: John 14:17
verses.text: the Spirit of truth, whom the world is not able to receive, because it does not see him or know <transChange type="added">him</transChange>.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> You know him, because he resides with you and will be in you.  <div eID="gen26694" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 14:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11256"/><div sID="gen26695" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11256"/>“I will not leave you <transChange type="added">as</transChange> orphans; I am coming to you.

verses.name: John 14:19
verses.text: Yet a little <transChange type="added">time</transChange> and the world will see me no longer, but you will see me; because I live, you also will live.

verses.name: John 14:20
verses.text: On that day you will know that I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> in my Father, and you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> in me, and I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> in you.

verses.name: John 14:21
verses.text: The one who has my commandments and keeps them—that one is the one who loves me. And the one who loves me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him and will reveal myself to him.”  <div eID="gen26695" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 14:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11257"/><div sID="gen26696" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11257"/>Judas (not Iscariot) said to him, “Lord, why<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “and why”</note> is it that you are going to reveal yourself to us and not to the world?”

verses.name: John 14:23
verses.text: Jesus answered and said to him, “If anyone loves me he will keep my word, and my Father will love him, and we will come to him and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞will take up residence with him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “will make abode with him”</note>

verses.name: John 14:24
verses.text: The one who does not love me does not keep my words, and the word that you hear is not mine, but the Father’s who sent me.

verses.name: John 14:25
verses.text: These <transChange type="added">things</transChange> I have spoken to you <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the participle (“residing”) which is understood as temporal</note> residing with you.

verses.name: John 14:26
verses.text: But the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name—that one will teach you all <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, and will remind you of everything that I said to you.  <div eID="gen26696" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 14:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11258"/><div sID="gen26697" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11258"/>“Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you—not as the world gives, I give to you. Do not let your hearts be troubled, and do not let <transChange type="added">them</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> be afraid.

verses.name: John 14:28
verses.text: You have heard that I said to you, ‘I am going away, and I am coming to you.’ If you loved me, you would have rejoiced that I am going to the Father, because the Father is greater than I <transChange type="added">am</transChange>.

verses.name: John 14:29
verses.text: And now I have told you before <transChange type="added">it</transChange> happens, so that when it happens, you may believe.

verses.name: John 14:30
verses.text: I will no longer speak much with you, for the ruler of the world is coming, and he has <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞no power⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “nothing”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞over⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in”</note> me.

verses.name: John 14:31
verses.text: But so that the world may know that I love the Father, and just as the Father has commanded me, thus I am doing. Get up, let us go from here!  <chapter eID="John.14"/>

verses.name: John 15:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11259"/><title type="x-s">The Vine and the Branches</title> <div sID="gen26698" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11259"/>“I am the true vine, and my Father is the vinedresser.

verses.name: John 15:2
verses.text: Every branch that does not bear fruit in me, he removes it, and every <transChange type="added">branch</transChange> that bears fruit, he prunes it in order that it may bear more fruit.

verses.name: John 15:3
verses.text: You are already clean because of the word that I have spoken to you.

verses.name: John 15:4
verses.text: Remain in me, and I in you. Just as the branch is not able to bear fruit from itself unless it remains in the vine, so neither <transChange type="added">can</transChange> you, unless you remain in me.  <div eID="gen26698" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 15:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11260"/><div sID="gen26699" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11260"/>“I am the vine; you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the branches. The one who remains in me and I in him—this one bears much fruit, for apart from me you are not able to do anything.

verses.name: John 15:6
verses.text: If anyone does not remain in me, he is thrown out as a branch, and dries up, and they gather them and throw <transChange type="added">them</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> into the fire, and they are burned.

verses.name: John 15:7
verses.text: If you remain in me and my words remain in you, ask whatever you want and it will be done for you.

verses.name: John 15:8
verses.text: My Father is glorified by this: that you bear much fruit, and prove to be my disciples.  <div eID="gen26699" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 15:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11261"/><div sID="gen26700" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11261"/>“Just as the Father has loved me, I also have loved you. Remain in my love.

verses.name: John 15:10
verses.text: If you keep my commandments, you will remain in my love, just as I have kept my Father’s commandments and remain in his love.

verses.name: John 15:11
verses.text: I have spoken these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> to you in order that my joy may be in you, and your joy may be made complete.

verses.name: John 15:12
verses.text: This is my commandment: that you love one another just as I have loved you.

verses.name: John 15:13
verses.text: No one has greater love than this: that someone lay down his life for his friends.

verses.name: John 15:14
verses.text: You are my friends if you do what I command you.

verses.name: John 15:15
verses.text: No longer do I call you slaves, because the slave does not know what his master is doing. But I have called you friends, because everything that I have heard from my Father I have revealed to you.

verses.name: John 15:16
verses.text: You did not choose me, but I chose you and appointed you that you should go and bear fruit, and your fruit should remain, in order that whatever you ask the Father in my name he will give you.

verses.name: John 15:17
verses.text: These <transChange type="added">things</transChange> I command you: that you love one another.  <div eID="gen26700" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 15:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11262"/><title type="x-s">The World’s Hatred for the Disciples</title> <div sID="gen26701" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11262"/>If the world hates you, you know that it has hated me before <transChange type="added">it hated</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the verb “hated” is an understood repetition of the verb earlier in this verse</note> you.

verses.name: John 15:19
verses.text: If you were of the world, the world would love its own. But because you are not of the world, but I chose you out of the world, for this <transChange type="added">reason</transChange> the world hates you.

verses.name: John 15:20
verses.text: Remember the word that I said to you: ‘A slave is not greater than his master.’ If they persecuted me, they will also persecute you. If they kept my word, they will keep yours also.

verses.name: John 15:21
verses.text: But they will do all these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> to you on account of my name, because they do not know the one who sent me.

verses.name: John 15:22
verses.text: If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not have sin. But now they do not have a valid excuse for their sin.

verses.name: John 15:23
verses.text: The one who hates me hates my Father also.

verses.name: John 15:24
verses.text: If I had not done among them the works that no one else did, they would not have sin. But now they have both seen and hated both me and my Father.

verses.name: John 15:25
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">this happened</transChange><note placement="foot">*The phrase “this happened” is not in the Greek text but is implied</note> so that the word that is written in their law would be fulfilled, ‘They hated me without a reason.’  <div eID="gen26701" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 15:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11263"/><div sID="gen26702" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11263"/>“When the Advocate comes, whom I will send to you from the Father—the Spirit of truth, who proceeds from the Father—that one will testify about me.

verses.name: John 15:27
verses.text: And you also will testify, because you have been with me from the beginning.  <chapter eID="John.15"/>

verses.name: John 16:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11264"/><title type="x-s">Persecution of Disciples Predicted</title> <div sID="gen26703" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11264"/>“I have said these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> to you so that you will not fall away.

verses.name: John 16:2
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞They will expel you from the synagogue⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “they will make you expelled from the synagogue”</note> but an hour is coming that everyone who kills you will think they are offering service to God.

verses.name: John 16:3
verses.text: And they will do these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> because they do not know the Father or me.

verses.name: John 16:4
verses.text: But I have said these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> to you so that when their hour comes, you may remember that I told you about them. <div eID="gen26703" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">Jesus’ Departure and the Coming of the Holy Spirit</title> <div sID="gen26704" type="x-p"/> “And I have not said these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> to you from the beginning, because I was with you.

verses.name: John 16:5
verses.text: But now I am going away to the one who sent me, and none of you is asking me, ‘Where are you going?’

verses.name: John 16:6
verses.text: But because I have said these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> to you, sorrow has filled your hearts.

verses.name: John 16:7
verses.text: But I tell you the truth, it is better for you that I go away. For if I do not go away, the Advocate will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you.

verses.name: John 16:8
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“comes”) which is understood as temporal</note> comes, he will convict the world concerning sin and concerning righteousness and concerning judgment:

verses.name: John 16:9
verses.text: concerning sin, because they do not believe in me,

verses.name: John 16:10
verses.text: and concerning righteousness, because I am going away to the Father and you will see me no more,

verses.name: John 16:11
verses.text: and concerning judgment, because the ruler of this world has been condemned.  <div eID="gen26704" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 16:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11265"/><div sID="gen26705" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11265"/>I still have many <transChange type="added">things</transChange> to say to you, but you are not able to bear <transChange type="added">them</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> now.

verses.name: John 16:13
verses.text: But when he—the Spirit of truth—comes, he will guide you into all the truth. For he will not speak from himself, but whatever he hears he will speak, and he will proclaim to you the things to come.

verses.name: John 16:14
verses.text: He will glorify me, because he will take from what <transChange type="added">is</transChange> mine and will proclaim <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to you.

verses.name: John 16:15
verses.text: Everything that the Father has is mine. For this <transChange type="added">reason</transChange> I said that he takes from what <transChange type="added">is</transChange> mine and will proclaim <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to you.  <div eID="gen26705" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 16:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11266"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Predicts His Return to the Disciples</title> <div sID="gen26706" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11266"/>“A little <transChange type="added">while</transChange> and you will see me no more, and again a little <transChange type="added">while</transChange> and you will see me.

verses.name: John 16:17
verses.text: So some of his disciples said to one another, “What is this that he is saying to us, ‘A little <transChange type="added">while</transChange> and you will not see me, and again a little <transChange type="added">while</transChange> and you will see me,’ and ‘Because I am going away to the Father’?”

verses.name: John 16:18
verses.text: So they kept on saying, “What is this that he is saying, ‘A little <transChange type="added">while</transChange>’? We do not understand what he is speaking about!”  <div eID="gen26706" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 16:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11267"/><div sID="gen26707" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11267"/>Jesus knew that they were wanting to ask him, and he said to them, “Are you deliberating with one another about this—that I said, ‘A little <transChange type="added">while</transChange>, and you will not see me, and again a little <transChange type="added">while</transChange> and you will see me’?

verses.name: John 16:20
verses.text: Truly, truly I say to you, that you will weep and lament, but the world will rejoice; you will become sorrowful, but your sorrow will change to joy.

verses.name: John 16:21
verses.text: A woman, when she gives birth, experiences pain because her hour has come. But when <transChange type="added">her</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> child is born, she no longer remembers the affliction, on account of the joy that a human being has been born into the world.

verses.name: John 16:22
verses.text: So you also are experiencing sorrow now, but I will see you again, and your hearts will rejoice, and no one will take away your joy from you.

verses.name: John 16:23
verses.text: And on that day you will ask me nothing. Truly, truly I say to you, whatever you ask the Father in my name, he will give you.

verses.name: John 16:24
verses.text: Until now you have asked nothing in my name. Ask and you will receive, so that your joy may be complete.  <div eID="gen26707" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 16:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11268"/><title type="x-s">Jesus’ Victory Over the World</title> <div sID="gen26708" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11268"/>“I have said these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> to you in figurative sayings. An hour is coming when I will speak to you in figurative sayings no longer, but I will tell you plainly about the Father.

verses.name: John 16:26
verses.text: On that day you will ask in my name, and I do not say to you that I will ask the Father on your behalf.

verses.name: John 16:27
verses.text: For the Father himself loves you, because you have loved me and have believed that I came from God.

verses.name: John 16:28
verses.text: I have gone out from the Father and have come into the world; again, I am leaving the world and am going to the Father.”  <div eID="gen26708" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 16:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11269"/><div sID="gen26709" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11269"/>His disciples said, “Behold, now you are speaking <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞plainly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “with plainness”</note> and are telling us<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> no figurative saying!

verses.name: John 16:30
verses.text: Now we know that you know everything and do not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞need for⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “have need that”</note> anyone to ask you questions.<note placement="foot">*Here the word “questions” is not in the Greek text but is implied</note> By this we believe that you have come from God.”  <div eID="gen26709" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 16:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11270"/><div sID="gen26710" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11270"/>Jesus replied to them, “Now do you believe?

verses.name: John 16:32
verses.text: Behold, an hour is coming—and has come—that you will be scattered each one to his own <transChange type="added">home</transChange>,<note placement="foot">Or “to his own things”; or “to his own people” (i.e., family); the Greek text is somewhat ambiguous here</note> and you will leave me alone. And I am not alone, because the Father is with me.

verses.name: John 16:33
verses.text: I have said these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> to you so that in me you may have peace. In the world you have affliction, but have courage! I have conquered the world.”  <chapter eID="John.16"/>

verses.name: John 17:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11271"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Prays to be Glorified</title> <div sID="gen26711" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11271"/>Jesus said these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, and lifting up his eyes to heaven he said, “Father, the hour has come! Glorify your Son, in order that your Son may glorify you—

verses.name: John 17:2
verses.text: just as you have given him authority over all flesh, in order that he would give eternal life to them—everyone whom you have given him.

verses.name: John 17:3
verses.text: Now this is eternal life: that they know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom you have sent.

verses.name: John 17:4
verses.text: I have glorified you on earth <transChange type="added">by</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“completing”) which is understood as means</note> completing the work that you have given me <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to do⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “that I may do it”</note>

verses.name: John 17:5
verses.text: And now, Father, you glorify me <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞at your side⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by the side of yourself”</note> with the glory that I had <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞at your side⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by the side of you”</note> before the world existed.  <div eID="gen26711" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 17:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11272"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Prays for His Disciples</title> <div sID="gen26712" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11272"/>“I have revealed your name to the men whom you gave me out of the world. They were yours, and you have given them to me, and they have kept your word.

verses.name: John 17:7
verses.text: Now they understand that all <transChange type="added">the things</transChange> that<note placement="foot">Literally “whatever”</note> you have given me are from you,

verses.name: John 17:8
verses.text: because the words that you gave to me I have given to them, and they received <transChange type="added">them</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and know truly that I have come from you, and they have believed that you have sent me.

verses.name: John 17:9
verses.text: I am asking on behalf of them. I am not asking on behalf of the world, but on behalf of those whom you have given me, because they are yours,

verses.name: John 17:10
verses.text: and all my <transChange type="added">things</transChange> are yours, and your <transChange type="added">things</transChange> <transChange type="added">are</transChange> mine, and I have been glorified in<note placement="foot">Or “by”; or “through”</note> them.

verses.name: John 17:11
verses.text: And I am no longer in the world, and they are in the world, and I am coming to you. Holy Father, keep them in your name, which you have given to me, so that they may be one, just as we <transChange type="added">are</transChange>.

verses.name: John 17:12
verses.text: When I was with them, I kept them in your name, which you have given to me, and guarded <transChange type="added">them</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and none of them has perished except the son of destruction, in order that the scripture would be fulfilled.

verses.name: John 17:13
verses.text: And now I am coming to you, and I am saying these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> in the world so that they may have my joy completed in themselves.

verses.name: John 17:14
verses.text: I have given them your word, and the world has hated them, because they are not of the world just as I am not of the world.

verses.name: John 17:15
verses.text: I do not ask that you take them out of the world, but that you protect them from the evil one.

verses.name: John 17:16
verses.text: They are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.

verses.name: John 17:17
verses.text: Sanctify them in the truth—your word is truth.

verses.name: John 17:18
verses.text: Just as you sent me into the world, I also have sent them into the world.

verses.name: John 17:19
verses.text: And for them I sanctify myself, so that <transChange type="added">they</transChange> themselves also may be sanctified in the truth.  <div eID="gen26712" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 17:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11273"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Prays for the Unity of Believers</title> <div sID="gen26713" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11273"/>“And I do not ask on behalf of these only, but also on behalf of those who believe in me through their word,

verses.name: John 17:21
verses.text: that they all may be one, just as you, Father, <transChange type="added">are</transChange> in me and I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> in you, that they also may be in us, in order that the world may believe that you sent me.

verses.name: John 17:22
verses.text: And the glory that you have given to me, I have given to them, in order that they may be one, just as we <transChange type="added">are</transChange> one—

verses.name: John 17:23
verses.text: I in them, and you in me, in order that they may be completed in one, so that the world may know that you sent me, and you have loved them just as you have loved me.  <div eID="gen26713" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 17:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11274"/><div sID="gen26714" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11274"/>“Father, <transChange type="added">those</transChange> whom you have given to me—I want that those also may be with me where I am, in order that they may see my glory that you have given me because you loved me before the foundation of the world.

verses.name: John 17:25
verses.text: Righteous Father, although the world does not know you, yet I have known you, and these <transChange type="added">men</transChange> have come to know that you sent me.

verses.name: John 17:26
verses.text: And I made known to them your name, and will make <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> known, in order that the love <transChange type="added">with</transChange> which you loved me may be in them, and I <transChange type="added">may be</transChange> in them.”  <chapter eID="John.17"/>

verses.name: John 18:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11275"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Is Betrayed and Arrested</title> <div sID="gen26715" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11275"/><transChange type="added">When</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had said”) which is understood as temporal</note> Jesus had said these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, he went out with his disciples to the other side of the ravine of the Kidron, where <transChange type="added">there</transChange> was a garden into which he and his disciples entered.

verses.name: John 18:2
verses.text: (Now Judas, the one who betrayed him, also knew about the place, because Jesus often gathered there with his disciples.)

verses.name: John 18:3
verses.text: So Judas, taking the cohort and officers from the chief priests and from the Pharisees, came there with lanterns and torches and weapons.

verses.name: John 18:4
verses.text: Then Jesus, <transChange type="added">because he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“knew”) which is understood as causal</note> knew all the things that were coming upon him, went out and said to them, “Who are you looking for?”

verses.name: John 18:5
verses.text: They replied to him, “Jesus the Nazarene.” He said to them, “I am <transChange type="added">he</transChange>.”<note placement="foot">*Here the predicate nominative is supplied from context in the English translation</note> (Now Judas, the one who betrayed him, was also standing with them.)

verses.name: John 18:6
verses.text: So when he said to them, “I am <transChange type="added">he</transChange>,”<note placement="foot">*Here the predicate nominative is supplied from context in the English translation</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they drew back⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “they went to the back”</note> and fell to the ground.

verses.name: John 18:7
verses.text: Then he asked them again, “Who are you looking for?” And they said, “Jesus the Nazarene.”

verses.name: John 18:8
verses.text: Jesus replied, “I said to you that I am <transChange type="added">he</transChange>!<note placement="foot">*Here the predicate nominative is supplied from context in the English translation</note> So if you are looking for me, let these <transChange type="added">men</transChange> go,”

verses.name: John 18:9
verses.text: in order that the word that he had spoken would be fulfilled: “Those whom you have given to me—I have not lost anyone of them.”<note placement="foot">A paraphrase of the statement in <reference osisRef="John.17.12">John 17:12</reference></note>  <div eID="gen26715" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 18:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11276"/><div sID="gen26716" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11276"/>Then Simon Peter, who had a sword, drew it and struck the slave of the high priest and cut off his right ear. (Now the name of the slave was Malchus.)

verses.name: John 18:11
verses.text: So Jesus said to Peter, “Put the sword into <transChange type="added">its</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> sheath! The cup that the Father has given me—shall I not drink it?”  <div eID="gen26716" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 18:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11277"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Taken to Annas</title> <div sID="gen26717" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11277"/>Then the cohort and the military tribune and the officers of the Jews seized Jesus and tied him up,

verses.name: John 18:13
verses.text: and brought <transChange type="added">him</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to Annas first, for he was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, who was high priest that year.

verses.name: John 18:14
verses.text: (Now it was Caiaphas who had advised the Jews that it was better <transChange type="added">that</transChange> one man die for the people.)  <div eID="gen26717" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 18:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11278"/><title type="x-s">Peter Denies Jesus the First Time</title> <div sID="gen26718" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11278"/>So Simon Peter and another disciple followed Jesus. (Now that disciple was known to the high priest, and entered with Jesus into the courtyard of the high priest.)

verses.name: John 18:16
verses.text: But Peter was standing by the door outside. So the other disciple <transChange type="added">who was</transChange> known to the high priest went out and spoke to the doorkeeper and brought Peter in.

verses.name: John 18:17
verses.text: Then the female slave <transChange type="added">who was</transChange> the doorkeeper said to Peter, “You are not also <transChange type="added">one</transChange> of the disciples of this man, <transChange type="added">are you</transChange>?”<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here, indicated in the translation by the phrase “are you”</note> He said, “I am not!”

verses.name: John 18:18
verses.text: (Now the slaves and the officers were standing there, having made a charcoal fire because it was cold, and they were warming themselves. And Peter was also standing there with them and warming himself.)  <div eID="gen26718" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 18:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11279"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Before Annas</title> <div sID="gen26719" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11279"/>So the high priest questioned Jesus about his disciples and about his teaching.

verses.name: John 18:20
verses.text: Jesus replied to him, “I have spoken openly to the world. I always taught in the synagogue and in the temple <transChange type="added">courts</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> where all the Jews assemble, and I have said nothing in secret.

verses.name: John 18:21
verses.text: Why are you asking me? Ask those who heard what I have said to them! Behold, these <transChange type="added">people</transChange> know what I said.”

verses.name: John 18:22
verses.text: Now <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“had said”)</note> he had said these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, one of the officers who was standing by gave a slap in the face to Jesus, saying, “Do you reply to the high priest in this way?”

verses.name: John 18:23
verses.text: Jesus replied to him, “If I have spoken wrongly, testify about what <transChange type="added">is</transChange> wrong! But if <transChange type="added">I have spoken</transChange><note placement="foot">*The phrase “I have spoken” is an implied repetition of the earlier phrase in this verse</note> correctly, why do you strike me?”

verses.name: John 18:24
verses.text: Then Annas sent him, tied up, to Caiaphas the high priest.  <div eID="gen26719" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 18:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11280"/><title type="x-s">Peter Denies Jesus the Second and Third Times</title> <div sID="gen26720" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11280"/>Now Simon Peter was standing there and warming himself. So they said to him, “You are not also <transChange type="added">one</transChange> of his disciples, <transChange type="added">are you</transChange>?”<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here, indicated in the translation by the phrase “are you”</note> He denied it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and said, “I am not!”

verses.name: John 18:26
verses.text: One of the slaves of the high priest, who was related to the one whose ear Peter had cut off, said, “Did I not see you in the garden with him?”

verses.name: John 18:27
verses.text: So Peter denied <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> again, and immediately a rooster crowed.  <div eID="gen26720" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 18:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11281"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Brought Before Pilate</title> <div sID="gen26721" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11281"/>Then they brought Jesus from Caiaphas to the governor’s residence. Now it was early, and they did not enter into the governor’s residence so that they would not be defiled, but could eat the Passover.

verses.name: John 18:29
verses.text: So Pilate came outside to them and said, “What accusation do you bring against this man?”

verses.name: John 18:30
verses.text: They answered and said to him, “If this man were not doing evil, we would not have handed him over to you!”

verses.name: John 18:31
verses.text: So Pilate said to them, “You take him and judge him according to your law!” The Jews said to him, “It is not permitted for us to kill anyone,”

verses.name: John 18:32
verses.text: in order that the word of Jesus would be fulfilled that he had spoken, indicating by what sort of death he was going to die.  <div eID="gen26721" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 18:33
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11282"/><title type="x-s">Pilate Questions Jesus</title> <div sID="gen26722" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11282"/>Then Pilate entered again into the governor’s residence and summoned Jesus and said to him, “Are you the king of the Jews?”

verses.name: John 18:34
verses.text: Jesus replied, “Do you say this from yourself, or have others said <transChange type="added">this</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to you about me?”

verses.name: John 18:35
verses.text: Pilate replied, “I am not a Jew, <transChange type="added">am I</transChange>?<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here, indicated in the translation by the phrase “am I”</note> Your people and the chief priests handed you over to me! What have you done?”

verses.name: John 18:36
verses.text: Jesus replied, “My kingdom is not of this world. If my kingdom were of this world, my servants would be fighting so that I would not be handed over to the Jews. But now my kingdom is not from here.”

verses.name: John 18:37
verses.text: Then Pilate said to him, “So then you are a king!” Jesus replied, “You say that I am a king. For this <transChange type="added">reason</transChange> I was born, and for this reason I have come into the world: in order that I can testify to the truth. Everyone who is of the truth hears my voice.”

verses.name: John 18:38
verses.text: Pilate said to him, “What is truth?” <div eID="gen26722" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen26723" type="x-p"/> And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had said”) which is understood as temporal</note> had said this, he went out again to the Jews and said to them, “I find no basis for an accusation against him.

verses.name: John 18:39
verses.text: But it is your custom that I release for you one <transChange type="added">prisoner</transChange><note placement="foot">*The word “prisoner” is not in the Greek text, but is implied</note> at the Passover. So do you want me<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to release for you the king of the Jews?”

verses.name: John 18:40
verses.text: Then they shouted again, saying, “Not this man, but Barabbas!” (Now Barabbas was a revolutionary.)<note placement="foot">Or perhaps “robber”</note>  <chapter eID="John.18"/>

verses.name: John 19:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11283"/><title type="x-s">Pilate Attempts to Release Jesus</title> <div sID="gen26724" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11283"/>So then Pilate took Jesus and had him flogged.<note placement="foot">*This verb has causative force in context; Pilate did not personally carry out the sentence</note>

verses.name: John 19:2
verses.text: And the soldiers wove a crown of thorns and placed <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> on his head, and put a purple robe on him,

verses.name: John 19:3
verses.text: and were coming up to him and saying, “Hail, king of the Jews!” and were giving him slaps in the face.  <div eID="gen26724" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 19:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11284"/><div sID="gen26725" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11284"/>And Pilate came outside again and said to them, “Behold, I am bringing him outside to you, so that you will know that I find no basis for an accusation against him.”

verses.name: John 19:5
verses.text: Then Jesus came outside wearing the crown of thorns and the purple robe, and he said to them, “Behold the man!”

verses.name: John 19:6
verses.text: So when they saw him, the chief priests and the officers shouted, saying, “Crucify! Crucify!” Pilate said to them, “You take him and crucify <transChange type="added">him</transChange>!<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> For I do not find a basis for an accusation against him.”

verses.name: John 19:7
verses.text: The Jews replied to him, “We have a law, and according to the law he ought to die, because he made himself out to be the Son of God!”  <div eID="gen26725" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 19:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11285"/><div sID="gen26726" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11285"/>So when Pilate heard this statement, he was even more afraid,

verses.name: John 19:9
verses.text: and he entered into the governor’s residence again and said to Jesus, “Where are you from?” But Jesus did not give him an answer.

verses.name: John 19:10
verses.text: So Pilate said to him, “Will you not speak to me? Do you not know that I have authority to release you, and I have authority to crucify you?”

verses.name: John 19:11
verses.text: Jesus replied to him, “You would not have any authority over me unless it was given to you from above. For this <transChange type="added">reason</transChange> the one who handed me over to you has greater sin.”  <div eID="gen26726" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 19:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11286"/><div sID="gen26727" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11286"/>From this <transChange type="added">point on</transChange> Pilate was seeking to release him, but the Jews shouted, saying, “If you release this man, you are not a friend of Caesar! Everyone who makes himself out to be a king opposes Caesar!”

verses.name: John 19:13
verses.text: So Pilate, <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard these words, brought Jesus outside and sat down on the judgment seat, in the place called The Stone Pavement (but <hi type="italic">Gabbatha</hi> in Aramaic).

verses.name: John 19:14
verses.text: (Now it was the day of preparation of the Passover; it was about the sixth hour.) And he said to the Jews, “Behold your king!”  <div eID="gen26727" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 19:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11287"/><div sID="gen26728" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11287"/>Then those shouted, “Away <transChange type="added">with him</transChange>! Away <transChange type="added">with him</transChange>! Crucify him!” Pilate said to them, “Shall I crucify your king?” The chief priests replied, “We do not have a king except Caesar!”

verses.name: John 19:16
verses.text: So then he handed him over to them in order that he could be crucified. <div eID="gen26728" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">Jesus Is Crucified</title> <div sID="gen26729" type="x-p"/> So they took Jesus,

verses.name: John 19:17
verses.text: and carrying for himself the cross, he went out to the <transChange type="added">place</transChange> called The Place of a Skull (which is called <hi type="italic">Golgotha</hi> in Aramaic),

verses.name: John 19:18
verses.text: where they crucified him, and with him two others, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞one on each side⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “from here and from here”</note> and Jesus in the middle.

verses.name: John 19:19
verses.text: And Pilate also wrote a notice and placed <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> on the cross, and it was written: “Jesus the Nazarene, the king of the Jews.”

verses.name: John 19:20
verses.text: So many of the Jews read this notice, because the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city. And it was written in Aramaic, in Latin, <transChange type="added">and</transChange> in Greek.

verses.name: John 19:21
verses.text: Then the chief priests of the Jews said to Pilate, “Do not write ‘The king of the Jews,’ but, ‘He said, I am king of the Jews.’ ”

verses.name: John 19:22
verses.text: Pilate replied, “What I have written, I have written.”  <div eID="gen26729" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 19:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11288"/><div sID="gen26730" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11288"/>Then the soldiers, when they had crucified Jesus, took his clothing and made four shares—for each soldier a share—and the tunic. (Now the tunic was seamless, woven from the top <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in a single piece⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.)<note placement="foot">Literally “through the whole”</note>

verses.name: John 19:24
verses.text: So they said to one another, “Let us not tear it apart, but cast lots for it, <transChange type="added">to see</transChange> whose it will be,” so that the scripture would be fulfilled that says, <div eID="gen26730" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen26731"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26732"/>“They divided my garments among themselves,<l eID="gen26732" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26733"/>and for my clothing they cast lots.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.22.18">Ps 22:18</reference></note><l eID="gen26733" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen26731"/> <div sID="gen26734" type="x-p"/> Thus the soldiers did these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>.  <div eID="gen26734" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 19:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11289"/><div sID="gen26735" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11289"/>Now his mother and the sister of his mother, Mary the <transChange type="added">wife</transChange> of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene were standing near the cross of Jesus.

verses.name: John 19:26
verses.text: So Jesus, seeing <transChange type="added">his</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> mother and the disciple whom he loved standing there, said to his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> mother, “Woman, behold your son!”

verses.name: John 19:27
verses.text: Then he said to the disciple, “Behold your mother!” And from that hour the disciple took her into his own <transChange type="added">home</transChange>.  <div eID="gen26735" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 19:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11290"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Dies on the Cross</title> <div sID="gen26736" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11290"/>After this, Jesus, knowing that now at last everything was completed, in order that the scripture would be fulfilled, said, “I am thirsty.”

verses.name: John 19:29
verses.text: A jar full of sour wine was standing there, so <transChange type="added">they</transChange> put a sponge full of the sour wine on a <transChange type="added">branch of</transChange> hyssop <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“put”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> brought it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to his mouth.

verses.name: John 19:30
verses.text: Then when he had received the sour wine, Jesus said, “It is completed,”<note placement="foot">Or (traditionally) “it is finished”</note> and bowing his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> head, he gave up his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> spirit.  <div eID="gen26736" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 19:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11291"/><div sID="gen26737" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11291"/>Then the Jews, because it was the day of preparation, so that the bodies would not remain on the cross on the Sabbath (for that Sabbath was an important day), asked Pilate that their legs could be broken and they could be taken away.

verses.name: John 19:32
verses.text: So the soldiers came and broke the legs of the first and of the other who had been crucified with him.

verses.name: John 19:33
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“came”) which is understood as temporal</note> came to Jesus, after they saw he was already dead, they did not break his legs.

verses.name: John 19:34
verses.text: But one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and blood and water came out immediately.

verses.name: John 19:35
verses.text: And the one who has seen <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> has testified, and his testimony is true, and that person knows that he is telling the truth, so that you also may believe.

verses.name: John 19:36
verses.text: For these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> happened in order that the scripture would be fulfilled: “Not a bone of his will be broken.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Exod.12.46">Exod 12:46</reference>, <reference osisRef="Num.9.12">Num 9:12</reference>, and <reference osisRef="Ps.34.20">Ps 34:20</reference></note>

verses.name: John 19:37
verses.text: And again another scripture says, “They will look on <transChange type="added">the one</transChange> whom they have pierced.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Zech.12.10">Zech 12:10</reference></note>  <div eID="gen26737" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 19:38
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11292"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Is Buried</title> <div sID="gen26738" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11292"/>And after these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, Joseph <transChange type="added">who was</transChange> from Arimathea, who was a disciple of Jesus (but a secret one for fear of the Jews), asked Pilate that he might take away the body of Jesus. And Pilate allowed <transChange type="added">it</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> so he came and took away his body.

verses.name: John 19:39
verses.text: And Nicodemus—the one who had come to him formerly at night—also came, bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes <transChange type="added">weighing</transChange> about a hundred pounds.<note placement="foot">The Greek term refers to a Roman pound, 327.45 grams (approximately 12 ounces)</note>

verses.name: John 19:40
verses.text: So they took the body of Jesus and wrapped it in <transChange type="added">strips of</transChange> linen cloth with the fragrant spices, as is the Jews’ custom to prepare for burial.

verses.name: John 19:41
verses.text: Now <transChange type="added">there</transChange> was a garden at the place where he was crucified, and in the garden a new tomb in which no one was yet buried.

verses.name: John 19:42
verses.text: So there, on account of the day of preparation of the Jews, because the tomb was close by, they buried Jesus.  <chapter eID="John.19"/>

verses.name: John 20:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11293"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Is Raised</title> <div sID="gen26739" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11293"/>Now on the first <transChange type="added">day</transChange> of the week, Mary Magdalene came to the tomb early, <transChange type="added">while it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was”)</note> was still dark, and saw the stone had been taken away from the tomb.

verses.name: John 20:2
verses.text: So she ran and came to Simon Peter and to the other disciple whom Jesus loved and said to them, “They have taken away the Lord from the tomb and we do not know where they have put him!”

verses.name: John 20:3
verses.text: Then Peter and the other disciple went out and were going to the tomb.

verses.name: John 20:4
verses.text: And the two were running together, and the other disciple ran ahead, faster than Peter, and came to the tomb first.

verses.name: John 20:5
verses.text: And bending over to look, he saw the <transChange type="added">strips of</transChange> linen cloth lying there, though he did not go in.

verses.name: John 20:6
verses.text: Then Simon Peter also came following him, and he went into the tomb and saw the <transChange type="added">strips of</transChange> linen cloth lying there,

verses.name: John 20:7
verses.text: and the facecloth that was on his head—not lying with the <transChange type="added">strips of</transChange> linen cloth, but folded up separately in one place.

verses.name: John 20:8
verses.text: So then the other disciple who had come to the tomb first also went in, and he saw and believed.

verses.name: John 20:9
verses.text: (For they did not yet know the scripture that it was necessary for him to rise from the dead.)  <div eID="gen26739" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 20:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11294"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Appears to Mary Magdalene</title> <div sID="gen26740" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11294"/>Then the disciples went away again to their <transChange type="added">own homes</transChange>.<note placement="foot">*The phrase “own homes” is not in the Greek text but is implied</note>

verses.name: John 20:11
verses.text: But Mary stood outside at the tomb, weeping. Then, while she was weeping, she bent over to look into the tomb,

verses.name: John 20:12
verses.text: and she saw two angels in white, seated one at the head and one at the feet where the body of Jesus had been lying.

verses.name: John 20:13
verses.text: And they said to her, “Woman, why are you weeping?” She said to them, “They have taken away my Lord, and I do not know where they have put him!”

verses.name: John 20:14
verses.text: <transChange type="added">When she</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had said”) which is understood as temporal</note> had said these things, she turned <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞around⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the back”</note> and saw Jesus standing there, and she did not know that it was Jesus.  <div eID="gen26740" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 20:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11295"/><div sID="gen26741" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11295"/>Jesus said to her, “Woman, why are you weeping? Who are you looking for?” She thought that it was the gardener, <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“thought”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to him, “Sir, if you have carried him away, tell me where you have put him, and I will take him.”

verses.name: John 20:16
verses.text: Jesus said to her, “Mary.” She turned around <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“turned around”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to him in Aramaic, “<hi type="italic">Rabboni</hi>” (which means “Teacher”).

verses.name: John 20:17
verses.text: Jesus said to her, “Do not touch me, for I have not yet ascended to the Father. But go to my brothers and tell them, ‘I am ascending to my Father and your Father, and my God and your God.’ ”

verses.name: John 20:18
verses.text: Mary Magdalene came <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the participle (“announced”) has been translated as a finite verb in keeping with English style</note> announced to the disciples, “I have seen the Lord,” and he had said these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> to her.  <div eID="gen26741" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 20:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11296"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Appears to the Disciples</title> <div sID="gen26742" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11296"/>Now <transChange type="added">when it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was”)</note> was evening on that day—the first <transChange type="added">day</transChange> of the week—and the doors had been shut where the disciples were because of fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood in their midst and said to them, “Peace to you.”

verses.name: John 20:20
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had said”) which is understood as temporal</note> had said this, he showed his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> hands and his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> side to them. Then the disciples rejoiced when they<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw the Lord.

verses.name: John 20:21
verses.text: So Jesus said to them again, “Peace to you. As the Father has sent me, I also send you.”

verses.name: John 20:22
