verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had said”) which is understood as temporal</note> had said this, he breathed on them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and said to them, “Receive the Holy Spirit.

verses.name: John 20:23
verses.text: If you forgive the sins of any, they are forgiven them. If you retain <transChange type="added">the sins</transChange><note placement="foot">*An understood repetition of the phrase from earlier in the verse</note> of any, they are retained.”  <div eID="gen26742" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 20:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11297"/><title type="x-s">Thomas Doubts But Later Believes</title> <div sID="gen26743" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11297"/>Now Thomas, one of the twelve, who was called Didymus,<note placement="foot">The Greek term means “the Twin”</note> was not with them when Jesus came.

verses.name: John 20:25
verses.text: So the other disciples said to him, “We have seen the Lord!” But he said to them, “Unless I see in his hands the mark of the nails, and put my finger into the mark of the nails, and put my hand into his side, I will never believe!”  <div eID="gen26743" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 20:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11298"/><div sID="gen26744" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11298"/>And after eight days his disciples were again inside, and Thomas with them. <transChange type="added">Although</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had been shut”) which is understood as concessive</note> the doors had been shut, Jesus came and stood in their midst and said, “Peace to you.”

verses.name: John 20:27
verses.text: Then he said to Thomas, “Place your finger here and see my hands, and place your hand and put <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> into my side. And do not be unbelieving, but believing!”

verses.name: John 20:28
verses.text: Thomas answered and said to him, “My Lord and my God!”

verses.name: John 20:29
verses.text: Jesus said to him, “Because you have seen me, have you believed? Blessed <transChange type="added">are</transChange> those who have not seen and have believed.”  <div eID="gen26744" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 20:30
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11299"/><title type="x-s">Why This Book Was Written</title> <div sID="gen26745" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11299"/>Now Jesus also performed many other signs in the presence of the disciples<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “his disciples”</note> which are not recorded in this book,

verses.name: John 20:31
verses.text: but these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> are recorded in order that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that <transChange type="added">by</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“believing”) which is understood as means</note> believing you may have life in his name.  <chapter eID="John.20"/>

verses.name: John 21:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11300"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Appears to the Disciples in Galilee</title> <div sID="gen26746" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11300"/>After these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> Jesus revealed himself again to the disciples by the Sea of Tiberias. Now he revealed <transChange type="added">himself</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> in this way:

verses.name: John 21:2
verses.text: Simon Peter and Thomas (who was called Didymus)<note placement="foot">The Greek term means “the Twin”</note> and Nathanael from Cana in Galilee and the <transChange type="added">sons</transChange> of Zebedee and two others of his disciples were together.

verses.name: John 21:3
verses.text: Simon Peter said to them, “I am going fishing!” They said to him, “We also are coming with you.” They went out and got into the boat, and during that night they caught nothing.  <div eID="gen26746" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 21:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11301"/><div sID="gen26747" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11301"/>Now <transChange type="added">when it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was”)</note> was already early morning, Jesus stood on the beach. However, the disciples did not know that it was Jesus.

verses.name: John 21:5
verses.text: So Jesus said to them, “Children, you do not have any fish to eat, <transChange type="added">do you</transChange>?<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here, indicated in the translation by the phrase “do you”</note> They answered him, “No.”

verses.name: John 21:6
verses.text: And he said to them, “Throw the net on the right side of the boat, and you will find <transChange type="added">some</transChange>.”<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> So they threw it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and were no longer able to haul it in from the large number of the fish.  <div eID="gen26747" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 21:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11302"/><div sID="gen26748" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11302"/>Then that disciple whom Jesus loved said to Peter, “It is the Lord!” So Simon Peter, <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard that it was the Lord, tied around himself his outer garment (for he was naked)<note placement="foot">I.e., “he was naked underneath the outer garment,” which he tucked into his belt; alternatively, this could mean “for he was stripped for work”</note> and threw himself into the sea.

verses.name: John 21:8
verses.text: But the other disciples came in the boat, dragging the net of fish, because they were not far from the land, but about two hundred cubits<note placement="foot">Approximately 100 yards or 92 meters, based on a cubit of 18 inches.</note> away.  <div eID="gen26748" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 21:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11303"/><div sID="gen26749" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11303"/>So when they got out on the land, they saw a charcoal fire laid <transChange type="added">there</transChange>, and a fish lying on <transChange type="added">it</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and bread.

verses.name: John 21:10
verses.text: Jesus said to them, “Bring some of the fish that you have just now caught.”

verses.name: John 21:11
verses.text: So Simon Peter got into <transChange type="added">the boat</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and hauled the net to the land, full of large fish—one hundred fifty-three—and although there<note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“were”) which is understood as concessive</note> were so many, the net was not torn.

verses.name: John 21:12
verses.text: Jesus said to them, “Come, eat breakfast!” But none of the disciples dared to ask him, “Who are you?” <transChange type="added">because they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“knew”) which is understood as causal</note> knew that it was the Lord.

verses.name: John 21:13
verses.text: Jesus came and took the bread and gave <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to them, and the fish likewise.

verses.name: John 21:14
verses.text: This <transChange type="added">was</transChange> now <transChange type="added">the</transChange> third <transChange type="added">time</transChange> Jesus was revealed to the disciples <transChange type="added">after he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had been raised”) which is understood as temporal</note> had been raised from the dead.  <div eID="gen26749" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 21:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11304"/><title type="x-s">Peter Is Restored Three Times</title> <div sID="gen26750" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11304"/>Now when they had eaten breakfast, Jesus said to Simon Peter, “Simon <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of John, do you love me more than these?” He said to him, “Yes, Lord, you know that I love you.” He said to him, “Feed my lambs!”

verses.name: John 21:16
verses.text: He said to him again a second time, “Simon <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of John, do you love me?” He said to him, “Yes, Lord, you know that I love you.” He said to him, “Shepherd my sheep!”

verses.name: John 21:17
verses.text: He said to him a third <transChange type="added">time</transChange>, “Simon <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of John, do you love me?” Peter was distressed because he said to him a third <transChange type="added">time</transChange>, “Do you love me?” and he said to him, “Lord, you know everything! You know that I love you!” Jesus said to him, “Feed my sheep!

verses.name: John 21:18
verses.text: Truly, truly I say to you, when you were young, you tied <transChange type="added">your clothes</transChange><note placement="foot">*The words “your clothes” are not in the Greek text but are implied</note> around yourself and walked wherever you wanted. But when you grow old, you will stretch out your hands, and someone else will tie you up and carry you where you do not want to go.<note placement="foot">*The words “to go” are not in the Greek text but are implied</note>

verses.name: John 21:19
verses.text: (Now he said this to indicate by what kind of death he would glorify God.) And <transChange type="added">after he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had said”) which is understood as temporal</note> had said this, he said to him, “Follow me!”  <div eID="gen26750" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 21:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11305"/><title type="x-s">Peter and the Other Disciple Jesus Loved</title> <div sID="gen26751" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11305"/>Peter turned <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“turned”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> saw the disciple whom Jesus loved following them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> (who also leaned back on his chest at the dinner and said, “Lord, who is the one betraying you?”)

verses.name: John 21:21
verses.text: So <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw this one, Peter said to Jesus, “Lord, but what about this one?”

verses.name: John 21:22
verses.text: Jesus said to him, “If I want him to remain until I come, what <transChange type="added">is that</transChange><note placement="foot">*The words “is that” are not in the Greek text but are supplied in keeping with English style</note> to you? You follow me!”

verses.name: John 21:23
verses.text: So this saying went out to the brothers that that disciple would not die. But Jesus did not say to him that he would not die, but “If I want him to remain until I come, what <transChange type="added">is that</transChange><note placement="foot">*The words “is that” are not in the Greek text but are supplied in keeping with English style</note> to you?”  <div eID="gen26751" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: John 21:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11306"/><title type="x-s">A Concluding Word of Testimony</title> <div sID="gen26752" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11306"/>This is the disciple who is testifying about these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, and who has written down these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>. And we know that his testimony is true.

verses.name: John 21:25
verses.text: Now there are also many other <transChange type="added">things</transChange> that Jesus did, which—if they were written down one after the other—I suppose not even the world itself could contain the books that would be written.  <chapter eID="John.21"/> <div eID="gen26752" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen26539" osisID="John" type="book"/>

verses.name: Acts 1:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11307"/><title type="x-s">The Preface</title> <div sID="gen26754" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11307"/>I produced the former account, O Theophilus, about all <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞that⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “of what”</note> Jesus began to do and to teach,

verses.name: Acts 1:2
verses.text: until the day he was taken up, <transChange type="added">after he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had given orders”) which is understood as temporal</note> had given orders through the Holy Spirit to the apostles whom he had chosen,

verses.name: Acts 1:3
verses.text: to whom he also presented himself alive after he suffered, with many convincing proofs, appearing to them over a period of forty days and speaking the things about the kingdom of God.

verses.name: Acts 1:4
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">while he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was with”) which is understood as temporal</note> was with<note placement="foot">Or “was assembling with,” or “was sharing a meal with”</note> them,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> he commanded them, “Do not depart from Jerusalem, but wait for what was promised by the Father, which you heard about from me.

verses.name: Acts 1:5
verses.text: For John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞not many days from now⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “not many days after these”</note>  <div eID="gen26754" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 1:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11308"/><title type="x-s">The Ascension</title> <div sID="gen26755" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11308"/>So <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had come together”) which is understood as temporal</note> they had come together, they began asking<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began asking”)</note> him, saying, “Lord, <transChange type="added">is it</transChange> at this time you are restoring the kingdom to Israel?”

verses.name: Acts 1:7
verses.text: But he said to them, “It is not for you to know <transChange type="added">the</transChange> times or seasons that the Father has set by his own authority.

verses.name: Acts 1:8
verses.text: But you will receive power <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“has come”)</note> the Holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the farthest part of the earth.”

verses.name: Acts 1:9
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had said”) which is understood as temporal</note> had said these things, while<note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“were watching”)</note> they were watching, he was taken up, and a cloud received him from their sight.

verses.name: Acts 1:10
verses.text: And as they were staring into the sky <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was departing”)</note> he was departing, behold, two men in white clothing stood by them

verses.name: Acts 1:11
verses.text: who also said, “Men <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞of Galilee⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “Galileans”</note> why do you stand there looking<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “gazing”</note> into the sky? This Jesus who was taken up from you into heaven like this will come back in the same way you saw him departing into heaven!”  <div eID="gen26755" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 1:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11309"/><title type="x-s">Matthias Chosen to Replace Judas</title> <div sID="gen26756" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11309"/>Then they returned to Jerusalem from the mountain that is called Olive Grove<note placement="foot">This is a variation of the name “Mount of Olives”</note> which is near Jerusalem, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a Sabbath day’s journey away⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “having a journey of a Sabbath”</note>

verses.name: Acts 1:13
verses.text: And when they had entered, they went up to the upstairs room where they were staying—Peter and John and James and Andrew, Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew, James <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Alphaeus and Simon the Zealot and Judas <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of James.

verses.name: Acts 1:14
verses.text: All these were busily engaged with one mind in prayer, together with the women and Mary the mother of Jesus and with<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts omit “with”</note> his brothers.  <div eID="gen26756" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 1:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11310"/><div sID="gen26757" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11310"/>And in those days Peter stood up in the midst of the brothers (and it was a crowd of persons of about one hundred twenty at the same <transChange type="added">place</transChange>) <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“stood up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said,

verses.name: Acts 1:16
verses.text: “Men <transChange type="added">and</transChange> brothers, it was necessary <transChange type="added">that</transChange> the scripture be fulfilled, which the Holy Spirit proclaimed beforehand through the mouth of David concerning Judas, who became a guide to those who arrested Jesus,

verses.name: Acts 1:17
verses.text: because he was counted among us and received a share in this ministry.”

verses.name: Acts 1:18
verses.text: (Now this man acquired a field for the wages of <transChange type="added">his</transChange> wickedness, and falling headlong, he burst open in the middle and all his intestines spilled out.

verses.name: Acts 1:19
verses.text: And it became known to all who live in Jerusalem, so that that field was called in their own language<note placement="foot">That is, Aramaic</note> “Akeldama,” that is, “Field of Blood.”)

verses.name: Acts 1:20
verses.text: “For it is written in the book of Psalms, <div eID="gen26757" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen26758"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26759"/>‘Let his residence become deserted,<l eID="gen26759" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26760"/>and let there be no one to live in it,’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.69.25">Ps 69:25</reference></note><l eID="gen26760" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen26758"/> <div sID="gen26761" type="x-p"/> and, <div eID="gen26761" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen26762"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26763"/>‘Let another person take his position.’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.109.8">Ps 109:8</reference></note> <l eID="gen26763" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen26762"/>

verses.name: Acts 1:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11311"/><div sID="gen26764" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11311"/>Therefore it is necessary for <transChange type="added">one</transChange> of the men who have accompanied us during all the time <transChange type="added">in</transChange> which the Lord Jesus went in and went out among us,

verses.name: Acts 1:22
verses.text: beginning from the baptism of John until the day <transChange type="added">on</transChange> which he was taken up from us—one of these <transChange type="added">men</transChange> must become a witness of his resurrection together with us.”

verses.name: Acts 1:23
verses.text: And they proposed two <transChange type="added">men</transChange>, Joseph called Barsabbas (who was called Justus) and Matthias.

verses.name: Acts 1:24
verses.text: And they prayed <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“prayed”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “You, Lord, who know the hearts of all, show clearly which one of these two you have chosen

verses.name: Acts 1:25
verses.text: to take the place in this ministry and apostleship from which Judas turned aside to depart to his own place.”

verses.name: Acts 1:26
verses.text: And they cast lots for them, and the lot fell on Matthias, and he was added <transChange type="added">to serve</transChange><note placement="foot">*The words “to serve” are not in the Greek text, but are implied</note> with the eleven apostles.  <chapter eID="Acts.1"/>

verses.name: Acts 2:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11312"/><title type="x-s">Pentecost and the Coming of the Holy Spirit</title> <div sID="gen26765" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11312"/>And when the day of Pentecost had come, they were all together in the same <transChange type="added">place</transChange>.

verses.name: Acts 2:2
verses.text: And suddenly a sound like a violent rushing wind came from heaven and filled the whole house where they were sitting.

verses.name: Acts 2:3
verses.text: And divided<note placement="foot">Or perhaps “distributed”</note> tongues like fire appeared to them and rested on each one of them.

verses.name: Acts 2:4
verses.text: And they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other languages<note placement="foot">Or “tongues”</note> as the Spirit gave them <transChange type="added">ability</transChange> to speak out.  <div eID="gen26765" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 2:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11313"/><div sID="gen26766" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11313"/>Now there were Jews residing in Jerusalem, devout men from every nation under heaven.

verses.name: Acts 2:6
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“happened”)</note> this sound occurred, the crowd gathered and was in confusion, because each one was hearing them speaking in his own language.

verses.name: Acts 2:7
verses.text: And they were astounded and astonished, saying, “Behold, are not all these who are speaking Galileans?

verses.name: Acts 2:8
verses.text: And how do we hear, each one <transChange type="added">of us</transChange>, in <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞our own native language⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?<note placement="foot">Literally “our own language in which we were born”</note>

verses.name: Acts 2:9
verses.text: Parthians and Medes and Elamites and those residing <transChange type="added">in</transChange> Mesopotamia, Judea and Cappadocia, Pontus and Asia,<note placement="foot">A reference to the Roman province of Asia (modern Asia Minor)</note>

verses.name: Acts 2:10
verses.text: Phrygia and Pamphylia, Egypt and the parts of Libya toward Cyrene, and the Romans who were in town,

verses.name: Acts 2:11
verses.text: both Jews and proselytes, Cretans and Arabs—we hear them speaking in our <transChange type="added">own</transChange> languages the great deeds of God!”

verses.name: Acts 2:12
verses.text: And all were amazed and greatly perplexed, saying <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to one another⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “one to the other”</note> “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞What can this mean?⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>”<note placement="foot">Literally “what does this want to be”</note>

verses.name: Acts 2:13
verses.text: But others jeered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“jeered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “They are full of sweet new wine!”  <div eID="gen26766" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 2:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11314"/><title type="x-s">Peter’s Sermon on the Day of Pentecost</title> <div sID="gen26767" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11314"/>But Peter, standing with the eleven, raised his voice and declared to them, “Judean men, and all those who live <transChange type="added">in</transChange> Jerusalem, let this be known to you, and pay attention to my words!

verses.name: Acts 2:15
verses.text: For these <transChange type="added">men</transChange> are not drunk, as you assume, because it is the third hour of the day.

verses.name: Acts 2:16
verses.text: But this is what was spoken through the prophet Joel:  <div eID="gen26767" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 2:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11315"/><lg sID="gen26768"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26769"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11315"/>‘And it will be in the last days,’ God says,<l eID="gen26769" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26770"/>‘I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh,<l eID="gen26770" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen26771"/>and your sons and your daughters will prophesy,<l eID="gen26771" level="3"/> <l level="3" sID="gen26772"/>and your young men will see visions,<l eID="gen26772" level="3"/> <l level="3" sID="gen26773"/>and your old men will dream dreams. <l eID="gen26773" level="3"/>

verses.name: Acts 2:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11316"/><l level="1" sID="gen26774"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11316"/>And even on my male slaves and on my female slaves<l eID="gen26774" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26775"/>I will pour out my Spirit in those days, and they will prophesy. <l eID="gen26775" level="2"/>

verses.name: Acts 2:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11317"/><l level="1" sID="gen26776"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11317"/>And I will cause wonders in the heaven<note placement="foot">Or “sky”</note> above<l eID="gen26776" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26777"/>and signs on the earth below,<l eID="gen26777" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26778"/>blood and fire and vapor of smoke. <l eID="gen26778" level="2"/>

verses.name: Acts 2:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11318"/><l level="1" sID="gen26779"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11318"/>The sun will be changed to darkness<l eID="gen26779" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26780"/>and the moon to blood,<l eID="gen26780" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26781"/>before the great and glorious day of the Lord comes. <l eID="gen26781" level="2"/>

verses.name: Acts 2:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11319"/><l level="1" sID="gen26782"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11319"/>And it will be <transChange type="added">that</transChange> everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord will be saved.’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Joel.2.28-Joel.2.32">Joel 2:28–32</reference></note> <l eID="gen26782" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen26768"/>

verses.name: Acts 2:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11320"/><div sID="gen26783" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11320"/>“Israelite men, listen to these words! Jesus the Nazarene, a man attested to you by God with deeds of power and wonders and signs that God did through him in your midst, just as <transChange type="added">you</transChange> yourselves know—

verses.name: Acts 2:23
verses.text: this man, delivered up by the determined plan and foreknowledge of God, you executed <transChange type="added">by</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“nailing to”) which is understood as means</note> nailing to a cross<note placement="foot">*The words “a cross” are not in the Greek text but are implied by the nature of the verb</note> through the hand of lawless men.

verses.name: Acts 2:24
verses.text: God raised <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “whom”; it is necessary to specify “him” in the translation to avoid confusion with the “lawless men” in the previous verse</note> up, having brought to an end the pains of death, because it was not possible <transChange type="added">for</transChange> him to be held by it.

verses.name: Acts 2:25
verses.text: For David says with reference to him, <div eID="gen26783" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen26784"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26785"/>‘I saw the Lord before me <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞continually⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “through everything”</note><l eID="gen26785" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26786"/>for he is at my right hand so that I will not be shaken. <l eID="gen26786" level="2"/>

verses.name: Acts 2:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11321"/><l level="1" sID="gen26787"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11321"/>For this <transChange type="added">reason</transChange> my heart was glad<l eID="gen26787" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26788"/>and my tongue rejoiced greatly,<l eID="gen26788" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26789"/>furthermore also my flesh will live in hope, <l eID="gen26789" level="2"/>

verses.name: Acts 2:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11322"/><l level="1" sID="gen26790"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11322"/>because you will not abandon my soul in Hades,<l eID="gen26790" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26791"/>nor will you permit your Holy One to experience decay. <l eID="gen26791" level="2"/>

verses.name: Acts 2:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11323"/><l level="1" sID="gen26792"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11323"/>You have made known to me the paths of life;<l eID="gen26792" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26793"/>you will fill me with gladness with your presence.’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.16.8-Ps.16.11">Ps 16:8–11</reference></note> <l eID="gen26793" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen26784"/>

verses.name: Acts 2:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11324"/><div sID="gen26794" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11324"/>“Men <transChange type="added">and</transChange> brothers, it is possible to speak with confidence to you about the patriarch David, that he both died and was buried, and his tomb is with us until this day.

verses.name: Acts 2:30
verses.text: Therefore, <transChange type="added">because he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was”) which is understood as causal</note> was a prophet and knew that God had sworn to him with an oath to seat <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞one of his descendants⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from the fruit of his loins”</note> on his throne,

verses.name: Acts 2:31
verses.text: <transChange type="added">by</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“having foreseen”) which is understood as means</note> having foreseen this,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> he spoke about the resurrection of the Christ,<note placement="foot">Or “Messiah”</note> that neither was he abandoned in Hades nor did his flesh experience decay.

verses.name: Acts 2:32
verses.text: This Jesus God raised up, of which<note placement="foot">Or “of whom,” referring to Jesus</note> we all are witnesses.

verses.name: Acts 2:33
verses.text: Therefore, having been exalted to the right hand of God and having received the promise of the Holy Spirit from the Father, he has poured out this that you see and hear.<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “both see and hear”</note>

verses.name: Acts 2:34
verses.text: For David did not ascend into heaven, but he himself says, <div eID="gen26794" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen26795"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26796"/>‘The Lord said to my Lord,<l eID="gen26796" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26797"/>“Sit at my right hand, <l eID="gen26797" level="1"/>

verses.name: Acts 2:35
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11325"/><l level="1" sID="gen26798"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11325"/>until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.” ’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.110.1">Ps 110:1</reference></note> <l eID="gen26798" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen26795"/>

verses.name: Acts 2:36
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11326"/><div sID="gen26799" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11326"/>Therefore let all the house of Israel know beyond a doubt, that God has made him both Lord and Christ—this Jesus whom you crucified!”  <div eID="gen26799" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 2:37
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11327"/><title type="x-s">The Response to Peter’s Sermon</title> <div sID="gen26800" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11327"/>Now <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard this,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> they were pierced to the heart and said to Peter and the other apostles, “What should we do, men <transChange type="added">and</transChange> brothers?”

verses.name: Acts 2:38
verses.text: And Peter <transChange type="added">said</transChange><note placement="foot">Some manuscripts explicitly add “said”</note> to them, “Repent and be baptized, each one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.

verses.name: Acts 2:39
verses.text: For the promise is for you and for your children, and for all those <transChange type="added">who are</transChange> far away, as many as the Lord our God calls to himself.”

verses.name: Acts 2:40
verses.text: And with many other words he solemnly urged and exhorted them, saying, “Be saved from this crooked generation!”

verses.name: Acts 2:41
verses.text: So those who accepted his message were baptized, and on that day about three thousand souls were added.  <div eID="gen26800" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 2:42
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11328"/><title type="x-s">The Fellowship of the First Believers</title> <div sID="gen26801" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11328"/>And they were devoting themselves to the teaching of the apostles and to fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayers.

verses.name: Acts 2:43
verses.text: And fear came on every soul, and many wonders and signs were being performed by the apostles.

verses.name: Acts 2:44
verses.text: And all who believed were in the same <transChange type="added">place</transChange>, and had everything in common.

verses.name: Acts 2:45
verses.text: And they began selling<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began selling”)</note> their<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> possessions and property, and distributing these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> to all, to the degree that anyone had need.

verses.name: Acts 2:46
verses.text: And every day, devoting themselves <transChange type="added">to meeting</transChange><note placement="foot">*The words “to meeting” are not in the Greek text but are implied</note> with one purpose in the temple courts<note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> and breaking bread from house <transChange type="added">to house</transChange>, they were eating <transChange type="added">their</transChange> food with joy and simplicity of heart,

verses.name: Acts 2:47
verses.text: praising God and having favor with all the people. And the Lord was adding every day to the total <transChange type="added">of</transChange> those who were being saved.  <chapter eID="Acts.2"/>

verses.name: Acts 3:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11329"/><title type="x-s">A Lame Beggar Healed at the Temple</title> <div sID="gen26802" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11329"/>Now Peter and John were going up to the temple at the hour of prayer, the ninth <transChange type="added">hour</transChange>.

verses.name: Acts 3:2
verses.text: And a certain man was being carried who was lame <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from birth⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “from his mother’s womb”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞He⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “who,” but a new sentence was begun here in the translation in keeping with English style</note> was placed every day at the gate of the temple called “Beautiful,” so that he could ask for charitable gifts from those who were going into the temple courts.<note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note>

verses.name: Acts 3:3
verses.text: <transChange type="added">When he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw Peter and John about to go into the temple courts,<note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> he began asking to receive alms.

verses.name: Acts 3:4
verses.text: And Peter looked intently at him, together with John, <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“looked intently”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “Look at us!”

verses.name: Acts 3:5
verses.text: So he fixed his attention on them, expecting to receive something from them.

verses.name: Acts 3:6
verses.text: But Peter said, “Silver and gold <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I do not possess⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “is not to me”</note> but what I have, this I give to you—in the name of Jesus Christ the Nazarene, walk!”<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “get up and walk”</note>

verses.name: Acts 3:7
verses.text: And taking hold of him by the right hand, he raised him up, and immediately his feet and ankles were made strong.

verses.name: Acts 3:8
verses.text: And leaping up, he stood and began walking around<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began walking around”)</note> and entered into the temple courts<note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> with them, walking and leaping and praising God.

verses.name: Acts 3:9
verses.text: And all the people saw him walking and praising God,

verses.name: Acts 3:10
verses.text: And they recognized him, that this one<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “that he himself”</note> was the one who used to sit <transChange type="added">asking</transChange> for alms at the Beautiful Gate of the temple, and they were filled with awe and astonishment at what had happened to him.  <div eID="gen26802" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 3:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11330"/><title type="x-s">Peter’s Sermon in Solomon’s Portico</title> <div sID="gen26803" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11330"/>And <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was holding fast to”)</note> he was holding fast to Peter and John, all the people ran together to them in the portico called Solomon’s, utterly astonished.

verses.name: Acts 3:12
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> Peter replied to the people, “Men <transChange type="added">and</transChange> Israelites, why are you astonished at this? Or why are you staring at us, as <transChange type="added">if</transChange> by our own power or godliness we have made him walk?

verses.name: Acts 3:13
verses.text: The God of Abraham and of Isaac<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “the God of Isaac”</note> and of Jacob,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “the God of Jacob”</note> the God of our fathers, has glorified his servant Jesus, whom you handed over and denied in the presence of Pilate, after<note placement="foot">Or “although”; this genitive absolute construction can be understood as either temporal “after” or concessive “although”</note> he had decided to release him.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Acts 3:14
verses.text: But you denied the Holy and Righteous One and demanded <transChange type="added">that</transChange> a man—a murderer—be granted to you.

verses.name: Acts 3:15
verses.text: And you killed the originator of life, whom God raised from the dead, of which we are witnesses!

verses.name: Acts 3:16
verses.text: And on the basis of faith in his name, his name has made this man strong, whom you see and know, and the faith <transChange type="added">that is</transChange> through him has given him this perfect health in the presence of you all.

verses.name: Acts 3:17
verses.text: And now, brothers, I know that you acted in ignorance, just as your rulers did also.

verses.name: Acts 3:18
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">the things</transChange> which God foretold through the mouth of all the prophets, <transChange type="added">that</transChange> his Christ<note placement="foot">Or “Messiah”</note> would suffer, he has fulfilled in this way.

verses.name: Acts 3:19
verses.text: Therefore repent and turn back, so that your sins may be blotted out,

verses.name: Acts 3:20
verses.text: so that times of refreshing may come from the presence of the Lord, and he may send the Christ<note placement="foot">Or “Messiah”</note> appointed for you—Jesus,

verses.name: Acts 3:21
verses.text: whom heaven must receive until the times of the restoration of all <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, about which God spoke through the mouth of his holy prophets from earliest times.

verses.name: Acts 3:22
verses.text: Moses said, ‘The Lord God<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “The Lord your God”</note> will raise up for you a prophet like me from your brothers. You will listen to him in everything that he says to you.<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Deut.18.15">Deut 18:15</reference></note>

verses.name: Acts 3:23
verses.text: And it will be <transChange type="added">that</transChange> every soul who does not listen to that prophet will be destroyed utterly from the people.’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Deut.18.19">Deut 18:19 </reference>and <reference osisRef="Lev.23.29">Lev 23:29</reference></note>

verses.name: Acts 3:24
verses.text: And indeed, all the prophets from Samuel and all those who followed <transChange type="added">him</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> have spoken <transChange type="added">about</transChange> and proclaimed these days.

verses.name: Acts 3:25
verses.text: You are the sons of the prophets and of the covenant that God ordained with your fathers, saying to Abraham, ‘And in your offspring all the nations of the earth will be blessed.’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Gen.22.18">Gen 22:18</reference></note>

verses.name: Acts 3:26
verses.text: God, <transChange type="added">after he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had raised up”) which is understood as temporal</note> had raised up his servant, sent him to you first, to bless you by turning each <transChange type="added">of you</transChange> back from your wickedness!”  <chapter eID="Acts.3"/>

verses.name: Acts 4:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11331"/><title type="x-s">Peter and John Arrested</title> <div sID="gen26804" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11331"/>And <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“were speaking”)</note> they were speaking to the people, the priests and the captain of the temple and the Sadducees approached them,

verses.name: Acts 4:2
verses.text: greatly annoyed because they were teaching the people and proclaiming in Jesus the resurrection from the dead.

verses.name: Acts 4:3
verses.text: And they laid hands on them and put <transChange type="added">them</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> in custody until the next day, because it was already evening.

verses.name: Acts 4:4
verses.text: But many of those who listened to the message believed, and the number of the men was approximately five thousand.  <div eID="gen26804" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 4:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11332"/><title type="x-s">Peter and John on Trial Before the Sanhedrin</title> <div sID="gen26805" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11332"/>And it happened that on the next day, their rulers and elders and scribes came together in Jerusalem,

verses.name: Acts 4:6
verses.text: and Annas the high priest, and Caiaphas and John and Alexander, and all those who were from the high priest’s family.

verses.name: Acts 4:7
verses.text: And they made them stand in <transChange type="added">their</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> midst and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“stand”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> began to ask,<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to ask”)</note> “By what power or by what name did you do this?”

verses.name: Acts 4:8
verses.text: Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to them, “Rulers of the people and elders,

verses.name: Acts 4:9
verses.text: if we are being examined today concerning a good deed <transChange type="added">done to</transChange> a sick man—by what <transChange type="added">means</transChange><note placement="foot">Or “through whom”</note> this man was healed—

verses.name: Acts 4:10
verses.text: let it be known to all of you and to all the people of Israel that by the name of Jesus Christ the Nazarene, whom you crucified, whom God raised from the dead—by him this man stands before you healthy!

verses.name: Acts 4:11
verses.text: This one<note placement="foot">“This one” refers to Jesus</note> is the stone that was rejected by you, the builders, that has become <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the cornerstone⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “the head of the corner”; this verse is an allusion to <reference osisRef="Ps.118.22">Ps 118:22</reference></note>

verses.name: Acts 4:12
verses.text: And there is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven that is given among people by which we must be saved.”  <div eID="gen26805" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 4:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11333"/><div sID="gen26806" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11333"/>Now <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw the boldness of Peter and John, and understood that they were uneducated and untrained men, they were astonished, and recognized them, that they had been with Jesus.

verses.name: Acts 4:14
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">because they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as causal</note> saw the man who had been healed standing there with them, they had nothing to say in return.

verses.name: Acts 4:15
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">after they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had ordered”) which is understood as temporal</note> had ordered them to go outside the Sanhedrin,<note placement="foot">Or “council”</note> they began to confer<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to confer”)</note> with one another,

verses.name: Acts 4:16
verses.text: saying, “What should we do with these men? For that a remarkable sign has taken place through them <transChange type="added">is</transChange> evident to all those who live <transChange type="added">in</transChange> Jerusalem, and we are not able to deny <transChange type="added">it</transChange>!<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Acts 4:17
verses.text: But in order that it may not spread much <transChange type="added">further</transChange> among the people, let us warn them to speak no more in this name <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to anyone at all⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “to no man”</note>

verses.name: Acts 4:18
verses.text: And they called them <transChange type="added">back</transChange> <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“called”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> commanded them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> not to speak or to teach at all in the name of Jesus.

verses.name: Acts 4:19
verses.text: But Peter and John answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to them, “Whether it is right in the sight of God to listen to you rather than God, you decide!

verses.name: Acts 4:20
verses.text: For we are not able to refrain from speaking about <transChange type="added">the things</transChange> that we have seen and heard.”

verses.name: Acts 4:21
verses.text: So <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“threatening … further”) which is understood as temporal</note> threatening them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> further, they released them, finding no way to punish them on account of the people, because they were all praising God for what had happened.

verses.name: Acts 4:22
verses.text: For the man on whom this sign of healing had been performed was more <transChange type="added">than</transChange> forty years <transChange type="added">old</transChange>.  <div eID="gen26806" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 4:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11334"/><title type="x-s">The Believers Pray for Continued Bold Witness</title> <div sID="gen26807" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11334"/>And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“were released”) which is understood as temporal</note> were released, they went to their own <transChange type="added">people</transChange> and reported all that the chief priests and the elders had said to them.

verses.name: Acts 4:24
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> they lifted <transChange type="added">their</transChange> voices with one mind to God and said, “Master, you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the one who made the heaven and the earth and the sea and all the things in them,

verses.name: Acts 4:25
verses.text: the one who said by the Holy Spirit through the mouth of our father David, your servant, <div eID="gen26807" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen26808"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26809"/>‘Why do the nations<note placement="foot">Or “Gentiles”; the same Greek word can be translated “nations” or “Gentiles” depending on the context</note> rage,<l eID="gen26809" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26810"/>and the peoples conspire in vain? <l eID="gen26810" level="2"/>

verses.name: Acts 4:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11335"/><l level="1" sID="gen26811"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11335"/>The kings of the earth stood opposed,<l eID="gen26811" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26812"/>and the rulers assembled together at the same <transChange type="added">place</transChange>,<l eID="gen26812" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26813"/>against the Lord and against his Christ.’<note placement="foot">Or “Messiah”; this is a quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.2.1-Ps.2.2">Ps 2:1–2</reference></note> <l eID="gen26813" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen26808"/>

verses.name: Acts 4:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11336"/><div sID="gen26814" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11336"/>For in truth both Herod and Pontius Pilate, together with the Gentiles and the peoples of Israel, assembled together in this city against your holy servant Jesus whom you anointed,

verses.name: Acts 4:28
verses.text: to do all that your hand and plan<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “and your plan”</note> had predestined to take place.

verses.name: Acts 4:29
verses.text: And now, Lord, concern yourself with their threats and grant your slaves to speak your message with all boldness,

verses.name: Acts 4:30
verses.text: <transChange type="added">as</transChange> you extend your hand to heal and signs and wonders are performed through the name of your holy servant Jesus.”

verses.name: Acts 4:31
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“had prayed”)</note> they had prayed, the place in which they were gathered was shaken, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to speak”)</note> the word<note placement="foot">Or “message”</note> of God with boldness.  <div eID="gen26814" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 4:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11337"/><title type="x-s">The Believers Share All Things in Common</title> <div sID="gen26815" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11337"/>Now the group of those who believed were one heart and soul, and no one said anything of what belonged to him was his own, but all <transChange type="added">things</transChange> were theirs in common.

verses.name: Acts 4:33
verses.text: And with great power the apostles were giving testimony <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the resurrection of the Lord Jesus, and great grace was on them all.

verses.name: Acts 4:34
verses.text: For there was not even anyone needy among them, because all those who were owners of plots of land or houses were selling <transChange type="added">them</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“were selling”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> bringing the proceeds of the things that were sold

verses.name: Acts 4:35
verses.text: and placing <transChange type="added">them</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> at the feet of the apostles. And it was being distributed to each as anyone had need.

verses.name: Acts 4:36
verses.text: So Joseph, who was called Barnabas by the apostles (which is translated “son of encouragement”), a Levite of Cyprus by nationality,

verses.name: Acts 4:37
verses.text: sold a field<note placement="foot">Or “a farm”</note> that belonged to him and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“sold”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> brought the money and placed it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> at the feet of the apostles.  <chapter eID="Acts.4"/>

verses.name: Acts 5:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11338"/><title type="x-s">Ananias and Sapphira Lie to the Holy Spirit</title> <div sID="gen26816" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11338"/>Now a certain man <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞named⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by name”</note> Ananias, together with his wife Sapphira, sold a piece of property,

verses.name: Acts 5:2
verses.text: and he kept back for himself <transChange type="added">some</transChange> of the proceeds, and <transChange type="added">his</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> wife was aware of it.<note placement="foot">*Here the participle “was aware of” in this genitive absolute construction has been translated as a finite verb in keeping with English style</note> And he brought a certain part and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“brought”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> placed it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> at the feet of the apostles.

verses.name: Acts 5:3
verses.text: But Peter said, “Ananias, for what <transChange type="added">reason</transChange> has Satan filled your heart, <transChange type="added">that</transChange> you lied to the Holy Spirit and kept back for yourself <transChange type="added">some</transChange> of the proceeds of the piece of land?

verses.name: Acts 5:4
verses.text: <transChange type="added">When it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“remained”) which is understood as temporal</note> remained to you, did it not remain yours? And when it<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was sold”) which is understood as temporal</note> was sold, was it at your disposal? How <transChange type="added">is it</transChange> that you have contrived this deed in your heart? You have not lied to people, but to God!”  <div eID="gen26816" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 5:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11339"/><div sID="gen26817" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11339"/>And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> Ananias heard these words, he fell down and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“fell down”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> died. And great fear came on all those who heard about it.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Acts 5:6
verses.text: So the young men stood up, wrapped him up, and carried <transChange type="added">him</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> out and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“carried … out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> buried him.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Acts 5:7
verses.text: And it happened that <transChange type="added">there was</transChange> an interval of about three hours, and his wife came in, not knowing what had happened.

verses.name: Acts 5:8
verses.text: And Peter said to her, “Tell me whether you <transChange type="added">both</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “both” reflects the second person plural verb, which refers to both Ananias and Sapphira</note> were paid this much <transChange type="added">for</transChange> the piece of land.” And she said, “Yes, this much.”

verses.name: Acts 5:9
verses.text: So Peter <transChange type="added">said</transChange> to her, “How <transChange type="added">is it</transChange> that it was agreed by you <transChange type="added">two</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “two” is supplied in the translation to indicate that the pronoun (“you”) is plural in the Greek text</note> to test the Spirit of the Lord? Behold, the feet of those who buried your husband <transChange type="added">are</transChange> at the door, and they will carry you out!”

verses.name: Acts 5:10
verses.text: And immediately she fell down at his feet and died. So <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“came in”) which is understood as temporal</note> the young men came in, they found her dead, and carried her<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> out and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“carried … out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> buried her<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> with her husband.

verses.name: Acts 5:11
verses.text: And great fear came on the whole church and on all who heard about these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>.  <div eID="gen26817" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 5:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11340"/><title type="x-s">Many Signs and Wonders Are Performed by the Apostles</title> <div sID="gen26818" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11340"/>Now many signs and wonders were being performed among the people through the hands of the apostles. And they were all together<note placement="foot">Or perhaps “by common consent”</note> in Solomon’s Portico.

verses.name: Acts 5:13
verses.text: And none of the rest dared to join them, but the people spoke highly of them.

verses.name: Acts 5:14
verses.text: And even more believers in the Lord<note placement="foot">Or “even more believers were being added to the Lord”</note> were being added, large numbers of both men and women,

verses.name: Acts 5:15
verses.text: so that they even carried out the sick into the streets and put <transChange type="added">them</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> on cots and mats<note placement="foot">Or “mattresses”</note> so that when<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“came by”)</note> Peter came by, at least his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> shadow would fall on some of them.

verses.name: Acts 5:16
verses.text: And the people of the towns around Jerusalem also came together, bringing the sick and those tormented by unclean spirits, who were all being healed.  <div eID="gen26818" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 5:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11341"/><title type="x-s">The Apostles Arrested and Imprisoned</title> <div sID="gen26819" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11341"/>Now the high priest rose up and all those <transChange type="added">who were</transChange> with him (that is, the party of the Sadducees), <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“rose up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> they were filled with jealousy.

verses.name: Acts 5:18
verses.text: And they laid hands on the apostles and put them in the public prison.

verses.name: Acts 5:19
verses.text: But during the night an angel of the Lord opened the doors of the prison and led them <transChange type="added">out</transChange> <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the two previous participles (“opened” and “led”) have been translated as finite verbs</note> said,

verses.name: Acts 5:20
verses.text: “Go and stand in the temple <transChange type="added">courts</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“stand”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> proclaim to the people all the words of this life.”

verses.name: Acts 5:21
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard this,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> they entered at daybreak into the temple courts<note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> and began teaching.<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began teaching”)</note> <div eID="gen26819" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen26820" type="x-p"/> Now <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“arrived”) which is understood as temporal</note> the high priest and those with him arrived, they summoned the Sanhedrin—even the whole council of elders of the sons of Israel—and sent to the prison to have them brought.

verses.name: Acts 5:22
verses.text: But the officers who came<note placement="foot">Or “when they came”</note> did not find them in the prison, and they returned and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“returned”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> reported,

verses.name: Acts 5:23
verses.text: saying, “We found the prison locked with all security and the guards standing at the doors, but <transChange type="added">when we</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“opened”) which is understood as temporal</note> opened them,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> we found no one inside!”

verses.name: Acts 5:24
verses.text: Now when both the captain of the temple and the chief priests heard these words, they were greatly perplexed concerning them, <transChange type="added">as to</transChange> what this might be.

verses.name: Acts 5:25
verses.text: But someone came <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> reported to them, “Behold, the men whom you put in prison are standing in the temple courts<note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> and teaching the people!”

verses.name: Acts 5:26
verses.text: Then the captain went with the officers <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> brought them, not with force (for they were afraid of the people, lest they be stoned by them).<note placement="foot">*The words “by them” are not in the Greek text but are implied</note>  <div eID="gen26820" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 5:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11342"/><title type="x-s">The Apostles on Trial Before the Sanhedrin</title> <div sID="gen26821" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11342"/>And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had brought”) which is understood as temporal</note> had brought them, they made them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> stand in the Sanhedrin,<note placement="foot">Or “council”</note> and the high priest put a question to them,

verses.name: Acts 5:28
verses.text: saying, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞We strictly commanded⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “we commanded with a commandment”</note> you<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “Did we not strictly command you”</note> not to teach in this name? And behold, you have filled Jerusalem with your teaching! And you are intending to bring upon us the blood of this man!”

verses.name: Acts 5:29
verses.text: But Peter and the apostles answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “It is necessary to obey God rather than men!

verses.name: Acts 5:30
verses.text: The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom you killed <transChange type="added">by</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“hanging”) which is understood as means</note> hanging him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> on a tree.

verses.name: Acts 5:31
verses.text: This one God has exalted to his right hand <transChange type="added">as</transChange> Leader and Savior to grant repentance to Israel and forgiveness of sins.

verses.name: Acts 5:32
verses.text: And we are witnesses of these things, and <transChange type="added">so is</transChange><note placement="foot">*The words “so is” are not in the Greek text but are implied</note> the Holy Spirit whom God has given to those who obey him.”

verses.name: Acts 5:33
verses.text: Now <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> they heard this,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> they were infuriated, and were wanting to execute them.

verses.name: Acts 5:34
verses.text: But a certain man stood up in the Sanhedrin,<note placement="foot">Or “council”</note> a Pharisee <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞named⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by name”</note> Gamaliel, a teacher of the law respected by all the people, and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“stood up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> gave orders to put the men outside for a short time.

verses.name: Acts 5:35
verses.text: And he said to them, “Men <transChange type="added">and</transChange> Israelites, take care for yourselves what you are about to do to these men!

verses.name: Acts 5:36
verses.text: For before these days, Theudas rose up saying he was somebody. A number of men, about four hundred, joined <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “to whom”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞He⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “who”</note> was executed, and all who followed him were dispersed and came to nothing.

verses.name: Acts 5:37
verses.text: After this man, Judas the Galilean rose up in the days of the census and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞caused people to follow him in revolt⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “caused people to revolt after him”</note> And that one perished, and all who followed him were scattered.

verses.name: Acts 5:38
verses.text: And now I tell you, keep away from these men, and leave them alone, because if this plan or this matter is from people, it will be overthrown.<note placement="foot">Or “it will fail”</note>

verses.name: Acts 5:39
verses.text: But if it is from God, you will not be able to overthrow them, lest you even be found fighting against God.” So they were persuaded by him.

verses.name: Acts 5:40
verses.text: And they summoned the apostles, beat <transChange type="added">them</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> commanded them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> not to speak in the name of Jesus, and released them.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Acts 5:41
verses.text: So they went out from the presence of the Sanhedrin<note placement="foot">Or “council”</note> rejoicing, because they had been considered worthy to be dishonored for the sake of the name.

verses.name: Acts 5:42
verses.text: Every day, both in the temple <transChange type="added">courts</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> and from house to house, they did not stop teaching and proclaiming the good news that the Christ<note placement="foot">Or “Messiah”</note> <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Jesus.  <chapter eID="Acts.5"/>

verses.name: Acts 6:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11343"/><title type="x-s">The First Seven Deacons Appointed</title> <div sID="gen26822" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11343"/>Now in these days, <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“were increasing”)</note> the disciples were increasing in number,<note placement="foot">*The words “in number” are not in the Greek text but are implied</note> a complaint arose by the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Greek-speaking Jews⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Hellenists”</note> against the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Hebraic Jews⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “Hebrews”</note> because<note placement="foot">Or “that”</note> their widows were being overlooked in the daily distribution of food.<note placement="foot">*The words “of food” are not in the Greek text but are implied</note>

verses.name: Acts 6:2
verses.text: So the twelve summoned the community of disciples <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“summoned”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “It is not desirable <transChange type="added">that</transChange> we neglect the word of God to serve tables.

verses.name: Acts 6:3
verses.text: So, brothers, select from among you seven men <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞of good reputation⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “well spoken of”</note> full of the Spirit and wisdom, whom we will put in charge of this need.

verses.name: Acts 6:4
verses.text: But we will devote ourselves to prayer and to the ministry of the word.”

verses.name: Acts 6:5
verses.text: And the statement pleased the whole group, and they chose Stephen (a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit), and Philip, and Prochorus, and Nicanor, and Timon, and Parmenas, and Nicolaus (a convert from Antioch),

verses.name: Acts 6:6
