verses.text: whom they stood before the apostles. And they prayed <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“prayed”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> placed their<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> hands on them.  <div eID="gen26822" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 6:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11344"/><div sID="gen26823" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11344"/>And the word of God kept spreading, and the number of disciples in Jerusalem was increasing greatly, and a large number of priests began obeying<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began obeying”)</note> the faith.  <div eID="gen26823" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 6:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11345"/><title type="x-s">Stephen Arrested</title> <div sID="gen26824" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11345"/>Now Stephen, full of grace and power, was performing great wonders and signs among the people.

verses.name: Acts 6:9
verses.text: But some of those from the Synagogue of the Freedmen (<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as it was called⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>),<note placement="foot">Literally “called”</note> both Cyrenians and Alexandrians, and those from Cilicia and Asia,<note placement="foot">A reference to the Roman province of Asia (modern Asia Minor)</note> stood up and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the participle (“disputed”) has been translated as a finite verb in keeping with English style</note> disputed with Stephen.

verses.name: Acts 6:10
verses.text: And they were not able to resist the wisdom and the Spirit with which he was speaking.

verses.name: Acts 6:11
verses.text: Then they secretly instigated men who said, “We have heard him speaking blasphemous words against Moses and God!”

verses.name: Acts 6:12
verses.text: And they incited the people and the elders and the scribes, and they came up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> seized him and brought him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to the Sanhedrin.<note placement="foot">Or “council”</note>

verses.name: Acts 6:13
verses.text: And they put forward false witnesses who said, “This man does not stop speaking words against the holy place<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “this holy place”</note> and the law!

verses.name: Acts 6:14
verses.text: For we have heard him saying that this Nazarene Jesus will destroy this place and will change the customs that Moses handed down to us.”

verses.name: Acts 6:15
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">as they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“looked intently”) which is understood as temporal</note> looked intently at him, all those who were sitting in the Sanhedrin<note placement="foot">Or “council”</note> saw his face <transChange type="added">was</transChange> like the face of an angel.  <chapter eID="Acts.6"/>

verses.name: Acts 7:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11346"/><title type="x-s">Stephen’s Defense</title> <div sID="gen26825" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11346"/>And the high priest said, “Is it so concerning these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>?”

verses.name: Acts 7:2
verses.text: So he said, “Men—brothers and fathers—listen: The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham <transChange type="added">while he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was”) which is understood as temporal</note> was in Mesopotamia, before he settled in Haran,

verses.name: Acts 7:3
verses.text: and said to him, ‘Go out from your land and from your relatives and come to the land that I will show you.’

verses.name: Acts 7:4
verses.text: Then he went out from the land of the Chaldeans <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> settled in Haran. And from there, after his father died, he caused him to move to this land in which you now live.

verses.name: Acts 7:5
verses.text: And he did not give him an inheritance in it—not even a footstep<note placement="foot">Literally “a step of a foot”</note>—and he promised to give it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to him for his possession, and to his descendants after him, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞although he did not have⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “not being to him”</note><note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied in the translation as a component of the participle (“was”) which is understood as concessive</note> a child.

verses.name: Acts 7:6
verses.text: But God spoke like this: ‘His descendants will be foreigners in a foreign land, and they will enslave them and mistreat <transChange type="added">them</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> four hundred years,

verses.name: Acts 7:7
verses.text: and the nation <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞that⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to which”</note> they will serve as slaves, I will judge,’ God said, ‘and after these things they will come out<note placement="foot">Verses <reference osisRef="Acts.7.6-Acts.7.7">6–7</reference> are a quotation from <reference osisRef="Gen.15.13-Gen.15.14">Gen 15:13–14</reference></note> and will worship me in this place.’<note placement="foot">The final phrase is an allusion to <reference osisRef="Exod.3.12">Exod 3:12</reference></note>

verses.name: Acts 7:8
verses.text: And he gave him the covenant of circumcision, and so he became the father of Isaac and circumcised him on the eighth day, and Isaac <transChange type="added">did so with</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the words “did so with” are not in the Greek text but are implied; in view of the “covenant of circumcision” mentioned earlier in the verse, it is probable that circumcision and not just fatherhood is involved</note> Jacob, and Jacob did so with<note placement="foot">*Here the words “did so with” are not in the Greek text but are implied; see the note on the same phrase earlier in this verse</note> the twelve patriarchs.

verses.name: Acts 7:9
verses.text: And the patriarchs, <transChange type="added">because they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“were jealous of”) which is understood as causal</note> were jealous of Joseph, sold him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> into Egypt. And God was with him,

verses.name: Acts 7:10
verses.text: and rescued him from all his afflictions and granted him favor and wisdom in the sight of Pharaoh king of Egypt. And he appointed him ruler over Egypt and all<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “over all”</note> his household.

verses.name: Acts 7:11
verses.text: And a famine came over all Egypt and Canaan and great affliction, and our fathers could not find food.

verses.name: Acts 7:12
verses.text: So <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> Jacob heard <transChange type="added">there</transChange> was grain in Egypt, he sent out our fathers first.

verses.name: Acts 7:13
verses.text: And on the second <transChange type="added">visit</transChange><note placement="foot">*The word “visit” is not in the Greek text but is implied</note> Joseph was made known to his brothers, and the family of Joseph became known to Pharaoh.

verses.name: Acts 7:14
verses.text: So Joseph sent <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“sent”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> summoned his father Jacob and all his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> relatives, seventy-five persons in <transChange type="added">all</transChange>.

verses.name: Acts 7:15
verses.text: And Jacob went down to Egypt and died, he and our fathers.

verses.name: Acts 7:16
verses.text: And they were brought back to Shechem and buried in the tomb that Abraham had bought for a sum of silver from the sons of Hamor in Shechem.  <div eID="gen26825" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 7:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11347"/><div sID="gen26826" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11347"/>“But as the time of the promise that God had made to Abraham was drawing near, the people increased and multiplied in Egypt

verses.name: Acts 7:18
verses.text: until another king arose over Egypt who did not know Joseph.

verses.name: Acts 7:19
verses.text: This man deceitfully took advantage of our<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> people and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“deceitfully took advantage of”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> mistreated our ancestors, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞causing them to abandon their infants⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “making their infants be abandoned”</note> so that they would not be kept alive.

verses.name: Acts 7:20
verses.text: At this time Moses was born, and he was beautiful to God. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞He⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “who”</note> was brought up for three months in his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> father’s house,

verses.name: Acts 7:21
verses.text: and <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was abandoned”)</note> he was abandoned, the daughter of Pharaoh took him up and brought him up <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as her own son⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “for a son to herself”</note>

verses.name: Acts 7:22
verses.text: And Moses was educated in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and was powerful in his words and deeds.  <div eID="gen26826" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 7:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11348"/><div sID="gen26827" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11348"/>“But when <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he was forty years old⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “a period of time of forty years was fulfilled for him”</note> it entered in his heart to visit his brothers, the sons of Israel.

verses.name: Acts 7:24
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw one of them being unjustly harmed, he defended him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞avenged⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “produced vengeance for”</note> the one who had been oppressed by<note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“striking down”) which is understood as means</note> striking down the Egyptian.

verses.name: Acts 7:25
verses.text: And he thought his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> brothers would understand that God was granting deliverance to them by his hand, but they did not understand.

verses.name: Acts 7:26
verses.text: And on the following day, he made an appearance to them <transChange type="added">while they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the participle (“were fighting”) which is understood as temporal</note> were fighting and was attempting to reconcile<note placement="foot">*Here the imperfect verb has been translated as conative (“was attempting to reconcile”)</note> them in peace, saying, ‘Men <transChange type="added">and</transChange> brothers, why are you doing wrong to one another?’

verses.name: Acts 7:27
verses.text: But the one who was doing wrong to <transChange type="added">his</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> neighbor pushed him aside, saying, ‘Who appointed you a ruler and a judge over us?

verses.name: Acts 7:28
verses.text: You do not want to do away with me <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the same way⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in the manner in which”</note> you did away with the Egyptian yesterday, do you?’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Exod.2.14">Exod 2:14; </reference>the negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here, indicated by “do you”</note>

verses.name: Acts 7:29
verses.text: And at this statement, Moses fled and became a foreigner in the land of Midian, where he became the father of two sons.  <div eID="gen26827" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 7:30
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11349"/><div sID="gen26828" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11349"/>“And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“had been completed”)</note> forty years had been completed, an angel appeared to him in the desert of Mount Sinai in the flame of a burning bush.

verses.name: Acts 7:31
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> Moses saw it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> he was astonished at the sight, and when<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“approached”)</note> he approached to look at it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> the voice of the Lord came:

verses.name: Acts 7:32
verses.text: ‘I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham and of Isaac and of Jacob!’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Exod.3.6">Exod 3:6</reference></note> So Moses began trembling and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“began”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> did not dare to look at it.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Acts 7:33
verses.text: And the Lord said to him, ‘Untie the sandals from your feet, for the place on which you are standing is holy ground.

verses.name: Acts 7:34
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I have certainly seen⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “seeing I have seen”</note> the mistreatment of my people who are in Egypt and have heard their groaning, and I have come down to deliver them. And now come, I will send you to Egypt.’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Exod.3.5">Exod 3:5</reference>, <reference osisRef="Exod.3.7-Exod.3.8">7–8</reference>, <reference osisRef="Exod.3.10">10</reference></note>

verses.name: Acts 7:35
verses.text: This Moses whom they had repudiated, saying, ‘Who appointed you a ruler and a judge?’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Exod.2.14">Exod 2:14 </reference>(see v. <reference osisRef="Acts.7.27">27</reference> above)</note>—this man God sent as both ruler and redeemer with <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the help⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “hand”</note> of the angel who appeared to him in the bush.

verses.name: Acts 7:36
verses.text: This man led them out, performing wonders and signs in the land of Egypt and at the Red Sea and in the wilderness <transChange type="added">for</transChange> forty years.  <div eID="gen26828" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 7:37
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11350"/><div sID="gen26829" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11350"/>“This is the Moses who said to the sons of Israel, ‘God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers.’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Deut.18.15">Deut 18:15</reference></note>

verses.name: Acts 7:38
verses.text: This is the one who was in the congregation in the wilderness with the angel who spoke to him at Mount Sinai, and who <transChange type="added">with</transChange> our fathers received living oracles to give to us,

verses.name: Acts 7:39
verses.text: to whom our fathers were not willing to become obedient, but rejected <transChange type="added">him</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and turned <transChange type="added">back</transChange> in their hearts to Egypt,

verses.name: Acts 7:40
verses.text: saying to Aaron, ‘Make us gods who will go on before us! For this Moses, who led us out from the land of Egypt—we do not know what has happened to him!’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Exod.32.1">Exod 32:1</reference>, <reference osisRef="Exod.32.23">23</reference></note>

verses.name: Acts 7:41
verses.text: And they manufactured a calf in those days, and offered up a sacrifice to the idol, and began rejoicing<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began rejoicing”)</note> in the works of their hands.

verses.name: Acts 7:42
verses.text: But God turned away and gave them over to worship the host of heaven, just as it is written in the book of the prophets: <div eID="gen26829" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen26830"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26831"/>‘You did not bring offerings and sacrifices to me<l eID="gen26831" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26832"/><transChange type="added">for</transChange> forty years in the wilderness, <transChange type="added">did you</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here, indicated by “did you”</note> house of Israel? <l eID="gen26832" level="2"/>

verses.name: Acts 7:43
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11351"/><l level="1" sID="gen26833"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11351"/>And you took along the tabernacle<note placement="foot">Or “tent”</note> of Moloch<l eID="gen26833" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26834"/>and the star of the god<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “of your god”</note> Rephan,<l eID="gen26834" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26835"/>the images that you made, to worship them,<l eID="gen26835" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26836"/>and I will deport you beyond Babylon!’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Amos.5.25-Amos.5.27">Amos 5:25–27</reference></note> <l eID="gen26836" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen26830"/>

verses.name: Acts 7:44
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11352"/><div sID="gen26837" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11352"/>The tabernacle of the testimony <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞belonged⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “was”</note> to our fathers in the wilderness, just as the one who spoke to Moses directed him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to make it according to the design that he had seen,

verses.name: Acts 7:45
verses.text: and which, <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“receiving”) which is understood as temporal</note> receiving it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> in turn, our fathers brought in with Joshua <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞when they dispossessed the⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in the possession of the”</note> nations that God drove out from the presence of our fathers, until the days of David,

verses.name: Acts 7:46
verses.text: who found favor in the sight of God and asked to find a habitation for the God of Jacob.<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “for the house of Jacob”</note>

verses.name: Acts 7:47
verses.text: But Solomon built a house for him.

verses.name: Acts 7:48
verses.text: But the Most High does not live in <transChange type="added">houses</transChange><note placement="foot">Or “temples made by human hands”; either word (“houses” or “temples”) is understood here</note> made by human hands, just as the prophet says,  <div eID="gen26837" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 7:49
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11353"/><lg sID="gen26838"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26839"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11353"/>‘Heaven <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my throne<l eID="gen26839" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26840"/>and earth <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the footstool for my feet.<l eID="gen26840" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26841"/>What kind of house will you build for me, says the Lord,<l eID="gen26841" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26842"/>or what <transChange type="added">is the</transChange> place of my rest? <l eID="gen26842" level="2"/>

verses.name: Acts 7:50
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11354"/><l level="1" sID="gen26843"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11354"/>Did not my hand make all these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>?’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.66.1-Isa.66.2">Isa 66:1–2</reference></note> <l eID="gen26843" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen26838"/>

verses.name: Acts 7:51
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11355"/><div sID="gen26844" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11355"/>“<transChange type="added">You</transChange> stiff-necked <transChange type="added">people</transChange> and uncircumcised in hearts and in <transChange type="added">your</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> ears! You constantly resist the Holy Spirit! As your fathers <transChange type="added">did</transChange>, <transChange type="added">so</transChange> also <transChange type="added">do</transChange> you!

verses.name: Acts 7:52
verses.text: Which of the prophets did your fathers not persecute? And they killed those who announced beforehand about the coming of the Righteous One, whose betrayers and murderers you have now become,

verses.name: Acts 7:53
verses.text: <transChange type="added">you</transChange> who received the law by directions of angels and have not observed <transChange type="added">it</transChange>!”  <div eID="gen26844" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 7:54
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11356"/><title type="x-s">Stephen’s Martyrdom</title> <div sID="gen26845" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11356"/>Now <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard these things, they were infuriated in their hearts and gnashed their<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> teeth at him.

verses.name: Acts 7:55
verses.text: But he, being full of the Holy Spirit, looked intently into heaven <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“looked intently”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing at the right hand of God.

verses.name: Acts 7:56
verses.text: And he said, “Behold, I see the heavens opened and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God!”

verses.name: Acts 7:57
verses.text: But crying out with a loud voice, they stopped their ears and rushed at him with one purpose.

verses.name: Acts 7:58
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had driven”) which is understood as temporal</note> had driven him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> out of the city, they began to stone<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began stoning”)</note> him,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and the witnesses laid aside their cloaks at the feet of a young man named Saul.

verses.name: Acts 7:59
verses.text: And they kept on stoning Stephen <transChange type="added">as he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was calling out”) which is understood as temporal</note> was calling out and saying, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit!”

verses.name: Acts 7:60
verses.text: And falling to <transChange type="added">his</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> knees, he cried out with a loud voice, “Lord, do not hold this sin against them!” And after he<note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“said”) which is understood as temporal</note> said this, he fell asleep.<note placement="foot">Or “he passed away”</note>  <chapter eID="Acts.7"/>

verses.name: Acts 8:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11357"/><title type="x-s">Saul Attempts to Destroy the Church</title> <div sID="gen26846" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11357"/>And Saul was agreeing with his murder. Now there happened on that day a great persecution against the church in Jerusalem, and they were all scattered throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria, except the apostles.

verses.name: Acts 8:2
verses.text: And devout men buried Stephen and made loud lamentation over him.

verses.name: Acts 8:3
verses.text: But Saul was attempting to destroy the church. Entering <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞house after house⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “from house” to house</note> he dragged off both men and women and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“dragged off”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> delivered them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to prison.  <div eID="gen26846" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 8:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11358"/><title type="x-s">Philip Proclaims Christ in Samaria</title> <div sID="gen26847" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11358"/>Now those who had been scattered went about proclaiming the good news <transChange type="added">of</transChange> the word.

verses.name: Acts 8:5
verses.text: And Philip came down to the city of Samaria <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came down”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> began proclaiming<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began proclaiming”)</note> the Christ<note placement="foot">Or “Messiah”</note> to them.

verses.name: Acts 8:6
verses.text: And the crowds with one mind were paying attention to what was being said by Philip, <transChange type="added">as</transChange> they heard <transChange type="added">him</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and saw the signs that he was performing.

verses.name: Acts 8:7
verses.text: For many of those who had unclean spirits, they were coming out <transChange type="added">of them</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*The words “of them” are supplied in the translation to indicate that the unclean spirits were coming out of the people</note> crying out with a loud voice, and many who were paralyzed and lame were healed.

verses.name: Acts 8:8
verses.text: And there was great joy in that city.  <div eID="gen26847" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 8:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11359"/><title type="x-s">Simon the Magician</title> <div sID="gen26848" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11359"/>Now a certain man <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞named⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by name”</note> Simon had been in the city practicing magic and astonishing the people of Samaria, saying he was someone great.

verses.name: Acts 8:10
verses.text: They were all paying attention to <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “whom”</note> from the least to the greatest, saying, “This man is the power of God that is called ‘Great.’ ”

verses.name: Acts 8:11
verses.text: And they were paying attention to him because for a long time he had astonished them with <transChange type="added">his</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> magic.

verses.name: Acts 8:12
verses.text: But when they believed Philip <transChange type="added">as he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was proclaiming the good news”) which is understood as temporal</note> was proclaiming the good news about the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, both men and women were being baptized.

verses.name: Acts 8:13
verses.text: And Simon himself also believed, and <transChange type="added">after he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was baptized”) which is understood as temporal</note> was baptized he was <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞keeping close company with⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “attaching himself to”</note> Philip. And when he<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw the signs and great miracles that were taking place, he was astonished.  <div eID="gen26848" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 8:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11360"/><div sID="gen26849" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11360"/>Now <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> the apostles in Jerusalem heard that Samaria had accepted the word of God, they sent Peter and John to them,

verses.name: Acts 8:15
verses.text: who went down <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went down”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> prayed for them so that they would receive the Holy Spirit.

verses.name: Acts 8:16
verses.text: (For he had not yet fallen on any of them, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞but they had only been baptized⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “but they were only having been baptized”</note> in the name of the Lord Jesus.)

verses.name: Acts 8:17
verses.text: Then they placed <transChange type="added">their</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> hands on them and they received the Holy Spirit.  <div eID="gen26849" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 8:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11361"/><div sID="gen26850" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11361"/>Now Simon, <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw that the Spirit was given through the laying on of the apostles’ hands, offered them money,

verses.name: Acts 8:19
verses.text: saying, “Give to me also this power, so that whomever I place <transChange type="added">my</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> hands on may receive the Holy Spirit!”

verses.name: Acts 8:20
verses.text: But Peter said to him, “May your silver <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞be destroyed along with you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “be for destruction with you”</note> because you thought <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you could acquire⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to acquire”</note> the gift of God by means of money!

verses.name: Acts 8:21
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞You have no⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “there is for you no”</note> part or share in this matter, because your heart is not right before God.

verses.name: Acts 8:22
verses.text: Therefore repent of this wickedness of yours, and ask the Lord if perhaps the intent of your heart may be forgiven you!”

verses.name: Acts 8:23
verses.text: For I see you are in <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a state of bitter envy⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the gall of bitterness”</note> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞bound by unrighteousness⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “the fetter of unrighteousness”</note>

verses.name: Acts 8:24
verses.text: But Simon answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “You pray to the Lord for me so that nothing of what you have said will come upon me.”

verses.name: Acts 8:25
verses.text: So <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had solemnly testified”) which is understood as temporal</note> they had solemnly testified and spoken the word of the Lord, they turned back toward Jerusalem, and were proclaiming the good news <transChange type="added">to</transChange> many villages of the Samaritans.  <div eID="gen26850" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 8:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11362"/><title type="x-s">Philip and the Ethiopian Eunuch</title> <div sID="gen26851" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11362"/>Now an angel of the Lord spoke to Philip, saying, “Get up and go toward the south<note placement="foot">Or “go about noon”</note> on the road that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza.” (This is a desert <transChange type="added">road</transChange>.)

verses.name: Acts 8:27
verses.text: And he got up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“got up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> went, and behold, there was a man, an Ethiopian eunuch (a court official of Candace,<note placement="foot">Or “the Candace” (the title of the queen of Ethiopia)</note> queen of the Ethiopians, who was over all her treasury) who had come to worship in Jerusalem

verses.name: Acts 8:28
verses.text: and was returning and sitting in his chariot, and reading aloud the prophet Isaiah.

verses.name: Acts 8:29
verses.text: And the Spirit said to Philip, “Approach and join this chariot.”

verses.name: Acts 8:30
verses.text: So Philip ran up to <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“ran up to”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> heard him reading aloud Isaiah the prophet and said, “So then, do you understand what you are reading?”

verses.name: Acts 8:31
verses.text: And he said, “So how could I, unless someone will guide me?” And he invited Philip to come up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“come up”) has been translated as an infinitive</note> sit with him.

verses.name: Acts 8:32
verses.text: Now the passage of scripture that he was reading aloud was this: <div eID="gen26851" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen26852"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26853"/>“He was led like a sheep to the slaughter,<l eID="gen26853" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26854"/>and like a lamb before its shearer <transChange type="added">is</transChange> silent,<l eID="gen26854" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26855"/>so he did not open his mouth. <l eID="gen26855" level="1"/>

verses.name: Acts 8:33
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11363"/><l level="2" sID="gen26856"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11363"/>In his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> humiliation justice was taken from him.<l eID="gen26856" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26857"/>Who can describe his <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞descendants⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?<note placement="foot">Or perhaps “family history”; literally “generation”</note><l eID="gen26857" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26858"/>For his life was taken away from the earth.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.53.7-Isa.53.8">Isa 53:7–8</reference></note> <l eID="gen26858" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen26852"/>

verses.name: Acts 8:34
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11364"/><div sID="gen26859" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11364"/>And the eunuch answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to Philip, “I ask you, about whom does the prophet say this—about himself or about someone else?”

verses.name: Acts 8:35
verses.text: So Philip opened his mouth and beginning from this scripture, proclaimed the good news to him <transChange type="added">about</transChange> Jesus.

verses.name: Acts 8:36
verses.text: And as they were traveling down the road, they came to some water. And the eunuch said, “Look! Water! What prevents me from being baptized?”<note placement="foot">A few later manuscripts add v. <reference osisRef="Acts.8.37">37</reference>, with minor variations: “He said to him, ‘If you believe with your whole heart, you may.’ And he answered and said, ‘I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God.’ ” The verse is almost certainly not an original part of the text of Acts.</note>

verses.name: Acts 8:38
verses.text: And he ordered the chariot to stop, and they both went down into the water—Philip and the eunuch—and he baptized him.

verses.name: Acts 8:39
verses.text: And when they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord carried Philip away, and the eunuch did not see him any longer, for he went on his way rejoicing.

verses.name: Acts 8:40
verses.text: But Philip found himself at Azotus, and <transChange type="added">as he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“passed through”) which is understood as temporal</note> passed through, he proclaimed the good news <transChange type="added">to</transChange> all the towns until he came to Caesarea.  <chapter eID="Acts.8"/>

verses.name: Acts 9:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11365"/><title type="x-s">Saul’s Conversion on the Damascus Road</title> <div sID="gen26860" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11365"/>But Saul, still breathing threats and murder against the disciples of the Lord, went to the high priest

verses.name: Acts 9:2
verses.text: <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the participle in the previous verse (“went to”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> asked for letters from him to the synagogues in Damascus, so that if he found any who were of the Way, both men and women, he could bring them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> tied up<note placement="foot">Or figuratively “bring them under arrest”</note> to Jerusalem.

verses.name: Acts 9:3
verses.text: Now as <transChange type="added">he</transChange> proceeded, it happened that <transChange type="added">when</transChange> he approached Damascus, suddenly a light from heaven flashed around him.

verses.name: Acts 9:4
verses.text: And falling to the ground, he heard a voice saying to him, “Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?”

verses.name: Acts 9:5
verses.text: So he said, “Who are you, Lord?” And he <transChange type="added">said</transChange>, “I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting!

verses.name: Acts 9:6
verses.text: But get up and enter into the city, and it will be told to you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞what you must do⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “what thing it is necessary that you do”</note>

verses.name: Acts 9:7
verses.text: (Now the men who were traveling together with him stood speechless, <transChange type="added">because they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as causal</note> heard the voice but saw no one.)

verses.name: Acts 9:8
verses.text: So Saul got up from the ground, but <transChange type="added">although</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the genitive absolute participle (“were open”) which is understood as concessive</note> his eyes were open he could see nothing. And leading him by the hand, they brought <transChange type="added">him</transChange> into Damascus.

verses.name: Acts 9:9
verses.text: And he was <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞unable to see⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “not seeing”</note> <transChange type="added">for</transChange> three days, and he did not eat or drink.  <div eID="gen26860" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 9:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11366"/><title type="x-s">Ananias Sent to Saul</title> <div sID="gen26861" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11366"/>Now there was a certain disciple in Damascus <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞named⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by name”</note> Ananias, and the Lord said to him in a vision, “Ananias!” And he said, “Behold, <transChange type="added">here</transChange> I <transChange type="added">am</transChange>, Lord!”

verses.name: Acts 9:11
verses.text: And the Lord <transChange type="added">said</transChange> to him, “Get up, go to the street called ‘Straight’ and in the house of Judas look for <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a man named Saul from Tarsus⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “Saul by name of Tarsus”</note> For behold, he is praying,

verses.name: Acts 9:12
verses.text: and he has seen in a vision a man <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞named⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by name”</note> Ananias coming in and placing hands<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “placing his hands”</note> on him so that he may regain <transChange type="added">his</transChange> sight.”

verses.name: Acts 9:13
verses.text: But Ananias replied, “Lord, I have heard from many <transChange type="added">people</transChange> about this man, how much harm he has done to your saints in Jerusalem,

verses.name: Acts 9:14
verses.text: and here he has authority from the chief priests to tie up<note placement="foot">Or figuratively “to arrest” or “to imprison”</note> all who call upon your name!”

verses.name: Acts 9:15
verses.text: But the Lord said to him, “Go, because this man is my chosen instrument to carry my name before Gentiles<note placement="foot">The same Greek word can be translated “nations” or “Gentiles” depending on the context</note> and kings and the sons of Israel.

verses.name: Acts 9:16
verses.text: For I will show him how much he must suffer for the sake of my name.”

verses.name: Acts 9:17
verses.text: So Ananias departed and entered into the house, and placing <transChange type="added">his</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> hands on him, he said, “Brother Saul, the Lord Jesus, who appeared to you on the road by which you came, has sent me so that you may regain <transChange type="added">your</transChange> sight and be filled with the Holy Spirit.”

verses.name: Acts 9:18
verses.text: And immediately <transChange type="added">something</transChange> like scales fell from his eyes and he regained <transChange type="added">his</transChange> sight and got up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“got up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> was baptized,

verses.name: Acts 9:19
verses.text: and <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“taking”) which is understood as temporal</note> taking food, he regained his strength. And he was with the disciples in Damascus several days.  <div eID="gen26861" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 9:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11367"/><title type="x-s">Saul Proclaims Christ in Damascus</title> <div sID="gen26862" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11367"/>And immediately he began proclaiming<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began proclaiming”)</note> Jesus in the synagogues: “This one is the Son of God!”

verses.name: Acts 9:21
verses.text: And all who heard <transChange type="added">him</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> were amazed, and were saying, “Is this not the one who was wreaking havoc in Jerusalem on those who call upon this name, and had come here for this reason, that he could bring them tied up<note placement="foot">Or figuratively “bring them under arrest”</note> to the chief priests?”

verses.name: Acts 9:22
verses.text: But Saul was increasing in strength even more, and was confounding the Jews who lived in Damascus <transChange type="added">by</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“proving”) which is understood as means</note> proving that this one is the Christ.<note placement="foot">Or “Messiah”</note>  <div eID="gen26862" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 9:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11368"/><div sID="gen26863" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11368"/>And when many days had elapsed, the Jews plotted to do away with him.

verses.name: Acts 9:24
verses.text: But their plot became known to Saul, and they were also watching the gates both day and night so that they could do away with him.

verses.name: Acts 9:25
verses.text: But his disciples took <transChange type="added">him</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> at night and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> let him down through the wall by<note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“lowering”) which is understood as means</note> lowering him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> in a basket.  <div eID="gen26863" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 9:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11369"/><title type="x-s">Saul in Jerusalem</title> <div sID="gen26864" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11369"/>And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“arrived”) which is understood as temporal</note> arrived in Jerusalem, he was attempting to associate with the disciples, and they were all afraid of him, because they<note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“believe”) which is understood as causal</note> did not believe that he was a disciple.

verses.name: Acts 9:27
verses.text: But Barnabas took him <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> brought him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to the apostles and related to them how he had seen the Lord on the road and that he had spoken to him, and how in Damascus he had spoken boldly in the name of Jesus.

verses.name: Acts 9:28
verses.text: And he was going in and going out among them in Jerusalem, speaking boldly in the name of the Lord.

verses.name: Acts 9:29
verses.text: And he was speaking and debating with the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Greek-speaking Jews⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “Hellenists”</note> but they were trying to do away with him.

verses.name: Acts 9:30
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“found out”) which is understood as temporal</note> the brothers found out, they brought him down to Caesarea and sent him away to Tarsus.  <div eID="gen26864" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 9:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11370"/><div sID="gen26865" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11370"/>Then the church throughout all of Judea and Galilee and Samaria had peace, being strengthened. And living in the fear of the Lord and the encouragement of the Holy Spirit, it was increasing <transChange type="added">in numbers</transChange>.<note placement="foot">*The words “in numbers” are not in the Greek text but are implied</note>  <div eID="gen26865" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 9:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11371"/><title type="x-s">Aeneas Healed</title> <div sID="gen26866" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11371"/>Now it happened that <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was traveling”) which is understood as temporal</note> Peter was traveling through all the places,<note placement="foot">*The words “the places” are not in the Greek text but are implied</note> <transChange type="added">he</transChange> also came down to the saints who lived <transChange type="added">in</transChange> Lydda.

verses.name: Acts 9:33
verses.text: And he found there a certain man <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞named⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by name”</note> Aeneas who was paralyzed, who had been lying on a mat<note placement="foot">Or “mattress”</note> for eight years.

verses.name: Acts 9:34
verses.text: And Peter said to him, “Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you! Get up and make your bed yourself!” And immediately he got up.

verses.name: Acts 9:35
verses.text: And all those who lived <transChange type="added">in</transChange> Lydda and Sharon saw him, who <transChange type="added">all</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “all” is supplied to indicate the relative pronoun is plural</note> indeed turned to the Lord.  <div eID="gen26866" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 9:36
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11372"/><title type="x-s">Dorcas Raised</title> <div sID="gen26867" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11372"/>Now in Joppa there was a certain female disciple <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞named⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by name”</note> Tabitha (which translated means “Dorcas”).<note placement="foot">“Dorcas” is the Greek translation of the Aramaic name “Tabitha” which means “deer” or “gazelle”</note> She was full of good deeds and charitable giving which she was constantly doing.<note placement="foot">*Here the imperfect verb is translated as a customary imperfect (“was constantly doing”)</note>

verses.name: Acts 9:37
verses.text: Now it happened that in those days <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“becoming sick”) which is understood as temporal</note> becoming sick, she died. And after<note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“washing”) which is understood as temporal</note> washing her,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> they placed her in an upstairs room.

verses.name: Acts 9:38
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">because</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was”) which is understood as causal</note> Lydda was near Joppa, the disciples, when they<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard that Peter was in <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Lydda⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “in it”</note> sent two men to him, urging, “Do not delay to come to us!”

verses.name: Acts 9:39
verses.text: So Peter got up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“got up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> accompanied them. When he<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“arrived”) which is understood as temporal</note> arrived, they brought him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> up to the upstairs room, and all the widows came to him, weeping and showing him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> tunics and other clothing that Dorcas used to make while she<note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was”) which is understood as temporal</note> was with them.

verses.name: Acts 9:40
verses.text: But Peter sent <transChange type="added">them</transChange> all outside, and, falling to <transChange type="added">his</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> knees, he prayed. And turning toward the body, he said, “Tabitha, get up!” And she opened her eyes, and when she<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw Peter, she sat up.

verses.name: Acts 9:41
verses.text: And he gave her <transChange type="added">his</transChange> hand <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“gave”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> raised her up. And he called the saints and the widows and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“called”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> presented her alive.

verses.name: Acts 9:42
verses.text: And it became known throughout all Joppa, and many believed in the Lord.

verses.name: Acts 9:43
verses.text: And it happened that <transChange type="added">he</transChange> stayed many days in Joppa with a certain Simon, a tanner.<note placement="foot">Or “with a certain Simon Berseus”; most modern English versions treat the word as Simon’s profession (“Simon the tanner”), but the word may actually be a surname (“Simon Berseus” or “Simon Tanner”)</note>  <chapter eID="Acts.9"/>

verses.name: Acts 10:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11373"/><title type="x-s">Cornelius Has a Vision</title> <div sID="gen26868" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11373"/>Now <transChange type="added">there was</transChange> a certain man in Caesarea <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞named⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by name”</note> Cornelius, a centurion of what was called the Italian Cohort,

verses.name: Acts 10:2
verses.text: devout and fearing God together with all his household, doing many charitable deeds for the people and praying to God <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞continually⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “through everything”</note>

verses.name: Acts 10:3
verses.text: About the ninth hour of the day, he saw clearly in a vision an angel of God coming to him and saying to him, “Cornelius.”

verses.name: Acts 10:4
verses.text: And he stared at him and became terrified <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“became”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “What is <transChange type="added">it</transChange>, Lord?” And he said to him, “Your prayers and your charitable deeds have gone up for a memorial offering before God.

verses.name: Acts 10:5
verses.text: And now, send men to Joppa and summon a certain Simon, who is also called Peter.

verses.name: Acts 10:6
verses.text: This man is staying as a guest with a certain Simon, a tanner,<note placement="foot">Or “with a certain Simon Berseus”; most modern English versions treat the word as Simon’s profession (“Simon the tanner”), but the word may actually be a surname (“Simon Berseus” or “Simon Tanner”)</note> whose house is by the sea.”

verses.name: Acts 10:7
verses.text: And when the angel who spoke to him departed, he summoned two of the household slaves and a devout soldier from those who attended him,

verses.name: Acts 10:8
verses.text: and <transChange type="added">after he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had explained”) which is understood as temporal</note> had explained everything to them, he sent them to Joppa.  <div eID="gen26868" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 10:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11374"/><title type="x-s">Peter Has a Vision</title> <div sID="gen26869" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11374"/>And the next day, <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“were on their way”)</note> they were on their way and approaching the city, Peter went up on the housetop to pray <transChange type="added">at</transChange> about the sixth hour.

verses.name: Acts 10:10
verses.text: And he became hungry and wanted to eat. But <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“were preparing”)</note> they were preparing the food,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> a trance came over him.

verses.name: Acts 10:11
verses.text: And he saw heaven opened and an object something like a large sheet coming down, being let down to the earth by its four corners,

verses.name: Acts 10:12
verses.text: in which were all the four-footed animals and reptiles of the earth and birds of the sky.

verses.name: Acts 10:13
verses.text: And a voice came to him, “Get up, Peter, slaughter and eat!”

verses.name: Acts 10:14
verses.text: But Peter said, “Certainly not, Lord! For I have never eaten anything common and unclean!”

verses.name: Acts 10:15
verses.text: And the voice <transChange type="added">came</transChange> again to him for the second time: “<transChange type="added">The things</transChange> which God has made clean, you must not consider unclean!”

verses.name: Acts 10:16
verses.text: And this happened three times, and immediately the object was taken up into heaven.  <div eID="gen26869" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 10:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11375"/><div sID="gen26870" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11375"/>Now while Peter was greatly perplexed within himself <transChange type="added">as to</transChange> what the vision that he had seen might be, behold, the men who had been sent by Cornelius, having found the house of Simon by asking around, stood at the gate.

verses.name: Acts 10:18
verses.text: And they called out <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“called out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> asked if Simon who was also called Peter was staying there as a guest.

verses.name: Acts 10:19
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was reflecting”)</note> Peter was reflecting about the vision, the Spirit said to him, “Behold, men<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “three men”</note> are looking for you.

verses.name: Acts 10:20
verses.text: But get up, go down, and go with them—not hesitating at all, because I have sent them.”

verses.name: Acts 10:21
verses.text: So Peter went down to the men <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went down”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “Behold, I am <transChange type="added">he</transChange> whom you are looking for! What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the reason for which you have come?”

verses.name: Acts 10:22
verses.text: And they said, “Cornelius, a centurion, a righteous and God-fearing man—and well spoken of by the whole nation of the Jews—was directed by a holy angel to summon you to his house and to hear words from you.”

verses.name: Acts 10:23
verses.text: So he invited them in <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“invited … in”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> entertained them as guests, and on the next day he got up and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“got up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> went away with them. And some of the brothers from Joppa accompanied him.

verses.name: Acts 10:24
verses.text: And on the next day he entered into Caesarea. <div eID="gen26870" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">Peter Visits Cornelius</title> <div sID="gen26871" type="x-p"/> Now Cornelius was waiting for them, <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“waiting for”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> had called together his relatives and close friends.

verses.name: Acts 10:25
verses.text: So it happened that when Peter entered, Cornelius met him, fell at <transChange type="added">his</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> feet, and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“fell”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> worshiped him.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Acts 10:26
verses.text: But Peter helped him up, saying, “Get up! I myself am also a man!”

verses.name: Acts 10:27
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">as he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“conversed with”) which is understood as temporal</note> conversed with him, he went in and found many <transChange type="added">people</transChange> gathered.

verses.name: Acts 10:28
verses.text: And he said to them, “You know that it is forbidden for a Jewish man to associate with or to approach a foreigner. And to me God has shown <transChange type="added">that</transChange> I should call no man common or unclean.

verses.name: Acts 10:29
verses.text: Therefore—and without raising any objection—I came <transChange type="added">when I</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was sent for”) which is understood as temporal</note> was sent for. So I ask for what reason you sent for me.”  <div eID="gen26871" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 10:30
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11376"/><div sID="gen26872" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11376"/>And Cornelius said, “<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Four days ago at this hour⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “from the fourth day until this hour”</note> <transChange type="added">the</transChange> ninth, I was praying in my house. And behold, a man in shining clothing stood before me

verses.name: Acts 10:31
verses.text: and said, ‘Cornelius, your prayer has been heard, and your charitable deeds have been remembered before God.

verses.name: Acts 10:32
verses.text: Therefore send to Joppa and summon Simon who is also called Peter. This man is staying as a guest in the house of Simon, a tanner,<note placement="foot">Or “of Simon Berseus”; most modern English versions treat the word as Simon’s profession (“Simon the tanner”), but the word may actually be a surname (“Simon Berseus” or “Simon Tanner”)</note> by the sea.

verses.name: Acts 10:33
verses.text: Therefore I sent for you at once, and you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞were kind enough to come⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “have done rightly coming”</note> So now we all are present before God to hear all the things that have been commanded to you by the Lord.”  <div eID="gen26872" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 10:34
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11377"/><div sID="gen26873" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11377"/>So Peter opened <transChange type="added">his</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> mouth and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“opened”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “In truth I understand that God is not one who shows partiality,

verses.name: Acts 10:35
verses.text: but in every nation the one who fears him and who does what is right is acceptable to him.

verses.name: Acts 10:36
verses.text: <transChange type="added">As for</transChange><note placement="foot">*The words “As for” are not in the Greek text, but are supplied in the translation in keeping with English style</note> the message that he sent to the sons of Israel, proclaiming the good news of peace through Jesus Christ—this one is Lord of all—

verses.name: Acts 10:37
verses.text: you know the thing that happened throughout all Judea, beginning from Galilee, after the baptism that John proclaimed:

verses.name: Acts 10:38
verses.text: Jesus of Nazareth—how God anointed him with the Holy Spirit and with power, who went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, because God was with him.

verses.name: Acts 10:39
verses.text: And we <transChange type="added">are</transChange> witnesses of all <transChange type="added">the things</transChange> that he did both in the land of the Judeans and in Jerusalem, whom they also executed <transChange type="added">by</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“hanging”) which is understood as means</note> hanging him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> on a tree.

verses.name: Acts 10:40
verses.text: God raised this one up on the third day and granted <transChange type="added">that</transChange> he should become visible,

verses.name: Acts 10:41
verses.text: not to all the people but to us who had been chosen beforehand by God <transChange type="added">as</transChange> witnesses, who ate and drank with him after he rose from the dead.

verses.name: Acts 10:42
verses.text: And he commanded us to preach to the people and to testify solemnly that this one is the one appointed<note placement="foot">Or “one who is designated”</note> by God <transChange type="added">as</transChange> judge of the living and of the dead.

verses.name: Acts 10:43
verses.text: To this one all the prophets testify, <transChange type="added">that</transChange> through his name everyone who believes in him receives forgiveness of sins.”  <div eID="gen26873" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 10:44
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11378"/><title type="x-s">The Holy Spirit Given to Gentiles</title> <div sID="gen26874" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11378"/><transChange type="added">While</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was … speaking”)</note> Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit fell on all those who were listening to the message.

verses.name: Acts 10:45
verses.text: And those believers from the circumcision who had accompanied Peter were astonished that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out even on the Gentiles,

verses.name: Acts 10:46
verses.text: for they heard them speaking in tongues and glorifying God. Then Peter said,

verses.name: Acts 10:47
verses.text: “Surely no one can withhold the water for these <transChange type="added">people</transChange> to be baptized, who have received the Holy Spirit as we also did!”

verses.name: Acts 10:48
verses.text: So he ordered <transChange type="added">that</transChange> they be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Then they asked him to stay for several days.  <chapter eID="Acts.10"/>

verses.name: Acts 11:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11379"/><title type="x-s">Peter’s Explanation to the Church in Jerusalem</title> <div sID="gen26875" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11379"/>Now the apostles and the brothers who were throughout Judea heard that the Gentiles also had accepted the word<note placement="foot">Or “message”</note> of God.

verses.name: Acts 11:2
verses.text: So when Peter went up to Jerusalem, those of the circumcision took issue with him,

verses.name: Acts 11:3
verses.text: saying, “You went to men <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who were uncircumcised⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “who had uncircumcision</note> and ate with them!”

verses.name: Acts 11:4
verses.text: But Peter began <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“began”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> explained it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to them in an orderly sequence, saying,

verses.name: Acts 11:5
verses.text: “I was in the city of Joppa praying, and in a trance I saw a vision—an object something like a large sheet coming down, being let down from heaven by its four corners, and it came to me.

verses.name: Acts 11:6
verses.text: <transChange type="added">As I</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“looked intently”) which is understood as temporal</note> looked intently into it, I was considering it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and I saw the four-footed animals of the earth and the wild animals and the reptiles and the birds of the sky.

verses.name: Acts 11:7
verses.text: And I also heard a voice saying to me, ‘Get up, Peter, slaughter and eat!’

verses.name: Acts 11:8
verses.text: But I said, ‘Certainly not, Lord! For nothing common or unclean has ever entered into my mouth!’

verses.name: Acts 11:9
verses.text: But the voice replied from heaven for the second time, ‘<transChange type="added">The things</transChange> which God has made clean, you must not consider unclean!’

verses.name: Acts 11:10
verses.text: And this happened three times, and everything was pulled up into heaven again.

verses.name: Acts 11:11
verses.text: And behold, at once three men who had been sent to me from Caesarea approached the house in which we were <transChange type="added">staying</transChange>.<note placement="foot">*Here the word “staying” is not in the Greek text but is implied</note>

verses.name: Acts 11:12
verses.text: And the Spirit told me to accompany them, not hesitating <transChange type="added">at all</transChange>. So these six brothers also went with me, and we entered into the man’s house.

verses.name: Acts 11:13
verses.text: And he reported to us how he had seen the angel standing in his house and saying, ‘Send to Joppa and summon Simon, who is also called Peter,

verses.name: Acts 11:14
verses.text: who will speak words to you by which you will be saved, you and all your household.’

verses.name: Acts 11:15
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">as</transChange> I was beginning to speak, the Holy Spirit fell on them, just as also on us at the beginning.

verses.name: Acts 11:16
verses.text: And I remembered the word of the Lord, how he said, ‘John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.’<note placement="foot">An allusion to <reference osisRef="Acts.1.5">Acts 1:5</reference></note>

verses.name: Acts 11:17
verses.text: Therefore if God gave them the same gift as also to us <transChange type="added">when we</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“believed”) which is understood as temporal</note> believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I <transChange type="added">to be</transChange> able to hinder God?”

verses.name: Acts 11:18
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard these things, they became silent<note placement="foot">*Here the aorist verb is translated as ingressive (“became silent”)</note> and praised God, saying, “Then God has granted the repentance <transChange type="added">leading</transChange> to life to the Gentiles also!”  <div eID="gen26875" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 11:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11380"/><title type="x-s">Developments in the Church in Antioch</title> <div sID="gen26876" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11380"/>Now those who had been scattered because of the persecution that took place over Stephen traveled as far as Phoenicia and Cyprus and Antioch, proclaiming the message to no one except Jews alone.

verses.name: Acts 11:20
verses.text: But some of them were men from Cyprus and Cyrene, who, <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“came”) which is understood as temporal</note> came to Antioch, began to speak<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to speak”)</note> to the Hellenists<note placement="foot">*Here this term could refer to (1) Greek-speaking Jews or (2) Greek-speaking non-Jews (i.e., Gentiles)</note> also, proclaiming the good news about the Lord Jesus.

verses.name: Acts 11:21
verses.text: And the hand of the Lord was with them, and a large number who believed turned to the Lord.

verses.name: Acts 11:22
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And the report came to the attention⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and the report was heard in the ears”</note> of the church that was in Jerusalem about them, and they sent out Barnabas as far as<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “to go as far as”</note> Antioch,

verses.name: Acts 11:23
verses.text: who, <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“arrived”) which is understood as temporal</note> arrived and saw the grace of God, rejoiced and encouraged them all to remain true to the Lord with <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞devoted hearts⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “purpose of heart”</note>

verses.name: Acts 11:24
verses.text: because he was a good man and full of the Holy Spirit and of faith. And a large number were added<note placement="foot">Or “were brought”</note> to the Lord.

verses.name: Acts 11:25
verses.text: So he departed for Tarsus to look for Saul.

verses.name: Acts 11:26
