verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“found”) which is understood as temporal</note> found him,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> he brought him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to Antioch. And it happened to them also that they met together for a whole year with the church and taught a large number of people.<note placement="foot">*The words “of people” are not in the Greek text but are implied</note> And in Antioch the disciples were first called Christians.  <div eID="gen26876" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 11:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11381"/><div sID="gen26877" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11381"/>Now in those days prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch.

verses.name: Acts 11:28
verses.text: And one of them <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞named⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by name”</note> Agabus stood up and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“stood up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> indicated by the Spirit <transChange type="added">that</transChange> a great famine was about to come over the whole inhabited earth (which took place in the time of Claudius).

verses.name: Acts 11:29
verses.text: So from the disciples, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞according to their ability to give⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “to the degree that anyone was prospering”</note> each one of them determined to send financial aid<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> for support to the brothers who lived in Judea,

verses.name: Acts 11:30
verses.text: which they also did, sending <transChange type="added">the aid</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to the elders by the hand of Barnabas and Saul.  <chapter eID="Acts.11"/>

verses.name: Acts 12:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11382"/><title type="x-s">Herod Kills James and Imprisons Peter</title> <div sID="gen26878" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11382"/>Now at that time, Herod the king laid hands on some of those from the church to harm <transChange type="added">them</transChange>.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Acts 12:2
verses.text: So he executed James the brother of John with a sword.

verses.name: Acts 12:3
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw that it was pleasing to the Jews, he proceeded to arrest Peter also. (<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Now this was during the feast⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “now these were the days”</note> of Unleavened Bread.)

verses.name: Acts 12:4
verses.text: <transChange type="added">After he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had arrested”) which is understood as temporal</note> had arrested <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “whom”</note> he also put him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> in prison, handing him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> over to four squads of soldiers to guard him, intending to bring him <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞out for public trial⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the people”</note> after the Passover.

verses.name: Acts 12:5
verses.text: Thus Peter was kept in the prison, but prayer was fervently being made to God by the church for him.  <div eID="gen26878" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 12:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11383"/><title type="x-s">Peter Rescued by an Angel</title> <div sID="gen26879" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11383"/>Now when Herod was about to bring him <transChange type="added">out</transChange>, on that <transChange type="added">very</transChange> night Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains, and guards before the door were watching the prison.

verses.name: Acts 12:7
verses.text: And behold, an angel of the Lord stood near <transChange type="added">him</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and a light shone in the prison cell. And striking Peter’s side, he woke him up, saying, “Get up <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞quickly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!”<note placement="foot">Literally “with quickness”</note> And his chains fell off of his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> hands.

verses.name: Acts 12:8
verses.text: And the angel said to him, “Gird yourself and put on your sandals!” And he did so. And he said to him, “Wrap your cloak around you and follow me!”

verses.name: Acts 12:9
verses.text: And he went out <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> was following him.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> And he did not know that what was being done by the angel was real, but was thinking <transChange type="added">he</transChange> was seeing a vision.

verses.name: Acts 12:10
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had passed”) which is understood as temporal</note> had passed the first and second guard, they came to the iron gate that leads to the city, which opened for them by itself, and they went out and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> went forward <transChange type="added">along</transChange> one narrow street, and at once the angel departed from him.  <div eID="gen26879" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 12:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11384"/><div sID="gen26880" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11384"/>And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“came”) which is understood as temporal</note> Peter came to himself, he said, “Now I know truly that the Lord has sent out his angel and rescued me from the hand of Herod and all <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞that the Jewish people expected⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!”<note placement="foot">Literally “the expectation of the people of the Jews”</note>

verses.name: Acts 12:12
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“realized”) which is understood as temporal</note> realized this,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> he went to the house of Mary, the mother of John (who is also called Mark), where many <transChange type="added">people</transChange> were gathered together and were praying.

verses.name: Acts 12:13
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“knocked”)</note> he knocked at the door of the gateway, a female slave <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞named⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by name”</note> Rhoda came up to answer.

verses.name: Acts 12:14
verses.text: And recognizing Peter’s voice, because of <transChange type="added">her</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> joy she did not open the gate, but ran in and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“ran in”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> announced <transChange type="added">that</transChange> Peter was standing at the gate.

verses.name: Acts 12:15
verses.text: But they said to her, “You are out of your mind!” But she kept insisting<note placement="foot">*This imperfect verb is translated as an iterative imperfect (“kept insisting”)</note> it was so. And they kept saying,<note placement="foot">*This imperfect verb is translated as an iterative imperfect (“kept saying”)</note> “It is his angel!”

verses.name: Acts 12:16
verses.text: But Peter was continuing to knock, and <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“opened”) which is understood as temporal</note> opened the door<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> they saw him and were astonished.

verses.name: Acts 12:17
verses.text: But motioning to them with <transChange type="added">his</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> hand to be silent, he related to them how the Lord had brought him out of the prison. And he said, “Report these things to James and to the brothers,” and he departed and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“departed”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> went to another place.  <div eID="gen26880" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 12:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11385"/><div sID="gen26881" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11385"/>Now <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“came”)</note> day came, there was not a little commotion among the soldiers <transChange type="added">as to</transChange> what then had become of Peter.

verses.name: Acts 12:19
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had searched for”) which is understood as temporal</note> Herod had searched for him and did not find him,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> he questioned the guards and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“questioned”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> ordered that they be led away to execution. And he came down from Judea to Caesarea and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came down”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> stayed <transChange type="added">there</transChange>.  <div eID="gen26881" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 12:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11386"/><title type="x-s">Herod’s Gruesome Death</title> <div sID="gen26882" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11386"/>Now he was very angry with the Tyrians and Sidonians. So they came to him with one purpose, and <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“persuading”) which is understood as temporal</note> persuading Blastus, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the king’s chamberlain⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the one over the bedroom of the king”</note> they asked for peace, because their country was supported with food from the king’s country.

verses.name: Acts 12:21
verses.text: So on an appointed day Herod, <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“putting on”) which is understood as temporal</note> putting on royal clothing and sitting down on the judgment seat, began to deliver a public address to them.

verses.name: Acts 12:22
verses.text: But the people began to call out loudly,<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to call out loudly”)</note> “The voice of a god and not of a man!”

verses.name: Acts 12:23
verses.text: And immediately an angel of the Lord struck him down <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞because⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in return for which”</note> he did not give the glory to God. And he was eaten by worms and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“was”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> died.

verses.name: Acts 12:24
verses.text: But the word of God kept on increasing<note placement="foot">*This imperfect verb has been translated as customary (“kept on increasing”)</note> and multiplying.  <div eID="gen26882" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 12:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11387"/><div sID="gen26883" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11387"/>So Barnabas and Saul returned to<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts read “from”</note> Jerusalem when they<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had completed”) which is understood as temporal</note> had completed their<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> service, having taken along with them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> John (who is also called Mark).  <chapter eID="Acts.12"/>

verses.name: Acts 13:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11388"/><title type="x-s">Barnabas and Saul Sent Out from Antioch</title> <div sID="gen26884" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11388"/>Now there were prophets and teachers in Antioch in the church that was there: Barnabas, and Simeon (who was called Niger), and Lucius the Cyrenian, and Manaen (a close friend of Herod the tetrarch), and Saul.

verses.name: Acts 13:2
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“were serving”)</note> they were serving the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, “Set apart now for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.”

verses.name: Acts 13:3
verses.text: Then, <transChange type="added">after they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had fasted”) which is understood as temporal</note> had fasted and prayed and placed their<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> hands on them, they sent them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> away.  <div eID="gen26884" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 13:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11389"/><title type="x-s">Confronting a Magician on Cyprus</title> <div sID="gen26885" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11389"/>Therefore, sent out by the Holy Spirit, they came down to Seleucia, and from there they sailed away to Cyprus.

verses.name: Acts 13:5
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“came”) which is understood as temporal</note> came to Salamis, they began to proclaim the word of God in the synagogues of the Jews. And they also had John <transChange type="added">as</transChange> assistant.

verses.name: Acts 13:6
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had crossed over”) which is understood as temporal</note> had crossed over the whole island as far as Paphos, they found a certain man, a magician, a Jewish false prophet whose name <transChange type="added">was</transChange> Bar-Jesus,

verses.name: Acts 13:7
verses.text: who was with the proconsul Sergius Paulus, an intelligent man. This man summoned Barnabas and Saul <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“summoned”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> wished to hear the word of God.

verses.name: Acts 13:8
verses.text: But Elymas the magician (for his name is translated in this way) opposed them, attempting to turn the proconsul away from the faith.

verses.name: Acts 13:9
verses.text: But Saul (also called Paul), filled with the Holy Spirit, looked intently at him

verses.name: Acts 13:10
verses.text: <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the participle in the previous verse (“looked intently at”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “O <transChange type="added">you who are</transChange> full of all deceit and of all unscrupulousness, <transChange type="added">you</transChange> son of the devil, <transChange type="added">you</transChange> enemy of all righteousness! Will you not stop making crooked the straight paths of the Lord!

verses.name: Acts 13:11
verses.text: And now behold, the hand of the Lord <transChange type="added">is</transChange> against you, and you will be blind, not seeing the sun <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞for a while⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “until the time”</note> And immediately mist and darkness fell over him, and he was going around looking for people<note placement="foot">*In Greek the direct object (“people”) is understood and must be supplied in the English translation; since the following noun is plural, “people” rather than “someone” is used here</note> to lead him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> by the hand.

verses.name: Acts 13:12
verses.text: Then <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> the proconsul saw what had happened, he believed, because he<note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was astounded”) which is understood as causal</note> was astounded at the teaching about<note placement="foot">*Here “about” reflects an objective genitive (“the Lord” is the object of the teaching)</note> the Lord.  <div eID="gen26885" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 13:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11390"/><title type="x-s">Preaching in the Synagogue at Pisidian Antioch</title> <div sID="gen26886" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11390"/>Now <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Paul and his companions⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “those around Paul”</note> put out to sea from Paphos and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“put out to sea”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> came to Perga in Pamphylia, but John departed from them and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“departed”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> returned to Jerusalem.

verses.name: Acts 13:14
verses.text: And they went on from Perga <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went on”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> arrived at Pisidian Antioch. And they entered into the synagogue on the day of the Sabbath and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“entered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> sat down.

verses.name: Acts 13:15
verses.text: So after the reading from the law and the prophets, the rulers of the synagogue sent <transChange type="added">word</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to them, saying, “Men and brothers, if there is any message of exhortation by you for the people, say it.”<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>  <div eID="gen26886" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 13:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11391"/><div sID="gen26887" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11391"/>So Paul stood up,<note placement="foot">*Here the participle (“stood up”) is translated as a finite verb because of English style</note> and motioning with his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> hand, he said, “Israelite men, and those who fear God, listen!

verses.name: Acts 13:17
verses.text: The God of this people Israel chose our fathers and exalted the people during <transChange type="added">their</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> stay in the land of Egypt, and with uplifted arm he led them out of it.

verses.name: Acts 13:18
verses.text: And for a period of time <transChange type="added">of</transChange> about forty years, he put up with them in the wilderness.

verses.name: Acts 13:19
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“destroying”) which is understood as temporal</note> destroying seven nations in the land of Canaan, he gave their land to his people<note placement="foot">*The words “to his people” are supplied as a clarification of who received the land</note> as an inheritance.

verses.name: Acts 13:20
verses.text: <transChange type="added">This took</transChange><note placement="foot">*The words “This took” are not in the Greek text but are supplied in keeping with English style</note> about four hundred and fifty years. And after these things, he gave them<note placement="foot">*Here the indirect object “them” is not in the Greek text but is implied</note> judges until Samuel the prophet.

verses.name: Acts 13:21
verses.text: And then they asked for a king, and God gave them Saul son of Kish, a man from the tribe of Benjamin, <transChange type="added">for</transChange> forty years.

verses.name: Acts 13:22
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“removing”) which is understood as temporal</note> removing him, he raised up David for their king, about whom he also said, testifying, ‘I have found David the son of Jesse to be a man in accordance with my heart, who will carry out all my will.’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="1Sam.13.14">1 Sam 13:14</reference></note>

verses.name: Acts 13:23
verses.text: From the descendants of this man, according to <transChange type="added">his</transChange> promise, God brought to Israel a Savior, Jesus.

verses.name: Acts 13:24
verses.text: Before <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his coming⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the presence of his coming”</note> John had publicly proclaimed<note placement="foot">*Here the participle (“had publicly proclaimed”) has been translated as a finite verb in keeping with English style</note> a baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel.

verses.name: Acts 13:25
verses.text: But while John was completing <transChange type="added">his</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> mission, he said, ‘What do you suppose me to be? I am not he! But behold, one is coming after me of whom I am not worthy to untie the sandals of his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> feet!’  <div eID="gen26887" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 13:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11392"/><div sID="gen26888" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11392"/>“Men <transChange type="added">and</transChange> brothers, sons of the family of Abraham and those among you who fear God—to us the message of this salvation has been sent!

verses.name: Acts 13:27
verses.text: For those who live in Jerusalem and their rulers, <transChange type="added">because they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“did not recognize”) which is understood as causal</note> did not recognize this one, and the voices of the prophets that are read on every Sabbath, fulfilled them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> by<note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“condemning”) which is understood as means</note> condemning him.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Acts 13:28
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">although they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the genitive absolute participle (“found”) which is understood as concessive</note> found no charge <transChange type="added">worthy</transChange> of death, they asked Pilate <transChange type="added">that</transChange> he be executed.

verses.name: Acts 13:29
verses.text: And when they had carried out all the things that were written about him, they took <transChange type="added">him</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> down from the tree and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took … down”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> placed him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> in a tomb.

verses.name: Acts 13:30
verses.text: But God raised him from the dead,

verses.name: Acts 13:31
verses.text: who appeared for many days to those who had come up with him from Galilee to Jerusalem—who are now his witnesses to the people.

verses.name: Acts 13:32
verses.text: And we proclaim the good news to you: that the promise that was made to the fathers,

verses.name: Acts 13:33
verses.text: this <transChange type="added">promise</transChange><note placement="foot">It is necessary to repeat the word “promise” from the previous verse for clarity here</note> God has fulfilled to our children<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “to us their children”</note> by<note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“raising”) which is understood as means</note> raising Jesus, as it is also written in the second psalm, <div eID="gen26888" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen26889"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26890"/>‘You are my Son;<l eID="gen26890" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26891"/>today I have fathered you.’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.2.7">Ps 2:7</reference></note> <l eID="gen26891" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen26889"/>

verses.name: Acts 13:34
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11393"/><div sID="gen26892" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11393"/>But that he has raised him from the dead, no more going to return to decay, he has spoken in this way: ‘I will give you the reliable divine decrees of David.’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.55.3">Isa 55:3</reference></note>

verses.name: Acts 13:35
verses.text: Therefore he also says in another <transChange type="added">psalm</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*The word “psalm” is not in the Greek text but is implied</note> <div eID="gen26892" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen26893"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26894"/>‘You will not permit your Holy One to experience decay.’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.16.10">Ps 16:10</reference></note> <l eID="gen26894" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen26893"/>

verses.name: Acts 13:36
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11394"/><div sID="gen26895" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11394"/>For David, <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“serving”) which is understood as temporal</note> serving the purpose of God in his own generation, fell asleep and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞was buried with⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “was gathered to”</note> his fathers, and experienced decay.

verses.name: Acts 13:37
verses.text: But he whom God raised up did not experience decay.  <div eID="gen26895" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 13:38
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11395"/><div sID="gen26896" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11395"/>“Therefore let it be known to you, men <transChange type="added">and</transChange> brothers, that through this one forgiveness of sins is proclaimed to you, and from all <transChange type="added">the things</transChange> from which you were not able to be justified by the law of Moses,

verses.name: Acts 13:39
verses.text: by this one everyone who believes is justified!

verses.name: Acts 13:40
verses.text: Watch out, therefore, lest what is stated by the prophets come upon <transChange type="added">you</transChange>:<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>  <div eID="gen26896" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 13:41
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11396"/><lg sID="gen26897"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26898"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11396"/>‘Look, you scoffers,<l eID="gen26898" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26899"/>and be astonished and perish!<l eID="gen26899" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26900"/>For I am doing a work in your days,<l eID="gen26900" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26901"/>a work that you would never believe<l eID="gen26901" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen26902"/><transChange type="added">even</transChange> if someone were to tell <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to you.’ ”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Hab.1.5">Hab 1:5</reference></note> <l eID="gen26902" level="3"/> <lg eID="gen26897"/>

verses.name: Acts 13:42
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11397"/><title type="x-s">Response to the Message in Pisidian Antioch</title> <div sID="gen26903" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11397"/>And <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“were going out”)</note> they were going out, they began urging<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began urging”)</note> <transChange type="added">that</transChange> these things be spoken about to them on the next Sabbath.

verses.name: Acts 13:43
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“had broken up”)</note> the synagogue had broken up, many of the Jews and the devout<note placement="foot">Or “God-fearing”</note> proselytes followed Paul and Barnabas, who were speaking to them and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“were speaking to”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> were persuading them to continue in the grace of God.

verses.name: Acts 13:44
verses.text: And on the coming Sabbath, nearly the whole city came together to hear the word of the Lord.

verses.name: Acts 13:45
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> the Jews saw the crowds, they were filled with jealousy, and began contradicting what was being said by Paul by<note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“reviling”) which is understood as means</note> reviling him.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Acts 13:46
verses.text: Both Paul and Barnabas spoke boldly <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“spoke boldly”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “It was necessary <transChange type="added">that</transChange> the word of God be spoken first to you, since you reject it and do not consider yourselves worthy of eternal life! Behold, we are turning to the Gentiles!

verses.name: Acts 13:47
verses.text: For so the Lord has commanded us: <div eID="gen26903" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen26904"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26905"/>‘I have appointed you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to be⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for”</note> a light for the Gentiles,<l eID="gen26905" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26906"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞that you would bring⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “that you would bring”</note> salvation to the end of the earth.’<note placement="foot">An allusion to <reference osisRef="Isa.42.6">Isa 42:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.49.6">49:6</reference></note> <l eID="gen26906" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen26904"/>

verses.name: Acts 13:48
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11398"/><div sID="gen26907" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11398"/>And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> the Gentiles heard this,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> they began to rejoice<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to rejoice”)</note> and to glorify the word of the Lord. And all those who were designated for eternal life believed.

verses.name: Acts 13:49
verses.text: So the word of the Lord was carried through the whole region.

verses.name: Acts 13:50
verses.text: But the Jews incited the devout women of high social standing and the most prominent men of the city, and stirred up persecution against Paul and Barnabas and threw them out of their district.

verses.name: Acts 13:51
verses.text: So <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“shaking off”) which is understood as temporal</note> shaking off the dust from <transChange type="added">their</transChange> feet against them, they went to Iconium.

verses.name: Acts 13:52
verses.text: And the disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.  <chapter eID="Acts.13"/>

verses.name: Acts 14:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11399"/><title type="x-s">Preaching in Iconium</title> <div sID="gen26908" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11399"/>Now it happened that in Iconium they entered <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞together⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “according to the same”</note> into the synagogue of the Jews and spoke in such a way that a large number of both Jews and Greeks believed.

verses.name: Acts 14:2
verses.text: But the Jews who were disobedient stirred up and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞poisoned the minds⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “embittered the souls”</note> of the Gentiles against the brothers.

verses.name: Acts 14:3
verses.text: So they stayed <transChange type="added">there</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> for a considerable time, speaking boldly for the Lord, who testified to the message of his grace, granting signs and wonders to be performed through their hands.

verses.name: Acts 14:4
verses.text: But the population of the city was divided, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞some⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “those on the one hand”</note> were with the Jews <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞and some⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “those on the other hand”</note> with the apostles.

verses.name: Acts 14:5
verses.text: So when an inclination took place <transChange type="added">on the part</transChange> of both the Gentiles and the Jews, together with their rulers, to mistreat <transChange type="added">them</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and to stone them,

verses.name: Acts 14:6
verses.text: they became aware of <transChange type="added">it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“became aware of”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> fled to the Lycaonian cities—Lystra and Derbe and the surrounding region.

verses.name: Acts 14:7
verses.text: And there they were continuing to proclaim the good news.  <div eID="gen26908" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 14:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11400"/><title type="x-s">Mistaken for Gods in Lystra</title> <div sID="gen26909" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11400"/>And in Lystra a certain man was sitting powerless in his feet, lame from <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞birth⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “his mother’s womb”</note> who had never walked.

verses.name: Acts 14:9
verses.text: This man listened <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was speaking”)</note> Paul was speaking. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Paul⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “who”</note> looking intently at him and seeing that he had faith to be healed,

verses.name: Acts 14:10
verses.text: said with a loud voice, “Stand upright on your feet!” And he leaped up and began walking.<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began walking”)</note>

verses.name: Acts 14:11
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> the crowds saw what Paul had done, they raised their voices in the Lycaonian language, saying, “The gods have become like men and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“have become like”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> have come down to us!”

verses.name: Acts 14:12
verses.text: And they began calling<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began calling”)</note> Barnabas Zeus and Paul Hermes, because he was the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞principal speaker⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “leader of the message”</note>

verses.name: Acts 14:13
verses.text: And the priest of the <transChange type="added">temple</transChange><note placement="foot">*The word “temple” is not in the Greek text but is implied</note> of Zeus that was just outside the city brought bulls and garlands to the gates and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“brought”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> was wanting to offer sacrifice, along with the crowds.

verses.name: Acts 14:14
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard about”) which is understood as temporal</note> the apostles Barnabas and Paul heard about it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> they tore their clothing and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“tore”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> rushed out into the crowd, shouting

verses.name: Acts 14:15
verses.text: and saying, “Men, why are you doing these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>? We also are men with the same nature as you, proclaiming the good news <transChange type="added">that</transChange> you should turn from these worthless things to the living God, who made the heaven and the earth and the sea and all the things <transChange type="added">that are</transChange> in them—

verses.name: Acts 14:16
verses.text: who in generations that are past permitted all the nations<note placement="foot">Or “Gentiles”; the same Greek word can be translated “nations” or “Gentiles” depending on the context</note> to go their <transChange type="added">own</transChange> ways.

verses.name: Acts 14:17
verses.text: And yet he did not leave himself without witness <transChange type="added">by</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“doing good”) which is understood as means</note> doing good, giving you rain from heaven and fruitful seasons, satisfying you<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> with food and your hearts with gladness.”

verses.name: Acts 14:18
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">although</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“said”) which is understood as concessive</note> they said these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, <transChange type="added">only</transChange> with difficulty did they dissuade the crowds from offering sacrifice to them.  <div eID="gen26909" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 14:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11401"/><div sID="gen26910" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11401"/>But Jews arrived from Antioch and Iconium, and <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had won over”) which is understood as temporal</note> had won over the crowds and stoned Paul, they dragged him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> outside the city, thinking he was dead.

verses.name: Acts 14:20
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“surrounded”)</note> the disciples surrounded him, he got up and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“got up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> went into the city. And on the next day he departed with Barnabas for Derbe.  <div eID="gen26910" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 14:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11402"/><title type="x-s">Paul and Barnabas Return to Antioch in Syria</title> <div sID="gen26911" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11402"/>And <transChange type="added">after they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had proclaimed the good news”) which is understood as temporal</note> had proclaimed the good news in that city and made many disciples, they returned to Lystra and to Iconium and to Antioch,

verses.name: Acts 14:22
verses.text: strengthening the souls of the disciples, encouraging <transChange type="added">them</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to continue in the faith and saying,<note placement="foot">*The word “saying” is not in the Greek text but is implied</note> “Through many persecutions<note placement="foot">Or “afflictions”</note> it is necessary <transChange type="added">for</transChange> us to enter into the kingdom of God.”

verses.name: Acts 14:23
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had appointed”) which is understood as temporal</note> had appointed elders for them in every church, after<note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“praying”) which is understood as temporal</note> praying with fasting, they entrusted them to the Lord, in whom they had believed.

verses.name: Acts 14:24
verses.text: And they passed through Pisidia <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“passed through”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> came to Pamphylia.

verses.name: Acts 14:25
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“proclaimed”) which is understood as temporal</note> they proclaimed the message in Perga, they went down to Attalia,

verses.name: Acts 14:26
verses.text: and from there they sailed away to Antioch where they had been commended to the grace of God for the work that they had completed.

verses.name: Acts 14:27
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“arrived”) which is understood as temporal</note> arrived and called the church together, they reported all that God had done with them, and that he had opened a door of faith for the Gentiles.<note placement="foot">Or “nations”; the same Greek word can be translated “nations” or “Gentiles” depending on the context</note>

verses.name: Acts 14:28
verses.text: And they stayed no little time with the disciples.  <chapter eID="Acts.14"/>

verses.name: Acts 15:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11403"/><title type="x-s">The Jerusalem Council</title> <div sID="gen26912" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11403"/>And some men came down from Judea <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came down”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> began teaching<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began teaching”)</note> the brothers, “Unless you are circumcised according to the custom <transChange type="added">prescribed</transChange> by Moses, you cannot be saved.”

verses.name: Acts 15:2
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was”)</note> there was no little strife and debate by Paul and Barnabas against them, they appointed Paul and Barnabas and some others from among them to go up to the apostles and elders in Jerusalem concerning this issue.

verses.name: Acts 15:3
verses.text: So they were sent on their way by the church, <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“were sent on their way”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> passed through both Phoenicia and Samaria, telling in detail the conversion of the Gentiles and bringing great joy to all the brothers.

verses.name: Acts 15:4
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“arrived”) which is understood as temporal</note> arrived in Jerusalem, they were received by the church and the apostles and the elders, and reported all that God had done with them.

verses.name: Acts 15:5
verses.text: But some of those who had believed from the party of the Pharisees stood up, saying, “It is necessary to circumcise them and to command <transChange type="added">them</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to observe the law of Moses!”  <div eID="gen26912" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 15:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11404"/><div sID="gen26913" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11404"/>Both the apostles and the elders assembled to deliberate concerning this matter.

verses.name: Acts 15:7
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was”)</note> there was much debate, Peter stood up and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“stood up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to them, “Men and brothers, you know that in the early days<note placement="foot">Or “from ancient days”</note> God chose among you through my mouth <transChange type="added">that</transChange> the Gentiles should hear the message of the gospel and believe.

verses.name: Acts 15:8
verses.text: And God, who knows the heart, testified to them <transChange type="added">by</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“giving”) which is understood as means</note> giving them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> the Holy Spirit, just as he also <transChange type="added">did</transChange> to us.

verses.name: Acts 15:9
verses.text: And he made no distinction between us and them, cleansing their hearts by faith.

verses.name: Acts 15:10
verses.text: So now why are you putting God to the test <transChange type="added">by</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the infinitive (“placing”) which is understood as means</note> placing on the neck of the disciples a yoke that neither our fathers nor we have been able to bear?

verses.name: Acts 15:11
verses.text: But we believe <transChange type="added">we</transChange> will be saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus in <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the same⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “which”</note> way those also <transChange type="added">are</transChange>.”

verses.name: Acts 15:12
verses.text: And the whole group became silent and listened to Barnabas and Paul describing all the signs and wonders God had done among the Gentiles through them.

verses.name: Acts 15:13
verses.text: And after they had stopped speaking, James answered, saying, “Men <transChange type="added">and</transChange> brothers, listen to me!

verses.name: Acts 15:14
verses.text: Simeon has described how God first concerned himself to take from among the Gentiles a people for his name.

verses.name: Acts 15:15
verses.text: And with this the words of the prophets agree, just as it is written:  <div eID="gen26913" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 15:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11405"/><lg sID="gen26914"/> <l level="1" sID="gen26915"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11405"/>‘After these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> I will return<l eID="gen26915" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26916"/>and build up again the tent of David that has fallen,<l eID="gen26916" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26917"/>and the <transChange type="added">parts</transChange> of it that had been torn down I will build up again<l eID="gen26917" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26918"/>and will restore it, <l eID="gen26918" level="2"/>

verses.name: Acts 15:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11406"/><l level="1" sID="gen26919"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11406"/>so that the rest of humanity may seek the Lord,<l eID="gen26919" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26920"/>even all the Gentiles<note placement="foot">The same Greek word can be translated “nations” or “Gentiles” depending on the context</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who are called by my name⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “on whom my name has been called on them”</note><l eID="gen26920" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen26921"/>says the Lord,<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Amos.9.11-Amos.9.12">Amos 9:11–12</reference></note> who makes these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>

verses.name: Acts 15:18
verses.text: known from of old.’<note placement="foot">The last phrase of v. <reference osisRef="Acts.15.17">17</reference> and all of v. <reference osisRef="Acts.15.18">18</reference> is an allusion to <reference osisRef="Isa.45.21">Isa 45:21</reference></note> <l eID="gen26921" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen26914"/>

verses.name: Acts 15:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11407"/><div sID="gen26922" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11407"/>Therefore I conclude we should not cause difficulty for those from among the Gentiles who turn to God,

verses.name: Acts 15:20
verses.text: but we should write a letter to them to abstain from the pollution of idols and from sexual immorality and from what has been strangled and from blood.

verses.name: Acts 15:21
verses.text: For Moses has those who proclaim him in every city from ancient generations, <transChange type="added">because he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“is read aloud”) which is understood as causal</note> is read aloud in the synagogues on every Sabbath.”  <div eID="gen26922" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 15:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11408"/><title type="x-s">The Letter from the Council</title> <div sID="gen26923" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11408"/>Then it seemed best to the apostles and the elders, together with the whole church, to send men chosen from among them to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas—Judas who was called Barsabbas and Silas, men <transChange type="added">who were</transChange> leaders among the brothers—

verses.name: Acts 15:23
verses.text: writing <transChange type="added">this letter</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to be delivered by them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>:<note placement="foot">Literally “by their hand”</note> <div eID="gen26923" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen26924" type="x-p"/> The apostles and the elders, brothers. <div eID="gen26924" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen26925" type="x-p"/> To the brothers <transChange type="added">who are</transChange> from among the Gentiles in Antioch and Syria and Cilicia. <block> <div eID="gen26925" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen26926" type="x-p"/> Greetings!  <div eID="gen26926" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 15:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11409"/><div sID="gen26927" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11409"/>Because we have heard that some have gone out from among us—to whom we gave no orders—<transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“have gone out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> have thrown you into confusion by words upsetting your <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞minds⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “souls”</note>

verses.name: Acts 15:25
verses.text: it seemed best to us, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞having reached a unanimous decision⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “having become of one mind”</note> and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied in keeping with English style</note> having chosen men, to send them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to you together with our dear friends Barnabas and Paul,

verses.name: Acts 15:26
verses.text: men who have risked their lives on behalf of the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.name: Acts 15:27
verses.text: Therefore we have sent Judas and Silas, and they will report the same <transChange type="added">things</transChange> by word of mouth.

verses.name: Acts 15:28
verses.text: For it seemed best to the Holy Spirit and to us to place on you no greater burden except these necessary things:

verses.name: Acts 15:29
verses.text: <transChange type="added">that you</transChange> abstain from food sacrificed to idols, and from blood, and from what has been strangled, and from sexual immorality. <transChange type="added">If you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “if” is supplied as a component of the participle (“keep”) which is understood as conditional</note> keep yourselves from <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞these things⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “which things”</note> you will do well. <div eID="gen26927" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen26928" type="x-p"/> Farewell. </block>  <div eID="gen26928" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 15:30
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11410"/><title type="x-s">The Letter Is Delivered to Antioch</title> <div sID="gen26929" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11410"/>So <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“were sent off”) which is understood as temporal</note> they were sent off, they came down to Antioch, and after<note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“calling together”) which is understood as temporal</note> calling together the community, they delivered the letter.

verses.name: Acts 15:31
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“read … aloud”) which is understood as temporal</note> read it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> aloud, they rejoiced at the encouragement.

verses.name: Acts 15:32
verses.text: Both Judas and Silas, who were also prophets themselves, encouraged and strengthened the brothers by a long message.

verses.name: Acts 15:33
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“spending”) which is understood as temporal</note> spending some time, they were sent away in peace from the brothers to those who had sent them.<note placement="foot">A few later manuscripts add v. <reference osisRef="Acts.15.34">34</reference>, “But Silas decided to stay there.”</note>

verses.name: Acts 15:35
verses.text: But Paul and Barnabas remained in Antioch teaching and proclaiming the word of the Lord with many others also.  <div eID="gen26929" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 15:36
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11411"/><title type="x-s">Paul and Barnabas Disagree and Part Company</title> <div sID="gen26930" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11411"/>And after some days, Paul said to Barnabas, “Come then,<transChange type="added">let us</transChange> return <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“return”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> visit the brothers in every town in which we proclaimed the word of the Lord, <transChange type="added">to see</transChange> how they are <transChange type="added">doing</transChange>.”

verses.name: Acts 15:37
verses.text: Now Barnabas wanted to take John who was called Mark along also,

verses.name: Acts 15:38
verses.text: but Paul held the opinion they should not take this one along, who departed from them in Pamphylia and did not accompany them in the work.

verses.name: Acts 15:39
verses.text: And a sharp disagreement took place, so that they separated from one another. And Barnabas took along Mark <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took along”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> sailed away to Cyprus,

verses.name: Acts 15:40
verses.text: but Paul chose Silas <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“chose”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> departed, after<note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“being commended”) which is understood as temporal</note> being commended to the grace of the Lord by the brothers.

verses.name: Acts 15:41
verses.text: And he traveled through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches.  <chapter eID="Acts.15"/>

verses.name: Acts 16:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11412"/><title type="x-s">Timothy Accompanies Paul and Silas</title> <div sID="gen26931" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11412"/>And he came also to Derbe and to Lystra. And behold, a certain disciple was there <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞named⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by name”</note> Timothy, the son of a believing Jewish woman but of a Greek father,

verses.name: Acts 16:2
verses.text: who was well spoken of by the brothers in Lystra and Iconium.

verses.name: Acts 16:3
verses.text: Paul wanted this one to go with him, and he took <transChange type="added">him</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> circumcised him because of the Jews who were in those places, for <transChange type="added">they</transChange> all knew that his father was Greek.

verses.name: Acts 16:4
verses.text: And as they went through the towns, they passed on to them to observe the rules that had been decided by the apostles and elders <transChange type="added">who were</transChange> in Jerusalem.

verses.name: Acts 16:5
verses.text: So the churches were being strengthened in the faith and were growing in number every day.  <div eID="gen26931" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 16:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11413"/><title type="x-s">Paul’s Vision of a Man of Macedonia</title> <div sID="gen26932" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11413"/>And they traveled through the Phrygian and Galatian region, having been prevented by the Holy Spirit from speaking the message in Asia.<note placement="foot">A reference to the Roman province of Asia (modern Asia Minor)</note>

verses.name: Acts 16:7
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“came”) which is understood as temporal</note> came to Mysia, they attempted to go into Bithynia, and the Spirit of Jesus did not permit them.

verses.name: Acts 16:8
verses.text: So going through Mysia, they went down to Troas.

verses.name: Acts 16:9
verses.text: And a vision appeared to Paul during the night: a certain Macedonian man was standing there and imploring him and saying, “Come over to Macedonia <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“come over”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> help us!”

verses.name: Acts 16:10
verses.text: And when he had seen the vision, we wanted at once to go away to Macedonia, concluding that God had called us to proclaim the good news to them.  <div eID="gen26932" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 16:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11414"/><title type="x-s">The Conversion of Lydia at Philippi</title> <div sID="gen26933" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11414"/>So putting out to sea from Troas, we sailed a straight course to Samothrace, and on the following <transChange type="added">day</transChange> to Neapolis,

verses.name: Acts 16:12
verses.text: and from there to Philippi, which is a leading city <transChange type="added">of that</transChange> district of Macedonia, a <transChange type="added">Roman</transChange> colony. And we were staying in this city for some days.

verses.name: Acts 16:13
verses.text: And on the day of the Sabbath, we went outside the <transChange type="added">city</transChange> gate beside the river, where we thought there was a place of prayer, and we sat down <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“sat down”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> spoke to the women assembled <transChange type="added">there</transChange>.

verses.name: Acts 16:14
verses.text: And a certain woman <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞named⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by name”</note> Lydia from the city of Thyatira, a merchant dealing in purple cloth who showed reverence for God, was listening. The Lord opened <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞her⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “whose”</note> heart to pay attention to what was being said by Paul.

verses.name: Acts 16:15
verses.text: And after she was baptized, and her household, she urged <transChange type="added">us</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> saying, “If you consider me to be a believer in the Lord, come to my house and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“come”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> stay.” And she prevailed upon us.  <div eID="gen26933" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 16:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11415"/><title type="x-s">Paul and Silas Imprisoned</title> <div sID="gen26934" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11415"/>And it happened that <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“were going”)</note> we were going to the place of prayer, a certain female slave who had a spirit of divination<note placement="foot">Literally “a spirit of Python”; Python was the name of the serpent or dragon that guarded the Delphic oracle at the foot of Mt. Parnassus and the word eventually came to be used for a spirit of divination</note> met us, who was bringing a large profit to her owners by<note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the infinitive (“fortune-telling”) which is understood as means</note> fortune-telling.

verses.name: Acts 16:17
verses.text: She followed Paul and us <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“followed”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> was crying out, saying, “These men are slaves of the Most High God, who are proclaiming to you the way of salvation!”

verses.name: Acts 16:18
verses.text: And she was doing this for many days. But Paul, becoming greatly annoyed and turning around, said to the spirit, “I command you in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her!” And it came out <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞immediately⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “that same hour”</note>  <div eID="gen26934" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 16:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11416"/><div sID="gen26935" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11416"/>But <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> her owners saw that their hope of profit was gone, they seized Paul and Silas and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“seized”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> dragged them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> into the marketplace before the rulers.

verses.name: Acts 16:20
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had brought”) which is understood as temporal</note> had brought them to the chief magistrates, they said, “These men are throwing our city into confusion, being Jews,

verses.name: Acts 16:21
verses.text: and are proclaiming customs that are not permitted for us to accept or to practice, <transChange type="added">because we</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“are”) which is understood as causal</note> are Romans!”

verses.name: Acts 16:22
verses.text: And the crowd joined in attacking them, and the chief magistrates tore off their clothing <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“tore off”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> gave orders to beat them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> with rods.

verses.name: Acts 16:23
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had inflicted”) which is understood as temporal</note> had inflicted many blows on them, they threw them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> into prison, giving orders to the jailer to guard them securely.

verses.name: Acts 16:24
verses.text: Having received such an order, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “who”</note> put them in the inner prison and fastened their feet in the stocks.<note placement="foot">Or possibly “to the block of wood,” referring to a log to which the prisoners were chained or tied</note>  <div eID="gen26935" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 16:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11417"/><title type="x-s">The Conversion of the Philippian Jailer</title> <div sID="gen26936" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11417"/>Now about midnight, Paul and Silas were praying <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“were praying”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> singing hymns to God, and the prisoners were listening to them.

verses.name: Acts 16:26
verses.text: And suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken. And immediately all the doors were opened and all the bonds<note placement="foot">Or “chains”</note> were unfastened.

verses.name: Acts 16:27
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was”) which is understood as temporal</note> the jailer was awake and saw the doors of the prison open, he drew his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> sword and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“drew”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> was about to kill himself, because he<note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“thought”) which is understood as causal</note> thought the prisoners had escaped.

verses.name: Acts 16:28
verses.text: But Paul called out with a loud voice, saying, “Do no harm to yourself, for we are all here!”

verses.name: Acts 16:29
verses.text: And demanding lights, he rushed in and, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞beginning to tremble⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “became trembling”</note> fell down at the feet of Paul and Silas.

verses.name: Acts 16:30
verses.text: And he brought them outside <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“brought”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “Sirs, what must I do so that I can be saved?”

verses.name: Acts 16:31
verses.text: And they said, “Believe in the Lord Jesus and you will be saved, you and your household!”

verses.name: Acts 16:32
verses.text: And they spoke the message of the Lord to him, together with all those in his house.

verses.name: Acts 16:33
verses.text: And he took them at that <transChange type="added">very</transChange> hour of the night <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> washed their<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> wounds, and he himself was baptized at once, and all those of his household.<note placement="foot">*The word “household” is not in the Greek text, but is supplied from the previous verse</note>

verses.name: Acts 16:34
verses.text: And he brought them up into <transChange type="added">his</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> house and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“brought … up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> set a meal before them,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and rejoiced greatly that he had believed in God with his whole household.  <div eID="gen26936" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 16:35
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11418"/><title type="x-s">Paul and Silas Receive an Official Apology</title> <div sID="gen26937" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11418"/>And <transChange type="added">when it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was”)</note> was day, the chief magistrates sent the police officers, saying, “Release those men.”

verses.name: Acts 16:36
verses.text: And the jailer reported these words to Paul: “The chief magistrates have sent <transChange type="added">an order</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> that you should be released. So come out now and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“come out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> go in peace!”

verses.name: Acts 16:37
verses.text: But Paul said to them, “They beat us in public without due process—men who are Roman citizens—<transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“beat”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> threw us<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> into prison, and now they are wanting to release us secretly? Certainly not! Rather let them come themselves and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“come”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> bring us out!”

verses.name: Acts 16:38
verses.text: So the police officers reported these words to the chief magistrates, and they were afraid <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard that they were Roman citizens.

verses.name: Acts 16:39
verses.text: And they came <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> apologized to<note placement="foot">Or “reassured”; or “conciliated”</note> them, and after they<note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“brought … out”) which is understood as temporal</note> brought them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> out they asked them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to depart from the city.

verses.name: Acts 16:40
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“came out”) which is understood as temporal</note> came out of the prison, they went to Lydia and when they<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw them,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> they encouraged the brothers and departed.  <chapter eID="Acts.16"/>

verses.name: Acts 17:1
