verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11419"/><title type="x-s">Attacked by a Mob in Thessalonica</title> <div sID="gen26938" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11419"/>Now <transChange type="added">after they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“traveled through”) which is understood as temporal</note> traveled through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a synagogue of the Jews.

verses.name: Acts 17:2
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞And as was his custom⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “and in accordance with what he was accustomed to”</note> Paul went in to them and on three Sabbath <transChange type="added">days</transChange> he discussed with them from the scriptures,

verses.name: Acts 17:3
verses.text: explaining and demonstrating that it was necessary <transChange type="added">for</transChange> the Christ<note placement="foot">Or “Messiah”</note> to suffer and to rise from the dead, and saying, “This Jesus whom I am proclaiming to you is the Christ.”<note placement="foot">Or “Messiah”</note>

verses.name: Acts 17:4
verses.text: And some of them were persuaded and joined Paul and Silas, and <transChange type="added">also</transChange> a large number of God-fearing Greeks and not a few of the prominent women.  <div eID="gen26938" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 17:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11420"/><div sID="gen26939" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11420"/>But the Jews were filled with jealousy and, taking along some worthless men from the rabble in the marketplace and forming a mob, threw the city into an uproar. And attacking Jason’s house, they were looking for them to bring <transChange type="added">them</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> out to the popular assembly.

verses.name: Acts 17:6
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“find”) which is understood as temporal</note> did not find them, they dragged Jason and some brothers before the city officials, shouting, “These people who have stirred up trouble throughout the world<note placement="foot">Or “empire”</note> have come here also,

verses.name: Acts 17:7
verses.text: whom Jason has entertained as guests! And these <transChange type="added">people</transChange> <transChange type="added">are</transChange> all acting contrary to the decrees of Caesar, saying there is another king, Jesus!”

verses.name: Acts 17:8
verses.text: And they threw the crowd into confusion, and the city officials who heard these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>.

verses.name: Acts 17:9
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“taking”) which is understood as temporal</note> taking money as security from Jason and the rest, they released them.  <div eID="gen26939" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 17:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11421"/><title type="x-s">Paul and Silas in Berea</title> <div sID="gen26940" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11421"/>Now the brothers sent away both Paul and Silas at once, during the night, to Berea. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞They⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “who” (referring to Paul and Silas)</note> went into the synagogue of the Jews when they<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“arrived”) which is understood as temporal</note> arrived.

verses.name: Acts 17:11
verses.text: Now these were more open-minded than those in Thessalonica. <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞They⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “who”</note> accepted the message with all eagerness, examining the scriptures every day <transChange type="added">to see</transChange> if these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> were so.

verses.name: Acts 17:12
verses.text: Therefore many of them believed, and not a few of the prominent Greek women and men.

verses.name: Acts 17:13
verses.text: But when the Jews from Thessalonica found out that the message of God had been proclaimed by Paul in Berea also, they came there too, inciting and stirring up the crowds.

verses.name: Acts 17:14
verses.text: So then the brothers sent Paul away at once to go to the sea, and both Silas and Timothy remained there.

verses.name: Acts 17:15
verses.text: And those who conducted Paul brought <transChange type="added">him</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> as far as Athens, and after<note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“receiving”) which is understood as temporal</note> receiving an order for Silas and Timothy that they should come to him as soon as possible, they went away.  <div eID="gen26940" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 17:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11422"/><title type="x-s">Paul in Athens</title> <div sID="gen26941" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11422"/>Now while Paul was waiting for them in Athens, his spirit was provoked within him <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“observed”) which is understood as temporal</note> observed the city was full of idols.

verses.name: Acts 17:17
verses.text: So he was discussing in the synagogue with the Jews and the God-fearing <transChange type="added">Gentiles</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the word “Gentiles” is not in the Greek text but is implied</note> and in the marketplace every day with those who happened to be there.

verses.name: Acts 17:18
verses.text: And even some of the Epicurean and Stoic philosophers were conversing with him, and some were saying, “What does this babbler want to say?” But <transChange type="added">others said</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*The words “others said” are not in the Greek text but are implied</note> “He appears to be a proclaimer of foreign deities,” because he was proclaiming the good news <transChange type="added">about</transChange> Jesus and the resurrection.

verses.name: Acts 17:19
verses.text: And they took hold of him <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took hold of”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> brought him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to the Areopagus, saying, “May we learn what <transChange type="added">is</transChange> this new teaching being proclaimed by you?

verses.name: Acts 17:20
verses.text: For you are bringing some astonishing things to our ears. Therefore we want to know what <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞these things mean⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “these things want to be”</note>

verses.name: Acts 17:21
verses.text: (Now all the Athenians and the foreigners who stayed there used to spend <transChange type="added">their</transChange> time in nothing else than telling something or listening to something new.)  <div eID="gen26941" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 17:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11423"/><title type="x-s">Paul Speaks to the Areopagus</title> <div sID="gen26942" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11423"/>So Paul stood there in the middle of the Areopagus <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“stood there”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “Men of Athens, I see you are very religious <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in every respect⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “with respect to all things”</note>

verses.name: Acts 17:23
verses.text: For <transChange type="added">as I</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was passing through”) which is understood as temporal</note> was passing through and observing carefully your objects of worship, I even found an altar on which was inscribed, ‘To an unknown God.’ Therefore what you worship without knowing it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> this I proclaim to you—

verses.name: Acts 17:24
verses.text: the God who made the world and all the things in it. This one, being Lord of heaven and earth, does not live in temples made by human hands,

verses.name: Acts 17:25
verses.text: nor is he served by human hands <transChange type="added">as if he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as if” is supplied as a component of the conditional adverbial participle (“needed”)</note> needed anything, because<note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“gives”) which is understood as causal</note> he himself gives to everyone life and breath and everything.

verses.name: Acts 17:26
verses.text: And he made from one <transChange type="added">man</transChange> every nation of humanity to live on all the face of the earth, determining <transChange type="added">their</transChange> fixed times and the fixed boundaries of their habitation,

verses.name: Acts 17:27
verses.text: to search for God, if perhaps indeed they might feel around for him and find <transChange type="added">him</transChange>.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> And indeed he is not far away from each one of us,

verses.name: Acts 17:28
verses.text: for in him we live and move and exist,<note placement="foot">Some interpreters hold that the phrase “in him we live and move and exist” is a quotation from Epimenides of Crete, but more likely it is a traditional Greek formula</note> as even some of <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞your own⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “with respect to you”</note> poets have said: ‘For we also are <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “of him”</note> offspring.’<note placement="foot">A quotation from Aratus, <hi type="italic">Phaenomena</hi> 5</note>

verses.name: Acts 17:29
verses.text: Therefore, <transChange type="added">because we</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“are”) which is understood as causal</note> are offspring of God, we ought not to think the divine being is like gold or silver or stone, an image formed by human skill and thought.

verses.name: Acts 17:30
verses.text: Therefore <transChange type="added">although</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“has overlooked”) which is understood as concessive</note> God has overlooked the times of ignorance, he now commands all people everywhere to repent,

verses.name: Acts 17:31
verses.text: because he has set a day on which he is going to judge the world in righteousness by the man who he has appointed, having provided proof to everyone <transChange type="added">by</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“raising”) which is understood as means</note> raising him from the dead.”

verses.name: Acts 17:32
verses.text: Now <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard about”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard about the resurrection of the dead, <transChange type="added">some</transChange> scoffed, but <transChange type="added">others</transChange> said, “We will hear you about this again also.”

verses.name: Acts 17:33
verses.text: So Paul went out from the midst of them.

verses.name: Acts 17:34
verses.text: But some people<note placement="foot">*Here the Greek term “men” is used as a generic for “people”; note the presence of of a woman (Damaris) in the group</note> joined him and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“joined”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> believed, among whom also were Dionysius the Areopagite and a woman <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞named⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by name”</note> Damaris and others with them.  <chapter eID="Acts.17"/>

verses.name: Acts 18:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11424"/><title type="x-s">Paul, Silas, and Timothy in Corinth</title> <div sID="gen26943" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11424"/>After these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> he departed from Athens <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“departed”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> went to Corinth.

verses.name: Acts 18:2
verses.text: And he found a certain Jew <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞named⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by name”</note> Aquila, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a native⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by nationality”</note> of Pontus who had arrived recently from Italy <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞along with⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “and”</note> Priscilla his wife, because Claudius had ordered all the Jews to depart from Rome, and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“found”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> he went to them.

verses.name: Acts 18:3
verses.text: And because <transChange type="added">he</transChange> was practicing the same trade, he stayed with them and worked, for they were tentmakers by trade.

verses.name: Acts 18:4
verses.text: And he argued in the synagogue every Sabbath, attempting to persuade<note placement="foot">*Here the imperfect verb has been translated as conative (“attempting to persuade”)</note> both Jews and Greeks.  <div eID="gen26943" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 18:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11425"/><div sID="gen26944" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11425"/>Now when both Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia, Paul began to be occupied with<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to be occupied with”)</note> the message, solemnly testifying to the Jews that the Christ<note placement="foot">Or “Messiah”</note> was Jesus.

verses.name: Acts 18:6
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“resisted”)</note> they resisted and reviled him,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> he shook out his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> clothes and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“shook out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to them, “Your blood <transChange type="added">be</transChange> on your <transChange type="added">own</transChange> heads! I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> guiltless! From now on I will go to the Gentiles!”

verses.name: Acts 18:7
verses.text: And leaving there, he entered into the house of someone <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞named⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by name”</note> Titius Justus, a worshiper<note placement="foot">Or “a God-fearer”</note> of God whose house was next door to the synagogue.

verses.name: Acts 18:8
verses.text: And Crispus, the ruler of the synagogue, believed in the Lord together with his whole household. And many of the Corinthians, <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard about”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard about it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> believed and were baptized.

verses.name: Acts 18:9
verses.text: And the Lord said to Paul by a vision in the night, “Do not be afraid, but speak and do not keep silent,

verses.name: Acts 18:10
verses.text: because I am with you and no one will attack you to harm you, because many people are mine in this city.”

verses.name: Acts 18:11
verses.text: So he stayed a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.  <div eID="gen26944" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 18:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11426"/><title type="x-s">Paul Accused Before the Proconsul Gallio</title> <div sID="gen26945" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11426"/>Now <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was”)</note> Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews rose up with one purpose against Paul and brought him before the judgment seat,

verses.name: Acts 18:13
verses.text: saying, “This man is persuading people to worship God contrary to the law!”

verses.name: Acts 18:14
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was about”)</note> Paul was about to open his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> mouth, Gallio said to the Jews, “If it was some crime or wicked villainy, O Jews, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I would have been justified in accepting⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “with respect to a motive I would have accepted”</note> your complaint.

verses.name: Acts 18:15
verses.text: But if it is questions concerning a word and names and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞your own law⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “the according to you law”</note> see to it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> yourselves! I do not wish to be a judge of these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>.”

verses.name: Acts 18:16
verses.text: And he drove them away from the judgment seat.

verses.name: Acts 18:17
verses.text: So they all seized Sosthenes, the ruler of the synagogue, <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“seized”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> began beating<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began beating”)</note> him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> in front of the judgment seat. And none of these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> was a concern to Gallio.  <div eID="gen26945" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 18:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11427"/><title type="x-s">Paul Returns to Antioch in Syria</title> <div sID="gen26946" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11427"/>So Paul, <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“remaining”) which is understood as temporal</note> remaining many days longer, said farewell to the brothers and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“said farewell”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> sailed away to Syria, and with him Priscilla and Aquila. He shaved his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> head at Cenchrea, because he had <transChange type="added">taken</transChange> a vow.

verses.name: Acts 18:19
verses.text: So they arrived at Ephesus, and those he left behind there, but he himself entered into the synagogue <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“entered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> discussed with the Jews.

verses.name: Acts 18:20
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“asked”)</note> they asked him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to stay for a longer time, he did not give his consent,

verses.name: Acts 18:21
verses.text: but saying farewell and telling <transChange type="added">them</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> “I will return to you again if<note placement="foot">*Here “if” is supplied as a component of the conditional adverbial participle (“wills”)</note> God wills,” he set sail from Ephesus.  <div eID="gen26946" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 18:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11428"/><div sID="gen26947" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11428"/>And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“arrived”) which is understood as temporal</note> arrived at Caesarea, he went up and greeted the church, and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the two previous participles (“went up” and “greeted”) have been translated as finite verbs</note> went down to Antioch.

verses.name: Acts 18:23
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“spending”) which is understood as temporal</note> spending some time <transChange type="added">there</transChange>, he departed, traveling through one <transChange type="added">place</transChange> after another <transChange type="added">in</transChange> the Galatian region and Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples.  <div eID="gen26947" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 18:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11429"/><title type="x-s">The Early Ministry of Apollos</title> <div sID="gen26948" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11429"/>Now a certain Jew <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞named⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by name”</note> Apollos, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a native⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by nationality”</note> Alexandrian, arrived in Ephesus—an eloquent man who was well-versed in the scriptures.

verses.name: Acts 18:25
verses.text: This man had been instructed <transChange type="added">in</transChange> the way of the Lord, and being enthusiastic in spirit, he was speaking and teaching accurately the <transChange type="added">things</transChange> about Jesus, <transChange type="added">although he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“knew”) which is understood as concessive</note> knew only the baptism of John.

verses.name: Acts 18:26
verses.text: And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue, but <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him aside and explained the way of God to him more accurately.

verses.name: Acts 18:27
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“wanted”)</note> he wanted to cross over to Achaia, the brothers encouraged him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“encouraged”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> wrote to the disciples to welcome him. When he<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“arrived”) which is understood as temporal</note> arrived, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “who”</note> assisted greatly those who had believed through grace.

verses.name: Acts 18:28
verses.text: For he was vigorously refuting the Jews in public, demonstrating through the scriptures <transChange type="added">that</transChange> the Christ<note placement="foot">Or “Messiah”</note> was Jesus.  <chapter eID="Acts.18"/>

verses.name: Acts 19:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11430"/><title type="x-s">Paul Finds Disciples of John the Baptist in Ephesus</title> <div sID="gen26949" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11430"/>And it happened that <transChange type="added">while</transChange> Apollos was in Corinth, Paul traveled through the inland regions <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“traveled through”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> came<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “and came down”</note> to Ephesus and found some disciples.

verses.name: Acts 19:2
verses.text: And he said to them, “Did you receive the Holy Spirit <transChange type="added">when you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“believed”) which is understood as temporal</note> believed?” And they <transChange type="added">said</transChange> to him, “But we have not even heard that there is a Holy Spirit!”

verses.name: Acts 19:3
verses.text: And he said, “Into what then were you baptized?” And they said, “Into the baptism of John.”

verses.name: Acts 19:4
verses.text: And Paul said, “John baptized <transChange type="added">with</transChange> a baptism of repentance, telling the people that they should believe in the one who was to come after him—that is, in Jesus.”

verses.name: Acts 19:5
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard this,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.

verses.name: Acts 19:6
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“laid”)</note> Paul laid hands<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “placed his hands”</note> on them, the Holy Spirit came upon them and they began to speak<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to speak”)</note> in tongues and to prophesy.

verses.name: Acts 19:7
verses.text: (Now the total <transChange type="added">number</transChange> <transChange type="added">of</transChange> men was about twelve.)  <div eID="gen26949" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 19:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11431"/><div sID="gen26950" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11431"/>So he entered into the synagogue <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“entered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> was speaking boldly for three months, discussing and attempting to convince<note placement="foot">The present tense participle has been translated as a conative present (“attempting to convince”)</note> them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> concerning<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “of the things concerning”</note> the kingdom of God.

verses.name: Acts 19:9
verses.text: But when some became hardened and were disobedient, reviling the Way before the congregation, he departed from them <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“departed”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> took away the disciples, leading discussions every day in the lecture hall of Tyrannus.

verses.name: Acts 19:10
verses.text: And this took place for two years, so that all who lived in Asia<note placement="foot">A reference to the Roman province of Asia (modern Asia Minor)</note> heard the word of the Lord, both Jews and Greeks.  <div eID="gen26950" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 19:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11432"/><title type="x-s">Would-be Exorcists</title> <div sID="gen26951" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11432"/>And God was performing <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞extraordinary⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “not the ordinary”</note> miracles by the hands of Paul,

verses.name: Acts 19:12
verses.text: so that even handkerchiefs or work aprons <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞that had touched his skin⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from his skin”</note> were carried away to those who were sick, and their<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> diseases left them and the evil spirits came out of them.<note placement="foot">*The words “of them” are not in the Greek text but are implied</note>

verses.name: Acts 19:13
verses.text: But some itinerant Jewish exorcists also attempted to pronounce the name of the Lord Jesus over those who had evil spirits, saying, “I adjure you by Jesus whom Paul preaches!”

verses.name: Acts 19:14
verses.text: (Now seven sons of a certain Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, were doing this.)

verses.name: Acts 19:15
verses.text: But the evil spirit answered <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to them, “Jesus I know, and Paul I am acquainted with, but who are you?”

verses.name: Acts 19:16
verses.text: And the man <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who had the evil spirit⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in whom the evil spirit was”</note> leaped on them, subdued all of them, and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the two previous participles (“leaped” and “subdued”) have been translated as finite verbs</note> prevailed against them, so that they ran away from that house naked and wounded.

verses.name: Acts 19:17
verses.text: And this became known to all who lived in Ephesus, both Jews and Greeks, and fear fell upon them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was exalted.

verses.name: Acts 19:18
verses.text: And many of those who had believed came, confessing and disclosing their practices,

verses.name: Acts 19:19
verses.text: and many of those who practiced magic brought together <transChange type="added">their</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> books and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“brought together”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> burned them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> up in the sight of everyone. And they counted up their value and found it was <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞fifty thousand silver coins⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “five ten thousands of silver coins”</note>

verses.name: Acts 19:20
verses.text: In this way the word of the Lord was growing in power and was prevailing.  <div eID="gen26951" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 19:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11433"/><title type="x-s">A Major Riot in Ephesus</title> <div sID="gen26952" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11433"/>Now when these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> were completed, Paul resolved in the Spirit to go to Jerusalem, passing through Macedonia and Achaia, saying, “After I have been there, it is necessary <transChange type="added">for</transChange> me to see Rome also.”

verses.name: Acts 19:22
verses.text: So <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“sending”) which is understood as temporal</note> sending two of those who were assisting him, Timothy and Erastus, to Macedonia, he himself stayed some time in Asia.<note placement="foot">A reference to the Roman province of Asia (modern Asia Minor)</note>  <div eID="gen26952" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 19:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11434"/><div sID="gen26953" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11434"/>Now there happened at that time no little disturbance concerning the Way.

verses.name: Acts 19:24
verses.text: For someone <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞named⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by name”</note> Demetrius, a silversmith who made silver replicas of the temple of Artemis, was bringing no little business to the craftsmen.

verses.name: Acts 19:25
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞These⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “whom”</note> he gathered together, and the workers occupied with such things, and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“gathered together”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “Men, you know that from this business <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞we get our prosperity⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “prosperity is to us”</note>

verses.name: Acts 19:26
verses.text: and you see and hear that not only in Ephesus but in almost all of Asia<note placement="foot">A reference to the Roman province of Asia (modern Asia Minor)</note> this man Paul has persuaded and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“has persuaded”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> turned away a large crowd by<note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saying”) which is understood as means</note> saying that the <transChange type="added">gods</transChange> made by hands are not gods.

verses.name: Acts 19:27
verses.text: So not only is there a danger this line of business of ours <transChange type="added">will</transChange> come into disrepute, but also the temple of the great goddess Artemis <transChange type="added">will</transChange> be regarded as nothing—and <transChange type="added">she</transChange> is about to be brought down even from her grandeur, <transChange type="added">she</transChange> whom the whole <transChange type="added">of</transChange> Asia<note placement="foot">A reference to the Roman province of Asia (modern Asia Minor)</note> and the <transChange type="added">entire</transChange> world worship!”  <div eID="gen26953" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 19:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11435"/><div sID="gen26954" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11435"/>And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard this<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and became full of rage, they began to shout,<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to shout”)</note> saying, “Great <transChange type="added">is</transChange> Artemis of the Ephesians!”

verses.name: Acts 19:29
verses.text: And the city was filled with the tumult, and with one purpose they rushed into the theater, seizing Gaius and Aristarchus, Macedonians <transChange type="added">who were</transChange> traveling companions of Paul.

verses.name: Acts 19:30
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“wanted”)</note> Paul wanted to enter into the popular assembly, the disciples would not let him.

verses.name: Acts 19:31
verses.text: And even some of the Asiarchs<note placement="foot">Or “provincial authorities”</note> who were his friends sent word<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to him and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“sent”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> were urging him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> not to risk himself <transChange type="added">by going</transChange> into the theater.

verses.name: Acts 19:32
verses.text: So some were shouting <transChange type="added">one thing</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and some another, for the assembly was in confusion, and the majority did not know <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞why⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “on account of what”</note> they had assembled.

verses.name: Acts 19:33
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">some</transChange> of the crowd advised<note placement="foot">Or “concluded it was about”</note> Alexander, when<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“put … forward”)</note> the Jews put him forward. But Alexander, motioning with his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> hand, was wanting to defend himself to the popular assembly.

verses.name: Acts 19:34
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“recognized”) which is understood as temporal</note> recognized that he was a Jew, they were shouting with one voice from all <transChange type="added">of them</transChange> for about two hours, “Great <transChange type="added">is</transChange> Artemis of the Ephesians!”

verses.name: Acts 19:35
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had quieted”) which is understood as temporal</note> the city secretary had quieted the crowd, he said, “Ephesian men, for who is there among men who does not know the Ephesian city is honorary temple keeper of the great Artemis and of her<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> image fallen from heaven?

verses.name: Acts 19:36
verses.text: Therefore <transChange type="added">because</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the causal genitive absolute participle (“are”)</note> these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> are undeniable, it is necessary <transChange type="added">that</transChange> you be quiet and do nothing rash!

verses.name: Acts 19:37
verses.text: For you have brought these men <transChange type="added">here</transChange> <transChange type="added">who are</transChange> neither temple robbers nor blasphemers of our goddess.

verses.name: Acts 19:38
verses.text: If then Demetrius and the craftsmen <transChange type="added">who are</transChange> with him have a complaint against anyone, the court days are observed and there are proconsuls—let them bring charges against one another!

verses.name: Acts 19:39
verses.text: But if you desire anything further, it will be settled in the lawful assembly.

verses.name: Acts 19:40
verses.text: For indeed we are in danger of being accused of rioting concerning today, <transChange type="added">since there</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “since” is supplied as a component of the causal genitive absolute participle (“is”)</note> is no cause in relation to which we will be able to give an account concerning this disorderly gathering!” And when he<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had said”) which is understood as temporal</note> had said these things, he dismissed the assembly.<note placement="foot">Verse <reference osisRef="Acts.19.41">41</reference> in the English Bible is included as part of v. <reference osisRef="Acts.19.40">40</reference> in the standard editions of the Greek text</note>  <chapter eID="Acts.19"/>

verses.name: Acts 20:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11436"/><title type="x-s">Paul Travels Through Macedonia and Greece</title> <div sID="gen26955" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11436"/>Now after the turmoil had ceased, Paul summoned<note placement="foot">*Here the participle (“summoned”) has been translated as a finite verb in keeping with English style</note> the disciples, and after<note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“encouraging”) which is understood as temporal</note> encouraging them,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> he said farewell and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“departed”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> departed to travel to Macedonia.

verses.name: Acts 20:2
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had gone through”) which is understood as temporal</note> had gone through those regions and encouraged them <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞at length⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “with many a word”</note> he came to Greece

verses.name: Acts 20:3
verses.text: and stayed<note placement="foot">*Here the participle (“stayed”) has been translated as a finite verb in keeping with English style</note> three months. Because<note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the causal genitive absolute participle (“was made”)</note> a plot was made against him by the Jews as he<note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was about to”) which is understood as temporal</note> was about to set sail for Syria, he came to a decision to return through Macedonia.

verses.name: Acts 20:4
verses.text: And Sopater <transChange type="added">son</transChange> of Pyrrhus from Berea, and Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica, and Gaius from Derbe, and Timothy, and Tychicus and Trophimus from Asia, were accompanying him.

verses.name: Acts 20:5
verses.text: And these had gone on ahead <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“had gone on ahead”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> were waiting for us in Troas.

verses.name: Acts 20:6
verses.text: And we sailed away from Philippi after the days of Unleavened Bread and came to them at Troas within five days, where we stayed seven days.  <div eID="gen26955" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 20:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11437"/><title type="x-s">Eutychus Falls from a Window</title> <div sID="gen26956" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11437"/>And on the first <transChange type="added">day</transChange> of the week, <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“had assembled”)</note> we had assembled to break bread, Paul began conversing<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began conversing”)</note> with them, because he<note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was going to”) which is understood as causal</note> was going to leave on the next day, and he extended his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> message until midnight.

verses.name: Acts 20:8
verses.text: Now there were quite a few lamps in the upstairs room where we were gathered.

verses.name: Acts 20:9
verses.text: And a certain young man <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞named⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by name”</note> Eutychus who was sitting in the window was sinking into a deep sleep while<note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was conversing”)</note> Paul was conversing at length. Being overcome by sleep, he fell down from the third story and was picked up dead.

verses.name: Acts 20:10
verses.text: But Paul went down <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went down”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> threw himself on him, and putting his arms around him,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> said, “Do not be distressed, for his life is in him.”

verses.name: Acts 20:11
verses.text: So he went up and broke bread,<note placement="foot">*This participle and the previous one (“went up”) have been translated as finite verbs in keeping with English style</note> and when he<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had eaten”) which is understood as temporal</note> had eaten and talked for a long <transChange type="added">time</transChange>, until dawn, then he departed.

verses.name: Acts 20:12
verses.text: And they led the youth away alive, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞were greatly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “were not moderately”</note> comforted.  <div eID="gen26956" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 20:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11438"/><title type="x-s">The Voyage to Miletus</title> <div sID="gen26957" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11438"/>But we went on ahead to the ship <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went on ahead”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> put out to sea for Assos, intending to take Paul on board there. For having made arrangements in this way, he himself was intending to travel by land.

verses.name: Acts 20:14
verses.text: And when he met us at Assos, we took him on board <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took … on board”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> went to Mitylene.

verses.name: Acts 20:15
verses.text: And we sailed from there on the next <transChange type="added">day</transChange>, <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“sailed”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> arrived opposite Chios. And on the next <transChange type="added">day</transChange> we approached Samos, and on the following <transChange type="added">day</transChange> we came to Miletus.

verses.name: Acts 20:16
verses.text: For Paul had decided to sail past Ephesus so that he would not be <transChange type="added">having</transChange> to spend time in Asia.<note placement="foot">A reference to the Roman province of Asia (modern Asia Minor)</note> For he was hurrying if it could be possible for him to be in Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost.  <div eID="gen26957" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 20:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11439"/><title type="x-s">Paul’s Farewell to the Ephesian Elders</title> <div sID="gen26958" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11439"/>And from Miletus he sent <transChange type="added">word</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to Ephesus and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“sent”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> summoned the elders of the church.

verses.name: Acts 20:18
verses.text: And when they came to him, he said to them, “You know from the first day on which I set foot in Asia<note placement="foot">A reference to the Roman province of Asia (modern Asia Minor)</note> how I was the whole time with you—

verses.name: Acts 20:19
verses.text: serving the Lord with all humility and with tears, and with the trials that happened to me through the plots of the Jews—

verses.name: Acts 20:20
verses.text: how I did not shrink from proclaiming to you anything that would be profitable, and <transChange type="added">from</transChange> teaching you in public and from house <transChange type="added">to house</transChange>,

verses.name: Acts 20:21
verses.text: testifying both to Jews and to Greeks with respect to repentance toward God and faith in our Lord Jesus.  <div eID="gen26958" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 20:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11440"/><div sID="gen26959" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11440"/>“And now behold, bound by the Spirit I am traveling to Jerusalem, not knowing the things that will happen to me <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞there⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “in it”</note>

verses.name: Acts 20:23
verses.text: except that the Holy Spirit testifies to me in town <transChange type="added">after town</transChange>, saying that bonds and persecutions await me.

verses.name: Acts 20:24
verses.text: But I consider <transChange type="added">my</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> life as worth <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞nothing⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Or “not a single word”; literally “not any thing”</note> to myself, in order to finish my mission and the ministry that I received from the Lord Jesus, to testify <transChange type="added">to</transChange> the gospel of the grace of God.  <div eID="gen26959" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 20:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11441"/><div sID="gen26960" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11441"/>“And now behold, I know that all <transChange type="added">of</transChange> you, among whom I went about proclaiming the kingdom, will see my face no more.

verses.name: Acts 20:26
verses.text: Therefore I testify to you on this very day that I am guiltless of the blood of all <transChange type="added">of you</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*The words “of you” are not in the Greek text but are implied</note>

verses.name: Acts 20:27
verses.text: for I did not shrink from proclaiming to you the whole purpose of God.

verses.name: Acts 20:28
verses.text: Be on guard for yourselves and for all the flock among which the Holy Spirit has appointed you <transChange type="added">as</transChange> overseers, to shepherd the church of God which he obtained through the blood of his own <transChange type="added">Son</transChange>.<note placement="foot">Or “through his own blood”; the Greek construction can be taken either way, with “Son” implied if the meaning is “through the blood of his own”</note>

verses.name: Acts 20:29
verses.text: I know that after my departure fierce wolves will come in among you, not sparing the flock.

verses.name: Acts 20:30
verses.text: And from among you yourselves men will arise, speaking <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞perversions of the truth⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “crooked things”</note> in order to draw away the disciples after them.

verses.name: Acts 20:31
verses.text: Therefore be on the alert, remembering that night and day <transChange type="added">for</transChange> three years I did not stop warning each one <transChange type="added">of you</transChange><note placement="foot">*The words “of you” are not in the Greek text but are implied</note> with tears.  <div eID="gen26960" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 20:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11442"/><div sID="gen26961" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11442"/>“And now I entrust you to God and to the message of his grace, which is able to build <transChange type="added">you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> up and to give you<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> the inheritance among all those who are sanctified.

verses.name: Acts 20:33
verses.text: I have desired no one’s silver or gold or clothing!

verses.name: Acts 20:34
verses.text: You yourselves know that these hands served <transChange type="added">to meet</transChange><note placement="foot">*The words “to meet” are not in the Greek text but are supplied for clarity</note> my needs and the needs of<note placement="foot">*The words “the needs of” are supplied in keeping with English style to maintain the parallelism with the earlier phrase “my needs”</note> those who were with me.

verses.name: Acts 20:35
verses.text: I have shown you <transChange type="added">with respect to</transChange> all <transChange type="added">things</transChange> that <transChange type="added">by</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“working hard”) which is understood as means</note> working hard in this way it is necessary to help those who are in need, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus that he himself said, “It is more blessed to give than to receive.”<note placement="foot">Perhaps an allusion to <reference osisRef="Matt.10.8">Matt 10:8; </reference>these exact words are not found in the NT gospels</note>  <div eID="gen26961" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 20:36
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11443"/><div sID="gen26962" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11443"/>And <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had said”) which is understood as temporal</note> had said these things, he fell to his knees and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“fell to”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> prayed with them all.

verses.name: Acts 20:37
verses.text: And there was considerable weeping by all, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞hugging⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “falling on the neck of”</note> Paul, they kissed him,

verses.name: Acts 20:38
verses.text: especially distressed at the statement that he had said, that they were going to see his face no more. And they accompanied him to the ship.  <chapter eID="Acts.20"/>

verses.name: Acts 21:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11444"/><title type="x-s">Paul Travels on to Jerusalem</title> <div sID="gen26963" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11444"/>And it happened that after we tore ourselves away<note placement="foot">*Here the participle (“tore ourselves away”) has been translated as a finite verb in keeping with English style</note> from them, we put out to sea, and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous infinitive (“put out to sea”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> running a straight course we came to Cos and on the next <transChange type="added">day</transChange> to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.

verses.name: Acts 21:2
verses.text: And finding a ship that was crossing over to Phoenicia, we went aboard <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went aboard”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> put out to sea.

verses.name: Acts 21:3
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after we</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“sighted”) which is understood as temporal</note> sighted Cyprus and left it behind <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞on the port side⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “left”</note> we sailed to Syria and arrived at Tyre, because the ship was to unload its<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> cargo there.

verses.name: Acts 21:4
verses.text: And we stayed there seven days <transChange type="added">after we</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“found”) which is understood as temporal</note> found the disciples, who kept telling Paul through the Spirit not to set foot in Jerusalem.

verses.name: Acts 21:5
verses.text: And it happened that when our days were over, we departed <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“departed”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> went on our way, while<note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“accompanied”)</note> all of them accompanied us, together with their<note placement="foot">*The word “their” is not in the Greek text but is implied</note> wives and children, as far as outside the city. And after<note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“falling to”) which is understood as temporal</note> falling to our knees on the beach and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied to join this and the previous participle (“falling to”) in keeping with English style</note> praying,

verses.name: Acts 21:6
verses.text: we said farewell to one another and embarked in the ship, and they returned to their own <transChange type="added">homes</transChange>.  <div eID="gen26963" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 21:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11445"/><div sID="gen26964" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11445"/>And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had completed”) which is understood as temporal</note> we had completed the voyage from Tyre, we arrived at Ptolemais. And after we<note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“greeted”) which is understood as temporal</note> greeted the brothers, we stayed one day with them.

verses.name: Acts 21:8
verses.text: And on the next day we departed <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied to join this and the previous participle (“departed”) in keeping with English style</note> came to Caesarea, and entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, who was one of the seven, and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied to join this and the previous participle (“was”) in keeping with English style</note> stayed with him.

verses.name: Acts 21:9
verses.text: (<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Now this man had⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “now to this man were”</note> four virgin daughters who prophesied.)  <div eID="gen26964" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 21:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11446"/><div sID="gen26965" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11446"/>And <transChange type="added">while we</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“were staying”)</note> were staying there<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> many days, a certain prophet <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞named⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by name”</note> Agabus came down from Judea.

verses.name: Acts 21:11
verses.text: And he came to us and took Paul’s belt. Tying up his own feet and hands, he said, “This is what the Holy Spirit says: ‘In this way the Jews in Jerusalem will tie up the man whose belt this is, and will deliver <transChange type="added">him</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> into the hands of the Gentiles.’ ”

verses.name: Acts 21:12
verses.text: And when we heard these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, both we and the local residents urged him not to go up to Jerusalem.

verses.name: Acts 21:13
verses.text: Then Paul replied, “What are you doing weeping and breaking my heart? For I am ready not only to be tied up, but even to die in Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus!”

verses.name: Acts 21:14
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">because</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the causal genitive absolute participle (“be persuaded”)</note> he would not be persuaded, we remained silent, saying, “The will of the Lord be done.”  <div eID="gen26965" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 21:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11447"/><div sID="gen26966" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11447"/>So after these days we got ready <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“got ready”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> went up to Jerusalem.

verses.name: Acts 21:16
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">some</transChange> of the disciples from Caesarea also traveled together with us, bringing <transChange type="added">us</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to a certain Mnason of Cyprus, a disciple of long standing,<note placement="foot">Or perhaps “one of the original disciples”</note> with whom we were to be entertained as guests.  <div eID="gen26966" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 21:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11448"/><title type="x-s">Paul Visits the Leaders of the Jerusalem Church</title> <div sID="gen26967" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11448"/>And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“came”)</note> we came to Jerusalem, the brothers welcomed us gladly.

verses.name: Acts 21:18
verses.text: And on the next <transChange type="added">day</transChange> Paul went in with us to James, and all the elders were present.

verses.name: Acts 21:19
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“greeting”) which is understood as temporal</note> greeting them, he began to relate<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to relate”)</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞one after the other⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “with respect to each one”</note> <transChange type="added">the things</transChange> which God had done among the Gentiles through his ministry.

verses.name: Acts 21:20
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> they heard this,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> they began to glorify<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to glorify”)</note> God. And they said to him, “You see, brother, how many ten thousands there are among the Jews who have believed, and they are all zealous adherents of the law.

verses.name: Acts 21:21
verses.text: And they have been informed about you that you are teaching all the Jews <transChange type="added">who are</transChange> among the Gentiles <transChange type="added">the</transChange> abandonment of Moses, telling them not to circumcise <transChange type="added">their</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> children or to live according to our<note placement="foot">Literally “according to the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> customs.

verses.name: Acts 21:22
verses.text: What then <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞is to be done⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>?<note placement="foot">Literally “is it”</note> Doubtless they will all hear that you have come!

verses.name: Acts 21:23
verses.text: Therefore do this that we tell you: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞we have⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “there are to us”</note> four men who have taken a vow upon themselves.<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “on themselves”</note>

verses.name: Acts 21:24
verses.text: Take these <transChange type="added">men</transChange> <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“take”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> purify yourself along with them and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞pay their expenses⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “spend on them”</note> so that they can shave their<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> heads, and everyone will know that <transChange type="added">the things</transChange> which they had been informed about you are nothing, but you yourself also agree with observing the law.

verses.name: Acts 21:25
verses.text: But concerning the Gentiles who have believed, we have written a letter <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“deciding”) which is understood as temporal</note> deciding they should avoid food sacrificed to idols and blood and <transChange type="added">what has been</transChange> strangled and sexual immorality.”

verses.name: Acts 21:26
verses.text: Then Paul took along the men on the next day, <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” has been supplied in keeping with English style</note> after he<note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had purified”) which is understood as temporal</note> had purified himself together with them, he entered into the temple courts,<note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> announcing the completion of the days of purification until <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the time⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “which time”</note> the offering would be presented on behalf of each one of them.  <div eID="gen26967" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 21:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11449"/><title type="x-s">Paul Arrested in the Temple Courts</title> <div sID="gen26968" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11449"/>But when the seven days were about to be completed, the Jews from Asia<note placement="foot">A reference to the Roman province of Asia (modern Asia Minor)</note> who had seen him in the temple courts<note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> stirred up the whole crowd and laid hands on him,

verses.name: Acts 21:28
verses.text: shouting, “Israelite men, help! This is the man who is teaching everyone everywhere against the people and the law and this place! And furthermore he also brought Greeks into the temple, and has defiled this holy place!”

verses.name: Acts 21:29
verses.text: (For they had previously seen Trophimus the Ephesian in the city with him, whom they thought that Paul had brought into the temple.)

verses.name: Acts 21:30
verses.text: And the whole city was stirred up, and the people came running together, and they seized Paul <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“seized”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> dragged him outside of the temple courts,<note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> and immediately the doors were shut.  <div eID="gen26968" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 21:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11450"/><div sID="gen26969" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11450"/>And <transChange type="added">as they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“were seeking”)</note> were seeking to kill him, a report came up to the military tribune of the cohort that all Jerusalem was in confusion.

verses.name: Acts 21:32
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞He⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “who”</note> immediately took along soldiers and centurions and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took along”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> ran down to them. And when<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> they saw the military tribune and the soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.

verses.name: Acts 21:33
verses.text: Then the military tribune came up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> arrested him and ordered him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to be bound with two chains, and inquired who he was and what it was that he had done.

verses.name: Acts 21:34
verses.text: But some in the crowd were shouting one thing <transChange type="added">and</transChange> others <transChange type="added">another</transChange>, and <transChange type="added">because</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the causal genitive absolute participle (“able”)</note> he was not able to find out the truth on account of the commotion, he gave orders to bring him into the barracks.<note placement="foot">Or “headquarters”</note>

verses.name: Acts 21:35
verses.text: And when he came to the steps, it happened that he had to be carried by the soldiers on account of the violence of the crowd,

verses.name: Acts 21:36
verses.text: for the crowd of people was following <transChange type="added">them</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> shouting, “Away with him!”  <div eID="gen26969" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 21:37
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11451"/><title type="x-s">Paul Permitted to Address the Crowd</title> <div sID="gen26970" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11451"/>And <transChange type="added">as he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was about to”) which is understood as temporal</note> was about to be brought into the barracks,<note placement="foot">Or “headquarters”</note> Paul said to the military tribune, “Is it permitted for me to say something to you?” And he said, “Do you know Greek?

verses.name: Acts 21:38
verses.text: Then you are not the Egyptian who before these days raised a revolt and led out into the wilderness the four thousand men of the Assassins?”<note placement="foot">Also known as the “Sicarii” from the Latin word “sicarius” = dagger, after the short dagger used to assassinate political opponents</note>

verses.name: Acts 21:39
verses.text: But Paul said, “I am a Jewish man from Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no unimportant city. Now I ask you, allow me to speak to the people.”

verses.name: Acts 21:40
verses.text: So <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“permitted”)</note> he permitted him,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> Paul, standing there on the steps, motioned with his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> hand to the people. And when there<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was”)</note> was a great silence, he addressed them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> in the Aramaic language, saying,  <chapter eID="Acts.21"/> <div eID="gen26970" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 22:1
verses.text: “Men—brothers and fathers—listen to my defense to you now!”

verses.name: Acts 22:2
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard that he was addressing them in the Aramaic language, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they became even more silent⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “they showed even more silence”</note> And he said,

verses.name: Acts 22:3
verses.text: “I am a Jewish man born in Tarsus in Cilicia, but brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, educated according to the exactness of the law received from our fathers, being zealous for God, just as all <transChange type="added">of</transChange> you are today.

verses.name: Acts 22:4
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “who”</note> persecuted this Way to the death, tying up and delivering to prison both men and women,

verses.name: Acts 22:5
verses.text: as indeed the high priest and the whole council of elders can testify about me, from whom also I received letters to the brothers in Damascus, <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“received”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> was traveling there<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to lead away those who were there also tied up to Jerusalem so that they could be punished.  <div eID="gen26971" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 22:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11452"/><title type="x-s">Paul Tells of His Conversion on the Damascus Road</title> <div sID="gen26972" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11452"/>“And it happened that <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was traveling”) which is understood as temporal</note> I was traveling and approaching Damascus around noon, suddenly a very bright light from heaven flashed around me,

verses.name: Acts 22:7
verses.text: and I fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to me, ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?’

verses.name: Acts 22:8
verses.text: And I answered, ‘Who are you, Lord?’ And he said to me, ‘I am Jesus the Nazarene whom you are persecuting.’

verses.name: Acts 22:9
verses.text: (Now those who were with me saw the light but did not hear the voice of the one who was speaking to me.)

verses.name: Acts 22:10
verses.text: So I said, ‘What should I do, Lord?’ And the Lord said to me, ‘Get up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“get up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> proceed to Damascus, and there it will be told to you about all <transChange type="added">the things</transChange> that have been appointed for you to do.’

verses.name: Acts 22:11
verses.text: And as I could not see as a result of the brightness of that light, I arrived in Damascus led by the hand of those who were with me.

verses.name: Acts 22:12
verses.text: And a certain Ananias, a devout man according to the law, well spoken of by all the Jews who live <transChange type="added">there</transChange>,

verses.name: Acts 22:13
verses.text: came to me and stood by <transChange type="added">me</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“stood by”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to me, ‘Brother Saul, regain your sight!’ And at that same time I looked up at him and saw him.<note placement="foot">*The words “and saw him” are not in the Greek text but are supplied in the translation for clarity</note>

verses.name: Acts 22:14
verses.text: And he said, ‘The God of our fathers has appointed you to know his will, and to see the Righteous One and to hear a voice from his mouth,

verses.name: Acts 22:15
verses.text: because you will be a witness for him<note placement="foot">Or “to him”</note> to all people of what you have seen and heard.

verses.name: Acts 22:16
