verses.text: And now why are you delaying? Get up, be baptized, and wash away your sins, calling on his name!’  <div eID="gen26972" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 22:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11453"/><div sID="gen26973" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11453"/>“And it happened that <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“returned”) which is understood as temporal</note> I returned to Jerusalem and I was praying in the temple courts,<note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> I was in a trance,

verses.name: Acts 22:18
verses.text: and saw him saying to me, ‘Hurry and depart <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞quickly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “with quickness”</note> from Jerusalem, because they will not accept your testimony about me.’

verses.name: Acts 22:19
verses.text: And I said, ‘Lord, they themselves know that from synagogue <transChange type="added">to synagogue</transChange> I was imprisoning and beating those who believed in you.

verses.name: Acts 22:20
verses.text: And when the blood of your witness Stephen was being shed, I myself also was standing near and was approving, and was guarding the cloaks of those who were killing him.’

verses.name: Acts 22:21
verses.text: And he said to me, ‘Go, because I will send you far away to the Gentiles!’ ”  <div eID="gen26973" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 22:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11454"/><title type="x-s">Paul Questioned by the Military Tribune</title> <div sID="gen26974" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11454"/>Now they were listening to him until this word, and they raised their voices, saying, “Away with such a man from the earth! For it is not fitting <transChange type="added">for</transChange> him to live!”

verses.name: Acts 22:23
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“were screaming”)</note> they were screaming and throwing off their<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> cloaks and throwing dust into the air,

verses.name: Acts 22:24
verses.text: the military tribune ordered him to be brought into the barracks,<note placement="foot">Or “headquarters”</note> saying he was to be examined with a lash so that he could find out for what reason they were crying out against him in this way.

verses.name: Acts 22:25
verses.text: But when they had stretched him out for the lash,<note placement="foot">Or “with straps” (in order to lash him)</note> Paul said to the centurion standing there, “Is it permitted for you to flog a man <transChange type="added">who is</transChange> a Roman citizen and uncondemned?”

verses.name: Acts 22:26
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> the centurion heard this,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> he went to the military tribune and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went to”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> reported it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> saying, “What are you about to do? For this man is a Roman citizen!”

verses.name: Acts 22:27
verses.text: So the military tribune came <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to him, “Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?” And he said, “Yes.”

verses.name: Acts 22:28
verses.text: And the military tribune replied, “I acquired this citizenship for a large sum of money.” And Paul said, “But I indeed was born <transChange type="added">a citizen</transChange>.<note placement="foot">*The words “a citizen” are not in the Greek text but are implied</note>

verses.name: Acts 22:29
verses.text: Then immediately those who were about to examine him kept away from him, and the military tribune also was afraid <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“realized”) which is understood as temporal</note> realized that he was a Roman citizen and that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he had tied him up⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “he was having tied him up”</note>

verses.name: Acts 22:30
verses.text: But on the next day, <transChange type="added">because he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“wanted”) which is understood as causal</note> wanted to know the true reason why he was being accused by the Jews, he released him and ordered the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin to assemble, and he brought down Paul and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“brought down”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> had him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> stand before them.  <chapter eID="Acts.22"/>

verses.name: Acts 23:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11455"/><title type="x-s">Paul Before the Sanhedrin</title> <div sID="gen26975" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11455"/>And looking intently at the Sanhedrin, Paul said, “Men <transChange type="added">and</transChange> brothers, I have lived my life in all good conscience before God to this day.”

verses.name: Acts 23:2
verses.text: So the high priest Ananias ordered those standing near him to strike his mouth.

verses.name: Acts 23:3
verses.text: Then Paul said to him, “God is going to strike you, <transChange type="added">you</transChange> whitewashed wall! And are you sitting <transChange type="added">there</transChange> judging me according to the law, and acting contrary to the law do you order me to be struck?”

verses.name: Acts 23:4
verses.text: And those who stood nearby said, “Are you reviling the high priest of God?”

verses.name: Acts 23:5
verses.text: And Paul said, “I did not know, brothers, that he was high priest. For it is written, ‘You must not speak evil <transChange type="added">of</transChange> a ruler of your people.’ ”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Exod.22.28">Exod 22:28</reference></note>  <div eID="gen26975" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 23:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11456"/><div sID="gen26976" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11456"/>Now <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“realized”) which is understood as temporal</note> Paul realized that one part were Sadducees and the other Pharisees, he shouted out in the Sanhedrin, “Men <transChange type="added">and</transChange> brothers! I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees! I am being judged concerning the hope and the resurrection of the dead!”

verses.name: Acts 23:7
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“said”)</note> he said this, a dispute developed between the Pharisees and Sadducees, and the assembly was divided.

verses.name: Acts 23:8
verses.text: (For the Sadducees say there is no resurrection or angel or spirit, but the Pharisees acknowledge <transChange type="added">them</transChange> all.)

verses.name: Acts 23:9
verses.text: And there was loud shouting, and some of the scribes from the party of the Pharisees stood up <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“stood up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> contended sharply, saying, “We find nothing wrong with this man! But <transChange type="added">what</transChange> if a spirit or an angel has spoken to him?”

verses.name: Acts 23:10
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“became”)</note> the dispute became severe, the military tribune, fearing lest Paul be torn apart by them, ordered the detachment to go down, take him away from their midst, and bring him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> into the barracks.<note placement="foot">Or “headquarters”</note>

verses.name: Acts 23:11
verses.text: And the next night the Lord stood by him <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“stood by”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “Have courage, for as you have testified about me in Jerusalem, so you must also testify in Rome.”  <div eID="gen26976" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 23:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11457"/><title type="x-s">A Conspiracy to Kill Paul</title> <div sID="gen26977" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11457"/>And <transChange type="added">when it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was”)</note> was day, the Jews made a conspiracy and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“made”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> bound themselves under a curse, saying they would<note placement="foot">Literally “saying neither to eat nor to drink”; the words “they would” are supplied for smoother English style</note> neither eat nor drink until they had killed Paul.

verses.name: Acts 23:13
verses.text: Now there were more <transChange type="added">than</transChange> forty who had made this conspiracy,

verses.name: Acts 23:14
verses.text: who went to the chief priests and the elders <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went to”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “We have bound ourselves under a curse to partake of nothing until we have killed Paul.

verses.name: Acts 23:15
verses.text: Therefore, now you along with the Sanhedrin explain to the military tribune that he should bring him down to you, as <transChange type="added">if you</transChange> were going to determine more accurately the things concerning him. And we are ready to do away with him before he comes near.”  <div eID="gen26977" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 23:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11458"/><div sID="gen26978" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11458"/>But <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard about”) which is understood as temporal</note> the son of Paul’s sister heard about the ambush, he came and entered into the barracks<note placement="foot">Or “headquarters”</note> and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the two previous participles (“came” and “entered”) have been translated as finite verbs</note> reported it<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to Paul.

verses.name: Acts 23:17
verses.text: So Paul called one of the centurions <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“called”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “Bring this young man to the military tribune, because he has something to report to him.”

verses.name: Acts 23:18
verses.text: So he took him <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> brought him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to the military tribune and said, “The prisoner Paul called me and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“called”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> asked me<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to bring this young man to you because he<note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“has”) which is understood as causal</note> has something to tell you.”

verses.name: Acts 23:19
verses.text: And the military tribune, taking hold of his hand and withdrawing privately, asked, “What is it that you have to report to me?”

verses.name: Acts 23:20
verses.text: And he said, “The Jews have agreed to ask you that you bring Paul down to the Sanhedrin tomorrow, as <transChange type="added">if they</transChange> were going to inquire somewhat more accurately concerning him.

verses.name: Acts 23:21
verses.text: You therefore do not be persuaded by them, because more <transChange type="added">than</transChange> forty men of <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞their number⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “them”</note> are lying in wait for him, who have bound themselves under a curse neither to eat nor to drink until they have done away with him. And now they are ready, waiting for <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you to agree⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “the assurance of agreement from you”</note>

verses.name: Acts 23:22
verses.text: So the military tribune sent the young man away, directing <transChange type="added">him</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> “Tell no one that you have revealed these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> to me.”  <div eID="gen26978" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 23:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11459"/><div sID="gen26979" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11459"/>And he summoned two of the centurions <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“summoned”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “Make ready from the third hour of the night two hundred soldiers and seventy horsemen and two hundred spearmen,<note placement="foot">A word of uncertain meaning, probably a military technical term</note> in order that they may proceed as far as Caesarea.

verses.name: Acts 23:24
verses.text: And provide mounts so that they can put Paul on them <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“put … on”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> bring him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> safely to Felix the governor.”

verses.name: Acts 23:25
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞He wrote⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “writing”</note> a letter that had this form:<note placement="foot">Or “content”</note>  <div eID="gen26979" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 23:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11460"/><div sID="gen26980" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11460"/>Claudius Lysias. <div eID="gen26980" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen26981" type="x-p"/> To his excellency Governor Felix. <block> <div eID="gen26981" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen26982" type="x-p"/> Greetings!  <div eID="gen26982" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 23:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11461"/><div sID="gen26983" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11461"/>This man was seized by the Jews and was about to be killed by them <transChange type="added">when I</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“came upon”) which is understood as temporal</note> came upon them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> with the detachment and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came upon”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> rescued him,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> because I<note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“learned”) which is understood as causal</note> learned that he was a Roman citizen.

verses.name: Acts 23:28
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">because I</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“wanted”) which is understood as causal</note> wanted to know the charge for which they were accusing him, I brought him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> down to their Sanhedrin.<note placement="foot">Or “council”</note>

verses.name: Acts 23:29
verses.text: I found <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “whom”</note> was accused concerning controversial questions of their law, but having no charge deserving death or imprisonment.

verses.name: Acts 23:30
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was made known”) which is understood as temporal</note> was made known to me there would be a plot against the man, I sent him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to you immediately, also ordering his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> accusers to speak against him<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “to state the charges against him” (literally, “to speak the things against him”)</note> before you. </block>  <div eID="gen26983" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 23:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11462"/><div sID="gen26984" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11462"/>Therefore the soldiers, in accordance with <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞their orders⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “what was ordered to them”</note> took Paul and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“took”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> brought him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to Antipatris during the night.

verses.name: Acts 23:32
verses.text: And on the next day they let the horsemen go on with him, <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“let”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> they returned to the barracks.<note placement="foot">Or “headquarters”</note>

verses.name: Acts 23:33
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞The horsemen⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “who”</note> when they<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“came”) which is understood as temporal</note> came to Caesarea and delivered the letter to the governor, also presented Paul to him.

verses.name: Acts 23:34
verses.text: So <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“reading”) which is understood as temporal</note> reading the letter<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and asking what province he was from, and learning that <transChange type="added">he was</transChange> from Cilicia,

verses.name: Acts 23:35
verses.text: he said, “I will give you a hearing whenever your accusers arrive also,” giving orders <transChange type="added">for</transChange> him to be guarded in the praetorium<note placement="foot">The “praetorium” of Herod refers to the palace of Herod the Great in Caesarea Maritima</note> of Herod.  <chapter eID="Acts.23"/>

verses.name: Acts 24:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11463"/><title type="x-s">Paul Before Felix at Caesarea Maritima</title> <div sID="gen26985" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11463"/>And after five days the high priest Ananias came down with some elders and an attorney, a certain Tertullus, all of whom brought charges against Paul to the governor.

verses.name: Acts 24:2
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“had been summoned”)</note> he had been summoned, Tertullus began to accuse him,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> saying, “We have experienced<note placement="foot">*Here this participle (“have experienced”) and the following participle (“are taking place”) have been translated as finite verbs in keeping with English style</note> much<note placement="foot">Or “many years,” with “years” understood</note> peace through you, and reforms are taking place in this nation through your foresight.

verses.name: Acts 24:3
verses.text: Both in every <transChange type="added">way</transChange> and everywhere we acknowledge <transChange type="added">this</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> most excellent Felix, with all gratitude.

verses.name: Acts 24:4
verses.text: But so that I may not impose on you for longer, I implore you to hear us briefly with your <transChange type="added">customary</transChange> graciousness.

verses.name: Acts 24:5
verses.text: For we have found<note placement="foot">*Here this participle (“found”) has been translated as a finite verb in keeping with English style</note> this man to be a public menace and one who causes riots among all the Jews throughout the Roman Empire<note placement="foot">Literally “the inhabited earth,” but here this is probably rhetorical hyperbole for the Roman Empire, especially since Felix, the Roman governor, is being addressed</note> and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes,

verses.name: Acts 24:6
verses.text: who even attempted to desecrate the temple, and we arrested <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞him<note placement="foot">Literally “whom”</note>⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Some later manuscripts include the following additional material between v. <reference osisRef="Acts.24.6">6</reference> and v. <reference osisRef="Acts.24.8">8</reference>: “and we wanted to judge him according to our law, (24:7) but Lysius the military tribune came and took him from our hands with much violence, (24:8) ordering his accusers to come before you.”</note>

verses.name: Acts 24:8
verses.text: <transChange type="added">When</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“examine”) which is understood as temporal</note> you yourself examine him<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> you will be able to find out from <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “whom”</note> about all these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> of which we are accusing him.”

verses.name: Acts 24:9
verses.text: And the Jews also joined in the attack, asserting these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> were so.  <div eID="gen26985" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 24:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11464"/><div sID="gen26986" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11464"/>And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“gestured”)</note> the governor gestured for him to speak, Paul replied, “Because I<note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“know”) which is understood as causal</note> know you have been a judge over this nation for many years, I defend myself cheerfully <transChange type="added">with respect to</transChange> the things concerning myself.

verses.name: Acts 24:11
verses.text: You can ascertain that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞it has not been more than⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “there are not to me more than”</note> twelve days <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞since⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from which time”</note> I went up to Jerusalem to worship.

verses.name: Acts 24:12
verses.text: And neither did they find me arguing with anyone or making a crowd develop in the temple <transChange type="added">courts</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> nor in the synagogues nor throughout the city.

verses.name: Acts 24:13
verses.text: Nor can they prove <transChange type="added">the things</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to you concerning which they are now accusing me.

verses.name: Acts 24:14
verses.text: But I do confess this to you, that according to the Way (which they call a sect), so I worship the God of our fathers, believing all things <transChange type="added">that are</transChange> in accordance with the law and that are written in the prophets,

verses.name: Acts 24:15
verses.text: having a hope in God which these <transChange type="added">men</transChange> also themselves await: <transChange type="added">that</transChange> there is going to be a resurrection of both the righteous and the unrighteous.

verses.name: Acts 24:16
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞For this reason⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by this”</note> also I myself <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞always⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “through everything”</note> do my best to have a clear conscience toward God and people.

verses.name: Acts 24:17
verses.text: So after many years, I came to practice charitable giving and offerings to my people,<note placement="foot">Or “nation”</note>

verses.name: Acts 24:18
verses.text: in which they found me purified in the temple <transChange type="added">courts</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> not with a crowd or with a disturbance.

verses.name: Acts 24:19
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">there are</transChange> some Jews from Asia<note placement="foot">A reference to the Roman province of Asia (modern Asia Minor)</note> who ought to be present before you and bring charges against me,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> if they have anything against me,

verses.name: Acts 24:20
verses.text: or these <transChange type="added">men</transChange> themselves should say what crime they found <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“stood”)</note> I stood before the Sanhedrin,<note placement="foot">Or “council”</note>

verses.name: Acts 24:21
verses.text: other than concerning this one declaration that I shouted <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the participle (“standing there”) which is understood as temporal</note> standing there before them: ‘I am being judged before you today concerning the resurrection of the dead!’ ”  <div eID="gen26986" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 24:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11465"/><title type="x-s">Paul Held Awaiting Trial</title> <div sID="gen26987" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11465"/>But Felix, <transChange type="added">because he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“understood”) which is understood as causal</note> understood the facts concerning the Way more accurately, put them off, saying, “When Lysias the military tribune comes down, I will decide <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞your case⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.”<note placement="foot">Literally “the case with respect to you”</note>

verses.name: Acts 24:23
verses.text: <transChange type="added">He</transChange> ordered<note placement="foot">*Here this participle (“ordered”) has been translated as a finite verb in keeping with English style</note> the centurion for him to be guarded and to have some freedom, and in no way to prevent any of his own people<note placement="foot">This could refer to either friends or relatives</note> <transChange type="added">from</transChange> serving him.  <div eID="gen26987" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 24:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11466"/><div sID="gen26988" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11466"/>And after some days, <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“arrived”) which is understood as temporal</note> Felix arrived with his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish, he sent for Paul and listened to him concerning faith in Christ Jesus.

verses.name: Acts 24:25
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was discussing”)</note> he was discussing about righteousness and self control and the judgment that is to come, Felix became afraid and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“became”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> replied, “Go away for the present, and when I<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“have”) which is understood as temporal</note> have an opportunity, I will summon you.”

verses.name: Acts 24:26
verses.text: At the same time he was also hoping that money would be given to him by Paul. For this reason also he sent for him as often as possible <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“sent for”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> talked with him.

verses.name: Acts 24:27
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“had passed”)</note> two years had passed, Felix received as successor Porcius Festus. And because he<note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“wanted”) which is understood as causal</note> wanted to do a favor for the Jews, Felix left Paul behind <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as a prisoner⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “bound”</note>  <chapter eID="Acts.24"/>

verses.name: Acts 25:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11467"/><title type="x-s">Paul Appeals to Caesar</title> <div sID="gen26989" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11467"/>Now <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“set foot in”) which is understood as temporal</note> Festus set foot in the province, after three days he went up to Jerusalem from Caesarea.

verses.name: Acts 25:2
verses.text: And the chief priests and the most prominent men of the Jews brought charges against Paul to him, and were urging him,

verses.name: Acts 25:3
verses.text: asking for a favor against him, that he summon him to Jerusalem, <transChange type="added">because they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“were preparing ”) which is understood as causal</note> were preparing an ambush to do away with him along the way.

verses.name: Acts 25:4
verses.text: Then Festus replied <transChange type="added">that</transChange> Paul was being kept at Caesarea, and <transChange type="added">he</transChange> himself was about to go <transChange type="added">there</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> in a short time.

verses.name: Acts 25:5
verses.text: So he said, “Let those among you <transChange type="added">who are</transChange> prominent go down with <transChange type="added">me</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“go down with”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> if there is any wrong in the man, let them bring charges against him.”  <div eID="gen26989" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 25:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11468"/><div sID="gen26990" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11468"/>And <transChange type="added">after he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had stayed”) which is understood as temporal</note> had stayed among them not more than eight or ten days, he went down to Caesarea. On the next day he sat down on the judgment seat and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“sat down”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> gave orders <transChange type="added">for</transChange> Paul to be brought.

verses.name: Acts 25:7
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“arrived”)</note> he arrived, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him, bringing many and serious charges that they were not able to prove,

verses.name: Acts 25:8
verses.text: <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“said in his defense”)</note> Paul said in his defense, “Neither against the law of the Jews nor against the temple nor against Caesar have I sinned with reference to anything!”

verses.name: Acts 25:9
verses.text: But Festus, <transChange type="added">because he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“wanted”) which is understood as causal</note> wanted to do a favor for the Jews, answered and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“answered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said to Paul, “Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem to be tried before me there concerning these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>?”

verses.name: Acts 25:10
verses.text: But Paul said, “I am standing before the judgment seat of Caesar, where it is necessary <transChange type="added">for</transChange> me to be judged. I have done no wrong to the Jews, as you also know very well.

verses.name: Acts 25:11
verses.text: If then I am doing wrong<note placement="foot">Or “I am in the wrong”</note> and have done anything deserving death, I am not trying to avoid<note placement="foot">*Here the present tense has been translated as conative (“trying to avoid”)</note> dying. But if there is nothing <transChange type="added">true</transChange> of <transChange type="added">the things</transChange> which these <transChange type="added">people</transChange> are accusing me, no one can give me up to them. I appeal to Caesar!”

verses.name: Acts 25:12
verses.text: Then Festus, <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“discussing”) which is understood as temporal</note> discussing this<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> with his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> council, replied, “You have appealed to Caesar—to Caesar you will go!”  <div eID="gen26990" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 25:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11469"/><title type="x-s">Festus Asks King Agrippa for Advice</title> <div sID="gen26991" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11469"/>Now <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“had passed”)</note> some days had passed, King Agrippa and Bernice arrived at Caesarea to welcome Festus.

verses.name: Acts 25:14
verses.text: And while they were staying there many days, Festus laid out the <transChange type="added">case</transChange> against Paul to the king, saying, “There is a certain man left behind by Felix <transChange type="added">as</transChange> a prisoner,

verses.name: Acts 25:15
verses.text: concerning whom <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was”)</note> I was in Jerusalem the chief priests and the elders of the Jews presented evidence, asking for a sentence of condemnation against him.

verses.name: Acts 25:16
verses.text: To <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “whom”</note> I replied that it was not the custom of the Romans to give up any man before the one who had been accused met his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> accusers face to <transChange type="added">face</transChange> and received an opportunity for a defense concerning the accusation.

verses.name: Acts 25:17
verses.text: Therefore, <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“had assembled”)</note> they had assembled here, I made<note placement="foot">*Here this participle (“made”) has been translated as a finite verb in keeping with English style</note> no delay; on the next day I sat down on the judgment seat and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the two previous participles (“made” and “sat down”) have been translated as finite verbs</note> gave orders <transChange type="added">for</transChange> the man to be brought.

verses.name: Acts 25:18
verses.text: <transChange type="added">When they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“stood up”) which is understood as temporal</note> stood up, his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> accusers began bringing<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began bringing”)</note> no charge concerning <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “whom”</note> of the evil deeds that I was suspecting,

verses.name: Acts 25:19
verses.text: but they had some issues with him concerning their own religion, and concerning a certain Jesus, who was dead, whom Paul claimed to be alive.

verses.name: Acts 25:20
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">because</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was at a loss”) which is understood as causal</note> I was at a loss with regard to the investigation concerning these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, I asked if he was willing to go to Jerusalem and to be judged there concerning these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>.

verses.name: Acts 25:21
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“appealed”)</note> Paul appealed <transChange type="added">that</transChange> he be kept under guard for the decision of His Majesty the Emperor, I gave orders <transChange type="added">for</transChange> him to be kept under guard until I could send him to Caesar.”

verses.name: Acts 25:22
verses.text: So Agrippa <transChange type="added">said</transChange> to Festus, “I want to hear the man myself also.” “Tomorrow,” he said, “you will hear him.”  <div eID="gen26991" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 25:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11470"/><div sID="gen26992" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11470"/>So on the next day, Agrippa and Bernice came with great pageantry and entered into the audience hall, along with military tribunes and the most prominent men of the city. And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“gave the order”)</note> Festus gave the order, Paul was brought in.

verses.name: Acts 25:24
verses.text: And Festus said, “King Agrippa and all who are present with us, you see this man about whom the whole population of the Jews appealed to me, both in Jerusalem and here, shouting <transChange type="added">that</transChange> he must not live any longer.

verses.name: Acts 25:25
verses.text: But I understood <transChange type="added">that</transChange> he had done nothing deserving death himself, and <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“appealed to”)</note> this man appealed to His Majesty the Emperor, I decided to send him.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Acts 25:26
verses.text: I do not have anything definite to write to <transChange type="added">my</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> lord about <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “whom”</note> Therefore I have brought him before you all<note placement="foot">*Here “all” is supplied in the translation to indicate that the pronoun (“you”) is plural</note>—and especially before you, King Agrippa—so that after<note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“has taken place”)</note> this preliminary hearing has taken place, I may have something to write.

verses.name: Acts 25:27
verses.text: For it seems unreasonable to me to send a prisoner and not to indicate the charges against him.”  <chapter eID="Acts.25"/>

verses.name: Acts 26:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11471"/><title type="x-s">Paul Makes His Defense Before King Agrippa</title> <div sID="gen26993" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11471"/>So Agrippa said to Paul, “It is permitted for you to speak for yourself.” Then Paul extended <transChange type="added">his</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> hand and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“extended”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> began to defend himself:<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began to defend himself”)</note>  <div eID="gen26993" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 26:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11472"/><div sID="gen26994" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11472"/>“Concerning all <transChange type="added">the things</transChange> of which I am accused by the Jews, King Agrippa, I consider myself fortunate <transChange type="added">that</transChange> before you I am about to defend myself today,

verses.name: Acts 26:3
verses.text: <transChange type="added">because</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“are”) which is understood as causal</note> you are especially acquainted with both all the customs and controversial questions with respect to the Jews. Therefore I beg you<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to listen to me with patience.  <div eID="gen26994" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 26:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11473"/><div sID="gen26995" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11473"/>“Now all the Jews know my manner of life from <transChange type="added">my</transChange> youth, that had taken place from the beginning among my <transChange type="added">own</transChange> people<note placement="foot">Or “nation”</note> and in Jerusalem,

verses.name: Acts 26:5
verses.text: having known me for a long time, if they are willing to testify, that in accordance with the strictest party of our religion I lived <transChange type="added">as</transChange> a Pharisee.

verses.name: Acts 26:6
verses.text: And now I stand here on trial on the basis of hope in the promise made by God to our fathers,

verses.name: Acts 26:7
verses.text: to which our twelve tribes hope to attain as <transChange type="added">they</transChange> earnestly serve <transChange type="added">him</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> night and day. Concerning this hope I am being accused by the Jews, O king!

verses.name: Acts 26:8
verses.text: Why is it thought incredible by you <transChange type="added">people</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “people” is supplied in the translation to indicate that the pronoun (“you”) is plural</note> that God raises the dead?

verses.name: Acts 26:9
verses.text: Indeed, I myself thought it was necessary to do many <transChange type="added">things</transChange> opposed to the name of Jesus the Nazarene,

verses.name: Acts 26:10
verses.text: which I also did in Jerusalem, and not only did I lock up many of the saints in prison, having received authority from the chief priests, but also <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“were being executed”)</note> they were being executed, I cast my vote<note placement="foot">Literally “voting pebble,” but here “vote” rather than “voting pebble” is used in the translation to avoid the idea that this small stone was actually thrown at the accused (it was used as a method of voting)</note> against them.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Acts 26:11
verses.text: And throughout all the synagogues I punished them often <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“punished”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> tried to force<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as conative here (“tried to force”)</note> them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to blaspheme, and because I<note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was enraged”) which is understood as causal</note> was enraged at them beyond measure, I was pursuing them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> even as far as to foreign cities.

verses.name: Acts 26:12
verses.text: In <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞this activity⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “which”</note> I was traveling to Damascus with the authority and full power of the chief priests.

verses.name: Acts 26:13
verses.text: In the middle of the day along the road, O king, I saw a light from heaven, more than the brightness of the sun, shining around me and those who were traveling with me.

verses.name: Acts 26:14
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“had … fallen”)</note> we had all fallen to the ground, I heard a voice saying to me in the Aramaic language, ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me? <transChange type="added">It is</transChange> hard for you to kick against the goads!’

verses.name: Acts 26:15
verses.text: So I said, ‘Who are you, Lord?’ And the Lord said, ‘I am Jesus whom you are persecuting.

verses.name: Acts 26:16
verses.text: But get up and stand on your feet, because for this <transChange type="added">reason</transChange> I have appeared to you, to appoint you a servant and witness both <transChange type="added">to the things</transChange> in which you saw me and <transChange type="added">to the things</transChange> in which I will appear to you,

verses.name: Acts 26:17
verses.text: rescuing you from the people and from the Gentiles to whom I am sending you,

verses.name: Acts 26:18
verses.text: to open their eyes <transChange type="added">so that they</transChange> may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, <transChange type="added">so that</transChange> they may receive forgiveness of sins and a share among those who are sanctified by faith in me.’  <div eID="gen26995" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 26:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11474"/><div sID="gen26996" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11474"/>“Therefore, O King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision,

verses.name: Acts 26:20
verses.text: but to those in Damascus first, and in Jerusalem and all the region of Judea and to the Gentiles, I proclaimed <transChange type="added">that they should</transChange> repent and turn to God, doing deeds worthy of repentance.

verses.name: Acts 26:21
verses.text: On account of these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> the Jews seized me in<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “while I was in”</note> the temple courts<note placement="foot">*Here “courts” is supplied to distinguish this area from the interior of the temple building itself</note> and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“seized”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> were attempting to kill me.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Acts 26:22
verses.text: Therefore I have experienced help from God until this day, <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“have experienced”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> I stand here testifying to both small and great, saying nothing except what both the prophets and Moses have said were going to happen,

verses.name: Acts 26:23
verses.text: that the Christ<note placement="foot">Or “Messiah”</note> was to suffer <transChange type="added">and</transChange> that <transChange type="added">as</transChange> the first of the resurrection from the dead, he was going to proclaim light both to the people and to the Gentiles.”  <div eID="gen26996" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 26:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11475"/><div sID="gen26997" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11475"/>And <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was saying … in his defense”)</note> he was saying these things in his defense, Festus said with a loud voice, “You are out of your mind, Paul! Your<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> great learning <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞is driving⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “is turning”</note> you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞insane⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>!”<note placement="foot">Literally “to madness”</note>

verses.name: Acts 26:25
verses.text: But Paul said, “I am not out of my mind, most excellent Festus, but am speaking words of truth and rationality.

verses.name: Acts 26:26
verses.text: For the king knows about these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, to whom also I am speaking freely, for I am not convinced <transChange type="added">that</transChange> these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> in any way have escaped<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “that any of these things in any way has escaped”</note> his notice, because this <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞was⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “is”</note> not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞done⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “having been done”</note> in a corner.

verses.name: Acts 26:27
verses.text: Do you believe the prophets, King Agrippa? I know that you believe.”

verses.name: Acts 26:28
verses.text: But Agrippa <transChange type="added">said</transChange> to Paul, “In a short time are you persuading me to become a Christian?”<note placement="foot">Or “In a short time you are persuading me to become a Christian”</note>

verses.name: Acts 26:29
verses.text: And Paul <transChange type="added">replied</transChange>, “I pray to God, whether in a short time or in a long time, not only you but also all those who are listening to me today may become such <transChange type="added">people</transChange> as I also am, except for these bonds!”  <div eID="gen26997" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 26:30
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11476"/><div sID="gen26998" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11476"/>Both the king and the governor got up, and Bernice and those who were sitting with them.

verses.name: Acts 26:31
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">as they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“were going out”)</note> were going out, they were talking to one another, saying, “This man is not doing anything deserving death or imprisonment.”

verses.name: Acts 26:32
verses.text: And Agrippa said to Festus, “This man could have been released if he had not appealed to Caesar.”  <chapter eID="Acts.26"/>

verses.name: Acts 27:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11477"/><title type="x-s">Paul and His Associates Sail for Rome</title> <div sID="gen26999" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11477"/>And when it was decided <transChange type="added">that</transChange> we would sail away to Italy, they handed over Paul and some other prisoners to a centurion <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞named⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by name”</note> Julius of the Augustan<note placement="foot">The meaning and significance of the title “Augustan” is highly debated, as is the precise identification of this military unit; it may be an honorary unit designation given to auxiliary or provincial troops</note> Cohort.

verses.name: Acts 27:2
verses.text: And we went aboard a ship from Adramyttium that was about to sail to the places along the <transChange type="added">coast</transChange><note placement="foot">*The word “coast” is not in the Greek text but is implied</note> of Asia<note placement="foot">A reference to the Roman province of Asia (modern Asia Minor)</note> and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“went aboard”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> put out to sea. Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica, was with us.

verses.name: Acts 27:3
verses.text: And on the next <transChange type="added">day</transChange>, we put in at Sidon. And Julius, treating Paul kindly, allowed <transChange type="added">him</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> to go to his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> friends <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to be cared for⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “to experience care”</note>

verses.name: Acts 27:4
verses.text: And from there we put out to sea <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“put out to sea”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> sailed under the lee of Cyprus, because the winds were against us.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Acts 27:5
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after we</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had sailed across”) which is understood as temporal</note> had sailed across the open sea along Cilicia and Pamphylia, we put in at Myra in Lycia.

verses.name: Acts 27:6
verses.text: And there the centurion found an Alexandrian ship sailing for Italy <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“found”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> put us <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞on board⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “into”</note> it.

verses.name: Acts 27:7
verses.text: And sailing slowly, in many days and with difficulty we came<note placement="foot">*Here this participle (“came”) has been translated as a finite verb in keeping with English style</note> to Cnidus. Because<note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the causal genitive absolute participle (“permit … to go further”)</note> the wind did not permit us to go further, we sailed under the lee of Crete off Salmone.

verses.name: Acts 27:8
verses.text: And sailing along its coast with difficulty, we came to a certain place called Fair Havens, near which was the town <transChange type="added">of</transChange> Lasea.  <div eID="gen26999" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 27:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11478"/><div sID="gen27000" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11478"/>And <transChange type="added">because</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the causal genitive absolute participle (“had passed”)</note> considerable time had passed and the voyage was now dangerous because even the Fast<note placement="foot">A reference to the Jewish Day of Atonement (Yom Kippur) which occurs in mid-autumn</note> was already over, Paul strongly recommended,

verses.name: Acts 27:10
verses.text: saying to them, “Men, I perceive that the voyage is going <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to end⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to be”</note> with disaster and great loss, not only of the cargo and the ship, but also of our lives!”

verses.name: Acts 27:11
verses.text: But the centurion was convinced even more by the shipmaster and the shipowner than by what was said by Paul.

verses.name: Acts 27:12
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">because</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the causal genitive absolute participle (“was”)</note> the harbor was unsuitable for spending the winter in, the majority decided on a plan to put out to sea from there, if somehow they could arrive at Phoenix, a harbor of Crete facing toward the southwest and toward the northwest, to spend the winter there.<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>  <div eID="gen27000" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 27:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11479"/><title type="x-s">A Violent Storm at Sea</title> <div sID="gen27001" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11479"/>And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“began to blow gently”)</note> a southwest wind began to blow gently, because they<note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“thought”) which is understood as causal</note> thought they could accomplish their purpose, they weighed anchor and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“weighed anchor”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> sailed close along Crete.

verses.name: Acts 27:14
verses.text: But not long afterward a wind like a hurricane, called the northeaster,<note placement="foot">Literally “Euraquilo,” a violent northern wind</note> rushed down from it.<note placement="foot">That is, from the island of Crete</note>

verses.name: Acts 27:15
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was caught”)</note> the ship was caught and was not able to head into the wind, we gave way and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“gave way”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> were driven <transChange type="added">along</transChange>.

verses.name: Acts 27:16
verses.text: And running under the lee of a certain small island called Cauda, we were able with difficulty to get the ship’s boat under control.

verses.name: Acts 27:17
verses.text: <transChange type="added">After</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“hoisting”) which is understood as temporal</note> hoisting <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞it up⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “which”</note> they made use of supports to undergird the ship. And because they<note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“were afraid”) which is understood as causal</note> were afraid lest they run aground on the Syrtis, they lowered the sea anchor and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“lowered”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> thus were driven <transChange type="added">along</transChange>.

verses.name: Acts 27:18
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">because</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the causal genitive absolute participle (“battered by the storm”)</note> we were violently battered by the storm, on the next day <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they began⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “they began to carry out”</note> jettisoning the cargo,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note>

verses.name: Acts 27:19
verses.text: and on the third <transChange type="added">day</transChange> they threw overboard the gear of the ship with their own hands.

verses.name: Acts 27:20
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“appeared”)</note> neither sun nor stars appeared for many days, and with not a little bad weather confronting us,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> finally all hope was abandoned <transChange type="added">that</transChange> we would be saved.  <div eID="gen27001" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 27:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11480"/><div sID="gen27002" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11480"/>And <transChange type="added">because</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the causal genitive absolute participle (“were experiencing”)</note> many were experiencing lack of appetite, at that time Paul stood up in their midst and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“stood up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> said, “Men, <transChange type="added">you</transChange> ought to have followed my <transChange type="added">advice</transChange> not to put out to sea from Crete, and <transChange type="added">thus</transChange> avoided this damage and loss!

verses.name: Acts 27:22
verses.text: And now I urge you to cheer up, for there will be no loss of life from among you, but only of the ship.

verses.name: Acts 27:23
verses.text: For this night an angel of the God whose I am and whom I serve came to me,

verses.name: Acts 27:24
verses.text: saying, ‘Do not be afraid, Paul! It is necessary <transChange type="added">for</transChange> you to stand before Caesar, and behold, God has graciously granted you all who are sailing with you.’

verses.name: Acts 27:25
verses.text: Therefore keep up your courage, men, for I believe God that it will be like this—according to <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “which”</note> way it was told to me.

verses.name: Acts 27:26
verses.text: But it is necessary <transChange type="added">that</transChange> we run aground on some island.”  <div eID="gen27002" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 27:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11481"/><div sID="gen27003" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11481"/>And when the fourteenth night had come, <transChange type="added">as</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“were being driven”)</note> we were being driven in the Adriatic Sea about the middle of the night, the sailors suspected <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they were approaching some land⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “some land was approaching them”</note>

verses.name: Acts 27:28
verses.text: And taking soundings, they found twenty fathoms. So going on a little <transChange type="added">further</transChange> and taking soundings again, they found fifteen fathoms.

verses.name: Acts 27:29
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">because they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“were afraid”) which is understood as causal</note> were afraid lest somewhere we run aground against rough places, they threw down four anchors from the stern and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“threw down”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> prayed for day to come.

verses.name: Acts 27:30
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“were seeking”)</note> the sailors were seeking to escape from the ship and were lowering the ship’s boat into the sea, pretending as if they were going to lay out anchors from the bow,

verses.name: Acts 27:31
verses.text: Paul said to the centurion and the soldiers, “Unless these <transChange type="added">men</transChange> remain with the ship, you cannot be saved!”

verses.name: Acts 27:32
verses.text: Then the soldiers cut away the ropes of the ship’s boat and let it fall away.<note placement="foot">Or “let it drift away”</note>  <div eID="gen27003" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 27:33
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11482"/><div sID="gen27004" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11482"/>And until the day was about to come, Paul was urging <transChange type="added">them</transChange> all to take <transChange type="added">some</transChange> food, saying, “Today <transChange type="added">is the</transChange> fourteenth day you have waited <transChange type="added">anxiously</transChange>, <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“have waited”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> you have continued without eating, having taken nothing.

verses.name: Acts 27:34
verses.text: Therefore I urge you to take <transChange type="added">some</transChange> food, for this is necessary for your preservation. For not a hair from your head will be lost.”

verses.name: Acts 27:35
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“said”) which is understood as temporal</note> said these things and took bread, he gave thanks to God in front of them all, and after<note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“breaking”) which is understood as temporal</note> breaking it,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> he began to eat.

verses.name: Acts 27:36
verses.text: So they all were<note placement="foot">*Here this participle (“were”) has been translated as a finite verb in keeping with English style</note> encouraged and partook of food themselves.

verses.name: Acts 27:37
verses.text: (Now we were <transChange type="added">in</transChange> all two hundred seventy six persons on the ship.)

verses.name: Acts 27:38
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had eaten their fill”) which is understood as temporal</note> had eaten their fill of food, they lightened the ship by<note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“throwing”) which is understood as means</note> throwing the wheat<note placement="foot">Or “grain”</note> into the sea.  <div eID="gen27004" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 27:39
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11483"/><title type="x-s">The Shipwreck</title> <div sID="gen27005" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11483"/>Now when day came, they did not recognize the land, but they noticed a certain bay having a beach, onto which they decided to run the ship ashore if they could.

verses.name: Acts 27:40
verses.text: And slipping the anchors, they left <transChange type="added">them</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> in the sea, at the same time loosening the ropes<note placement="foot">Or “bands” (referring to the linkage that tied the steering oars together)</note> of the steering oars. And hoisting the foresail to the <transChange type="added">wind</transChange> that was blowing, they held course for the beach.

verses.name: Acts 27:41
verses.text: But falling into a place of crosscurrents,<note placement="foot">Or “a reef”; literally “a place of two seas,” an expression of uncertain meaning but most likely a nautical technical term for some adverse sea condition</note> they ran the ship aground. And the bow stuck fast and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“stuck fast”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> stayed immovable, but the stern was being broken up by the violence.<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “the violence of the waves”</note>

verses.name: Acts 27:42
verses.text: Now the plan of the soldiers was that they would kill the prisoners lest any escape <transChange type="added">by</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“swimming away”) which is understood as means</note> swimming away,

verses.name: Acts 27:43
verses.text: but the centurion, <transChange type="added">because he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“wanted”) which is understood as causal</note> wanted to save Paul, prevented them <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from doing what they intended⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “of the intention”</note> and gave orders <transChange type="added">that</transChange> those who were able to swim should jump in first to get to the land,

verses.name: Acts 27:44
verses.text: and <transChange type="added">then</transChange> the rest, <transChange type="added">some</transChange> of whom <transChange type="added">floated</transChange><note placement="foot">*The word “floated” is not in the Greek text, but is supplied in the translation for clarity</note> on planks and <transChange type="added">some</transChange> of whom on anything <transChange type="added">that was</transChange> from the ship. And in this way all were brought safely to the land.  <chapter eID="Acts.27"/>

verses.name: Acts 28:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11484"/><title type="x-s">Paul on Malta</title> <div sID="gen27006" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11484"/>And <transChange type="added">after we</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“were brought safely through”) which is understood as temporal</note> were brought safely through, then we found out that the island was called Malta.

verses.name: Acts 28:2
verses.text: And the local inhabitants showed <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞extraordinary⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “not the ordinary”</note> kindness to us, for they lit a fire and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“lit”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> welcomed us all, because of the rain that had begun and because of the cold.

verses.name: Acts 28:3
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“had gathered”)</note> Paul had gathered a large number of sticks and was placing them<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> on the fire, a viper came out because of the heat and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came out”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> fastened itself on his hand.

verses.name: Acts 28:4
verses.text: And when the local people saw the creature hanging from his hand, they began saying<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began saying”)</note> to one another, “Doubtless this man is a murderer whom, although he<note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was rescued”) which is understood as concessive</note> was rescued from the sea, Justice<note placement="foot">*Here personified as a goddess</note> has not permitted to live!”

verses.name: Acts 28:5
verses.text: He, in turn, shook off the creature into the fire <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“shook off”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> suffered no harm.

verses.name: Acts 28:6
verses.text: But they were expecting <transChange type="added">that</transChange> he was going to swell up<note placement="foot">Or “to burn with fever” (either meaning is possible here)</note> or suddenly to fall down dead. So after<note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“had waited”)</note> they had waited for a long time and saw nothing unusual happen to him, they changed their minds and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“changed their minds”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> began saying<note placement="foot">*The imperfect tense has been translated as ingressive here (“began saying”)</note> <transChange type="added">that</transChange> he was a god.  <div eID="gen27006" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 28:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11485"/><div sID="gen27007" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11485"/>Now in the <transChange type="added">regions</transChange> around that place were fields belonging to the chief official of the island, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞named⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by name”</note> Publius, who welcomed us and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“welcomed”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> entertained us<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> hospitably <transChange type="added">for</transChange> three days.

verses.name: Acts 28:8
verses.text: And it happened that the father of Publius was lying down, afflicted with fever and dysentery. Paul went<note placement="foot">*Here this participle (“went”) has been translated as a finite verb in keeping with English style</note> to <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “whom”</note> and after<note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“praying”) which is understood as temporal</note> praying, he placed his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> hands on him and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“placed”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> healed him.

verses.name: Acts 28:9
