verses.text: And <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“had taken place”)</note> this had taken place, the rest of those on the island who had diseases were coming and being healed also.

verses.name: Acts 28:10
verses.text: They also honored us with many honors, and <transChange type="added">when we</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“putting out to sea”) which is understood as temporal</note> were putting out to sea, they gave us<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> the things <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞we needed⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “for the needs”</note>  <div eID="gen27007" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 28:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11486"/><title type="x-s">Paul Arrives in Rome at Last</title> <div sID="gen27008" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11486"/>Now after three months we put out to sea in a ship that had wintered at the island, an Alexandrian <transChange type="added">one</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞with the twin gods Castor and Pollux as its insignia⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>.<note placement="foot">Literally “marked with the Dioscuri” (a joint name for the twin gods Castor and Pollux)</note>

verses.name: Acts 28:12
verses.text: And putting in at Syracuse, we stayed <transChange type="added">there</transChange> three days.

verses.name: Acts 28:13
verses.text: From there we got underway<note placement="foot">Or “we sailed along” (with “the coast” understood); the exact meaning of the text as it stands is disputed and various additional terms have to be supplied in any case</note> and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“got underway”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> arrived at Rhegium, and after one day a south wind came up and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“came up”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> on the second day we came to Puteoli,

verses.name: Acts 28:14
verses.text: where we found brothers, <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“found”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> were implored to stay with them seven days. And in this way we came to Rome.

verses.name: Acts 28:15
verses.text: And from there the brothers, <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard the news about us, came to meet us as far as the Forum of Appius and Three Taverns. When he<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as temporal</note> saw them, Paul gave thanks to God and<note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“gave thanks”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> took courage.

verses.name: Acts 28:16
verses.text: And when we entered into Rome, Paul was allowed to stay by himself with the soldier who was guarding him.  <div eID="gen27008" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 28:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11487"/><title type="x-s">Paul and the Jewish Community in Rome</title> <div sID="gen27009" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11487"/>Now it happened that after three days, he called together those who were the most prominent of the Jews. And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“had assembled”)</note> they had assembled, he said to them, “Men and brothers, although<note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had done”) which is understood as concessive</note> I had done nothing against our<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> people or the customs of our fathers, from Jerusalem I was delivered <transChange type="added">as</transChange> a prisoner into the hands of the Romans,

verses.name: Acts 28:18
verses.text: who, <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had examined”) which is understood as temporal</note> had examined me, were wanting to release me,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> because there was no basis for an accusation <transChange type="added">worthy</transChange> of death with me.

verses.name: Acts 28:19
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">because</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the causal genitive absolute participle (“objected”)</note> the Jews objected, I was forced to appeal to Caesar (not as if I<note placement="foot">*Here “if” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had”) which is understood as concessive</note> had any charge to bring against my own people).<note placement="foot">Or “nation”</note>

verses.name: Acts 28:20
verses.text: Therefore for this reason I have requested to see you and to speak with <transChange type="added">you</transChange>,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object is supplied from context in the English translation</note> for because of the hope of Israel I am wearing this chain!”

verses.name: Acts 28:21
verses.text: And they said to him, “We have received no letters about you from Judea, nor has any of the brothers come <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“come”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> reported or spoken anything evil about you.

verses.name: Acts 28:22
verses.text: But we would like to hear from you what you think, for concerning this sect it is known to us that it is spoken against everywhere.”  <div eID="gen27009" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 28:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11488"/><div sID="gen27010" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11488"/>And <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had set”) which is understood as temporal</note> had set a day with him, many more came to him at his lodging place, to whom he was explaining from early in the morning until evening, testifying about the kingdom of God and attempting to convince<note placement="foot">*Here the present tense has been translated as conative (“attempting to convince”)</note> them about Jesus from both the law of Moses and the prophets.

verses.name: Acts 28:24
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">some</transChange> were convinced <transChange type="added">by</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“what was said”) which is understood as means</note> what was said, but <transChange type="added">others</transChange> refused to believe.

verses.name: Acts 28:25
verses.text: So being in disagreement with one another, they began to leave <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“made”)</note> Paul made one statement: “The Holy Spirit spoke rightly through the prophet Isaiah to your fathers,

verses.name: Acts 28:26
verses.text: saying, <div eID="gen27010" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27011"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27012"/>‘Go to this people and say,<l eID="gen27012" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27013"/>“<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞You will keep on hearing⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “hearing you will hear”</note> and will never understand,<l eID="gen27013" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27014"/>and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you will keep on seeing⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “seeing you will see”</note> and will never perceive. <l eID="gen27014" level="1"/>

verses.name: Acts 28:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11489"/><l level="2" sID="gen27015"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11489"/>For the heart of this people has become dull,<l eID="gen27015" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27016"/>and with <transChange type="added">their</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> ears they hear with difficulty,<l eID="gen27016" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27017"/>and they have shut their eyes,<l eID="gen27017" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27018"/>lest they see with <transChange type="added">their</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> eyes,<l eID="gen27018" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27019"/>and hear with <transChange type="added">their</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> ears,<l eID="gen27019" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27020"/>and understand with <transChange type="added">their</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> heart,<l eID="gen27020" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27021"/>and turn, and I would heal them.” ’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.6.9-Isa.6.10">Isa 6:9–10</reference></note> <l eID="gen27021" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen27011"/>

verses.name: Acts 28:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11490"/><div sID="gen27022" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11490"/>Therefore let it be known to you that this salvation of God has been sent to the Gentiles. They also will listen!”<note placement="foot">Some later manuscripts include v. <reference osisRef="Acts.28.29">29</reference>: “And when he had said these things, the Jews departed, having a great dispute among themselves.”</note>  <div eID="gen27022" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 28:30
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11491"/><div sID="gen27023" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11491"/>So he stayed two whole years in his own rented house, and welcomed all who came to him,

verses.name: Acts 28:31
verses.text: proclaiming the kingdom of God and teaching the <transChange type="added">things</transChange> concerning the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness, without hindrance.  <chapter eID="Acts.28"/> <div eID="gen27023" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen26753" osisID="Acts" type="book"/>

verses.name: Romans 1:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11492"/><title type="x-s">Greeting</title> <div sID="gen27025" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11492"/>Paul, a slave of Christ Jesus, called <transChange type="added">to be</transChange> an apostle, set apart for the gospel of God,

verses.name: Romans 1:2
verses.text: which he promised previously through his prophets in the holy scriptures,

verses.name: Romans 1:3
verses.text: concerning his Son, who was born <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a descendant⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “of the seed”</note> of David according to the flesh,

verses.name: Romans 1:4
verses.text: who was declared Son of God in power according to <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the Holy Spirit⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the Spirit of holiness”</note> by the resurrection from the dead of Jesus Christ our Lord,

verses.name: Romans 1:5
verses.text: through whom we have received grace and apostleship for the obedience of faith among all the Gentiles<note placement="foot">Or “nations”; the same Greek word can be translated “nations” or “Gentiles” depending on the context</note> on behalf of his name,

verses.name: Romans 1:6
verses.text: among whom you also are <transChange type="added">the</transChange> called of Jesus Christ.

verses.name: Romans 1:7
verses.text: To all those in Rome who are loved by God, called <transChange type="added">to be</transChange> saints. Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.  <div eID="gen27025" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 1:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11493"/><title type="x-s">Paul Wants to Visit Rome</title> <div sID="gen27026" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11493"/>First, I give thanks to my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because your faith is being proclaimed in the whole world.

verses.name: Romans 1:9
verses.text: For God, whom I serve with my spirit in the gospel of his Son, is my witness, how constantly I make mention of you,

verses.name: Romans 1:10
verses.text: always asking in my prayers if somehow now at last I may succeed to come to you in the will of God.

verses.name: Romans 1:11
verses.text: For I desire to see you, in order that I may impart some spiritual gift to you, in order to strengthen you,

verses.name: Romans 1:12
verses.text: that is, to be encouraged together with you through <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞our mutual faith⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the in one another faith”</note>, both yours and mine.

verses.name: Romans 1:13
verses.text: Now I do not want you to be ignorant, brothers, that often I intended to come to you, and was prevented until now, in order that I might have some fruit among you also, just as also among the rest of the Gentiles.<note placement="foot">Or “nations”; the same Greek word can be translated “nations” or “Gentiles” depending on the context</note>

verses.name: Romans 1:14
verses.text: I am under obligation both to Greeks and to barbarians, both to the wise and to the foolish.

verses.name: Romans 1:15
verses.text: Thus <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I am eager⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the according to me eagerness”</note> to proclaim the gospel also to you who <transChange type="added">are</transChange> in Rome.  <div eID="gen27026" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 1:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11494"/><title type="x-s">The Gospel’s Power for Salvation</title> <div sID="gen27027" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11494"/>For I am not ashamed of the gospel, for it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes, to the Jew first and also to the Greek.

verses.name: Romans 1:17
verses.text: For the righteousness of God is revealed in it from faith to faith, just as it is written, “But the one who is righteous by faith will live.”<note placement="foot">Or “But the one who is righteous will live by faith” (differing only in word order)</note>  <div eID="gen27027" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 1:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11495"/><title type="x-s">God’s Wrath Revealed Against Sinful Humanity</title> <div sID="gen27028" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11495"/>For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all impiety and unrighteousness of people, who suppress the truth in unrighteousness,

verses.name: Romans 1:19
verses.text: because what can be known about God is evident among<note placement="foot">Or “in”; or “within”</note> them, for God made <transChange type="added">it</transChange> clear to them.

verses.name: Romans 1:20
verses.text: For from the creation of the world, his invisible <transChange type="added">attributes</transChange>, both his eternal power and deity, are discerned clearly, being understood in the things created, so that they are without excuse.

verses.name: Romans 1:21
verses.text: For <transChange type="added">although they</transChange> knew God, they did not honor <transChange type="added">him</transChange> as God or give thanks, but they became futile in their reasoning, and their senseless hearts were darkened.

verses.name: Romans 1:22
verses.text: Claiming to be wise, they became fools,

verses.name: Romans 1:23
verses.text: and exchanged the glory of the immortal God with the likeness of an image of mortal human beings and birds and quadrupeds and reptiles.  <div eID="gen27028" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 1:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11496"/><div sID="gen27029" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11496"/>Therefore God gave them over in the desires of their hearts to immorality, <transChange type="added">that</transChange> their bodies would be dishonored among themselves,

verses.name: Romans 1:25
verses.text: who exchanged the truth of God with a lie, and worshiped and served the creation rather than the Creator, who is blessed for eternity. Amen.  <div eID="gen27029" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 1:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11497"/><title type="x-s">God Hands Sinful Humanity over to Depravity</title> <div sID="gen27030" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11497"/>Because of this, God gave them over to degrading passions, for their females exchanged the natural relations for those contrary to nature,

verses.name: Romans 1:27
verses.text: and likewise also the males, abandoning the natural relations with the female, were inflamed in their desire toward one another, males with males committing the shameless deed, and receiving in themselves the penalty that was necessary for their error.

verses.name: Romans 1:28
verses.text: And just as they did not see fit <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to recognize God⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to have God in recognition”</note>, God gave them over to a debased mind, to do the things <transChange type="added">that are</transChange> not proper,

verses.name: Romans 1:29
verses.text: being filled with all unrighteousness, wickedness, greediness, malice, full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, malevolence. <transChange type="added">They are</transChange> gossipers,

verses.name: Romans 1:30
verses.text: slanderers, haters of God, insolent, arrogant, boasters, contrivers of evil, disobedient to parents,

verses.name: Romans 1:31
verses.text: senseless, faithless, unfeeling, unmerciful,

verses.name: Romans 1:32
verses.text: who, <transChange type="added">although they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“know”) which is understood as concessive</note> know the requirements of God, that those who do such things are worthy of death, not only do they do the same <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, but also they approve of those who do <transChange type="added">them</transChange>.  <chapter eID="Rom.1"/>

verses.name: Romans 2:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11498"/><title type="x-s">The Righteous and Impartial Judgment of God</title> <div sID="gen27031" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11498"/>Therefore you are without excuse, O man, every one <transChange type="added">of you</transChange> who passes judgment. For in that which you pass judgment on someone else, you condemn yourself, for you who are passing judgment are doing the same <transChange type="added">things</transChange>.

verses.name: Romans 2:2
verses.text: Now we know that the judgment of God is according to truth against those who do such things.

verses.name: Romans 2:3
verses.text: But do you think this, O man who passes judgment on those who do such things, and who does the same <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, that you will escape the judgment of God?

verses.name: Romans 2:4
verses.text: Or do you despise the wealth of his kindness and forbearance and patience, not knowing that the kindness of God leads you to repentance?

verses.name: Romans 2:5
verses.text: But because of your stubbornness and unrepentant heart, you are storing up for yourself wrath in the day of wrath and of the revelation of the righteous judgment of God,

verses.name: Romans 2:6
verses.text: who will reward each one according to his works:

verses.name: Romans 2:7
verses.text: to those who, by perseverance in good work, seek glory and honor and immortality, eternal life,

verses.name: Romans 2:8
verses.text: but to those <transChange type="added">who act</transChange> from selfish ambition and who disobey the truth, but who obey unrighteousness, wrath and anger.

verses.name: Romans 2:9
verses.text: <transChange type="added">There will be</transChange> affliction and distress for every <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞human being⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “soul of man”</note> who does evil, of the Jew first and of the Greek,

verses.name: Romans 2:10
verses.text: but glory and honor and peace to everyone who does good, to the Jew first and to the Greek.

verses.name: Romans 2:11
verses.text: For <transChange type="added">there</transChange> is no partiality with God.  <div eID="gen27031" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 2:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11499"/><div sID="gen27032" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11499"/>For as many as have sinned without law will also perish without law, and as many as have sinned under the law will be judged by the law.

verses.name: Romans 2:13
verses.text: For it is not the hearers of the law <transChange type="added">who are</transChange> righteous in the sight of God, but the doers of the law will be declared righteous.<note placement="foot">Or “will be justified”</note>

verses.name: Romans 2:14
verses.text: For whenever the Gentiles, who do not have the law, do by nature the things of the law, these, <transChange type="added">although they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“have”) which is understood as concessive</note> do not have the law, are a law to themselves,

verses.name: Romans 2:15
verses.text: who show the work of the law written on their hearts, their conscience bearing witness and their thoughts <transChange type="added">one</transChange> after another accusing or even defending them

verses.name: Romans 2:16
verses.text: on the day when God judges the secret things of people, according to my gospel, through<note placement="foot">Or “by”</note> Christ Jesus.  <div eID="gen27032" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 2:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11500"/><title type="x-s">Jews also Condemned by the Law</title> <div sID="gen27033" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11500"/>But if you call yourself a Jew and rely on the law and boast in God

verses.name: Romans 2:18
verses.text: and know his will and approve the things that are superior, <transChange type="added">because you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“are instructed”) which is understood as causal</note> are instructed by the law,

verses.name: Romans 2:19
verses.text: and are confident <transChange type="added">that</transChange> you yourself are a guide of the blind, a light of those in darkness,

verses.name: Romans 2:20
verses.text: an instructor of the foolish, a teacher of the immature, having the embodiment of knowledge and of the truth in the law.

verses.name: Romans 2:21
verses.text: Therefore, the one who teaches someone else, do you not teach yourself? The one who preaches not to steal, do you steal?

verses.name: Romans 2:22
verses.text: The one who says not to commit adultery, do you commit adultery? The one who abhors idols, do you rob temples?

verses.name: Romans 2:23
verses.text: Who boast in the law, by the transgression of the law you dishonor God!<note placement="foot">Or “do you dishonor God?” (a number of translators and interpreters take this phrase as a final rhetorical question; the present translation regards it as a final summary statement to be taken ironically)</note>

verses.name: Romans 2:24
verses.text: For just as it is written, “The name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.52.5">Isa 52:5</reference></note>  <div eID="gen27033" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 2:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11501"/><div sID="gen27034" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11501"/>For circumcision is of value if you do the law, but if you should be a transgressor of the law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision.

verses.name: Romans 2:26
verses.text: Therefore, if the uncircumcised person follows the requirements of the law, will not his uncircumcision be credited for circumcision?

verses.name: Romans 2:27
verses.text: And the uncircumcised person by nature who carries out the law will judge you who, <transChange type="added">though provided</transChange> with <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the precise written code⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the letter”</note> and circumcision <transChange type="added">are</transChange> a transgressor of the law.

verses.name: Romans 2:28
verses.text: For the Jew is not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞one outwardly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in the open”</note>, nor is circumcision <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞outwardly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in the open”</note>, in the flesh.

verses.name: Romans 2:29
verses.text: But the Jew <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞is one inwardly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in secret”</note>, and circumcision <transChange type="added">is</transChange> of the heart, by the Spirit, not by the letter, whose praise <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not from people but from God.  <chapter eID="Rom.2"/>

verses.name: Romans 3:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11502"/><title type="x-s">Jews Still Have an Advantage</title> <div sID="gen27035" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11502"/>Therefore, what <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the advantage of the Jew, or what <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the use of circumcision?

verses.name: Romans 3:2
verses.text: Much in every way. For first, that they were entrusted with the oracles of God.

verses.name: Romans 3:3
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞What is the result⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for what”</note> if some refused to believe? Their unbelief will not nullify the faithfulness of God, <transChange type="added">will it</transChange>?

verses.name: Romans 3:4
verses.text: May it never be! But let God be true but every human being a liar, just as it is written, <div eID="gen27035" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27036"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27037"/>“In order that you may be justified in your words,<l eID="gen27037" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27038"/>and may prevail when you are<note placement="foot">*Or, if the form is understood as middle voice, “when you yourself judge”</note> judged.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.51.4">Ps 51:4</reference></note> <l eID="gen27038" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen27036"/>

verses.name: Romans 3:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11503"/><div sID="gen27039" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11503"/>But if our unrighteousness demonstrates the righteousness of God, what shall we say? God, who inflicts wrath, <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not unjust, <transChange type="added">is he</transChange>? (I am speaking according to a human perspective.)

verses.name: Romans 3:6
verses.text: May it never be! For otherwise, how will God judge the world?

verses.name: Romans 3:7
verses.text: But if by my lying, the truth of God abounded to his glory, why am I also still condemned as a sinner?

verses.name: Romans 3:8
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">why</transChange> not (as we are slandered, and as some affirm that we say), “Let us do evil, in order that good may come <transChange type="added">of it</transChange>? Their<note placement="foot">Literally “whose”</note> condemnation is just!  <div eID="gen27039" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 3:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11504"/><title type="x-s">The Entire World Guilty of Sin</title> <div sID="gen27040" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11504"/>What then? Do we have an advantage? Not at all. For we have already charged both Jews and Greeks are all under sin,

verses.name: Romans 3:10
verses.text: just as it is written, <div eID="gen27040" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27041"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27042"/>“<transChange type="added">There</transChange> is no one righteous, not even one; <l eID="gen27042" level="1"/>

verses.name: Romans 3:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11505"/><l level="2" sID="gen27043"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11505"/><transChange type="added">there</transChange> is no one who understands;<l eID="gen27043" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27044"/><transChange type="added">there</transChange> is no one who seeks God. <l eID="gen27044" level="2"/>

verses.name: Romans 3:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11506"/><l level="1" sID="gen27045"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11506"/>All have turned aside together; they have become worthless;<l eID="gen27045" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27046"/><transChange type="added">There</transChange> is no one who practices kindness;<l eID="gen27046" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27047"/><transChange type="added">there</transChange> is not even one.<note placement="foot">Verses <reference osisRef="Rom.3.10-Rom.3.12">10–12</reference> are a quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.14.1-Ps.14.3">Ps 14:1–3</reference></note> <l eID="gen27047" level="2"/>

verses.name: Romans 3:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11507"/><l level="1" sID="gen27048"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11507"/>Their throat <transChange type="added">is</transChange> an opened grave;<l eID="gen27048" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27049"/>they deceive with their tongues;<l eID="gen27049" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27050"/>the venom of asps <transChange type="added">is</transChange> under their lips,<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.5.9">Ps 5:9 </reference>and <reference osisRef="Ps.140.3">Ps 140:3</reference></note> <l eID="gen27050" level="1"/>

verses.name: Romans 3:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11508"/><l level="2" sID="gen27051"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11508"/>whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness.<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.10.7">Ps 10:7</reference></note> <l eID="gen27051" level="2"/>

verses.name: Romans 3:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11509"/><l level="1" sID="gen27052"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11509"/>Their feet <transChange type="added">are</transChange> swift to shed blood; <l eID="gen27052" level="1"/>

verses.name: Romans 3:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11510"/><l level="2" sID="gen27053"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11510"/>destruction and distress <transChange type="added">are</transChange> in their paths, <l eID="gen27053" level="2"/>

verses.name: Romans 3:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11511"/><l level="1" sID="gen27054"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11511"/>and they have not known the way of peace.<note placement="foot">Verses <reference osisRef="Rom.3.15-Rom.3.17">15–17</reference> are a quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.59.7-Isa.59.8">Isa 59:7–8</reference></note> <l eID="gen27054" level="1"/>

verses.name: Romans 3:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11512"/><l level="2" sID="gen27055"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11512"/>The fear of God is not before their eyes.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.36.1">Ps 36:1</reference></note> <l eID="gen27055" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen27041"/>

verses.name: Romans 3:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11513"/><div sID="gen27056" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11513"/>Now we know that whatever the law says, it speaks to those under the law, in order that every mouth may be closed and the whole world may become accountable to God.

verses.name: Romans 3:20
verses.text: For by the works of the law <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞no person will be declared righteous⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “all flesh will not be declared righteous”</note> before him, for through the law <transChange type="added">comes</transChange> knowledge of sin.  <div eID="gen27056" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 3:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11514"/><title type="x-s">Righteousness through Faith Revealed</title> <div sID="gen27057" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11514"/>But now, apart from the law, the righteousness of God has been revealed, being testified about by the law and the prophets—

verses.name: Romans 3:22
verses.text: that is, the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ<note placement="foot">Or “through the faithfulness of Jesus Christ”</note> to all who believe. For <transChange type="added">there</transChange> is no distinction,

verses.name: Romans 3:23
verses.text: for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God,

verses.name: Romans 3:24
verses.text: being justified as a gift by his grace, through the redemption which is in Christ Jesus,

verses.name: Romans 3:25
verses.text: whom God made publicly available as the mercy seat<note placement="foot">Or “as the place of propitiation”</note> through faith in his blood, for a demonstration of his righteousness, because of the passing over of previously committed sins,

verses.name: Romans 3:26
verses.text: in the forbearance of God, for the demonstration of his righteousness in the present time, so that he should be just and the one who justifies the <transChange type="added">person</transChange> by faith<note placement="foot">Or “by Jesus’ faithfulness”</note> in Jesus.  <div eID="gen27057" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 3:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11515"/><div sID="gen27058" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11515"/>Therefore, where <transChange type="added">is</transChange> boasting? It has been excluded. By what kind of law? Of works? No, but by a law<note placement="foot">Or “a principle”</note> of faith.

verses.name: Romans 3:28
verses.text: For we consider a person to be justified by faith apart from the works of the law.

verses.name: Romans 3:29
verses.text: Or <transChange type="added">is God</transChange> the God of the Jews only? <transChange type="added">Is he</transChange> not also <transChange type="added">the God</transChange> of the Gentiles? Yes, also of the Gentiles,

verses.name: Romans 3:30
verses.text: since God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> one, who will justify <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞those who are circumcised⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “circumcision”</note> by faith and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞those who are uncircumcised⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “uncircumcision”</note> through faith.

verses.name: Romans 3:31
verses.text: Therefore, do we nullify the law through faith? May it never be! But we uphold the law.  <chapter eID="Rom.3"/>

verses.name: Romans 4:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11516"/><title type="x-s">Abraham’s Faith Counted as Righteousness</title> <div sID="gen27059" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11516"/>What then shall we say <transChange type="added">that</transChange> Abraham, our ancestor according to the flesh, has found?

verses.name: Romans 4:2
verses.text: For if Abraham was justified by works, he has something to boast about, but not before God.

verses.name: Romans 4:3
verses.text: For what does the scripture say? “And Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him for righteousness.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Gen.15.6">Gen 15:6</reference></note>

verses.name: Romans 4:4
verses.text: Now to the one who works, his pay is not credited according to grace, but according to his due.

verses.name: Romans 4:5
verses.text: But to the one who does not work, but who believes in the one who justifies the ungodly, his faith is credited for righteousness,

verses.name: Romans 4:6
verses.text: just as David also speaks about the blessing of the person to whom God credits righteousness apart from works:  <div eID="gen27059" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 4:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11517"/><lg sID="gen27060"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27061"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11517"/>“Blessed <transChange type="added">are they</transChange> whose lawless deeds have been forgiven,<l eID="gen27061" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27062"/>and whose sins are covered over. <l eID="gen27062" level="2"/>

verses.name: Romans 4:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11518"/><l level="1" sID="gen27063"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11518"/>Blessed <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the person against whom the Lord will never count sin.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.32.1-Ps.32.2">Ps 32:1–2</reference></note> <l eID="gen27063" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen27060"/>

verses.name: Romans 4:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11519"/><div sID="gen27064" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11519"/>Therefore, <transChange type="added">is</transChange> this blessing for <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞those who are circumcised⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the circumcision”</note>, or also for <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞those who are uncircumcised⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the uncircumcision”</note>? For we say, “Faith was credited to Abraham for righteousness.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Gen.15.6">Gen 15:6</reference></note>

verses.name: Romans 4:10
verses.text: How then was it credited? <transChange type="added">While he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was”) which is understood as temporal</note> was <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞circumcised⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in circumcision”</note> or <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞uncircumcised⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in uncircumcision”</note>? Not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞while circumcised⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in circumcision”</note> but <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞while uncircumcised⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in uncircumcision”</note>!

verses.name: Romans 4:11
verses.text: And he received the sign of circumcision <transChange type="added">as</transChange> a seal<note placement="foot">Or “confirmation”</note> of the righteousness by faith which he had <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞while uncircumcised⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in uncircumcision”</note>, so that he could be the father of all who believe <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞although they are uncircumcised⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “through uncircumcision”</note>, so that righteousness could be credited to them,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “could be credited to them also”</note>

verses.name: Romans 4:12
verses.text: and the father <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞of those who are circumcised⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “of the circumcision”</note> to those who are not only from the circumcision, but who also follow in the footsteps of the faith of our father Abraham <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞which he had while uncircumcised⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “of the in uncircumcision faith of our father Abraham”</note>.  <div eID="gen27064" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 4:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11520"/><title type="x-s">The Promise to Abraham Secured through Faith</title> <div sID="gen27065" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11520"/>For the promise to Abraham or to his descendants, <transChange type="added">that</transChange> he would be heir of the world, <transChange type="added">was</transChange> not through the law, but through the righteousness by faith.

verses.name: Romans 4:14
verses.text: For if those of the law <transChange type="added">are</transChange> heirs, faith is rendered void and the promise is nullified.

verses.name: Romans 4:15
verses.text: For the law produces wrath, but where <transChange type="added">there</transChange> is no law, neither <transChange type="added">is there</transChange> transgression.

verses.name: Romans 4:16
verses.text: Because of this, <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> by faith, in order that <transChange type="added">it may be</transChange> according to grace, so that the promise may be secure to all the descendants, not only to those of the law, but also to those of the faith of Abraham, who is the father of us all

verses.name: Romans 4:17
verses.text: (just as it is written, “I have made you the father of many nations”)<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Gen.17.5">Gen 17:5</reference></note> before God, in whom he believed, the one who makes the dead alive and who calls the things that are not as <transChange type="added">though</transChange> they are,

verses.name: Romans 4:18
verses.text: who against hope believed in hope, so that he became the father of many nations, according to what was said, “so will your descendants be.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Gen.15.5">Gen 15:5</reference></note>

verses.name: Romans 4:19
verses.text: And not being weak in faith, he considered his own body as good as dead,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “already as good as dead”</note> because he<note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was”) which is understood as causal</note> was approximately a hundred years old, and the deadness of Sarah’s womb.

verses.name: Romans 4:20
verses.text: And he did not waver in unbelief at the promise of God, but was strengthened in faith, giving glory to God

verses.name: Romans 4:21
verses.text: and being fully convinced that what he had promised, he was also able to do.

verses.name: Romans 4:22
verses.text: Therefore<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “Therefore, indeed,”</note> it was credited to him for righteousness.

verses.name: Romans 4:23
verses.text: But it was not written for the sake of him alone that it was credited to him,

verses.name: Romans 4:24
verses.text: but also for the sake of us to whom it is going to be credited, to those who believe in the one who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead,

verses.name: Romans 4:25
verses.text: who was handed over on account of our trespasses, and was raised up in the interest of our justification.<note placement="foot">Or “vindication”; or “acquittal”</note>  <chapter eID="Rom.4"/>

verses.name: Romans 5:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11521"/><title type="x-s">Reconciliation with God through Faith in Christ</title> <div sID="gen27066" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11521"/>Therefore, <transChange type="added">because we</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“have been declared righteous”) which is understood as causal</note> have been declared righteous by faith, we have<note placement="foot">Although a number of important manuscripts read the subjunctive mood here (“let us have”), almost all English versions prefer the indicative mood (“we have”) which is supported by many other manuscripts</note> peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ,

verses.name: Romans 5:2
verses.text: through whom also we have <transChange type="added">obtained</transChange> access by faith into this grace in which we stand, and we boast in the hope of the glory of God.

verses.name: Romans 5:3
verses.text: And not only <transChange type="added">this</transChange>, but we also boast in our afflictions, <transChange type="added">because we</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“know”) which is understood as causal</note> know that affliction produces patient endurance,

verses.name: Romans 5:4
verses.text: and patient endurance, proven character, and proven character, hope,

verses.name: Romans 5:5
verses.text: and hope does not disappoint, because the love of God has been poured out in our hearts through the Holy Spirit who was given to us.  <div eID="gen27066" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 5:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11522"/><div sID="gen27067" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11522"/>For <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the participle (“were”) which is understood as temporal</note> we were still helpless, yet at the proper time Christ died for the ungodly.

verses.name: Romans 5:7
verses.text: For only rarely will someone die on behalf of a righteous person (for on behalf of a good person possibly someone might even dare to die),

verses.name: Romans 5:8
verses.text: but God demonstrates his own love for us, <transChange type="added">in</transChange> that <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the participle (“were”) which is understood as temporal</note> we were still sinners, Christ died for us.

verses.name: Romans 5:9
verses.text: Therefore, by much more, <transChange type="added">because we</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“have been declared righteous”) which is understood as causal</note> have been declared righteous now by his blood, we will be saved through him from the wrath.

verses.name: Romans 5:10
verses.text: For if, <transChange type="added">while we</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the participle (“were”) which is understood as temporal</note> were enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son, by much more, having been reconciled, we will be saved by his life.

verses.name: Romans 5:11
verses.text: And not only <transChange type="added">this</transChange>, but also <transChange type="added">we are</transChange> boasting in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received the reconciliation.  <div eID="gen27067" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 5:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11523"/><title type="x-s">Death Came through Adam but Life Comes through Christ</title> <div sID="gen27068" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11523"/>Because of this, just as sin entered into the world through one man, and death through sin, so also death spread to all people because all sinned.

verses.name: Romans 5:13
verses.text: For until the law, sin was in the world, but sin is not charged to one’s account <transChange type="added">when there</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“is”) which is understood as temporal</note> is no law.

verses.name: Romans 5:14
verses.text: But death reigned from Adam until Moses even over those who did not sin in the likeness of the transgression of Adam, who is a type of the one who is to come.

verses.name: Romans 5:15
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞But the gift is not like the trespass⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “but not like the trespass so also the gift”</note>, for if by the trespass of the one, the many died, by much more did the grace of God and the gift by the grace of the one man, Jesus Christ, multiply to the many.

verses.name: Romans 5:16
verses.text: And the gift <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not as through the one who sinned, for on the one hand, judgment from the one <transChange type="added">sin</transChange> <transChange type="added">led</transChange> to condemnation, but the gift, from many trespasses, <transChange type="added">led</transChange> to justification.

verses.name: Romans 5:17
verses.text: For if by the trespass of the one <transChange type="added">man</transChange>, death reigned through the one <transChange type="added">man</transChange>, much more will those who receive the abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness reign in life through the one, Jesus Christ.

verses.name: Romans 5:18
verses.text: Consequently therefore, as through one trespass <transChange type="added">came</transChange> condemnation to all people, so also through one righteous deed <transChange type="added">came</transChange> justification of life to all people.

verses.name: Romans 5:19
verses.text: For just as through the disobedience of the one man, the many were made sinners, so also through the obedience of the one, the many will be made righteous.

verses.name: Romans 5:20
verses.text: Now the law came in as a side issue, in order that the trespass could increase, but where sin increased, grace was present in greater abundance,

verses.name: Romans 5:21
verses.text: so that just as sin reigned in death, so also grace would reign through righteousness to eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.  <chapter eID="Rom.5"/>

verses.name: Romans 6:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11524"/><title type="x-s">Formerly Dead to Sin, Now Alive in Christ</title> <div sID="gen27069" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11524"/>What therefore shall we say? Shall we continue in sin, in order that grace may increase?

verses.name: Romans 6:2
verses.text: May it never be! How can we who died to sin still live in it?

verses.name: Romans 6:3
verses.text: Or do you not know that as many as were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death?

verses.name: Romans 6:4
verses.text: Therefore we have been buried with him through baptism into death, in order that just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, so also we may live <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a new way of life⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in newness of life”</note>.

verses.name: Romans 6:5
verses.text: For if we have become identified with <transChange type="added">him</transChange> in the likeness of his death, certainly also we will be <transChange type="added">identified with him in the likeness</transChange><note placement="foot">The elliptical phrase “identified with him in the likeness” has been supplied in the translation for clarity</note> of <transChange type="added">his</transChange> resurrection,

verses.name: Romans 6:6
verses.text: knowing this, that our old man was crucified together with <transChange type="added">him</transChange>, in order that the body of sin may be done away with, <transChange type="added">that</transChange> we may no longer be enslaved to sin.

verses.name: Romans 6:7
verses.text: For the one who has died has been freed from sin.  <div eID="gen27069" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 6:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11525"/><div sID="gen27070" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11525"/>Now if we died with Christ, we believe that we will also live with him,

verses.name: Romans 6:9
verses.text: knowing that Christ, <transChange type="added">because he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“has been raised”) which is understood as causal</note> has been raised from the dead, is going to die no more, death no longer being master over him.

verses.name: Romans 6:10
verses.text: For that <transChange type="added">death</transChange> he died, he died to sin once and never again, but that <transChange type="added">life</transChange> he lives, he lives to God.

verses.name: Romans 6:11
verses.text: So also you, consider yourselves to be dead to sin, but alive to God in Christ Jesus.  <div eID="gen27070" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 6:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11526"/><div sID="gen27071" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11526"/>Therefore do not let sin reign in your mortal body, so that <transChange type="added">you</transChange> obey its desires,

verses.name: Romans 6:13
verses.text: and do not present your members to sin <transChange type="added">as</transChange> instruments of unrighteousness, but present yourselves to God as those who are alive from the dead, and your members to God <transChange type="added">as</transChange> instruments of righteousness.

verses.name: Romans 6:14
verses.text: For sin will not be master over you, because you are not under law, but under grace.  <div eID="gen27071" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 6:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11527"/><title type="x-s">Set Free from Sin</title> <div sID="gen27072" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11527"/>What then? Shall we sin because we are not under law but under grace? May it never be!

verses.name: Romans 6:16
verses.text: Do you not know that to whomever you present yourselves <transChange type="added">as</transChange> slaves for obedience, you are slaves to whomever you obey, whether sin, <transChange type="added">leading</transChange> to death, or obedience, <transChange type="added">leading</transChange> to righteousness?

verses.name: Romans 6:17
verses.text: But thanks <transChange type="added">be</transChange> to God that you were slaves of sin, but you have obeyed from the heart the pattern of teaching to which you were entrusted,

verses.name: Romans 6:18
verses.text: and having been set free from sin, you became enslaved to righteousness.

verses.name: Romans 6:19
verses.text: (I am speaking in human terms because of the weakness of your flesh.) For just as you presented your members <transChange type="added">as</transChange> slaves to immorality and lawlessness, <transChange type="added">leading</transChange> to lawlessness, so now present your members <transChange type="added">as</transChange> slaves to righteousness, <transChange type="added">leading</transChange> to sanctification.

verses.name: Romans 6:20
verses.text: For when you were slaves of sin, you were free with respect to righteousness.  <div eID="gen27072" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 6:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11528"/><div sID="gen27073" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11528"/>Therefore what sort of fruit did you have then, about which you are now ashamed? For the end of those <transChange type="added">things</transChange> <transChange type="added">is</transChange> death.

verses.name: Romans 6:22
verses.text: But now, having been set free from sin and having been enslaved to God, you have your fruit <transChange type="added">leading</transChange> to sanctification, and its end <transChange type="added">is</transChange> eternal life.

verses.name: Romans 6:23
verses.text: For the compensation due sin <transChange type="added">is</transChange> death, but the gift of God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.  <chapter eID="Rom.6"/>

verses.name: Romans 7:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11529"/><title type="x-s">Released from the Law through Death</title> <div sID="gen27074" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11529"/>Or do you not know, brothers (for I am speaking to those who know the law), that the law is master of a person for as long a time <transChange type="added">as</transChange> he lives?

verses.name: Romans 7:2
verses.text: For the married woman is bound by law to <transChange type="added">her</transChange> husband while he lives, but if her husband dies, she is released from the law of the husband.

verses.name: Romans 7:3
verses.text: Therefore as a result, if she belongs to another man <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the participle (“is living”) which is understood as temporal</note> her husband is living, she will be called an adulteress. But if her husband dies, she is free from the law, so that she is not an adulteress if she<note placement="foot">*Here “if” is supplied as a component of the participle (“belongs”) which is understood as conditional</note> belongs to another man.

verses.name: Romans 7:4
verses.text: So then, my brothers, you also were brought to death with respect to the law through the body of Christ, so that you may belong to another, to the one who was raised from the dead, in order that we may bear fruit for God.

verses.name: Romans 7:5
verses.text: For when we were in the flesh, sinful desires were working through the law in our members, to bear fruit for death.

verses.name: Romans 7:6
verses.text: But now we have been released from the law, <transChange type="added">because we</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“have died”) which is understood as causal</note> have died <transChange type="added">to that</transChange> by which we were bound, so that we may serve in newness of the Spirit and not in oldness of the letter <transChange type="added">of the law</transChange>.  <div eID="gen27074" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 7:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11530"/><title type="x-s">Knowledge of Sin Comes through the Law</title> <div sID="gen27075" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11530"/>What then shall we say? <transChange type="added">Is</transChange> the law sin? May it never be! But I would not have known sin except through the law, for I would not have known covetousness if the law had not said, “Do not covet.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Exod.20.17">Exod 20:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="Deut.5.21">Deut 5:21</reference></note>

verses.name: Romans 7:8
verses.text: But sin, seizing an opportunity through the commandment, produced in me all <transChange type="added">kinds of</transChange> covetousness. For apart from the law, sin <transChange type="added">is</transChange> dead.

verses.name: Romans 7:9
verses.text: And I was alive once, apart from the law, but <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“came”) which is understood as temporal</note> the commandment came, sin sprang to life

verses.name: Romans 7:10
verses.text: and I died, and this commandment which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> to <transChange type="added">lead to</transChange> life was found with respect to me to <transChange type="added">lead to</transChange> death.

verses.name: Romans 7:11
verses.text: For sin, seizing the opportunity through the commandment, deceived me and through it killed <transChange type="added">me</transChange>.

verses.name: Romans 7:12
verses.text: So then, the law <transChange type="added">is</transChange> holy, and the commandment <transChange type="added">is</transChange> holy and righteous and good.  <div eID="gen27075" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 7:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11531"/><title type="x-s">Internal Conflict with Sin</title> <div sID="gen27076" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11531"/>Therefore, <transChange type="added">did that which is</transChange> good become death to me? May it never be! Rather <transChange type="added">it was</transChange> sin, in order that it might be recognized <transChange type="added">as</transChange> sin, producing death through <transChange type="added">what is</transChange> good for me, in order that sin might become sinful to an extraordinary degree through the commandment.

verses.name: Romans 7:14
verses.text: For we know that the law is spiritual, but I am fleshly, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞sold into slavery to sin⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “sold under sin”</note>.

verses.name: Romans 7:15
verses.text: For what I am doing I do not understand, because what I want <transChange type="added">to do</transChange>, this I do not practice, but what I hate, this I do.

verses.name: Romans 7:16
verses.text: But if what I do not want <transChange type="added">to do</transChange>, this I do, I agree with the law that <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> good.

verses.name: Romans 7:17
verses.text: But now I am no longer the one doing it, but sin that lives in me.

verses.name: Romans 7:18
verses.text: For I know that good does not live in me, that is, in my flesh. For the willing is present in me, but the doing <transChange type="added">of</transChange> the good <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not.

verses.name: Romans 7:19
verses.text: For the good that I want <transChange type="added">to do</transChange>, I do not do, but the evil that I do not want <transChange type="added">to do</transChange>, this I do.

verses.name: Romans 7:20
verses.text: But if what I do not want <transChange type="added">to do</transChange>, this I am doing, I am no longer the one doing it, but sin that lives in me.  <div eID="gen27076" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 7:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11532"/><div sID="gen27077" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11532"/>Consequently, I find the principle with me, the one who wants to do good, that evil is present with me.<note placement="foot">Or “in me”</note>

verses.name: Romans 7:22
verses.text: For I joyfully agree with the law of God in my inner person,

verses.name: Romans 7:23
verses.text: but I observe another law in my members, at war with the law of my mind and making me captive to the law of sin that exists in my members.

verses.name: Romans 7:24
verses.text: Wretched man <transChange type="added">that</transChange> I <transChange type="added">am</transChange>! Who will rescue me from this body of death?

verses.name: Romans 7:25
verses.text: Thanks <transChange type="added">be</transChange><note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “But thanks be”</note> to God through Jesus Christ our Lord! So then, I myself with my mind am enslaved to the law of God, but with my flesh <transChange type="added">I am enslaved</transChange> to the law of sin.  <chapter eID="Rom.7"/>

verses.name: Romans 8:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11533"/><title type="x-s">Set Free from the Law of Sin and Death</title> <div sID="gen27078" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11533"/>Consequently, <transChange type="added">there is</transChange> now no condemnation for those <transChange type="added">who are</transChange> in Christ Jesus.

verses.name: Romans 8:2
verses.text: For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has set you free from the law of sin and death.

verses.name: Romans 8:3
verses.text: For what <transChange type="added">was</transChange> impossible for the law, in that it was weak through the flesh, God <transChange type="added">did</transChange>. <transChange type="added">By</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“sending”) which is understood as means</note> sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh and concerning sin, he condemned sin in the flesh,

verses.name: Romans 8:4
verses.text: in order that the requirement of the law would be fulfilled in us, who do not live according to the flesh but according to the Spirit.

verses.name: Romans 8:5
verses.text: For those who are <transChange type="added">living</transChange> according to the flesh are intent on the things of the flesh, but those <transChange type="added">who are living</transChange> according to the Spirit <transChange type="added">are intent on</transChange> the things of the Spirit.

verses.name: Romans 8:6
verses.text: For the mindset of the flesh <transChange type="added">is</transChange> death, but the mindset of the Spirit <transChange type="added">is</transChange> life and peace,

verses.name: Romans 8:7
verses.text: because the mindset of the flesh <transChange type="added">is</transChange> enmity toward God, for <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> not subjected to the law of God, for <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> not able <transChange type="added">to do so</transChange>,

verses.name: Romans 8:8
verses.text: and those who are in the flesh are not able to please God.  <div eID="gen27078" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 8:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11534"/><div sID="gen27079" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11534"/>But you are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if indeed the Spirit of God lives in you. But if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, this person <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞does not belong to him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “is not of him”</note>.

verses.name: Romans 8:10
verses.text: But if Christ <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in you, the body <transChange type="added">is</transChange> dead because of sin, but the Spirit <transChange type="added">is</transChange> life because of righteousness.

verses.name: Romans 8:11
verses.text: And if the Spirit of the one who raised Jesus from the dead lives in you, the one who raised Christ Jesus<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts omit “Jesus”</note> from the dead will also make alive your mortal bodies through his Spirit who lives in you.  <div eID="gen27079" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 8:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11535"/><div sID="gen27080" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11535"/>So then, brothers, we are obligated not to the flesh, to live according to the flesh.

verses.name: Romans 8:13
verses.text: For if you live according to the flesh, you are going to die, but if by the Spirit you put to death the deeds of the body, you will live.

verses.name: Romans 8:14
verses.text: For all those who are led by the Spirit of God, these are sons of God.

verses.name: Romans 8:15
verses.text: For you have not received a spirit of slavery <transChange type="added">leading</transChange> to fear again, but you have received the Spirit of adoption, by whom we cry out, “Abba!<note placement="foot">“Abba” means “father” in Aramaic</note> Father!”

verses.name: Romans 8:16
verses.text: The Spirit himself confirms to our spirit that we are children of God,

verses.name: Romans 8:17
verses.text: and if children, also heirs—heirs of God and fellow heirs with Christ, if indeed we suffer together <transChange type="added">with him</transChange> so that we may also be glorified together <transChange type="added">with him</transChange>.  <div eID="gen27080" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 8:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11536"/><title type="x-s">The Glory that is to be Revealed</title> <div sID="gen27081" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11536"/>For I consider that the sufferings of the present time are not worthy <transChange type="added">to be compared</transChange> with the glory that is about to be revealed to us.

verses.name: Romans 8:19
verses.text: For the eagerly expecting creation awaits eagerly the revelation of the sons of God.

verses.name: Romans 8:20
verses.text: For the creation has been subjected to futility, not willingly, but because of the one who subjected <transChange type="added">it</transChange>, in hope

verses.name: Romans 8:21
verses.text: that the creation itself also will be set free from its servility to decay, into the glorious freedom of the children of God.

verses.name: Romans 8:22
verses.text: For we know that the whole creation groans together and suffers agony together until now.

verses.name: Romans 8:23
verses.text: Not only <transChange type="added">this</transChange>, but we ourselves also, having the first fruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves <transChange type="added">while we</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the participle (“await eagerly”) which is understood as temporal</note> await eagerly <transChange type="added">our</transChange> adoption, the redemption of our body.

verses.name: Romans 8:24
verses.text: For in hope we were saved, but hope that is seen is not hope, for who hopes for what he sees?

verses.name: Romans 8:25
verses.text: But if we hope for what we do not see, we await <transChange type="added">it</transChange> eagerly with patient endurance.  <div eID="gen27081" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 8:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11537"/><div sID="gen27082" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11537"/>And likewise also, the Spirit helps <transChange type="added">us</transChange> in our weakness, for we do not know how to pray as one ought, but the Spirit himself intercedes <transChange type="added">for us</transChange> <transChange type="added">with</transChange> unexpressed groanings.

verses.name: Romans 8:27
verses.text: And the one who searches our hearts knows what the mindset of the Spirit <transChange type="added">is</transChange>, because he intercedes on behalf of the saints according to <transChange type="added">the will of</transChange> God.

verses.name: Romans 8:28
verses.text: And we know that all <transChange type="added">things</transChange> work together for good for those who love God, for those who are called according to <transChange type="added">his</transChange> purpose,

verses.name: Romans 8:29
verses.text: because <transChange type="added">those</transChange> whom he foreknew, he also predestined <transChange type="added">to be</transChange> conformed to the image of his Son, so that he should be the firstborn among many brothers.

verses.name: Romans 8:30
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">those</transChange> whom he predestined, these <transChange type="added">he</transChange> also called, and <transChange type="added">those</transChange> whom he called, these <transChange type="added">he</transChange> also justified, and <transChange type="added">those</transChange> whom he justified, these <transChange type="added">he</transChange> also glorified.  <div eID="gen27082" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 8:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11538"/><title type="x-s">Victory in Christ</title> <div sID="gen27083" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11538"/>What then shall we say about these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>? If God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> for us, who <transChange type="added">can be</transChange> against us?

verses.name: Romans 8:32
verses.text: Indeed, <transChange type="added">he</transChange> who did not spare his own Son, but gave him up for us all, how will he not also, together with him, freely give us all <transChange type="added">things</transChange>?

verses.name: Romans 8:33
verses.text: Who will bring charges against God’s elect? God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the one who justifies.

verses.name: Romans 8:34
verses.text: Who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the one who condemns? Christ<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “Christ Jesus”</note> <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the one who died, and more than that, who was raised, who is also at the right hand of God, who also intercedes for us.

verses.name: Romans 8:35
verses.text: Who will separate us from the love of Christ? <transChange type="added">Will</transChange> affliction or distress or persecution or hunger or lack of sufficient clothing or danger or the sword?

verses.name: Romans 8:36
verses.text: Just as it is written, <div eID="gen27083" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27084"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27085"/>“On account of you we are being put to death the whole day <transChange type="added">long</transChange>;<l eID="gen27085" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27086"/>we are considered as sheep for slaughter.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.44.22">Ps 44:22</reference></note> <l eID="gen27086" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen27084"/>

verses.name: Romans 8:37
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11539"/><div sID="gen27087" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11539"/><transChange type="added">No</transChange>, but in all these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> we prevail completely through the one who loved us.

verses.name: Romans 8:38
verses.text: For I am convinced that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor rulers, nor things present, nor things to come, nor powers,

verses.name: Romans 8:39
verses.text: nor height, nor depth, nor any other created thing, will be able to separate us from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus our Lord.  <chapter eID="Rom.8"/>

verses.name: Romans 9:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11540"/><title type="x-s">Israel’s Rejection</title> <div sID="gen27088" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11540"/>I am telling the truth in Christ—<transChange type="added">I am</transChange> not lying; my conscience bears witness to me in the Holy Spirit—

verses.name: Romans 9:2
verses.text: that my grief is great and <transChange type="added">there is</transChange> constant distress in my heart.

verses.name: Romans 9:3
verses.text: For I could wish myself to be accursed from Christ for the sake of my brothers, my fellow countrymen according to the flesh,

verses.name: Romans 9:4
verses.text: who are Israelites, <transChange type="added">to</transChange> whom <transChange type="added">belong</transChange> the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the law, and the <transChange type="added">temple</transChange> service, and the promises,

verses.name: Romans 9:5
verses.text: <transChange type="added">to</transChange> whom <transChange type="added">belong</transChange> the patriarchs, and from whom <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the Christ according to human descent, who is God over all, blessed <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for eternity”</note>! Amen.  <div eID="gen27088" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 9:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11541"/><div sID="gen27089" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11541"/>But <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> not as if the word of God had failed. For not all those <transChange type="added">who are descended</transChange> from Israel <transChange type="added">are truly</transChange> Israel,

verses.name: Romans 9:7
verses.text: nor <transChange type="added">are they</transChange> all children because they are descendants of Abraham, but “In Isaac will your descendants be named.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Gen.21.12">Gen 21:12</reference></note>

verses.name: Romans 9:8
verses.text: That is, <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> not the children <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞by human descent⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “of the flesh”</note> <transChange type="added">who are</transChange> children of God, but the children of the promise are counted as descendants.

verses.name: Romans 9:9
verses.text: For the statement of the promise <transChange type="added">is</transChange> this: “At this time I will return and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Sarah will have⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “there will be to Sarah”</note> a son.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Gen.18.10">Gen 18:10</reference>, <reference osisRef="Gen.18.14">14</reference></note>

verses.name: Romans 9:10
verses.text: And not only <transChange type="added">this</transChange>, but also <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“having conception” = “conceived”) which is understood as temporal</note> Rebecca conceived children by one man,<note placement="foot">Or perhaps “by one act of sexual intercourse”</note> Isaac our father—

verses.name: Romans 9:11
verses.text: for <transChange type="added">although they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“been born”) which is understood as concessive</note> had not yet been born, or done anything good or evil, in order that the purpose of God according to election might remain,

verses.name: Romans 9:12
verses.text: not by works but by the one who calls—it was said to her, “The older will serve the younger,”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Gen.25.23">Gen 25:23</reference></note>

verses.name: Romans 9:13
