verses.text: just as it is written, “Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Mal.1.2-Mal.1.3">Mal 1:2–3</reference></note>  <div eID="gen27089" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 9:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11542"/><title type="x-s">God’s Sovereign Choice to Show Mercy</title> <div sID="gen27090" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11542"/>What then shall we say? <transChange type="added">There is</transChange> no injustice with God, <transChange type="added">is there</transChange>?<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here</note> May it never be!

verses.name: Romans 9:15
verses.text: For to Moses he says, “I will have mercy on whomever I have mercy, and I will have compassion on whomever I have compassion.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Exod.33.19">Exod 33:19</reference></note>

verses.name: Romans 9:16
verses.text: Consequently therefore, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞it does not depend on the⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “not of the”</note> one who wills or on the one who runs, but on God who shows mercy.

verses.name: Romans 9:17
verses.text: For the scripture says to Pharaoh, “For this very <transChange type="added">reason</transChange> I have raised you up, so that I may demonstrate my power in you, and so that my name might be proclaimed in all the earth.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Exod.9.16">Exod 9:16</reference></note>

verses.name: Romans 9:18
verses.text: Consequently therefore, he has mercy on whomever he wishes, and he hardens whomever he wishes.  <div eID="gen27090" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 9:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11543"/><div sID="gen27091" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11543"/>Therefore you will say to me, “Why then does he still find fault? For who has resisted<note placement="foot">Or “who resists”</note> his will?

verses.name: Romans 9:20
verses.text: On the contrary, O man, who are you who answers back to God? Will what is molded say to the one who molded <transChange type="added">it</transChange>, “Why did you make me like this”?<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.29.16">Isa 29:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.45.9">45:9</reference></note>

verses.name: Romans 9:21
verses.text: Or does the potter not have authority over the clay, to make from the same lump a vessel that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> for <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞honorable use⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “honor”</note> and one that is for <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞ordinary use⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “dishonor”</note>?

verses.name: Romans 9:22
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">what</transChange> if God, wanting to demonstrate his wrath and to make known his power, endured with much patience vessels of wrath prepared for destruction?

verses.name: Romans 9:23
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">he did so</transChange><note placement="foot">*The words “he did so” are not in the Greek text, but are an understood repetition from the previous clause</note> in order that he could make known the riches of his glory upon vessels of mercy that he prepared beforehand for glory,

verses.name: Romans 9:24
verses.text: us whom he also called, not only from the Jews but also from the Gentiles?

verses.name: Romans 9:25
verses.text: As he also says in Hosea, <div eID="gen27091" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27092"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27093"/>“I will call those <transChange type="added">who were</transChange> not my people, ‘My people,’<l eID="gen27093" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27094"/>and those <transChange type="added">who were</transChange> not loved, ‘Loved.’<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Hos.2.23">Hos 2:23</reference></note> <l eID="gen27094" level="2"/>

verses.name: Romans 9:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11544"/><l level="1" sID="gen27095"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11544"/>And it will be in the place where it was said to them, ‘You <transChange type="added">are</transChange> not my people,’<l eID="gen27095" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27096"/>there they will be called ‘sons of the living God.’ ”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Hos.1.10">Hos 1:10</reference></note> <l eID="gen27096" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen27092"/>

verses.name: Romans 9:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11545"/><div sID="gen27097" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11545"/>And Isaiah cries out concerning Israel, <div eID="gen27097" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27098"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27099"/>“<transChange type="added">Even</transChange> if the number of the sons of Israel is like the sand of the sea,<l eID="gen27099" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27100"/>the remnant will be saved, <l eID="gen27100" level="2"/>

verses.name: Romans 9:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11546"/><l level="1" sID="gen27101"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11546"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞for the Lord will execute his sentence thoroughly and decisively⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for the Lord will act, closing the account and cutting short”</note> upon the earth.”<note placement="foot">A paraphrased quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.10.22-Isa.10.23">Isa 10:22–23</reference></note> <l eID="gen27101" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen27098"/>

verses.name: Romans 9:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11547"/><div sID="gen27102" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11547"/>And just as Isaiah foretold, <div eID="gen27102" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27103"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27104"/>“If the Lord of hosts had not left us descendants,<l eID="gen27104" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27105"/>we would have become like Sodom<l eID="gen27105" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen27106"/>and would have resembled Gomorrah.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.1.9">Isa 1:9</reference></note> <l eID="gen27106" level="3"/> <lg eID="gen27103"/>

verses.name: Romans 9:30
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11548"/><div sID="gen27107" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11548"/>What then shall we say? That the Gentiles, who did not pursue righteousness, attained righteousness—even the righteousness <transChange type="added">that is</transChange> by faith.

verses.name: Romans 9:31
verses.text: But Israel, pursuing the law of righteousness, did not attain to the law.

verses.name: Romans 9:32
verses.text: Why that? Because <transChange type="added">they did</transChange> not <transChange type="added">pursue it</transChange> by faith, but as <transChange type="added">if</transChange> by works. They stumbled over the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞stone that causes people to stumble⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “stone of stumbling”</note>,

verses.name: Romans 9:33
verses.text: just as it is written, <div eID="gen27107" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27108"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27109"/>“Behold, I am laying in Zion <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a stone that causes people to stumble⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a stone of stumbling”</note>,<l eID="gen27109" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27110"/>and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a rock that causes them to fall⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “a rock of offense”</note>,<l eID="gen27110" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27111"/>and the one who believes in him will not be put to shame.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.28.16">Isa 28:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.8.14">8:14</reference></note> <l eID="gen27111" level="1"/><lg eID="gen27108"/> <chapter eID="Rom.9"/>

verses.name: Romans 10:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11549"/><title type="x-s">The Righteousness of God through Faith in Christ</title> <div sID="gen27112" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11549"/>Brothers, the desire of my heart and my prayer to God on behalf of them <transChange type="added">is</transChange> for <transChange type="added">their</transChange> salvation.

verses.name: Romans 10:2
verses.text: For I testify about them that they have a zeal for God, but not according to knowledge.

verses.name: Romans 10:3
verses.text: For ignoring the righteousness of God, and seeking to establish their own,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “their own righteousness”</note> they did not subject themselves to the righteousness of God.

verses.name: Romans 10:4
verses.text: For Christ <transChange type="added">is the</transChange> end of the law for righteousness to everyone who believes.  <div eID="gen27112" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 10:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11550"/><div sID="gen27113" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11550"/>For Moses writes about the righteousness <transChange type="added">that is</transChange> from the law: “The person who does <transChange type="added">this</transChange><note placement="foot">Some manuscripts explicitly state “these things”</note> will live by it.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Lev.18.5">Lev 18:5</reference></note><note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “them”</note>

verses.name: Romans 10:6
verses.text: But the righteousness from faith speaks like this: “Do not say in your heart,<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Deut.9.4">Deut 9:4</reference></note> ‘Who will ascend into heaven?’ ”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Deut.30.12">Deut 30:12</reference></note> (that is, to bring Christ down),

verses.name: Romans 10:7
verses.text: or “Who will descend into the abyss?”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Deut.30.13">Deut 30:13</reference></note> (that is, to bring Christ up from the dead).

verses.name: Romans 10:8
verses.text: But what does it say? “The word is near to you, in your mouth and in your heart”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Deut.30.14">Deut 30:14</reference></note> (that is, the word of faith that we proclaim),

verses.name: Romans 10:9
verses.text: that<note placement="foot">Or “because”</note> if you confess with your mouth “Jesus <transChange type="added">is</transChange> Lord” and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.

verses.name: Romans 10:10
verses.text: For with the heart one believes, resulting in righteousness, and with the mouth one confesses, resulting in salvation.

verses.name: Romans 10:11
verses.text: For the scripture says, “Everyone who believes in him will not be put to shame.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.28.16">Isa 28:16</reference></note>

verses.name: Romans 10:12
verses.text: For <transChange type="added">there</transChange> is no distinction between Jew and Greek, for the same <transChange type="added">Lord</transChange> <transChange type="added">is</transChange> Lord of all, who is rich to all who call upon him.

verses.name: Romans 10:13
verses.text: For “everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord will be saved.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Joel.2.32">Joel 2:32</reference></note>  <div eID="gen27113" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 10:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11551"/><div sID="gen27114" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11551"/>How then will they call upon <transChange type="added">him</transChange> in whom they have not believed? And how will they believe <transChange type="added">in him</transChange> about whom they have not heard? And how will they hear about <transChange type="added">him</transChange> without one who preaches <transChange type="added">to them</transChange>?

verses.name: Romans 10:15
verses.text: And how will they preach, unless they are sent? Just as it is written, “How timely <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the feet of those who bring good news of good things.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.52.7">Isa 52:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="Nah.1.15">Nah 1:15</reference></note>

verses.name: Romans 10:16
verses.text: But not all have obeyed the good news, for Isaiah says, “Lord, who has believed our report?”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.53.1">Isa 53:1</reference></note>

verses.name: Romans 10:17
verses.text: Consequently, faith <transChange type="added">comes</transChange> by hearing, and hearing through the word about Christ.  <div eID="gen27114" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 10:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11552"/><div sID="gen27115" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11552"/>But I say, they have not heard, have they?<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here</note> On the contrary, <div eID="gen27115" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27116"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27117"/>“Their voice has gone out to all the earth,<l eID="gen27117" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27118"/>and their words to the ends of the inhabited world.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.19.4">Ps 19:4</reference></note> <l eID="gen27118" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen27116"/>

verses.name: Romans 10:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11553"/><div sID="gen27119" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11553"/>But I say, Israel did not know, did they?<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here</note> First, Moses says, <div eID="gen27119" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27120"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27121"/>“I will provoke you <transChange type="added">to jealousy</transChange> by <transChange type="added">those who are</transChange> not a nation;<l eID="gen27121" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27122"/>by a senseless nation I will provoke you <transChange type="added">to anger</transChange>.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Deut.32.21">Deut 32:21</reference></note> <l eID="gen27122" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen27120"/>

verses.name: Romans 10:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11554"/><div sID="gen27123" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11554"/>And Isaiah is very bold and says, <div eID="gen27123" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27124"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27125"/>“I was found by those who did not seek me;<l eID="gen27125" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27126"/>I became known to those who did not ask for me.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.65.1">Isa 65:1</reference></note> <l eID="gen27126" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen27124"/>

verses.name: Romans 10:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11555"/><div sID="gen27127" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11555"/>But about Israel he says, <div eID="gen27127" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27128"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27129"/>“The whole day <transChange type="added">long</transChange> I held out my hands<l eID="gen27129" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27130"/>to a disobedient and resistant people.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.65.2">Isa 65:2</reference></note> <l eID="gen27130" level="2"/><lg eID="gen27128"/> <chapter eID="Rom.10"/>

verses.name: Romans 11:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11556"/><title type="x-s">A Remnant of Israel Remains</title> <div sID="gen27131" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11556"/>Therefore I say, God has not rejected his people, has he?<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here</note> May it never be! For I also am an Israelite, from the descendants of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.

verses.name: Romans 11:2
verses.text: God has not rejected his people, whom he foreknew! Or do you not know, in <transChange type="added">the passage about</transChange><note placement="foot">*The words “the passage about” are not in the Greek text, but are supplied for clarity</note> Elijah, what the scripture says—how he appeals to God against Israel?

verses.name: Romans 11:3
verses.text: “Lord, they have killed your prophets, they have torn down your altars, and I alone am left, and they are seeking my life!”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="1Kgs.19.10">1 Kgs 19:10</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Kgs.19.14">14</reference></note>

verses.name: Romans 11:4
verses.text: But what does the divine response say to him? “I have left for myself seven thousand people<note placement="foot">Or perhaps “males,” referring to men only</note> who have not bent the knee to Baal.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="1Kgs.19.18">1 Kgs 19:18</reference></note>

verses.name: Romans 11:5
verses.text: So in this way also at the present time, there is a remnant <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞selected by grace⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “according to selection of grace”</note>.

verses.name: Romans 11:6
verses.text: But if by grace, <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> no longer by works, for otherwise grace would no longer be grace.  <div eID="gen27131" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 11:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11557"/><div sID="gen27132" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11557"/>What then? What Israel was searching for, this it did not obtain. But the elect obtained <transChange type="added">it</transChange>, and the rest were hardened,

verses.name: Romans 11:8
verses.text: just as it is written, <div eID="gen27132" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27133"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27134"/>“God gave them a spirit of stupor,<l eID="gen27134" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27135"/>eyes that do not see and ears that do not hear,<l eID="gen27135" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27136"/>until this very day.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Deut.29.4">Deut 29:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.29.10">Isa 29:10</reference></note> <l eID="gen27136" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen27133"/>

verses.name: Romans 11:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11558"/><div sID="gen27137" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11558"/>And David says, <div eID="gen27137" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27138"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27139"/>“Let their table become a snare and a trap,<l eID="gen27139" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27140"/>and a cause for stumbling and a retribution to them; <l eID="gen27140" level="2"/>

verses.name: Romans 11:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11559"/><l level="1" sID="gen27141"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11559"/>let their eyes be darkened so that they do not see,<l eID="gen27141" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27142"/>and cause their backs to bend <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞continually⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “throughout everything”</note>.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.69.22-Ps.69.23">Ps 69:22–23</reference></note> <l eID="gen27142" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen27138"/>

verses.name: Romans 11:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11560"/><div sID="gen27143" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11560"/>I say then, they did not stumble so that they fell, <transChange type="added">did they</transChange>?<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here</note> May it never be! But by their trespass, salvation has come to the Gentiles, in order to provoke them to jealousy.<note placement="foot">*The words “to jealousy” are not in the Greek text, but are supplied for clarity</note>

verses.name: Romans 11:12
verses.text: And if their trespass <transChange type="added">means</transChange> riches for the world and their loss <transChange type="added">means</transChange> riches for the Gentiles, how much more <transChange type="added">will</transChange> their fullness <transChange type="added">mean</transChange>?  <div eID="gen27143" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 11:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11561"/><title type="x-s">Gentile Branches Grafted in</title> <div sID="gen27144" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11561"/>Now I am speaking to you Gentiles. Therefore, inasmuch as I am apostle to the Gentiles, I promote my ministry,

verses.name: Romans 11:14
verses.text: if somehow I may provoke my people to jealousy and save some of them.

verses.name: Romans 11:15
verses.text: For if their rejection <transChange type="added">means</transChange> the reconciliation of the world, what <transChange type="added">will</transChange> their acceptance <transChange type="added">mean</transChange> except life from the dead?

verses.name: Romans 11:16
verses.text: Now if the first fruits <transChange type="added">are</transChange> holy, <transChange type="added">so</transChange> also <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the <transChange type="added">whole</transChange> batch of dough, and if the root <transChange type="added">is</transChange> holy, <transChange type="added">so</transChange> also <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the branches.  <div eID="gen27144" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 11:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11562"/><div sID="gen27145" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11562"/>Now if some of the branches were broken off, and you, <transChange type="added">although you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“were”) which is understood as concessive</note> were a wild olive tree, were grafted in among them and became a sharer of the root of the olive tree’s richness,

verses.name: Romans 11:18
verses.text: do not boast against the branches. But if you boast against <transChange type="added">them</transChange>, you do not support the root, but the root <transChange type="added">supports</transChange> you.

verses.name: Romans 11:19
verses.text: Then you will say, “Branches were broken off in order that I could be grafted in.”

verses.name: Romans 11:20
verses.text: Well said! They were broken off because of unbelief, but you stand firm because of faith. Do not think arrogant <transChange type="added">thoughts</transChange>, but be afraid.

verses.name: Romans 11:21
verses.text: For if God did not spare the <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞natural⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “according to nature”</note> branches, neither will he spare you.<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “perhaps he will not spare you either”</note>

verses.name: Romans 11:22
verses.text: See, then, the kindness and severity of God: severity upon those who have fallen, but upon you the kindness of God—if you continue in his kindness, for otherwise you also will be cut off.

verses.name: Romans 11:23
verses.text: And those also, if they do not persist in unbelief, will be grafted in, because God is able to graft them in again.

verses.name: Romans 11:24
verses.text: For if you were cut off from what is by nature a wild olive tree, and contrary to nature were grafted into a cultivated olive tree, how much more will these who are <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞natural branches⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by nature”</note> be grafted into their own olive tree?  <div eID="gen27145" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 11:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11563"/><title type="x-s">All Israel to be Saved</title> <div sID="gen27146" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11563"/>For I do not want you to be ignorant, brothers, of this mystery, so that you will not be wise <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in your own sight⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/>,<note placement="foot">Literally “in yourselves”</note> that a partial hardening has happened to Israel, until the full number of the Gentiles has come in,

verses.name: Romans 11:26
verses.text: and so all Israel will be saved, just as it is written, <div eID="gen27146" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27147"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27148"/>“The deliverer will come out of Zion;<l eID="gen27148" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27149"/>he will turn away ungodliness from Jacob. <l eID="gen27149" level="2"/>

verses.name: Romans 11:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11564"/><l level="1" sID="gen27150"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11564"/>And this <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the covenant from me with them<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.59.20-Isa.59.21">Isa 59:20–21</reference></note><l eID="gen27150" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27151"/>when I take away their sins.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.27.9">Isa 27:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.31.33-Jer.31.34">Jer 31:33–34</reference></note> <l eID="gen27151" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen27147"/>

verses.name: Romans 11:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11565"/><div sID="gen27152" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11565"/>With respect to the gospel, <transChange type="added">they are</transChange> enemies for your sake, but with respect to election, <transChange type="added">they are</transChange> dearly loved for the sake of the fathers.

verses.name: Romans 11:29
verses.text: For the gifts and the calling of God <transChange type="added">are</transChange> irrevocable.

verses.name: Romans 11:30
verses.text: For just as you formerly were disobedient to God, but now have been shown mercy because of the disobedience of these,

verses.name: Romans 11:31
verses.text: so also these have now been disobedient for your mercy, in order that they also may now be shown mercy.

verses.name: Romans 11:32
verses.text: For God confined them all in disobedience, in order that he could have mercy on them all.  <div eID="gen27152" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 11:33
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11566"/><lg sID="gen27153"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27154"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11566"/>Oh, the depth of the riches<l eID="gen27154" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27155"/>and the wisdom and the knowledge of God!<l eID="gen27155" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27156"/>How unsearchable <transChange type="added">are</transChange> his judgments<l eID="gen27156" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27157"/>and <transChange type="added">how</transChange> incomprehensible <transChange type="added">are</transChange> his ways! <l eID="gen27157" level="2"/>

verses.name: Romans 11:34
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11567"/><l level="1" sID="gen27158"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11567"/>“For who has known the mind of the Lord,<l eID="gen27158" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27159"/>or who has been his counselor?<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.40.13">Isa 40:13</reference></note> <l eID="gen27159" level="2"/>

verses.name: Romans 11:35
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11568"/><l level="1" sID="gen27160"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11568"/>Or who has given in advance to him,<l eID="gen27160" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27161"/>and it will be paid back to him?”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Job.41.11">Job 41:11</reference></note> <l eID="gen27161" level="2"/>

verses.name: Romans 11:36
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11569"/><l level="1" sID="gen27162"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11569"/>For from him and through him and to him <transChange type="added">are</transChange> all <transChange type="added">things</transChange>.<l eID="gen27162" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27163"/>To him <transChange type="added">be</transChange> glory for eternity! Amen. <l eID="gen27163" level="2"/><lg eID="gen27153"/> <chapter eID="Rom.11"/>

verses.name: Romans 12:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11570"/><title type="x-s">A Life Dedicated to God</title> <div sID="gen27164" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11570"/>Therefore I exhort you, brothers, through the mercies of God, to present your bodies <transChange type="added">as</transChange> a living sacrifice, holy <transChange type="added">and</transChange> pleasing to God, <transChange type="added">which is</transChange> your reasonable service.

verses.name: Romans 12:2
verses.text: And do not be conformed to this age, but be transformed by the renewal of your mind, so that you may approve what <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the good and well-pleasing and perfect will of God.  <div eID="gen27164" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 12:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11571"/><title type="x-s">A Variety of Gifts in the Body of Christ</title> <div sID="gen27165" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11571"/>For by the grace given to me I say to everyone who is among you not to think more highly of yourself than what one ought to think, but to think <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞sensibly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “so as to be sensible”</note>, as God has apportioned a measure of faith to each one.

verses.name: Romans 12:4
verses.text: For just as in one body we have many members, but all the members do not have the same function,

verses.name: Romans 12:5
verses.text: in the same way we who are many are one body in Christ, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞individually⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “with respect to one”</note> members of one another,

verses.name: Romans 12:6
verses.text: but having different gifts according to the grace given to us: if <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> prophecy, according to the proportion of <transChange type="added">his</transChange> faith;

verses.name: Romans 12:7
verses.text: if <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> service, by service; if <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> one who teaches, by teaching;

verses.name: Romans 12:8
verses.text: if <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> one who exhorts, by exhortation; one who gives, with sincerity; one who leads, with diligence; one who shows mercy, with cheerfulness.  <div eID="gen27165" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 12:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11572"/><title type="x-s">Living in Love</title> <div sID="gen27166" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11572"/>Love must be without hypocrisy. Abhor what <transChange type="added">is</transChange> evil; be attached to what <transChange type="added">is</transChange> good,

verses.name: Romans 12:10
verses.text: being devoted to one another in brotherly love, esteeming one another <transChange type="added">more highly</transChange> in honor,

verses.name: Romans 12:11
verses.text: not lagging in diligence, being enthusiastic in spirit, serving the Lord,

verses.name: Romans 12:12
verses.text: rejoicing in hope, enduring in affliction, being devoted to prayer,

verses.name: Romans 12:13
verses.text: contributing to the needs of the saints, pursuing hospitality.  <div eID="gen27166" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 12:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11573"/><div sID="gen27167" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11573"/>Bless those who persecute,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “who persecute you”</note> bless and do not curse <transChange type="added">them</transChange>.

verses.name: Romans 12:15
verses.text: Rejoice with those who rejoice; weep with those who weep.

verses.name: Romans 12:16
verses.text: Think the same <transChange type="added">thing</transChange> toward one another; <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞do not think arrogantly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “think not the arrogant”</note>, but associate with the lowly. Do not be wise <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in your own sight⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in the sight of yourselves”</note>.

verses.name: Romans 12:17
verses.text: Pay back no one evil for evil. Take thought for <transChange type="added">what is</transChange> good in the sight of all people.

verses.name: Romans 12:18
verses.text: If <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> possible on your <transChange type="added">part</transChange>, be at peace with all people.

verses.name: Romans 12:19
verses.text: Do not take revenge yourselves, dear friends, but give place to <transChange type="added">God’s</transChange> wrath, for it is written, “Vengeance <transChange type="added">is</transChange> mine, I will repay,”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Deut.32.35">Deut 32:35</reference></note> says the Lord.

verses.name: Romans 12:20
verses.text: But “if your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him <transChange type="added">something</transChange> to drink; for <transChange type="added">by</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“doing”) which is understood as means</note> doing this, you will heap up coals of fire upon his head.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Prov.25.21-Prov.25.22">Prov 25:21–22</reference></note>

verses.name: Romans 12:21
verses.text: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.  <chapter eID="Rom.12"/>

verses.name: Romans 13:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11574"/><title type="x-s">Obedience to the Governing Authorities</title> <div sID="gen27168" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11574"/>Let every person be subject to the governing authorities, for <transChange type="added">there</transChange> is no authority except by God, and those that exist are put in place by God.

verses.name: Romans 13:2
verses.text: So then, the one who resists authority resists the ordinance <transChange type="added">which is</transChange> from God, and those who resist will receive condemnation on themselves.

verses.name: Romans 13:3
verses.text: For rulers are not a <transChange type="added">cause of</transChange> terror for a good deed, but for bad <transChange type="added">conduct</transChange>. So do you want not to be afraid of authority? Do what <transChange type="added">is</transChange> good, and you will have praise from it,

verses.name: Romans 13:4
verses.text: for it is God’s servant to you for what <transChange type="added">is</transChange> good. But if you do what <transChange type="added">is</transChange> bad, be afraid, because it does not bear the sword to no purpose. For it is God’s servant, the one who avenges for punishment on the one who does <transChange type="added">what is</transChange> bad.

verses.name: Romans 13:5
verses.text: Therefore <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> necessary to be in subjection, not only because of wrath but also because of conscience.

verses.name: Romans 13:6
verses.text: For because of this you also pay taxes, for <transChange type="added">the authorities</transChange><note placement="foot">Literally “they”</note> are servants of God, busily engaged in this very <transChange type="added">thing</transChange>.

verses.name: Romans 13:7
verses.text: Pay to everyone <transChange type="added">what is</transChange> owed: <transChange type="added">pay</transChange> taxes to whom taxes <transChange type="added">are due</transChange>; <transChange type="added">pay</transChange> customs duties to whom customs duties <transChange type="added">are due</transChange>; <transChange type="added">pay</transChange> respect to whom respect <transChange type="added">is due</transChange>; <transChange type="added">pay</transChange> honor to whom honor <transChange type="added">is due</transChange>.<note placement="foot">Due to the very compressed style in this verse, many words must be supplied to make sense in English</note>  <div eID="gen27168" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 13:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11575"/><title type="x-s">Love Fulfills the Law</title> <div sID="gen27169" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11575"/>Owe nothing to anyone, except to love one another, for the one who loves someone else has fulfilled the law.

verses.name: Romans 13:9
verses.text: For the <transChange type="added">commandments</transChange>, “You shall not commit adultery, you shall not commit murder, you shall not steal, you shall not covet,”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Exod.20.13-Exod.20.15">Exod 20:13–15</reference>, <reference osisRef="Exod.20.17">17</reference>; <reference osisRef="Deut.5.17-Deut.5.19">Deut 5:17–19</reference>, <reference osisRef="Deut.5.21">21</reference></note> and if there is any other commandment, are summed up in this statement: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Lev.19.18">Lev 19:18</reference></note>

verses.name: Romans 13:10
verses.text: Love does not commit evil against a neighbor. Therefore love <transChange type="added">is the</transChange> fulfillment of the law.  <div eID="gen27169" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 13:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11576"/><div sID="gen27170" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11576"/>And <transChange type="added">do</transChange> this <transChange type="added">because you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“know”) which is understood as causal</note> know the time, that <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> already the hour for you to wake up from sleep. For our salvation <transChange type="added">is</transChange> nearer now than when we believed.

verses.name: Romans 13:12
verses.text: The night is far gone, and the day has drawn near. Therefore let us throw off<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “let us lay aside”</note> the deeds of darkness and put on the weapons of light.

verses.name: Romans 13:13
verses.text: Let us live decently, as in the day, not in carousing and drunkenness, not in sexual immorality and licentiousness, not in strife and jealousy.

verses.name: Romans 13:14
verses.text: But put on the Lord Jesus Christ and do not make provision for the desires of the flesh.  <chapter eID="Rom.13"/>

verses.name: Romans 14:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11577"/><title type="x-s">Do Not Pass Judgment on One Another</title> <div sID="gen27171" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11577"/>Now receive the one who is weak in faith, <transChange type="added">but</transChange> not for quarrels about opinions.

verses.name: Romans 14:2
verses.text: One believes <transChange type="added">he may</transChange> eat all <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, but the one who is weak eats <transChange type="added">only</transChange> vegetables.

verses.name: Romans 14:3
verses.text: The one who eats must not despise the one who does not eat, and the one who does not eat must not judge the one who eats, because God has accepted him.

verses.name: Romans 14:4
verses.text: Who are you, who passes judgment on the domestic slave belonging to someone else? To his own master he stands or falls, and he will stand, for the Lord is able to make him stand.  <div eID="gen27171" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 14:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11578"/><div sID="gen27172" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11578"/>One person<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “For one person”</note> prefers <transChange type="added">one</transChange> day over <transChange type="added">another</transChange> day, and another person regards every day <transChange type="added">alike</transChange>. Each one must be fully convinced in his own mind.

verses.name: Romans 14:6
verses.text: The one who is intent on the day is intent on <transChange type="added">it</transChange> for the Lord, and the one who eats eats for the Lord, because he is thankful to God, and the one who does not eat does not eat for the Lord, and he is thankful to God.

verses.name: Romans 14:7
verses.text: For none of us lives for himself and none dies for himself.

verses.name: Romans 14:8
verses.text: For if we live, we live for the Lord, and if we die, we die for the Lord. Therefore whether we live <transChange type="added">or</transChange> whether we die, we are the Lord’s.

verses.name: Romans 14:9
verses.text: For Christ died and became alive again for this <transChange type="added">reason</transChange>, in order that he might be Lord of both the dead and the living.  <div eID="gen27172" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 14:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11579"/><div sID="gen27173" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11579"/>But why do you judge your brother? Or also, why do you despise your brother? For we will all stand before the judgment seat of God.

verses.name: Romans 14:11
verses.text: For it is written, <div eID="gen27173" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27174"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27175"/>“As I live, says the Lord, every knee will bow to me,<l eID="gen27175" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27176"/>and every tongue will praise God.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.45.23">Isa 45:23</reference></note> <l eID="gen27176" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen27174"/>

verses.name: Romans 14:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11580"/><div sID="gen27177" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11580"/>So<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “So then,”</note> each one of us will give an account concerning himself.<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “an account concerning himself to God”</note>  <div eID="gen27177" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 14:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11581"/><div sID="gen27178" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11581"/>Therefore, let us no longer pass judgment on one another, but rather decide this: not to place a cause for stumbling or a temptation before a brother.

verses.name: Romans 14:14
verses.text: I know and am convinced in the Lord Jesus that nothing <transChange type="added">is</transChange> unclean of itself, except to the one who considers something to be unclean; to that person <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> unclean.

verses.name: Romans 14:15
verses.text: For if because of food, your brother is grieved, you are no longer living according to love. Do not destroy by your food that person for whom Christ died.

verses.name: Romans 14:16
verses.text: Therefore do not let your good be slandered.

verses.name: Romans 14:17
verses.text: For the kingdom of God is not eating and drinking, but righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit.

verses.name: Romans 14:18
verses.text: For the one who serves Christ in this <transChange type="added">way</transChange> <transChange type="added">is</transChange> well-pleasing to God and approved by people.  <div eID="gen27178" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 14:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11582"/><div sID="gen27179" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11582"/>So then, let us pursue <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞what promotes peace⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the things of peace”</note> and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞what edifies one another⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the things of edification toward one another”</note>.

verses.name: Romans 14:20
verses.text: Do not destroy the work of God on account of food. All <transChange type="added">things</transChange> <transChange type="added">are</transChange> clean, but <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> wrong for the person <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞who eats and stumbles in the process⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “who eats with stumbling”</note>.

verses.name: Romans 14:21
verses.text: <transChange type="added">It is</transChange> good not to eat meat or to drink wine or <transChange type="added">to do anything</transChange> by which your brother stumbles or is offended or is weakened.<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts omit “or is offended or is weakened”</note>

verses.name: Romans 14:22
verses.text: The faith that you have, have with respect to yourself before God. Blessed <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the one who does not pass judgment on himself by what he approves.

verses.name: Romans 14:23
verses.text: But the one who doubts is condemned if he eats, because he does not <transChange type="added">do so</transChange> from faith, and everything that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not from faith is sin.  <chapter eID="Rom.14"/>

verses.name: Romans 15:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11583"/><title type="x-s">Accept One Another according to Christ’s Example</title> <div sID="gen27180" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11583"/>But we who are strong ought to bear the weaknesses of the weak, and not to please ourselves.

verses.name: Romans 15:2
verses.text: Let each one of us please his neighbor for his good, for the purpose of edification.

verses.name: Romans 15:3
verses.text: For even Christ did not please himself, but just as it is written, “The insults of those who insult you have fallen on me.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.69.9">Ps 69:9</reference></note>

verses.name: Romans 15:4
verses.text: For whatever was written beforehand was written for our instruction, in order that through patient endurance and through the encouragement of the scriptures we may have hope.

verses.name: Romans 15:5
verses.text: Now may the God of patient endurance and of encouragement grant you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to be in agreement⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to think the same”</note> with one another, in accordance with Christ Jesus,

verses.name: Romans 15:6
verses.text: so that with one mind you may glorify with one mouth the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.name: Romans 15:7
verses.text: Therefore accept one another, just as Christ also has accepted you, to the glory of God.  <div eID="gen27180" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 15:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11584"/><div sID="gen27181" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11584"/>For I say, Christ has become a servant of the circumcision on behalf of the truth of God, in order to confirm the promises to the fathers,

verses.name: Romans 15:9
verses.text: and that the Gentiles may glorify God for <transChange type="added">his</transChange> mercy, just as it is written, <div eID="gen27181" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27182"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27183"/>“Because of this, I will praise you among the Gentiles,<l eID="gen27183" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27184"/>and I will sing praise to your name.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.18.49">Ps 18:49</reference></note> <l eID="gen27184" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen27182"/>

verses.name: Romans 15:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11585"/><div sID="gen27185" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11585"/>And again it says, <div eID="gen27185" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27186"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27187"/>“Rejoice, Gentiles, with his people.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Deut.32.43">Deut 32:43</reference></note> <l eID="gen27187" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen27186"/>

verses.name: Romans 15:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11586"/><div sID="gen27188" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11586"/>And again, <div eID="gen27188" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27189"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27190"/>“Praise the Lord, all the Gentiles,<l eID="gen27190" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27191"/>and let all the peoples praise him.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.117.1">Ps 117:1</reference></note> <l eID="gen27191" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen27189"/>

verses.name: Romans 15:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11587"/><div sID="gen27192" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11587"/>And again Isaiah says, <div eID="gen27192" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27193"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27194"/>“The root of Jesse will come,<l eID="gen27194" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27195"/>even the one who rises to rule over the Gentiles;<l eID="gen27195" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27196"/>in him the Gentiles will put their hope.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.11.10">Isa 11:10</reference></note> <l eID="gen27196" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen27193"/>

verses.name: Romans 15:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11588"/><div sID="gen27197" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11588"/>Now may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, so that you may abound in hope by the power of the Holy Spirit.  <div eID="gen27197" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 15:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11589"/><title type="x-s">Paul’s Ministry to the Gentiles</title> <div sID="gen27198" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11589"/>Now I myself also am convinced about you, my brothers, that <transChange type="added">you</transChange> yourselves also are full of goodness, filled with all knowledge, able also to instruct one another.

verses.name: Romans 15:15
verses.text: But I have written to you more boldly on <transChange type="added">some</transChange> points, so as to remind you <transChange type="added">again</transChange> because of the grace that has been given to me by God,

verses.name: Romans 15:16
verses.text: with the result that I am a servant of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles, serving the gospel of God as a priest, in order that the offering of the Gentiles may become acceptable, sanctified by the Holy Spirit.

verses.name: Romans 15:17
verses.text: Therefore I have a reason for boasting in Christ Jesus regarding the things concerning God.

verses.name: Romans 15:18
verses.text: For I will not dare to speak about anything except <transChange type="added">that</transChange> which Christ has accomplished through me, resulting in the obedience of the Gentiles by word and deed,

verses.name: Romans 15:19
verses.text: by the power of signs and wonders, by the power of the Spirit,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “of the Spirit of God”</note> so that from Jerusalem and <transChange type="added">traveling</transChange> around as far as Illyricum I have fully proclaimed the gospel of Christ.

verses.name: Romans 15:20
verses.text: And so, having as my ambition to proclaim the gospel where Christ has not been named, in order that I will not build on the foundation belonging to someone else,

verses.name: Romans 15:21
verses.text: but just as it is written, <div eID="gen27198" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27199"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27200"/>“<transChange type="added">Those</transChange> to whom <transChange type="added">it was</transChange> not announced concerning him will see,<l eID="gen27200" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27201"/>and <transChange type="added">those</transChange> who have not heard will understand.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.52.15">Isa 52:15</reference></note> <l eID="gen27201" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen27199"/>

verses.name: Romans 15:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11590"/><title type="x-s">Paul’s Travel Plans</title> <div sID="gen27202" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11590"/>For this reason also I was hindered many <transChange type="added">times</transChange> from coming to you,

verses.name: Romans 15:23
verses.text: and now, no longer having a place in these regions, but having a desire for many years to come to you

verses.name: Romans 15:24
verses.text: whenever I travel to Spain. For I hope <transChange type="added">while I</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the participle (“passing through”) which is understood as temporal</note> am passing through to see you and to be sent on my way by you, whenever I have first enjoyed your <transChange type="added">company</transChange> for a while.

verses.name: Romans 15:25
verses.text: But now I am traveling to Jerusalem, serving the saints.

verses.name: Romans 15:26
verses.text: For Macedonia and Achaia were pleased to make some contribution for the poor among the saints in Jerusalem.

verses.name: Romans 15:27
verses.text: For they were pleased <transChange type="added">to do so</transChange>, and they are obligated to them. For if the Gentiles have shared in their spiritual <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, they ought also to serve them in material <transChange type="added">things</transChange>.

verses.name: Romans 15:28
verses.text: Therefore, <transChange type="added">after I</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“have accomplished”) which is understood as temporal</note> have accomplished this and sealed this fruit <transChange type="added">for delivery</transChange> to them, I will depart by way of you for Spain,

verses.name: Romans 15:29
verses.text: and I know that <transChange type="added">when I</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“come”) which is understood as temporal</note> come to you, I will come in the fullness of the blessing of Christ.  <div eID="gen27202" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 15:30
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11591"/><div sID="gen27203" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11591"/>Now I exhort you, brothers, through our Lord Jesus Christ and through the love of the Spirit, to contend along with me in your prayers on my behalf to God,

verses.name: Romans 15:31
verses.text: that I may be rescued from those who are disobedient in Judea, and my ministry in Jerusalem may be acceptable to the saints,

verses.name: Romans 15:32
verses.text: so that, coming to you with joy by the will of God, I may rest with you.

verses.name: Romans 15:33
verses.text: Now <transChange type="added">may</transChange> the God of peace <transChange type="added">be</transChange> with all of you. Amen.  <chapter eID="Rom.15"/>

verses.name: Romans 16:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11592"/><title type="x-s">Many Personal Greetings</title> <div sID="gen27204" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11592"/>Now I commend to you Phoebe our sister, who is also a servant<note placement="foot">Or “a deaconess”; some interpreters understand this term to refer to a specific office (deacon/deaconess) which Phoebe held in the local church at Cenchrea</note> of the church in Cenchrea,

verses.name: Romans 16:2
verses.text: in order that you may welcome her in the Lord in a manner worthy of the saints, and help her in whatever task she may have need from you, for she herself also has been a helper of many, even me myself.  <div eID="gen27204" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 16:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11593"/><div sID="gen27205" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11593"/>Greet Prisca and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus,

verses.name: Romans 16:4
verses.text: who risked their own necks for my life, for which not only I am thankful, but also all the churches of the Gentiles;

verses.name: Romans 16:5
verses.text: also <transChange type="added">greet</transChange><note placement="foot">The verb is supplied as an understood repetition from v. <reference osisRef="Rom.16.3">3</reference></note> the church in their house. Greet Epenetus my dear friend, who is <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the first convert⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the first fruits”</note> of Asia for Christ.

verses.name: Romans 16:6
verses.text: Greet Mary, who <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞has worked hard⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “has labored much”</note> for you.

verses.name: Romans 16:7
verses.text: Greet Andronicus and Junia,<note placement="foot">Or “Junias,” the masculine form of the same name</note> my compatriots<note placement="foot">Or “relatives”</note> and my fellow prisoners, who are well known to<note placement="foot">Or “are outstanding among”</note> the apostles, who were also in Christ before me.

verses.name: Romans 16:8
verses.text: Greet Ampliatus, my dear <transChange type="added">friend</transChange> in the Lord.

verses.name: Romans 16:9
verses.text: Greet Urbanus, our fellow worker in Christ, and my dear <transChange type="added">friend</transChange> Stachys.

verses.name: Romans 16:10
verses.text: Greet Apelles, who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> approved in Christ. Greet those of the <transChange type="added">household</transChange> of Aristobulus.

verses.name: Romans 16:11
verses.text: Greet Herodion my compatriot.<note placement="foot">Or “relative”</note> Greet those of the <transChange type="added">household</transChange> of Narcissus who are in the Lord.

verses.name: Romans 16:12
verses.text: Greet Tryphena and Tryphosa, the laborers in the Lord. Greet Persis, the dear <transChange type="added">friend</transChange> who <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞has worked hard⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “has labored much”</note> in the Lord.

verses.name: Romans 16:13
verses.text: Greet Rufus, the chosen one in the Lord, and his mother and mine.

verses.name: Romans 16:14
verses.text: Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers with them.

verses.name: Romans 16:15
verses.text: Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas, and all the saints <transChange type="added">who are</transChange> with them.

verses.name: Romans 16:16
verses.text: Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the churches of Christ greet you.  <div eID="gen27205" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 16:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11594"/><title type="x-s">Concluding Exhortations</title> <div sID="gen27206" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11594"/>Now I exhort you, brothers, to look out for those who cause dissensions and temptations contrary to the teaching which you learned, and stay away from them.

verses.name: Romans 16:18
verses.text: For such people do not serve our Lord Christ, but their own stomach, and by smooth speech and flattery they deceive the hearts of the unsuspecting.

verses.name: Romans 16:19
verses.text: For <transChange type="added">the report of</transChange> your obedience has reached to all; therefore I am rejoicing over you, and I want you to be wise toward what <transChange type="added">is</transChange> good, but innocent toward what <transChange type="added">is</transChange> evil.

verses.name: Romans 16:20
verses.text: And in a short time the God of peace will crush Satan under your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts omit “Christ”</note> <transChange type="added">be</transChange> with you.  <div eID="gen27206" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 16:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11595"/><title type="x-s">Greetings from Paul’s Associates</title> <div sID="gen27207" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11595"/>Timothy, my fellow worker, greets you, and Lucius and Jason and Sosipater, my compatriots.<note placement="foot">Or “relatives”</note>  <div eID="gen27207" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 16:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11596"/><div sID="gen27208" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11596"/>I, Tertius, the one who wrote this letter, greet you in the Lord.  <div eID="gen27208" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 16:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11597"/><div sID="gen27209" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11597"/>Gaius, my host and <transChange type="added">the host</transChange> of the whole church, greets you. Erastus the city treasurer greets you, and Quartus the brother.  <div eID="gen27209" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 16:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11598"/><title type="x-s">Benediction</title> <div sID="gen27210" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11598"/>The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ <transChange type="added">be</transChange> with all of you. Amen.<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts include vv. <reference osisRef="Rom.16.25-Rom.16.27">25–27</reference>, “25 Now to the one who is able to strengthen you according to my gospel and the preaching of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the mystery that had been kept secret for eternal ages, 26 but now has been revealed, and through the prophetic scriptures has been made known according to the command of the eternal God, resulting in obedience of faith to all the Gentiles, 27 to the only wise God, through Jesus Christ, to whom be the glory for eternity. Amen.”</note>  <chapter eID="Rom.16"/> <div eID="gen27210" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen27024" osisID="Rom" type="book"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 1:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11599"/><title type="x-s">Greeting</title> <div sID="gen27212" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11599"/>Paul, called <transChange type="added">to be</transChange> an apostle of Christ Jesus through the will of God, and Sosthenes our brother,

verses.name: I Corinthians 1:2
verses.text: to the church of God sanctified in Christ Jesus that is in Corinth,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “to the church of God that is in Corinth, sanctified in Christ Jesus”</note> called to be saints, together with all those who call upon the name of our Lord Jesus Christ in every place, their Lord<note placement="foot">*Here “Lord” must be supplied to indicate the referent; otherwise this could be understood as “their place and ours”</note> and ours.

verses.name: I Corinthians 1:3
verses.text: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.  <div eID="gen27212" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 1:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11600"/><title type="x-s">Thanksgiving for the Corinthian Believers</title> <div sID="gen27213" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11600"/>I give thanks to my God always concerning you, because of the grace of God which was given to you in Christ Jesus,

verses.name: I Corinthians 1:5
verses.text: that<note placement="foot">*Or “because”; the conjunction either (1) introduces a content clause (“that”) giving the content of Paul’s thanks, or (2) introduces a causal clause (“because”) giving the reason for Paul’s thanks</note> in everything you were made rich in him, in all speech and all knowledge,

verses.name: I Corinthians 1:6
verses.text: just as the testimony about Christ has been confirmed in you,

verses.name: I Corinthians 1:7
verses.text: so that you do not lack in any spiritual gift <transChange type="added">as you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“eagerly await”) which is understood as temporal</note> eagerly await the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ,

verses.name: I Corinthians 1:8
verses.text: who will also confirm you until the end, blameless in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.name: I Corinthians 1:9
verses.text: God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> faithful, by whom you were called to fellowship with his Son Jesus Christ our Lord.  <div eID="gen27213" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 1:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11601"/><title type="x-s">Divisions in the Church at Corinth</title> <div sID="gen27214" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11601"/>Now I exhort you, brothers, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you all say the same <transChange type="added">thing</transChange> and there not be divisions among you, and that you be made complete in the same mind and with the same purpose.

verses.name: I Corinthians 1:11
verses.text: For it has been made clear to me concerning you, my brothers, by <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Chloe’s people⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “those of Chloe”</note>, that there are quarrels among you.

verses.name: I Corinthians 1:12
verses.text: But I say this, that each of you is saying, “I am with Paul,” and “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> with Apollos,” and “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> with Cephas,” and “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> with Christ.”

verses.name: I Corinthians 1:13
verses.text: Has Christ been divided? Paul was not crucified for you, was he?<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here</note> Or were you baptized in the name of Paul?

verses.name: I Corinthians 1:14
verses.text: I give thanks<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “I give thanks to God”</note> that I baptized none of you except Crispus and Gaius,

verses.name: I Corinthians 1:15
verses.text: lest anyone should say that you were baptized in my name.

verses.name: I Corinthians 1:16
verses.text: (Now I also baptized the household of Stephanas. Beyond that I do not know if I baptized anyone else.)

verses.name: I Corinthians 1:17
verses.text: For Christ did not send me to baptize, but to proclaim the gospel, not with <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞clever speech⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “wisdom of word”</note>, lest the cross of Christ be emptied.  <div eID="gen27214" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 1:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11602"/><title type="x-s">Christ Crucified, the Power and Wisdom of God</title> <div sID="gen27215" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11602"/>For the message about the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.

verses.name: I Corinthians 1:19
verses.text: For it is written, <div eID="gen27215" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27216"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27217"/>“I will destroy the wisdom of the wise,<l eID="gen27217" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27218"/>and the intelligence of the intelligent I will confound.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.29.14">Isa 29:14</reference></note> <l eID="gen27218" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen27216"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 1:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11603"/><div sID="gen27219" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11603"/>Where <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the wise person? Where <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the scribe? Where <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the debater of this age? Has not God made foolish the wisdom of the world?

verses.name: I Corinthians 1:21
verses.text: For since, in the wisdom of God, the world through its wisdom did not know God, God was pleased through the foolishness of preaching to save those who believe.

verses.name: I Corinthians 1:22
verses.text: For indeed, Jews ask for sign miracles and Greeks seek wisdom,

verses.name: I Corinthians 1:23
verses.text: but we preach Christ crucified, to the Jews a cause for stumbling, but to the Gentiles foolishness,

verses.name: I Corinthians 1:24
verses.text: but to those <transChange type="added">who are</transChange> called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the power of God and the wisdom of God.

verses.name: I Corinthians 1:25
verses.text: For the foolishness of God is wiser than human <transChange type="added">wisdom</transChange>,<note placement="foot">Literally “man”</note> and the weakness of God is stronger than human strength.<note placement="foot">Literally “man”</note>  <div eID="gen27219" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 1:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11604"/><title type="x-s">Boast in the Lord</title> <div sID="gen27220" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11604"/>For consider your calling, brothers, that not many <transChange type="added">were</transChange> wise according to human standards,<note placement="foot">Literally “according to flesh”</note> not many <transChange type="added">were</transChange> powerful, not many <transChange type="added">were</transChange> well born.

verses.name: I Corinthians 1:27
verses.text: But the foolish <transChange type="added">things</transChange> of the world God chose in order that he might put to shame the wise, and the weak <transChange type="added">things</transChange> of the world God chose in order that he might put to shame the strong,

verses.name: I Corinthians 1:28
verses.text: and the insignificant of the world, and the despised, God chose, the things that are not, in order that he might abolish the things that are,

verses.name: I Corinthians 1:29
verses.text: so that all flesh may not boast before God.

verses.name: I Corinthians 1:30
verses.text: But from him you are in Christ Jesus, who became wisdom to us from God, and righteousness and sanctification and redemption,

verses.name: I Corinthians 1:31
verses.text: so that, just as it is written, “The one who boasts, let him boast in the Lord.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Jer.9.24">Jer 9:24</reference></note>  <chapter eID="1Cor.1"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 2:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11605"/><title type="x-s">Paul’s Approach to Ministry in Corinth</title> <div sID="gen27221" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11605"/>And I, <transChange type="added">when I</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“came”) which is understood as temporal</note> came to you, brothers, did not come with superiority of speech or of wisdom, proclaiming to you the testimony<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “mystery”</note> of God.

verses.name: I Corinthians 2:2
verses.text: For I decided not to know anything among you except Jesus Christ and him crucified.

verses.name: I Corinthians 2:3
verses.text: And I came to you in weakness and in fear and with much trembling,

verses.name: I Corinthians 2:4
verses.text: and my speech and my preaching <transChange type="added">were</transChange> not with the persuasiveness<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “with persuasive words”</note> of wisdom, but with a demonstration of the Spirit and power,

verses.name: I Corinthians 2:5
verses.text: in order that your faith would not be in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God.  <div eID="gen27221" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 2:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11606"/><title type="x-s">The Wisdom Revealed by the Spirit</title> <div sID="gen27222" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11606"/>Now we do speak wisdom among the mature, but wisdom not of this age or of the rulers of this age, who are perishing,

verses.name: I Corinthians 2:7
verses.text: but we speak the hidden wisdom of God in a mystery, which God predestined before the ages for our glory,

verses.name: I Corinthians 2:8
verses.text: which none of the rulers of this age knew. For if they had known <transChange type="added">it</transChange>, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.

verses.name: I Corinthians 2:9
verses.text: But just as it is written, <div eID="gen27222" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27223"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27224"/>“<transChange type="added">Things</transChange> which eye has not seen and ear has not heard,<l eID="gen27224" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27225"/>and have not entered into the heart of man,<l eID="gen27225" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27226"/>all that<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “which”</note> God has prepared for those who love him.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.64.4">Isa 64:4</reference></note> <l eID="gen27226" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen27223"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 2:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11607"/><div sID="gen27227" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11607"/>For<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “But to us God has revealed them”</note> to us God has revealed <transChange type="added">them</transChange> through the Spirit. For the Spirit searches all <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, even the depths of God.

verses.name: I Corinthians 2:11
verses.text: For who among men knows the things of a man, except the spirit of the man that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in him? Thus also no one knows the things of God except the Spirit of God.

verses.name: I Corinthians 2:12
verses.text: Now we have received not the spirit of the world, but the Spirit who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> from God, in order that we may know the things freely given to us by God,

verses.name: I Corinthians 2:13
verses.text: <transChange type="added">things</transChange> which we also speak, not in words taught by human wisdom, but in <transChange type="added">words</transChange> taught by the Spirit, explaining spiritual <transChange type="added">things</transChange> to spiritual <transChange type="added">people</transChange>.<note placement="foot">Or “in spiritual words”</note>

verses.name: I Corinthians 2:14
verses.text: But the natural man does not accept the things of the Spirit of God, for they are foolishness to him, and he is not able to understand <transChange type="added">them</transChange>, because they are spiritually discerned.

verses.name: I Corinthians 2:15
verses.text: Now the spiritual <transChange type="added">person</transChange> discerns all <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, but he himself is judged by no one.

verses.name: I Corinthians 2:16
verses.text: “For who has known the mind of the Lord; who has advised him?”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.40.13">Isa 40:13</reference></note> But we have the mind of Christ.  <chapter eID="1Cor.2"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 3:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11608"/><title type="x-s">Divisiveness and Immaturity</title> <div sID="gen27228" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11608"/>And I, brothers, was not able to speak to you as to spiritual <transChange type="added">people</transChange>, but as to fleshly <transChange type="added">people</transChange>, as to infants in Christ.

verses.name: I Corinthians 3:2
verses.text: I gave you milk to drink, not solid food, for you were not yet able <transChange type="added">to eat it</transChange>. But now you are still not able,

verses.name: I Corinthians 3:3
verses.text: for you are still fleshly. For where <transChange type="added">there is</transChange> jealousy and strife among you, are you not fleshly, and do you not live like <transChange type="added">unregenerate</transChange> people?<note placement="foot">That is, like people who do not possess the Spirit at all</note>

verses.name: I Corinthians 3:4
verses.text: For whenever anyone says, “I am with Paul,” and another, “I <transChange type="added">am</transChange> with Apollos,” are you not <transChange type="added">merely</transChange> human?  <div eID="gen27228" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 3:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11609"/><div sID="gen27229" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11609"/>Therefore, what is Apollos and what is Paul? Servants through whom you believed, and to each as the Lord gave.

verses.name: I Corinthians 3:6
verses.text: I planted, Apollos watered, but God was causing <transChange type="added">it</transChange> to grow.

verses.name: I Corinthians 3:7
verses.text: So then, neither the one who plants nor the one who waters is anything, but God who is causing <transChange type="added">it</transChange> to grow.

verses.name: I Corinthians 3:8
verses.text: Now the one who plants and the one who waters are one, but each one will receive his own reward according to his own labor.

verses.name: I Corinthians 3:9
verses.text: For we are God’s fellow workers; you are God’s field, God’s building.  <div eID="gen27229" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 3:10
