verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11610"/><div sID="gen27230" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11610"/>According to the grace of God given to me, like a skilled master builder I laid a foundation, and another is building upon <transChange type="added">it</transChange>. But each one must direct his attention to how he is building upon <transChange type="added">it</transChange>.

verses.name: I Corinthians 3:11
verses.text: For no one is able to lay another foundation than the one which is laid, which is Jesus Christ.

verses.name: I Corinthians 3:12
verses.text: Now if anyone builds upon the foundation <transChange type="added">with</transChange> gold, silver, precious stones, wood, grass, straw,

verses.name: I Corinthians 3:13
verses.text: the work of each one will become evident. For the day will reveal <transChange type="added">it</transChange>, because it will be revealed with fire, and the fire itself will test the work of each one, of what sort it is.

verses.name: I Corinthians 3:14
verses.text: If anyone’s work that he has built upon <transChange type="added">it</transChange> remains, he will receive a reward.

verses.name: I Corinthians 3:15
verses.text: If anyone’s work is burned up, he will suffer loss, but he himself will be saved, but so as through fire.  <div eID="gen27230" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 3:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11611"/><div sID="gen27231" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11611"/>Do you not know that you are God’s temple and the Spirit of God dwells in you?

verses.name: I Corinthians 3:17
verses.text: If anyone destroys God’s temple, God will destroy this one. For God’s temple is holy, which you are.  <div eID="gen27231" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 3:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11612"/><div sID="gen27232" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11612"/>Let no one deceive himself. If anyone thinks <transChange type="added">himself</transChange> to be wise among you in this age, let him become a fool, in order that he may become wise.

verses.name: I Corinthians 3:19
verses.text: For the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God, for it is written, “The one who catches the wise in their craftiness,”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Job.5.13">Job 5:13</reference></note>

verses.name: I Corinthians 3:20
verses.text: and again, “The Lord knows the thoughts of the wise, that they are futile.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.94.11">Ps 94:11</reference></note>

verses.name: I Corinthians 3:21
verses.text: So then, let no one boast in people. For all <transChange type="added">things</transChange> are yours,

verses.name: I Corinthians 3:22
verses.text: whether Paul or Apollos or Cephas or the world or life or death or things present or things to come, all <transChange type="added">things</transChange> <transChange type="added">are</transChange> yours,

verses.name: I Corinthians 3:23
verses.text: and you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> Christ’s, and Christ <transChange type="added">is</transChange> God’s.  <chapter eID="1Cor.3"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 4:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11613"/><title type="x-s">Christ’s Servant, God’s Steward</title> <div sID="gen27233" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11613"/>Thus let a person consider us as servants of Christ and stewards of God’s mysteries.

verses.name: I Corinthians 4:2
verses.text: In this case, moreover, it is sought in stewards that one be found faithful.

verses.name: I Corinthians 4:3
verses.text: But to me it is a very little matter that I be judged by you or by a human court,<note placement="foot">Literally “day”</note> but I do not <transChange type="added">even</transChange> judge myself.

verses.name: I Corinthians 4:4
verses.text: For I am conscious of nothing against myself, but not by this am I vindicated. But the one who judges me is the Lord.

verses.name: I Corinthians 4:5
verses.text: Therefore do not judge anything before the time, until the Lord should come, who will both enlighten the hidden things of darkness and will reveal the counsels of hearts, and then praise will come to each one from God.  <div eID="gen27233" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 4:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11614"/><title type="x-s">The Apostles’ Humility</title> <div sID="gen27234" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11614"/>Now I have applied these things, brothers, to myself and Apollos for your sake, in order that in us you may learn not <transChange type="added">to go</transChange> beyond what is written, lest someone be inflated with pride on behalf of one <transChange type="added">person</transChange> against the other.

verses.name: I Corinthians 4:7
verses.text: For who concedes you <transChange type="added">superiority</transChange>? And what do you have that you did not receive? But if indeed you received <transChange type="added">it</transChange>, why do you boast as <transChange type="added">if you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “if” is supplied as a component of the participle (“receive”) which is understood as conditional</note> did not receive <transChange type="added">it</transChange>?

verses.name: I Corinthians 4:8
verses.text: Already you are satiated! Already you are rich! Apart from us you reign as kings! And would that indeed you reigned as kings, in order that we also might reign as kings with you!

verses.name: I Corinthians 4:9
verses.text: For, I think, God has exhibited us apostles last of all, as condemned to death, because we have become a spectacle to the world and to angels and to people.

verses.name: I Corinthians 4:10
verses.text: We <transChange type="added">are</transChange> fools for the sake of Christ, but you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> prudent in Christ! We <transChange type="added">are</transChange> weak, but you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> strong! You <transChange type="added">are</transChange> honored, but we <transChange type="added">are</transChange> dishonored!

verses.name: I Corinthians 4:11
verses.text: Until the present hour we are both hungry and thirsty and poorly clothed and roughly treated and homeless,

verses.name: I Corinthians 4:12
verses.text: and we toil, working with our own hands. <transChange type="added">When we are</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“reviled”) which is understood as temporal</note> reviled, we bless; when we are<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“persecuted”) which is understood as temporal</note> persecuted, we endure;

verses.name: I Corinthians 4:13
verses.text: <transChange type="added">when we are</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“slandered”) which is understood as temporal</note> slandered, we encourage. We have become like the refuse of the world, the offscouring of all <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, until now.  <div eID="gen27234" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 4:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11615"/><title type="x-s">Paul’s Concern for the Corinthian Believers</title> <div sID="gen27235" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11615"/>I am not writing these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> to shame you, but admonishing <transChange type="added">you</transChange> as my dear children.

verses.name: I Corinthians 4:15
verses.text: For if you have ten thousand guardians in Christ, yet <transChange type="added">you do</transChange> not <transChange type="added">have</transChange> many fathers, for in Christ Jesus I fathered you through the gospel.

verses.name: I Corinthians 4:16
verses.text: Therefore I exhort you, become imitators of me.

verses.name: I Corinthians 4:17
verses.text: Because of this, I have sent to you Timothy, who is my dear and faithful child in the Lord, who will remind you of my ways in Christ Jesus, just as I teach everywhere in every church.

verses.name: I Corinthians 4:18
verses.text: But some have become arrogant, as <transChange type="added">if</transChange> I were not coming to you.

verses.name: I Corinthians 4:19
verses.text: But I am coming to you soon, if the Lord wills, and I will know not the talk of the ones who have become arrogant, but the power.

verses.name: I Corinthians 4:20
verses.text: For the kingdom of God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not with talk, but with power.

verses.name: I Corinthians 4:21
verses.text: What do you want? Shall I come to you with a rod, or with love and a spirit of gentleness?  <chapter eID="1Cor.4"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 5:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11616"/><title type="x-s">Immoral Behavior and Church Discipline</title> <div sID="gen27236" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11616"/>It is reported everywhere <transChange type="added">that there</transChange> is sexual immorality among you, and sexual immorality of such a kind which <transChange type="added">does</transChange> not <transChange type="added">even exist</transChange> among the Gentiles, so that someone has the wife of <transChange type="added">his</transChange> father.

verses.name: I Corinthians 5:2
verses.text: And you are inflated with pride, and should you not rather have mourned, so that the one who has done this deed would be removed from your midst?

verses.name: I Corinthians 5:3
verses.text: For <transChange type="added">although I</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“am absent”) which is understood as concessive</note> am absent in body but present in spirit, I have already passed judgment on the one who has done this in this way, as if I<note placement="foot">*Here “if” is supplied as a component of the participle (“were present”) which is understood as conditional</note> were present.

verses.name: I Corinthians 5:4
verses.text: In the name of our Lord Jesus, <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“are assembled”)</note> you are assembled, and my spirit, together with the power of our Lord Jesus,

verses.name: I Corinthians 5:5
verses.text: <transChange type="added">I have decided</transChange><note placement="foot">*The words “I have decided” are implied from the statement “I have already passed judgment” in v. <reference osisRef="1Cor.5.3">3</reference></note> to hand over such a person to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, in order that his spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord.  <div eID="gen27236" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 5:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11617"/><div sID="gen27237" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11617"/>Your boasting <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not good. Do you not know that a little leaven leavens the whole batch of dough?

verses.name: I Corinthians 5:7
verses.text: Clean out the old leaven in order that you may be a new batch of dough, just as you are unleavened. For Christ our Passover has been sacrificed.

verses.name: I Corinthians 5:8
verses.text: So then, let us celebrate the feast, not with the old leaven or with the leaven of wickedness and sinfulness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.  <div eID="gen27237" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 5:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11618"/><div sID="gen27238" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11618"/>I wrote to you in the letter not to associate with sexually immoral people.

verses.name: I Corinthians 5:10
verses.text: By no means <transChange type="added">did I mean</transChange> the sexually immoral people of this world or the greedy people and swindlers or idolaters, since then you would have to depart out of the world.

verses.name: I Corinthians 5:11
verses.text: But now I have written to you not to associate with any so-called brother, if he is a sexually immoral person or a greedy person or an idolater or an abusive person or a drunkard or a swindler—with such a person not even to eat.

verses.name: I Corinthians 5:12
verses.text: For what <transChange type="added">is it</transChange> to me to judge those outside? Should you not judge those inside?

verses.name: I Corinthians 5:13
verses.text: But those outside God will judge. Remove the evil person <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from among yourselves⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from you of them”</note>.  <chapter eID="1Cor.5"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 6:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11619"/><title type="x-s">Lawsuits between Believers</title> <div sID="gen27239" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11619"/>Does anyone among you, <transChange type="added">if he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “if” is supplied as a component of the participle (“has”) which is understood as conditional</note> has a matter against someone else, dare to go to court before the unrighteous, and not before the saints?

verses.name: I Corinthians 6:2
verses.text: Or do you not know that the saints will judge the world? And if by you the world is judged, are you unworthy of the most insignificant courts?

verses.name: I Corinthians 6:3
verses.text: Do you not know that we will judge angels, not to mention ordinary matters?

verses.name: I Corinthians 6:4
verses.text: Therefore, if you have courts with regard to ordinary matters, do you seat<note placement="foot">Or “seat” (imperative); the Greek verb can be either indicative mood or imperative mood by its form</note> these despised <transChange type="added">people</transChange> in the church?

verses.name: I Corinthians 6:5
verses.text: I say <transChange type="added">this</transChange> to your shame. So is there not anyone wise among you who will be able to render a decision between his brothers?

verses.name: I Corinthians 6:6
verses.text: But brother goes to court with brother, and this before unbelievers!

verses.name: I Corinthians 6:7
verses.text: Therefore it is already completely a loss for you that you have lawsuits with one another. Why not rather be wronged? Why not rather be defrauded?

verses.name: I Corinthians 6:8
verses.text: But you wrong and defraud, and <transChange type="added">do</transChange> this <transChange type="added">to</transChange> brothers!  <div eID="gen27239" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 6:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11620"/><div sID="gen27240" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11620"/>Or do you not know that the unrighteous will not inherit the kingdom of God? Do not be deceived! Neither sexually immoral people, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor passive homosexual partners, nor dominant homosexual partners,

verses.name: I Corinthians 6:10
verses.text: nor thieves, nor greedy persons, not drunkards, not abusive persons, not swindlers will inherit the kingdom of God.

verses.name: I Corinthians 6:11
verses.text: And some of you were these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, but you were washed, but you were sanctified, but you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “of the Lord Jesus Christ”</note> and by the Spirit of our God.  <div eID="gen27240" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 6:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11621"/><title type="x-s">Avoid Sexual Immorality</title> <div sID="gen27241" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11621"/>All <transChange type="added">things</transChange> are permitted for me, but not all <transChange type="added">things</transChange> are profitable. All <transChange type="added">things</transChange> are permitted for me, but I will not be controlled by anything.

verses.name: I Corinthians 6:13
verses.text: Food <transChange type="added">is</transChange> for the stomach, and the stomach for food, but God will abolish <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞both of them⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “both this and these”</note>. Now the body <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not for sexual immorality, but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body.

verses.name: I Corinthians 6:14
verses.text: And God both raised up the Lord and will raise us up by his power.

verses.name: I Corinthians 6:15
verses.text: Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ? Therefore, shall I take away the members of Christ <transChange type="added">and</transChange> make <transChange type="added">them</transChange> members of a prostitute? May it never be!

verses.name: I Corinthians 6:16
verses.text: Or do you not know that the one who joins himself to a prostitute is one body <transChange type="added">with her</transChange>? For it says, “The two will become one flesh.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Gen.2.24">Gen 2:24</reference></note>

verses.name: I Corinthians 6:17
verses.text: But the one who joins himself to the Lord is one spirit <transChange type="added">with him</transChange>.

verses.name: I Corinthians 6:18
verses.text: Flee sexual immorality. Every sin that a person commits is outside his body, but the one who commits sexual immorality sins against his own body.

verses.name: I Corinthians 6:19
verses.text: Or do you not know that your body is the temple of the Holy Spirit <transChange type="added">who is</transChange> in you, whom you have from God, and you are not your own?

verses.name: I Corinthians 6:20
verses.text: For you were bought at a price; therefore glorify God with your body.  <chapter eID="1Cor.6"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11622"/><title type="x-s">Concerning Christian Marriage</title> <div sID="gen27242" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11622"/>Now concerning <transChange type="added">the things</transChange> about which you wrote: “<transChange type="added">It is</transChange> good for a man not to touch<note placement="foot">I.e., in a sexual sense</note> a woman.”

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:2
verses.text: But because of sexual immorality, let each man have<note placement="foot">I.e., in the sense of “have sexual relations with”</note> his own wife and let each woman have her own husband.

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:3
verses.text: The husband must fulfill his obligation to his wife, and likewise also the wife to her husband.

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:4
verses.text: The wife does not have authority over her own body, but her husband <transChange type="added">does</transChange>. And likewise also the husband does not have authority over his own body, but his wife <transChange type="added">does</transChange>.

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:5
verses.text: Do not defraud one another, except perhaps by agreement, for a time, in order that you may devote yourselves to prayer, and <transChange type="added">then</transChange> you should be <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞together⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “at the same”</note> again, lest Satan tempt you because of your lack of self control.

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:6
verses.text: But I say this as a concession, not as a command.

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:7
verses.text: I wish all people could be like myself, but each one has his own gift from God, one in this way and another in that way.  <div eID="gen27242" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11623"/><div sID="gen27243" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11623"/>Now I say to the unmarried and to the widows: <transChange type="added">It is</transChange> good for them if they remain as I <transChange type="added">am</transChange>.

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:9
verses.text: But if they cannot control themselves, they should marry, for it is better to marry than to burn <transChange type="added">with sexual desire</transChange>.  <div eID="gen27243" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11624"/><div sID="gen27244" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11624"/>To the married I command—not I, but the Lord—a wife must not separate from <transChange type="added">her</transChange> husband.

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:11
verses.text: But if indeed she does separate, she must remain unmarried or be reconciled to her husband. And a husband must not divorce <transChange type="added">his</transChange> wife.  <div eID="gen27244" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11625"/><div sID="gen27245" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11625"/>Now to the rest I say—not the Lord—if any brother has an unbelieving wife and she consents to live with him, he must not divorce her.

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:13
verses.text: And if any wife has an unbelieving husband and he consents to live with her, she must not divorce her husband.

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:14
verses.text: For the unbelieving husband is sanctified by his wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified by the brother, since otherwise your children are unclean, but now they are holy.

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:15
verses.text: But if the unbeliever leaves, let him leave. The brother or the sister is not bound in such <transChange type="added">cases</transChange>. But God has called us<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “you” (plural)</note> in peace.

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:16
verses.text: For how do you know, wife, whether you will save your husband? Or how do you know, husband, whether you will save your wife?  <div eID="gen27245" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11626"/><div sID="gen27246" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11626"/>But to each one as the Lord has apportioned. As God has called each one, thus let him live—and thus I order in all the churches.

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:18
verses.text: Was anyone called <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“being circumcised”) which is understood as temporal</note> being circumcised? He must not undo his circumcision. Was anyone called in uncircumcision? He must not become circumcised.

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:19
verses.text: Circumcision is nothing and uncircumcision is nothing, but the keeping of the commandments of God.

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:20
verses.text: Each one in the calling in which he was called—in this he should remain.

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:21
verses.text: Were you called <transChange type="added">while</transChange> a slave? Do not let it be a concern to you. But if indeed you are able to become free, rather make use of <transChange type="added">it</transChange>.

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:22
verses.text: For the one who is called in the Lord <transChange type="added">while</transChange> a slave is the Lord’s freedperson. Likewise the one who is called <transChange type="added">while</transChange> free is a slave of Christ.

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:23
verses.text: You were bought at a price; do not become slaves of men.

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:24
verses.text: Each one in <transChange type="added">the situation</transChange> in which he was called, brothers—in this he should remain with God.  <div eID="gen27246" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11627"/><title type="x-s">Concerning the Unmarried</title> <div sID="gen27247" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11627"/>Now concerning virgins I do not have a command from the Lord, but I am giving an opinion as one shown mercy by the Lord to be trustworthy.

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:26
verses.text: Therefore, I consider this to be good because of the impending distress, that <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> good for a man to be thus.

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:27
verses.text: Are you bound to a wife? Do not seek release. Are you free from a wife? Do not seek a wife.

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:28
verses.text: But if you marry, you have not sinned, and if the virgin marries, she has not sinned. But such people will have affliction in the flesh, and I would spare you.

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:29
verses.text: But I say this, brothers: the time is shortened, that from now on even those who have wives should be as <transChange type="added">if they</transChange> do not have <transChange type="added">wives</transChange>,

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:30
verses.text: and those who weep as <transChange type="added">if they</transChange> do not weep, and those who rejoice as <transChange type="added">if they</transChange> do not rejoice, and those who buy as <transChange type="added">if they</transChange> do not possess,

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:31
verses.text: and those who make use of the world as <transChange type="added">if they</transChange> do not make full use of <transChange type="added">it</transChange>. For the present form of this world is passing away.  <div eID="gen27247" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11628"/><div sID="gen27248" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11628"/>But I want you to be free from care. The unmarried person cares for the things of the Lord, how he may please the Lord.

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:33
verses.text: But the one who is married cares for the things of the world, how he may please his wife,

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:34
verses.text: and he is divided. And the unmarried woman or the virgin cares for the things of the Lord, in order that she may be holy both in body and in spirit. But the married woman cares for the things of the world, how she may please her husband.

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:35
verses.text: Now I am saying this for your own benefit, not that I may put a restriction on you, but to promote appropriate and devoted service to the Lord without distraction.  <div eID="gen27248" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:36
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11629"/><div sID="gen27249" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11629"/>But if anyone thinks he is behaving dishonorably concerning his virgin, if she is past her prime<note placement="foot">Or “if his passions are strong” (it is not clear in context whether this term refers to the man or to the woman)</note> and it ought to be thus, let him do what he wishes. He does not sin. Let them marry.

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:37
verses.text: But he who stands firm in his heart, not having necessity, but has authority concerning his own will, and has decided this in his own heart, to keep his own virgin, he will do well.

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:38
verses.text: So then, the one who marries<note placement="foot">Or perhaps “the one who gives in marriage”</note> his own virgin does well, and the one who does not marry <transChange type="added">her</transChange> will do better.  <div eID="gen27249" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:39
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11630"/><div sID="gen27250" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11630"/>A wife is bound for as long a time <transChange type="added">as</transChange> her husband lives. But if her husband <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞dies⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “falls asleep”</note>, she is free to marry whomever she wishes, only in the Lord.

verses.name: I Corinthians 7:40
verses.text: But she is happier if she remains thus, according to my opinion—and I think I have the Spirit of God.  <chapter eID="1Cor.7"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 8:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11631"/><title type="x-s">Concerning Food Sacrificed to Idols</title> <div sID="gen27251" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11631"/>Now concerning food sacrificed to idols, we know that “we all have knowledge.”<note placement="foot">Considered by many interpreters to be a slogan used by the Corinthians to justify their behavior</note> Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.

verses.name: I Corinthians 8:2
verses.text: If anyone thinks he knows anything, he has not yet known as it is necessary to know.

verses.name: I Corinthians 8:3
verses.text: But if anyone loves God, this one is known by him.  <div eID="gen27251" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 8:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11632"/><div sID="gen27252" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11632"/>Therefore, concerning the eating of food sacrificed to idols, we know that “an idol <transChange type="added">is</transChange> nothing in the world” and that “<transChange type="added">there is</transChange> no God except one.”<note placement="foot">Considered by many interpreters to be slogans used by the Corinthians to justify their behavior</note>

verses.name: I Corinthians 8:5
verses.text: For even if after all <transChange type="added">there</transChange> are so-called gods, whether in heaven or on earth, just as <transChange type="added">there</transChange> are many gods and many lords,  <div eID="gen27252" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 8:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11633"/><lg sID="gen27253"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27254"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11633"/>yet to us <transChange type="added">there is</transChange> one God, the Father,<l eID="gen27254" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27255"/>from whom <transChange type="added">are</transChange> all <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, and we <transChange type="added">are</transChange> for him,<l eID="gen27255" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27256"/>and <transChange type="added">there is</transChange> one Lord, Jesus Christ,<l eID="gen27256" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27257"/>through whom <transChange type="added">are</transChange> all <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, and we <transChange type="added">are</transChange> through him. <l eID="gen27257" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen27253"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 8:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11634"/><div sID="gen27258" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11634"/>But this knowledge <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not in everyone. But some, being accustomed until now to the idol, eat <transChange type="added">this food</transChange> as food sacrificed to idols, and their conscience, <transChange type="added">because it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“is”) which is understood as causal</note> is weak, is defiled.

verses.name: I Corinthians 8:8
verses.text: But food does not bring us close to God. For neither if we eat do we have more, nor if we do not eat do we lack.<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts omit “For” and have “Neither if we do not eat do we lack, nor if we do eat do we have more”</note>

verses.name: I Corinthians 8:9
verses.text: But watch out lest somehow this right of yours becomes a cause for stumbling to the weak.

verses.name: I Corinthians 8:10
verses.text: For if someone should see you who has knowledge reclining for a meal in an idol’s temple, will not his conscience, <transChange type="added">because it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“is”) which is understood as causal</note> is weak, be strengthened so that <transChange type="added">he</transChange> eats the food sacrificed to idols?

verses.name: I Corinthians 8:11
verses.text: For the one who is weak—the brother for whom Christ died—is destroyed by your knowledge.

verses.name: I Corinthians 8:12
verses.text: Now <transChange type="added">if you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “if” is supplied as a component of the participle (“sin”) which is understood as conditional</note> sin in this way against the brothers and wound their conscience, which is weak, you sin against Christ.

verses.name: I Corinthians 8:13
verses.text: Therefore, if food causes my brother to sin, I will never eat meat <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for the age”</note>, in order that I may not cause my brother to sin.  <chapter eID="1Cor.8"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 9:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11635"/><title type="x-s">Paul Gives Up His Rights as an Apostle</title> <div sID="gen27259" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11635"/>Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen Jesus our Lord? Are you not my work in the Lord?

verses.name: I Corinthians 9:2
verses.text: If to others I am not an apostle, yet indeed I am to you, for you are my seal of apostleship in the Lord.

verses.name: I Corinthians 9:3
verses.text: My defense to those who examine me is this:

verses.name: I Corinthians 9:4
verses.text: Do we not have the right to eat and drink?

verses.name: I Corinthians 9:5
verses.text: Do we not have the right to take along a sister <transChange type="added">as</transChange> wife, like the rest of the apostles and the brothers of the Lord and Cephas?

verses.name: I Corinthians 9:6
verses.text: Or do only I and Barnabas not have the right <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to refrain from working⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “not to work”</note>?

verses.name: I Corinthians 9:7
verses.text: Who ever serves as a soldier at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard and does not eat the fruit of it? Who<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “Or who”</note> shepherds a flock and does not drink<note placement="foot">Literally “eat”</note> from the milk of the flock?

verses.name: I Corinthians 9:8
verses.text: I am not saying these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> according to a human perspective. Or does the law not also say these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>?

verses.name: I Corinthians 9:9
verses.text: For in the law of Moses it is written, “You must not muzzle an ox <transChange type="added">while it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the participle (“threshing”) which is understood as temporal</note> is threshing.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Deut.25.4">Deut 25:4</reference></note> It is not about oxen God is concerned, is it?<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here</note>

verses.name: I Corinthians 9:10
verses.text: Or doubtless does he speak <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞for our sake⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for the sake of us”</note>? For it is written <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞for our sake⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for the sake of us”</note>, because the one who plows ought to plow in hope and the one who threshes <transChange type="added">ought to do so</transChange> in hope of a share.

verses.name: I Corinthians 9:11
verses.text: If we have sown spiritual <transChange type="added">things</transChange> among you, <transChange type="added">is it too</transChange> great <transChange type="added">a thing</transChange> if we reap material <transChange type="added">things</transChange> from you?

verses.name: I Corinthians 9:12
verses.text: If others share this right over you, do we not <transChange type="added">do so</transChange> even more? Yet we have not made use of this right, but we endure all <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, in order that we may not cause any hindrance to the gospel of Christ.  <div eID="gen27259" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 9:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11636"/><div sID="gen27260" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11636"/>Do you not know that those performing the holy services eat the things from the temple, <transChange type="added">and</transChange> those attending to the altar have a share with the altar?

verses.name: I Corinthians 9:14
verses.text: In the <transChange type="added">same</transChange> way also the Lord ordered those who proclaim the gospel to live from the gospel.

verses.name: I Corinthians 9:15
verses.text: But I have not made use of any of these <transChange type="added">rights</transChange>. And I am not writing these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> in order that it may be thus with me. For <transChange type="added">it would be</transChange> better to me rather to die than <transChange type="added">for</transChange> anyone to deprive me of my reason for boasting.

verses.name: I Corinthians 9:16
verses.text: For if I proclaim the gospel, it is not to me a reason for boasting, for necessity is imposed on me. For woe is to me if I do not proclaim the gospel.

verses.name: I Corinthians 9:17
verses.text: For if I do this voluntarily, I have a reward, but if <transChange type="added">I do so</transChange> unwillingly, I have been entrusted with a stewardship.

verses.name: I Corinthians 9:18
verses.text: What then is my reward? That <transChange type="added">when I</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“proclaim the gospel”) which is understood as temporal</note> proclaim the gospel, I may offer the gospel free of charge, in order not to make full use of my right in the gospel.  <div eID="gen27260" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 9:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11637"/><div sID="gen27261" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11637"/>For <transChange type="added">although I</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“am”) which is understood as concessive</note> am free from all <transChange type="added">people</transChange>, I have enslaved myself to all, in order that I may gain more.

verses.name: I Corinthians 9:20
verses.text: I have become like a Jew to the Jews, in order that I may gain the Jews. To those under the law <transChange type="added">I became</transChange> as under the law (<transChange type="added">although I</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“am”) which is understood as concessive</note> myself am not under the law) in order that I may gain those under the law.

verses.name: I Corinthians 9:21
verses.text: To those outside the law <transChange type="added">I became</transChange> as outside the law (<transChange type="added">although I</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“am”) which is understood as concessive</note> am not outside the law of God, but subject to the law of Christ) in order that I may gain those outside the law.

verses.name: I Corinthians 9:22
verses.text: To the weak I became weak, in order that I may gain the weak. I have become all <transChange type="added">things</transChange> to all <transChange type="added">people</transChange>, in order that by all means I may save some.

verses.name: I Corinthians 9:23
verses.text: I do all <transChange type="added">this</transChange> for the sake of the gospel, in order that I may become a participant with it.  <div eID="gen27261" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 9:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11638"/><div sID="gen27262" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11638"/>Do you not know that those who run in the stadium all run, but one receives the prize? Run in such a way that you may win.

verses.name: I Corinthians 9:25
verses.text: And everyone who competes exercises self-control in all <transChange type="added">things</transChange>. Thus those <transChange type="added">do so</transChange> in order that they may receive a perishable crown, but we an imperishable <transChange type="added">one</transChange>.

verses.name: I Corinthians 9:26
verses.text: Therefore I run in this way, not as <transChange type="added">running</transChange> aimlessly; I box in this way, not as beating the air.

verses.name: I Corinthians 9:27
verses.text: But I discipline my body and subjugate <transChange type="added">it</transChange>, lest somehow <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“preaching”) which is understood as temporal</note> preaching to others, <transChange type="added">I</transChange> myself should become disqualified.  <chapter eID="1Cor.9"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11639"/><title type="x-s">A History Lesson from Israel</title> <div sID="gen27263" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11639"/>For I do not want you to be ignorant, brothers, that our fathers were all under the cloud and all went through the sea,

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:2
verses.text: and all were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea,

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:3
verses.text: and all ate the same spiritual food,

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:4
verses.text: and all drank the same spiritual drink. For they drank from the spiritual rock that followed <transChange type="added">them</transChange>, and the rock was Christ.

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:5
verses.text: But God was not pleased with the majority of them, for they were struck down in the desert.  <div eID="gen27263" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11640"/><div sID="gen27264" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11640"/>Now these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> happened <transChange type="added">as</transChange> examples for us, so that we should not be desirers of evil <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, just as those also desired <transChange type="added">them</transChange>,

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:7
verses.text: and not become idolaters, as some of them <transChange type="added">did</transChange>, just as it is written, “The people sat down to eat and drink, and stood up to play,”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Exod.32.6">Exod 32:6</reference></note>

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:8
verses.text: nor commit sexual immorality, as some of them committed sexual immorality, and twenty-three thousand fell in one day,

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:9
verses.text: nor put Christ to the test, as some of them tested <transChange type="added">him</transChange>, and were destroyed by snakes,

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:10
verses.text: nor grumble, just as some of them grumbled, and were destroyed by the destroyer.

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:11
verses.text: Now these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> happened to those <transChange type="added">people</transChange> as an example, but are written for our instruction, on whom the ends of the ages have come.

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:12
verses.text: Therefore, the one who thinks that he stands must watch out lest he fall.

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:13
verses.text: Temptation has not come upon you except <transChange type="added">what is</transChange> common to humanity. But God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> faithful, who will not permit you to be tempted beyond what you are able, but will also make a way out together with the temptation, <transChange type="added">so that you</transChange> may be able to endure <transChange type="added">it</transChange>.  <div eID="gen27264" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11641"/><title type="x-s">Warning Against Idolatry</title> <div sID="gen27265" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11641"/>Therefore, my dear friends, flee from idolatry.

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:15
verses.text: I am speaking as to sensible <transChange type="added">people</transChange>; you judge what I am saying.

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:16
verses.text: The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not a participation in the blood of Christ? The bread which we break, is it not a participation in the body of Christ?

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:17
verses.text: Because <transChange type="added">there is</transChange> one bread, <transChange type="added">we</transChange> who <transChange type="added">are</transChange> many are one body, for <transChange type="added">we</transChange> all share from the one bread.

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:18
verses.text: Consider Israel according to the flesh: are not the ones who eat the sacrifices sharers in the altar?

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:19
verses.text: Therefore, what am I saying? That food sacrificed to idols is anything, or that an idol is anything?

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:20
verses.text: <transChange type="added">No</transChange>, but that <transChange type="added">the things</transChange> which they sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons and not to God, and I do not want you to become sharers with demons.

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:21
verses.text: You are not able to drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons. You are not able to share the table of the Lord and the table of demons.

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:22
verses.text: Or are we attempting to provoke the Lord to jealousy? We are not stronger than he <transChange type="added">is, are we</transChange>?<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here</note>  <div eID="gen27265" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11642"/><title type="x-s">Freedom in Christ</title> <div sID="gen27266" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11642"/>All <transChange type="added">things</transChange> are permitted, but not all <transChange type="added">things</transChange> are profitable. All <transChange type="added">things</transChange> are permitted, but not all <transChange type="added">things</transChange> build up.

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:24
verses.text: Let no one seek <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his own good⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the - of himself”; “good” is implied</note> but the <transChange type="added">good</transChange> of the other.

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:25
verses.text: Eat everything that is sold in the meat market, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞asking no questions⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “questioning nothing”</note> for the sake of the conscience,

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:26
verses.text: for “the earth <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the Lord’s, and its fullness.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.24.1">Ps 24:1, </reference>and an allusion to <reference osisRef="Ps.50.12">Ps 50:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.89.11">89:11</reference></note>

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:27
verses.text: If any of the unbelievers invites you, and you want to go, eat everything that is set before you, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞asking no questions⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “questioning nothing”</note> for the sake of the conscience.

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:28
verses.text: But if someone says to you, “This is offered to idols,” do not eat <transChange type="added">it</transChange>, for the sake of that one who informed <transChange type="added">you</transChange> and the conscience.

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:29
verses.text: Now I am not speaking about your own conscience, but the <transChange type="added">conscience</transChange> of the other <transChange type="added">person</transChange>. For why <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my freedom judged by another’s conscience?

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:30
verses.text: If I partake with thankfulness, why am I slandered concerning that for which I give thanks?  <div eID="gen27266" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11643"/><div sID="gen27267" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11643"/>Therefore, whether you eat or you drink or whatever you do, do all <transChange type="added">things</transChange> for the glory of God.

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:32
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Give no offense⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “be blameless”</note> both to Jews and to Greeks and to the church of God,

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:33
verses.text: just as I also please all <transChange type="added">people</transChange> in all <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, not seeking my own benefit, but the <transChange type="added">benefit</transChange> of the many, in order that they may be saved.  <chapter eID="1Cor.10"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11644"/><title type="x-s">Concerning Head Coverings in Worship</title> <div sID="gen27268" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11644"/>Become imitators of me, just as I also <transChange type="added">am</transChange> of Christ.  <div eID="gen27268" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11645"/><div sID="gen27269" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11645"/>Now I praise you that you remember me <transChange type="added">in</transChange> all <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, and just as I handed over to you the traditions, you hold fast to <transChange type="added">them</transChange>.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:3
verses.text: But I want you to know that Christ is the head of every man, and the man <transChange type="added">is the</transChange> head of the woman, and <transChange type="added">the</transChange> head of Christ <transChange type="added">is</transChange> God.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:4
verses.text: Every man who prays or prophesies <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the participle (“having”) which is understood as temporal</note> having something<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object must be supplied from context, but the exact nature of the object is not clear from the context, so “something” is used in the English translation</note> on <transChange type="added">his</transChange> head dishonors his head,

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:5
verses.text: but every woman who prays or prophesies with uncovered head dishonors her head, for she is one and the same with the one whose <transChange type="added">head</transChange> is shaved.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:6
verses.text: For if a woman does not cover herself, let her <transChange type="added">hair</transChange> be shorn off. But if <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> shameful for a woman to <transChange type="added">have her head</transChange><note placement="foot">Literally “to be”</note> shorn or shaved, let her cover her head.<note placement="foot">Literally “herself”</note>

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:7
verses.text: For indeed a man ought not to cover his head, <transChange type="added">because he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“is”) which is understood as causal</note> is the image and glory of God, but the woman is the glory of the man.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:8
verses.text: For man is not from woman, but woman from man.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:9
verses.text: For indeed man was not created for the sake of the woman, but woman for the sake of the man.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:10
verses.text: Because of this, the woman ought to have <transChange type="added">a symbol of</transChange> authority on her head, on account of the angels.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:11
verses.text: Nevertheless, neither <transChange type="added">is</transChange> woman <transChange type="added">anything</transChange> apart from man, nor <transChange type="added">is</transChange> man <transChange type="added">anything</transChange> apart from woman in the Lord.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:12
verses.text: For just as the woman <transChange type="added">is</transChange> from the man, thus also the man <transChange type="added">is</transChange> through the woman. But all <transChange type="added">things</transChange> <transChange type="added">are</transChange> from God.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:13
verses.text: You judge <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞for yourselves⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in you yourselves”</note>: is it fitting for a woman to pray to God with her head<note placement="foot">*Here the words “with her head” have been supplied as a necessary clarification</note> uncovered?

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:14
verses.text: And does not nature itself teach you that a man, if he wears long hair, it is a dishonor to him?

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:15
verses.text: But a woman, if she wears long hair, it is her glory, because her hair is given<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “is given to her”</note> for a covering.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:16
verses.text: But if anyone is disposed to be contentious, we have no such custom, nor do the churches of God.  <div eID="gen27269" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11646"/><title type="x-s">Improper Conduct at the Lord’s Supper</title> <div sID="gen27270" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11646"/>But in giving this instruction I do not praise <transChange type="added">you</transChange>, because you come together not for the better but for the worse.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:18
verses.text: For in the first place, <transChange type="added">when you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“come together”)</note> come together as a church, I hear there are divisions among you, and in part I believe it.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:19
verses.text: For indeed it is necessary that there be factions among you, in order that those who are approved may become evident among you.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:20
verses.text: Therefore, <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“come together”)</note> you come together in the same <transChange type="added">place</transChange>, it is not to eat the Lord’s supper.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:21
verses.text: For <transChange type="added">when you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal infinitive (“eat”)</note> eat <transChange type="added">it</transChange>, each one of you goes ahead to take his own supper, and one is hungry and another is drunk.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:22
verses.text: For do you not have houses for eating and drinking? Or do you despise the church of God and humiliate those who do not have <transChange type="added">anything</transChange>? What shall I say to you? Shall I praise you? In this I will not praise <transChange type="added">you</transChange>!  <div eID="gen27270" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11647"/><div sID="gen27271" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11647"/>For I received from the Lord what I also passed on to you, that the Lord Jesus, on the night in which he was betrayed, took bread,

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:24
verses.text: and <transChange type="added">after he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had given thanks”) which is understood as temporal</note> had given thanks, he broke <transChange type="added">it</transChange> and said, “This is my body which <transChange type="added">is</transChange> for you. Do this in remembrance of me.”

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:25
verses.text: Likewise also the cup, after they had eaten, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in my blood. Do this, as often as you drink <transChange type="added">it</transChange>, in remembrance of me.”

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:26
verses.text: For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until he comes.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:27
verses.text: So then, whoever eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord in an unworthy manner will be guilty of the body and the blood of the Lord.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:28
verses.text: But let a person examine himself, and in this way let him eat from the bread and let him drink from the cup.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:29
verses.text: For the one who eats and drinks, <transChange type="added">if he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “if” is supplied as a component of the participle (“recognize”) which is understood as conditional</note> does not recognize the body, eats and drinks judgment against himself.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:30
verses.text: Because of this, many <transChange type="added">are</transChange> weak and sick among you, and quite a few <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞have died⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “have fallen asleep”</note>.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:31
verses.text: But if we were evaluating ourselves, we would not be judged.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:32
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">if we</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “if” is supplied as a component of the participle (“are judged”) which is understood as conditional</note> are judged by the Lord, we are being disciplined, in order that we will not be condemned with the world.  <div eID="gen27271" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:33
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11648"/><div sID="gen27272" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11648"/>So then, my brothers, <transChange type="added">when you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“come together”) which is understood as temporal</note> come together in order to eat the Lord’s supper,<note placement="foot">*Here the direct object (“the Lord’s supper”) is supplied from context in the English translation</note> wait for one another.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:34
verses.text: If anyone is hungry, let him eat at home, lest you come together for judgment. And I will give directions about the remaining <transChange type="added">matters</transChange> whenever I come.  <chapter eID="1Cor.11"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11649"/><title type="x-s">Varieties of Spiritual Gifts</title> <div sID="gen27273" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11649"/>Now concerning spiritual <transChange type="added">gifts</transChange>,<note placement="foot">Or “spiritual things”; possibly “those who possess spiritual gifts”</note> brothers, I do not want you to be ignorant.

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:2
verses.text: You know that when you were pagans, you were led astray to the speechless idols, however you were led.

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:3
verses.text: Therefore I make known to you that no one speaking by the Spirit of God says, “Jesus <transChange type="added">is</transChange> accursed,” and no one is able to say “Jesus <transChange type="added">is</transChange> Lord” except by the Holy Spirit.  <div eID="gen27273" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11650"/><div sID="gen27274" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11650"/>Now there are varieties of gifts, but the same Spirit,

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:5
verses.text: and there are varieties of ministries, and the same Lord,

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:6
verses.text: and there are varieties of activities, but the same God, who works all <transChange type="added">things</transChange> in all <transChange type="added">people</transChange>.

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:7
verses.text: But to each one is given the manifestation of the Spirit for what is beneficial <transChange type="added">to all</transChange>.

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:8
verses.text: For to one is given a word of wisdom through the Spirit, and to another a word of knowledge by the same Spirit,

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:9
verses.text: to another faith by the same Spirit, to another<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “and to another”</note> gifts of healing by the one Spirit,

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:10
verses.text: to another<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “and to another”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞miraculous powers⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “activities of power”</note>, to another<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “and to another”</note> prophecy, to another<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “and to another”</note> distinguishing of spirits, to another kinds of tongues, to another<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “and to another”</note> interpretation of tongues.

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:11
verses.text: But in all these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> one and the same Spirit is at work, distributing to each one individually just as he wishes.  <div eID="gen27274" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11651"/><title type="x-s">Unity in the Midst of Diversity</title> <div sID="gen27275" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11651"/>For just as the body is one and has many members, but all the members of the body, <transChange type="added">although they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“are”) which is understood as concessive</note> are many, are one body, thus also Christ.

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:13
verses.text: For by<note placement="foot">Or “in”</note> one Spirit we were all baptized into one body, whether Jews or Greeks, whether slaves or free <transChange type="added">persons</transChange>, and all were made to drink one Spirit.

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:14
verses.text: For the body is not one member, but many.

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:15
verses.text: If the foot should say, “Because I am not a hand, I am not <transChange type="added">a part</transChange> of the body,” not because of this is it not <transChange type="added">a part</transChange> of the body.

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:16
verses.text: And if the ear should say, “Because I am not an eye, I am not <transChange type="added">a part</transChange> of the body, not because of this is it not <transChange type="added">a part</transChange> of the body.

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:17
verses.text: If the whole body <transChange type="added">were</transChange> an eye, where <transChange type="added">would</transChange> the hearing <transChange type="added">be</transChange>? If the whole <transChange type="added">were</transChange> hearing, where <transChange type="added">would</transChange> the sense of smell <transChange type="added">be</transChange>?

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:18
verses.text: But now God has placed the members, each one of them, in the body just as he wanted.

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:19
verses.text: And if they all were one member, where <transChange type="added">would</transChange> the body <transChange type="added">be</transChange>?

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:20
verses.text: But now <transChange type="added">there are</transChange> many members, but one body.  <div eID="gen27275" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11652"/><div sID="gen27276" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11652"/>Now the eye is not able to say to the hand, “I do not have need of you,” or again, the head to the feet, “I do not have need of you.”

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:22
verses.text: But by much more the members of the body which are thought to be weaker are necessary,

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:23
verses.text: and <transChange type="added">the parts</transChange> of the body which we think to be less honorable, these we clothe with more abundant honor, and our unpresentable <transChange type="added">parts</transChange> come to have more abundant presentability,

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:24
verses.text: but our presentable <transChange type="added">parts</transChange> do not have need <transChange type="added">of this</transChange>. Yet God composed the body by giving more abundant honor to the part which lacked <transChange type="added">it</transChange>,

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:25
verses.text: in order that there not be a division in the body, but the members would have the same concern for one another.

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:26
verses.text: And if one member suffers, all the members suffer together; if a member<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “one member”</note> is honored, all the members rejoice with <transChange type="added">it</transChange>.  <div eID="gen27276" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11653"/><div sID="gen27277" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11653"/>Now you are the body of Christ, and members <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞of it individually⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by part”</note>,

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:28
verses.text: and whom God has appointed in the church: first, apostles, second, prophets, third, teachers, then miracles, then gifts of healing, helps, administrations, kinds of tongues.

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:29
verses.text: Not all <transChange type="added">are</transChange> apostles, <transChange type="added">are they</transChange>?<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here</note> Not all are prophets, are they?<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here</note> Not all are teachers, are they?<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here</note> Not all are workers of miracles, are they?<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here</note>

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:30
verses.text: Not all have gifts of healing, <transChange type="added">do they</transChange>?<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here</note> Not all speak with tongues, do they?<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here</note> Not all interpret, do they?<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here</note>

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:31
verses.text: But strive<note placement="foot">Or “you are striving” (some understand the form of this verb to be indicative mood rather than imperative mood)</note> for the greater gifts. And I will show you a still more excellent way.  <chapter eID="1Cor.12"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 13:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11654"/><title type="x-s">Love, the More Excellent Way</title> <div sID="gen27278" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11654"/>If I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, but do not have love, I have become a ringing brass gong or a clashing cymbal.

verses.name: I Corinthians 13:2
verses.text: And if I have <transChange type="added">the gift of</transChange> prophecy and I know all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have all faith so that <transChange type="added">I can</transChange> remove mountains, but do not have love, I am nothing.

verses.name: I Corinthians 13:3
verses.text: And if I parcel out all my possessions, and if I hand over my body in order that I will be burned,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “in order that I may boast”</note> but do not have love, it benefits <transChange type="added">me</transChange> nothing.  <div eID="gen27278" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 13:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11655"/><div sID="gen27279" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11655"/>Love is patient, love is kind, love is not jealous, <transChange type="added">it</transChange> does not boast, <transChange type="added">it</transChange> does not become conceited,

verses.name: I Corinthians 13:5
verses.text: <transChange type="added">it</transChange> does not behave dishonorably, <transChange type="added">it</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞is not selfish⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “does not seek the things of itself”</note>, <transChange type="added">it</transChange> does not become angry, <transChange type="added">it</transChange> does not keep a record of wrongs,

verses.name: I Corinthians 13:6
verses.text: <transChange type="added">it</transChange> does not rejoice at unrighteousness, but rejoices with the truth,

verses.name: I Corinthians 13:7
verses.text: bears all <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, believes all <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, hopes all <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, endures all <transChange type="added">things</transChange>.  <div eID="gen27279" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 13:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11656"/><div sID="gen27280" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11656"/>Love never ends. But if <transChange type="added">there are</transChange> prophecies, they will pass away. If <transChange type="added">there are</transChange> tongues, they will cease. If <transChange type="added">there is</transChange> knowledge, it will pass away.

verses.name: I Corinthians 13:9
verses.text: For we know in part and we prophesy in part,

verses.name: I Corinthians 13:10
verses.text: but whenever the perfect comes, the partial will pass away.

verses.name: I Corinthians 13:11
verses.text: When I was a child, I spoke like a child, I thought like a child, I reasoned like a child. When I became a man, I set aside the things of a child.

verses.name: I Corinthians 13:12
verses.text: For now we see through a mirror <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞indirectly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in an indirect image”</note>, but then face to face. Now I know in part, but then I will know completely, just as I have also been completely known.

verses.name: I Corinthians 13:13
verses.text: And now these three <transChange type="added">things</transChange> remain: faith, hope, <transChange type="added">and</transChange> love. But the greatest of these <transChange type="added">is</transChange> love.  <chapter eID="1Cor.13"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11657"/><title type="x-s">Appropriate Use of Prophecy and Tongues</title> <div sID="gen27281" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11657"/>Pursue love, and strive for spiritual <transChange type="added">gifts</transChange>, but especially that you may prophesy.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:2
verses.text: For the one who speaks in a tongue does not speak to people but to God, because no one understands, but by the Spirit<note placement="foot">Or “in the Spirit”; or “in his spirit”</note> he speaks mysteries.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:3
verses.text: But the one who prophesies speaks to people edification and encouragement and consolation.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:4
verses.text: The one who speaks in a tongue edifies himself, but the one who prophesies edifies the church.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:5
verses.text: Now I want you all to speak with tongues, but even more that you may prophesy. The one who prophesies <transChange type="added">is</transChange> greater than the one who speaks with tongues, unless he interprets, in order that the church may receive edification.  <div eID="gen27281" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11658"/><div sID="gen27282" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11658"/>But now, brothers, if I come to you speaking with tongues, how do I benefit you, unless I speak to you either with a revelation or with knowledge or with a prophecy or with a teaching?

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:7
verses.text: Likewise, the inanimate things which produce a sound, whether flute or lyre, if they do not produce a distinction in the tones, how will it be known what is played on the flute or on the lyre?

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:8
verses.text: For indeed, if the trumpet produces an indistinct sound, who will prepare for battle?

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:9
verses.text: And so you through the tongue, unless you produce a clear message, how will it be known what is spoken? For you will be speaking into the air.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:10
verses.text: There are probably so many kinds of languages in the world, and none without meaning.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:11
verses.text: Therefore, if I do not know the meaning of the language, I will be a barbarian to the one who is speaking, and the one who is speaking <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> a barbarian in my <transChange type="added">judgment</transChange>.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:12
verses.text: In this way also you, since you are zealous of spiritual <transChange type="added">gifts</transChange>, seek for the edification of the church, in order that you may abound.  <div eID="gen27282" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11659"/><div sID="gen27283" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11659"/>Therefore the one who speaks in a tongue must pray that he may interpret.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:14
verses.text: For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays but my mind is unproductive.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:15
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Therefore what should I do⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “what therefore is it”</note>? I will pray with my spirit, but I will also pray with my mind. I will sing praise with my spirit, but I will also sing praise with my mind.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:16
verses.text: For otherwise, if you praise in <transChange type="added">your</transChange> spirit, how will the one who fills the place of the outsider say the “amen” at your thanksgiving, because he does not know what you are saying?

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:17
verses.text: For indeed you are giving thanks well, but the other person is not edified.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:18
verses.text: I give thanks to God <transChange type="added">that</transChange> I speak with tongues more than all of you,

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:19
verses.text: but in the church I prefer to speak five words with my mind, in order that I may instruct other <transChange type="added">people</transChange>, than ten thousand words in a tongue.  <div eID="gen27283" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11660"/><div sID="gen27284" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11660"/>Brothers, do not become children in <transChange type="added">your</transChange> understanding, but with respect to wickedness be as a child, and in <transChange type="added">your</transChange> understanding be mature.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:21
verses.text: In the law it is written: <div eID="gen27284" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27285"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27286"/>“By those who speak a foreign language<l eID="gen27286" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27287"/>and by the lips of others<l eID="gen27287" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27288"/>I will speak to this people,<l eID="gen27288" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27289"/>and not even in this way will they obey me,”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.28.11-Isa.28.12">Isa 28:11–12</reference></note><l eID="gen27289" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen27285"/> <div sID="gen27290" type="x-p"/> says the Lord.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:22
verses.text: So then, tongues are for a sign not to those who believe, but to unbelievers, but prophecy <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not for unbelievers, but for those who believe.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:23
verses.text: Therefore, if the whole church comes together at the same <transChange type="added">time</transChange> and all speak with tongues, and outsiders or unbelievers enter, will they not say that you are out of your minds?

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:24
verses.text: But if all prophesy, and some unbeliever or outsider enters, he is convicted by all, he is judged by all,

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:25
verses.text: the secret things of his heart become evident, and so, falling on <transChange type="added">his</transChange> face, he will worship God, proclaiming, “God is truly among you!”  <div eID="gen27290" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:26
