verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11661"/><title type="x-s">Specific Instructions for Orderly Worship Services</title> <div sID="gen27291" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11661"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Therefore what should you do⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “what therefore is it”</note>, brothers? Whenever you come together, each one of you has a psalm, has a teaching, has a revelation, has a tongue, has an interpretation. All <transChange type="added">things</transChange> must be <transChange type="added">done</transChange> for edification.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:27
verses.text: If anyone speaks in a tongue, <transChange type="added">it must be</transChange> on one occasion two or at most three, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞one after the other⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in turn”</note>, and one must interpret.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:28
verses.text: But if there is no interpreter, he must be silent in the church, but let him speak to himself and to God.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:29
verses.text: Let two or three prophets speak, and the others evaluate.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:30
verses.text: And if <transChange type="added">something</transChange> is revealed to another who is seated, the first must be silent.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:31
verses.text: For you are all able to prophesy <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in turn⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “one at a time</note>, in order that all may learn and all may be encouraged,

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:32
verses.text: and the spirits of prophets are subject to prophets.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:33
verses.text: For God is not <transChange type="added">a God of</transChange> disorder but of peace. <div eID="gen27291" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen27292" type="x-p"/> As in all the churches of the saints,

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:34
verses.text: the women must be silent in the churches, for it is not permitted for them to speak, but they must be in submission, just as the law also says.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:35
verses.text: But if they want to learn something, let them ask their own husbands at home, for it is shameful for a woman to speak in church.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:36
verses.text: Or has the word of God gone out from you, or has it come to you only?  <div eID="gen27292" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:37
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11662"/><div sID="gen27293" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11662"/>If anyone thinks he is a prophet or spiritual,<note placement="foot">Or “or one who possesses the Spirit”</note> he should recognize that the things which I am writing to you are of the Lord.<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “are a command of the Lord”</note>

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:38
verses.text: But if anyone ignores <transChange type="added">this</transChange>, he is ignored.<note placement="foot">Or “if anyone is ignorant, let him be ignorant”</note>

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:39
verses.text: So then, my brothers, desire to prophesy, and do not prevent speaking with tongues.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:40
verses.text: But let all <transChange type="added">things</transChange> be <transChange type="added">done</transChange> decently and according to proper procedure.  <chapter eID="1Cor.14"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11663"/><title type="x-s">Paul’s Gospel and the Resurrection of Christ</title> <div sID="gen27294" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11663"/>Now I make known to you, brothers, the gospel which I proclaimed to you, which you have also received, in which you also stand,

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:2
verses.text: by which you are also being saved, if you hold fast to the message I proclaimed to you, unless you believed to no purpose.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:3
verses.text: For I passed on to you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as of first importance⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “among the first things”</note> what I also received, that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures,

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:4
verses.text: and that he was buried, and that he was raised up on the third day according to the scriptures,

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:5
verses.text: and that he appeared to Cephas, then to the twelve,

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:6
verses.text: then he appeared to more than five hundred brothers at once, the majority of whom remain until now, but some have fallen asleep.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:7
verses.text: Then he appeared to James, then to all the apostles,

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:8
verses.text: and last of all, as it were to one born at the wrong time, he appeared also to me.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:9
verses.text: For I am the least of the apostles, not worthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:10
verses.text: But by the grace of God I am what I am, and his grace to me has not been in vain, but I labored even more than all of them, and not I, but the grace of God with me.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:11
verses.text: Therefore whether I or those, in this way we preached, and in this way you believed.  <div eID="gen27294" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11664"/><title type="x-s">Concerning the Resurrection of the Dead</title> <div sID="gen27295" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11664"/>Now if Christ is preached as raised up from the dead, how do some among you say that <transChange type="added">there</transChange> is no resurrection of the dead?

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:13
verses.text: But if <transChange type="added">there</transChange> is no resurrection of the dead, Christ has not been raised <transChange type="added">either</transChange>.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:14
verses.text: But if Christ has not been raised, then<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “then both”</note> our preaching <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in vain, and your faith <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in vain.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:15
verses.text: And also we are found <transChange type="added">to be</transChange> false witnesses of God, because we testified against God that he raised Christ, whom he did not raise if after all, then, the dead are not raised.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:16
verses.text: For if the dead are not raised, Christ has not been raised <transChange type="added">either</transChange>.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:17
verses.text: But if Christ has not been raised, your faith <transChange type="added">is</transChange> empty; you are still in your sins.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:18
verses.text: And as a further result, those who have fallen asleep in Christ have perished.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:19
verses.text: If <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞we have put our hope⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “we are having put our hope”</note> in Christ in this life only, we are of all people most pitiable.  <div eID="gen27295" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11665"/><div sID="gen27296" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11665"/>But now Christ has been raised from the dead, the first fruits of those who have fallen asleep.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:21
verses.text: For since through a man <transChange type="added">came</transChange> death, also through a man <transChange type="added">came</transChange> the resurrection of the dead.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:22
verses.text: For just as in Adam all die, so also in Christ all will be made alive.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:23
verses.text: But each in his own group: Christ the first fruits, then those <transChange type="added">who are</transChange> Christ’s at his coming,

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:24
verses.text: then the end, when he hands over the kingdom to the God and Father, when he has abolished all rule and all authority and power.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:25
verses.text: For it is necessary for him to reign until he has put all his enemies under his feet.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:26
verses.text: The last enemy to be abolished <transChange type="added">is</transChange> death.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:27
verses.text: For “he subjected all <transChange type="added">things</transChange> under his feet.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.8.6">Ps 8:6</reference></note> But when it says “all <transChange type="added">things</transChange>” are subjected, <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> clear that the one who subjected all <transChange type="added">things</transChange> to him <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not included.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:28
verses.text: But whenever all <transChange type="added">things</transChange> are subjected to him, then the Son himself will be subjected<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “also will be subjected”</note> to the one who subjected all <transChange type="added">things</transChange> to him, in order that God may be all in all.  <div eID="gen27296" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11666"/><div sID="gen27297" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11666"/>Otherwise, why do they do <transChange type="added">it</transChange>, those who are being baptized on behalf of the dead? If the dead are not raised at all, why indeed are they being baptized on behalf of them?

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:30
verses.text: And why are we in danger every hour?

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:31
verses.text: I die every day—yes indeed, by my boasting in you,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “in you, brothers,”</note> which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord!

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:32
verses.text: If according to a human perspective I fought wild beasts at Ephesus, what benefit <transChange type="added">is it</transChange> to me? If the dead are not raised, let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.<note placement="foot">An allusion to <reference osisRef="Isa.22.13">Isa 22:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.56.12">56:12</reference></note>

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:33
verses.text: Do not be deceived! “Bad company corrupts good morals.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from the Greek poet Menander’s comedy <hi type="italic">Thais</hi>, 218</note>

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:34
verses.text: Sober up correctly and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞stop sinning⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “do not sin”</note>, for some have no knowledge of God—I say <transChange type="added">this</transChange> to your shame.  <div eID="gen27297" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:35
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11667"/><title type="x-s">Questions Concerning the Resurrection Body</title> <div sID="gen27298" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11667"/>But someone will say, “How are the dead raised? And with what sort of body do they come?”

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:36
verses.text: Foolish person! What you sow does not come to life unless it dies.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:37
verses.text: And what you sow <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not the body which it will become, but you sow the bare seed, whether perhaps of wheat or of some of the rest.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:38
verses.text: But God gives to it a body just as he wishes, and to each one of the seeds its own body.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:39
verses.text: Not all flesh <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the same, but <transChange type="added">there is</transChange> one flesh of human beings, and another flesh of animals, and another flesh of birds, and another of fish,

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:40
verses.text: and heavenly bodies and earthly bodies. But the glory of the heavenly <transChange type="added">bodies</transChange> <transChange type="added">is</transChange> of one kind, and the <transChange type="added">glory</transChange> of the earthly <transChange type="added">bodies</transChange> <transChange type="added">is</transChange> of another kind.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:41
verses.text: <transChange type="added">There is</transChange> one glory of the sun, and another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars, for star differs from star in glory.  <div eID="gen27298" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:42
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11668"/><div sID="gen27299" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11668"/>Thus also <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the resurrection of the dead. It is sown in corruption, it is raised in incorruptibility.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:43
verses.text: It is sown in dishonor, it is raised in glory. It is sown in weakness, it is raised in power.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:44
verses.text: It is sown a natural body, it is raised a spiritual body. If <transChange type="added">there</transChange> is a natural body, <transChange type="added">there</transChange> is also a spiritual <transChange type="added">body</transChange>.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:45
verses.text: Thus also it is written, “The first man, Adam, became a living soul”;<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Gen.2.7">Gen 2:7</reference></note> the last Adam <transChange type="added">became</transChange> a life-giving spirit.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:46
verses.text: But the spiritual <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not first, but the natural; then the spiritual.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:47
verses.text: The first man <transChange type="added">is</transChange> from the earth, made of earth; the second man <transChange type="added">is</transChange> from heaven.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:48
verses.text: As the one <transChange type="added">who is</transChange> made of earth, so also <transChange type="added">are</transChange> those <transChange type="added">who are</transChange> made of earth, and as the heavenly, so also <transChange type="added">are</transChange> those <transChange type="added">who are</transChange> heavenly.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:49
verses.text: And just as we have borne the image of the <transChange type="added">one who is</transChange> made of earth, we will also bear the image of the heavenly.  <div eID="gen27299" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:50
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11669"/><div sID="gen27300" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11669"/>But I say this, brothers, that flesh and blood is not able to inherit the kingdom of God, nor can corruption inherit incorruptibility.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:51
verses.text: Behold, I tell you a mystery: we will not all fall asleep, but we will all be changed,

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:52
verses.text: in a moment, in the blink of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound, and the dead will be raised imperishable, and we will be changed.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:53
verses.text: For it is necessary <transChange type="added">for</transChange> this perishable <transChange type="added">body</transChange> to put on incorruptibility, and this mortal <transChange type="added">body</transChange> to put on immortality.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:54
verses.text: But whenever this perishable <transChange type="added">body</transChange> puts on incorruptibility and this mortal <transChange type="added">body</transChange> puts on immortality, then the saying that is written will take place: <div eID="gen27300" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27301"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27302"/>“Death is swallowed up in victory. <l eID="gen27302" level="1"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:55
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11670"/><l level="1" sID="gen27303"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11670"/>Where, O death, <transChange type="added">is</transChange> your victory?<l eID="gen27303" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27304"/>Where, O death, <transChange type="added">is</transChange> your sting? <l eID="gen27304" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen27301"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:56
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11671"/><div sID="gen27305" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11671"/>Now the sting of death <transChange type="added">is</transChange> sin, and the power of sin <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the law.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:57
verses.text: But thanks <transChange type="added">be</transChange> to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ!

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:58
verses.text: So then, my dear brothers, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, <transChange type="added">because you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“know”) which is understood as causal</note> know that your labor is not <transChange type="added">in</transChange> vain in the Lord.  <chapter eID="1Cor.15"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11672"/><title type="x-s">Concerning the Collection for the Saints</title> <div sID="gen27306" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11672"/>Now concerning the collection for the saints: just as I gave directions about <transChange type="added">it</transChange> to the churches of Galatia, so you do also.

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:2
verses.text: On the first <transChange type="added">day</transChange> of the week, each one of you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞put aside⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “put from himself”</note> something, saving up <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to whatever extent he has prospered⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “whatever if anything he has been prospered”</note>, in order that whenever I come, at that time collections do not take place.

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:3
verses.text: And whenever I arrive, whomever you approve by letters, I will send these to take your gift to Jerusalem.

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:4
verses.text: And if it is worthwhile for me to go also, they will travel with me.  <div eID="gen27306" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11673"/><title type="x-s">Travel Plans for Paul and Associates</title> <div sID="gen27307" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11673"/>But I will come to you whenever I go through Macedonia (for I am going through Macedonia),

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:6
verses.text: and perhaps I will stay with you, or even spend the winter, so that you may send me on my way wherever I may go.

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:7
verses.text: For I do not want to see you now in passing, for I hope to remain some time with you, if the Lord allows <transChange type="added">it</transChange>.

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:8
verses.text: But I will remain in Ephesus until Pentecost,

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:9
verses.text: for a great and effective door has opened for me, and <transChange type="added">there are</transChange> many opponents.  <div eID="gen27307" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11674"/><div sID="gen27308" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11674"/>But if Timothy comes, see that he is with you without cause to fear, for he is carrying out the Lord’s work, as I also <transChange type="added">am</transChange>.

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:11
verses.text: Therefore do not let anyone disdain him, but send him <transChange type="added">on his way</transChange> in peace in order that he may come to me, for I am expecting him with the brothers.  <div eID="gen27308" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11675"/><div sID="gen27309" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11675"/>Now concerning Apollos our brother, I urged him many <transChange type="added">times</transChange> that he should come to you with the brothers, and he was not at all willing that he should come now, but he will come whenever he has <transChange type="added">an</transChange> opportunity.  <div eID="gen27309" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11676"/><title type="x-s">Concluding Exhortations</title> <div sID="gen27310" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11676"/>Be on the alert, stand firm in the faith, act courageously, be strong.

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:14
verses.text: All your <transChange type="added">actions</transChange> must be done in love.  <div eID="gen27310" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11677"/><div sID="gen27311" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11677"/>Now I urge you, brothers—you know about the household of Stephanas, that they are the first fruits of Achaia, and they have devoted themselves to the ministry for the saints—

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:16
verses.text: that you also be subject to such people, and to all those who work together and labor.

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:17
verses.text: Now I rejoice over the arrival of Stephanas and Fortunatus and Achaicus, because these make up for your absence,

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:18
verses.text: for they have refreshed my spirit and yours. Therefore recognize such people.  <div eID="gen27311" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11678"/><title type="x-s">Final Greetings and Benediction</title> <div sID="gen27312" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11678"/>The churches of <transChange type="added">the province of</transChange> Asia<note placement="foot">That is, the Roman province of Asia, known today as Asia Minor</note> greet you. Aquila and Prisca greet you in the Lord many <transChange type="added">times</transChange>, together with the church in their house.

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:20
verses.text: All the brothers greet you. Greet one another with a holy kiss.  <div eID="gen27312" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11679"/><div sID="gen27313" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11679"/>The greeting <transChange type="added">is</transChange> by my hand—Paul’s.

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:22
verses.text: If anyone does not love the Lord, let him be accursed. O Lord, come!<note placement="foot">The Aramaic expression <hi type="italic">marana tha</hi> (“O Lord, come!”) can also be rendered <hi type="italic">maran atha</hi> (“our Lord has come”); it is used here by Paul without explanation</note>  <div eID="gen27313" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11680"/><div sID="gen27314" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11680"/>The grace of the Lord Jesus <transChange type="added">be</transChange> with you.

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:24
verses.text: My love <transChange type="added">be</transChange> with all of you in Christ Jesus.  <chapter eID="1Cor.16"/> <div eID="gen27314" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen27211" osisID="1Cor" type="book"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11681"/><title type="x-s">Greeting</title> <div sID="gen27316" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11681"/>Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus through the will of God, and Timothy our brother, to the church of God that is in Corinth, together with all the saints who are in all Achaia.

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:2
verses.text: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.  <div eID="gen27316" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11682"/><title type="x-s">Thanksgiving for God’s Compassion and Comfort</title> <div sID="gen27317" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11682"/>Blessed <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and God of all comfort,

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:4
verses.text: who comforts us in all our affliction, so that we may be able to comfort those <transChange type="added">who are</transChange> in all affliction with the comfort with which <transChange type="added">we</transChange> ourselves are comforted by God.

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:5
verses.text: For just as the sufferings of Christ overflow to us, thus through Christ our comfort overflows also.

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:6
verses.text: But if we are afflicted, <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> for your comfort and salvation; if we are comforted, <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> for your comfort that is at work in the patient endurance of the same sufferings that we also suffer.

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:7
verses.text: And our hope for you <transChange type="added">is</transChange> firm, <transChange type="added">because we</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“is”) which is understood as causal</note> know that as you are sharers in the sufferings, so also <transChange type="added">you will be sharers</transChange> in the comfort.  <div eID="gen27317" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11683"/><div sID="gen27318" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11683"/>For we do not want you to be ignorant, brothers, concerning our affliction that happened in the <transChange type="added">province of</transChange> Asia,<note placement="foot">A reference to the Roman province of Asia (modern Asia Minor)</note> that we were burdened to an extraordinary degree, beyond <transChange type="added">our</transChange> strength, so that we were in despair even of living.

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:9
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">we</transChange> ourselves had the sentence of death in ourselves, so that we would not be putting confidence in ourselves, but in God who raises the dead,

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:10
verses.text: who delivered us from so great <transChange type="added">a risk</transChange> of death, and will deliver <transChange type="added">us</transChange>, in whom we have put our hope that he will also deliver <transChange type="added">us</transChange> again,

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:11
verses.text: <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“join in helping”)</note> you also join in helping <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞on our behalf⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “on behalf of us”</note> by prayer, so that thanks may be given <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞on our behalf⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “on behalf of us”</note> by many persons for this gracious gift <transChange type="added">given</transChange> to us through <transChange type="added">the help</transChange> of many.  <div eID="gen27318" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11684"/><title type="x-s">Paul’s Clear Conscience</title> <div sID="gen27319" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11684"/>For our reason for boasting is this: the testimony of our conscience that we conducted ourselves in the world, and especially toward you, in holiness<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “sincerity”</note> and purity of motive from God, not<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “and not”</note> in merely human wisdom, but by the grace of God.

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:13
verses.text: For we are not writing <transChange type="added">anything</transChange> else to you except what you can read or also understand. But I hope that you will understand <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞completely⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the end”</note>,

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:14
verses.text: just as you have also understood us in part, that we are your reason for boasting, just as you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> also ours in the day of our Lord Jesus.  <div eID="gen27319" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11685"/><title type="x-s">Paul Delays His Visit to Corinth</title> <div sID="gen27320" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11685"/>And with this confidence, I was wanting to come to you previously, in order that you may have a second proof of my goodwill,

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:16
verses.text: and through you to go to Macedonia, and to come to you again from Macedonia, and to be sent on my way by you to Judea.

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:17
verses.text: Therefore, <transChange type="added">when I</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was wanting”) which is understood as temporal</note> was wanting to do this, perhaps then was I making use of vacillation? Or was I deciding what I was deciding according to the flesh, in order that with me my “yes” may be “yes” and my “no” may be “no” at the same time?<note placement="foot">*The words “at the same time” are supplied for clarity</note>

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:18
verses.text: But God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> faithful, so that our word to you is not “yes” and “no.”

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:19
verses.text: For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, the one who was proclaimed among you by us, by me and Silvanus and Timothy, did not become “yes” and “no,” but has become “yes” in him.

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:20
verses.text: For as many as <transChange type="added">are the</transChange> promises of God, in him <transChange type="added">they are</transChange> “yes”; therefore also through him <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the “amen” to the glory of God through us.

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:21
verses.text: Now the one who establishes us together with you in Christ and who anoints us <transChange type="added">is</transChange> God,

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:22
verses.text: <transChange type="added">who</transChange> also sealed us and gave the down payment of the Spirit in our hearts.  <div eID="gen27320" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11686"/><div sID="gen27321" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11686"/>But I call upon God <transChange type="added">as</transChange> witness against my life, that <transChange type="added">in order to</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “in order to” is supplied as a component of the participle (“spare”) which is understood as purpose</note> spare you, I did not come again to Corinth.

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:24
verses.text: Not that we lord it over your faith, but we are fellow workers for your joy, because by faith you stand firm.  <chapter eID="2Cor.1"/> <div eID="gen27321" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 2:1
verses.text: For I have decided this for myself, not to come to you again in sorrow.

verses.name: II Corinthians 2:2
verses.text: For if I <transChange type="added">cause</transChange> you sorrow, then who will make me glad except the one who is caused to be sad by me?

verses.name: II Corinthians 2:3
verses.text: And I wrote this very <transChange type="added">thing</transChange> in order that <transChange type="added">when I</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“came”) which is understood as temporal</note> came, I would not experience sorrow from those who ought to have made me glad, because I<note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“have confidence”) which is understood as causal</note> have confidence about you all, that my joy <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞belongs to all of you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “is of all of you”</note>.

verses.name: II Corinthians 2:4
verses.text: For out of great distress and anguish of heart I wrote to you through many tears, not so that you may be caused to be sad, but so that you may know the love that I have especially for you.  <div eID="gen27322" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 2:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11687"/><title type="x-s">Forgive and Comfort the Offender</title> <div sID="gen27323" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11687"/>But if anyone has caused sorrow, he has not caused me sorrow, but <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to some degree⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in part”</note>—<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in order not to say too much⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in order not to burden”</note>—<transChange type="added">to</transChange> all <transChange type="added">of</transChange> you.

verses.name: II Corinthians 2:6
verses.text: This punishment by the majority <transChange type="added">is</transChange> sufficient for such a person.

verses.name: II Corinthians 2:7
verses.text: So then, you should rather forgive and comfort him, lest somehow this person should be overwhelmed by excessive sorrow.

verses.name: II Corinthians 2:8
verses.text: Therefore I urge you to confirm <transChange type="added">your</transChange> love for him.

verses.name: II Corinthians 2:9
verses.text: Because for this <transChange type="added">reason</transChange> also I wrote, in order that I could know your proven character, whether you are obedient in everything.

verses.name: II Corinthians 2:10
verses.text: Now to whomever you forgive anything, I also <transChange type="added">do</transChange>; for indeed, whatever I have forgiven, if I have forgiven anything, <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞for your sake⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for the sake of you”</note> in the presence of Christ,

verses.name: II Corinthians 2:11
verses.text: in order that we may not be exploited by Satan (for we are not ignorant of his schemes).  <div eID="gen27323" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 2:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11688"/><title type="x-s">Triumphant Ministry in Christ</title> <div sID="gen27324" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11688"/>Now <transChange type="added">when I</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“arrived”) which is understood as temporal</note> arrived in Troas for the gospel of Christ and a door was opened for me by the Lord,

verses.name: II Corinthians 2:13
verses.text: I did not experience rest in my spirit, <transChange type="added">because</transChange><note placement="foot">This infinitive (“find”) is understood as causal</note> I did not find Titus my brother, but saying farewell to them, I departed for Macedonia.

verses.name: II Corinthians 2:14
verses.text: But thanks <transChange type="added">be</transChange> to God, who always leads us in triumphal procession in Christ, and who reveals the fragrance of the knowledge of him through us in every place.

verses.name: II Corinthians 2:15
verses.text: For we are the aroma of Christ to God among those who are being saved and among those who are perishing,

verses.name: II Corinthians 2:16
verses.text: to those on the one hand an odor from death to death, <transChange type="added">and</transChange> to those on the other hand a fragrance from life to life. And who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> qualified for these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>?

verses.name: II Corinthians 2:17
verses.text: For we are not like the majority who peddle the word of God, but as from pure motives—but as from God—we speak before God in Christ.  <chapter eID="2Cor.2"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 3:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11689"/><title type="x-s">New Covenant Ministry</title> <div sID="gen27325" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11689"/>Are we beginning to commend ourselves again? Or <transChange type="added">do we</transChange>, like some, need letters of recommendation to you or from you?

verses.name: II Corinthians 3:2
verses.text: You are our letter, inscribed on our hearts, known and read by all people,

verses.name: II Corinthians 3:3
verses.text: revealing that you are a letter of Christ, delivered by us, inscribed not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on stone tablets but on tablets of human hearts.  <div eID="gen27325" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 3:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11690"/><div sID="gen27326" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11690"/>Now we possess such confidence through Christ toward God.

verses.name: II Corinthians 3:5
verses.text: Not that we are adequate in ourselves to consider anything as from ourselves, but our adequacy <transChange type="added">is</transChange> from God,

verses.name: II Corinthians 3:6
verses.text: who also makes us adequate <transChange type="added">as</transChange> servants of a new covenant, not of the letter, but of the Spirit, for the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.  <div eID="gen27326" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 3:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11691"/><div sID="gen27327" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11691"/>But if the ministry of death in letters carved on stone came with glory, so that the sons of Israel were not able to look intently into the face of Moses because of the glory of his face, which was transitory,

verses.name: II Corinthians 3:8
verses.text: how will the ministry of the Spirit not be even more with glory?

verses.name: II Corinthians 3:9
verses.text: For if <transChange type="added">there was</transChange> glory in the ministry of condemnation, by much more will the ministry of righteousness overflow with glory.

verses.name: II Corinthians 3:10
verses.text: For indeed what had been glorified has not been glorified in this case, on account of the glory that surpasses <transChange type="added">it</transChange>.

verses.name: II Corinthians 3:11
verses.text: For if what was transitory <transChange type="added">came</transChange> with glory, by much more what remains <transChange type="added">is</transChange> with glory.  <div eID="gen27327" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 3:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11692"/><div sID="gen27328" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11692"/>Therefore, <transChange type="added">because we</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“have”) which is understood as causal</note> have such a hope, we use much boldness,

verses.name: II Corinthians 3:13
verses.text: and not as Moses used to place a veil over his face, in order that the sons of Israel would not stare at the end of what was transitory.

verses.name: II Corinthians 3:14
verses.text: But their minds were hardened. For until this very day, the same veil remains upon the reading of the old covenant, not being uncovered, because it is done away with in Christ.

verses.name: II Corinthians 3:15
verses.text: But until today, whenever Moses is read aloud, a veil lies upon their heart,

verses.name: II Corinthians 3:16
verses.text: but whenever one turns to the Lord, the veil is removed.

verses.name: II Corinthians 3:17
verses.text: Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord <transChange type="added">is, there is</transChange> freedom.

verses.name: II Corinthians 3:18
verses.text: And we all, with unveiled face, reflecting<note placement="foot">Or “contemplating”</note> the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into the same image from glory into glory, just as from the Lord, the Spirit.  <chapter eID="2Cor.3"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 4:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11693"/><title type="x-s">Proclaiming Jesus Christ as Lord</title> <div sID="gen27329" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11693"/>Because of this, <transChange type="added">since we</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “since” is supplied as a component of the participle (“have”) which is understood as causal</note> have this ministry, just as we have been shown mercy, we do not lose heart,

verses.name: II Corinthians 4:2
verses.text: but we have renounced shameful hidden things, not behaving with craftiness or adulterating the word of God, but with the open proclamation of the truth commending ourselves to every person’s conscience before God.

verses.name: II Corinthians 4:3
verses.text: But if indeed our gospel is veiled, it is veiled among those who are perishing,

verses.name: II Corinthians 4:4
verses.text: among whom the god of this age has blinded the minds of the unbelievers, so that they would not see the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God.

verses.name: II Corinthians 4:5
verses.text: For we do not proclaim ourselves, but Christ Jesus<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “Jesus Christ”</note> <transChange type="added">as</transChange> Lord, and ourselves <transChange type="added">as</transChange> your slaves for the sake of Jesus.

verses.name: II Corinthians 4:6
verses.text: For God who said, “Light will shine out of darkness,”<note placement="foot">An allusion to <reference osisRef="Gen.1.3">Gen 1:3</reference></note> is the one who has shined in our hearts for the enlightenment of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Christ.<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “in the face of Jesus Christ”</note>  <div eID="gen27329" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 4:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11694"/><title type="x-s">Treasure in Earthenware Jars</title> <div sID="gen27330" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11694"/>But we have this treasure in earthenware jars, in order that the extraordinary degree of the power may be from God and not from us.

verses.name: II Corinthians 4:8
verses.text: We are afflicted in every <transChange type="added">way</transChange>, but not crushed; perplexed, but not despairing;

verses.name: II Corinthians 4:9
verses.text: persecuted, but not abandoned; struck down, but not destroyed;

verses.name: II Corinthians 4:10
verses.text: always carrying around the death of Jesus in our body, in order that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our body.

verses.name: II Corinthians 4:11
verses.text: For we who are alive <transChange type="added">are</transChange> continually being handed over to death because of Jesus, in order that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our mortal flesh.

verses.name: II Corinthians 4:12
verses.text: So then, death is at work in us, but life in you.

verses.name: II Corinthians 4:13
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">because we</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“have”) which is understood as causal</note> have the same spirit of faith in accordance with what is written, “I believed, therefore I spoke,”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.116.10">Ps 116:10</reference></note> we also believe, therefore we also speak,

verses.name: II Corinthians 4:14
verses.text: <transChange type="added">because we</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“know”) which is understood as causal</note> know that the one who raised Jesus<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “the Lord Jesus”</note> will also raise us together with Jesus and present <transChange type="added">us</transChange> together with you.

verses.name: II Corinthians 4:15
verses.text: For all <transChange type="added">these things</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞are for your sake⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for the sake of you”</note>, in order that the grace that is increasing through the many may cause thanksgiving to abound to the glory of God.  <div eID="gen27330" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 4:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11695"/><div sID="gen27331" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11695"/>Therefore we do not lose heart, but even if our outer person is being destroyed, yet our inner <transChange type="added">person</transChange> is being renewed day after day.

verses.name: II Corinthians 4:17
verses.text: For our momentary light affliction is producing in us an eternal weight of glory <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞beyond all measure and proportion⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “according to an extraordinary degree to an extraordinary degree”</note>,

verses.name: II Corinthians 4:18
verses.text: <transChange type="added">because</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the causal genitive absolute participle (“looking at”)</note> we are not looking at what is seen, but what is not seen. For what is seen <transChange type="added">is</transChange> temporary, but what is not seen <transChange type="added">is</transChange> eternal.  <chapter eID="2Cor.4"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11696"/><title type="x-s">Absent from the Body and at Home with the Lord</title> <div sID="gen27332" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11696"/>For we know that if our earthly house, the tent, is destroyed, we have a building from God, a house not made by hands, eternal in the heavens.

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:2
verses.text: For indeed, in this <transChange type="added">house</transChange> we groan, <transChange type="added">because we</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“desire”) which is understood as causal</note> desire to put on our dwelling from heaven,

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:3
verses.text: if indeed, even <transChange type="added">after we</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“have taken off”) which is understood as temporal</note> have taken it off,<note placement="foot">A number of important early manuscripts read “have put it on” here</note> we will not be found naked.

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:4
verses.text: For indeed we who are in this tent groan, being burdened <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞for this reason, that⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in that”</note> we do not want to be unclothed, but to be clothed, in order that what is mortal may be swallowed up by life.

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:5
verses.text: Now the one who has prepared us for this very <transChange type="added">thing</transChange> <transChange type="added">is</transChange> God, who has given us the down payment, the Spirit.  <div eID="gen27332" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11697"/><div sID="gen27333" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11697"/>Therefore, <transChange type="added">although we are</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“confident”) which is understood as concessive</note> always confident and know that while we<note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the participle (“are at home”) which is understood as temporal</note> are at home in the body we are absent from the Lord—

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:7
verses.text: for we live by faith, not by sight—

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:8
verses.text: so we are confident and prefer rather to be absent from the body and to be at home with the Lord.

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:9
verses.text: Therefore indeed we have as our ambition, whether at home <transChange type="added">in the body</transChange> or absent <transChange type="added">from the body</transChange>, to be acceptable to him.

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:10
verses.text: For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, in order that each one may receive back the <transChange type="added">things</transChange> through the body according to what he has done, whether good or bad.  <div eID="gen27333" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11698"/><title type="x-s">Controlled by the Love of Christ</title> <div sID="gen27334" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11698"/>Therefore, <transChange type="added">because we</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“know”) which is understood as causal</note> know the fear of the Lord, we are attempting to persuade people, but we are revealed to God, and I hope to be revealed in your consciences.

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:12
verses.text: We are not commending ourselves to you again, but are giving you an opportunity to boast about us, in order that you may have <transChange type="added">an answer</transChange> for those who boast in appearance and not in heart.

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:13
verses.text: For if we are out of our senses, <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> for God; if we are of sound mind, <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> for you.

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:14
verses.text: For the love of Christ controls us, <transChange type="added">because we</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“have concluded”) which is understood as causal</note> have concluded this: that one died for all; as a result all died.

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:15
verses.text: And he died for all, in order that those who live should no longer live for themselves, but for the one who died for them and was raised.  <div eID="gen27334" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11699"/><div sID="gen27335" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11699"/>So then, from now on we know no one <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from a human point of view⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “according to the flesh”</note>, if indeed we have known Christ <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞from a human point of view⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “according to the flesh”</note>, but now we know <transChange type="added">him this way</transChange> no longer.

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:17
verses.text: Therefore if anyone <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in Christ, <transChange type="added">he is</transChange> a new creation; the old <transChange type="added">things</transChange> have passed away; behold, new <transChange type="added">things</transChange> have come.

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:18
verses.text: And all these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> <transChange type="added">are</transChange> from God, who has reconciled us to himself through Christ, and who has given us the ministry of reconciliation,

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:19
verses.text: namely, that God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself, not counting their trespasses against them, and entrusting to us the message of reconciliation.

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:20
verses.text: Therefore we are ambassadors on behalf of Christ, as <transChange type="added">if</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “if” is supplied as a component of the participle (“were imploring”) which is understood as conditional</note> God were imploring <transChange type="added">you</transChange> through us. We beg <transChange type="added">you</transChange> on behalf of Christ, be reconciled to God.

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:21
verses.text: He made the one who did not know sin <transChange type="added">to be</transChange> sin on our behalf, in order that we could become the righteousness of God in him.  <chapter eID="2Cor.5"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 6:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11700"/><title type="x-s">Afflictions of God’s Servants</title> <div sID="gen27336" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11700"/>Now <transChange type="added">because we</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“are fellow workers”) which is understood as causal</note> are fellow workers, we also urge you not to receive the grace of God in vain.

verses.name: II Corinthians 6:2
verses.text: For he says, <div eID="gen27336" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27337"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27338"/>“At the acceptable time I heard you,<l eID="gen27338" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27339"/>and in the day of salvation I helped you.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.49.8">Isa 49:8</reference></note><l eID="gen27339" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen27337"/> <div sID="gen27340" type="x-p"/> Behold, now <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the acceptable time; behold, now <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the day of salvation!

verses.name: II Corinthians 6:3
verses.text: <transChange type="added">We are</transChange> giving no one an occasion for taking offense in anything, in order that our ministry will not have fault found <transChange type="added">with it</transChange>,

verses.name: II Corinthians 6:4
verses.text: but commending ourselves as servants of God in every <transChange type="added">way</transChange>, in much endurance, in afflictions, in distresses, in difficulties,

verses.name: II Corinthians 6:5
verses.text: in beatings, in prisons, in disturbances, in troubles, in sleepless nights, in going hungry,

verses.name: II Corinthians 6:6
verses.text: in purity, in knowledge, in patience, in kindness, in the Holy Spirit, in love without hypocrisy,

verses.name: II Corinthians 6:7
verses.text: in the word of truth, in the power of God, with the weapons of righteousness for the right hand and left hand,

verses.name: II Corinthians 6:8
verses.text: through glory and dishonor, through slander and good repute, <transChange type="added">regarded</transChange> as deceivers and <transChange type="added">yet</transChange> truthful,

verses.name: II Corinthians 6:9
verses.text: as unknown and <transChange type="added">yet</transChange> known completely, as dying, and behold, we go on living, as disciplined, and <transChange type="added">yet</transChange> not put to death,

verses.name: II Corinthians 6:10
verses.text: as grieving, but always rejoicing, as poor, but making many rich, as having nothing, and possessing everything.  <div eID="gen27340" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 6:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11701"/><div sID="gen27341" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11701"/><milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞We have spoken freely and openly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the mouth of us has opened”</note> to you, Corinthians; our heart is open wide.

verses.name: II Corinthians 6:12
verses.text: You are not restricted by us, but you are restricted in your affections.

verses.name: II Corinthians 6:13
verses.text: Now the same <transChange type="added">way</transChange> <transChange type="added">in</transChange> exchange (I am speaking as to children), you open wide <transChange type="added">your hearts</transChange> also.  <div eID="gen27341" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 6:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11702"/><title type="x-s">Do Not Become Unevenly Yoked with Unbelievers</title> <div sID="gen27342" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11702"/>Do not become unevenly yoked with unbelievers, for what participation <transChange type="added">is there between</transChange> righteousness and lawlessness? Or what fellowship <transChange type="added">does</transChange> light <transChange type="added">have</transChange> with darkness?

verses.name: II Corinthians 6:15
verses.text: And what agreement <transChange type="added">does</transChange> Christ <transChange type="added">have</transChange> with Beliar? Or what share <transChange type="added">does</transChange> a believer <transChange type="added">have</transChange> with an unbeliever?

verses.name: II Corinthians 6:16
verses.text: And what agreement <transChange type="added">does the</transChange> temple of God <transChange type="added">have</transChange> with idols? For we are the temple of the living God, just as God said, <div eID="gen27342" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27343"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27344"/>“I will live in<note placement="foot">Or “with”</note> them and will walk about <transChange type="added">among them</transChange>,<l eID="gen27344" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27345"/>and I will be their God and they will be my people.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Lev.26.12">Lev 26:12 </reference>(also similar to <reference osisRef="Jer.32.38">Jer 32:38</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ezek.37.27">Ezek 37:27</reference>)</note> <l eID="gen27345" level="1"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 6:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11703"/><l level="1" sID="gen27346"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11703"/>Therefore “come out from their midst<l eID="gen27346" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27347"/>and be separate,” says the Lord,<l eID="gen27347" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27348"/>“and do not touch what is unclean,<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.52.11">Isa 52:11</reference></note><l eID="gen27348" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27349"/>and I will welcome you,<note placement="foot">A paraphrased quotation from <reference osisRef="Ezek.20.41">Ezek 20:41</reference></note> <l eID="gen27349" level="1"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 6:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11704"/><l level="1" sID="gen27350"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11704"/>and I will be a father to you,<l eID="gen27350" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27351"/>and you will be sons and daughters to me,”<note placement="foot">A paraphrased quotation from <reference osisRef="2Sam.7.14">2 Sam 7:14 </reference>and <reference osisRef="Isa.43.6">Isa 43:6</reference></note><l eID="gen27351" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27352"/>says the all-powerful Lord. <l eID="gen27352" level="1"/><lg eID="gen27343"/> <chapter eID="2Cor.6"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 7:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11705"/><title type="x-s">Paul’s Joy at the Corinthians’ Repentance</title> <div sID="gen27353" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11705"/>Therefore <transChange type="added">since we</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “since” is supplied as a component of the participle (“have”) which is understood as causal</note> have these promises, dear friends, let us cleanse ourselves from all defilement of body and spirit, accomplishing holiness in the fear of God.

verses.name: II Corinthians 7:2
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Make room for us in your hearts⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “make room for us”</note>. We have wronged no one, we have ruined no one, we have defrauded no one.

verses.name: II Corinthians 7:3
verses.text: I do not say <transChange type="added">this</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to condemn you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for condemnation”</note>, because I have already said that you are in our hearts, so that we die together and we live together.

verses.name: II Corinthians 7:4
verses.text: Great <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my confidence toward you; great <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my boasting on your behalf; I am filled with encouragement; I am overflowing with joy in all our affliction.  <div eID="gen27353" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 7:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11706"/><div sID="gen27354" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11706"/>For even <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“arrived”)</note> we arrived in Macedonia, our body had no rest, but we were afflicted in every <transChange type="added">way</transChange>—quarrels outside, fears within.

verses.name: II Corinthians 7:6
verses.text: But God, who comforts the humble, comforted us by the coming of Titus,

verses.name: II Corinthians 7:7
verses.text: and not only by his coming, but also by the comfort <transChange type="added">with</transChange> which he was comforted among you, <transChange type="added">because he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“reported”) which is understood as causal</note> reported to us your longing, your mourning, your zeal for me, so that I rejoiced even more.

verses.name: II Corinthians 7:8
verses.text: For if indeed I grieved you by my letter, I do not regret <transChange type="added">it</transChange>. Even if I did regret <transChange type="added">it</transChange> (I see<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “for I see”</note> that that letter grieved you, even though for <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞a short time⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “an hour”</note>),

verses.name: II Corinthians 7:9
verses.text: now I rejoice, not that you were grieved, but that you were grieved to repentance. For you were grieved according to <transChange type="added">the will of</transChange> God, so that you suffered loss in no way through us.

verses.name: II Corinthians 7:10
verses.text: For grief according to <transChange type="added">the will of</transChange> God brings about a repentance <transChange type="added">leading</transChange> to salvation, not to be regretted, but worldly grief brings about death.

verses.name: II Corinthians 7:11
verses.text: For behold how much diligence this very <transChange type="added">thing</transChange>, being grieved according to <transChange type="added">the will of</transChange> God, has brought about in you: what defense <transChange type="added">of yourselves</transChange>, what indignation, what fear, what longing, what zeal, what punishment! In everything you have demonstrated yourselves to be innocent in this matter.

verses.name: II Corinthians 7:12
verses.text: Consequently, even if I wrote to you, it was not because of the one who did wrong or because of the one who had been wronged, but in order that your diligence <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞on our behalf⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “on behalf of us”</note> might be revealed to you before God.

verses.name: II Corinthians 7:13
verses.text: Because of this we have been encouraged, and in addition to our encouragement, we rejoiced much more over the joy of Titus, because his spirit had been refreshed by all of you.

verses.name: II Corinthians 7:14
verses.text: For if I have boasted anything to him about you, I have not been put to shame, but as I have spoken everything to you in truth, thus also our boasting to Titus <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞has proven to be true⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “has become truth”</note>.

verses.name: II Corinthians 7:15
verses.text: And his affection for you is all the more <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“remembers”) which is understood as temporal</note> remembers the obedience of all of you as you welcomed him with fear and trembling.

verses.name: II Corinthians 7:16
verses.text: I rejoice, because in everything I am completely confident in you.  <chapter eID="2Cor.7"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11707"/><title type="x-s">Generosity in Giving</title> <div sID="gen27355" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11707"/>Now we make known to you, brothers, the grace of God that has been given among the churches of Macedonia,

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:2
verses.text: that with a great ordeal of affliction, the abundance of their joy and the extreme depth of their poverty have overflowed to the wealth of their generosity.

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:3
verses.text: I testify that <transChange type="added">they gave</transChange><note placement="foot">*The words “they gave” are not in the Greek text, but are implied</note> according to <transChange type="added">their</transChange> ability, and beyond <transChange type="added">their</transChange> ability, by their own choice,

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:4
verses.text: requesting of us with much exhortation the favor and the fellowship of the ministry to the saints,

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:5
verses.text: and not just as we had hoped, but they gave themselves first to the Lord and <transChange type="added">then</transChange> to us, by the will of God.

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:6
verses.text: So we urged Titus that, just as he had previously begun <transChange type="added">it</transChange>, thus he would also complete for you this <transChange type="added">act of</transChange> grace.

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:7
verses.text: But just as you excel in everything—in faith and in speaking and in knowledge and with all diligence and in the love from us <transChange type="added">that is</transChange> in you—so may you excel in this grace also.

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:8
verses.text: I am not saying <transChange type="added">this</transChange> as a command, but proving the genuineness of your love by means of the diligence of others.

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:9
verses.text: For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that <transChange type="added">although he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was”) which is understood as concessive</note> was rich, for your sake he became poor, in order that you, by his poverty, may become rich.

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:10
verses.text: And I am giving an opinion in this <transChange type="added">matter</transChange>, because this is profitable for you who not only began previously, a year ago, to do <transChange type="added">something</transChange>, but also to want <transChange type="added">to do it</transChange>.

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:11
verses.text: So now also complete the doing <transChange type="added">of it</transChange>, in order that just as <transChange type="added">you have</transChange> the eagerness to want <transChange type="added">to do it</transChange>, thus also <transChange type="added">you may</transChange> complete <transChange type="added">it</transChange> from <transChange type="added">what you</transChange> have.

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:12
verses.text: For if the eagerness is present <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞according to what one has⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the degree that if he might have”</note>, it is acceptable not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞according to what one does not have⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the degree that he might not have”</note>.

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:13
verses.text: For <transChange type="added">this is</transChange> not that for others <transChange type="added">there may be</transChange> relief, <transChange type="added">and</transChange> for you difficult circumstances, but <transChange type="added">as a matter</transChange> of equality.

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:14
verses.text: At the present time your abundance <transChange type="added">will be</transChange> for their need, in order that their abundance may also be for your need, so that there may be equality,

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:15
verses.text: just as it is written, “The <transChange type="added">one</transChange> who <transChange type="added">gathered</transChange> much did not have too much, and the <transChange type="added">one</transChange> who <transChange type="added">gathered</transChange> little did not have too little.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Exod.16.18">Exod 16:18</reference></note>  <div eID="gen27355" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11708"/><title type="x-s">Arrangements for Administering the Corinthians’ Gift</title> <div sID="gen27356" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11708"/>But thanks <transChange type="added">be</transChange> to God, who has put in the heart of Titus the same devotion <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞on your behalf⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “on behalf of you”</note>,

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:17
verses.text: because he not only welcomed our request, but being very earnest, by his own choice he went out<note placement="foot">*Or “he is going out” (if this verb is understood as an epistolary aorist)</note> to you.

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:18
verses.text: And we have sent at the same time with him the brother whose praise in the gospel <transChange type="added">has become known</transChange> throughout all the churches.

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:19
verses.text: And not only <transChange type="added">this</transChange>, but he was also chosen by the churches <transChange type="added">as</transChange> our traveling companion together with this gift that is being administered by us to the glory of the Lord himself and <transChange type="added">to show</transChange> our readiness <transChange type="added">to help</transChange>.

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:20
verses.text: <transChange type="added">We are</transChange> trying to avoid this, lest anyone should find fault with us in this abundant gift that is being administered by us.

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:21
verses.text: For we are taking into consideration what is honorable not only before the Lord, but also before people.

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:22
verses.text: And we are sending with them our brother whom we have tested many times in many <transChange type="added">things</transChange> that he is diligent, but now much more diligent <transChange type="added">because of his</transChange> great confidence in you.

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:23
verses.text: If <transChange type="added">there is a question</transChange> concerning Titus, <transChange type="added">he is</transChange> my partner and fellow worker for you. If <transChange type="added">there is a question concerning</transChange> our brothers, <transChange type="added">they are</transChange> messengers of the churches, the glory of Christ.

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:24
verses.text: Therefore show to them the proof of your love and our boasting about you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞openly before⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the face of”</note> the churches.  <chapter eID="2Cor.8"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 9:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11709"/><title type="x-s">God Loves a Cheerful Giver</title> <div sID="gen27357" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11709"/>For it is unnecessary for me to write to you concerning the ministry to the saints,

verses.name: II Corinthians 9:2
verses.text: because I know your readiness <transChange type="added">to help</transChange>, <transChange type="added">concerning</transChange> which I keep on boasting to the Macedonians about you, that Achaia has been ready <transChange type="added">to help</transChange> since last year, and your zeal has stirred up the majority <transChange type="added">of them</transChange>.

verses.name: II Corinthians 9:3
verses.text: But I am sending the brothers in order that our boasting about you would not prove to be empty in this case, so that you may be prepared just as I was saying,

verses.name: II Corinthians 9:4
verses.text: lest somehow if Macedonians should come with me and find you unprepared, we—<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞not to speak of you⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “so that we do not speak about you”; some manuscripts have “so that I do not speak about you”</note>—would be humiliated in connection with this project.

verses.name: II Corinthians 9:5
verses.text: Therefore I considered <transChange type="added">it</transChange> necessary to urge the brothers that they should go on ahead to you and make arrangements in advance for your generous gift that was promised previously, so this would be prepared as a generous gift and not as grudgingly granted.  <div eID="gen27357" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 9:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11710"/><div sID="gen27358" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11710"/>Now <transChange type="added">the point is</transChange> this: the one who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and the one who sows bountifully will also reap bountifully.

verses.name: II Corinthians 9:7
verses.text: Each one <transChange type="added">should give</transChange> as he has decided in his heart, not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞reluctantly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “out of sorrow”</note> or from compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver.

verses.name: II Corinthians 9:8
verses.text: And God is able to cause all grace to abound to you, so that in everything at all times, <transChange type="added">because you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“have”) which is understood as causal</note> have enough of everything, you may overflow in every good work.

verses.name: II Corinthians 9:9
verses.text: Just as it is written, <div eID="gen27358" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27359"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27360"/>“He scattered widely, he gave to the poor;<l eID="gen27360" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27361"/>his righteousness remains <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for the age”</note>.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.112.9">Ps 112:9</reference></note> <l eID="gen27361" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen27359"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 9:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11711"/><div sID="gen27362" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11711"/>Now the one who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food will provide and multiply your seed, and will cause the harvest of your righteousness to grow,

verses.name: II Corinthians 9:11
verses.text: being made rich in every <transChange type="added">way</transChange> for all generosity, which is producing through us thanksgiving to God,

verses.name: II Corinthians 9:12
verses.text: because the service of this ministry is not only supplying the needs of the saints, but also is overflowing through many <transChange type="added">expressions of</transChange> thanksgiving to God.

verses.name: II Corinthians 9:13
verses.text: Through the proven character of this service <transChange type="added">they will</transChange> glorify God because of the submission of your confession to the gospel of Christ and the generosity of <transChange type="added">your</transChange> participation toward them and toward everyone,

verses.name: II Corinthians 9:14
verses.text: and <transChange type="added">they are</transChange> longing for you in their prayers for you, because of the surpassing grace of God to you.

verses.name: II Corinthians 9:15
verses.text: Thanks <transChange type="added">be</transChange> to God for his indescribable gift!  <chapter eID="2Cor.9"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 10:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11712"/><title type="x-s">Paul’s Ministry Defended</title> <div sID="gen27363" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11712"/>Now I, Paul, appeal to you myself by the humility and gentleness of Christ, who <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞when I am present in person⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the face”</note> am humble among you, but when I<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“am absent”) which is understood as temporal</note> am absent am bold toward you—

verses.name: II Corinthians 10:2
verses.text: now I ask <transChange type="added">when I</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“am present”) which is understood as temporal</note> am present <transChange type="added">that I will</transChange> not <transChange type="added">need</transChange> to be bold with the confidence <transChange type="added">with</transChange> which I propose to show boldness toward some who consider us as behaving according to the flesh.
