verses.text: However, the solid foundation of God stands firm, having this seal: “The Lord knows those who are his,”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Num.16.5">Num 16:5</reference></note> and “Everyone who names the name of the Lord must abstain from unrighteousness.”  <div eID="gen27568" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Timothy 2:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11872"/><div sID="gen27569" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11872"/>Now in a great house <transChange type="added">there</transChange> are not only gold and silver vessels, but also wooden and earthenware <transChange type="added">ones</transChange>, some of which <transChange type="added">are</transChange> for honorable use, and some of which <transChange type="added">are</transChange> for ordinary use.

verses.name: II Timothy 2:21
verses.text: Therefore, if someone cleanses himself from these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, he will be a vessel for honorable use, set apart, useful to the Master, prepared for every good work.  <div eID="gen27569" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Timothy 2:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11873"/><div sID="gen27570" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11873"/>But flee from youthful desires, and pursue righteousness, faith, love, <transChange type="added">and</transChange> peace, in company with those who call upon the Lord from a pure heart.

verses.name: II Timothy 2:23
verses.text: But avoid foolish and uninformed controversies, <transChange type="added">because you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“know”) which is understood as causal</note> know that they produce quarrels.

verses.name: II Timothy 2:24
verses.text: And the slave of the Lord must not quarrel, but be kind toward everyone, skillful in teaching, tolerant,

verses.name: II Timothy 2:25
verses.text: correcting those who are opposed with gentleness, <transChange type="added">seeing</transChange> whether perhaps God may grant them repentance to a knowledge of the truth,

verses.name: II Timothy 2:26
verses.text: and they will come to their senses again <transChange type="added">and escape</transChange> from the trap of the devil, being held captive by him to <transChange type="added">do</transChange> his will.  <chapter eID="2Tim.2"/>

verses.name: II Timothy 3:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11874"/><title type="x-s">Difficult Times Ahead in the Last Days</title> <div sID="gen27571" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11874"/>But know this, that in the last days difficult times will come,

verses.name: II Timothy 3:2
verses.text: for people will be lovers of themselves, lovers of money, boasters, arrogant, slanderers, disobedient to parents, ungrateful, unholy,

verses.name: II Timothy 3:3
verses.text: hardhearted, irreconcilable, slanderous, without self-control, savage, with no interest for what is good,

verses.name: II Timothy 3:4
verses.text: traitors, reckless, conceited, loving pleasure rather than loving God,

verses.name: II Timothy 3:5
verses.text: maintaining a form of godliness, but denying its power. Avoid these <transChange type="added">people</transChange>.

verses.name: II Timothy 3:6
verses.text: For from these are those who slip into houses and captivate foolish women loaded down with sins, led by various kinds of desires,

verses.name: II Timothy 3:7
verses.text: always learning and never able to come to a knowledge of the truth.

verses.name: II Timothy 3:8
verses.text: And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞just as⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in the manner in which”</note> Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, so also these oppose the truth, people corrupted in mind, disqualified concerning the faith.

verses.name: II Timothy 3:9
verses.text: But they will not progress to a greater extent, for their folly will be quite evident to everyone, as also the <transChange type="added">folly</transChange> of those <transChange type="added">two</transChange> was.  <div eID="gen27571" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Timothy 3:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11875"/><title type="x-s">The Value of the Scriptures</title> <div sID="gen27572" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11875"/>But you have faithfully followed my teaching, way of life, purpose, faith, patience, love, endurance,

verses.name: II Timothy 3:11
verses.text: persecutions, <transChange type="added">and</transChange> sufferings that happened to me in Antioch, in Iconium, <transChange type="added">and</transChange> in Lystra, what sort of persecutions I endured, and the Lord delivered me from all <transChange type="added">of them</transChange>.

verses.name: II Timothy 3:12
verses.text: And indeed, all those who want to live in a godly manner in Christ Jesus will be persecuted.

verses.name: II Timothy 3:13
verses.text: But evil people and imposters will progress to the worse, deceiving and being deceived.

verses.name: II Timothy 3:14
verses.text: But you continue in <transChange type="added">the things</transChange> which you have learned and are convinced <transChange type="added">of</transChange>, <transChange type="added">because you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“know”) which is understood as causal</note> know from whom you learned <transChange type="added">them</transChange>,

verses.name: II Timothy 3:15
verses.text: and that from childhood you have known the holy writings that are able <transChange type="added">to make</transChange> you wise for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus.

verses.name: II Timothy 3:16
verses.text: All scripture <transChange type="added">is</transChange> inspired by God and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, for training in righteousness,

verses.name: II Timothy 3:17
verses.text: in order that the person of God may be competent, equipped for every good work.  <chapter eID="2Tim.3"/>

verses.name: II Timothy 4:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11876"/><title type="x-s">Paul’s Charge to Timothy</title> <div sID="gen27573" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11876"/>I solemnly charge <transChange type="added">you</transChange> before God and Christ Jesus, who is going to judge the living and the dead, and by his appearing and his kingdom,

verses.name: II Timothy 4:2
verses.text: preach the word, be ready in season <transChange type="added">and</transChange> out of season, reprove, rebuke, exhort, with all patience and instruction.

verses.name: II Timothy 4:3
verses.text: For there will be a time when they will not put up with sound teaching, but in accordance with their own desires, they will accumulate for themselves teachers, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞because they have an insatiable curiosity⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “feeling an itching in the ear”; “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“feeling an itching”) which is understood as causal</note>,

verses.name: II Timothy 4:4
verses.text: and they will turn away from the hearing of the truth, but will turn to myths.

verses.name: II Timothy 4:5
verses.text: But you, be self-controlled in all <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, bear hardship patiently, do the work of an evangelist, fulfill your ministry.  <div eID="gen27573" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Timothy 4:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11877"/><div sID="gen27574" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11877"/>For I am already being poured out as a drink offering, and the time of my departure is imminent.

verses.name: II Timothy 4:7
verses.text: I have fought the good fight, I have completed the race, I have kept the faith.

verses.name: II Timothy 4:8
verses.text: Finally, the crown of righteousness is reserved for me, that the Lord, the righteous Judge, will award to me on that day, and not only to me, but also to all who have loved his appearing.  <div eID="gen27574" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Timothy 4:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11878"/><title type="x-s">Final Instructions to Timothy</title> <div sID="gen27575" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11878"/>Make haste to come to me quickly.

verses.name: II Timothy 4:10
verses.text: For Demas deserted me, <transChange type="added">because he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“loved”) which is understood as causal</note> loved the present age, and went to Thessalonica. Crescens <transChange type="added">went</transChange> to Galatia; Titus <transChange type="added">went</transChange> to Dalmatia.

verses.name: II Timothy 4:11
verses.text: Luke alone is with me. Take along Mark <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied because the previous participle (“take along”) has been translated as a finite verb</note> bring <transChange type="added">him</transChange> with you, because he is useful to me for ministry.

verses.name: II Timothy 4:12
verses.text: But I have sent Tychicus to Ephesus.

verses.name: II Timothy 4:13
verses.text: <transChange type="added">When you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“come”) which is understood as temporal</note> come, bring the cloak that I left behind in Troas with Carpus, and the scrolls, especially the parchments.

verses.name: II Timothy 4:14
verses.text: Alexander the metalworker did me much harm; may the Lord pay back to him according to his deeds,

verses.name: II Timothy 4:15
verses.text: against whom you also be on guard, because he vehemently opposed our words.

verses.name: II Timothy 4:16
verses.text: At my first defense, no one came to my <transChange type="added">aid</transChange>, but <transChange type="added">they</transChange> all deserted me; may it not be counted against them.

verses.name: II Timothy 4:17
verses.text: But the Lord helped me and strengthened me, so that through me the proclamation might be fulfilled and all the Gentiles might hear, and he rescued <transChange type="added">me</transChange> from the lion’s mouth.

verses.name: II Timothy 4:18
verses.text: The Lord will rescue me from every evil deed, and will save <transChange type="added">me</transChange> for his heavenly kingdom, to whom <transChange type="added">be</transChange> the glory <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever and ever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the ages of the ages”</note>. Amen.  <div eID="gen27575" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Timothy 4:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11879"/><title type="x-s">Final Greetings and Benediction</title> <div sID="gen27576" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11879"/>Greet Prisca and Aquila and the household of Onesiphorus.

verses.name: II Timothy 4:20
verses.text: Erastus remained in Corinth, but Trophimus I left behind in Miletus <transChange type="added">because he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was sick”) which is understood as causal</note> was sick.

verses.name: II Timothy 4:21
verses.text: Make haste to come before winter. Eubulus and Pudens and Linus and Claudia and all the brothers greet you.

verses.name: II Timothy 4:22
verses.text: The Lord <transChange type="added">be</transChange> with your spirit. Grace <transChange type="added">be</transChange> with you.  <chapter eID="2Tim.4"/> <div eID="gen27576" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen27556" osisID="2Tim" type="book"/>

verses.name: Titus 1:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11880"/><title type="x-s">Greeting</title> <div sID="gen27578" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11880"/>Paul, a slave of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ for the faith of the chosen of God and the knowledge of the truth that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> according to godliness,

verses.name: Titus 1:2
verses.text: in the hope of eternal life which God, who does not lie, promised before eternal ages,

verses.name: Titus 1:3
verses.text: but at the proper time has disclosed his message in the proclamation <transChange type="added">with</transChange> which I was entrusted according to the command of God our Savior,

verses.name: Titus 1:4
verses.text: to Titus, <transChange type="added">my</transChange> true child according to a common faith. Grace and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Savior.  <div eID="gen27578" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Titus 1:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11881"/><title type="x-s">Instructions to Titus in Crete</title> <div sID="gen27579" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11881"/>On account of this, I left you behind in Crete, in order that what remains may be set in order and you may appoint elders in every town, as I ordered you.

verses.name: Titus 1:6
verses.text: If anyone is blameless, <transChange type="added">the</transChange> husband of one wife, having faithful<note placement="foot">Or “believing”</note> children, not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞accused of dissipation⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “with an accusation of dissipation”</note> or rebellious.

verses.name: Titus 1:7
verses.text: For it is necessary <transChange type="added">for</transChange> the overseer to be blameless as God’s steward, not self-willed, not quick-tempered, not addicted to wine, not violent, not greedy for dishonest gain,

verses.name: Titus 1:8
verses.text: but hospitable, loving what is good, prudent, just, devout, self-controlled,

verses.name: Titus 1:9
verses.text: holding fast to the faithful message according to the teaching, in order that he may be able both to exhort with sound instruction and to reprove those who speak against <transChange type="added">it</transChange>.  <div eID="gen27579" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Titus 1:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11882"/><div sID="gen27580" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11882"/>For there are many rebellious <transChange type="added">people</transChange>, idle talkers and deceivers, especially those of the circumcision,

verses.name: Titus 1:11
verses.text: whom it is necessary to silence, whoever are ruining whole families <transChange type="added">by</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“teaching”) which is understood as means</note> teaching <transChange type="added">things</transChange> which must not be <transChange type="added">taught</transChange> for the sake of dishonest gain.

verses.name: Titus 1:12
verses.text: A certain one of them, <transChange type="added">one of</transChange> their own prophets, has said, “Cretans <transChange type="added">are</transChange> always liars, evil beasts, lazy gluttons.”

verses.name: Titus 1:13
verses.text: This testimony is true, for which reason reprove them severely, in order that they may be sound in the faith,

verses.name: Titus 1:14
verses.text: not paying attention to Jewish myths and commandments of people who turn away from the truth.

verses.name: Titus 1:15
verses.text: To the pure all <transChange type="added">things</transChange> <transChange type="added">are</transChange> pure, but to those who are defiled and unbelieving nothing <transChange type="added">is</transChange> pure, but both their mind and conscience are defiled.

verses.name: Titus 1:16
verses.text: They profess to know God, but by their deeds they deny <transChange type="added">him</transChange>, <transChange type="added">because they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“are”) which is understood as causal</note> are detestable and disobedient, and unfit for every good deed.  <chapter eID="Titus.1"/>

verses.name: Titus 2:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11883"/><title type="x-s">Sound Instruction and Consistent Behavior</title> <div sID="gen27581" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11883"/>But you, speak <transChange type="added">the things</transChange> which are fitting for sound instruction.

verses.name: Titus 2:2
verses.text: Older men are to be temperate, worthy of respect, self-controlled, sound in faith, in love, <transChange type="added">and</transChange> in endurance.

verses.name: Titus 2:3
verses.text: Older women likewise <transChange type="added">are to be</transChange> reverent in <transChange type="added">their</transChange> behavior, not slanderous, not enslaved to much wine, teaching what is good,

verses.name: Titus 2:4
verses.text: in order that they may encourage the young women to love their husbands <transChange type="added">and to</transChange> love their children,

verses.name: Titus 2:5
verses.text: <transChange type="added">to be</transChange> self-controlled, pure, busy at home, good, being subject to their own husbands, in order that the word of God may not be slandered.

verses.name: Titus 2:6
verses.text: Likewise, exhort the young men to be self-controlled,

verses.name: Titus 2:7
verses.text: concerning everything showing yourself <transChange type="added">to be</transChange> an example of good deeds, in your teaching <transChange type="added">demonstrating</transChange> soundness, dignity,

verses.name: Titus 2:8
verses.text: <transChange type="added">a</transChange> sound message beyond reproach, in order that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞an opponent⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “one from the opposed”</note> may be put to shame, because he<note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“has”) which is understood as causal</note> has nothing bad to say concerning us.  <div eID="gen27581" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Titus 2:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11884"/><div sID="gen27582" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11884"/>Slaves must be subject to their own masters in everything, to be well-pleasing, not to talk back,

verses.name: Titus 2:10
verses.text: not stealing, but demonstrating all good faith, in order that they may do credit to the teaching of God our Savior in everything.

verses.name: Titus 2:11
verses.text: For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all people,

verses.name: Titus 2:12
verses.text: training us in order that, denying impiety and worldly desires, we may live self-controlled and righteously and godly in the present age,

verses.name: Titus 2:13
verses.text: looking forward to the blessed hope and the glorious appearing of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ,

verses.name: Titus 2:14
verses.text: who gave himself for us, in order that he might redeem us from all lawlessness and purify for himself a people for his own possession, zealous for good deeds.

verses.name: Titus 2:15
verses.text: Speak these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> and exhort and reprove with all authority. Let no one disregard you.  <chapter eID="Titus.2"/>

verses.name: Titus 3:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11885"/><title type="x-s">Conduct Toward All People</title> <div sID="gen27583" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11885"/>Remind them to be subject to the rulers <transChange type="added">and</transChange> to the authorities, to obey, to be prepared for every good work,

verses.name: Titus 3:2
verses.text: to speak evil of no one, to be peaceable, gentle, showing all courtesy to all people.

verses.name: Titus 3:3
verses.text: For we also were once foolish, disobedient, led astray, enslaved to various desires and pleasures, spending our lives in wickedness and envy, despicable, hating one another.

verses.name: Titus 3:4
verses.text: But when the kindness and love for mankind of God our Savior appeared,

verses.name: Titus 3:5
verses.text: he saved us, not by deeds of righteousness that we have done, but because of his mercy, through the washing of regeneration and renewal by the Holy Spirit,

verses.name: Titus 3:6
verses.text: whom he poured out on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Savior,

verses.name: Titus 3:7
verses.text: so that, having been justified by his grace, we may become heirs according to the hope of eternal life.  <div eID="gen27583" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Titus 3:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11886"/><title type="x-s">Final Instructions to Titus</title> <div sID="gen27584" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11886"/>The saying <transChange type="added">is</transChange> trustworthy, and I want you to insist concerning these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, so that those who have believed in God may be careful to engage in good deeds. These things are good and beneficial for people.

verses.name: Titus 3:9
verses.text: But avoid foolish controversies and genealogies and contentions and quarrels about the law, for they are useless and fruitless.

verses.name: Titus 3:10
verses.text: Reject a divisive person after a first and second admonition,

verses.name: Titus 3:11
verses.text: knowing that such a person is perverted and is sinning, being self-condemned.  <div eID="gen27584" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Titus 3:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11887"/><div sID="gen27585" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11887"/>When I send Artemas or Tychicus to you, make haste to come to me in Nicopolis, for I have decided to spend the winter there.

verses.name: Titus 3:13
verses.text: Diligently send on their way Zenas the lawyer and Apollos, so that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they may lack nothing⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “nothing may lack to them”</note>.

verses.name: Titus 3:14
verses.text: But also our <transChange type="added">people</transChange> must learn to engage in good deeds for necessary needs, so that they will not be unfruitful.

verses.name: Titus 3:15
verses.text: All those with me greet you. Greet those who love us in the faith. Grace <transChange type="added">be</transChange> with all of you.  <chapter eID="Titus.3"/> <div eID="gen27585" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen27577" osisID="Titus" type="book"/>

verses.name: Philemon 1:1
verses.text: Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus, and Timothy our brother, to Philemon, our dear friend and fellow worker,

verses.name: Philemon 1:2
verses.text: and to Apphia our sister, and to Archippus our fellow soldier, and to the church in your house.

verses.name: Philemon 1:3
verses.text: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.  <div eID="gen27587" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Philemon 1:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11888"/><title type="x-s">Thanksgiving and Prayer for Philemon</title> <div sID="gen27588" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11888"/>I thank my God, always making mention of you in my prayers,

verses.name: Philemon 1:5
verses.text: <transChange type="added">because I</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“hear about”) which is understood as causal</note> hear about your love and faith which you have toward the Lord Jesus and for all the saints.

verses.name: Philemon 1:6
verses.text: <transChange type="added">I pray</transChange> that the fellowship of your faith may become effective in the knowledge <transChange type="added">of</transChange> every good <transChange type="added">thing</transChange> that <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in us for Christ.

verses.name: Philemon 1:7
verses.text: For I have great joy and encouragement from your love, because the hearts of the saints have been refreshed through you, brother.  <div eID="gen27588" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Philemon 1:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11889"/><title type="x-s">Paul’s Appeal for Onesimus</title> <div sID="gen27589" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11889"/>Therefore, <transChange type="added">although I</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“have”) which is understood as concessive</note> have great confidence in Christ to order you <transChange type="added">to do what</transChange> is proper,

verses.name: Philemon 1:9
verses.text: instead I appeal to <transChange type="added">you</transChange> because of love, <transChange type="added">since I</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “since” is supplied as a component of the participle (“am”) which is understood as causal</note> am such a one as Paul, now an old man and also a prisoner of Christ Jesus.

verses.name: Philemon 1:10
verses.text: I am appealing to you concerning my child whom I became the father of during my imprisonment, Onesimus.

verses.name: Philemon 1:11
verses.text: Once he <transChange type="added">was</transChange> useless to you, but now <transChange type="added">he is</transChange> useful to you<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “both to you”</note> and to me,

verses.name: Philemon 1:12
verses.text: whom I have sent back to you himself, that is, my heart,

verses.name: Philemon 1:13
verses.text: whom I wanted to keep with me, in order that he might serve me on behalf of you during my imprisonment for the gospel.

verses.name: Philemon 1:14
verses.text: But apart from your consent, I wanted to do nothing, in order that your good <transChange type="added">deed</transChange> might be not as according to necessity, but according to <transChange type="added">your own</transChange> free will.

verses.name: Philemon 1:15
verses.text: For perhaps because of this, he was separated <transChange type="added">from you</transChange> for a time, in order that you might have him back forever,

verses.name: Philemon 1:16
verses.text: no longer as a slave, but more than a slave, a beloved brother, especially to me, but how much more to you, both in the flesh and in the Lord.  <div eID="gen27589" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Philemon 1:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11890"/><title type="x-s">Paul’s Request to Philemon</title> <div sID="gen27590" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11890"/>If therefore you consider me a partner, receive him as <transChange type="added">you would</transChange> me.

verses.name: Philemon 1:18
verses.text: But if in anything he has caused you loss or owes <transChange type="added">you anything</transChange>, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞charge this to my account⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “this to me charge to my account”</note>.

verses.name: Philemon 1:19
verses.text: I, Paul, write <transChange type="added">this</transChange> with my <transChange type="added">own</transChange> hand: I will pay it back, lest I mention to you that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you owe me even your very self besides⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “even yourself to me you owe besides”</note>.

verses.name: Philemon 1:20
verses.text: Yes, brother, I ought to have some benefit of you in the Lord; refresh my heart in Christ.  <div eID="gen27590" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Philemon 1:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11891"/><div sID="gen27591" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11891"/>Confident of your obedience, I am writing to you <transChange type="added">because I</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“know”) which is understood as causal</note> know that you will do even beyond what I say.

verses.name: Philemon 1:22
verses.text: At the same time also, prepare a guest room for me, for I hope that through your prayers I will be restored to you.  <div eID="gen27591" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Philemon 1:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11892"/><title type="x-s">Final Greetings and Benediction</title> <div sID="gen27592" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11892"/>Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus, greets you,

verses.name: Philemon 1:24
verses.text: <transChange type="added">and so do</transChange> Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, <transChange type="added">and</transChange> Luke, my fellow workers.

verses.name: Philemon 1:25
verses.text: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ <transChange type="added">be</transChange> with your spirit.  <chapter eID="Phlm.1"/> <div eID="gen27592" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen27586" osisID="Phlm" type="book"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 1:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11893"/><title type="x-s">God’s Full and Final Revelation in the Son</title> <div sID="gen27594" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11893"/><transChange type="added">Although</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“spoke”) which is understood as concessive</note> God spoke long ago in many parts<note placement="foot">Or “portions”</note> and in many ways to the fathers by the prophets,

verses.name: Hebrews 1:2
verses.text: in these last days he has spoken to us by a Son, whom he appointed heir of all <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, through whom also he made the world,<note placement="foot">Or “the universe”; literally “the ages”</note>

verses.name: Hebrews 1:3
verses.text: who is the radiance of his glory and the representation of his essence, sustaining all <transChange type="added">things</transChange> by the word of power.<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “by the word of his power. When he had made purification for sins, he sat down”</note> When he<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“had made”) which is understood as temporal</note> had made purification for sins through him, he sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high,

verses.name: Hebrews 1:4
verses.text: having become by so much better than the angels, by as much as he has inherited a more excellent name than theirs.  <div eID="gen27594" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 1:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11894"/><title type="x-s">The Son Superior to the Angels</title> <div sID="gen27595" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11894"/>For to which of the angels did he ever say, <div eID="gen27595" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27596"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27597"/>“You are my son,<l eID="gen27597" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27598"/>today I have begotten you,”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.2.7">Ps 2:7</reference></note><l eID="gen27598" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen27596"/> <div sID="gen27599" type="x-p"/> and again, <div eID="gen27599" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27600"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27601"/>“I will be <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his father⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to him for a father”</note>,<l eID="gen27601" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27602"/>and he will be <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞my son⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to me for a son”</note>”?<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="2Sam.7.14">2 Sam 7:14 </reference>(cf. <reference osisRef="1Chr.17.13">1 Chr 17:13</reference>)</note> <l eID="gen27602" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen27600"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 1:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11895"/><div sID="gen27603" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11895"/>And again, when he brings the firstborn into the world, he says, <div eID="gen27603" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27604"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27605"/>“And let all <transChange type="added">the</transChange> angels of God worship him.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Deut.32.43">Deut 32:43 </reference>and <reference osisRef="Ps.97.7">Ps 97:7</reference></note> <l eID="gen27605" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen27604"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 1:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11896"/><div sID="gen27606" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11896"/>And concerning the angels he says, <div eID="gen27606" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27607"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27608"/>“The one who makes his angels winds,<l eID="gen27608" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27609"/>and his servants a flame of fire,”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.104.4">Ps 104:4</reference></note> <l eID="gen27609" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen27607"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 1:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11897"/><div sID="gen27610" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11897"/>but concerning the Son, <div eID="gen27610" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27611"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27612"/>“Your throne, O God, <transChange type="added">is</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever and ever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for the age of the age”</note>,<l eID="gen27612" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27613"/>and the scepter of righteous <transChange type="added">is the</transChange> scepter of your kingdom. <l eID="gen27613" level="1"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 1:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11898"/><l level="2" sID="gen27614"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11898"/>You have loved righteousness and hated lawlessness;<l eID="gen27614" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27615"/>because of this God, your God, has anointed you<l eID="gen27615" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27616"/>with the olive oil of joy more than your companions.<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.45.6-Ps.45.7">Ps 45:6–7</reference></note> <l eID="gen27616" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen27611"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 1:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11899"/><div sID="gen27617" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11899"/>And, <div eID="gen27617" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27618"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27619"/>“You, Lord, laid the foundation of the earth in the beginning,<l eID="gen27619" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27620"/>and the heavens are the works of your hands; <l eID="gen27620" level="1"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 1:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11900"/><l level="1" sID="gen27621"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11900"/>they will perish, but you continue,<l eID="gen27621" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27622"/>and they will all become old like a garment, <l eID="gen27622" level="2"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 1:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11901"/><l level="1" sID="gen27623"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11901"/>and like a robe you will roll them up,<l eID="gen27623" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27624"/>and like a garment they will be changed;<l eID="gen27624" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27625"/>but you are the same, and your years will not run out.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.102.25-Ps.102.27">Ps 102:25–27</reference></note> <l eID="gen27625" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen27618"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 1:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11902"/><div sID="gen27626" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11902"/>But to which of the angels has he ever said, <div eID="gen27626" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27627"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27628"/>“Sit down at my right hand,<l eID="gen27628" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27629"/>until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.110.1">Ps 110:1</reference></note> <l eID="gen27629" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen27627"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 1:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11903"/><div sID="gen27630" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11903"/>Are they not all spirits engaged in special service, sent on assignment for the sake of those who are going to inherit salvation?  <chapter eID="Heb.1"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 2:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11904"/><title type="x-s">Warning Not to Neglect Salvation</title> <div sID="gen27631" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11904"/>Because of this, <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> all the more necessary <transChange type="added">that</transChange> we pay attention to the <transChange type="added">things</transChange> we have heard, lest we drift away.

verses.name: Hebrews 2:2
verses.text: For if the word spoken through angels was binding and every transgression and act of disobedience received a just penalty,

verses.name: Hebrews 2:3
verses.text: how will we escape <transChange type="added">if we</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “if” is supplied as a component of the participle (“neglect”) which is understood as conditional</note> neglect so great a salvation which had its beginning when it<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal infinitive (“was spoken”)</note> was spoken through the Lord <transChange type="added">and</transChange> was confirmed to us by those who heard,

verses.name: Hebrews 2:4
verses.text: <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was testifying at the same time”)</note> God was testifying at the same time by signs and wonders and various miracles and distributions of the Holy Spirit according to his will.  <div eID="gen27631" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 2:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11905"/><title type="x-s">The Son’s Humiliation and Suffering</title> <div sID="gen27632" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11905"/>For he did not subject to angels the world to come, about which we are speaking.

verses.name: Hebrews 2:6
verses.text: But someone testified somewhere, saying, <div eID="gen27632" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27633"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27634"/>“What is man, that you remember him,<l eID="gen27634" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27635"/>or the son of man, that you care for him? <l eID="gen27635" level="2"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 2:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11906"/><l level="1" sID="gen27636"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11906"/>You made him for a short <transChange type="added">time</transChange> lower than the angels;<l eID="gen27636" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27637"/>you crowned him with glory and honor;<note placement="foot">Several important manuscripts add “and placed him over the works of your hands” to the end of v. <reference osisRef="Heb.2.7">7</reference></note> <l eID="gen27637" level="2"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 2:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11907"/><l level="2" sID="gen27638"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11907"/>you subjected all <transChange type="added">things</transChange> under his feet.<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.8.4-Ps.8.6">Ps 8:4–6</reference></note><l eID="gen27638" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen27633"/> <div sID="gen27639" type="x-p"/> For in subjecting all <transChange type="added">things</transChange>,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “subjecting all things to him”</note> he left nothing <transChange type="added">that was</transChange> not subject to him. But now we do not yet see all <transChange type="added">things</transChange> subjected to him,

verses.name: Hebrews 2:9
verses.text: but we see Jesus, for a short <transChange type="added">time</transChange> made lower than the angels, because of the suffering of death crowned with glory and honor, so that apart from God<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “so that by the grace of God”</note> he might taste death on behalf of everyone.

verses.name: Hebrews 2:10
verses.text: For it was fitting for him for whom <transChange type="added">are</transChange> all <transChange type="added">things</transChange> and through whom <transChange type="added">are</transChange> all <transChange type="added">things</transChange> in bringing many sons to glory to perfect the originator of their salvation through sufferings.

verses.name: Hebrews 2:11
verses.text: For both the one who sanctifies and the ones who are sanctified <transChange type="added">are</transChange> all from one, for which reason he is not ashamed to call them brothers,

verses.name: Hebrews 2:12
verses.text: saying, <div eID="gen27639" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27640"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27641"/>“I will proclaim your name to my brothers;<l eID="gen27641" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27642"/>in the midst of the assembly I will sing in praise of you.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.22.22">Ps 22:22</reference></note> <l eID="gen27642" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen27640"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 2:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11908"/><div sID="gen27643" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11908"/>And again, <div eID="gen27643" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27644"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27645"/>“I will trust in him.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.8.17">Isa 8:17</reference></note><l eID="gen27645" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen27644"/> <div sID="gen27646" type="x-p"/> And again, <div eID="gen27646" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27647"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27648"/>“Behold, I and the children God has given me.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.8.18">Isa 8:18</reference></note> <l eID="gen27648" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen27647"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 2:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11909"/><div sID="gen27649" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11909"/>Therefore, since the children share in blood and flesh, he also in like manner shared in these <transChange type="added">same things</transChange>, in order that through death he could destroy the one who has the power of death, that is, the devil,

verses.name: Hebrews 2:15
verses.text: and could set free these who through fear of death were subject to slavery throughout all their lives.

verses.name: Hebrews 2:16
verses.text: For surely he is not concerned with angels, but he is concerned with the descendants of Abraham.

verses.name: Hebrews 2:17
verses.text: Therefore he was obligated to be made like his brothers in all <transChange type="added">respects</transChange>, in order that he could become a merciful and faithful high priest in the things relating to God, in order to make atonement for the sins of the people.

verses.name: Hebrews 2:18
verses.text: For in that which he himself suffered <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was tempted”) which is understood as temporal</note> was tempted, he is able to help those who are tempted.  <chapter eID="Heb.2"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 3:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11910"/><title type="x-s">The Superiority of Jesus to Moses</title> <div sID="gen27650" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11910"/>Therefore, holy brothers, sharers in a heavenly calling, consider Jesus, the apostle and high priest of our confession,

verses.name: Hebrews 3:2
verses.text: who was faithful to the one who appointed him, as Moses also <transChange type="added">was</transChange> in his household.<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “in all his household”</note>

verses.name: Hebrews 3:3
verses.text: For this one is considered worthy of greater glory than Moses, inasmuch as the one who builds it has greater honor than the house.

verses.name: Hebrews 3:4
verses.text: For every house is built by someone, but the one who built all <transChange type="added">things</transChange> <transChange type="added">is</transChange> God.

verses.name: Hebrews 3:5
verses.text: And Moses <transChange type="added">was</transChange> faithful in all his house as a servant, for a testimony to the things that would be spoken,

verses.name: Hebrews 3:6
verses.text: but Christ <transChange type="added">was faithful</transChange><note placement="foot">*The words “was faithful” are not in the Greek text, but are an understood repetition from the previous verse and v. <reference osisRef="Heb.3.2">2</reference></note> as a son over his house, whose house we are, if<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “if indeed”</note> we hold fast to our confidence and the hope we can be proud of.  <div eID="gen27650" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 3:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11911"/><title type="x-s">A Serious Warning Against Unbelief</title> <div sID="gen27651" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11911"/>Therefore, just as the Holy Spirit says, <div eID="gen27651" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27652"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27653"/>“Today, if you hear his voice, <l eID="gen27653" level="1"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 3:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11912"/><l level="1" sID="gen27654"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11912"/>do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion,<l eID="gen27654" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27655"/>in the day of testing in the wilderness, <l eID="gen27655" level="2"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 3:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11913"/><l level="1" sID="gen27656"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11913"/>where your fathers tested <transChange type="added">me</transChange> by trial<l eID="gen27656" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27657"/>and saw my works

verses.name: Hebrews 3:10
verses.text: <transChange type="added">for</transChange> forty years.<l eID="gen27657" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27658"/>Therefore I was angry with this generation,<l eID="gen27658" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27659"/>and I said, ‘They always go astray in their heart,<l eID="gen27659" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27660"/>and they do not know my ways.’ <l eID="gen27660" level="1"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 3:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11914"/><l level="2" sID="gen27661"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11914"/>As I swore in my anger,<l eID="gen27661" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27662"/>‘<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞They will never enter⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “if they will enter”</note> into my rest.’ ”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.95.7b-Ps.95.11">Ps 95:7b-11</reference></note> <l eID="gen27662" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen27652"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 3:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11915"/><div sID="gen27663" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11915"/>Watch out, brothers, lest there be in some of you an evil, unbelieving heart, <transChange type="added">with the result that you</transChange> fall away<note placement="foot">*Here “with the result that” is supplied as a component of the infinitive (“fall away”) which is understood as result</note> from the living God.

verses.name: Hebrews 3:13
verses.text: But encourage one another <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞day by day⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by each day”</note>, as long as it is called “today,” so that <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞none of you become hardened⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “not anyone of you be hardened”</note> by the deception of sin.

verses.name: Hebrews 3:14
verses.text: For we have become partners of Christ, if indeed we hold fast the beginning of <transChange type="added">our</transChange> commitment steadfast until the end,

verses.name: Hebrews 3:15
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞while it is said⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in the saying”</note>, <div eID="gen27663" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27664"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27665"/>“Today, if you hear his voice,<l eID="gen27665" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27666"/>do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.95.7b-Ps.95.8">Ps 95:7b-8</reference></note> <l eID="gen27666" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen27664"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 3:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11916"/><div sID="gen27667" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11916"/>For who, <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“heard”) which is understood as temporal</note> heard <transChange type="added">it</transChange>, were disobedient? Surely <transChange type="added">it was</transChange> not all who went out from Egypt through Moses?

verses.name: Hebrews 3:17
verses.text: And with whom was he angry <transChange type="added">for</transChange> forty years? <transChange type="added">Was it</transChange> not with those who sinned, whose dead bodies fell in the wilderness?

verses.name: Hebrews 3:18
verses.text: And to whom did he swear <transChange type="added">they would</transChange> not enter into his rest, except those who were disobedient?

verses.name: Hebrews 3:19
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">so</transChange> we see that they were not able to enter because of unbelief.  <chapter eID="Heb.3"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 4:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11917"/><title type="x-s">The Rest that Remains for the People of God</title> <div sID="gen27668" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11917"/>Therefore let us fear, <transChange type="added">while there</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the participle (“remains”) which is understood as temporal</note> remains a promise of entering into his rest, that none of you appear to fall short of <transChange type="added">it</transChange>.

verses.name: Hebrews 4:2
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞For we also have had the good news proclaimed to us⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for we are also having had the good news proclaimed”</note>, just as those also did, but the message <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they heard⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “of hearing”</note> did not benefit them, because they<note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“united”) which is understood as causal</note> were not united with those who heard <transChange type="added">it</transChange> in faith.

verses.name: Hebrews 4:3
verses.text: For we who have believed enter into rest,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “that rest”</note> just as he has said, <div eID="gen27668" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27669"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27670"/>“As I swore in my anger,<l eID="gen27670" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27671"/>‘<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞They will never enter⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “if they will enter”</note> into my rest.’ ”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.95.11">Ps 95:11</reference></note><l eID="gen27671" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen27669"/> <div sID="gen27672" type="x-p"/> And yet these works have been accomplished from the foundation of the world.

verses.name: Hebrews 4:4
verses.text: For he has spoken somewhere about the seventh <transChange type="added">day</transChange> in this way: “And God rested on the seventh day from all his works,”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Gen.2.2">Gen 2:2</reference></note>

verses.name: Hebrews 4:5
verses.text: and in this <transChange type="added">passage</transChange> again, ‘<milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞They will never enter⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “if they will enter”</note> into my rest.’ ”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.95.11">Ps 95:11</reference></note>

verses.name: Hebrews 4:6
verses.text: Since therefore it remains <transChange type="added">for</transChange> some to enter into it, and the ones to whom the good news was proclaimed previously did not enter because of disobedience,

verses.name: Hebrews 4:7
verses.text: again he ordains a certain day, today, speaking by David after so long a time, just as had been said before, <div eID="gen27672" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27673"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27674"/>“Today, if you hear his voice,<l eID="gen27674" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27675"/>do not harden your hearts.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.95.7b-Ps.95.8">Ps 95:7b-8 </reference>(see also <reference osisRef="Heb.3.7-Heb.3.8">Heb 3:7–8</reference>, <reference osisRef="Heb.3.15">15</reference>)</note> <l eID="gen27675" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen27673"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 4:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11918"/><div sID="gen27676" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11918"/>For if Joshua had caused them to rest, he would not have spoken about another day after these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>.

verses.name: Hebrews 4:9
verses.text: Consequently a sabbath rest remains for the people of God.

verses.name: Hebrews 4:10
verses.text: For the one who has entered into his rest has also himself rested from his works, just as God <transChange type="added">did</transChange> from his own <transChange type="added">works</transChange>.  <div eID="gen27676" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 4:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11919"/><div sID="gen27677" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11919"/>Therefore, let us make every effort to enter into that rest, in order that no one may fall in the same pattern of disobedience.

verses.name: Hebrews 4:12
verses.text: For the word of God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> living and active and sharper than any double-edged sword, and piercing as far as the division of soul and spirit, both joints and marrow, and able to judge the reflections and thoughts of the heart.

verses.name: Hebrews 4:13
verses.text: And no creature is hidden in the sight of him, but all <transChange type="added">things are</transChange> naked and laid bare to the eyes of him to whom <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞we must give our account⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “our account”</note>.  <div eID="gen27677" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 4:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11920"/><title type="x-s">Jesus Our Great High Priest</title> <div sID="gen27678" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11920"/>Therefore, <transChange type="added">because we</transChange> have a great high priest who has gone through the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast to our confession.

verses.name: Hebrews 4:15
verses.text: For we do not have a high priest who is not able to sympathize with our weaknesses, but who has been tempted in all <transChange type="added">things</transChange> in the same way, without sin.

verses.name: Hebrews 4:16
verses.text: Therefore let us approach with confidence to the throne of grace, in order that we may receive mercy and find grace to help in time of need.  <chapter eID="Heb.4"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 5:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11921"/><title type="x-s">A High Priest Like Melchizedek</title> <div sID="gen27679" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11921"/>For every high priest taken from among men is appointed on behalf of people in the things relating to God, in order that he can offer both gifts and sacrifices on behalf of sins,

verses.name: Hebrews 5:2
verses.text: being able to deal gently with those who are ignorant and led astray, since he himself also is surrounded by weakness,

verses.name: Hebrews 5:3
verses.text: and because of it he is obligated to offer <transChange type="added">sacrifices</transChange> for sins <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞for himself also, as well as for the people⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “as for the people so also for himself”</note>.

verses.name: Hebrews 5:4
verses.text: And someone does not take for himself the honor, but is called by God, just as Aaron also <transChange type="added">was</transChange>.

verses.name: Hebrews 5:5
verses.text: Thus also Christ did not glorify himself to become high priest, but the one who said to him, <div eID="gen27679" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27680"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27681"/>“You are my Son, today I have begotten you,”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.2.7">Ps 2:7</reference></note> <l eID="gen27681" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen27680"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 5:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11922"/><div sID="gen27682" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11922"/>just as also in another <transChange type="added">place</transChange> he says, <div eID="gen27682" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27683"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27684"/>“You <transChange type="added">are</transChange> a priest <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for the age”</note> according to the order of Melchizedek,”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.110.4">Ps 110:4</reference></note> <l eID="gen27684" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen27683"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 5:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11923"/><div sID="gen27685" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11923"/>who in the days of his flesh offered up both prayers and supplications, with loud crying and tears, to the one who was able to save him from death, and he was heard as a result of his reverence.

verses.name: Hebrews 5:8
verses.text: Although he was a son, he learned obedience from what he suffered,

verses.name: Hebrews 5:9
verses.text: and being perfected, he became the source of eternal salvation to all those who obey him,

verses.name: Hebrews 5:10
verses.text: being designated by God a high priest according to the order of Melchizedek.  <div eID="gen27685" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 5:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11924"/><title type="x-s">Advanced Teaching Hindered by Immaturity</title> <div sID="gen27686" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11924"/>Concerning this<note placement="foot">Literally “which”</note> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞we have much to say and it is difficult to explain⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “great for us the message and hard to explain to say”</note>, since you have become sluggish in hearing.

verses.name: Hebrews 5:12
verses.text: For indeed, <transChange type="added">although you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“ought”) which is understood as concessive</note> ought to be teachers <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞by this time⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “because of the time”</note>, you have need of someone to teach you again the beginning elements of the oracles of God, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞you have need of⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “you are having need of”</note> milk, not<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “and not”</note> solid food.

verses.name: Hebrews 5:13
verses.text: For everyone who partakes of milk <transChange type="added">is</transChange> unacquainted with the message of righteousness, because he is an infant.

verses.name: Hebrews 5:14
verses.text: But solid food is for the mature, who because of practice have trained their faculties for the distinguishing of both good and evil.  <chapter eID="Heb.5"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 6:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11925"/><title type="x-s">A Serious Warning Against Falling Away</title> <div sID="gen27687" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11925"/>Therefore, leaving behind the elementary message about Christ, let us move on to maturity, not laying again a foundation of repentance from dead works and faith in God,

verses.name: Hebrews 6:2
verses.text: teaching about baptisms and laying on of hands, and resurrection of the dead and eternal judgment.

verses.name: Hebrews 6:3
verses.text: And this we will do, if God permits.

verses.name: Hebrews 6:4
verses.text: For <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> impossible <transChange type="added">concerning</transChange> those who have once been enlightened, and have tasted the heavenly gift, and become sharers of the Holy Spirit,

verses.name: Hebrews 6:5
verses.text: and have tasted the good word of God and the powers of the coming age,

verses.name: Hebrews 6:6
verses.text: and having fallen away, to renew <transChange type="added">them</transChange> again to repentance, <transChange type="added">because they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“have crucified again”) which is understood as causal</note> have crucified again for themselves the Son of God and held him up to contempt.

verses.name: Hebrews 6:7
verses.text: For ground that drinks the rain that comes often upon it, and brings forth vegetation usable to those <transChange type="added">people</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞for whose sake⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for the sake of whom”</note> <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> also cultivated, shares a blessing from God.

verses.name: Hebrews 6:8
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">if it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “if” is supplied as a component of the participle (“produces”) which is understood as conditional</note> produces thorns and thistles, <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> worthless and near to a curse, whose end <transChange type="added">is</transChange> for burning.  <div eID="gen27687" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 6:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11926"/><div sID="gen27688" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11926"/>But even if we are speaking in this way, dear friends, we are convinced of better <transChange type="added">things</transChange> concerning you, and belonging to salvation.

verses.name: Hebrews 6:10
verses.text: For God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not unjust, <transChange type="added">so as</transChange> to forget your work and the love which you demonstrated for his name <transChange type="added">by</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“having served”) which is understood as means</note> having served the saints, and continuing to serve <transChange type="added">them</transChange>.

verses.name: Hebrews 6:11
verses.text: And we desire each one of you to demonstrate the same diligence for the full assurance of <transChange type="added">your</transChange> hope until the end,

verses.name: Hebrews 6:12
verses.text: in order that you may not be sluggish, but imitators of those who inherit the promises through faith and patience.  <div eID="gen27688" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 6:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11927"/><title type="x-s">The Reliability of God’s Promise</title> <div sID="gen27689" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11927"/>For <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal participle (“made a promise”)</note> God made a promise to Abraham, since he had no one greater to swear by, he swore by himself,

verses.name: Hebrews 6:14
verses.text: saying, <div eID="gen27689" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27690"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27691"/>“Surely <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I will greatly bless⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “blessing I will bless”</note> you, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞I will greatly multiply⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “multiplying I will multiply”</note> you.” <l eID="gen27691" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen27690"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 6:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11928"/><div sID="gen27692" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11928"/>And so, <transChange type="added">by</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“persevering”) which is understood as means</note> persevering, he obtained the promise.

verses.name: Hebrews 6:16
verses.text: For people swear by what is greater <transChange type="added">than themselves</transChange>, and the oath for confirmation <transChange type="added">is the</transChange> end of all dispute for them.

verses.name: Hebrews 6:17
verses.text: In the same way God, <transChange type="added">because he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“wanted”) which is understood as causal</note> wanted to show even more to the heirs of the promise the unchangeableness of his resolve, guaranteed <transChange type="added">it</transChange> with an oath,

verses.name: Hebrews 6:18
verses.text: in order that through two unchangeable things, in which <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> impossible for God to lie, we who have taken refuge may have powerful encouragement to hold fast to the hope set before <transChange type="added">us</transChange>,

verses.name: Hebrews 6:19
verses.text: which we have like an anchor of the soul, both firm and steadfast, and entering into the inside of the curtain,

verses.name: Hebrews 6:20
verses.text: where Jesus, the forerunner for us, entered, <transChange type="added">because he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“became”) which is understood as causal</note> became a high priest <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the age”</note> according to the order of Melchizedek.  <chapter eID="Heb.6"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 7:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11929"/><title type="x-s">The Greatness of Melchizedek</title> <div sID="gen27693" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11929"/>For this Melchizedek, king of Salem, priest of the most high God, who met Abraham <transChange type="added">as he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was returning”) which is understood as temporal</note> was returning from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him,<note placement="foot">This verse contains a number of quotations from <reference osisRef="Gen.14.17-Gen.14.19">Gen 14:17–19</reference></note>

verses.name: Hebrews 7:2
verses.text: to whom also Abraham apportioned a tenth of everything<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Gen.14.20">Gen 14:20</reference></note>—in the first place, <transChange type="added">his name</transChange> is translated “king of righteousness,” and then also “king of Salem,” that is, “king of peace”;

verses.name: Hebrews 7:3
verses.text: without father, without mother, without genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, but resembling the Son of God—he remains a priest for all time.  <div eID="gen27693" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 7:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11930"/><div sID="gen27694" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11930"/>But see how great this man <transChange type="added">was</transChange>, to whom Abraham<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “even Abraham”</note> the patriarch gave a tenth from the spoils!

verses.name: Hebrews 7:5
verses.text: And indeed those of the sons of Levi who receive the priesthood have a commandment to collect a tenth from the people according to the law, that is, from their brothers, although <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞they are descended from Abraham⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “coming forth from the loins of Abraham”</note>.

verses.name: Hebrews 7:6
verses.text: But the one who did not trace <transChange type="added">his</transChange> descent from them collected tithes from Abraham and blessed the one who had the promises.

verses.name: Hebrews 7:7
verses.text: Now without any dispute the inferior is blessed by the more prominent.

verses.name: Hebrews 7:8
verses.text: And in this case mortal men receive tithes, but in that case it is testified that he lives.

verses.name: Hebrews 7:9
verses.text: And, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞so to speak⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “as if to say a word”</note>, even Levi, the one who receives tithes, has paid tithes through Abraham.

verses.name: Hebrews 7:10
verses.text: For he was still in the loins of his father when Melchizedek met him.  <div eID="gen27694" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 7:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11931"/><title type="x-s">The Superiority of Jesus to Melchizedek</title> <div sID="gen27695" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11931"/>Thus if perfection was through the Levitical priesthood, for on the basis of it the people received the law, what further need <transChange type="added">is there</transChange> for another priest to arise according to the order of Melchizedek and not said to be according to the order of Aaron?

verses.name: Hebrews 7:12
verses.text: For <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“changes”)</note> the priesthood changes, of necessity there is a change of the law also.

verses.name: Hebrews 7:13
verses.text: For the one about whom these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> are spoken belongs to another tribe from which no one has officiated at the altar.

verses.name: Hebrews 7:14
verses.text: For <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> evident that our Lord is a descendant of Judah, a tribe <transChange type="added">with reference</transChange> to which Moses said nothing concerning priests.

verses.name: Hebrews 7:15
verses.text: And it is still more clear, if another priest according to the likeness of Melchizedek arises,

verses.name: Hebrews 7:16
verses.text: who has become <transChange type="added">a priest</transChange> not according to a law of physical requirement, but according to the power of an indestructible life.

verses.name: Hebrews 7:17
verses.text: For it is testified, <div eID="gen27695" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27696"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27697"/>“You <transChange type="added">are</transChange> a priest <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for the age”</note> according to the order of Melchizedek.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.110.4">Ps 110:4 </reference>(see also <reference osisRef="Heb.5.6">Heb 5:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Heb.6.20">6:20</reference>)</note> <l eID="gen27697" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen27696"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 7:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11932"/><div sID="gen27698" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11932"/>For on the one hand a preceding commandment is set aside because of its weakness and uselessness

verses.name: Hebrews 7:19
verses.text: (for the law <transChange type="added">made</transChange> nothing perfect), but on the other hand <transChange type="added">there is</transChange> the introduction of a better hope through which we draw near to God.

verses.name: Hebrews 7:20
verses.text: And by as much as <transChange type="added">this was</transChange> not without an oath (for these on the one hand <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞have become priests⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “are having become priests”</note> without an oath,

verses.name: Hebrews 7:21
verses.text: but he with an oath by the one who said to him, <div eID="gen27698" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27699"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27700"/>“The Lord has sworn and will not change his mind,<l eID="gen27700" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27701"/>‘You <transChange type="added">are</transChange> a priest <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for the age”</note>’ ”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.110.4">Ps 110:4 </reference>(see also <reference osisRef="Heb.5.6">Heb 5:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Heb.6.20">6:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="Heb.7.17">7:17</reference>)</note>), <l eID="gen27701" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen27699"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 7:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11933"/><div sID="gen27702" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11933"/>by so much more<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “so much more also”</note> Jesus has become the guarantee of a better covenant.  <div eID="gen27702" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 7:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11934"/><div sID="gen27703" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11934"/>And indeed many <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞have become⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “are having become”</note> priests, because they were prevented by death from continuing <transChange type="added">in office</transChange>,

verses.name: Hebrews 7:24
verses.text: but he, because he continues <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for the age”</note>, holds the priesthood permanently.

verses.name: Hebrews 7:25
verses.text: Therefore also he is able to save completely those who draw near to God through him, <transChange type="added">because he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“lives”) which is understood as causal</note> always lives in order to intercede on their behalf.  <div eID="gen27703" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 7:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11935"/><div sID="gen27704" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11935"/>For a high priest such as this indeed is fitting for us, holy, innocent, undefiled, separated from sinners, and having become exalted <transChange type="added">above</transChange> the heavens,

verses.name: Hebrews 7:27
verses.text: who does not <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞need every day⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “have necessity every day”</note> like the former high priests to offer up sacrifices for his own sins and then for the sins of the people, because he did this once for all when he<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal participle (“offered up”)</note> offered up himself.

verses.name: Hebrews 7:28
verses.text: For the law appoints men <transChange type="added">as</transChange> high priests who have weakness, but the statement of the oath, after the law, <transChange type="added">appoints</transChange> a Son, who is made perfect <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for the age”</note>.  <chapter eID="Heb.7"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 8:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11936"/><title type="x-s">The Mediator of a New and Better Covenant</title> <div sID="gen27705" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11936"/>Now <transChange type="added">this is</transChange> the main point in what has been said: we have a high priest such as this, who sat down at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in heaven,

verses.name: Hebrews 8:2
verses.text: a minister of the sanctuary and of the true tabernacle which the Lord set up, not man.

verses.name: Hebrews 8:3
verses.text: For every high priest is appointed in order to offer both gifts and sacrifices; therefore <transChange type="added">it was</transChange><note placement="foot">*Or “it is”; either a present or a past tense verb may be supplied here</note> necessary <transChange type="added">for</transChange> this one also to have something that he offers.

verses.name: Hebrews 8:4
verses.text: Now if he were on earth, he would not even be a priest, <transChange type="added">because there</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“are”) which is understood as causal</note> are those who offer the gifts according to the law,

verses.name: Hebrews 8:5
verses.text: who serve a sketch and shadow of the heavenly <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, just as Moses was warned <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal participle (“about”)</note> was about to complete the tabernacle, for he says, “See to it that you make everything according to the pattern which was shown to you on the mountain.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Exod.25.40">Exod 25:40</reference></note>
