verses.name: Hebrews 8:6
verses.text: But now he has attained a more excellent ministry, by as much as he is also mediator of a better covenant which has been enacted upon better promises.

verses.name: Hebrews 8:7
verses.text: For if that first <transChange type="added">covenant</transChange> had been faultless, occasion would not have been sought for a second.

verses.name: Hebrews 8:8
verses.text: For in finding fault with them he says, <div eID="gen27705" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27706"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27707"/>“Behold, days are coming, says the Lord,<l eID="gen27707" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27708"/>when I will complete a new covenant with the house of Israel<l eID="gen27708" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27709"/>and with the house of Judah, <l eID="gen27709" level="2"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 8:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11937"/><l level="1" sID="gen27710"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11937"/>not like the covenant which I made with their fathers<l eID="gen27710" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27711"/>on the day I took hold of them by my hand<l eID="gen27711" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27712"/>to lead them out of the land of Egypt,<l eID="gen27712" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27713"/>because they did not continue in my covenant<l eID="gen27713" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27714"/>and I disregarded them, says the Lord. <l eID="gen27714" level="2"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 8:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11938"/><l level="1" sID="gen27715"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11938"/>For this <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the covenant that I will decree with the house of Israel<l eID="gen27715" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27716"/>after those days, says the Lord:<l eID="gen27716" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27717"/>I am putting my laws in their minds<l eID="gen27717" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27718"/>and I will write them on their hearts,<l eID="gen27718" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27719"/>and I will be <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞their⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to them for”</note> God<l eID="gen27719" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27720"/>and they will be <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞my⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to me for”</note> people. <l eID="gen27720" level="2"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 8:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11939"/><l level="1" sID="gen27721"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11939"/>And they will not teach each one his fellow citizen<l eID="gen27721" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27722"/>and each one his brother, saying, ‘Know the Lord,’<l eID="gen27722" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27723"/>because they will all know me,<l eID="gen27723" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27724"/>from the least of them to the greatest. <l eID="gen27724" level="2"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 8:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11940"/><l level="1" sID="gen27725"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11940"/>For I will be merciful toward their wrongdoings,<l eID="gen27725" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27726"/>and I will not remember their sins <transChange type="added">any</transChange> longer.” <l eID="gen27726" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen27706"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 8:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11941"/><div sID="gen27727" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11941"/>In calling <transChange type="added">it</transChange> new, he has declared the former <transChange type="added">to be old</transChange>. Now what is becoming obsolete and growing old <transChange type="added">is</transChange> near to disappearing.  <chapter eID="Heb.8"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 9:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11942"/><title type="x-s">The Earthly Ministry of the Old Covenant</title> <div sID="gen27728" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11942"/>Now<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “Now even”</note> the first <transChange type="added">covenant</transChange> had regulations for worship and the earthly sanctuary.

verses.name: Hebrews 9:2
verses.text: For a tent was prepared, the first <transChange type="added">one</transChange>, in which <transChange type="added">were</transChange> the lampstand and the table and the presentation of the loaves, which is called the holy place.

verses.name: Hebrews 9:3
verses.text: And after the second curtain <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a tent called the holy of holies,

verses.name: Hebrews 9:4
verses.text: containing the golden incense altar and the ark of the covenant covered on all sides with gold, in which <transChange type="added">were</transChange> a golden jar containing the manna and the rod of Aaron that budded and the tablets of the covenant.

verses.name: Hebrews 9:5
verses.text: And above it <transChange type="added">were</transChange> the cherubim of glory overshadowing the mercy seat, about which it is not now <transChange type="added">possible</transChange> to speak in detail.  <div eID="gen27728" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 9:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11943"/><div sID="gen27729" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11943"/>Now these things having been prepared in this way, the priests enter into the first tent <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞continually⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “throughout all”</note> as they<note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal participle (“accomplish”)</note> accomplish their service,

verses.name: Hebrews 9:7
verses.text: but only the high priest <transChange type="added">enters</transChange> into the second <transChange type="added">tent</transChange> once a year, not without blood, which he offers on behalf of himself and the <transChange type="added">sins</transChange> of the people committed in ignorance.

verses.name: Hebrews 9:8
verses.text: The Holy Spirit <transChange type="added">was</transChange> making this clear, <transChange type="added">that</transChange> the way <transChange type="added">into</transChange> the holy place <transChange type="added">was</transChange> not yet revealed, <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal participle (“was”)</note> the first tent was still in existence,

verses.name: Hebrews 9:9
verses.text: which <transChange type="added">was</transChange> a symbol for the present time, in which both the gifts and sacrifices which were offered were not able to perfect the worshiper with respect to the conscience,

verses.name: Hebrews 9:10
verses.text: concerning <transChange type="added">instead</transChange> only food and drink and different washings, regulations of outward things imposed until the time of setting <transChange type="added">things</transChange> right.  <div eID="gen27729" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 9:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11944"/><title type="x-s">The Heavenly Ministry of the New Covenant</title> <div sID="gen27730" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11944"/>But Christ has arrived <transChange type="added">as</transChange> a high priest of the good <transChange type="added">things</transChange> to come. Through the greater and more perfect tent not made by hands, that is, not of this creation,

verses.name: Hebrews 9:12
verses.text: and not by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood, he entered once for all into the <transChange type="added">most</transChange> holy place, obtaining eternal redemption.

verses.name: Hebrews 9:13
verses.text: For if the blood of goats and bulls and the ashes of a young cow sprinkled on those who are defiled sanctify <transChange type="added">them</transChange> for the ritual purity of the flesh,

verses.name: Hebrews 9:14
verses.text: how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without blemish to God, cleanse our consciences from dead works to serve <transChange type="added">the</transChange> living God?  <div eID="gen27730" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 9:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11945"/><div sID="gen27731" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11945"/>And because of this, he is the mediator of a new covenant, in order that, <transChange type="added">because</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“has taken place”) which is understood as causal</note> a death has taken place for the redemption of transgressions <transChange type="added">committed</transChange> during the first covenant, those who are the called may receive the promise of the eternal inheritance.

verses.name: Hebrews 9:16
verses.text: For where <transChange type="added">there is</transChange> a will, <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> a necessity <transChange type="added">for</transChange> the death of the one who made the will to be established.

verses.name: Hebrews 9:17
verses.text: For a will <transChange type="added">is</transChange> in force concerning those who are dead, since <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> never in force when the one who made the will is alive.

verses.name: Hebrews 9:18
verses.text: Therefore not even the first <transChange type="added">covenant</transChange> was ratified without blood.

verses.name: Hebrews 9:19
verses.text: For <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal participle (“had been spoken”)</note> every commandment had been spoken by Moses to all the people according to the law, he took the blood of calves<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “calves and goats”</note> with water and scarlet wool and hyssop <transChange type="added">and</transChange> sprinkled both the scroll itself and all the people,

verses.name: Hebrews 9:20
verses.text: saying, <div eID="gen27731" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27732"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27733"/>“This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the blood of the covenant that God has commanded for you.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Exod.24.8">Exod 24:8</reference></note> <l eID="gen27733" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen27732"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 9:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11946"/><div sID="gen27734" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11946"/>And likewise he sprinkled both the tabernacle and all the utensils of service with the blood.

verses.name: Hebrews 9:22
verses.text: Indeed, nearly everything is purified with blood according to the law, and apart from the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness.  <div eID="gen27734" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 9:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11947"/><div sID="gen27735" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11947"/>Therefore <transChange type="added">it was</transChange> necessary <transChange type="added">for</transChange> the sketches of the <transChange type="added">things</transChange> in heaven to be purified with these <transChange type="added">sacrifices</transChange>, but the heavenly <transChange type="added">things</transChange> themselves <transChange type="added">to be purified</transChange> with better sacrifices than these.

verses.name: Hebrews 9:24
verses.text: For Christ did not enter into a sanctuary made by hands, a <transChange type="added">mere</transChange> copy of the true <transChange type="added">one</transChange>, but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God on our behalf,

verses.name: Hebrews 9:25
verses.text: and not in order that he can offer himself many times, as the high priest enters into the sanctuary <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞year by year⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “according to year”</note> with blood not his own,

verses.name: Hebrews 9:26
verses.text: since it would have been necessary for him to suffer many times from the foundation of the world, but now he has appeared once at the end of the ages for the removal of sin by the sacrifice of himself.

verses.name: Hebrews 9:27
verses.text: And <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞just as⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in as much as”</note> it is destined for people to die once, and after this, judgment,

verses.name: Hebrews 9:28
verses.text: thus also Christ, having been offered once in order to bear the sins of many, will appear for the second time without reference to sin to those who eagerly await him for salvation.  <chapter eID="Heb.9"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 10:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11948"/><title type="x-s">Christ’s One Sacrifice for Sin</title> <div sID="gen27736" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11948"/>For the law, possessing a shadow of the good <transChange type="added">things</transChange> that are about to come, not the form of things itself, <transChange type="added">is</transChange> never able <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞year by year⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “according to year”</note> by means of the same sacrifices which they offer without interruption to make perfect those who draw near.

verses.name: Hebrews 10:2
verses.text: For otherwise, would they not have ceased to be offered, because the ones who worship, having been purified once and for all, would no longer have any consciousness of sins?

verses.name: Hebrews 10:3
verses.text: But in them <transChange type="added">there is</transChange> a reminder of sins <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞year by year⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “according to year”</note>.

verses.name: Hebrews 10:4
verses.text: For <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> impossible <transChange type="added">for</transChange> the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.  <div eID="gen27736" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 10:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11949"/><div sID="gen27737" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11949"/>Therefore, <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal participle (“came”)</note> came into the world, he said, <div eID="gen27737" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27738"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27739"/>“Sacrifice and offering you did not want,<l eID="gen27739" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27740"/>but a body you prepared for me; <l eID="gen27740" level="2"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 10:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11950"/><l level="1" sID="gen27741"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11950"/>you did not delight in whole burnt offerings and <transChange type="added">offerings</transChange> for sins. <l eID="gen27741" level="1"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 10:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11951"/><l level="2" sID="gen27742"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11951"/>Then I said, ‘Behold, I have come—<l eID="gen27742" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27743"/>in the roll of the book it is written about me—<l eID="gen27743" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27744"/>to do your will, O God.’ <l eID="gen27744" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen27738"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 10:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11952"/><div sID="gen27745" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11952"/><transChange type="added">When he</transChange> says above, <div eID="gen27745" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27746"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27747"/>“Sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and <transChange type="added">offerings</transChange> for sin<l eID="gen27747" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27748"/>you did not want, nor did you delight in,”<note placement="foot">Various phrases from the quotation of <reference osisRef="Ps.40.6">Ps 40:6 </reference>in <reference osisRef="Heb.10.5-Heb.10.6">Heb 10:5–6 </reference>are repeated here</note><l eID="gen27748" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen27746"/> <div sID="gen27749" type="x-p"/> which are offered according to the law,

verses.name: Hebrews 10:9
verses.text: then he has said, <div eID="gen27749" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27750"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27751"/>“Behold, I have come to do your will.”<note placement="foot">A repetition of <reference osisRef="Ps.40.8">Ps 40:8 </reference>from <reference osisRef="Heb.10.7">Heb 10:7; </reference>many later manuscripts add “O God,” making the quotation conform to <reference osisRef="Heb.10.7">Heb 10:7 </reference>more closely</note><l eID="gen27751" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen27750"/> <div sID="gen27752" type="x-p"/> He takes away the first in order to establish the second,

verses.name: Hebrews 10:10
verses.text: by which will we are made holy through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.  <div eID="gen27752" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 10:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11953"/><div sID="gen27753" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11953"/>And every priest stands every day serving and offering the same sacrifices many times, which are never able to take away sins.

verses.name: Hebrews 10:12
verses.text: But this one, <transChange type="added">after he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the temporal participle (“had offered”)</note> had offered one sacrifice for sins for all time, sat down at the right hand of God,

verses.name: Hebrews 10:13
verses.text: from now on waiting until his enemies are made a footstool for his feet.

verses.name: Hebrews 10:14
verses.text: For by one offering he has perfected for all time those who are made holy.

verses.name: Hebrews 10:15
verses.text: And the Holy Spirit also testifies to us, for after saying,  <div eID="gen27753" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 10:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11954"/><lg sID="gen27754"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27755"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11954"/>“This <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the covenant that I will decree for them<l eID="gen27755" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27756"/>after those days, says the Lord:<l eID="gen27756" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27757"/>I am putting my laws on their hearts,<l eID="gen27757" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27758"/>and I will write them on their minds.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Jer.31.33">Jer 31:33</reference></note> <l eID="gen27758" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen27754"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 10:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11955"/><div sID="gen27759" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11955"/><transChange type="added">He</transChange> also <transChange type="added">says</transChange>, <div eID="gen27759" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27760"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27761"/>“Their sins and their lawless deeds I will never remember again.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Jer.31.34">Jer 31:34</reference></note> <l eID="gen27761" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen27760"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 10:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11956"/><div sID="gen27762" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11956"/>Now where <transChange type="added">there is</transChange> forgiveness of these, <transChange type="added">there is</transChange> no longer an offering for sin.  <div eID="gen27762" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 10:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11957"/><title type="x-s">Hold Fast the Confession of Our Hope</title> <div sID="gen27763" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11957"/>Therefore, brothers, <transChange type="added">since we</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “since” is supplied as a component of the participle (“have”) which is understood as causal</note> have confidence for the entrance into the sanctuary by the blood of Jesus,

verses.name: Hebrews 10:20
verses.text: <transChange type="added">by the</transChange> new and living way which he inaugurated for us through the curtain, that is, his flesh,

verses.name: Hebrews 10:21
verses.text: and <transChange type="added">since we have</transChange><note placement="foot">These words are an implied repetition from v. <reference osisRef="Heb.10.19">19</reference> for clarity</note> a great priest over the house of God,

verses.name: Hebrews 10:22
verses.text: let us approach with a true heart in the full assurance of faith, our hearts sprinkled <transChange type="added">clean</transChange> from an evil conscience and our bodies washed with pure water.

verses.name: Hebrews 10:23
verses.text: Let us hold fast to the confession of <transChange type="added">our</transChange> hope without wavering, for the one who promised <transChange type="added">is</transChange> faithful.

verses.name: Hebrews 10:24
verses.text: And let us think about <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞how to stir one another up to love⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “one another for the stirring up of love”</note> and good works,

verses.name: Hebrews 10:25
verses.text: not abandoning <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞our meeting together⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the meeting of ourselves”</note>, as <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the habit of some, but encouraging <transChange type="added">each other</transChange>, and by so much more as you see the day drawing near.  <div eID="gen27763" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 10:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11958"/><title type="x-s">A Serious Warning Against Continuing Deliberate Sin</title> <div sID="gen27764" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11958"/>For <transChange type="added">if</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “if” is supplied as a component of the conditional genitive absolute participle (“keep on sinning”)</note> we keep on sinning deliberately after receiving the knowledge of the truth, there no longer remains a sacrifice for sins,

verses.name: Hebrews 10:27
verses.text: but a certain fearful expectation of judgment and a fury of fire that is about to consume the adversaries.

verses.name: Hebrews 10:28
verses.text: Anyone who rejected the law of Moses dies without mercy on <transChange type="added">the testimony of</transChange> two or three witnesses.

verses.name: Hebrews 10:29
verses.text: How much worse punishment do you think the person will be considered worthy of who treats with disdain the Son of God and who considers ordinary the blood of the covenant by which he was made holy and who insults the Spirit of grace?

verses.name: Hebrews 10:30
verses.text: For we know the one who said, <div eID="gen27764" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27765"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27766"/>“Vengeance <transChange type="added">is</transChange> mine, I will repay,”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Deut.32.35">Deut 32:35</reference></note><l eID="gen27766" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen27765"/> <div sID="gen27767" type="x-p"/> and again, <div eID="gen27767" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27768"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27769"/>“The Lord will judge his people.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Deut.32.36">Deut 32:36</reference></note> <l eID="gen27769" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen27768"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 10:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11959"/><div sID="gen27770" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11959"/><transChange type="added">It is</transChange> a terrifying <transChange type="added">thing</transChange> to fall into the hands of the living God.  <div eID="gen27770" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 10:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11960"/><div sID="gen27771" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11960"/>But remember the former days in which, <transChange type="added">after you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the temporal participle (“were enlightened”)</note> were enlightened, you endured a great struggle with sufferings,

verses.name: Hebrews 10:33
verses.text: sometimes being publicly exposed both to insults and to afflictions, and sometimes becoming sharers with those who were treated in this way.

verses.name: Hebrews 10:34
verses.text: For you both sympathized with the prisoners and put up with the seizure of your belongings with joy <transChange type="added">because you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“knew”) which is understood as causal</note> knew that you yourselves had a better and permanent possession.

verses.name: Hebrews 10:35
verses.text: Therefore do not throw away your confidence, which has great reward.

verses.name: Hebrews 10:36
verses.text: For you have need of endurance, in order that <transChange type="added">after you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the temporal participle (“have done”)</note> have done the will of God, you may receive what was promised.

verses.name: Hebrews 10:37
verses.text: For yet <div eID="gen27771" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27772"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27773"/>“a very, very little <transChange type="added">while</transChange>,<l eID="gen27773" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27774"/><transChange type="added">and</transChange> the one who is coming will come and will not delay. <l eID="gen27774" level="2"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 10:38
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11961"/><l level="1" sID="gen27775"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11961"/>But my righteous one will live by faith,<l eID="gen27775" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27776"/>and if he shrinks back, my soul is not well pleased with him.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Hab.2.3-Hab.2.4">Hab 2:3–4</reference></note> <l eID="gen27776" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen27772"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 10:39
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11962"/><div sID="gen27777" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11962"/>But we are not among those who shrink back to destruction, but among those who have faith to the preservation of <transChange type="added">our</transChange> souls.  <chapter eID="Heb.10"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 11:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11963"/><title type="x-s">Examples of Faith in Action</title> <div sID="gen27778" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11963"/>Now faith is the realization of what is hoped for, the proof of things not seen.

verses.name: Hebrews 11:2
verses.text: For by this the people of old were approved.

verses.name: Hebrews 11:3
verses.text: By faith we understand the worlds were created by the word of God, in order that what is seen did not come into existence from what is visible.  <div eID="gen27778" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 11:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11964"/><div sID="gen27779" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11964"/>By faith Abel offered to God a greater sacrifice than Cain, by which he was approved that he was righteous, <transChange type="added">because</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal participle (“was”)</note> God approved him for his gifts, and through it<note placement="foot">I.e., his faith</note> he still speaks, although he<note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“is dead”) which is understood as concessive</note> is dead.

verses.name: Hebrews 11:5
verses.text: By faith Enoch was taken up, so that he did not experience death, and he was not found, because God took him up. For before his removal, he had been approved <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞as having been pleasing⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to be pleasing”</note> to God.

verses.name: Hebrews 11:6
verses.text: Now without faith <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> impossible to please <transChange type="added">him</transChange>, for the one who approaches God must believe that he exists and is a rewarder of those who seek him.

verses.name: Hebrews 11:7
verses.text: By faith Noah, having been warned about things not yet seen, out of reverence constructed an ark for the deliverance of his family, by which he pronounced sentence on the world and became an heir of the righteousness that comes by faith.  <div eID="gen27779" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 11:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11965"/><div sID="gen27780" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11965"/>By faith Abraham, <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal participle (“was called”)</note> was called, obeyed to go out to a place that he was going to receive for an inheritance, and he went out, not knowing where he was going.

verses.name: Hebrews 11:9
verses.text: By faith he lived in the land of promise as a stranger, living in tents with Isaac and Jacob, the fellow heirs of the same promise.

verses.name: Hebrews 11:10
verses.text: For he was expecting the city that has foundations, whose architect and builder <transChange type="added">is</transChange> God.

verses.name: Hebrews 11:11
verses.text: By faith also, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞with Sarah⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “with her, Sarah”</note>,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “even though Sarah herself was barren”</note> he received <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the ability to procreate⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “power to deposit seed”</note> even <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞past the normal age⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “beyond the time of maturity”</note>, because he regarded the one who had promised <transChange type="added">to be</transChange> faithful.

verses.name: Hebrews 11:12
verses.text: And therefore these were fathered from one man, and <transChange type="added">he</transChange> being as good as dead, as the stars of heaven in number and like the innumerable sand by the shore of the sea.  <div eID="gen27780" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 11:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11966"/><div sID="gen27781" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11966"/>These all died in faith without receiving the promises, but seeing them from a distance and welcoming <transChange type="added">them</transChange>, and admitting that they were strangers and temporary residents on the earth.

verses.name: Hebrews 11:14
verses.text: For those who say such <transChange type="added">things</transChange> make clear that they are seeking a homeland.

verses.name: Hebrews 11:15
verses.text: And if they remember<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “they had been remembering”</note> that <transChange type="added">land</transChange> from which they went out, they would have had opportunity to return.

verses.name: Hebrews 11:16
verses.text: But now they aspire to a better <transChange type="added">land</transChange>, that is, a heavenly <transChange type="added">one</transChange>. Therefore God is not ashamed of them, to be called their God, for he has prepared for them a city.  <div eID="gen27781" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 11:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11967"/><div sID="gen27782" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11967"/>By faith Abraham, <transChange type="added">when he</transChange> was tested, offered Isaac, and the one who received the promises was ready to offer his one and only <transChange type="added">son</transChange>,

verses.name: Hebrews 11:18
verses.text: with reference to whom it was said, “In Isaac your descendants will be named,”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Gen.21.12">Gen 21:12</reference></note>

verses.name: Hebrews 11:19
verses.text: having reasoned that God <transChange type="added">was</transChange> able even to raise <transChange type="added">him</transChange> from the dead, from which he received him back also as a symbol.

verses.name: Hebrews 11:20
verses.text: By faith also Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau concerning things that were going to happen.

verses.name: Hebrews 11:21
verses.text: By faith Jacob, <transChange type="added">as he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal participle (“was dying”)</note> was dying, blessed each of the sons of Joseph and worshiped, <transChange type="added">leaning</transChange> on the top of his staff.

verses.name: Hebrews 11:22
verses.text: By faith Joseph, <transChange type="added">as he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal participle (“was dying”)</note> was dying, mentioned about the exodus of the sons of Israel and gave instructions about his bones.  <div eID="gen27782" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 11:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11968"/><div sID="gen27783" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11968"/>By faith Moses, <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal participle (“afraid of”)</note> was born, was hidden for three months by his parents, because they saw the child <transChange type="added">was</transChange> handsome, and they were not afraid of the edict of the king.

verses.name: Hebrews 11:24
verses.text: By faith Moses, <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal participle (“was”)</note> was grown up, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter,

verses.name: Hebrews 11:25
verses.text: choosing instead to be mistreated with the people of God <transChange type="added">rather</transChange> than to experience the transitory enjoyment of sin,

verses.name: Hebrews 11:26
verses.text: considering <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞reproach endured for the sake of Christ⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the reproach of Christ”</note> greater wealth than the treasures of Egypt, for he was looking to the reward.

verses.name: Hebrews 11:27
verses.text: By faith he left Egypt, not fearing the anger of the king, for he persevered as <transChange type="added">if he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “if” is supplied as a component of the participle (“saw”) which is understood as conditional</note> saw the invisible one.

verses.name: Hebrews 11:28
verses.text: By faith he kept the Passover and the sprinkling of blood, in order that the one who destroyed the firstborn would not touch them.

verses.name: Hebrews 11:29
verses.text: By faith they crossed the Red Sea as if on dry land; the Egyptians, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞when they made the attempt⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “of which attempt making”</note>, were drowned.

verses.name: Hebrews 11:30
verses.text: By faith the walls of Jericho fell down <transChange type="added">after they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the temporal participle (“had been marched around”)</note> had been marched around for seven days.

verses.name: Hebrews 11:31
verses.text: By faith Rahab the prostitute did not perish with those who were disobedient, <transChange type="added">because she</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“welcomed”) which is understood as causal</note> welcomed the spies in peace.  <div eID="gen27783" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 11:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11969"/><div sID="gen27784" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11969"/>And what more shall I say? For time would fail me to tell about Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, and Samuel and the prophets,

verses.name: Hebrews 11:33
verses.text: who through faith conquered kingdoms, accomplished justice, obtained what was promised, shut the mouths of lions,

verses.name: Hebrews 11:34
verses.text: extinguished the effectiveness of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, were made strong from weakness, became mighty in battle, put to flight enemy battle lines.

verses.name: Hebrews 11:35
verses.text: Women received back their dead by resurrection. But others were tortured, not accepting release, in order that they might gain a better resurrection.

verses.name: Hebrews 11:36
verses.text: And others <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞experienced mocking and flogging⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “received experience of mocking and flogging”</note>, and in addition bonds and imprisonment.

verses.name: Hebrews 11:37
verses.text: They were stoned, they were sawed in two, they died by murder with a sword, they wandered about in sheepskins, in goatskins, impoverished, afflicted, mistreated,

verses.name: Hebrews 11:38
verses.text: of whom the world was not worthy, wandering about on deserts and mountains and in caves and in holes in the ground.

verses.name: Hebrews 11:39
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">although they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“were approved”) which is understood as concessive</note> all were approved<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “And all these, although they were approved”</note> through their faith, they did not receive what was promised,

verses.name: Hebrews 11:40
verses.text: <transChange type="added">because</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the causal genitive absolute participle (“had provided”)</note> God had provided something better for us, so that they would not be made perfect without us.  <chapter eID="Heb.11"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 12:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11970"/><title type="x-s">The Example of Jesus’ Suffering</title> <div sID="gen27785" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11970"/>Therefore, <transChange type="added">since</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “since” is supplied as a component of the participle (“have”) which is understood as causal</note> we also have such a great cloud of witnesses surrounding us, putting aside every weight and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the sin that so easily ensnares us⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the easily ensnaring sin”</note>, let us run with patient endurance the race that has been set before us,

verses.name: Hebrews 12:2
verses.text: fixing our eyes on Jesus, the originator and perfecter of faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, disregarding the shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.

verses.name: Hebrews 12:3
verses.text: For consider the one who endured such hostility by sinners against himself,<note placement="foot">*The plural reflexive pronoun can still be translated as singular; see Louw-Nida 92.25</note> so that you will not grow weary in your souls <transChange type="added">and</transChange> give up.

verses.name: Hebrews 12:4
verses.text: You have not yet resisted to the point of <transChange type="added">shedding your</transChange><note placement="foot">*The words “shedding your” are not in the Greek text but are supplied for clarity</note> blood as you<note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the temporal participle (“struggle”)</note> struggle against sin.

verses.name: Hebrews 12:5
verses.text: And have you completely forgotten the exhortation which instructs you as sons? <div eID="gen27785" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27786"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27787"/>“My son, do not make light of the Lord’s discipline,<l eID="gen27787" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27788"/>or give up <transChange type="added">when you</transChange> are corrected by him. <l eID="gen27788" level="2"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 12:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11971"/><l level="1" sID="gen27789"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11971"/>For the Lord disciplines the one whom he loves,<l eID="gen27789" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27790"/>and punishes every son whom he accepts.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Prov.3.11-Prov.3.12">Prov 3:11–12</reference></note> <l eID="gen27790" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen27786"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 12:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11972"/><div sID="gen27791" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11972"/>Endure <transChange type="added">it</transChange> for discipline. God is dealing with you as sons. For what son <transChange type="added">is there</transChange> whom a father does not discipline?

verses.name: Hebrews 12:8
verses.text: But if you are without discipline, in which all <transChange type="added">legitimate sons</transChange><note placement="foot">*The phrase “legitimate sons” is not in the Greek text but is implied</note> have become participants, then you are illegitimate and not sons.

verses.name: Hebrews 12:9
verses.text: Furthermore, we have had <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞our earthly fathers⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the flesh of our fathers”</note> who disciplined <transChange type="added">us</transChange>, and we respected <transChange type="added">them</transChange>. Will we not much rather subject ourselves to the Father of spirits and live?

verses.name: Hebrews 12:10
verses.text: For they disciplined <transChange type="added">us</transChange> for a few days according to what seemed <transChange type="added">appropriate</transChange> to them, but he <transChange type="added">does so</transChange> for our benefit, in order that <transChange type="added">we</transChange> can have a share in his holiness.

verses.name: Hebrews 12:11
verses.text: Now all discipline seems for the moment not to be joyful but painful, but later it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness for those who are trained by it.  <div eID="gen27791" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 12:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11973"/><title type="x-s">A Serious Warning Against Refusing God</title> <div sID="gen27792" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11973"/>Therefore strengthen your slackened hands and your weakened knees,

verses.name: Hebrews 12:13
verses.text: and make straight paths for your feet, so that what is lame will not be dislocated, but rather be healed.

verses.name: Hebrews 12:14
verses.text: Pursue peace with everyone, and holiness, without which no one will see the Lord.

verses.name: Hebrews 12:15
verses.text: Take care <transChange type="added">that</transChange> no one falls short of the grace of God; <transChange type="added">that</transChange> no one growing up <transChange type="added">like</transChange> a root of bitterness causes trouble, and by it many become defiled;

verses.name: Hebrews 12:16
verses.text: <transChange type="added">that</transChange> no one <transChange type="added">be</transChange> a sexually immoral or totally worldly <transChange type="added">person</transChange> like Esau, who for one meal traded his own birthright.

verses.name: Hebrews 12:17
verses.text: For you know that also afterwards, <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal participle (“wanted”)</note> wanted to inherit the blessing, he was rejected, because he did not find an occasion for repentance, although he sought it with tears.  <div eID="gen27792" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 12:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11974"/><div sID="gen27793" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11974"/>For you have not come to something that can be touched, and to a burning fire, and to darkness, and to gloom, and to a whirlwind,

verses.name: Hebrews 12:19
verses.text: and to the noise of a trumpet, and to the sound of words which those who heard begged <transChange type="added">that</transChange> not <transChange type="added">another</transChange> word be spoken to them.

verses.name: Hebrews 12:20
verses.text: For they could not endure what was commanded: “If even an animal touches the mountain, it must be stoned.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Exod.19.12-Exod.19.13">Exod 19:12–13</reference></note>

verses.name: Hebrews 12:21
verses.text: And the spectacle was so terrifying <transChange type="added">that</transChange> Moses said, “I am terrified and trembling.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Deut.9.19">Deut 9:19</reference></note>

verses.name: Hebrews 12:22
verses.text: But you have come to Mount Zion, and to the city of the living God, to the heavenly Jerusalem, and to tens of thousands of angels, to the festal gathering

verses.name: Hebrews 12:23
verses.text: and assembly of the firstborn who are enrolled in heaven, and to God the judge of all, and to the spirits of righteous <transChange type="added">people</transChange> made perfect,

verses.name: Hebrews 12:24
verses.text: and to Jesus, the mediator of a new covenant, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to the sprinkled blood⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the blood of sprinkling”</note> that speaks better than Abel’s <transChange type="added">does</transChange>.  <div eID="gen27793" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 12:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11975"/><div sID="gen27794" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11975"/>Watch out that you do not refuse the one who is speaking! For if those did not escape <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal participle (“refused”)</note> refused the one who warned them on earth, much less will we escape,<note placement="foot">*Here the verb “will … escape” is an understood repetition from the previous clause</note> if we<note placement="foot">*Here “if” is supplied as a component of the participle (“reject”) which is understood as conditional</note> reject the <transChange type="added">one who warns</transChange> from heaven,

verses.name: Hebrews 12:26
verses.text: whose voice shook the earth at that time, but now he has promised, saying, <div eID="gen27794" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27795"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27796"/>“Yet once <transChange type="added">more</transChange> I will shake not only the earth but also heaven.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Hag.2.6">Hag 2:6</reference></note> <l eID="gen27796" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen27795"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 12:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11976"/><div sID="gen27797" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11976"/>Now the <transChange type="added">phrase</transChange> “yet once <transChange type="added">more</transChange>” indicates the removal of what is shaken, namely, things that have been created, in order that the things that are not shaken may remain.

verses.name: Hebrews 12:28
verses.text: Therefore, <transChange type="added">since we</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “since” is supplied as a component of the participle (“are receiving”) which is understood as causal</note> are receiving an unshakable kingdom, let us be thankful, through which let us serve God acceptably, with awe and reverence.

verses.name: Hebrews 12:29
verses.text: For indeed our God <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a consuming fire.  <chapter eID="Heb.12"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 13:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11977"/><title type="x-s">Concluding Ethical Instructions</title> <div sID="gen27798" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11977"/>Brotherly love must continue.

verses.name: Hebrews 13:2
verses.text: Do not neglect hospitality, because through this some have received angels as guests without knowing <transChange type="added">it</transChange>.

verses.name: Hebrews 13:3
verses.text: Remember the prisoners, as <transChange type="added">though you were</transChange> fellow-prisoners; <transChange type="added">remember</transChange><note placement="foot">*This is an understood repetition of the verb from the previous clause</note> the mistreated, as though you yourselves also are being mistreated<note placement="foot">*This is an understood repetition of the participle from the previous clause</note> in the body.

verses.name: Hebrews 13:4
verses.text: Marriage <transChange type="added">must be</transChange> held in honor by all, and the marriage bed <transChange type="added">be</transChange> undefiled, because God will judge sexually immoral people and adulterers.

verses.name: Hebrews 13:5
verses.text: Your lifestyle <transChange type="added">must be</transChange> free from the love of money, being content with what you have. For he himself has said, “I will never desert you, and I will never abandon you.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Deut.31.6">Deut 31:6</reference>, <reference osisRef="Deut.31.8">8</reference></note>

verses.name: Hebrews 13:6
verses.text: So then, we can say with confidence, <div eID="gen27798" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27799"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27800"/>“The Lord <transChange type="added">is</transChange> my helper, I will not be afraid.<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “and I will not be afraid”</note><l eID="gen27800" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27801"/>What will man do to me?”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.118.6">Ps 118:6</reference></note> <l eID="gen27801" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen27799"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 13:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11978"/><div sID="gen27802" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11978"/>Remember your leaders, who spoke the word of God to you; <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞considering the outcome of their way of life⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “of whom considering the outcome of the way of life”</note>, imitate their faith.

verses.name: Hebrews 13:8
verses.text: Jesus Christ <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the same yesterday and today and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the ages”</note>.

verses.name: Hebrews 13:9
verses.text: Do not be carried away by various and strange teachings, for <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> good <transChange type="added">for</transChange> the heart to be strengthened by grace, not by foods by which those who participate have not benefited.

verses.name: Hebrews 13:10
verses.text: We have an altar from which those who serve in the tabernacle do not have the right to eat.

verses.name: Hebrews 13:11
verses.text: For the bodies of those animals whose blood is brought into the sanctuary by the high priest for sins are burned up outside the camp.

verses.name: Hebrews 13:12
verses.text: Therefore Jesus also suffered outside the gate, in order that he might sanctify the people by his own blood.

verses.name: Hebrews 13:13
verses.text: So we must go out to him outside the camp, bearing his reproach.

verses.name: Hebrews 13:14
verses.text: For here we do not have a permanent city, but we seek the <transChange type="added">city</transChange> that is to come.

verses.name: Hebrews 13:15
verses.text: Therefore through him let us offer up a sacrifice of praise <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞continually⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “through all”</note> to God, that is, the fruit of lips that confess his name.

verses.name: Hebrews 13:16
verses.text: And do not neglect doing good and generosity, for God is pleased with such sacrifices.  <div eID="gen27802" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 13:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11979"/><div sID="gen27803" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11979"/>Obey your leaders and submit <transChange type="added">to them</transChange>, for they keep watch over your souls as those who will give an account, so that they can do this with joy and not <transChange type="added">with</transChange> groaning, for this <transChange type="added">would be</transChange> unprofitable for you.  <div eID="gen27803" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 13:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11980"/><div sID="gen27804" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11980"/>Pray for us, for we are convinced that we have a good conscience, <transChange type="added">and</transChange> want to conduct ourselves commendably in every <transChange type="added">way</transChange>.

verses.name: Hebrews 13:19
verses.text: And I especially urge <transChange type="added">you</transChange> to do this, so that I may be restored to you more quickly.  <div eID="gen27804" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 13:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11981"/><title type="x-s">Benediction</title> <div sID="gen27805" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11981"/>Now may the God of peace, who brought up from the dead our Lord Jesus, the great shepherd of the sheep, by the blood of the eternal covenant,

verses.name: Hebrews 13:21
verses.text: equip you with every good <transChange type="added">thing</transChange> to do his will, carrying out in us <transChange type="added">what is</transChange> pleasing before him through Jesus Christ, to whom <transChange type="added">be</transChange> the glory <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the ages”</note>.<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “forever and ever” (literally, “to the ages of the ages”)</note> Amen.  <div eID="gen27805" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Hebrews 13:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11982"/><title type="x-s">Conclusion</title> <div sID="gen27806" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11982"/>Now I urge you, brothers, bear with my word of exhortation, for indeed I have written to you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞briefly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “through few words”</note>.

verses.name: Hebrews 13:23
verses.text: Know <transChange type="added">that</transChange> our brother Timothy has been released, with whom I will see you, if he comes quickly <transChange type="added">enough</transChange>.

verses.name: Hebrews 13:24
verses.text: Greet all your leaders and all the saints. Those from Italy greet you.

verses.name: Hebrews 13:25
verses.text: Grace <transChange type="added">be</transChange> with all of you.  <chapter eID="Heb.13"/> <div eID="gen27806" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen27593" osisID="Heb" type="book"/>

verses.name: James 1:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11983"/><title type="x-s">Greeting</title> <div sID="gen27808" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11983"/>James, a slave of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes in the dispersion. Greetings!  <div eID="gen27808" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: James 1:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11984"/><title type="x-s">Trials, Testing, and Faith</title> <div sID="gen27809" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11984"/>Consider <transChange type="added">it</transChange> all joy, my brothers, whenever you encounter various trials,

verses.name: James 1:3
verses.text: <transChange type="added">because you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“know”) which is understood as causal</note> know that the testing of your faith produces endurance.

verses.name: James 1:4
verses.text: And let endurance have <transChange type="added">its</transChange> perfect effect, so that you may be mature and complete, lacking in nothing.  <div eID="gen27809" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: James 1:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11985"/><div sID="gen27810" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11985"/>Now if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask for <transChange type="added">it</transChange> from God, who gives to all without reservation and not reproaching, and it will be given to him.

verses.name: James 1:6
verses.text: But let him ask for <transChange type="added">it</transChange> in faith, without any doubting, for the one who doubts is like the surf of the sea, driven by the wind and tossed about.

verses.name: James 1:7
verses.text: For that person must not suppose that he will receive anything from the Lord;

verses.name: James 1:8
verses.text: <transChange type="added">he is</transChange> a double-minded man, unstable in all his ways.  <div eID="gen27810" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: James 1:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11986"/><div sID="gen27811" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11986"/>Now let the brother of humble circumstances boast in his high position,

verses.name: James 1:10
verses.text: but the rich person in his humiliation, because he will pass away like a flower of the grass.

verses.name: James 1:11
verses.text: For the sun rises with its burning heat and dries up the grass, and its flower falls off, and the beauty of its appearance is lost. So also the rich person in his pursuits<note placement="foot">Or “on his (business) journeys”; or “in his ways”</note> will wither away.  <div eID="gen27811" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: James 1:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11987"/><div sID="gen27812" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11987"/>Blessed <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the person<note placement="foot">Literally “the man,” but clearly in a generic sense here meaning “someone, a person”</note> who endures testing, because when he<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“is”) which is understood as temporal</note> is approved he will receive the crown of life that he<note placement="foot">Most manuscripts read “the Lord” here, while others read “God”</note> has promised to those who love him.

verses.name: James 1:13
verses.text: No one who is being tempted should say, “I am being tempted by God,” for God <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞cannot be tempted⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “is without temptation”</note> by evil, and he himself tempts no one.

verses.name: James 1:14
verses.text: But each one is tempted <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“is dragged away”) which is understood as temporal</note> is dragged away and enticed by his own desires.

verses.name: James 1:15
verses.text: Then desire, <transChange type="added">after it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“has conceived”) which is understood as temporal</note> has conceived, gives birth to sin, and sin, when it<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“is brought to completion”) which is understood as temporal</note> is brought to completion, gives birth to death.  <div eID="gen27812" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: James 1:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11988"/><div sID="gen27813" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11988"/>Do not be deceived, my dear brothers.

verses.name: James 1:17
verses.text: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom there is no variation or shadow of change.

verses.name: James 1:18
verses.text: <transChange type="added">By his</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“will”) which is understood as means</note> will he gave birth to us through the message of truth, so that we should be a kind of first fruits of his creatures.  <div eID="gen27813" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: James 1:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11989"/><title type="x-s">Doers of the Message, Not Just Hearers</title> <div sID="gen27814" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11989"/>Understand <transChange type="added">this</transChange>, my dear brothers: every person must be quick to hear, slow to speak, slow to anger,

verses.name: James 1:20
verses.text: for human<note placement="foot">Literally “man’s”</note> anger does not accomplish the righteousness of God.

verses.name: James 1:21
verses.text: Therefore, putting aside all moral uncleanness and wicked excess, welcome<note placement="foot">Or “receive”</note> with humility the implanted message which is able to save your souls.  <div eID="gen27814" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: James 1:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11990"/><div sID="gen27815" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11990"/>But be doers of the message and not hearers only,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “not only hearers”</note> deceiving yourselves,

verses.name: James 1:23
verses.text: because if anyone is a hearer of the message and not a doer, this one is like someone<note placement="foot">Literally “a man,” but clearly in a generic sense here meaning “someone, a person”</note> staring at <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞his own face⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the face of his existence”</note> in a mirror,

verses.name: James 1:24
verses.text: for he looks at himself and goes away and immediately forgets what sort of <transChange type="added">person</transChange> he was.

verses.name: James 1:25
verses.text: But the one who looks into the perfect law of liberty and continues <transChange type="added">to do it</transChange>, not being a forgetful hearer but a doer who acts, this one will be blessed <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞in what he does⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “in his doing”</note>.  <div eID="gen27815" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: James 1:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11991"/><div sID="gen27816" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11991"/>If anyone thinks he is religious, <transChange type="added">although he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“bridle”) which is understood as concessive</note> does not bridle his tongue but deceives his heart, this person’s religion <transChange type="added">is</transChange> worthless.

verses.name: James 1:27
verses.text: Pure and undefiled religion in the sight of our<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> God and Father is this: to look after orphans and widows in their affliction, <transChange type="added">and</transChange> to keep oneself unstained by the world.  <chapter eID="Jas.1"/>

verses.name: James 2:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11992"/><title type="x-s">Partiality Forbidden</title> <div sID="gen27817" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11992"/>My brothers, do not hold your faith in our glorious Lord Jesus Christ with partiality.

verses.name: James 2:2
verses.text: For if someone<note placement="foot">Literally “a man,” but clearly in a generic sense here meaning “someone, a person”</note> enters into your assembly<note placement="foot">Literally “synagogue,” but here probably referring to a Christian assembly</note> in fine clothing with a gold ring on his finger, and a poor person in filthy clothing also enters,

verses.name: James 2:3
verses.text: and you look favorably on the one wearing the fine clothing and you say, “Be seated here in a good place,” and to the poor person you say, “You stand or be seated there<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “you stand there or be seated”</note> by my footstool,”

verses.name: James 2:4
verses.text: have you not made distinctions among yourselves and become judges with evil thoughts?

verses.name: James 2:5
verses.text: Listen, my dear brothers! Did not God choose the poor of the world <transChange type="added">to be</transChange> rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom that he has promised to those who love him?

verses.name: James 2:6
verses.text: But you have dishonored the poor! Are not the rich exploiting you and they themselves dragging you into the courts?

verses.name: James 2:7
verses.text: Do they themselves not blaspheme the good name <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞of the one to whom you belong⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “that was called over you”</note>?  <div eID="gen27817" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: James 2:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11993"/><div sID="gen27818" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11993"/>However, if you carry out the royal law according to the scripture, “You shall love your neighbor as yourself,”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Lev.19.18">Lev 19:18</reference></note> you are doing well.

verses.name: James 2:9
verses.text: But if you show partiality, you commit sin, <transChange type="added">and thus</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and thus” is supplied as a component of the participle (“are convicted”) which is understood as result</note> are convicted by the law as transgressors.

verses.name: James 2:10
verses.text: For whoever keeps the whole law but stumbles in one <transChange type="added">point only</transChange> has become guilty of all <transChange type="added">of it</transChange>.

verses.name: James 2:11
verses.text: For the one who said “Do not commit adultery”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Exod.20.14">Exod 20:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="Deut.5.18">Deut 5:18</reference></note> also said “Do not murder.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Exod.20.13">Exod 20:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="Deut.5.17">Deut 5:17</reference></note> Now if you do not commit adultery but you do murder, you have become a transgressor of the law.

verses.name: James 2:12
verses.text: Thus speak and thus act as those who are going to be judged by the law of liberty.

verses.name: James 2:13
verses.text: For judgment <transChange type="added">is</transChange> merciless to the one who has not practiced mercy. Mercy triumphs over judgment.  <div eID="gen27818" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: James 2:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11994"/><title type="x-s">Faith and Works</title> <div sID="gen27819" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11994"/>What <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the benefit, my brothers, if someone says <transChange type="added">that he</transChange> has faith but does not have works? That faith <transChange type="added">is</transChange> not able to save him, <transChange type="added">is it</transChange>?<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here</note>

verses.name: James 2:15
verses.text: If a brother or a sister is poorly clothed and lacking food for the day,

verses.name: James 2:16
verses.text: and one of you should say to them, “Go in peace, keep warm and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞eat well⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally, “be satisfied”</note>,” but does not give them what is necessary for the body, what <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the benefit?

verses.name: James 2:17
verses.text: Thus also faith, if it does not have works, is dead by itself.  <div eID="gen27819" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: James 2:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11995"/><div sID="gen27820" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11995"/>But someone will say, “You have faith and I have works.”<note placement="foot">Some see the quotation by “someone” extending to the end of v. <reference osisRef="Jas.2.18">18</reference>, while others see it extending through v. <reference osisRef="Jas.2.19">19</reference></note> Show me your faith apart from your<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> works, and I will show you my<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> faith by my works.

verses.name: James 2:19
verses.text: You believe that God is one; you do well. Even the demons believe, and shudder!

verses.name: James 2:20
verses.text: But do you want to know, O foolish person, that faith apart from works is useless?

verses.name: James 2:21
verses.text: Was not Abraham our father justified by works <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“offered up”) which is understood as temporal</note> offered up his son Isaac on the altar?

verses.name: James 2:22
verses.text: You see that faith was working together with his works, and by the works the faith was perfected.

verses.name: James 2:23
verses.text: And the scripture was fulfilled that says, “And Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him for righteousness,”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Gen.15.6">Gen 15:6</reference></note> and he was called God’s friend.

verses.name: James 2:24
verses.text: You see that a person is justified by works and not by faith alone.

verses.name: James 2:25
verses.text: And likewise was not Rahab the prostitute also justified by works <transChange type="added">when she</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“welcomed”) which is understood as temporal</note> welcomed the messengers and sent <transChange type="added">them</transChange> out by a different route?

verses.name: James 2:26
verses.text: For just as the body without the spirit is dead, so also faith without works is dead.  <chapter eID="Jas.2"/>

verses.name: James 3:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11996"/><title type="x-s">Restraining the Tongue</title> <div sID="gen27821" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11996"/>Not many should become teachers, my brothers, <transChange type="added">because you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“know”) which is understood as causal</note> know that we will receive a greater judgment.<note placement="foot">Or “greater condemnation”</note>

verses.name: James 3:2
verses.text: For we all stumble <transChange type="added">in</transChange> many <transChange type="added">ways</transChange>. If anyone does not stumble in what he says, he <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a perfect individual,<note placement="foot">Literally “man,” but clearly in a generic sense here meaning “someone, a person”</note> able to hold in check his whole body also.

verses.name: James 3:3
verses.text: And if we put bits in the mouths of horses so that they obey us, we also guide their whole bodies.

verses.name: James 3:4
verses.text: Behold also ships: <transChange type="added">although they</transChange> are so large and are driven by strong winds, they are guided by a very small rudder wherever the inclination of the pilot wishes.

verses.name: James 3:5
verses.text: So also the tongue is a small member <transChange type="added">of the body</transChange><note placement="foot">*The words “of the body” are not in the Greek text but are supplied for clarity</note> and boasts great <transChange type="added">things</transChange>. Behold how small a fire sets ablaze how great a forest!

verses.name: James 3:6
verses.text: And the tongue <transChange type="added">is</transChange> a fire! The world of unrighteousness,<note placement="foot">Or “a fire, the world of unrighteousness! The tongue is set among our members”</note> the tongue, is set among our members, defiling the whole body and setting on fire <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the course of human existence⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the wheel of origin”</note>, being set on fire by hell.  <div eID="gen27821" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: James 3:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11997"/><div sID="gen27822" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11997"/>For every species of animals and birds, of reptiles and sea creatures, is being tamed and has been tamed by the human species,

verses.name: James 3:8
verses.text: but no human being is able to tame the tongue. <transChange type="added">It is</transChange> a restless evil, full of deadly poison.

verses.name: James 3:9
verses.text: With it we bless the<note placement="foot">*Or possibly “our,” if the Greek article is understood as a possessive pronoun</note> Lord and Father, and with it we curse people who are made in the likeness of God.

verses.name: James 3:10
verses.text: From the same mouth come blessing and cursing. My brothers, these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> ought not to be so!

verses.name: James 3:11
verses.text: A spring does not pour forth from the same opening fresh and bitter <transChange type="added">water, does it</transChange>?<note placement="foot">*The negative construction in Greek anticipates a negative answer here</note>

verses.name: James 3:12
verses.text: A fig tree is not able, my brothers, to produce olives, or a grapevine figs. Neither can a saltwater spring produce fresh water.  <div eID="gen27822" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: James 3:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11998"/><title type="x-s">The Wisdom That Comes Down from Above</title> <div sID="gen27823" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11998"/>Who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> wise and understanding among you? Let him show by his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> good behavior his works, with the humility of wisdom.

verses.name: James 3:14
verses.text: But if you have bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your hearts, do not boast and tell lies against the truth.

verses.name: James 3:15
verses.text: This is not the wisdom that comes down from above, but <transChange type="added">is</transChange> earthly, unspiritual, demonic.

verses.name: James 3:16
verses.text: For where <transChange type="added">there is</transChange> jealousy and selfish ambition, there <transChange type="added">is</transChange> disorder and every evil practice.

verses.name: James 3:17
verses.text: But the wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceful, gentle, obedient, full of mercy and good fruits, nonjudgmental, without hypocrisy,

verses.name: James 3:18
verses.text: And the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace among<note placement="foot">Or “for”; or possibly “by”</note> those who make peace.  <chapter eID="Jas.3"/>

verses.name: James 4:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11999"/><title type="x-s">Subject Yourselves to God</title> <div sID="gen27824" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11999"/>From where <transChange type="added">are</transChange> conflicts and from where <transChange type="added">are</transChange> quarrels among you? <transChange type="added">Is it</transChange> not from this, from your pleasures that wage war among your members?

verses.name: James 4:2
verses.text: You desire and do not have; you murder and are filled with envy, and are not able to obtain; you fight and quarrel. You do not have because you do not ask.

verses.name: James 4:3
verses.text: You ask and do not receive, because you ask with wrong motives, in order that you may spend <transChange type="added">it</transChange> on your pleasures.  <div eID="gen27824" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: James 4:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12000"/><div sID="gen27825" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12000"/>Adulterous people! Do you not know that friendship with the world is enmity with God? Therefore whoever wants to be a friend of the world makes <transChange type="added">himself</transChange> an enemy of God.

verses.name: James 4:5
verses.text: Or do you think that in vain the scripture says, “The spirit which he caused to dwell in us desires jealously”?<note placement="foot">This translation takes “spirit” to be the capacity within people that produces a divided mind and conflicts regarding God; other translations take this to refer to the Holy Spirit: “He (God) jealously desires the Spirit which he caused to dwell in us”</note>

verses.name: James 4:6
verses.text: But he gives greater grace. Therefore it says, <div eID="gen27825" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27826"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27827"/>“God opposes the proud,<l eID="gen27827" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27828"/>but gives grace to the humble.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Prov.3.34">Prov 3:34</reference></note> <l eID="gen27828" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen27826"/>

verses.name: James 4:7
