verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12001"/><div sID="gen27829" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12001"/>Therefore subject yourselves to God. But resist the devil, and he will flee from you.

verses.name: James 4:8
verses.text: Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Cleanse <transChange type="added">your</transChange> hands, <transChange type="added">you</transChange> sinners, and purify <transChange type="added">your</transChange> hearts, <transChange type="added">you</transChange> double-minded!

verses.name: James 4:9
verses.text: Lament and mourn and weep! Let your laughter be turned to mourning, and your<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> joy to gloominess.

verses.name: James 4:10
verses.text: Humble yourselves before the Lord, and he will exalt you.  <div eID="gen27829" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: James 4:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12002"/><div sID="gen27830" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12002"/>Do not speak evil of one another, brothers. The one who speaks evil of a brother or judges his brother speaks evil of the law and judges the law. But if you judge the law, you are not a doer of the law but a judge <transChange type="added">of the law</transChange>.<note placement="foot">The words “of the law” are not in the Greek text, but are an understood repetition from the previous clause</note>

verses.name: James 4:12
verses.text: There is one lawgiver and judge who is able to save and to destroy. But who are you to judge your<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> neighbor?  <div eID="gen27830" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: James 4:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12003"/><title type="x-s">Arrogant Boasting About the Future</title> <div sID="gen27831" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12003"/>Come now, you who say, “Today or tomorrow we will travel to such and such a city and spend a year there, and carry on business and make a profit,”

verses.name: James 4:14
verses.text: you who do not know <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞what will happen tomorrow⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the circumstance of tomorrow”</note>, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞what your life will be like⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “of what sort your life”</note>. For you are a smoky vapor that appears for a short time and then disappears.

verses.name: James 4:15
verses.text: Instead you should say, “If the Lord wills, we will live and do this or that.”

verses.name: James 4:16
verses.text: But now you boast in your arrogance. All such boasting is evil.

verses.name: James 4:17
verses.text: Therefore, to the one who knows to do good and does not do <transChange type="added">it</transChange>, to him it is sin.  <chapter eID="Jas.4"/>

verses.name: James 5:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12004"/><title type="x-s">Woes on the Rich Who Oppress Others</title> <div sID="gen27832" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12004"/>Come now, you rich people, weep <transChange type="added">and</transChange> cry aloud over the miseries that are coming upon you!

verses.name: James 5:2
verses.text: Your wealth has rotted, and your clothing has become moth-eaten.

verses.name: James 5:3
verses.text: Your gold and silver have become corroded, and their corrosion will be a witness against you, and it will consume your flesh like fire. You have stored up treasure in the last days.

verses.name: James 5:4
verses.text: Behold, the wages that were held back by you from the workers who reap your fields cry out, and the cries of the reapers have come to the ears of the Lord of hosts.

verses.name: James 5:5
verses.text: You have lived self-indulgently on the earth<note placement="foot">Or “land”</note> and have lived luxuriously. You have fattened your hearts in the day of slaughter.

verses.name: James 5:6
verses.text: You have condemned, you have murdered the righteous <transChange type="added">person</transChange>; he does not resist you.  <div eID="gen27832" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: James 5:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12005"/><title type="x-s">Exhortation to Patience</title> <div sID="gen27833" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12005"/>Therefore be patient, brothers, until the coming of the Lord. Behold, the farmer waits for the precious fruit of the soil, being patient concerning it until it receives the early and late rains.

verses.name: James 5:8
verses.text: You also be patient. Strengthen your hearts, because the coming of the Lord is near.

verses.name: James 5:9
verses.text: Brothers, do not complain against one another, in order that you may not be judged. Behold, the judge stands before the doors!

verses.name: James 5:10
verses.text: Brothers, take <transChange type="added">as an</transChange> example of perseverance and endurance the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord.

verses.name: James 5:11
verses.text: Behold, we consider blessed those who have endured. You have heard about the patient endurance of Job, and you saw the outcome from the Lord, that the Lord is compassionate and merciful.

verses.name: James 5:12
verses.text: Now above all, my brothers, do not swear either by heaven or by earth or by any other oath, but let your yes be yes and your no, no, in order that you may not fall under judgment.  <div eID="gen27833" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: James 5:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12006"/><title type="x-s">The Effective Prayer of Faith</title> <div sID="gen27834" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12006"/>Is anyone among you suffering misfortune? He should pray. Is anyone cheerful? He should sing praise.

verses.name: James 5:14
verses.text: Is anyone among you sick? He should summon the elders of the church and they should pray over him, anointing him with olive oil in the name of the Lord.

verses.name: James 5:15
verses.text: And the prayer of faith will save the one who is sick, and the Lord will raise him up, and if he has committed sins <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he will be forgiven⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “it will be forgiven him”</note>.

verses.name: James 5:16
verses.text: Therefore confess your sins to one another, and pray for one another, so that you may be healed. The effective prayer of a righteous person accomplishes much.

verses.name: James 5:17
verses.text: Elijah was a human being<note placement="foot">Literally “man,” but in a generic sense; the emphasis is not on Elijah’s masculine gender but his shared humanity</note> with the same nature as us, and <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he prayed fervently⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “he prayed with prayer”</note> for <transChange type="added">it</transChange> not to rain, and it did not rain on the land <transChange type="added">for</transChange> three years and six months.

verses.name: James 5:18
verses.text: And he prayed again, and the sky gave rain and the earth produced its fruit.  <div eID="gen27834" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: James 5:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12007"/><div sID="gen27835" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12007"/>My brothers, if anyone among you should wander away from the truth and someone turns him back,

verses.name: James 5:20
verses.text: he should know that the one who turns a sinner back from the error of his way will save that person’s<note placement="foot">Literally “his,” but in context this refers to the sinner, not the person who turns the sinner back</note> soul from death, and will cover over a great number of sins.  <chapter eID="Jas.5"/> <div eID="gen27835" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen27807" osisID="Jas" type="book"/>

verses.name: I Peter 1:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12008"/><title type="x-s">Greeting</title> <div sID="gen27837" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12008"/>Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the chosen<note placement="foot">Or “elect”</note> who are residing temporarily in the dispersion in Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia,

verses.name: I Peter 1:2
verses.text: according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, by the sanctification of the Spirit, for obedience and <transChange type="added">for</transChange> sprinkling with the blood of Jesus Christ. May grace and peace be multiplied to you.  <div eID="gen27837" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Peter 1:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12009"/><title type="x-s">A New Birth to a Living Hope</title> <div sID="gen27838" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12009"/>Blessed <transChange type="added">be</transChange> the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to his great mercy has caused us to be born again to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,

verses.name: I Peter 1:4
verses.text: into an inheritance imperishable and undefiled and unfading, reserved in heaven for you

verses.name: I Peter 1:5
verses.text: who are being protected by the power of God through faith for a salvation ready to be revealed in the last time,

verses.name: I Peter 1:6
verses.text: in which you rejoice greatly, <transChange type="added">although</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“are distressed”) which is understood as concessive</note> now for a short time, if necessary,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “if it is necessary”</note> you are distressed by various trials,

verses.name: I Peter 1:7
verses.text: so that the genuineness of your faith, more valuable than gold that is passing away, but is tested by fire, may be found to <transChange type="added">result in</transChange> praise and glory and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ,

verses.name: I Peter 1:8
verses.text: whom, <transChange type="added">although you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“seen”) which is understood as concessive</note> have not seen, you love; in whom now you believe, although you<note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“see”) which is understood as concessive</note> do not see <transChange type="added">him</transChange>, and you rejoice greatly with joy inexpressible and full of glory,

verses.name: I Peter 1:9
verses.text: obtaining the goal of your faith, the salvation of <transChange type="added">your</transChange><note placement="foot">*This is an understood repetition of the previous “your”</note> souls.  <div eID="gen27838" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Peter 1:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12010"/><div sID="gen27839" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12010"/>Concerning this<note placement="foot">Literally “which”</note> salvation, the prophets who prophesied about the grace meant for you sought and made careful inquiry,

verses.name: I Peter 1:11
verses.text: investigating for what <transChange type="added">person</transChange> or which time the Spirit of Christ in them was indicating <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“testified beforehand”) which is understood as temporal</note> testified beforehand to the sufferings with reference to Christ and the glories after these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>,

verses.name: I Peter 1:12
verses.text: to whom it was revealed that they were serving not themselves but you with reference to the same <transChange type="added">things</transChange> which now have been announced to you through those who proclaimed the gospel to you by the Holy Spirit sent from heaven, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞things into which⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “into which things”</note> angels desire to look.  <div eID="gen27839" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Peter 1:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12011"/><title type="x-s">Be Holy in All Your Conduct</title> <div sID="gen27840" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12011"/>Therefore, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞when you have prepared your minds for action⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “having girded up the loins of your mind”</note> by<note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“being self-controlled”) which is understood as means</note> being self-controlled, put your hope completely in the grace that will be brought to you at the revelation of Jesus Christ.

verses.name: I Peter 1:14
verses.text: As obedient children, do not be conformed to the former desires <transChange type="added">you used to conform to</transChange><note placement="foot">*This is an understood repetition of the earlier verb “be conformed to”</note> in your ignorance,

verses.name: I Peter 1:15
verses.text: but as the one who called you <transChange type="added">is</transChange> holy, <transChange type="added">you</transChange> yourselves be holy in all <transChange type="added">your</transChange> conduct,

verses.name: I Peter 1:16
verses.text: for it is written, “You will be holy, because I <transChange type="added">am</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here the verb is understood in Greek and is supplied in the translation</note> holy.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Lev.19.2">Lev 19:2</reference></note><note placement="foot">Some manuscripts explicitly state “I am holy”</note>

verses.name: I Peter 1:17
verses.text: And if you call on <transChange type="added">him</transChange> <transChange type="added">as</transChange> Father who judges impartially according to each one’s work, conduct yourselves with fear during the time of your temporary residence,

verses.name: I Peter 1:18
verses.text: <transChange type="added">because you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“know”) which is understood as causal</note> know that you were redeemed from your futile way of life inherited from your ancestors not with perishable things like silver or gold,

verses.name: I Peter 1:19
verses.text: but with the precious blood of Christ, like <transChange type="added">that of</transChange> an unblemished and spotless lamb

verses.name: I Peter 1:20
verses.text: who was foreknown before the foundation of the world, but has been revealed in these last times for you

verses.name: I Peter 1:21
verses.text: who through him <transChange type="added">are</transChange> believing in God, who raised him from the dead and gave him glory, so that your faith and hope are in God.  <div eID="gen27840" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Peter 1:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12012"/><div sID="gen27841" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12012"/>Having purified your souls by your obedience to the truth for sincere brotherly love, love one another fervently from the heart,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “from a pure heart”</note>

verses.name: I Peter 1:23
verses.text: <transChange type="added">because you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“have been born again”) which is understood as causal</note> have been born again, not from perishable seed but imperishable, through the living and enduring word of God.

verses.name: I Peter 1:24
verses.text: For <div eID="gen27841" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27842"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27843"/>“all flesh <transChange type="added">is</transChange> like grass,<l eID="gen27843" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27844"/>and all its glory like the flower of the grass.<l eID="gen27844" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27845"/>The grass withers and the flower falls off, <l eID="gen27845" level="1"/>

verses.name: I Peter 1:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12013"/><l level="2" sID="gen27846"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12013"/>but the word of the Lord endures <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for the age”</note>.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.40.6">Isa 40:6</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.40.8">8</reference></note><l eID="gen27846" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen27842"/> <div sID="gen27847" type="x-p"/> And this is the word that has been proclaimed to you.  <chapter eID="1Pet.1"/>

verses.name: I Peter 2:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12014"/><title type="x-s">Chosen as Living Stones</title> <div sID="gen27848" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12014"/>Therefore, ridding yourselves of all malice and all deceit and hypocrisy and envy and all slander,

verses.name: I Peter 2:2
verses.text: like newborn infants long for the unadulterated spiritual milk, so that by it you may grow up to salvation,

verses.name: I Peter 2:3
verses.text: if you have tasted that the Lord <transChange type="added">is</transChange> kind,<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.34.8">Ps 34:8</reference></note>

verses.name: I Peter 2:4
verses.text: to whom you are drawing near, a living stone rejected by men but chosen <transChange type="added">and</transChange> precious in the sight of God.

verses.name: I Peter 2:5
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">you</transChange> yourselves, as living stones, are being built up <transChange type="added">as</transChange> a spiritual house for a holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.

verses.name: I Peter 2:6
verses.text: For it stands in scripture, <div eID="gen27848" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27849"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27850"/>“Behold, I am laying in Zion a stone, a chosen <transChange type="added">and</transChange> precious cornerstone,<l eID="gen27850" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27851"/>and the one who believes in him will never be put to shame.”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.28.16">Isa 28:16</reference></note> <l eID="gen27851" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen27849"/>

verses.name: I Peter 2:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12015"/><div sID="gen27852" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12015"/>Therefore the honor <transChange type="added">is</transChange> for you who believe, but for those who refuse to believe, <div eID="gen27852" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27853"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27854"/>“The stone that the builders rejected,<l eID="gen27854" level="1"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27855"/>this one has become <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the cornerstone⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “into the head of the corner”</note>,” <l eID="gen27855" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen27853"/>

verses.name: I Peter 2:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12016"/><div sID="gen27856" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12016"/>and <div eID="gen27856" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27857"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27858"/>“A stone of stumbling and a rock of offense,”<note placement="foot">A quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.8.14">Isa 8:14</reference></note><l eID="gen27858" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen27857"/> <div sID="gen27859" type="x-p"/> who stumble <transChange type="added">because they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“disobey”) which is understood as causal</note> disobey the word to which also they were consigned.

verses.name: I Peter 2:9
verses.text: But you <transChange type="added">are</transChange> a chosen race,<note placement="foot">Or “people,” or “generation,” or “nation”</note> a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for <transChange type="added">God’s</transChange> possession, so that you may proclaim the virtues of the one who called you out of darkness into his marvelous light,

verses.name: I Peter 2:10
verses.text: who once <transChange type="added">were</transChange> not a people, but now <transChange type="added">are</transChange> the people of God, the ones <transChange type="added">who were</transChange> not shown mercy, but now are shown mercy.<note placement="foot">This verse contains quotations from <reference osisRef="Hos.1.6">Hos 1:6</reference>, <reference osisRef="Hos.1.9">9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Hos.2.23">2:23</reference></note>  <div eID="gen27859" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Peter 2:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12017"/><div sID="gen27860" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12017"/>Dear friends, I urge <transChange type="added">you</transChange> as foreigners and temporary residents to abstain from fleshly desires which wage war against your<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> soul,

verses.name: I Peter 2:12
verses.text: maintaining your good conduct among the Gentiles, so that in <transChange type="added">the things</transChange> in which they slander you as evildoers, by seeing your good deeds they may glorify God on the day of visitation.  <div eID="gen27860" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Peter 2:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12018"/><title type="x-s">Submission to Established Authority</title> <div sID="gen27861" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12018"/>Subject yourselves to every human authority for the sake of the Lord, whether to a king<note placement="foot">Or “to the emperor”</note> as having supreme authority,

verses.name: I Peter 2:14
verses.text: or to governors as those sent out by him for the punishment of those who do evil and the praise of those who do good.

verses.name: I Peter 2:15
verses.text: For the will of God is as follows: <transChange type="added">by</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“doing good”) which is understood as means</note> doing good to silence the ignorance of foolish people.

verses.name: I Peter 2:16
verses.text: <transChange type="added">Live</transChange> as free <transChange type="added">persons</transChange>, and not using your<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> freedom as a covering for evil, but as slaves of God.

verses.name: I Peter 2:17
verses.text: Honor all <transChange type="added">people</transChange>, love the community of believers, fear God, honor the king.<note placement="foot">Or “the emperor”</note>  <div eID="gen27861" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Peter 2:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12019"/><div sID="gen27862" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12019"/>Domestic slaves, be subject to your<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> masters with all respect, not only to those <transChange type="added">who are</transChange> good and gentle, but also to those <transChange type="added">who are</transChange> unjust.

verses.name: I Peter 2:19
verses.text: For this <transChange type="added">finds</transChange> favor, if because of consciousness of God someone endures sorrows <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the participle (“suffering”) which is understood as temporal</note> suffering unjustly.

verses.name: I Peter 2:20
verses.text: For what credit <transChange type="added">is it</transChange> if, <transChange type="added">when you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“sin”) which is understood as temporal</note> sin and are beaten for it, you endure? But if you endure when you<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“do good”) which is understood as temporal</note> do good and suffer <transChange type="added">for it</transChange>, this <transChange type="added">finds</transChange> favor with God.

verses.name: I Peter 2:21
verses.text: For to this you were called, because Christ also suffered for you, leaving you an example, so that you should follow in his footsteps,

verses.name: I Peter 2:22
verses.text: who did not commit sin, nor was deceit found in his mouth,<note placement="foot">This verse contains quotations from <reference osisRef="Isa.53.9">Isa 53:9</reference></note>

verses.name: I Peter 2:23
verses.text: who <transChange type="added">when he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“was reviled”) which is understood as temporal</note> was reviled, did not revile in return; when<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“suffering”) which is understood as temporal</note> suffering, he did not threaten, but entrusted <transChange type="added">himself</transChange> to the one who judges justly,

verses.name: I Peter 2:24
verses.text: who himself bore our sins in his body on the tree, so that <transChange type="added">we</transChange> may die to sins <transChange type="added">and</transChange> live to righteousness, by whose wounds you were healed.

verses.name: I Peter 2:25
verses.text: For you were going astray like sheep, but you have turned back now to the shepherd and guardian of your souls.  <chapter eID="1Pet.2"/>

verses.name: I Peter 3:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12020"/><title type="x-s">Wives and Husbands</title> <div sID="gen27863" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12020"/>In the same way, wives, be subject to your own husbands, so that even if some are disobedient to the word, they may be won over without a word by the conduct of their wives,

verses.name: I Peter 3:2
verses.text: <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“see”) which is understood as temporal</note> see your respectful, pure conduct.

verses.name: I Peter 3:3
verses.text: Let your<note placement="foot">Literally “of whom,” referring to the wives</note> adornment not be the external <transChange type="added">kind</transChange>, braiding hair and putting on gold jewelry or putting on <transChange type="added">fine</transChange> clothing,

verses.name: I Peter 3:4
verses.text: but the hidden person of the heart, with the imperishable <transChange type="added">quality</transChange> of a gentle and quiet spirit, which is highly valuable in the sight of God.

verses.name: I Peter 3:5
verses.text: For in the <transChange type="added">same</transChange> way formerly the holy women also, who hoped in God, used to adorn themselves <transChange type="added">by</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“being subject”) which is understood as means</note> being subject to their own husbands,

verses.name: I Peter 3:6
verses.text: like Sarah obeyed Abraham, calling him lord, whose children you have become <transChange type="added">when you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“do good”) which is understood as temporal</note> do good and are not frightened with respect to any terror.  <div eID="gen27863" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Peter 3:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12021"/><div sID="gen27864" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12021"/>Husbands, in the same way live with <transChange type="added">your wives</transChange> <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞knowledgeably⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “according to knowledge”</note>, as with the weaker female vessel, showing <transChange type="added">them</transChange> honor as fellow heirs also of the grace of life, so that your prayers will not be hindered.  <div eID="gen27864" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Peter 3:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12022"/><title type="x-s">Called to Inherit a Blessing</title> <div sID="gen27865" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12022"/>And finally, all <transChange type="added">of you be</transChange> harmonious, sympathetic, showing mutual affection, compassionate, humble,

verses.name: I Peter 3:9
verses.text: not repaying evil for evil or insult for insult, but on the other hand blessing <transChange type="added">others</transChange>, because for this <transChange type="added">reason</transChange> you were called, so that you could inherit a blessing.

verses.name: I Peter 3:10
verses.text: For <div eID="gen27865" type="x-p"/> <lg sID="gen27866"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27867"/>“The one who wants to love life<l eID="gen27867" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27868"/>and see good days<l eID="gen27868" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27869"/>must keep his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> tongue from evil<l eID="gen27869" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27870"/>and <transChange type="added">his</transChange> lips must not speak deceit. <l eID="gen27870" level="2"/>

verses.name: I Peter 3:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12023"/><l level="1" sID="gen27871"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12023"/>And he must turn away from evil and do good;<l eID="gen27871" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27872"/>he must seek peace and pursue it. <l eID="gen27872" level="2"/>

verses.name: I Peter 3:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12024"/><l level="1" sID="gen27873"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12024"/>For the eyes of the Lord <transChange type="added">are</transChange> on the righteous,<l eID="gen27873" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27874"/>and his ears <transChange type="added">are open to</transChange> their prayer.<l eID="gen27874" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27875"/>But the face of the Lord <transChange type="added">is</transChange> against those who do evil.<note placement="foot">Verses <reference osisRef="1Pet.3.10-1Pet.3.12">10–12</reference> are a quotation from <reference osisRef="Ps.34.12-Ps.34.16">Ps 34:12–16</reference></note> <l eID="gen27875" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen27866"/>

verses.name: I Peter 3:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12025"/><title type="x-s">Suffer for Doing What is Good</title> <div sID="gen27876" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12025"/>And who <transChange type="added">is</transChange> the one who will harm you if you are a zealous adherent for what is good?

verses.name: I Peter 3:14
verses.text: But even if you might suffer for the sake of righteousness, <transChange type="added">you are</transChange> blessed. And do not be afraid of their intimidation or be disturbed,<note placement="foot">The second half of this verse contains a quotation from <reference osisRef="Isa.8.12">Isa 8:12</reference></note>

verses.name: I Peter 3:15
verses.text: but set Christ apart <transChange type="added">as</transChange> Lord in your hearts, always ready to <transChange type="added">make</transChange> a defense to anyone who asks you <transChange type="added">for</transChange> an accounting concerning the hope <transChange type="added">that is</transChange> in you.

verses.name: I Peter 3:16
verses.text: But <transChange type="added">do so</transChange> with courtesy and respect, having a good conscience, so that in <transChange type="added">the things</transChange> in which you are slandered, the ones who malign your good conduct in Christ may be put to shame.

verses.name: I Peter 3:17
verses.text: For <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> better to suffer for doing good, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞if God wills it⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “if the will of God wills”</note>, than for doing evil.  <div eID="gen27876" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Peter 3:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12026"/><lg sID="gen27877"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27878"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12026"/>For Christ also suffered once for sins,<l eID="gen27878" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27879"/>the just for the unjust,<l eID="gen27879" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27880"/>in order that he could bring you to God,<l eID="gen27880" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen27881"/>being put to death in the flesh,<l eID="gen27881" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen27882"/>but made alive in the spirit, <l eID="gen27882" level="1"/>

verses.name: I Peter 3:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12027"/><l level="1" sID="gen27883"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12027"/>in which also he went <transChange type="added">and</transChange> proclaimed to the spirits in prison, <l eID="gen27883" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen27877"/>

verses.name: I Peter 3:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12028"/><div sID="gen27884" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12028"/>who were formerly disobedient, when the patience of God waited in the days of Noah, <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was being constructed”)</note> an ark was being constructed, in which a few—that is, eight souls—were rescued through water.

verses.name: I Peter 3:21
verses.text: And<note placement="foot">Literally “which”</note> also, corresponding to <transChange type="added">this</transChange>, baptism now saves you, not the removal of dirt from the flesh, but an appeal to God for a good conscience through the resurrection of Jesus Christ,

verses.name: I Peter 3:22
verses.text: who is at the right hand of God, having gone into heaven, with angels and authorities and powers having been subjected to him.  <chapter eID="1Pet.3"/>

verses.name: I Peter 4:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12029"/><title type="x-s">The Time for Behaving Like the Gentiles is Past</title> <div sID="gen27885" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12029"/>Therefore, <transChange type="added">because</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“suffered”) which is understood as causal</note> Christ suffered in the flesh, you also equip yourselves with the same way of thinking, because the one who has suffered in the flesh has ceased from sin,

verses.name: I Peter 4:2
verses.text: in order to live the remaining time in the flesh no longer for human desires, but for the will of God.

verses.name: I Peter 4:3
verses.text: For the time that has passed <transChange type="added">was</transChange> sufficient <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to do what the Gentiles desire to do⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to do the intention of the Gentiles”</note>, having lived in licentiousness, <transChange type="added">evil</transChange> desires, drunkenness, carousing, drinking parties, and wanton idolatries,

verses.name: I Peter 4:4
verses.text: with respect to which they are surprised <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“run with”) which is understood as temporal</note> you do not run with them into the same flood of dissipation, and so they<note placement="foot">*Here “and so” is supplied as a component of the participle (“revile”) which is understood as result</note> revile <transChange type="added">you</transChange>.

verses.name: I Peter 4:5
verses.text: They<note placement="foot">Literally “who”</note> will give an account to the one who is ready to judge the living and the dead.

verses.name: I Peter 4:6
verses.text: Because for this reason also the gospel was preached to those who are dead, so that they were judged <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞by human standards⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “according to men”</note> in the flesh, but they may live in the spirit <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞by God’s standards⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “according to God”</note>.  <div eID="gen27885" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Peter 4:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12030"/><title type="x-s">Serving to the Glory of God</title> <div sID="gen27886" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12030"/>Now the end of all <transChange type="added">things</transChange> draws near. Therefore be self-controlled and sober-minded for <transChange type="added">your</transChange> prayers.

verses.name: I Peter 4:8
verses.text: Above all, keep<note placement="foot">Literally “having”</note> your love for one another constant, because love covers a large number of sins.

verses.name: I Peter 4:9
verses.text: <transChange type="added">Be</transChange> hospitable to one another without complaining.

verses.name: I Peter 4:10
verses.text: Just as each one has received a gift, <transChange type="added">use</transChange> it for serving one another, as good stewards of the varied grace of God.

verses.name: I Peter 4:11
verses.text: If anyone speaks, <transChange type="added">let it be</transChange> as the oracles of God; if anyone serves, <transChange type="added">let it be</transChange> as by the strength that God provides, so that in all <transChange type="added">things</transChange> God will be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom is the glory and the power <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever and ever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for the ages of the ages”</note>. Amen.  <div eID="gen27886" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Peter 4:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12031"/><title type="x-s">Sharing the Sufferings of Christ</title> <div sID="gen27887" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12031"/>Dear friends, do not be surprised at the fiery ordeal among you, <transChange type="added">when it</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“takes place”) which is understood as temporal</note> takes place to test you, as <transChange type="added">if</transChange> <transChange type="added">something</transChange> strange were happening to you.

verses.name: I Peter 4:13
verses.text: But to the degree that you share in the sufferings of Christ, rejoice, so that also at the revelation of his glory you may rejoice <transChange type="added">and</transChange> be glad.

verses.name: I Peter 4:14
verses.text: If you are reviled on account of the name of Christ, <transChange type="added">you are</transChange> blessed, because the Spirit of glory and of God rests on you.

verses.name: I Peter 4:15
verses.text: By all means do not let anyone of you suffer as a murderer or a thief or an evildoer or as a meddler.

verses.name: I Peter 4:16
verses.text: But if <transChange type="added">someone suffers</transChange> as a Christian, he must not be ashamed, but must glorify God with this name.

verses.name: I Peter 4:17
verses.text: For <transChange type="added">it is</transChange> the time for the judgment to begin out from the household of God. But if <transChange type="added">it begins</transChange> out from us first, what will be the outcome for those who are disobedient to the gospel of God?

verses.name: I Peter 4:18
verses.text: And if the righteous are saved with difficulty, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞what will become of the ungodly and the sinner⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the ungodly and sinner where will he appear”</note>?<note placement="foot">This verse contains a quotation from <reference osisRef="Prov.11.31">Prov 11:31</reference></note>

verses.name: I Peter 4:19
verses.text: So then also those who suffer according to the will of God must entrust their souls to a faithful Creator in doing good.  <chapter eID="1Pet.4"/>

verses.name: I Peter 5:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12032"/><title type="x-s">Leadership and Humility</title> <div sID="gen27888" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12032"/>Therefore <transChange type="added">I, your</transChange> fellow elder and a witness of the sufferings of Christ, <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*The conjunction “and” is supplied here to make it clear that the following phrase refers also to the author of the letter and not to Christ</note> also a sharer of the glory that is going to be revealed, exhort the elders among you:

verses.name: I Peter 5:2
verses.text: shepherd the flock of God among you, exercising oversight not by compulsion but willingly, in accordance with God, and not greedily but eagerly,

verses.name: I Peter 5:3
verses.text: and not as lording it over <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞those under your care⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the portion”</note>, but being examples for the flock.

verses.name: I Peter 5:4
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“appears”)</note> the chief Shepherd appears, you will receive the unfading crown of glory.  <div eID="gen27888" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Peter 5:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12033"/><div sID="gen27889" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12033"/>In the same way, younger men, be subject to the elders, and all <transChange type="added">of you</transChange> clothe yourselves with humility toward one another, because God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble.

verses.name: I Peter 5:6
verses.text: Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, so that he may exalt you at the <transChange type="added">right</transChange> time,

verses.name: I Peter 5:7
verses.text: casting all your cares on him, because <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞he cares⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “it is a care to him”</note> for you.  <div eID="gen27889" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Peter 5:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12034"/><div sID="gen27890" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12034"/>Be sober; be on the alert. Your adversary the devil walks around like a roaring lion, looking for someone to devour.

verses.name: I Peter 5:9
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞Resist him⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to whom resist”</note>, steadfast in your<note placement="foot">Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> faith, because you<note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“know”) which is understood as causal</note> know the same <transChange type="added">kinds</transChange> of sufferings are being accomplished by your community of believers in the world.

verses.name: I Peter 5:10
verses.text: And the God of all grace, who called you to his eternal glory in Christ,<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “in Christ Jesus”</note> after you<note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“have suffered”) which is understood as temporal</note> have suffered for a short time, will himself restore, confirm, strengthen, <transChange type="added">and</transChange> establish <transChange type="added">you</transChange>.

verses.name: I Peter 5:11
verses.text: To him <transChange type="added">be</transChange> the power <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever and ever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to the ages of the ages”</note>.<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “forever” (literally “to the ages”)</note> Amen.  <div eID="gen27890" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Peter 5:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12035"/><title type="x-s">Conclusion and Final Greetings</title> <div sID="gen27891" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12035"/>Through Silvanus, the faithful brother (as I consider <transChange type="added">him</transChange>), I have written to you <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞briefly⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “by a few”</note> to encourage <transChange type="added">you</transChange> and to attest that this is the true grace of God. Stand firm in it.

verses.name: I Peter 5:13
verses.text: She <transChange type="added">who is</transChange> in Babylon, chosen the same as <transChange type="added">you</transChange>, greets you, and <transChange type="added">so does</transChange> my son Mark.

verses.name: I Peter 5:14
verses.text: Greet one another with a loving kiss. Peace to all of you who are in Christ.  <chapter eID="1Pet.5"/> <div eID="gen27891" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen27836" osisID="1Pet" type="book"/>

verses.name: II Peter 1:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12036"/><title type="x-s">Greeting</title> <div sID="gen27893" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12036"/>Simeon Peter, a slave and apostle of Jesus Christ, to those who have obtained a faith equal in value to ours by the righteousness of our God and Savior Jesus Christ.

verses.name: II Peter 1:2
verses.text: May grace and peace be multiplied to you in the knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord,

verses.name: II Peter 1:3
verses.text: because his divine power has bestowed on us all <transChange type="added">things</transChange> <transChange type="added">that are</transChange> necessary for life and godliness, through the knowledge of the one who called us by his own glory and excellence of character,

verses.name: II Peter 1:4
verses.text: through which things he has bestowed on us his precious and very great promises, so that through these you may become sharers of the divine nature <transChange type="added">after</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“escaping from”) which is understood as temporal</note> escaping from the corruption <transChange type="added">that is</transChange> in the world because of evil desire,

verses.name: II Peter 1:5
verses.text: and <transChange type="added">for</transChange> this same <transChange type="added">reason</transChange>, and <transChange type="added">by</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“applying”) which is understood as means</note> applying all diligence, supply with your faith excellence of character, and with excellence of character, knowledge,

verses.name: II Peter 1:6
verses.text: and with knowledge, self-control, and with self-control, patient endurance, and with patient endurance, godliness,

verses.name: II Peter 1:7
verses.text: and with godliness, brotherly love, and with brotherly love, love.  <div eID="gen27893" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Peter 1:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12037"/><title type="x-s">Make Your Calling and Election Secure</title> <div sID="gen27894" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12037"/>For <transChange type="added">if</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “if” is supplied as a component of the participle (“are”) which is understood as conditional</note> these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> are yours and are increasing, this does not make <transChange type="added">you</transChange> useless or unproductive in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.name: II Peter 1:9
verses.text: For <transChange type="added">the one</transChange> for whom these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> <transChange type="added">are</transChange> not present is blind, being nearsighted, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞having forgotten the cleansing⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “receiving forgetfulness of the cleansing”</note> of his former sins.

verses.name: II Peter 1:10
verses.text: Therefore, brothers, be zealous even more to make your calling and election secure, because <transChange type="added">if you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “if” is supplied as a component of the participle (“do”) which is understood as conditional</note> do these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, you will never ever stumble.

verses.name: II Peter 1:11
verses.text: For in this way entrance into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ will be richly supplied for you.  <div eID="gen27894" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Peter 1:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12038"/><div sID="gen27895" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12038"/>Therefore I intend to remind you continually concerning these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, although <transChange type="added">you</transChange> know <transChange type="added">them</transChange> and are established in the truth that you have.

verses.name: II Peter 1:13
verses.text: But I consider <transChange type="added">it</transChange> right, for as long as I am in this habitation, to stir you up by a reminder,

verses.name: II Peter 1:14
verses.text: <transChange type="added">because I</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“know”) which is understood as causal</note> know that the removal of my habitation is imminent, as indeed our Lord Jesus Christ made clear to me.

verses.name: II Peter 1:15
verses.text: And I will also make every effort <transChange type="added">that</transChange> you are able at any time, after my departure, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞to recall these things to mind⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “to make recollection of these”</note>.  <div eID="gen27895" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Peter 1:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12039"/><title type="x-s">The Reliable Prophetic Word of Testimony</title> <div sID="gen27896" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12039"/>For we did not make known to you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ <transChange type="added">by</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“following”) which is understood as means</note> following ingeniously concocted myths, but by<note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“being”) which is understood as means</note> being eyewitnesses of that one’s majesty.

verses.name: II Peter 1:17
verses.text: For <transChange type="added">he</transChange> received honor and glory from God the Father <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the temporal genitive absolute participle (“was brought”)</note> a voice such as this was brought to him by the Majestic Glory, “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.”

verses.name: II Peter 1:18
verses.text: And <transChange type="added">we</transChange> ourselves heard this voice brought from heaven <transChange type="added">when we</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“were”) which is understood as temporal</note> were with him on the holy mountain,

verses.name: II Peter 1:19
verses.text: and we possess <transChange type="added">as</transChange> more reliable the prophetic word, to which you do well <transChange type="added">if you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “if” is supplied as a component of the participle (“pay attention to”) which is understood as conditional</note> pay attention to <transChange type="added">it</transChange> as to a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts,

verses.name: II Peter 1:20
verses.text: recognizing this above all, that every prophecy of scripture does not come about from one’s own interpretation,

verses.name: II Peter 1:21
verses.text: for no prophecy was ever produced by the will of man, but men carried along by the Holy Spirit spoke from God.  <chapter eID="2Pet.1"/>

verses.name: II Peter 2:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12040"/><title type="x-s">The Rise and Fall of the False Teachers</title> <div sID="gen27897" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12040"/>But there were also false prophets among the people, as there will be false teachers among you also, who will bring in <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞destructive heresies⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “heresies of destruction”</note>, even denying the Master who bought them, thus<note placement="foot">*Here “thus” is supplied as a component of the participle (“bringing on”) which is understood as result</note> bringing on themselves swift destruction.

verses.name: II Peter 2:2
verses.text: And many will follow their licentious ways, because of whom the way of truth will be reviled.

verses.name: II Peter 2:3
verses.text: And in greediness they will exploit you with false words, whose condemnation <transChange type="added">from</transChange> long ago is not idle, and their destruction is not asleep.  <div eID="gen27897" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Peter 2:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12041"/><div sID="gen27898" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12041"/>For if God did not spare the angels who sinned, but held <transChange type="added">them</transChange> captive in Tartarus with chains of darkness <transChange type="added">and</transChange> handed <transChange type="added">them</transChange> over to be kept for judgment,

verses.name: II Peter 2:5
verses.text: and did not spare the ancient world, but preserved Noah, a proclaimer of righteousness, <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞and seven others⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “eighth”</note> when he<note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“brought”) which is understood as temporal</note> brought a flood on the world of the ungodly,

verses.name: II Peter 2:6
verses.text: and condemned the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah to destruction, reducing them to ashes, having appointed <transChange type="added">them</transChange> <transChange type="added">as</transChange> an example for those who are going to be ungodly,

verses.name: II Peter 2:7
verses.text: and rescued righteous Lot, worn down by the way of life of lawless persons in licentiousness

verses.name: II Peter 2:8
verses.text: (for that righteous man, <transChange type="added">as he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“lived”) which is understood as temporal</note> lived among them day after day, was tormenting <transChange type="added">his</transChange> righteous soul by the lawless deeds <transChange type="added">he was</transChange> seeing and hearing),

verses.name: II Peter 2:9
verses.text: <transChange type="added">then</transChange> the Lord knows how to rescue the godly from trials and to reserve the unrighteous to be punished at<note placement="foot">Or “until”</note> the day of judgment,

verses.name: II Peter 2:10
verses.text: and especially those who go after the flesh in defiling lust<note placement="foot">Literally “in lust of defilement,” translated here as an attributive genitive</note> and who despise authority. <div eID="gen27898" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen27899" type="x-p"/> Bold <transChange type="added">and</transChange> arrogant, they do not tremble in awe <transChange type="added">as they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“blaspheme”) which is understood as temporal</note> blaspheme majestic beings,

verses.name: II Peter 2:11
verses.text: whereas angels, who are greater in strength and power, do not bring against them a demeaning judgment.<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “a demeaning judgment from the Lord”</note>

verses.name: II Peter 2:12
verses.text: But these persons, like irrational animals born <transChange type="added">only with</transChange> natural <transChange type="added">instincts</transChange> for capture and killing, blaspheming <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞about things⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “with reference to which”</note> they do not understand, in their destruction will also be destroyed,

verses.name: II Peter 2:13
verses.text: being harmed <transChange type="added">as the</transChange> wages of unrighteousness. Considering reveling in the daytime a pleasure, <transChange type="added">they are</transChange> stains and blemishes, carousing in their deceitful pleasures <transChange type="added">when they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“feast together”) which is understood as temporal</note> feast together with you,

verses.name: II Peter 2:14
verses.text: having eyes full of <transChange type="added">desire for</transChange> an adulteress and unceasing from sin, enticing unstable persons, <transChange type="added">and</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “and” is supplied in keeping with English style</note> having hearts trained for greediness. Accursed children!

verses.name: II Peter 2:15
verses.text: <transChange type="added">By</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“leaving”) which is understood as means</note> leaving the straight path, they have gone astray, because they<note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“followed”) which is understood as causal</note> followed the way of Balaam the son of Bosor,<note placement="foot">Although some English versions use “Beor” here, this is due to harmonization with the Old Testament; the vast majority of Greek manuscripts read “Bosor” here</note> who loved the wages of unrighteousness,

verses.name: II Peter 2:16
verses.text: but received a rebuke for his own lawlessness: a speechless donkey, speaking with a human voice, restrained <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞the prophet’s madness⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “the of the prophet madness”</note>.  <div eID="gen27899" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Peter 2:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12042"/><div sID="gen27900" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12042"/>These <transChange type="added">people</transChange> are waterless springs and mists driven by a hurricane, for whom the gloom of darkness has been reserved.

verses.name: II Peter 2:18
verses.text: <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞For by speaking high-sounding but empty words⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for speaking pompous words of emptiness”</note>, they entice with desires of the flesh <transChange type="added">and</transChange> with licentiousness those who are scarcely escaping from those who live in error,

verses.name: II Peter 2:19
verses.text: promising them freedom <transChange type="added">although they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “although” is supplied as a component of the participle (“are”) which is understood as concessive</note> themselves are slaves of depravity. For to whatever someone succumbs, by this he is also<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts omit “also”</note> enslaved.

verses.name: II Peter 2:20
verses.text: For if, <transChange type="added">after they</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“have escaped from”) which is understood as temporal</note> have escaped from the defilements of the world through the knowledge of the Lord<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “of our Lord”</note> and Savior Jesus Christ, and they are again entangled in these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> <transChange type="added">and</transChange> succumb to <transChange type="added">them</transChange>, the last <transChange type="added">state</transChange> has become worse for them than the first.

verses.name: II Peter 2:21
verses.text: For it would have been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness than having known <transChange type="added">it</transChange>, to turn back from the holy commandment that had been delivered to them.

verses.name: II Peter 2:22
verses.text: The <transChange type="added">statement</transChange> of the true proverb has happened to them, “A dog returns to its own vomit,”<note placement="foot">A paraphrased quotation from <reference osisRef="Prov.26.11">Prov 26:11</reference></note> and “A sow, after<note placement="foot">*Here “after” is supplied as a component of the participle (“washing herself”) which is understood as temporal</note> washing herself, returns<note placement="foot">*The verb “returns” is not in the Greek text, but is an understood repetition from the previous clause</note> to wallowing in the mud.”<note placement="foot">The source of this quotation is uncertain</note>  <chapter eID="2Pet.2"/>

verses.name: II Peter 3:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12043"/><title type="x-s">The Coming Day of the Lord</title> <div sID="gen27901" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12043"/>Dear friends, this <transChange type="added">is</transChange> already the second letter I am writing to you, in <transChange type="added">both of</transChange> which I am attempting to stir up your sincere mind by a reminder,

verses.name: II Peter 3:2
verses.text: to remember the words proclaimed beforehand by the holy prophets and the commandment of the Lord and Savior through your apostles,

verses.name: II Peter 3:3
verses.text: above all knowing this, that in the last days scoffers will come with scoffing, following according to their own desires

verses.name: II Peter 3:4
verses.text: and saying, “Where is the promise of his coming? For <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞ever since⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “from which time”</note> the fathers fell asleep, all <transChange type="added">things</transChange> have continued just as they have been from the beginning of creation.”

verses.name: II Peter 3:5
verses.text: For <transChange type="added">when</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “when” is supplied as a component of the participle (“maintain”) which is understood as temporal</note> they maintain this, it escapes <transChange type="added">their</transChange> notice that the heavens existed long ago and the earth held together out of water and through water by the word of God,

verses.name: II Peter 3:6
verses.text: by means of which things the world that existed at that time was destroyed <transChange type="added">by</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“being inundated”) which is understood as means</note> being inundated with water.

verses.name: II Peter 3:7
verses.text: But by the same word the present heavens and earth are reserved for fire, being kept for the day of judgment and destruction of ungodly people.  <div eID="gen27901" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Peter 3:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12044"/><div sID="gen27902" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12044"/>Now, dear friends, do not let this one thing escape your <transChange type="added">notice</transChange>, that one day with the Lord <transChange type="added">is</transChange> like a thousand years, and a thousand years <transChange type="added">is</transChange> like one day.

verses.name: II Peter 3:9
verses.text: The Lord is not delaying the promise, as some consider slowness, but is being patient toward you, <transChange type="added">because he</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“want”) which is understood as causal</note> does not want any to perish, but all to come to repentance.

verses.name: II Peter 3:10
verses.text: But the day of the Lord will come like a thief, in which the heavens will disappear with a rushing noise, and the celestial bodies will be destroyed <transChange type="added">by</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“being burned up”) which is understood as means</note> being burned up, and the earth and the deeds <transChange type="added">done</transChange> on it will be disclosed.

verses.name: II Peter 3:11
verses.text: <transChange type="added">Because</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“are being destroyed”) which is understood as causal</note> all these things are being destroyed in this way, what sort of <transChange type="added">people</transChange> must you be in holy behavior and godliness,

verses.name: II Peter 3:12
verses.text: <transChange type="added">while</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “while” is supplied as a component of the participle (“waiting for”) which is understood as temporal</note> waiting for and hastening the coming of the day of God, because of which the heavens will be destroyed by<note placement="foot">*Here “by” is supplied as a component of the participle (“being burned up”) which is understood as means</note> being burned up and the celestial bodies will melt as they<note placement="foot">*Here “as” is supplied as a component of the participle (“are consumed by heat”) which is understood as temporal</note> are consumed by heat!

verses.name: II Peter 3:13
verses.text: But according to his promise, we are waiting for new heavens and a new earth in which righteousness resides.  <div eID="gen27902" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Peter 3:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12045"/><title type="x-s">Final Exhortations and Conclusion</title> <div sID="gen27903" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12045"/>Therefore, dear friends, <transChange type="added">because you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“are waiting for”) which is understood as causal</note> are waiting for these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, make every effort to be found at peace, spotless and unblemished in him.

verses.name: II Peter 3:15
verses.text: And regard the patience of our Lord as salvation, just as also our dear brother Paul wrote to you, according to the wisdom that was given to him,

verses.name: II Peter 3:16
verses.text: as <transChange type="added">he does</transChange> also in all his<note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note><note placement="foot">Some manuscripts do not explicitly state “his”</note> letters, speaking in them about these <transChange type="added">things</transChange>, in which there are some <transChange type="added">things</transChange> hard to understand, which the ignorant and unstable distort to their own destruction, as <transChange type="added">they</transChange> also <transChange type="added">do</transChange> the rest of the scriptures.

verses.name: II Peter 3:17
verses.text: Therefore, dear friends, <transChange type="added">because you</transChange><note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“know beforehand”) which is understood as causal</note> know this beforehand, guard yourselves so that you do not lose your own safe position because you<note placement="foot">*Here “because” is supplied as a component of the participle (“have been led away”) which is understood as causal</note> have been led away by the error of lawless persons.

verses.name: II Peter 3:18
verses.text: But grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. To him <transChange type="added">be</transChange> the glory, both now and to the day of eternity. Amen.  <chapter eID="2Pet.3"/> <div eID="gen27903" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen27892" osisID="2Pet" type="book"/>

verses.name: I John 1:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12046"/><title type="x-s">Prologue</title> <div sID="gen27905" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12046"/>What was from the beginning, what we have heard, what we have seen with our eyes, what we have looked at and our hands have touched, concerning the word of life—

verses.name: I John 1:2
verses.text: and the life was revealed, and we have seen and testify and announce to you the eternal life which was with the Father and was revealed to us—

verses.name: I John 1:3
verses.text: what we have seen and heard, we announce to you also, in order that you also may have fellowship with us, and indeed our fellowship <transChange type="added">is</transChange> with the Father and with his Son Jesus Christ.

verses.name: I John 1:4
verses.text: And these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> we write, in order that our joy may be complete.  <div eID="gen27905" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I John 1:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12047"/><title type="x-s">God is Light, so Walk in the Light</title> <div sID="gen27906" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12047"/>And this is the message which we have heard from him and announce to you, that God is light and there <transChange type="added">is</transChange> no darkness in him at all.

verses.name: I John 1:6
verses.text: If we say that we have fellowship with him and walk in the darkness, we lie and do not practice the truth.<note placement="foot">Or “we are lying and are not practicing the truth”</note>

verses.name: I John 1:7
verses.text: But if we walk in the light as he is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus his Son cleanses us from all sin.

verses.name: I John 1:8
verses.text: If we say that we do not have sin, we deceive ourselves and the truth is not in us.

verses.name: I John 1:9
verses.text: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just, so that he will forgive us <transChange type="added">our</transChange><note placement="foot">*Literally “the”; the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun</note> sins and will cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

verses.name: I John 1:10
verses.text: If we say that we have not sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us.  <chapter eID="1John.1"/>

verses.name: I John 2:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12048"/><title type="x-s">Keeping the New Commandment</title> <div sID="gen27907" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12048"/>My little children, I am writing these <transChange type="added">things</transChange> to you in order that you may not sin. And if anyone sins, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous <transChange type="added">one</transChange>,

verses.name: I John 2:2
verses.text: and he<note placement="foot">Or “he himself” (emphatic)</note> is the propitiation<note placement="foot">Or “expiation”; or “atoning sacrifice”</note> for our sins, and not for ours only, but also for <transChange type="added">the sins of</transChange> the whole world.

verses.name: I John 2:3
verses.text: And by this we know that we have come to know him, if we keep his commandments.

verses.name: I John 2:4
verses.text: The one who says “I have come to know him,” and does not keep his commandments is a liar, and the truth is not in this person.

verses.name: I John 2:5
verses.text: But whoever keeps his word, truly in this person the love of God has been perfected. By this we know that we are in him.

verses.name: I John 2:6
verses.text: The one who says <transChange type="added">that he</transChange> resides in him ought also to walk<note placement="foot">Some manuscripts have “to walk in this way”</note> just as that one walked.  <div eID="gen27907" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I John 2:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12049"/><div sID="gen27908" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12049"/>Dear friends, I am not writing a new commandment to you, but an old commandment which you have had from the beginning. The old commandment is the message which you have heard.

verses.name: I John 2:8
verses.text: Again, I am writing a new commandment to you, which is true in him and in you, because<note placement="foot">Or perhaps “that”</note> the darkness is passing away and the true light already is shining.

verses.name: I John 2:9
verses.text: The one who says <transChange type="added">he</transChange> is in the light and hates his brother is in the darkness until now.

verses.name: I John 2:10
verses.text: The one who loves his brother resides in the light, and <transChange type="added">there</transChange> is no cause for stumbling in him.

verses.name: I John 2:11
verses.text: But the one who hates his brother is in the darkness, and walks in the darkness, and does not know where he is going, because the darkness has blinded his eyes.  <div eID="gen27908" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I John 2:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12050"/><title type="x-s">Encouragement and Assurance</title> <div sID="gen27909" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12050"/>I am writing to you, little children, because<note placement="foot">Or “that”</note> your sins have been forgiven you on account of his name.

verses.name: I John 2:13
verses.text: I am writing to you, fathers, because<note placement="foot">Or “that”</note> you have known the One who is from the beginning. I am writing to you, young men, because<note placement="foot">Or “that”</note> you have conquered the evil one.

verses.name: I John 2:14
verses.text: I have written to you, children, because<note placement="foot">Or “that”</note> you have known the Father. I have written to you, fathers, because<note placement="foot">Or “that”</note> you have known the One who is from the beginning. I have written to you, young men, because<note placement="foot">Or “that”</note> you are strong, and the word of God resides in you, and you have conquered the evil one.  <div eID="gen27909" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I John 2:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12051"/><title type="x-s">Do Not Love the World</title> <div sID="gen27910" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12051"/>Do not love the world or the things in the world. If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him,

verses.name: I John 2:16
verses.text: because everything <transChange type="added">that is</transChange> in the world—the desire of the flesh and the desire of the eyes and the arrogance of material possessions—is not from the Father, but is from the world.

verses.name: I John 2:17
verses.text: And the world is passing away, and its desire,<note placement="foot">Or “and the desire for it”</note> but the one who does the will of God remains <milestone type="x-idiom-start"/>⌞forever⌟<milestone type="x-idiom-end"/><note placement="foot">Literally “for the age”</note>.  <div eID="gen27910" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I John 2:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12052"/><title type="x-s">Departure of the False Teachers</title> <div sID="gen27911" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12052"/>Children, it is the last hour, and just as you have heard that antichrist is coming, even now many antichrists have arisen, by which we know that it is the last hour.

verses.name: I John 2:19
verses.text: They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would have remained with us. But <transChange type="added">they went out</transChange><note placement="foot">*This is an understood repetition of the phrase “they went out” from the beginning of v. <reference osisRef="1John.2.19">19</reference></note>, in order that it might be shown that all of them are not of us.  <div eID="gen27911" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I John 2:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12053"/><div sID="gen27912" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12053"/>And you have an anointing from the Holy One, and you all know.

verses.name: I John 2:21
verses.text: I have not written to you because<note placement="foot">Or “that”</note> you do not know the truth, but because<note placement="foot">Or “that”</note> you do know it, and because<note placement="foot">Or “that”</note> every lie is not of the truth.

verses.name: I John 2:22
verses.text: Who is the liar except the one who denies that Jesus is the Christ? This person is the antichrist, the one who denies the Father and the Son.

verses.name: I John 2:23
verses.text: Everyone who denies the Son does not have the Father <transChange type="added">either</transChange>; the one who confesses the Son has the Father also.  <div eID="gen27912" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I John 2:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12054"/><div sID="gen27913" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12054"/><transChange type="added">As for</transChange> you, what you have heard from the beginning must remain in you. If what you have heard from the beginning remains in you, you also will remain in the Son and in the Father.

verses.name: I John 2:25
verses.text: And this is the promise which he himself promised us: eternal life.

verses.name: I John 2:26
verses.text: These <transChange type="added">things</transChange> I have written to you concerning the ones who are trying to deceive you.  <div eID="gen27913" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I John 2:27
